analyzers/Analyze.ml
19118
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Analyze.mli *)

module D = Datalog

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

let usage = "usage: mini-analyze [-r rules-dir] [-Idir] [-Dname=value] [-L lib] [-facts | -flow | -flow-answers] [-dead | -caps | -exn | -bugs] [-root f]... file.c|file.ml...   (-h: how)"

let help = {|usage: mini-analyze [-r rules-dir] [-Idir] [-Dname=value] [-L lib] [-facts | -flow | -flow-answers] [-dead | -caps | -exn | -bugs] [-root f]... file.c|file.ml...
The C files read as one program, each call through a pointer said with the
functions it may reach, by an analysis of where each pointer may point
(points_to/'s: Andersen's first pass, then a context file, -context):
  mini-analyze -r analyzers/datalog -I include prog/*.c
  walk.c:56: in walk, through f: hide, show
  main.c:76: in main, through table[]: show
and the bugs the same answers show (bugs/pointers.dl), each a "may":
  bug? bugs.c:65: in main, free may be given a string (line 64), not the heap's
  bug? bugs.c: scratch may return the address of tmp[], a local of scratch
The ML files the same, with the library's units they name (lib_core's, by
-L): each call of a function held in a variable, which functions it may
reach (Andersen's, by object: a closure is a pointer to a function), and the
program's functions that its toplevel never reaches (calls.dl):
  mini-analyze tests/ml/handlers/*.ml
  Events.ml:15: in Events:fun at line 15, through h.on_key: Events.beep, Main:fun at line 4
  Events.ml:17: in Events.twice, through f: Events.log
  never reached: Events.unused (Events.ml:19)
-dead: instead, what no run can reach (dead.dl), from main and the toplevels:
  dead.c:12: dead: unused, nothing names it
  dead.c:18: dead: hide, named only by dead code: unused
  dead.c:24: dead: orphan, in main but no call goes through the pointer
  dead.c:31: dead code: in main, after a return
-caps: instead, whether ML's own functions hold the capabilities they need
(capabilities.dl), from their types' < Cap.x; .. > and what they reach:
  Log.ml:5: Log.log: no capability, needs Cap.stdout (Pervasives.print_string)
  Fs.ml:9: Fs.get: has < Cap.stdout >, needs Cap.open_in|Cap.open_out (Unix.openfile)
  Run.ml:3: Run.go: has < Cap.fork; Cap.stdout >, may not need Cap.fork
-exn: instead, the exceptions an ML program's toplevels may let escape
(exceptions.dl), with where they may be raised:
  Main.ml: the toplevel may let Empty escape, raised at Main.ml:11 (Main.first)
-bugs: instead, an ML program's bugs that may be, each named by its analysis
(docs/plans/done/plan_bug_analyses.md; C's are bugs/pointers.dl's, above):
  Before.ml:6: physeq: in Before.loop, != of a Some made there: always true
  Css.ml:13: stack: Css.components calls itself, not a tail call, over a list
  Process.ml:46: swallowed: in fork, Sys_error silenced, a constant answered
  Sha1.ml:6: int31: in Sha1's toplevel, 0xffffffff: not on the Pi 1's 31 bits
  Unbox.ml:129: order: in Unbox.func, a table's order reaches the output at
  Asm.ml:214
  Poly1305.ml: init: Poly1305's start reads Bignum.modulus (in Poly1305's
  toplevel), Bignum starting after it (-start: the units' order, mini-ml's)
  TinyMachine.ml:66: race: console_type, run by a signal's handler
  (TinyMachine.ml:52), writes a console's queue, as console_poll does
  Event.ml:70: wait: in Event.basic_sync, Condition.wait not in a while
  CLI.ml:31: leak: in CLI.read_file, taken here, given back at CLI.ml:33,
  not when CLI.ml:32 raises End_of_file
  given C files and ML ones (the runtime's, lib_core's): each external's
  [@@raise E] against what its C raises (bugs/raises.dl)
-root f: f is also entered from where the facts do not go (assembly)
-start "units": their order of start, mini-ml -start's, for -bugs's init
-context file: of points_to/, C's (call1_heap1), -exn's (call1_rec) and
  -bugs's (insensitive); the sharper, the longer
-library: every function may be called from outside, not main alone: a runtime
  ML calls, a library; without it what main does not reach is not looked at
-r: the directory of points_to/ and the .dl files (analyzers/datalog)
-I, -D: as mini-cc's; -L: lib_core's directory (lib_core)
-facts, -flow, -flow-answers: facts printed, nothing analyzed. -facts: the
facts the analyses load, not the analysis; -alone: an ML file's own facts, without those of the
library units it names; -no-models: List's, Hashtbl's and @'s code read as
written, not their models at each call (analyzers/ml/Models: to compare, slower)
-flow: ML's files each as its functions in SSA form, the facts of
analyzers/datalog/liveness_ssa.dl and dominators.dl (Ssa_facts, by mini-ml's
own way to its SSA: Ml_flow); C's as each function's stack code, the facts of
liveness.dl (Ir_facts, by mini-cc's simple back end: C_flow); -flow-answers:
the compiler's own answers on those facts, its liveness (ML's dominators
too), what the rules must find (analyzers/ml/tests/ and analyzers/c/tests/):
  mini-analyze -flow -L lib_core fact.ml > fact.dl
  mini-datalog -q 'live_in(V, B)' analyzers/datalog/liveness_ssa.dl fact.dl
  mini-analyze -flow hello.c > flow.dl
  mini-datalog -q 'across_call(V, P)' analyzers/datalog/liveness.dl flow.dl|}

module C = Ix_analyze_c

(* the C program's report, the facts given with bugs/pointers.dl's kinds of
 * places (C_report); the ML program's (Ml_report): mini-analyze
 * -dotnet's too (analyzers/dotnet/Analyze_rt) *)
module R = C_report

let locate = R.locate
let given = R.given
let report = R.report
let ml_report = Ml_report.ml_report

let dead_report = Dead_report.dead_report
let caps_report = Caps_report.caps_report
let exn_report = Exn_report.exn_report
let bugs_report = Bugs_report.bugs_report
let raises_report = Bugs_report.raises_report

(* a fact as a line, for -facts *)
let line (relation : string) (args : C.Facts.arg list) : string =
  let show = function C.Facts.Sym s -> "'" ^ String.concat "\\'" (String.split_on_char '\'' s) ^ "'" | C.Facts.Num n -> string_of_int n in
  relation ^ "(" ^ String.concat ", " (List.map show args) ^ ")."

(* a file's unit: Bugs.ml, Bugs *)
let unit_of_file (f : string) : string =
  String.capitalize_ascii (Filename.remove_extension (Filename.basename f))

(* bugs/intwidth.dl's unit_dir: the directories of a unit's file from
 * the top of the tree, lib_core's parent: kernels, kernels/lib_machine,
 * kernels/lib_machine/pi4, whether read from kernels/9pi or the top *)
let dirs_from (caps : < Cap.readdir; .. >) (lib : string) (file : string) :
    string list =
  let parts (s : string) : string list =
    let s =
      if Filename.is_relative s then Filename.concat (FS.getcwd caps ()) s
      else s in
    List.rev
      (List.fold_left
         (fun (acc : string list) (c : string) ->
           match c with
           | "" | "." -> acc
           | ".." -> (match acc with _ :: r -> r | [] -> [])
           | c -> c :: acc)
         [] (String.split_on_char '/' s)) in
  let rec under (top : string list) (l : string list) : string list option =
    match top, l with
    | [], l -> Some l
    | t :: ts, c :: cs when t = c -> under ts cs
    | _ -> None in
  if file = "" then []
  else
    match under (parts (Filename.dirname lib)) (parts (Filename.dirname file)) with
    | None -> []
    | Some ds ->
        List.mapi
          (fun (k : int) _ ->
            String.concat "/" (List.filteri (fun j _ -> j <= k) ds))
          ds

(* bugs/init.dl's: unit_start; starts_before, the units' starts in
 * -start's order, or (none given) the library's before the files', no
 * order known among either; unit_file, Ml_front.homes *)
let start_facts (fact : string -> C.Facts.arg list -> unit) (start : string)
    (ml : string list) : unit =
  let read (u : string) : bool =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f <> "" | None -> false in
  let sym (s : string) : C.Facts.arg = C.Facts.Sym s in
  let init (u : string) : C.Facts.arg = sym (u ^ ":init") in
  Hashtbl.iter
    (fun (u : string) _ -> if read u then fact "unit_start" [ sym u; init u ])
    Ml_front.files;
  let before (u : string) (v : string) : unit =
    fact "starts_before" [ init u; init v ] in
  let rec in_order (l : string list) : unit =
    match l with
    | [] -> ()
    | u :: more -> List.iter (before u) more; in_order more in
  if start <> "" then
    in_order (List.filter read (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.trim start)))
  else begin
    let unit_of (f : string) : string =
      String.capitalize_ascii (Filename.remove_extension (Filename.basename f)) in
    let mine = List.map unit_of ml in
    Hashtbl.iter
      (fun (u : string) _ ->
        if read u && not (List.mem u mine) then List.iter (before u) mine)
      Ml_front.files
  end;
  Hashtbl.iter
    (fun (u : string) (fs : string list) ->
      List.iter (fun (f : string) -> fact "unit_file" [ sym u; sym f ]) fs)
    Ml_front.homes

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : int =
  let rules = ref "analyzers/datalog" and lib = ref "lib_core" and only = ref false and incs = ref [] and defs = ref [] and files = ref [] in
  let dead = ref false and ambient = ref false and roots = ref [] and context = ref "" and library = ref false in
  let fingerprint = ref false and exns = ref false and flow = ref false and answers = ref false in
  let bugs = ref false and start = ref "" in
  let options =
    Logging.flags
    @ [ ("-r", Arg.Set_string rules, " the directory of points_to/ and bugs/");
        ("-facts", Arg.Set only, " the facts, not the analysis");
        ("-alone", Arg.Set Ml_front.alone, " ML: the files' facts alone, not their library's units'");
        ("-no-models", Arg.Clear Models.on, " ML: List's and Hashtbl's code as written, not their models");
        ("-summaries",
         Arg.String
           (fun (f : string) ->
             Models.derived_on := true;
             List.iter (fun (s, m) -> Hashtbl.replace Models.derived s m)
               (Summaries.of_text (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f)))),
         " file: ML: the library's summaries derived from its code (analyzers/summaries/), Models' own for the rest");
        ("-flow", Arg.Set flow, " ML's functions in SSA form, C's stack code, as facts");
        ("-flow-answers", Arg.Set answers,
         " the compiler's own liveness and dominators on -flow's facts, as facts");
        ("-dead", Arg.Set dead, " what no run can reach, not the calls and the bugs");
        ("-caps", Arg.Set ambient, " whether ML's own functions hold the capabilities they need");
        ("-exn", Arg.Set exns, " the exceptions ML's toplevels may let escape");
        ("-bugs", Arg.Set bugs, " the bugs an ML program may have (plan_bug_analyses.md)");
        ("-start", Arg.Set_string start,
         " ML: the units in the order they start, as mini-ml -start's (-bugs)");
        ("-root", Arg.String (fun f -> roots := f :: !roots), " a function entered from where the facts do not go");
        ("-context", Arg.Set_string context, " the context file of points_to/: C's (call1_heap1), -exn's (call1_rec)");
        ("-library", Arg.Set library, " every function may be called from outside: a runtime, a library");
        ("-fingerprint", Arg.Set fingerprint, " after the report, one number of every answer (Answers, Fingerprint)");
        ("-L", Arg.Set_string lib, " lib_core's directory, for an ML program's library");
        ("-I", Arg.String (fun d -> incs := d :: !incs), " a directory of #include's");
        ("-D", Arg.String (fun d -> defs := d :: !defs), " name=value, as #define") ] in
  (* (-Idir and -Dx in one word too, as mini-cc's) *)
  let split a =
    if String.length a > 2 && (String.sub a 0 2 = "-I" || String.sub a 0 2 = "-D") then [ String.sub a 0 2; String.sub a 2 (String.length a - 2) ]
    else [ a ] in
  let argv = Array.of_list (List.concat_map split (Array.to_list argv)) in
  match Arg.parse_argv argv options (fun (f : string) -> files := f :: !files) usage with
  | exception Arg.Help _ -> Console.print caps (help ^ "\n"); 0
  | exception Arg.Bad msg -> Console.eprint caps msg; 1
  | () -> (
      (* (-exn's: a recursive call in its caller's context, else
       * List.fold_left's callers are one: exceptions.dl's design note) *)
      let context = if !context <> "" then !context else if !exns then "call1_rec" else if !bugs then "insensitive" else "call1_heap1" in
      let path s = match FS.path s with Ok p -> p | Error m -> failwith m in
      try
        if !files = [] then failwith usage;
        let incs = List.map path (List.rev !incs) in
        if !flow || !answers then begin
          let mls = List.filter (fun f -> not (Filename.check_suffix f ".c")) !files in
          let own_dirs = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map (fun f -> Fpath.parent (path f)) mls) in
          let dirs = own_dirs @ incs @ Ml_front.library caps !lib in
          List.fold_left
            (fun status (f : string) ->
              let c own =
                C.C_flow.file caps ~own (List.rev !defs, incs) (path f) in
              (* (C's: mini-cc's stack code, Ir_facts) *)
              if Filename.check_suffix f ".c" then
                let none = Ok "" in
                match (if !flow then c false else none),
                      (if !answers then c true else none) with
                | Ok a, Ok b -> Console.print caps (a ^ b); status
                | Error m, _ | _, Error m -> Console.eprint caps (m ^ "\n"); 1
              else
              match Ml_flow.file ~sites:true caps dirs (path f) with
              | Ok fns ->
                  let unit_name = unit_of_file f in
                  if !flow then
                    List.iter (fun fn -> Console.print caps (Ssa_facts.func ~unit_name fn)) fns;
                  if !answers then List.iter (fun fn -> Console.print caps (Ssa_facts.own fn)) fns;
                  status
              | Error m -> Console.eprint caps (m ^ "\n"); 1)
            0 (List.rev !files)
        end
        else
        let failed = ref 0 in
        let p = D.create () in
        let ml, c = List.partition (fun f -> Filename.check_suffix f ".ml") (List.rev !files) in
        let text = Buffer.create 4096 in
        let fact = if !only then (fun r args -> Buffer.add_string text (line r args ^ "\n")) else given p in
        if not !only then
          List.iter
            (fun (r : string) ->
              let rules = Fpath.append (path !rules) (Fpath.v r) in
              D.load p ~from:(Fpath.to_string rules) (FS.read caps rules))
            (if !dead || !ambient then
               [ "points_to/instructions.dl"; "points_to/contexts.dl"; "points_to/insensitive.dl"; "dead.dl" ]
               @ if !ambient then [ "capabilities.dl" ] else []
             else if !bugs && c <> [] && ml <> [] then [ "bugs/raises.dl" ]
             else if !bugs && c = [] then
               [ "points_to/instructions.dl"; "points_to/contexts.dl"; "points_to/" ^ context ^ ".dl"; "exceptions.dl";
                 "bugs/physeq.dl"; "bugs/stack.dl"; "bugs/swallowed.dl";
                 "bugs/intwidth.dl"; "bugs/order.dl"; "bugs/init.dl";
                 "bugs/races.dl"; "bugs/pairs.dl";
                 "bugs/unused.dl"; "bugs/layout.dl"; "bugs/evalorder.dl" ]
             else if !exns then
               [ "points_to/instructions.dl"; "points_to/andersen.dl"; "points_to/contexts.dl";
                 "points_to/" ^ context ^ ".dl"; "exceptions.dl" ]
             else
               [ "points_to/instructions.dl"; "points_to/andersen.dl" ]
               @ (if c <> [] then [ "points_to/contexts.dl"; "points_to/" ^ context ^ ".dl"; "bugs/pointers.dl" ] else [])
               @ if ml <> [] then [ "calls.dl" ] else []);
        List.iter (fun (f : string) -> given p "entry" [ C.Facts.Sym f ]) !roots;
        if !library then D.load p ~from:"-library" "entry(F) :- function(F).\n";
        C.Facts.added := fact;
        Closure_facts.added :=
          (fun r args -> fact r (List.map (function Closure_facts.Sym s -> C.Facts.Sym s | Closure_facts.Num n -> C.Facts.Num n) args));
        List.iter
          (fun (f : string) ->
            Logs.info (fun m -> m "reading %s" f);
            match C.C_front.file caps (List.rev !defs, incs) (path f) with
            | Ok () -> ()
            | Error m -> Console.eprint caps (m ^ "\n"); incr failed)
          c;
        if ml <> [] then
          List.iter (fun m -> Console.eprint caps (m ^ "\n"); incr failed) (Ml_front.program caps (incs @ Ml_front.library caps !lib) (List.map path ml));
        if !bugs then start_facts (given p) !start ml;
        (* (the program's own files in SSA form, their calls named as
         * Closure_facts' sites: bugs/pairs.dl's paths, ssa_ before each
         * relation; a file mini-ml's lowering refuses, none) *)
        if !bugs then begin
          (* (the units it names in each of the program's directories,
           * _mk's generated parsers, a subfolder's) *)
          let own_dirs = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map (fun f -> Fpath.parent (path f)) ml) in
          let dirs = own_dirs @ incs @ Ml_front.library caps !lib in
          List.iter
            (fun (f : string) ->
              let unit_name = unit_of_file f in
              match Ml_flow.file ~sites:true caps dirs (path f) with
              | Ok fns ->
                  List.iter
                    (fun fn -> D.load p ~from:f (Ssa_facts.func ~prefix:"ssa_" ~unit_name fn))
                    fns
              | Error m -> Logs.info (fun l -> l "no SSA: %s" m))
            ml;
        end;
        if !bugs then
          Hashtbl.iter
            (fun (u : string) (f : string) ->
              List.iter
                (fun (d : string) ->
                  given p "unit_dir" [ C.Facts.Sym u; C.Facts.Sym d ])
                (dirs_from caps !lib f))
            Ml_front.files;
        (* (what they call would be reported dead) *)
        if !dead || !ambient then List.iter (fun m -> Console.eprint caps ("not read: " ^ m ^ "\n"); incr failed) !Ml_front.unread;
        if !ambient || !bugs then
          Hashtbl.iter (fun u () -> given p "own_unit" [ C.Facts.Sym u ]; given p "own_init" [ C.Facts.Sym (u ^ ":init") ]) Ml_front.own;
        if !only then Console.print caps (Buffer.contents text)
        else begin
          ignore (Datalog_eval.run ~naive:false p);
          if !ambient then caps_report caps p
          else if !exns then exn_report caps p
          else if !dead then dead_report caps p (ml <> [])
          else if !bugs && c <> [] && ml <> [] then raises_report caps p
          else if !bugs && c = [] then bugs_report caps p
          else begin
            if c <> [] then report caps p;
            if ml <> [] then ml_report caps p
          end;
          if !fingerprint then Console.print caps ("fingerprint of the answers: " ^ Answers.hex (Answers.fingerprint p) ^ "\n")
        end;
        if !failed > 0 then 1 else 0
      with
      | D.Error (msg, at) -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s\n" at msg); 1
      | Failure msg | Sys_error msg -> Console.eprint caps (msg ^ "\n"); 1)
analyzers/Analyze.mli
5091
(* mini-analyze: a whole program's calls through pointers, which
 * functions each may reach, and the bugs the same answers show (a
 * free of what no allocator gave, a function returning its frame's
 * address: bugs/pointers.dl) (docs/plans/done/plan_dotnet_languages.md, its step 0). One program of three parts that were three commands:
 * mini-cc's front end reads the C files, Facts says each function as
 * the facts of a pointer analysis (mini-cc -facts), and mini-datalog's
 * evaluator runs analyzers/datalog/points_to/'s rules on them; the answers
 * are read back here, not printed by another program.
 *
 *    a.c b.c ...                   points_to/, bugs/ (the rules, read at run time)
 *        |                              |
 *    mini-cc's front end                |
 *    (Pre, Lexer, Parser, Declare)      |
 *        |  each function's tree        |
 *    Facts: assign(p, q).  ...          |
 *        |  each a tuple, as found      v
 *    Datalog.add ----------------> Datalog_eval.run
 *                                       |  target(I, F), pts(V, M)
 *                                  the report: a.c:12: in walk, through f: hide, show
 *
 *     mini-analyze -r analyzers/datalog prog/*.c
 *
 * With -dead, other rules on the same facts and another report: what no
 * run can reach from main and the toplevels (dead.dl, whose header says
 * why from the roots, and what is taken as alive).
 *
 * A call's site is Facts's name, the function and the global line
 * (_in_walk_line_56_1); the line is found back in its file by the
 * #includes' history (Pre.history, 5c's), as the linker does.
 *
 * design:
 * The facts pass from Facts to Datalog as values (Facts.added, a
 * tuple of symbols each), where they were text between the commands;
 * next, each part in the language that suits it, compiled to .NET's
 * IL: the front end ML, the rules a Datalog module, the report maybe
 * C#. The boundaries are here to be seen first. mini-cc's front end
 * is compiled a second time, wrapped (c/): mini-ml's and mini-cc's
 * units share names (Lexer, Parser, Emit) in OCaml's one namespace,
 * which .NET's assemblies and namespaces would keep apart.
 * Where the time goes, Plan 9's rc (goken's, 30 files, 215
 * functions): the front end 0.3 s for 7,850 facts, the rules 7 s
 * (29 rounds, 20 million lookups for 44,000 tuples): the evaluator,
 * which a Datalog compiled (Soufflé's way, the plan's decision 5)
 * is for.
 * Datalog or OCaml: what is a fixpoint over the whole program is
 * Datalog's (what points where, the call graph, where an exception
 * may go, what a handler or a unit's start runs, where a table's
 * order flows). Written in OCaml, each analysis would write its own
 * worklist and closure again; here they are points_to/'s and
 * exceptions.dl's relations, and an analysis is 10 to 50 lines of
 * joins over them (bugs/races.dl 30, bugs/init.dl 10), its negations
 * checked by the strata, each relation between asked by mini-datalog
 * -q while it is written. What is local, in order or of the syntax
 * is OCaml's, the facts' (Closure_facts' in_loop, a call in a while;
 * wide_int, a literal), and so are numbers and their intervals (a
 * lattice, which plain Datalog has not) and the reports, each as long
 * as its rules. bugs/pairs.dl is on the line: whether a call between
 * an open and its close may raise is the call graph's, Datalog's, but
 * the order of a function's calls is only the walk's (call_seq), its
 * branches one after the other; a pass over the tree, or the SSA's
 * blocks, would say it exactly.
 *
 * others:
 * Doop (Martin Bravenboer, Yannis Smaragdakis, OOPSLA 2009) runs
 * Datalog's pointer analyses on Java's bytecode, its facts made by a
 * separate program (Soot), first on LogicBlox's engine, then Soufflé's;
 * there the analyses of twenty years (Andersen's, k-CFA, object and
 * type sensitivity) are each a choice of contexts in the same rules,
 * which is where pointer.dl would grow: a context a column more
 * (calls.dl says how). Both split the work as here: a front end
 * makes the local facts, the rules the whole program's. Infer
 * (Facebook, from Cristiano Calcagno and others' bi-abduction, POPL
 * 2009) is the other way, all in OCaml: abstract interpretation, a
 * summary for each function. CodeQL (Semmle, from .QL, Oege de Moor, 2007)
 * a database of a program's facts queried in a Datalog with classes;
 * Flix (Magnus Madsen, 2016) the rules inside the language that makes
 * the facts.
 *
 * References: Martin Bravenboer, Yannis Smaragdakis, "Strictly
 * declarative specification of sophisticated points-to analyses"
 * (OOPSLA 2009); Yannis Smaragdakis, George Balatsouras, "Pointer
 * Analysis" (Foundations and Trends in Programming Languages, 2015). *)

 * own line, by the history (the oldest first) *)
val locate : (string option * int) list -> int -> (string * int) option

val main : < caps; .. > -> string array -> int

(* See C_flow.mli *)

(* (was mini-cc's flow_backend) *)
let file (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) ~(own : bool) (defs, incs) (file : Fpath.t) :
    (string, string) result =
  let text = Buffer.create 1024 in
  let passes : string list =
    List.filter (fun (p : string) -> p <> "regs") (List.map fst Opti.passes) in
  let init () =
    Check.xcom := Lower.calls64;
    Check.outstring := Emit.outstring;
    Declare.gextern := Emit.gextern;
    Emit.init () in
  let codgen (f : Tree.sym) (body : Tree.stmt) =
    let fn = Opti.run passes (Lower.func f body) in
    Buffer.add_string text (if own then Ir_facts.own fn else Ir_facts.func fn) in
  match C_front.read caps (defs, incs) ~init ~codgen file with
  | Ok () -> Ok (Buffer.contents text)
  | Error m -> Error m

(* A C file's functions as their stack code's facts (Ir_facts), for
 * mini-analyze -flow and -flow-answers: the file read by mini-cc's front end
 * (C_front.read), each function lowered by the simple back end (Lower)
 * and through Opti's passes but regs, as mini-cc -simple -O does. The
 * facts are those of the code mini-cc compiles: Opti's own liveness
 * (-flow-answers) is checked against the rules' (analyzers/c/tests/run.sh).
 *
 * On arm64 (-m 7, the tests'). Was mini-cc -flow and -dflow until
 * 2026-11-02, as ML's (Ml_flow): out of the compilers, so that a
 * change to the facts does not relink them. *)

(* the file's functions' facts, Ir_facts.func's (own: Ir_facts.own's,
 * Opti's liveness); the -D's, the -I's; the error, file and line *)
val file :
  < Cap.open_in; .. > -> own:bool -> string list * Fpath.t list -> Fpath.t ->
  (string, string) result
analyzers/c/C_front.ml
2152
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See C_front.mli *)

let owner : (string, string) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 101
let histories : (string, (string option * int) list) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 17

(* mini-cc's CLI.compile, on arm64, the listing and the object left out:
 * init sets the front end's hooks, codgen is given each function *)
let read (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (defs, incs) ~(init : unit -> unit)
    ~(codgen : Tree.sym -> Tree.stmt -> unit) (file : Fpath.t) :
    (unit, string) result =
  let f = Fpath.to_string file in
  Tree_helpers.mach := Some Machines.arm64;
  Tree_helpers.init_types ();
  Pre.profile := true;
  Lexer.init ();
  let s = Tree_helpers.lookup ".string" in
  let t = Tree_helpers.typ Tree.Tarray (Some (Tree_helpers.ty Tree.Tchar)) in
  t.width <- 0;
  s.sclass <- Tree.Cstatic;
  s.typ <- Some t;
  List.iter Pre.dodefine defs;
  Pre.includes := Fpath.parent file :: incs;
  Pre.read_file := FS.read_opt caps;
  init ();
  Declare.on_function := codgen;
  match FS.read_opt caps file with
  | None -> Error (Printf.sprintf "cannot open %s" f)
  | Some text -> (
      Tree_helpers.lineno := 1;
      Pre.history := [];
      Pre.push_file f text;
      match Parser.prog Lexer.token (Lexer.lexbuf ()) with
      | () -> Hashtbl.replace histories f (List.rev !Pre.history); Ok ()
      | exception Tree_helpers.Error m -> Error (Printf.sprintf "%s:%s" f m)
      | exception Parsing.Parse_error -> Error (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: syntax error" f !Tree_helpers.lineno))

(* no code: the pointer facts (was mini-cc -facts's back end) *)
let file (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (defs, incs) (file : Fpath.t) :
    (unit, string) result =
  let f = Fpath.to_string file in
  let init () =
    Check.xcom := (fun (n : Tree.expr) -> n);
    Check.outstring := (fun (_ : string) (_ : int) -> 0);
    Declare.gextern :=
      (fun (s : Tree.sym) (x : Tree.expr) (o : int) (_ : int) -> Facts.global s x o);
    Emit.init () in
  let codgen (fn : Tree.sym) body =
    Hashtbl.replace owner fn.name f;
    Facts.func fn body in
  read caps (defs, incs) ~init ~codgen file

(* C files through mini-cc's front end into Facts (what was mini-cc
 * -facts: CLI's compile with a facts back end): the facts of a whole
 * program, each file's #includes' history, each function's file *)

(* a file read; its facts added to Facts's; the -D's, the -I's *)
val file : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string list * Fpath.t list -> Fpath.t -> (unit, string) result

(* a file read by mini-cc's front end, on arm64: init sets its hooks
 * (Check's, Declare.gextern), codgen is given each function; the
 * error, file and line (C_flow's way in too) *)
val read :
  < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string list * Fpath.t list -> init:(unit -> unit) ->
  codgen:(Tree.sym -> Tree.stmt -> unit) -> Fpath.t -> (unit, string) result

(* the file a function was read from (the last of that name) *)

(* each file's history of #includes (Pre.history's), the oldest first *)

analyzers/c/Facts.ml
15956
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Facts.mli *)

(* the facts, the last first, and the ones said already *)
let lines : string list ref = ref []
let said : (string, unit) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 1021

(* the function being read, and its temporaries' and its calls' numbers *)
let scope : string ref = ref "_init"
let temps : int ref = ref 0
let calls : int ref = ref 0

(* a fact's argument: a name, or a number (an argument's position) *)
type arg = Sym of string | Num of int

let quote (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s + 2) in
  Buffer.add_char b '\'';
  String.iter (fun (c : char) -> if c = '\'' || c = '\\' then Buffer.add_char b '\\'; Buffer.add_char b c) s;
  Buffer.add_char b '\'';
  Buffer.contents b

let sym (s : string) : arg = Sym s

let added : (string -> arg list -> unit) ref = ref (fun (_ : string) (_ : arg list) -> ())

let fact (relation : string) (args : arg list) : unit =
  let show = function Sym s -> quote s | Num n -> string_of_int n in
  let line = relation ^ "(" ^ String.concat ", " (List.map show args) ^ ")." in
  if not (Hashtbl.mem said line) then begin
    Hashtbl.add said line ();
    lines := line :: !lines;
    !added relation args
  end

let text () : string = String.concat "\n" (List.rev !lines) ^ "\n"

let temp () : string =
  incr temps;
  let t = Printf.sprintf "%s__t%d" !scope !temps in
  fact "var_in" [ sym t; sym !scope ];
  t

(* what holds a value no pointer analysis follows: a number, 0, arithmetic.
 * So a variable with nothing in it is one no run has reached (Closure_facts's
 * scalar): what lets an analysis choose a context by an argument's object *)
let constant () : string =
  fact "var_in" [ sym "_const"; sym !scope ];
  fact "global_var" [ sym "_const" ];
  fact "scalar" [ sym "_const" ];
  "_const"

let some_value (v : string option) : string =
  match v with Some v -> v | None -> constant ()

(* a place a function's frame makes: which function, for type sensitivity *)
let alloc (t : string) (place : string) : unit =
  fact "point_to" [ sym t; sym place ];
  fact "alloc_in" [ sym place; sym !scope ]

let field (s : Tree.sym) : string = "_fld__" ^ s.name

(* a name as the analysis's variable: a local is its function's *)
let variable (x : Tree.expr) (s : Tree.sym) (c : Tree.cls) : string =
  let v : string =
    match c with
    | Tree.Cauto | Tree.Cparam | Tree.Clocal -> !scope ^ "__" ^ s.name
    | _ -> s.name in
  fact "var_in" [ sym v; sym !scope ];
  (* (a static local is one place too, whatever the call) *)
  if c <> Tree.Cauto && c <> Tree.Cparam then fact "global_var" [ sym v ];
  (* an array's elements are one place, which the array's name points to *)
  if x.t.etype = Tree.Tarray then alloc v ("_array_elt_" ^ v);
  v

(* the allocators: each call's result points to a place of its own *)
let allocators : string list = [ "malloc"; "mallocz"; "calloc"; "realloc"; "kalloc"; "smalloc"; "xalloc"; "emalloc"; "sbrk" ]

(* the variable that holds an expression's value; None: nothing a
 * pointer could be (a constant, a comparison) *)
let rec value (x : Tree.expr) : string option =
  match x.e with
  | Tree.Name (s, c, _) -> Some (variable x s c)
  | Tree.Const _ | Tree.Fconst _ | Tree.Reg _ | Tree.Indreg _ | Tree.Sizeof_type _ -> None
  | Tree.Sizeof _ -> None
  | Tree.Str _ | Tree.Lstr _ ->
      let t = temp () in
      alloc t (Printf.sprintf "_str_in_%s_line_%d" !scope x.line);
      Some t
  | Tree.Typed a -> value a
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, { e = Tree.Binary (Tree.Add, a, i); _ }) ->
      (* a[i] *)
      ignore (value i);
      load "assign_array_elt" (value a)
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, a) -> load "assign_content" (value a)
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Addr, a) -> address a
  | Tree.Unary ((Tree.Cast | Tree.Preinc | Tree.Predec | Tree.Postinc | Tree.Postdec | Tree.Pos), a) -> value a
  | Tree.Unary (_, a) ->
      ignore (value a);
      None
  | Tree.Binary ((Tree.Add | Tree.Sub), a, b) -> (
      (* a pointer moved is the same pointer here *)
      let va = value a in
      let vb = value b in
      match va with Some _ -> va | None -> vb)
  | Tree.Binary (Tree.Comma, a, b) ->
      ignore (value a);
      value b
  | Tree.Binary (_, a, b) ->
      ignore (value a);
      ignore (value b);
      None
  | Tree.Assign (_, l, r) ->
      let v = value r in
      store l (Some (some_value v));
      v
  | Tree.Cond (c, a, b) -> (
      ignore (value c);
      let va = value a in
      let vb = value b in
      match (va, vb) with
      | None, None -> None
      | _ ->
          let t = temp () in
          fact "assign" [ sym t; sym (some_value va) ];
          fact "assign" [ sym t; sym (some_value vb) ];
          Some t)
  | Tree.Call (f, args) -> call x f args
  | Tree.Elem (a, s) ->
      let t = temp () in
      Option.iter (fun (v : string) -> fact "assign_load_field" [ sym t; sym v; sym (field s) ]) (structure a);
      Some t
  | Tree.Dot (a, _) -> value a

(* p = *q, p = a[i]: a temporary for what is read *)
and load (relation : string) (from : string option) : string option =
  match from with
  | None -> None
  | Some v ->
      let t = temp () in
      fact relation [ sym t; sym v ];
      Some t

(* the variable that holds a structure's address, for x.m and x->m *)
and structure (a : Tree.expr) : string option =
  match a.e with
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, p) -> value p
  | _ -> address a

(* &x *)
and address (a : Tree.expr) : string option =
  match a.e with
  | Tree.Name (s, c, _) ->
      let v = variable a s c in
      (* (a function's name and an array's are their address already) *)
      if a.t.etype = Tree.Tfunc || a.t.etype = Tree.Tarray then Some v
      else begin
        let t = temp () in
        fact "assign_address" [ sym t; sym v ];
        Some t
      end
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, { e = Tree.Binary (Tree.Add, arr, i); _ }) -> (
      ignore (value i);
      match value arr with
      | None -> None
      | Some v ->
          let t = temp () in
          fact "assign_array_element_address" [ sym t; sym v ];
          Some t)
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, p) -> value p
  | Tree.Elem (b, s) -> (
      match structure b with
      | None -> None
      | Some v ->
          let t = temp () in
          fact "assign_field_address" [ sym t; sym v; sym (field s) ];
          Some t)
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Cast, b) | Tree.Typed b -> address b
  | _ ->
      ignore (value a);
      None

(* l = v *)
and store (l : Tree.expr) (v : string option) : unit =
  let put (relation : string) (target : string option) : unit =
    match (target, v) with
    | Some t, Some v -> fact relation [ sym t; sym v ]
    | _ -> () in
  match l.e with
  | Tree.Name (s, c, _) -> put "assign" (Some (variable l s c))
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, { e = Tree.Binary (Tree.Add, a, i); _ }) ->
      ignore (value i);
      put "assign_array_deref" (value a)
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, p) -> put "assign_deref" (value p)
  | Tree.Elem (a, s) -> (
      match (structure a, v) with
      | Some t, Some v -> fact "assign_store_field" [ sym t; sym (field s); sym v ]
      | _ -> ())
  | Tree.Unary (Tree.Cast, a) | Tree.Typed a -> store a v
  | _ -> ignore (value l)

and call (x : Tree.expr) (f : Tree.expr) (args : Tree.expr list) : string option =
  let values = List.map value args in
  let direct : string option =
    match f.e with
    | Tree.Name (s, c, _) when f.t.etype = Tree.Tfunc && c <> Tree.Cauto && c <> Tree.Cparam -> Some s.name
    | _ -> None in
  let t = temp () in
  match direct with
  | Some name when List.mem name allocators ->
      alloc t (Printf.sprintf "_malloc_in_%s_line_%d" !scope x.line);
      fact "allocator_call" [ sym name; sym !scope ];
      Some t
  | _ ->
      incr calls;
      let site = sym (Printf.sprintf "_in_%s_line_%d_%d" !scope x.line !calls) in
      fact "in_function" [ site; sym !scope ];
      List.iteri
        (fun (i : int) (v : string option) ->
          fact "argument" [ site; Num (i + 1); sym (some_value v) ])
        values;
      fact "call_ret" [ site; sym t ];
      (match direct with
       | Some name -> fact "call_direct" [ site; sym name ]
       | None -> (
           (* a pointer's star called and the pointer called are the same call;
            * not an array's: table[0]() is *table once folded, or table,
            * an element called *)
           let rec bare (x : Tree.expr) : Tree.expr =
             match x.e with
             | Tree.Typed a | Tree.Unary ((Tree.Cast | Tree.Ind), a) | Tree.Binary (Tree.Add, a, _) -> bare a
             | _ -> x in
           let base = bare f in
           let target : string option =
             match base.e with
             | Tree.Name _ when base.t.etype = Tree.Tarray -> load "assign_array_elt" (value base)
             | _ -> (match f.e with Tree.Unary (Tree.Ind, p) -> value p | _ -> value f) in
           match target with
           | Some v -> fact "call_indirect" [ site; sym v ]
           | None -> ()));
      Some t

(* a statement's line, if an expression of it says *)
let rec first_line (s : Tree.stmt) : int option =
  match s with
  | Tree.Expr x | Tree.If (x, _, _) | Tree.While (x, _) | Tree.Switch (x, _) | Tree.Return (Some x, _) -> Some x.line
  | Tree.Dowhile (a, _) | Tree.For (a, _, _, _) -> first_line a
  | Tree.Block l -> List.find_map first_line l
  | _ -> None

(* a label or a case in it, however deep: a way in from elsewhere *)
let rec entered (s : Tree.stmt) : bool =
  match s with
  | Tree.Label _ | Tree.Case _ -> true
  | Tree.Block l -> List.exists entered l
  | Tree.If (_, a, None) -> entered a
  | Tree.If (_, a, Some b) -> entered a || entered b
  | Tree.While (_, a) | Tree.Dowhile (a, _) | Tree.For (_, _, _, a) | Tree.Switch (_, a) -> entered a
  | _ -> false

(* what follows a jump in a block, until a way in, no run reaches *)
let rec after_jumps (jumped : bool) (l : Tree.stmt list) : unit =
  match l with
  | [] -> ()
  | s :: rest when entered s -> after_jumps false rest
  | (Tree.Used _ | Tree.Set _) :: rest -> after_jumps jumped rest
  | s :: rest ->
      if jumped then Option.iter (fun (n : int) -> fact "dead_stmt" [ sym !scope; Num n ]) (first_line s);
      after_jumps
        (jumped || match s with Tree.Return _ | Tree.Goto _ | Tree.Break | Tree.Continue -> true | _ -> false)
        rest

let rec statement (s : Tree.stmt) : unit =
  match s with
  | Tree.Expr x -> ignore (value x)
  | Tree.Block l ->
      after_jumps false l;
      List.iter statement l
  | Tree.If (c, a, b) ->
      ignore (value c);
      statement a;
      Option.iter statement b
  | Tree.While (c, a) | Tree.Dowhile (a, c) | Tree.Switch (c, a) ->
      ignore (value c);
      statement a
  | Tree.For (start, test, step, body) ->
      statement start;
      Option.iter (fun (c : Tree.expr) -> ignore (value c)) test;
      statement step;
      statement body
  | Tree.Return (Some x, _) -> fact "assign" [ sym ("ret_" ^ !scope); sym (some_value (value x)) ]
  | Tree.Used l | Tree.Set l -> List.iter (fun (x : Tree.expr) -> ignore (value x)) l
  | Tree.Case _ | Tree.Label _ | Tree.Goto _ | Tree.Break | Tree.Continue | Tree.Return (None, _) -> ()

(* the parameters' places in the frame, in order, as Declare.argmark
 * lays them: a parameter is known in the body by its place *)
let parameter_offsets (f : Tree.sym) : int list =
  match f.typ with
  | None -> []
  | Some t ->
      let offset = ref (match t.link with Some r -> Declare.align 0 r Declare.Aarg0 | None -> 0) in
      let rec go (p : Tree.typ option) : int list =
        match p with
        | None -> []
        | Some p ->
            offset := Declare.align !offset p Declare.Aarg1;
            let here = !offset in
            offset := Declare.align !offset p Declare.Aarg2;
            here :: go p.down in
      go t.down

(* the parameters the body names: each with its place *)
let rec parameters_in (x : Tree.expr) (acc : (string * int) list ref) : unit =
  let sub (a : Tree.expr) : unit = parameters_in a acc in
  match x.e with
  | Tree.Name (s, Tree.Cparam, offset) -> if not (List.mem_assoc s.name !acc) then acc := (s.name, offset) :: !acc
  | Tree.Name _ | Tree.Const _ | Tree.Fconst _ | Tree.Str _ | Tree.Lstr _ | Tree.Reg _ | Tree.Indreg _ | Tree.Sizeof_type _ -> ()
  | Tree.Unary (_, a) | Tree.Elem (a, _) | Tree.Dot (a, _) | Tree.Sizeof a | Tree.Typed a -> sub a
  | Tree.Binary (_, a, b) | Tree.Assign (_, a, b) -> sub a; sub b
  | Tree.Cond (a, b, c) -> sub a; sub b; sub c
  | Tree.Call (f, args) -> sub f; List.iter sub args

let rec parameters_of (s : Tree.stmt) (acc : (string * int) list ref) : unit =
  let expr (x : Tree.expr) : unit = parameters_in x acc in
  match s with
  | Tree.Expr x -> expr x
  | Tree.Block l -> List.iter (fun (s : Tree.stmt) -> parameters_of s acc) l
  | Tree.If (c, a, b) -> expr c; parameters_of a acc; Option.iter (fun (s : Tree.stmt) -> parameters_of s acc) b
  | Tree.While (c, a) | Tree.Dowhile (a, c) | Tree.Switch (c, a) -> expr c; parameters_of a acc
  | Tree.For (start, test, step, body) ->
      parameters_of start acc; Option.iter expr test; parameters_of step acc; parameters_of body acc
  | Tree.Return (Some x, _) -> expr x
  | Tree.Used l | Tree.Set l -> List.iter expr l
  | Tree.Case _ | Tree.Label _ | Tree.Goto _ | Tree.Break | Tree.Continue | Tree.Return (None, _) -> ()

let func (f : Tree.sym) (body : Tree.stmt) : unit =
  scope := f.name;
  temps := 0;
  calls := 0;
  fact "point_to" [ sym f.name; sym f.name ];
  fact "return" [ sym f.name; sym ("ret_" ^ f.name) ];
  fact "var_in" [ sym ("ret_" ^ f.name); sym f.name ];
  fact "defined" [ sym f.name; Num (match first_line body with Some n -> n | None -> 0) ];
  let named : (string * int) list ref = ref [] in
  parameters_of body named;
  List.iteri
    (fun (i : int) (offset : int) ->
      List.iter
        (fun ((name, o) : string * int) ->
          if o = offset then begin
            fact "parameter" [ sym f.name; Num (i + 1); sym (f.name ^ "__" ^ name) ];
            fact "var_in" [ sym (f.name ^ "__" ^ name); sym f.name ]
          end)
        !named)
    (parameter_offsets f);
  statement body;
  scope := "_init"

(* the member at an offset of a global's type, the innermost, an
 * array's element's when it is an array of structures *)
let rec member (t : Tree.typ) (o : int) : Tree.sym option =
  match t.etype with
  | Tree.Tarray -> (match t.link with Some e when e.width > 0 -> member e (o mod e.width) | _ -> None)
  | Tree.Tstruct | Tree.Tunion ->
      let rec find (m : Tree.typ option) =
        match m with
        | None -> None
        | Some m when o >= m.offset && o < m.offset + max m.width 1 -> (
            match member m (o - m.offset) with Some f -> Some f | None -> m.tsym)
        | Some m -> find m.down in
      find t.link
  | _ -> None

let global (s : Tree.sym) (x : Tree.expr) (o : int) : unit =
  let array : bool = match s.typ with Some t -> t.etype = Tree.Tarray | None -> false in
  fact "var_in" [ sym s.name; sym !scope ];
  fact "global_var" [ sym s.name ];
  fact "global_def" [ sym s.name; sym !scope ];
  if array then fact "point_to" [ sym s.name; sym ("_array_elt_" ^ s.name) ];
  (* a structure's member, by its name as x->f is (Dev consdev = { "cons", consread }) *)
  let put (v : string) : unit =
    match Option.bind s.typ (fun t -> member t o) with
    | Some f -> fact "assign_store_field" [ sym s.name; sym (field f); sym v ]
    | None -> fact (if array then "assign_array_deref" else "assign") [ sym s.name; sym v ] in
  (* a global's initializer is a constant: a name in it is an address,
   * whether the & is still there or the typing has taken it *)
  let rec named (x : Tree.expr) : Tree.expr option =
    match x.e with
    | Tree.Name _ -> Some x
    | Tree.Typed a | Tree.Unary ((Tree.Cast | Tree.Addr), a) -> named a
    | _ -> None in
  match named x with
  | Some n -> Option.iter put (address n)
  | None -> Option.iter put (value x)
analyzers/c/Facts.mli
4745
(* A C file as Datalog facts (docs/plans/plan_prolog.md, stage 8): what
 * each function does to pointers, said in the relations of the
 * author's pointer analysis (analyzers/datalog/pointer.dl, 2014), for
 * mini-datalog to run its rules on. mini-cc -facts.
 *
 * Each expression is made a few simple instructions over variables, a
 * temporary for each value in between (pfff's datalog_c.ml did the
 * same over its own tree; this one is written over Tree, before the
 * typing: a member still has its name there). Nothing is said of the
 * order of the instructions, nor of what is no pointer: the analysis
 * asks neither.
 *
 *   p = q          assign(p, q).              p = &x      assign_address(p, x).
 *   p = *q         assign_content(p, q).      *p = q      assign_deref(p, q).
 *   p = a[i]       assign_array_elt(p, a).    a[i] = q    assign_array_deref(a, q).
 *   p = &a[i]      assign_array_element_address(p, a).
 *   p = x->f       assign_load_field(p, x, F).     x->f = q   assign_store_field(x, F, q).
 *   p = &x->f      assign_field_address(p, x, F).
 *   r = f(a, b)    call_direct(I, f). argument(I, 1, a). argument(I, 2, b). call_ret(I, r).
 *   r = p(a)       call_indirect(I, p). ...   (p a pointer to a function; or its star, called)
 *   a function f   parameter(f, 1, V). return(f, ret_f). point_to(f, f).
 *   "..."          point_to(T, S).            malloc(n)   point_to(T, M).
 *   an array a     point_to(a, E): its elements are one place.
 *
 * And, for what pointer.dl does not ask (analyzers/datalog/points_to/):
 * var_in(V, F), the function F names V; global_var(V), V is one place
 * whatever the call (a global, a static, a function); in_function(I, F);
 * alloc_in(H, F), the function that makes H; and for dead.dl, defined(F,
 * Line), global_def(G, '_init'), dead_stmt(F, Line), allocator_call(A, F)
 * (a call of an allocator is an object above, not a call). A value that is no
 * pointer (a constant, arithmetic) is the variable _const, scalar(_const).
 *
 * A local x of f is f__x, a temporary f__tN, a member m is _fld__m
 * (whatever its structure: the analysis is by field's name), a call
 * _in_f_line_N_K.
 *
 * The compiler's part ends at the facts; the answer is the rules':
 * point_to(V, M), which variable may hold the address of which
 * place, and from it call_edge(I, F), which functions a call through
 * a pointer may reach. A kernel is where that is worth asking: its
 * drivers are tables of pointers to functions, and no grep says who
 * calls a driver's read. mini-ml's Closure_facts says a unit of ML in
 * the same relations, where every call is such a call.
 *
 * terminology:
 * The analysis is the cheapest of its family in three ways, each a
 * word. Flow-insensitive: a function is a set of assignments, their
 * order forgotten (so p = &x; p = &y; says p may point to both, at
 * any line). Context-insensitive: a function is analyzed once for
 * all its callers, whose arguments are mixed. Field-based: x->f is
 * one place for every x. Each could be refined, at a price; this
 * one is the base the others are measured against.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * It is Lars Andersen's analysis (1994): each assignment a
 * constraint that one set of places includes another, solved to a
 * fixpoint, cubic in the worst case. Bjarne Steensgaard's (1996)
 * makes the sets equal instead of included, by union-find, in
 * nearly linear time and with coarser answers. The step to Datalog
 * was to see that such constraints are rules of logic and their
 * solving a database's work (John Whaley and Monica Lam, 2004, for
 * Java, with relations stored as binary decision diagrams; Doop
 * after them), which is how the author's pointer.dl is written.
 *
 * References: Lars Ole Andersen, "Program Analysis and Specialization
 * for the C Programming Language" (his thesis, Copenhagen, 1994);
 * Bjarne Steensgaard, "Points-to analysis in almost linear time"
 * (POPL 1996); John Whaley and Monica Lam, "Cloning-based
 * context-sensitive pointer alias analysis using binary decision
 * diagrams" (PLDI 2004). *)

(* a fact's argument: a name, or a number (an argument's position) *)
type arg = Sym of string | Num of int

(* each fact as it is found, the first time, besides its line in text:
 * mini-analyze's, its facts given to Datalog as values *)
val added : (string -> arg list -> unit) ref

(* a function's name and its body, as the parser gives them *)
val func : Tree.sym -> Tree.stmt -> unit

(* a global's initializer: the symbol, a value put in it, at that offset of
 * it (Declare.gextern's): a member's, assign_store_field *)
val global : Tree.sym -> Tree.expr -> int -> unit

(* the facts so far, a line each, in the order found, each once *)
val text : unit -> string

(* See Ir_facts.mli *)

let quote (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s + 2) in
  Buffer.add_char b '\'';
  String.iter (fun (c : char) -> if c = '\'' || c = '\\' then Buffer.add_char b '\\'; Buffer.add_char b c) s;
  Buffer.add_char b '\'';
  Buffer.contents b

let fact (b : Buffer.t) (relation : string) (args : string list) : unit =
  Buffer.add_string b (relation ^ "(" ^ String.concat ", " args ^ ").\n")

let point (fn : Ir.func) (i : int) : string = quote (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d" fn.name.name i)

let variable (fn : Ir.func) (m : Ir.mem) : string =
  let name : string = match m.name with Some (n : Asm.name) -> n.sym | None -> "" in
  quote (Printf.sprintf "%s:%s/%Ld" fn.name.name name m.off)

let func (fn : Ir.func) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create 1024 in
  let code : Ir.t array = Array.of_list fn.code in
  let vars : Ir.mem list = List.map fst (Opti.variables code) in
  let named (m : Ir.mem) : string list = if List.mem m vars then [ variable fn m ] else [] in
  fact b "function" [ quote fn.name.name ];
  let succ : int list array = Opti.successors code in
  Array.iteri
    (fun (i : int) (ins : Ir.t) ->
      let here = point fn i in
      fact b "point" [ here; quote fn.name.name ];
      List.iter (fun (j : int) -> fact b "succ" [ here; point fn j ]) succ.(i);
      match ins with
      | Ir.LoadAt (m, _) -> List.iter (fun (v : string) -> fact b "use" [ v; here ]) (named m)
      | Ir.StoreAt (m, _) | Ir.PutAt (m, _) -> List.iter (fun (v : string) -> fact b "def" [ v; here ]) (named m)
      | Ir.Call _ -> fact b "call" [ here ]
      | _ -> ())
    code;
  Buffer.contents b

let own (fn : Ir.func) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create 1024 in
  let code : Ir.t array = Array.of_list fn.code in
  let vars : Ir.mem array = Array.of_list (List.map fst (Opti.variables code)) in
  let index (m : Ir.mem) : int option =
    let rec go (i : int) : int option = if i >= Array.length vars then None else if vars.(i) = m then Some i else go (i + 1) in
    go 0 in
  let live : int Set_.t array = Opti.liveness code (Opti.successors code) index in
  Array.iteri
    (fun (i : int) (s : int Set_.t) -> List.iter (fun (v : int) -> fact b "own_live_out" [ variable fn vars.(v); point fn i ]) (Set_.elements s))
    live;
  Buffer.contents b

 * stage 9): each instruction a point, who follows whom, and the

val func : Ir.func -> string

 * against (mini-analyze -flow-answers): Opti's liveness, own_live_out(V, P). *)
val own : Ir.func -> string

(* Claude Code

(* See Analyze_rt.mli *)

module D = Datalog

(* a fact as Facts finds it: a tuple of symbols, bugs/pointers.dl's kinds of its
 * places (C_report's, the native mini-analyze's) *)
let given = C_report.given

(* an option of one word: -Idir, -Ldir *)
let flag (pre : string) (a : string) : string option =
  if String.length a > 2 && String.sub a 0 2 = pre then Some (String.sub a 2 (String.length a - 2)) else None

let main (texts : string array) (queries : string array) (rules : D.t -> unit) : unit =
  Cap.main (fun (caps : Cap.all_caps) ->
      let argv = CapSys.argv caps in
      (* (-I dir and -L dir as mini-analyze's, two words: made one) *)
      let rec joined (l : string list) =
        match l with
        | (("-I" | "-L") as o) :: d :: rest -> (o ^ d) :: joined rest
        | a :: rest -> a :: joined rest
        | [] -> [] in
      let args = joined (Array.to_list (Array.sub argv 1 (Array.length argv - 1))) in
      let path (f : string) = match FS.path f with Ok p -> p | Error m -> failwith m in
      let incs = List.map path (List.filter_map (flag "-I") args) in
      let lib = match List.filter_map (flag "-L") args with l :: _ -> l | [] -> "lib_core" in
      let dead = List.mem "-dead" args and ambient = List.mem "-caps" args and exns = List.mem "-exn" args in
      let fingerprint = List.mem "-fingerprint" args in
      let files =
        List.filter
          (fun (a : string) -> flag "-I" a = None && flag "-L" a = None && not (List.mem a [ "-dead"; "-caps"; "-exn"; "-fingerprint" ]))
          args in
      let p = D.create () in
      let failed = ref 0 in
      let complain (m : string) = Console.eprint caps (m ^ "\n"); incr failed in
      (try
         for i = 0 to (Array.length texts / 2) - 1 do
           D.load p ~from:texts.(2 * i) texts.((2 * i) + 1)
         done;
         Facts.added := given p;
         (* (ML's facts the same: mini-analyze's Closure_facts.added) *)
         Closure_facts.added :=
           (fun (r : string) (args : Closure_facts.arg list) ->
             given p r
               (List.map
                  (fun (a : Closure_facts.arg) ->
                    match a with Closure_facts.Sym s -> Facts.Sym s | Closure_facts.Num n -> Facts.Num n)
                  args));
         let ml = List.filter (fun (f : string) -> Filename.check_suffix f ".ml") files in
         List.iter
           (fun (f : string) ->
             if Filename.check_suffix f ".c" then
               (match C_front.file caps ([], incs) (path f) with Ok () -> () | Error m -> complain m)
             else if Filename.check_suffix f ".ml" then ()
             else
               match FS.read_opt caps (path f) with
               | Some text -> D.load p ~from:f text
               | None -> complain (f ^ ": cannot be read"))
           files;
         (* an ML program: its units and the library's they name *)
         if ml <> [] then
           List.iter complain (Ml_front.program caps (incs @ Ml_front.library caps lib) (List.map path ml));
         (* (-caps: the program's own units and their toplevels, as
          * mini-analyze gives them) *)
         if ambient then
           Hashtbl.iter
             (fun (u : string) () -> given p "own_unit" [ Facts.Sym u ]; given p "own_init" [ Facts.Sym (u ^ ":init") ])
             Ml_front.own;
         rules p;
         (* (no query: mini-analyze's reports, C's then ML's) *)
         if queries <> [||] then Datalog_rt.answers caps p queries
         else if ambient then Caps_report.caps_report caps p
         else if exns then Exn_report.exn_report caps p
         else if dead then Dead_report.dead_report caps p (ml <> [])
         else begin
           if List.exists (fun (f : string) -> Filename.check_suffix f ".c") files then C_report.report caps p;
           if ml <> [] then Ml_report.ml_report caps p
         end;
         if fingerprint then Console.print caps ("fingerprint of the answers: " ^ Answers.hex (Answers.fingerprint p) ^ "\n")
       with
       | D.Error (msg, at) -> complain (at ^ ": " ^ msg)
       | Failure m -> complain m);
      flush (Console.stdout caps);
      if !failed > 0 then CapStdlib.exit caps 1)

analyzers/dotnet/fingerprint.c
849
// Claude Code
// Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt.
//
// mini-analyze's fingerprint on its .NET road (Fingerprint.mli): FNV-1a
// over 64 bits, the arithmetic unsigned, which C says as it is and ML
// cannot (its int is signed, 63 bits natively). Compiled by mini-cc
// -dotnet into fingerprint.dll, whose class fingerprint's methods
// mini-ml -dotnet's Fingerprint calls (its externals): uint64 here,
// int64 there, the same bits, nothing converted between them.

typedef unsigned long long uvlong;

// FNV's offset basis
uvlong
fp_basis(void)
{
	return 0xcbf29ce484222325ULL;
}

// a byte mixed in: xor, then times FNV's prime
uvlong
fp_mix(uvlong h, int b)
{
	return (h ^ (b & 0xff)) * 0x100000001b3ULL;
}

// two fingerprints together, in any order: their sum
uvlong
fp_add(uvlong a, uvlong b)
{
	return a + b;
}
analyzers/ml/Closure_facts.ml
