(* See Models.mli for what a model is.
 *
 * An optimization of the pointer analysis, before any of its precision:
 * the time is the facts' (analyzers/datalog/points_to/andersen.dl's, run
 * first by every analysis), not the engine's.
 *
 * Found by the hot rule's joins. mini-datalog -profile: on mini-cc,
 * andersen.dl's
 *
 *     flow(P, L) :- load(P, X, F), pt(X, O), fpt(O, F, L).
 *
 * 70.7 million firings for 1.1 million facts, 26 s of the 36; each
 * answer found some 60 times. Counting each load's objects times their
 * field's set: half on con:::.0, a list cell's head, of List's code, as
 * written in lib_core:
 *
 *     let rec iter f = function [] -> () | a :: l -> f a; iter f l
 *
 *     List.iter's l       one variable for every caller: 637 cells
 *     each cell's head    949 elements, every list's of the program
 *     a = hd l            637 x 949 joins, for 1,205 answers
 *
 * and the same in map, mem, assoc, fold_left, ... (each its parameter,
 * its cells), in @ (one cell site for every append: a list made by @ is
 * one list, mini-ml's 1,500 cells), and in Hashtbl's buckets (one for all
 * 50 tables of mini-cc, 526 keys each). The types do not separate them
 * (an 'a list's cell holds any element); a model at each call does: a
 * list passed there has its own cells, and List.iter's a only its
 * elements.
 *
 * Measured, mini-analyze on this machine (64 arm64 cores, one run each,
 * 2026-11-03), HEAD before the models against the models; the units of
 * each program's mkfile (analyzers/datalog/tests/mk_units.sh):
 *
 *     mini-cc (41 units)  before            the models
 *     the call graph      36.1 s  1.1 GB    12.4 s  0.37 GB
 *     -dead               35.7 s  3.8 GB    12.3 s  1.2 GB
 *     -caps               36.0 s  3.8 GB    12.4 s  1.2 GB
 *     -exn                247 s  12.3 GB    46.2 s  3.8 GB
 *
 *     mini-ml (47 units)  before            the models
 *     the call graph      70.3 s  1.4 GB    21.0 s  0.28 GB
 *     -dead               51.3 s  3.8 GB    10.1 s  1.0 GB
 *     -caps               51.0 s  3.9 GB    10.4 s  1.0 GB
 *     -exn                out of memory at 14 GB, both
 *                         (66 s, 5.7 GB: call1_rec.dl's held objects)
 *
 * mini-cc's -exn read for the first time in the sweep's 180 s (its 6
 * exceptions; analyzers/datalog/tests/exn_ix.txt). Each model's share, on
 * mini-cc's Andersen alone (mini-datalog, its facts): 70.7 million
 * firings; Hashtbl's 64.4; and List's 13.7. On mini-ml, List and Hashtbl
 * without @ were slower than none, 134 s against 70: the lists made by @
 * still one list, a model's c = c.tl walked it whole at each call, 2.5
 * times the lookups; with @, 21 s.
 *
 * Precision came with it, a call's closures its own: -exn 14 reports
 * fewer in 11 programs, none more (10 tried on the programs, each caught:
 * awk's Exit_program, shell's Word.Error, the linker's Link.Error, ...),
 * List.iter's one call of f having been every closure given to any
 * List.iter; mini-cc's call graph 12 functions fewer reached (Signature's
 * decoders, called by List.init's one call of f). -dead's and -caps's
 * reports the same on the 44 programs (sweep.sh); dynamic.sh none missed.
 *
 * road-not-taken: contexts, the textbook answer to a polymorphic
 * function's callers merged. One for each call of a polymorphic or
 * higher-order function (call-site sensitivity for those alone): 152
 * million firings against 159 without contexts; the merge moved to
 * Hashtbl's buckets, made in replace's local replace_bucket, whose key
 * and info, captured, have one set for all callers (contexts.dl's
 * global). Then a local function in its closure's context (m-CFA's, as
 * contexts.dl's curried stages): 123 million, and mini-prolog's Halt
 * reported again. Cells of one type made one (every int list's): 5%.
 *
 * Why a model does what a clone, or a context, would not, though it is
 * one, the library's code copied at each call:
 *  - the whole call tree, to any depth. A context names a call by one
 *    call site; the library calls its own helpers (replace's
 *    replace_bucket, rev's rev_append, init's init_aux), whose context
 *    is then their one call site in the library, every caller's. A
 *    model has no call inside: its objects are named by the caller's
 *    call, however deep the real code went;
 *  - no closure. What a closure captures is one set for every context
 *    (contexts.dl's global, m-CFA's flat environment: followed by
 *    context, exponential), and Hashtbl's code is closures over key and
 *    info;
 *  - simpler than the code. A clone keeps its shape, an array of
 *    buckets, their Cons chains, resize copying them; a model is one
 *    object and two fields. And a loop over a list, to a flow-insensitive
 *    analysis, is its two facts, c = l and c = c.tl: the clone reduced to
 *    what this analysis can see of it;
 *  - in the facts, so in every analysis. Contexts come after andersen.dl,
 *    which had the merge itself (26 of mini-cc's 36 s), and multiply
 *    what they keep (pt/6 3.9 million tuples, pt/2 1.1): never cheaper
 *    than the analysis without them. A model makes that one cheaper, and
 *    -dead, -caps and the call graph, which have no context, with it.
 * Its price is a model to write, and check, for each function; the
 * contexts are automatic. Worth it for a few containers, called
 * everywhere: 53 functions here (16 of Hashtbl, 36 of List, @).
 *
 * design: what keeps it sound. A modeled function's body is not read, so
 * the model and the real code never meet (Models.mli). The facts after a
 * model are named as without it (Closure_facts.call: the calls' and the
 * temporaries' numbers it replaces), so a change of the facts is only
 * the model's. Its calls of what it is given say so (model_call), for
 * bugs/stack.dl, which follows only a unit's own calls. dynamic.sh does
 * not check what the models replace (it ran, and no fact says it). A
 * model raises what its function's code may (analyzers/tests/models/:
 * each one called, what escapes and what is called the same as with
 * mini-analyze -no-models, the library read as written; the numbers
 * above, the same option against none).
 *
 * old: List's and Hashtbl's bodies read as written, as every unit's;
 * lib_core's ML code, so no external's copy at each call (Closure_facts's
 * prim_body) applied to them. *)

type v = Arg of int | Ret | Tmp of int

type op =
  | New of v
  | Load of v * v * string
  | Store of v * string * v
  | Assign of v * v
  | Scalar of v
  | Call of v * v * v
  | Raise of string
  | Global of v * string

let failure : string = "caml_exn_Failure"
(* (what the real code may raise: compare's Invalid_argument, a functional
 * value compared, in every find, mem and assoc; Array.make's, in create
 * and a resize; checked by analyzers/tests/models/) *)
let invalid : string = "caml_exn_Invalid_argument"
let not_found : string = "caml_exn_Not_found"

(* ---- Hashtbl: a table one object, its keys a field, its values another *)

let key : string = "tbl:key"
let value : string = "tbl:val"

(* every binding of the table in Arg 2: its key in Tmp 1, its value in Tmp 2 *)
let bindings : op list = [ Load (Tmp 1, Arg 2, key); Load (Tmp 2, Arg 2, value) ]

(* f k v, a call for each argument, f's result in Tmp 4 *)
let each_binding : op list =
  bindings @ [ Call (Tmp 3, Arg 1, Tmp 1); Call (Tmp 4, Tmp 3, Tmp 2) ]

let stored : op list =
  [ Store (Arg 1, key, Arg 2); Store (Arg 1, value, Arg 3); Scalar Ret;
    Raise invalid ]

let hashtbl : (string * (int * op list)) list =
  [ ("create", (1, [ New Ret; Raise invalid ]));
    ("clear", (1, [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("reset", (1, [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("copy", (1, [ New Ret; Raise invalid;
                   Load (Tmp 1, Arg 1, key); Store (Ret, key, Tmp 1);
                   Load (Tmp 2, Arg 1, value); Store (Ret, value, Tmp 2) ]));
    ("length", (1, [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("add", (3, stored));
    ("replace", (3, stored));
    ("remove", (2, [ Scalar Ret; Raise invalid ]));
    ("mem", (2, [ Scalar Ret; Raise invalid ]));
    ("find", (2, [ Load (Ret, Arg 1, value); Raise not_found; Raise invalid ]));
    (* (a list: its cell's tail the cell itself, or []) *)
    ("find_all", (2, [ New Ret; Raise invalid; Load (Tmp 1, Arg 1, value);
                       Store (Ret, "con:::.0", Tmp 1); Store (Ret, "con:::.1", Ret);
                       Scalar Ret ]));
    ("find_opt", (2, [ New Ret; Raise invalid; Load (Tmp 1, Arg 1, value);
                       Store (Ret, "con:Some.0", Tmp 1); Scalar Ret ]));
    ("iter", (2, each_binding @ [ Scalar Ret ]));
    (* f k v acc, acc first init then what f returned *)
    ("fold", (3, bindings @ [ Assign (Tmp 5, Arg 3); Call (Tmp 3, Arg 1, Tmp 1);
                              Call (Tmp 4, Tmp 3, Tmp 2); Call (Tmp 5, Tmp 4, Tmp 5);
                              Assign (Ret, Tmp 5) ]));
    (* f k v: None, or Some v', the binding's new value *)
    ("filter_map_inplace",
     (2, each_binding @ [ Load (Tmp 5, Tmp 4, "con:Some.0");
                          Store (Arg 2, value, Tmp 5); Scalar Ret ])) ]

(* ---- List: the real cells, a model of a loop over them
 *
 * design:
 * A list is not abstract: its cells are made and taken apart by every
 * caller (::, a match), so the model reads and writes them, con:::.0
 * and con:::.1, and the functions not modeled stay as written. A loop
 * over a list is two facts, flow-insensitive: c = l, then c = c.tl, so
 * c points to every cell of l, and x = c.hd to every element. A list
 * made is one cell of this call, its tail itself or [] *)

let hd : string = "con:::.0"
let tl : string = "con:::.1"

(* the elements of the list in a, in Tmp e (its cells in Tmp (e + 1)) *)
let elements (a : v) (e : int) : op list =
  [ Assign (Tmp (e + 1), a); Load (Tmp (e + 1), Tmp (e + 1), tl);
    Load (Tmp e, Tmp (e + 1), hd) ]

(* the result a list of what is in x *)
let made (x : v) : op list =
  [ New Ret; Store (Ret, hd, x); Store (Ret, tl, Ret); Scalar Ret ]

let some (x : v) : op list = [ New Ret; Store (Ret, "con:Some.0", x); Scalar Ret ]

(* f called on each element of Arg 2 (in Tmp 1), its result in Tmp 3 *)
let each : op list = elements (Arg 2) 1 @ [ Call (Tmp 3, Arg 1, Tmp 1) ]

(* f i x: an index first *)
let each_i : op list =
  elements (Arg 2) 1
  @ [ Scalar (Tmp 4); Call (Tmp 5, Arg 1, Tmp 4); Call (Tmp 3, Tmp 5, Tmp 1) ]

(* a pair's second field in Tmp 3, of the elements of Arg 2 (assoc's) *)
let second : op list = elements (Arg 2) 1 @ [ Load (Tmp 3, Tmp 1, "tuple:2.1") ]

(* cmp x y, of the elements of Arg 2 *)
let compared : op list = each @ [ Call (Tmp 4, Tmp 3, Tmp 1) ]

let list : (string * (int * op list)) list =
  [ ("length", (1, [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("hd", (1, [ Load (Ret, Arg 1, hd); Raise failure ]));
    ("tl", (1, [ Load (Ret, Arg 1, tl); Raise failure ]));
    ("nth", (2, elements (Arg 1) 1
                @ [ Assign (Ret, Tmp 1); Raise failure; Raise invalid ]));
    ("rev", (1, elements (Arg 1) 1 @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("rev_append", (2, elements (Arg 1) 1 @ made (Tmp 1) @ [ Assign (Ret, Arg 2) ]));
    ("iter", (2, each @ [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("iteri", (2, each_i @ [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("map", (2, each @ made (Tmp 3)));
    ("rev_map", (2, each @ made (Tmp 3)));
    ("mapi", (2, each_i @ made (Tmp 3)));
    ("filter", (2, each @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("find_all", (2, each @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("filteri", (2, each_i @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("filter_map", (2, each @ [ Load (Tmp 4, Tmp 3, "con:Some.0") ] @ made (Tmp 4)));
    ("concat_map", (2, each @ elements (Tmp 3) 4 @ made (Tmp 4)));
    (* f acc x, acc first init then what f returned *)
    ("fold_left", (3, [ Assign (Tmp 3, Arg 2) ] @ elements (Arg 3) 1
                      @ [ Call (Tmp 4, Arg 1, Tmp 3); Call (Tmp 3, Tmp 4, Tmp 1);
                          Assign (Ret, Tmp 3) ]));
    ("fold_right", (3, [ Assign (Tmp 3, Arg 3) ] @ elements (Arg 2) 1
                       @ [ Call (Tmp 4, Arg 1, Tmp 1); Call (Tmp 3, Tmp 4, Tmp 3);
                           Assign (Ret, Tmp 3) ]));
    ("mem", (2, [ Scalar Ret; Raise invalid ]));
    ("memq", (2, [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("mem_assoc", (2, [ Scalar Ret; Raise invalid ]));
    ("exists", (2, each @ [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("for_all", (2, each @ [ Scalar Ret ]));
    ("find", (2, each @ [ Assign (Ret, Tmp 1); Raise not_found ]));
    ("find_opt", (2, each @ some (Tmp 1)));
    ("find_map", (2, each @ [ Assign (Ret, Tmp 3); Scalar Ret ]));
    ("assoc", (2, second @ [ Assign (Ret, Tmp 3); Raise not_found; Raise invalid ]));
    ("assq", (2, second @ [ Assign (Ret, Tmp 3); Raise not_found ]));
    ("assoc_opt", (2, second @ some (Tmp 3) @ [ Raise invalid ]));
    ("assq_opt", (2, second @ some (Tmp 3)));
    ("remove_assoc", (2, elements (Arg 2) 1 @ made (Tmp 1) @ [ Raise invalid ]));
    ("init", (2, [ Scalar (Tmp 1); Call (Tmp 2, Arg 2, Tmp 1); Raise invalid ]
                 @ made (Tmp 2)));
    ("sort", (2, compared @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("stable_sort", (2, compared @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("sort_uniq", (2, compared @ made (Tmp 1)));
    ("iter2", (3, elements (Arg 2) 1 @ elements (Arg 3) 3
                  @ [ Call (Tmp 5, Arg 1, Tmp 1); Call (Tmp 6, Tmp 5, Tmp 3);
                      Scalar Ret; Raise invalid ]));
    ("concat", (1, elements (Arg 1) 1 @ elements (Tmp 1) 3 @ made (Tmp 3)));
    ("flatten", (1, elements (Arg 1) 1 @ elements (Tmp 1) 3 @ made (Tmp 3))) ]

(* (l1 @ l2: l1's elements in a cell of this call, then l2's cells; written,
 * one cell site for every append, every list made by @ one list, which a
 * model's c = c.tl walked whole: mini-ml's 1,500 cells, 1,353 elements) *)
let pervasives : (string * (int * op list)) list =
  [ ("@", (2, elements (Arg 1) 1 @ made (Tmp 1) @ [ Assign (Ret, Arg 2) ])) ]

let units : (string * (string * (int * op list)) list) list =
  [ ("Hashtbl", hashtbl); ("List", list); ("Pervasives", pervasives) ]

let on : bool ref = ref true
let derived : (string, int * op list) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 256
let derived_on : bool ref = ref false

(* (Models' own even with the derived ones: a sort's result is a list of
 * its own, in its own order, what bugs/order.dl needs; the code says it
 * only as cells, some of them the input's: a list shorter than 2 comes
 * back itself) *)
let meant : string list = [ "List.sort"; "List.stable_sort"; "List.sort_uniq" ]

let find (sym : string) : (int * op list) option =
  match String.index_opt sym '.' with
  | Some _ when not !on -> None
  (* (a derived one first, plan_analysis_scale.md's step 3; these for
   * what has none) *)
  | Some _ when !derived_on && Hashtbl.mem derived sym && not (List.mem sym meant) ->
      Hashtbl.find_opt derived sym
  | Some i -> (
      match List.assoc_opt (String.sub sym 0 i) units with
      | Some fs ->
          List.assoc_opt (String.sub sym (i + 1) (String.length sym - i - 1)) fs
      | None -> None)
  | None -> None

(* (a unit with a derived summary too: a let group of its whose every
 * function has a model or a summary is then replaced by them, its
 * functions used as values the model's, List.sort compare; old, with
 * -summaries: none such, a value's call ran lib_core's own code) *)
let modeled_unit (name : string) : bool =
  !on
  && (List.mem_assoc name units
      || (!derived_on
          && Hashtbl.fold (fun s _ b -> b || String.length s > String.length name
                                              && String.sub s 0 (String.length name + 1) = name ^ ".") derived false))
analyzers/ml/Models.mli
3610
(* What a library's container does, for the facts: written at each call
 * given all its arguments, in place of the call (Closure_facts.call), as
 * an external's is, and once as the library's own function, for what
 * names it as a value (List.map (Hashtbl.find h) l).
 *
 * design:
 * A container written in ML is one set of cells for its whole program.
 * Hashtbl's buckets are made in Hashtbl.replace, so every table's are
 * one object: mini-cc's 50 tables gave each bucket all their 526 keys,
 * and a find in any of them found the keys of all. Contexts do not
 * separate them: the bucket is made in replace's replace_bucket, a local
 * function whose key and info, captured, have one set for all callers
 * (contexts.dl's global). A model has no cells: a table is one object,
 * made where Hashtbl.create is called, its keys one field, its values
 * another, as an array's elements are one (Closure_facts's arr:elt).
 *
 * The same for List: a list's cells, each function's parameter, held
 * every list of the program, 949 elements, and each load of a List
 * function's body went through them all; @'s cells too, one site for
 * every append. What it saves, measured: Models.ml (mini-analyze -dead on
 * mini-cc 36 s to 12 s, on mini-ml 51 s to 10 s).
 *
 * A modeled function's body is not read (its unit's binding: the model as
 * a function instead), so the model and the real code never meet: for
 * Hashtbl, every function of an interface whose type is abstract, none of
 * its cells seen by a caller; for List, a type not abstract, the model
 * reads and writes its real cells, and what is not modeled (partition,
 * split, map2) stays as written; Pervasives' @ too, alone of its unit.
 * dynamic.sh does not check what the models replace: List's and Hashtbl's
 * functions, and a function whose closure is a model's (model:...,
 * written where the real one is).
 *
 * others: Doop analyzes the JDK's collections as written, and pays for
 * it (its "heap abstractions" for HashMap); Infer and Facebook's Pulse
 * model them; Soot's Spark and WALA give a few native methods models.
 *)

(* a model's variables: its k-th argument (1 ...), its result, a variable
 * of its own *)
type v = Arg of int | Ret | Tmp of int

type op =
  | New of v                    (* an object of the result's type made here *)
  | Load of v * v * string      (* dst, from, the field *)
  | Store of v * string * v     (* into, the field, what *)
  | Assign of v * v             (* dst, src *)
  | Scalar of v                 (* a number, unit, a constant constructor *)
  | Call of v * v * v           (* dst, the function, its argument *)
  | Raise of string             (* the exception's symbol, caml_exn_Not_found *)
  | Global of v * string        (* holds what the global does (a derived
                                   summary's: List.hd's Pervasives.failwith) *)

(* false: no model, the library's code read as written (mini-analyze
 * -no-models: to compare, Models.ml's numbers, tests/models/) *)
val on : bool ref

(* the summaries derived from the library's code (analyzers/summaries/,
 * plan_analysis_scale.md, step 3), by symbol; with [derived_on], read
 * first, the models written here for the rest (mini-analyze -summaries) *)
val derived : (string, int * op list) Hashtbl.t
val derived_on : bool ref

(* a global's model, by its symbol (Hashtbl.find): its arity and what it does *)
val find : string -> (int * op list) option

(* the units whose let groups are replaced, each whose every function is
 * modeled or summarized (Hashtbl whole, List in part) *)
val modeled_unit : string -> bool

(* Claude Code

(* See Ssa_facts.mli *)

(* an atom, quoted: a function's name has a capital, a dot, a <> *)
let quote (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s + 2) in
  Buffer.add_char b '\'';
  String.iter (fun (c : char) -> if c = '\'' || c = '\\' then Buffer.add_char b '\\'; Buffer.add_char b c) s;
  Buffer.add_char b '\'';
  Buffer.contents b

let name (fn : Ssa.func) (kind : char) (n : int) : string = quote (Printf.sprintf "%s:%c%d" fn.name kind n)

let fact (b : Buffer.t) (relation : string) (args : string list) : unit =
  Buffer.add_string b (relation ^ "(" ^ String.concat ", " args ^ ").\n")

(* a call's application, as Closure_facts names it (site_key) *)
let key (unit_name : string) ((a, z) : int * int) : string =
  Printf.sprintf "%s:%d-%d" unit_name a z

let func ?(prefix = "") ?(unit_name = "") (fn : Ssa.func) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create 1024 in
  let fact b relation args = fact b (prefix ^ relation) args in
  let block (n : int) : string = name fn 'b' n and value (v : Ssa.value) : string = name fn 'v' v in
  fact b "function" [ quote fn.name ];
  if Array.length fn.blocks > 0 then fact b "entry" [ block 0 ];
  Array.iter
    (fun (bl : Ssa.block) ->
      let here = block bl.id and last = name fn 't' bl.id in
      fact b "block" [ here; quote fn.name ];
      List.iter
        (fun (v : Ssa.value) ->
          fact b "phi" [ value v; here ];
          match Hashtbl.find fn.defs v with
          | Ssa.Phi ops -> List.iter (fun ((p, x) : int * Ssa.value) -> fact b "phi_arg" [ value v; block p; value x ]) ops
          | _ -> ())
        bl.phis;
      (* the points, in order: each instruction, then the end *)
      let points : string list = List.map value bl.body @ [ last ] in
      fact b "first" [ here; List.hd points ];
      let rec chain (ps : string list) : unit =
        match ps with
        | p :: (q :: _ as rest) -> fact b "next" [ p; q ]; chain rest
        | _ -> () in
      chain points;
      fact b "last" [ here; last ];
      List.iter
        (fun (v : Ssa.value) ->
          let ins : Ssa.ins = Hashtbl.find fn.defs v in
          fact b "def" [ value v; value v ];
          (* (zero: no storage, as Alloc's real says: the constant 0, and a
           * constant made where it is read) *)
          (match ins with Ssa.Zero | Ssa.Const _ | Ssa.Blk _ | Ssa.Symb _ -> fact b "zero" [ value v ] | _ -> ());
          List.iter (fun (x : Ssa.value) -> fact b "use" [ value x; value v ]) (Ssa_build.operands ins))
        bl.body;
      let used : Ssa.value list =
        match bl.term with
        | Ssa.Br (v, _, _) | Ssa.Switch (v, _) | Ssa.Ret v | Ssa.Raise v | Ssa.Reraise v -> [ v ]
        | Ssa.Tail (_, vs) -> vs
        | Ssa.Jmp _ | Ssa.Try _ -> [] in
      List.iter (fun (x : Ssa.value) -> fact b "use" [ value x; last ]) used;
      let after : int list =
        match bl.term with
        | Ssa.Jmp s -> [ s ]
        | Ssa.Br (_, s, t) | Ssa.Try (_, s, t) -> [ s; t ]
        | Ssa.Switch _ -> Ssa_build.successors_of bl
        | Ssa.Ret _ | Ssa.Raise _ | Ssa.Reraise _ | Ssa.Tail _ -> [] in
      List.iter (fun (s : int) -> fact b "succ" [ here; block s ]) after;
      (* (Lower.sites: the calls by their application) *)
      List.iter
        (fun (v : Ssa.value) ->
          Option.iter
            (fun sp -> fact b "site" [ value v; quote (key unit_name sp) ])
            (Hashtbl.find_opt fn.sites v))
        bl.body;
      Option.iter
        (fun sp -> fact b "site" [ last; quote (key unit_name sp) ])
        (Hashtbl.find_opt fn.tail_sites bl.id))
    fn.blocks;
  Buffer.contents b

let own (fn : Ssa.func) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create 1024 in
  let block (n : int) : string = name fn 'b' n and value (v : Ssa.value) : string = name fn 'v' v in
  let live_in, live_out = Alloc.liveness fn in
  Array.iteri (fun (n : int) (live : int Set_.t) -> List.iter (fun (v : int) -> fact b "own_live_in" [ value v; block n ]) (Set_.elements live)) live_in;
  Array.iteri (fun (n : int) (live : int Set_.t) -> List.iter (fun (v : int) -> fact b "own_live_out" [ value v; block n ]) (Set_.elements live)) live_out;
  Array.iteri (fun (n : int) (d : int) -> if n <> 0 && d >= 0 then fact b "own_idom" [ block d; block n ]) (Ssa_build.dominators fn);
  Buffer.contents b
analyzers/ml/Ssa_facts.mli
4095
(* A function's SSA form as Datalog facts (docs/plans/plan_prolog.md,
 * stage 9): its blocks and who follows whom, each instruction as a
 * point of the program with the value it defines and those it uses,
 * the phis. mini-analyze -flow, for mini-datalog to run
 * analyzers/datalog/liveness_ssa.dl and dominators.dl on.
 *
 * A name is its function's: 'f1_sum:b2' a block, 'f1_sum:v7' a value
 * and the instruction that makes it, 'f1_sum:t2' the end of block 2
 * (its jump, its return).
 *   function(F). block(B, F). entry(B). succ(B, S).
 *   first(B, P)   the block's first point (its end, if it has no instruction)
 *   next(P, Q)    in a block, the point after P
 *   last(B, T)    the block's end
 *   def(V, P). use(V, P).
 *   phi(V, B). phi_arg(V, Pred, X)   entered from Pred, V is X
 *   zero(V)       a slot never written: a value that needs no place
 *   site(P, K)    the call at P (a value, or a block's tail call) is the
 *                 application K, unit:start-stop of its function's span,
 *                 as Closure_facts' site_key names it (when Lower.sites)
 * Nothing is computed here: what is live where is the rules' to find.
 * prefix: before each relation's name (-bugs' ssa_, whose function and
 * entry are another's there); unit_name: the keys' unit.
 *
 * design:
 * What SSA gives an analysis that ignores the order. points_to/ is
 * flow-insensitive: a variable has one set of objects for its whole
 * function, whatever was written in it before or after. In C that
 * loses much: p = malloc(n); free(p); p = &x is one p, pointing to
 * both. SSA renames each write, p1 and p2, and a flow-insensitive
 * analysis of the names is then as sharp as a flow-sensitive one for
 * them: the order was in which write a read sees, and the names now
 * say it. ML's let-variables need no renaming, being written once
 * (Appel's "SSA is functional programming", Ssa.mli): Closure_facts'
 * variables are SSA's already, and points_to/ is flow-sensitive for
 * them for free. What stays insensitive is what is written more than
 * once: a ref's contents, a field, an array's element (the heap: its
 * updates would need a flow-sensitive analysis's strong ones).
 * The names do not give the order of the effects, a call before
 * another, nor the paths: those are the blocks. next and succ are the
 * paths; a definition dominates each of its uses, so a value's flow
 * is an order too; X dominates N when no path from the entry to N
 * avoids X (dominators.dl), and a path from A that avoids R is the
 * question "R on every path after A?" (bugs/pairs.dl's held, R a
 * close, A an open, a raise on such a path a leak). A phi says where
 * paths meet and which value came by which edge; what a branch tested
 * it does not say, and a property true on one path only (a close
 * `when o != c`, 62d811be) needs the conditions too: path-sensitive.
 * The two kinds of facts meet at the calls: an SSA call is named by
 * its application (site), as Closure_facts names its sites
 * (site_key), so a rule asks points-to what a call takes and the
 * blocks when. The SSA is mini-ml's own, the compiler's, lowered
 * (closures called by their code, a curried call checked at run
 * time): one graph for the compiler and the analyses, no second.
 *
 * References: Rebecca Hasti, Susan Horwitz, "Using static single
 * assignment form to improve flow-insensitive pointer analysis" (PLDI
 * 1998); Ben Hardekopf, Calvin Lin, "Flow-sensitive pointer analysis
 * for millions of lines of code" (CGO 2011), the semi-sparse one;
 * Ondrej Lhotak, Kwok-Chiang Andrew Chung, "Points-to analysis with
 * efficient strong updates" (POPL 2011). *)
val func : ?prefix:string -> ?unit_name:string -> Ssa.func -> string

(* a call's application as a key: Unit:start-stop *)
val key : string -> int * int -> string

(* What the compiler itself computed, as facts of other names, to check
 * the rules' answers against (mini-analyze -flow-answers): Alloc's liveness
 * (own_live_in(V, B), own_live_out(V, B)) and Ssa_build's dominators
 * (own_idom(D, B)). *)
val own : Ssa.func -> string

(* See Tree_facts.mli *)

open Scope

let fact (r : string) (args : Closure_facts.arg list) : unit = !Closure_facts.added r args

let kind (e : exp) : string =
  match e with
  | Evar _ -> "var" | Econst _ -> "const" | Elet _ -> "let" | Efunction _ -> "function"
  (* (a && b, a || b: b after a, if at all; not an application) *)
  | Eapply ({ e = Evar (Prim (("%sequand" | "%sequor"), _, _)); _ }, _) ->
      "andor"
  | Eapply _ -> "apply" | Ematch _ -> "match" | Etry _ -> "try" | Etuple _ -> "tuple"
  | Econs _ -> "cons" | Erecord _ -> "record" | Ewith _ -> "with" | Efield _ -> "field"
  | Esetfield _ -> "setfield" | Earray _ -> "array" | Eif _ -> "if" | Eseq _ -> "seq"
  | Ewhile _ -> "while" | Efor _ -> "for" | Eassert _ -> "assert"
  | Econstraint _ -> "constraint"

(* an expression's children, in the text's order *)
let children (e : exp) : expr list =
  let cases (cs : case list) =
    List.concat_map (fun ((_, g, b) : case) -> Option.to_list g @ [ b ]) cs in
  match e with
  | Evar _ | Econst _ -> []
  | Elet (_, bs, body) -> List.map snd bs @ [ body ]
  | Efunction cs -> cases cs
  | Eapply (f, args) -> f :: args
  | Ematch (x, cs) | Etry (x, cs) -> x :: cases cs
  | Etuple es | Econs (_, es) | Earray es -> es
  | Erecord (_, fs) -> List.map snd fs
  | Ewith (x, _, fs) -> x :: List.map snd fs
  | Efield (x, _) | Eassert x | Econstraint (x, _) -> [ x ]
  | Esetfield (x, _, v) -> [ x; v ]
  | Eif (c, a, b) -> c :: a :: Option.to_list b
  | Eseq (a, b) | Ewhile (a, b) -> [ a; b ]
  | Efor (_, lo, hi, _, body) -> [ lo; hi; body ]

let unit_ (name : string) (text : string) (items : item list) : unit =
  let count = ref 0 in
  (* each line's first offset *)
  let starts = ref [ 0 ] in
  String.iteri (fun (i : int) (c : char) -> if c = '\n' then starts := (i + 1) :: !starts) text;
  let starts = Array.of_list (List.rev !starts) in
  let line_of (off : int) : int =
    (* (the last start at or before off: a binary search) *)
    let rec go lo hi = if lo >= hi then lo else
        let mid = (lo + hi + 1) / 2 in if starts.(mid) <= off then go mid hi else go lo (mid - 1) in
    go 0 (Array.length starts - 1) in
  let rec walk (x : expr) : string =
    incr count;
    let n = Printf.sprintf "%s:e%d" name !count in
    let a, _ = x.span in
    fact "expr" [ Sym n; Sym (kind x.e) ];
    (* (an application by its function's span, as Closure_facts' site_key) *)
    (match x.e with
     | Eapply (f, _) ->
         let a, b = f.span in
         fact "tree_site" [ Sym n; Sym (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d-%d" name a b) ]
     | _ -> ());
    if a >= 0 && a < String.length text then begin
      let l = line_of a in
      let col = a - starts.(l) in
      fact "pos" [ Sym n; Num (l + 1); Num col ];
      (* (nothing but blanks before it on its line) *)
      let lead = ref true in
      for i = starts.(l) to a - 1 do if text.[i] <> ' ' && text.[i] <> '\t' then lead := false done;
      if !lead then fact "leading" [ Sym n ]
    end;
    List.iteri (fun (k : int) (c : expr) -> fact "child" [ Sym n; Num k; Sym (walk c) ]) (children x.e);
    n in
  List.iter
    (fun (i : item) ->
      match i with
      | Ieval e -> ignore (walk e)
      | Ivalue (_, bs, _) -> List.iter (fun ((_, e) : pattern * expr) -> ignore (walk e)) bs
      | Iexception _ | Iexternal _ -> ())
    items
analyzers/ml/Tree_facts.mli

(* An ML unit's tree as Datalog facts
 * (docs/plans/done/plan_bug_analyses.md, A12): each expression a node,
 * its kind, its children in the text's order, where it starts in the
 * file. For rules over the text's shape,
 * bugs/layout.dl first, joined if need be with the others' facts:
 *
 *   expr(N, Kind)        N is an expression: if, seq, apply, let, ...
 *   child(P, K, N)       N is P's K-th child (an if: its test 0, its
 *                        then 1, its else 2; a seq: 0 then 1)
 *   pos(N, Line, Col)    where N starts (Col from 0)
 *   leading(N)           nothing but blanks before N on its line
 *
 * Only the program's own units (Ml_front), not the library's: what a
 * layout rule reports is the program's text.
 *
 * design:
 * The tree is mini-ml's scoped one (Scope), the one Closure_facts reads:
 * a parenthesis is gone, but an expression's span still says where it
 * starts. A text rewritten by mlpp (a class, a [@@deriving]) has its
 * spans in the rewritten text: its columns may be off.
 *
 * others:
 * CodeQL keeps a program's whole tree in its database beside the
 * data flow (its AST classes, Expr.getParent()); Semgrep matches
 * patterns on the tree without a database; Datalog over a tree goes
 * back to Paul Klint's and Jurgen Vinju's Rascal and to "Scalable and
 * flexible ... Doop"'s fact generators, which also say each node. *)

(* the unit [name]'s facts, through Closure_facts.added; [text] the file's,
 * for the lines and the columns *)
val unit_ : string -> string -> Scope.item list -> unit

module D = Datalog

let fingerprint (p : D.t) : Int64.t =
  let total = ref 0L in
  Hashtbl.iter
    (fun (_ : string) (r : D.relation) ->
      if r.rules > 0 then
        List.iter
          (fun (t : int array) ->
            let h = ref (Fingerprint.basis ()) in
            String.iter
              (fun (ch : char) -> h := Fingerprint.mix !h (Char.code ch))
              (D.show p r t);
            total := Fingerprint.add !total !h)
          (D.tuples r))
    p.relations;
  !total

let hex (x : Int64.t) : string =
  String.init 16 (fun (i : int) ->
      let digit = Int64.logand (Int64.shift_right_logical x (4 * (15 - i))) 15L in
      "0123456789abcdef".[Int64.to_int digit])

module D = Datalog

let name = C_report.name

(* Main:11:c6: its file as given, and the line (Exn_report.site's, the
 * file's name alone: two Opti.ml in ix) *)
let site (r : string) : string =
  match String.split_on_char ':' r with
  | u :: l :: _ -> (match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f | None -> u ^ ".ml") ^ ":" ^ l
  | _ -> r

let bugs_report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) : unit =
  let tuples r n = List.map (fun (t : int array) -> Array.map (name p) t) (D.tuples (D.relation p r n)) in
  let unit_of (s : string) : string = match String.index_opt s ':' with Some i -> String.sub s 0 i | None -> s in
  let physeq =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let i = t.(0) and f = t.(1) and op = t.(2) and what = t.(3) in
        if not (Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own (unit_of i)) then None
        else
          let what = if what.[0] >= 'A' && what.[0] <= 'Z' then "a " ^ what else what in
          Some (Printf.sprintf "%s: physeq: in %s, %s of %s made there: always %s" (site i)
                  (Ml_report.ml_function f) op what (if op = "==" then "false" else "true")))
      (tuples "always" 4) in
  (* a cache's identity of a value changed in place: a line a comparison,
   * the first object (where it is made) *)
  let stale = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      if Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own (unit_of t.(0)) then begin
        let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt stale (t.(0), t.(1)) with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
        Hashtbl.replace stale (t.(0), t.(1)) (t.(2) :: l)
      end)
    (tuples "stale" 3);
  let physeq =
    physeq
    @ Hashtbl.fold
        (fun ((i, f) : string * string) (hs : string list) acc ->
          let h = List.hd (List.sort compare hs) in
          (* (Before:block1@11: made at line 11) *)
          let h =
            match String.index_opt h '@', String.index_opt h ':' with
            | Some a, Some c -> String.sub h 0 c ^ ":" ^ String.sub h (a + 1) (String.length h - a - 1)
            | _ -> h in
          Printf.sprintf
            "%s: physeq: in %s, a kept value compared by identity with one \
             changed in place (%s): its change not seen"
            (site i) (Ml_report.ml_function f) (site h)
          :: acc)
        stale [] in
  let handlers = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter (fun (t : string array) -> Hashtbl.replace handlers t.(0) ()) (tuples "in_handler" 2);
  let own (i : string) : bool = Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own (unit_of i) in
  let in_try =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let i = t.(0) and f = Ml_report.ml_function t.(1) in
        if not (own i) then None
        else
          Some (Printf.sprintf "%s: stack: %s calls itself in a try's %s: no tail call by mini-ml" (site i)
                  f (if Hashtbl.mem handlers i then "handler" else "body")))
      (tuples "in_try_rec" 3) in
  let on_list =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let i = t.(0) and f = Ml_report.ml_function t.(1) in
        if not (own i) then None
        else Some (Printf.sprintf "%s: stack: %s calls itself, not a tail call, over a list" (site i) f))
      (tuples "on_list" 2) in
  let stack = List.sort_uniq compare (in_try @ on_list) in
  (* Main:try2@11: the try's line, its function, what may arrive *)
  let fn = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter (fun (t : string array) -> Hashtbl.replace fn t.(0) t.(1)) (tuples "try_in_function" 2);
  let errors = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let e = match C_report.prefix "caml_exn_" t.(1) with Some x -> x | None -> t.(1) in
      Hashtbl.replace errors t.(0) (e :: (match Hashtbl.find_opt errors t.(0) with Some l -> l | None -> [])))
    (tuples "swallowed" 2);
  let swallowed =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun (t : string) (es : string list) acc ->
        if not (own t) then acc
        else
          let line = match String.index_opt t '@' with Some i -> String.sub t (i + 1) (String.length t - i - 1) | None -> "?" in
          let f = match Hashtbl.find_opt fn t with Some f -> Ml_report.ml_function f | None -> "?" in
          Printf.sprintf "%s: swallowed: in %s, %s silenced, a constant answered" (site (unit_of t ^ ":" ^ line)) f
            (String.concat " or " (List.sort_uniq compare es))
          :: acc)
      errors [] in
  (* a program's own exception (Main.Error, not lib_core's Not_found)
   * caught by all, the handler raising another: a crash where it was
   * an error (exceptions.dl's ends_in) *)
  let raises = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let e = match C_report.prefix "caml_exn_" t.(1) with
        | Some x -> x
        | None -> t.(1) in
      let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt raises t.(0) with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
      Hashtbl.replace raises t.(0) (e :: l))
    (tuples "handler_raises" 2);
  let crash =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let tr = t.(0) and e = t.(1) in
        if not (own tr && Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own (Exn_report.unit_of e)) then None
        else
          let f = match Hashtbl.find_opt fn tr with
            | Some f -> Ml_report.ml_function f
            | None -> "?" in
          let e2 = match Hashtbl.find_opt raises tr with
            | Some l -> String.concat " or " (List.sort_uniq compare l)
            | None -> "?" in
          Some (Printf.sprintf "%s: crash: in %s, %s caught by all, the handler raising %s"
                  (site (unit_of tr ^ ":" ^ Exn_report.try_line tr)) f e e2))
      (tuples "ends_in" 2) in
  let crash = List.sort_uniq compare crash in
  (* an int of 63 bits in code for the Pi 1 too (intwidth.dl): a line a
   * function, at its first, a table of constants one report *)
  let by_fun = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let s = t.(0) in
      if own s then begin
        let line = match String.split_on_char ':' s with _ :: l :: _ -> int_of_string l | _ -> 0 in
        let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt by_fun (t.(1), t.(2)) with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
        Hashtbl.replace by_fun (t.(1), t.(2)) ((line, s, t.(3)) :: l)
      end)
    (tuples "int31" 4);
  let int31 =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun ((u, f) : string * string) (l : (int * string * string) list) acc ->
        let l = List.sort_uniq compare l in
        let f = if Filename.check_suffix f ":init" then u ^ "'s toplevel" else Ml_report.ml_function f in
        let _, s, _ = List.hd l in
        (* (as written, each once) *)
        let ws =
          List.fold_left (fun acc ((_, _, w) : int * string * string) -> if List.mem w acc then acc else acc @ [ w ]) [] l in
        let n = List.length ws in
        let shown = String.concat "; " (List.filteri (fun k _ -> k < 3) ws) in
        let more = if n > 3 then Printf.sprintf " and %d more" (n - 3) else "" in
        Printf.sprintf "%s: int31: in %s, %s%s: not on the Pi 1's 31 bits" (site s) f shown more :: acc)
      by_fun [] in
  (* a table's order given to an output (order.dl): a line a walk, the
   * outputs it reaches; a Marshal sharing what the compiler shared *)
  let outs = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt outs t.(0) with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
      Hashtbl.replace outs t.(0) (t.(1) :: l))
    (tuples "order_out" 2);
  let walk_fn = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter (fun (t : string array) -> Hashtbl.replace walk_fn t.(0) t.(1))
    (tuples "in_function" 2);
  let fun_of (u : string) (f : string) : string =
    if Filename.check_suffix f ":init" then u ^ "'s toplevel"
    else Ml_report.ml_function f in
  let order =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun (s0 : string) (is : string list) acc ->
        if not (own s0) then acc
        else
          let f =
            (* (the closure's call, S0:call1, is in the walk's function) *)
            match Hashtbl.find_opt walk_fn (s0 ^ ":call1") with
            | Some f -> fun_of (unit_of s0) f
            | None -> "?" in
          let is = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map site is) in
          let n = List.length is in
          let shown = String.concat ", " (List.filteri (fun k _ -> k < 3) is) in
          let more = if n > 3 then Printf.sprintf " and %d more" (n - 3) else "" in
          Printf.sprintf "%s: order: in %s, a table's order reaches the output at %s%s"
            (site s0) f shown more
          :: acc)
      outs [] in
  let sharing =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        if not (own t.(0)) then None
        else
          Some
            (Printf.sprintf "%s: sharing: in %s, Marshal without No_sharing: its bytes the compiler's"
               (site t.(0)) (fun_of (unit_of t.(0)) t.(1))))
      (tuples "shared" 2) in
  (* a start reading what a later one makes (init.dl): a line a pair of
   * units, the first global; two files of one unit's name *)
  let reads = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let i = t.(0) and j = t.(3) in
      if own i then begin
        let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt reads (i, j) with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
        Hashtbl.replace reads (i, j) ((t.(1), t.(2)) :: l)
      end)
    (tuples "early" 4);
  let init =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun ((i, j) : string * string) (l : (string * string) list) acc ->
        let u = unit_of i and v = unit_of j in
        let g, f = List.hd (List.sort compare l) in
        let n = List.length (List.sort_uniq compare (List.map fst l)) in
        let more = if n > 1 then Printf.sprintf " and %d more" (n - 1) else "" in
        let file =
          match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f | None -> u ^ ".ml" in
        Printf.sprintf "%s: init: %s's start reads %s%s (in %s), %s starting after it"
          file u g more (fun_of u f) v
        :: acc)
      reads [] in
  let link =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        if t.(1) < t.(2) then
          Some
            (Printf.sprintf "%s: link: two units %s, %s and %s: which one is linked the build's"
               t.(1) t.(0) t.(1) t.(2))
        else None)
      (tuples "twice" 3) in
  (* a write of a root's racing another (races.dl): a line a function
   * of the root and a field, its first other writer; a wait not in a
   * loop. A function's line is its closure's (f' is f's) *)
  let lines = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) -> Hashtbl.replace lines t.(0) (t.(1) ^ ":" ^ t.(2)))
    (tuples "closure" 3);
  let rec line_of (f : string) : string =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt lines f with
    | Some l -> site l
    | None ->
        let n = String.length f in
        if n > 0 && f.[n - 1] = '\'' then line_of (String.sub f 0 (n - 1))
        else unit_of f ^ ".ml" in
  let htypes = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter (fun (t : string array) -> Hashtbl.replace htypes t.(0) t.(1))
    (tuples "htype" 2);
  (* (a record's fields named, a ref, an array, a table by where made) *)
  let written (h : string) (flds : string list) : string =
    let labels = List.filter_map (C_report.prefix "fld:") flds in
    match flds with
    | [ "fld:contents" ] -> "the ref of " ^ site h
    | _ when labels <> [] && not (List.mem "contents" labels) ->
        let t =
          match Hashtbl.find_opt htypes h with Some t -> t | None -> "record" in
        Printf.sprintf "a %s's %s" t (String.concat " and " labels)
    | [ "arr:elt" ] -> "the array of " ^ site h
    | _ when List.for_all (fun f -> C_report.prefix "tbl:" f <> None) flds ->
        "the table of " ^ site h
    | _ -> Printf.sprintf "%s of %s" (String.concat " and " flds) (site h) in
  let writers = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let k = (t.(2), t.(3), t.(0)) in
      let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt writers k with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
      Hashtbl.replace writers k ((t.(1), t.(4)) :: l))
    (tuples "raced" 5);
  let race =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun ((f1, r, h) : string * string * string) (l : (string * string) list)
           acc ->
        let flds = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map fst l) in
        let fs = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map snd l) in
        let n = List.length fs in
        let shown = List.filteri (fun k _ -> k < 2) fs in
        let others =
          String.concat ", " (List.map (fun f -> fun_of (unit_of f) f) shown)
          ^ (if n > 2 then Printf.sprintf " and %d more" (n - 2) else "") in
        Printf.sprintf
          "%s: race: %s, run by a signal's handler (%s), writes %s, as %s does"
          (line_of f1) (fun_of (unit_of f1) f1) (line_of r) (written h flds)
          others
        :: acc)
      writers [] in
  let wait =
    List.map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        Printf.sprintf
          "%s: wait: in %s, Condition.wait not in a while: woken for another, \
           it goes on"
          (site t.(0)) (fun_of (unit_of t.(0)) t.(1)))
      (tuples "wait_once" 2) in
  (* a resource not given back when a call between raises (pairs.dl): a
   * line a call taking it, its first such call and exception *)
  let leaks = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : string array) ->
      let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt leaks t.(0) with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
      Hashtbl.replace leaks t.(0) ((t.(1), t.(3), t.(2)) :: l))
    (tuples "leak" 4);
  let exn_name (e : string) : string =
    match C_report.prefix "caml_exn_" e with Some x -> x | None -> e in
  let leak =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun (a : string) (l : (string * string * string) list) acc ->
        if not (own a) then acc
        else
          let l = List.sort compare l in
          let c, e, r = List.hd l in
          let n = List.length (List.sort_uniq compare (List.map (fun (c, _, _) -> c) l)) in
          let more = if n > 1 then Printf.sprintf " (and %d more calls)" (n - 1) else "" in
          let f = match Hashtbl.find_opt walk_fn a with Some f -> fun_of (unit_of a) f | None -> "?" in
          Printf.sprintf "%s: leak: in %s, taken here, given back at %s, not when %s raises %s%s"
            (site a) f (site r) (site c) (exn_name e) more
          :: acc)
      leaks [] in
  (* a variable never read (unused.dl): Main:x/12, x *)
  let unused =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let f = t.(0) and v = t.(1) in
        (* (the variable's unit: Before:b/12; a function is Before.first) *)
        if not (own v) then None
        else
          let name =
            match String.index_opt v ':', String.rindex_opt v '/' with
            | Some a, Some z when z > a -> String.sub v (a + 1) (z - a - 1)
            | _ -> v in
          Some
            (Printf.sprintf "%s: unused: in %s, %s is never read (_%s if meant)"
               (line_of f) (fun_of (unit_of f) f) name name))
      (tuples "unused_var" 2) in
  let unused = List.sort_uniq compare unused in
  (* a statement laid out in an if's branch, run after it (layout.dl) *)
  let layout =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let u = unit_of t.(0) in
        if not (Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own u) then None
        else
          Some
            (Printf.sprintf
               "%s: layout: in the column of the if's branch above, not in it: run whatever the test"
               (site (u ^ ":" ^ t.(3)))))
      (tuples "dangling" 4) in
  let layout = List.sort_uniq compare layout in
  (* two operands with an effect, which first the compiler's
   * (evalorder.dl): a line an expression, where its operands start *)
  let pos = Hashtbl.create 1024 in
  List.iter (fun (t : string array) -> Hashtbl.replace pos t.(0) (t.(1), t.(2))) (tuples "pos" 3);
  let at (n : string) : string =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt pos n with Some (l, c) -> l ^ ":" ^ c | None -> "?" in
  let unordered =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        let u = unit_of t.(0) in
        if not (Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own u) then None
        else
          let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt pos t.(0) with Some (l, _) -> l | None -> "?" in
          Some
            (Printf.sprintf
               "%s: evalorder: operands at %s and %s, both with an effect: \
                their order the compiler's"
               (site (u ^ ":" ^ l)) (at t.(1)) (at t.(2))))
      (tuples "unordered" 3) in
  let unordered = List.sort_uniq compare unordered in
  (* inside a function that gives back its argument, a raise before it
   * does (pairs.dl's leak_in): a line a call *)
  let leak =
    leak
    @ List.filter_map
        (fun (t : string array) ->
          let f = t.(0) and c = t.(1) and r = t.(2) in
          if not (own c) then None
          else
            Some
              (Printf.sprintf "%s: leak: in %s, its argument given back at %s, not when this raises %s"
                 (site c) (fun_of (unit_of c) f) (site r) (exn_name t.(3))))
        (tuples "leak_in" 4) in
  let order = List.sort_uniq compare order in
  let sharing = List.sort_uniq compare sharing in
  let race = List.sort_uniq compare race and wait = List.sort_uniq compare wait in
  let all =
    List.sort_uniq compare
      (physeq @ stack @ swallowed @ crash @ int31 @ order @ sharing @ init @ link
       @ race @ wait @ leak @ unused @ layout @ unordered) in
  List.iter (fun b -> Console.print caps ("bug? " ^ b ^ "\n")) all;
  (* (the analyses that report, by their number: within 80 columns) *)
  let counts =
    List.filter_map
      (fun ((k, l) : string * string list) ->
        if l = [] then None else Some (Printf.sprintf "%s %d" k (List.length l)))
      [ ("physeq", physeq); ("stack", stack); ("swallowed", swallowed);
        ("crash", crash); ("int31", int31); ("order", order);
        ("sharing", sharing); ("init", init); ("link", link); ("race", race);
        ("wait", wait); ("leak", leak); ("unused", unused);
        ("layout", layout); ("evalorder", unordered) ] in
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%d bugs?%s\n" (List.length all)
       (if counts = [] then "" else " (" ^ String.concat ", " counts ^ ")"))

let raises_report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) : unit =
  let tuples r = List.map (fun (t : int array) -> Array.map (name p) t) (D.tuples (D.relation p r 3)) in
  let exn (e : string) : string = match C_report.prefix "caml_exn_" e with Some x -> x | None -> e in
  (* Sys.remove: Sys.ml, its unit's file *)
  let file (g : string) : string =
    let u = match String.index_opt g '.' with Some i -> String.sub g 0 i | None -> g in
    match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f | None -> u ^ ".ml" in
  let lines =
    List.map
      (fun (t : string array) ->
        Printf.sprintf "%s: raises: %s's C (%s) may raise %s, not said ([@@raise %s])" (file t.(0)) t.(0) t.(1)
          (exn t.(2)) (exn t.(2)))
      (tuples "undeclared")
    @ List.map
        (fun (t : string array) ->
          Printf.sprintf "%s: raises: %s says [@@raise %s], its C (%s) never raises it" (file t.(0)) t.(0)
            (exn t.(2)) t.(1))
        (tuples "overdeclared") in
  let lines = List.sort_uniq compare lines in
  List.iter (fun l -> Console.print caps ("bug? " ^ l ^ "\n")) lines;
  Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%d bugs? (raises %d)\n" (List.length lines) (List.length lines))

(* See C_report.mli *)

module D = Datalog

(* An included file's lines take global lines: the file's own line is
 * the global one less where it began and less the lines of the files
 * it included before it. A stack of the files open at that point:
 * (name, its first global line, the lines its includes took) *)
let locate (hist : (string option * int) list) (l : int) : (string * int) option =
  let rec go stack = function
    | (Some f, at) :: rest when at <= l -> go ((f, at, 0) :: stack) rest
    | (None, at) :: rest when at <= l -> (
        match stack with
        | (_, s, _) :: (p, ps, pk) :: up -> go ((p, ps, pk + (at - s)) :: up) rest
        | _ -> go [] rest)
    | _ -> (match stack with (f, s, k) :: _ -> Some (f, l - s - k + 1) | [] -> None) in
  go [] hist

(* _in_walk_line_56_1: the function and the global line *)
let site (s : string) : (string * int) option =
  let rec last i = if i < 0 then None else if i + 6 <= String.length s && String.sub s i 6 = "_line_" then Some i else last (i - 1) in
  match last (String.length s - 6) with
  | Some i when String.length s > 4 && String.sub s 0 4 = "_in_" -> (
      let f = String.sub s 4 (i - 4) in
      let rest = String.sub s (i + 6) (String.length s - i - 6) in
      match String.index_opt rest '_' with
      | Some j -> Option.map (fun n -> (f, n)) (int_of_string_opt (String.sub rest 0 j))
      | None -> None)
  | _ -> None

(* walk__f: f; a temporary loaded from a member or an array, d->read or
 * devtab[] (the facts' assign_load_field and assign_array_elt, by the
 * temporary: what it was loaded from, what is said after it); another,
 * what the call computes *)
let rec through (loads : (string, string * string) Hashtbl.t) (f : string) (v : string) : string =
  let pre = f ^ "__" in
  let strip pre s = if String.length s > String.length pre && String.sub s 0 (String.length pre) = pre then Some (String.sub s (String.length pre) (String.length s - String.length pre)) else None in
  match Hashtbl.find_opt loads v, strip pre v with
  | Some (x, after), _ -> (match through loads f x with "a computed pointer" -> "(...)" | x -> x) ^ after
  | None, Some x when String.length x > 1 && x.[0] = 't' && String.for_all (fun c -> c >= '0' && c <= '9') (String.sub x 1 (String.length x - 1)) -> "a computed pointer"
  | None, Some x -> x
  | None, None -> v

let name (p : D.t) (i : int) : string = match p.terms.(i) with Prolog.Atom s -> s | Prolog.Int n -> string_of_int n | _ -> "?"

let prefix (pre : string) (s : string) : string option =
  let n = String.length pre in
  if String.length s > n && String.sub s 0 n = pre then Some (String.sub s n (String.length s - n)) else None

(* a place's kind, by Facts's names: an allocator's ('_malloc_in_f_line_N'),
 * a string's ('_str_in_...'), a function's own (f__x, its local or
 * parameter; '_array_elt_f__x', its local array's elements), and the
 * function; None: a global's *)
type place = Heap | Literal | Local of string * string | Global

let place (s : string) : place =
  (* f__x: the longest f that is a function read *)
  let local v =
    let rec go i =
      if i < 1 then None
      else if String.sub v i 2 = "__" && Hashtbl.mem C_front.owner (String.sub v 0 i) then
        Some (String.sub v 0 i, String.sub v (i + 2) (String.length v - i - 2))
      else go (i - 1) in
    go (String.length v - 3) in
  match prefix "_malloc_in_" s, prefix "_str_in_" s, prefix "_array_elt_" s with
  | _ when s = ".string" -> Literal
  | Some _, _, _ -> Heap
  | _, Some _, _ -> Literal
  | _, _, Some v -> (match local v with Some (f, x) -> Local (f, x ^ "[]") | None -> Global)
  | _ -> (match local s with Some (f, x) -> Local (f, x) | None -> Global)

(* the facts as Facts finds them, each a tuple of the relation, its
 * names Datalog's symbols: no text between them
 * (old: Facts.text () given to D.load, the text parsed again); and
 * bugs/pointers.dl's heap, local and literal of each name seen *)
let rec given (p : D.t) (relation : string) (args : Facts.arg list) : unit =
  let r = D.relation p relation (List.length args) in
  let value = function Facts.Sym s -> D.symbol p (Prolog.Atom s) | Facts.Num n -> D.symbol p (Prolog.Int n) in
  if D.add r (Array.of_list (List.map value args)) then begin
    r.given <- r.given + 1;
    List.iter
      (function
        | Facts.Sym s when relation <> "heap" && relation <> "local" && relation <> "literal" -> (
            match place s with
            | Heap -> given p "heap" [ Sym s ]
            | Literal -> given p "literal" [ Sym s ]
            | Local (f, _) -> given p "local" [ Sym s; Sym f ]
            | Global -> ())
        | _ -> ())
      args
  end

(* a function's global line, in its file *)
let where (f : string) (l : int) : string * int =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt C_front.owner f with
  | Some file -> (match locate (Hashtbl.find C_front.histories file) l with Some w -> w | None -> (file, l))
  | None -> ("?", l)

(* a place as the C says it *)
let said (s : string) : string =
  match place s with
  | Heap -> "what an allocator gave"
  | Literal when s = ".string" -> "a string (an initializer's)"
  | Literal -> (match site ("_in_" ^ Option.get (prefix "_str_in_" s) ^ "_0") with Some (f, l) -> Printf.sprintf "a string (line %d)" (snd (where f l)) | None -> "a string")
  | Local (f, x) -> Printf.sprintf "%s, a local of %s" x f
  | Global -> (match prefix "_array_elt_" s with Some v -> v ^ "[], a global" | None -> if Hashtbl.mem C_front.owner s then "the function " ^ s else s ^ ", a global")

(* the analysis on the facts: each call through a pointer, where, and
 * what it may reach; then what bugs/pointers.dl finds *)

let report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) : unit =
  let tuples r = D.tuples (D.relation p r 2) in
  let loads = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : int array) ->
      let fld = name p t.(2) in
      let fld = if String.length fld > 6 && String.sub fld 0 6 = "_fld__" then String.sub fld 6 (String.length fld - 6) else fld in
      Hashtbl.replace loads (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1), "->" ^ fld))
    (D.tuples (D.relation p "assign_load_field" 3));
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.replace loads (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1), "[]")) (tuples "assign_array_elt");
  let edges = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.add edges (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1))) (tuples "target");
  (* (the calls in code that runs: what is not reached has no answers) *)
  let running = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.replace running (name p t.(0)) ()) (D.tuples (D.relation p "running" 3));
  let calls =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : int array) ->
        let s = name p t.(0) and v = name p t.(1) in
        match site s with
        | _ when not (Hashtbl.mem running s) -> None
        | None -> None
        | Some (f, l) ->
            let file, line = where f l in
            Some (file, line, f, through loads f v, List.sort_uniq compare (Hashtbl.find_all edges s)))
      (tuples "call_indirect") in
  let calls = List.sort_uniq compare calls in
  List.iter
    (fun (file, line, f, v, targets) ->
      Console.print caps
        (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: in %s, through %s: %s\n" file line f v
           (if targets = [] then "nothing found" else String.concat ", " targets)))
    calls;
  (* a free's places together, a string's lines in one *)
  let frees = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.add frees (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1))) (tuples "bad_free");
  let sites = List.sort_uniq compare (Hashtbl.fold (fun i _ acc -> i :: acc) frees []) in
  let bugs =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (i : string) ->
        match site i with
        | Some (f, l) ->
            let file, line = where f l in
            let places = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map said (Hashtbl.find_all frees i)) in
            let strings, others = List.partition (fun x -> prefix "a string" x <> None) places in
            let strings =
              match strings with
              | [] -> []
              | [ x ] -> [ x ]
              | xs ->
                  let line x = Option.bind (prefix "a string (line " x) (fun n -> int_of_string_opt (String.sub n 0 (String.length n - 1))) in
                  let lines = List.sort compare (List.filter_map line xs) in
                  [ Printf.sprintf "%d strings (%slines %s)" (List.length xs)
                      (if List.length lines < List.length xs then "an initializer's, " else "")
                      (String.concat ", " (List.map string_of_int lines)) ] in
            Some (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: in %s, free may be given %s, not the heap's" file line f (String.concat "; " (others @ strings)))
        | None -> None)
      sites
    @ List.map
        (fun (t : int array) ->
          let f = name p t.(0) in
          let file = match Hashtbl.find_opt C_front.owner f with Some file -> file | None -> "?" in
          Printf.sprintf "%s: %s may return the address of %s" file f (said (name p t.(1))))
        (tuples "dangling") in
  List.iter (fun b -> Console.print caps ("bug? " ^ b ^ "\n")) (List.sort_uniq compare bugs);
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%d functions, %d calls through a pointer, %d of them reaching nothing; %d bugs?\n"
       (Hashtbl.length C_front.owner) (List.length calls)
       (List.length (List.filter (fun (_, _, _, _, t) -> t = []) calls))
       (List.length (List.sort_uniq compare bugs)))

(* A C program's analysis said (mini-analyze's report, Analyze.mli):
 * each call through a pointer, where, through what, and the functions
 * it may reach (points_to/'s target); then what bugs/pointers.dl finds, a free
 * of what no allocator gave, a function returning its frame's address.
 * And the facts as Facts finds them given to Datalog as values, with
 * bugs/pointers.dl's heap, local and literal of each place. Both of
 * mini-analyze's roads use it: the native one, whose rules
 * mini-datalog's evaluator runs, and the .NET one, whose rules are
 * compiled (analyzers/dotnet/Analyze_rt). *)

(* a global line of a file read with its #includes: the file and its
 * own line, by the history (the oldest first) *)
val locate : (string option * int) list -> int -> (string * int) option

(* a symbol's text *)
val name : Datalog.t -> int -> string

(* s after pre, if it starts so *)
val prefix : string -> string -> string option

(* a place's kind, by Facts's names: an allocator's, a string's, a
 * function's local (the function, the name), a global's *)

 * its places *)

 * it was loaded from (the facts' assign_load_field, assign_array_elt) *)

(* See Caps_report.mli *)

module D = Datalog

let name = C_report.name
let prefix = C_report.prefix
let ml_function = Ml_report.ml_function

(* -caps: what capabilities.dl finds, a line a function: what it holds, what is
 * missing and by what, what it holds for nothing *)
let caps_report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) : unit =
  let tuples r n = List.map (fun (t : int array) -> Array.map (name p) t) (D.tuples (D.relation p r n)) in
  let file_of u = match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f | None -> u in
  let lines = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter (fun t -> Hashtbl.replace lines t.(0) (file_of t.(1), int_of_string t.(2))) (tuples "closure" 3);
  let at (o : string) : string * int =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt lines o with
    | Some w -> w
    | None -> (file_of (String.sub o 0 (String.index o ':')), 0) in
  let requires = tuples "requires" 2 in
  (* Cap.open_in|Cap.open_out: what allows S *)
  let need (s : string) : string =
    String.concat "|"
      (List.sort compare (List.filter_map (fun t -> if t.(0) = s then Some ("Cap." ^ t.(1)) else None) requires)) in
  let held (o : string) : string list =
    List.sort_uniq compare
      (List.filter_map (fun t -> if t.(0) = o then Some ("Cap." ^ t.(1)) else None) (tuples "declared_by" 2)) in
  (* one function's needs, each with the ways: Cap.stdout (Pervasives.print_string) *)
  let needs (r : string array list) (o : string) : string =
    let mine = List.filter (fun t -> t.(0) = o) r in
    let by_need =
      List.sort_uniq compare (List.map (fun t -> need t.(1)) mine)
      |> List.map (fun n ->
             let ways =
               List.sort_uniq compare
                 (List.filter_map
                    (fun t ->
                      if need t.(1) <> n then None
                      else if t.(2) <> "itself" then Some (ml_function t.(2))
                      else match prefix "prim:" t.(1) with Some x -> Some x | None -> Some t.(1))
                    mine) in
             Printf.sprintf "%s (%s)" n (String.concat ", " ways)) in
    String.concat ", " by_need in
  let functions r = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map (fun t -> t.(0)) r) in
  let none = tuples "no_cap" 3 and wrong = tuples "wrong_cap" 3 and unused = tuples "unused_cap" 2 in
  (* a function a line *)
  let report =
    List.map
      (fun o ->
        let f, l = at o in
        let unneeded = List.sort compare (List.filter_map (fun t -> if t.(0) = o then Some ("Cap." ^ t.(1)) else None) unused) in
        let says =
          (if List.exists (fun t -> t.(0) = o) none then [ "no capability, needs " ^ needs none o ] else [])
          @ (if List.exists (fun t -> t.(0) = o) wrong then [ "needs " ^ needs wrong o ] else [])
          @ if unneeded = [] then [] else [ "may not need " ^ String.concat ", " unneeded ] in
        let has = match held o with [] -> "" | h -> Printf.sprintf "has < %s >, " (String.concat "; " h) in
        (f, l, Printf.sprintf "%s: %s%s" (ml_function o) has (String.concat "; " says)))
      (functions (none @ wrong @ List.map (fun t -> [| t.(0) |]) unused)) in
  List.iter
    (fun (f, l, msg) -> Console.print caps (if l > 0 then Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: %s\n" f l msg else Printf.sprintf "%s: %s\n" f msg))
    (List.sort compare report);
  (* what is asked for most: where to start *)
  let counts = Hashtbl.create 17 in
  List.iter
    (fun t ->
      let n = need t.(1) in
      Hashtbl.replace counts n ((try Hashtbl.find counts n with Not_found -> []) @ [ t.(0) ]))
    (none @ wrong);
  let by_cap =
    Hashtbl.fold (fun n os acc -> (List.length (List.sort_uniq compare os), n) :: acc) counts []
    |> List.sort (fun a b -> compare b a)
    |> List.map (fun (k, n) -> Printf.sprintf "%s %d" n k) in
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%d functions with no capability, %d with the wrong one, %d with one they may not need%s\n"
       (List.length (functions none)) (List.length (functions wrong)) (List.length (functions unused))
       (if by_cap = [] then "" else "; missing: " ^ String.concat ", " by_cap))

(* the report, on the facts and the rules' answers *)

(* See Dead_report.mli *)

module D = Datalog

let name = C_report.name
let prefix = C_report.prefix
let where = C_report.where
let ml_function = Ml_report.ml_function

(* -dead: what dead.dl finds, each with where it is written *)
let dead_report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) (ml : bool) : unit =
  let tuples r n = List.map (fun (t : int array) -> Array.map (name p) t) (D.tuples (D.relation p r n)) in
  let unit_of (f : string) : string =
    let stop c = match String.index_opt f c with Some i -> i | None -> String.length f in
    String.sub f 0 (min (stop ':') (stop '.')) in
  let is_own (f : string) : bool = (not ml) || Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own (unit_of f) in
  let file_of u = match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f | None -> u in
  let shown (f : string) : string = if ml then ml_function f else f in
  let lines = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter (fun t -> Hashtbl.replace lines t.(0) (file_of t.(1), int_of_string t.(2))) (tuples "closure" 3);
  List.iter
    (fun t ->
      let f = t.(0) in
      Hashtbl.replace lines f (match where f (int_of_string t.(1)) with (file, _) when t.(1) = "0" -> (file, 0) | w -> w))
    (tuples "defined" 2);
  let at (f : string) : string * int =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt lines f with
    | Some w -> w
    | None -> ((if ml then file_of (unit_of f) else match Hashtbl.find_opt C_front.owner f with Some x -> x | None -> "?"), 0) in
  let one (f, l, msg) =
    if f = "?" then msg else if l > 0 then Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: %s" f l msg else Printf.sprintf "%s: %s" f msg in
  let names r n f = List.sort_uniq compare (List.filter_map (fun t -> if t.(0) = f then Some (shown t.(1)) else None) (tuples r n)) in
  let unnamed = List.map (fun t -> t.(0)) (tuples "never_named" 1) in
  let dead = List.filter is_own (List.map (fun t -> t.(0)) (tuples "dead" 1)) in
  let functions =
    List.map
      (fun f ->
        let file, l = at f in
        let why =
          if List.mem f unnamed then "nothing names it"
          else match names "named_in_live" 2 f with
            | [] -> "named only by dead code: " ^ String.concat ", " (names "named_in_dead" 2 f)
            | g -> "in " ^ String.concat ", " g ^ " but no call goes through the pointer" in
        (file, l, Printf.sprintf "dead: %s, %s" (shown f) why))
      dead in
  let globals =
    List.filter_map
      (fun t ->
        let g = t.(0) in
        if not (is_own g) then None else
        let file, l = at g in
        Some (file, l, Printf.sprintf "dead global: %s, nothing live names it" (shown g)))
      (tuples "dead_global" 1) in
  let stmts =
    List.map
      (fun t ->
        let file, l = where t.(0) (int_of_string t.(1)) in
        (file, l, Printf.sprintf "dead code: in %s, after a jump" t.(0)))
      (tuples "dead_stmt" 2) in
  let field (f : string) : string option =
    match prefix "_fld__" f, prefix "fld:" f with Some x, _ | _, Some x -> Some x | None, None -> None in
  (* a field or a constructor once, at its first place *)
  let by_function (r : string) (msg : string -> string -> string) keep =
    let seen = Hashtbl.create 17 in
    List.filter_map
      (fun t ->
        if is_own t.(1) && keep t.(0) && not (Hashtbl.mem seen t.(0)) then begin
          Hashtbl.add seen t.(0) ();
          let file, l = at t.(1) in
          Some (file, l, msg t.(0) (shown t.(1)))
        end
        else None)
      (List.sort compare (tuples r 2)) in
  let fields =
    by_function "dead_field"
      (fun f g -> Printf.sprintf "dead field: %s stored in %s, nothing live reads it" (Option.get (field f)) g)
      (fun f -> field f <> None) in
  let constructors =
    by_function "never_built"
      (fun c g -> Printf.sprintf "never built: %s, matched in %s" (match prefix "con:" c with Some x -> x | None -> c) g)
      (fun c -> prefix "con:" c <> None) in
  let all = functions @ globals @ stmts @ fields @ constructors in
  List.iter (fun x -> Console.print caps (one x ^ "\n")) (List.sort_uniq compare all);
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%d functions dead (%d nothing names), %d only through a pointer; %d globals, %d fields, %d constructors, %d statements\n"
       (List.length dead) (List.length (List.filter is_own unnamed)) (List.length (tuples "through_pointer" 1))
       (List.length globals) (List.length fields) (List.length constructors) (List.length stmts))

(* Claude Code

(* See Exn_report.mli *)

module D = Datalog

let name = C_report.name
let prefix = C_report.prefix

(* an exception as written: Main.Empty, Not_found (caml_exn_Not_found) *)
let exn (e : string) : string =
  match prefix "caml_exn_" e with Some x -> x | None -> if e = "?" then "an exception not known" else e

(* Main:11:r6: Main.ml:11 *)
let site (r : string) : string =
  match String.split_on_char ':' r with
  | u :: l :: _ ->
      let file = match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> Filename.basename f | None -> u ^ ".ml" in
      file ^ ":" ^ l
  | _ -> r

(* Main:init, Main.trap, Main:try2@67: Main *)
let unit_of (f : string) : string =
  let n = String.length f in
  let rec go i =
    if i >= n || f.[i] = ':' || f.[i] = '.' then String.sub f 0 i
    else go (i + 1) in
  go 0

(* Main:try2@67: 67 *)
let try_line (t : string) : string =
  match String.index_opt t '@' with
  | Some i -> String.sub t (i + 1) (String.length t - i - 1)
  | None -> "?"

let find (h : (string, string) Hashtbl.t) (k : string) (default : string) =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt h k with Some v -> v | None -> default

let exn_report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) : unit =
  let tuples r =
    List.map (fun (t : int array) -> Array.map (name p) t)
      (D.tuples (D.relation p r 2)) in
  let table (r : string) : (string, string) Hashtbl.t =
    let h = Hashtbl.create 101 in
    List.iter (fun t -> Hashtbl.replace h t.(0) t.(1)) (tuples r);
    h in
  let inside = table "raise_in" and fn = table "try_in_function" in
  let raised = tuples "raised" in
  (* where e may be raised: Main.ml:11 (Main.first) *)
  let sites (e : string) : string list =
    List.sort_uniq compare
      (List.filter_map
         (fun r ->
           if r.(0) <> e then None
           else
             let g = match Hashtbl.find_opt inside r.(1) with
               | Some g -> " (" ^ Ml_report.ml_function g ^ ")"
               | None -> "" in
             Some (site r.(1) ^ g))
         raised) in
  (* who: of a toplevel, a function C calls (trap), a try (Main:try2@67) *)
  let report (rel : string) (who : string -> string -> string -> string) =
    List.iter
      (fun t ->
        let f = t.(0) and e = t.(1) in
        let u = unit_of f in
        if Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own u then begin
          let file = match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with
            | Some x -> Filename.basename x
            | None -> u in
          let at = match sites e with
            | [] -> ""
            | l -> ", raised at " ^ String.concat ", " l in
          Console.print caps (who file f (exn e) ^ at ^ "\n")
        end)
      (List.sort_uniq compare (tuples rel)) in
  report "uncaught" (fun file _ e ->
      file ^ ": the toplevel may let " ^ e ^ " escape");
  report "from_c" (fun file f e ->
      Printf.sprintf "%s: %s, called from C, may let %s escape" file
        (Ml_report.ml_function f) e);
  report "ends_in" (fun file t e ->
      Printf.sprintf "%s:%s: the try in %s, its handler raising, may be reached by %s"
        file (try_line t) (Ml_report.ml_function (find fn t "?")) e)

analyzers/report/Ml_report.ml
4893
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Ml_report.mli *)

module D = Datalog

let name (p : D.t) (i : int) : string = match p.terms.(i) with Prolog.Atom s -> s | Prolog.Int n -> string_of_int n | _ -> "?"

(* (not String.ends_with: mini-ml knows another unit's labels only by
 * its type given) *)
let ends_with (suffix : string) (s : string) : bool =
  let n = String.length suffix and m = String.length s in
  m >= n && String.sub s (m - n) n = suffix

let prefix (pre : string) (s : string) : string option =
  let n = String.length pre in
  if String.length s > n && String.sub s 0 n = pre then Some (String.sub s n (String.length s - n)) else None

(* an ML function as said: Use.f, a local Use:go/3 as go, a lambda
 * Use:fun1@11 as "Use:fun at line 11", an external prim:name *)
let rec ml_function (f : string) : string =
  (* (f' is f given its first argument: f for the reader) *)
  if String.length f > 1 && f.[String.length f - 1] = '\'' then ml_function (String.sub f 0 (String.length f - 1)) else
  match prefix "prim:" f with
  | Some x -> x ^ " (external)"
  | None -> (
      match String.index_opt f ':' with
      | None -> f
      | Some i -> (
          let u = String.sub f 0 i and rest = String.sub f (i + 1) (String.length f - i - 1) in
          match String.index_opt rest '@', String.index_opt rest '/' with
          | Some j, _ when prefix "fun" rest <> None -> Printf.sprintf "%s:fun at line %s" u (String.sub rest (j + 1) (String.length rest - j - 1))
          | _, Some j -> String.sub rest 0 j
          | _ -> rest))

(* the ML part: each call through a variable of the program's own
 * units, its targets; the program's functions its toplevel does not
 * reach (calls.dl's unreached) *)
let ml_report (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) : unit =
  let tuples r = D.tuples (D.relation p r 2) in
  let edges = Hashtbl.create 101 and inside = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.add edges (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1))) (tuples "call_edge");
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.replace inside (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1))) (tuples "in_function");
  let file u = match Hashtbl.find_opt Ml_front.files u with Some f -> f | None -> u in
  (* a temporary loaded from a field: h.on_key *)
  let loads = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter
    (fun (t : int array) ->
      let fld = name p t.(2) in
      Hashtbl.replace loads (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1), match prefix "fld:" fld with Some x -> x | None -> fld))
    (D.tuples (D.relation p "assign_load_field" 3));
  let through v =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt loads v with
    | Some (x, fld) when String.contains x '/' -> Some (ml_function x ^ "." ^ fld)
    | Some _ -> None
    | None -> if String.contains v '/' then Some (ml_function v) else None in
  (* Use:11:c3: the unit and the line; a variable Use:h/4 *)
  let calls =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : int array) ->
        let i = name p t.(0) and v = name p t.(1) in
        match String.split_on_char ':' i, String.split_on_char ':' v with
        | [ u; line; _ ], [ _; _ ] when Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own u -> (
            match through v with
            | Some v -> (
                let line = int_of_string line in
                let f = match Hashtbl.find_opt inside i with Some f -> ml_function f | None -> "?" in
                match List.sort_uniq compare (List.map ml_function (Hashtbl.find_all edges i)) with
                (* (a let rec's call of itself, its name a local) *)
                | [ t ] when t = v || ends_with ("." ^ v) t -> None
                | targets -> Some (file u, line, f, v, targets))
            | None -> None)
        | _ -> None)
      (tuples "call_indirect") in
  let calls = List.sort_uniq compare calls in
  List.iter
    (fun (file, line, f, v, targets) ->
      Console.print caps
        (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: in %s, through %s: %s\n" file line f v
           (if targets = [] then "nothing found" else String.concat ", " targets)))
    calls;
  let lines = Hashtbl.create 101 in
  List.iter (fun (t : int array) -> Hashtbl.replace lines (name p t.(0)) (name p t.(1), name p t.(2))) (D.tuples (D.relation p "closure" 3));
  let unreached =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (t : int array) ->
        let f = name p t.(0) in
        match Hashtbl.find_opt lines f with
        | Some (u, l) when Hashtbl.mem Ml_front.own u -> Some (Printf.sprintf "never reached: %s (%s:%s)" (ml_function f) (file u) l)
        | _ -> None)
      (D.tuples (D.relation p "unreached" 1)) in
  List.iter (fun l -> Console.print caps (l ^ "\n")) (List.sort_uniq compare unreached);
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%d units (%d the program's), %d calls through a variable, %d functions never reached\n"
       (Hashtbl.length Ml_front.files) (Hashtbl.length Ml_front.own) (List.length calls) (List.length unreached))

val ml_function : string -> string

(* Claude Code
