(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Map_window.mli *)

module P = Playground

type caps = Map_services.caps

module S = Map_services

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Types *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a tile in memory: its own picture, or its ancestor's enlarged *)
type tile = { image : Rgba_image.t; sharp : bool; mutable used : int }

(* a forecast: asked, or come and when; asked again after a quarter of an
 * hour, how often the service makes a new one *)
type forecast = Asked | Came of float * (Weather.t, string) result

(* r: where from, then the next place marked is where to *)
type routing = No_route | From of Place.t | Asking of Place.t | Shown of Routing.t

type model = {
  z : int;
  cx : int; (* the window's centre, a pixel of the world at zoom z *)
  cy : int;
  grab : (float * float * int * int) option; (* a drag: the mouse and the centre when it began *)
  wheel : float; (* the wheel's notches not yet a zoom's level *)
  store : (string, tile) Hashtbl.t;
  failed : (string, float) Hashtbl.t; (* a tile that failed: when to ask again *)
  ticks : int; (* a frame's number, for the least recently used *)
  generation : int; (* changes with what the store has for the view *)
  said : string; (* what went wrong last with a tile *)
  finding : string option; (* the Find box open, what is typed in it *)
  place : Place.t option; (* the place found: its marker, its name *)
  known : (string * Place.t) list; (* the last places, by what was typed: not asked again *)
  notice : string; (* what the search says, until the map moves *)
  asked_at : float; (* when the service was last asked *)
  start : string option; (* the place on the command line, asked at the first frame *)
  held : string list; (* the keys down at the last frame *)
  ask : string -> unit; (* a place asked of the service, by the worker *)
  weather_at : (string * float * float) option; (* the panel open: the place it is of *)
  forecasts : (string, forecast) Hashtbl.t; (* by where, to two decimals *)
  ask_forecast : string -> float -> float -> unit; (* by the worker *)
  save : (string * Place.t) list -> unit; (* the last places written down *)
  routing : routing;
  ask_route : Place.t -> Place.t -> unit; (* by the worker *)
}

let kept = 120
let again_after = 30.
let credit = "\xc2\xa9 OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL"
let default_tiles = "https://tile.openstreetmap.org"
let forecast_good = 900.
let places_kept = 20
let rows_shown = 6
let default_cache_megabytes = 32

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A tile *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the tile, by the rules of Tile_cache.mli: on the disk and good, it is
 * not asked; on the disk and old, asked if it changed, and shown if the
 * server does not answer; else asked *)
let fetch (caps : caps) (base : string) (cache : Tile_cache.t option) (key : Tiles.key) : (Rgba_image.t, string) result =
  let name = Tiles.name key in
  let now = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () in
  let ask (more : Http.header list) : (Http.response, string) result =
    Map_http.get caps ~more (Tiles.url base key)
  in
  let kept (e : Tile_cache.entry) : unit = Option.iter (fun (c : Tile_cache.t) -> Tile_cache.put c name e) cache in
  (* what a server gave: kept if it may be *)
  let given (r : Http.response) : (Rgba_image.t, string) result =
    if r.status <> 200 then Error (Printf.sprintf "%d %s" r.status r.reason)
    else begin
      (match Tile_cache.lifetime ~now r.headers with
      | Some expires -> kept { bytes = r.body; expires; etag = Http.header "ETag" r.headers }
      | None -> ());
      Ok (Png.decode r.body)
    end
  in
  (* (a file cut short by a crash: not a tile, asked again) *)
  let read (e : Tile_cache.entry) : Rgba_image.t option = try Some (Png.decode e.bytes) with Failure _ -> None in
  let afresh () : (Rgba_image.t, string) result =
    match ask [] with Ok r -> given r | Error why -> Error why
  in
  match Option.bind cache (fun (c : Tile_cache.t) -> Tile_cache.find c name) with
  | None -> afresh ()
  | Some e -> (
      match read e with
      | None -> afresh ()
      | Some image when e.expires > now -> Ok image
      | Some image -> (
          let more = match e.etag with Some tag -> [ ("If-None-Match", tag) ] | None -> [] in
          match ask more with
          | Ok r when r.status = 304 ->
              (match Tile_cache.lifetime ~now r.headers with
              | Some expires -> kept { e with expires }
              | None -> ());
              Ok image
          | Ok r when r.status = 200 -> given r
          | Ok _ | Error _ -> Ok image))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The store *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the tiles over [kept], the least recently shown *)
let trimmed (m : model) : unit =
  let over = Hashtbl.length m.store - kept in
  if over > 0 then begin
    let all = Hashtbl.fold (fun (k : string) (t : tile) acc -> (t.used, k) :: acc) m.store [] in
    List.iteri
      (fun (i : int) ((_, k) : int * string) -> if i < over then Hashtbl.remove m.store k)
      (List.sort compare all)
  end

let collected (now : float) (m : model) : model =
  match Map_worker.take () with
  | [] -> m
  | done_ ->
      let said =
        List.fold_left
          (fun (_ : string) ((key, r) : Tiles.key * (Rgba_image.t, string) result) ->
            let k = Tiles.name key in
            match r with
            | Ok image ->
                Hashtbl.remove m.failed k;
                Hashtbl.replace m.store k { image; sharp = true; used = m.ticks };
                ""
            | Error why ->
                Hashtbl.replace m.failed k (now +. again_after);
                Printf.sprintf "tile %s: %s" k why)
          m.said done_
      in
      trimmed m;
      { m with said; generation = m.generation + 1 }

(* the tile's own picture or, while it has not come, a part of its nearest
 * ancestor that is there, kept in the store *)
let placeholder (m : model) (key : Tiles.key) : Rgba_image.t option =
  let rec up (n : int) : Rgba_image.t option =
    if n > 4 || n > key.z then None
    else
      match Hashtbl.find_opt m.store (Tiles.name (Tiles.ancestor key n)) with
      | Some { sharp = true; image; _ } -> Some (Tiles.enlarged image key n)
      | _ -> up (n + 1)
  in
  up 1

(* what the view shows: each tile marked as used, an enlarged one made if
 * it can be, and those to fetch *)
let in_store (now : float) (m : model) (visible : Tiles.placed list) : model * Tiles.key list =
  let changed = ref false in
  let missing =
    List.filter
      (fun (p : Tiles.placed) ->
        let k = Tiles.name p.key in
        let sharp =
          match Hashtbl.find_opt m.store k with
          | Some t -> t.used <- m.ticks; t.sharp
          | None -> (
              match placeholder m p.key with
              | Some image ->
                  Hashtbl.replace m.store k { image; sharp = false; used = m.ticks };
                  changed := true;
                  false
              | None -> false)
        in
        (not sharp) && match Hashtbl.find_opt m.failed k with Some at -> now >= at | None -> true)
      visible
  in
  let rec unique (seen : string list) (l : Tiles.placed list) : Tiles.key list =
    match l with
    | [] -> []
    | p :: rest ->
        let k = Tiles.name p.key in
        if List.mem k seen then unique seen rest else p.key :: unique (k :: seen) rest
  in
  (trimmed m;
   if !changed then { m with generation = m.generation + 1 } else m),
  unique [] missing

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Where the window is *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let zoomed (dz : int) (px : int) (py : int) (h : int) (m : model) : model =
  let z = max 0 (min Tiles.max_zoom (m.z + dz)) in
  if z = m.z then m
  else
    let cx, cy = Tiles.rezoomed ~dz:(z - m.z) ~px ~py m.cx m.cy in
    let cx, cy = Tiles.centred z cx cy h in
    { m with z; cx; cy; grab = None }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A place *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* what the worker found: the query and its answer, for the window to take *)
let found : (string * (Place.t list, string) result) option ref = ref None

let search (caps : caps) (base : string) (query : string) : unit =
  let r =
    match Map_http.get caps ~more:[] (Place.search_url base query) with
    | Error why -> Error why
    | Ok r when r.status <> 200 -> Error (Printf.sprintf "%d %s" r.status r.reason)
    | Ok r -> ( try Ok (Place.of_json r.body) with Failure why -> Error why)
  in
  found := Some (query, r)

(* the window at the place, the place first among the last ones *)
let go_to (w : int) (h : int) (query : string) (p : Place.t) (m : model) : model =
  let z = Place.zoom_for ~at_most:14 p w h in
  let cx, cy = Tiles.centred z (Mercator.x_of_longitude z p.lon) (Mercator.y_of_latitude z p.lat) h in
  let others = List.filter (fun ((q, _) : string * Place.t) -> q <> Place.normal query) m.known in
  let known = List.filteri (fun (i : int) (_ : string * Place.t) -> i < places_kept) ((Place.normal query, p) :: others) in
  m.save known;
  { m with z; cx; cy; place = Some p; known; notice = ""; finding = None; grab = None }

(* [query] asked: from the last places if it is there; at most one request
 * a second, Nominatim's rule (the box stays open, for Enter again) *)
let asked (now : float) (w : int) (h : int) (query : string) (m : model) : model =
  match List.assoc_opt (Place.normal query) m.known with
  | Some p -> go_to w h query p m
  | None ->
      if now -. m.asked_at < 1. then { m with notice = "one search a second: the service's rule" }
      else begin
        m.ask query;
        { m with finding = None; asked_at = now; notice = Printf.sprintf "finding %s..." query }
      end

let took (w : int) (h : int) (m : model) : model =
  match !found with
  | None -> m
  | Some (query, r) -> (
      found := None;
      match r with
      | Ok (p :: _) -> go_to w h query p m
      | Ok [] -> { m with notice = Printf.sprintf "no place called %s" query }
      | Error why -> { m with notice = Printf.sprintf "%s: %s" query why })

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The forecast *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let forecast_found : (string * (Weather.t, string) result) option ref = ref None

let forecast_key (lat : float) (lon : float) : string = Printf.sprintf "%.2f,%.2f" lat lon

(* the panel for that place, the forecast asked unless it is known and good *)
let weather_for (now : float) ((name, lat, lon) : string * float * float) (m : model) : model =
  let key = forecast_key lat lon in
  let good =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt m.forecasts key with
    | Some Asked -> true
    | Some (Came (at, Ok _)) -> now -. at < forecast_good
    | Some (Came (at, Error _)) -> now -. at < again_after
    | None -> false
  in
  if not good then begin
    Hashtbl.replace m.forecasts key Asked;
    m.ask_forecast key lat lon
  end;
  { m with weather_at = Some (name, lat, lon) }

let took_forecast (now : float) (m : model) : model =
  match !forecast_found with
  | None -> m
  | Some (key, r) ->
      forecast_found := None;
      Hashtbl.replace m.forecasts key (Came (now, r));
      { m with generation = m.generation + 1 }

let lat_lon_words (lat : float) (lon : float) : string =
  Printf.sprintf "%.3f %c  %.3f %c" (Float.abs lat) (if lat >= 0. then 'N' else 'S') (Float.abs lon)
    (if lon >= 0. then 'E' else 'W')

(* what w asks about: the place marked, else the window's centre *)
let subject (m : model) : string * float * float =
  match m.place with
  | Some p -> (p.name, p.lat, p.lon)
  | None ->
      let lat = Mercator.latitude_of_y m.z m.cy and lon = Mercator.longitude_of_x m.z m.cx in
      (lat_lon_words lat lon, lat, lon)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A route *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let route_found : (Routing.t, string) result option ref = ref None

(* the worker waits, a moment: a yield would not do. mini-ml's scheduler reads
 * the keys and the clock only when no thread can run (Source), so a worker
 * always ready leaves the window, which waits for them, asleep. *)
let worker_waits (caps : caps) : unit -> unit =
  let clock = ref None in
  fun () ->
    let c =
      match !clock with
      | Some c -> c
      | None ->
          let c = Source.timer caps 0.01 in
          clock := Some c;
          c
    in
    Event.sync (Event.receive c)

(* r: from the place marked; again, none *)
let route_key (m : model) : model =
  let m = { m with generation = m.generation + 1 } in
  match (m.routing, m.place) with
  | No_route, Some p ->
      { m with routing = From p; notice = "a route: now find or click where to" }
  | No_route, None -> { m with notice = "a route: find or click where from, then r" }
  | _ -> { m with routing = No_route; notice = "" }

(* the next place marked is where to *)
let route_asked (m : model) : model =
  match (m.routing, m.place) with
  | From a, Some b when (a.lat, a.lon) <> (b.lat, b.lon) ->
      m.ask_route a b;
      { m with routing = Asking a; notice = "a route: asking for the roads..." }
  | _ -> m

(* the route come: the window shows all of it *)
let took_route (w : int) (h : int) (m : model) : model =
  match !route_found with
  | None -> m
  | Some (Error why) ->
      route_found := None;
      { m with routing = No_route; notice = "a route: " ^ why; generation = m.generation + 1 }
  | Some (Ok r) ->
      route_found := None;
      let fold (f : float -> float -> float) (pick : float * float -> float) : float =
        Array.fold_left (fun (acc : float) (p : float * float) -> f acc (pick p)) (pick r.points.(0)) r.points
      in
      let south = fold Float.min fst and north = fold Float.max fst in
      let west = fold Float.min snd and east = fold Float.max snd in
      let all : Place.t =
        { name = ""; lat = (south +. north) /. 2.; lon = (west +. east) /. 2.;
          box = Some (south, north, west, east) }
      in
      let z = Place.zoom_for ~at_most:14 all (w - 40) (h - 80) in
      let cx, cy = Tiles.centred z (Mercator.x_of_longitude z all.lon) (Mercator.y_of_latitude z all.lat) h in
      { m with z; cx; cy; grab = None; routing = Shown r; notice = ""; generation = m.generation + 1 }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The Find box *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let row_height = 22.
let text (color : P.color) (x : float) (y : float) (s : string) : P.shape * float = Map_look.text color ~size:14. x y s
let width_of = Map_look.width_of
let cut = Map_look.cut

(* the box's line, then the last places under it while it is open *)
let box_lines (fw : float) (m : model) : string list =
  (* (what the panel leaves) *)
  let room = fw -. 28. -. if m.weather_at <> None then 306. else 0. in
  match m.finding with
  | Some typed ->
      cut room ("find: " ^ typed ^ "_")
      :: List.filteri (fun (i : int) (_ : string) -> i < rows_shown)
           (List.map (fun ((_, p) : string * Place.t) -> cut room p.name) m.known)
  | None -> [ (match m.place with Some p -> cut room p.name | None -> "/ to find a place") ]

(* which line of the box the mouse is on *)
let line_at (fw : float) (fh : float) (m : model) (mx : float) (my : float) : int option =
  let left = (-.fw /. 2.) +. 6. and top = (fh /. 2.) -. 6. in
  let hit (i : int) (line : string) : bool =
    let y = top -. (float_of_int i *. row_height) in
    mx >= left && mx <= left +. width_of line +. 12. && my <= y && my > y -. row_height
  in
  let rec find (i : int) (l : string list) : int option =
    match l with
    | [] -> None
    | line :: rest -> if hit i line then Some i else find (i + 1) rest
  in
  find 0 (box_lines fw m)

(* the characters typed: in the box when it is open; / opens it, + and -
 * zoom, w the forecast, r a route *)
let typed (now : float) (h : int) (s : string) (m : model) : model =
  List.fold_left
    (fun (m : model) (c : string) ->
      match (m.finding, c) with
      | Some t, _ when String.length c > 1 || (c.[0] >= ' ' && c.[0] <> '\127') -> { m with finding = Some (t ^ c) }
      | Some _, _ -> m
      | None, "/" -> { m with finding = Some "" }
      | None, ("+" | "=") -> zoomed 1 0 0 h m
      | None, "-" -> zoomed (-1) 0 0 h m
      | None, "w" -> if m.weather_at = None then weather_for now (subject m) m else { m with weather_at = None }
      | None, "r" -> route_key m
      | None, _ -> m)
    m (Text.chars s)

(* Enter, Escape, Backspace in the box; a click on it, or on a place in it *)
let in_box (now : float) (w : int) (h : int) (computer : P.computer) (m : model) : model =
  let pressed (k : string) : bool = Set_.mem k computer.keyboard.keys && not (List.mem k m.held) in
  let m =
    match m.finding with
    | None -> if pressed "Escape" then { m with weather_at = None } else m
    | Some t ->
        if pressed "Escape" then { m with finding = None; notice = "" }
        else if pressed "Enter" then if String.trim t = "" then { m with finding = None } else asked now w h t m
        else if pressed "Backspace" then
          match List.rev (Text.chars t) with
          | [] -> m
          | _ :: rest -> { m with finding = Some (String.concat "" (List.rev rest)) }
        else m
  in
  if not computer.mouse.mclick then m
  else
    match (line_at (float_of_int w) (float_of_int h) m computer.mouse.mx computer.mouse.my, m.finding) with
    | Some 0, None -> { m with finding = Some "" }
    | Some i, Some _ when i > 0 -> (
        match List.nth_opt m.known (i - 1) with
        | Some (q, p) -> go_to w h q p m
        | None -> m)
    | _ -> m

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Update *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let update (computer : P.computer) (m : model) : model =
  let (P.Time now) = computer.time in
  let mouse = computer.mouse and keys = computer.keyboard in
  let w = int_of_float computer.screen.width and h = int_of_float computer.screen.height in
  let px = int_of_float (Float.round mouse.mx) and py = -int_of_float (Float.round mouse.my) in
  let m = { m with ticks = m.ticks + 1 } in
  let m = collected now m in
  let m = took w h m in
  let m = took_forecast now m in
  let m = took_route w h m in
  let m =
    match m.start with
    | Some query -> asked now w h query { m with start = None; asked_at = now -. 1. }
    | None -> m
  in
  let before = (m.z, m.cx, m.cy) in
  let m = typed now h keys.typed m in
  let m = in_box now w h computer m in
  let fw = computer.screen.width and fh = computer.screen.height in
  let over =
    line_at fw fh m mouse.mx mouse.my <> None
    || (m.weather_at <> None && Weather_panel.inside fw fh mouse.mx mouse.my)
  in
  (* the wheel and a double click: at the mouse *)
  let notches = m.wheel +. mouse.mwheel in
  let steps = int_of_float notches in
  let m = { m with wheel = notches -. float_of_int steps } in
  let m = if steps <> 0 then zoomed steps px py h m else m in
  let m = if mouse.mdouble then zoomed 1 px py h m else m in
  (* a drag: the map under the mouse; the arrows *)
  let m =
    match (m.grab, mouse.mdown) with
    | None, true -> if over then m else { m with grab = Some (mouse.mx, mouse.my, m.cx, m.cy) }
    | Some (_, _, cx, cy), false ->
        (* a click, not a drag: a place marked there, which w will ask about *)
        if mouse.mclick && (cx, cy) = (m.cx, m.cy) && not over then
          let x = m.cx + px and y = max 0 (min (Mercator.world_size m.z - 1) (m.cy + py)) in
          let lat = Mercator.latitude_of_y m.z y and lon = Mercator.longitude_of_x m.z (fst (Tiles.centred m.z x y h)) in
          { m with grab = None; place = Some { name = lat_lon_words lat lon; lat; lon; box = None } }
        else { m with grab = None }
    | Some (mx, my, cx, cy), true ->
        let cx, cy =
          Tiles.centred m.z
            (cx + int_of_float (Float.round (mx -. mouse.mx)))
            (cy + int_of_float (Float.round (mouse.my -. my)))
            h
        in
        { m with cx; cy }
    | None, false -> m
  in
  let dx = (if keys.kright then 8 else 0) - if keys.kleft then 8 else 0 in
  let dy = (if keys.kdown then 8 else 0) - if keys.kup then 8 else 0 in
  let m =
    if dx = 0 && dy = 0 then m
    else
      let cx, cy = Tiles.centred m.z (m.cx + dx) (m.cy + dy) h in
      { m with cx; cy }
  in
  (* (the panel follows the place) *)
  let m =
    match (m.weather_at, m.place) with
    | Some (name, _, _), Some p when name <> p.name -> weather_for now (p.name, p.lat, p.lon) m
    | _ -> m
  in
  (* (what the search said, until the map moves; the keys for next time) *)
  let m = if (m.z, m.cx, m.cy) <> before then { m with notice = "" } else m in
  let m = route_asked m in
  let held = List.filter (fun (k : string) -> Set_.mem k keys.keys) [ "Enter"; "Escape"; "Backspace" ] in
  let m = { m with held } in
  let m, missing = in_store now m (Tiles.in_view m.z m.cx m.cy w h) in
  Map_worker.want missing;
  (* (mini-ml's threads: the worker's turn) *)
  if Map_worker.out () then Thread.yield ();
  m

(*****************************************************************************)
(* View *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a line of text on a band at the window's foot, from the left or the right *)
let band (w : float) (h : float) (from_right : bool) (s : string) : P.shape list =
  let _, tw = text P.black 0. 0. s in
  let room = tw +. 8. and bh = 20. in
  let left = if from_right then (w /. 2.) -. room else -.w /. 2. in
  let foot = -.h /. 2. in
  let t, _ = text P.black (left +. 4.) (foot +. 6.) s in
  [ P.rectangle (P.rgb 240 240 240) room bh |> P.move (left +. (room /. 2.)) (foot +. (bh /. 2.)); t ]

let where (m : model) : string =
  let lat = Mercator.latitude_of_y m.z m.cy and lon = Mercator.longitude_of_x m.z m.cx in
  Printf.sprintf "%s  zoom %d" (lat_lon_words lat lon) m.z

let weather (fw : float) (fh : float) (m : model) : P.shape list =
  match m.weather_at with
  | None -> []
  | Some (name, lat, lon) ->
      let state : Weather_panel.state =
        match Hashtbl.find_opt m.forecasts (forecast_key lat lon) with
        | Some (Came (_, Ok f)) -> Weather_panel.Came f
        | Some (Came (_, Error why)) -> Weather_panel.Failed why
        | Some Asked | None -> Weather_panel.Waiting
      in
      Weather_panel.panel fw fh name state

(* the place's marker, where it is on the window, whichever side of the
 * world's edge *)
let marker (fw : float) (fh : float) (m : model) : P.shape list =
  match m.place with
  | None -> []
  | Some p ->
      let world = Mercator.world_size m.z in
      let dx = Mercator.x_of_longitude m.z p.lon - m.cx in
      let dx = if dx > world / 2 then dx - world else if dx < -(world / 2) then dx + world else dx in
      let dy = Mercator.y_of_latitude m.z p.lat - m.cy in
      let x = float_of_int dx and y = -.float_of_int dy in
      if Float.abs x > fw || Float.abs y > fh then []
      else
        [ P.circle P.white 8. |> P.move x y; P.circle P.red 6. |> P.move x y ]

(* the way, and where it starts from *)
let route (fw : float) (fh : float) (m : model) : P.shape list =
  let start (lat : float) (lon : float) : P.shape list =
    let x = float_of_int (Mercator.x_of_longitude m.z lon - m.cx) in
    let y = -.float_of_int (Mercator.y_of_latitude m.z lat - m.cy) in
    [ P.circle P.white 8. |> P.move x y; P.circle P.green 6. |> P.move x y ]
  in
  match m.routing with
  | No_route -> []
  | From p | Asking p -> start p.lat p.lon
  | Shown r ->
      let lat, lon = r.points.(0) in
      Routing.shapes r ~z:m.z ~cx:m.cx ~cy:m.cy fw fh @ start lat lon

(* the band's left: what was said, the route, a tile's failure, or where the
 * window is *)
let said_line (m : model) : string =
  if m.notice <> "" then m.notice
  else
    match m.routing with
    | Shown r -> Routing.summary r
    (* (the map moved meanwhile has taken the notice away) *)
    | Asking _ -> "a route: asking for the roads..."
    | _ -> if m.said <> "" then m.said else where m

(* the Find box, at the window's top left *)
let box (fw : float) (fh : float) (m : model) : P.shape list =
  let left = (-.fw /. 2.) +. 6. and top = (fh /. 2.) -. 6. in
  List.concat
    (List.mapi
       (fun (i : int) (line : string) ->
         let y = top -. (float_of_int i *. row_height) in
         let t, tw = text P.black (left +. 6.) (y -. 16.) line in
         let room = tw +. 12. in
         let back = if i = 0 then P.rgb 255 255 255 else P.rgb 240 240 240 in
         [ P.rectangle back room row_height |> P.move (left +. (room /. 2.)) (y -. (row_height /. 2.)); t ])
       (box_lines fw m))

let drawn (w : int) (h : int) (m : model) : P.shape list =
  let fw = float_of_int w and fh = float_of_int h in
  let tile (p : Tiles.placed) : P.shape option =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt m.store (Tiles.name p.key) with
    | None -> None
    | Some t ->
        let half = float_of_int Tiles.size /. 2. in
        Some
          (P.bitmap (float_of_int Tiles.size) (float_of_int Tiles.size) t.image
          |> P.move
               (float_of_int p.left +. half -. (fw /. 2.))
               ((fh /. 2.) -. float_of_int p.top -. half))
  in
  (P.rectangle (P.rgb 200 200 200) fw fh
  :: List.filter_map tile (Tiles.in_view m.z m.cx m.cy w h))
  @ route fw fh m
  @ marker fw fh m
  @ box fw fh m
  @ weather fw fh m
  @ band fw fh false (said_line m)
  @ band fw fh true credit

(* the same list while nothing it shows changed: a window at rest costs no
 * drawing (the same as mini-netscape's) *)
let last : ((int * int * int * int * int * int * string * string * string list * string * string) * P.shape list) option ref = ref None

let view (computer : P.computer) (m : model) : P.shape list =
  let w = int_of_float computer.screen.width and h = int_of_float computer.screen.height in
  let name = match m.place with Some p -> p.name | None -> "" in
  let now = (w, h, m.z, m.cx, m.cy, m.generation, m.said, m.notice, box_lines (float_of_int w) m, name, match m.weather_at with Some (n, _, _) -> n | None -> "") in
  match !last with
  | Some (was, shapes) when was = now -> shapes
  | _ ->
      let shapes = drawn w h m in
      last := Some (now, shapes);
      shapes

(* Entry point *)

let initial (caps : caps) (flags : P.flags) : model =
  let number (name : string) : float option = Option.bind (List.assoc_opt name flags) float_of_string_opt in
  let z =
    match List.assoc_opt "zoom" flags with
    | Some s -> max 0 (min Tiles.max_zoom (int_of_string s))
    | None -> if number "lat" = None then 1 else 12
  in
  let at (name : string) : float = match number name with Some v -> v | None -> 0. in
  let cx, cy = (Mercator.x_of_longitude z (at "lon"), Mercator.y_of_latitude z (at "lat")) in
  if List.assoc_opt "worker" flags = Some "wait" then Map_worker.mode := Map_worker.Waited;
  let base = match List.assoc_opt "tiles" flags with Some b -> b | None -> default_tiles in
  let limit =
    match Option.bind (List.assoc_opt "cache-size" flags) int_of_string_opt with
    | Some megabytes -> megabytes * 1_000_000
    | None -> default_cache_megabytes * 1_000_000
  in
  let cache = Option.bind (S.cache_dir caps flags) (fun (dir : string) -> Tile_cache.create caps ~dir ~limit) in
  Map_worker.start (fetch caps base cache);
  let places = S.places_base_of flags in
  let weather_base = S.weather_base_of flags in
  let roads = S.roads_base_of flags in
  let dir = S.cache_dir caps flags in
  let known = S.known_places caps flags and save = S.save_places caps flags in
  let words = S.words_of flags in
  let start = if words = [] then None else Some (String.concat " " words) in
  { z; cx; cy; grab = None; wheel = 0.; store = Hashtbl.create 200; failed = Hashtbl.create 20; ticks = 0; generation = 0; said = "";
    finding = None; place = None; known; notice = ""; asked_at = -1000.; start; held = [];
    ask = (fun (query : string) -> Map_worker.job (fun () -> search caps places query)); save;
    weather_at = None; forecasts = Hashtbl.create 16; routing = No_route;
    ask_route =
      (fun (a : Place.t) (b : Place.t) ->
        Map_worker.job (fun () ->
            (* (a domain beside the window needs not give it a turn) *)
            let give = if Worker_spawn.parallel then None else Some (worker_waits caps) in
            route_found := Some (Result.map fst (Routing.find caps ~base:roads ~dir ~give ~dijkstra:false a b))));
    ask_forecast =
      (fun (key : string) (lat : float) (lon : float) ->
        Map_worker.job (fun () -> forecast_found := Some (key, S.forecast_of caps weather_base lat lon))) }

(* Map_window: the map as a window, moved and zoomed.

     mouse, keys  --> where the window is: a zoom and a centre, whole pixels
                        |
                        | Tiles.in_view
                        v
                      the tiles it overlaps --> those missing --> Map_worker
                        |                                            |
                        v                                            |
                      the store of tiles  <------- what comes --------
                        |
                        v
                      a Bitmap each, enlarged from an ancestor until its own
                      comes; and the credit, which OSM's licence asks of us

   And a place found (Place), on Enter in the Find box (/, or a click on
   it): the worker asks, the window goes there and marks it, and the last
   ones are listed in the box, kept and not asked again. A click on the
   map marks a place there, by its numbers.

   And the forecast (Weather, Weather_panel), of the place marked or of the
   window's centre: w opens it and closes it, Escape too, it follows the
   place, and it is asked again only after a quarter of an hour.

   The store keeps a hundred tiles or so, in memory, the least recently
   shown going first: three screens' worth, what a drag back finds at
   once. A tile is 256 KB as pixels, so the store is 30 MB at most. *)

type model

(* what the window needs of the system *)
type caps = Map_services.caps

(* [initial caps flags]: from the flags lat=, lon=, zoom= (the world, by
 * default), a word (a place to find), tiles= and places= (the servers,
 * OSM's by default), forecast= (Open-Meteo by default), roads= (Overpass by
 * default), cache= (a directory
 * or off; the user's by default), cache-size= (in megabytes), worker=wait
 * (the tests': Map_worker.Waited). The worker is started. *)
val initial : caps -> Playground.flags -> model

val update : Playground.computer -> model -> model
val view : Playground.computer -> model -> Playground.shape list

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Map_worker.mli *)

type mode = Beside | Waited

let mode : mode ref = ref Beside
let lock = Mutex.create ()
let signal = Condition.create ()
let wanted : Tiles.key list ref = ref []
let jobs : (unit -> unit) list ref = ref []
let fetching : Tiles.key option ref = ref None
let running = ref false
let made : (Tiles.key * (Rgba_image.t, string) result) list ref = ref []

let worker (fetch : Tiles.key -> (Rgba_image.t, string) result) () : unit =
  while true do
    Mutex.lock lock;
    while !wanted = [] && !jobs = [] do Condition.wait signal lock done;
    (match !jobs with
    | job :: rest ->
        jobs := rest;
        running := true;
        Mutex.unlock lock;
        (* (what the job says of its own failure is in its result) *)
        (try job () with _ -> ());
        Mutex.lock lock;
        running := false
    | [] ->
        let key = List.hd !wanted in
        wanted := List.tl !wanted;
        fetching := Some key;
        Mutex.unlock lock;
        let r = try fetch key with e -> Error (Printexc.to_string e) in
        Mutex.lock lock;
        fetching := None;
        made := (key, r) :: !made);
    Condition.broadcast signal;
    Mutex.unlock lock;
    (* (mini-ml's threads: the window's turn, between two pieces) *)
    Thread.yield ()
  done

let start (fetch : Tiles.key -> (Rgba_image.t, string) result) : unit =
  Worker_spawn.spawn (worker fetch)

let want (keys : Tiles.key list) : unit =
  Mutex.lock lock;
  (* (Waited: one a frame, so a frame's tiles are known) *)
  let busy = !fetching <> None || !made <> [] || !running || !jobs <> [] in
  let asked = List.filter (fun (k : Tiles.key) -> Some k <> !fetching) keys in
  wanted :=
    (match (!mode, asked) with
    | Beside, _ -> asked
    | Waited, k :: _ when not busy -> [ k ]
    | Waited, _ -> []);
  if !wanted <> [] then Condition.broadcast signal;
  Mutex.unlock lock

let job (f : unit -> unit) : unit =
  Mutex.lock lock;
  jobs := !jobs @ [ f ];
  Condition.broadcast signal;
  Mutex.unlock lock

let pending () : bool = !wanted <> [] || !fetching <> None || !running || !jobs <> []

let take () : (Tiles.key * (Rgba_image.t, string) result) list =
  Mutex.lock lock;
  if !mode = Waited then while pending () do Condition.wait signal lock done;
  let r = List.rev !made in
  made := [];
  Mutex.unlock lock;
  r

let out () : bool =
  Mutex.lock lock;
  let r = pending () || !made <> [] in
  Mutex.unlock lock;
  r
apps/maps/Map_worker.mli
2306
(* Map_worker: what is fetched beside the window, which does not wait: the
   tiles, and now and then a place or a forecast (a job, before the tiles).

   Http_client blocks, and a map cannot: it must move under the mouse
   while a tile is on its way. So one worker (Worker_spawn: a thread)
   fetches and reads the tiles, one after the other, and the window draws
   what it has:

      window                             worker
      ------                             ------
      want [a; b; c]      ----------->   takes the first: a
      moves; want [d; e]: what is no     fetches it, reads its PNG
        longer in view is not fetched      |
      take () <------------------------  (a, its picture)
                                         takes the first: d

   [want] replaces the list, so that the map asks only for what is in
   view at that moment, as OSM's tile policy asks: a window dragged across
   a country fetches what it stops on, not all that it went over.

   One worker, one connection kept open (Keep_alive), which is what the
   policy prefers too; a browser would have six, and the mini-chrome's
   numbers (Keep_alive.mli) say what that buys.

   Waited: for the tests. The window gives one tile and waits for it, each
   frame: the frame n of a session has n tiles, on any machine. Under
   mini-ml a thread runs until it waits or yields, a system call stopping
   all of them: the window yields at each frame while tiles are out, and
   the worker gives its turn back after each tile. A long job does more, or
   the window stops with it: Routing asks by a process of its own and gives
   the window its turn all along. *)

type mode = Beside | Waited

val mode : mode ref

(* [start fetch]: the worker; [fetch] is what it does of a tile *)
val start : (Tiles.key -> (Rgba_image.t, string) result) -> unit

(* the tiles the window wants now, the first first (those being fetched
 * ignored) *)
val want : Tiles.key list -> unit

(* the tiles done since the last call, with what the fetch gave *)
val take : unit -> (Tiles.key * (Rgba_image.t, string) result) list

(* [job f]: [f] run by the worker, before any more tiles; it leaves what
 * it finds where the window looks *)
val job : (unit -> unit) -> unit

(* something asked and not taken yet? *)
val out : unit -> bool

(* mini-maps: a map moved and zoomed, fetched from the internet

 * User-Agent, answers kept, one request a second at most for Nominatim. They

(* the words before and after "to" *)
let rec split_at_to (before : string list) (l : string list) : (string * string) option =
  match l with
  | [] -> None
  | "to" :: after when before <> [] && after <> [] ->
      Some (String.concat " " (List.rev before), String.concat " " after)
  | w :: rest -> split_at_to (w :: before) rest

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      Exit.exit caps @@ Exit.catch @@ fun () ->
      Logging.setup caps ~name:"mini-maps";
      let flags = Playground_platform.flags caps in
      let wcaps = (caps :> Map_window.caps) in
      match Map_services.words_of flags with
      | "weather" :: place ->
          if place = [] then (Console.eprint caps "usage: mini-maps weather PLACE\n"; Exit.Err "usage")
          else (
            match Map_services.forecast_lines wcaps flags (String.concat " " place) with
            | Ok lines -> List.iter (fun (l : string) -> Console.print caps (l ^ "\n")) lines; Exit.OK
            | Error why -> Exit.Err why)
      | "route" :: words -> (
          match split_at_to [] words with
          | None -> Console.eprint caps "usage: mini-maps route PLACE to PLACE\n"; Exit.Err "usage"
          | Some (from, goal) -> (
              match Map_services.route_lines wcaps flags from goal with
              | Ok lines -> List.iter (fun (l : string) -> Console.print caps (l ^ "\n")) lines; Exit.OK
              | Error why -> Exit.Err why))
      | _ ->
      (* heap=modest: tiles are kept, tens of megabytes (mini-netscape's);
       * the screen as large as the window *)
      let flags = ("heap", "modest") :: (if List.mem_assoc "window" flags then flags else ("window", "") :: flags) in
      Playground_platform.run_app caps flags
        (Playground.game Map_window.view Map_window.update (Map_window.initial wcaps flags));
      Exit.OK)

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Mercator.mli *)

let pi = 3.14159265358979323846
let max_latitude : float = 85.05112878
let world_size (z : int) : int = 256 lsl z

let x_of_longitude (z : int) (lon : float) : int =
  int_of_float (floor ((lon +. 180.) /. 360. *. float_of_int (world_size z)))

let y_of_latitude (z : int) (lat : float) : int =
  let lat = Float.max (-.max_latitude) (Float.min max_latitude lat) in
  let t = log (tan ((pi /. 4.) +. (lat *. pi /. 360.))) in
  let y = int_of_float (floor ((1. -. (t /. pi)) /. 2. *. float_of_int (world_size z))) in
  (* (at the very top the rounding gives -1) *)
  max 0 (min (world_size z - 1) y)

let longitude_of_x (z : int) (x : int) : float =
  (float_of_int x /. float_of_int (world_size z) *. 360.) -. 180.

let latitude_of_y (z : int) (y : int) : float =
  let t = pi *. (1. -. (2. *. float_of_int y /. float_of_int (world_size z))) in
  ((2. *. atan (exp t)) -. (pi /. 2.)) *. 180. /. pi
apps/maps/Mercator.mli
2842
(* Mercator: the Earth on a square, a latitude and a longitude to a pixel
   and back.

   Gerardus Mercator's world map of 1569 was made for sailors: a straight
   line on it keeps one compass bearing all the way, the loxodrome a ship
   can actually steer. To get that, a place's north-south distance must
   grow as fast as its east-west one does, and the meridians, which meet
   at the pole on the globe, stay parallel on the paper: at latitude phi
   everything is stretched by 1/cos phi, both ways. Adding up that
   stretch from the equator gives the height on the map:

       y = ln (tan (pi/4 + phi/2))

   Mercator drew it by hand; the formula came after him (Edward Wright's
   tables, 1599, and the logarithm, seen in them by Henry Bond around
   1645). It is why Greenland looks as large as Africa, which is fourteen
   times larger: at 72 degrees north the stretch is 3.2, and its area 10.

   The web's version (Google Maps, 2005; EPSG:3857) takes that y with the
   Earth a sphere, and cuts the map where it comes out square:

       x from -pi to pi, y from -pi to pi: the latitude where
       ln (tan (pi/4 + phi/2)) = pi, 85.0511 degrees

   which is why a web map stops short of the poles; y would go to
   infinity at 90. Keeping the map's shape was worth more than the two
   polar caps nobody asks directions to. Then the square is pixels, at a
   zoom z 256 * 2^z on a side, y growing downward as a screen's:

       longitude   -180 ............ 0 ............ 180
       x           0 .............. 128 ............ 256      (z = 0)

       latitude     85.05 .......... 0 ........... -85.05
       y            0 .............. 128 ............ 256

   Going back is the inverse function (the Gudermannian):

       phi = 2 atan (exp t) - pi/2,   t = pi (1 - 2 y / size)

   design:
   Only here are places floats. What the window keeps is whole pixels at
   the current zoom, so that a tile is drawn on whole pixels (the
   renderer's fast path), a drag moves it by exactly what the mouse did,
   and a frame is the same bytes on the two compilers (OCaml's arm64 and
   mini-ml round a*b+c differently).

   Reference: John P. Snyder, "Map Projections: A Working Manual" (USGS,
   1987), chapter 7; Mark Monmonier, "Rhumb Lines and Map Wars" (2004),
   the history, the quarrel over Greenland included. *)

(* where the map stops, north and south, in degrees *)
val max_latitude : float

(* a side of the whole world at zoom [z], in pixels: 256 * 2^z *)
val world_size : int -> int

(* [x_of_longitude z lon], [y_of_latitude z lat]: the pixel, from the
 * world's top left corner; a latitude beyond [max_latitude] is taken at it *)
val x_of_longitude : int -> float -> int
val y_of_latitude : int -> float -> int

(* and back *)
val longitude_of_x : int -> int -> float
val latitude_of_y : int -> int -> float

(* See Place.mli *)

type t = { name : string; lat : float; lon : float; box : (float * float * float * float) option }

let search_url (base : string) (query : string) : string =
  Printf.sprintf "%s/search?%s" base
    (Urlencoded.encode [ ("q", query); ("format", "jsonv2"); ("limit", "1") ])

let number (v : Json.t) : float =
  match v with
  | Json.String s -> (
      match float_of_string_opt s with Some f -> f | None -> failwith ("not a number: " ^ s))
  | _ -> Json.float v

let of_json (text : string) : t list =
  let place (j : Json.t) : t =
    let box =
      match Json.member "boundingbox" j with
      | Json.List [ s; n; w; e ] -> Some (number s, number n, number w, number e)
      | _ -> None
    in
    { name = Json.string (Json.member "display_name" j);
      lat = number (Json.member "lat" j);
      lon = number (Json.member "lon" j);
      box }
  in
  match Json.of_text text with
  | exception Json.Error why -> failwith why
  | j -> ( try List.map place (Json.list j) with Json.Error why -> failwith why)

let zoom_for ~(at_most : int) (p : t) (w : int) (h : int) : int =
  match p.box with
  | None -> at_most
  | Some (south, north, west, east) ->
      let fits (z : int) : bool =
        Mercator.x_of_longitude z east - Mercator.x_of_longitude z west <= w
        && Mercator.y_of_latitude z south - Mercator.y_of_latitude z north <= h
      in
      let rec highest (z : int) : int = if z <= 0 || fits z then z else highest (z - 1) in
      highest at_most

let to_line ((query, p) : string * t) : string =
  let box =
    match p.box with
    | Some (s, n, w, e) -> Printf.sprintf "%g %g %g %g" s n w e
    | None -> ""
  in
  String.concat "\t" [ query; Printf.sprintf "%.6f" p.lat; Printf.sprintf "%.6f" p.lon; box; p.name ]

let of_line (line : string) : (string * t) option =
  match String.split_on_char '\t' line with
  | [ query; lat; lon; box; name ] -> (
      match (float_of_string_opt lat, float_of_string_opt lon) with
      | Some lat, Some lon ->
          let box =
            match List.map float_of_string_opt (String.split_on_char ' ' box) with
            | [ Some s; Some n; Some w; Some e ] -> Some (s, n, w, e)
            | _ -> None
          in
          Some (query, { name; lat; lon; box })
      | _ -> None)
  | _ -> None

let normal (query : string) : string = String.lowercase_ascii (String.trim query)

(* Place: a name to a place on the Earth, asked of Nominatim.

   Geocoding: a street map is a database of names and shapes, so a place's
   name can be looked up in it, and the answer is a latitude, a longitude
   and the box the place fills:

     GET /search?q=tours&format=jsonv2&limit=1
     [ { "lat": "47.39", "lon": "0.68", "display_name": "Tours, ...",
         "boundingbox": ["47.34", "47.44", "0.65", "0.74"] } ]

   (numbers as strings, the way the service gives them; and south, north,
   west, east, in that order, which is nobody's first guess.) The box is
   what says how far to zoom: a town and a country are not looked at from
   the same height.

   The service is run by OSM's volunteers and says what it asks: one
   request a second at most, none as the user types (a search is on Enter,
   never an autocomplete), an answer kept rather than asked again, and a
   User-Agent of our own. So the window keeps the last places, and a name
   already found is not asked again; they are in the file places of the
   cache's directory.

   cs-history:
   Nominatim ("by name", in Latin) is Brian Quinion's, for OpenStreetMap,
   from 2008 or so. Geocoding is much older: the US Census Bureau's DIME
   files (1967) gave each stretch of street its range of house numbers, to
   place the census's addresses on a map; TIGER (1989) put the whole
   country in, which is what the first web maps and, imported in 2007,
   OSM's American streets stood on.

   Reference: https://nominatim.org/release-docs/latest/api/Search/ and
   https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/. *)

type t = {
  name : string; (* the name the service gives, the long one *)
  lat : float;
  lon : float;
  box : (float * float * float * float) option; (* south, north, west, east *)
}

(* [search_url base query] *)
val search_url : string -> string -> string

(* the places in the service's answer, the best first; Failure if it is not
 * such an answer *)
val of_json : string -> t list

(* the highest zoom (at most [at_most]) at which the place's box fits a
 * window of [w] by [h], [at_most] without a box *)
val zoom_for : at_most:int -> t -> int -> int -> int

(* a query and its place as a line of the file, and back; None for a line
 * that is not one *)
val to_line : string * t -> string
val of_line : string -> (string * t) option

(* the query as it is compared: "  Tours " is "tours" *)
val normal : string -> string

(* Claude Code

(* See Roads.mli *)

type t = {
  lat : float array;
  lon : float array;
  x : float array;
  y : float array;
  shrink : float;
  first : int array;
  origin : int array;
  target : int array;
  millis : int array;
  metres : int array;
  name : int array;
  names : string array;
  linked : bool array;
  top_speed : float;
}

let max_side = 0.5
let all_roads_side = 0.1

(* km/h, by what the road says it is; the list is also what is asked for *)
let speeds : (string * float) list =
  [ ("motorway", 110.); ("trunk", 90.); ("primary", 70.); ("secondary", 60.);
    ("tertiary", 50.); ("unclassified", 40.); ("residential", 30.);
    ("living_street", 10.); ("motorway_link", 60.); ("trunk_link", 50.);
    ("primary_link", 40.); ("secondary_link", 40.); ("tertiary_link", 30.) ]

let minor = [ "residential"; "living_street" ]

let all_roads ((s, w, n, e) : float * float * float * float) : bool =
  n -. s <= all_roads_side && e -. w <= all_roads_side

let url (base : string) ((s, w, n, e) as box : float * float * float * float) : string =
  let wanted (c : string) : bool = all_roads box || not (List.mem c minor) in
  let classes = String.concat "|" (List.filter wanted (List.map fst speeds)) in
  let query =
    Printf.sprintf
      "[out:json][timeout:60];way[\"highway\"~\"^(%s)$\"]\
       [\"access\"!~\"^(private|no)$\"](%.3f,%.3f,%.3f,%.3f);\
       out body;>;out skel qt;"
      classes s w n e
  in
  Printf.sprintf "%s/api/interpreter?%s" base (Urlencoded.encode [ ("data", query) ])

let metres_a_degree = 111_195.

(* the way's directions: forward, backward *)
let directions (highway : string) (tag : string -> string) : bool * bool =
  match tag "oneway" with
  | "yes" | "true" | "1" -> (true, false)
  | "-1" | "reverse" -> (false, true)
  | "no" -> (true, true)
  | _ ->
      if tag "junction" = "roundabout" || highway = "motorway"
      then (true, false)
      else (true, true)

(* union-find, by halving; the largest piece's nodes *)
let largest_piece (nodes : int) (origin : int array) (target : int array) : bool array =
  let parent = Array.init nodes (fun (i : int) -> i) in
  let rec root (i : int) : int =
    let p = parent.(i) in
    if p = i then i
    else begin
      parent.(i) <- parent.(p);
      root parent.(i)
    end
  in
  Array.iteri (fun (e : int) (a : int) -> parent.(root a) <- root target.(e)) origin;
  let count = Array.make nodes 0 in
  for i = 0 to nodes - 1 do
    let r = root i in
    count.(r) <- count.(r) + 1
  done;
  let best = ref 0 in
  Array.iteri (fun (i : int) (c : int) -> if c > count.(!best) then best := i) count;
  Array.init nodes (fun (i : int) -> nodes > 0 && root i = !best)

let of_json_turning (turn : unit -> unit) (text : string) : t =
  let elements =
    try Json.list (Json.member "elements" (Json.of_text_turning turn text))
    with Json.Error why -> failwith why
  in
  let kind (e : Json.t) : string =
    turn ();
    Json.string (Json.member "type" e)
  in
  try
    let nodes = List.filter (fun (e : Json.t) -> kind e = "node") elements in
    let ways = List.filter (fun (e : Json.t) -> kind e = "way") elements in
    let number (k : string) (e : Json.t) : float =
      turn ();
      Json.float (Json.member k e)
    in
    let lat = Array.of_list (List.map (number "lat") nodes) in
    let lon = Array.of_list (List.map (number "lon") nodes) in
    let count = Array.length lat in
    (* (an id is a float: past 2^31, more than a 32-bit int) *)
    let index : (float, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create (2 * count + 1) in
    List.iteri
      (fun (i : int) (e : Json.t) ->
        turn ();
        Hashtbl.replace index (Json.float (Json.member "id" e)) i)
      nodes;
    let middle =
      if count = 0 then 0. else (Array.fold_left (+.) 0. lat /. float_of_int count)
    in
    let shrink = cos (middle *. Float.pi /. 180.) in
    let x = Array.map (fun (l : float) -> l *. shrink *. metres_a_degree) lon in
    let y = Array.map (fun (l : float) -> l *. metres_a_degree) lat in
    let named : (string, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 1000 in
    let names = ref [] in
    let name_of (s : string) : int =
      match Hashtbl.find_opt named s with
      | Some i -> i
      | None ->
          let i = Hashtbl.length named in
          Hashtbl.replace named s i;
          names := s :: !names;
          i
    in
    (* the edges, as (from, to, millis, metres, name); those of a node
     * missing from the answer left out *)
    let top = ref 1. in
    let edges = ref [] in
    let edge (speed : float) (name : int) (a : int) (b : int) : unit =
      let dx = x.(a) -. x.(b) and dy = y.(a) -. y.(b) in
      let m = sqrt ((dx *. dx) +. (dy *. dy)) in
      let ms = int_of_float (ceil (m /. speed *. 1000.)) in
      edges := (a, b, ms, int_of_float (ceil m), name) :: !edges
    in
    List.iter
      (fun (w : Json.t) ->
        turn ();
        let tags = Json.member "tags" w in
        let tag (k : string) : string =
          match tags with
          | Json.Assoc _ -> (
              match Json.member k tags with Json.String s -> s | _ -> "")
          | _ -> ""
        in
        let highway = tag "highway" in
        match List.assoc_opt highway speeds with
        | None -> ()
        | Some kmh ->
            let speed = kmh /. 3.6 in
            if speed > !top then top := speed;
            let name = name_of (tag "name") in
            let forward, backward = directions highway tag in
            let rec steps (l : Json.t list) : unit =
              match l with
              | a :: (b :: _ as rest) ->
                  (match
                     ( Hashtbl.find_opt index (Json.float a),
                       Hashtbl.find_opt index (Json.float b) )
                   with
                  | Some a, Some b ->
                      if forward then edge speed name a b;
                      if backward then edge speed name b a
                  | _ -> ());
                  steps rest
              | _ -> ()
            in
            steps (Json.list (Json.member "nodes" w)))
      ways;
    (* by origin: a node's edges together *)
    let all = Array.of_list !edges in
    let total = Array.length all in
    let first = Array.make (count + 1) 0 in
    Array.iter
      (fun ((a, _, _, _, _) : int * int * int * int * int) ->
        first.(a + 1) <- first.(a + 1) + 1)
      all;
    for i = 1 to count do
      first.(i) <- first.(i) + first.(i - 1)
    done;
    let next = Array.sub first 0 (count + 1) in
    let origin = Array.make total 0 and target = Array.make total 0 in
    let millis = Array.make total 0 and metres = Array.make total 0 in
    let name = Array.make total 0 in
    Array.iter
      (fun ((a, b, ms, m, n) : int * int * int * int * int) ->
        turn ();
        let e = next.(a) in
        next.(a) <- e + 1;
        origin.(e) <- a;
        target.(e) <- b;
        millis.(e) <- ms;
        metres.(e) <- m;
        name.(e) <- n)
      all;
    { lat; lon; x; y; shrink; first; origin; target; millis; metres; name;
      names = Array.of_list (List.rev !names);
      linked = largest_piece count origin target;
      top_speed = !top }
  with Json.Error why -> failwith why

let of_json (text : string) : t = of_json_turning ignore text

let nearest_turning (turn : unit -> unit) (g : t) (lat : float) (lon : float) : (int * float) option =
  if Array.length g.lat = 0 then None
  else begin
    let px = lon *. g.shrink *. metres_a_degree and py = lat *. metres_a_degree in
    let best = ref (-1) and far = ref infinity in
    Array.iteri
      (fun (i : int) (on : bool) ->
        turn ();
        if on then begin
          let dx = g.x.(i) -. px and dy = g.y.(i) -. py in
          let d = (dx *. dx) +. (dy *. dy) in
          if d < !far then begin
            far := d;
            best := i
          end
        end)
      g.linked;
    if !best < 0 then None else Some (!best, sqrt !far)
  end

let nearest (g : t) (lat : float) (lon : float) : (int * float) option =
  nearest_turning ignore g lat lon
apps/maps/Roads.mli
4585
(* Roads: a small piece of the world's road network, as a graph.

   OpenStreetMap's roads are ways, each a list of nodes, each node a
   latitude and a longitude. Overpass answers a query over them, and what
   mini-maps asks is "the roads a car may use in this box":

     way["highway"~"^(motorway|...|residential)$"](47.3,0.6,47.5,1.0);
     out body; >; out skel qt;

     { "type": "way", "id": 4898610, "nodes": [ 11197711196, 275726429 ],
       "tags": { "highway": "tertiary", "name": "Rue Saint-Barthelemy" } }
     { "type": "node", "id": 275726429, "lat": 47.39, "lon": 0.69 }

   A graph is made of it: a node to each OSM node, an edge to each step of
   a way, two when it may be driven both ways (oneway, a roundabout and a
   motorway say otherwise). An edge's cost is the time, its length at a
   speed given by the road's class:

     residential 30 km/h, tertiary 50, ... motorway 110

   which is a guess: no maxspeed, no traffic, no turn restrictions (OSM
   has them, as relations), no time lost at a junction. So a route here is
   a good way to go, and its minutes are an estimate.

   Costs are whole milliseconds, rounded up: the search then compares
   integers, and both compilers (one fuses a*b+c, Float's rounding differs
   in the last bit) find the same route.

   The Earth is flat here: over half a degree, x is a longitude times the
   cosine of the box's middle latitude, y a latitude, and a distance is
   Pythagoras's (off by about 1% at most over that box). It has one more use:
   a real plane's distances obey the triangle inequality, which A* needs
   (Route).

   Only the largest connected piece is kept. A car park cut off by the
   box's edge or by a road not asked for would otherwise be what the
   nearest node to a click belongs to, and no way would be found.

   The size. A box of 0.12 by 0.41 degrees around Tours and Amboise was
   124,996 nodes and 16,230 ways, 17 MB of JSON, 2.6 MB gzipped, 46 seconds
   of the service (2026-10-31). Overpass's rule for regular use is about
   100 queries and 10 MB a day; and a string on a 32-bit machine stops at
   16 MB. So a box past [all_roads_side] does without the residential
   streets, half of that answer (a long trip hardly uses them; its ends are
   then on the nearest larger road, which is what a road atlas gives). And
   [max_side] limits a box, one extract is kept (Routing), and a route
   across France is not something this does.

   design:
   OSRM's demo server would answer in a few lines of code, but then the
   route is computed elsewhere, and there is nothing left to read here.
   Asking Overpass still needs the network; the search does not.

   cs-history:
   OSM is Steve Coast's, from 2004, when Britain's maps were the Ordnance
   Survey's to sell. Overpass is Roland Olbricht's, a database made for
   reading OSM by what the objects say, not only by where they are.

   Reference: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API and
   https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:highway; the data is OSM's,
   under the ODbL, and credited. *)

type t = {
  lat : float array; (* by node *)
  lon : float array;
  x : float array; (* metres, on the flat Earth above *)
  y : float array;
  shrink : float; (* the cosine that makes a longitude's x *)
  first : int array; (* a node's edges: first.(n) to first.(n+1) - 1 *)
  origin : int array; (* by edge *)
  target : int array;
  millis : int array;
  metres : int array;
  name : int array; (* an index in names *)
  names : string array; (* "" for a road with none *)
  linked : bool array; (* by node: in the largest piece *)
  top_speed : float; (* metres a second, the fastest edge's *)
}

(* the largest side of a box, in degrees *)
val max_side : float

(* the largest side of a box that has the residential streets *)
val all_roads_side : float

(* does the query for that box ask for them? *)
val all_roads : float * float * float * float -> bool

(* the query's address, for a box (south, west, north, east) *)
val url : string -> float * float * float * float -> string

(* the graph of the service's answer; Failure if it is not such an answer *)
val of_json : string -> t

(* the same, [turn ()] called all along: the window's (Routing) *)
val of_json_turning : (unit -> unit) -> string -> t

(* the node of the largest piece nearest to a place, and how many metres

(* See Route.mli *)

type t = { edges : int list; millis : int; metres : int; settled : int }

(* a binary heap: the children of i at 2i+1 and 2i+2, each no less than
 * its parent; two arrays, doubled as needed *)
type heap = { mutable costs : int array; mutable nodes : int array; mutable size : int }

let push (h : heap) (cost : int) (node : int) : unit =
  if h.size = Array.length h.costs then begin
    let grown (a : int array) : int array =
      Array.append a (Array.make (Array.length a) 0)
    in
    h.costs <- grown h.costs;
    h.nodes <- grown h.nodes
  end;
  let i = ref h.size in
  h.size <- h.size + 1;
  while !i > 0 && h.costs.((!i - 1) / 2) > cost do
    let parent = (!i - 1) / 2 in
    h.costs.(!i) <- h.costs.(parent);
    h.nodes.(!i) <- h.nodes.(parent);
    i := parent
  done;
  h.costs.(!i) <- cost;
  h.nodes.(!i) <- node

(* the smallest; the heap is not empty *)
let pop (h : heap) : int * int =
  let top = (h.costs.(0), h.nodes.(0)) in
  h.size <- h.size - 1;
  let cost = h.costs.(h.size) and node = h.nodes.(h.size) in
  let i = ref 0 and placed = ref false in
  while not !placed do
    let left = (2 * !i) + 1 and right = (2 * !i) + 2 in
    let c =
      if right < h.size && h.costs.(right) < h.costs.(left) then right else left
    in
    if c < h.size && h.costs.(c) < cost then begin
      h.costs.(!i) <- h.costs.(c);
      h.nodes.(!i) <- h.nodes.(c);
      i := c
    end
    else placed := true
  done;
  h.costs.(!i) <- cost;
  h.nodes.(!i) <- node;
  top

let search_turning (turn : unit -> unit) (g : Roads.t) ~(guess : bool) (from : int) (goal : int) : t option =
  let count = Array.length g.lat in
  (* what is left, rounded down as the edges are rounded up, so that it
   * stays consistent *)
  let left (n : int) : int =
    if not guess then 0
    else
      let dx = g.x.(n) -. g.x.(goal) and dy = g.y.(n) -. g.y.(goal) in
      int_of_float (sqrt ((dx *. dx) +. (dy *. dy)) /. g.top_speed *. 1000.)
  in
  let cost = Array.make count max_int in
  let came = Array.make count (-1) in
  let settled = Array.make count false in
  let queue = { costs = Array.make 1024 0; nodes = Array.make 1024 0; size = 0 } in
  cost.(from) <- 0;
  push queue (left from) from;
  let taken = ref 0 and found = ref false in
  while (not !found) && queue.size > 0 do
    turn ();
    let _, n = pop queue in
    if not settled.(n) then begin
      settled.(n) <- true;
      incr taken;
      if n = goal then found := true
      else
        for e = g.first.(n) to g.first.(n + 1) - 1 do
          let m = g.target.(e) in
          let c = cost.(n) + g.millis.(e) in
          if c < cost.(m) then begin
            cost.(m) <- c;
            came.(m) <- e;
            push queue (c + left m) m
          end
        done
    end
  done;
  if not !found then None
  else begin
    let rec back (n : int) (acc : int list) : int list =
      if n = from then acc
      else
        let e = came.(n) in
        back g.origin.(e) (e :: acc)
    in
    let edges = back goal [] in
    let metres = List.fold_left (fun (s : int) (e : int) -> s + g.metres.(e)) 0 edges in
    Some { edges; millis = cost.(goal); metres; settled = !taken }
  end

let search (g : Roads.t) ~(guess : bool) (from : int) (goal : int) : t option =
  search_turning ignore g ~guess from goal

(* Route: the quickest way between two nodes, by A*.

   Dijkstra's idea: settle the nodes in the order of their distance from
   the start. The nearest node not settled has no shorter way to it, since
   any other way passes through a node at least as far (costs being
   positive). So it spreads like a ring on water, all directions alike:

       Dijkstra: everything nearer           A*: leaning to the goal
       than the goal, on all sides
              . . . . .                               . . .
            . . . . . . .                           . . . . .
          . . . S . . . . G                       S . . . . . G
            . . . . . . .                           . . . . .
              . . . . .                               . . .

   A*'s idea: the same, the order being the distance so far plus an
   estimate of what is left, h(n):

       f(n) = g(n) + h(n)

   Here h is the straight line, at the fastest speed there is in the
   graph. No road is shorter than the straight line and none is faster, so
   h never overestimates ("admissible"), and A* still finds the best way.
   It obeys more, h(a) <= cost(a,b) + h(b), the triangle inequality
   ("consistent"), so that a node once settled stays settled, as in
   Dijkstra's. With h = 0, it is Dijkstra's: one function here, and the
   count of nodes each settles is the lesson, printed by mini-maps route.

   How much better depends on h. In a town at 30 km/h, with a motorway in
   the box, h believes everything can go at 110, and the ring is hardly
   leaning.

   The queue is a binary heap of (f, node). A node whose cost improves is
   pushed again, and the older entry skipped when it comes out, rather than
   looked for ("lazy deletion"): a larger heap, and no index to maintain.

   cs-history:
   Edsger Dijkstra found his algorithm in 1956, on a cafe's terrace in
   Amsterdam, in twenty minutes and with no pencil, to show what the ARMAC,
   a new computer, could do: the way between 64 Dutch towns, for an audience
   who could check it. Published in 1959, three pages. A* comes from
   Stanford Research Institute (Hart, Nilsson and Raphael, 1968), for
   Shakey, a robot that planned where it went. The heap is J. W. J.
   Williams's (1964), for sorting.

   modern:
   Nobody runs this on a continent. A preprocessing step, as Contraction
   Hierarchies (Geisberger and others, 2008) which OSRM uses, adds shortcuts
   over the unimportant roads, and a query across Europe then settles a few
   hundred nodes, in under a millisecond. This is also why a server answers
   so fast. *)

type t = {
  edges : int list; (* in the order driven *)
  millis : int;
  metres : int;
  settled : int; (* the nodes the search took out of its queue *)
}

(* [search g ~guess from goal]: the quickest way, None if there is none;
 * [guess] false is h = 0, Dijkstra's *)
val search : Roads.t -> guess:bool -> int -> int -> t option

(* the same, [turn ()] called at each step: the window's (Routing) *)
val search_turning : (unit -> unit) -> Roads.t -> guess:bool -> int -> int -> t option

(* Claude Code
