(* See Routing.mli *)

module P = Playground

type t = {
  from : string;
  goal : string;
  points : (float * float) array;
  millis : int;
  metres : int;
  settled : int;
  nodes : int;
  steps : (string * int) list;
}

type box = float * float * float * float

let kept_for = 30. *. 86400.

(* a road further than this from a place is not its road: a click at sea *)
let road_at_most = 2000.

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The extract *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let in_box ((s, w, n, e) : box) (p : Place.t) : bool =
  p.lat >= s && p.lat <= n && p.lon >= w && p.lon <= e

(* around both places: a route may leave the straight line *)
let box_of (a : Place.t) (b : Place.t) : box =
  let margin (d : float) : float = Float.max 0.02 (d *. 0.15) in
  let dlat = margin (Float.abs (a.lat -. b.lat)) in
  let dlon = margin (Float.abs (a.lon -. b.lon)) in
  ( Float.min a.lat b.lat -. dlat, Float.min a.lon b.lon -. dlon,
    Float.max a.lat b.lat +. dlat, Float.max a.lon b.lon +. dlon )

let too_big ((s, w, n, e) : box) : bool =
  n -. s > Roads.max_side || e -. w > Roads.max_side

(* (the answer's length: a full disk cuts a file short, and says nothing) *)
let header ((s, w, n, e) : box) (now : float) (body : string) : string =
  Printf.sprintf "%.3f %.3f %.3f %.3f %.0f %d\n" s w n e now (String.length body)

(* the file's box and answer, if it holds a recent one *)
let read_kept (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (now : float) (file : Fpath.t) : (box * string) option =
  match FS.read_opt caps file with
  | None -> None
  | Some text -> (
      match String.index_opt text '\n' with
      | None -> None
      | Some i -> (
          let first = String.sub text 0 i in
          let rest = String.sub text (i + 1) (String.length text - i - 1) in
          match List.map float_of_string_opt (String.split_on_char ' ' first) with
          | [ Some s; Some w; Some n; Some e; Some at; Some len ]
            when now -. at < kept_for && int_of_float len = String.length rest ->
              Some ((s, w, n, e), rest)
          | _ -> None))

(* the graph of the last extract, in memory *)
let last : (box * Roads.t) option ref = ref None

(* the window's turn at most this often, in seconds *)
let slice = 0.05

(* [give] called when a slice has gone by (the clock read now and then: this
 * is called at each value of a JSON text) *)
let breather (caps : < Cap.clock; .. >) (give : unit -> unit) : unit -> unit =
  let calls = ref 0 and last = ref (CapUnix.gettimeofday caps ()) in
  fun () ->
    incr calls;
    if !calls land 255 = 0 && CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () -. !last > slice then begin
      give ();
      last := CapUnix.gettimeofday caps ()
    end

(* Overpass is silent until it has it all, for most of a minute at times *)
let asked (caps : < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; .. >) (url : string) : (string, string) result =
  let usual = !Tcp.timeout in
  Tcp.timeout := 90.;
  let r = Map_http.get_once caps url in
  Tcp.timeout := usual;
  match r with
  | Error why -> Error why
  | Ok r when r.status <> 200 -> Error (Printf.sprintf "%d %s" r.status r.reason)
  | Ok r -> Ok r.body

(* a file in small pieces, a rest after each: on mini-9pi a file of 7 MB is most
 * of a minute of system calls, and written at once it halves the speed of the
 * search and of the window, which have the same core's kernel to go through *)
let write_gently (caps : < Cap.open_out; Cap.clock; .. >) (f : Fpath.t) (text : string) : unit =
  let fd = FS.open_out_fd caps (Fpath.to_string f) 0o644 in
  let small = 16384 in
  let n = String.length text and at = ref 0 in
  while !at < n do
    at := !at + Unix.write_substring fd text !at (min small (n - !at));
    CapUnix.sleepf caps 0.2
  done;
  Unix.close fd

(* the last process that asked, perhaps still writing its file *)
let asker : int option ref = ref None

(* longer than [asked]'s silence, should the process die without a word *)
let patience = 120.

(* a piece of the answer between two turns of the window *)
let piece = 65536

(* [asked] by a process of its own: a read would stop all of mini-ml's threads
 * for as long as the service is silent (Thread). It removes a file to say it
 * has the answer, which then comes through a pipe, a piece at a time: a read
 * of a pipe with something coming is short. Then it does [keep] of the answer,
 * not waited for: the route has no need of it. A fork after the graph is made
 * would stop the window, for the heap: this one is early. *)
let asked_beside (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.kill; Cap.wait; Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    Cap.clock; Cap.pipe; .. >)
    (give : unit -> unit) ~(keep : string -> unit) (url : string) : (string, string) result =
  (match !asker with
  | Some pid -> ( try ignore (CapUnix.waitpid caps [] pid) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ())
  | None -> ());
  let file = Filename.temp_file "mini-maps" ".roads" in
  let from_it, to_me = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:false () in
  match CapUnix.fork caps () with
  | 0 ->
      Unix.close from_it;
      let r = try asked caps url with e -> Error (Printexc.to_string e) in
      let text = match r with Ok body -> "+" ^ body | Error why -> "-" ^ why in
      (try
         FS.remove caps (Fpath.v file);
         let n = String.length text and at = ref 0 in
         while !at < n do
           at := !at + Unix.write_substring to_me text !at (min piece (n - !at))
         done
       with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
      Unix.close to_me;
      (match r with Ok body -> keep body | Error _ -> ());
      Unix._exit 0
  | pid ->
      Unix.close to_me;
      let until = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () +. patience in
      while Sys.file_exists file && CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () < until do give () done;
      let silent = Sys.file_exists file in
      if silent then begin
        (try CapUnix.kill caps pid Sys.sigkill with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
        (try FS.remove caps (Fpath.v file) with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> ())
      end;
      let text = Buffer.create piece in
      let b = Bytes.create piece in
      let rec all () : unit =
        let n = Unix.read from_it b 0 piece in
        if n > 0 then begin
          Buffer.add_subbytes text b 0 n;
          give ();
          all ()
        end
      in
      if not silent then all ();
      Unix.close from_it;
      asker := Some pid;
      let n = Buffer.length text in
      if silent || n = 0 then Error "no answer from the service"
      else if Buffer.nth text 0 = '+' then Ok (Buffer.sub text 1 (n - 1))
      else Error (Buffer.sub text 1 (n - 1))

(* the graph for those two places: from memory, from the file, or asked *)
let graph (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.kill; Cap.wait; Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    Cap.clock; Cap.pipe; .. >) ~(base : string)
    ~(dir : string option) ~(give : (unit -> unit) option) (a : Place.t) (b : Place.t) : (Roads.t, string) result =
  (* (a town's route is not made over an extract without its streets) *)
  let covers (box : box) : bool =
    in_box box a && in_box box b && Roads.all_roads box = Roads.all_roads (box_of a b)
  in
  let now = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () in
  let file = Option.map (fun (d : string) -> Fpath.v (Filename.concat d "roads")) dir in
  let made (box : box) (text : string) : (Roads.t, string) result =
    let turn = match give with Some f -> breather caps f | None -> ignore in
    match Roads.of_json_turning turn text with
    | g ->
        last := Some (box, g);
        Ok g
    | exception Failure why -> Error why
  in
  let kept_one () : (Roads.t, string) result option =
    match Option.bind file (read_kept caps now) with
    | Some (box, text) when covers box -> (
        (* (a file that cannot be read is asked for again, not kept 30 days) *)
        match made box text with Ok g -> Some (Ok g) | Error _ -> None)
    | _ -> None
  in
  match !last with
  | Some (box, g) when covers box -> Ok g
  | _ -> (
      match kept_one () with
      | Some r -> r
      | None ->
          let box = box_of a b in
          if too_big box then
            Error
              (Printf.sprintf "too far for a small extract: %g degrees at most"
                 Roads.max_side)
          else (
            let url = Roads.url base box in
            let keep (write : Fpath.t -> string -> unit) (body : string) : unit =
              match file with
              | Some f -> (
                  try write f (header box now body ^ body)
                  with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> ())
              | None -> ()
            in
            match give with
            | Some f -> (
                (* (what proves not to be understood is asked for again) *)
                match asked_beside caps f ~keep:(keep (write_gently caps)) url with
                | Error why -> Error why
                | Ok body -> made box body)
            | None -> (
                match asked caps url with
                | Error why -> Error why
                | Ok body ->
                    let result = made box body in
                    (* (only what was understood is kept) *)
                    if Result.is_ok result then keep (FS.write caps) body;
                    result)))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The route *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* consecutive edges of one road as one step *)
let steps_of (g : Roads.t) (edges : int list) : (string * int) list =
  let add (acc : (string * int) list) (e : int) : (string * int) list =
    let name = g.names.(g.name.(e)) in
    match acc with
    | (n, m) :: rest when n = name -> (n, m + g.metres.(e)) :: rest
    | _ -> (name, g.metres.(e)) :: acc
  in
  List.rev (List.fold_left add [] edges)

let find (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.kill; Cap.wait; Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    Cap.clock; Cap.pipe; .. >) ~(base : string)
    ~(dir : string option) ~(give : (unit -> unit) option) ~(dijkstra : bool) (a : Place.t)
    (b : Place.t) : (t * int option, string) result =
  (* (it runs in the worker, which must outlive a thing too large for this
   * machine: an answer past a 32-bit string's 16 MB) *)
  match
    try graph caps ~base ~dir ~give a b with
    | Failure why | Invalid_argument why -> Error why
    | Out_of_memory | Stack_overflow -> Error "too large for this machine"
  with
  | Error why -> Error why
  | Ok g -> (
      let turn = match give with Some f -> breather caps f | None -> ignore in
      let near (p : Place.t) : (int, string) result =
        match Roads.nearest_turning turn g p.lat p.lon with
        | Some (n, far) when far <= road_at_most -> Ok n
        | _ -> Error (Printf.sprintf "no road near %s" p.name)
      in
      match (near a, near b) with
      | Error why, _ | _, Error why -> Error why
      | Ok na, Ok nb -> (
          match Route.search_turning turn g ~guess:true na nb with
          | None -> Error "no way between them by the roads known"
          | Some r ->
              let point (n : int) : float * float = (g.lat.(n), g.lon.(n)) in
              let points = point na :: List.map (fun (e : int) -> point g.target.(e)) r.edges in
              let plain =
                if not dijkstra then None
                else
                  Option.map (fun (d : Route.t) -> d.settled)
                    (Route.search g ~guess:false na nb)
              in
              Ok
                ( { from = a.name; goal = b.name; points = Array.of_list points;
                    millis = r.millis; metres = r.metres; settled = r.settled;
                    nodes = Array.length g.lat; steps = steps_of g r.edges },
                  plain )))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* In words *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let length_words (metres : int) : string =
  if metres < 1000 then Printf.sprintf "%d m" metres
  else Printf.sprintf "%d.%d km" (metres / 1000) (metres mod 1000 / 100)

let time_words (millis : int) : string =
  let minutes = (millis + 30_000) / 60_000 in
  if minutes < 60 then Printf.sprintf "%d min" minutes
  else Printf.sprintf "%d h %02d" (minutes / 60) (minutes mod 60)

let summary (r : t) : string =
  Printf.sprintf "%s, %s" (length_words r.metres) (time_words r.millis)

let lines (r : t) (plain : int option) : string list =
  let road ((name, metres) : string * int) : string =
    Printf.sprintf "%8s  %s" (length_words metres)
      (if name = "" then "(a road with no name)" else name)
  in
  [ r.from; "to " ^ r.goal; summary r ]
  @ List.map road r.steps
  @ [ Printf.sprintf "A* settled %d nodes of %d" r.settled r.nodes ]
  @ (match plain with
    | Some n -> [ Printf.sprintf "Dijkstra settled %d" n ]
    | None -> [])
  @ [ "times by road class: no traffic, no turn restrictions";
      "Roads (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL" ]

(*****************************************************************************)
(* On the map *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let width = 2.

let shapes (r : t) ~(z : int) ~(cx : int) ~(cy : int) (fw : float) (fh : float) : P.shape list =
  let color = P.rgb 40 90 220 in
  let pixel ((lat, lon) : float * float) : int * int =
    (Mercator.x_of_longitude z lon - cx, Mercator.y_of_latitude z lat - cy)
  in
  let on_window (x : int) (y : int) : bool =
    Float.abs (float_of_int x) <= fw && Float.abs (float_of_int y) <= fh
  in
  (* a segment as a quadrilateral across it *)
  let segment ((ax, ay) : int * int) ((bx, by) : int * int) : P.shape =
    let x0 = float_of_int ax and y0 = -.float_of_int ay in
    let x1 = float_of_int bx and y1 = -.float_of_int by in
    let dx = x1 -. x0 and dy = y1 -. y0 in
    let len = sqrt ((dx *. dx) +. (dy *. dy)) in
    let nx = -.dy /. len *. width and ny = dx /. len *. width in
    P.polygon color
      [ (x0 +. nx, y0 +. ny); (x1 +. nx, y1 +. ny); (x1 -. nx, y1 -. ny); (x0 -. nx, y0 -. ny) ]
  in
  let close ((ax, ay) : int * int) ((bx, by) : int * int) : bool =
    abs (ax - bx) < 3 && abs (ay - by) < 3
  in
  let drawn = ref [] in
  let at = ref (pixel r.points.(0)) in
  Array.iter
    (fun (p : float * float) ->
      let next = pixel p in
      if not (close !at next) then begin
        let ax, ay = !at and bx, by = next in
        if on_window ax ay || on_window bx by then drawn := segment !at next :: !drawn;
        at := next
      end)
    r.points;
  !drawn
apps/maps/Routing.mli

(* Routing: from two places to a route: the extract, the search, the words.

     two places --> a box around them --> the extract --> Roads --> Route
                                          kept on disk

   One extract is kept, in the file roads of the cache's directory, its
   first line saying its box and when it was fetched. It serves any route
   whose two ends are in its box, for 30 days (roads change slowly, and
   Overpass asks for little: Roads.mli). The graph of the last one is kept
   in memory as well: making it is the slow part. *)

type t = {
  from : string;
  goal : string;
  points : (float * float) array; (* latitude, longitude, in the order driven *)
  millis : int;
  metres : int;
  settled : int; (* by A* *)
  nodes : int; (* in the extract *)
  steps : (string * int) list; (* the roads driven, their metres; "" for no name *)
}

(* [find caps ~base ~dir ~give ~dijkstra a b]: the route, with [dir] the
 * cache's directory if there is one; with [dijkstra], how many nodes Dijkstra's
 * search settles too (the terminal's lesson); or what went wrong.
 * [give]: a window waits, on the same core: the extract is asked by a process

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Tile_cache.mli *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out >
type entry = { bytes : string; expires : float; etag : string option }

type t = {
  caps : caps;
  dir : string;
  limit : int;
  uses : (string, int * int) Hashtbl.t; (* a file's: the last use, its size *)
  mutable tick : int;
  mutable total : int;
  mutable unsaved : int;
}

(*****************************************************************************)
(* How long it is good *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let lifetime ~(now : float) (headers : Http.header list) : float option =
  let directives =
    match Http.header "Cache-Control" headers with
    | None -> []
    | Some v -> List.map (fun (d : string) -> String.lowercase_ascii (String.trim d)) (String.split_on_char ',' v)
  in
  let max_age =
    List.find_map
      (fun (d : string) ->
        if String.starts_with ~prefix:"max-age=" d then int_of_string_opt (String.sub d 8 (String.length d - 8)) else None)
      directives
  in
  let age =
    match Option.bind (Http.header "Age" headers) int_of_string_opt with Some a -> a | None -> 0
  in
  if List.mem "no-store" directives then None
  else if List.mem "no-cache" directives then Some 0.
  else
    match (max_age, Option.bind (Http.header "Expires" headers) Cookie.date) with
    | Some n, _ -> Some (now +. float_of_int (n - age))
    | None, Some date -> Some date
    | None, None -> Some 0.

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The files *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* "4/8/5" -> dir/4-8-5 *)
let file (c : t) (name : string) : Fpath.t =
  Fpath.v (Filename.concat c.dir (String.concat "-" (String.split_on_char '/' name)))

let index (c : t) : Fpath.t = Fpath.v (Filename.concat c.dir "index")

let save_index (c : t) : unit =
  let lines =
    Hashtbl.fold
      (fun (name : string) ((tick, size) : int * int) (acc : string list) ->
        Printf.sprintf "%s %d %d\n" name tick size :: acc)
      c.uses []
  in
  (try FS.write c.caps (index c) (String.concat "" lines) with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
  c.unsaved <- 0

let load_index (c : t) : unit =
  match FS.read_opt c.caps (index c) with
  | None -> ()
  | Some text ->
      List.iter
        (fun (line : string) ->
          match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
          | [ name; tick; size ] -> (
              match (int_of_string_opt tick, int_of_string_opt size) with
              | Some tick, Some size ->
                  Hashtbl.replace c.uses name (tick, size);
                  c.tick <- max c.tick tick;
                  c.total <- c.total + size
              | _ -> ())
          | _ -> ())
        (String.split_on_char '\n' text)

let rec made (caps : caps) (dir : string) : unit =
  if not (Sys.file_exists dir) then begin
    made caps (Filename.dirname dir);
    FS.mkdir caps dir 0o755
  end

let create (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) ~(dir : string) ~(limit : int) : t option =
  let caps = (caps :> caps) in
  match made caps dir with
  | exception (Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _) -> None
  | () ->
      let c = { caps; dir; limit; uses = Hashtbl.create 500; tick = 0; total = 0; unsaved = 0 } in
      load_index c;
      Some c

(* a use: known, in the index, at the next save *)
let used (c : t) (name : string) (size : int) : unit =
  (match Hashtbl.find_opt c.uses name with
  | Some (_, was) -> c.total <- c.total - was
  | None -> ());
  c.tick <- c.tick + 1;
  c.total <- c.total + size;
  c.unsaved <- c.unsaved + 1;
  Hashtbl.replace c.uses name (c.tick, size);
  if c.unsaved >= 16 then save_index c

(* down to nine tenths of the limit, the oldest first *)
let trimmed (c : t) : unit =
  if c.total > c.limit then begin
    let all =
      Hashtbl.fold (fun (name : string) ((tick, size) : int * int) acc -> (tick, name, size) :: acc) c.uses []
    in
    List.iter
      (fun ((_, name, size) : int * string * int) ->
        if c.total > c.limit / 10 * 9 then begin
          (try FS.remove c.caps (file c name) with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
          Hashtbl.remove c.uses name;
          c.total <- c.total - size
        end)
      (List.sort compare all);
    save_index c
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A tile *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the file: "expires etag\n", then the tile's bytes *)
let find (c : t) (name : string) : entry option =
  match FS.read_opt c.caps (file c name) with
  | None -> None
  | Some text -> (
      match String.index_opt text '\n' with
      | None -> None
      | Some i -> (
          let bytes = String.sub text (i + 1) (String.length text - i - 1) in
          let head = String.sub text 0 i in
          let found (expires : string) (etag : string option) : entry option =
            match float_of_string_opt expires with
            | None -> None
            | Some expires ->
                used c name (String.length text);
                Some { bytes; expires; etag }
          in
          match String.index_opt head ' ' with
          | None -> found head None
          | Some j -> found (String.sub head 0 j) (Some (String.sub head (j + 1) (String.length head - j - 1)))))

let put (c : t) (name : string) (e : entry) : unit =
  (* (down: rounded up, a tile of max-age=0 would be good for half a second) *)
  let head = Printf.sprintf "%.0f%s\n" (floor e.expires) (match e.etag with Some t -> " " ^ t | None -> "") in
  let text = head ^ e.bytes in
  match FS.write c.caps (file c name) text with
  | exception (Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _) -> ()
  | () ->
      used c name (String.length text);
      trimmed c

let size (c : t) : int * int = (Hashtbl.length c.uses, c.total)

(* Tile_cache: the tiles on disk, for as long as the server says.

   A map shows the same streets for years, and OSM's servers are paid for
   by donations: its policy asks a client to keep what it was given, for
   as long as the answer says it stays good, and to ask politely when it
   no longer does. That is HTTP's caching (RFC 9111), which comes down to
   two questions.

   How long is it good? The answer says, and it is a date computed when
   the answer comes:

       Cache-Control: max-age=604800      good for a week from now
       Age: 3600                          of which a proxy used an hour
       Expires: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 ...      the old way (HTTP/1.0), when
                                          there is no max-age
       Cache-Control: no-cache            keep it, but ask before using
       Cache-Control: no-store            do not keep it

   And when it is no longer good? It is often still right, so the client
   asks "has it changed?", saying which version it has:

       GET /4/8/5.png                     HTTP/1.1 200 OK
                                          ETag: "abc"
                                          Cache-Control: max-age=604800
                                          (25 KB)
       ... a week later ...
       GET /4/8/5.png                     HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
       If-None-Match: "abc"               Cache-Control: max-age=604800
                                          (nothing)

   A few hundred bytes instead of 25 KB, and a second week. The ETag is
   whatever the server likes, a hash of the file usually; only the server
   ever compares it.

   And when the server does not answer at all, an old tile is shown rather
   than none: a map a week old is still a map.

   Kept within a size: past [limit] bytes the least recently used go, down
   to nine tenths of it, so that the work is not done again at the next
   tile. The cost is one number a tile, kept in the file index and
   written now and then: a crash loses the last few uses, not a tile.

   Only the worker uses it (Map_worker), so no lock.

   cs-history:
   Caches were on the web before there was much of a web: CERN's httpd
   (Ari Luotonen and Kevin Altis, 1994) was a proxy keeping pages, for a
   laboratory's one slow line. HTTP/1.0 had If-Modified-Since, by the
   clock, a second being too coarse and a server's clock not to be
   trusted. HTTP/1.1 (RFC 2068, 1997; Jeffrey Mogul, for a good part) gave
   the ETag and Cache-Control; the rest of the web's speed, CDNs from
   Akamai (1998) on, is built on those few headers.

   Reference: RFC 9111, "HTTP Caching" (Fielding, Nottingham and Reschke,
   2022); OSM's Tile Usage Policy,
   https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/. *)

type t

(* a tile as kept: its file, until when it is good (seconds since 1970), the
 * server's name for this version *)
type entry = { bytes : string; expires : float; etag : string option }

(* [lifetime ~now headers]: until when an answer with these headers stays
 * good (0. when it must be asked again each time: nothing said, no-cache);
 * None when it must not be kept *)
val lifetime : now:float -> Http.header list -> float option

(* [create caps ~dir ~limit]: the cache in [dir], made if it is not there,
 * of at most [limit] bytes; None if it cannot be made *)
val create : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. > -> dir:string -> limit:int -> t option

(* the tile of this name ("4/8/5") *)
val find : t -> string -> entry option

(* kept, or kept again, the least recently used going if it is too much *)
val put : t -> string -> entry -> unit

(* how many tiles and bytes are kept (the tests) *)
val size : t -> int * int

(* See Tiles.mli *)

let size : int = 256
let max_zoom : int = 19

type key = { z : int; x : int; y : int }
type placed = { key : key; left : int; top : int }

let name (k : key) : string = Printf.sprintf "%d/%d/%d" k.z k.x k.y
let url (base : string) (k : key) : string = Printf.sprintf "%s/%s.png" base (name k)

(* (division and remainder rounding down: left of the world is negative) *)
let floor_div (a : int) (b : int) : int = if a >= 0 then a / b else -((b - 1 - a) / b)
let wrap (a : int) (n : int) : int = a - (floor_div a n * n)

let in_view (z : int) (cx : int) (cy : int) (w : int) (h : int) : placed list =
  let left = cx - (w / 2) and top = cy - (h / 2) in
  let n = 1 lsl z in
  let x0 = floor_div left size and x1 = floor_div (left + w - 1) size in
  let y0 = max 0 (floor_div top size) and y1 = min (n - 1) (floor_div (top + h - 1) size) in
  let rec cols (x : int) (acc : placed list) : placed list =
    if x > x1 then acc
    else
      let rec rows (y : int) (acc : placed list) : placed list =
        if y > y1 then acc
        else
          rows (y + 1)
            ({ key = { z; x = wrap x n; y }; left = (x * size) - left; top = (y * size) - top } :: acc)
      in
      cols (x + 1) (rows y0 acc)
  in
  (* the distance of a tile's centre from the window's, squared *)
  let far (p : placed) : int =
    let dx = p.left + (size / 2) - (w / 2) and dy = p.top + (size / 2) - (h / 2) in
    (dx * dx) + (dy * dy)
  in
  List.stable_sort (fun (a : placed) (b : placed) -> compare (far a) (far b)) (cols x0 [])

let rezoomed ~(dz : int) ~(px : int) ~(py : int) (cx : int) (cy : int) : int * int =
  let moved (c : int) (p : int) : int =
    let world = c + p in
    (if dz >= 0 then world lsl dz else floor_div world (1 lsl -dz)) - p
  in
  (moved cx px, moved cy py)

let centred (z : int) (cx : int) (cy : int) (h : int) : int * int =
  let world = size lsl z in
  let cy = if world <= h then world / 2 else max (h / 2) (min (world - (h - (h / 2))) cy) in
  (wrap cx world, cy)

let ancestor (k : key) (n : int) : key = { z = k.z - n; x = k.x lsr n; y = k.y lsr n }

let enlarged (parent : Rgba_image.t) (k : key) (n : int) : Rgba_image.t =
  let img = Rgba_image.create ~width:size ~height:size in
  let cell = 1 lsl n in
  let from_x = (k.x land (cell - 1)) * (size / cell) and from_y = (k.y land (cell - 1)) * (size / cell) in
  for y = 0 to size - 1 do
    let row = 4 * size * (from_y + (y / cell)) in
    for x = 0 to size - 1 do
      Bytes.blit parent.rgba (row + (4 * (from_x + (x / cell)))) img.rgba (4 * ((y * size) + x)) 4
    done
  done;
  img

(* Tiles: the map cut in squares of 256 pixels, at every zoom.

   A map of the world at street level would be a picture of a billion
   pixels on a side; nobody can send one, and nobody looks at more than a
   window of it. So it is cut in a pyramid, each level four times the
   one above:

       z = 0     1 tile: the world
       z = 1     2 x 2
       z = 2     4 x 4
       ...
       z = 19    2^19 x 2^19: 275 billion tiles, a house about 30 pixels

     a tile's address is z/x/y, x from the left and y from the top, and
     its four children at z + 1 are (2x, 2y), (2x+1, 2y), (2x, 2y+1),
     (2x+1, 2y+1):

       +-------+         +---+---+
       | 1/0/0 |   -->   |2/0/0 2/1/0|
       |       |         |2/0/1 2/1/1|
       +-------+         +---+---+

   A window needs the tiles it overlaps and no others, some twenty at
   most on a large screen, whatever the zoom: that is the whole idea. The
   tiles are plain files, so that any web server or cache in between
   can serve them, and a program with a PNG reader can draw them.

   And what to show of a tile that has not come yet: its ancestor is
   usually there, a quarter of it (a sixteenth...) enlarged. It is coarse
   for the moment it takes, the map never blank where it was just seen.

   cs-history:
   Keyhole's EarthViewer (2001, Google Earth in 2005) streamed its
   pictures this way; MapQuest and every web map before 2005 sent one
   picture per request, the page reloaded at each click on an arrow.
   Google Maps (February 2005; Lars and Jens Rasmussen's Where 2
   Technologies) put tiles of 256 pixels side by side in a page and moved
   them with JavaScript, which is what made people say "Ajax". Quadkeys
   and the pyramid are older: image pyramids from Burt and Adelson's
   Laplacian pyramid (1983), mipmaps from Lance Williams (1983), which
   are the same structure for textures. OpenStreetMap (Steve Coast, 2004)
   gave the world's streets as data anyone may use, and z/x/y became the
   convention of everyone's tiles but Google's own.

   modern:
   Vector tiles (Mapbox's, 2014; Google's since 2013): the same pyramid,
   of streets and labels as shapes drawn by the client, so that a map
   turns and scales smoothly and is much smaller. Here they are pictures,
   which ask only a PNG reader.

   Reference: "Slippy map tilenames" on the OpenStreetMap wiki, the
   arithmetic; Burt and Adelson, "The Laplacian Pyramid as a Compact Image
   Code" (IEEE Trans. Communications, 1983). *)

val size : int

(* a tile's address *)
type key = { z : int; x : int; y : int }

(* "4/8/5" *)
val name : key -> string

(* [url base key]: "base/4/8/5.png" *)
val url : string -> key -> string

(* the highest zoom asked of a server: OSM's *)
val max_zoom : int

(* a tile of the window, and its left and top on the window *)
type placed = { key : key; left : int; top : int }

(* [in_view z cx cy w h]: the tiles a window of [w] by [h] overlaps, its
 * centre at pixel ([cx], [cy]) of the world at zoom [z], the nearest to
 * the centre first (what the eye is on is fetched first). East and west
 * wrap round, so a key may be there twice at low zoom; north and south
 * of the map there is nothing. *)
val in_view : int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> placed list

(* the same centre at another zoom, [dz] levels from [z], the world's
 * pixel that is [px], [py] from the centre of the window staying where
 * it is: (cx, cy) at z to (cx', cy') at z + dz *)
val rezoomed : dz:int -> px:int -> py:int -> int -> int -> int * int

(* [centred z cx cy h]: the centre kept on the map: east and west wrapped
 * round; north and south, the window's edge not past the world's, and the
 * world in the middle when it is smaller than the window *)
val centred : int -> int -> int -> int -> int * int

(* [ancestor key n]: the tile [n] levels above that contains [key] *)
val ancestor : key -> int -> key

(* [enlarged parent key n]: the part of [parent], [n] levels above [key],
 * that [key] covers, at the size of a tile, each pixel 2^n by 2^n *)
val enlarged : Rgba_image.t -> key -> int -> Rgba_image.t

  time : string;
  temperature : float;
  code : int;
  wind : float;
  hours : (string * float) list;
  days : day list;

let url (base : string) (lat : float) (lon : float) : string =
  Printf.sprintf
    "%s/v1/forecast?latitude=%.4f&longitude=%.4f&current=temperature_2m,weather_code,wind_speed_10m&hourly=temperature_2m&daily=weather_code,temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum&forecast_days=7&forecast_hours=24&timezone=auto"
    base lat lon

let of_json (text : string) : t =
  try
    let j = Json.of_text text in
    let current = Json.member "current" j and hourly = Json.member "hourly" j and daily = Json.member "daily" j in
    let column (o : Json.t) (name : string) : Json.t list = Json.list (Json.member name o) in
    let floats (o : Json.t) (name : string) : float list = List.map Json.float (column o name) in
    let times (o : Json.t) : string list = List.map Json.string (column o "time") in
    let rec days (d : string list) (c : Json.t list) (h : float list) (l : float list) (r : float list) : day list =
      match (d, c, h, l, r) with
      | date :: d, code :: c, high :: h, low :: l, rain :: r ->
          { date; code = Json.int code; high; low; rain } :: days d c h l r
      | _ -> []
    in
    { time = Json.string (Json.member "time" current);
      temperature = Json.float (Json.member "temperature_2m" current);
      code = Json.int (Json.member "weather_code" current);
      wind = Json.float (Json.member "wind_speed_10m" current);
      hours = List.combine (times hourly) (floats hourly "temperature_2m");
      days =
        days (times daily) (column daily "weather_code") (floats daily "temperature_2m_max")
          (floats daily "temperature_2m_min") (floats daily "precipitation_sum") }
  with
  | Json.Error why -> failwith ("not a forecast: " ^ why)
  | Invalid_argument _ -> failwith "not a forecast: its columns differ"

let kind (code : int) : kind =
  if code = 0 || code = 1 then Clear
  else if code = 2 then Partly
  else if code = 3 then Overcast
  else if code = 45 || code = 48 then Fog
  else if code >= 51 && code <= 57 then Drizzle
  else if (code >= 61 && code <= 67) || (code >= 80 && code <= 82) then Rain
  else if (code >= 71 && code <= 77) || code = 85 || code = 86 then Snow
  else if code >= 95 then Storm
  else Overcast

  match code with
  | 0 -> "clear"
  | 1 -> "mainly clear"
  | 2 -> "partly cloudy"
  | 3 -> "overcast"
  | 45 -> "fog"
  | 48 -> "freezing fog"
  | 51 | 53 | 55 -> "drizzle"
  | 56 | 57 -> "freezing drizzle"
  | 61 -> "slight rain"
  | 63 -> "rain"
  | 65 -> "heavy rain"
  | 66 | 67 -> "freezing rain"
  | 71 -> "slight snow"
  | 73 -> "snow"
  | 75 -> "heavy snow"
  | 77 -> "snow grains"
  | 80 | 81 -> "showers"
  | 82 -> "heavy showers"
  | 85 | 86 -> "snow showers"
  | 95 -> "thunderstorm"
  | 96 | 99 -> "thunderstorm, hail"
  | _ -> Printf.sprintf "code %d" code

let day_name (date : string) : string =
  match List.map int_of_string_opt (String.split_on_char '-' date) with
  | [ Some year; Some month; Some day ] ->
      let name = Civil.weekday_name (Civil.weekday (Civil.days_from_civil { year; month; day })) in
      Printf.sprintf "%s %d" (String.sub name 0 3) day
  | _ -> date

let degrees (t : float) : string =
  let whole = int_of_float (Float.round t) in
  Printf.sprintf "%d\xc2\xb0" whole

let lines (name : string) (f : t) : string list =
  [ name;
    Printf.sprintf "%s: %s, %s, wind %.0f km/h" f.time (degrees f.temperature) (words f.code) f.wind ]
  @ List.map
      (fun (d : day) ->
        let rain = if d.rain > 0. then Printf.sprintf ", %.1f mm" d.rain else "" in
        Printf.sprintf "%-7s %s to %s, %s%s" (day_name d.date) (degrees d.low) (degrees d.high) (words d.code) rain)
      f.days

(* Weather: a place's forecast, asked of Open-Meteo.

     GET /v1/forecast?latitude=47.39&longitude=0.69&current=...&daily=...
         &timezone=auto
     { "current": { "time": "2026-10-30T20:30", "temperature_2m": 10.5,
                    "weather_code": 0, "wind_speed_10m": 12.7 },
       "hourly":  { "time": [...], "temperature_2m": [...] },
       "daily":   { "time": ["2026-10-30", ...], "weather_code": [1, ...],
                    "temperature_2m_max": [...], ... } }

   An answer as columns, one array a quantity, not one object an hour:
   a table, as it is computed. timezone=auto: the service works out the
   place's time zone, so a day is the place's day and not ours or UTC's,
   which a forecast for the other side of the world gets wrong otherwise.

   What it says of the sky is a number from the World Meteorological
   Organization's table of "present weather" (code table 4677), made for
   observers sending telegrams in a few digits: 0 clear, 45 fog, 61 slight
   rain, 95 thunderstorm. A hundred codes, of which a model gives some
   thirty; here they are eight kinds of picture.

   cs-history:
   Forecasting by computing is older than the computer. Vilhelm Bjerknes
   said in 1904 that the weather is a problem in mechanics and physics: a
   few equations and the present state. Lewis Fry Richardson did it, by
   hand, on the Western Front where he drove an ambulance: six weeks of
   sums for six hours of weather over two points of Germany, published in
   "Weather Prediction by Numerical Process" (1922), and wrong by a factor
   of a hundred, for a reason understood only later (his starting data was
   unbalanced). He imagined a hall of 64,000 people computing to keep up
   with the real weather. In 1950 Jule Charney, Ragnar Fjørtoft and John
   von Neumann ran the first forecast on ENIAC, a simplified atmosphere:
   24 hours took about 24 hours. Edward Lorenz, in 1963, rounding a number
   on his LGP-30, found why it can never be perfect: chaos. A forecast
   today is an ensemble of runs from slightly different starts, on the
   largest machines of ECMWF and the national services, and those are what
   Open-Meteo hands on: all we do here is read a table.

   modern:
   GraphCast (DeepMind, 2023) and its kind, trained on forty years of past
   weather, now compete with the equations for a tiny part of the cost.

   Reference: Peter Lynch, "The Emergence of Numerical Weather Prediction:
   Richardson's Dream" (Cambridge, 2006); https://open-meteo.com/en/docs;
   its data is CC BY 4.0, hence the credit under the forecast. *)

type kind = Clear | Partly | Overcast | Fog | Drizzle | Rain | Snow | Storm

type day = { date : string; code : int; high : float; low : float; rain : float }

type t = {
  time : string; (* "2026-10-30T20:30", the place's *)
  temperature : float;
  code : int;
  wind : float; (* km/h *)
  hours : (string * float) list; (* the next hours' temperatures *)
  days : day list;
}

val url : string -> float -> float -> string

(* Failure if it is not such an answer *)
val of_json : string -> t

(* the WMO's code: its picture and its words *)
val kind : int -> kind
val words : int -> string

(* "2026-10-31" -> "Sat 31" *)
val day_name : string -> string

(* a temperature in whole degrees, "10°", never "-0°" *)
val degrees : float -> string

(* the forecast as lines of text (mini-maps weather), the place's name first *)
val lines : string -> t -> string list

(* See Weather_panel.mli *)

module P = Playground

type state = Waiting | Came of Weather.t | Failed of string

let width (fw : float) : float = Float.min 300. (fw -. 12.)
let left (fw : float) : float = (fw /. 2.) -. width fw -. 6.
let top (fh : float) : float = (fh /. 2.) -. 6.
let foot (fh : float) : float = (-.fh /. 2.) +. 26.

let inside (fw : float) (fh : float) (mx : float) (my : float) : bool =
  mx >= left fw && mx <= left fw +. width fw && my <= top fh && my >= foot fh

(* a picture of the sky of [size] (its width) at (x, y) *)
let icon (kind : Weather.kind) (size : float) (x : float) (y : float) : P.shape list =
  let u = size /. 12. in
  let at (s : P.shape) (dx : float) (dy : float) : P.shape = s |> P.move (x +. (dx *. u)) (y +. (dy *. u)) in
  let sun (dx : float) (dy : float) (r : float) : P.shape = at (P.circle (P.rgb 245 180 30) (r *. u)) dx dy in
  let cloud (c : P.color) : P.shape list =
    [ at (P.circle c (2.5 *. u)) (-2.5) 0.; at (P.circle c (3.2 *. u)) 0.5 1.;
      at (P.circle c (2.2 *. u)) 3. (-0.3); at (P.rectangle c (7.5 *. u) (2.6 *. u)) 0.3 (-1.2) ]
  in
  let grey = P.rgb 150 150 160 and light = P.rgb 195 195 205 in
  let drops (c : P.color) : P.shape list =
    List.map (fun (dx : float) -> at (P.rectangle c (0.8 *. u) (2. *. u)) dx (-4.2)) [ -2.5; 0.; 2.5 ]
  in
  match kind with
  | Clear -> [ sun 0. 0. 4. ]
  | Partly -> sun 2. 2. 3. :: cloud light
  | Overcast -> cloud grey
  | Fog -> List.map (fun (dy : float) -> at (P.rectangle light (9. *. u) (1. *. u)) 0. dy) [ 2.5; 0.; -2.5 ]
  | Drizzle -> cloud light @ drops (P.rgb 120 170 230)
  | Rain -> cloud grey @ drops (P.rgb 40 90 200)
  | Snow -> cloud light @ List.map (fun (dx : float) -> at (P.circle (P.rgb 130 170 230) (0.8 *. u)) dx (-4.2)) [ -2.5; 0.; 2.5 ]
  | Storm -> cloud (P.rgb 100 100 115) @ [ at (P.polygon (P.rgb 245 180 30) [ (0.5 *. u, 0.); (-1.5 *. u, -3. *. u); (0., -3. *. u); (-1. *. u, -5.5 *. u); (2. *. u, -2. *. u); (0.5 *. u, -2. *. u) ]) 0. (-0.5) ]

(* a temperature in tenths of a degree, a whole number *)
let tenths (t : float) : int = int_of_float (Float.round (t *. 10.))

(* the next hours, a bar each: whole tenths to whole pixels *)
let bars (x : float) (y : float) (room : float) (height : int) (hours : (string * float) list) : P.shape list =
  match hours with
  | [] -> []
  | _ ->
      let values = List.map (fun ((_, t) : string * float) -> tenths t) hours in
      let lo = List.fold_left min max_int values and hi = List.fold_left max min_int values in
      let n = List.length values in
      let step = int_of_float room / n in
      List.mapi
        (fun (i : int) (v : int) ->
          let h = 4 + ((v - lo) * (height - 4) / max 1 (hi - lo)) in
          P.rectangle (P.rgb 240 150 60) (float_of_int (step - 1)) (float_of_int h)
          |> P.move (x +. float_of_int ((i * step) + (step / 2))) (y +. (float_of_int h /. 2.)))
        values

let panel (fw : float) (fh : float) (name : string) (state : state) : P.shape list =
  let x = left fw +. 10. and room = width fw -. 20. in
  let ink = P.rgb 20 20 20 and soft = P.rgb 90 90 90 in
  let line (color : P.color) (y : float) (s : string) : P.shape = fst (Map_look.text color ~size:14. x y (Map_look.cut room s)) in
  let back =
    P.rectangle (P.rgb 252 252 248) (width fw) (top fh -. foot fh)
    |> P.move (left fw +. (width fw /. 2.)) ((top fh +. foot fh) /. 2.)
  in
  let y0 = top fh -. 20. in
  let title = line ink y0 name in
  let body =
    match state with
    | Waiting -> [ line soft (y0 -. 24.) "asking the forecast..." ]
    | Failed why -> [ line soft (y0 -. 24.) why ]
    | Came f ->
        let big = y0 -. 40. in
        let now = fst (Map_look.text ink ~size:30. (x +. 64.) (big -. 12.) (Weather.degrees f.temperature)) in
        let says = line ink (big -. 42.) (Printf.sprintf "%s, wind %.0f km/h" (Weather.words f.code) f.wind) in
        let hot = List.map snd f.hours in
        let range =
          match hot with
          | [] -> ""
          | t :: _ ->
              let lo = List.fold_left Float.min t hot and hi = List.fold_left Float.max t hot in
              Printf.sprintf "the next %d hours: %s to %s" (List.length hot) (Weather.degrees lo) (Weather.degrees hi)
        in
        let row (i : int) (d : Weather.day) : P.shape list =
          let y = big -. 134. -. (float_of_int i *. 24.) in
          if y < foot fh +. 24. then []
          else
            (* (a tenth under 10 mm: 0.2 mm is not "0 mm") *)
            let rain =
              if d.rain >= 10. then Printf.sprintf "%.0f mm" d.rain
              else if d.rain > 0. then Printf.sprintf "%.1f mm" d.rain
              else ""
            in
            [ fst (Map_look.text ink ~size:14. x y (Weather.day_name d.date));
              fst (Map_look.text ink ~size:14. (x +. 92.) y (Weather.degrees d.low ^ " to " ^ Weather.degrees d.high));
              fst (Map_look.text soft ~size:14. (x +. 205.) y rain) ]
            @ icon (Weather.kind d.code) 20. (x +. 72.) (y +. 5.)
        in
        (icon (Weather.kind f.code) 52. (x +. 28.) (big -. 2.) @ [ now; says; line soft (big -. 62.) range ])
        @ bars x (big -. 114.) room 44 f.hours
        @ List.concat (List.mapi row f.days)
        @ [ line soft (foot fh +. 8.) "Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0" ]
  in
  back :: title :: body

      +------------------------------+

   The pictures of the sky are made of circles and rectangles, so they

(* See Film.mli *)

(* ix: what shows a film of the author's playground's
 * apps/media/TinyMediaPlayer.ml (its deck, movie_frame), alone: not its
 * playlist, its pictures, its scope *)

open Playground

(* an MPEG-1's decisions, for the analyzer; what was sent, made when asked *)
type analysis = { header : Mpeg1.header; info : int -> Mpeg1.info; sent : unit -> Movie.t }

type t = { movie : Movie.t; sound : Signal.stereo option; loops : bool; mpeg : analysis option }

(* the frames, and what the analyzer wants of them *)
let of_mpeg1 (bytes : string) (sound : Signal.stereo option) : t =
  let header, movie, info = Mpeg1.of_string ~residual:false bytes in
  let made = ref None in
  let sent () =
    match !made with
    | Some m -> m
    | None ->
        let _, m, _ = Mpeg1.of_string ~residual:true bytes in
        made := Some m;
        m
  in
  { movie; sound; loops = false; mpeg = Some { header; info; sent } }

let is_film (kind : string) : bool =
  List.mem kind [ "video/x-y4m"; "video/x-flic"; "video/x-msvideo"; "video/mpeg"; "image/gif" ]

(* an MP2's samples at our rate *)
let mpeg_sound (bytes : string) : Signal.stereo option =
  match Mpeg_audio.decode bytes with
  | Error _ -> None
  | Ok ((h : Mpeg_audio_header.t), (s : Signal.stereo)) ->
      let at_our_rate (x : Signal.t) = if h.sample_rate = Signal.rate then x else Resample.to_rate Cubic h.sample_rate x in
      Some { left = at_our_rate s.left; right = at_our_rate s.right }

(* [s] starting [seconds] later (earlier if negative): silence added
 * before it, or its start cut *)
let delayed (seconds : float) (s : Signal.t) : Signal.t =
  let n = int_of_float (Float.round (seconds *. float_of_int Signal.rate)) in
  if n >= 0 then Array.append (Array.make n 0.) s
  else Array.sub s (min (-n) (Array.length s)) (max 0 (Array.length s + n))

(* a system stream, its first video and audio: the sound moved so that its
 * time 0 is the first picture's (their first timestamps) *)
let of_system_stream (bytes : string) : (t, string) result =
  let streams = Mpeg_system.of_string bytes in
  match Mpeg_system.video streams with
  | None -> Error "no video stream"
  | Some video ->
      let sound =
        match Mpeg_system.audio streams with
        | None -> None
        | Some audio ->
            let offset = match (audio.first_pts, video.first_pts) with Some a, Some v -> a -. v | _ -> 0. in
            let moved (s : Signal.stereo) : Signal.stereo = { left = delayed offset s.left; right = delayed offset s.right } in
            Option.map moved (mpeg_sound audio.bytes)
      in
      Ok (of_mpeg1 video.bytes sound)

let read ~(kind : string) (bytes : string) : (t, string) result =
  match kind with
  | "video/x-y4m" -> Ok { movie = snd (Y4m.of_string bytes); sound = None; loops = false; mpeg = None }
  | "video/x-flic" -> Ok { movie = snd (Fli.of_string bytes); sound = None; loops = false; mpeg = None }
  | "image/gif" -> Ok { movie = Movie.of_frames (Gif.animation bytes); sound = None; loops = true; mpeg = None }
  | "video/x-msvideo" ->
      let _, movie, sound = Avi.of_string bytes in
      let at_rate ((rate, mono) : int * float array) : Signal.stereo =
        let s = Resample.to_rate Linear rate mono in
        { left = s; right = s }
      in
      Ok { movie; sound = Option.map at_rate sound; loops = false; mpeg = None }
  | "video/mpeg" when String.length bytes > 3 && bytes.[3] = '\xBA' -> of_system_stream bytes
  | "video/mpeg" -> Ok (of_mpeg1 bytes None)
  | _ -> Error ("not a film: " ^ kind)
  | exception Failure why -> Error why

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The sound's side: the mixer pulls its blocks between frames *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [heard]: the furthest the sound has been heard, in seconds *)
type deck = { mutable samples : Signal.stereo; mutable pos : int; mutable paused : bool; mutable heard : float }

let deck = { samples = { left = [||]; right = [||] }; pos = 0; paused = false; heard = 0. }

let fill (out : Signal.stereo) : unit =
  let n = Array.length out.left in
  Array.fill out.left 0 n 0.;
  Array.fill out.right 0 n 0.;
  if not deck.paused then (
    let k = max 0 (min n (Array.length deck.samples.left - deck.pos)) in
    Array.blit deck.samples.left deck.pos out.left 0 k;
    Array.blit deck.samples.right deck.pos out.right 0 k;
    deck.pos <- deck.pos + k)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The picture's side *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type model = {
  film : t;
  clock : float; (* seconds of the film shown, when the sound does not say *)
  last : float option; (* the time of the frame before *)
  paused : bool;
  changes : bool; (* d: what changed from the frame before, the rest dimmed *)
  blocks : bool; (* a: an MPEG-1's macroblocks and vectors drawn over it *)
  residual : bool; (* r: an MPEG-1 as what was sent, the prediction off *)
  held : string Set_.t;
}

(* where the film is: the sound's, once it has begun. What was pulled less
 * what is still queued: the queue grows when a frame is slow, up to a third
 * of a second, and the picture would leap ahead of the ear. Never back, when
 * it grows: a frame further back is decoded from the film's start. *)
let position (m : model) : float =
  if deck.pos > 0 then begin
    deck.heard <- Float.max deck.heard ((float_of_int deck.pos /. float_of_int Signal.rate) -. Audio.latency ());
    deck.heard
  end
  else if m.film.loops then Float.rem m.clock m.film.movie.duration
  else m.clock

let status_bar = 26.

let update (caps : Cap.all_caps) (computer : computer) (m : model) : model =
  if m.film.sound <> None then
    ignore
      (Audio.instrument "film" (fun () ->
           { Instrument.note_on = (fun _ _ -> ()); note_off = ignore; set = (fun _ _ -> ()); fill }));
  let keys = computer.keyboard.keys in
  let pressed (name : string) = Set_.mem name keys && not (Set_.mem name m.held) in
  if computer.keyboard.typed = "q" then CapStdlib.exit caps 0;
  let paused = if pressed "space" then not m.paused else m.paused in
  deck.paused <- paused;
  let typed = computer.keyboard.typed in
  let m =
    { m with
      changes = (if typed = "d" then not m.changes else m.changes);
      blocks = (if typed = "a" then not m.blocks else m.blocks);
      residual = (if typed = "r" then not m.residual else m.residual) }
  in
  (* the arrows, five seconds: the sound's place, and the timer's *)
  let m =
    let step = if pressed "ArrowRight" then 5. else if pressed "ArrowLeft" then -5. else 0. in
    if step = 0. then m
    else
      let t = Float.max 0. (Float.min (m.film.movie.duration -. 0.001) (position m +. step)) in
      deck.pos <- int_of_float (t *. float_of_int Signal.rate);
      deck.heard <- t;
      { m with clock = t }
  in
  let (Time now) = computer.time in
  (* (a step of more than a second is no film's: the platform's first time,
   * or a machine that stopped, which goes on from where it was) *)
  let passed = match m.last with Some t when now -. t <= 1. -> now -. t | _ -> 0. in
  { m with clock = (if paused then m.clock else m.clock +. passed); last = Some now; paused; held = keys }

(* a whole number of pixels a pixel when enlarged: at 8.75, the rows fall
 * between pixels; made smaller to fit, it can't be *)
let fit (m : Movie.t) (w : float) (h : float) : float =
  let f = Float.min (w /. float_of_int m.width) (h /. float_of_int m.height) in
  if f >= 1. then Float.of_int (int_of_float f) else f

(* what changed: the pixels the same as the frame before's at a quarter of
 * their brightness, the others as they are: what a delta frame stores
 * (Fli.mli), seen; the first frame all changed *)
let changed (movie : Movie.t) (i : int) : Rgba_image.t =
  let img = movie.frame i in
  if i = 0 then img
  else
    let before = movie.frame (i - 1) in
    let out = Rgba_image.create ~width:img.width ~height:img.height in
    let get (b : Bytes.t) (at : int) = Bytes.get_uint8 b at in
    for p = 0 to (img.width * img.height) - 1 do
      let o = 4 * p in
      let same =
        get img.rgba o = get before.rgba o
        && get img.rgba (o + 1) = get before.rgba (o + 1)
        && get img.rgba (o + 2) = get before.rgba (o + 2)
      in
      for c = 0 to 2 do
        let v = get img.rgba (o + c) in
        Bytes.set_uint8 out.rgba (o + c) (if same then v / 4 else v)
      done;
      Bytes.set_uint8 out.rgba (o + 3) 255
    done;
    out

let segment (color : color) ((x1, y1) : float * float) ((x2, y2) : float * float) : shape =
  let dx = x2 -. x1 and dy = y2 -. y1 in
  rectangle color (sqrt ((dx *. dx) +. (dy *. dy)) +. 1.) 2.
  |> rotate (atan2 (y2 -. y1) (x2 -. x1) *. 180. /. Float.pi)
  |> move ((x1 +. x2) /. 2.) ((y1 +. y2) /. 2.)

let kind_color (kind : Mpeg1.kind) : color =
  match kind with I -> rgb 230 60 50 | P -> rgb 60 200 80 | B -> rgb 60 130 240

(* the analyzer, over an MPEG-1: each macroblock tinted by how it was coded
 * (intra red, from the past green, from the future blue, from both purple, a
 * P's with no vector grey, skipped not at all), its vectors drawn from its
 * centre to where its pixels come from, white forward, cyan backward; under
 * the picture, the frames' kinds in the order shown, the one shown tall.
 * ix: the playground's TinyMediaPlayer, its analysis *)
let blocks_over (a : analysis) (movie : Movie.t) (f : float) (centre_y : float) (bottom_y : float) (w : float) (i : int) : shape list =
  let left = -.(float_of_int movie.width *. f /. 2.) in
  let top = centre_y +. (float_of_int movie.height *. f /. 2.) in
  let picture_bottom = top -. (float_of_int movie.height *. f) in
  let inf = a.info i in
  let cell = 16. *. f in
  let macroblock (at : int) ((how, fv, bv) : Mpeg1.how * (int * int) * (int * int)) : shape list =
    let cx = left +. ((float_of_int (at mod inf.mb_width) +. 0.5) *. cell) in
    let cy = top -. ((float_of_int (at / inf.mb_width) +. 0.5) *. cell) in
    (* the last row's can run past the picture: their tint cut at its edge *)
    let tint_h = Float.min (cell -. 2.) (cy +. (cell /. 2.) -. picture_bottom -. 1.) in
    let tint =
      match how with
      | Intra -> [ rgb 230 60 50 ]
      | Forward -> [ rgb 60 200 80 ]
      | Backward -> [ rgb 60 130 240 ]
      | Both -> [ rgb 180 80 220 ]
      | Zero -> [ rgb 150 150 150 ]
      | Skipped -> []
    in
    let arrow ((dx, dy) : int * int) (color : color) : shape list =
      if dx = 0 && dy = 0 then []
      else
        [ segment color (cx, cy) (cx +. (float_of_int dx /. 2. *. f), cy -. (float_of_int dy /. 2. *. f));
          move cx cy (circle color 3.) ]
    in
    List.map
      (fun (c : color) -> move cx (cy +. (cell /. 2.) -. 1. -. (tint_h /. 2.)) (fade 0.35 (rectangle c (cell -. 2.) tint_h)))
      tint
    @ arrow fv (rgb 250 250 250)
    @ arrow bv (rgb 90 230 230)
  in
  let n = Array.length a.header.kinds in
  let side = Float.min 14. ((w -. 40.) /. float_of_int n) in
  let strip =
    List.mapi
      (fun (k : int) (kind : Mpeg1.kind) ->
        move
          ((-.(float_of_int n *. side /. 2.)) +. ((float_of_int k +. 0.5) *. side))
          bottom_y
          (rectangle (kind_color kind) (side -. 2.) (if k = i then 22. else 10.)))
      (Array.to_list a.header.kinds)
  in
  List.concat (List.mapi macroblock (Array.to_list inf.macroblocks)) @ strip

(* The picture at its size in the window, kept while it is the same one: the
 * view is asked 60 times a second, a film has 25 pictures. *)
type sized = { i : int; changes_on : bool; residual_on : bool; tw : int; th : int; image : Rgba_image.t }

let last_sized : sized option ref = ref None

let sized (m : model) (i : int) (tw : int) (th : int) : Rgba_image.t =
  match !last_sized with
  | Some s when s.i = i && s.changes_on = m.changes && s.residual_on = m.residual && s.tw = tw && s.th = th -> s.image
  | _ ->
      let shown = match m.film.mpeg with Some a when m.residual -> a.sent () | _ -> m.film.movie in
      let picture = if m.changes then changed shown i else shown.frame i in
      let image = if picture.width = tw && picture.height = th then picture else Blit.resized picture ~width:tw ~height:th in
      last_sized := Some { i; changes_on = m.changes; residual_on = m.residual; tw; th; image };
      image

(* a black rectangle by its corners in pixels from the window's top left, if
 * it has any size *)
let bar (w : float) (h : float) ((x0, y0, x1, y1) : int * int * int * int) : shape list =
  if x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0 then []
  else
    let width = float_of_int (x1 - x0) and height = float_of_int (y1 - y0) in
    [ move (float_of_int x0 +. (width /. 2.) -. (w /. 2.)) ((h /. 2.) -. float_of_int y0 -. (height /. 2.)) (rectangle black width height) ]

(* the status line's size: smaller in a window that it would run out of *)
let line_scale (w : float) (line : string) : float =
  let _, length = Hershey.layout line in
  Float.min 1.6 ((w -. 8.) /. (length *. words_font_size /. Hershey.units_per_em))

let view (computer : computer) (m : model) : shape list =
  let movie = m.film.movie in
  let w = computer.screen.width and h = computer.screen.height in
  let i = Movie.index_at movie (position m) in
  let f = fit movie w (h -. status_bar) in
  let line =
    let mpeg =
      match m.film.mpeg with
      | Some a ->
          let kind = match a.header.kinds.(i) with I -> "I" | P -> "P" | B -> "B" in
          Printf.sprintf " (%s)   a r: blocks, what was sent" kind
      | None -> ""
    in
    Printf.sprintf "frame %d of %d%s   d: changes   arrows: 5 s   %s   q: the end" (i + 1) (Movie.frame_count movie) mpeg
      (if m.paused then "space: go on" else "space: pause")
  in
  (* in whole pixels, drawn as they are (Blit.draw_copy); the bars around it,
   * no black under it: what is a frame's cost is the pixels *)
  let tw = max 1 (int_of_float (f *. float_of_int movie.width)) and th = max 1 (int_of_float (f *. float_of_int movie.height)) in
  let ww = int_of_float w and wh = int_of_float h in
  let x0 = (ww - tw) / 2 and y0 = (wh - int_of_float status_bar - th) / 2 in
  let cx = float_of_int x0 +. (float_of_int tw /. 2.) -. (w /. 2.) in
  let cy = (h /. 2.) -. float_of_int y0 -. (float_of_int th /. 2.) in
  let analysis =
    match m.film.mpeg with
    | Some a when m.blocks ->
        blocks_over a movie f (status_bar /. 2.) ((-.h /. 2.) +. status_bar +. 14.) w i
    | _ -> []
  in
  bar w h (0, 0, ww, y0)
  @ bar w h (0, y0 + th, ww, wh)
  @ bar w h (0, y0, x0, y0 + th)
  @ bar w h (x0 + tw, y0, ww, y0 + th)
  @ [ move cx cy (bitmap (float_of_int tw) (float_of_int th) (sized m i tw th)) ]
  @ analysis
  @ [
    move 0. ((-.h /. 2.) +. (status_bar /. 2.)) (scale (line_scale w line) (words (rgb 200 200 200) line)) ]

(* The window a film opens with: as many times its size as fit in 800 pixels,
 * where every pixel is one more to draw at each frame (352 by 288, twice its
 * size: 21 ms of a picture; three times: 33), the status line under it. A
 * film too large for that: the platform's own size, the picture made to fit. *)
let window_flag (movie : Movie.t) : string =
  let k = min (800 / movie.width) ((800 - int_of_float status_bar) / movie.height) in
  if k < 1 then ""
  else Printf.sprintf "%dx%d" (k * movie.width) ((k * movie.height) + int_of_float status_bar)

let run (caps : Cap.all_caps) (film : t) : unit =
  (match film.sound with Some s -> deck.samples <- s | None -> ());
  Playground_platform.run_app caps
    (Playground_platform.flags caps @ [ ("window", window_flag film.movie) ])
    (Playground.game view (update caps) { film; clock = 0.; last = None; paused = false; changes = false; blocks = false; residual = false; held = Set_.empty })

(* Film: mini-play's window, a film as a Playground program.

       the file --Y4m, Fli, Avi, Gif, Mpeg1--> Movie.t, its sound
                                          |          | pulled by the mixer,
                                          |          v block by block (Audio)
                     the frame at the -- index_at <-- the sound's position
                     sound's clock

   The picture follows the sound and not the other way round: a frame
   skipped is hardly seen, a sound skipped is always heard. Until the sound
   has begun, and for a film without one, a timer runs the picture, so that
   a machine with no sound does not stay on the first frame.

   cs-history:
   Muybridge's horse (1878) made a movement into a row of pictures, and film
   stayed that for a century. On a computer the trouble was the size: at 320
   by 240, 25 pictures a second is 5.7 MB of them a second, against a CD-ROM's
   150 KB. FLI (Autodesk Animator, 1989) stores only what changed; AVI
   (Video for Windows, 1992) separates a container from its codec; MPEG-1
   (1993) moves blocks of the last picture. Movie.mli says what they share.
   Going back is slow for what depends on the past: a seek decodes forward
   from the start, as a group of pictures' entry would spare it. *)

(* an MPEG-1's decisions (Mpeg1.mli), for the analyzer; what was sent, the
   prediction off, decoded the first time it is asked for *)
type analysis = { header : Mpeg1.header; info : int -> Mpeg1.info; sent : unit -> Movie.t }

type t = {
  movie : Movie.t;
  sound : Signal.stereo option; (* at Signal.rate *)
  loops : bool; (* begun again at its end: a GIF's way *)
  mpeg : analysis option;
}

(* can [kind] (File_kind's) be read as a film? *)
val is_film : string -> bool

(* the file's bytes and its kind; Error in words *)
val read : kind:string -> string -> (t, string) result

(* the window: space pauses, the arrows go five seconds back or on, q leaves;
   and what is the reason ix has video at all, the keys that show how it is
   stored: d dims what did not change since the frame before, and for an
   MPEG-1 a draws its macroblocks and vectors, r shows only what was sent *)
val run : Cap.all_caps -> t -> unit

(* What an .mpg costs, a part at a time, to be run under mini-5i -s (the
 * instructions counted) or by a clock on a board:
 *   mpg_bench open film.mpg      the file read and its streams apart
 *   mpg_bench sound film.mpg     and its sound decoded whole
 *   mpg_bench frames film.mpg n  and its first n pictures, not the sound
 *   mpg_bench draw film.mpg n w h f [floats]  and each drawn in a w by h
 *     window, f times its size, on black, by Blit.resized or as draw_fast
 * Each run's count less the run before it is the part's cost.
 * ix: the author's playground's libs/graphics/videos/tests/Mpg_bench.ml, by
 * parts and no clock of its own *)

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      let argv = CapSys.argv caps in
      let bytes =
        match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v argv.(2)) with Some b -> b | None -> failwith "can't read the file"
      in
      let streams = Mpeg_system.of_string bytes in
      let video = Option.get (Mpeg_system.video streams) and audio = Option.get (Mpeg_system.audio streams) in
      match argv.(1) with
      | "open" -> ()
      | "sound" -> ignore (Mpeg_audio.decode audio.bytes)
      | "frames" ->
          let h, movie, _ = Mpeg1.of_string ~residual:false video.bytes in
          let n = min (int_of_string argv.(3)) (Movie.frame_count movie) in
          Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%dx%d, %d frames, %d asked\n" h.width h.height (Movie.frame_count movie) n);
          for i = 0 to n - 1 do
            ignore (movie.frame i)
          done
      | "draw" ->
          let h, movie, _ = Mpeg1.of_string ~residual:false video.bytes in
          let n = min (int_of_string argv.(3)) (Movie.frame_count movie) in
          let w = int_of_string argv.(4) and wh = int_of_string argv.(5) and f = float_of_string argv.(6) in
          let options = { Shape_render_software.default_options with antialiasing = true } in
          for i = 0 to n - 1 do
            let picture = movie.frame i in
            let fb = Framebuffer.create ~width:w ~height:wh in
            let tw = int_of_float (f *. float_of_int h.width) and th = int_of_float (f *. float_of_int h.height) in
            let bitmap =
              if Array.length argv > 7 && argv.(7) = "floats" then Playground.bitmap (float_of_int tw) (float_of_int th) picture
              else
                Playground.bitmap (float_of_int tw) (float_of_int th) (Blit.resized picture ~width:tw ~height:th)
                |> Playground.move (if (w - tw) land 1 = 1 then 0.5 else 0.) (if (wh - th) land 1 = 1 then 0.5 else 0.)
            in
            let shapes =
              [ Playground.rectangle Playground.black (float_of_int w) (float_of_int wh); bitmap ]
            in
            Shape_render_software.render ~options ~scale:1. fb shapes
          done
      | _ -> failwith "usage: mpg_bench open|sound|frames|draw file [n [w h f [floats]]]")

apps/media/play/Play.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-play: a file of music played: its samples written to
 * /dev/audio, or to standard output:
 *
 *     mini-play song.mod                       on mini-9pi
 *     mini-play -c song.mp3 | aplay -f cd      on Linux
 *
 * old: standard output always, mini-play song.mod > /dev/audio (the
 * author, 2026-10-13, having played on the Pi 1: "I think it would be
 * better for play to use directly /dev/audio"). A filter is 9front's
 * way and kept as -c; what one types to hear a file is its name.
 *
 * The samples are what Plan 9's /dev/audio takes and what a CD holds:
 * 16 bits signed, the low byte first, the left channel then the right,
 * 44,100 of each a second (176,400 bytes a second). No header: a pipe
 * has no length to write in one.
 *
 *     the file's bytes --> Player (by the name's end: Mod_player,
 *                          Music, Mpeg_audio, Wav)
 *                             |  a block of 4,096 samples, floats
 *                             v
 *                          16 bits, clipped --> /dev/audio (or -c)
 *
 * The file is read whole (a song is a few megabytes); its samples are
 * not: a block is computed when the last was written, so the program
 * waits where its reader waits, and a device that plays at its own
 * pace paces it. Nothing here knows the device.
 *
 * others:
 * 9front's play(1) is a script over a decoder a format (audio/mp3dec,
 * audio/wavdec, games/midi ...), each a filter of this shape; one
 * program here (Player says more).
 *
 * A film is the same command with a window: mini-play clip.avi (Film; its
 * kind is the file's first bytes, File_kind, where a sound's is the name's
 * end, Player). -c and -s are for sounds.
 *
 * References: Plan 9's audio(3), for the samples' layout. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

let usage = "usage: mini-play [-c] [-s seconds] file
  the file's sound (.mod, .mid, .mp3, .mp2, .wav, .abc) played: written
  to /dev/audio, 16 bits, little-endian, two channels, 44,100 a second;
  a film (.y4m, .fli, .flc, .avi, .mpg, .m1v, an animated .gif) in a window
  -c: the samples to standard output (mini-play -c file | aplay -f cd)
  -s seconds: no more than that much of it"

let device = "/dev/audio"

let block = 4096

(* [play out p limit]: [p]'s blocks written, to its end or [limit] samples *)
let play (out : Unix.file_descr) (p : Player.t) (limit : int) : unit =
  let samples : Signal.stereo = { left = Array.make block 0.; right = Array.make block 0. } in
  let bytes = Bytes.create (4 * block) in
  let written = ref 0 in
  while (not (p.finished ())) && !written < limit do
    p.fill samples;
    let n = min block (limit - !written) in
    (* old: Bytes.set_uint16_le bytes (4 * i) (Signal.to_int16
     * samples.left.(i) land 0xFFFF), and the right one's: Float.round
     * and two checked stores a sample, a tenth of a MIDI file's
     * instructions on arm (machine/tests/profile.sh, 2026-10-13).
     * Audio_source.s16's way: to the nearest, a half away from zero,
     * by a truncation; the places are within [bytes]. *)
    for i = 0 to (2 * n) - 1 do
      let x = if i land 1 = 0 then Array.unsafe_get samples.left (i lsr 1) else Array.unsafe_get samples.right (i lsr 1) in
      let y = x *. 32767. in
      let v = if y >= 0. then int_of_float (y +. 0.5) else - int_of_float (0.5 -. y) in
      let v = if v > 32767 then 32767 else if v < -32768 then -32768 else v in
      Bytes.unsafe_set bytes (2 * i) (Char.unsafe_chr (v land 0xff));
      Bytes.unsafe_set bytes ((2 * i) + 1) (Char.unsafe_chr ((v lsr 8) land 0xff))
    done;
    if Unix.write out bytes 0 (4 * n) <> 4 * n then failwith "short write";
    written := !written + n
  done

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let error why = Console.eprint caps ("mini-play: " ^ why ^ "\n"); Exit.Err "play" in
  let run (stdout : bool) (limit : int) (file : string) : Exit.t =
    match FS.path file with
    | Error why -> error why
    | Ok path -> (
        match FS.read_opt caps path with
        | None -> error ("can't read " ^ file)
        | Some bytes -> (
            match Player.of_file file bytes with
            | Error why -> error (file ^ ": " ^ why)
            | Ok p -> (
                match if stdout then Some (Console.stdout_fd caps) else (try Some (FS.open_device_fd caps device) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> None) with
                | None -> error ("can't open " ^ device ^ " (-c: the samples to standard output)")
                | Some out -> (
                    match play out p limit with
                    | () -> Exit.OK
                    | exception Failure why -> error why
                    | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> error (Unix.error_message e)))))
  in
  (* mini-ml's collector copies all that is alive each time, and what
   * is alive here is the song (a MOD's instruments, a float a sample):
   * 37 of a hundred instructions of a MOD were its copying, measured on
   * arm (2026-10-13; the author, of tune.mod on the Pi 1: "not playing
   * smoothly"). A heap eight times what is alive is collected an eighth
   * as often (Plan9_loop's, for a game's floats). OCaml's own collector
   * takes the number as a hint and is not changed by it. *)
  Gc.set { (Gc.get ()) with Gc.space_overhead = 700 };
  let rec args (stdout : bool) (limit : int) (l : string list) : Exit.t =
    match l with
    | "-c" :: rest -> args true limit rest
    | "-s" :: seconds :: rest -> (
        match float_of_string_opt seconds with
        | Some s when s >= 0. -> args stdout (Signal.samples s) rest
        | _ -> error usage)
    | [ file ] when file <> "" && file.[0] <> '-' -> run stdout limit file
    | _ -> error usage in
  args false max_int (List.tl (Array.to_list argv))

(* the last argument, when it is a film: its kind and its bytes *)
let film_of (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (argv : string array) : Film.t option =
  let last = argv.(Array.length argv - 1) in
  if Array.length argv < 2 || last = "" || last.[0] = '-' then None
  else
    match FS.path last with
    | Error _ -> None
    | Ok path -> (
        match File_kind.of_path caps path with
        | exception Sys_error _ -> None
        | kind when not (Film.is_film kind) -> None
        | kind -> (
            match Option.map (Film.read ~kind) (FS.read_opt caps path) with
            | Some (Ok film) -> Some film
            | Some (Error why) -> failwith (last ^ ": " ^ why)
            | None -> None))

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      Exit.exit caps
        (Exit.catch (fun () ->
             let argv = CapSys.argv caps in
             match film_of caps argv with
             | Some film ->
                 Film.run caps film;
                 Exit.OK
             | None -> main caps argv)))
apps/misc/Colors.ml
6219
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-colors: Plan 9's colors (principia's apps/misc/colors.c):
 * the 256 colours of Plan 9's colour map, a square each, 16 a row, the
 * last one first. The left button on a square says its number and its
 * red, green and blue; the right button's menu has exit. -r: a ramp of
 * 256 greys instead; -x: the numbers in hexadecimal.
 *
 * A graphical program like any: it draws where Display.screen says, in
 * its window under mini-rio (windows/rio/), on the whole screen without.
 *
 * It is also the smallest program in ix that talks to the draw
 * device itself, and so the skeleton of all of them (mini-rio, the
 * Playground platform that mini-office runs on):
 *
 *   Display.init          the connection opened (/dev/draw)
 *   Display.color         a colour is an image: one pixel, repeated
 *   Display.screen        the image to draw in: the window's, or the
 *                         whole screen's
 *   Draw.fill             a message kept; nothing shows yet
 *   Display.flush         the messages sent: now it shows
 *   Mouse.receive         wait for the mouse; what comes says the
 *                         buttons, the place, and whether the window
 *                         was resized: then Display.screen again, and
 *                         everything painted again
 *
 * The map itself, worked on a few numbers ([cmap2rgb]): 0 is black
 * and 255 white; 0x00, 0x11, 0x22 and 0x33 are the four darkest
 * greys (0, 17, 34, 51), and there are sixteen greys in all, each a
 * multiple of 17. A number is a hue (four reds by four greens by
 * four blues, 64) and one of four values of it.
 *
 * design:
 * 256 colours, and how to spend them. The even way is a cube: six
 * levels each of red, green and blue is 216 colours, the palette the
 * web called safe, and it has six greys. Plan 9's map takes a
 * smaller cube, 64 hues, and gives each four levels of brightness,
 * because the eye tells two brightnesses apart much better than two
 * hues: a photograph reduced to it keeps its shading. The reasoning
 * is in the manual's color(6).
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * The loop repaints in one case only, a resize. A window covered and
 * uncovered needs nothing from the program: rio keeps each window's
 * pixels and puts them back itself. Under X a program is sent an
 * event for every part of its window that comes back into view and
 * must draw it again, so every program has that code; here the
 * resize is the one case left, and comes as one more thing read
 * from the mouse. *)

type caps = < Cap.draw; Cap.mouse; Cap.fork; Cap.stderr >

(* Plan 9's colour map (libdraw's cmap2rgb): a colour's number is two
 * bits of red, two of "value" (how bright), and four that are green
 * and blue once the first two are taken from them; the brightest of
 * the three is given the value, the others in proportion *)
let cmap2rgb c =
  let r = c lsr 6 and v = (c lsr 4) land 3 in
  let j = (c - v + r) land 15 in
  let g = j lsr 2 and b = j land 3 in
  let den = max r (max g b) in
  if den = 0 then v * 17, v * 17, v * 17
  else let num = 17 * ((4 * den) + v) in r * num / den, g * num / den, b * num / den

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let ramp = ref false and hex = ref false in
  let known = List.for_all (fun a -> match a with "-r" -> ramp := true; true | "-x" -> hex := true; true | "-rx" | "-xr" -> ramp := true; hex := true; true | _ -> false)
      (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) in
  if not known then begin Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "Usage: %s [-rx]\n" argv.(0)); Exit.Err "usage" end
  else begin
    let display = Display.init caps in
    let font = Font.default display and mouse = Mouse.init caps in
    let white = Display.color display Display.white and black = Display.color display Display.black in
    let rgb i = if !ramp then i, i, i else cmap2rgb i in
    let colors = Array.init 256 (fun i -> let r, g, b = rgb i in Display.color display (Display.rgb r g b)) in
    (* the squares: 16 rows of 16 under a line for the text, 5 pixels in, a pixel between two *)
    let square (view : Display.image) i : Rectangle.t =
      let r : Rectangle.t = Rectangle.inset view.r 5 in
      let top = r.min.y + 20 in
      let k = 255 - i in
      let x = k mod 16 and y = k / 16 in
      let at_x n = r.min.x + ((r.max.x - r.min.x) * n / 16) and at_y n = top + ((r.max.y - top) * n / 16) in
      Rectangle.inset (Rectangle.v (at_x x) (at_y y) (at_x (x + 1)) (at_y (y + 1))) 1 in
    let paint (view : Display.image) =
      Draw.fill view view.r white;
      Array.iteri (fun i c -> Draw.fill view (square view i) c) colors;
      Display.flush display in
    let say (view : Display.image) i =
      let cr, cg, cb = rgb i in
      let text =
        if !hex then Printf.sprintf "index %2X r %3X g %3X b %3X 0x%02X%02X%02XFF       " i cr cg cb cr cg cb
        else Printf.sprintf "index %3d r %3d g %3d b %3d 0x%02X%02X%02XFF        " i cr cg cb cr cg cb in
      let p : Point.t = Point.add view.r.min (Point.v 2 2) in
      Draw.fill view (Rectangle.v p.x p.y (p.x + Font.width font text) (p.y + Font.height font)) white;
      ignore (Font.string view p black font text);
      Display.flush display in
    let rec loop view shown =
      let m : Mouse.state = Event.sync (Mouse.receive mouse) in
      (* its window moved or made another size: the squares again, in the new one *)
      if m.resized then begin let view = Display.screen display in paint view; loop view None end
      else if m.buttons = 1 then begin
        let rec find i = if i = 256 then None else if Rectangle.contains (square view i) m.pos then Some i else find (i + 1) in
        match find 0 with
        | Some i when Some i <> shown -> say view i; loop view (Some i)
        | _ -> loop view shown
      end
      else if m.buttons = 4 then (match Menu.hit view font mouse 4 [ "exit" ] 0 m.pos with Some _ -> () | None -> loop view shown)
      else loop view shown in
    let view = Display.screen display in
    paint view;
    loop view None;
    Exit.OK
  end

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
apps/music/rebirth/Patch_text.ml
