let tile i : Widget.box = { Widget.x = -360. +. (float_of_int i *. 180.); y = 30.; w = 150.; h = 180. }

let text_keys computer m =
  let k = computer.keyboard in
  let now = Set_.elements k.keys in
  let pressed key = List.mem key now && not (List.mem key m.was) in
  let d = doc m in
  match current_text d with
  | None -> m
  | Some r ->
      let text = Rich.to_string r and c = Rich.caret r in
      let move to_ = { m with history = Undo.amend (edit_text (Rich.at to_) m) m.history; run = false } in
      if k.typed <> "" then a_run ~name:"Typing" (edit_text (Rich.insert k.typed) m) m
      else if pressed "Enter" then a_run ~name:"Typing" (edit_text (Rich.insert "\n") m) m
      else if pressed "Backspace" then a_run ~name:"Typing" (edit_text Rich.delete_backward m) m
      else if pressed "ArrowLeft" then move (Text.prev_char text c)
      else if pressed "ArrowRight" then move (Text.next_char text c)
      else m

(* the mouse went down on the page, not on the object being edited *)
let press m (mx, my) =
  let d = doc m in
  let m = { m with pressed_at = (mx, my); again = false; run = false } in
  match Option.bind m.selected (fun i -> Option.map (fun c -> (i, c)) (corner_at d i (mx, my))) with
  | Some (_, c) when m.editing = None -> { m with drag = Some (Resizing c); live = Some d }
  | _ -> (
      match object_at d (mx, my) with
      | Some i ->
          let m = put_down m in
          let d = doc m in
          let o = List.nth (placed d) i in
          let b = obj_box d o in
          {
            m with
            again = m.selected = Some i;
            selected = Some i;
            drag = Some (Moving (mx -. Widget.left b, Widget.top b -. my));
            live = Some d;
          }
      | None -> (
          let m = { (put_down m) with selected = None } in
          let d = doc m in
          (* in a text, the caret goes where the click was *)
          match layout d with
          | Some (_, page) ->
              let px, py = to_page d (mx, my) in
              (* in a document's top or bottom margin: its header or its
                 footer, on the page clicked *)
              let k = int_of_float (Float.max 0. (py /. pitch d.kind)) in
              let y = py -. (float_of_int k *. pitch d.kind) in
              let area =
                if d.kind <> Document then Body
                else if y < margin then Header k
                else if y > snd (page_size d.kind) -. margin then Footer k
                else Body
              in
              let d = { d with area } in
              let o =
                match area with
                | Body -> Page.offset_at page (px -. margin, py -. margin)
                | Header _ -> Page.offset_at (band_layout d Head d.header) (px -. margin, y -. band_top d Head)
                | Footer _ -> Page.offset_at (band_layout d Foot d.footer) (px -. margin, y -. band_top d Foot)
              in
              let m = { m with history = Undo.amend d m.history } in
              { m with history = Undo.amend (edit_text (Rich.at o) m) m.history }
          | None -> m))

let dragging m (mx, my) =
  let base = Undo.now m.history in
  match (m.drag, m.selected) with
  | Some (Moving (gx, gy)), Some i ->
      let x, y = to_page base (mx -. gx, my +. gy) in
      let o = List.nth base.objects i in
      { m with live = Some (place base i ~x ~y ~w:o.w ~h:o.h) }
  | Some (Resizing c), Some i ->
      let o = List.nth (placed base) i in
      let px, py = to_page base (mx, my) in
      (* the opposite corner stays where it is *)
      let ax = if c = 0 || c = 3 then o.x +. o.w else o.x and ay = if c = 0 || c = 1 then o.y +. o.h else o.y in
      let x = Float.min ax px and y = Float.min ay py in
      let w = Float.max 30. (Float.abs (px -. ax)) and h = Float.max 30. (Float.abs (py -. ay)) in
      { m with live = Some (place base i ~x ~y ~w ~h) }
  | _ -> m

let release m (mx, my) =
  let before = Undo.now m.history in
  let boxes d = List.map (fun o -> (o.x, o.y, o.w, o.h)) d.objects in
  let moved = Float.abs (mx -. fst m.pressed_at) +. Float.abs (my -. snd m.pressed_at) > 3. in
  let m =
    match (m.drag, m.live) with
    (* a click on the object already selected, with no drag: edit it
       where it is *)
    | Some (Moving _), _ when m.again && not moved -> { m with editing = Some before; live = None }
    | Some drag, Some l when boxes l <> boxes before ->
        (* an object tied to a paragraph and moved is tied to the one
           it now stands beside *)
        let l = match (drag, m.selected) with Moving _, Some i when (List.nth l.objects i).anchor <> None -> tie l i | _ -> l in
        { (record ~name:(match drag with Moving _ -> "Move" | Resizing _ -> "Resize") l m) with live = None }
    | _ -> { m with live = None }
  in
  { m with drag = None }

(* the pages scrolled by dy, no further than the first page's top and
   the last page's *)
let scrolled dy m =
  let d = doc m in
  let scroll = Float.max 0. (Float.min (float_of_int (pages d - 1) *. pitch d.kind) (d.scroll +. dy)) in
  if d.kind <> Document || scroll = d.scroll then m else { m with history = Undo.amend { d with scroll } m.history }

(* after typing, the pages scrolled for the caret to stay in view *)
let follow m =
  let d = doc m in
  match (d.kind, layout d) with
  | Document, Some (r, page) when d.area = Body ->
      let _, baseline, h = Page.caret_at page (Rich.caret r) in
      let y = snd (origin d) -. margin -. baseline in
      if y < -420. then scrolled (-420. -. y) m else if y +. h > 440. then scrolled (440. -. y -. h) m else m
  | _ -> m

let reopened (r : saved File_menu.result) model =
  match r with
  | File_menu.Nothing -> model
  | File_menu.New -> { initial with start = true; file = model.file }
  | File_menu.Opened d -> { initial with start = false; history = Undo.start ~limit:100 (of_saved d); file = model.file }
  (* ix: Insert > Image...'s file *)
  | File_menu.Chosen (name, bytes) -> (
      try insert_image bytes model with Failure why -> { model with file = File_menu.say (name ^ ": " ^ why) model.file })

(* where the start screen's Open... is *)
let open_button : Widget.box = { Widget.x = 0.; y = -220.; w = 140.; h = 36. }

let update caps ~(exported : model -> string) computer model =
  let mouse = computer.mouse in
  let now = Set_.elements computer.keyboard.keys in
  let current () = to_saved (doc (put_down model)) in
  if File_menu.busy model.file then
    let file, r = File_menu.dialog caps Document.file_kind computer ~current model.file in
    reopened r { model with file; was = now; was_down = mouse.mdown }
  else
  let pressed key = List.mem key now && not (List.mem key model.was) in
  let press_edge = mouse.mdown && not model.was_down in
  let model =
    if model.start then
      (* the start screen: the kinds, as tiles -- or a document saved
         before *)
      if Gui.button_in ~enabled:true computer open_button "Open..." then
        let file, r = File_menu.command caps Document.file_kind ~current "Open..." model.file in
        reopened r { model with file }
      else
      match List.find_opt (fun (i, _) -> press_edge && Widget.contains (tile i) mouse.mx mouse.my) (List.mapi (fun i k -> (i, k)) kinds) with
      | Some (_, k) -> { initial with start = false; history = Undo.start ~limit:100 (fresh k); file = File_menu.start }
      | None -> model
    else if model.show then
      (* the show: a click or the keys on to the next slide, past the
         last back to editing *)
      let d = doc model in
      let go dir =
        let slide = d.slide + dir in
        match d.body with
        | Texts ts when slide >= 0 && slide < List.length ts -> { model with history = Undo.amend { d with slide } model.history }
        | _ when dir > 0 -> { model with show = false }
        | _ -> model
      in
      if pressed "Escape" then { model with show = false }
      else if mouse.mclick || pressed "ArrowRight" || pressed " " || pressed "PageDown" then go 1
      else if pressed "ArrowLeft" || pressed "PageUp" then go (-1)
      else model
    else
      let model =
        List.fold_left
          (fun model (i, items) ->
            if i = 0 then
              (* ix: Export is a PDF of the pages (docs/plans/done/plan_pdf.md),
                 where the playground's menu writes the document as
                 Save does; the menu's other items are File_menu's *)
              let item = List.nth File_menu.items (Gui.menu_in computer (menu_box i) File_menu.items 0) in
              if item = "Export" then { model with file = File_menu.export caps ~extension:".pdf" (exported (put_down model)) model.file }
              else if item = "File" then model
              else
              let file, r = File_menu.command caps Document.file_kind ~current item model.file in
              reopened r { model with file }
            else
            match List.nth_opt items (Gui.menu_in computer (menu_box i) items 0) with
            (* ix: a file to choose: the File menu's dialog, and its
               capabilities, which a command has not *)
            | Some "Image..." -> { model with file = File_menu.choose caps ~extensions:Image_file.extensions model.file }
            | Some c when c <> List.hd items -> command ~menu:(List.hd items) c model
            | _ -> model)
          model
          (List.mapi (fun i items -> (i, items)) (menus model))
      in
      if Gui.modal () then model
      else
        let d = doc model in
        let p = (mouse.mx, mouse.my) in
        let in_active =
          match (model.editing, model.selected) with
          | Some _, Some i -> ( match List.nth_opt (placed d) i with Some o -> Widget.contains (obj_box d o) mouse.mx mouse.my | None -> false)
          | _ -> false
        in
        let model =
          match model.drag with
          | Some _ when mouse.mdown -> dragging model p
          | Some _ -> release model p
          (* a press on the menu bar is the menu's, not the page's under it *)
          | None when press_edge && (not in_active) && mouse.my < Widget.bottom (menu_box 0) -> press model p
          | None -> model
        in
        let d = doc model in
        (* who gets the mouse and the keys: the object edited in place,
           or else -- no object selected -- the document's own content *)
        let model =
          match (model.editing, model.selected, d.body) with
          | Some d, Some i, _ -> (
              match List.nth_opt (placed d) i with
              | Some o ->
                  let part = Component.input_in ~scaled:o.scaled o.part computer (obj_box d o) in
                  let model = { model with editing = Some (set_obj i (fun o -> { o with part }) d) } in
                  if pressed "Escape" then put_down model else model
              | None -> model)
          | None, Some _, _ ->
              if pressed "Backspace" || pressed "Delete" then command ~menu:"Edit" "Delete" model
              else if pressed "Escape" then { model with selected = None }
              else model
          | None, None, Main p when model.drag = None ->
              let p' = p.input computer (main_box d p) in
              if p'.save () <> p.save () then a_run ~name:"Edit" { d with body = Main p' } model
              else { model with history = Undo.amend { d with body = Main p' } model.history }
          | None, None, Texts _ ->
              let model' = text_keys computer model in
              if model' != model then follow model' else model
          | _ -> model
        in
        (* the wheel, and the page keys, scroll a document's pages *)
        if model.editing <> None || model.drag <> None then model
        else if mouse.mwheel <> 0. then scrolled (-.mouse.mwheel *. 60.) model
        else if pressed "PageDown" then scrolled 700. model
        else if pressed "PageUp" then scrolled (-700.) model
        else model
  in
  { model with was = now; was_down = mouse.mdown }
apps/office/suite/Office_update.mli
3175
(* mini-office's update: a frame's mouse and keys given to the start
 * screen, the File menu's dialog, the menus, the object edited in
 * place, the page.
 *
 * Who gets a frame's input, in the order the code asks. The first
 * that applies takes the frame; inside the last, each line is tried
 * in turn:
 *
 *   a File dialog is up     File_menu.dialog, and nothing else
 *   the start screen        its Open..., its five tiles
 *   the show                next slide, the one before, Escape
 *   a page being edited:
 *     the menu bar          Gui.menu_in for each menu; an item chosen
 *                           is Office_edit.command, or File_menu's.
 *                           A menu open stops here (Gui.modal)
 *     the mouse on the page a drag going on; its release; or a press:
 *                           on a corner of the selected object (it is
 *                           resized), on an object (selected, moved),
 *                           on the text (the caret goes there), in a
 *                           page's margin (its header or footer)
 *     the keys, and the     to the object edited in place
 *     mouse again           (Component.input_in), or the object
 *                           selected (Delete, Escape), or the main
 *                           part, or the text (typing)
 *     the wheel, the        the pages scrolled
 *     page keys
 *
 * An object's three states are made of two clicks: a press selects
 * it and may drag it; a press and release without moving, on the one
 * already selected, starts editing it in place, the menu bar then its
 * own; Escape, or a press elsewhere, puts it down. Editing in place
 * is nothing but the line above: the part is given the computer and
 * its box, and answers with the part it has become.
 *
 * It is one function from the model to the model, with no effect but
 * the File menu's, which is why the capabilities come this far and
 * no further: the parts and the kits are given none, and cannot
 * reach a file.
 *
 * design:
 * There is no event, no handler and no table of which widget has
 * the focus. Routing is the order of the tests above, read top to
 * bottom, and a modal state is a test near the top. It is the
 * simplest thing that works and it is honest about its cost: every
 * new way to take the mouse is a new line in this one function,
 * which must be put at the right height. A retained toolkit moves
 * that knowledge into a tree of widgets and the rules for walking
 * it (Retained.mli; the browser's events, which go down the tree
 * and bubble back up). *)

(* where the start screen's five kinds and its Open... are (the view's too) *)
val tile : int -> Widget.box

val open_button : Widget.box

(* a frame: the computer's mouse and keys, the model after them. The
   capabilities are the File menu's: a document stored, fetched, the
   store listed. [exported]: the document as the bytes Export writes
   (Office_export.pdf: given, the view's shapes being what it writes
   and the view coming after this) *)
val update : File_menu.caps -> exported:(Office_model.model -> string) -> Playground.computer -> Office_model.model -> Office_model.model

let kind_icon k (b : Widget.box) =
  let at dx dy s = s |> move (b.x +. dx) (b.y +. dy) in
  let ink = rgb 60 60 70 in
  match k with
  | Document -> List.init 6 (fun i -> at 0. (40. -. (float_of_int i *. 14.)) (rectangle ink (if i = 5 then 50. else 80.) 4.))
  | Spreadsheet ->
      List.init 5 (fun i -> at 0. (40. -. (float_of_int i *. 18.)) (rectangle ink 90. 2.))
      @ List.init 4 (fun i -> at (-45. +. (float_of_int i *. 30.)) 4. (rectangle ink 2. 74.))
  | Presentation -> [ at 0. 10. (rectangle ink 96. 66.); at 0. 10. (rectangle white 90. 60.); at 0. 30. (rectangle ink 60. 6.); at 0. 4. (rectangle ink 40. 4.) ]
  | Picture -> [ at 0. 10. (rectangle ink 90. 70.); at 0. 10. (rectangle white 84. 64.); at 20. 25. (circle (rgb 120 120 120) 10.); at 0. (-12.) (rectangle ink 84. 3.) ]
  | Drawing_doc -> [ at (-20.) 20. (rectangle ink 40. 30.); at 25. 0. (oval (rgb 150 150 150) 40. 30.); at 0. 10. (rectangle ink 30. 2. |> rotate 30.) ]

let start_view model =
  [ rectangle (rgb 235 236 240) 1000. 1000.; words (rgb 30 30 40) "TinyOffice" |> scale 2.5 |> move 0. 260.; words (rgb 100 100 110) "What would you like to make?" |> move 0. 190. ]
  @ List.concat
      (List.mapi
         (fun i k ->
           let b = tile i in
           [ rectangle (rgb 200 200 205) (b.w +. 4.) (b.h +. 4.) |> move (b.x +. 3.) (b.y -. 3.); rectangle white b.w b.h |> move b.x b.y ]
           @ kind_icon k b
           @ [ words (rgb 40 40 50) (name k) |> move b.x (b.y -. 70.) ])
         kinds)
  @ [ words (rgb 120 120 130) "each kind can hold the others: a sheet in a document, a drawing on a sheet, a picture on a slide" |> move 0. (-150.) ]
  @ [ words (rgb 60 60 70) (File_menu.said model.file) |> move 0. (-280.) ]
  @ File_menu.view model.file
  @ Gui.draw ()

let glyphs_at_simple ink page ~x ~y =
  List.concat_map
    (fun (g : Page.glyph) ->
      if g.text = "\n" || g.text = " " then [] else Stroke_text.glyph ink g.style g.text ~x:(x +. g.x) ~baseline:(y -. g.baseline))
    (Page.glyphs page)

(* Optimization (Opti.enabled; ix's): a page's letters as shapes, kept
   while the same page is asked for in the same ink at the same place
   (Office_page says why). They are 8,000 shapes of a page of text,
   and they are one shape, a group, the same one given again: a
   platform that asks whether a frame is the last one does not look
   into it, and the view does not copy 8,000 places of a list to put
   the rest after them (on mini-9pi under QEMU a frame of a page
   nobody touches, the mouse moving over it, was 11 ms of view and 30
   of the platform's comparison, the processor never idle, and the
   mouse's own process waited for it: the author, 2026-10-09, "it is
   still very slow; just moving the cursor is slow"). *)
let glyphs_at : Playground.color -> Page.t -> x:float -> y:float -> Playground.shape list =
  let last : (Playground.color * Page.t * float * float * Playground.shape list) option ref = ref None in
  fun (ink : Playground.color) (page : Page.t) ~(x : float) ~(y : float) ->
    match !last with
    | Some (ink', page', x', y', shapes) when page' == page && ink' = ink && x' = x && y' = y && !Opti.enabled -> shapes
    | _ ->
        let shapes = glyphs_at_simple ink page ~x ~y in
        (* (the bands' few letters do not take the body's place)
         * old: the letters themselves, not their group:
         *   if List.length shapes > 200 then last := Some (ink, page, x, y, shapes); shapes *)
        if List.length shapes > 200 && !Opti.enabled then begin
          let shapes = [ Playground.group shapes ] in
          last := Some (ink, page, x, y, shapes);
          shapes
        end
        else shapes

let caret_at ink page offset ~x ~y =
  let cx, baseline, h = Page.caret_at page offset in
  [ rectangle ink 2. (h *. 0.8) |> move (x +. cx) (y -. baseline +. (h *. 0.25)) ]

(* what is on the pages: the main part, the text, the header and
   footer of every page, and the objects -- with [~chrome] the caret and
   the selection too, without them for the show *)
let page_shapes ~chrome (d : doc) model =
  let pw, _ = page_size d.kind in
  let l, t = origin d in
  let ink = rgb 20 20 20 and dim = rgb 150 150 150 in
  let text =
    match layout d with
    | Some (r, page) ->
        (* the body dimmed while the header or footer is edited, as
           Word does *)
        glyphs_at (if d.area = Body then ink else dim) page ~x:(l +. margin) ~y:(t -. margin)
        @ if chrome && model.selected = None && d.area = Body then caret_at ink page (Rich.caret r) ~x:(l +. margin) ~y:(t -. margin) else []
    | None -> []
  in
  let n = pages d in
  let bands =
    if d.kind <> Document then []
    else
      List.concat
        (List.init n (fun k ->
             let top = t -. (float_of_int k *. pitch d.kind) in
             List.concat_map
               (fun (which, r, here) ->
                 let shown = if here then r else with_fields ~page:(k + 1) ~pages:n r in
                 let page = band_layout d which shown in
                 let y = top -. band_top d which in
                 let edge = if which = Head then top -. margin +. 4. else top -. snd (page_size d.kind) +. margin -. 4. in
                 glyphs_at (if here then ink else rgb 110 110 110) page ~x:(l +. margin) ~y
                 @
                 if here && chrome then
                   (* where the header ends, or the footer starts *)
                   [ rectangle (rgb 40 90 200) (pw -. (2. *. margin)) 1. |> move (l +. (pw /. 2.)) edge ]
                   @ caret_at ink page (Rich.caret r) ~x:(l +. margin) ~y
                 else [])
               [ (Head, d.header, d.area = Header k); (Foot, d.footer, d.area = Footer k) ]))
  in
  let main = match d.body with Main p -> Component.draw_in ~scaled:false p (main_box d p) ~active:(chrome && model.selected = None) | Texts _ -> [] in
  let objects =
    List.concat
      (List.mapi
         (fun i o ->
           if not (on_slide d o) then []
           else
             let b = obj_box d o in
             let selected = chrome && model.selected = Some i in
             let active = selected && model.editing <> None in
             let frame =
               if active then Gui.shapes (Widget.frame (rgb 90 90 90) 4. { b with w = b.w +. 10.; h = b.h +. 10. })
               else if selected then
                 Gui.shapes (Widget.frame (rgb 40 90 200) 1. b) @ List.map (fun (x, y) -> rectangle (rgb 40 90 200) 9. 9. |> move x y) (corners b)
               else []
             in
             (* an object in front of the text keeps its page's white
                from hiding the lines under it *)
             (if o.wrap = In_front then [] else [ rectangle white b.w b.h |> move b.x b.y ])
             @ Component.draw_in ~scaled:o.scaled o.part b ~active @ frame)
         (placed d))
  in
  main @ text @ bands @ objects

(* the show: the slide scaled to fill the screen's width, on black *)
let show_view (d : doc) model =
  let pw, ph = page_size d.kind in
  let l, t = origin d in
  let k = 1000. /. pw in
  let slide = (rectangle white pw ph |> move (l +. (pw /. 2.)) (t -. (ph /. 2.))) :: page_shapes ~chrome:false d model in
  [ rectangle black 1000. 1000.; group [ group slide |> move (-.(l +. (pw /. 2.))) (-.(t -. (ph /. 2.))) ] |> scale k ]

let view _computer model =
  if model.start then start_view model
  else
    let d = doc model in
    if model.show then show_view d model
    else
    let pw, ph = page_size d.kind in
    let l, t = origin d in
    let n = pages d in
    let slides =
      match d.body with
      | Texts ts when d.kind = Presentation -> Printf.sprintf "     slide %d of %d" (d.slide + 1) (List.length ts)
      | _ when d.kind = Document -> Printf.sprintf "     %d page%s" n (if n > 1 then "s" else "")
      | _ -> ""
    in
    let status =
      Printf.sprintf "%s     %s%s     %s"
        (if File_menu.said model.file <> "" then File_menu.said model.file else File_menu.title model.file)
        (name d.kind) slides
        (match (model.editing, model.selected, d.area, Undo.undo_name model.history) with
        | Some _, _, _, _ -> "editing the object in place -- Escape to go back to the " ^ String.lowercase_ascii (name d.kind)
        | None, Some _, _, _ -> "selected: drag it, drag a corner, or click it again to edit it"
        | None, None, Header _, _ -> "editing the header, the same on every page -- click the page to go back"
        | None, None, Footer _, _ -> "editing the footer: {page} and {pages} are filled in by each page"
        | None, None, Body, Some u -> "Undo " ^ u
        | None, None, Body, None -> "")
    in
    let sheet k =
      let t = t -. (float_of_int k *. pitch d.kind) in
      [ rectangle (rgb 120 120 128) pw ph |> move (l +. (pw /. 2.) +. 5.) (t -. (ph /. 2.) -. 5.); rectangle white pw ph |> move (l +. (pw /. 2.)) (t -. (ph /. 2.)) ]
    in
    (rectangle (rgb 165 168 175) 1000. 1000. :: List.concat (List.init n sheet))
    @ page_shapes ~chrome:true d model
    (* the menu bar and the status line over the pages scrolled under them *)
    @ [
        rectangle (Gui.theme ()).face 1000. 48. |> move 0. 476.;
        rectangle (rgb 165 168 175) 1000. 60. |> move 0. (-470.);
        words (rgb 40 40 40) status |> move 0. (-455.);
      ]
    @ File_menu.view model.file
    @ Gui.draw ()
apps/office/suite/Office_view.mli

(* mini-office's view: the start screen, the pages with their objects,
 * a presentation's show, the menu bar and the status line.
 *
 * A function from the model to a list of shapes, back to front; what
 * is later in the list covers what is before it:
 *
 *   the desk             a grey rectangle
 *   the sheets of paper  a white rectangle a page, and its shadow
 *   [page_shapes]        the main part, or the text's letters and the
 *                        caret; each page's header and footer, their
 *                        fields filled; the objects in their order,
 *                        each on a white box (but one in front of the
 *                        text), with its frame and corners if selected
 *   the bars             the menu bar's and the status line's grounds,
 *                        over the pages scrolled under them
 *   File_menu.view       a dialog's panel, if one is up
 *   Gui.draw ()          the widgets the update asked for this frame:
 *                        the menus, a dialog's buttons and list
 *
 * Nothing is remembered of the frame before and nothing is erased:
 * the whole picture is said again at each frame, and what makes that
 * affordable is below this program: a view is data, so a platform
 * compares a frame's shapes with the last one's and draws again only
 * where they differ (Redraw). That is why a page's letters are given
 * as one group, the same value while the page is the same: one
 * comparison, not thousands.
 *
 * design:
 * [page_shapes] is written once and used three times: on the screen
 * with the caret and the selection, in the show without them and
 * scaled to the screen, and by Office_export, which writes the same
 * shapes to a PDF. So the slide shown and the page printed cannot
 * differ from the one edited: there is no second drawing code to
 * keep in step. It costs a flag, [chrome], for what belongs to the
 * editing and not to the document.
 *
 * A page's letters are shapes (Playground's Letters), not pixels: the
 * platform keeps each letter, at a size and a look, as a mask (on
 * Linux, Shape_render_software's) or as an image of the kernel's (on
 * mini-9pi, the draw platform's), and a frame lays each letter from
 * it, a message a letter on mini-9pi. The text changes as it is typed,
 * and a letter typed is one shape more, not a page drawn again.
 * mini-page does the other: a PDF's page, which does not change, drawn
 * whole in the program, its letters from the file's fonts (Pdf_render's
 * own cache of glyphs), then given to the kernel once as one picture,
 * and a frame is one copy of it (docs/notes/notes_font.md, section 2). *)

(* what is on the pages, in the screen's coordinates (Office_page's
   origin): with [chrome] the caret, the selection and an object's
   frame, without them what the show and Export (Office_export) take *)
val page_shapes : chrome:bool -> Document.doc -> Office_model.model -> Playground.shape list

val view : Playground.computer -> Office_model.model -> Playground.shape list

(* mini-page: a PDF file's pages, or a picture, looked at
 * (docs/plans/done/plan_pdf.md), after Plan 9's page(1).
 *
 * Plan 9's page is a viewer round other programs: Ghostscript draws a
 * PostScript or a PDF file's pages, jpg and png read a picture, and
 * page shows what they give it. Here the drawing is in the program:
 * lib_graphics/pdf reads the file and draws a page (Pdf_render), each
 * page is a picture, a Bitmap of Playground's, and the pages are one
 * under another, a gap of grey between, the window going along them
 * (as most viewers today; Plan 9's page shows one page, and the next
 * is a key away). No PostScript: there is no interpreter of it here.
 *
 *   file's bytes --Pdf--> pages --Pdf_render, at a zoom--> pictures
 *                                                             |
 *                     keys and mouse: which page, the         v
 *                     zoom, a turn, how far down     the window's Bitmaps
 *
 * A page is drawn when it first comes into the window at a zoom and a
 * turn; the pictures in the window are kept, and the last few others
 * (a page is megabytes): going back to the page before is at once.
 * The model is a value, as every Playground program's; a page's
 * picture is made in the update (the view only shows), which is why a
 * key that changes the page takes the time of its drawing, unless the
 * page was drawn ahead: once the window is still, the next page and
 * the one before are drawn, a page a frame (ahead). Where each page's
 * top is down the pages comes from their sizes (tops), kept at a zoom
 * and a turn: a book's thousand pages are not gone through each
 * frame.
 *
 * How a page reaches the screen. Pdf_render draws the whole page in
 * this program's memory, its letters with the rest: each glyph filled
 * once from the PDF's own font, a mask kept by its font, size and
 * quarter pixel, then laid wherever it comes again (Pdf_render's
 * cache, for the pages after too). The page is one picture, a
 * Playground Bitmap; on mini-9pi the draw platform loads it into an
 * image of the kernel's once (megabytes: 40 to 70 ms under QEMU) and
 * each frame after is one copy from it, however many letters the page
 * has. mini-office's text goes the other way (Office_view): its
 * letters are shapes, each kept as an image of the kernel's, and a
 * frame is a message a letter. That fits a text that changes as it is
 * typed, in one stroke font of a few looks; a PDF's page does not
 * change, and its text may be clipped, transparent, filled with a
 * pattern or over a picture, which Pdf_render does and the kernel's
 * device would have to: one picture, and scrolling is one message a
 * frame, not a page's three thousand letters. What it costs is the
 * moment a page is new: drawn here, then loaded, which drawing ahead
 * does while the reader reads (docs/notes/notes_font.md, section 2).
 *
 * A picture (PNG, JPEG) is a document of one page, scaled and turned
 * as it is shown, not drawn again.
 *
 * A link of a page (Pdf.links) is followed by a click: to a page of
 * the file, at the height it names, or to an address, given to
 * mini-netscape (Plan 9's page would plumb it). Over one the cursor is
 * a hand and the status line says where it leads; b goes back to
 * where the last link was followed from, as a browser's Back: a
 * book's references are a jump there and a jump back.
 *
 * A file is opened where it was left: its place (how far down, the
 * zoom, the turn) kept in a file of places, written once the window
 * has been still half a second, and on q (a window closed or Ctrl+Q
 * ends the program without a word to it: a place kept only at the end
 * would be lost). -v says which file (Logs.info).
 *
 * Not done: page's menu of the pages (a number and Enter goes to
 * one); a file's outline; text found or copied (-t prints a file's
 * words).
 *
 * Where it stands. It is the reader of what mini-office writes:
 * Office_export makes a document a PDF file (Shape_render_pdf,
 * Pdf_write) and this program shows it, so the two ends of the
 * format are in ix and the tests of the one use the other. The
 * readers of pictures are mini-office's too (Image_file, over Png
 * and Jpeg). Like mini-office it is a
 * Playground program and knows no window: Colors (apps/misc) is the
 * other kind, a program that talks to the draw device itself.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * PostScript (Adobe, 1984) describes a page by a program: a
 * language with loops and procedures whose running draws, which is
 * why showing page 300 means running the 299 before it, and why a
 * viewer of it is an interpreter. PDF (Adobe, 1993) kept
 * PostScript's way of drawing and dropped the language: each page a
 * plain list of operators, the pages found by a table at the end of
 * the file, so that any page can be shown first (Pdf_render.mli,
 * Pdf_write.mli). Plan 9's page handed both to Ghostscript, a
 * PostScript interpreter that also reads PDF; with PDF alone the
 * interpreter is not needed, and the whole reader fits in a
 * library.
 *
 * References: page(1). ISO 32000-1:2008, the PDF 1.7 reference.
 * docs/plans/done/plan_pdf.md. *)

let usage =
  "usage: mini-page file            a PDF file or a picture (PNG, JPEG) in a window\n\
  \       mini-page -v file         and says where it keeps the files' places\n\
  \       mini-page places=off file not where it was left (places=FILE: another)\n\
  \       mini-page -t file         the words of each page, printed\n\
  \       mini-page -ppm n file out page n to out (a PPM), a pixel a point\n\
   in the window:\n\
  \  space, PageDown, right        the next page\n\
  \  Backspace, PageUp, left       the page before\n\
  \  a number, then Enter          that page\n\
  \  up, down, the wheel           the pages moved along\n\
  \  the mouse's button held       drags them\n\
  \  a link, clicked               followed: a page; an address, in mini-netscape\n\
  \  b                             back to where the last link was followed from\n\
  \  + and -                       larger, smaller;  f  the window's width again\n\
  \  r                             a quarter turn;   q  the end\n"

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A document *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type source =
  | Pages of Pdf.t * Pdf_render.cache * Pdf.page array
  | Picture of Rgba_image.t
  (* why not, shown in the window *)
  | Nothing of string

(* a file by its first bytes *)
let source (bytes : string) : source =
  try
    if Pdf.sniff bytes then
      let pdf = Pdf.of_string bytes in
      Pages (pdf, Pdf_render.cache (), Array.of_list (Pdf.pages pdf))
    else if Image_file.known bytes then Picture (Image_file.decode bytes)
    else Nothing "neither a PDF file nor a picture (PNG, JPEG)"
  with Failure why -> Nothing why

let count (s : source) : int = match s with Pages (_, _, pages) -> Array.length pages | Picture _ | Nothing _ -> 1

(* a page's size in points (a picture's: its pixels), turned *)
let size (s : source) (page : int) (turn : int) : float * float =
  let w, h =
    match s with
    | Pages (_, _, pages) -> Pdf_render.size pages.(page)
    | Picture img -> (float img.width, float img.height)
    | Nothing _ -> (1., 1.)
  in
  if turn mod 2 = 1 then (h, w) else (w, h)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The model *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a file's place: how far down its pages at a zoom of 1 (the pages'
 * heights are a zoom's multiple), the zoom, the turn. A zoom of 0: as
 * wide as the window, whatever its width when the file is opened
 * again (a zoom kept as a number, fitted to a window made larger,
 * opened the page too large for the next one) *)
type place = float * float * int

(* a picture kept: of which page, at which zoom (in thousandths) and
 * turn; and the page's links, read with it (a book's named
 * destinations are a tree of objects to walk: not each frame) *)
type kept = {
  page : int;
  zoom : int;
  turn : int;
  image : Rgba_image.t;
  links : Pdf.link list;
}

type model = {
  name : string;
  source : source;
  (* from 0: the one gone to, or at the window's middle once moved along *)
  page : int;
  zoom : float; (* pixels a point *)
  (* the window's width the zoom fits (f), if it does: fitted again
   * when the window changes (the platform's window known after the
   * start, a window made larger) *)
  fitted : float option;
  (* the window's width at the last frame, and for how many frames it
   * has been the same: fitted again once the window is left alone *)
  seen : float * int;
  turn : int; (* quarter turns, clockwise: 0 to 3 *)
  (* the pages one under another: how far down them the window's top
   * is, in pixels, and where their middle is across the window *)
  down : float;
  x : float;
  (* the pictures drawn, those in the window first *)
  kept : kept list;
  (* a page's number being typed *)
  number : string;
  (* where links were followed from: a page and how far down, at a
   * zoom of 1 (the pages' heights are a zoom's multiple) *)
  back : (int * float) list;
  (* the frame before: the keys held, where the mouse held the pages,
   * where its button went down (a click there, not a drag, follows a
   * link), and whether the cursor is a hand *)
  was : string list;
  held : (float * float) option;
  pressed : float * float;
  hand : bool;
  (* the place of the frame before, for how many frames it has not
   * changed, and the one kept last in the file of places *)
  place : place;
  still : int;
  saved : place;
  remember : place -> unit;
  quit : unit -> unit;
  (* an address shown, by another program *)
  open_url : string -> unit;
  (* the last view and what it was made from: the same shapes again,
   * the very value, when nothing changed, which the platform then
   * does not show again (draw's show: [==] at once; a new list was
   * compared to the last one down to the pages' pixels, and every
   * frame was shown again, 155 ms a frame under QEMU) *)
  last : (view_key * Playground.shape list) option ref;
  (* the pages' tops (tops) at a zoom and a turn: a book's thousand
   * pages were gone through several times a frame, 65 ms of each under
   * QEMU (principia's Kernel, 1083 pages) *)
  tops : (float * int * float array) option ref;
}

(* the status line, down, across, the zoom, the turn, the screen's size,
 * the pictures kept *)
and view_key =
  string * float * float * float * int * float * float
  * (int * int * int) list

(* pictures kept besides the window's *)
let keep = 3

let thousandths (zoom : float) : int =
  int_of_float (Float.round (zoom *. 1000.))

(* points between two pages, and above the first and below the last *)
let gap = 8.

(* where each page's top is down the pages, in pixels; the last of the
 * array is their whole height *)
let tops (m : model) : float array =
  match !(m.tops) with
  | Some (zoom, turn, a) when zoom = m.zoom && turn = m.turn -> a
  | _ ->
      let n = count m.source in
      let a = Array.make (n + 1) (gap *. m.zoom) in
      for i = 0 to n - 1 do
        let _, h = size m.source i m.turn in
        a.(i + 1) <- a.(i) +. ((h +. gap) *. m.zoom)
      done;
      m.tops := Some (m.zoom, m.turn, a);
      a

(* the window's height above the status line *)
let status_line = 30.
let room (s : Playground.screen) : float = s.height -. status_line

(* the pages in the window *)
let shown (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) : int list =
  let tops = tops m in
  let inside (i : int) =
    tops.(i + 1) -. (gap *. m.zoom) > m.down && tops.(i) < m.down +. room s
  in
  List.filter inside (List.init (count m.source) (fun (i : int) -> i))

(* the page at the window's middle *)
let middle (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) : int =
  let tops = tops m and at = m.down +. (room s /. 2.) in
  let rec find (i : int) : int =
    if i + 1 < count m.source && tops.(i + 1) <= at then find (i + 1) else i
  in
  find 0

(* the window within the pages: not past their ends; pages shorter
 * than the window in its middle *)
let within (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) : model =
  let total = (tops m).(count m.source) and room = room s in
  let down =
    if total <= room then (total -. room) /. 2.
    else Float.max 0. (Float.min m.down (total -. room))
  in
  { m with down }

(* the window's pages' pictures, drawn if they are not kept. A PDF's
 * page is drawn at the zoom and turned by the reader (sharp at any
 * size); a picture is kept as it is, and the view scales and turns it *)
(* a page's picture kept: at the model's zoom and turn *)
let is (m : model) (i : int) (k : kept) : bool =
  k.page = i && k.zoom = thousandths m.zoom && k.turn = m.turn

(* a page's picture drawn, and its links read *)
let draw (pdf : Pdf.t) (cache : Pdf_render.cache) (pages : Pdf.page array)
    (m : model) (i : int) : kept =
  Logs.debug (fun f -> f "page %d drawn at %d%%" (i + 1) (thousandths m.zoom / 10));
  let p = pages.(i) in
  let p = { p with rotate = (p.rotate + (90 * m.turn)) mod 360 } in
  let image =
    Pdf_render.render ~options:Pdf_render.full ~stroke_glyph:Pdf_render.hershey
      pdf cache p ~scale:m.zoom
  in
  { page = i; zoom = thousandths m.zoom; turn = m.turn; image;
    links = Pdf.links pdf pages p }

let drawn (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) : model =
  match m.source with
  | Pages (pdf, cache, pages) ->
      let is = is m and draw = draw pdf cache pages m in
      let shown = shown s m in
      let now =
        List.map
          (fun (i : int) ->
            match List.find_opt (is i) m.kept with
            | Some k -> k
            | None -> draw i)
          shown
      in
      let others =
        List.filter
          (fun (k : kept) -> not (List.exists (fun (i : int) -> is i k) shown))
          m.kept
      in
      let others = List.filteri (fun (i : int) (_ : kept) -> i < keep) others in
      { m with kept = now @ others }
  | Picture _ | Nothing _ -> m

(* A page drawn ahead while the window is still: the one after the
 * window's last, then the one before its first, a page a frame, kept
 * first among the others. Under QEMU on mini-9pi a page of a book is
 * seconds to draw, and the scrolling stopped at each new one (the
 * author: "scrolling with the mousewheel still feel very sluggish",
 * then "looks like rendering the next page while idle might help").
 * A key pressed meanwhile waits for it *)
let ahead (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) : model =
  match (m.source, shown s m) with
  | Pages (pdf, cache, pages), (first :: _ as shown) ->
      let last = List.fold_left max first shown in
      let wanted (i : int) =
        i >= 0 && i < Array.length pages
        && not (List.exists (is m i) m.kept)
      in
      (match List.find_opt wanted [ last + 1; first - 1 ] with
       | Some i ->
           let now, others =
             List.partition
               (fun (k : kept) -> List.exists (fun (j : int) -> is m j k) shown)
               m.kept
           in
           { m with kept = now @ (draw pdf cache pages m i :: others) }
       | None -> m)
  | _ -> m

(* another page, its top at the window's *)
let go (page : int) (m : model) : model =
  let page = max 0 (min (count m.source - 1) page) in
  { m with page; down = (tops m).(page) -. (gap *. m.zoom) }

(* the page as wide as the window, less a margin each side (a picture:
 * no larger than it is; no page: as it is), from its top *)
let fit_zoom (width : float) (m : model) : float =
  let w, _ = size m.source m.page m.turn in
  let zoom = (width -. 40.) /. w in
  match m.source with
  | Picture _ -> Float.min 1. zoom
  | Nothing _ -> 1.
  | Pages _ -> zoom

let fit (width : float) (m : model) : model =
  go m.page { m with zoom = fit_zoom width m; fitted = Some width; x = 0. }

let place_of (m : model) : place =
  (m.down /. m.zoom, (if m.fitted = None then m.zoom else 0.), m.turn)

(* the file's pages, at the place it was left if one is kept *)
let start (name : string) (bytes : string) ~(was : place option)
    ~(remember : place -> unit) ~(quit : unit -> unit)
    ~(open_url : string -> unit) : model =
  let s =
    Playground.to_screen Playground.default_width Playground.default_height
  in
  let m =
    { name; source = source bytes; page = 0; zoom = 1.; fitted = None;
      seen = (-1., 0); turn = 0; down = 0.; x = 0.; kept = []; number = "";
      back = [];
      was = []; held = None; pressed = (0., 0.); hand = false;
      place = (0., 1., 0); still = 0; saved = (0., 1., 0); remember; quit;
      open_url; last = ref None; tops = ref None }
  in
  let m = within s (fit s.width m) in
  let m =
    match was with
    | Some (down, zoom, turn)
      when zoom >= 0.1 && zoom <= 8. && turn >= 0 && turn < 4 ->
        let m =
          within s { m with zoom; fitted = None; turn; down = down *. zoom }
        in
        { m with page = middle s m }
    | Some (down, zoom, turn) when zoom = 0. && turn >= 0 && turn < 4 ->
        let m = fit s.width { m with turn } in
        let m = within s { m with down = down *. m.zoom } in
        { m with page = middle s m }
    | _ -> m
  in
  { m with place = place_of m; saved = place_of m }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Links *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* how a page is turned, its own turn and ours: 0, 90, 180 or 270 *)
let turned (pages : Pdf.page array) (i : int) (m : model) : int =
  (pages.(i).rotate + (90 * m.turn)) mod 360

(* the link under a point of the window, if a page's picture is there *)
let link_at (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) ((px, py) : float * float) :
    Pdf.target option =
  match m.source with
  | Pages (_, _, pages) ->
      let tops = tops m and zoom = thousandths m.zoom in
      let on (i : int) : Pdf.target option =
        let _, h = size m.source i m.turn in
        let y = s.top -. (tops.(i) +. (h *. m.zoom /. 2.) -. m.down) in
        (* from the page's middle, in points, y up; turned back *)
        let dx = (px -. m.x) /. m.zoom and dy = (py -. y) /. m.zoom in
        let a, b =
          match turned pages i m with
          | 90 -> (-.dy, dx)
          | 180 -> (-.dx, -.dy)
          | 270 -> (dy, -.dx)
          | _ -> (dx, dy)
        in
        let x0, y0, x1, y1 = pages.(i).box in
        let u = ((x0 +. x1) /. 2.) +. a and v = ((y0 +. y1) /. 2.) +. b in
        let inside ((l : Pdf.link)) =
          let lx0, ly0, lx1, ly1 = l.rect in
          lx0 <= u && u <= lx1 && ly0 <= v && v <= ly1
        in
        match
          List.find_opt
            (fun (k : kept) -> k.page = i && k.zoom = zoom && k.turn = m.turn)
            m.kept
        with
        | Some k -> (
            match List.find_opt inside k.links with
            | Some l -> Some l.target
            | None -> None)
        | None -> None
      in
      List.fold_left
        (fun (found : Pdf.target option) (i : int) ->
          match found with Some _ -> found | None -> on i)
        None (shown s m)
  | Picture _ | Nothing _ -> None

(* what the status line says of a link *)
let leads (t : Pdf.target) : string =
  match t with
  | Page (i, _) -> Printf.sprintf "to page %d" (i + 1)
  | Uri u -> "to " ^ u

(* a link followed: its page, at the height it names (a page turned:
 * its top), where we were kept for b; or its address shown *)
let follow (t : Pdf.target) (m : model) : model =
  match (t, m.source) with
  | Uri u, _ -> m.open_url u; m
  | Page (i, top), Pages (_, _, pages) -> (
      let m' = go i { m with back = (m.page, m.down /. m.zoom) :: m.back } in
      let _, _, _, y1 = pages.(m'.page).box in
      match top with
      | Some top when turned pages m'.page m' = 0 ->
          (* (go's down has a gap above the page; one more: the
           * height named is a line's foot, pdfTeX's anchors) *)
          { m' with down = m'.down +. ((y1 -. top -. gap) *. m'.zoom) }
      | _ -> m')
  | Page _, (Picture _ | Nothing _) -> m

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The update *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let zoomed (s : Playground.screen) (by : float) (m : model) : model =
  let zoom = Float.max 0.1 (Float.min 8. (m.zoom *. by)) in
  (* what is at the window's middle stays there *)
  let half = room s /. 2. and by = zoom /. m.zoom in
  { m with zoom; fitted = None; x = m.x *. by;
           down = ((m.down +. half) *. by) -. half }

(* the zoom fitted to another window's width, what is at the window's
 * top staying there; once the width has stayed the same 10 frames (a
 * window being made larger by the mouse is a new width at each frame,
 * and each had its pages drawn again), or at once for the first one *)
let refitted (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) : model =
  let seen =
    match m.seen with
    | width, n when width = s.width -> (width, n + 1)
    | width, _ when width < 0. -> (s.width, 10)
    | _ -> (s.width, 0)
  in
  let m = { m with seen } in
  match m.fitted with
  | Some width when width <> s.width && snd seen >= 10 ->
      let zoom = fit_zoom s.width m in
      let by = zoom /. m.zoom in
      { m with zoom; fitted = Some s.width; x = m.x *. by;
               down = m.down *. by }
  | _ -> m

let update (computer : Playground.computer) (m : model) : model =
  let s = computer.screen in
  let k = computer.keyboard and mouse = computer.mouse in
  let now = Set_.elements k.keys in
  let pressed (key : string) = List.mem key now && not (List.mem key m.was) in
  let digits =
    String.concat ""
      (List.filter
         (fun (s : string) -> s >= "0" && s <= "9")
         (List.init (String.length k.typed) (fun (i : int) ->
              String.make 1 k.typed.[i])))
  in
  let typed (c : char) = String.contains k.typed c in
  let m = refitted s { m with number = m.number ^ digits } in
  let m =
    if pressed "Enter" && m.number <> "" then
      { (go (int_of_string m.number - 1) m) with number = "" }
    else if pressed "Escape" then { m with number = "" }
    else if pressed "space" || pressed "PageDown" || pressed "ArrowRight"
    then go (m.page + 1) m
    else if pressed "Backspace" || pressed "PageUp" || pressed "ArrowLeft"
    then go (m.page - 1) m
    else if typed '+' || typed '=' then zoomed s 1.25 m
    else if typed '-' then zoomed s 0.8 m
    else if typed 'f' then fit s.width m
    else if typed 'r' then fit s.width { m with turn = (m.turn + 1) mod 4 }
    else if typed 'q' then (
      if place_of m <> m.saved then m.remember (place_of m);
      m.quit ();
      m)
    else if typed 'b' then
      match m.back with
      | (page, down) :: back -> { m with page; down = down *. m.zoom; back }
      | [] -> m
    else m
  in
  let m = within s m in
  (* the pages moved along: the arrows held, the wheel, the mouse
   * dragging them; the page is then the one at the middle *)
  let step =
    (if k.kup then -30. else 0.) +. (if k.kdown then 30. else 0.)
    -. (mouse.mwheel *. 60.)
  in
  let before = m.down in
  let m = { m with down = m.down +. step } in
  let m =
    match (mouse.mdown, m.held) with
    | true, Some (hx, hy) -> { m with x = mouse.mx -. hx; down = mouse.my +. hy }
    | true, None ->
        { m with held = Some (mouse.mx -. m.x, m.down -. mouse.my);
                 pressed = (mouse.mx, mouse.my) }
    | false, _ -> { m with held = None }
  in
  let m = within s m in
  let m = if m.down <> before then { m with page = middle s m } else m in
  (* a click, where the button went down: the link there followed *)
  let px, py = m.pressed in
  let still = Float.abs (mouse.mx -. px) < 4. && Float.abs (mouse.my -. py) < 4. in
  let m =
    match link_at s m (mouse.mx, mouse.my) with
    | Some t when mouse.mclick && still -> within s (follow t m)
    | _ -> m
  in
  let m = drawn s { m with was = now } in
  (* the cursor a hand over a link *)
  let hand = link_at s m (mouse.mx, mouse.my) <> None in
  if hand <> m.hand then
    Playground_platform.set_cursor
      (if hand then Playground.Hand else Playground.Arrow);
  (* the place kept once still half a second (at 60 frames a second) *)
  let place = place_of m in
  let still = if place = m.place then m.still + 1 else 0 in
  let m = if still >= 10 then ahead s m else m in
  if still = 30 && place <> m.saved then (
    m.remember place;
    { m with hand; place; still; saved = place })
  else { m with hand; place; still }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Where each file was left *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the file of places: places=FILE, or none with places=off; else
 * $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mini-page/places, ~/.config/mini-page/places, or on
 * Plan 9 $home/lib/mini-page/places (mini-netscape's profile's ways) *)
let places_file (caps : < Cap.env ; .. >) (flags : Playground.flags) :
    string option =
  let env (name : string) : string option =
    match CapSys.getenv caps name with
    | "" -> None
    | v -> Some v
    | exception Not_found -> None
  in
  let ( / ) = Filename.concat in
  match List.assoc_opt "places" flags with
  | Some "off" -> None
  | Some file -> Some file
  | None -> (
      match (env "XDG_CONFIG_HOME", env "HOME", env "home") with
      | Some config, _, _ -> Some (config / "mini-page" / "places")
      | None, Some home, _ -> Some (home / ".config" / "mini-page" / "places")
      | None, None, Some home -> Some (home / "lib" / "mini-page" / "places")
      | None, None, None -> None)

(* a line a file, the last left first: "down zoom turn path" *)
let read_places (caps : < Cap.open_in ; .. >) (file : string) :
    (string * place) list =
  match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v file) with
  | None ->
      Logs.info (fun m -> m "places: no %s yet" file);
      []
  | Some text ->
      Logs.info (fun m -> m "places: reading %s" file);
      List.filter_map
        (fun (line : string) ->
          match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
          | down :: zoom :: turn :: (_ :: _ as path) -> (
              match
                ( float_of_string_opt down,
                  float_of_string_opt zoom,
                  int_of_string_opt turn )
              with
              | Some down, Some zoom, Some turn ->
                  Some (String.concat " " path, (down, zoom, turn))
              | _ -> None)
          | _ -> None)
        (String.split_on_char '\n' text)

(* the files kept, the last left first *)
let kept_places = 100

let write_places (caps : < Cap.open_out ; .. >) (file : string)
    (places : (string * place) list) : unit =
  Logs.info (fun m -> m "places: writing %s" file);
  (* the directories made where they are not (Store's way: one there,
   * or that may not be made, is the write's error) *)
  let rec mkdir (dir : string) =
    if dir <> "/" && dir <> "." && dir <> "" then begin
      mkdir (Filename.dirname dir);
      try FS.mkdir caps dir 0o755 with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()
    end
  in
  let line ((path, (down, zoom, turn)) : string * place) =
    (* (%.17g: read back the same number, the same picture) *)
    Printf.sprintf "%.17g %.17g %d %s\n" down zoom turn path
  in
  try
    mkdir (Filename.dirname file);
    FS.write caps (Fpath.v file) (String.concat "" (List.map line places))
  with Sys_error why ->
    Logs.warn (fun m -> m "places: %s" why)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The view *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let shapes (s : Playground.screen) (m : model) (status : string) :
    Playground.shape list =
  let tops = tops m in
  let page (i : int) : Playground.shape list =
    (* its middle, up the window *)
    let _, h = size m.source i m.turn in
    let y = s.top -. (tops.(i) +. (h *. m.zoom /. 2.) -. m.down) in
    match m.source with
    | Pages _ -> (
        let zoom = thousandths m.zoom in
        let is (k : kept) = k.page = i && k.zoom = zoom && k.turn = m.turn in
        match List.find_opt is m.kept with
        | Some k ->
            (* its corner on a pixel, not its centre (a picture of an odd
             * width has its centre in the middle of one): the pixels are
             * then shown as they are, none blended with its neighbour.
             * The window's pixels count from its left and its top, and
             * its middle, the playground's 0, is in the middle of a pixel
             * when it is odd: a window made a pixel wider drew every page
             * from four pixels each, each frame (1281 by 901, the Kernel
             * book scrolled: 120 frames in 16.9 s, 2.4 at 1280 by 900).
             * old: Float.round (centre -. (size /. 2.)) +. (size /. 2.) *)
            let w = float k.image.width and h = float k.image.height in
            let left = m.x -. (w /. 2.) +. (s.width /. 2.)
            and top = (s.height /. 2.) -. y -. (h /. 2.) in
            let x = m.x -. (left -. Float.round left)
            and y = y +. (top -. Float.round top) in
            [ Playground.bitmap w h k.image |> Playground.move x y ]
        | None -> [])
    | Picture img ->
        (* (turned by the shape's angle, which goes the other way) *)
        let w = float img.width *. m.zoom and h = float img.height *. m.zoom in
        [ Playground.bitmap w h img
          |> Playground.rotate (-90. *. float m.turn)
          |> Playground.move m.x y ]
    | Nothing why -> [ Playground.words Playground.black why ]
  in
  let grey = Playground.rgb 120 120 128 in
  let bar = s.bottom +. (status_line /. 2.) in
  (Playground.rectangle grey s.width s.height
   :: List.concat_map page (shown s m))
  @ [
      Playground.rectangle (Playground.rgb 225 225 225) s.width status_line
      |> Playground.move 0. bar;
      Playground.words (Playground.rgb 40 40 40) status
      |> Playground.move 0. bar;
    ]

let view (computer : Playground.computer) (m : model) : Playground.shape list =
  let s = computer.screen in
  let w, h = size m.source m.page m.turn in
  let status =
    Printf.sprintf "%s     page %d of %d     %d%%     %d by %d%s" m.name
      (m.page + 1) (count m.source)
      (int_of_float (Float.round (m.zoom *. 100.)))
      (int_of_float (Float.round w)) (int_of_float (Float.round h))
      (match (m.number, link_at s m (computer.mouse.mx, computer.mouse.my)) with
       | "", None -> ""
       | "", Some t -> "     a link " ^ leads t
       | number, _ -> "     go to page " ^ number)
  in
  let key : view_key =
    ( status, m.down, m.x, m.zoom, m.turn, s.width, s.height,
      (* (the pictures of the pages shown: one drawn ahead is not) *)
      List.map
        (fun (k : kept) -> (k.page, k.zoom, k.turn))
        (List.filter (fun (k : kept) -> List.mem k.page (shown s m)) m.kept) )
  in
  match !(m.last) with
  | Some (k, shapes) when k = key -> shapes
  | _ ->
      let shapes = shapes s m status in
      m.last := Some (key, shapes);
      shapes

(* Without a window *)

(* a picture as a PPM: three bytes a pixel after a line of text *)
let ppm (img : Rgba_image.t) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create ((3 * img.width * img.height) + 20) in
  Buffer.add_string b (Printf.sprintf "P6\n%d %d\n255\n" img.width img.height);
  for i = 0 to (img.width * img.height) - 1 do
    Buffer.add_string b (Bytes.sub_string img.rgba (4 * i) 3)
  done;
  Buffer.contents b

let pages_of (bytes : string) : Pdf.t * Pdf_render.cache * Pdf.page array =
  match source bytes with
  | Pages (pdf, cache, pages) -> (pdf, cache, pages)
  | Picture _ -> failwith "a picture has no pages"
  | Nothing why -> failwith why

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      let read (file : string) : string = FS.read caps (Fpath.v file) in
      (* (-help: the usage, and the end, Exit.ExitCode) *)
      Exit.exit caps @@ Exit.catch @@ fun () ->
      (try
        match Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps) with
        | [ _; "-t"; file ] ->
            let pdf, cache, pages = pages_of (read file) in
            Array.iteri
              (fun (i : int) (p : Pdf.page) -> Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "-- page %d\n%s\n" (i + 1) (Pdf_render.text pdf cache p)))
              pages
        | [ _; "-ppm"; n; file; out ] ->
            let pdf, cache, pages = pages_of (read file) in
            let n = int_of_string n in
            if n < 1 || n > Array.length pages then failwith (Printf.sprintf "%s has %d page(s)" file (Array.length pages));
            FS.write caps (Fpath.v out) (ppm (Pdf_render.render ~options:Pdf_render.full ~stroke_glyph:Pdf_render.hershey pdf cache pages.(n - 1) ~scale:1.))
        | _ -> (
            (* the traces' reporter, before the flags: -v, -debug (Session) *)
            Logging.setup caps ~name:"mini-page";
            let flags = Playground_platform.flags caps in
            (* the file: the first word that is no name=value *)
            match List.find_opt (fun ((_, value) : string * string) -> value = "") flags with
            | None -> failwith usage
            | Some (file, _) ->
                (* an address: to mini-netscape, a program of its own *)
                let open_url (url : string) =
                  try
                    ignore
                      (Procs.create_process caps "mini-netscape" [ url ]
                         ~stdin:Unix.stdin ~stdout:Unix.stdout)
                  with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) ->
                    Console.eprint caps
                      (Printf.sprintf "mini-netscape %s: %s\n" url
                         (Unix.error_message e))
                in
                let quit () = CapStdlib.exit caps 0 in
                (* the file by its whole path, the same from anywhere *)
                let path =
                  FS.cleanname
                    (if Filename.is_relative file then
                       Filename.concat (FS.getcwd caps ()) file
                     else file)
                in
                let places_file = places_file caps flags in
                let places =
                  ref
                    (match places_file with
                    | Some f -> read_places caps f
                    | None -> [])
                in
                let remember (place : place) =
                  match places_file with
                  | Some f ->
                      let rest = List.remove_assoc path !places in
                      places :=
                        List.filteri
                          (fun (i : int) (_ : string * place) -> i < kept_places)
                          ((path, place) :: rest);
                      write_places caps f !places
                  | None -> ()
                in
                let was = List.assoc_opt path !places in
                let model =
                  start (Filename.basename file) (read file) ~was ~remember
                    ~quit ~open_url
                in
                (* heap=modest: a page's picture is megabytes kept, not a
                 * game's floats of a frame (Plan9_loop says what it changes);
                 * window: the screen is the window, a unit a pixel (a page
                 * drawn at the pixels it is shown: the draw platform's
                 * fit) *)
                Playground_platform.run_app caps
                  (* (the command line's first: window=WxH there wins;
                   * idle=wait: looked at 4 times a second when nothing
                   * changes: Plan9_loop) *)
                  (flags @ [ ("heap", "modest"); ("window", ""); ("idle", "wait") ])
                  (Playground.game view update model))
      with Failure msg ->
        Console.eprint caps (msg ^ "\n");
        CapStdlib.exit caps 1);
      Exit.OK)

(* mini-maild: mail taken by SMTP, kept a file a message, and read by
 * IMAP, on this machine only (127.0.0.1): the other end of mini-pim's
 * mail for its tests, so that they never talk to Gmail
 * (docs/plans/done/plan_mail.md). After the author's playground's
 * tiny_maild, whose Mail_server it runs the SMTP half of (Smtp_server),
 * with IMAP for its POP3 (Imap_server).
 *
 *     mini-pim send ---SMTP---> mini-maild ----> spool/bob/1
 *                                          ----> spool/bob/2
 *     mini-pim list <--IMAP---- (flags and labels in the process)
 *
 * One client at a time, as mini-httpd, on either port; any user and
 * password (a test's server); mail for its domain only (-d, "ix"). A
 * message is a file, numbered in its user's directory as it comes, the
 * number its UID, the bytes Smtp_server made of it, its Received: line
 * on top. Its flags and labels (\Inbox when it comes) are kept while
 * mini-maild runs, not written. Each message taken is a line on
 * standard output: the user, its number, its subject. *)

type caps = < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir;
              Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.clock >

let usage = "usage: mini-maild [-p port] [-i port] [-d domain] [-a name] spool
  -p  SMTP's port (2525; 0: one the system chooses, said on the first line)
  -i  IMAP's port (1143; 0 as for -p)
  -d  the domain taken mail for (ix)
  -a  All Mail's name ([Gmail]/All Mail; a French Gmail's:
      '[Gmail]/Tous les messages')"

let say (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (line : string) : unit =
  Console.print caps (line ^ "\n");
  flush (Console.stdout caps)

(* the numbers of a user's messages, in order *)
let numbers (_caps : < Cap.readdir; .. >) (dir : string) : int list =
  if not (Sys.file_exists dir) then []
  else
    List.sort compare
      (List.filter_map int_of_string_opt (Array.to_list (Sys.readdir dir)))

(* the message into each user's directory, the next number *)
let keep (caps : < caps; .. >) ~(spool : string) (d : Smtp_server.delivery) :
    unit =
  List.iter
    (fun user ->
      let dir = Filename.concat spool user in
      if not (Sys.file_exists dir) then FS.mkdir caps dir 0o755;
      let n = List.fold_left max 0 (numbers caps dir) + 1 in
      FS.write caps (Fpath.v (Filename.concat dir (string_of_int n)))
        (Mail.to_string d.mail);
      let subject =
        match Mail.get d.mail "subject" with Some s -> s | None -> ""
      in
      say caps (Printf.sprintf "%s %d %s" user n subject))
    d.users

(* IMAP's store: the files, and the flags and labels of each
 * (user, UID) changed since mini-maild started *)
let store (caps : < caps; .. >) ~(spool : string) ~(all_mail : string) :
    Imap_server.store =
  let marks : (string * int, string list * string list) Hashtbl.t =
    Hashtbl.create 16
  in
  let messages user =
    let dir = Filename.concat spool user in
    List.map
      (fun uid ->
        let flags, labels =
          match Hashtbl.find_opt marks (user, uid) with
          | Some m -> m
          | None -> ([], [ "\\Inbox" ])
        in
        { Imap_server.uid;
          text = FS.read caps (Fpath.v (Filename.concat dir (string_of_int uid)));
          flags; labels })
      (numbers caps dir)
  in
  { all_mail;
    messages;
    change = (fun user uid ~flags ~labels ->
      Hashtbl.replace marks (user, uid) (flags, labels)) }

(* a client's dialogue, its machine's greeting first, until it is done
 * or gone *)
let dialogue (conn : Lines.t) (greeting : string list)
    (step : 'm -> string -> 'm * string list) (machine : 'm)
    (ended : 'm -> bool) : unit =
  List.iter (Lines.send_line conn) greeting;
  let rec go m =
    if not (ended m) then
      match Lines.line conn with
      | None -> ()
      | Some l ->
          let m, answer = step m l in
          List.iter (Lines.send_line conn) answer;
          go m
  in
  go machine

let smtp (caps : < caps; .. >) ~(spool : string) ~(domain : string)
    (conn : Lines.t) : unit =
  let s, greeting = Smtp_server.start ~domain in
  let step s l =
    let s, answer, delivered =
      Smtp_server.step s ~now:(CapUnix.gettimeofday caps ()) l
    in
    (match delivered with Some d -> keep caps ~spool d | None -> ());
    (s, answer)
  in
  dialogue conn greeting step s Smtp_server.ended

let imap (store : Imap_server.store) (conn : Lines.t) : unit =
  let t, greeting = Imap_server.start () in
  dialogue conn greeting (Imap_server.step store) t Imap_server.ended

let listen (_caps : < Cap.network; .. >) (port : int) : Unix.file_descr * int =
  let sock = Unix.socket Unix.PF_INET Unix.SOCK_STREAM 0 in
  Unix.setsockopt sock Unix.SO_REUSEADDR true;
  Unix.bind sock (Unix.ADDR_INET (Unix.inet_addr_loopback, port));
  Unix.listen sock 16;
  (sock, match Unix.getsockname sock with Unix.ADDR_INET (_, p) -> p | _ -> port)

(* the next client, on either socket, served to its end *)
let rec serve (sockets : (Unix.file_descr * (Lines.t -> unit)) list) : 'a =
  let ready, _, _ = Unix.select (List.map fst sockets) [] [] (-1.) in
  List.iter
    (fun sock ->
      let fd, _ = Unix.accept sock in
      let conn = Lines.of_fd fd in
      (try (List.assoc sock sockets) conn
       with Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _ -> ());
      Lines.close conn)
    ready;
  serve sockets

type options = {
  port : int;
  imap_port : int;
  domain : string;
  all_mail : string;
  spool : string;
}

let rec options (o : options) (args : string list) : options option =
  let port p f = match int_of_string_opt p with Some p -> f p | None -> None in
  match args with
  | [] -> if o.spool = "" then None else Some o
  | "-p" :: p :: rest -> port p (fun p -> options { o with port = p } rest)
  | "-i" :: p :: rest -> port p (fun p -> options { o with imap_port = p } rest)
  | "-d" :: d :: rest -> options { o with domain = d } rest
  | "-a" :: a :: rest -> options { o with all_mail = a } rest
  | flag :: _ when String.length flag > 1 && flag.[0] = '-' -> None
  | dir :: rest -> options { o with spool = dir } rest

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let default =
    { port = 2525; imap_port = 1143; domain = "ix";
      all_mail = "[Gmail]/All Mail"; spool = "" }
  in
  match options default (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) with
  | None -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "\n"); Exit.Err "usage"
  | Some o when not (Sys.file_exists o.spool && Sys.is_directory o.spool) ->
      Console.eprint caps (o.spool ^ ": not a directory\n");
      Exit.Err "spool"
  | Some o -> (
      match (listen caps o.port, listen caps o.imap_port) with
      | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) ->
          Console.eprint caps (Unix.error_message e ^ "\n");
          Exit.Err "port"
      | (s, p), (i, q) ->
          Sys.set_signal Sys.sigpipe Sys.Signal_ignore;
          say caps
            (Printf.sprintf
               "serving %s: SMTP on 127.0.0.1:%d, IMAP on 127.0.0.1:%d"
               o.domain p q);
          let spool = o.spool in
          serve
            [ (s, smtp caps ~spool ~domain:o.domain);
              (i, imap (store caps ~spool ~all_mail:o.all_mail)) ])

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
