(* See Proc.mli *)

open Ast

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.kill; Cap.env >

let error fmt = Printf.ksprintf (fun s -> raise (Eval.Error s)) fmt

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The program *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the a.out's header (Exe's, -H2): its text at 0x1020, after the
 * header, its data on the page after the text; or an ELF's (Linux's:
 * gcc's, mini-ld -H7's), its loads', its symbols moved by bias once a
 * process of it runs (a PIE's, gcc's default, is put anywhere) *)
type program = {
  path : string;
  file : string;
  txtaddr : int64;
  txtsz : int64;
  dataddr : int64;
  datsz : int64;
  table : Symbols.t option;
  arch : string;            (* arm, arm64 *)
  elf : Elf_file.t option;
  bias : int64;
  dwarf : Dwarf_line.t option;   (* an ELF's lines (gcc's), its addresses the file's *)
}

let prog : program option ref = ref None

(* the disassembler's symbols, the program's *)
let das_table = ref (Das.table [])

let be32 s o =
  Int64.logor (Int64.shift_left (Int64.of_int (Char.code s.[o])) 24)
    (Int64.of_int ((Char.code s.[o + 1] lsl 16) lor (Char.code s.[o + 2] lsl 8) lor Char.code s.[o + 3]))

let elf_header file path (e : Elf_file.t) =
  let seg = function Some (g : Elf_file.segment) -> Int64.of_int g.vaddr, Int64.of_int g.filesz | None -> 0L, 0L in
  let txtaddr, txtsz = seg (Elf_file.text_segment e) and dataddr, datsz = seg (Elf_file.data_segment e) in
  let text_start = Int64.to_int txtaddr and text_end = Int64.to_int (Int64.add txtaddr txtsz) in
  (* (mini-ld -g's: Plan 9's tables in two sections, their lines and
   * locals; else ELF's names, gcc's) *)
  let table : Symbols.t =
    match Elf_file.section e ".plan9.syms", Elf_file.section e ".plan9.lines" with
    | Some s, Some l -> Symbols.of_tables (Elf_file.bytes file s) (Elf_file.bytes file l) text_start text_end
    | _ -> { syms = Elf_file.symbols file e; text_start; text_end; lines = "" } in
  let arch = match e.machine with 183 -> "arm64" | 40 -> "arm" | m -> error "%s: an ELF of machine %d, not arm's nor arm64's" path m in
  { path; file; txtaddr; txtsz; dataddr; datsz; arch; elf = Some e; bias = 0L; dwarf = Dwarf_line.read file e;
    table = Some table }

let header file path =
  match Elf_file.read file with
  | Some e -> elf_header file path e
  | None ->
  if String.length file < 32 || be32 file 0 <> 0x647L then error "%s: not an arm plan 9 executable" path;
  let text = be32 file 4 and data = be32 file 8 in
  let txtaddr = 0x1020L in
  { path; file; txtaddr; txtsz = text;
    dataddr = Int64.logand (Int64.add (Int64.add txtaddr text) 0xfffL) (Int64.lognot 0xfffL);
    datsz = data; table = Symbols.read file; arch = "arm"; elf = None; bias = 0L; dwarf = None }

let arm64 () = match !prog with Some p -> p.arch = "arm64" | None -> false

(* the symbols of a kind, the text's or the data's *)
let syms text =
  match !prog with
  | Some { table = Some t; _ } ->
      List.filter (fun (s : Symbols.sym) ->
        if text then String.contains "TtLl" s.typ else String.contains "DdBb" s.typ) t.syms
  | _ -> []

(* findsym: the symbol at or below an address, of the text if it is in
 * the text, else of the data *)
let findsym v =
  let text = match !prog with
    | Some p -> v >= p.txtaddr && v < Int64.add p.txtaddr p.txtsz
    | None -> false in
  List.fold_left (fun best (s : Symbols.sym) ->
    let sv = Int64.of_int s.value in
    if sv <= v then (match best with Some (b : Symbols.sym) when b.value >= s.value -> best | _ -> Some s) else best)
    None (syms text)

(* libmach's symoff (the a format): name+0xoff, the name, or the number;
 * on arm64 an address of 64 bits (Das's are 5db's, 32) *)
let symoff v =
  if (match !prog with Some p -> p.arch = "arm64" | None -> false) then
    match (if v = 0L then None else findsym v) with
    | Some s when Int64.sub v (Int64.of_int s.value) = 0L -> s.name
    | Some s when String.contains "Tt" s.typ || Int64.sub v (Int64.of_int s.value) < 4096L ->
        Printf.sprintf "%s+0x%Lx" s.name (Int64.sub v (Int64.of_int s.value))
    | _ -> Printf.sprintf "0x%Lx" v
  else Das.symoff !das_table false v

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The process *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let pid = ref 0
let mem : Unix.file_descr option ref = ref None
let regs : Unix.file_descr option ref = ref None
let stacktop = ref 0L
(* the processes attached, their ctl files (acid's ptab); on Linux
 * none, the process's ptrace's *)
let ctls : (int * Unix.file_descr option) list ref = ref []

(* Linux: a process's last stop, its signal (TYPE in its registers) *)
let linux = Ptrace.available
let stops : (int * int) list ref = ref []

(* arm's Ureg: 18 words; arm64's user_pt_regs on Linux (x0 to x30, sp,
 * pc, pstate: 34 words) and TYPE after it, the signal *)
let regsize () = if arm64 () then 280L else 72L

let pread fd off n =
  ignore (Unix.LargeFile.lseek fd off Unix.SEEK_SET);
  let b = Bytes.create n in
  let rec go k = if k < n then (match Unix.read fd b k (n - k) with 0 -> k | r -> go (k + r)) else k in
  let k = go 0 in
  Bytes.sub_string b 0 k

let pwrite fd off s =
  ignore (Unix.LargeFile.lseek fd off Unix.SEEK_SET);
  ignore (Unix.write fd (Bytes.of_string s) 0 (String.length s))

(* the maps (libmach's map.c): what is at an address, n bytes *)
let load core addr n =
  let fail () = error "indir: can't translate address 0x%Lx" addr in
  let within lo hi = addr >= lo && Int64.add addr (Int64.of_int n) <= hi in
  let got s = if String.length s < n then fail () else s in
  match !prog, !mem, !regs with
  | Some _, Some m, None when core && linux ->
      if within 0L (regsize ()) then
        let r = Ptrace.getregs !pid ^ Bytes.to_string (let b = Bytes.make 8 '\000' in Bytes.set_int64_le b 0 (Int64.of_int (match List.assoc_opt !pid !stops with Some s -> s | None -> 0)); b) in
        String.sub r (Int64.to_int addr) n
      else got (pread m addr n)
  | Some p, Some m, Some r when core ->
      if within 0L (regsize ()) then got (pread r addr n)
      else if within p.txtaddr (Int64.add p.txtaddr p.txtsz) || within p.dataddr !stacktop then got (pread m addr n)
      else fail ()
  | Some ({ elf = Some e; _ } as p), _, _ ->
      (match Elf_file.file_offset e (Int64.to_int (Int64.sub addr p.bias)) with
       | Some off when off + n <= String.length p.file -> String.sub p.file off n
       | _ -> fail ())
  | Some p, _, _ ->
      let off =
        if within p.txtaddr (Int64.add p.txtaddr p.txtsz) then Int64.sub addr 0x1000L
        else if within p.dataddr (Int64.add p.dataddr p.datsz) then Int64.add (Int64.add 32L p.txtsz) (Int64.sub addr p.dataddr)
        else fail () in
      String.sub p.file (Int64.to_int off) n
  | None, _, _ -> (if core then error "no map for *" else error "no map for @")

let store addr s =
  match !mem, !regs with
  | Some m, None when linux ->
      if addr < 272L then begin
        let r = Bytes.of_string (Ptrace.getregs !pid) in
        Bytes.blit_string s 0 r (Int64.to_int addr) (min (String.length s) (272 - Int64.to_int addr));
        Ptrace.setregs !pid (Bytes.to_string r)
      end
      else if addr >= regsize () then pwrite m addr s
  | Some m, Some r -> if addr < regsize () then pwrite r addr s else pwrite m addr s
  | _ -> error "no map for *"

let set name v = Eval.set_global name v

let install (caps : < caps; .. >) p =
  if not (List.mem_assoc p !ctls) then begin
    let fd = if linux then None else
      Some (try FS.open_rw_fd caps (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/ctl" p) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> error "pid=%d: open ctl: process exited" p) in
    ctls := (p, fd) :: !ctls;
    set "proclist" (Value.list (List.map (fun (p, _) -> Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int p)) !ctls))
  end

let deinstall p =
  (match List.assoc_opt p !ctls with Some (Some fd) -> (try Unix.close fd with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()) | _ -> ());
  stops := List.remove_assoc p !stops;
  ctls := List.remove_assoc p !ctls;
  set "proclist" (Value.list (List.map (fun (p, _) -> Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int p)) !ctls));
  if !pid = p then (pid := 0; set "pid" (Value.int 'D' 0L))

(* Linux: a ctl message by ptrace; a stop's signal kept (a breakpoint's
 * SIGTRAP is not given back to the process at the next start, another
 * is: a SIGSEGV kills it then, as without a debugger) *)
let linux_msg (caps : < caps; .. >) p m =
  let wait () =
    match Ptrace.wait p with
    | s when s > 0 -> stops := (p, s) :: List.remove_assoc p !stops
    | _ -> deinstall p; error "msg: pid=%d %s: process exited" p m in
  let start () =
    let s = match List.assoc_opt p !stops with Some s when s <> 5 && s <> 19 -> s | _ -> 0 in
    stops := List.remove_assoc p !stops;
    (try Ptrace.cont p s with Failure _ -> deinstall p; error "msg: pid=%d %s: process exited" p m) in
  match m with
  | "start" -> start ()
  | "startstop" -> start (); wait ()
  | "waitstop" -> if not (List.mem_assoc p !stops) then wait ()
  | "stop" -> if not (List.mem_assoc p !stops) then (Ptrace.signal caps p 19; wait ())
  | "kill" -> Ptrace.signal caps p 9; (try ignore (Ptrace.wait p) with Failure _ -> ())
  | _ -> error "msg: pid=%d: %s: not on Linux" p m

(* a message to a process's ctl *)
let msg (caps : < caps; .. >) p m =
  match List.assoc_opt p !ctls with
  | None -> error "msg: pid=%d: not found for %s" p m
  | Some None -> linux_msg caps p m
  | Some (Some fd) ->
      (try ignore (Unix.write fd (Bytes.of_string m) 0 (String.length m))
       with Unix.Unix_error _ -> deinstall p; error "msg: pid=%d %s: process exited" p m)

(* Linux's signals as Plan 9's notes say them *)
let signame = function
  | 5 -> "sys: breakpoint" | 11 -> "sys: trap: fault (SIGSEGV)" | 7 -> "sys: trap: bus error (SIGBUS)"
  | 4 -> "sys: trap: illegal instruction (SIGILL)" | 8 -> "sys: trap: arithmetic (SIGFPE)" | 6 -> "sys: abort (SIGABRT)"
  | 19 -> "sys: stop (SIGSTOP)" | 2 -> "interrupt (SIGINT)" | s -> Printf.sprintf "signal %d" s

(* its pending notes, read (and so taken) from its note file *)
let notes (caps : < caps; .. >) p =
  if linux then set "notes" (Value.list (match List.assoc_opt p !stops with Some s -> [ Value.string (signame s) ] | None -> []))
  else
  let fd = try FS.open_in_fd caps (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/note" p) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> error "pid=%d: open note: process exited" p in
  let rec all acc =
    let b = Bytes.create 128 in
    match Unix.read fd b 0 128 with
    | 0 -> List.rev acc
    | n -> all (Value.string (Bytes.sub_string b 0 n) :: acc)
    | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> List.rev acc in
  let l = all [] in
  Unix.close fd;
  set "notes" (Value.list l)

let dostop p = Eval.call_if_defined "stopped" [ Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int p) ]

(* Linux's maps, each {name, base, end, offset} (/proc/$pid/maps) *)
let linux_maps (caps : < caps; .. >) p =
  match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/maps" p)) with
  | None -> []
  | Some s ->
      List.filter_map (fun l ->
        match List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' l) with
        | range :: perms :: off :: _ :: _ :: rest when String.length perms > 0 && perms.[0] = 'r' ->
            (match String.index_opt range '-' with
             | Some i ->
                 let hex x = Int64.of_string ("0x" ^ x) in
                 Some ((match rest with n :: _ -> n | [] -> "anon"), hex (String.sub range 0 i),
                       hex (String.sub range (i + 1) (String.length range - i - 1)), hex off)
             | None -> None)
        | _ -> None) (String.split_on_char '\n' s)

(* libmach's stacktop: the first line of its segment file, the stack's *)
let top (caps : < caps; .. >) p =
  if linux then (match List.find_opt (fun (n, _, _, _) -> n = "[stack]") (linux_maps caps p) with Some (_, _, e, _) -> e | None -> 0L)
  else
  match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/segment" p)) with
  | Some s when String.length s > 5 && String.sub s 0 5 = "Stack" ->
      (match List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.sub s 5 (String.length s - 5))) with
       | _ :: t :: _ -> (try Int64.of_string ("0x" ^ t) with Failure _ -> 0L)
       | _ -> 0L)
  | _ -> 0L

let attach (caps : < caps; .. >) p =
  if !prog = None then error "no map";
  let fd name = try FS.open_rw_fd caps (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/%s" p name) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> error "setproc: open /proc/%d/%s: process exited" p name in
  (match !mem with Some m -> Unix.close m | None -> ());
  (match !regs with Some r -> Unix.close r | None -> ());
  mem := Some (fd "mem");
  regs := if linux then None else Some (fd "regs");
  stacktop := top caps p;
  pid := p;
  set "pid" (Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int p));
  install caps p

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The variables *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* principia's 5db: the registers, their offsets in the Ureg *)
let reglist = [
  "TYPE", 60; "PSR", 64; "PC", 68; "SP", 52; "R15", 68; "R14", 56; "R13", 52; "R12", 48; "R11", 44;
  "R10", 40; "R9", 36; "R8", 32; "R7", 28; "R6", 24; "R5", 20; "R4", 16; "R3", 12; "R2", 8; "R1", 4; "R0", 0 ]

(* arm64's on Linux, user_pt_regs': R29 the frame pointer, R30 the
 * link; TYPE ours, the stop's signal *)
let reglist64 =
  [ "TYPE", 272; "PSR", 264; "PC", 256; "SP", 248; "LR", 240; "FP", 232 ]
  @ List.init 31 (fun i -> Printf.sprintf "R%d" (30 - i), 8 * (30 - i))

let regs_of () = if arm64 () then reglist64 else reglist

let registers () =
  List.iter (fun (name, off) -> set name (Value.int (if arm64 () then 'Y' else 'X') (Int64.of_int off))) (regs_of ());
  set "registers" (Value.list (List.map (fun (n, _) -> Value.string n) (regs_of ())));
  (* 5db's bpinst, BKPT; arm64's BRK #0 *)
  set "bpinst" (Value.string (if arm64 () then "\x00\x00\x20\xd4" else "\x70\x00\x20\xe1"))

let program (caps : < caps; .. >) path =
  let file = match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v path) with Some f -> f | None -> error "%s: can't open %s: file does not exist" path path in
  let p = header file path in
  prog := Some p;
  das_table :=
    Das.table (match p.table with Some (t : Symbols.t) -> t.syms | None -> []);
  Eval.print [ Value.string (path ^ (if p.elf <> None then ":" ^ p.arch ^ " linux executable" else ":arm plan 9 executable")) ];
  set "objtype" (Value.string p.arch);
  Eval.addr_size := (if p.arch = "arm64" then 8 else 4);
  set "textfile" (Value.string path);
  registers ()

(* the program's own declarations of its types, acid's text, if it has
 * them (mini-ld -g's .acid: decision 14 of plan_debugger.md), from
 * its file *)
let declarations () =
  match !prog with
  (* (an ELF of gcc's: its DWARF types as acid's, Acid_dwarf) *)
  | Some ({ elf = Some e; table = Some t; _ } as p)
    when not (List.exists (fun (s : Symbols.sym) -> s.name = ".acid") t.syms) && Elf_file.section e ".debug_info" <> None ->
      (match Acid_dwarf.decls (Dwarf_info.read p.file e) with "" -> None | text -> Some text)
  | Some ({ table = Some t; _ } as p) ->
      (match List.find_opt (fun (s : Symbols.sym) -> s.name = ".acid" && String.contains "Dd" s.typ) t.syms with
       | Some s ->
           let off = match p.elf with
             | Some e -> (match Elf_file.file_offset e s.value with Some o -> o | None -> -1)
             | None -> Int64.to_int (Int64.add (Int64.add 32L p.txtsz) (Int64.sub (Int64.of_int s.value) p.dataddr)) in
           (match String.index_from_opt p.file off '\000' with
            | Some e when off >= 0 -> Some (String.sub p.file off (e - off))
            | _ -> None)
       | None -> None)
  | _ -> None

let symbols () =
  let l = List.filter_map (fun (s : Symbols.sym) ->
    if String.contains "TLDBbdlt" s.typ && s.name <> "" && s.name.[0] <> '.' then begin
      (* (a complex variable's address its format a: acid's symbols,
       * read after the libraries, 5c -a's complex T name among them) *)
      set s.name (Value.int (if Eval.complex_type s.name <> None then 'a' else 'X') (Int64.of_int s.value));
      Some (Value.list [ Value.string s.name; Value.int 'c' (Int64.of_int (Char.code s.typ)); Value.int 'X' (Int64.of_int s.value) ])
    end else None)
    (match !prog with Some { table = Some t; _ } -> t.syms | _ -> []) in
  set "symbols" (Value.list l);
  if l = [] then Eval.print [ Value.string "no symbol information" ]

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The builtins *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let int name = function [ { kind = Int i; _ } ] -> i | _ -> error "%s(integer)" name

(* 5db's armexcep: a trap's name by the Ureg's type *)
let excep t =
  match Int64.to_int t land 0x1f with
  | 0x11 -> "Fiq interrupt" | 0x12 -> "Mirq interrupt" | 0x13 -> "SVC/SWI Exception"
  | 0x17 -> "Prefetch Abort/Breakpoint" | 0x18 -> "Data Abort"
  | 0x1b -> "Undefined instruction/Breakpoint" | 0x1f -> "Sys trap" | _ -> "Undefined trap"

(* the function around an address: its start, and the next's *)
let fnbound v =
  let fs = List.sort compare (List.map (fun (s : Symbols.sym) -> Int64.of_int s.value) (syms true)) in
  let rec go = function
    | a :: (b :: _ as rest) -> if a <= v && v < b then Some (a, b) else go rest
    | _ -> None in
  go fs

let file_line v =
  match !prog with
  | Some { dwarf = Some d; bias; _ } -> Dwarf_line.file_line d (Int64.to_int (Int64.sub v bias))
  | Some { table = Some t; _ } -> Symbols.file_line t (Int64.to_int v)
  | _ -> None

(* a word at an address, little-endian, of the process (core) or of
 * the program's file *)
let word core a =
  let w = !Eval.load core a 4 in
  List.fold_left (fun v k ->
    Int64.logor (Int64.shift_left v 8) (Int64.of_int (Char.code w.[k])))
    0L [ 3; 2; 1; 0 ]

let get core a = try Some (word core a) with Eval.Error _ -> None

(* a register's value, from the Ureg or user_pt_regs: 8 bytes on arm64 *)
let reg name =
  match List.assoc_opt name (regs_of ()) with
  | Some off when arm64 () -> Bytes.get_int64_le (Bytes.of_string (!Eval.load true (Int64.of_int off) 8)) 0
  | Some off -> word true (Int64.of_int off)
  | None -> error "rget: %s" name

let instruction core a =
  if arm64 () then Some (Das_arm64.instruction symoff (get core) a) else Das.instruction !das_table (get core) a

(* the instruction that runs after the one at an address (machdata's
 * foll, 5db's: its condition evaluated), the registers read from the
 * Ureg *)
let follow v =
  if !mem = None then error "follow(addr): can't read instruction: get4: invalid map";
  match (if arm64 () then Das_arm64.follow (get true) reg v else Das.follow (get true) reg v) with
  | Some a -> [ a ]
  | None -> error "follow(addr): can't read instruction"

(* libmach's risctrace: the frames from (pc, sp, link), each its
 * function's symbol, its table's entries (.frame, parameters p, locals
 * a), its sp once its frame is left, its return address: a function's
 * frame its .frame (0 at its first instruction), its return address the
 * link's (a leaf, or before its save) or the word at its sp; to _main,
 * not said, 40 frames at most *)
(* a function's entries in the table: those after its symbol, to the
 * next function's *)
let autos start =
  let entries = match !prog with Some { table = Some t; _ } -> t.syms | _ -> [] in
  let rec locals = function
    | (s : Symbols.sym) :: rest when not (String.contains "TtLl" s.typ) -> s :: locals rest
    | _ -> [] in
  let rec find_fn = function
    | (s : Symbols.sym) :: rest when String.contains "TtLl" s.typ && Int64.of_int s.value = start -> locals rest
    | _ :: rest -> find_fn rest
    | [] -> [] in
  find_fn entries

let walk pc sp link =
  let word a = word true a in
  let in_text v = match !prog with Some p -> v >= p.txtaddr && v < Int64.add p.txtaddr p.txtsz | None -> false in
  let rec go pc sp n acc =
    match (if in_text pc then findsym pc else None) with
    | Some (s : Symbols.sym) when n <= 40 && s.name <> "_main" && s.name <> "_mainp" ->
        let start = Int64.of_int s.value in
        let autos = autos start in
        let frame = if pc = start then Some 0L else
          (match List.find_opt (fun (e : Symbols.sym) -> e.typ = 'm' && e.name = ".frame") autos with
           | Some e -> Some (Int64.of_int e.value) | None -> None) in
        (match frame with
         | None -> List.rev acc
         | Some size ->
             let next = if s.typ = 'L' || s.typ = 'l' || pc <= Int64.add start 4L then Some link
               else (try Some (word sp) with Eval.Error _ -> None) in
             (match next with
              | None -> List.rev acc
              | Some ret ->
                  if ret = 0L || (ret = pc && size = 0L) then List.rev acc
                  else let sp = Int64.add sp size in go ret sp (n + 1) ((s, autos, sp, ret) :: acc)))
    | _ -> List.rev acc in
  go pc sp 0 []

(* a parameter's address, past the return address over the frame; a
 * local's, under the frame's top *)
let param_addr sp off = Int64.add (Int64.add sp 4L) (Int64.of_int off)
let auto_addr sp off = Int64.sub sp (Int64.of_int off)

(* arm64's frames, by Frame64 (the walk from the registers); a frame's
 * variables by DWARF in a program of gcc's (no Plan 9 table), else by
 * the table *)
let dwarf_units : (string * Dwarf_info.die list) option ref = ref None
let walk64 () =
  let read8 a = try Some (Bytes.get_int64_le (Bytes.of_string (!Eval.load true a 8)) 0) with Eval.Error _ -> None in
  let start v = Option.map (fun (s : Symbols.sym) -> Int64.of_int s.value) (findsym v) in
  let isstart a = match findsym a with Some s -> s.name = "main" | None -> false in
  Frame64.walk read8 (get false) start isstart (reg "PC") (reg "SP") (reg "R30") (reg "R29")
let vars64 (f : Frame64.frame) =
  match !prog with
  | Some ({ elf = Some e; bias; _ } as p)
    when Elf_file.section e ".debug_info" <> None && Elf_file.section e ".plan9.syms" = None ->
      let units = match !dwarf_units with
        | Some (path, u) when path = p.path -> u
        | _ -> let u = Dwarf_info.read p.file e in dwarf_units := Some (p.path, u); u in
      Frame64.dwarf units (Int64.to_int (Int64.sub f.start bias)) f.cfa
  | _ -> Frame64.plan9 (autos f.start) f.cfa

(* the frames as acid's lists: {its function, where it was called from
 * (the return less 8, arm's pc; arm64's less 4), its parameters, its
 * locals}, each of those {name, value} *)
let strace pc sp link =
  if arm64 () then begin
    let value (v : Frame64.var) =
      let b = try Some (!Eval.load true v.addr v.size) with Eval.Error _ -> None in
      Option.map (fun b ->
        let n = ref 0L in
        String.iteri (fun i c -> n := Int64.logor !n (Int64.shift_left (Int64.of_int (Char.code c)) (8 * i))) b;
        Value.list [ Value.string v.vname; Value.int (if v.size > 4 then 'Y' else 'X') !n ]) b in
    let frame (f : Frame64.frame) =
      let vs = vars64 f in
      let pick param = List.filter_map (fun (v : Frame64.var) -> if v.param = param then value v else None) vs in
      Value.list [ Value.int 'Y' f.start; Value.int 'Y' (Int64.sub f.ret 4L); Value.list (pick true); Value.list (pick false) ] in
    match walk64 () with
    | [] -> error "no stack frame"
    | frames -> Value.list (List.map frame frames)
  end else
  let var name v = Value.list [ Value.string name; Value.int 'X' v ] in
  let frame ((s : Symbols.sym), autos, sp, ret) =
    let read off = try Some (word true off) with Eval.Error _ -> None in
    let pick typ f = List.filter_map (fun (e : Symbols.sym) ->
      if e.typ = typ && e.name <> "" && e.name.[0] <> '.' then
        Option.map (var e.name) (read (f sp e.value)) else None) autos in
    (* (libmach's localsym: the table's order reversed, the last
     * written first) *)
    let params = List.rev (pick 'p' param_addr) in
    let locals = List.rev (pick 'a' auto_addr) in
    Value.list [ Value.int 'X' (Int64.of_int s.value); Value.int 'Y' (Int64.sub ret 8L); Value.list params; Value.list locals ] in
  match walk pc sp link with
  | [] -> error "no stack frame"
  | frames -> Value.list (List.map frame frames)

(* f:v, libmach's localaddr: v's address in the innermost frame of f,
 * from the stopped process's registers *)
let local_addr f v =
  if !mem = None then error "colon: no process";
  if arm64 () then
    match List.find_opt (fun (fr : Frame64.frame) -> match findsym fr.start with Some s -> s.name = f | None -> false) (walk64 ()) with
    | None -> error "colon: function %s not in the stack" f
    | Some fr ->
        match List.find_opt (fun (x : Frame64.var) -> x.vname = v) (vars64 fr) with
        | Some x -> x.addr, x.size
        | None -> error "colon: %s has no local %s" f v
  else
  match List.find_opt (fun ((s : Symbols.sym), _, _, _) -> s.name = f) (walk (reg "PC") (reg "SP") (reg "R14")) with
  | None -> error "colon: function %s not in the stack" f
  | Some (_, autos, sp, _) ->
      match List.find_opt (fun (e : Symbols.sym) -> e.name = v && (e.typ = 'p' || e.typ = 'a')) autos with
      | Some e when e.typ = 'p' -> param_addr sp e.value, 4
      | Some e -> auto_addr sp e.value, 4
      | None -> error "colon: %s has no local %s" f v

(* a PIE's symbols moved where Linux put it: its entry's address,
 * auxv's AT_ENTRY, less the file's *)
let rebias (caps : < caps; .. >) p =
  match !prog with
  | Some ({ elf = Some e; table = Some t; _ } as pr) ->
      let auxv = match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/auxv" p)) with Some a -> a | None -> "" in
      let rec entry o = if o + 16 > String.length auxv then None
        else let b = Bytes.of_string (String.sub auxv o 16) in
          if Bytes.get_int64_le b 0 = 9L then Some (Bytes.get_int64_le b 8) else entry (o + 16) in
      (match entry 0 with
       | Some a when Int64.sub a (Int64.of_int e.entry) <> pr.bias ->
           let b = Int64.sub a (Int64.of_int e.entry) in
           let d = Int64.to_int (Int64.sub b pr.bias) in
           let t = { t with syms = List.map (fun (s : Symbols.sym) -> { s with value = s.value + d }) t.syms;
                            text_start = t.text_start + d; text_end = t.text_end + d } in
           prog := Some { pr with bias = b; table = Some t; txtaddr = Int64.add pr.txtaddr (Int64.of_int d);
                                  dataddr = Int64.add pr.dataddr (Int64.of_int d) };
           das_table := Das.table t.syms;
           symbols ()
       | _ -> ())
  | _ -> ()

let attached () = List.map fst !ctls

let init (caps : < caps; .. >) =
  (* (a process gone between two reads: acid's error, not a crash) *)
  let exited f = try f () with Unix.Unix_error _ -> error "process exited" in
  Eval.load := (fun core a n -> exited (fun () -> load core a n));
  Eval.store := (fun a s -> exited (fun () -> store a s));
  Eval.symbol := symoff;
  Eval.local_addr := local_addr;
  Value.das := instruction;
  let def name f = Hashtbl.replace Eval.builtins name (fun vs -> exited (fun () -> f vs)) in
  let none = Value.empty in
  def "setproc" (fun vs -> attach caps (Int64.to_int (int "setproc" vs)); none);
  def "start" (fun vs -> msg caps (Int64.to_int (int "start" vs)) "start"; none);
  let stopping name = def name (fun vs ->
    let p = Int64.to_int (int name vs) in
    msg caps p name; notes caps p; dostop p; none) in
  stopping "stop"; stopping "startstop"; stopping "waitstop";
  def "kill" (fun vs -> let p = Int64.to_int (int "kill" vs) in msg caps p "kill"; deinstall p; none);
  def "status" (fun vs ->
    let p = Int64.to_int (int "status" vs) in
    if linux then
      (* (stat's third field, its state: t traced and stopped) *)
      match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/stat" p)) with
      | Some st ->
          (match String.rindex_opt st ')' with
           | Some i when i + 2 < String.length st ->
               Value.string (match st.[i + 2] with 't' | 'T' -> "Stopped" | 'Z' | 'X' -> "Broken" | 'R' -> "Running" | _ -> "Pending")
           | _ -> error "bad status for %d" p)
      | None -> error "open /proc/%d/status: process exited" p
    else
    match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/status" p)) with
    (* (its fields of fixed widths, devproc's: the name 28, the user 28,
     * the state 12; by place, not by blanks: a user may be empty) *)
    | Some s when String.length s >= 68 -> Value.string (String.trim (String.sub s 56 12))
    | Some s ->
        (match List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' s) with
         | _ :: _ :: state :: _ -> Value.string state
         | _ -> error "bad status for %d" p)
    | None -> error "open /proc/%d/status: process exited" p);
  def "reason" (fun vs ->
    let t = int "reason" vs in
    Value.string (if linux then (match Int64.to_int t with 5 -> "Breakpoint/Trace trap" | s -> signame s) else excep t));
  (* the maps, each {name, base, end, offset}: the process's (its text,
   * its data to the stack's top) or else the file's, as load reads them
   * (acid's map(), without its argument that moves one) *)
  def "map" (fun _ ->
    let seg name b e f = Value.list [ Value.string name; Value.int 'X' b; Value.int 'X' e; Value.int 'X' f ] in
    match !prog, !mem with
    | Some _, Some _ when linux ->
        Value.list (List.map (fun (n, b, e, f) -> seg n b e f) (linux_maps caps !pid))
    | Some p, Some _ -> Value.list [ seg "text" p.txtaddr (Int64.add p.txtaddr p.txtsz) p.txtaddr; seg "data" p.dataddr !stacktop p.dataddr ]
    | Some p, None ->
        Value.list [ seg "text" p.txtaddr (Int64.add p.txtaddr p.txtsz) 32L;
                     seg "data" p.dataddr (Int64.add p.dataddr p.datsz) (Int64.add 32L p.txtsz) ]
    | None, _ -> Value.empty);
  def "fnbound" (fun vs ->
    match fnbound (int "fnbound" vs) with
    | Some (a, b) -> Value.list [ Value.int 'X' a; Value.int 'X' b ]
    | None -> none);
  def "pcfile" (fun vs -> match file_line (int "pcfile" vs) with Some (f, _) -> Value.string f | None -> Value.string "?file?");
  def "pcline" (fun vs -> match file_line (int "pcline" vs) with Some (_, l) -> Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int l) | None -> Value.int 'D' 0L);
  def "strace" (function
    | [ { kind = Int pc; _ }; { kind = Int sp; _ }; { kind = Int link; _ } ] -> strace pc sp link
    | [ _; _; _ ] -> error "strace(pc, sp, link): bad type"
    | _ -> error "strace(pc, sp, link): arg count");
  (* "file:line": its first address (libmach's file2pc), a breakpoint's *)
  def "filepc" (fun vs ->
    match vs with
    | [ { kind = String w; _ } ] ->
        (match String.rindex_opt w ':' with
         | Some i ->
             let file = String.sub w 0 i and line = int_of_string_opt (String.sub w (i + 1) (String.length w - i - 1)) in
             (match !prog, line with
              | Some { dwarf = Some d; bias; _ }, Some l ->
                  (match Dwarf_line.file_pc d file l with
                   | Some pc -> Value.int 'V' (Int64.add (Int64.of_int pc) bias)
                   | None -> error "filepc: can't find address for: %s" w)
              | Some { table = Some t; _ }, Some l ->
                  (match Symbols.file_pc t file l with
                   | Some pc -> Value.int 'V' (Int64.of_int pc)
                   | None -> error "filepc: can't find address for: %s" w)
              | _ -> error "filepc: can't find address for: %s" w)
         | None -> error "filepc(\"file:line\")")
    | _ -> error "filepc(\"file:line\")");
  def "follow" (fun vs -> Value.list (List.map (Value.int 'X') (follow (int "follow" vs))));
  def "newproc" (fun vs ->
    let aout = match !prog with Some p -> p.path | None -> error "no program" in
    let args = match vs with
      | [ { kind = String s; _ } ] -> List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.map (fun c -> if c = '\t' then ' ' else c) s))
      | [] -> []
      | _ -> error "newproc(string)" in
    if linux then begin
      let child = try Ptrace.spawn caps aout (Array.of_list (aout :: args)) with Failure m -> error "newproc: %s" m in
      stops := (child, 5) :: List.remove_assoc child !stops;
      install caps child;
      attach caps child;
      rebias caps child;
      notes caps child;
      dostop child;
      Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int child)
    end else
    match CapUnix.fork caps () with
    | 0 ->
        (try
          let fd = FS.open_rw_fd caps (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/ctl" (CapUnix.getpid caps ())) in
          ignore (Unix.write fd (Bytes.of_string "hang") 0 4);
          Unix.close fd;
          CapUnix.execv caps aout (Array.of_list (aout :: args)); exit 1
        with _ -> exit 1)
    | child ->
        install caps child;
        msg caps child "waitstop";
        notes caps child;
        attach caps child;
        dostop child;
        Value.int 'D' (Int64.of_int child))

(* What acid looks at: the program (its a.out, its symbol and line
 * tables: lib_executable's Symbols) and the process run from it,
 * through Plan 9's /proc/$pid files (principia's acid: proc.c,
 * util.c's varsym and varreg, libmach's map.c), as on Plan 9 and under
 * mini-5i (plan_debugger.md, decision 12).
 *
 * The maps, libmach's: an address of the process, as * reads it, is in its
 * registers below the Ureg's size (/proc/$pid/regs: the variables R0,
 * PC, SP... hold their offsets there), in its text and its data up to
 * its stack's top (/proc/$pid/mem); without a process, and for @, in
 * the program's file (its text and data, as the a.out has them). The
 * symbols are acid's variables, each its address in X; symbols is the
 * list of them, {name, type, address}.
 *
 * A process: started by newproc, hung at its exec (ctl's hang) and
 * waited for; a stop (stop, startstop, waitstop) reads its notes
 * (notes) and calls the acid function stopped(pid), the library's
 * (port.acid prints where and why).
 *
 * On Linux (Ptrace.available: dune's mini-acid), the same by ptrace
 * (Ptrace.mli has the table): an ELF's program (gcc's, arm64), its
 * symbols moved where a PIE is put, /proc/$pid/mem, the registers
 * arm64's user_pt_regs and TYPE, the stop's signal; ctl's messages
 * are ptrace's calls, a note the signal's name. A frame's parameters
 * and locals (strace, f:v) by libmach's walk on arm, by Frame64's on
 * arm64: by the table's entries (7c's, mini-ld -g's .plan9.syms) or,
 * in a program of gcc's, by DWARF. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.kill; Cap.env >

(* the program read (the a.out's path): its variables made, the
 * registers' too; its line ("prog:arm plan 9 executable") printed *)
val program : < caps; .. > -> string -> unit

(* the symbols as variables (acid's varsym, after the libraries) *)
val symbols : unit -> unit

(* the program's declarations of its types, acid's text: the data
 * .acid, mini-ld -g's of mini-cc -g's (and mini-ml's) *)
val declarations : unit -> string option

(* the registers' variables and bpinst, the default set without a
 * program (varreg) *)
val registers : unit -> unit

(* the process attached (setproc) *)
val attach : < caps; .. > -> int -> unit

(* the processes attached, the last first (acid's proclist: at its end
 * it says how to kill them) *)
val attached : unit -> int list

(* the builtins of the program and the process put in Eval.builtins, the
 * maps put in Eval's load, store and symbol *)
val init : < caps; .. > -> unit

(* Linux's side of a process (plan_debugger.md, stage 8a; decision 12's
 * third side): what /proc/$pid's files give mini-acid on Plan 9, by
 * ptrace on Linux, as plan9port's libmach does (Linux.c):
 *
 *     Plan 9's /proc/$pid      Linux
 *     mem                      /proc/$pid/mem (a tracer's to read, write)
 *     regs (a Ureg)            PTRACE_GETREGSET (arm64's user_pt_regs)
 *     ctl: start, waitstop     PTRACE_CONT, waitpid
 *     ctl: stop, kill          SIGSTOP, SIGKILL
 *     a hung child's exec      PTRACE_TRACEME, then execv: stopped
 *
 * A signal's numbers are Linux's (5 SIGTRAP, a breakpoint's). Two
 * implementations: linux/'s (dune's, a C stub, linux/ptrace.c) and
 * linux/mini-ml/'s (the mkfile's: no ptrace, available false). *)

(* whether this build has ptrace (mini-acid on Linux, dune's) *)
val available : bool

(* a program run traced, stopped at its exec, its addresses not
 * randomized: its pid *)
val spawn : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; .. > -> string -> string array -> int

(* its registers' bytes, and written back *)
val getregs : int -> string
val setregs : int -> string -> unit

(* continued, a signal delivered (0: none) *)
val cont : int -> int -> unit

(* waited for: stopped by a signal (> 0, its number), exited (-1 - its
 * status), killed (-1000 - the signal) *)
val wait : int -> int

(* a signal sent (19 SIGSTOP, 9 SIGKILL) *)
val signal : < Cap.kill; .. > -> int -> int -> unit

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Value.mli *)

open Ast

type t = Ast.value

let int fmt i = { kind = Int i; fmt; comt = None }
let string s = { kind = String s; fmt = 's'; comt = None }
let empty = { kind = List None; fmt = 'X'; comt = None }

let list vs =
  let rec go = function [] -> None | v :: rest -> Some { value = v; next = go rest } in
  { kind = List (go vs); fmt = 'X'; comt = None }

let rec elements = function None -> [] | Some (c : cell) -> c.value :: elements c.next

let type_name (v : t) =
  match v.kind with Int _ -> "integer" | Float _ -> "float" | String _ -> "string" | List _ -> "list" | Code _ -> "code"

let formats = "aBbcCdDfFgGiIoOqQrRsSuUVWxXYZ38"

let size = function
  | 'A' | 'B' | 'D' | 'O' | 'Q' | 'R' | 'S' | 'U' | 'X' | 'a' | 's' -> 4
  | 'F' | 'G' | 'V' | 'W' | 'Y' | 'Z' -> 8
  | 'C' | 'b' | 'c' -> 1
  | 'd' | 'o' | 'q' | 'r' | 'u' | 'x' -> 2
  | 'f' | 'g' -> 4
  | '3' | '8' -> 10
  | _ -> 0

let truth (v : t) =
  match v.kind with
  | Int i -> i <> 0L
  | Float f -> f <> 0.0
  | String s -> s <> ""
  | List l -> l <> None
  | Code _ -> false

let rec equal (a : t) (b : t) =
  match a.kind, b.kind with
  | Int x, Int y -> x = y
  | Int x, Float y | Float y, Int x -> Int64.to_float x = y
  | Float x, Float y -> x = y
  | String x, String y -> x = y
  | List x, List y -> cells x y
  | _ -> false

and cells x y =
  match x, y with
  | None, None -> true
  | Some (c : cell), Some (d : cell) ->
      (match c.value.kind, d.value.kind with
       | Int _, Int _ | Float _, Float _ | String _, String _ | List _, List _ -> equal c.value d.value && cells c.next d.next
       | _ -> false)
  | _ -> false

(* the low bits of an integer, as C's casts of acid's patom take them *)
let low bits i = Int64.logand i (Int64.sub (Int64.shift_left 1L bits) 1L)
let signed32 i = Int64.of_int32 (Int64.to_int32 i)

(* the instruction at an address (Proc's, through Das): from the
 * process (core) or the program's file; None when it can't be read *)
let das : (bool -> int64 -> string option) ref = ref (fun _ _ -> None)

(* patom: an atom by its format *)
let atom ~symbol (v : t) =
  let i = match v.kind with Int i -> i | _ -> 0L in
  let wrong () = Printf.sprintf "*%c<%s>*" v.fmt (type_name v) in
  match v.fmt, v.kind with
  | 'c', _ -> String.make 1 (Char.chr (Int64.to_int (low 8 i)))
  | 'C', _ ->
      let c = Int64.to_int (low 8 i) in
      if c < 32 || c >= 127 then Printf.sprintf "%3d" c else "  " ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr c)
  | 'r', _ -> String.make 1 (Char.chr (Int64.to_int (low 8 i)))
  | 'B', _ -> "0b" ^ String.init 32 (fun k -> if Int64.logand i (Int64.shift_left 1L (31 - k)) <> 0L then '1' else '0')
  | 'b', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0x%02Lx" (low 8 i)
  | 'X', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0x%08Lx" (low 32 i)
  | 'x', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0x%04Lx" (low 16 i)
  | 'D', _ -> Int64.to_string (signed32 i)
  | 'd', _ | 'u', _ -> Int64.to_string (low 16 i)
  | 'U', _ -> Int64.to_string (low 32 i)
  | 'Z', _ -> Printf.sprintf "%Lu" i
  | 'V', _ -> Int64.to_string i
  | 'W', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0x%08Lx" i
  | 'Y', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0x%016Lx" i
  | 'o', _ | 'q', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0%011Lo" (low 16 i)
  | 'O', _ | 'Q', _ -> Printf.sprintf "0%06Lo" (low 32 i)
  | ('f' | 'F' | '3' | '8'), Float f -> Printf.sprintf "%g" f
  | ('f' | 'F' | '3' | '8'), _ -> wrong ()
  | ('s' | 'g' | 'G' | 'R'), String s -> s
  | ('s' | 'g' | 'G' | 'R'), _ -> wrong ()
  | ('a' | 'A'), _ -> symbol i
  | ('i' | 'I'), Int a ->
      (match !das false a with Some s -> s | None -> "no instruction")
  | ('i' | 'I'), _ -> wrong ()
  | _ -> ""

let rec show ~symbol (v : t) =
  match v.kind with
  | List l ->
      "{" ^ String.concat ", " (List.map (fun (e : t) ->
        match e.kind with String _ -> "\"" ^ atom ~symbol e ^ "\"" | _ -> show ~symbol e) (elements l)) ^ "}"
  | Code e -> Code.expr e ^ ";\n"
  | _ -> atom ~symbol v
debuggers/acid/Value.mli

(* acid's values (principia's acid.h: Store, List, Value): an integer,
 * a float, a string, a list, or code (eval's), each with its format,
 * a letter that says how it prints and how many bytes it is in
 * memory: X a word in hexadecimal, D a word in decimal, b a byte, s a
 * string, a an address said as a symbol and an offset... A constant is
 * W (8 bytes, hexadecimal), and a result takes its left operand's
 * format, so that a pointer stays one through arithmetic: p+4 is
 * printed as p is, and p++ adds what p's format says (8 for W, 4 for
 * X or D, 1 for b).
 *
 * The lists are acid's: cells linked, and changed in place by append
 * and +, as acid's (a variable's list grows where it is). The integers
 * are 64 bits (acid's vlong), whatever the machine running mini-acid. *)

type t = Ast.value

val int : char -> int64 -> t
val string : string -> t
val list : t list -> t
val empty : t

(* the list's values, in order *)
val elements : Ast.cell option -> t list

(* acid's typenames: integer, float, string, list, code *)
val type_name : t -> string

(* the bytes of the format in memory (fsize; 0: none) *)
val size : char -> int

(* true as acid's fbool: not 0, not empty *)
val truth : t -> bool

(* acid's equality (oeq: listcmp for lists) *)
val equal : t -> t -> bool

(* a value as print prints it (patom, blprint); [symbol] names an
 * address for the a and A formats ("0x..." without symbols) *)
val show : symbol:(int64 -> string) -> t -> string

(* the instruction at an address, the i format's: [!das core addr],
 * from the process (core) or the program's file (Proc's, by Das);
 * None when it can't be read *)
val das : (bool -> int64 -> string option) ref

(* the formats print and fmt know (acid's vfmt) *)
val formats : string

/* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. */
/* Linux's ptrace for mini-acid (Ptrace.mli): a program run traced,
 * stopped before its first instruction; its registers read and
 * written (arm64's user_pt_regs, by PTRACE_GETREGSET); continued, a
 * signal given or not; waited for. Its memory is /proc/PID/mem,
 * which the tracer reads and writes as a file (Ptrace.ml). */

#include <caml/mlvalues.h>
#include <caml/memory.h>
#include <caml/alloc.h>
#include <caml/fail.h>

#ifdef __linux__
#include <sys/ptrace.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <sys/user.h>
#include <sys/personality.h>
#include <elf.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/* the program forked and executed, traced (PTRACE_TRACEME), its
 * addresses not randomized (a session's are the same each run); the
 * exec's stop waited for */
value ml_ptrace_spawn(value path, value argv)
{
	CAMLparam2(path, argv);
	int n = Wosize_val(argv), i, st;
	char **a = malloc((n + 1) * sizeof(char *));
	char *p = strdup(String_val(path));
	pid_t pid;

	for(i = 0; i < n; i++)
		a[i] = strdup(String_val(Field(argv, i)));
	a[n] = NULL;
	pid = fork();
	if(pid == 0){
		ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME, 0, NULL, NULL);
		personality(ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE);
		execv(p, a);
		_exit(127);
	}
	for(i = 0; i < n; i++)
		free(a[i]);
	free(a);
	free(p);
	if(pid < 0)
		caml_failwith("fork");
	if(waitpid(pid, &st, 0) < 0 || !WIFSTOPPED(st))
		caml_failwith("exec");
	/* (the program killed if mini-acid dies) */
	ptrace(PTRACE_SETOPTIONS, pid, NULL, (void *)PTRACE_O_EXITKILL);
	CAMLreturn(Val_int(pid));
}

#ifdef __aarch64__
value ml_ptrace_getregs(value pid)
{
	CAMLparam1(pid);
	CAMLlocal1(s);
	struct user_regs_struct r;
	struct iovec io = { &r, sizeof r };

	if(ptrace(PTRACE_GETREGSET, Int_val(pid), (void *)NT_PRSTATUS, &io) < 0)
		caml_failwith(strerror(errno));
	s = caml_alloc_string(sizeof r);
	memcpy(Bytes_val(s), &r, sizeof r);
	CAMLreturn(s);
}

value ml_ptrace_setregs(value pid, value s)
{
	CAMLparam2(pid, s);
	struct user_regs_struct r;
	struct iovec io = { &r, sizeof r };

	if(caml_string_length(s) != sizeof r)
		caml_failwith("setregs: size");
	memcpy(&r, String_val(s), sizeof r);
	if(ptrace(PTRACE_SETREGSET, Int_val(pid), (void *)NT_PRSTATUS, &io) < 0)
		caml_failwith(strerror(errno));
	CAMLreturn(Val_unit);
}
#else
value ml_ptrace_getregs(value pid) { caml_failwith("ptrace: arm64's registers only"); }
value ml_ptrace_setregs(value pid, value s) { caml_failwith("ptrace: arm64's registers only"); }
#endif

value ml_ptrace_cont(value pid, value sig)
{
	if(ptrace(PTRACE_CONT, Int_val(pid), NULL, (void *)(long)Int_val(sig)) < 0)
		caml_failwith(strerror(errno));
	return Val_unit;
}

/* stopped: the signal (> 0); exited: -1 - its status; killed: -1000
 * - the signal */
value ml_ptrace_wait(value pid)
{
	int st;

	if(waitpid(Int_val(pid), &st, 0) < 0)
		caml_failwith(strerror(errno));
	if(WIFSTOPPED(st))
		return Val_int(WSTOPSIG(st));
	if(WIFEXITED(st))
		return Val_int(-1 - WEXITSTATUS(st));
	return Val_int(-1000 - WTERMSIG(st));
}

value ml_ptrace_signal(value pid, value sig)
{
	kill(Int_val(pid), Int_val(sig));
	return Val_unit;
}
#else
value ml_ptrace_spawn(value path, value argv) { caml_failwith("ptrace: Linux's only"); }
value ml_ptrace_getregs(value pid) { caml_failwith("ptrace: Linux's only"); }
value ml_ptrace_setregs(value pid, value s) { caml_failwith("ptrace: Linux's only"); }
value ml_ptrace_cont(value pid, value sig) { caml_failwith("ptrace: Linux's only"); }
value ml_ptrace_wait(value pid) { caml_failwith("ptrace: Linux's only"); }
value ml_ptrace_signal(value pid, value sig) { caml_failwith("ptrace: Linux's only"); }
#endif
debuggers/where/Where.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-where: the addresses of a trace named, by the program's own
 * symbol table and pc/line table (mini-ld -g's; lib_executable):
 * a function, the offset in it, and the file and the line.
 *
 *     mini-where tinybreakout 9c30 9cf0
 *     9c30 f12_brick_at<>+0x48 Breakout.ml:137
 *     9cf0 f12_move_ball<>+0x1c4 Breakout.ml:150
 *
 * An address is hexadecimal, 0x before it or not; what mini-9pi's
 * trace line has (lr=0x1698) and what an exception's (raised at:) can
 * be pasted, words that are no address left out. A line is the line of
 * the address's function, mini-ml's (plan_debugger.md, stage 1b), of
 * its instruction in an assembler's program.
 *
 * design:
 * The names come from the program that ran, not from a file beside it
 * that may be another link's (mini-ld -map's, which scripts/where.sh
 * read before): an executable says what it is (plan_debugger.md's
 * principles).
 *
 * References: Plan 9's src(1), which names a symbol's file and line
 * through acid. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

(* a word's address: hexadecimal, after an = or 0x *)
let address w =
  let w = match String.index_opt w '=' with Some i -> String.sub w (i + 1) (String.length w - i - 1) | None -> w in
  let w = if String.length w > 0 && w.[String.length w - 1] = ':' then String.sub w 0 (String.length w - 1) else w in
  let w = if String.length w > 2 && String.sub w 0 2 = "0x" then String.sub w 2 (String.length w - 2) else w in
  if w <> "" && String.for_all (fun c -> (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')) w then int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ w)
  else None

(* an a.out's tables, or an ELF's two sections of them (mini-ld -g's, as
 * mini-acid reads them) *)
let tables (bytes : string) : Symbols.t option =
  match Elf_file.read bytes with
  | None -> Symbols.read bytes
  | Some e -> (
      match Elf_file.section e ".plan9.syms", Elf_file.section e ".plan9.lines", Elf_file.text_segment e with
      | Some s, Some l, Some (g : Elf_file.segment) ->
          Some (Symbols.of_tables (Elf_file.bytes bytes s) (Elf_file.bytes bytes l) g.vaddr (g.vaddr + g.filesz))
      | _ -> None)

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  match List.tl (Array.to_list argv) with
  | prog :: (_ :: _ as words) -> (
      match FS.read caps (Fpath.v prog) with
      | exception Sys_error m -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "where: %s: %s\n" prog m); Exit.Err "open"
      | bytes ->
          match tables bytes with
          | None -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "where: %s: no symbol table (link it with mini-ld -g)\n" prog); Exit.Err "no table"
          | Some t ->
              List.iter (fun w ->
                match address w with
                | None -> ()
                | Some a ->
                    let name = match Symbols.func t a with Some (n, 0) -> n | Some (n, o) -> Printf.sprintf "%s+0x%x" n o | None -> "?" in
                    let line = match Symbols.file_line t a with Some (f, l) -> Printf.sprintf " %s:%d" (Filename.basename f) l | None -> "" in
                    Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%x %s%s\n" a name line)) words;
              Exit.OK)
  | _ -> Console.eprint caps "usage: where program address...\n"; Exit.Err "usage"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

editors/drscheme/DrScheme.mli

(* A toy version of DrScheme (PLT: Matthias Felleisen, Robert Bruce
 * Findler, Matthew Flatt, Shriram Krishnamurthi and others, Rice
 * University, 1995; renamed DrRacket in 2010), in the look of version
 * 209 (2004): the program in the Definitions window above, a prompt in
 * the Interactions window below, and Execute between them (-h says the
 * keys).
 *
 * DrScheme was made for teaching, with How to Design Programs (2001),
 * and everything in it follows from that: two windows, so that a
 * student defines, then experiments, as a mathematician does; teaching
 * languages that print a value as the expression making it ((list 1
 * 2), not (1 2)) and forbid what a beginner only gets wrong with;
 * errors that say what was expected, the culprit painted pink in the
 * program; images as values, printed as pictures; and the stepper,
 * evaluation shown as algebra.
 *
 * What's new here:
 *
 *  - Two windows over one machine (DrScheme_run): Execute makes a new
 *    Scheme machine (languages/scheme's Scheme_eval, a CESK machine),
 *    runs the definitions a form at a time, and leaves it for the
 *    prompt, whose expressions see the definitions -- the REPL, the
 *    oldest interface of Lisp, next to an editor.
 *
 *  - The program runs a budget of steps a frame (DrScheme_run's fuel):
 *    the machine stops where it is and goes on at the next frame, so an
 *    endless loop keeps the window alive, the running indicator
 *    turning, and Break is simply not running it any more. DrScheme
 *    needed a thread and a custodian for that; a machine whose stack is
 *    data needs a counter.
 *
 *  - Errors with their place (the model's pink): the language keeps
 *    each expression's span in the text (languages/sexpr), so the one
 *    that failed is painted, DrScheme's pink.
 *
 *  - Images as values (DrScheme_draw): (circle 20 "solid" "red") at
 *    the prompt prints a red disc. The language only describes images
 *    (Scheme_image); drawing them is the Playground's Bigbang way,
 *    whose combinators are 2htdp/image's.
 *
 *  - big-bang in the IDE (DrScheme_run): the machine stops at
 *    (big-bang ...) and hands the world to the host, which opens a
 *    window, calls the handlers -- each a nested run of the machine --
 *    on ticks, keys and the mouse, and gives the last world back as
 *    big-bang's value.
 *
 *  - The stepper (DrScheme_run): Beginning Student's evaluation as
 *    a series of rewritings (Scheme_step), the redex in green, what
 *    replaced it in purple.
 *
 * What it uses: languages/scheme and languages/sexpr (the language:
 * the reader, the machine, the stepper), gui's Text_edit (the two
 * texts: a piece table, undo for free), the Bigbang way (the images
 * drawn, HtDP's key and mouse events). Not Physics, not Camera2d.
 *
 * Exercises: Check Syntax (the arrows from each use to its binding,
 * the spans are there), check-expect and its report, Intermediate
 * Student (lambda, local), the teachpacks' own functions
 * (on-mouse's pointer shape, key-release), a file saved and opened,
 * the images inside a printed list drawn too, a garbage collector for
 * the machine's store.
 *
 * What Execute does, and the prompt after it:
 *
 *     the Definitions' text (a Text_edit)
 *        | Sexpr_read.read_all       the forms, each expression with
 *        |                           its span in the text
 *     a job: the forms to run        one at a time (DrScheme_run's work):
 *        | Scheme_syntax.top         a form checked, made an expression
 *        | Scheme_eval.start, run    a budget of steps a frame; then
 *        |-- Running                 on at the next frame
 *        |-- Done v                  v printed below; the next form
 *        |-- Failed err              said below, err's span pink above
 *        '-- World spec              big-bang: the host runs the world
 *     the machine, kept              Enter at the prompt: what was
 *                                    typed is a job on the same machine
 *
 * The program's parts, each with its own part of the story:
 *
 *     DrScheme          the first text, the first model, -h, the main
 *       | a frame: update, then view (the Playground's game)
 *       |-- DrScheme_update  the keys and the mouse, to whom they go; a
 *       |                    text changed by keys
 *       '-- DrScheme_view    the windows, back to front
 *     both over:
 *       DrScheme_run         Execute, Break, a budget of steps; a
 *                            big-bang run by the host; the stepper
 *       DrScheme_draw        where things are; text in cells, its colours;
 *                            an image described, drawn
 *       DrScheme_model       the types
 *
 * Where it stands in ix: a program of the Playground, as the games
 * are (a model, an update, a view of shapes; its window SDL's on
 * Linux, mini-rio's on mini-9pi), not a Tui program of cells as
 * mini-emacs and mini-turbopascal. The other programming environment
 * of ix, mini-turbopascal, is the same loop for another school: a
 * text, a key, the program run by a machine that gives the screen
 * back (Turbo_debug's slice is DrScheme_run's fuel). What differs is
 * what comes after the run: there a debugger over the machine's
 * stack, here a prompt in the program's own language and a stepper
 * that shows no machine at all.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The prompt is Lisp's read-eval-print loop, as old as Lisp: type an
 * expression, see its value, the definitions made so far all there.
 * What DrScheme added is the Execute button's rule: the prompt
 * always talks to the program as it is written above, run from
 * nothing. In a Lisp or a Smalltalk left running for days, what the
 * prompt knows and what the text says drift apart (a function
 * renamed is still there under its old name); a beginner cannot
 * tell which is wrong. Starting a new machine at each Execute
 * removes the question, at the price of running everything again.
 *
 * why-study:
 * It is the one editor here whose design starts from who uses it.
 * Each of its parts answers something a beginner was seen to
 * stumble on: the language levels, an error message that otherwise
 * speaks of features not yet taught; the pink, a message without a
 * place; the stepper, "what does the computer do with this?". The
 * editors for programmers (mini-ed, mini-emacs) assume the model is
 * known and make its use short.
 *
 * References: Robert Bruce Findler, John Clements, Cormac Flanagan,
 * Matthew Flatt, Shriram Krishnamurthi, Paul Steckler and Matthias
 * Felleisen, "DrScheme: A Programming Environment for Scheme"
 * (Journal of Functional Programming, 2002): the design told by its
 * authors, the levels, the stepper, Check Syntax. Felleisen,
 * Findler, Flatt and Krishnamurthi, "How to Design Programs" (MIT
 * Press, 2001), the course it was made for. Scheme_step.mli and
 * Scheme_eval.mli have the stepper's paper and the machine's.
 *)

(* ix: the author's playground's apps/devtools/TinyDrScheme.ml, its window's geometry and what every part draws with: the buttons, the lines of a text, the sections View: the texts and View: images; a string's characters are taken without a Seq, and text_view's x and y are a pair (docs/plans/plan_scheme.md) *)

open Playground

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The window's geometry *)

(* from the window's top-left corner, y going down, to the Playground's
 * centre *)
let at (x : float) (y : float) (s : shape) : shape = s |> move (x -. 500.) (500. -. y)
let box (c : color) (x : float) (y : float) (w : float) (h : float) : shape = rectangle c w h |> at (x +. (w /. 2.)) (y +. (h /. 2.))

let frame (c : color) (x : float) (y : float) (w : float) (h : float) : shape list =
  [ box c x y w 1.; box c x (y +. h -. 1.) w 1.; box c x y 1. h; box c (x +. w -. 1.) y 1. h ]

(* a character's cell: the text drawn in columns, as a code editor's *)
let cw = 11.
let lh = 20.

let glyph (c : color) (x : float) (y : float) (ch : char) : shape list =
  if ch = ' ' || ch = '\n' then [] else [ words c (String.make 1 ch) |> scale 1.55 |> at (x +. (cw /. 2.)) (y +. (lh /. 2.)) ]

let label (c : color) (x : float) (y : float) (s : string) : shape list = List.concat (List.mapi (fun i ch -> glyph c (x +. (float_of_int i *. cw)) y ch) (List.init (String.length s) (String.get s)))

(* the text in a proportional font, for the window's own words *)
let caption (c : color) (x : float) (y : float) (size : float) (s : string) : shape = words c s |> scale (size /. 10.) |> at x y

let break_button = (890., 42., 100., 46.)
let language_button = (10., 964., 360., 32.)

(* a toolbar button: raised, its icon and its word *)
let button ((x, y, w, h) : float * float * float * float) (icon : shape list) (word : string) (enabled : bool) : shape list =
  [ box (rgb 250 250 245) x y w h ] @ frame (rgb 160 160 150) x y w h @ List.map (at (x +. 20.) (y +. (h /. 2.))) icon
  @ [ caption (if enabled then black else rgb 160 160 160) (x +. 24. +. ((w -. 24.) /. 2.)) (y +. (h /. 2.)) 16. word ]

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The lines of a text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the lines of a text, each with the offset it starts at *)
let lines (s : string) : (int * string) list =
  let rec go start acc = match String.index_from_opt s start '\n' with Some j -> go (j + 1) ((start, String.sub s start (j - start)) :: acc) | None -> List.rev ((start, String.sub s start (String.length s - start)) :: acc) in
  go 0 []

(* the line and column of an offset *)
let place (s : string) (pos : int) : int * int =
  let ls = lines s in
  let rec go i = function (start, l) :: rest -> if pos <= start + String.length l || rest = [] then (i, pos - start) else go (i + 1) rest | [] -> (0, 0) in
  go 0 ls

let offset (s : string) (line : int) (col : int) : int =
  match List.nth_opt (lines s) line with Some (start, l) -> start + max 0 (min col (String.length l)) | None -> String.length s

(*****************************************************************************)
(* View: the texts *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* DrScheme's colours for its program text *)
let paren_color = rgb 132 60 36
let symbol_color = rgb 38 38 128
let constant_color = rgb 41 128 38
let comment_color = rgb 194 116 31

(* each character's colour: a small lexer over the whole text *)
let colors (s : string) : color array =
  let n = String.length s in
  let a = Array.make n symbol_color in
  let fill i j c = for k = i to min (n - 1) (j - 1) do a.(k) <- c done in
  let delim c = String.contains " \n\t()[]\";'" c in
  let rec go i =
    if i < n then
      match s.[i] with
      | ';' ->
          let j = match String.index_from_opt s i '\n' with Some j -> j | None -> n in
          fill i j comment_color; go j
      | '"' ->
          let rec close j = if j >= n then n else if s.[j] = '\\' then close (j + 2) else if s.[j] = '"' then j + 1 else close (j + 1) in
          let j = close (i + 1) in
          fill i j constant_color; go j
      | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' -> a.(i) <- paren_color; go (i + 1)
      | '\'' -> a.(i) <- constant_color; go (i + 1)
      | c when delim c -> go (i + 1)
      | _ ->
          let j = ref i in
          while !j < n && not (delim s.[!j]) do incr j done;
          let tok = String.sub s i (!j - i) in
          if s.[i] = '#' || float_of_string_opt tok <> None || tok = "true" || tok = "false" || tok = "empty" then fill i !j constant_color;
          go !j
  in
  go 0;
  a

(* the parenthesis matching the one beside the caret: DrScheme greys
   the expression between them *)
let matching (s : string) (caret : int) : (int * int) option =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec back i depth = if i < 0 then None else match s.[i] with ')' | ']' -> back (i - 1) (depth + 1) | '(' | '[' -> if depth = 1 then Some i else back (i - 1) (depth - 1) | _ -> back (i - 1) depth in
  let rec fwd i depth = if i >= n then None else match s.[i] with '(' | '[' -> fwd (i + 1) (depth + 1) | ')' | ']' -> if depth = 1 then Some (i + 1) else fwd (i + 1) (depth - 1) | _ -> fwd (i + 1) depth in
  if caret > 0 && (s.[caret - 1] = ')' || s.[caret - 1] = ']') then Option.map (fun i -> (i, caret)) (back (caret - 1) 0)
  else if caret < n && (s.[caret] = '(' || s.[caret] = '[') then Option.map (fun j -> (caret, j)) (fwd caret 0)
  else None

(* [text_view ...]: lines of text from line [top], with backgrounds over
   character ranges *)
(* (ix: at, where it was ~x and ~y: eight parameters are one more than
 * mini-ml's code for arm takes) *)
let text_view ~(at : float * float) ~(rows : int) ~(top : int) (s : string) (color_of : int -> color) (shades : ((int * int) * color) list) (caret : int option) : shape list =
  let x, y = at in
  let shapes = ref [] in
  let push l = shapes := l @ !shapes in
  List.iteri
    (fun i (start, l) ->
      let row = i - top in
      if row >= 0 && row < rows then begin
        let ly = y +. (float_of_int row *. lh) in
        let len = min cols (String.length l) in
        (* the shades first, under the characters *)
        List.iter
          (fun ((a, b), c) ->
            let a = max a start and b = min b (start + len + 1) in
            if a < b then push [ box c (x +. (float_of_int (a - start) *. cw)) ly (float_of_int (b - a) *. cw) lh ])
          shades;
        for k = 0 to len - 1 do
          push (glyph (color_of (start + k)) (x +. (float_of_int k *. cw)) ly l.[k])
        done;
        match caret with
        | Some c when c >= start && c <= start + String.length l -> push [ box black (x +. (float_of_int (c - start) *. cw) -. 1.) (ly +. 1.) 2. (lh -. 2.) ]
        | _ -> ()
      end)
    (lines s);
  List.rev !shapes

let color_of_name (name : string) : color =
  match name with
  | "red" -> rgb 255 0 0
  | "green" -> rgb 0 160 0
  | "blue" -> rgb 0 0 255
  | "yellow" -> rgb 255 255 0
  | "gold" -> rgb 255 215 0
  | "orange" -> rgb 255 165 0
  | "purple" -> rgb 160 32 240
  | "black" -> black
  | "white" -> white
  | "gray" | "grey" -> rgb 190 190 190
  | "darkgray" | "darkgrey" -> rgb 110 110 110
  | "brown" -> rgb 165 42 42
  | "pink" -> rgb 255 192 203
  | "cyan" -> rgb 0 255 255
  | "magenta" -> rgb 255 0 255
  | "lightblue" -> rgb 173 216 230
  | "darkgreen" -> rgb 0 100 0
  | "navy" -> rgb 0 0 128
  | "tan" -> rgb 210 180 140
  | _ -> rgb 128 128 128

(* the language's description drawn by the Bigbang way's combinators *)
let rec picture (i : Scheme_image.t) : Bigbang.image =
  let mode (m : Scheme_image.mode) : Bigbang.mode = match m with Solid -> Solid | Outline -> Outline in
  match i with
  | Circle (r, md, c) -> Bigbang.circle r (mode md) (color_of_name c)
  | Ellipse (w, h, md, c) -> Bigbang.ellipse w h (mode md) (color_of_name c)
  | Rectangle (w, h, md, c) -> Bigbang.rectangle w h (mode md) (color_of_name c)
  | Triangle (s, md, c) -> Bigbang.triangle s (mode md) (color_of_name c)
  | Text (s, size, c) -> Bigbang.text s size (color_of_name c)
  | Scene (w, h) -> Bigbang.empty_scene w h
  | Beside (a, b) -> Bigbang.beside (picture a) (picture b)
  | Above (a, b) -> Bigbang.above (picture a) (picture b)
  | Overlay (a, b) -> Bigbang.overlay (picture a) (picture b)
  | Place (a, x, y, s) -> Bigbang.place_image (picture a) x y (picture s)

(* DrScheme_draw: what every part of mini-drscheme draws with: where
   things are in the window, a program's text in cells, an image of the
   language. Its window is the Playground's, 1000 by 1000 whatever the
   size on the screen, and it is laid out as DrScheme 209 was on Windows
   XP:

       y    0 +------------------------------------------+
              | title bar                                |  34
           34 +------------------------------------------+
              | Untitled (define ...)  Step Execute Break|  62, the toolbar
           96 +------------------------------------------+
              | Definitions                              |
              |   89 columns, 23 lines                   | 468
              |                                          |
          564 +------------------- ---- -----------------+   8, the divider
          572 +------------------------------------------+
              | Interactions                             | 386
              |   > (fact 5)                             |
              |   120                                    |
          958 +------------------------------------------+
          960 | Language: ... (click)      running 1:0   |  40, the status
         1000 +------------------------------------------+

   The Playground's coordinates have (0, 0) in the centre and y going up,
   for games; a window with lines of text wants its top-left corner and
   y going down. [at] is the one place that knows, and [mouse_at] the way
   back: every other number in the program counts from the corner.

   A program's text is drawn in cells of 11 by 20, a character a shape,
   as a code editor's: a column is a multiplication away, and the mouse
   finds its character by a division. The window's own words (a button,
   the title) are in a proportional font, [caption]. Text_edit knows
   offsets and DrScheme knows lines, so a key going up goes through both:

       "(define x\n  1)\n"     the caret at 12
         place              -> line 1, column 2
         ArrowUp, offset    -> line 0, column 2: the offset 2

   Each character has its colour, the expression at the caret greyed:

       (define (fact n)     parentheses brown, symbols dark blue,
         ;; n is a number   comments orange,
         (cond [else "x"])) constants green: numbers, strings, #t, empty,
                            quote

   [colors] is a small lexer over the whole text, made at each frame, and
   it is not Sexpr_read, for a reason: the text coloured is being typed.
   The reader stops at the first thing wrong, and raises; a colourer must
   go on to the end over a string not yet closed or an extra parenthesis,
   and needs to know no more than where a token ends. It returns an array
   of a colour by offset, so that [text_view] has no lexing to do and
   stays the same for any function from an offset to a colour. [matching]
   counts depth outward from the caret, in the text and not in the forms
   read, for the same reason: DrScheme's way of showing what a closing
   parenthesis closes.

   [picture] is the whole border between the language, which is text and
   numbers and can be tested without a screen (Scheme_image.mli says
   why), and the program that has a window:

       (beside (circle 20 "solid" "red") (circle 20 "solid" "gold"))
         the language: Beside (Circle (20., Solid, "red"), Circle ...)
         | picture
         | Bigbang.beside (Bigbang.circle 20. Solid red) (...)
         | Bigbang.to_shape, then scaled and placed by the caller
         v
       the Playground's shape, for a frame

   It is a fold over the tree: each constructor one of the Bigbang way's
   combinators, which are the same ones under the same names. A colour is
   a name in the language, a word in a string as in 2htdp/image, and the
   names known are a few of those a program of the book uses. A name not
   known is grey rather than a failure: nothing here would say where the
   mistake is, and a grey disc can be seen.

   others:
   mini-emacs's colours come from Highlight_code, the same categories for
   every language, each turning its own tokens into them; Emacs itself
   colours by regular expressions on the lines shown (font-lock), which
   sees little and costs little. For Scheme, whose syntax is parentheses
   and tokens, a small function does it. *)
