(* Render: what the player sees, Doom's way (r_main.c, r_bsp.c,
 * r_segs.c, r_plane.c, r_draw.c, r_sky.c): a picture of the palette's
 * indices, a byte a pixel, 320 by 200, made column by column with no
 * polygon and no z-buffer.
 *
 * 1. The tree, nearest first (R_RenderBSPNode): at each node, the side
 *    the eye is on, then the other if its box can be seen at all
 *    (R_CheckBBox: its corners' angles within the view, and not in
 *    columns already closed). A subsector's segs come out in an order
 *    where nothing drawn later is in front of what is already there.
 *
 * 2. A seg (R_AddLine): its two ends' angles from the eye; seen from
 *    behind (more than half a turn between them) or out of the view's
 *    90 degrees, nothing; else the columns it covers, x1 to x2. A wall
 *    (one-sided, or a door closed) closes them; a seg between two
 *    sectors only narrows them, the next sector seen through it.
 *
 * 3. Its columns (R_StoreWallRange, R_RenderSegLoop), from the left,
 *    its scale (1 / distance: linear across the screen) stepped:
 *
 *        ceilingclip ---  .........   the ceiling's visplane: from the
 *                         |  top   |  clip down to the wall's top
 *            worldhigh -> |========|  an upper texture (the next
 *                         |        |  sector's ceiling is lower)
 *                         | (open) |  the next sector, drawn later
 *             worldlow -> |========|  a lower texture (a step)
 *                         | bottom |  the floor's visplane
 *          floorclip ---  .........
 *
 *    The texture's column at x is the seg's offset less the tangent of
 *    the ray's angle to the seg's normal times its distance; its rows
 *    are a step of 1 / scale texels a pixel (R_DrawColumn), through the
 *    colormap of its light.
 *
 * 4. The floors and ceilings (R_DrawPlanes): each wall marked, column
 *    by column, which rows of which visplane (a height, a flat, a
 *    light) show above and below it. A visplane's columns are then
 *    drawn as rows (R_MakeSpans): along a row of the screen a flat is
 *    at one distance, height * yslope, its texels a step of distance /
 *    projection a pixel (R_MapPlane, R_DrawSpan: Mode 7's idea). The
 *    sky is a texture by the view's angle, four times a turn, always
 *    bright.
 *
 * 5. The things and the see-through (R_DrawMasked, r_things.c): each
 *    seg drawn left a drawseg, its columns, its scales and the clips
 *    as they were; each thing in a sector the tree went through was
 *    projected (R_ProjectSprite: its picture's columns, its scale, the
 *    rotation seen). They are drawn farthest first, each clipped by the
 *    drawsegs nearer than it (their silhouettes: what is above a step's
 *    top, below a window's lintel); a two-sided line's middle texture
 *    (a grate, a platform's edge) is drawn the same way, its columns
 *    the posts of its patch, after the things behind it.
 *
 * 6. The light (R_InitLightTables): a sector's 0 to 255 is 16 levels;
 *    a wall's colormap is its level less its scale's half (48 steps), a
 *    flat's its level less 80 / distance's half (128 steps of 16 units);
 *    a wall along x a level darker, along y a level lighter (the "fake
 *    contrast" that shows the corners).
 *
 * What is id's and what is not: the order, the tables and the
 * formulas are r_*.c's, named in comments by their functions. Its
 * fixed point is 16.16 in 32 bits, which a map's coordinates overflow
 * on the Pi1's 31-bit ints: the geometry here is floats (a seg's
 * angles, its scale, a column's texture), the loops of pixels integers
 * (16.16 in a column, a flat's coordinates taken modulo 64 before). A
 * texture's height wraps where it is (id's wrapped at 128).
 * Not here: the player's weapon (psprites), the fuzz of a spectre, the
 * limits (MAXVISPLANES, MAXDRAWSEGS: none here).
 *
 * Its parts are id's files: View (r_main.c, r_draw.c: the state, the
 * tables, R_DrawColumn), Bsp (r_bsp.c: 1, 2), Segs (r_segs.c: 3),
 * Planes (r_plane.c: 4), Sprites (r_things.c: 5), and this one,
 * R_RenderView (r_main.c), the frame from the five.
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-doom: Doom.ml asks a frame of it with the
 * player's eye; Play's moves change what Level holds, which it draws as
 * it is.
 *
 * history:
 * The BSP is Henry Fuchs, Zvi Kedem and Bruce Naylor's ("On Visible
 * Surface Generation by A Priori Tree Structures", SIGGRAPH 1980);
 * John Carmack used it for Doom (1993) in its front-to-back order with
 * the clip arrays, after Wolfenstein 3D's raycaster. The playground's
 * TinyDoom (games/fps in ~/playground) draws the same order with
 * shapes and flat colours; ocamldoom (François Pessaux, 1997) with
 * textures, over its own BSP. *)

type t

(* [create width height]: a renderer of that picture (320 by 200 is
 * Doom's; any size, the view's 90 degrees across its width) *)
val create : int -> int -> t

(* the picture: width * height indices of the palette, row after row *)
val screen : t -> Bytes.t
val width : t -> int
val height : t -> int

(* [frame r level textures sprites things tic x y z angle]: the picture
 * of the eye at (x, y), height z, looking at angle (radians); the
 * things by their sectors' numbers, each at its frame of that tic *)
val frame : t -> Level.t -> Textures.t -> Things.sprites -> Things.mobj list array -> int -> float -> float -> float -> float -> unit

(* this frame's: the segs drawn, the visplanes *)
val segs_drawn : t -> int
val planes_drawn : t -> int

(* [set_extralight r n]: the next frames lit [n] levels more (a shot's
 * flash: Weapons' Light1, Light2) *)
val set_extralight : t -> int -> unit

(* [hand r textures sprites light psprites]: R_DrawPlayerSprites: the
 * weapon in hand and its flash, each a state and its place, over the
 * last frame, lit by [light] (the player's sector's) *)
val hand :
  t -> Textures.t -> Things.sprites -> int ->
  (Info.state * float * float) list -> unit
games/fps/doom/render/Segs.ml
9888
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Segs.mli *)

(* OPTIMIZATION: Int's min and max, not Stdlib's polymorphic ones (as
 * View's) *)
let min = Int.min and max = Int.max

(* R_StoreWallRange: the seg's columns start to stop, which are open;
 * [angle1] its first end's angle (rw_angle1) *)
let store_wall_range (r : View.t) (textures : Textures.t) (level : Level.t) (pl : View.planes) (seg : Level.seg) (angle1 : float) (start : int)
    (stop : int) : unit =
  r.segs <- r.segs + 1;
  let side = seg.side and line = level.lines.(seg.seg_line) and front = seg.front_sector in
  let normalangle = View.norm (seg.angle +. View.half_pi) in
  let offsetangle = Float.min View.half_pi (Float.abs (View.signed (normalangle -. angle1))) in
  let distangle = View.half_pi -. offsetangle in
  let hyp = View.point_to_dist r seg.sv1.x seg.sv1.y in
  let distance = hyp *. View.fsin distangle in
  (* R_ScaleFromGlobalAngle *)
  let scale_at (visangle : float) : float =
    let sinea = View.fsin (View.half_pi +. (visangle -. r.viewangle)) and sineb = View.fsin (View.half_pi +. (visangle -. normalangle)) in
    let num = r.projection *. sineb and den = distance *. sinea in
    if den > num /. 65536. then Float.max (1. /. 256.) (Float.min 64. (num /. den)) else 64. in
  let scale1 = scale_at (r.viewangle +. r.xtoviewangle.(start)) in
  let scalestep = if stop > start then (scale_at (r.viewangle +. r.xtoviewangle.(stop)) -. scale1) /. float (stop - start) else 0. in
  let worldtop0 = front.ceiling -. r.viewz and worldbottom = front.floor -. r.viewz in
  let theight (k : int) : float = if k < 0 then 0. else float textures.textures.(k).height in
  let midtexture = ref (-1) and toptexture = ref (-1) and bottomtexture = ref (-1) in
  let midmid = ref 0. and topmid = ref 0. and bottommid = ref 0. in
  let worldtop = ref worldtop0 and worldhigh = ref 0. and worldlow = ref 0. in
  let markfloor = ref true and markceiling = ref true in
  (match seg.back_sector with
  | None ->
      midtexture := side.middle;
      midmid := (if line.flags land Level.lower_unpegged <> 0 then front.floor +. theight side.middle -. r.viewz else worldtop0) +. side.yoffset
  | Some back ->
      worldhigh := back.ceiling -. r.viewz;
      worldlow := back.floor -. r.viewz;
      (* (a sky above both: no wall between, the sky goes on) *)
      if front.ceilingpic = textures.sky_flat && back.ceilingpic = textures.sky_flat then worldtop := !worldhigh;
      markfloor := !worldlow <> worldbottom || back.floorpic <> front.floorpic || back.light <> front.light;
      markceiling := !worldhigh <> !worldtop || back.ceilingpic <> front.ceilingpic || back.light <> front.light;
      (* (a door closed) *)
      if back.ceiling <= front.floor || back.floor >= front.ceiling then begin markceiling := true; markfloor := true end;
      if !worldhigh < !worldtop then begin
        toptexture := side.top;
        topmid := (if line.flags land Level.upper_unpegged <> 0 then !worldtop else back.ceiling +. theight side.top -. r.viewz) +. side.yoffset
      end;
      if !worldlow > worldbottom then begin
        bottomtexture := side.bottom;
        bottommid := (if line.flags land Level.lower_unpegged <> 0 then !worldtop else !worldlow) +. side.yoffset
      end);
  let worldtop = !worldtop and worldhigh = !worldhigh and worldlow = !worldlow in
  (* the drawseg: what this seg hides of the things behind it *)
  let masked = match seg.back_sector with Some _ -> side.middle >= 0 | None -> false in
  let ds : View.drawseg =
    { dx1 = start; dx2 = stop; dscale1 = scale1; dscale2 = scale1 +. (scalestep *. float (stop - start)); dscalestep = scalestep;
      silhouette = 0; bsilheight = 0.; tsilheight = 0.; sprtopclip = [||]; sprtopoff = 0; sprbottomclip = [||]; sprbottomoff = 0;
      maskedcol = (if masked then Array.make (stop - start + 1) View.unset else [||]); dseg = seg } in
  (match seg.back_sector with
  | None ->
      ds.silhouette <- 3;
      ds.sprtopclip <- r.screenheightarray;
      ds.sprbottomclip <- r.negonearray;
      ds.bsilheight <- infinity;
      ds.tsilheight <- neg_infinity
  | Some back ->
      if front.floor > back.floor then begin ds.silhouette <- 1; ds.bsilheight <- front.floor end
      else if back.floor > r.viewz then begin ds.silhouette <- 1; ds.bsilheight <- infinity end;
      if front.ceiling < back.ceiling then begin ds.silhouette <- ds.silhouette lor 2; ds.tsilheight <- front.ceiling end
      else if back.ceiling < r.viewz then begin ds.silhouette <- ds.silhouette lor 2; ds.tsilheight <- neg_infinity end;
      if back.ceiling <= front.floor then begin ds.sprbottomclip <- r.negonearray; ds.bsilheight <- infinity; ds.silhouette <- ds.silhouette lor 1 end;
      if back.floor >= front.ceiling then begin ds.sprtopclip <- r.screenheightarray; ds.tsilheight <- neg_infinity; ds.silhouette <- ds.silhouette lor 2 end);
  r.drawsegs <- ds :: r.drawsegs;
  (* the texture's first column, and the lights *)
  let rel = View.signed (normalangle -. angle1) in
  let offset = hyp *. View.fsin (Float.min View.half_pi (Float.abs rel)) in
  let offset = (if rel > 0. then -.offset else offset) +. side.xoffset +. seg.offset in
  let lightnum =
    View.light_level front.light + r.extralight + (if seg.sv1.y = seg.sv2.y then -1 else if seg.sv1.x = seg.sv2.x then 1 else 0) in
  let walllights = r.scalelight.(max 0 (min (View.lightlevels - 1) lightnum)) in
  (* (a plane on the eye's other side is not seen) *)
  if front.floor >= r.viewz then markfloor := false;
  if front.ceiling <= r.viewz && front.ceilingpic <> textures.sky_flat then markceiling := false;
  let markfloor = !markfloor && pl.floorplane <> None and markceiling = !markceiling && pl.ceilingplane <> None in
  let cy = float r.centery in
  let topfrac = ref (cy -. (worldtop *. scale1)) and topstep = -.(scalestep *. worldtop) in
  let bottomfrac = ref (cy -. (worldbottom *. scale1)) and bottomstep = -.(scalestep *. worldbottom) in
  let pixhigh = ref (cy -. (worldhigh *. scale1)) and pixhighstep = -.(scalestep *. worldhigh) in
  let pixlow = ref (cy -. (worldlow *. scale1)) and pixlowstep = -.(scalestep *. worldlow) in
  let ceilingplane = match pl.ceilingplane with Some p when markceiling -> Some (Planes.check_plane r p start stop) | p -> p in
  let floorplane = match pl.floorplane with Some p when markfloor -> Some (Planes.check_plane r p start stop) | p -> p in
  pl.ceilingplane <- ceilingplane;
  pl.floorplane <- floorplane;
  let tex (k : int) : Textures.texture = textures.textures.(textures.texture_translation.(k)) in
  let colormaps = textures.colormaps in
  let lightscale = 16. *. 320. /. float r.width in
  let centerangle = View.half_pi +. r.viewangle -. normalangle in
  let scale = ref scale1 in
  let ceilingclip = r.ceilingclip and floorclip = r.floorclip in
  (* R_RenderSegLoop *)
  for x = start to stop do
    let yl = max (View.iceil !topfrac) (ceilingclip.(x) + 1) in
    (match ceilingplane with
    | Some p when markceiling ->
        let top = ceilingclip.(x) + 1 and bottom = min (yl - 1) (floorclip.(x) - 1) in
        if top <= bottom then begin p.top.(x + 1) <- top; p.bottom.(x + 1) <- bottom end
    | _ -> ());
    let yh = min (View.ifloor !bottomfrac) (floorclip.(x) - 1) in
    (match floorplane with
    | Some p when markfloor ->
        let top = max (yh + 1) (ceilingclip.(x) + 1) and bottom = floorclip.(x) - 1 in
        if top <= bottom then begin p.top.(x + 1) <- top; p.bottom.(x + 1) <- bottom end
    | _ -> ());
    let sc = !scale in
    let texturecolumn = View.ifloor (offset -. (View.ftan90 (centerangle +. r.xtoviewangle.(x)) *. distance)) in
    let column (t : Textures.texture) : int = texturecolumn land t.width_mask in
    if masked then ds.maskedcol.(x - start) <- texturecolumn;
    let cmap = walllights.(max 0 (min (View.maxlightscale - 1) (int_of_float (sc *. lightscale)))) in
    if !midtexture >= 0 then begin
      let t = tex !midtexture in
      View.draw_column r x yl yh !midmid sc t.source t.columns.(column t) colormaps cmap;
      ceilingclip.(x) <- r.height;
      floorclip.(x) <- -1
    end
    else begin
      if !toptexture >= 0 then begin
        let mid = min (View.ifloor !pixhigh) (floorclip.(x) - 1) in
        if mid >= yl then begin
          let t = tex !toptexture in
          View.draw_column r x yl mid !topmid sc t.source t.columns.(column t) colormaps cmap;
          ceilingclip.(x) <- mid
        end
        else ceilingclip.(x) <- yl - 1
      end
      else if markceiling then ceilingclip.(x) <- yl - 1;
      if !bottomtexture >= 0 then begin
        let mid = max (View.iceil !pixlow) (ceilingclip.(x) + 1) in
        if mid <= yh then begin
          let t = tex !bottomtexture in
          View.draw_column r x mid yh !bottommid sc t.source t.columns.(column t) colormaps cmap;
          floorclip.(x) <- mid
        end
        else floorclip.(x) <- yh + 1
      end
      else if markfloor then floorclip.(x) <- yh + 1
    end;
    scale := sc +. scalestep;
    topfrac := !topfrac +. topstep;
    bottomfrac := !bottomfrac +. bottomstep;
    pixhigh := !pixhigh +. pixhighstep;
    pixlow := !pixlow +. pixlowstep
  done;
  (* the clips as they are now, for the things behind *)
  if (ds.silhouette land 2 <> 0 || masked) && Array.length ds.sprtopclip = 0 then begin
    ds.sprtopclip <- Array.sub ceilingclip start (stop - start + 1);
    ds.sprtopoff <- start
  end;
  if (ds.silhouette land 1 <> 0 || masked) && Array.length ds.sprbottomclip = 0 then begin
    ds.sprbottomclip <- Array.sub floorclip start (stop - start + 1);
    ds.sprbottomoff <- start
  end;
  if masked && ds.silhouette land 2 = 0 then begin ds.silhouette <- ds.silhouette lor 2; ds.tsilheight <- neg_infinity end;
  if masked && ds.silhouette land 1 = 0 then begin ds.silhouette <- ds.silhouette lor 1; ds.bsilheight <- infinity end
games/fps/doom/render/Segs.mli
1926
(* Segs: a seg's columns drawn (Doom's r_segs.c), the walls.
 *
 * The seg's scale (1 / distance, times the projection) at its first
 * and last columns (R_ScaleFromGlobalAngle), stepped linearly between
 * (1 / z is linear across the screen); in each column, from the
 * ceiling down:
 *
 *        ceilingclip ---  .........   the ceiling's visplane: from the
 *                         |  top   |  clip down to the wall's top
 *            worldhigh -> |========|  an upper texture (the next
 *                         |        |  sector's ceiling is lower)
 *                         | (open) |  the next sector, drawn later
 *             worldlow -> |========|  a lower texture (a step)
 *                         | bottom |  the floor's visplane
 *          floorclip ---  .........
 *
 * A one-sided seg (a wall) draws its middle texture and closes the
 * column; a two-sided one draws its upper and lower textures and
 * narrows the clips, through which what is behind is seen. The
 * texture's column at x is the seg's offset less the tangent of the
 * ray's angle to the seg's normal times its distance; its rows are
 * pegged to the ceiling or the floor by the line's flags; its light is
 * the sector's, darker with the distance, a level less along x and
 * more along y (the "fake contrast").
 *
 * Each seg leaves a drawseg: its columns, scales, the clips as they
 * were, what of the things behind it it hides (its silhouette), and a
 * two-sided line's middle texture's columns, drawn last (Sprites).
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-doom: Render's walk of the tree calls it for
 * each run of open columns a seg covers. *)

(* [store_wall_range r textures level planes seg angle1 start stop]
 * (R_StoreWallRange): the seg's columns start to stop; [angle1] its
 * first end's angle from the eye *)
val store_wall_range : View.t -> Textures.t -> Level.t -> View.planes -> Level.seg -> float -> int -> int -> unit
games/fps/doom/render/Sprites.ml
9368
(* Claude Code

(* See Sprites.mli *)

(* OPTIMIZATION: Int's min and max, not Stdlib's polymorphic ones (as
 * View's) *)
let min = Int.min and max = Int.max

(* R_ProjectSprite: a thing's picture's columns and scale, if it can be
 * seen *)
let project_sprite (r : View.t) (sprites : Things.sprites) (tic : int) (m : Things.mobj) : unit =
  let tr_x = m.mx -. r.viewx and tr_y = m.my -. r.viewy in
  let viewcos = View.fcos r.viewangle and viewsin = View.fsin r.viewangle in
  let tz = (tr_x *. viewcos) +. (tr_y *. viewsin) in
  (* (behind the eye, or too near) *)
  if tz >= 4. then begin
    let xscale = r.projection /. tz in
    let tx = (tr_x *. viewsin) -. (tr_y *. viewcos) in
    if Float.abs tx <= 4. *. tz then
      match Things.frame sprites m tic with
      | None -> ()
      | Some (f, bright) ->
          (* (the rotation: the eye's angle to it less its own, in eighths
           * of a turn, the front's eighth centred on 0) *)
          let rot = if f.rotates then int_of_float (View.norm (View.point_to_angle r m.mx m.my -. m.mangle +. (9. *. View.pi /. 8.)) /. (View.pi /. 4.)) land 7 else 0 in
          let patch = f.lumps.(rot) and flip = f.flip.(rot) in
          if patch <> "" then begin
            let width = Wad.short patch 0 and left = Wad.short patch 4 and top = Wad.short patch 6 in
            let tx = tx -. float left in
            let x1 = View.ifloor (r.centerx +. (tx *. xscale)) in
            let x2 = View.ifloor (r.centerx +. ((tx +. float width) *. xscale)) - 1 in
            if x1 <= r.width && x2 >= 0 then begin
              let iscale = 1. /. xscale in
              let vx1 = max 0 x1 and vx2 = min (r.width - 1) x2 in
              let start, step = if flip then (float width -. (1. /. 65536.), -.iscale) else (0., iscale) in
              let lights = r.scalelight.(View.lit r m.sector.light) in
              r.vissprites <-
                ({ vx1; vx2; gx = m.mx; gy = m.my; gz = m.mz; gzt = m.mz +. float top; vscale = xscale; xiscale = step;
                  texturemid = m.mz +. float top -. r.viewz; startfrac = start +. (step *. float (vx1 - x1));
                  patch = Bytes.unsafe_of_string patch;
                  vcmap = (if bright then 0 else lights.(min (View.maxlightscale - 1) (int_of_float (xscale *. 16. *. 320. /. float r.width)))) }
                  : View.vissprite)
                :: r.vissprites
            end
          end
  end

(* R_DrawMaskedColumn: a picture's column, its posts from [ofs] in
 * [src], between the clips *)
let draw_masked_column (r : View.t) (x : int) (src : Bytes.t) (ofs : int) (texturemid : float) (scale : float) (colormaps : Bytes.t) (cmap : int)
    (ceiling : int) (floor : int) : unit =
  let cy = float r.centery in
  let sprtopscreen = cy -. (texturemid *. scale) in
  let i = ref ofs and n = Bytes.length src in
  while !i + 1 < n && Char.code (Bytes.get src !i) <> 0xff do
    let topdelta = Char.code (Bytes.get src !i) and length = Char.code (Bytes.get src (!i + 1)) in
    let topscreen = sprtopscreen +. (scale *. float topdelta) in
    let bottomscreen = topscreen +. (scale *. float length) in
    let yl = max (View.iceil topscreen) (ceiling + 1) and yh = min (View.iceil bottomscreen - 1) (floor - 1) in
    if yl <= yh && !i + 3 + length <= n then View.draw_column r x yl yh (texturemid -. float topdelta) scale src (!i + 3) colormaps cmap;
    i := !i + length + 4
  done

(* R_RenderMaskedSegRange: a two-sided line's middle texture, its
 * columns x1 to x2 not drawn yet *)
let render_masked_seg_range (r : View.t) (textures : Textures.t) (level : Level.t) (ds : View.drawseg) (x1 : int) (x2 : int) : unit =
  let seg = ds.dseg in
  match seg.back_sector with
  | None -> ()
  | Some back ->
      let front = seg.front_sector and line = level.lines.(seg.seg_line) in
      let tex = textures.textures.(textures.texture_translation.(seg.side.middle)) in
      let lightnum = View.light_level front.light + r.extralight + (if seg.sv1.y = seg.sv2.y then -1 else if seg.sv1.x = seg.sv2.x then 1 else 0) in
      let walllights = r.scalelight.(max 0 (min (View.lightlevels - 1) lightnum)) in
      let mid =
        (if line.flags land Level.lower_unpegged <> 0 then Float.max front.floor back.floor +. float tex.height -. r.viewz
         else Float.min front.ceiling back.ceiling -. r.viewz)
        +. seg.side.yoffset in
      let lightscale = 16. *. 320. /. float r.width in
      for x = x1 to x2 do
        let c = ds.maskedcol.(x - ds.dx1) in
        if c <> View.unset then begin
          let scale = ds.dscale1 +. (float (x - ds.dx1) *. ds.dscalestep) in
          let cmap = walllights.(max 0 (min (View.maxlightscale - 1) (int_of_float (scale *. lightscale)))) in
          (* (the column's posts: 3 bytes before its pixels, id's
           * R_GetColumn - 3; a composited column has none, and shows
           * what is there: the "medusa") *)
          draw_masked_column r x tex.source (tex.columns.(c land tex.width_mask) - 3) mid scale textures.colormaps cmap
            ds.sprtopclip.(x - ds.sprtopoff) ds.sprbottomclip.(x - ds.sprbottomoff);
          ds.maskedcol.(x - ds.dx1) <- View.unset
        end
      done

(* R_DrawSprite: the parts of the walls in front of it clip it; the
 * masked middle textures behind it are drawn first *)
let draw_sprite (r : View.t) (textures : Textures.t) (level : Level.t) (spr : View.vissprite) : unit =
  let clipbot = Array.make r.width (-2) and cliptop = Array.make r.width (-2) in
  List.iter
    (fun (ds : View.drawseg) ->
      if not (ds.dx1 > spr.vx2 || ds.dx2 < spr.vx1 || (ds.silhouette = 0 && Array.length ds.maskedcol = 0)) then begin
        let r1 = max ds.dx1 spr.vx1 and r2 = min ds.dx2 spr.vx2 in
        let scale = Float.max ds.dscale1 ds.dscale2 and lowscale = Float.min ds.dscale1 ds.dscale2 in
        let seg = ds.dseg in
        if
          scale < spr.vscale
          || (lowscale < spr.vscale && Level.side_of spr.gx spr.gy seg.sv1.x seg.sv1.y (seg.sv2.x -. seg.sv1.x) (seg.sv2.y -. seg.sv1.y) = 0)
        then (if Array.length ds.maskedcol > 0 then render_masked_seg_range r textures level ds r1 r2)
        else begin
          let sil = ref ds.silhouette in
          if spr.gz >= ds.bsilheight then sil := !sil land 2;
          if spr.gzt <= ds.tsilheight then sil := !sil land 1;
          for x = r1 to r2 do
            if !sil land 1 <> 0 && clipbot.(x) = -2 then clipbot.(x) <- ds.sprbottomclip.(x - ds.sprbottomoff);
            if !sil land 2 <> 0 && cliptop.(x) = -2 then cliptop.(x) <- ds.sprtopclip.(x - ds.sprtopoff)
          done
        end
      end)
    r.drawsegs;
  (* R_DrawVisSprite *)
  let frac = ref spr.startfrac and width = Wad.short (Bytes.unsafe_to_string spr.patch) 0 in
  for x = spr.vx1 to spr.vx2 do
    let col = max 0 (min (width - 1) (View.ifloor !frac)) in
    let ofs = Wad.int32 (Bytes.unsafe_to_string spr.patch) (8 + (4 * col)) in
    draw_masked_column r x spr.patch ofs spr.texturemid spr.vscale textures.colormaps spr.vcmap
      (if cliptop.(x) = -2 then -1 else cliptop.(x)) (if clipbot.(x) = -2 then r.height else clipbot.(x));
    frac := !frac +. spr.xiscale
  done

(* R_DrawMasked: the things, farthest first, then the masked middle
 * textures left *)
let draw_masked (r : View.t) (textures : Textures.t) (level : Level.t) : unit =
  let sorted = List.stable_sort (fun (a : View.vissprite) (b : View.vissprite) -> compare a.vscale b.vscale) r.vissprites in
  List.iter (draw_sprite r textures level) sorted;
  List.iter (fun (ds : View.drawseg) -> if Array.length ds.maskedcol > 0 then render_masked_seg_range r textures level ds ds.dx1 ds.dx2) r.drawsegs

(* R_DrawPSprite: a picture of the hand, at (sx, sy) of a screen of 320
 * by 200 (the weapon's top at 32 held, 128 lowered), as many times
 * larger as the view is wider; over everything, unclipped; lit by the
 * player's sector (full light if bright) *)
let draw_psprite (r : View.t) (textures : Textures.t) (sprites : Things.sprites)
    (light : int) ((st, sx, sy) : Info.state * float * float) : unit =
  let name = st.sprite ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr (Char.code 'A' + st.frame)) in
  match Things.find sprites name with
  | None -> ()
  | Some f ->
      let patch = f.lumps.(0) in
      if patch <> "" then begin
        let width = Wad.short patch 0 and left = Wad.short patch 4 in
        let top = Wad.short patch 6 in
        let scale = float r.width /. 320. in
        let tx = sx -. 160. -. float left in
        let x1 = View.ifloor (r.centerx +. (tx *. scale)) in
        let x2 = View.ifloor (r.centerx +. ((tx +. float width) *. scale)) - 1 in
        let texturemid = (float r.centery /. scale) -. (sy -. float top) in
        let cmap =
          if st.bright then 0
          else r.scalelight.(View.lit r light).(View.maxlightscale - 1) in
        let src = Bytes.unsafe_of_string patch in
        let step = 1. /. scale in
        for x = max 0 x1 to min (r.width - 1) x2 do
          let frac = float (x - x1) *. step in
          let col = max 0 (min (width - 1) (View.ifloor frac)) in
          let col = if f.flip.(0) then width - 1 - col else col in
          let ofs = Wad.int32 patch (8 + (4 * col)) in
          draw_masked_column r x src ofs texturemid scale textures.colormaps
            cmap (-1) r.height
        done
      end
games/fps/doom/render/Sprites.mli

(* Sprites: the things, and what is seen through (Doom's r_things.c).
 *
 * As the tree is walked, the things of each sector reached are
 * projected (R_AddSprites, R_ProjectSprite): the thing's place in the
 * eye's frame, its scale, the columns its picture covers (the
 * picture's offsets: its feet at the thing's place), the rotation seen
 * (eighths of a turn between the eye's angle to it and its own), the
 * light (its sector's by its scale; a bright frame at full light): a
 * vissprite. After the walls and the planes (R_DrawMasked) they are
 * drawn farthest first, each clipped column by column by the drawsegs
 * in front of it (R_DrawSprite: a seg nearer than the thing, by its
 * scale or by the side the thing is on, clips it from above or below,
 * as its silhouette says), each column its posts, transparent between
 * (R_DrawMaskedColumn).
 *
 * A two-sided line's middle texture (a grate, a window's bars) is
 * drawn the same way, its columns read as posts (R_RenderMaskedSegRange:
 * a column of one patch is that patch's; one of several has no posts,
 * and shows what is there, the "medusa"), after the things behind it
 * and before those in front.
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-doom: Render calls project_sprite from its
 * walk and draw_masked at the end of a frame. *)

(* [project_sprite r sprites tic thing]: a vissprite of the thing, if
 * it can be seen *)
val project_sprite : View.t -> Things.sprites -> int -> Things.mobj -> unit

(* R_DrawMasked: the vissprites, farthest first, then the masked
 * middle textures left *)
val draw_masked : View.t -> Textures.t -> Level.t -> unit

(* [draw_psprite r textures sprites light (state, sx, sy)]: the
 * player's weapon, or its flash, over the view (R_DrawPSprite) *)
val draw_psprite :
  View.t -> Textures.t -> Things.sprites -> int -> Info.state * float * float ->
  unit
games/fps/doom/render/View.ml
11670
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See View.mli *)

(* OPTIMIZATION: min and max on ints here, Int's: Stdlib's are
 * polymorphic, a call of the runtime's compare each time, and the
 * renderer takes them for each column and span (a column's light, its
 * clipped top and bottom). With OCaml 4.14 on arm64 a frame of
 * mini-doom's was 7.59 million instructions, 5.52 with these, the same
 * picture; with mini-ml 16.25 and 16.10.
 * old: Stdlib's min and max *)
let min = Int.min and max = Int.max

let pi = 4. *. atan 1.
let two_pi = 2. *. pi
let half_pi = pi /. 2.

(* an angle in [0, 2 pi): id's angles are unsigned, a turn 2^32.
 * Inlined, it and fine, fsin, fcos: id's tables read by a shift of an
 * integer angle, ours by these floats' few operations, which a call
 * would add to, its float argument and result boxed (norm alone 2.3%
 * of a frame, 624,183 calls in 61) *)
let[@inline] norm (a : float) : float = if a >= 0. && a < two_pi then a else a -. (two_pi *. floor (a /. two_pi))

(* the same in [-pi, pi) *)
let signed (a : float) : float = let a = norm a in if a >= pi then a -. two_pi else a

(* id's tables (tables.c): a turn is 8192 fine angles, an angle's sine
 * and tangent the table's at its fine angle's middle; angles are
 * quantized there, which is where a texel lands (floats with the exact
 * sine put a few in every hundred pixels a texel apart) *)
let fineangles = 8192
let finestep = two_pi /. float fineangles
(* (their values id's fixed_t, 16 bits of fraction: libm's sin and tan
 * are not the same to the last bit on x86 and arm64, and a frame
 * recorded on one is then another on the other) *)
let fixed (v : float) : float = Float.round (v *. 65536.) /. 65536.
let finesine = Array.init (fineangles + (fineangles / 4)) (fun (i : int) -> fixed (sin ((float i +. 0.5) *. finestep)))
let finetangent = Array.init (fineangles / 2) (fun (i : int) -> fixed (tan ((float (i - (fineangles / 4)) +. 0.5) *. finestep)))

(* an angle's fine angle (angle >> ANGLETOFINESHIFT) *)
let[@inline] fine (a : float) : int = int_of_float (norm a /. finestep) land (fineangles - 1)
let[@inline] fsin (a : float) : float = finesine.(fine a)
let[@inline] fcos (a : float) : float = finesine.(fine a + (fineangles / 4))

(* the tangent of an angle given plus 90 degrees (finetangent[(a +
 * ANG90) >> ANGLETOFINESHIFT]: a in -90 to 90) *)
let ftan90 (a : float) : float = finetangent.(min (fineangles / 2 - 1) (fine a))

let ifloor (v : float) : int = let i = int_of_float v in if float i > v then i - 1 else i
let iceil (v : float) : int = let i = int_of_float v in if float i < v then i + 1 else i

(* the light's constants (r_main.h) *)
let lightlevels = 16
let numcolormaps = 32
let maxlightscale = 48
let maxlightz = 128

(* a visplane (r_plane.c): a height, a flat and a light, and for each of
 * its columns the rows it shows, top to bottom (top > bottom: none).
 * Its arrays are a column more at each end (R_DrawPlanes reads them) *)
type plane = {
  mutable pheight : float;
  mutable pic : int;
  mutable plight : int;
  mutable minx : int;
  mutable maxx : int;
  top : int array;
  bottom : int array;
}

let unset = 0x7fff

(* a drawseg (r_defs.h): a seg drawn, kept for the sprites and the
 * masked middle textures drawn after (R_DrawMasked): its columns and
 * scales, which of its sides hides what is behind (the silhouette: 1
 * below, 2 above, 3 both) and from which heights, the clips at that
 * moment (the value at column x is clip.(x - off)), and a masked
 * texture's columns *)
type drawseg = {
  dx1 : int;
  dx2 : int;
  dscale1 : float;
  dscale2 : float;
  dscalestep : float;
  mutable silhouette : int;
  mutable bsilheight : float;
  mutable tsilheight : float;
  mutable sprtopclip : int array;
  mutable sprtopoff : int;
  mutable sprbottomclip : int array;
  mutable sprbottomoff : int;
  maskedcol : int array; (* x - dx1: the texture's column, or unset once drawn; empty: none *)
  dseg : Level.seg;
}

(* a vissprite (r_defs.h): a thing projected, to draw after the walls *)
type vissprite = {
  vx1 : int;
  vx2 : int;
  gx : float;
  gy : float;
  gz : float;
  gzt : float;
  vscale : float;
  xiscale : float;
  texturemid : float;
  startfrac : float;
  patch : Bytes.t;
  vcmap : int;
}

type t = {
  width : int;
  height : int;
  centerx : float;
  centery : int;
  projection : float;
  (* a column's left edge's angle from the view's middle, and a fine
   * angle's column (R_InitTextureMapping) *)
  xtoviewangle : float array;
  viewangletox : int array;
  distscale : float array; (* 1 / cos of it *)
  yslope : float array; (* a row's distance for a plane 1 unit away *)
  scalelight : int array array; (* by level, by scale: a colormap's offset *)
  zlight : int array array; (* by level, by distance *)
  screen : Bytes.t;
  (* the columns closed: id's solidsegs, ranges first to last, sorted,
   * none touching another (Bsp) *)
  mutable solidsegs : (int * int) list;
  ceilingclip : int array;
  floorclip : int array;
  (* the visplanes: those of this frame are the first [nplanes] *)
  mutable planes : plane array;
  mutable nplanes : int;
  spanstart : int array;
  mutable drawsegs : drawseg list; (* the last drawn first *)
  mutable vissprites : vissprite list;
  mutable sector_seen : int array; (* a sector's things projected at this frame *)
  mutable frame_number : int;
  negonearray : int array;
  screenheightarray : int array;
  (* the eye *)
  mutable viewx : float;
  mutable viewy : float;
  mutable viewz : float;
  mutable viewangle : float;
  mutable segs : int;
  mutable extralight : int;
}

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The tables *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let create (width : int) (height : int) : t =
  let centerx = float (width / 2) and centery = height / 2 in
  let projection = centerx in
  (* (the view's 90 degrees across the width: its edges' tangent is
   * the table's, a bit more than 1, so the focal length a bit less
   * than half the width) *)
  let focallength = centerx /. finetangent.((fineangles / 4) + (fineangles / 8)) in
  let viewangletox =
    Array.init (fineangles / 2) (fun (i : int) ->
        let t = finetangent.(i) in
        if t > 2. then -1 else if t < -2. then width + 1 else max (-1) (min (width + 1) (iceil (centerx -. (t *. focallength))))) in
  let xtoviewangle =
    Array.init (width + 1) (fun (x : int) ->
        let i = ref 0 in
        while viewangletox.(!i) > x do incr i done;
        (float !i *. finestep) -. half_pi) in
  let viewangletox = Array.map (fun (x : int) -> max 0 (min width x)) viewangletox in
  (* R_InitLightTables, R_ExecuteSetViewSize: a level's first colormap,
   * then darker by the distance; the scale's steps as a 320 wide
   * screen's *)
  let startmap (i : int) : int = (lightlevels - 1 - i) * 2 * numcolormaps / lightlevels in
  let clampmap (l : int) : int = 256 * max 0 (min (numcolormaps - 1) l) in
  { width; height; centerx; centery; projection; xtoviewangle; viewangletox;
    distscale = Array.map (fun (a : float) -> 1. /. Float.abs (fcos a)) xtoviewangle;
    yslope = Array.init height (fun (y : int) -> (float width /. 2.) /. Float.abs (float (y - centery) +. 0.5));
    scalelight = Array.init lightlevels (fun (i : int) -> Array.init maxlightscale (fun (j : int) -> clampmap (startmap i - (j / 2))));
    zlight =
      Array.init lightlevels (fun (i : int) ->
          Array.init maxlightz (fun (j : int) -> clampmap (startmap i - ((655360 / (j + 1)) lsr 12 / 2))));
    screen = Bytes.make (width * height) '\000';
    solidsegs = [];
    ceilingclip = Array.make width (-1); floorclip = Array.make width height;
    planes = [||]; nplanes = 0; spanstart = Array.make height 0;
    drawsegs = []; vissprites = []; sector_seen = [||]; frame_number = 0;
    negonearray = Array.make width (-1); screenheightarray = Array.make width height;
    viewx = 0.; viewy = 0.; viewz = 0.; viewangle = 0.; segs = 0; extralight = 0 }

(* a sector's light level, 0 to 15 *)
let light_level (light : int) : int = max 0 (min (lightlevels - 1) (light asr 4))

let lit (r : t) (light : int) : int =
  max 0 (min (lightlevels - 1) ((light asr 4) + r.extralight))

let clipangle (r : t) : float = r.xtoviewangle.(0)

(* an angle from the view's middle (within the view's) to a column:
 * the first column whose left edge is to its right (viewangletox) *)
let x_of_angle (r : t) (a : float) : int = r.viewangletox.(min (fineangles / 2 - 1) (fine (a +. half_pi)))

(* R_PointToAngle: a point's angle from the eye by its octant and the
 * slope in it, 2048 slopes an octant (SlopeDiv: truncated, as its
 * integers are; tantoangle: their angles) *)
let slope_div (num : float) (den : float) : float =
  let d = floor (den *. 256.) in
  if d < 2. then 2048. else Float.min 2048. (floor (num *. 524288. /. d))

(* (id's table of 2049, an angle of 2^32 a turn: atan's last bits not
 * the frame's) *)
let tantoangle_table =
  let unit = two_pi /. 4294967296. in
  Array.init 2049 (fun (i : int) -> Float.round (atan (float i /. 2048.) /. unit) *. unit)
let tantoangle (slope : float) : float = tantoangle_table.(int_of_float slope)

let point_to_angle (r : t) (x : float) (y : float) : float =
  let x = x -. r.viewx and y = y -. r.viewy in
  if x = 0. && y = 0. then 0.
  else
    let a =
      if x >= 0. then
        if y >= 0. then (if x > y then tantoangle (slope_div y x) else half_pi -. tantoangle (slope_div x y))
        else
          let y = -.y in
          if x > y then -.tantoangle (slope_div y x) else (3. *. half_pi) +. tantoangle (slope_div x y)
      else
        let x = -.x in
        if y >= 0. then (if x > y then pi -. tantoangle (slope_div y x) else half_pi +. tantoangle (slope_div x y))
        else
          let y = -.y in
          if x > y then pi +. tantoangle (slope_div y x) else (3. *. half_pi) -. tantoangle (slope_div x y) in
    norm a

(* R_PointToDist: the larger side over the sine of the angle the slope
 * says *)
let point_to_dist (r : t) (x : float) (y : float) : float =
  let dx = Float.abs (x -. r.viewx) and dy = Float.abs (y -. r.viewy) in
  let dx, dy = if dy > dx then (dy, dx) else (dx, dy) in
  if dx = 0. then 0. else dx /. fsin (tantoangle (Float.min 2048. (floor (dy /. dx *. 2048.))) +. half_pi)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The columns *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* R_DrawColumn: rows yl to yh of column x, a column of pixels at [base]
 * in [source] (a texture's, a picture's post) from [mid] (its row at
 * the view's height) a step of 1 / scale, its pixels through the
 * colormap at [cmap]; its row & 127, as id's *)
let draw_column (r : t) (x : int) (yl : int) (yh : int) (mid : float) (scale : float) (source : Bytes.t) (base : int)
    (colormaps : Bytes.t) (cmap : int) : unit =
  if yl <= yh then begin
    let step = int_of_float (65536. /. scale) in
    let frac = ref (int_of_float (mid *. 65536.) + ((yl - r.centery) * step)) in
    let screen = r.screen and w = r.width in
    let ofs = ref ((yl * w) + x) in
    for _n = yl to yh do
      Bytes.unsafe_set screen !ofs (Bytes.unsafe_get colormaps (cmap + Char.code (Bytes.unsafe_get source (base + ((!frac asr 16) land 127)))));
      frac := !frac + step;
      ofs := !ofs + w
    done
  end
[@@zero_alloc]

(* View: the renderer's state and what all its parts share (Doom's
 * r_main.c, r_draw.c, r_defs.h, tables.c): the screen, the eye, the
 * tables, the clips of the columns, the visplanes, drawsegs and
 * vissprites of a frame, and R_DrawColumn, the loop every wall, sky
 * and sprite ends in.
 *
 * The tables (R_InitTextureMapping, R_InitLightTables, tables.c): a
 * turn is 8,192 fine angles and a sine or a tangent is the table's at
 * the fine angle's middle; the view's 90 degrees across the width are
 * a focal length of 159.76 at 320 wide (the table's tangent at 45
 * degrees is a bit more than 1); xtoviewangle is each column's left
 * edge's angle, viewangletox each fine angle's column. id's angles
 * are those quantized ones, and so are a texel's place and a light's
 * level: with the exact sine, a few pixels in every hundred are
 * another texel (Render.mli, plan_doom.md's table). Their values are
 * id's fixed_t too (16 bits of fraction), and tantoangle id's table of
 * 2,049 angles: libm's sin, tan and atan differ in their last bits
 * between x86 and arm64, which the rounding keeps out of a frame; the
 * player's thrust, bob and use line take the same sine, as id's.
 *
 *   the light: a sector's 0-255 is 16 levels; level i starts at
 *   colormap (15 - i) * 4 and darkens
 *     scalelight.(i).(j): by a wall's scale (j = scale * 16), 48 of them
 *     zlight.(i).(j): by a flat's distance (j = distance / 16), 128
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-doom: Render makes one (create) and draws a
 * frame through Planes, Segs and Sprites, which all read and write it. *)

(* See Mus.mli *)

(* a MIDI number of variable length: 7 bits a byte, the first ones
 * with their high bit *)
let add_vlq (b : Buffer.t) (n : int) : unit =
  let rec bytes (n : int) (acc : int list) : int list =
    if n < 128 then n :: acc else bytes (n lsr 7) ((n land 127) :: acc)
  in
  match bytes n [] with
  | [] -> ()
  | l ->
      let k = List.length l in
      List.iteri
        (fun (i : int) (v : int) ->
          Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr (if i < k - 1 then v lor 128 else v)))
        l

(* MUS's controllers 1 to 9, MIDI's: the bank, the modulation, the
 * volume, the pan, the expression, the reverb, the chorus, the sustain
 * pedal, the soft pedal *)
let controllers = [| 0; 0; 1; 7; 10; 11; 91; 93; 64; 67 |]

(* its system events 10 to 14, MIDI's controllers: all sounds off, all
 * notes off, mono, poly, reset *)
let system = [| 120; 123; 126; 127; 121 |]

let convert (mus : string) : string =
  let u8 (i : int) : int =
    if i < String.length mus then Char.code mus.[i] else 0
  in
  let u16 (i : int) : int = u8 i lor (u8 (i + 1) lsl 8) in
  let start = u16 6 in
  let track = Buffer.create (String.length mus * 2) in
  let channels = Array.make 16 (-1) and volumes = Array.make 16 127 in
  let next_channel = ref 0 and delay = ref 0 in
  (* (MUS's 15 the drums, MIDI's 9; the others in turn, 9 skipped) *)
  let midi_channel (c : int) : int =
    if c = 15 then 9
    else begin
      if channels.(c) < 0 then begin
        channels.(c) <- !next_channel;
        next_channel := !next_channel + if !next_channel = 8 then 2 else 1
      end;
      channels.(c)
    end
  in
  let event (bytes : int list) : unit =
    add_vlq track !delay;
    delay := 0;
    List.iter
      (fun (v : int) -> Buffer.add_char track (Char.chr (v land 255)))
      bytes
  in
  let i = ref start and ended = ref false in
  while (not !ended) && !i < String.length mus do
    let desc = u8 !i in
    incr i;
    let c = midi_channel (desc land 15) in
    (match (desc lsr 4) land 7 with
    | 0 ->
        event [ 0x80 lor c; u8 !i land 127; 64 ];
        incr i
    | 1 ->
        let note = u8 !i in
        incr i;
        if note land 128 <> 0 then begin
          volumes.(desc land 15) <- u8 !i land 127;
          incr i
        end;
        event [ 0x90 lor c; note land 127; volumes.(desc land 15) ]
    | 2 ->
        (* (8 bits of the wheel to MIDI's 14) *)
        let v = u8 !i * 64 in
        incr i;
        event [ 0xe0 lor c; v land 127; (v lsr 7) land 127 ]
    | 3 ->
        let k = u8 !i in
        incr i;
        if k >= 10 && k <= 14 then event [ 0xb0 lor c; system.(k - 10); 0 ]
    | 4 ->
        let k = u8 !i and v = u8 (!i + 1) land 127 in
        i := !i + 2;
        if k = 0 then event [ 0xc0 lor c; v ]
        else if k < 10 then event [ 0xb0 lor c; controllers.(k); v ]
    | 6 -> ended := true
    | _ -> ());
    if desc land 128 <> 0 then begin
      let d = ref 0 and more = ref true in
      while !more && !i < String.length mus do
        let v = u8 !i in
        incr i;
        d := (!d lsl 7) lor (v land 127);
        more := v land 128 <> 0
      done;
      delay := !delay + !d
    end
  done;
  event [ 0xff; 0x2f; 0 ];
  let b = Buffer.create (Buffer.length track + 22) in
  let add32 (n : int) : unit =
    List.iter
      (fun (s : int) -> Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr ((n lsr s) land 255)))
      [ 24; 16; 8; 0 ]
  in
  let add16 (n : int) : unit =
    Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr ((n lsr 8) land 255));
    Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr (n land 255))
  in
  (* (format 0, one track, 70 tics a beat; the tempo MIDI's 120 by
   * default: 140 tics a second) *)
  Buffer.add_string b "MThd";
  add32 6;
  add16 0;
  add16 1;
  add16 70;
  Buffer.add_string b "MTrk";
  add32 (Buffer.length track);
  Buffer.add_buffer b track;
  Buffer.contents b

let to_midi (lump : string) : string =
  if String.length lump >= 4 && String.sub lump 0 4 = "MUS\026" then
    convert lump
  else lump

(* Mus: Doom's music format made a Standard MIDI File, which
 * lib_playground's Audio.midi plays (the ports' mus2mid, i_sound.c's
 * job of DMX's in id's DOS game).
 *
 * id's WADs keep a level's music (D_E1M1) as MUS: Paul Radek's DMX
 * sound library's own, a MIDI made smaller for the cards of 1993. Its
 * events are MIDI's, fewer and packed, at 140 tics a second:
 *
 *   a byte: last (1 bit) | the event (3) | the channel (4)
 *     0 a note let go       its note
 *     1 a note played       its note (bit 7: a volume follows)
 *     2 the pitch wheel     0 to 255 (128 in the middle)
 *     3 a system event      all off, mono, poly, reset
 *     4 a controller        which (0 the instrument, 3 the volume, 4
 *                           the pan ...), its value
 *     6 the end
 *   last: the delay to the next event follows, 7 bits a byte, the
 *   high bit saying more
 *
 * MUS's channel 15 is the drums, MIDI's 9; the others take MIDI's in
 * the order they are first heard. The file made: one track, 70 tics a
 * beat at 120 beats a minute (140 a second, MUS's).
 *
 * Freedoom keeps its music as MIDI already (a WAD may hold either:
 * Doom's ports read both); [to_midi] gives a MIDI file as it is.
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-doom: Sound plays a level's music through
 * it. *)

(* [to_midi lump]: the MIDI file of a music lump (MUS, or MIDI already) *)
val to_midi : string -> string

(* Claude Code

(* See Sound.mli *)

type t = {
  wad : Wad.t;
  three_d : bool;
  (* the sounds made, by name; None: not in the WAD *)
  cache : (string, Audio.sound option) Hashtbl.t;
}

let create (wad : Wad.t) (three_d : bool) : t =
  { wad; three_d; cache = Hashtbl.create 64 }

let dmx_to_wav (lump : string) : string option =
  if String.length lump < 8 + 32 || Wad.short lump 0 <> 3 then None
  else begin
    (* (the rate unsigned: 44,100 is past a short) *)
    let rate = Wad.u8 lump 2 lor (Wad.u8 lump 3 lsl 8)
    and count = Wad.int32 lump 4 in
    let count = min count (String.length lump - 8) in
    (* (the pads: 16 bytes at each end) *)
    let first = 8 + 16 and n = max 0 (count - 32) in
    let b = Buffer.create (44 + (2 * n)) in
    let add32 (v : int) : unit =
      List.iter
        (fun (s : int) -> Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr ((v lsr s) land 255)))
        [ 0; 8; 16; 24 ]
    in
    let add16 (v : int) : unit =
      Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr (v land 255));
      Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr ((v lsr 8) land 255))
    in
    Buffer.add_string b "RIFF";
    add32 (36 + (2 * n));
    Buffer.add_string b "WAVEfmt ";
    add32 16;
    add16 1;
    add16 1;
    add32 rate;
    add32 (rate * 2);
    add16 2;
    add16 16;
    Buffer.add_string b "data";
    add32 (2 * n);
    for i = first to first + n - 1 do
      add16 ((Char.code lump.[i] - 128) * 256)
    done;
    Some (Buffer.contents b)
  end

let sound (s : t) (name : string) : Audio.sound option =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt s.cache name with
  | Some v -> v
  | None ->
      let v =
        Option.bind
          (Wad.find s.wad ("DS" ^ String.uppercase_ascii name))
          (fun (l : Wad.lump) -> Option.map Audio.wav (dmx_to_wav l.data))
      in
      Hashtbl.replace s.cache name v;
      v

(* s_sound.c's numbers *)
let clipping_dist = 1200.
let close_dist = 160.
let stereo_swing = 96. /. 128.

(* S_AdjustSoundParams: the loudness and the pan, None too far *)
let adjust (p : World.player) (x : float) (y : float) : (float * float) option =
  let d = World.approx_distance (x -. p.x) (y -. p.y) in
  if d > clipping_dist then None
  else begin
    let a = Float.atan2 (y -. p.y) (x -. p.x) -. p.angle in
    let pan = -.stereo_swing *. Float.sin a in
    let vol =
      if d < close_dist then 1.
      else (clipping_dist -. d) /. (clipping_dist -. close_dist)
    in
    if vol <= 0. then None else Some (vol, pan)
  end

let play (s : t) (w : World.t) : unit =
  let p = w.player in
  (* (one of a name a tic: a shotgun's seven pellets, one bang) *)
  let seen = Hashtbl.create 8 in
  List.iter
    (fun (e : World.sound) ->
      if not (Hashtbl.mem seen (e.sfx, e.origin)) then begin
        Hashtbl.replace seen (e.sfx, e.origin) ();
        match (sound s e.sfx, e.origin) with
        | None, _ -> ()
        | Some snd, None -> Audio.play snd
        | Some snd, Some (x, y) -> (
            if s.three_d then begin
              let m (v : float) : float = v /. 32. in
              let ears =
                Audio3d.facing ~velocity:(0., 0., 0.)
                  (m p.x, m p.y, m p.viewz)
                  p.angle
              in
              Audio.play
                (Audio3d.heard ears ~velocity:(0., 0., 0.)
                   ~reference:(close_dist /. 32.) ~speed_of_sound:343.
                   (m x, m y, m p.viewz)
                   snd)
            end
            else
              match adjust p x y with
              | Some (vol, pan) ->
                  (* old: Audio.play (snd |> Audio.louder vol |> Audio.pan pan) *)
                  Audio.play_at ~volume:vol ~pan snd
              | None -> ())
      end)
    (List.rev w.sounds);
  w.sounds <- []

let music (wad : Wad.t) (map : string) : unit =
  match Wad.find wad ("D_" ^ map) with
  | Some l -> Audio.play_midi "music" (Mus.to_midi l.data)
  | None -> ()
games/fps/doom/sound/Sound.mli
2112
(* Sound: what the player hears (Doom's s_sound.c, and i_sound.c's
 * loading), through lib_playground's Audio.
 *
 * A sound effect is a lump of the WAD, DS and its name (DSPISTOL),
 * DMX's format: 3, its rate (11,025 samples a second in id's WADs,
 * 22,050 and others in Freedoom's), its length, then bytes of 8 bits
 * (128 the silence), the first and last 16 a pad. Here each is made a
 * WAV of 16 bits once, the first time it is heard, and Audio.wav plays
 * it (Audio resamples it to its 44,100).
 *
 * Where a sound comes from changes it (S_AdjustSoundParams): from the
 * player itself, as it is; from a place, quieter with the distance
 * (id's own, without a square root: P_AproxDistance), full within 160,
 * silent past 1,200, and to the side it is on, at most three quarters
 * of the way to a speaker:
 *
 *   loudness 1 |------.
 *              |       `-.             the pan: -0.75 sin a, a the
 *              |          `-.          angle from where the player
 *            0 +------+-------`----    looks to the sound (to the
 *                    160      1200     left: the left speaker)
 *
 * With sound=3d, the playground's Audio3d instead (its ears where the
 * eye is: the distance's law, the air dulling what is far, the time
 * between the ears; a unit of Doom's taken as 1/32 of a meter, the
 * player being 56 high).
 *
 * The music: the level's D_ lump (D_E1M1), MUS or MIDI (Mus), looped
 * by Audio's MIDI player, its 8-bit band.
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-doom: Doom.ml plays each tic's sounds
 * (World's [sounds]) and starts the level's music. *)

type t

(* [create wad three_d]: the sounds of the WAD, made when first heard *)
val create : Wad.t -> bool -> t

(* [play s world]: the sounds of the last tics, from where they were
 * made, heard where the player is now *)
val play : t -> World.t -> unit

(* [music wad map]: the level's music, looping, if the WAD has it *)
val music : Wad.t -> string -> unit

(* [dmx_to_wav lump]: a DS lump as a WAV file's bytes (16 bits, one
 * channel, its rate); None if it is not one *)
val dmx_to_wav : string -> string option
games/fps/doom/tools/Mkwad.ml
19738
(* Claude Code

(* mini-mkwad: mini-doom's WAD made from Freedoom's source tree (its
 * git repository, github.com/freedoom/freedoom: levels/, patches/,
 * flats/, lumps/), the few lumps the given levels need:
 *
 *   PLAYPAL   the palette (lumps/playpal/playpal-base.lmp), one of
 *             Doom's fourteen: the others are its tints (pain, items)
 *   COLORMAP  34 maps of 256 indices: 32 levels of light, each the
 *             palette blended towards black by (32 - i) / 32 then the
 *             nearest colour of the palette; the inverse one; black
 *             (Freedoom's lumps/colormap/colormap script, the same
 *             numbers)
 *   E1M1 ...  each level's lumps as levels/e1m1.wad has them, its
 *             nodes built
 *   TEXTURE1, PNAMES  the textures the levels' sides name, from
 *             lumps/textures/textures.cfg (with DOOM1_VERSIONS: Doom
 *             1's sky), and the switches' other face, the animations'
 *             other frames
 *   the patches they are made of, each a PNG of patches/ made Doom's
 *             picture (columns of posts, its transparent pixels left
 *             out), its colours the palette's nearest
 *   F_START ... F_END  the flats the sectors name, 64 by 64 bytes
 *   S_START ... S_END  the sprites of the levels' things, and those of
 *             the states mini-doom has (Info: the weapons, the shots'
 *             puffs and blood, the fireballs, the barrel's blast)
 *   DSPISTOL ...  the sounds mini-doom makes (Info.sounds), each
 *             sounds/ds*.wav (8 bits, one channel) made DMX's lump
 *   D_E1M1 ...  each level's music, musics/d_*.mid, as MIDI (Freedoom's
 *             WADs keep it so; id's kept MUS)
 *
 * usage: mini-mkwad freedoom-dir out.wad E1M1 [MAP...]
 *
 * deutex is what Freedoom builds its WADs with (and its own
 * build-textures script, in Python); this is the part of both that a
 * walk through a level needs, in OCaml (no Python in ix's build). *)

let usage = "usage: mini-mkwad freedoom-dir out.wad E1M1 [MAP...]"

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The palette and its light *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let palette_of (pal : string) : (float * float * float) array =
  Array.init 256 (fun (i : int) -> (float (Wad.u8 pal (3 * i)), float (Wad.u8 pal ((3 * i) + 1)), float (Wad.u8 pal ((3 * i) + 2))))

(* the nearest colour, the first of equals (colormap's search_palette) *)
let nearest (pal : (float * float * float) array) ((r, g, b) : float * float * float) : int =
  let best = ref 0 and best_d = ref infinity in
  Array.iteri
    (fun (i : int) ((r', g', b') : float * float * float) ->
      let d = ((r -. r') *. (r -. r')) +. ((g -. g') *. (g -. g')) +. ((b -. b') *. (b -. b')) in
      if d < !best_d then begin best := i; best_d := d end)
    pal;
  !best

let colormap (pal : (float * float * float) array) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (34 * 256) in
  let add (f : int -> float * float * float) : unit = for c = 0 to 255 do Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr (nearest pal (f c))) done in
  for i = 0 to 31 do
    let k = float (32 - i) /. 32. in
    add (fun (c : int) -> let r, g, bl = pal.(c) in (r *. k, g *. k, bl *. k))
  done;
  (* (Python's round: halves to even) *)
  let round_even (v : float) : float =
    let f = Float.floor v in
    if v -. f > 0.5 then f +. 1. else if v -. f < 0.5 then f else if Float.rem f 2. = 0. then f else f +. 1. in
  add (fun (c : int) ->
      let r, g, bl = pal.(c) in
      let inv = 255. -. round_even ((r *. 0.2126) +. (g *. 0.7152) +. (bl *. 0.0722)) in
      (inv, inv, inv));
  add (fun (_ : int) -> (0., 0., 0.));
  Buffer.contents b

(* a picture's pixels as the palette's indices, -1 where transparent
 * (its alpha, or deutex's cyan) *)
let indices (pal : (float * float * float) array) (cache : (int, int) Hashtbl.t) (img : Rgba_image.t) : int array =
  Array.init (img.width * img.height) (fun (i : int) ->
      let c (k : int) : int = Char.code (Bytes.get img.rgba ((4 * i) + k)) in
      let r = c 0 and g = c 1 and b = c 2 in
      if c 3 < 128 || (r = 0 && g = 255 && b = 255) then -1
      else
        let key = (r lsl 16) lor (g lsl 8) lor b in
        match Hashtbl.find_opt cache key with
        | Some k -> k
        | None ->
            let k = nearest pal (float r, float g, float b) in
            Hashtbl.replace cache key k;
            k)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Pictures *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Doom's picture (a patch, a sprite): its size and offsets, where each
 * column starts, then each column's posts (a run of opaque pixels: its
 * first row, its length, a byte unused, the pixels, a byte unused),
 * 255 its end. A post starts at row 254 at most. *)
let patch_of (w : int) (h : int) ((left, top) : int * int) (px : int array) : string =
  let cols = Buffer.create 4096 in
  let starts = Array.make w 0 in
  for x = 0 to w - 1 do
    starts.(x) <- (8 + (4 * w)) + Buffer.length cols;
    let y = ref 0 in
    while !y < h do
      if px.((!y * w) + x) < 0 then incr y
      else begin
        let y0 = !y in
        while !y < h && px.((!y * w) + x) >= 0 && !y - y0 < 128 do incr y done;
        if y0 > 254 then failwith "a picture taller than Doom's posts can say";
        Buffer.add_char cols (Char.chr y0);
        Buffer.add_char cols (Char.chr (!y - y0));
        Buffer.add_char cols '\000';
        for k = y0 to !y - 1 do Buffer.add_char cols (Char.chr px.((k * w) + x)) done;
        Buffer.add_char cols '\000'
      end
    done;
    Buffer.add_char cols '\255'
  done;
  let b = Buffer.create (8 + (4 * w) + Buffer.length cols) in
  Wad.add_short b w;
  Wad.add_short b h;
  Wad.add_short b left;
  Wad.add_short b top;
  Array.iter (Wad.add_int32 b) starts;
  Buffer.add_buffer b cols;
  Buffer.contents b

(* a PNG's offsets, ZDoom's grAb chunk (two ints, big-endian) *)
let grab (png : string) : int * int =
  match List.assoc_opt "grAb" (Png.chunks png) with
  | Some d when String.length d = 8 ->
      let be (i : int) : int =
        let v = (Char.code d.[i] lsl 24) lor (Char.code d.[i + 1] lsl 16) lor (Char.code d.[i + 2] lsl 8) lor Char.code d.[i + 3] in
        if v >= 0x80000000 then v - 0x100000000 else v in
      (be 0, be 4)
  | _ -> (0, 0)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Textures *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a texture: its size and its patches, each at an offset *)
type texture = { tname : string; width : int; height : int; patches : (string * int * int) list }

let words (l : string) : string list = List.filter (fun (w : string) -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.map (fun (c : char) -> if c = '\t' then ' ' else c) l))

(* a file's lines through the few lines of cpp Freedoom's have
 * (#ifdef, #ifndef, #else, #endif; #define and #include left out),
 * [defined] defined, each line's words, its remark (;) cut *)
let cpp (defined : string list) (text : string) : string list list =
  let stack = ref [] in
  let on () : bool = List.for_all (fun (b : bool) -> b) !stack in
  List.filter_map
    (fun (line : string) ->
      let line = match String.index_opt line ';' with Some i -> String.sub line 0 i | None -> line in
      match words line with
      | "#ifdef" :: d :: _ -> stack := List.mem d defined :: !stack; None
      | "#ifndef" :: d :: _ -> stack := not (List.mem d defined) :: !stack; None
      | "#else" :: _ -> (match !stack with b :: rest -> stack := not b :: rest | [] -> failwith "#else alone"); None
      | "#endif" :: _ -> (match !stack with _ :: rest -> stack := rest | [] -> failwith "#endif alone"); None
      | ("#define" | "#undef" | "#include") :: _ -> None
      | w when on () -> Some w
      | _ -> None)
    (String.split_on_char '\n' text)

(* textures.cfg, DOOM1_VERSIONS defined *)
let textures_of (cfg : string) : texture list =
  let acc = ref [] in
  List.iter
    (fun (w : string list) ->
      match w with
      | "*" :: p :: x :: y :: _ -> (
          match !acc with
          | t :: rest -> acc := { t with patches = t.patches @ [ (String.uppercase_ascii p, int_of_string x, int_of_string y) ] } :: rest
          | [] -> failwith "a patch before any texture")
      (* (and a remark after, at times: "SLADAGN 64 128 : AGM version of sladwall.") *)
      | n :: w :: h :: _ when int_of_string_opt w <> None -> acc := { tname = String.uppercase_ascii n; width = int_of_string w; height = int_of_string h; patches = [] } :: !acc
      | [] -> ()
      | _ -> failwith ("textures.cfg: " ^ String.concat " " w))
    (cpp [ "DOOM1_VERSIONS" ] cfg);
  (* (a name defined twice: the last, as the C preprocessor's file read
   * by deutex keeps; there is none once #ifdef is followed) *)
  List.rev !acc

(* Doom's animations (p_spec.c's animdefs): a frame used, all its
 * frames kept; and a switch's other face (p_switch.c's alphSwitchList,
 * SW1 and SW2) *)
let flat_anims =
  [ [ "NUKAGE1"; "NUKAGE2"; "NUKAGE3" ]; [ "FWATER1"; "FWATER2"; "FWATER3"; "FWATER4" ]; [ "SWATER1"; "SWATER2"; "SWATER3"; "SWATER4" ];
    [ "LAVA1"; "LAVA2"; "LAVA3"; "LAVA4" ]; [ "BLOOD1"; "BLOOD2"; "BLOOD3" ] ]

let texture_anims =
  [ [ "BLODGR1"; "BLODGR2"; "BLODGR3"; "BLODGR4" ]; [ "SLADRIP1"; "SLADRIP2"; "SLADRIP3" ]; [ "BLODRIP1"; "BLODRIP2"; "BLODRIP3"; "BLODRIP4" ];
    [ "FIREWALA"; "FIREWALB"; "FIREWALL" ]; [ "GSTFONT1"; "GSTFONT2"; "GSTFONT3" ]; [ "FIRELAVA"; "FIRELAV3" ];
    [ "FIREMAG1"; "FIREMAG2"; "FIREMAG3" ]; [ "FIREBLU1"; "FIREBLU2" ]; [ "ROCKRED1"; "ROCKRED2"; "ROCKRED3" ];
    [ "BFALL1"; "BFALL2"; "BFALL3"; "BFALL4" ]; [ "SFALL1"; "SFALL2"; "SFALL3"; "SFALL4" ]; [ "WFALL1"; "WFALL2"; "WFALL3"; "WFALL4" ];
    [ "DBRAIN1"; "DBRAIN2"; "DBRAIN3"; "DBRAIN4" ] ]

let with_anims (anims : string list list) (names : string list) : string list =
  List.concat_map (fun (n : string) -> match List.find_opt (List.mem n) anims with Some a -> a | None -> [ n ]) names

let with_switches (names : string list) : string list =
  List.concat_map
    (fun (n : string) ->
      if String.length n > 3 && (String.sub n 0 3 = "SW1" || String.sub n 0 3 = "SW2") then
        let rest = String.sub n 3 (String.length n - 3) in
        [ "SW1" ^ rest; "SW2" ^ rest ]
      else [ n ])
    names

let uniq (l : string list) : string list =
  List.rev (List.fold_left (fun (acc : string list) (x : string) -> if List.mem x acc then acc else x :: acc) [] l)

(* a WAV of 8 bits, one channel, as DMX's sound lump: 3, the rate, the
 * length with the pads, the first sample 16 times, the samples, the
 * last 16 times (what deutex makes of it) *)
let dmx_of_wav (name : string) (wav : string) : string =
  let le32 (i : int) : int = Wad.int32 wav i in
  let rec chunks (i : int) (acc : (string * int * int) list)
      : (string * int * int) list =
    if i + 8 > String.length wav then acc
    else
      let n = le32 (i + 4) in
      chunks (i + 8 + n + (n land 1)) ((String.sub wav i 4, i + 8, n) :: acc) in
  let all = chunks 12 [] in
  let find (id : string) : int * int =
    match List.find_opt (fun ((c, _, _) : string * int * int) -> c = id) all with
    | Some (_, at, n) -> (at, n)
    | None -> failwith (name ^ ": no " ^ id ^ " chunk") in
  let fmt, _ = find "fmt " and data, n = find "data" in
  if Wad.short wav (fmt + 2) <> 1 || Wad.short wav (fmt + 14) <> 8 then
    failwith (name ^ ": not 8 bits, one channel");
  let samples = String.sub wav data n in
  let b = Buffer.create (n + 40) in
  Wad.add_short b 3;
  Wad.add_short b (le32 (fmt + 4));
  Wad.add_int32 b (n + 32);
  Buffer.add_string b (String.make 16 (if n > 0 then samples.[0] else '\128'));
  Buffer.add_string b samples;
  Buffer.add_string b (String.make 16 (if n > 0 then samples.[n - 1] else '\128'));
  Buffer.contents b

(* buildcfg.txt's [sprites]: each sprite's lump, its offsets (Phase 1:
 * Freedoom's Doom, not Doom II's nor FreeDM's) *)
let sprites_of (cfg : string) : (string * int * int) list =
  let section = ref "" in
  List.filter_map
    (fun (w : string list) ->
      match w with
      | [ s ] when String.length s > 2 && s.[0] = '[' -> section := s; None
      | n :: x :: y :: _ when !section = "[sprites]" -> (
          match (int_of_string_opt x, int_of_string_opt y) with Some x, Some y -> Some (String.uppercase_ascii n, x, y) | _ -> None)
      | _ -> None)
    (cpp [ "PHASE1" ] cfg)

let level_lumps = [ "THINGS"; "LINEDEFS"; "SIDEDEFS"; "VERTEXES"; "SEGS"; "SSECTORS"; "NODES"; "SECTORS"; "REJECT"; "BLOCKMAP" ]

let make (caps : < Cap.open_in ; Cap.open_out ; Cap.stdout ; .. >) (dir : string) (out : string) (maps : string list) : unit =
  let read (path : string) : string = FS.read caps (Fpath.v (Filename.concat dir path)) in
  let pal_bytes = read "lumps/playpal/playpal-base.lmp" in
  let pal = palette_of pal_bytes in
  let cache = Hashtbl.create 1024 in
  (* the levels, and what their sides and sectors name *)
  let levels =
    List.map
      (fun (m : string) ->
        let wad = Wad.parse (read (Printf.sprintf "levels/%s.wad" (String.lowercase_ascii m))) in
        (m, List.map (fun (n : string) -> { Wad.name = n; data = Wad.get wad n }) level_lumps))
      maps in
  let names_in (lump : string) (size : int) (offsets : int list) : string list =
    List.concat_map
      (fun ((_, lumps) : string * Wad.lump list) ->
        let d = (List.find (fun (l : Wad.lump) -> l.name = lump) lumps).data in
        List.concat (List.init (String.length d / size) (fun (k : int) -> List.map (fun (o : int) -> Wad.name8 d ((k * size) + o)) offsets)))
      levels
    |> List.filter (fun (n : string) -> n <> "" && n <> "-") in
  (* (SKY1: episode 1's sky, which no side names; F_SKY1 the flat that
   * says the sky is there) *)
  (* (AASHITTY first: Doom's texture 0 is drawn as none, and Freedoom
   * keeps a texture nobody uses there) *)
  let wanted_textures = uniq (with_switches (with_anims texture_anims ("AASHITTY" :: "SKY1" :: names_in "SIDEDEFS" 30 [ 4; 12; 20 ]))) in
  let wanted_flats = uniq (with_anims flat_anims ("F_SKY1" :: names_in "SECTORS" 26 [ 4; 12 ])) in
  let all = textures_of (read "lumps/textures/textures.cfg") in
  let textures =
    List.filter_map
      (fun (n : string) ->
        match List.find_opt (fun (t : texture) -> t.tname = n) (List.rev all) with
        | Some t -> Some t
        | None -> Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "no texture %s in textures.cfg\n" n); None)
      wanted_textures in
  let pnames = uniq (List.concat_map (fun (t : texture) -> List.map (fun ((p, _, _) : string * int * int) -> p) t.patches) textures) in
  let picture (path : string) : string =
    let png = read path in
    let img = Png.decode png in
    patch_of img.width img.height (grab png) (indices pal cache img) in
  let patches = List.map (fun (p : string) -> { Wad.name = p; data = picture (Printf.sprintf "patches/%s.png" (String.lowercase_ascii p)) }) pnames in
  let flats =
    List.map
      (fun (f : string) ->
        let img = Png.decode (read (Printf.sprintf "flats/%s.png" (String.lowercase_ascii f))) in
        if img.width <> 64 || img.height <> 64 then failwith (f ^ ": a flat is 64 by 64");
        let px = indices pal cache img in
        { Wad.name = f; data = String.init 4096 (fun (i : int) -> Char.chr (max 0 px.(i))) })
      wanted_flats in
  (* the sprites of every thing of the levels *)
  let kinds = List.concat_map (fun ((_, lumps) : string * Wad.lump list) ->
    let d = (List.find (fun (l : Wad.lump) -> l.name = "THINGS") lumps).data in
    List.init (String.length d / 10) (fun (k : int) -> Wad.short d ((10 * k) + 6))) levels in
  let names = uniq (Things.sprite_names kinds @ Info.sprites) in
  let sprites =
    List.filter_map
      (fun ((n, x, y) : string * int * int) ->
        if String.length n >= 6 && List.mem (String.sub n 0 4) names then begin
          let png = read (Printf.sprintf "sprites/%s.png" (String.lowercase_ascii n)) in
          let img = Png.decode png in
          Some { Wad.name = n; data = patch_of img.width img.height (x, y) (indices pal cache img) }
        end
        else None)
      (sprites_of (read "buildcfg.txt")) in
  let texture1 =
    let b = Buffer.create 16384 in
    let n = List.length textures in
    Wad.add_int32 b n;
    let sizes = List.map (fun (t : texture) -> 22 + (10 * List.length t.patches)) textures in
    ignore (List.fold_left (fun (pos : int) (s : int) -> Wad.add_int32 b pos; pos + s) (4 + (4 * n)) sizes);
    List.iter
      (fun (t : texture) ->
        Wad.add_name8 b t.tname;
        Wad.add_int32 b 0;
        Wad.add_short b t.width;
        Wad.add_short b t.height;
        Wad.add_int32 b 0;
        Wad.add_short b (List.length t.patches);
        List.iter
          (fun ((p, x, y) : string * int * int) ->
            let rec idx (k : int) (l : string list) : int = match l with q :: rest -> if q = p then k else idx (k + 1) rest | [] -> assert false in
            Wad.add_short b x; Wad.add_short b y; Wad.add_short b (idx 0 pnames); Wad.add_short b 1; Wad.add_short b 0)
          t.patches)
      textures;
    Buffer.contents b in
  let pnames_lump =
    let b = Buffer.create 4096 in
    Wad.add_int32 b (List.length pnames);
    List.iter (Wad.add_name8 b) pnames;
    Buffer.contents b in
  let sounds =
    List.map
      (fun (n : string) ->
        let path = Printf.sprintf "sounds/ds%s.wav" n in
        let data = dmx_of_wav path (read path) in
        { Wad.name = String.uppercase_ascii ("ds" ^ n); data })
      Info.sounds in
  let musics =
    List.filter_map
      (fun ((m, _) : string * Wad.lump list) ->
        let path = Printf.sprintf "musics/d_%s.mid" (String.lowercase_ascii m) in
        try Some { Wad.name = "D_" ^ m; data = read path }
        with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> None)
      levels in
  let lumps =
    [ { Wad.name = "PLAYPAL"; data = pal_bytes }; { Wad.name = "COLORMAP"; data = colormap pal } ]
    @ List.concat_map (fun ((m, l) : string * Wad.lump list) -> { Wad.name = m; data = "" } :: l) levels
    @ [ { Wad.name = "TEXTURE1"; data = texture1 }; { Wad.name = "PNAMES"; data = pnames_lump } ]
    @ [ { Wad.name = "P_START"; data = "" } ] @ patches @ [ { Wad.name = "P_END"; data = "" } ]
    @ [ { Wad.name = "F_START"; data = "" } ] @ flats @ [ { Wad.name = "F_END"; data = "" } ]
    @ [ { Wad.name = "S_START"; data = "" } ] @ sprites @ [ { Wad.name = "S_END"; data = "" } ]
    @ sounds @ musics in
  let bytes = Wad.write "IWAD" lumps in
  FS.write caps (Fpath.v out) bytes;
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%s: %d levels, %d textures of %d patches, %d flats\n" out
       (List.length levels) (List.length textures) (List.length patches)
       (List.length flats)
     ^ Printf.sprintf "%d sprites' pictures, %d sounds, %d musics, %d bytes\n"
         (List.length sprites) (List.length sounds) (List.length musics)
         (String.length bytes))

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      Exit.exit caps @@ Exit.catch @@ fun () ->
      (match Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps) with
      | _ :: dir :: out :: (_ :: _ as maps) -> make caps dir out (List.map String.uppercase_ascii maps)
      | _ -> failwith usage);
      Exit.OK)
