(* Play: the player's walk (Quake's sv_user.c: SV_ClientThink,
 * SV_UserFriction, SV_Accelerate, SV_AirAccelerate, SV_WaterMove;
 * sv_phys.c: SV_WalkMove, SV_FlyMove, SV_PushEntity; cl_input.c's
 * speeds; view.c's bob), and the level's moving things (Brushes).
 *
 * Each frame, the keys make a wish: a direction and a speed (200 units
 * a second forward, 400 running, 350 aside). On the ground, friction
 * slows the player (4 times the speed a second, at least 100: a stop in
 * a quarter of a second), then the wish accelerates it (10 times the
 * wish a second, up to the wish's speed); in the air, the wish only
 * steers, 30 at most: Quake's air control, which players learned to
 * use (strafe-jumping: a wish at an angle to the speed adds to it).
 * Gravity, 800 units a second squared; a jump, 270 up.
 *
 * The move (SV_FlyMove): the box traced along the velocity (Trace);
 * stopped by a plane, the velocity is made parallel to it (clipped) and
 * the rest of the time traced again, up to four times: the player
 * slides along walls and into corners. A wall that stops it at the
 * feet may be a step (SV_WalkMove): the move is tried again 18 units
 * up, then put down; kept if it ends on a floor (a normal's z above
 * 0.7: 45 degrees), else the move without the step.
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-quake: the game calls frame each frame of
 * the playground, with the time since the last; Render draws from eye,
 * pitch, yaw. *)

type command = {
  forward : bool;
  back : bool;
  left : bool;
  right : bool;
  strafe_left : bool;
  strafe_right : bool;
  jump : bool;
  run : bool;
  look_up : bool;
  look_down : bool;
  use_key : bool;
}

type t = {
  level : Model.t;
  brushes : Brushes.t;
  (* the player: where, how fast, which way, on what *)
  body : Brushes.body;
  mutable pitch : float;
  (* 0 dry, 1 feet, 2 waist, 3 eyes under (SV_CheckWater) *)
  mutable waterlevel : int;
  mutable jump_released : bool;
  mutable use_released : bool;
  (* the time since the start, seconds *)
  mutable time : float;
  (* the light styles' strings, 64 of them (world.qc's, and the
   * switched lights') *)
  styles : string array;
  (* the horizontal speed, for the bob *)
  mutable bob_speed : float;
  (* the boxes in the player's way besides the level's: the monsters'
   * (their absolute mins and maxs), given by the game *)
  mutable boxes : unit -> (Model.vec * Model.vec) list;
}

(* [create m]: the player at info_player_start *)
val create : Model.t -> t

(* [place p origin yaw pitch]: the player there, still *)
val place : t -> Model.vec -> float -> float -> unit

(* [frame p dt c]: dt seconds of the game *)
val frame : t -> float -> command -> unit

(* the eye: 22 units above the origin, bobbing as it walks (V_CalcBob) *)
val eye : t -> Model.vec

(* the yaw *)
val yaw : t -> float

(* the brush models to draw: (entity, model, origin, frame) *)
val bmodels : t -> (int * int * Model.vec * int) list

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Trace.mli *)

open Model

type trace = {
  fraction : float;
  endpos : vec;
  normal : vec;
  startsolid : bool;
  allsolid : bool;
  hit : int;
}

(* what a trace learns on its way (trace_t, filled by the walk) *)
type state = {
  mutable sfraction : float;
  mutable send : vec;
  mutable snormal : vec;
  mutable sstartsolid : bool;
  mutable sallsolid : bool;
}

let dist_epsilon = 0.03125

let plane_dist (p : plane) (q : vec) : float =
  match p.kind with
  | 0 -> q.x -. p.dist
  | 1 -> q.y -. p.dist
  | 2 -> q.z -. p.dist
  | _ -> dot p.normal q -. p.dist

let rec hull_point_contents (h : hull) (num : int) (p : vec) : int =
  if num < 0 then num
  else
    hull_point_contents h
      (if plane_dist h.cplanes.(num) p >= 0. then h.front.(num)
       else h.back.(num))
      p

let point_contents (m : Model.t) (p : vec) : contents =
  Model.contents_of
    (hull_point_contents m.hulls.(0) m.submodels.(0).headnode.(0) p)

(* SV_RecursiveHullCheck: false when the segment was stopped *)
let rec check (h : hull) (root : int) (num : int) (p1f : float) (p2f : float)
    (p1 : vec) (p2 : vec) (st : state) : bool =
  if num < 0 then begin
    if num <> -2 then st.sallsolid <- false else st.sstartsolid <- true;
    true
  end
  else begin
    let pl = h.cplanes.(num) in
    let t1 = plane_dist pl p1 and t2 = plane_dist pl p2 in
    if t1 >= 0. && t2 >= 0. then check h root h.front.(num) p1f p2f p1 p2 st
    else if t1 < 0. && t2 < 0. then check h root h.back.(num) p1f p2f p1 p2 st
    else begin
      (* the crossing, put DIST_EPSILON on the near side *)
      let frac =
        if t1 < 0. then (t1 +. dist_epsilon) /. (t1 -. t2)
        else (t1 -. dist_epsilon) /. (t1 -. t2)
      in
      let frac = Float.max 0. (Float.min 1. frac) in
      let at (f : float) : float * vec =
        (p1f +. ((p2f -. p1f) *. f), add p1 (scale f (sub p2 p1)))
      in
      let midf, mid = at frac in
      let near, far =
        if t1 < 0. then (h.back.(num), h.front.(num))
        else (h.front.(num), h.back.(num))
      in
      if not (check h root near p1f midf p1 mid st) then false
      else if hull_point_contents h far mid <> -2 then
        check h root far midf p2f mid p2 st
      else if st.sallsolid then false
      else begin
        (* the other side is solid: the impact *)
        st.snormal <- (if t1 < 0. then scale (-1.) pl.normal else pl.normal);
        (* (backed up while in solid: the floats of the hulls) *)
        let frac = ref frac
        and midf = ref midf
        and mid = ref mid
        and gave_up = ref false in
        while (not !gave_up) && hull_point_contents h root !mid = -2 do
          frac := !frac -. 0.1;
          if !frac < 0. then gave_up := true
          else begin
            let f, q = at !frac in
            midf := f;
            mid := q
          end
        done;
        st.sfraction <- !midf;
        st.send <- !mid;
        false
      end
    end
  end

let hull_check (m : Model.t) (hull_num : int) (headnode : int) (start : vec)
    (finish : vec) : trace =
  let h = m.hulls.(hull_num) in
  let st =
    {
      sfraction = 1.;
      send = finish;
      snormal = zero;
      sstartsolid = false;
      sallsolid = true;
    }
  in
  ignore (check h headnode headnode 0. 1. start finish st);
  {
    fraction = st.sfraction;
    endpos = st.send;
    normal = st.snormal;
    startsolid = st.sstartsolid;
    allsolid = st.sallsolid;
    hit = -1;
  }

let move (m : Model.t) (hull_num : int) (start : vec) (finish : vec)
    (solids : (int * int * vec) list) : trace =
  let world =
    hull_check m hull_num m.submodels.(0).headnode.(hull_num) start finish
  in
  List.fold_left
    (fun (best : trace) ((ent, k, origin) : int * int * vec) ->
      (* (the segment in the model's space) *)
      let t =
        hull_check m hull_num
          m.submodels.(k).headnode.(hull_num)
          (sub start origin) (sub finish origin)
      in
      let t = { t with endpos = add t.endpos origin; hit = ent } in
      if t.allsolid || t.startsolid || t.fraction < best.fraction then
        (* (SV_ClipToLinks: a start in solid wins) *)
        if best.startsolid then { t with startsolid = true } else t
      else best)
    world solids

(* SV_HullForBox's question for a segment: where it enters the box
 * (mins, maxs), by the slabs, the box already grown by the mover's
 * own (an entity's box is a hull of its own in world.c) *)
let box (start : vec) (finish : vec) (mins : vec) (maxs : vec) : trace option =
  let d = sub finish start in
  let enter = ref (-1.) and leave = ref 2. and normal = ref zero in
  let ok = ref true in
  let axis (s : float) (dv : float) (lo : float) (hi : float) (n : vec) : unit =
    if dv = 0. then (if s <= lo || s >= hi then ok := false)
    else begin
      let t1 = (lo -. s) /. dv and t2 = (hi -. s) /. dv in
      let tin, tout, nin =
        if t1 < t2 then (t1, t2, scale (-1.) n) else (t2, t1, n)
      in
      if tin > !enter then begin
        enter := tin;
        normal := nin
      end;
      if tout < !leave then leave := tout
    end
  in
  axis start.x d.x mins.x maxs.x { x = 1.; y = 0.; z = 0. };
  axis start.y d.y mins.y maxs.y { x = 0.; y = 1.; z = 0. };
  axis start.z d.z mins.z maxs.z { x = 0.; y = 0.; z = 1. };
  if (not !ok) || !enter > !leave || !enter > 1. || !leave < 0. then None
  else if !enter < 0. then
    Some
      {
        fraction = 0.;
        endpos = start;
        normal = zero;
        startsolid = true;
        allsolid = !leave > 1.;
        hit = -1;
      }
  else
    (* (1/32 back, DIST_EPSILON, as the hull's) *)
    let len = length d in
    let f = Float.max 0. (!enter -. if len > 0. then 0.03125 /. len else 0.) in
    Some
      {
        fraction = f;
        endpos = add start (scale f d);
        normal = !normal;
        startsolid = false;
        allsolid = false;
        hit = -1;
      }
games/fps/quake/server/Trace.mli

(* Trace: a box moved through the level, where it stops (Quake's
 * world.c: SV_RecursiveHullCheck, SV_HullPointContents,
 * SV_ClipMoveToEntity).
 *
 * The player is a box of 32 by 32 by 56, and testing a box against
 * every wall is costly; qbsp made instead, besides the tree drawn,
 * trees of the same space with each wall pushed out by the box's
 * half-size (the hulls, Model's clipnodes). In hull 1 the player is a
 * point: its move is a segment, and where the segment first enters
 * solid space is where the box would touch a wall:
 *
 *      hull 0 (the walls)          hull 1 (pushed out by 16)
 *      |                           |   |
 *      |   [box]  ---> move        |   |  .  ---> the box's center,
 *      |                           |   |         a point
 *
 * The walk down the tree: a node whose plane the segment does not
 * cross sends it to one side; one it crosses splits it, the near half
 * first; the first solid leaf reached is the impact, the plane crossed
 * last its normal, the point put 1/32 of a unit back (DIST_EPSILON) so
 * that the next move does not start in the wall.
 *
 * A brush model (a door) is the same with its own hulls, the segment
 * moved by its origin. *)

type trace = {
  (* the part of the move made, 0 to 1 *)
  fraction : float;
  endpos : Model.vec;
  (* the plane hit: its normal, towards the mover *)
  normal : Model.vec;
  (* started in solid, all in solid *)
  startsolid : bool;
  allsolid : bool;
  (* what was hit: -1 the world, else the brush model's entity *)
  hit : int;
}

(* [move m hull_num start finish solids]: the move of a point of hull
 * hull_num (1: the player's) from start to finish, through the world
 * and the solid brush models given (their entity, their model, their
 * origin); the nearest impact *)
val move :
  Model.t ->
  int ->
  Model.vec ->
  Model.vec ->
  (int * int * Model.vec) list ->
  trace

(* [point_contents m p]: the contents at p in hull 0 *)
val point_contents : Model.t -> Model.vec -> Model.contents

(* [hull_check m hull_num headnode start finish]: one model's trace,
 * its points in its own space *)
val hull_check : Model.t -> int -> int -> Model.vec -> Model.vec -> trace

(* [box start finish mins maxs]: a point's move against a box (an
 * entity's, grown by the mover's half-size: world.c's box hull), if it
 * enters it *)
val box : Model.vec -> Model.vec -> Model.vec -> Model.vec -> trace option

(* See Sound.mli *)

open Model

type t = {
  read : string -> string option;
  three_d : bool;
  cache : (string, Audio.sound option) Hashtbl.t;
}

let create (read : string -> string option) (three_d : bool) : t =
  { read; three_d; cache = Hashtbl.create 64 }

let sound (s : t) (name : string) : Audio.sound option =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt s.cache name with
  | Some v -> v
  | None ->
      let v = Option.map Audio.wav (s.read ("sound/" ^ name ^ ".wav")) in
      Hashtbl.replace s.cache name v;
      v

(* snd_dma.c's sound_nominal_clip_dist *)
let clip_dist = 1000.

(* the effects' master volume (Quake's "volume", 0.7 by default): a
 * fight's sounds at once stay under the music's top *)
let volume = 0.5

let play (s : t) (sounds : Edict.sound list) (eye : vec) (yaw : float) : unit =
  let a = yaw *. Float.pi /. 180. in
  (* (the listener's right: the yaw less a quarter turn) *)
  let right = { x = Float.sin a; y = -.Float.cos a; z = 0. } in
  (* (one of a name a frame: a shotgun's pellets' ricochets, one) *)
  let heard = Hashtbl.create 8 in
  List.iter
    (fun (e : Edict.sound) ->
      if not (Hashtbl.mem heard e.sfx) then begin
        Hashtbl.replace heard e.sfx ();
        match (sound s e.sfx, e.at) with
        | None, _ -> ()
        | Some snd, None -> Audio.play (Audio.louder volume snd)
        | Some snd, Some o ->
            if s.three_d then begin
              let m (v : vec) : float * float * float =
                (v.x /. 32., v.y /. 32., v.z /. 32.)
              in
              let ears = Audio3d.facing ~velocity:(0., 0., 0.) (m eye) a in
              Audio.play
                (Audio3d.heard ears ~velocity:(0., 0., 0.)
                   ~reference:(clip_dist /. 32. /. 8.)
                   ~speed_of_sound:343. (m o) (Audio.louder volume snd))
            end
            else begin
              let d = sub o eye in
              let dist = length d *. e.attenuation /. clip_dist in
              let vol = if e.attenuation = 0. then 1. else 1. -. dist in
              if vol > 0. then begin
                let pan =
                  if length d < 1. then 0. else dot right (normalize d)
                in
                (* old: Audio.play (snd |> Audio.louder (volume *. vol)
                 *   |> Audio.pan pan) *)
                Audio.play_at ~volume:(volume *. vol) ~pan snd
              end
            end
      end)
    sounds

(* Sound: what the player hears (Quake's snd_dma.c: S_StartSound,
 * SND_Spatialize; snd_mem.c: a sound's WAV loaded), through
 * lib_playground's Audio.
 *
 * A sound is a WAV of sound/ (sound/weapons/bounce.wav), 8 or 16
 * bits, at its own rate (Audio.wav takes either, and resamples it),
 * loaded the first time it is heard (Quake's precache did it at the
 * level's start).
 *
 * Where it comes from changes it (SND_Spatialize): quieter with the
 * distance, by the sound's attenuation (1 a monster's or a weapon's,
 * 2 an idle growl's: twice as fast), silent at 1,000 units over the
 * attenuation; and to the side it is on, by the dot of the listener's
 * right with the way to the sound:
 *
 *   loudness = 1 - distance x attenuation / 1000 (times the master
 *              volume, 0.5)
 *   pan = right . (source - ear) / |source - ear|      (-1 left, 1 right)
 *
 * With sound=3d, the playground's Audio3d (the distance's law, the
 * air's dulling, the time between the ears; 32 units a meter).
 *
 * Where it stands in mini-quake: Quake.ml plays each frame's sounds
 * (Game's), from where the player is. *)

type t

(* [create read three_d]: [read] a file beside the level (sound/x.wav) *)
val create : (string -> string option) -> bool -> t

(* [play s sounds eye yaw]: the sounds, heard at eye facing yaw
 * (degrees) *)
val play : t -> Edict.sound list -> Model.vec -> float -> unit
games/fps/quake/tools/Light.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-light: a level's lightmaps baked, id's light (qutils' light.c,
 * ltface.c, trace.c, 1996), the last of the three tools a Quake map
 * went through (qbsp, vis, light). It reads the .bsp qbsp made, and
 * writes it again with its LIGHTING lump and each face's light styles
 * and lightmaps' offset.
 *
 * Quake's light is computed here, once, for hours on id's machines;
 * the game only reads it (Surfcache). For each face:
 *
 * 1. Its samples: a point every 16 texels of its texture's s and t,
 *    from its extents (Model), a grid of (w + 1) by (h + 1) points
 *    lifted 1 unit off the face (CalcFaceVectors, CalcPoints). A
 *    point inside the rock (a face's corner against a wall) is moved
 *    towards the face's middle until a ray from the middle reaches it.
 *
 *        +---------------+      x  a sample; the face's texture
 *        x   x   x   x   x         is 64 texels wide, the samples
 *        |               |         16 apart: 5 of them a row
 *        x   x   x   x   x
 *        +---------------+
 *
 * 2. For each light of the map's entities (light, light_torch_..., its
 *    "light" value, 300 by default), each sample asks: does a straight
 *    line from the light reach me through the empty leaves of the BSP
 *    (trace: the tree's walk of the segment, split at each plane it
 *    crosses)? If so, it adds
 *
 *         (light - distance) x (0.5 + 0.5 cos angle)
 *
 *    linear in the distance, a light of 300 reaches 300 units; the
 *    angle between the face's normal and the light (half of it a
 *    constant: id's scalecos, so a wall in grazing light is not black).
 *    A shadow is only that: a sample the line does not reach.
 *
 * 3. Each light has a style (0 the steady light; 1 to 12 flicker,
 *    pulse, strobe: world.qc's strings; 32 and up a light switched by
 *    a trigger). A face keeps a lightmap a style that reaches it, up to
 *    4: the game adds them, each scaled by its style's value at the
 *    time. That is how Quake's lights flicker with lightmaps baked
 *    once: the flickering part is a map of its own.
 *
 * 4. The sums halved (id's rangescale) and clamped to 255, a byte a
 *    sample: 128 is the texture as painted (the colormap's row 32).
 *
 * Beyond id's, what LibreQuake's map asks of ericw-tools, where it is
 * small: "wait" (the falloff's scale: light - distance x wait),
 * "mangle" (a spotlight, its cone "angle", 40 degrees), "_sunlight"
 * (a sample whose ray towards the sun, "_sun_mangle", ends in a sky
 * face is lit, by the angle only) and "_sunlight2" (the same from 32
 * directions of the sky's dome, the light shared among them), the
 * worldspawn's "light" (the least a sample gets), and "_bounce": the
 * light the walls send back, after the direct light and before the
 * sums are halved (section 2 below: a radiosity of a few passes;
 * "_bouncescale" scales it). Not: "_dirt" (corners darkened), colours
 * (a .lit file), "delay" (other falloffs), surface lights.
 *
 * history:
 * id's light (1996) had the direct light only: Quake's rooms are dark
 * where no lamp sees, their corners black. Radiosity (Goral, Torrance,
 * Greenberg and Battaile, "Modeling the Interaction of Light Between
 * Diffuse Surfaces", SIGGRAPH 1984) was what offline renderers did; id
 * baked it for Quake II's lightmaps (qrad3, 1997), and ericw-tools
 * gave Quake's maps a bounce in the 2010s.
 *
 * usage: mini-light in.bsp out.bsp [palette.lmp]
 *   palette: the textures' colours, for how much they reflect (half,
 *   without it) *)

let usage = "usage: mini-light in.bsp out.bsp [palette.lmp]"

open Model

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The trace (trace.c) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the contents where the segment p1 -> p2 first stops: -2 the rock, -6
 * the sky; -1 if it goes through (water and slime let light through) *)
let rec first_hit (h : hull) (num : int) (p1 : vec) (p2 : vec) : int =
  if num < 0 then if num = -2 || num = -6 then num else -1
  else begin
    let pl = h.cplanes.(num) in
    let d1 = dot pl.normal p1 -. pl.dist and d2 = dot pl.normal p2 -. pl.dist in
    if d1 >= -0.1 && d2 >= -0.1 then first_hit h h.front.(num) p1 p2
    else if d1 < 0.1 && d2 < 0.1 then first_hit h h.back.(num) p1 p2
    else begin
      (* split where it crosses: the side of p1 first *)
      let f = d1 /. (d1 -. d2) in
      let mid = add p1 (scale f (sub p2 p1)) in
      let near, far =
        if d1 >= 0. then (h.front.(num), h.back.(num))
        else (h.back.(num), h.front.(num))
      in
      let c = first_hit h near p1 mid in
      if c <> -1 then c else first_hit h far mid p2
    end
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The lights *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type light = {
  origin : vec;
  value : float;
  style : int;
  wait : float;
  (* a spotlight's direction, and the cosine of its cone's half *)
  spot : (vec * float) option;
}

let deg (a : float) : float = a *. 4. *. atan 1. /. 180.

(* yaw pitch roll: a direction (pitch 90 is up) *)
let direction (s : string) : vec =
  let a = vec_of_string s in
  let yaw = deg a.x and pitch = deg a.y in
  { x = cos pitch *. cos yaw; y = cos pitch *. sin yaw; z = sin pitch }

let float_value (e : (string * string) list) (k : string) (default : float) :
    float =
  match value e k with
  | Some v -> (
      match float_of_string_opt (String.trim v) with
      | Some f -> f
      | None -> default)
  | None -> default

let lights_of (entities : (string * string) list list) : light list =
  (* a light switched by a trigger: a style of 32 and up a name *)
  let named = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  List.filter_map
    (fun (e : (string * string) list) ->
      match value e "classname" with
      | Some c when String.length c >= 5 && String.sub c 0 5 = "light" -> (
          match value e "origin" with
          | None -> None
          | Some o ->
              let style = int_of_float (float_value e "style" 0.) in
              let style =
                match value e "targetname" with
                | Some t when style = 0 && t <> "" -> (
                    match Hashtbl.find_opt named t with
                    | Some s -> s
                    | None ->
                        let s = 32 + Hashtbl.length named in
                        Hashtbl.add named t s;
                        s)
                | _ -> style
              in
              let spot =
                Option.map
                  (fun (m : string) ->
                    (direction m, cos (deg (float_value e "angle" 40. /. 2.))))
                  (value e "mangle")
              in
              Some
                {
                  origin = vec_of_string o;
                  value = float_value e "light" 300.;
                  style;
                  wait = float_value e "wait" 1.;
                  spot;
                })
      | _ -> None)
    entities

(* the entities again, each switched light with its style written (as
 * id's light did: the game's light.qc reads it, lightstyle(style, "a")) *)
let with_styles (entities : (string * string) list list) : string =
  let named = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let b = Buffer.create 65536 in
  List.iter
    (fun (e : (string * string) list) ->
      let e =
        match (value e "classname", value e "targetname") with
        | Some c, Some t
          when String.length c >= 5
               && String.sub c 0 5 = "light"
               && t <> ""
               && int_of_float (float_value e "style" 0.) = 0 ->
            let s =
              match Hashtbl.find_opt named t with
              | Some s -> s
              | None ->
                  let s = 32 + Hashtbl.length named in
                  Hashtbl.add named t s;
                  s
            in
            List.filter (fun ((k, _) : string * string) -> k <> "style") e
            @ [ ("style", string_of_int s) ]
        | _ -> e
      in
      Buffer.add_string b "{\n";
      List.iter
        (fun ((k, v) : string * string) ->
          Buffer.add_string b (Printf.sprintf "\"%s\" \"%s\"\n" k v))
        e;
      Buffer.add_string b "}\n")
    entities;
  (* (the lump ends with a zero, as qbsp's) *)
  Buffer.add_char b '\000';
  Buffer.contents b

(* the sky's dome: 32 directions above, by a golden spiral *)
let dome : vec list =
  List.init 32 (fun (k : int) ->
      let z = (float k +. 0.5) /. 32. in
      let r = sqrt (1. -. (z *. z)) and a = float k *. 2.39996 in
      { x = r *. cos a; y = r *. sin a; z })

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A face (ltface.c) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the face's samples, in the world, (w + 1) by (h + 1) *)
let points (m : Model.t) (f : surface) : vec array * int * int =
  let ti = f.texinfo in
  let normal = if f.back then scale (-1.) f.plane.normal else f.plane.normal in
  let dist = if f.back then -.f.plane.dist else f.plane.dist in
  (* from texture space back to the world (CalcFaceVectors): along the
   * texture's normal, a point keeps its s and t *)
  let texnormal = normalize (cross ti.t ti.s) in
  let distscale = dot texnormal normal in
  let texnormal = if distscale < 0. then scale (-1.) texnormal else texnormal in
  let distscale = 1. /. Float.abs distscale in
  let back_of (v : vec) : vec =
    let len = length v in
    let d = dot v normal *. distscale in
    scale (1. /. (len *. len)) (sub v (scale d texnormal))
  in
  let tw_s = back_of ti.s and tw_t = back_of ti.t in
  let org = add (scale (-.ti.s_offset) tw_s) (scale (-.ti.t_offset) tw_t) in
  (* (on the face's plane, then 1 unit off it) *)
  let d = (dot org normal -. dist -. 1.) *. distscale in
  let org = sub org (scale d texnormal) in
  let at (s : float) (t : float) : vec =
    add org (add (scale s tw_s) (scale t tw_t))
  in
  let smin, tmin = f.texturemins and ew, eh = f.extents in
  let w = ew / 16 and h = eh / 16 in
  let mids = float smin +. (float ew /. 2.)
  and midt = float tmin +. (float eh /. 2.) in
  let mid = at mids midt in
  let hull = m.hulls.(0) and root = m.submodels.(0).headnode.(0) in
  let pts =
    Array.init
      ((w + 1) * (h + 1))
      (fun (k : int) ->
        let us = ref (float (smin + (k mod (w + 1) * 16)))
        and ut = ref (float (tmin + (k / (w + 1) * 16))) in
        (* (towards the middle, 8 texels a try, until the middle sees it) *)
        let rec try_ (i : int) : vec =
          let p = at !us !ut in
          if i = 5 || first_hit hull root mid p = -1 then p
          else begin
            let toward (u : float ref) (mid : float) : unit =
              if !u > mid then u := Float.max mid (!u -. 8.)
              else u := Float.min mid (!u +. 8.)
            in
            if i land 1 = 1 then toward us mids else toward ut midt;
            try_ (i + 1)
          end
        in
        try_ 0)
  in
  (pts, w, h)

(* a face being lit: its samples, its side, its sums a style *)
type lit = {
  face : surface;
  pts : vec array;
  (* the grid's columns: w + 1 *)
  cols : int;
  normal : vec;
  mutable maps : (int * float array) list;
}

(* 1. the direct light: each light, the sun, the sky's dome *)
let direct (m : Model.t) (lights : light list) (sun : (vec * float) list)
    (f : surface) : lit =
  let pts, w, _ = points m f in
  let n = Array.length pts in
  let normal = if f.back then scale (-1.) f.plane.normal else f.plane.normal in
  let dist = if f.back then -.f.plane.dist else f.plane.dist in
  let hull = m.hulls.(0) and root = m.submodels.(0).headnode.(0) in
  (* a lightmap a style, in the order they came *)
  let maps : (int * float array) list ref = ref [] in
  let map_of (style : int) : float array =
    match List.assoc_opt style !maps with
    | Some a -> a
    | None ->
        let a = Array.make n 0. in
        maps := !maps @ [ (style, a) ];
        a
  in
  List.iter
    (fun (l : light) ->
      let d = dot l.origin normal -. dist in
      (* (behind the face, or too far for its light) *)
      if d > 0. && d *. l.wait < l.value then begin
        let acc = Array.make n 0. and hit = ref false in
        Array.iteri
          (fun (k : int) (p : vec) ->
            let incoming = sub l.origin p in
            let dist = length incoming in
            let incoming = scale (1. /. Float.max dist 1.) incoming in
            let in_cone =
              match l.spot with
              | None -> true
              | Some (dir, cone) -> -.dot dir incoming >= cone
            in
            let add =
              (l.value -. (dist *. l.wait))
              *. (0.5 +. (0.5 *. dot incoming normal))
            in
            if in_cone && add > 0. && first_hit hull root l.origin p = -1 then begin
              acc.(k) <- add;
              if add > 1. then hit := true
            end)
          pts;
        if !hit then begin
          let a = map_of l.style in
          Array.iteri (fun (k : int) (v : float) -> a.(k) <- a.(k) +. v) acc
        end
      end)
    lights;
  (* the sun, and the sky's dome *)
  List.iter
    (fun ((dir, value) : vec * float) ->
      let towards = scale (-1.) dir in
      let c = dot towards normal in
      if c > 0. then begin
        let a = map_of 0 in
        Array.iteri
          (fun (k : int) (p : vec) ->
            if first_hit hull root p (add p (scale 16384. towards)) = -6 then
              a.(k) <- a.(k) +. (value *. (0.5 +. (0.5 *. c))))
          pts
      end)
    sun;
  { face = f; pts; cols = w + 1; normal; maps = !maps }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* 2. The bounce (ericw-tools' _bounce) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A wall lit sends part of its light back: what makes a room lit
 * from one lamp not black where the lamp does not see. The faces' own
 * samples are the senders, by 4 by 4 (a patch of 64 by 64 texels,
 * its light their mean, as much as its texture's colour reflects), and
 * the receivers: what a receiver gets of a patch falls with the square
 * of the distance, and by the cosines at both ends (a patch seen
 * edge-on sends nothing):
 *
 *     received = light x reflectivity x area x cos e x cos r / (pi d^2)
 *
 * so a sample before a wide wall of light L gets about L times its
 * reflectivity, as a sample would in the real world. The patch must
 * see the sample (a trace) from a leaf that may (the PVS). Each pass
 * sends what the pass before received: the map's _bounce says how
 * many. Only the steady light (style 0) bounces. *)

type patch = {
  pos : vec;
  pnormal : vec;
  flux : float;
  reach2 : float;
  leaf : int;
}

(* a texture's reflectivity: its mean colour, 0 to 1 (0.5 without the
 * palette) *)
let reflectivity (palette : string option) (t : texture) : float =
  match palette with
  | None -> 0.5
  | Some pal ->
      let mip = t.mips.(3) in
      let sum = ref 0 in
      String.iter
        (fun (c : char) ->
          let i = 3 * Char.code c in
          sum :=
            !sum
            + Char.code pal.[i]
            + Char.code pal.[i + 1]
            + Char.code pal.[i + 2])
        mip;
      float !sum /. (3. *. 255. *. float (String.length mip))

let pi = 4. *. atan 1.

(* the light a sample must get from a patch to count: a quarter of a
 * level of the lightmap's 256 (before id's halving) *)
let least = 0.05

let bounce (m : Model.t) (lits : lit array) (palette : string option)
    (passes : int) (bouncescale : float) : unit =
  let hull = m.hulls.(0) and root = m.submodels.(0).headnode.(0) in
  let pvs_rows = Hashtbl.create 256 in
  let row (leaf : int) : Bytes.t =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt pvs_rows leaf with
    | Some r -> r
    | None ->
        let r = Model.pvs m m.leaves.(leaf) in
        Hashtbl.add pvs_rows leaf r;
        r
  in
  (* each receiver: its middle, its radius, its leaf (a little off it:
   * not the rock's) *)
  let middle (l : lit) : vec =
    scale (1. /. float (Array.length l.pts)) (Array.fold_left add zero l.pts)
  in
  let mids = Array.map middle lits in
  let radius =
    Array.mapi
      (fun (i : int) (l : lit) ->
        Array.fold_left
          (fun (r : float) (p : vec) -> Float.max r (length (sub p mids.(i))))
          0. l.pts)
      lits
  in
  let leaves =
    Array.mapi
      (fun (i : int) (l : lit) ->
        (Model.leaf_at m (add mids.(i) (scale 4. l.normal))).lindex)
      lits
  in
  let sent =
    ref
      (Array.map
         (fun (l : lit) ->
           match List.assoc_opt 0 l.maps with
           | Some a -> a
           | None -> Array.make (Array.length l.pts) 0.)
         lits)
  in
  for _pass = 1 to passes do
    (* the patches of what was received last *)
    let patches =
      List.concat
        (Array.to_list
           (Array.mapi
              (fun (i : int) (l : lit) ->
                let ti = l.face.texinfo in
                let refl = bouncescale *. reflectivity palette ti.texture in
                (* (a sample's area: 16 texels each way, in units) *)
                let area = 16. /. length ti.s *. (16. /. length ti.t) in
                let a = !sent.(i) in
                let groups = Hashtbl.create 16 in
                Array.iteri
                  (fun (k : int) (p : vec) ->
                    let key = (k mod l.cols / 4, k / l.cols / 4) in
                    let sp, sl, n =
                      match Hashtbl.find_opt groups key with
                      | Some g -> g
                      | None -> (zero, 0., 0)
                    in
                    Hashtbl.replace groups key (add sp p, sl +. a.(k), n + 1))
                  l.pts;
                Hashtbl.fold
                  (fun _ ((sp, sl, n) : vec * float * int) (acc : patch list) ->
                    let flux = sl *. refl *. area in
                    if flux <= 0. then acc
                    else
                      let pos = scale (1. /. float n) sp in
                      {
                        pos;
                        pnormal = l.normal;
                        flux;
                        (* (at most 1,024 units: the time bounded) *)
                        reach2 =
                          Float.min (1024. *. 1024.) (flux /. (pi *. least));
                        leaf =
                          (Model.leaf_at m (add pos (scale 4. l.normal))).lindex;
                      }
                      :: acc)
                  groups []
                |> List.sort compare)
              lits))
    in
    let got =
      Array.map (fun (l : lit) -> Array.make (Array.length l.pts) 0.) lits
    in
    List.iter
      (fun (pa : patch) ->
        let vis = row pa.leaf in
        let reach = sqrt pa.reach2 in
        Array.iteri
          (fun (i : int) (l : lit) ->
            let r = leaves.(i) in
            (* in a leaf the patch's may see; near enough; each in
             * front of the other *)
            let seen =
              r > 0
              && Char.code (Bytes.get vis ((r - 1) lsr 3))
                 land (1 lsl ((r - 1) land 7))
                 <> 0
            in
            let to_mid = sub mids.(i) pa.pos in
            if
              seen
              && length to_mid -. radius.(i) < reach
              && dot to_mid pa.pnormal > -.radius.(i)
              && -.dot to_mid l.normal > -.radius.(i)
            then
              Array.iteri
                (fun (k : int) (p : vec) ->
                  let d = sub p pa.pos in
                  let d2 = dot d d in
                  if d2 < pa.reach2 then begin
                    let dl = sqrt d2 in
                    let ce = dot d pa.pnormal /. dl
                    and cr = -.dot d l.normal /. dl in
                    if ce > 0. && cr > 0. then begin
                      (* (no nearer than a patch's size: no infinity
                       * where it touches) *)
                      let e =
                        pa.flux *. ce *. cr /. (pi *. Float.max d2 1024.)
                      in
                      if e > least && first_hit hull root pa.pos p = -1 then
                        got.(i).(k) <- got.(i).(k) +. e
                    end
                  end)
                l.pts)
          lits)
      patches;
    (* what each face got, added to its steady light, and sent next *)
    Array.iteri
      (fun (i : int) (l : lit) ->
        match List.assoc_opt 0 l.maps with
        | Some a ->
            Array.iteri
              (fun (k : int) (v : float) -> a.(k) <- a.(k) +. v)
              got.(i)
        | None ->
            if Array.exists (fun (v : float) -> v > 1.) got.(i) then
              l.maps <- (0, Array.copy got.(i)) :: l.maps)
      lits;
    sent := got
  done

(* 3. the sums made bytes: the least light, style 0 first, 4 at most,
 * halved (id's rangescale), clamped *)
let finish (minlight : float) (l : lit) : (int * string) list =
  let n = Array.length l.pts in
  let maps = ref l.maps in
  let map_of (style : int) : float array =
    match List.assoc_opt style !maps with
    | Some a -> a
    | None ->
        let a = Array.make n 0. in
        maps := !maps @ [ (style, a) ];
        a
  in
  if minlight > 0. then begin
    let a = map_of 0 in
    Array.iteri
      (fun (k : int) (v : float) -> if v < minlight then a.(k) <- minlight)
      a
  end;
  (* (style 0 first, as the game reads them; 4 at most) *)
  let sorted =
    List.filter (fun ((s, _) : int * float array) -> s = 0) !maps
    @ List.filter (fun ((s, _) : int * float array) -> s <> 0) !maps
  in
  let kept = List.filteri (fun (i : int) _ -> i < 4) sorted in
  List.map
    (fun ((style, a) : int * float array) ->
      ( style,
        String.init n (fun (k : int) ->
            Char.chr (max 0 (min 255 (int_of_float (a.(k) *. 0.5))))) ))
    kept

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The level *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let make (caps : < Cap.open_in ; Cap.open_out ; Cap.stdout ; .. >)
    (input : string) (output : string) (palette : string option) : unit =
  let bsp = Bspfile.parse (FS.read caps (Fpath.v input)) in
  let m = Model.load bsp in
  let world = match m.entities with w :: _ -> w | [] -> [] in
  let lights = lights_of m.entities in
  let sun =
    (let v = float_value world "_sunlight" 0. in
     if v = 0. then []
     else
       [
         ( (match value world "_sun_mangle" with
           | Some s -> direction s
           | None -> { x = 0.; y = 0.; z = -1. }),
           v );
       ])
    @
    let v = float_value world "_sunlight2" 0. in
    if v = 0. then []
    else List.map (fun (d : vec) -> (scale (-1.) d, v /. 32.)) dome
  in
  let minlight = float_value world "light" 0. in
  let lits =
    Array.of_list
      (List.filter_map
         (fun (f : surface) ->
           if f.texinfo.special then None else Some (direct m lights sun f))
         (Array.to_list m.surfaces))
  in
  let passes = int_of_float (float_value world "_bounce" 0.) in
  let bouncescale = float_value world "_bouncescale" 1. in
  if passes > 0 then bounce m lits palette passes bouncescale;
  let by_face = Array.make (Array.length m.surfaces) None in
  Array.iter (fun (l : lit) -> by_face.(l.face.index) <- Some l) lits;
  let data = Buffer.create 1_000_000 in
  let faces = Bytes.of_string bsp.lumps.(Bspfile.faces) in
  let lit = ref 0 in
  Array.iter
    (fun (f : surface) ->
      let o = f.index * 20 in
      let maps =
        match by_face.(f.index) with Some l -> finish minlight l | None -> []
      in
      List.iteri
        (fun (i : int) ((s, _) : int * string) ->
          Bytes.set faces (o + 12 + i) (Char.chr s))
        maps;
      for i = List.length maps to 3 do
        Bytes.set faces (o + 12 + i) '\255'
      done;
      let ofs = if maps = [] then -1 else Buffer.length data in
      let b = Buffer.create 4 in
      Bspfile.add_int32 b ofs;
      Bytes.blit_string (Buffer.contents b) 0 faces (o + 16) 4;
      if maps <> [] then incr lit;
      List.iter (fun ((_, s) : int * string) -> Buffer.add_string data s) maps)
    m.surfaces;
  let lumps = Array.copy bsp.lumps in
  lumps.(Bspfile.entities) <- with_styles m.entities;
  lumps.(Bspfile.faces) <- Bytes.to_string faces;
  lumps.(Bspfile.lighting) <- Buffer.contents data;
  FS.write caps (Fpath.v output) (Bspfile.write { bsp with lumps });
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%s: %d lights, %d faces of %d lit, %d bytes of lightmaps\n"
       output (List.length lights) !lit (Array.length m.surfaces)
       (Buffer.length data))

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      Exit.exit caps @@ Exit.catch
      @@ fun () ->
      (match Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps) with
      | [ _; i; o ] -> make caps i o None
      | [ _; i; o; p ] -> make caps i o (Some (FS.read caps (Fpath.v p)))
      | _ -> failwith usage);
      Exit.OK)

(* mini-mkwad2: a WAD2 of Quake's textures made from a directory of
 * PNGs (LibreQuake's texture-wads/lq_tech/ ...), what qbsp reads the
 * textures a map names from (the map's "wad" key) and copies into the
 * .bsp. A WAD2 is Doom's WAD grown up:
 *
 *   0   "WAD2", the number of lumps, where the directory is
 *   12  the lumps: here each a miptex
 *   ... the directory, 32 bytes a lump: where, its size twice (packed
 *       and not: never packed), its type ('D', a miptex), a byte of
 *       compression (none), two bytes of nothing, its name (16)
 *
 *   a miptex: its name (16), width, height, four offsets, then the
 *   texture four times, each half the size of the one before (the
 *   mips: 1, 1/4, 1/16, 1/64 of its bytes), a byte a pixel
 *
 * The name of a texture is its file's, but for what a file name cannot
 * say: star_water is *water (a liquid, drawn warped), plus_0button is
 * +0button (an animation's frame), and x_fbr.png is x with its
 * fullbright colours kept (LibreQuake's, as qpakman reads them).
 * Fullbright colours are the palette's last 32 (224 to 255): the
 * colormap keeps them bright in the dark (lamps, screens), so a
 * texture without _fbr is given the nearest colour of the other 224.
 * A transparent pixel (a texture whose name starts with {: a grate)
 * is 255.
 *
 * The mips as id's qlumpy made them: each pixel of a mip the average
 * of the 2 by 2, 4 by 4, 8 by 8 pixels it covers, made the palette's
 * nearest colour.
 *
 * usage: mini-mkwad2 palette.lmp out.wad png-dir... *)

let usage = "usage: mini-mkwad2 palette.lmp out.wad png-dir..."

let palette_of (pal : string) : (int * int * int) array =
  Array.init 256 (fun (i : int) ->
      ( Char.code pal.[3 * i],
        Char.code pal.[(3 * i) + 1],
        Char.code pal.[(3 * i) + 2] ))

(* the nearest colour of the first [n], the first of equals *)
let nearest (pal : (int * int * int) array) (n : int) (r : int) (g : int)
    (b : int) : int =
  let best = ref 0 and best_d = ref max_int in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    let r', g', b' = pal.(i) in
    let d =
      ((r - r') * (r - r')) + ((g - g') * (g - g')) + ((b - b') * (b - b'))
    in
    if d < !best_d then begin
      best := i;
      best_d := d
    end
  done;
  !best

let texture_name (file : string) : string * bool =
  let stem = Filename.remove_extension file in
  let fbr = Filename.check_suffix stem "_fbr" in
  let stem = if fbr then Filename.chop_suffix stem "_fbr" else stem in
  let prefixed (p : string) (c : string) (s : string) : string option =
    let n = String.length p in
    if String.length s > n && String.sub s 0 n = p then
      Some (c ^ String.sub s n (String.length s - n))
    else None
  in
  let name =
    match prefixed "star_" "*" stem with
    | Some s -> s
    | None -> (
        match prefixed "plus_" "+" stem with Some s -> s | None -> stem)
  in
  (name, fbr)

(* a texture's four mips, a byte a pixel *)
let miptex (pal : (int * int * int) array) (name : string) (fbr : bool)
    (img : Rgba_image.t) : string =
  let w = img.width and h = img.height in
  if w mod 16 <> 0 || h mod 16 <> 0 then
    failwith (Printf.sprintf "%s: %d by %d, not multiples of 16" name w h);
  let colours = if fbr then 256 else 224 in
  let transparent = String.length name > 0 && name.[0] = '{' in
  let cache = Hashtbl.create 256 in
  let index (r : int) (g : int) (b : int) : int =
    let key = (r lsl 16) lor (g lsl 8) lor b in
    match Hashtbl.find_opt cache key with
    | Some i -> i
    | None ->
        let i =
          nearest pal (if transparent then min colours 255 else colours) r g b
        in
        Hashtbl.add cache key i;
        i
  in
  let px (x : int) (y : int) (c : int) : int =
    Char.code (Bytes.get img.rgba ((4 * ((y * w) + x)) + c))
  in
  let mip (k : int) : string =
    let s = 1 lsl k in
    let mw = w / s and mh = h / s in
    String.init (mw * mh) (fun (i : int) ->
        let x0 = i mod mw * s and y0 = i / mw * s in
        let r = ref 0 and g = ref 0 and b = ref 0 and seen = ref 0 in
        for y = y0 to y0 + s - 1 do
          for x = x0 to x0 + s - 1 do
            if px x y 3 >= 128 then begin
              r := !r + px x y 0;
              g := !g + px x y 1;
              b := !b + px x y 2;
              incr seen
            end
          done
        done;
        (* (transparent where most of the block is) *)
        if transparent && 2 * !seen < s * s then '\255'
        else if !seen = 0 then Char.chr (index 0 0 0)
        else Char.chr (index (!r / !seen) (!g / !seen) (!b / !seen)))
  in
  let mips = List.init 4 mip in
  let b = Buffer.create (w * h * 2) in
  Bspfile.add_name b 16 name;
  Bspfile.add_int32 b w;
  Bspfile.add_int32 b h;
  ignore
    (List.fold_left
       (fun (pos : int) (m : string) ->
         Bspfile.add_int32 b pos;
         pos + String.length m)
       40 mips);
  List.iter (Buffer.add_string b) mips;
  Buffer.contents b

let wad2 (lumps : (string * string) list) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create 1_000_000 in
  let size =
    List.fold_left
      (fun (n : int) ((_, d) : string * string) -> n + String.length d)
      0 lumps
  in
  Buffer.add_string b "WAD2";
  Bspfile.add_int32 b (List.length lumps);
  Bspfile.add_int32 b (12 + size);
  List.iter (fun ((_, d) : string * string) -> Buffer.add_string b d) lumps;
  ignore
    (List.fold_left
       (fun (pos : int) ((name, d) : string * string) ->
         Bspfile.add_int32 b pos;
         Bspfile.add_int32 b (String.length d);
         Bspfile.add_int32 b (String.length d);
         Buffer.add_string b "D\000\000\000";
         Bspfile.add_name b 16 name;
         pos + String.length d)
       12 lumps);
  Buffer.contents b

let make (caps : < Cap.open_in ; Cap.open_out ; Cap.readdir ; Cap.stdout ; .. >)
    (palette : string) (out : string) (dirs : string list) : unit =
  let pal = palette_of (FS.read caps (Fpath.v palette)) in
  let lumps =
    List.concat_map
      (fun (dir : string) ->
        let files =
          List.sort compare
            (List.map
               (fun (e : Sys_plan9.dir) -> e.name)
               (Sys_plan9.dirread caps dir))
        in
        List.filter_map
          (fun (f : string) ->
            if not (Filename.check_suffix f ".png") then None
            else begin
              let name, fbr = texture_name f in
              if String.length name > 15 then begin
                Console.print caps
                  (Printf.sprintf "%s: a name longer than 15, left out\n" f);
                None
              end
              else
                Some
                  ( name,
                    miptex pal name fbr
                      (Png.decode
                         (FS.read caps (Fpath.v (Filename.concat dir f)))) )
            end)
          files)
      dirs
  in
  let bytes = wad2 lumps in
  FS.write caps (Fpath.v out) bytes;
  Console.print caps
    (Printf.sprintf "%s: %d textures, %d bytes\n" out (List.length lumps)
       (String.length bytes))

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
      Exit.exit caps @@ Exit.catch
      @@ fun () ->
      (match Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps) with
      | _ :: palette :: out :: (_ :: _ as dirs) -> make caps palette out dirs
      | _ -> failwith usage);
      Exit.OK)

open Playground

(* ix: the author's playground's games/puzzle/Tetris.ml (docs/plans/done/plan_playground.md).
 * What changed: its last line is ix's
 * (Playground_platform.mli says why); and two spellings mini-ml has not,
 * the only ones of their kind in the playground's games: a "+ 1" is "1",
 * and "let rec (stamp: ...) =" is "let rec stamp : ... =". *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Prelude *)
(*****************************************************************************)
(* Port of the Tetris clone https://github.com/w0rm/elm-flatris 
 * (itself a clone of https://github.com/skidding/flatris, 
 *  itself a clone of the venerable Tetris), 
 * but using OCaml instead of Elm, and using Playground instead of HTML/SVG.
 *
 * See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetris for more information on Tetris.
 *
 * extensions I've added:
 *  - space key to drop to the bottom the piece
 *
 * TODO finish porting of elm-flatris:
 *  - check end game
 *  - do not display piece when out of the well
 *  - handle Pause/Resume/Stopped
 *  - more complex input management where keeping the key pressed has
 *    an effect, rather that forcing the user to keyup
 *    (called confusingly "animation")
 *  - accelerate Tick as you clear more lines, manage "level" score
 *
 * claude: done since: levels (one every 10 lines, the pieces falling
 * faster), and sound (see "Sound" below): the theme, Korobeiniki, the
 * Russian folk song Tetris made famous (its melody: public domain, the
 * bass line our own, not the Game Boy's), its tempo rising with the
 * level (Audio.faster, Audio.change_loop: the music goes on from the same
 * note, faster); a thud when a piece lands, a chime when lines are
 * cleared, a bigger one for four at once (a "Tetris"), a flourish at a
 * new level. The flag music=off (?music=off in a browser) turns the
 * theme off.
 *
 * How it is made, which is Elm's way and worth seeing once in a
 * whole game. The well is not an array: it is the list of the cells
 * that are full, each with its place and its colour, and an empty
 * cell is a cell that is not in the list. A piece is such a list
 * too, four cells with places from 0 to 3. So the game is a few
 * functions from lists to lists, none of which changes anything:
 *
 *   collide   would the piece, put there, leave the well or sit on a
 *             full cell? asked before every move, turn and fall
 *   stamp     the piece's cells, moved to where it is, added to the
 *             well's: a piece that has landed
 *   clear_lines   a row with as many cells as the well is wide is
 *             taken out, and what is above it comes down by one
 *
 *     y                                   y
 *     17  . . # .                         17  . . . .
 *     18  # # # #   <- 4 cells, width 4   18  . . # .
 *     19  # . # #       : full            19  # . # #
 *
 * (y goes down, as in the well's picture, and the playground's goes
 * up: the view turns it over.) A move that collides is not made; a
 * fall that collides is a landing; a turn that collides is tried
 * again a cell or two to each side before it is given up, so that a
 * piece against a wall still turns. That is the whole of the rules.
 *
 * Where it stands: the game the playground was brought to ix for
 * (plan_playground.md), and the one its platforms are measured with
 * (Redraw.mli counts its falling piece's pixels). Plan 9 has its
 * own, games/4s.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Tetris is Alexey Pajitnov's, written in June 1984 at the Computing
 * Centre of the Soviet Academy of Sciences in Moscow, on an
 * Electronika 60, a machine with a text terminal and no graphics:
 * the first pieces were drawn with brackets. Pajitnov liked
 * pentominoes, the puzzle of the twelve shapes made of five squares
 * (Solomon Golomb named the polyominoes in 1953), and took the
 * shapes of four because twelve were too many to play with in real
 * time; the name is tetra, four, and tennis, his sport. Vadim
 * Gerasimov ported it to the IBM PC, copies went from hand to hand
 * across Moscow and then abroad, and the rights were fought over for
 * years, the Soviet state owning what its employee had made. The
 * Game Boy was sold with it in 1989, and that is the Tetris most
 * people first played.
 *
 * terminology:
 * A tetromino (the game writes tetrimino) is four squares joined by
 * their sides. There are five if a shape may be turned over, and
 * seven if it may only be turned, as on a screen: I, O, T, and the
 * two pairs that are each other's mirror, J and L, S and Z -- the
 * seven of [tetriminos] below.
 *
 * others:
 * How hard is it? Given the pieces to come in advance, deciding
 * whether the well can be cleared is NP-complete (Erik Demaine,
 * Susan Hohenberger and David Liben-Nowell, "Tetris is Hard, Even to
 * Approximate", 2003): a game a child learns in a minute sits with
 * the travelling salesman.
 *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Grid and pieces (model part 1) *)
(*****************************************************************************)
type color = Color.t

(* pad: I introduced this type.
 * The origin (0, 0) in the grid is at the top left corner of the tetris "well".
 * Pos can also have a negative y, meaning it is not yet visible.
 *)
type pos = {x: int; y: int }


(* orig: was polymorphic, but always use with color, so simpler to hardcode *)
type cell = {
  color: color;
  pos: pos;
}

(* an empty cell is represented as a non-existing cell.
 * alt: cell option array.
*)
type grid = cell list

let empty_grid = []


(* pad: I introduced this type.
 * note that x and y are between 0 and 3 for a piece.
*)
type piece = grid

(*****************************************************************************)
(* General Helpers *)
(*****************************************************************************)
(* those functions were in my common2.ml before, could put in a core/List_.ml *)

let sum xs = List.fold_left ( + ) 0 xs

let foldl1 p xs =
  match xs with
  | x :: xs -> List.fold_left p x xs
  | [] -> failwith "foldl1: empty list"

let maximum l = foldl1 max l

let exclude p xs = List.filter (fun x -> not (p x)) xs

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Helpers *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let (center_of_mass: piece -> pos) = fun piece ->
    let len = float (List.length piece) in
    let xs = piece |> List.map (fun cell -> cell.pos.x) in
    let ys = piece |> List.map (fun cell -> cell.pos.y) in
    { x = Basics.round (float (sum xs) /. len);
      y = Basics.round (float (sum ys) /. len);
    }

let (init_position: int -> piece -> pos) = fun wid piece ->
    let {x; _} = center_of_mass piece in
    let y = piece |> List.map (fun cell -> cell.pos.y) |> maximum in
    (* -y -1 to set as non visible the bottom of the piece *)
    { x = wid / 2 - x; 
      y = - y - 1 
    }

let (size: piece -> (int * int)) = fun piece ->
    let xs = piece |> List.map (fun cell -> cell.pos.x) in
    let ys = piece |> List.map (fun cell -> cell.pos.y) in
    let dim zs = 1 + maximum zs in
    dim xs, dim ys

(* put the piece in the grid *)
let rec stamp : pos -> piece -> grid -> grid = fun { x; y} piece grid ->
  match piece with
  | [] -> grid
  | cell::rest ->
    let newpos = { x = cell.pos.x + x; y = cell.pos.y + y } in
    (* todo: need exclude from grid cells with pos = newpos? *)
    stamp { x; y } rest ({ cell with pos = newpos }::grid)

(* check if the piece collide with the grid in the well (width x height) *)
let rec collide ({x; y} as pos) piece (width, height) grid =
  match piece with
  | [] -> false
  | cell::rest ->
    let x = cell.pos.x + x in
    let y = cell.pos.y + y in
    x >= width || x < 0 || y >= height || 
    (List.mem { x; y} (grid |> List.map (fun cell -> cell.pos))) ||
    collide pos rest (width, height) grid

(* rotate clockwise *)
let (rotate: piece -> piece) = fun piece ->
  let { x; y} = center_of_mass piece in

  piece |> List.map (fun cell ->
    let pos = cell.pos in
    (* ???? *)
    { cell with pos = { x = 1 + y - pos.y; y = - x + y + pos.x } }
  )

let rec full_line_opt width grid =
  match grid with
  | [] -> None
  | cell::_ ->
    let line_y = cell.pos.y in
    let same_line, other = 
      grid |> List.partition (fun { pos; _} -> pos.y = line_y) in
    if List.length same_line = width
    then Some line_y
    else full_line_opt width other

let rec clear_lines width grid =
  match full_line_opt width grid with
  | None -> grid, 0
  | Some line_y ->
    let cleared_grid = grid |> exclude (fun {pos; _} -> pos.y = line_y)in
    let (above, below) =
      cleared_grid |> List.partition (fun {pos; _} -> pos.y < line_y) in
    let dropped_above = 
      above |> List.map (fun cell -> 
        { cell with pos = { x = cell.pos.x; y = cell.pos.y + 1 } }
      ) in
    let (new_grid, nb_lines) = clear_lines width (dropped_above @ below) in
    (new_grid, nb_lines + 1)

let (from_list: color -> (int * int) list -> grid) = fun color xs ->
    xs |> List.map (fun (x, y) -> { color; pos = {x ; y} })

let (tetriminos: piece list) = [
  (* xxxx 
   *)
  Color.Rgb (60, 199, 214), [(0, 0); (1, 0); (2, 0); (3, 0)];
  (* xx
   * xx
   *)
  Color.Rgb (251, 180, 20), [(0, 0); (1, 0); (0, 1); (1, 1)];
  (* xxx
   *  x
   *)
  Color.Rgb (176, 68, 151), [(1, 0); (0, 1); (1, 1); (2, 1)];
  (* xxx
   * x
   *)
  Color.Rgb (57, 147, 208), [(0, 0); (0, 1); (1, 1); (2, 1)];
  (* xxx
   *   x
   *)
  Color.Rgb (237, 101, 47), [(2, 0); (0, 1); (1, 1); (2, 1)];
  (* xx
   *  xx
   *)
  Color.Rgb (149, 196, 61), [(1, 0); (2, 0); (0, 1); (1, 1)];
  (*  xx
   * xx
   *)
  Color.Rgb (232, 65, 56),  [(0, 0); (1, 0); (1, 1); (2, 1)];
 ] |> List.map (fun (color, xs) -> from_list color xs)

(* claude: drawn from the seed kept in the model (Playground.pick), not
 * OCaml's global Random: the same seed, the same pieces, in every run
 * and on every backend -- what golden frames, replays and two players
 * on two computers need (plan_networking_teaching.md, phase 0) *)
let random_tetrimino (seed : seed) : piece * seed = pick tetriminos seed

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Model *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* todo? need Stopped and Paused? *)
type state = 
  | Stopped
  | Playing
  | Paused

(* less: animationState? input *)
type model = {
  (* screen size (= Playground.initial_computer.screen) *)
  (* size: number * number; *)

  (* grid dimension *)
  width: int;
  height: int;

  (* current state of the grid *)
  grid: grid;

  (* current piece *)
  active: piece;
  (* leftest highest part of the piece.
   * using a float for y allows to handle speed of drop *)
  position: (int * float);
  (* next piece *)
  next: piece;

  score: int;
  lines: int;
  (* claude: lines / 10: the fall's speed and the music's tempo *)
  level: int;
  (* claude: the flag music=off *)
  music: bool;

  state: state;

  (* claude: the next piece's randomness (see random_tetrimino) *)
  seed: seed;
}

let spawn_tetrimino model =
  let active = model.next in
  let next, seed = random_tetrimino model.seed in
  let {x; y} = init_position model.width active in
  { model with next; active; position = (x, float y); seed }

(* claude: from a seed, the first two pieces drawn: the flag seed=n
 * (see Playground.flags), e.g. for the golden frame tests, else the
 * clock, read once here and never again *)
let initial_model (seed : seed) =
  let next, seed = random_tetrimino seed in
  spawn_tetrimino {

    (* coupling: Playground.initial_computer.screen *)
    (* size = (600., 600.); *)

    width = 10;
    height = 20;

    score = 0;
    lines = 0;
    level = 0;
    music = true;

    grid = empty_grid;

    active = empty_grid;
    position = (0, 0.);
    next;

    state = Stopped;

    seed;
  }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* View *)
(*****************************************************************************)
let fl = float

(* in pixels, height = 20 * 30 = 600 < 768 height in initial_computer.screen *)
let cell_size = 30

let move_box {width; height; _ } { x; y } shape =
  shape 
  (* go to (0, 0), top left corner of the well *)
  |> move_up (fl (height * cell_size / 2)) 
  |> move_left (fl (width * cell_size / 2))
  (* now move the piece to (x, y) *)
  |> move_right (fl (x * cell_size + cell_size / 2))
  |> move_down  (fl (y * cell_size + cell_size / 2))

let render_box model { color; pos } =
  square color (fl cell_size) |> move_box model pos

let render_well 
 ({ width; height; position = (posx, posy); active; grid; _ } as model) =
  let final_grid = 
    stamp { x = posx; y = int_of_float (floor posy) } active grid
  in
  [rectangle (Color.Rgb (236, 240, 241)) 
      (fl (width * cell_size))
      (fl (height * cell_size))
  ] @
  (final_grid |> List.map (render_box model)) @
  []

let render_panel { width; height; score; lines; next; _ } =
  let move x = 
    (* got to top right area *)
    x |> move_up (fl (height * cell_size / 2 - 2 * cell_size))
      |> move_right (fl (width * cell_size / 2 + 4 * cell_size))
  in
  (* less: bold *)
  let title = words (Color.Hex "#34495f")  "Flatris" |> move |> scale 5. in

  let move x = x |> move |> move_down (fl (cell_size * 3)) in
  let score_label = words (Color.Hex "#bdc3c7") "Score" |> move |> scale 2. in

  let move x = x |> move |> move_down (fl (cell_size * 2)) in 
  let score = 
    words (Color.Hex "#3993d0") (string_of_int score) |> move |> scale 3. in
  
  let move x = x |> move |> move_down (fl (cell_size * 3)) in
  let lines_label = 
    words (Color.Hex "#bdc3c7") "Lines Cleared" |> move |> scale 2. in

  let move x = x |> move |> move_down (fl (cell_size * 2)) in 
  let lines = 
    words (Color.Hex "#3993d0") (string_of_int lines) |> move |> scale 3. in

  let move x = x |> move |> move_down (fl (cell_size * 3)) in
  let next_label = 
    words (Color.Hex "#bdc3c7") "Next Shape" |> move |> scale 2. in

  let move x = x |> move |> move_down (fl (cell_size * 2)) in
  let { x; _} = center_of_mass next in
  let next = 
    next |> List.map (fun cell ->
        square cell.color (fl cell_size) |> move
        |> move_left (fl (x * cell_size))
        |> move_right (fl (cell.pos.x * cell_size))
        |> move_down  (fl (cell.pos.y * cell_size))) in


  [title; score_label; score; lines_label; lines; next_label] @ next

let view model =
  render_well model @
  render_panel model @
  []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Update *)
(*****************************************************************************)
type msg = 
  | Tick of float

  (* less: add bool to mean down/up (on/off) *)
  | MoveLeft
  | MoveRight
  | Rotate
  | Accelerate
  | FullDrop

  | Noop

let msg_of_key = function
  | "ArrowLeft"  -> MoveLeft
  | "ArrowRight" -> MoveRight
  | "ArrowDown" -> Accelerate
  | "ArrowUp" -> Rotate
  | "space" -> FullDrop
  | _ -> Noop

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Sound *)
(*****************************************************************************)
(* claude: Korobeiniki ("The Peddlers", a poem by Nikolay Nekrasov,
 * 1861, sung to a folk tune), the music of Tetris since its Soviet
 * version was ported to the West (Spectrum HoloByte, 1988; then the Game
 * Boy's, 1989). In ABC notation (audio/Abc.mli), two voices: the
 * melody, played on a square, and an octave bass on a triangle (the
 * NES's band: Music.to_sound), eight bars of eighths at 150 quarters a
 * minute, 12.8 s, looping. *)
let korobeiniki = {|X:1
T:Korobeiniki
L:1/8
Q:1/4=150
K:Am
V:1
e2 Bc d2 cB | A2 Ac e2 dc | B3 c d2 e2 | c2 A2 A4 |
z d2 f a2 gf | e3 c e2 dc | B2 Bc d2 e2 | c2 A2 A4 |
V:2
E,,E, E,,E, E,,E, E,,E, | A,,A, A,,A, A,,A, A,,A, | E,,E, E,,E, E,,E, E,,E, | A,,A, A,,A, A,,A, A,,A, |
D,,D, D,,D, D,,D, D,,D, | C,,C, C,,C, C,,C, C,,C, | E,,E, E,,E, E,,E, E,,E, | A,,A, A,,A, A,,A, A,,A, |
|}

let theme = Audio.abc korobeiniki |> Audio.louder 0.6

(* a tenth faster each level: 1.5 times as fast at level 5 *)
let music_at level = theme |> Audio.faster (1. +. (0.1 *. float level))

let landed = Audio.sfx { Sfx.step with frequency = 120.; slide = 60.; decay = 0.08; volume = 0.4 }
let cleared = Audio.sfx { Sfx.coin with frequency = 784.; slide = 784.; jump = 5.; jump_at = 0.06 }
(* four lines, a "Tetris": a major chord, arpeggiated (Pitch_effect.mli) *)
let tetris = Audio.sfx { Sfx.powerup with frequency = 523.; slide = 523.; sustain = 0.4 } |> Audio.arpeggio [ 0.; 4.; 7.; 12. ] 0.05
let level_up = Audio.powerup

let clear_lines_and_add_score model = 
  let grid, nblines = clear_lines model.width model.grid in
  let bonus =
    match nblines with
    | 0 -> 0
    | 1 -> 100
    | 2 -> 300
    | 3 -> 500
    | 4 -> 800
    | _ -> failwith "Impossible"
  in
  let lines = model.lines + nblines in
  let level = lines / 10 in
  (* claude: the sounds of a piece landing, of lines going *)
  if nblines = 4 then Audio.play tetris
  else if nblines > 0 then Audio.play cleared
  else Audio.play landed;
  if level > model.level then begin
    Audio.play level_up;
    if model.music then Audio.change_loop "music" (music_at level)
  end;
  { model with 
    grid; 
    score = model.score + bonus (* todo: level model *);
    lines;
    level;
  }

(* drop because Tick or Accelerate *)
let (drop_tetrimino: model -> float -> model * bool) = fun model dy ->
  let (x, y) = model.position in
  let new_pos = (x, y +. dy) in 
  if collide { x; y = int_of_float (floor (y +. dy)) } model.active
      (model.width, model.height) model.grid
  then
    let score = List.length model.active in
    { model with
      grid = stamp { x; y = int_of_float (floor y) } model.active model.grid;
      score = model.score + score;
    } 
    |> spawn_tetrimino
    |> clear_lines_and_add_score
    |> (fun model -> model, true)
  else { model with position = new_pos }, false

let rotate_tetrimino model = 
  let rotated = rotate model.active in
  let (x, y) = model.position in

  (* make sure the rotated tetrimino stays in the grid *)
  let rec shift_pos_if_collide deltas = 
    match deltas with
    | dx::rest ->
      if collide { x = x+dx; y = int_of_float (floor y) } rotated
               (model.width, model.height) model.grid
      then shift_pos_if_collide rest
      else { model with active = rotated; position = (x + dx, y) }
    | [] -> model
  in
  (* -2 + 2 range should be enough *)
  shift_pos_if_collide [0; 1; -1; 2; -2]

  

    
(* less: Resize/GetViewPort *)
let update msg model =
  (match msg with
  | Tick _ ->
    (* claude: a row a second at level 0, 30% faster each level; a Tick
     * is 1/60 s (the platforms' fixed step), not the time between two
     * Ticks on this machine's clock: the same game on every machine *)
    let dy = (1. /. 60.) *. (1. +. (0.3 *. float model.level)) in
    (* claude: harmless when already playing (Audio.loop) *)
    if model.music then Audio.loop "music" (music_at model.level);
    drop_tetrimino model dy |> fst

  | MoveLeft ->
    let (x, y) = model.position in
    let dx = - 1 in
    if collide { x = x+dx; y = int_of_float (floor y) } model.active 
               (model.width, model.height) model.grid
    then model
    else { model with position = (x+dx, y) }

  | MoveRight ->
    let (x, y) = model.position in
    let dx = 1 in
    if collide { x = x+dx; y = int_of_float (floor y) } model.active 
               (model.width, model.height) model.grid
    then model
    else { model with position = (x+dx, y) }

  | Rotate -> 
    rotate_tetrimino model

  | Accelerate -> 
    let dy = 1. in
    drop_tetrimino model dy |> fst

  | FullDrop ->
    let rec aux model =
       let (model, at_bottom) = drop_tetrimino model 1. in
       if at_bottom
       then model
       else aux model
     in
     aux model

  | Noop -> model
  ),
  Cmd.none

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Entry point *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the pieces' order without seed=n: the clock's milliseconds, read by
 * main, which holds Cap.clock *)
let clock_seed = ref 0

let app =
  { Playground.
    view;
    update;
    init = (fun flags ->
      let seed =
        match Option.bind (List.assoc_opt "seed" flags) int_of_string_opt with
        | Some n -> n
        | None -> !clock_seed
      in
      { (initial_model (initial_seed seed)) with music = List.assoc_opt "music" flags <> Some "off" }, Cmd.none);
    subscriptions  = (fun _ -> Sub.batch [
      Sub.on_animation_frame (fun x -> Tick x);
      Sub.on_key_down (fun key -> msg_of_key key);
    ]);
  }

(* (-help: the usage, and the end, Exit.ExitCode) *)
let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps @@ Exit.catch @@ fun () ->
  clock_seed := int_of_float (CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () *. 1000.);
  Playground_platform.run_app caps (Playground_platform.flags caps) app;
  Exit.OK)
games/racing/virtua/Virtua.ml

(* Claude Code
