(* A sorted index (Index.mli, Relset.mli): the relation again, sorted
 * with some of its columns (the key) first, then the others, in a
 * B-tree (Btree). The tuples with a key's values are a range of it, in
 * the order of their other columns:
 *
 *    assign(P, Q), its index on Q: the tuples as (Q, P), sorted
 *
 *      ... (q7, p2) (q7, p5) (q7, p9) (q8, p1) ...
 *          \___ assign(_, q7): p2, p5, p9 ____/
 *
 * A lookup gives the tuples themselves (a leaf's values, the columns
 * in the index's order: [at] says where each column is), not their
 * numbers in the relation's rows: no second place to read.
 *
 * design:
 * That the other columns come out sorted is what Souffle's speed is
 * made of: in point_to(P, L) :- assign(P, Q), point_to(Q, L), from a
 * new assign(P, Q), Q's point_to(Q, L) come out by L, so the heads
 * point_to(P, L1), point_to(P, L2)... tested one after the other are
 * neighbours in the relation's own sorted set, the same leaf mostly
 * (Btree's hint).
 * The other kind, Hash_index, gives the tuples in the order added,
 * read in the rows (Datalog's): a lookup and the next tuple each a
 * miss of the cache, and the tests after them scattered; but adding a
 * tuple is writing a slot, where a sorted leaf moves the tuples after
 * it.
 *
 * others:
 * Souffle's index selection finds the fewest orders that serve every
 * lookup of the rules (Subotic et al., VLDB 2018): an order (Q, P, R)
 * serves a lookup on Q and one on (Q, P). Here an index is made for
 * each set of columns asked (Datalog_eval's index), at its first
 * lookup. A hash index is what databases call the other kind (hash
 * join, Gamma and Grace, the 1980s); System R's were B-trees. *)

type t

(* the index of a relation of an arity on the columns given (their
 * numbers, in order) *)
val create : int -> int array -> t

(* the tuple whose column c is [value c] added *)
val add : t -> (int -> int) -> unit

(* [f keys base] for each tuple whose key's i-th value is [key i], in
 * order: its column c is keys.(base + (at t).(c)). Not while a tuple
 * is added. *)
val iter : t -> (int -> int) -> (int array -> int -> unit) -> unit

(* is there one? *)
val exists : t -> (int -> int) -> bool

(* each column's place in a tuple that iter gives *)
val at : t -> int array

(* the part of the tuple whose column c is [value c] (Btree's parts:
 * domains add at once the tuples of different parts) *)
val part_of : t -> (int -> int) -> int

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Tuples.mli *)

(* the parts, a power of two: a tuple's is its hash's low bits *)
let parts = 64
let part_bits = 6

(* slot k of a part is cells.(k * arity) to cells.(k * arity + arity - 1);
 * a free one has -1 first (a symbol is not negative). An arity 0 has
 * one tuple or none: part 0's [count] says. *)
type part = { mutable cells : int array; mutable size : int; mutable count : int }
type t = { arity : int; part : part array }

let create (arity : int) : t =
  { arity; part = Array.init parts (fun (_ : int) -> { cells = Array.make (8 * arity) (-1); size = 8; count = 0 }) }

let arity (t : t) : int = t.arity
let count (t : t) : int = Array.fold_left (fun (n : int) (p : part) -> n + p.count) 0 t.part

(* each column's value in turn, then the high bits brought down, so
 * that the slots' low bits depend on all of them (the constants fit
 * in mini-ml's 31 bits of arm) *)
let hash (arity : int) (value : int -> int) : int =
  let h = ref arity in
  for i = 0 to arity - 1 do
    h := (!h * 1000003) + value i
  done;
  let h = (!h lxor (!h lsr 16)) * 73244475 in
  (h lxor (h lsr 16)) land max_int

(* hash and find of a tuple in an array, written out: no closure called
 * for each value (mem2's measure, for any arity; on .NET a closure is
 * an object and a delegate's call: mini-datalog -dotnet's loops) *)
let hash_array (n : int) (a : int array) : int =
  let h = ref n in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    h := (!h * 1000003) + a.(i)
  done;
  let h = (!h lxor (!h lsr 16)) * 73244475 in
  (h lxor (h lsr 16)) land max_int

(* (loops: a local rec function of the free cells, n and a was a closure
 * made at each call, the most allocated words of mini-prolog's -exn;
 * old: let rec same base i = ... and walk k = ... in walk start) *)
let find_array (n : int) (p : part) (h : int) (a : int array) : int =
  let mask = p.size - 1 and cells = p.cells in
  let k = ref ((h lsr part_bits) land mask) and found = ref false in
  while not !found do
    let base = !k * n in
    if cells.(base) < 0 then found := true
    else begin
      let i = ref 0 in
      while !i < n && cells.(base + !i) = a.(!i) do
        incr i
      done;
      if !i = n then found := true else k := (!k + 1) land mask
    end
  done;
  !k

let part_of (t : t) (value : int -> int) : int = if t.arity = 0 then 0 else hash t.arity value land (parts - 1)

(* in part p, the slot of the tuple, or the free one where it would go *)
let find (n : int) (p : part) (h : int) (value : int -> int) : int =
  let mask = p.size - 1 and cells = p.cells in
  let rec same (base : int) (i : int) : bool = i = n || (cells.(base + i) = value i && same base (i + 1)) in
  let rec walk (k : int) : int = if cells.(k * n) < 0 || same (k * n) 0 then k else walk ((k + 1) land mask) in
  walk ((h lsr part_bits) land mask)

let mem_by (t : t) (value : int -> int) : bool =
  if t.arity = 0 then t.part.(0).count > 0
  else
    let h = hash t.arity value in
    let p = t.part.(h land (parts - 1)) in
    p.cells.(find t.arity p h value * t.arity) >= 0

(* old: mem_by t (fun (i : int) -> tuple.(i)) *)
let mem (t : t) (tuple : int array) : bool =
  if t.arity = 0 then t.part.(0).count > 0
  else
    let h = hash_array t.arity tuple in
    let p = t.part.(h land (parts - 1)) in
    p.cells.(find_array t.arity p h tuple * t.arity) >= 0

let put (n : int) (p : part) (k : int) (value : int -> int) : unit =
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    p.cells.((k * n) + i) <- value i
  done

(* twice the part's slots, each tuple put again *)
let grow (n : int) (p : part) : unit =
  let old = p.cells and size = p.size in
  p.size <- 2 * size;
  p.cells <- Array.make (p.size * n) (-1);
  for k = 0 to size - 1 do
    if old.(k * n) >= 0 then begin
      let value (i : int) : int = old.((k * n) + i) in
      put n p (find n p (hash n value) value) value
    end
  done

let add (t : t) (tuple : int array) : bool =
  if t.arity = 0 then begin
    let p = t.part.(0) in
    let fresh = p.count = 0 in
    p.count <- 1;
    fresh
  end
  else begin
    (* (old: through a closure of the tuple, hash and find's) *)
    let n = t.arity in
    let h = hash_array n tuple in
    let p = t.part.(h land (parts - 1)) in
    let k = find_array n p h tuple in
    if p.cells.(k * n) >= 0 then false
    else begin
      Array.blit tuple 0 p.cells (k * n) n;
      p.count <- p.count + 1;
      if 2 * p.count > p.size then grow n p;
      true
    end
  end

(* mem_by for pairs, written out (Btree.mem2_hint's measure: what a
 * test costs with no closure called for each value) *)
let mem2 (t : t) (a : int) (b : int) : bool =
  let h = (((2 * 1000003) + a) * 1000003) + b in
  let h = (h lxor (h lsr 16)) * 73244475 in
  let h = (h lxor (h lsr 16)) land max_int in
  let p = t.part.(h land (parts - 1)) in
  let mask = p.size - 1 and cells = p.cells in
  let rec walk (k : int) : bool =
    let x = cells.(2 * k) in
    if x < 0 then false else if x = a && cells.((2 * k) + 1) = b then true else walk ((k + 1) land mask) in
  walk ((h lsr part_bits) land mask)
languages/datalog/Tuples.mli
2661
(* A relation's tuples as a set: each tuple once, asked for by its
 * values. An array of slots (open addressing): a tuple is put at the
 * slot its hash says, or the next free one after it; a lookup walks
 * from that slot to the tuple or to a free slot. Half the slots at most
 * are used, so a walk is short. A slot is the tuple's values, in one
 * array of integers for all the slots: no pointer to follow. The
 * slots are in 64 parts, a tuple's part by its hash: each part its own
 * array, which grows alone, so that several domains add tuples at once
 * when each adds those of its own parts (Datalog_eval's -j).
 *
 * design:
 * Most of a pointer analysis's firings find a tuple that is there
 * already (mini-ml's own code by pointer.dl: 372 million firings of
 * point_to(P, L) :- assign(P, Q), point_to(Q, L) for 6.6 million new
 * tuples), so the test of a tuple that is there is the engine's
 * inner loop. Here it is asked from the values themselves, column by
 * column ([mem_by]), with no array made for a tuple that is then
 * dropped; the hash mixes integers, the comparison compares integers,
 * and they are where the slot is: with millions of tuples a lookup is
 * a miss of the cache, two when the slot points to an array (the rule
 * above: 147 s by Hashtbl, 104 s by slots of arrays, 81 s flat).
 * The parts cost a mask and a load more a lookup.
 * old: OCaml's Hashtbl of int arrays: the tuple made first, hashed by
 * the polymorphic hash (which walks any value), compared by the
 * polymorphic compare.
 *
 * others:
 * Souffle keeps a relation in a B-tree (sorted: a range of it is an
 * index's lookup too) or in a trie of its columns (its "brie", for
 * dense relations); databases since System R in B-trees; Python's
 * dict and Lua's tables are open addressing, as this is. *)

type t

(* the tuples of an arity *)
val create : int -> t

val count : t -> int
val arity : t -> int
val mem : t -> int array -> bool

(* is there the tuple whose i-th value is [value i]? *)
val mem_by : t -> (int -> int) -> bool

(* false: it was there *)
val add : t -> int array -> bool

(* mem_by of the pair (a, b), for pairs, written out *)
val mem2 : t -> int -> int -> bool

(* the hash of n values, the i-th [value i] (Index's too) *)
val hash : int -> (int -> int) -> int

(* the same of an array's n values (no closure: a compiled program's) *)
val hash_array : int -> int array -> int

(* the parts, and the part of the tuple whose i-th value is [value i]:
 * [add] of tuples of different parts may run at the same time *)
val parts : int
val part_bits : int             (* parts = 2^part_bits *)
val part_of : t -> (int -> int) -> int

(* See Compile_il.mli *)

module D = Datalog
module E = Datalog_eval
module S = Signature
module W = Writer

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The assembly, its references to datalog_rt's classes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type c = {
  w : W.t;
  cls : int;                                (* the program's class *)
  t : S.t;                                  (* Datalog.t *)
  rel : S.t;                                (* Datalog.relation *)
  rt : int;                                 (* Datalog_rt *)
  idx : S.t;                                (* Index.t *)
  p : int;                                  (* the field holding the program *)
  relations : (string, int) Hashtbl.t;      (* name/arity: its field *)
  symbols : (int, int) Hashtbl.t;           (* a constant: its field *)
  mutable inits : Il.op list list;          (* the fields set, reversed *)
}

let static (ps : S.t list) (r : S.t) : S.meth =
  { S.has_this = false; generic = 0; vararg = false; ret = r; params = ps }
let instance (ps : S.t list) (r : S.t) : S.meth =
  { (static ps r) with has_this = true }

let call (c : c) (name : string) (ps : S.t list) (r : S.t) : Il.op =
  Il.Call (W.member_ref c.w c.rt name (static ps r))

(* a relation's field, set at the start *)
let relation (c : c) (r : D.relation) : int =
  let key = Printf.sprintf "%s/%d" r.name r.arity in
  match Hashtbl.find_opt c.relations key with
  | Some f -> f
  | None ->
      let f = W.field_def c.w c.cls ("<rel>" ^ key) 0x0011 c.rel in
      Hashtbl.replace c.relations key f;
      c.inits <-
        [ Il.Ldsfld c.p; Il.Ldstr (W.user_string c.w r.name);
          Il.Ldc_i8 (Int64.of_int r.arity);
          call c "relation" [ c.t; S.String; S.I8 ] c.rel; Il.Stsfld f ]
        :: c.inits;
      f

(* a constant's field: its symbol in the program run, by its text *)
let symbol (c : c) (p : D.t) (k : int) : int =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt c.symbols k with
  | Some f -> f
  | None ->
      let f = W.field_def c.w c.cls (Printf.sprintf "<sym>%d" k) 0x0011 S.I8 in
      Hashtbl.replace c.symbols k f;
      c.inits <-
        [ Il.Ldsfld c.p; Il.Ldstr (W.user_string c.w (D.text p k));
          call c "symbol" [ c.t; S.String ] S.I8; Il.Stsfld f ]
        :: c.inits;
      f

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A method's code *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type code = {
  mutable ops : Il.op list;                 (* reversed *)
  mutable n : int;
  labels : (int, int) Hashtbl.t;
  mutable nlabels : int;
  mutable locals : S.t list;                (* reversed *)
  mutable nlocals : int;
}

let new_code () : code =
  { ops = []; n = 0; labels = Hashtbl.create 8; nlabels = 0; locals = [];
    nlocals = 0 }

let emit (k : code) (op : Il.op) : unit =
  k.ops <- op :: k.ops;
  k.n <- k.n + 1

let label (k : code) : int =
  k.nlabels <- k.nlabels + 1;
  k.nlabels

let place (k : code) (l : int) : unit = Hashtbl.replace k.labels l k.n

let local (k : code) (t : S.t) : int =
  k.locals <- t :: k.locals;
  k.nlocals <- k.nlocals + 1;
  k.nlocals - 1

let finish (c : c) (k : code) (meth : int) : unit =
  let at (l : int) : int = Hashtbl.find k.labels l in
  let ops =
    List.rev_map
      (fun (op : Il.op) ->
        match op with
        | Il.Br l -> Il.Br (at l)
        | Il.Brfalse l -> Il.Brfalse (at l)
        | Il.Brtrue l -> Il.Brtrue (at l)
        | Il.Bcmp (x, u, l) -> Il.Bcmp (x, u, at l)
        | op -> op)
      k.ops in
  W.set_body c.w meth (List.rev k.locals) (Array.of_list ops) []

(* a loop: i from the first (pushed) while below the end (pushed), the
 * body given where to go for the next *)
let loop (k : code) (i : int) (start : unit -> unit) (stop : unit -> unit)
    (one : Il.op) (body : int -> unit) : unit =
  let top = label k and next = label k and out = label k in
  start ();
  emit k (Il.Stloc i);
  place k top;
  emit k (Il.Ldloc i);
  stop ();
  emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Ge, false, out));
  body next;
  place k next;
  emit k (Il.Ldloc i);
  emit k one;
  emit k (Il.Binop Il.Add);
  emit k (Il.Stloc i);
  emit k (Il.Br top);
  place k out

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A plan: nested loops *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a rule's plan as a method: each scan a loop (over a range of the
 * relation's tuples, or the numbers an index gives), each test a
 * branch past what follows, the head's tuple added at the innermost *)
let plan (c : c) (p : D.t) (rule : D.rule) (steps : E.step list) (name : string)
    : int =
  let meth = W.method_def c.w c.cls name 0x0091 (static [] S.Void) in
  let k = new_code () in
  let env = Array.init rule.slots (fun (_ : int) -> local k S.I8) in
  let ints = S.SzArray S.I8 in
  let value (x : D.arg) : unit =
    match x with
    | D.Const s -> emit k (Il.Ldsfld (symbol c p s))
    | D.Slot v -> emit k (Il.Ldloc env.(v))
    | D.Any -> emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 (-1L)) in
  (* the method's start: each index it walks, each int64[] of keys it
   * fills, made once (in the order the steps below take them) *)
  let made : int Queue.t = Queue.create () in
  let int64 = W.type_ref c.w (W.assembly_ref c.w "System.Runtime") "System" "Int64" in
  let buffer (n : int) =
    let b = local k ints in
    emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int n)); emit k (Il.Newarr int64); emit k (Il.Stloc b);
    Queue.add b made in
  let index_of (r : D.relation) (mask : int) =
    let x = local k c.idx in
    emit k (Il.Ldsfld (relation c r)); emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 (Int64.of_int mask));
    emit k (call c "index" [ c.rel; S.I8 ] c.idx); emit k (Il.Stloc x);
    Queue.add x made in
  List.iter
    (fun (step : E.step) ->
      match step with
      | E.Test (D.Neg a) -> buffer (List.length (List.filter (fun (x : D.arg) -> x <> D.Any) (Array.to_list a.args)))
      | E.Test _ -> ()
      | E.Scan s when s.from_new || s.mask = 0 -> ()
      | E.Scan s when Array.length s.keys = s.atom.rel.arity -> buffer (Array.length s.keys)
      | E.Scan s -> index_of s.atom.rel s.mask; buffer (Array.length s.keys))
    steps;
  buffer rule.head.rel.arity;
  (* the next of them; an int64[] of them, its values put *)
  let made_next () = Queue.pop made in
  let array (xs : D.arg list) : unit =
    let b = made_next () in
    List.iteri
      (fun (i : int) (x : D.arg) ->
        emit k (Il.Ldloc b); emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int i)); value x;
        emit k (Il.Stelem Il.K_i8))
      xs;
    emit k (Il.Ldloc b) in
  let get (r : int) (id : unit -> unit) (col : int) : unit =
    emit k (Il.Ldsfld r);
    id ();
    emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 (Int64.of_int col));
    emit k (call c "get" [ c.rel; S.I8; S.I8 ] S.I8) in
  (* the tuple id's columns: those known compared (keys), the variables
   * bound, one bound again compared *)
  let tuple (s : E.scan) (r : int) (id : unit -> unit) (keys : bool) (skip : int) =
    let differs () = emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Ne, true, skip)) in
    if keys then
      Array.iter
        (fun ((col, x) : int * D.arg) -> get r id col; value x; differs ())
        s.keys;
    List.iter
      (fun ((col, v) : int * int) -> get r id col; emit k (Il.Stloc env.(v)))
      s.binds;
    List.iter
      (fun ((col, v) : int * int) ->
        get r id col; emit k (Il.Ldloc env.(v)); differs ())
      s.same in
  let rec steps_of (l : E.step list) : unit =
    match l with
    | [] ->
        emit k (Il.Ldsfld (relation c rule.head.rel));
        array (Array.to_list rule.head.args);
        emit k (call c "add" [ c.rel; ints ] S.Void)
    | E.Test t :: rest ->
        let skip = label k in
        test t skip;
        steps_of rest;
        place k skip
    | E.Scan s :: rest ->
        let r = relation c s.atom.rel in
        let keys = Array.to_list (Array.map snd s.keys) in
        if s.from_new || s.mask = 0 then begin
          (* (the range read once: what is added during it is the next
           * round's) *)
          let id = local k S.I8 and hi = local k S.I8 in
          let range (f : string) =
            emit k (Il.Ldsfld r); emit k (call c f [ c.rel ] S.I8) in
          range (if s.from_new then "delta_to" else "count");
          emit k (Il.Stloc hi);
          loop k id
            (fun () ->
              if s.from_new then range "delta_from" else emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 0L))
            (fun () -> emit k (Il.Ldloc hi))
            (Il.Ldc_i8 1L)
            (fun (next : int) ->
              tuple s r (fun () -> emit k (Il.Ldloc id)) true next;
              steps_of rest)
        end
        else if Array.length s.keys = s.atom.rel.arity then begin
          let skip = label k in
          emit k (Il.Ldsfld r);
          array keys;
          emit k (call c "mem" [ c.rel; ints ] S.Bool);
          emit k (Il.Brfalse skip);
          steps_of rest;
          place k skip
        end
        else begin
          (* (an index's chain: the tuples with the keys, the last first) *)
          let x = made_next () in
          let id = local k S.I8 in
          let top = label k and next = label k and stop = label k in
          emit k (Il.Ldloc x);
          array keys;
          emit k (call c "first" [ c.idx; ints ] S.I8);
          emit k (Il.Stloc id);
          place k top;
          emit k (Il.Ldloc id);
          emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 0L);
          emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Lt, false, stop));
          tuple s r (fun () -> emit k (Il.Ldloc id)) false next;
          steps_of rest;
          place k next;
          emit k (Il.Ldloc x);
          emit k (Il.Ldloc id);
          emit k (call c "next" [ c.idx; S.I8 ] S.I8);
          emit k (Il.Stloc id);
          emit k (Il.Br top);
          place k stop
        end
  (* to skip when the test fails *)
  and test (t : D.literal) (skip : int) : unit =
    match t with
    | D.Pos _ -> ()
    | D.Neg a ->
        let args = Array.to_list a.args in
        let known = List.filter (fun (x : D.arg) -> x <> D.Any) args in
        let bit (i : int) (x : D.arg) = if x = D.Any then 0 else 1 lsl i in
        let mask = List.fold_left ( + ) 0 (List.mapi bit args) in
        emit k (Il.Ldsfld (relation c a.rel));
        emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 (Int64.of_int mask));
        array known;
        emit k (call c "absent" [ c.rel; S.I8; ints ] S.Bool);
        emit k (Il.Brfalse skip)
    | D.Cmp (("=" | "=="), x, y) ->
        value x; value y; emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Ne, true, skip))
    | D.Cmp (("\\=" | "\\=="), x, y) ->
        value x; value y; emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Eq, false, skip))
    | D.Cmp (op, x, y) ->
        emit k (Il.Ldsfld c.p);
        value x;
        value y;
        emit k (call c "compare" [ c.t; S.I8; S.I8 ] S.I8);
        emit k (Il.Ldc_i8 0L);
        (* (the comparison's negation, to skip) *)
        let x =
          match op with "<" -> Il.Ge | ">" -> Il.Le | "=<" -> Il.Gt | _ -> Il.Lt in
        emit k (Il.Bcmp (x, false, skip)) in
  steps_of steps;
  emit k Il.Ret;
  finish c k meth;
  meth

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The program *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* each stratum: its heads, its rules' plans on everything and with an
 * atom from the new tuples (Datalog_eval.run's) *)
let strata (c : c) (p : D.t) : (int list * int list * int list) list =
  let top = E.stratify p in
  let rules = List.rev p.rule_list in
  let n = ref 0 in
  let compile (r : D.rule) (steps : E.step list) =
    incr n;
    plan c p r steps (Printf.sprintf "plan%d" !n) in
  List.init (top + 1) (fun (s : int) ->
      let mine = List.filter (fun (r : D.rule) -> r.head.rel.stratum = s) rules in
      let heads =
        List.fold_left
          (fun (acc : D.relation list) (r : D.rule) ->
            if List.memq r.head.rel acc then acc else r.head.rel :: acc)
          [] mine in
      let whole =
        List.map (fun (r : D.rule) -> compile r (E.plan r.slots None r.body)) mine in
      let by_new =
        List.concat_map
          (fun (r : D.rule) ->
            List.concat
              (List.mapi
                 (fun (k : int) (l : D.literal) ->
                   match l with
                   | D.Pos a when a.rel.stratum = s && a.rel.rules > 0 ->
                       [ compile r (E.from_new r k a) ]
                   | _ -> [])
                 r.body))
          mine in
      (List.map (relation c) heads, whole, by_new))

let assembly ((rt_name, entry) : string * string) (name : string) (p : D.t)
    (texts : (string * string) list) (queries : string list) : string =
  let w = W.create name in
  let runtime = W.assembly_ref w "System.Runtime" in
  let rt_asm = W.assembly_ref w rt_name in
  let datalog = W.type_ref w rt_asm "" "Datalog" in
  let rel_tok = W.type_ref w datalog "" "relation" in
  let idx = S.Class (W.type_ref w (W.type_ref w rt_asm "" "Index") "" "t") in
  let t = S.Class (W.type_ref w datalog "" "t") and rel = S.Class rel_tok in
  let rt = W.type_ref w rt_asm "" "Datalog_rt" in
  let obj = W.type_ref w runtime "System" "Object" in
  let cls = W.type_def w "" "Compiled" 0x00000181 obj in
  let pf = W.field_def w cls "<p>" 0x0011 t in
  let c =
    { w; cls; t; rel; rt; idx; p = pf; relations = Hashtbl.create 16;
      symbols = Hashtbl.create 16; inits = [] } in
  let strata = strata c p in
  (* rules(p): the fields set, then each stratum's rounds *)
  let rules_m = W.method_def w cls "rules" 0x0091 (static [ t ] S.Object) in
  let k = new_code () in
  emit k (Il.Ldarg 0);
  emit k (Il.Stsfld pf);
  List.iter (List.iter (emit k)) (List.rev c.inits);
  List.iter
    (fun ((heads, whole, by_new) : int list * int list * int list) ->
      let a = local k (S.SzArray rel) in
      emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int (List.length heads)));
      emit k (Il.Newarr rel_tok);
      List.iteri
        (fun (i : int) (f : int) ->
          emit k Il.Dup; emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int i)); emit k (Il.Ldsfld f);
          emit k (Il.Stelem Il.K_ref))
        heads;
      emit k (Il.Stloc a);
      let heads_call (f : string) (r : S.t) =
        emit k (Il.Ldloc a); emit k (call c f [ S.SzArray rel ] r) in
      heads_call "begin_stratum" S.Void;
      List.iter (fun (m : int) -> emit k (Il.Call m)) whole;
      let top = label k and stop = label k in
      place k top;
      heads_call "turn" S.Bool;
      emit k (Il.Brfalse stop);
      List.iter (fun (m : int) -> emit k (Il.Call m)) by_new;
      emit k (Il.Br top);
      place k stop;
      heads_call "end_stratum" S.Void)
    strata;
  emit k Il.Ldnull;
  emit k Il.Ret;
  finish c k rules_m;
  (* Main: datalog_rt's main given the texts, the queries, rules *)
  let string = W.type_ref w runtime "System" "String" in
  let strings (l : string list) =
    let one (i : int) (s : string) =
      [ Il.Dup; Il.Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int i); Il.Ldstr (W.user_string w s);
        Il.Stelem Il.K_ref ] in
    [ Il.Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int (List.length l)); Il.Newarr string ]
    @ List.concat (List.mapi one l) in
  let func_cls = W.type_ref w runtime "System" "Func`2" in
  let func = S.GenericInst (S.Class func_cls, [ t; S.Object ]) in
  let func_ctor =
    W.member_ref w (W.type_spec w func) ".ctor" (instance [ S.Object; S.I ] S.Void) in
  let rt_main = static [ S.SzArray S.String; S.SzArray S.String; func ] S.Void in
  let main =
    W.method_def w cls "Main" 0x0096 (static [ S.SzArray S.String ] S.Void) in
  let ops =
    strings (List.concat_map (fun ((n, text) : string * string) -> [ n; text ]) texts)
    @ strings queries
    @ [ Il.Ldnull; Il.Ldftn rules_m; Il.Newobj func_ctor;
        Il.Call (W.member_ref w (W.type_ref w rt_asm "" entry) "main" rt_main); Il.Ret ] in
  W.set_body w main [] (Array.of_list ops) [];
  W.set_entry_point w main;
  W.write w
languages/datalog/dotnet/Compile_il.mli
2336
(* mini-datalog -dotnet (plan_dotnet_languages.md, stage 6, decision 5):
 * a program's rules compiled to a .NET assembly, Souffle's way. What
 * the interpreter decides as it runs (Datalog_eval), the compiler
 * decides once: the strata, each rule's plans (its atoms' order, the
 * columns known at each, where each test goes), and writes the joins
 * they say as nested loops in IL:
 *
 *     path(X, Y) :- path(X, Z), edge(Z, Y).    from path's new tuples
 *
 *     for id in path's delta_from .. delta_to:     a scan of a range
 *       X = get(path, id, 0); Z = get(path, id, 1)
 *       for each id' in lookup(edge, mask 1, [Z]):   an index's tuples
 *         Y = get(edge, id', 1)
 *         add(path, [X, Y])
 *
 * and each stratum's rounds: the rules on everything, then while a
 * head has new tuples, each rule again with one of its atoms from them
 * (semi-naive). The relations are not compiled: they are mini-datalog's
 * own (Datalog, Relset, Index), compiled by mini-ml -dotnet into
 * datalog_rt.dll with Datalog_rt, the calls the code makes (get,
 * lookup, add, the rounds' ranges), and the program's entry: it reads
 * the rules' texts (kept in the assembly: their facts, their queries)
 * and the facts files it is given, runs the compiled rules, answers
 * the queries as the interpreter does. Souffle splits it so too: its
 * C++ for the rules, a library for the relations.
 *
 *     mini-datalog -dotnet -o p.dll -q 'call_edge(I, F)' pointer.dl
 *     dotnet p.dll pointers.facts          (datalog_rt.dll beside it)
 *
 * The symbols are the runtime's numbers: a constant of a rule is a
 * field set from its text when the program starts.
 *
 * others: Souffle (2016) compiles to C++ through its RAM, a language
 * of loops, scans and index lookups, Datalog_eval's plan here; the
 * interpreter it later got (2019) runs the same RAM. Here the plan is
 * the interpreter's, the same code choosing it for both. *)

(* the assembly's bytes: its runtime's assembly and the class whose
 * main is the entry (datalog_rt, Datalog_rt; mini-analyze's
 * analyze_rt, Analyze_rt), its name, the program loaded (its rules, a
 * relation's stratum set by its run), the files' names and texts, the
 * queries asked *)
val assembly :
  string * string -> string -> Datalog.t -> (string * string) list -> string list -> string

(* Claude Code

(* See Datalog_rt.mli *)

module D = Datalog

exception Failed of string

let fail (msg : string) : 'a = raise (Failed msg)

(* the program's facts: the rules' files' texts (name, text, ...),
 * then the files given *)
let load (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (texts : string array) (files : string array)
    : D.t =
  let p = D.create () in
  let load (from : string) (text : string) =
    try D.load p ~from text with D.Error (msg, at) -> fail (at ^ ": " ^ msg) in
  for i = 0 to (Array.length texts / 2) - 1 do
    load texts.(2 * i) texts.((2 * i) + 1)
  done;
  Array.iter
    (fun (f : string) ->
      match FS.path f with
      | Error msg -> fail msg
      | Ok path -> (
          match FS.read_opt caps path with
          | Some text -> load f text
          | None -> fail (f ^ ": cannot be read")))
    files;
  p

let relation (p : D.t) (name : string) (arity : int) : D.relation =
  D.relation p name arity

let symbol (p : D.t) (text : string) : int =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt p.symbols text with
  | Some k -> k
  | None -> fail ("no symbol " ^ text)

let count (r : D.relation) : int = r.count
let delta_from (r : D.relation) : int = r.delta_from
let delta_to (r : D.relation) : int = r.delta_to
let get (r : D.relation) (id : int) (col : int) : int = D.get r id col

(* the tuples whose mask's columns are the keys, by their numbers *)
let lookup (r : D.relation) (mask : int) (keys : int array) : int array =
  let found = ref [] in
  Index.iter (Datalog_eval.index r mask) r.rows r.arity (fun (i : int) -> keys.(i))
    (fun (_ : int array) (base : int) -> found := (base / r.arity) :: !found);
  Array.of_list (List.rev !found)

(* a relation's hashed index by the mask's columns (made the first
 * time), and its chain: the last tuple with the keys, the one before
 * with the same, -1 at the end (the compiled loop's, no allocation) *)
let index (r : D.relation) (mask : int) : Index.t = Datalog_eval.index r mask

let first (idx : Index.t) (keys : int array) : int = Index.first_array idx keys
let next (idx : Index.t) (id : int) : int = Index.next idx id

let mem (r : D.relation) (tuple : int array) : bool = Relset.mem_array r.set tuple

let absent (r : D.relation) (mask : int) (keys : int array) : bool =
  if mask = 0 then r.count = 0
  else if mask = (1 lsl r.arity) - 1 then not (mem r keys)
  else not (Index.exists_array (Datalog_eval.index r mask) keys)

let compare (p : D.t) (x : int) (y : int) : int =
  Prolog.compare p.terms.(x) p.terms.(y)

(* (the tuple is the caller's, filled again: copied when it is new) *)
let add (r : D.relation) (tuple : int array) : unit =
  if not (mem r tuple) then ignore (D.add r (Array.copy tuple))

(* a stratum's rounds: its heads' new tuples, Datalog_eval's ranges *)
let since (r : D.relation) (from : int) : unit =
  r.delta_from <- from;
  r.delta_to <- r.count

let begin_stratum (heads : D.relation array) : unit =
  Array.iter (fun (r : D.relation) -> since r r.count) heads

let turn (heads : D.relation array) : bool =
  let any = ref false in
  Array.iter
    (fun (r : D.relation) ->
      if r.count > r.delta_to then any := true;
      since r r.delta_to)
    heads;
  !any

let end_stratum (heads : D.relation array) : unit = begin_stratum heads

(* the queries' answers, the texts' then the program's, each sorted *)
let answers (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (p : D.t) (queries : string array) : unit =
  let asked =
    Array.to_list
      (Array.map
         (fun (q : string) ->
           try D.query p q with D.Error (msg, at) -> fail (at ^ ": " ^ msg))
         queries) in
  List.iter
    (fun (q : D.query) ->
      List.iter
        (fun (line : string) -> Console.print caps (line ^ "\n"))
        (Datalog_eval.answers p q))
    (List.rev p.queries @ asked)

let main (texts : string array) (queries : string array) (rules : D.t -> unit)
    : unit =
  Cap.main (fun (caps : Cap.all_caps) ->
      let argv = CapSys.argv caps in
      let files = Array.sub argv 1 (Array.length argv - 1) in
      match load caps texts files with
      | p ->
          rules p;
          answers caps p queries;
          flush (Console.stdout caps)
      | exception Failed msg ->
          Console.eprint caps (msg ^ "\n");
          CapStdlib.exit caps 1)

(* Claude Code

(* See CLI.mli *)

type caps =
  < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.env; Cap.chdir; Cap.stdin;
    Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.clock >

let usage = "usage: mini-dotnet [-v|-debug|-quiet] [-trace] [-s] [-jit [-tier n]] file.dll [arg...] | -S [-jit [-m 5|7 [-refs]]] | -tables | -size | -verify file.dll..."

(* a Stream that cannot seek: the console's *)
let unseekable () : 'a =
  ignore (Library.hooks.throw "System.NotSupportedException" "Stream does not support seeking.");
  assert false

(* the system's error .NET's IOException (a write to a file opened to
 * read...) *)
let io (f : unit -> 'a) : 'a =
  match f () with
  | x -> x
  | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) ->
      ignore (Library.hooks.throw "System.IO.IOException" (Unix.error_message e)); assert false

(* a file's Stream: its descriptor's bytes *)
let file_stream (fd : Unix.file_descr) : Value.stream =
  let rec write (b : Bytes.t) (off : int) (n : int) : unit =
    if n > 0 then (let k = io (fun () -> Unix.write fd b off n) in write b (off + k) (n - k)) in
  { sread = (fun b off n -> io (fun () -> Unix.read fd b off n)); swrite = write; sflush = (fun () -> ());
    sclose = (fun () -> io (fun () -> Unix.close fd));
    sposition = (fun () -> io (fun () -> Unix.lseek fd 0 Unix.SEEK_CUR));
    sseek = (fun (p : int) -> io (fun () -> ignore (Unix.lseek fd p Unix.SEEK_SET)));
    slength = (fun () -> io (fun () -> (Unix.fstat fd).st_size)) }

(* File's OpenRead, OpenWrite (made when it is not there, else written
 * as it is), Create (made or emptied); Exists *)
let open_file (caps : < caps; .. >) (how : string) (f : string) : Value.stream option =
  let exists () = match FS.open_in_fd caps f with fd -> Unix.close fd; true | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false in
  match how with
  | "Exists" -> if exists () then Some (file_stream Unix.stdin) else None
  | _ -> (
      match
        (match how with
         | "OpenRead" -> FS.open_in_fd caps f
         | "OpenWrite" when exists () -> FS.open_device_fd caps f
         | _ -> FS.open_out_fd caps f 0o666)
      with
      | fd -> Some (file_stream fd)
      | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> None)

(* a path's kind: 0 nothing, 1 a file, 2 a directory *)
let kind (_caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (f : string) : int =
  (* nosemgrep: use-caps *)
  match (Unix.stat f).st_kind with Unix.S_DIR -> 2 | _ -> 1 | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> 0

let rename (_caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) (a : string) (b : string) : bool =
  (* nosemgrep: use-caps *)
  match Sys.rename a b with () -> true | exception Sys_error _ -> false

(* (sorted: .NET's order is the system's, which may differ) *)
let entries (_caps : < Cap.readdir; .. >) (f : string) : string list option =
  (* nosemgrep: use-caps *)
  match Sys.readdir f with a -> Some (List.sort compare (Array.to_list a)) | exception Sys_error _ -> None

(* Library's system: each access by its capability; the clock the
 * milliseconds since the program started *)
let os (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string list) : Library.os =
  let start = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () in
  { argv;
    getenv = (fun (v : string) -> match CapSys.getenv caps v with s -> Some s | exception Not_found -> None);
    kind = kind caps;
    remove = (fun (f : string) -> match FS.remove_any caps f with () -> true | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false);
    rename = rename caps;
    mkdir = (fun (f : string) -> match FS.mkdir caps f 0o777 with () -> true | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false);
    entries = entries caps;
    cwd = (fun () -> FS.getcwd caps ());
    chdir = (fun (f : string) -> match CapUnix.chdir caps f with () -> true | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false);
    ticks = (fun () -> int_of_float ((CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () -. start) *. 1000.)) }

(* a program run: its output by the console's channel, its input
 * read a byte at a time; an exception no one catches said as .NET says
 * it, the exit then 134 (.NET's abort). The standard streams over the
 * same channels, so that Console.Write's and theirs come in order *)
let run (caps : < caps; .. >) (path : string) (img : Image.t) (argv : string list) (tracing : bool) (stats : bool) : int =
  let out = Console.stdout caps in
  let ic = Console.stdin caps in
  let err = Console.stderr caps in
  Library.hooks.out <- output_string out;
  Library.hooks.read <- (fun () -> flush out; match input_char ic with
    | c -> Char.code c | exception End_of_file -> -1);
  let std (fd : int) : Value.stream =
    let oc = if fd = 2 then err else out in
    { sread = (fun b off n -> if fd = 0 then (flush out; input ic b off n) else 0);
      swrite = (fun b off n -> if fd <> 0 then output oc b off n);
      sflush = (fun () -> if fd <> 0 then flush oc);
      sclose = (fun () -> ()); sposition = unseekable; sseek = (fun (_ : int) -> unseekable ()); slength = unseekable } in
  Library.hooks.std <- std;
  Library.hooks.file <- open_file caps;
  Library.hooks.os <- os caps (path :: argv);
  if tracing then Frame.trace := Some (fun s -> flush out; Console.eprint caps (s ^ "\n"));
  Machine.install ();
  (* the assemblies it references that are not .NET's, beside it, each
   * loaded before what references it (plan_dotnet_languages.md, stage
   * 7): a class is then found by its name in any of them *)
  let loaded = Hashtbl.create 4 in
  let rec references (img : Image.t) : unit =
    for r = 1 to img.rows.(Metadata.t_assembly_ref) do
      let name = Image.string img (Image.get img Metadata.t_assembly_ref r "Name") in
      let dll = match FS.path path with
        | Ok p -> Some Fpath.(parent p / (name ^ ".dll")) | Error _ -> None in
      match dll with
      | Some f when not (Hashtbl.mem loaded name) && name <> "System"
                    && not (String.length name > 7 && String.sub name 0 7 = "System.") -> (
          match FS.read_opt caps f with
          | Some data ->
              Hashtbl.replace loaded name ();
              let i = Image.read data in
              references i;
              ignore (Types.load i)
          | None -> ())
      | _ -> ()
    done in
  references img;
  let im = Types.load img in
  let finish () =
    flush out;
    if stats then Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "%d instructions\n" !Frame.steps);
    (match !Frame.profile with
     | Some h ->
         let all = max 1 !Frame.steps in
         let l = Hashtbl.fold (fun (name : string) (n : int ref) acc -> (!n, name) :: acc) h [] in
         List.iteri
           (fun (i : int) ((n, name) : int * string) ->
             if i < 25 then
               Console.eprint caps
                 (Printf.sprintf "%5.1f%% %12d  %s\n" (100. *. float n /. float all) n name))
           (List.sort (fun (a : int * string) b -> compare b a) l)
     | None -> ());
    if stats && !Jit_run.compiled > 0 then
      Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "%d methods compiled\n" !Jit_run.compiled) in
  match Machine.run_main im argv with
  | n -> finish (); n
  | exception Library.Exit n -> finish (); n
  | exception Frame.Stack_overflow -> finish (); Console.eprint caps "Stack overflow.\n"; 134
  | exception Frame.Unhandled (cls, msg) ->
      finish ();
      Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "Unhandled exception. %s: %s\n" cls msg);
      134
  | exception (Frame.Error msg | Types.Load_error msg) ->
      finish ();
      Console.eprint caps ("mini-dotnet: " ^ msg ^ "\n");
      1

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : int =
  let mode = ref "run" in
  let files = ref [] in
  let tracing = ref false and stats = ref false and jit = ref false and mach = ref 5 and refs = ref false in
  let options =
    Logging.flags @
    [ ("-trace", Arg.Set tracing, " each instruction said as it runs, to the standard error");
      ("-s", Arg.Set stats, " the instructions run, said at the end");
      ("-profile", Arg.Unit (fun () -> Frame.profile := Some (Hashtbl.create 64)),
       " each method's own instructions (its calls' not), the costliest first, at the end"); ("-tables", Arg.Unit (fun () -> mode := "tables"), " the metadata's tables, a row a line");
      ("-S", Arg.Unit (fun () -> mode := "S"), " the types and their methods' IL, as ildasm");
      ("-size", Arg.Unit (fun () -> mode := "size"), " its types, methods and bytes of IL (each body decoded)");
      ("-verify", Arg.Unit (fun () -> mode := "verify"), " each method's stack typed at each instruction: those refused, and why");
      ("-jit", Arg.Set jit, " the methods the JIT takes run as the machine's code (mini-ml's build, arm64); with -S, that code as mini-asm's text, why not the others");
      ("-tier", Arg.Set_int Machine.tier, " with -jit: the calls a method is interpreted before it is compiled (30; 0: at its first; a method with a loop at its first)");
      ("-m", Arg.Set_int mach, " with -S -jit: the machine, 5 (arm, the default) or 7 (arm64)");
      ("-refs", Arg.Set refs, " with -S -jit: references too, the code -jit runs (the assembly loaded)") ] in
  (* (running a program, the arguments after its .dll are its own, its
   * options too: mini-cc.dll -m 7 -x -a) *)
  let rec first_dll (i : int) =
    if i >= Array.length argv then Array.length argv
    else if Filename.check_suffix argv.(i) ".dll" && argv.(i - 1) <> "-tier" && argv.(i - 1) <> "-m" then i
    else first_dll (i + 1) in
  let cut = first_dll 1 in
  let own = Array.sub argv 0 (min (cut + 1) (Array.length argv)) in
  let program_args = if cut + 1 < Array.length argv then Array.to_list (Array.sub argv (cut + 1) (Array.length argv - cut - 1)) else [] in
  let verbs = Array.exists (fun (a : string) -> a = "-S" || a = "-tables" || a = "-size" || a = "-verify") own in
  let argv = if verbs then argv else own in
  match Arg.parse_argv argv options (fun (f : string) -> files := f :: !files) usage with
  | exception Arg.Help _ -> Console.print caps (usage ^ "\n"); 0
  | exception Arg.Bad msg -> Console.eprint caps msg; 1
  | () ->
      let read (f : string) : Image.t =
        let data = match FS.path f with
          | Error e -> failwith e
          | Ok p -> FS.read caps p in
        Logs.info (fun m -> m "read %s: %d bytes" f (String.length data));
        Image.read data in
      let one (f : string) : unit =
        let img = read f in
        let data = img.file in
        match !mode with
        | "tables" -> Console.print caps (Listing.tables img)
        | "S" when !jit ->
            let text, n, refused = Jit.assembly (if !mach = 7 then Jit.Arm64 else Jit.Arm) img
                (if !refs then Some (Types.load img) else None) in
            Console.print caps text;
            List.iter (fun (row, why) ->
                Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "// not compiled: %s: %s\n"
                                      (Listing.token_name img (Metadata.token Metadata.t_method_def row)) why)) refused;
            Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "// %s: %d methods compiled, %d not\n" (Filename.basename f) n (List.length refused))
        | "S" -> Console.print caps (Listing.listing img)
        | "size" ->
            let types, methods, il = Listing.sizes img in
            Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%s: %d bytes, %d types, %d methods, %d bytes of IL\n"
                                  (Filename.basename f) (String.length data) types methods il)
        | "verify" ->
            let ok, errors = Verifier.assembly img in
            List.iter (fun (row, msg) ->
                Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s\n"
                                      (Listing.token_name img (Metadata.token Metadata.t_method_def row)) msg)) errors;
            Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%s: %d methods verified, %d refused\n"
                                  (Filename.basename f) ok (List.length errors))
        | _ -> () in
      try
        if !mode = "run" then begin
          match List.rev !files with
          | [] -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "\n"); 1
          | f :: argv ->
              let argv = argv @ program_args in
              if !jit && not Code_memory.available then
                Logs.warn (fun m -> m "-jit ignored: this build has no JIT\n\
                                       (mini-ml's on arm64 has: _mk/7/languages/dotnet/mini-dotnet)");
              if !jit then Machine.jit := Some (Jit_run.jit caps);
              run caps f (read f) argv !tracing !stats
        end
        else (List.iter one (List.rev !files); 0)
      with
      | Failure msg | Sys_error msg -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-dotnet: " ^ msg ^ "\n"); 1
      | Image.Bad_image msg -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-dotnet: not an assembly: " ^ msg ^ "\n"); 1

3729
(* mini-dotnet: .NET's assemblies, as Microsoft's C# compiler writes
 * them, read and run (docs/plans/done/plan_dotnet.md). Its usage: [usage]
 * in CLI.ml.
 *
 *     hello.dll                 a PE file, its metadata a database
 *        | Image                the PE's sections, the metadata's
 *        |                      heaps and 45 tables (Metadata: their
 *        |                      shapes), a method's body
 *        | Signature, Il        the blobs' types; the IL's opcodes
 *        |---------- Listing    -tables, -S (as ildasm), -size
 *        | Types                a class loaded when first named: laid
 *        |                      out, its virtual methods' slots; the
 *        |                      tokens resolved, generics instantiated
 *        | Machine              the IL run on tagged values (Value);
 *        |                      the exceptions' two passes
 *     what it prints            Library: System's classes, ix's own,
 *                               OCaml functions over the machine's values
 *
 *     $ mini-dotnet survey/programs/fib.dll
 *     6765
 *     102334155
 *     -1323752223              the 47th, past int32: wrapped, as .NET
 *     $ mini-dotnet -s survey/programs/queens.dll
 *     15863724
 *     92 solutions
 *     360572 instructions
 *
 * Checked by running what Microsoft's compiler wrote and comparing
 * what is printed with what Microsoft's runtime prints for the same
 * file (tests/run.sh): the same file, two runtimes.
 *
 * history:
 * Microsoft's .NET Framework (2002) was its answer to Java: a virtual
 * machine, the CLR, with a library and C#, a language by Anders
 * Hejlsberg (Turbo Pascal's and Delphi's author). Its machine, the
 * CLI, was made a standard (ECMA-335, 2001; ISO 23271), and Microsoft
 * published a version of it as source, "Rotor" (2002), for teaching.
 * Mono (Miguel de Icaza, 2004) ran it on Linux. In 2016 .NET Core,
 * Microsoft's own, became open source and ran everywhere; it is
 * today's .NET, whose `dotnet` runs the same files as here.
 * Before: the runtime grew from COM's (COM+ 2.0, its codename
 * Lightning), and was announced in 2000 as NGWS, then .NET. Sun had
 * sued Microsoft in 1997 over its Java (J++, its own extensions); the
 * extensions (delegates, calls of native code) came back in C#, and
 * Hejlsberg came from J++.
 * Project 7 (1998-2000): some fifteen language groups, Eiffel,
 * Mercury, Haskell, Standard ML, Scheme, Oberon, Python, COBOL among
 * them, given the runtime before it shipped to port their languages;
 * the common type system was to be shared, a class of one language
 * subclassed in another, and their reports changed the machine (the
 * tail. prefix). Generics (.NET 2.0, 2005) came from Microsoft
 * Research Cambridge (Andrew Kennedy, Don Syme, PLDI 2001), reified
 * in the machine, where Java's (2004) are erased by its compiler; F#
 * (Syme, 2005) followed.
 * Singularity (Microsoft Research, Galen Hunt and Jim Larus, 2003-2008)
 * an operating system in C#: Bartok compiled the whole system's IL
 * ahead of time, the verifier's guarantee standing in for the MMU
 * (processes isolated by their types, one address space); Midori
 * (2008-2015) carried it on.
 *
 * References: ECMA-335, "Common Language Infrastructure", 6th edition
 * (2012): Partition I the concepts, II the file and its metadata, III
 * the instructions; David Stutz, Ted Neward, Geoff Shilling, "Shared
 * Source CLI Essentials" (O'Reilly, 2003), Rotor read; Serge Lidin,
 * ".NET IL Assembler" (Apress, 2014). *)

    Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.clock >

val main : < caps; .. > -> string array -> int

(* See Il.mli *)

type kind = K_i1 | K_u1 | K_i2 | K_u2 | K_i4 | K_u4 | K_i8 | K_u8
          | K_i | K_u | K_r4 | K_r8 | K_ref

type binop = Add | Sub | Mul | Div | Div_un | Rem | Rem_un
           | And | Or | Xor | Shl | Shr | Shr_un
           | Add_ovf | Add_ovf_un | Mul_ovf | Mul_ovf_un | Sub_ovf | Sub_ovf_un

type cmp = Eq | Ne | Ge | Gt | Le | Lt

type op =
  | Nop
  | Break
  | Ldarg of int | Ldarga of int | Starg of int
  | Ldloc of int | Ldloca of int | Stloc of int
  | Ldnull
  | Ldc_i4 of int32 | Ldc_i8 of int64 | Ldc_r of float
  | Dup | Pop
  | Jmp of int | Call of int | Calli of int | Callvirt of int
  | Ret
  | Br of int
  | Brfalse of int | Brtrue of int
  | Bcmp of cmp * bool * int
  | Switch of int array
  | Ldind of kind | Stind of kind
  | Binop of binop
  | Neg | Not
  | Conv of kind * bool * bool
  | Conv_r_un
  | Cpobj of int | Ldobj of int | Stobj of int
  | Ldstr of int
  | Newobj of int
  | Castclass of int | Isinst of int
  | Unbox of int | Unbox_any of int | Box of int
  | Throw | Rethrow
  | Ldfld of int | Ldflda of int | Stfld of int
  | Ldsfld of int | Ldsflda of int | Stsfld of int
  | Newarr of int | Ldlen
  | Ldelema of int
  | Ldelem of kind | Ldelem_any of int
  | Stelem of kind | Stelem_any of int
  | Refanyval of int | Mkrefany of int | Refanytype
  | Ckfinite
  | Ldtoken of int
  | Endfinally
  | Leave of int
  | Ceq | Cgt of bool | Clt of bool
  | Ldftn of int | Ldvirtftn of int
  | Arglist | Localloc | Endfilter
  | Initobj of int
  | Cpblk | Initblk
  | Sizeof of int
  | Constrained of int
  | Prefix of string

type instr = {
  at : int;
  name : string;
  op : op;
}

exception Bad_il of string

(* an operand's size and meaning *)
type operand =
  | No
  | S8              (* a signed byte: ldc.i4.s *)
  | U8              (* an unsigned byte: ldarg.s's number *)
  | U16
  | I32
  | I64
  | F32
  | F64
  | Tok
  | Br8             (* a branch, its distance from the next instruction *)
  | Br32
  | Sw              (* a count, then that many Br32 *)

(* Partition III, by their bytes; a code above 0xFF is 0xFE's second *)

let opcodes = List.map (fun (c, n, _) -> (c, n)) table

(* by their code: the one-byte ones, then 0xFE's *)
let one = Array.make 256 None
let two = Array.make 256 None
let () =
  List.iter (fun (c, n, o) ->
      if c < 0x100 then one.(c) <- Some (n, o) else two.(c land 0xFF) <- Some (n, o)) table

let kind_of (s : string) : kind =
  match s with
  | "i1" -> K_i1 | "u1" -> K_u1 | "i2" -> K_i2 | "u2" -> K_u2
  | "i4" -> K_i4 | "u4" -> K_u4 | "i8" -> K_i8 | "u8" -> K_u8
  | "i" -> K_i | "u" -> K_u | "r4" -> K_r4 | "r8" -> K_r8 | "ref" -> K_ref
  | _ -> raise (Bad_il ("a kind " ^ s))

let cmp_of (s : string) : cmp =
  match s with
  | "eq" -> Eq | "ne" -> Ne | "ge" -> Ge | "gt" -> Gt | "le" -> Le | "lt" -> Lt
  | _ -> raise (Bad_il ("a comparison " ^ s))

(* what was read after the opcode *)
type arg = A_none | A_int of int | A_i32 of int32 | A_i64 of int64
         | A_float of float | A_targets of int array

(* the op of a name and its operand; a branch's target already an
 * offset *)
let make (name : string) (arg : arg) : op =
  let n = match arg with A_int n -> n | _ -> 0 in
  let parts = String.split_on_char '.' name in
  match name, parts with
  | "nop", _ -> Nop
  | "break", _ -> Break
  | _, ["ldarg"; ("0" | "1" | "2" | "3" as k)] -> Ldarg (int_of_string k)
  | _, ["ldloc"; ("0" | "1" | "2" | "3" as k)] -> Ldloc (int_of_string k)
  | _, ["stloc"; ("0" | "1" | "2" | "3" as k)] -> Stloc (int_of_string k)
  | _, ("ldarg" :: _) -> Ldarg n
  | _, ("ldarga" :: _) -> Ldarga n
  | _, ("starg" :: _) -> Starg n
  | _, ("ldloc" :: _) -> Ldloc n
  | _, ("ldloca" :: _) -> Ldloca n
  | _, ("stloc" :: _) -> Stloc n
  | "ldnull", _ -> Ldnull
  | "ldc.i4.m1", _ -> Ldc_i4 Int32.minus_one
  | _, ["ldc"; "i4"; k] when k <> "s" -> Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int (int_of_string k))
  | _, ("ldc" :: "i4" :: _) ->
      (match arg with A_i32 v -> Ldc_i4 v | _ -> Ldc_i4 (Int32.of_int n))
  | "ldc.i8", _ -> (match arg with A_i64 v -> Ldc_i8 v | _ -> assert false)
  | ("ldc.r4" | "ldc.r8"), _ -> (match arg with A_float v -> Ldc_r v | _ -> assert false)
  | "dup", _ -> Dup
  | "pop", _ -> Pop
  | "jmp", _ -> Jmp n
  | "call", _ -> Call n
  | "calli", _ -> Calli n
  | "callvirt", _ -> Callvirt n
  | "ret", _ -> Ret
  | _, ("br" :: _) -> Br n
  | _, ("brfalse" :: _) -> Brfalse n
  | _, ("brtrue" :: _) -> Brtrue n
  | _, (("beq" | "bge" | "bgt" | "ble" | "blt" | "bne") as c :: rest) ->
      Bcmp (cmp_of (String.sub c 1 2), List.mem "un" rest, n)
  | "switch", _ -> (match arg with A_targets t -> Switch t | _ -> assert false)
  | _, ["ldind"; k] -> Ldind (kind_of k)
  | _, ["stind"; k] -> Stind (kind_of k)
  | "add", _ -> Binop Add | "sub", _ -> Binop Sub | "mul", _ -> Binop Mul
  | "div", _ -> Binop Div | "div.un", _ -> Binop Div_un
  | "rem", _ -> Binop Rem | "rem.un", _ -> Binop Rem_un
  | "and", _ -> Binop And | "or", _ -> Binop Or | "xor", _ -> Binop Xor
  | "shl", _ -> Binop Shl | "shr", _ -> Binop Shr | "shr.un", _ -> Binop Shr_un
  | "add.ovf", _ -> Binop Add_ovf | "add.ovf.un", _ -> Binop Add_ovf_un
  | "mul.ovf", _ -> Binop Mul_ovf | "mul.ovf.un", _ -> Binop Mul_ovf_un
  | "sub.ovf", _ -> Binop Sub_ovf | "sub.ovf.un", _ -> Binop Sub_ovf_un
  | "neg", _ -> Neg
  | "not", _ -> Not
  | "conv.r.un", _ -> Conv_r_un
  | _, ["conv"; "ovf"; k] -> Conv (kind_of k, true, false)
  | _, ["conv"; "ovf"; k; "un"] -> Conv (kind_of k, true, true)
  | _, ["conv"; k] -> Conv (kind_of k, false, false)
  | "cpobj", _ -> Cpobj n | "ldobj", _ -> Ldobj n | "stobj", _ -> Stobj n
  | "ldstr", _ -> Ldstr n
  | "newobj", _ -> Newobj n
  | "castclass", _ -> Castclass n | "isinst", _ -> Isinst n
  | "unbox", _ -> Unbox n | "unbox.any", _ -> Unbox_any n | "box", _ -> Box n
  | "throw", _ -> Throw | "rethrow", _ -> Rethrow
  | "ldfld", _ -> Ldfld n | "ldflda", _ -> Ldflda n | "stfld", _ -> Stfld n
  | "ldsfld", _ -> Ldsfld n | "ldsflda", _ -> Ldsflda n | "stsfld", _ -> Stsfld n
  | "newarr", _ -> Newarr n | "ldlen", _ -> Ldlen
  | "ldelema", _ -> Ldelema n
  | "ldelem", _ -> Ldelem_any n | "stelem", _ -> Stelem_any n
  | _, ["ldelem"; k] -> Ldelem (kind_of k)
  | _, ["stelem"; k] -> Stelem (kind_of k)
  | "refanyval", _ -> Refanyval n | "mkrefany", _ -> Mkrefany n
  | "refanytype", _ -> Refanytype
  | "ckfinite", _ -> Ckfinite
  | "ldtoken", _ -> Ldtoken n
  | "endfinally", _ -> Endfinally
  | _, ("leave" :: _) -> Leave n
  | "ceq", _ -> Ceq | "cgt", _ -> Cgt false | "cgt.un", _ -> Cgt true
  | "clt", _ -> Clt false | "clt.un", _ -> Clt true
  | "ldftn", _ -> Ldftn n | "ldvirtftn", _ -> Ldvirtftn n
  | "arglist", _ -> Arglist | "localloc", _ -> Localloc
  | "endfilter", _ -> Endfilter
  | "initobj", _ -> Initobj n
  | "cpblk", _ -> Cpblk | "initblk", _ -> Initblk
  | "sizeof", _ -> Sizeof n
  | "constrained.", _ -> Constrained n
  | _ -> Prefix name

let decode (code : string) : instr array =
  let len = String.length code in
  let s8 p = let b = Char.code code.[p] in if b >= 128 then b - 256 else b in
  let i32 p =
    Int32.logor (Int32.of_int (Binary.le16 code p))
      (Int32.shift_left (Int32.of_int (Binary.le16 code (p + 2))) 16) in
  let int32 p = Int32.to_int (i32 p) in
  let out = ref [] in
  let p = ref 0 in
  (try
     while !p < len do
       let at = !p in
       let b = Char.code code.[at] in
       let entry, q =
         if b = 0xFE then (two.(Char.code code.[at + 1]), at + 2) else (one.(b), at + 1) in
       let name, operand = match entry with
         | Some e -> e
         | None -> raise (Bad_il (Printf.sprintf "an opcode 0x%x at IL_%04x" b at)) in
       let arg, next =
         match operand with
         | No -> (A_none, q)
         | S8 -> (A_int (s8 q), q + 1)
         | U8 -> (A_int (Char.code code.[q]), q + 1)
         | U16 -> (A_int (Binary.le16 code q), q + 2)
         | I32 -> (A_i32 (i32 q), q + 4)
         | I64 -> (A_i64 (String.get_int64_le code q), q + 8)
         | F32 -> (A_float (Int32.float_of_bits (i32 q)), q + 4)
         | F64 -> (A_float (Int64.float_of_bits (String.get_int64_le code q)), q + 8)
         | Tok -> (A_int (Binary.le32 code q), q + 4)
         | Br8 -> (A_int (q + 1 + s8 q), q + 1)
         | Br32 -> (A_int (q + 4 + int32 q), q + 4)
         | Sw ->
             let n = Binary.le32 code q in
             let next = q + 4 + 4 * n in
             (A_targets (Array.init n (fun i -> next + int32 (q + 4 + 4 * i))), next) in
       out := { at; name; op = make name arg } :: !out;
       p := next
     done
   with Invalid_argument _ -> raise (Bad_il "a method's IL cut short"));
  let instrs = Array.of_list (List.rev !out) in
  (* the targets: offsets to indexes *)
  let idx = Hashtbl.create (Array.length instrs) in
  Array.iteri (fun i ins -> Hashtbl.replace idx ins.at i) instrs;
  Hashtbl.replace idx len (Array.length instrs);
  let target t = match Hashtbl.find_opt idx t with
    | Some i -> i
    | None -> raise (Bad_il (Printf.sprintf "a branch to IL_%04x, inside an instruction" t)) in
  Array.map (fun ins ->
      let op = match ins.op with
        | Br t -> Br (target t)
        | Brfalse t -> Brfalse (target t)
        | Brtrue t -> Brtrue (target t)
        | Bcmp (c, u, t) -> Bcmp (c, u, target t)
        | Leave t -> Leave (target t)
        | Switch ts -> Switch (Array.map target ts)
        | op -> op in
      { ins with op }) instrs

let index (instrs : instr array) (at : int) : int =
  let rec go lo hi =
    if lo >= hi then (if lo = Array.length instrs && at >= 0 then lo else raise Not_found)
    else
      let mid = (lo + hi) / 2 in
      if instrs.(mid).at = at then mid
      else if instrs.(mid).at < at then go (mid + 1) hi
      else go lo mid in
  if Array.length instrs > 0 && at > instrs.(Array.length instrs - 1).at then Array.length instrs
  else go 0 (Array.length instrs)

(* the writer's side *)

let code_of =
  let h = Hashtbl.create 256 in
  List.iter (fun (c, n, _) -> Hashtbl.replace h n c) table;
  fun (name : string) -> match Hashtbl.find_opt h name with
    | Some c -> c
    | None -> raise (Bad_il ("no opcode " ^ name))

let kind_name (k : kind) : string =
  match k with
  | K_i1 -> "i1" | K_u1 -> "u1" | K_i2 -> "i2" | K_u2 -> "u2"
  | K_i4 -> "i4" | K_u4 -> "u4" | K_i8 -> "i8" | K_u8 -> "u8"
  | K_i -> "i" | K_u -> "u" | K_r4 -> "r4" | K_r8 -> "r8" | K_ref -> "ref"

let cmp_name (c : cmp) : string =
  match c with Eq -> "eq" | Ne -> "ne" | Ge -> "ge" | Gt -> "gt" | Le -> "le" | Lt -> "lt"

let binop_name (b : binop) : string =
  match b with
  | Add -> "add" | Sub -> "sub" | Mul -> "mul" | Div -> "div" | Div_un -> "div.un"
  | Rem -> "rem" | Rem_un -> "rem.un" | And -> "and" | Or -> "or" | Xor -> "xor"
  | Shl -> "shl" | Shr -> "shr" | Shr_un -> "shr.un"
  | Add_ovf -> "add.ovf" | Add_ovf_un -> "add.ovf.un" | Mul_ovf -> "mul.ovf"
  | Mul_ovf_un -> "mul.ovf.un" | Sub_ovf -> "sub.ovf" | Sub_ovf_un -> "sub.ovf.un"

let add_i32 (b : Buffer.t) (v : int32) : unit = Buffer.add_int32_le b v
let add_int (b : Buffer.t) (v : int) : unit = add_i32 b (Int32.of_int v)

let encode (b : Buffer.t) (op : op) : unit =
  let opc name =
    let c = code_of name in
    if c > 0xFF then (Buffer.add_char b '\xFE'; Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr (c land 0xFF)))
    else Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr c) in
  let tok name t = opc name; add_int b t in
  (* a short form (one byte operand) or the long one; the numbered ones
   * (ldarg.0) for 0 to 3 *)
  let var short long numbered n =
    if numbered && n <= 3 then opc (short ^ "." ^ string_of_int n)
    else if n < 256 then (opc (short ^ ".s"); Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr n))
    else (opc long; Buffer.add_uint16_le b n) in
  (* a branch's target an offset: its distance from the end of this one *)
  let br name t = opc name; let here = Buffer.length b + 4 in add_int b (t - here) in
  match op with
  | Nop -> opc "nop" | Break -> opc "break"
  | Ldarg n -> var "ldarg" "ldarg" true n
  | Ldarga n -> var "ldarga" "ldarga" false n
  | Starg n -> var "starg" "starg" false n
  | Ldloc n -> var "ldloc" "ldloc" true n
  | Ldloca n -> var "ldloca" "ldloca" false n
  | Stloc n -> var "stloc" "stloc" true n
  | Ldnull -> opc "ldnull"
  | Ldc_i4 v ->
      let n = Int32.to_int v in
      if Int32.compare v (Int32.of_int (-1)) = 0 then opc "ldc.i4.m1"
      else if Int32.compare v Int32.zero >= 0 && Int32.compare v (Int32.of_int 8) <= 0 then
        opc ("ldc.i4." ^ string_of_int n)
      else if Int32.compare v (Int32.of_int (-128)) >= 0 && Int32.compare v (Int32.of_int 127) <= 0 then
        (opc "ldc.i4.s"; Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr (n land 0xFF)))
      else (opc "ldc.i4"; add_i32 b v)
  | Ldc_i8 v -> opc "ldc.i8"; Buffer.add_int64_le b v
  | Ldc_r f -> opc "ldc.r8"; Buffer.add_int64_le b (Int64.bits_of_float f)
  | Dup -> opc "dup" | Pop -> opc "pop"
  | Jmp t -> tok "jmp" t | Call t -> tok "call" t | Calli t -> tok "calli" t
  | Callvirt t -> tok "callvirt" t
  | Ret -> opc "ret"
  | Br t -> br "br" t
  | Brfalse t -> br "brfalse" t
  | Brtrue t -> br "brtrue" t
  | Bcmp (Ne, _, t) -> br "bne.un" t
  | Bcmp (c, u, t) -> br (if u then "b" ^ cmp_name c ^ ".un" else "b" ^ cmp_name c) t
  | Switch ts ->
      opc "switch"; add_int b (Array.length ts);
      let here = Buffer.length b + 4 * Array.length ts in
      Array.iter (fun t -> add_int b (t - here)) ts
  | Ldind k -> opc ("ldind." ^ kind_name k)
  | Stind k -> opc ("stind." ^ kind_name k)
  | Binop o -> opc (binop_name o)
  | Neg -> opc "neg" | Not -> opc "not"
  | Conv (k, ovf, un) ->
      opc ("conv." ^ (if ovf then "ovf." else "") ^ kind_name k ^ (if un then ".un" else ""))
  | Conv_r_un -> opc "conv.r.un"
  | Cpobj t -> tok "cpobj" t | Ldobj t -> tok "ldobj" t | Stobj t -> tok "stobj" t
  | Ldstr t -> tok "ldstr" t
  | Newobj t -> tok "newobj" t
  | Castclass t -> tok "castclass" t | Isinst t -> tok "isinst" t
  | Unbox t -> tok "unbox" t | Unbox_any t -> tok "unbox.any" t | Box t -> tok "box" t
  | Throw -> opc "throw" | Rethrow -> opc "rethrow"
  | Ldfld t -> tok "ldfld" t | Ldflda t -> tok "ldflda" t | Stfld t -> tok "stfld" t
  | Ldsfld t -> tok "ldsfld" t | Ldsflda t -> tok "ldsflda" t | Stsfld t -> tok "stsfld" t
  | Newarr t -> tok "newarr" t | Ldlen -> opc "ldlen"
  | Ldelema t -> tok "ldelema" t
  | Ldelem k -> opc ("ldelem." ^ kind_name k)
  | Ldelem_any t -> tok "ldelem" t
  | Stelem k -> opc ("stelem." ^ kind_name k)
  | Stelem_any t -> tok "stelem" t
  | Refanyval t -> tok "refanyval" t | Mkrefany t -> tok "mkrefany" t
  | Refanytype -> opc "refanytype"
  | Ckfinite -> opc "ckfinite"
  | Ldtoken t -> tok "ldtoken" t
  | Endfinally -> opc "endfinally"
  | Leave t -> br "leave" t
  | Ceq -> opc "ceq"
  | Cgt u -> opc (if u then "cgt.un" else "cgt")
  | Clt u -> opc (if u then "clt.un" else "clt")
  | Ldftn t -> tok "ldftn" t | Ldvirtftn t -> tok "ldvirtftn" t
  | Arglist -> opc "arglist" | Localloc -> opc "localloc" | Endfilter -> opc "endfilter"
  | Initobj t -> tok "initobj" t
  | Cpblk -> opc "cpblk" | Initblk -> opc "initblk"
  | Sizeof t -> tok "sizeof" t
  | Constrained t -> tok "constrained." t
  | Prefix p -> opc p

let map_tokens (f : int -> int) (op : op) : op =
  match op with
  | Jmp t -> Jmp (f t) | Call t -> Call (f t) | Calli t -> Calli (f t)
  | Callvirt t -> Callvirt (f t) | Cpobj t -> Cpobj (f t) | Ldobj t -> Ldobj (f t)
  | Stobj t -> Stobj (f t) | Ldstr t -> Ldstr (f t) | Newobj t -> Newobj (f t)
  | Castclass t -> Castclass (f t) | Isinst t -> Isinst (f t) | Unbox t -> Unbox (f t)
  | Unbox_any t -> Unbox_any (f t) | Box t -> Box (f t)
  | Ldfld t -> Ldfld (f t) | Ldflda t -> Ldflda (f t) | Stfld t -> Stfld (f t)
  | Ldsfld t -> Ldsfld (f t) | Ldsflda t -> Ldsflda (f t) | Stsfld t -> Stsfld (f t)
  | Newarr t -> Newarr (f t) | Ldelema t -> Ldelema (f t)
  | Ldelem_any t -> Ldelem_any (f t) | Stelem_any t -> Stelem_any (f t)
  | Refanyval t -> Refanyval (f t) | Mkrefany t -> Mkrefany (f t)
  | Ldtoken t -> Ldtoken (f t) | Ldftn t -> Ldftn (f t) | Ldvirtftn t -> Ldvirtftn (f t)
  | Initobj t -> Initobj (f t) | Sizeof t -> Sizeof (f t) | Constrained t -> Constrained (f t)
  | op -> op

(* Partition III's stack transitions; [call tok] is a method's
 * (arguments with `this`, has it a result) *)
let stack_effect (call : int -> int * bool) (returns : bool) (op : op) : int * int =
  match op with
  | Nop | Break | Br _ | Leave _ | Endfinally | Prefix _ | Constrained _ -> (0, 0)
  | Ldarg _ | Ldarga _ | Ldloc _ | Ldloca _ | Ldnull | Ldc_i4 _ | Ldc_i8 _ | Ldc_r _
  | Ldstr _ | Ldsfld _ | Ldsflda _ | Ldtoken _ | Ldftn _ | Sizeof _ | Arglist -> (0, 1)
  | Starg _ | Stloc _ | Pop | Brfalse _ | Brtrue _ | Switch _ | Stsfld _ | Throw
  | Initobj _ | Endfilter -> (1, 0)
  | Dup -> (1, 2)
  | Call t | Callvirt t | Jmp t -> let n, r = call t in (n, if r then 1 else 0)
  | Calli _ -> (1, 0)
  | Newobj t -> let n, _ = call t in (n - 1, 1)
  | Ret -> ((if returns then 1 else 0), 0)
  | Bcmp _ | Stind _ | Stfld _ | Stobj _ | Cpobj _ -> (2, 0)
  | Binop _ | Ceq | Cgt _ | Clt _ | Ldelem _ | Ldelem_any _ | Ldelema _ -> (2, 1)
  | Stelem _ | Stelem_any _ | Cpblk | Initblk -> (3, 0)
  | Ldind _ | Neg | Not | Conv _ | Conv_r_un | Ldobj _ | Castclass _ | Isinst _
  | Unbox _ | Unbox_any _ | Box _ | Ldfld _ | Ldflda _ | Newarr _ | Ldlen
  | Refanyval _ | Mkrefany _ | Refanytype | Ckfinite | Ldvirtftn _ | Localloc -> (1, 1)
  | Rethrow -> (0, 0)
languages/dotnet/assembly/Il.mli
5077
(* The instructions: CIL's opcodes as a table (a byte or two, a name,
 * an operand), a method's IL decoded to them, and their inverse, an
 * instruction's bytes (for Writer). ECMA-335, Partition III.
 *
 * The machine is a stack machine whose instructions are typed by what
 * is on the stack, not by their name: `add` adds two int32, two int64
 * or two floats, where the JVM has iadd, ladd, fadd, dadd. So the IL is
 * small (226 opcodes, the survey's programs use 86), and a pass must
 * know each slot's type before it can compile a method (the verifier,
 * the JIT); the interpreter (Machine) knows it by the tag of each value.
 *
 *     static int Rec(int n)              IL_0000: ldarg.0
 *     {                                  IL_0001: ldc.i4.2
 *       if (n < 2) return n;             IL_0002: bge.s IL_0006
 *       return Rec(n - 1) + Rec(n - 2);  IL_0004: ldarg.0
 *     }                                  IL_0005: ret
 *                                        IL_0006: ldarg.0
 *                                        IL_0007: ldc.i4.1
 *                                        IL_0008: sub
 *                                        IL_0009: call int32 Fib::Rec(int32)
 *                                        IL_000e: ldarg.0
 *                                        ...
 *
 * Many opcodes are one instruction in several sizes: ldarg.0 (1 byte),
 * ldarg.s 4 (2), ldarg 300 (4); br.s and br. Decoded, they are one
 * constructor of [op] (Ldarg 0): the machine has one case where the
 * file has three, and the name is kept beside for the listing.
 * A branch's target is the instruction's index in the method's array
 * once decoded, not a byte offset.
 *
 * others:
 * The JVM's bytecode (1995) is CIL's model: a stack, locals by number,
 * a method's code in its class's file. Its opcodes say their types
 * (iload, aload, fadd) because Java's first implementation was an
 * interpreter that would not keep tags; CIL (2000) was always meant to
 * be compiled, so its opcodes leave the types to be inferred. *)

(* a load's, a store's, a conversion's type *)
type kind = K_i1 | K_u1 | K_i2 | K_u2 | K_i4 | K_u4 | K_i8 | K_u8
          | K_i | K_u | K_r4 | K_r8 | K_ref

type binop = Add | Sub | Mul | Div | Div_un | Rem | Rem_un
           | And | Or | Xor | Shl | Shr | Shr_un
           | Add_ovf | Add_ovf_un | Mul_ovf | Mul_ovf_un | Sub_ovf | Sub_ovf_un

(* a conditional branch's comparison, with .un: unsigned, or unordered
 * for floats *)
type cmp = Eq | Ne | Ge | Gt | Le | Lt

type op =
  | Nop
  | Break
  | Ldarg of int | Ldarga of int | Starg of int
  | Ldloc of int | Ldloca of int | Stloc of int
  | Ldnull
  | Ldc_i4 of int32 | Ldc_i8 of int64 | Ldc_r of float
  | Dup | Pop
  | Jmp of int | Call of int | Calli of int | Callvirt of int
  | Ret
  | Br of int
  | Brfalse of int | Brtrue of int
  | Bcmp of cmp * bool * int        (* bool: .un *)
  | Switch of int array
  | Ldind of kind | Stind of kind
  | Binop of binop
  | Neg | Not
  | Conv of kind * bool * bool       (* .ovf, .un *)
  | Conv_r_un
  | Cpobj of int | Ldobj of int | Stobj of int
  | Ldstr of int
  | Newobj of int
  | Castclass of int | Isinst of int
  | Unbox of int | Unbox_any of int | Box of int
  | Throw | Rethrow
  | Ldfld of int | Ldflda of int | Stfld of int
  | Ldsfld of int | Ldsflda of int | Stsfld of int
  | Newarr of int | Ldlen
  | Ldelema of int
  | Ldelem of kind | Ldelem_any of int
  | Stelem of kind | Stelem_any of int
  | Refanyval of int | Mkrefany of int | Refanytype
  | Ckfinite
  | Ldtoken of int
  | Endfinally
  | Leave of int
  | Ceq | Cgt of bool | Clt of bool
  | Ldftn of int | Ldvirtftn of int
  | Arglist | Localloc | Endfilter
  | Initobj of int
  | Cpblk | Initblk
  | Sizeof of int
  (* the prefixes, an instruction of their own here *)
  | Constrained of int
  | Prefix of string                (* tail., volatile., readonly., unaligned., no. *)

type instr = {
  at : int;                         (* its offset in the method's IL *)
  name : string;                    (* as written: ldarg.0, br.s *)
  op : op;
}

exception Bad_il of string

(* a method's IL, its branches' targets as indexes in the array *)
val decode : string -> instr array
(* the index of the instruction at an offset (Not_found if none: an
 * exception clause's offsets are turned with it) *)
val index : instr array -> int -> int

(* the opcodes as they are written, for the listing and the writer:
 * (its bytes, 1 or 2, as a number: 0xFE01 for ceq, its name) *)
val opcodes : (int * string) list

(* an instruction's tokens, renumbered (the writer's, once its rows
 * are laid out) *)
val map_tokens : (int -> int) -> op -> op

(* what an instruction takes from the stack and leaves on it; a call's,
 * a ret's from the signature given *)
val stack_effect : (int -> int * bool) -> bool -> op -> int * int

(* an instruction's bytes, its branches' targets as offsets: the
 * shortest form (ldarg.0, ldc.i4.s); a branch in its long form, as the
 * writer cannot know the distance before it has laid the code out *)
val encode : Buffer.t -> op -> unit
