(* The JIT's code, as text (plan_dotnet.md, stage 8): a method's IL
 * turned into the machine's instructions, arm's, written as mini-asm
 * reads them (Plan 9's 5a), so that mini-asm assembles it and mini-ld
 * links it. `mini-dotnet -jit -S file.dll` prints it. Its input is
 * the verifier's: at each instruction the stack's depth and each
 * slot's type are known before the method runs, so each slot is a
 * place in the frame, and an instruction a few of the machine's:
 *
 *     static int Rec(int n)              TEXT  Fib_Rec(SB), 0, $16
 *                                        MOVW  R0, a0+0(FP)
 *       IL_0000: ldarg.0         []      MOVW  a0+0(FP), R1
 *                                        MOVW  R1, s0-4(SP)
 *       IL_0001: ldc.i4.2        [i4]    MOVW  $2, R1
 *                                        MOVW  R1, s1-8(SP)
 *       IL_0002: bge.s IL_0006   [i4 i4] MOVW  s0-4(SP), R1
 *                                        MOVW  s1-8(SP), R2
 *                                        CMP   R2, R1
 *                                        BGE   Fib_Rec_5
 *       ...
 *
 * A template JIT (decision 12): each instruction a fixed sequence,
 * the stack's slots in memory, no register kept between two
 * instructions. What it shows is what the types make possible: `add`
 * of two int32 is one ADD, where the interpreter (Machine) looks at
 * two tags, allocates a box, and goes round its loop. A cache of the
 * stack's top in registers would come after, measured.
 *
 * {b Its first methods} are those of int32s only: static, their
 * parameters, locals, result and every stack slot an int32 (a bool, a
 * char), their calls to such methods of the same assembly, no
 * exception clause. Such a method is a function of C's for 5c: its
 * first argument in R0, the others at 4(i+1) on the caller's stack,
 * its result in R0, its frame mini-ld's (TEXT's $size). So a C
 * program calls it, and the tests do: Fib's Rec and Loop, linked with
 * a C program by mini-ld and run under mini-5i, print what the
 * interpreter prints (tests/jit). A division by zero calls
 * jit_divide_by_zero, the runtime's (the test's C).
 *
 * {b Arm64's} (-m 7) are the same templates in 7c's convention: W
 * instructions on an int32 (ADDW...), a slot of 8 bytes, and a branch
 * over a move where arm has a conditional one (CSET mini-ld does not
 * encode). That code is the one mini-dotnet runs (Jit_run, `-jit`),
 * each method with an entry mini-ml calls as a closure ([program]).
 *
 * {b With references} (arm64's, in mini-dotnet: the assembly loaded,
 * its fields laid out by Types), instance methods too, and methods of
 * strings, objects, arrays: a reference, the interpreter's value, has
 * its slot on mini-ml's value stack (R26), where its collector finds
 * it and moves it, an int32 its slot on the machine's:
 *
 *     static int Sum(Node l)         l: a word of the value stack
 *       ldarg.0; ldfld Node::Value   MOV v(R26), R1; CMP $1, R1 (null?)
 *                                    MOV 0(R1), R1      Obj's store
 *                                    MOV 8(R1), R1      its bytes
 *                                    MOVW 0(R1), R1     the field
 *       callvirt Shape::Area()       MOV $7, R1 (call-out 3); MOV v, R2
 *                                    BL jit_out1(SB)    Machine.exec
 *
 * A field, an array's element and length are read and written by the
 * code (a reference stored but by a call-out: the collector's write
 * barrier); the rest, a call into the library, to a virtual method or
 * a constructor, new, ldstr, a static field, a cast, a box, throw, is
 * a call-out: an ML function called with the operands (an int32
 * tagged), which runs that instruction in the interpreter
 * (Machine.exec) and returns what it pushes. A call to a static method
 * compiled is a BL. A null and an index out of range call the
 * runtime's, which throw.
 *
 * {b Addresses}: a local's or an argument's (ldloca, ldarga: ref x,
 * out x, an int's x.ToString()) is nothing at run time, the local
 * being the code's and not the interpreter's: it is followed from
 * where it is pushed to the call-out that takes it, which is given the
 * local's value (the interpreter makes it a cell, Ptr (Slot ...)) and
 * gives back the new one, which the code puts in the local. A field's,
 * an element's (ldflda, ldelema) and a ref parameter are the
 * interpreter's Ptr, a reference to the code, read and written by
 * call-outs (ldind, stind). A delegate's method (ldftn) is followed
 * the same way to its newobj, the interpreter making it there.
 *
 * {b Generics}: a method of a generic class, or a generic method, is
 * compiled for each instance at the instance's first call
 * (instance_code), its type arguments its own: a T an int32 in
 * Stack<int>'s code, a reference in Stack<string>'s, the fields where
 * that instance's class has them; its calls all call-outs, run in its
 * context (T[]'s ldelem.any, constrained. callvirt, ldobj, stobj too).
 * So each instance has its code, as .NET's for value types; .NET shares
 * one code between the instances of references, a dictionary of the
 * types beside it.
 *
 * {b try, catch, finally}: a try's handler is a record on ML's own
 * chain of handlers, as ML's try pushes (Gen's ml_try: the stack
 * pointer, the value stack's top, where a raise comes back, the
 * record before; ml_handler's address the runtime's), pushed at the
 * try's start by jit_try, which returns 0, and where a raise returns
 * again with the exception; and a frame of the method's on
 * Frame.frames meanwhile, so that the first pass sees the try's
 * clauses. The handler asks the interpreter (a call-out: Machine.run's
 * rule) whether its catch takes the exception, else raises it again;
 * a finally keeps it, runs, and at its endfinally raises it again. A
 * leave pops the records and frames of the trys it leaves, the inner
 * first, each finally run on the way and coming back (its continuation
 * a number in the frame).
 *
 *     try {                    MOV $..., R1; BL jit_out0   (its frame)
 *                              MOV $record, R0; BL jit_try
 *                              CMP $0, R0; BNE handler
 *       ...                    the body's code
 *     } catch (E e) {          (handler: the exception to a call-out,
 *                               caught: on the stack, else raised)
 *
 * {b Structs}: a struct's value is the interpreter's Vt, a reference
 * to the code (its store where Obj has it: a field read the same),
 * copied where the IL copies it, a load (ldloc, ldarg, dup: a
 * call-out, Value.copy), so that two slots never share a store; a
 * struct local its zeros at the start (.locals init), as a constructor
 * called on its address writes in it; a field of a struct through its
 * address (its own methods' this), a struct field, ldtoken: call-outs.
 *
 * {b int64s} on arm64 (kind L, [longs]): the code's own, a word in a
 * register or a slot of the machine's stack, as an int32 is, their
 * templates X instructions (ADD where an int32's is ADDW, SDIV, a
 * shift's count its 6 bits); a field or an element of 8 bytes read
 * and written in place, conv.i8 a sign extension (MOVW), conv.u8 a
 * zero one (MOVWU). An int64 is ML's int (mini-ml -dotnet), so this is
 * what takes ML's code: fib's own method, interpreted before. One
 * crossing to ML is a value of its: given to a call-out, its high and
 * low 32 bits, tagged (two words, two registers); from ML, its Int64
 * block, read at 0 at once; an entry's result made a block by
 * jit_box, of its halves (as arm's int32 past 31 bits).
 *
 *     ldarg.0; ldc.i8 1; sub        MOV a0+0(FP), R1; MOV $1, R2
 *                                   SUB R2, R1
 *
 * {b doubles}, and int64s on arm (a pair of registers there, later):
 * the interpreter's R8 and I8, references to the code, their
 * arithmetic, conversions and comparisons (and every checked
 * operation) call-outs, a branch on them the interpreter's test, then
 * the code's branch: compiled, not fast.
 *
 * What it refuses is said with the reason: an address at a jump or
 * given to the code itself, an instruction without its template yet,
 * a filter or a fault clause; and in -S's text a generic method or
 * class (an instance's code is only made at run time).
 *
 * {b A method is compiled at its first call} (stubs, method_code): it
 * is called through its cell, a word holding its code's address, at
 * first its stub's, which compiles it, sets the cell, and calls it;
 * then the code itself:
 *
 *     caller: MOV $cell, R16; MOV 0(R16), R16; BL (R16)
 *               cell --> Rec_stub: compile Rec (jit_compile), the cell
 *                                  now Rec's code; call it; return
 *               cell --> Rec       (each call after)
 *
 * {b On arm} (mini-dotnet for Plan 9: mini-9pi, mini-5i), the same
 * code with references, 5c's names and words of 4 bytes, the value
 * stack's top R10; and two things arm64 has not to do. An int's 31
 * bits there do not hold an int32: one crosses to ML (an argument of
 * a call-out, an entry's result) tagged when it fits, else boxed
 * (jit_box: an Int32's block), and one from ML is either (TST $1).
 * The Pi 1's ARMv6 has no division: the runtime's unsigned one
 * (jit_udiv), the signs in the templates.
 *
 * others:
 * .NET's first JIT (2002) compiled a method at its first call through
 * a stub, as here; RyuJIT (2015) builds a tree of the IL, then SSA,
 * and allocates registers. Mono's first JIT was a tree-matching
 * code generator (monoburg); its later one, mini, SSA as RyuJIT's.
 * The JVM's HotSpot interprets first and compiles a method once it is
 * called often (C1, then C2): the tiers .NET Core took in 3.0.
 *
 * history:
 * L. Peter Deutsch and Allan Schiffman's Smalltalk-80 (POPL 1984):
 * the first JIT, a method translated to the machine's code at its
 * first call and cached, the bytecode kept; and the inline cache, a
 * send's last class and method remembered at the call site.
 * Self (Craig Chambers, David Ungar, Urs Hölzle, Stanford, 1989-1995):
 * code customized to the receiver's class, polymorphic inline caches
 * (1991), adaptive optimization (a method recompiled once hot, by
 * what its caches saw), deoptimization back to the interpreter's
 * frames. Its people made Strongtalk, which Sun bought (1997) to make
 * HotSpot (1999).
 * Inferno's Dis (Phil Winterbottom, Rob Pike, 1997, "The Design of
 * the Inferno Virtual Machine"): the other choice of machine, memory
 * to memory, three operands (add a, b, c), not a stack; so close to
 * the processor's that its JIT, at a module's load, is a translation
 * an instruction at a time, no stack to model. IL's stack, as the
 * JVM's, is smaller to write and to verify; this JIT models it at
 * compile time (a slot per depth), which Dis needs not.
 * V8 (Lars Bak, of Self, Strongtalk and HotSpot; Google, 2008):
 * JavaScript compiled at first, no interpreter (full-codegen), the
 * hidden classes and inline caches of Self; Crankshaft (2010) the
 * optimizing tier, then Ignition, an interpreter again, and TurboFan
 * (2016): tiers as HotSpot's.
 * Tracing JITs, the other road: not a method compiled but a loop's
 * path as it runs, HP's Dynamo (2000) on machine code, TraceMonkey
 * (Andreas Gal, Michael Franz, 2009) for JavaScript, LuaJIT 2 (Mike
 * Pall, 2009) the best known.
 * Here: Deutsch and Schiffman's scheme (a method at its first call,
 * templates, no optimizer) with HotSpot's tiers, without Self's
 * caches: IL's calls are typed, a virtual one found by its class's
 * slot (Types), no guess to cache. *)

(* why a method is not compiled *)
exception Refused of string

(* arm's (5c's), or arm64's (7c's: the same templates, W instructions
 * on the low 32 bits, a slot of 8 bytes, no conditional move) *)
type mach = Arm | Arm64

(* a slot's kind: an int32 (a native int) on the machine's stack, a
 * reference (the interpreter's value) on mini-ml's, an int64 (arm64,
 * with references) on the machine's, 64 bits: crossing to ML as its
 * block (Int64's), or as two tagged halves, its high and low 32 bits *)
type kind = I | R | L

(* a call-out: an instruction of a method (its row, its index) the
 * interpreter runs for the code (Machine.exec), its operands' kinds,
 * the bottom first, the form of each (Word: its value; Addr: a local's
 * address, its value given, to be put in a cell, and given back: the
 * call-out's answer then an array, the result, then their new values;
 * Made: nothing given, the value the instruction at that index makes,
 * ldftn's Fn), and its result's *)
type form = Word | Addr | Made of int
(* what a call-out does: an instruction run; for a try (its clause's
 * index), its frame pushed for the first pass and popped, the
 * exception caught or let go, raised again, rethrown; a struct copied
 * (loaded), a local's zeros (a struct's, an int64's, a double's); a
 * branch's test of int64s or doubles (1 or 0) *)
type op = Run | Enter of int | Leave_try | Catch of int | Reraise | Rethrow | Copy | Init of int
  | Test of Il.cmp * bool | Truthy
type site = { srow : int; sat : int; sargs : kind list; sform : form list; sret : kind option; sop : op }

(* the assembly's methods that are compiled, as mini-asm's text; how
 * many; the others' rows and why not. With the assembly loaded (and
 * arm64's), references too, the call-outs by their stubs' names *)
val assembly : mach -> Image.t -> Value.image option -> string * int * (int * string) list

(* the most operands of a call-out *)
val outs : int

(* In mini-dotnet (Jit_run), on arm64, with references: an assembly's
 * methods compiled each at its first call (decision 12). Each has a
 * cell, a word at an address that holds its code's address, its
 * stub's until then, and is called through it. *)

(* the assembly's methods the JIT takes, verified, their symbols *)
type prepared
val prepare : mach -> Value.image -> prepared
val rows : prepared -> int list
(* those it does not take, and why *)
val refused : prepared -> (int * string) list
val symbol_of : prepared -> int -> string

(* the runtime's functions, by their static closures' addresses: in
 * each piece of code (each its own copy). [throws] by name,
 * jit_divide_by_zero, jit_null, jit_range, of unit, which raise; [out]
 * the call-outs', by their operands (0 to outs), each taking the
 * call-out's number then the operands; [compile] the compiler's, of a
 * method's number; on arm [box], of an int32's two halves, tagged,
 * which returns its Int32 (an int32 past 31 bits crosses so) *)
val runtime : mach:mach -> throws:(string * int) list -> out:int array -> compile:int -> box:int ->
  handler:int -> string

(* the code at the start: for each method an entry, `Sym_entry`, which
 * mini-ml calls as a closure of one argument, an array of the
 * arguments (an int32 a tagged int), and which returns the result
 * likewise; and its stub, `Sym_stub`, which calls jit_compile with the
 * method's [number], then the method through its [cell]. The text, the
 * entries' symbols, the stubs' *)
val stubs : prepared -> cell:(int -> int) -> number:(int -> int) -> runtime:string ->
  string * (int * string) list * (int * string) list

(* jit_sp, a closure's code of unit returning the stack pointer in
 * words (a limit of the stack's put below it) *)
val sp_code : mach -> string

(* a method's code, at its first call: its text (`Sym`, then the
 * runtime's), its call-outs numbered from [base]; the machine's stack
 * pointer checked against [limit] (in words: jit_overflow below it) *)
val method_code : prepared -> int -> cell:(int -> int) -> base:int -> limit:int -> handler:int -> runtime:string ->
  string * site list

(* an instance of a generic method (of a generic class, or generic
 * itself), its type arguments those of the Value.meth: compiled alone,
 * at its own first call, each instance its code (a T an int32 in one,
 * a reference in another; its fields where the instance has them).
 * Its text (the method, its entry calling it directly, the runtime's),
 * the entry's symbol, its call-outs from [base]; None if refused *)
val instance_code : mach -> Value.meth -> base:int -> limit:int -> handler:int -> runtime:string ->
  (string * string * site list) option

(* See Jit_run.mli *)

open Value

let compiled = ref 0

(* the machine: arm64's on 64 bits, arm's on 32 (the Pi 1's) *)
let mach = if Sys.word_size = 64 then Jit.Arm64 else Jit.Arm

(* the text read and encoded at 0: its bytes, and each TEXT's offset *)
let encode_arm (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (text : string) : string * (string -> int) =
  let obj = Parser_asm.parse caps Asm.Arm (Fpath.v "jit.s") text in
  let (t : Arm.op Program.t) = Link.create Asm.Arm ~text_start:0 in
  Link.load_objects t ~decode:Arm.decode [ obj ];
  Arm.prepare t;
  Link.resolve t;
  Link.layout_data t;
  Link.drop_nops t;
  Arm.rewrite t;
  Arm.layout t;
  (Bytes.to_string (Arm.encode t), fun name -> (Hashtbl.find t.syms (name, 0)).value)

let encode (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (text : string) : string * (string -> int) =
  if mach = Jit.Arm then encode_arm caps text else
  let obj = Parser_asm.parse caps Asm.Arm64 (Fpath.v "jit.s") text in
  let (t : Arm64.op Program.t) = Link.create Asm.Arm64 ~text_start:0 in
  Link.load_objects t ~decode:Arm64.decode [ obj ];
  Arm64.prepare t;
  Link.resolve t;
  Link.layout_data t;
  Link.drop_nops t;
  Arm64.rewrite t;
  Arm64.layout t;
  (Bytes.to_string (Arm64.encode t), fun name -> (Hashtbl.find t.syms (name, 0)).value)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* The runtime's functions the code calls: static closures *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

let divide_by_zero () : unit = Frame.throw_new "System.DivideByZeroException" "Attempted to divide by zero."
let null_reference () : unit = Frame.null_ref ()
let out_of_range () : unit = Frame.out_of_range ()
let stack_overflow () : unit = raise Frame.Stack_overflow

(* the machine's stack's limit for the code, in words (0: not known
 * yet): 4 MB below where the first program was made (Linux's 8), 512 KB
 * on 32 bits (mini-5i's Plan 9 stack is 1 MB, mini-9pi's 8) *)
let limit = ref 0

(* the call-outs, by their numbers: each its operands to its result *)
let table : (Obj.t array -> Obj.t) array ref = ref [||]

let out0 (k : int) : Obj.t = (!table).(k) [||]
let out1 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) : Obj.t = (!table).(k) [| a |]
let out2 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) (b : Obj.t) : Obj.t = (!table).(k) [| a; b |]
let out3 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) (b : Obj.t) (c : Obj.t) : Obj.t = (!table).(k) [| a; b; c |]
let out4 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) (b : Obj.t) (c : Obj.t) (d : Obj.t) : Obj.t = (!table).(k) [| a; b; c; d |]
let out5 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) (b : Obj.t) (c : Obj.t) (d : Obj.t) (e : Obj.t) : Obj.t =
  (!table).(k) [| a; b; c; d; e |]
let out6 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) (b : Obj.t) (c : Obj.t) (d : Obj.t) (e : Obj.t) (f : Obj.t) : Obj.t =
  (!table).(k) [| a; b; c; d; e; f |]
let out7 (k : int) (a : Obj.t) (b : Obj.t) (c : Obj.t) (d : Obj.t) (e : Obj.t) (f : Obj.t) (g : Obj.t) : Obj.t =
  (!table).(k) [| a; b; c; d; e; f; g |]

(* an int32 past an int's 31 bits (arm), from its halves; on arm64 an
 * int64 (L) of its 32-bit halves *)
let box (hi : int) (lo : int) : Obj.t =
  if mach = Jit.Arm64 then Obj.repr (Int64.logor (Int64.shift_left (Int64.of_int hi) 32) (Int64.of_int lo))
  else Obj.repr (Int32.logor (Int32.shift_left (Int32.of_int hi) 16) (Int32.of_int lo))

(* a value of the code's, of its kind, as the interpreter's, and back *)
(* (an int32 a tagged int, or on arm past 31 bits its Int32 block) *)
let of_word (k : Jit.kind) (x : Obj.t) : value =
  match k with
  | Jit.I -> if Obj.is_int x then I4 (Int32.of_int (Obj.obj x : int)) else I4 (Obj.obj x : int32)
  | Jit.R -> (Obj.obj x : value)
  (* (an int64: its block, or its halves joined, of_words) *)
  | Jit.L -> if Obj.is_int x then I8 (Int64.of_int (Obj.obj x : int)) else I8 (Obj.obj x : int64)

(* a call-out's words, its operands: an int64's two, its halves *)
let of_words (kinds : Jit.kind array) (a : Obj.t array) : Obj.t array =
  let i = ref 0 in
  Array.map (fun (k : Jit.kind) ->
      let x = a.(!i) in
      incr i;
      if k = Jit.L then begin
        let lo = a.(!i) in
        incr i;
        box (Obj.obj x : int) (Obj.obj lo : int)
      end else x) kinds

let to_word (k : Jit.kind) (v : value) : Obj.t =
  match k, v with
  | Jit.I, I4 n -> let i = Int32.to_int n in if Int32.of_int i = n then Obj.repr i else Obj.repr n
  | Jit.I, _ -> Frame.error "the JIT's code: an int32 expected"
  | Jit.R, v -> Obj.repr v
  (* (an int64 to the code: its block, which it reads at 0) *)
  | Jit.L, I8 n -> Obj.repr n
  | Jit.L, _ -> Frame.error "the JIT's code: an int64 expected"

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* An assembly's code *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

(* the methods waiting for their first call, by their numbers: each
 * compiled when its stub calls compile *)
let pending : (unit -> unit) array ref = ref [||]

let compile (k : int) : unit = (!pending).(k) ()

(* an instruction run by the interpreter for the code *)
let run_site (m : meth) (code : code) (s : Jit.site) : Obj.t array -> Obj.t =
  let kinds = Array.of_list s.sargs and form = Array.of_list s.sform in
  let run = Machine.call_out m code s.sat in
  let result v = match s.sret with Some k -> to_word k v | None -> Obj.repr () in
  let operand j x = match form.(j) with
    | Jit.Made k -> Machine.exec m code k [||]
    | _ -> of_word kinds.(j) x in
  if not (List.mem Jit.Addr s.sform) then
    fun (a : Obj.t array) -> result (run (Array.mapi operand (of_words kinds a)))
  else
    (* a local's address: an interpreter's cell with its value, its
     * new value given back after the result *)
    fun (a : Obj.t array) ->
      let a = of_words kinds a in
      let cells = Array.map (fun x -> [| x |]) (Array.mapi operand a) in
      let v = run (Array.mapi (fun j (c : value array) -> if form.(j) = Jit.Addr then Ptr (Slot (c, 0)) else c.(0)) cells) in
      let back = List.filter (fun j -> form.(j) = Jit.Addr) (List.init (Array.length a) (fun j -> j)) in
      Obj.repr (Array.of_list (result v :: List.map (fun j -> to_word kinds.(j) cells.(j).(0)) back))

(* the call-outs of a method's code: an instruction run by the
 * interpreter in the method's code, or its trys' *)
let call_outs (codes : (int, meth * code) Hashtbl.t) (sites : Jit.site list) : unit =
  let calls = List.map (fun (s : Jit.site) ->
      let m, code = Hashtbl.find codes s.srow in
      match s.sop with
      | Jit.Run -> run_site m code s
      | Jit.Enter c ->
          (* the try's frame for the first pass (Frame.handled): the
           * method's clauses, at the try's start *)
          let at = code.clauses.(c).tstart in
          fun (_ : Obj.t array) ->
            let (f : Frame.frame) = { meth = m; code; args = [||]; locals = [||]; stack = [||]; sp = 0;
                                      pc = at; at; caught = None } in
            Frame.frames := f :: !Frame.frames;
            Obj.repr ()
      | Jit.Leave_try -> fun _ -> Frame.frames := List.tl !Frame.frames; Obj.repr ()
      | Jit.Catch c ->
          (* as Machine.run: a catch's class, or the first pass's choice;
           * a finally's every .NET exception (not the machine's own:
           * an unhandled one runs no finally) *)
          let cl = code.clauses.(c) in
          fun (a : Obj.t array) ->
            let f = List.hd !Frame.frames in
            Frame.frames := List.tl !Frame.frames;
            (match (Obj.obj a.(0) : exn), cl.ckind, cl.catch with
             | Thrown st, 0, Some k ->
                 let mine = match !Frame.chosen with Some (g, j) -> g == f && j = c | None -> false in
                 if subclass st.cls k || mine then Obj.repr (Obj st) else raise (Thrown st)
             | Thrown _, 2, _ -> a.(0)
             | e, _, _ -> raise e)
      | Jit.Reraise -> fun (a : Obj.t array) -> raise (Obj.obj a.(0) : exn)
      | Jit.Copy ->
          fun (a : Obj.t array) -> (match (Obj.obj a.(0) : value) with
            | Vt st -> Obj.repr (Vt (copy st))
            | _ -> a.(0))
      | Jit.Init l -> let t = code.locals.(l) in fun _ -> Obj.repr (zero t)
      | Jit.Test (c, un) ->
          fun (a : Obj.t array) -> Obj.repr (if Arith.test c un (Obj.obj a.(0)) (Obj.obj a.(1)) then 1 else 0)
      | Jit.Truthy -> fun (a : Obj.t array) -> Obj.repr (if Arith.truthy (Obj.obj a.(0)) then 1 else 0)
      | Jit.Rethrow ->
          fun (a : Obj.t array) -> match (Obj.obj a.(0) : value) with
            | Obj st -> Frame.throw st
            | _ -> Frame.error "rethrow of what is not an exception") sites in
  table := Array.append !table (Array.of_list calls)


(* the runtime's text, in each piece of code *)
let runtime () : string =
  let addr f = Code_memory.address (Obj.repr f) in
  Jit.runtime ~mach ~box:(addr box) ~handler:(Code_memory.handler ())
    ~throws:[ ("jit_divide_by_zero", addr divide_by_zero); ("jit_null", addr null_reference);
              ("jit_range", addr out_of_range); ("jit_overflow", addr stack_overflow) ]
    ~out:[| addr out0; addr out1; addr out2; addr out3; addr out4; addr out5; addr out6; addr out7 |]
    ~compile:(addr compile)

(* the stack's limit, once: below the stack pointer of now *)
let ensure_limit (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) : unit =
  if !limit = 0 then begin
    let code, offset = encode caps (Jit.sp_code mach) in
    let (sp : unit -> int) = Obj.obj (Code_memory.closure (Code_memory.load code + offset "jit_sp")) in
    limit := sp () - (if Sys.word_size = 64 then 4 * 1024 * 1024 else 512 * 1024) / 4
  end

(* a method's function for the interpreter: its arguments as words
 * (`this` first), its entry at [addr] called, its result back *)
let native (m : meth) (addr : int) : value array -> value =
  (* (a struct a reference to the code, its Vt; an enum an int32) *)
  let kind t = match t with
    | T_value c when c.kind = Struct -> Jit.R
    | T_i8 | T_u8 when mach = Jit.Arm64 -> Jit.L
    | T_i8 | T_u8 | T_r4 | T_r8 -> Jit.R
    | t -> if is_ref t then Jit.R else Jit.I in
  let ks = Array.of_list ((if m.static then [] else [ Jit.R ]) @ List.map kind m.params) in
  let ret = kind m.ret in
  let (f : Obj.t array -> Obj.t) = Obj.obj (Code_memory.closure addr) in
  fun (args : value array) ->
    let r = f (Array.mapi (fun j v -> to_word ks.(j) v) args) in
    if m.ret = T_void then Null else of_word ret r

(* each assembly's methods, by its name: a row's entry's address (its
 * function made by jit, of the method it is given, when the method is
 * hot: looking up all the methods at the start took 331 ms of a 437 ms
 * start, fib's); and the methods' IL decoded, by their rows, kept as
 * each is made Native (jit: its IL the interpreter's, decoded), for its
 * call-outs when it is compiled *)
let programs : (string, (int, int) Hashtbl.t * (int, meth * code) Hashtbl.t) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 4

let program (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (im : image) : (int, int) Hashtbl.t * (int, meth * code) Hashtbl.t =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt programs im.aname with
  | Some p -> p
  | None ->
      let p = Hashtbl.create 16 in
      let codes = Hashtbl.create 16 in
      Hashtbl.replace programs im.aname (p, codes);
      let prep = Jit.prepare mach im in
      let rows = Jit.rows prep in
      let name row = Listing.token_name im.img (Metadata.token Metadata.t_method_def row) in
      Logs.info (fun m -> m "JIT: %s: %d methods taken, %d not" im.aname (List.length rows) (List.length (Jit.refused prep)));
      List.iter (fun (row, why) -> Logs.debug (fun m -> m "JIT: not compiled: %s: %s" (name row) why)) (Jit.refused prep);
      if rows <> [] then begin
        let runtime = runtime () in
        ensure_limit caps;
        let index = Hashtbl.create 16 in
        List.iteri (fun i row -> Hashtbl.replace index row i) rows;
        let cells, set = Code_memory.cells (Array.make (List.length rows) 0) in
        let cell row = cells + (Sys.word_size / 8) * Hashtbl.find index row in
        let k0 = Array.length !pending in
        let text, entries, stubs = Jit.stubs prep ~cell ~number:(fun row -> k0 + Hashtbl.find index row) ~runtime in
        let code, offset = encode caps text in
        let base = Code_memory.load code in
        List.iter (fun (row, sym) -> set (Hashtbl.find index row) (base + offset sym)) stubs;
        (* (each method's IL decoded when it is compiled, not all of them
         * now: a method hot is in codes already, its IL kept by jit before
         * its body was Native; one compiled first by a call of the code,
         * its cell's stub, is decoded then, its body still the image's) *)
        pending := Array.append !pending (Array.of_list (List.map (fun row () ->
            if not (Hashtbl.mem codes row) then begin
              let m = Types.meth_of_def im row in
              Hashtbl.replace codes row (m, Types.code m)
            end;
            let text, sites = Jit.method_code prep row ~cell ~base:(Array.length !table) ~limit:!limit
                ~handler:(Code_memory.handler ()) ~runtime in
            let code, offset = encode caps text in
            let at = Code_memory.load code in
            Logs.info (fun m -> m "JIT: compiled %s (%d bytes, %d call-outs)" (name row) (String.length code) (List.length sites));
            Logs.debug (fun m -> m "JIT: %s's code at 0x%x" (name row) at);
            call_outs codes sites;
            incr compiled;
            set (Hashtbl.find index row) (at + offset (Jit.symbol_of prep row))) rows));
        (* (each method's body the interpreter's until it is hot:
         * Machine's tiers; then its entry, jit's) *)
        List.iter (fun (row, sym) -> Hashtbl.replace p row (base + offset sym)) entries
      end;
      (p, codes)

(* an instance of a generic method, compiled at its first call
 * (Jit.instance_code), its code its own *)
let instance (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (m : meth) (row : int) : (value array -> value) option =
  ensure_limit caps;
  let code = Types.code m in
  let name = m.mcls.name ^ "::" ^ m.mname in
  match Jit.instance_code mach m ~base:(Array.length !table) ~limit:!limit ~handler:(Code_memory.handler ())
          ~runtime:(runtime ()) with
  | None -> Logs.debug (fun f -> f "JIT: instance not compiled: %s" name); None
  | Some (text, entry, sites) ->
      let bytes, offset = encode caps text in
      let at = Code_memory.load bytes in
      Logs.info (fun f -> f "JIT: compiled the instance %s (%d bytes, %d call-outs)" name (String.length bytes) (List.length sites));
      let codes = Hashtbl.create 1 in
      Hashtbl.replace codes row (m, code);
      call_outs codes sites;
      incr compiled;
      Some (native m (at + offset entry))

let jit (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (m : meth) : (value array -> value) option =
  match m.def with
  | Some (im, row) when Code_memory.available ->
      if m.mcls.args <> [||] || m.margs <> [||] then instance caps m row
      else begin
        let p, codes = program caps im in
        match Hashtbl.find_opt p row with
        | Some addr ->
            (* (its IL kept now: its body is Native after this) *)
            if not (Hashtbl.mem codes row) then Hashtbl.replace codes row (m, Types.code m);
            Some (native m addr)
        | None -> None
      end
  | _ -> None
languages/dotnet/jit/Jit_run.mli
2583
(* The JIT run in mini-dotnet (plan_dotnet.md, decision 12; stage 9,
 * arm64's on Linux and arm's on Plan 9, mini-9pi's and mini-5i's, by
 * the word's size): `mini-dotnet -jit file.dll`. When one of an
 * assembly's methods is hot (Machine's tiers: its 31st call, or its
 * first with a loop), the interpreter asks here for its code: the methods Jit takes are found then (verified), each
 * given a cell (Code_memory.cells), an entry and a stub (Jit.stubs),
 * the text read by mini-asm's parser and encoded by mini-ld's passes
 * (Link, Arm64: the encoders as a library, as decision 12 has it), the
 * bytes made executable (Code_memory), and each method's entry called
 * as a closure of mini-ml's; a method is compiled when its stub is
 * first called (compile), the same way:
 *
 *     Machine.invoke m args       the first call of one of them
 *       | jit m                   its assembly's methods prepared
 *       |   Jit.stubs             entries and stubs
 *       |   Parser_asm.parse      an object of mini-asm's
 *       |   Link, Arm64 or Arm    laid out at 0, encoded: bytes
 *       |   Code_memory.load      executable: an address
 *       v
 *     m.body <- Native f          each method's: f args, the int32s as
 *                                 ints, the entry called, its result an
 *                                 I4 or the reference
 *     the entry -> m's cell -> m's stub -> compile: Jit.method_code,
 *                                 encoded, loaded, the cell set
 *
 * The code has no absolute address of its own (branches and the
 * literal pool are relative to the pc), so it is encoded at 0 and runs
 * where it is mapped. A method the JIT does not take stays the
 * interpreter's, which calls the JIT's as any Native method.
 *
 * The call-outs (Jit.site): the code calls jit_outN, a static
 * closure here of the call-out's number and its N operands, which
 * runs the instruction in its method's code (Machine.exec) on them as
 * the interpreter's values, and gives back what it pushes. So the
 * code calls the library, the interpreter and the methods compiled
 * (their Native) as the interpreter does, through it.
 *
 * A method's code calls another compiled through the other's cell, so
 * a method never called is never compiled (fib.dll: 3 of 4). *)

(* the code of a method (its assembly's image, its row), when the JIT
 * takes it and can run here; None: the interpreter's *)
val jit : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> Value.meth -> (Value.value array -> Value.value) option

(* how many methods were compiled, for -s *)
val compiled : int ref

(* See Verifier.mli *)

module M = Metadata
module S = Signature

type vt =
  | Int32
  | Int64
  | Native
  | Float
  | Obj of S.t option
  | Ptr of S.t
  | Value of S.t
  | Gen of S.t

exception Bad of string

let bad (msg : string) = raise (Bad msg)

let show (v : vt) : string =
  match v with
  | Int32 -> "int32" | Int64 -> "int64" | Native -> "native int" | Float -> "F"
  | Obj None -> "null" | Obj (Some t) -> S.show (fun _ -> "class") t
  | Ptr t -> S.show (fun _ -> "class") t ^ "&"
  | Value _ -> "a value type"
  | Gen t -> S.show (fun _ -> "class") t

let kind (v : vt) : string =
  match v with
  | Int32 -> "an int32" | Int64 -> "an int64" | Native -> "a native int" | Float -> "a float"
  | Obj _ -> "a reference" | Ptr _ -> "a managed pointer" | Value _ -> "a value type"
  | Gen _ -> "a type parameter's value"

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* Types: a signature's, as the stack holds it *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

(* is a token's type a value type? a TypeDef by what it extends, a
 * TypeRef by the library's knowledge (mini-dotnet's System) *)
let primitive_of_name (n : string) : vt option =
  match n with
  | "System.Boolean" | "System.Char" | "System.SByte" | "System.Byte" | "System.Int16"
  | "System.UInt16" | "System.Int32" | "System.UInt32" -> Some Int32
  | "System.Int64" | "System.UInt64" -> Some Int64
  | "System.IntPtr" | "System.UIntPtr" -> Some Native
  | "System.Single" | "System.Double" -> Some Float
  | _ -> None

let rec type_name (img : Image.t) (tok : int) : string =
  let row = M.token_row tok in
  let dotted ns n = if ns = "" then n else ns ^ "." ^ n in
  match M.token_table tok with
  | t when t = M.t_type_def ->
      dotted (Image.string img (Image.get img t row "TypeNamespace")) (Image.string img (Image.get img t row "TypeName"))
  | t when t = M.t_type_ref ->
      let st, sr = Image.decode M.resolution_scope (Image.get img t row "ResolutionScope") in
      let n = dotted (Image.string img (Image.get img t row "TypeNamespace")) (Image.string img (Image.get img t row "TypeName")) in
      if st = M.t_type_ref then type_name img (M.token st sr) ^ "+" ^ n else n
  | _ -> ""

(* an enum's underlying type: its instance field value__ *)
let enum_underlying (img : Image.t) (row : int) : vt =
  let ff, fl = Image.range img M.t_type_def row "FieldList" M.t_field in
  let rec go f =
    if f > fl then Int32
    else if Image.get img M.t_field f "Flags" land 0x10 = 0 then
      (match S.field (Image.blob img (Image.get img M.t_field f "Signature")) with
       | S.I8 | S.U8 -> Int64 | S.I | S.U -> Native | _ -> Int32)
    else go (f + 1) in
  go ff

let rec of_sig (img : Image.t) (t : S.t) : vt option =
  match t with
  | S.Void -> None
  | S.Bool | S.Char | S.I1 | S.U1 | S.I2 | S.U2 | S.I4 | S.U4 -> Some Int32
  | S.I8 | S.U8 -> Some Int64
  | S.I | S.U | S.FnPtr _ | S.Ptr _ -> Some Native
  | S.R4 | S.R8 -> Some Float
  | S.String | S.Object | S.Class _ | S.SzArray _ | S.Array _ -> Some (Obj (Some t))
  | S.GenericInst (S.Class _, _) -> Some (Obj (Some t))
  | S.GenericInst _ -> Some (Value t)
  | S.ByRef e -> Some (Ptr e)
  | S.Var _ | S.MVar _ -> Some (Gen t)
  | S.TypedRef -> Some (Value t)
  | S.ValueType tok -> Some (value_token img tok)

(* a value type named by its token: a primitive, an enum, a struct *)
and value_token (img : Image.t) (tok : int) : vt =
  match primitive_of_name (type_name img tok) with
  | Some v -> v
  | None ->
      if M.token_table tok = M.t_type_def then
        let row = M.token_row tok in
        let et, er = Image.decode M.type_def_or_ref (Image.get img M.t_type_def row "Extends") in
        if et >= 0 && type_name img (M.token et er) = "System.Enum" then enum_underlying img row
        else Value (S.ValueType tok)
      else Value (S.ValueType tok)

(* a token in an instruction (newarr T, box T): its signature *)
let token_sig (img : Image.t) (tok : int) : S.t =
  match M.token_table tok with
  | t when t = M.t_type_spec ->
      S.type_spec (Image.blob img (Image.get img t (M.token_row tok) "Signature"))
  | t when t = M.t_type_def ->
      let row = M.token_row tok in
      let et, er = Image.decode M.type_def_or_ref (Image.get img t row "Extends") in
      let parent = if et >= 0 then type_name img (M.token et er) else "" in
      if (parent = "System.ValueType" || parent = "System.Enum") && type_name img tok <> "System.Enum"
      then S.ValueType tok else S.Class tok
  | t when t = M.t_type_ref ->
      let n = type_name img tok in
      (match primitive_of_name n with
       | Some _ -> S.ValueType tok
       | None -> match Hashtbl.find_opt Library.specs n with
         | Some sp when sp.skind = Value.Struct || sp.skind = Value.Enum -> S.ValueType tok
         | _ -> if n = "System.String" then S.String else if n = "System.Object" then S.Object else S.Class tok)
  | _ -> S.Object

let token_vt (img : Image.t) (tok : int) : vt =
  match of_sig img (token_sig img tok) with Some v -> v | None -> bad "a type void"

(* the signature a call names: a MethodDef's, a MemberRef's (its class's
 * arguments put in for !0, when it is called on an instance of a
 * generic class), a MethodSpec's (its own put in for !!0) *)
let rec subst (cargs : S.t list) (margs : S.t list) (t : S.t) : S.t =
  let sub = subst cargs margs in
  match t with
  | S.Var n when n < List.length cargs -> List.nth cargs n
  | S.MVar n when n < List.length margs -> List.nth margs n
  | S.ByRef e -> S.ByRef (sub e) | S.Ptr e -> S.Ptr (sub e)
  | S.SzArray e -> S.SzArray (sub e) | S.Array (e, r) -> S.Array (sub e, r)
  | S.GenericInst (g, l) -> S.GenericInst (g, List.map sub l)
  | t -> t

let rec call_sig (img : Image.t) (tok : int) : S.meth * S.t option =
  (* (the signature, and the class it is on when known) *)
  let row = M.token_row tok in
  match M.token_table tok with
  | t when t = M.t_method_def -> (S.method_ (Image.blob img (Image.get img t row "Signature")), None)
  | t when t = M.t_member_ref ->
      let m = S.method_ (Image.blob img (Image.get img t row "Signature")) in
      let pt, pr = Image.decode M.member_ref_parent (Image.get img t row "Class") in
      let owner = if pt < 0 then None else Some (token_sig img (M.token pt pr)) in
      let cargs = match owner with Some (S.GenericInst (_, l)) -> l | _ -> [] in
      ({ m with ret = subst cargs [] m.ret; params = List.map (subst cargs []) m.params }, owner)
  | t when t = M.t_method_spec ->
      let mt, mr = Image.decode M.method_def_or_ref (Image.get img t row "Method") in
      let m, owner = call_sig img (M.token mt mr) in
      let margs = S.method_spec (Image.blob img (Image.get img t row "Instantiation")) in
      ({ m with ret = subst [] margs m.ret; params = List.map (subst [] margs) m.params }, owner)
  | _ -> bad (Printf.sprintf "a call to a token 0x%08x" tok)

let field_sig (img : Image.t) (tok : int) : S.t =
  let row = M.token_row tok in
  match M.token_table tok with
  | t when t = M.t_field -> S.field (Image.blob img (Image.get img t row "Signature"))
  | t when t = M.t_member_ref ->
      let f = S.field (Image.blob img (Image.get img t row "Signature")) in
      let pt, pr = Image.decode M.member_ref_parent (Image.get img t row "Class") in
      (match token_sig img (M.token pt pr) with S.GenericInst (_, l) -> subst l [] f | _ -> f)
  | _ -> bad "a field's token"

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* Compatibility, merging *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

(* can a stack's value of type [v] go where [want] is declared? *)
let fits (v : vt) (want : vt) : bool =
  match v, want with
  | (Int32 | Native), (Int32 | Native) -> true
  | Int64, Int64 | Float, Float -> true
  | Obj _, Obj _ -> true
  | Ptr _, (Ptr _ | Native) -> true
  (* (an unmanaged pointer, C#'s unsafe code, where a managed one is
   * asked: correct, not verifiable, and compiled the same) *)
  | Native, Ptr _ -> true
  | Value _, Value _ -> true
  | Gen _, _ | _, Gen _ -> true
  | _ -> false

let expect (what : string) (v : vt) (want : vt) : unit =
  if not (fits v want) then bad (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s where %s is expected" what (kind v) (kind want))

let merge (a : vt) (b : vt) : vt =
  match a, b with
  | Obj None, Obj _ -> b
  | Obj _, Obj _ -> a
  | (Int32 | Native), (Int32 | Native) when a <> b -> Native
  | _ when fits a b -> a
  | _ -> bad (Printf.sprintf "the stack differs where two paths join: %s and %s" (kind a) (kind b))

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* A method *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

type result = {
  stacks : vt list option array;     (* before each instruction, the top first; None: not reached *)
  instrs : Il.instr array;
}

let number (what : string) (v : vt) : unit =
  match v with
  | Int32 | Int64 | Native | Float -> ()
  | _ -> bad (Printf.sprintf "%s of %s" what (kind v))

(* Partition III, table 2 (binary numeric operations) and 5 (integer) *)
let binop (op : Il.binop) (a : vt) (b : vt) : vt =
  let name = match op with
    | Il.Add | Il.Add_ovf | Il.Add_ovf_un -> "add" | Il.Sub | Il.Sub_ovf | Il.Sub_ovf_un -> "sub"
    | Il.Mul | Il.Mul_ovf | Il.Mul_ovf_un -> "mul" | Il.Div | Il.Div_un -> "div"
    | Il.Rem | Il.Rem_un -> "rem" | Il.And -> "and" | Il.Or -> "or" | Il.Xor -> "xor"
    | Il.Shl -> "shl" | Il.Shr -> "shr" | Il.Shr_un -> "shr.un" in
  let fail () = bad (Printf.sprintf "%s of %s and %s" name (kind a) (kind b)) in
  match op with
  | Il.Shl | Il.Shr | Il.Shr_un ->
      (match a, b with
       | (Int32 | Int64 | Native), (Int32 | Native) -> a
       | _ -> fail ())
  | _ ->
      let integer = match op with
        | Il.And | Il.Or | Il.Xor | Il.Div_un | Il.Rem_un | Il.Add_ovf | Il.Add_ovf_un
        | Il.Sub_ovf | Il.Sub_ovf_un | Il.Mul_ovf | Il.Mul_ovf_un -> true
        | _ -> false in
      match a, b with
      | Int32, Int32 -> Int32
      | Int64, Int64 -> Int64
      | (Int32 | Native), (Int32 | Native) -> Native
      | Float, Float when not integer -> Float
      | Ptr _, (Int32 | Native) when op = Il.Add || op = Il.Sub -> a
      | (Int32 | Native), Ptr _ when op = Il.Add -> b
      | Ptr _, Ptr _ when op = Il.Sub -> Native
      | _ -> fail ()

let comparable (what : string) (a : vt) (b : vt) : unit =
  match a, b with
  | (Int32 | Native), (Int32 | Native) | Int64, Int64 | Float, Float -> ()
  | (Obj _ | Gen _), (Obj _ | Gen _) -> ()
  | Ptr _, Ptr _ -> ()
  | _ -> bad (Printf.sprintf "%s of %s and %s" what (kind a) (kind b))

let kind_vt (k : Il.kind) : vt =
  match k with
  | Il.K_i1 | Il.K_u1 | Il.K_i2 | Il.K_u2 | Il.K_i4 | Il.K_u4 -> Int32
  | Il.K_i8 | Il.K_u8 -> Int64
  | Il.K_i | Il.K_u -> Native
  | Il.K_r4 | Il.K_r8 -> Float
  | Il.K_ref -> Obj (Some S.Object)

let method_ (img : Image.t) (row : int) : result =
  let t = M.t_method_def in
  let rva = Image.get img t row "RVA" in
  if rva = 0 then bad "no body";
  let body = Image.body img rva in
  let instrs = Il.decode body.code in
  let n = Array.length instrs in
  let sg = S.method_ (Image.blob img (Image.get img t row "Signature")) in
  (* the owner: its `this` a reference, or a pointer for a struct's *)
  let owner =
    let rec find r = if r > img.rows.(M.t_type_def) then 1
      else let f, l = Image.range img M.t_type_def r "MethodList" t in
        if row >= f && row <= l then r else find (r + 1) in
    find 1 in
  let this_vt = match token_sig img (M.token M.t_type_def owner) with
    | S.ValueType _ as s -> Ptr s
    | s -> Obj (Some s) in
  let vt_of s = match of_sig img s with Some v -> v | None -> bad "a value of type void" in
  let args = Array.of_list ((if sg.has_this then [ this_vt ] else []) @ List.map vt_of sg.params) in
  let arg_sigs = Array.of_list ((if sg.has_this then [ S.Object ] else []) @ sg.params) in
  let locals =
    if body.locals_token = 0 then [||]
    else Array.of_list (S.locals (Image.blob img (Image.get img M.t_stand_alone_sig (M.token_row body.locals_token) "Signature"))) in
  let local_vt i = if i >= Array.length locals then bad (Printf.sprintf "no local %d" i) else vt_of locals.(i) in
  let ret = of_sig img sg.ret in
  let stacks = Array.make (n + 1) None in
  let work = ref [] in
  let flow (i : int) (s : vt list) =
    if i >= n then bad "the code falls off the method's end";
    match stacks.(i) with
    | None -> stacks.(i) <- Some s; work := i :: !work
    | Some old ->
        if List.length old <> List.length s then
          bad (Printf.sprintf "the stack is %d deep at IL_%04x by one path, %d by another"
                 (List.length old) instrs.(i).at (List.length s));
        let m = List.map2 merge old s in
        if m <> old then (stacks.(i) <- Some m; work := i :: !work) in
  flow 0 [];
  List.iter (fun (c : Image.clause) ->
      let i = Il.index instrs c.handler_start in
      (match c.kind with
       | 0 -> flow i [ Obj (Some (token_sig img c.class_token)) ]
       | 1 -> flow i [ Obj (Some S.Object) ]; flow (Il.index instrs c.class_token) [ Obj (Some S.Object) ]
       | _ -> flow i [])) body.clauses;
  let current = ref 0 in
  (try
     while !work <> [] do
       let i = List.hd !work in
       work := List.tl !work;
       current := i;
       let s = match stacks.(i) with Some s -> s | None -> [] in
       let ins = instrs.(i) in
       let st = ref s in
       let pop what = match !st with
         | v :: rest -> st := rest; v
         | [] -> bad (what ^ ": the stack is empty") in
       let push v = st := v :: !st in
       let next () = flow (i + 1) !st in
       let jump t = flow t !st in
       let call_args (m : S.meth) (what : string) =
         List.iter (fun p -> expect what (pop what) (vt_of p)) (List.rev m.params) in
       (match ins.op with
        | Il.Nop | Il.Break | Il.Prefix _ | Il.Constrained _ -> next ()
        | Il.Ldarg a -> if a >= Array.length args then bad "no such argument"; push args.(a); next ()
        | Il.Ldarga a -> if a >= Array.length args then bad "no such argument"; push (Ptr arg_sigs.(a)); next ()
        | Il.Starg a -> expect "starg" (pop "starg") args.(a); next ()
        | Il.Ldloc l -> push (local_vt l); next ()
        | Il.Ldloca l -> ignore (local_vt l); push (Ptr locals.(l)); next ()
        | Il.Stloc l -> expect "stloc" (pop "stloc") (local_vt l); next ()
        | Il.Ldnull -> push (Obj None); next ()
        | Il.Ldc_i4 _ -> push Int32; next ()
        | Il.Ldc_i8 _ -> push Int64; next ()
        | Il.Ldc_r _ -> push Float; next ()
        | Il.Ldstr _ -> push (Obj (Some S.String)); next ()
        | Il.Dup -> let v = pop "dup" in push v; push v; next ()
        | Il.Pop -> ignore (pop "pop"); next ()
        | Il.Call tok | Il.Callvirt tok ->
            let m, _ = call_sig img tok in
            call_args m "an argument";
            if m.has_this then begin
              let this = pop "this" in
              (match this with
               | Int32 | Int64 | Float -> bad (Printf.sprintf "a call's this: %s" (kind this))
               | _ -> ())
            end;
            (match of_sig img m.ret with Some v -> push v | None -> ());
            next ()
        | Il.Newobj tok ->
            let m, owner = call_sig img tok in
            call_args m "a constructor's argument";
            let cls = match owner with
              | Some o -> o
              | None ->
                  (* (a MethodDef: its TypeDef) *)
                  let r = M.token_row tok in
                  let rec find c = if c > img.rows.(M.t_type_def) then 1
                    else let f, l = Image.range img M.t_type_def c "MethodList" M.t_method_def in
                      if r >= f && r <= l then c else find (c + 1) in
                  token_sig img (M.token M.t_type_def (find 1)) in
            push (match vt_of cls with Value _ as v -> v | Int32 | Int64 | Native | Float as v -> v | _ -> Obj (Some cls));
            next ()
        | Il.Calli tok ->
            let m = S.method_ (Image.blob img (Image.get img M.t_stand_alone_sig (M.token_row tok) "Signature")) in
            expect "calli's function" (pop "calli") Native;
            call_args m "an argument";
            if m.has_this then ignore (pop "this");
            (match of_sig img m.ret with Some v -> push v | None -> ());
            next ()
        | Il.Ret ->
            (match ret with Some r -> expect "ret" (pop "ret") r | None -> ());
            if !st <> [] then bad (Printf.sprintf "ret with the stack %d deep, not empty" (List.length !st))
        | Il.Br t -> jump t
        | Il.Brfalse t | Il.Brtrue t ->
            (match pop "a branch's condition" with
             | Float | Value _ as v -> bad ("a branch on " ^ kind v)
             | _ -> ());
            jump t; next ()
        | Il.Bcmp (_, _, t) ->
            let b = pop "a comparison" in
            let a = pop "a comparison" in
            comparable "a branch's comparison" a b;
            jump t; next ()
        | Il.Switch ts ->
            expect "switch" (pop "switch") Int32;
            Array.iter jump ts; next ()
        | Il.Ldind k -> expect "ldind" (pop "ldind") (Ptr S.Object); push (kind_vt k); next ()
        | Il.Stind _ -> ignore (pop "stind"); expect "stind" (pop "stind") (Ptr S.Object); next ()
        | Il.Binop o -> let b = pop "an operand" in let a = pop "an operand" in push (binop o a b); next ()
        | Il.Neg -> let v = pop "neg" in number "neg" v; push v; next ()
        | Il.Not ->
            let v = pop "not" in
            (match v with Int32 | Int64 | Native -> push v | _ -> bad ("not of " ^ kind v));
            next ()
        | Il.Conv (k, _, _) ->
            let v = pop "conv" in
            (match v, k with
             | (Int32 | Int64 | Native | Float), _ -> ()
             | (Ptr _ | Obj _), (Il.K_i | Il.K_u | Il.K_i8 | Il.K_u8) -> ()
             | _ -> bad ("conv of " ^ kind v));
            push (kind_vt k); next ()
        | Il.Conv_r_un -> number "conv.r.un" (pop "conv.r.un"); push Float; next ()
        | Il.Ceq | Il.Cgt _ | Il.Clt _ ->
            let b = pop "a comparison" in
            let a = pop "a comparison" in
            comparable "a comparison" a b; push Int32; next ()
        | Il.Ldobj tok -> ignore (pop "ldobj"); push (token_vt img tok); next ()
        | Il.Stobj _ -> ignore (pop "stobj"); expect "stobj" (pop "stobj") (Ptr S.Object); next ()
        | Il.Cpobj _ -> ignore (pop "cpobj"); ignore (pop "cpobj"); next ()
        | Il.Ldfld tok | Il.Ldflda tok ->
            let o = pop "ldfld" in
            (match o with Int32 | Int64 | Float -> bad ("a field of " ^ kind o) | _ -> ());
            let f = field_sig img tok in
            push (match ins.op with Il.Ldflda _ -> Ptr f | _ -> vt_of f); next ()
        | Il.Stfld tok ->
            let v = pop "stfld" in
            expect "stfld" v (vt_of (field_sig img tok));
            let o = pop "stfld" in
            (match o with Int32 | Int64 | Float -> bad ("a field of " ^ kind o) | _ -> ());
            next ()
        | Il.Ldsfld tok -> push (vt_of (field_sig img tok)); next ()
        | Il.Ldsflda tok -> push (Ptr (field_sig img tok)); next ()
        | Il.Stsfld tok -> expect "stsfld" (pop "stsfld") (vt_of (field_sig img tok)); next ()
        | Il.Newarr tok ->
            expect "newarr's length" (pop "newarr") Int32;
            push (Obj (Some (S.SzArray (token_sig img tok)))); next ()
        | Il.Ldlen -> expect "ldlen" (pop "ldlen") (Obj None); push Native; next ()
        | Il.Ldelema tok ->
            expect "an index" (pop "ldelema") Int32; expect "an array" (pop "ldelema") (Obj None);
            push (Ptr (token_sig img tok)); next ()
        | Il.Ldelem k ->
            expect "an index" (pop "ldelem") Int32; expect "an array" (pop "ldelem") (Obj None);
            push (kind_vt k); next ()
        | Il.Ldelem_any tok ->
            expect "an index" (pop "ldelem") Int32; expect "an array" (pop "ldelem") (Obj None);
            push (token_vt img tok); next ()
        | Il.Stelem k ->
            expect "stelem" (pop "stelem") (kind_vt k);
            expect "an index" (pop "stelem") Int32; expect "an array" (pop "stelem") (Obj None); next ()
        | Il.Stelem_any tok ->
            expect "stelem" (pop "stelem") (token_vt img tok);
            expect "an index" (pop "stelem") Int32; expect "an array" (pop "stelem") (Obj None); next ()
        | Il.Box tok -> ignore (pop "box"); push (Obj (Some (token_sig img tok))); next ()
        | Il.Unbox tok -> expect "unbox" (pop "unbox") (Obj None); push (Ptr (token_sig img tok)); next ()
        | Il.Unbox_any tok -> ignore (pop "unbox.any"); push (token_vt img tok); next ()
        | Il.Castclass tok | Il.Isinst tok ->
            let v = pop "a cast" in
            (match v with Obj _ | Gen _ -> () | _ -> bad ("a cast of " ^ kind v));
            push (Obj (Some (token_sig img tok))); next ()
        | Il.Throw -> expect "throw" (pop "throw") (Obj None)
        | Il.Rethrow -> ()
        | Il.Leave t -> st := []; jump t
        | Il.Endfinally -> ()
        | Il.Endfilter -> expect "endfilter" (pop "endfilter") Int32
        | Il.Ldtoken tok ->
            push (Value (if M.token_table tok = M.t_field then S.I else S.ValueType tok)); next ()
        | Il.Ldftn _ -> push Native; next ()
        | Il.Ldvirtftn _ -> expect "ldvirtftn" (pop "ldvirtftn") (Obj None); push Native; next ()
        | Il.Initobj _ -> expect "initobj" (pop "initobj") (Ptr S.Object); next ()
        | Il.Sizeof _ -> push Int32; next ()
        | Il.Localloc -> expect "localloc" (pop "localloc") Native; push Native; next ()
        | Il.Cpblk | Il.Initblk -> ignore (pop "blk"); ignore (pop "blk"); ignore (pop "blk"); next ()
        | Il.Ckfinite -> expect "ckfinite" (pop "ckfinite") Float; push Float; next ()
        | Il.Jmp _ | Il.Arglist | Il.Mkrefany _ | Il.Refanyval _ | Il.Refanytype ->
            bad (ins.name ^ ": not verified by mini-dotnet"));
       if List.length !st > body.max_stack + 0 && body.max_stack >= 0 then
         (match ins.op with
          | Il.Ret | Il.Throw | Il.Rethrow | Il.Endfinally | Il.Endfilter | Il.Leave _ | Il.Br _ -> ()
          | _ -> if List.length !st > body.max_stack then
                bad (Printf.sprintf "the stack %d deep, past its .maxstack %d" (List.length !st) body.max_stack))
     done
   with Bad msg ->
     let at = if !current < n then instrs.(!current).at else 0 in
     bad (Printf.sprintf "IL_%04x: %s" at msg));
  { stacks; instrs }

let assembly (img : Image.t) : int * (int * string) list =
  let ok = ref 0 and errors = ref [] in
  for row = 1 to img.rows.(M.t_method_def) do
    if Image.get img M.t_method_def row "RVA" <> 0 then
      match method_ img row with
      | _ -> incr ok
      | exception Bad msg -> errors := (row, msg) :: !errors
      | exception (Il.Bad_il msg | Image.Bad_image msg) -> errors := (row, msg) :: !errors
      | exception e -> errors := (row, "not read: " ^ Printexc.to_string e) :: !errors
  done;
  (!ok, List.rev !errors)
languages/dotnet/jit/Verifier.mli
3611
(* The verifier: each method's stack, its depth and each slot's type,
 * at each instruction, found by going over the method's paths
 * (ECMA-335, Partition III, 1.8: "verifiability and correctness"); an
 * instruction refused, with its offset, when its operands are not of
 * the types it takes. Its result is the JIT's input (plan_dotnet.md,
 * decision 12): with each slot's type known before the method runs, a
 * slot is a place in the frame, and `add` an add of registers.
 *
 *     static int Rec(int n)          before each instruction:
 *       IL_0000: ldarg.0             []
 *       IL_0001: ldc.i4.2            [int32]
 *       IL_0002: bge.s IL_0006       [int32; int32]   two int32: comparable
 *       IL_0004: ldarg.0             []
 *       IL_0005: ret                 [int32]           the int32 returned
 *       IL_0006: ldarg.0             []                from IL_0002: the same
 *       ...
 *
 * {b The types on the stack} are few (Partition III, 1.1): int32,
 * int64, native int, F (every float), a reference (O), a managed
 * pointer (&), a value type's value. A bool, a char, a short are int32
 * on the stack; the instructions are typed by these (lesson 3).
 *
 * {b The paths} are followed from the first instruction and from each
 * handler's (a catch's starts with its exception), a worklist of the
 * instructions whose stack changed; where two paths join, their stacks
 * must have the same depth and their slots the same kind (a reference
 * and another: a reference). So the IL is a program in a typed
 * language whose types are found, not written: the verifier is its
 * type checker, as the JVM's is (its "type inference" verifier, before
 * Java 6's StackMapTable wrote the types at the joins).
 *
 * It reads the metadata only (Signature's types, the tokens), not the
 * classes as Types loads them: it can go over Microsoft's own library.
 * A reference's class is not checked against what is asked (a Shape
 * where an INamed is: Types would have to load both), nor are the
 * rules of access (private, protected); a kind is: an int32 where a
 * reference is asked is refused.
 *
 * others:
 * The CLR's verifier refused what it could not prove safe, and was the
 * base of .NET's code access security: an unverifiable method needed
 * full trust. .NET Core dropped both (2016): its JIT imports the IL with
 * the same walk, typing the stack, but trusts the program. *)

(* a slot's type: Partition III's stack types, a reference with its
 * type when known (None: null) *)
type vt =
  | Int32
  | Int64
  | Native
  | Float
  | Obj of Signature.t option
  | Ptr of Signature.t
  | Value of Signature.t
  | Gen of Signature.t             (* a type parameter's value: !0, !!0 *)

exception Bad of string

val show : vt -> string

type result = {
  stacks : vt list option array;   (* before each instruction, the top first; None: not reached *)
  instrs : Il.instr array;
}

(* a signature's type as the stack holds it (None: void) *)
val of_sig : Image.t -> Signature.t -> vt option

(* a type's token (newarr T, box T, a TypeDef): its signature, a
 * value type's ValueType *)
val token_sig : Image.t -> int -> Signature.t

(* a call's token (MethodDef, MemberRef, MethodSpec): its signature,
 * the class's arguments put in, and the class when a MemberRef says it *)
val call_sig : Image.t -> int -> Signature.meth * Signature.t option

(* a MethodDef's row verified: Bad with the offset and why *)
val method_ : Image.t -> int -> result

(* every method with a body: how many pass, the others' rows and why *)
val assembly : Image.t -> int * (int * string) list

(* Claude Code

(* See Code_memory.mli: mini-ml's build (the mkfile's), Linux's system
 * calls by their numbers, arm64's; Plan 9's on arm *)

(* the runtime's (unix.c), as lib_core's Unix declares it: a string's
 * argument its address, an int its value *)
external syscall : int -> Obj.t array -> int = "unix_syscall"

let plan9 = Sys.os_type = "Plan9"
let available = (Sys.os_type = "Unix" && Sys.word_size = 64) || plan9

let call (nr : int) (args : Obj.t list) : int =
  let a = Array.make 6 (Obj.repr 0) in
  List.iteri (fun i x -> a.(i) <- x) args;
  syscall nr a

(* the kernel's answer, a negative errno when it fails *)
let check (what : string) (n : int) : int =
  if n < 0 && n > -4096 then failwith (Printf.sprintf "the JIT's memory: %s: error %d" what (-n));
  n

(* Plan 9's (sys.h): pread 10, pwrite 11, pipe 27, segattach 28,
 * segflush 31. The memory a segment attached (zeros, class "memory"),
 * its bytes written through a pipe: ML writes no memory but its own
 * values' (and the collector moves those), the kernel writes where a
 * read is asked to put them; then segflush, the bytes in memory and
 * the instructions' cache emptied of what was there. Plan 9 runs its
 * processes' memory, arm having no right to run apart. *)
let segment (n : int) : int = check "segattach" (call 28 [ Obj.repr 0; Obj.repr "memory"; Obj.repr 0; Obj.repr n ])

let fds : (int * int) option ref = ref None

let poke (addr : int) (data : string) : unit =
  let r, w = match !fds with
    | Some p -> p
    | None ->
        let b = Bytes.create 8 in
        ignore (check "pipe" (call 27 [ Obj.repr b ]));
        let p = (Int32.to_int (Bytes.get_int32_le b 0), Int32.to_int (Bytes.get_int32_le b 4)) in
        fds := Some p;
        p in
  let n = String.length data in
  let rec chunks off =
    if off < n then begin
      (* (4 KB a time: the pipe holds 32, and no one else reads it) *)
      let k = min 4096 (n - off) in
      if check "pwrite" (call 11 [ Obj.repr w; Obj.repr (String.sub data off k); Obj.repr k; Obj.repr (-1); Obj.repr (-1) ]) <> k
      then failwith "the JIT's memory: a short write";
      let rec read got =
        if got < k then begin
          let m = check "pread" (call 10 [ Obj.repr r; Obj.repr (addr + off + got); Obj.repr (k - got); Obj.repr (-1); Obj.repr (-1) ]) in
          if m = 0 then failwith "the JIT's memory: the pipe's end";
          read (got + m)
        end in
      read 0;
      chunks (off + k)
    end in
  chunks 0

let load_plan9 (code : string) : int =
  let n = String.length code in
  let addr = segment n in
  poke addr code;
  ignore (check "segflush" (call 31 [ Obj.repr addr; Obj.repr n ]));
  addr

(* memfd_create 279, write 64, mmap 222 (PROT_READ|PROT_EXEC 5,
 * MAP_SHARED 1), close 57 *)
let load (code : string) : int =
  if plan9 then load_plan9 code else
  let fd = check "memfd_create" (call 279 [ Obj.repr "mini-dotnet-jit"; Obj.repr 0 ]) in
  let n = String.length code in
  if check "write" (call 64 [ Obj.repr fd; Obj.repr code; Obj.repr n ]) <> n then failwith "the JIT's memory: a short write";
  let addr = check "mmap" (call 222 [ Obj.repr 0; Obj.repr n; Obj.repr 5; Obj.repr 1; Obj.repr fd; Obj.repr 0 ]) in
  ignore (call 57 [ Obj.repr fd ]);
  addr

(* the words as bytes, little-endian *)
let words (a : int array) : string =
  let w = Sys.word_size / 8 in
  let b = Bytes.create (w * Array.length a) in
  Array.iteri (fun i x ->
      if w = 8 then Bytes.set_int64_le b (8 * i) (Int64.of_int x)
      else Bytes.set_int32_le b (4 * i) (Int32.of_int x)) a;
  Bytes.to_string b

(* mapped readable (PROT_READ 1), the file kept open; a word written by
 * pwrite64 (68), which the mapping, MAP_SHARED, sees *)
let cells (init : int array) : int * (int -> int -> unit) =
  if plan9 then begin
    (* (a segment's words, written through the pipe) *)
    let addr = segment (4 * Array.length init) in
    poke addr (words init);
    (addr, fun i x -> poke (addr + (4 * i)) (words [| x |]))
  end else
  let fd = check "memfd_create" (call 279 [ Obj.repr "mini-dotnet-cells"; Obj.repr 0 ]) in
  let data = words init in
  let n = String.length data in
  if check "write" (call 64 [ Obj.repr fd; Obj.repr data; Obj.repr n ]) <> n then failwith "the JIT's cells: a short write";
  let addr = check "mmap" (call 222 [ Obj.repr 0; Obj.repr n; Obj.repr 1; Obj.repr 1; Obj.repr fd; Obj.repr 0 ]) in
  (addr, fun i x ->
      if check "pwrite64" (call 68 [ Obj.repr fd; Obj.repr (words [| x |]); Obj.repr 8; Obj.repr (8 * i) ]) <> 8
      then failwith "the JIT's cells: a short write")

(* the runtime's (exceptions.c) *)
external handler_address : unit -> int = "ml_handler_address"
let handler () : int = handler_address ()

(* An address as a value, and back, through an int64's block (tag 255:
 * its field a word the collector does not look in): the field read
 * is the word itself, untagged. A word that is even and outside the
 * heap is a pointer the collector leaves alone, as the code's of a
 * static closure. *)
let closure (addr : int) : Obj.t =
  let word = Obj.field (Obj.repr (Int64.of_int addr)) 0 in
  let c = Obj.new_block 247 2 in
  Obj.set_field c 0 word;
  Obj.set_field c 1 word;
  c

let address (v : Obj.t) : int =
  (* (an int64's 8 bytes: two words on 32 bits, the second's bits past
   * the int's) *)
  let b = Obj.new_block 255 (8 / (Sys.word_size / 8)) in
  Obj.set_field b 0 v;
  Int64.to_int (Obj.obj b : int64)

open Value

type impl =
  | Impl of (value array -> value)
  | By_runtime
  | Abstract

type smeth = {
  mn : string;
  mstatic : bool;
  mvirt : bool;
  mparams : string list;
  mret : string;
  mgeneric : int;
  impl : impl;
}

type spec = {
  sname : string;
  sparent : string;
  skind : kind;
  sgeneric : int;
  sinterfaces : string list;
  sfields : (string * string) list;
  smethods : smeth list;

(* the system, by the program's capabilities (CLI's): its arguments,
 * the environment, files and directories, the time *)
type os = {
  argv : string list;
  getenv : string -> string option;
  kind : string -> int;
  remove : string -> bool;
  rename : string -> string -> bool;
  mkdir : string -> bool;
  entries : string -> string list option;
