/* ocaml-light's open_flag, in its order: a constant constructor's number */
enum { Open_rdonly, Open_wronly, Open_append, Open_creat, Open_trunc, Open_excl };

/* A file opened as Plan 9's: open, which doesn't make it, then create,
 * which makes it (and empties it); with Open_excl, create alone, which
 * fails when the file is there. Open_append is a seek to the end, once:
 * not Unix's O_APPEND, each write at the end whoever else writes */
value
sys_open(value name, value flags, value perm)
{
	int fd, set, mode;
	char *s;

	s = (char*)Bytes(name);
	set = 0;
	for(; !Is_int(flags); flags = Field(flags, 1))
		set |= 1 << Long_val(Field(flags, 0));
	/* (Open_append alone writes too: OCaml's flag for it is O_APPEND | O_WRONLY) */
	mode = (set & (1 << Open_wronly | 1 << Open_append)) ? OWRITE : OREAD;
	fd = -1;
	if(!(set & 1 << Open_creat))
		fd = open(s, mode | ((set & 1 << Open_trunc) ? OTRUNC : 0));
	else if(set & 1 << Open_excl)
		fd = create(s, mode | OEXCL, Long_val(perm));
	else{
		fd = open(s, mode | ((set & 1 << Open_trunc) ? OTRUNC : 0));
		if(fd < 0)
			fd = create(s, mode, Long_val(perm));
	}
	if(fd < 0)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, s);
	if(set & 1 << Open_append)
		seek(fd, 0, 2);
	return Val_int(fd);
}

value
sys_close(value fd)
{
	close(Long_val(fd));
	return Val_unit;
}

/* 0 a file, 1 a directory, -1 nothing */
static int
file_kind(value name)
{
	Dir *d;
	int k;

	d = dirstat((char*)Bytes(name));
	if(d == nil)
		return -1;
	k = (d->mode & DMDIR) != 0;
	free(d);
	return k;
}

value sys_file_exists(value name) { return Val_bool(file_kind(name) >= 0); }

value
sys_is_directory(value name)
{
	int k;

	k = file_kind(name);
	if(k < 0)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, (char*)Bytes(name));
	return Val_bool(k);
}

/* a file, or an empty directory (Sys.rmdir too: Plan 9's remove) */
value
sys_remove(value name)
{
	if(remove((char*)Bytes(name)) < 0)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, (char*)Bytes(name));
	return Val_unit;
}

value
sys_mkdir(value name, value perm)
{
	int fd;

	fd = create((char*)Bytes(name), OREAD, DMDIR | Long_val(perm));
	if(fd < 0)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, (char*)Bytes(name));
	close(fd);
	return Val_unit;
}

#ifndef __GNUC__
/* Plan 9's rename: a file's name changed in its directory (dirwstat) */
static int
rename_in_dir(char *from, char *to, char *name)
{
	Dir d;

	USED(to);
	nulldir(&d);
	d.name = name;
	return dirwstat(from, &d);
}

/* sh -c cmd, waited for: its exit status, 255 for a signal */
static int
shell(char *cmd)
{
#ifdef plan9
	/* Plan 9's: rc, and await's line (the pid, three times, the
	 * child's last word: empty when all went well), read here: the
	 * libc's wait wants its tokenize and runes for it */
	char buf[256], *s;
	int pid, n, i;

	pid = fork();
	if(pid == 0){
		execl("/bin/rc", "rc", "-c", cmd, nil);
		exits("exec");
	}
	if(pid < 0)
		return 127;
	for(;;){
		n = await(buf, sizeof buf - 1);
		if(n < 0)
			return 127;
		buf[n] = 0;
		if(atoi(buf) != pid)
			continue;
		s = buf;
		for(i = 0; i < 4 && s != nil; i++){
			s = strchr(s, ' ');
			if(s != nil)
				s++;
		}
		if(s == nil || s[0] == 0 || (s[0] == '\'' && s[1] == '\''))
			return 0;
		return s[0] >= '0' && s[0] <= '9' ? atoi(s) : 255;
	}
#else
	Waitmsg *w;
	int pid, st;

	pid = fork();
	if(pid == 0){
		execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-c", cmd, nil);
		exits("exec");
	}
	if(pid < 0)
		return 127;
	do{
		w = wait();
		if(w == nil)
			return 127;
		st = w->msg[0] == 0 ? 0 : w->msg[0] >= '0' && w->msg[0] <= '9' ? atoi(w->msg) : 255;
		st = w->pid == pid ? st : -1;
		free(w);
	}while(st < 0);
	return st;
#endif
}
#endif

/* the two names in one directory: Plan 9 has no other rename, and a
 * file moved to another directory is copied */
value
sys_rename(value from, value to)
{
	char *f, *t, *fb, *tb;

	f = (char*)Bytes(from);
	t = (char*)Bytes(to);
	fb = strrchr(f, '/');
	tb = strrchr(t, '/');
	fb = fb == nil ? f : fb + 1;
	tb = tb == nil ? t : tb + 1;
	if(fb - f != tb - t || strncmp(f, t, fb - f) != 0 || rename_in_dir(f, t, tb) < 0)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, f);
	return Val_unit;
}

value
sys_getcwd(value unit)
{
	char buf[1024];

	if(getwd(buf, sizeof buf) == nil)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, "getcwd");
	return ml_string(buf);
}

/* a directory's names, without . and .. */
value
sys_read_directory(value name)
{
	Dir *d;
	value a, s;
	long n, i;
	int fd;

	fd = open((char*)Bytes(name), OREAD);
	n = fd < 0 ? -1 : dirreadall(fd, &d);
	if(fd >= 0)
		close(fd);
	if(n < 0)
		raise_with(caml_exn_Sys_error, (char*)Bytes(name));
	a = make_vect(Val_int(n), Val_unit);
	for(i = 0; i < n; i++){
		push(a);
		s = ml_string(d[i].name);
		a = pop();
		Store_field(a, i, s);
	}
	free(d);
	return a;
}

value
sys_system_command(value cmd)
{
	return Val_int(shell((char*)Bytes(cmd)));
}

/* Signals. A handler is OCaml's (Sys.signal's function), and C can't
 * call it: here a signal is only noted, and the stdlib runs the
 * handlers of those noted where a program waits, when a read or a
 * system call comes back interrupted (Pervasives' run_signals). So a
 * handler runs between two instructions of OCaml's, never in the
 * middle of the collector; and not in a computation that asks nothing
 * of the system, where OCaml would run it at an allocation. */
static void
note_signal(int sig)
{
	/* an interrupt again, the first one's handler not run yet: the
	 * program computes and waits nowhere, so the system's default, its
	 * end (exit_group, 130 as a shell says it) */
	if(sig == 2 && signalled[sig])
#ifdef plan9
		exits("interrupt");
#else
		ux(W == 8 ? 94 : 248, 130, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
#endif
	signalled[sig] = 1;
	signalled[0] = 1;
}

#ifdef plan9
/* A note is a string: the signal of the same meaning (Linux's number,
 * as Sys gives it here), or 0. The handler continues the program
 * (noted's NCONT, 0) for a signal ignored or noted, and lets the
 * kernel end it (NDFLT, 1) for any other. */
static char note_how[65];

static void
note_handler(void *ureg, char *note)
{
	int sig;

	USED(ureg);
	sig = strncmp(note, "interrupt", 9) == 0 ? 2 : strncmp(note, "hangup", 6) == 0 ? 1 :
		strncmp(note, "alarm", 5) == 0 ? 14 : 0;
	if(sig == 0 || note_how[sig] == 0)
		noted(1);
	if(note_how[sig] == 2)
		note_signal(sig);
	noted(0);
}
#endif

#ifndef __GNUC__
/* rt_sigaction, by its number: the handler, no flag (a system call
 * interrupted says so, and is not started again), no mask */
static void
set_signal(int sig, int how)
{
	value act[5];	/* handler, flags, restorer, and a mask of 64 bits */

	act[0] = how == 0 ? 0 : how == 1 ? 1 : (value)note_signal;
	act[1] = act[2] = act[3] = act[4] = 0;
#ifdef plan9
	/* Plan 9's are notes: one handler for all (note_handler), which
	 * looks here for what to do with each */
	USED(act);
	if(sig > 0 && sig < 65)
		note_how[sig] = how;
	notify(note_handler);
#else
	ux(W == 8 ? 134 : 174, sig, (value)act, 0, 8, 0, 0);
#endif
}
#endif

/* how: 0 the system's default, 1 ignored, 2 noted */
value
ml_signal(value sig, value how)
{
	set_signal(Long_val(sig), Long_val(how));
	return Val_unit;
}

/* a signal noted, forgotten here, or 0 */
value
ml_signal_pending(value unit)
{
	int s;

	if(!signalled[0])	/* none: asked after each system call (Unix's check) */
		return Val_int(0);
	signalled[0] = 0;	/* before the look: a signal coming meanwhile sets it again */
	for(s = 1; s < 65; s++)
		if(signalled[s]){
			signalled[s] = 0;
			signalled[0] = 1;
			return Val_int(s);
		}
	return Val_int(0);
}
languages/ml/runtime/typed.c
10002
/* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. */
/* A part of mini-ml's runtime: runtime.c includes it. */

/*****************************************************************************/
/* An exception's arguments by their types */
/*****************************************************************************/

/* plan_debugger.md, stage 5: an uncaught exception says its arguments
 * as OCaml's toplevel says values,
 *     Bad(Rect (3, -4), {x = 1; y = 2; name = "origin"}, [1; 2], Some "why")
 * where their words say Bad(#1(3, -4), (1, 2, "origin"), (1, (2, 0)),
 * ("why")). The types are mini-ml -g's descriptions (Acid_ml), acid's
 * text in the program's .acid (mini-ld -g; frames.c finds it by the
 * table), lines of lists:
 *     mltypes = append mltypes, {"Typed.shape", {}, "variant",
 *         {"Empty"}, {"Circle", {"float"}}, {"Rect", {"int"}, {"int"}}};
 *     mlexns = append mlexns, {"Typed.Bad", {"Typed.shape"}, ...};
 * an exception found by its block's symbol (its value's first field).
 * The text is read in place, an element a pointer to its '{' or its
 * '"'. Nothing is allocated while a value is printed: it stays where it
 * is. Without a description (no table, an exception of a unit not
 * compiled with -g, a value not of its type's shape): the words.
 * port.acid's mlt prints a value by the same descriptions, in acid.
 * Here, not in Printexc: the runtime is in every program, where
 * Printexc and the String it needs are 190 KB a hello world does not
 * link (its to_string asks here, ml_exn_string). */

static char xbuf[1024];
static int xlen;

static void
xput(char *s, int n)
{
	int i;

	for(i = 0; i < n && xlen < sizeof xbuf - 1; i++)
		xbuf[xlen++] = s[i];
}

static void
xs(char *s)
{
	xput(s, strlen(s));
}

static void
xint(value n)
{
	char d[24];
	int s;

	if(n < 0){
		s = digits(-(uvalue)n, 10, 0, d, 24);
		d[--s] = '-';
	}else
		s = digits(n, 10, 0, d, 24);
	xput(d + s, 24 - s);
}

/* a character as %S and %C write it: the quote, the backslash, a line */
static void
xchar(int c, int quote)
{
	char e[2];

	e[0] = '\\';
	e[1] = c == '\n' ? 'n' : c == '\t' ? 't' : c;
	if(c == quote || c == '\\' || c == '\n' || c == '\t')
		xput(e, 2);
	else{
		e[0] = c;
		xput(e, 1);
	}
}

static void
xstring(value v)
{
	uchar *p;
	value i;

	p = (uchar*)Bytes(v);
	xs("\"");
	for(i = 0; i < length(v); i++)
		xchar(p[i], '"');
	xs("\"");
}

/* string_of_float's */
static void
xfloat(value v)
{
	char b[64];

	snprint(b, sizeof b, "%.12g", Double_val(v));
	xs(b);
}

/* a value by its words: an integer, a string, a float, a block's
 * fields (#tag first when it is not 0), d blocks deep */
static void
xwords(value v, int d)
{
	value i;

	if(Is_int(v))
		xint(Long_val(v));
	else if(Tag(v) == String_tag)
		xstring(v);
	else if(Tag(v) == Double_tag)
		xfloat(v);
	else if(Tag(v) == Closure_tag)
		xs("<fun>");
	else if(Tag(v) > Closure_tag)
		xs("_");
	else if(d == 0)
		xs("...");
	else{
		if(Tag(v) != 0){
			xs("#");
			xint(Tag(v));
		}
		xs("(");
		for(i = 0; i < Wosize(v); i++){
			if(i > 0)
				xs(", ");
			xwords(Field(v, i), d - 1);
		}
		xs(")");
	}
}

/* the descriptions' text, a list's elements: the one after e, past
 * the commas; nil at the list's end */
static char*
elskip(char *p)
{
	while(*p == ' ' || *p == ',' || *p == '\n')
		p++;
	return *p == '{' || *p == '"' ? p : nil;
}

static char*
elafter(char *e)
{
	int depth;

	if(*e == '"'){
		for(e++; *e != 0 && *e != '"'; e++)
			;
		return *e != 0 ? e + 1 : e;
	}
	depth = 0;
	for(; *e != 0; e++){
		if(*e == '"')
			e = elafter(e) - 1;
		else if(*e == '{')
			depth++;
		else if(*e == '}' && --depth == 0)
			return e + 1;
	}
	return e;
}

static char*
elfirst(char *l)
{
	return l != nil && *l == '{' ? elskip(l + 1) : nil;
}

static char*
elnext(char *e)
{
	return e != nil ? elskip(elafter(e)) : nil;
}

static char*
elnth(char *l, int n)
{
	char *e;

	for(e = elfirst(l); e != nil && n > 0; n--)
		e = elnext(e);
	return e;
}

static int
elcount(char *l)
{
	char *e;
	int n;

	n = 0;
	for(e = elfirst(l); e != nil; e = elnext(e))
		n++;
	return n;
}

/* whether e is the string s, of n characters */
static int
elis(char *e, char *s, int n)
{
	return e != nil && *e == '"' && memcmp(e + 1, s, n) == 0 && e[n + 1] == '"';
}

static int
eliss(char *e, char *s)
{
	return elis(e, s, strlen(s));
}

static int
ellen(char *e)
{
	char *q;

	for(q = e + 1; *q != 0 && *q != '"'; q++)
		;
	return q - e - 1;
}

/* the list on a line after key whose first element is the string name,
 * or nil (none, or no descriptions) */
static char*
described(char *key, char *name, int n)
{
#ifndef __GNUC__
	char *p;
	int k;

	k = strlen(key);
	for(p = acidtext(); p != nil && *p != 0; ){
		if(memcmp(p, key, k) == 0 && elis(elfirst(p + k), name, n))
			return p + k;
		while(*p != 0 && *p != '\n')
			p++;
		if(*p != 0)
			p++;
	}
#else
	USED(key);
	USED(name);
	USED(n);
#endif
	return nil;
}

/* a described type's variables: its params ({"'a", ...}), the type
 * that names it ({"Typed.tree", {"int"}}: the arguments after its
 * path), whose own variables are up's */
typedef struct Env Env;
struct Env {
	char *params;
	char *args;
	Env *up;
};

static void xval(value v, char *t, Env *env, int d);

/* in parentheses, what was printed since start, when it is a negative
 * number or a constructor's with arguments (OCaml's Some (-5)) */
static void
xparen(int start)
{
	int i, sp;

	sp = 0;
	for(i = start; i < xlen; i++)
		if(xbuf[i] == ' ')
			sp = 1;
	if(xlen == start || xlen + 2 >= sizeof xbuf
	|| !(xbuf[start] == '-' || (xbuf[start] >= 'A' && xbuf[start] <= 'Z' && sp)))
		return;
	memmove(xbuf + start + 1, xbuf + start, xlen - start);
	xbuf[start] = '(';
	xlen++;
	xs(")");
}

/* the fields of v from the types ts on, separated by sep */
static void
xfields(value v, char *ts, Env *env, int d, char *sep)
{
	value i;

	for(i = 0; ts != nil; i++, ts = elnext(ts)){
		if(i > 0)
			xs(sep);
		xval(Field(v, i), ts, env, d - 1);
	}
}

/* v by its type t (a list, its path first), d deep */
static void
xval(value v, char *t, Env *env, int d)
{
	char *n, *desc, *k, *e, *c;
	Env sub;
	value i;
	int at;

	/* a variable: the type it stands for */
	for(n = elfirst(t); n != nil && n[1] == '\'' && env != nil; n = elfirst(t)){
		for(e = elfirst(env->params), i = 1; e != nil && !elis(e, n + 1, ellen(n)); e = elnext(e))
			i++;
		if(e == nil)
			break;
		t = elnth(env->args, i);
		env = env->up;
	}
	if(n == nil || *n != '"' || n[1] == '\''){
		xwords(v, d);
		return;
	}
	if(d == 0){
		xs("...");
		return;
	}
	if(eliss(n, "int") && Is_int(v))
		xint(Long_val(v));
	else if(eliss(n, "char") && Is_int(v)){
		xs("'");
		xchar(Long_val(v), '\'');
		xs("'");
	}else if(eliss(n, "bool") && Is_int(v))
		xs(Long_val(v) ? "true" : "false");
	else if(eliss(n, "unit"))
		xs("()");
	else if(eliss(n, "->"))
		xs("<fun>");
	else if(eliss(n, "list")){
		xs("[");
		for(i = 0; !Is_int(v) && i < 32; i++){
			if(i > 0)
				xs("; ");
			xval(Field(v, 0), elnext(n), env, d - 1);
			v = Field(v, 1);
		}
		if(!Is_int(v))
			xs("; ...");
		xs("]");
	}else if(eliss(n, "array") && !Is_int(v) && Tag(v) == 0){
		xs("[|");
		for(i = 0; i < Wosize(v) && i < 32; i++){
			if(i > 0)
				xs("; ");
			xval(Field(v, i), elnext(n), env, d - 1);
		}
		xs("|]");
	}else if(eliss(n, "*") && !Is_int(v) && Tag(v) == 0 && Wosize(v) == elcount(t) - 1){
		xs("(");
		xfields(v, elnext(n), env, d, ", ");
		xs(")");
	}else if((eliss(n, "string") || eliss(n, "bytes")) && !Is_int(v) && Tag(v) == String_tag)
		xstring(v);
	else if(eliss(n, "float") && !Is_int(v) && Tag(v) == Double_tag)
		xfloat(v);
	else if((desc = described("mltypes = append mltypes, ", n + 1, ellen(n))) != nil
	&& elcount(elnth(desc, 1)) == elcount(t) - 1){
		/* {path, params, kind, ...} */
		sub.params = elnth(desc, 1);
		sub.args = t;
		sub.up = env;
		k = elnth(desc, 2);
		if(eliss(k, "="))
			xval(v, elnext(k), &sub, d);
		else if(eliss(k, "variant") && Is_int(v) && (e = elnth(elnext(k), Long_val(v))) != nil)
			xput(e + 1, ellen(e));
		else if(eliss(k, "variant") && !Is_int(v) && (c = elnth(desc, 4 + Tag(v))) != nil
		&& elcount(c) - 1 == Wosize(v)){
			/* {"C", t1, ...} */
			xput(elfirst(c) + 1, ellen(elfirst(c)));
			xs(" ");
			if(Wosize(v) == 1){
				at = xlen;
				xval(Field(v, 0), elnth(c, 1), &sub, d - 1);
				xparen(at);
			}else{
				xs("(");
				xfields(v, elnth(c, 1), &sub, d, ", ");
				xs(")");
			}
		}else if(eliss(k, "record") && !Is_int(v) && Tag(v) == 0 && Wosize(v) == elcount(desc) - 3){
			xs("{");
			for(i = 0, e = elnext(k); e != nil; i++, e = elnext(e)){
				if(i > 0)
					xs("; ");
				xput(elfirst(e) + 1, ellen(elfirst(e)));
				xs(" = ");
				xval(Field(v, i), elnth(e, 1), &sub, d - 1);
			}
			xs("}");
		}else
			xwords(v, d);
	}else
		xwords(v, d);
}

/* an exception, its name and its arguments, in xbuf: by their types
 * when the program describes them, else their words (a single tuple's
 * fields alone, as Match_failure's) */
static void
xexn(value exn)
{
	value id, name, b, i, start;
	char *d, *e;
#ifndef __GNUC__
	uchar *sym;
	long n;
#endif

	id = Field(exn, 0);
	name = Field(id, 0);
	xput((char*)Bytes(name), length(name));
	if(Wosize(exn) < 2)
		return;
	d = nil;
#ifndef __GNUC__
	if(acidtext() != nil && (sym = datasym((uvalue)id - sizeof(value), &n)) != nil)
		d = described("mlexns = append mlexns, ", (char*)sym, n);
#endif
	xs("(");
	if(d != nil && elcount(d) == Wosize(exn))
		for(i = 1, e = elnth(d, 1); e != nil; i++, e = elnext(e)){
			if(i > 1)
				xs(", ");
			xval(Field(exn, i), e, nil, 6);
		}
	else{
		b = exn;
		start = 1;
		if(Wosize(exn) == 2 && !Is_int(Field(exn, 1)) && Tag(Field(exn, 1)) == 0){
			b = Field(exn, 1);
			start = 0;
		}
		for(i = start; i < Wosize(b); i++){
			if(i > start)
				xs(", ");
			xwords(Field(b, i), 3);
		}
	}
	xs(")");
}

/* Printexc.to_string's, for an exception its printers do not know */
value
ml_exn_string(value exn)
{
	xlen = 0;
	xexn(exn);
	xbuf[xlen] = 0;
	return ml_string(xbuf);
}
languages/ml/runtime/unix.c

/* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. */
/* A part of mini-ml's runtime: runtime.c includes it. */

/*****************************************************************************/
/* Unix: a system call (Linux's) */
/*****************************************************************************/

/* The Unix module is OCaml (lib_core's Unix): each of its functions a
 * system call of Linux's, by its number, its structures packed and read
 * as bytes there. So here is only the call: nothing of a libc's, and
 * the same for goken's (its _syscall6) and for glibc (gnu.h's ux).
 * An argument is an int, a string or bytes (their address), or an
 * int32 or an int64 (their value: an int has 31 bits on arm). The
 * answer is the kernel's: a negative errno when it fails. */
static value
ux_arg(value v)
{
	if(Is_int(v))
		return Long_val(v);
	if(Tag(v) == Int32_tag)
		return Int32_val(v);
	if(Tag(v) == Int64_tag)
		return Int64_val(v);
	return v;
}

value
unix_syscall(value nr, value args)
{
	return Val_int(ux(Long_val(nr), ux_arg(Field(args, 0)), ux_arg(Field(args, 1)), ux_arg(Field(args, 2)),
		ux_arg(Field(args, 3)), ux_arg(Field(args, 4)), ux_arg(Field(args, 5))));
}

/* execve: its two arrays of strings, as C's, ended by nil */
static char**
ux_strings(value a)
{
	char **v;
	value i, n;

	n = Wosize(a);
	v = malloc((n + 1) * sizeof(char*));
	for(i = 0; i < n; i++)
		v[i] = (char*)Field(a, i);
	v[n] = nil;
	return v;
}

value
unix_execve(value path, value argv, value envp)
{
#ifdef plan9
	/* Plan 9's exec: no environment given (it is /env's files) */
	USED(envp);
	return Val_int(exec((char*)path, ux_strings(argv)));
#else
	return Val_int(ux(W == 8 ? 221 : 11, path, (value)ux_strings(argv), (value)ux_strings(envp), 0, 0, 0));
#endif
}

/* A thread's memory (thread_new's) is the system's (mmap, by its
 * number), n bytes of zeros. Not the C library's: its malloc (goken's,
 * a placeholder) gives 64 MB in all and takes nothing back. */
static void*
m_alloc(value n)
{
#ifdef __GNUC__
	void *p;

	p = calloc(n, 1);
	if(p == nil)
		fatal("Fatal error: out of memory\n");
	return p;
#else
	value p;

#ifdef plan9
	/* Plan 9's: the break moved up (zeros, the kernel's), not given back */
	p = (value)sbrk(n);
	if(p == -1)
		fatal("Fatal error: out of memory\n");
#else
	p = ux(W == 8 ? 222 : 192, 0, n, 3, 0x22, -1, 0);
	if(p < 0 && p > -4096)
		fatal("Fatal error: out of memory\n");
#endif
	return (void*)p;
#endif
}

/* and given back (gc.c's large blocks); not on Plan 9, whose break
 * only moves up */
static void
m_free(void *p, value n)
{
#ifdef __GNUC__
	free(p);
#else
#ifdef plan9
	USED(p);
	USED(n);
#else
	ux(W == 8 ? 215 : 91, (value)p, n, 0, 0, 0, 0);
#endif
#endif
}
languages/ml/simple/Fold.ml
7331
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Fold.mli *)

let on = ref false
let bits = ref 63

(* the constants known, by their global's symbol: the unit's and the
 * summaries' *)
let constants : (string, Scope.exp) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 64
let own : (string * Scope.expr) list ref = ref []

let reset () = Hashtbl.reset constants; own := []
let import cs = List.iter (fun (g, (e : Scope.expr)) -> Hashtbl.replace constants g e.e) cs
let exports () = List.rev !own

(* a value copied where it is used: not a string (a block, each copy
 * another one) nor a float (a block too) *)
let constant (e : Scope.expr) =
  match e.e with
  | Econst (Int _ | Char _) | Econs ({ kind = Const _; _ }, []) -> true
  | _ -> false

let cons name k (t : Scope.ty) : Scope.cons =
  { cname = name; kind = Const k; arity = 0; nconst = (if name = "()" then 1 else 2); nblock = 0;
    ctype = [], [], t; cinline = [] }

let make (e : Scope.expr) (x : Scope.exp) : Scope.expr = { e with e = x }
let int e n = make e (Econst (Int n))
let bool e b = make e (Econs ((if b then cons "true" 1 Resolve.bool_t else cons "false" 0 Resolve.bool_t), []))

let truth (e : Scope.expr) =
  match e.e with
  | Econs ({ cname = "true" | "false"; kind = Const k; _ }, []) -> Some (k = 1)
  | _ -> None

(* the target's integer: its bits, wrapped as its arithmetic does; None
 * when the host's int cannot hold it (mini-ml on arm compiling for
 * arm64: not folded there, which only costs the fold) *)
let wrap n =
  let s = 64 - !bits in
  let n = Int64.shift_right (Int64.shift_left n s) s in
  if Int64.of_int (Int64.to_int n) = n then Some (Int64.to_int n) else None

(* (a shift by bits or more, or a division by zero: the program's own,
 * left to run) *)
let int2 p a b =
  let a = Int64.of_int a and b = Int64.of_int b in
  let shift f = if b >= 0L && b < Int64.of_int !bits then Some (f a (Int64.to_int b)) else None in
  let ones = Int64.sub (Int64.shift_left 1L !bits) 1L in
  Option.bind
    (match p with
     | "%addint" -> Some (Int64.add a b)
     | "%subint" -> Some (Int64.sub a b)
     | "%mulint" -> Some (Int64.mul a b)
     | "%divint" when b <> 0L -> Some (Int64.div a b)
     | "%modint" when b <> 0L -> Some (Int64.rem a b)
     | "%andint" -> Some (Int64.logand a b)
     | "%orint" -> Some (Int64.logor a b)
     | "%xorint" -> Some (Int64.logxor a b)
     | "%lslint" -> shift Int64.shift_left
     | "%asrint" -> shift Int64.shift_right
     | "%lsrint" -> shift (fun a k -> Int64.shift_right_logical (Int64.logand a ones) k)
     | _ -> None)
    wrap

let int1 p a =
  let a = Int64.of_int a in
  Option.bind
    (match p with
     | "%negint" -> Some (Int64.neg a)
     | "%succint" -> Some (Int64.succ a)
     | "%predint" -> Some (Int64.pred a)
     | "%lnot" -> Some (Int64.lognot a)
     | _ -> None)
    wrap

(* a comparison of two constants of one type, by their order *)
let key (e : Scope.expr) =
  match e.e with
  | Econst (Int n) -> Some n
  | Econst (Char c) -> Some (Char.code c)
  | Econs ({ kind = Const k; _ }, []) -> Some k
  | _ -> None

let rel p (a : int) b =
  match p with
  | "%equal" | "%eq" -> Some (a = b)
  | "%notequal" | "%noteq" -> Some (a <> b)
  | "%lessthan" -> Some (a < b)
  | "%lessequal" -> Some (a <= b)
  | "%greaterthan" -> Some (a > b)
  | "%greaterequal" -> Some (a >= b)
  | _ -> None

let rec expr (e : Scope.expr) : Scope.expr =
  let cases cs = List.map (fun (p, g, b) -> p, Option.map expr g, expr b) cs in
  let fields fs = List.map (fun (l, x) -> l, expr x) fs in
  match e.e with
  | Evar (Global g) -> (match Hashtbl.find_opt constants g.gsym with Some c -> make e c | None -> e)
  (* a literal wrapped too, as the target reads it (the runtime's
   * int_of_string, its low bits): 0xffffffff is -1 on arm, so a summary
   * by mini-ml on Linux is the card's (old: kept whole, Chacha20's mask
   * another .inline on the card, self-mix) *)
  | Econst (Int n) -> (match wrap (Int64.of_int n) with Some m when m <> n -> int e m | _ -> e)
  | Evar _ | Econst _ -> e
  | Eapply (f, es) -> apply e (expr f) (List.map expr es)
  | Eif (c, a, b) -> (
      let c = expr c in
      match truth c, b with
      | Some true, _ -> expr a
      | Some false, Some b -> expr b
      | Some false, None -> make e (Econs (cons "()" 0 Resolve.unit_t, []))
      | None, _ -> make e (Eif (c, expr a, Option.map expr b)))
  | Elet (r, bs, b) -> make e (Elet (r, List.map (fun (p, x) -> p, expr x) bs, expr b))
  | Efunction cs -> make e (Efunction (cases cs))
  | Ematch (x, cs) -> make e (Ematch (expr x, cases cs))
  | Etry (x, cs) -> make e (Etry (expr x, cases cs))
  | Etuple es -> make e (Etuple (List.map expr es))
  | Econs (c, es) -> make e (Econs (c, List.map expr es))
  | Erecord (n, fs) -> make e (Erecord (n, fields fs))
  | Ewith (x, n, fs) -> make e (Ewith (expr x, n, fields fs))
  | Efield (x, l) -> make e (Efield (expr x, l))
  | Esetfield (a, l, b) -> make e (Esetfield (expr a, l, expr b))
  | Earray es -> make e (Earray (List.map expr es))
  | Eseq (a, b) -> make e (Eseq (expr a, expr b))
  | Ewhile (a, b) -> make e (Ewhile (expr a, expr b))
  | Efor (v, a, b, d, body) -> make e (Efor (v, expr a, expr b, d, expr body))
  | Eassert x -> make e (Eassert (expr x))
  | Econstraint (x, t) -> make e (Econstraint (expr x, t))

(* a primitive of constants computed; && and || of a constant first *)
and apply (e : Scope.expr) (f : Scope.expr) (es : Scope.expr list) =
  let folded =
    match f.e, es with
    | Evar (Prim (("%sequand" | "%sequor") as p, 2, _)), [ a; b ] -> (
        match p, truth a with
        | "%sequand", Some true | "%sequor", Some false -> Some b
        | "%sequand", Some false | "%sequor", Some true -> Some a
        | _ -> None)
    | Evar (Prim ("%boolnot", 1, _)), [ a ] -> Option.map (fun t -> bool e (not t)) (truth a)
    (* (Sys's, known when compiling: OCaml's) *)
    | Evar (Prim ("%word_size", 1, _)), [ { e = Econs (_, []); _ } ] -> Some (int e (!bits + 1))
    | Evar (Prim ("%int_size", 1, _)), [ { e = Econs (_, []); _ } ] -> Some (int e !bits)
    | Evar (Prim (p, 2, _)), [ a; b ] -> (
        match key a, key b with
        | Some x, Some y -> (
            match rel p x y, a.e, b.e with
            | Some r, _, _ -> Some (bool e r)
            | None, Econst (Int x), Econst (Int y) -> Option.map (int e) (int2 p x y)
            | None, _, _ -> None)
        | _ -> None)
    | Evar (Prim (p, 1, _)), [ { e = Econst (Int x); _ } ] -> Option.map (int e) (int1 p x)
    | _ -> None
  in
  match folded with Some x -> x | None -> make e (Eapply (f, es))

let rec var (p : Scope.pattern) = match p with Pvar v -> Some v | Pconstraint (p, _) -> var p | _ -> None

let items (its : Scope.item list) =
  List.map (fun (it : Scope.item) ->
    match it with
    | Ieval e -> Scope.Ieval (expr e)
    | Ivalue (r, bs, gs) ->
        let bs = List.map (fun (p, e) -> p, expr e) bs in
        (match r, bs, gs with
         | false, [ (p, e) ], [ ((v : Scope.var), (g : Scope.global)) ]
           when constant e && Option.map (fun (x : Scope.var) -> x.vid) (var p) = Some v.vid ->
             Hashtbl.replace constants g.gsym e.e;
             own := (g.gsym, Summary.strip e) :: !own
         | _ -> ());
        Scope.Ivalue (r, bs, gs)
    | Iexception _ | Iexternal _ -> it) its
languages/ml/simple/Fold.mli
1967
(* Constant folding, on Scope's tree before Lower: a toplevel value
 * whose definition is a constant (an integer, a character, a
 * constructor without arguments: a bool, an enumeration's) is that
 * constant where it is used; the integer primitives of constants are
 * computed, as the target's arithmetic would (31 bits on arm, 63 on
 * arm64); a comparison of constants is a bool; an if on a constant is
 * its branch. So
 *
 *   let wide = 1 lsl 20 > 1000          wide: true
 *   let mask w = if wide then w land 0xff else w
 *
 * makes mask's body w land 0xff, small enough to be inlined
 * (Lower.inline_most), with no test left in the copies. A unit's
 * constants go in its summary (Summary.t's constants), so that the
 * units after it fold them too: its directory's, and another's that
 * finds it by an -I (lib_core's Sys.word_size, %word_size).
 *
 * others:
 * ocamlopt's Closure (since 1996) gives each value an approximation,
 * Value_const among them, kept in the unit's .cmx: a constant global
 * of another unit is its constant there, a primitive of constants is
 * computed and an if on one is its branch, before and after inlining.
 * flambda does the same, and more. Here only the toplevel's values are
 * followed, not a local let's (a local constant is Lower's own: a
 * known value, no slot). *)

(* on: -O and -O3 (mkconfig's MLOPT); off: -O0, -no-fold *)
val on : bool ref

(* the target's int, in bits: 31 (arm) or 63 (arm64); %int_size's,
 * and %word_size's one more, folded or not (Lower) *)
val bits : int ref

(* a new unit: no constant known *)
val reset : unit -> unit

(* the constants of a summary read (Summary.t's constants) *)
val import : (string * Scope.expr) list -> unit

(* the items folded, in their order: a value folded is a constant for
 * the ones after it *)
val items : Scope.item list -> Scope.item list

(* the unit's own constants, by symbol, for its summary *)
val exports : unit -> (string * Scope.expr) list
languages/ml/simple/Gen.ml

(* Claude Code

(* See Gen.mli *)

open Ir

(* what differs between the machines *)
type mach = {
  arch : Asm.arch;
  w : int;                  (* a word's bytes *)
  mov : string;             (* a word's move *)
  nregs : int;              (* the stack machine's registers, from R1 *)
  tmp : int;                (* scratch *)
  vsp : int;                (* the value stack's top *)
  sp : string;
  link : string;
  frame : string;           (* TEXT's: no frame of mini-ld's *)
  aapcs : bool;             (* C's arguments: gcc's, R0-R3 then 0(SP); else 5c's, R0 then w*(i+1)(SP) *)
}

(* (vsp, R10 on arm: the value stack's top, handed to C in ml_vsp and
 * taken back after each call of it, c_bl: the conventions between ML
 * and C are listed in ssa's Emit) *)
let arm = { arch = Arm; w = 4; mov = "MOVW"; nregs = 8; tmp = 9; vsp = 10; sp = "R13"; link = "R14"; frame = "$-4"; aapcs = false }
let arm64 = { arch = Arm64; w = 8; mov = "MOV"; nregs = 15; tmp = 16; vsp = 26; sp = "RSP"; link = "R30"; frame = "$-8"; aapcs = false }
let gnu m = { m with aapcs = true }
let arch m = m.arch
let error fmt = Printf.ksprintf failwith fmt
let sprintf = Printf.sprintf

(* an ML integer tagged, in a word *)
let tagged m n =
  let v = Int64.add (Int64.mul 2L (Int64.of_int n)) 1L in
  if m.w = 4 then Int64.of_int32 (Int64.to_int32 v) else v

let round n a = (n + a - 1) / a * a

(* a slot at off (negative) from the value stack's top; on arm64 below
 * -256 its address computed in R19 first: for such an offset 7l's, and
 * so mini-ld's, constant is an ADD from SP (bugs/goken.md 24) *)
let slot_ref m off =
  if m.arch = Arm64 && off < -256 then sprintf "\tSUB\t$%d, R%d, R19\n" (-off) m.vsp, "0(R19)"
  else "", sprintf "%d(R%d)" off m.vsp
let glabels = ref 0
let glabel () = incr glabels; sprintf "M%d" !glabels

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A function *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The frames. On the value stack, f words below its top (raised by f at
 * the entry): slot 0 the closure, then the parameters, the variables,
 * and a slot per register of the stack machine, where a call or an
 * allocation spills it. On the machine stack, m bytes: the link at 0,
 * then C's outgoing arguments (5c's and 7c's: the first in R0, the
 * i-th at w*(i+1)), then a handler's record, 4 words, each from c. They
 * are known at the end, so each line is a function of them. *)
(* a raise, the exception in R0: on arm its address in R2 first (8
 * after the MOVW: the pc as an instruction reads it), where a trace's
 * walk starts (ml_raise) *)
let raise_ (arch : Asm.arch) =
  (if arch = Arm then [ "MOVW\tR15, R2" ] else []) @ [ "B\tml_raise(SB)" ]

(* a handler's raise of what it did not match: ml_reraise, the trace
 * kept as the first raise left it *)
let reraise_ = [ "B\tml_reraise(SB)" ]

let func m out (fn : func) =
  let w = m.w and mov = m.mov and vsp = m.vsp in
  let lines = ref [] in
  let line f = lines := f :: !lines in
  let ins fmt = Printf.ksprintf (fun s -> line (fun _ _ _ -> "\t" ^ s ^ "\n")) fmt in
  let lab l = line (fun _ _ _ -> l ^ ":\n") in
  let sp = ref 0 and maxsp = ref 0 and tries = ref 0 and cargs = ref (if m.arch = Arm then 1 else 0) and dead = ref false in
  let depth_at = Hashtbl.create 16 and catch_at = Hashtbl.create 4 in
  let get i r = line (fun f _ _ -> let pre, a = slot_ref m (w * (i - f)) in sprintf "%s\t%s\t%s, R%d\n" pre mov a r) in
  let put r i = line (fun f _ _ -> let pre, a = slot_ref m (w * (i - f)) in sprintf "%s\t%s\tR%d, %s\n" pre mov r a) in
  let spill_slot r = fn.nslots + r - 1 in
  let push () =
    incr sp;
    if !sp > m.nregs then error "%s: an expression too deep" fn.name;
    maxsp := max !maxsp !sp;
    !sp in
  let spill () = for r = 1 to !sp do put r (spill_slot r) done in
  let reload () = for r = 1 to !sp do get (spill_slot r) r done in
  let result () = ins "%s\tR0, R%d" mov (push ()) in
  let jump l = Hashtbl.replace depth_at l !sp in
  (* the link's slot: 0, or above gcc's outgoing arguments (4 words) *)
  let link = if m.aapcs then 4 * w else 0 in
  let epilogue () =
    line (fun f _ _ -> sprintf "\tSUB\t$%d, R%d\n" (w * f) vsp);
    ins "%s\t%d(%s), %s" mov link m.sp m.link;
    line (fun _ m' _ -> sprintf "\tADD\t$%d, %s\n" m' m.sp)
  in
  let record c k = c + (4 * w * k) in
  let at k d f = line (fun _ _ c -> "\t" ^ f (record c k + d) ^ "\n") in
  let shift = function Lsl -> (match m.arch with Arm -> "SLL" | Arm64 -> "LSL") | Lsr -> (match m.arch with Arm -> "SRL" | Arm64 -> "LSR")
                     | _ -> (match m.arch with Arm -> "SRA" | Arm64 -> "ASR") in
  let cond = function Eq -> "EQ" | Ne -> "NE" | Lt -> "LT" | Le -> "LE" | Gt -> "GT" | Ge -> "GE" in
  (* r's truth after a CMP, 1 (true) or 0, tagged, into d *)
  let set_bool r d =
    match m.arch with
    | Arm -> ins "MOVW\t$1, R%d" d; ins "MOVW.%s\t$3, R%d" (cond r) d
    | Arm64 -> ins "MOV\t$3, R%d" d; ins "B%s\t2(PC)" (cond r); ins "MOV\t$1, R%d" d
  in
  let branch_zero nonzero r l =
    match m.arch with
    | Arm -> ins "CMP\t$0, R%d" r; ins "%s\t%s" (if nonzero then "BNE" else "BEQ") l
    | Arm64 -> ins "%s\tR%d, %s" (if nonzero then "CBNZ" else "CBZ") r l
  in
  (* a call of C: the value stack's top handed over in ml_vsp, and
   * taken back after, the C free to use its register (ssa's Emit) *)
  let c_bl f =
    ins "%s\tR%d, ml_vsp(SB)" mov vsp;
    ins "BL\t%s(SB)" f;
    ins "%s\tml_vsp(SB), R%d" mov vsp
  in
  (* a call of C: its arguments from the slots, a..., R0 first *)
  let call_c f n =
    cargs := max !cargs n;
    get (spill_slot !sp) 0;
    for k = 1 to n - 1 do
      if m.aapcs && k < 4 then get (spill_slot (!sp - k)) k
      else (get (spill_slot (!sp - k)) m.tmp; ins "%s\tR%d, %d(%s)" mov m.tmp (if m.aapcs then w * (k - 4) else w * (k + 1)) m.sp)
    done;
    sp := !sp - n;
    c_bl f
  in
  (* a b by a op b in b's register *)
  let bin f = let a = !sp in decr sp; f a !sp in
  (* (the runtime's function for each of Lower's primitives: their
   * instructions where they are used, open-coded, are ssa's Emit's;
   * here a call each, the simple path)
   * old: Float2, Float1, FloatOfInt, IntOfFloat, Alloc and a float's
   * Poly compare in place too, ByteGet, ByteSet, StrLen and FloatCmp
   * always: Emit's ways, removed 2026-10-27 *)
  let op o =
    let a = !sp in
    match o with
    | Add -> bin (fun a b -> ins "ADD\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a b; ins "SUB\t$1, R%d" b)
    | Sub -> bin (fun a b -> ins "SUB\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a b; ins "ADD\t$1, R%d" b)
    | Mul -> bin (fun a b -> ins "SUB\t$1, R%d" a; ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Asr) b; ins "MUL\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a b; ins "ADD\t$1, R%d" b)
    | Div | Mod ->
        bin (fun a b ->
          ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Asr) a;
          ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Asr) b;
          ins "%s\tR%d, R%d, R%d" (match m.arch, o with Arm, Div -> "DIV" | Arm, _ -> "MOD" | _, Div -> "SDIV" | _ -> "REM") b a b;
          ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Lsl) b;
          ins "ADD\t$1, R%d" b)
    | And -> bin (fun a b -> ins "AND\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a b)
    | Or -> bin (fun a b -> ins "ORR\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a b)
    | Xor -> bin (fun a b -> ins "EOR\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a b; ins "ORR\t$1, R%d" b)
    | Lsl -> bin (fun a b -> ins "SUB\t$1, R%d" a; ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Asr) b; ins "%s\tR%d, R%d, R%d" (shift Lsl) b a b; ins "ORR\t$1, R%d" b)
    | Lsr | Asr -> bin (fun a b -> ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Asr) b; ins "%s\tR%d, R%d, R%d" (shift o) b a b; ins "ORR\t$1, R%d" b)
    | Cmp r -> bin (fun a b -> ins "CMP\tR%d, R%d" b a; set_bool r b)
    | Poly r ->
        (* integers compared here, the others by the runtime *)
        bin (fun a b ->
          let slow = glabel () and ok = glabel () in
          ins "AND\tR%d, R%d, R%d" b a m.tmp;
          ins "AND\t$1, R%d" m.tmp;
          branch_zero false m.tmp slow;
          ins "CMP\tR%d, R%d" b a;
          set_bool r b;
          ins "B\t%s" ok;
          lab slow;
          incr sp;
          spill ();
          call_c (Lower.poly_function r) 2;
          reload ();
          incr sp;
          ins "%s\tR0, R%d" mov !sp;
          lab ok)
    | Neg -> (match m.arch with Arm -> ins "RSB\t$0, R%d, R%d" a a | Arm64 -> ins "NEG\tR%d, R%d" a a); ins "ADD\t$2, R%d" a
    | Not -> ins "EOR\t$2, R%d" a
    | IsInt -> ins "AND\t$1, R%d" a; ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Lsl) a; ins "ORR\t$1, R%d" a
    | Tag -> ins "MOVBU\t%d(R%d), R%d" (-w) a a; ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Lsl) a; ins "ORR\t$1, R%d" a
    | Size -> ins "%s\t%d(R%d), R%d" mov (-w) a a; ins "%s\t$10, R%d" (shift Lsr) a; ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Lsl) a; ins "ORR\t$1, R%d" a
  in
  (* a block's i-th field's address into i's register, the index
   * checked against the block's size *)
  let index b i =
    ins "%s\t%d(R%d), R%d" mov (-w) b m.tmp;
    ins "%s\t$10, R%d" (shift Lsr) m.tmp;
    ins "%s\t$1, R%d" (shift Asr) i;
    ins "CMP\tR%d, R%d" m.tmp i;
    ins "BLO\t2(PC)";
    ins "BL\tcaml_array_bound_error(SB)";
    ins "%s\t$%d, R%d" (shift Lsl) (if w = 4 then 2 else 3) i;
    ins "ADD\tR%d, R%d" b i
  in
  (* OPTIMIZATION (generations: the runtime's gc.c): a block stored in
   * a field, ml_modify called (the start object's: it remembers the
   * field if the block is young and the field old), its value in R0
   * and the field's address, put by [field], in the scratch register;
   * nothing when the value is an integer. Not with gcc's C (-gas), whose
   * runtime has one generation. *)
  let modify v field =
    if not m.aapcs then begin
      let skip = glabel () in
      ins "AND\t$1, R%d, R0" v;
      branch_zero true 0 skip;
      ins "%s\tR%d, R0" mov v;
      field ();
      ins "BL\tml_modify(SB)";
      lab skip
    end
  in
  List.iter (fun i ->
    match i with
    | Label l ->
        (* after a jump, the depth the label was jumped to with *)
        (match Hashtbl.find_opt depth_at l with Some d when !dead -> sp := d | _ -> ());
        dead := false;
        lab (sprintf "L%d" l)
    | Catch k -> dead := false; sp := Hashtbl.find catch_at k; reload (); result ()
    (* (kept after a jump: the code after the next label is its line's) *)
    | Line n -> line (fun _ _ _ -> sprintf "\t// line %d\n" n)
    | Site _ -> ()
    | _ when !dead -> ()
    | Int n -> ins "%s\t$%Ld, R%d" mov (tagged m n) (push ())
    | Block s -> ins "%s\t$%s+%d(SB), R%d" mov s w (push ())
    | Sym s -> ins "%s\t$%s(SB), R%d" mov s (push ())
    | Get i -> get i (push ())
    | Set i -> put !sp i; decr sp
    | GetG g -> ins "%s\t%s(SB), R%d" mov g (push ())
    | SetG g -> ins "%s\tR%d, %s(SB)" mov !sp g; decr sp
    | Field k -> ins "%s\t%d(R%d), R%d" mov (w * k) !sp !sp
    | SetField (k, imm) ->
        let b = !sp in
        ins "%s\tR%d, %d(R%d)" mov (b - 1) (w * k) b;
        if not imm then modify (b - 1) (fun () -> ins "ADD\t$%d, R%d, R%d" (w * k) b m.tmp);
        sp := b - 2
    | Index -> let b = !sp in decr sp; index b !sp; ins "%s\t0(R%d), R%d" mov !sp !sp
    | SetIndex imm ->
        let b = !sp in
        index b (b - 1);
        ins "%s\tR%d, 0(R%d)" mov (b - 2) (b - 1);
        if not imm then modify (b - 2) (fun () -> ins "%s\tR%d, R%d" mov (b - 1) m.tmp);
        sp := b - 3
    (* the runtime's function, by the operands' count (a Float.Array's
     * float: a new float read, none written; ssa's Unbox: the
     * processor's load and store) *)
    | StrLen | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | IntOfFloat | FloatRound _
    | Int32 Neg | Int32OfInt | Int32ToInt ->
        spill (); call_c (Lower.runtime_function i) 1; reload (); result ()
    | ByteGet _ | FloatCmp _ | Float2 _ | FloatIndex _ | Int32 _ | BytesGet _ | MulHigh ->
        spill (); call_c (Lower.runtime_function i) 2; reload (); result ()
    | FloatCall (_, _, n) ->
        spill (); call_c (Lower.runtime_function i) n; reload (); result ()
    | ByteSet _ | FloatSetIndex _ | BytesSet _ ->
        spill (); call_c (Lower.runtime_function i) 3; reload ()
    | Alloc (tag, n) ->
        (* the collector may run: every value in a slot, the fields read back *)
        spill ();
        cargs := max !cargs 2;
        ins "%s\t$%d, R0" mov n;
        if m.aapcs then ins "%s\t$%d, R1" mov tag
        else (ins "%s\t$%d, R%d" mov tag m.tmp; ins "%s\tR%d, %d(%s)" mov m.tmp (2 * w) m.sp);
        c_bl "ml_alloc";
        for k = 0 to n - 1 do get (spill_slot (!sp - k)) m.tmp; ins "%s\tR%d, %d(R0)" mov m.tmp (w * k) done;
        sp := !sp - n;
        reload ();
        result ()
    | Op o -> op o
    | Call (t, slots, tail) ->
        spill ();
        List.iteri (fun k s -> if k <= m.nregs then get s k) slots;
        (* the arguments past the registers: each where the callee's
         * slot k will be, k words above the top (its frame starts at
         * the top), and its entry leaves them there. Nothing allocates
         * before it raises the top, so they need not be seen by the
         * collector meanwhile. A tail call's callee has its frame
         * where this one's is: they are copied down into this frame's
         * slots after all are read, so that none is overwritten
         * before it is. *)
        let extra = List.filteri (fun k _ -> k > m.nregs) (List.mapi (fun k s -> k, s) slots) in
        List.iter (fun (k, s) -> get s m.tmp; ins "%s\tR%d, %d(R%d)" mov m.tmp (w * k) vsp) extra;
        if tail then List.iter (fun (k, _) -> ins "%s\t%d(R%d), R%d" mov (w * k) vsp m.tmp; put m.tmp k) extra;
        let target = match t with Direct f -> f ^ "(SB)" | Code k -> ins "%s\t%d(R0), R%d" mov (w * k) m.tmp; sprintf "(R%d)" m.tmp in
        if tail then (epilogue (); ins "B\t%s" target; dead := true) else (ins "BL\t%s" target; reload (); result ())
    | CallC (f, n) -> spill (); call_c f n; reload (); result ()
    | Jmp l -> jump l; ins "B\tL%d" l; dead := true
    | Jz l -> let r = !sp in decr sp; jump l; ins "CMP\t$1, R%d" r; ins "BEQ\tL%d" l
    | Jnz l -> let r = !sp in decr sp; jump l; ins "CMP\t$1, R%d" r; ins "BNE\tL%d" l
    (* as Emit's *)
    | Switch ls ->
        let r = !sp in
        decr sp;
        List.iter jump ls;
        ins "%s\t$1, R%d, R%d" (shift Asr) r m.tmp;
        (match m.arch with
         | Arm -> ins "CASE\tR%d" m.tmp; ins "BCASE\tL%d" (List.hd ls)
         | Arm64 -> ins "CASE\tR%d, R%d" m.tmp r);
        List.iter (fun l -> ins "BCASE\tL%d" l) ls;
        dead := true
    | Drop -> decr sp
    | Ret ->
        ins "%s\tR%d, R0" mov !sp;
        decr sp;
        epilogue ();
        ins "%s" (match m.arch with Arm -> "RET" | Arm64 -> "RET\t(R30)");
        dead := true
    | Raise -> ins "%s\tR%d, R0" mov !sp; List.iter (ins "%s") (raise_ m.arch); dead := true
    | Reraise -> ins "%s\tR%d, R0" mov !sp; List.iter (ins "%s") reraise_; dead := true
    | TryEnter (k, handler) ->
        spill ();
        Hashtbl.replace catch_at k !sp;
        jump handler;
        tries := max !tries (k + 1);
        ins "%s\t%s, R0" mov m.sp;
        at k 0 (sprintf "ADD\t$%d, R0");
        ins "BL\tml_try(SB)";
        branch_zero true 0 (sprintf "L%d" handler)
    | TryExit k -> at k (3 * w) (fun o -> sprintf "%s\t%d(%s), R%d" mov o m.sp m.tmp); ins "%s\tR%d, ml_handler(SB)" mov m.tmp)
    fn.code;
  if m.aapcs && !cargs > 8 then error "%s: a call of C with %d arguments" fn.name !cargs;
  let f = fn.nslots + !maxsp and c = round (max (w * (!cargs + 1)) (link + w)) 16 in
  let msize = record c !tries in
  let pr fmt = Printf.bprintf out fmt in
  (* (the function's line, for the object: CLI's lines) *)
  pr "\t// line %d\n\tTEXT\t%s(SB), %s\n" fn.line fn.name m.frame;
  pr "\tSUB\t$%d, %s\n\t%s\t%s, %d(%s)\n\tADD\t$%d, R%d\n" msize m.sp mov m.link link m.sp (w * f) vsp;
  let slot i = let pre, a = slot_ref m (w * (i - f)) in pr "%s" pre; a in
  (* (the parameters past the registers already in their slots: Call) *)
  for i = 0 to min fn.nparams m.nregs do let a = slot i in pr "\t%s\tR%d, %s\n" mov i a done;
  (* the other slots zeroed: the collector scans them *)
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> for i = fn.nparams + 1 to f - 1 do let a = slot i in pr "\tMOV\tZR, %s\n" a done
   | Arm -> if f > fn.nparams + 1 then pr "\tMOVW\t$0, R%d\n" m.tmp; for i = fn.nparams + 1 to f - 1 do pr "\tMOVW\tR%d, %s\n" m.tmp (snd (slot_ref m (w * (i - f)))) done);
  List.iter (fun l -> Buffer.add_string out (l f msize c)) (List.rev !lines)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Data *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let header n tag = string_of_int ((n lsl 10) lor tag)

let words m out sym ws =
  List.iteri (fun i v -> Printf.bprintf out "\tDATA\t%s+%d(SB)/%d, $%s\n" sym (m.w * i) m.w v) ws;
  Printf.bprintf out "\tGLOBL\t%s(SB), $%d\n" sym (m.w * List.length ws)

let datum m out = function
  | String (sym, s) ->
      (* its words, the last byte the number of the others that are padding *)
      let n = (String.length s / m.w) + 1 in
      let b = Bytes.make (m.w * n) '\000' in
      Bytes.blit_string s 0 b 0 (String.length s);
      Bytes.set b ((m.w * n) - 1) (Char.chr ((m.w * n) - 1 - String.length s));
      let word i = if m.w = 4 then Int32.to_string (Bytes.get_int32_le b (4 * i)) else Int64.to_string (Bytes.get_int64_le b (8 * i)) in
      words m out sym (header n 252 :: List.init n word)
  | Float (sym, f) ->
      let bits = Int64.bits_of_float (float_of_string f) in
      if m.w = 8 then words m out sym [ header 1 253; Int64.to_string bits ]
      else words m out sym [ header 2 253; Int64.to_string (Int64.logand bits 0xffffffffL); Int64.to_string (Int64.shift_right_logical bits 32) ]
  (* the runtime's Int32_tag and Int64_tag; an int32 in a word, its sign
   * extended; 0xffffffffL is OCaml's -1l *)
  | Boxed_int (sym, 32, n) -> words m out sym [ header 1 254; Int32.to_string (Int32.of_string n) ]
  | Boxed_int (sym, _, n) ->
      let bits = Int64.of_string n in
      if m.w = 8 then words m out sym [ header 1 255; Int64.to_string bits ]
      else words m out sym [ header 2 255; Int64.to_string (Int64.logand bits 0xffffffffL); Int64.to_string (Int64.shift_right_logical bits 32) ]
  | Closure (sym, entry, code) -> words m out sym [ header 2 247; entry ^ "(SB)"; code ^ "(SB)" ]
  | Exception (sym, name) -> words m out sym [ header 1 0; sprintf "%s+%d(SB)" name m.w ]
  | Global (sym, None) -> Printf.bprintf out "\tGLOBL\t%s(SB), $%d\n" sym m.w
  | Global (sym, Some b) -> words m out sym [ sprintf "%s+%d(SB)" b m.w ]
  | Roots (sym, gs) -> words m out sym (string_of_int (List.length gs) :: List.map (fun g -> g ^ "(SB)") gs)

let unit_ m (u : unit_) =
  let out = Buffer.create 65536 in
  List.iter (func m out) u.funcs;
  List.iter (datum m out) u.data;
  Buffer.contents out

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The program's start *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let startup m compile units =
  let out = Buffer.create 4096 in
  let pr fmt = Printf.bprintf out fmt in
  let mov = m.mov and w = m.w and t = m.tmp in
  (* from C: the value stack's base, then the units' initializations *)
  pr "\tTEXT\tml_start(SB), %s\n\t%s\tR0, R%d\n\tB\tml_program(SB)\n" m.frame mov m.vsp;
  (* the handler's record in R0: SP, the value stack's top, the return
   * address (where raise returns), the previous record *)
  pr "\tTEXT\tml_try(SB), %s\n" m.frame;
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tMOV\tRSP, R%d\n\tMOV\tR%d, 0(R0)\n" t t
   | Arm -> pr "\tMOVW\tR13, 0(R0)\n");
  pr "\t%s\tR%d, %d(R0)\n\t%s\t%s, %d(R0)\n\t%s\tml_handler(SB), R%d\n\t%s\tR%d, %d(R0)\n" mov m.vsp w mov m.link (2 * w) mov t mov t (3 * w);
  pr "\t%s\tR0, ml_handler(SB)\n\t%s\t$0, R0\n\t%s\n" mov mov (match m.arch with Arm -> "RET" | Arm64 -> "RET\t(R30)");
  (* the exception in R0: back to the latest record *)
  (* (first, for a trace, when the runtime asks (ml_tracing): the 64
   * top words of the machine's stack kept in ml_raise_words, or those
   * up to the handler's own stack pointer, and how many of the 64
   * were not there in ml_raise_left; the runtime's exceptions.c reads
   * the return addresses in them. No register is anyone's at a raise
   * but R0's exception. On arm, also the registers a walk of the
   * frames starts from (frames.c): the raise's address (in R2, 8 after
   * it: a raise's MOVW R15, R2, or ml_raise_c's), the stack pointer,
   * the link register (a leaf's caller), and the handler's stack
   * pointer, above which the frames are still there after the raise) *)
  pr "\tTEXT\tml_raise(SB), %s\n\t%s\tml_handler(SB), R%d\n" m.frame mov t;
  pr "\t%s\tml_tracing(SB), R1\n\tCMP\t$0, R1\n\tBEQ\t%d(PC)\n" mov (match m.arch with Arm -> 19 | Arm64 -> 15);
  if m.arch = Arm then
    pr "\tMOVW\tR2, ml_raise_pc(SB)\n\tMOVW\tR13, ml_raise_sp(SB)\n\tMOVW\tR14, ml_raise_lr(SB)\n";
  pr "\t%s\t0(R%d), R1\n" mov t;
  if m.arch = Arm then pr "\tMOVW\tR1, ml_raise_top(SB)\n";
  pr "\t%s\t%s, R2\n\t%s\t$ml_raise_words(SB), R3\n\t%s\t$64, R4\n" mov (match m.arch with Arm -> "R13" | Arm64 -> "RSP") mov mov;
  pr "\tCMP\tR1, R2\n\tBHS\t8(PC)\n\t%s\t0(R2), R5\n\t%s\tR5, 0(R3)\n\tADD\t$%d, R2\n\tADD\t$%d, R3\n\tSUB\t$1, R4\n\tCMP\t$0, R4\n\tBNE\t-8(PC)\n" mov mov w w;
  pr "\t%s\tR4, ml_raise_left(SB)\n" mov;
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tMOV\t0(R%d), R18\n\tMOV\tR18, RSP\n\tMOV\t8(R%d), R26\n\tMOV\t24(R%d), R18\n\tMOV\tR18, ml_handler(SB)\n\tMOV\t16(R%d), R18\n\tB\t(R18)\n" t t t t
   | Arm -> pr "\tMOVW\t0(R9), R13\n\tMOVW\t4(R9), R10\n\tMOVW\t12(R9), R14\n\tMOVW\tR14, ml_handler(SB)\n\tMOVW\t8(R9), R9\n\tB\t(R9)\n");
  (* a handler's raise of what it did not match: the same, but what a
   * trace reads is the first raise's (OCaml's reraise: the exception's
   * own place, not the handler's that passed it on) *)
  pr "\tTEXT\tml_reraise(SB), %s\n\t%s\tml_handler(SB), R%d\n" m.frame mov t;
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tMOV\t0(R%d), R18\n\tMOV\tR18, RSP\n\tMOV\t8(R%d), R26\n\tMOV\t24(R%d), R18\n\tMOV\tR18, ml_handler(SB)\n\tMOV\t16(R%d), R18\n\tB\t(R18)\n" t t t t
   | Arm -> pr "\tMOVW\t0(R9), R13\n\tMOVW\t4(R9), R10\n\tMOVW\t12(R9), R14\n\tMOVW\tR14, ml_handler(SB)\n\tMOVW\t8(R9), R9\n\tB\t(R9)\n");
  (* C's raise (the runtime's): the call's address, 8 after it in R2 as
   * a raise in ML has it *)
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_raise_c(SB), $-8\n\tB\tml_raise(SB)\n"
   | Arm -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_raise_c(SB), $-4\n\tADD\t$4, R14, R2\n\tB\tml_raise(SB)\n");
  (* from C, a function of ML's called (the runtime's callback: a
   * kernel's trap): the closure in R0 as C gave it, its argument C's
   * second, the value stack's top back in its register, the closure's
   * code for one argument. mini-ld's frame keeps the link. Not with
   * gcc's C (-gas): it keeps values in registers across a call (R4-R11),
   * which are the stack machine's. *)
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_callback(SB), $16\n\tMOV\ta+8(FP), R1\n\tMOV\tml_vsp(SB), R%d\n\tMOV\t0(R0), R%d\n\tBL\t(R%d)\n\tRETURN\n" m.vsp t t
   | Arm when m.aapcs -> ()
   | Arm -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_callback(SB), $4\n\tMOVW\ta+4(FP), R1\n\tMOVW\tml_vsp(SB), R%d\n\tMOVW\t0(R0), R%d\n\tBL\t(R%d)\n\tRET\n" m.vsp t t);
  (* from C, the runtime's thread_switch: R0 has two addresses, the
   * running thread's context and another's, each three words: the
   * machine's stack pointer, the return address, the value stack's top
   * (its register). The first saved, the second put back: the return is
   * into the other thread, where it called here (or at its start:
   * thread_new's context). C keeps nothing else in a register across a
   * call (5c's and 7c's). *)
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_swtch(SB), $-8\n\tMOV\t0(R0), R1\n\tMOV\t8(R0), R2\n\tMOV\tRSP, R%d\n\tMOV\tR%d, 0(R1)\n\tMOV\tR30, 8(R1)\n\tMOV\tR%d, 16(R1)\n\tMOV\t16(R2), R%d\n\tMOV\t8(R2), R30\n\tMOV\t0(R2), R%d\n\tMOV\tR%d, RSP\n\tRET\t(R30)\n" t t m.vsp m.vsp t t
   | Arm when m.aapcs -> ()
   | Arm -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_swtch(SB), $-4\n\tMOVW\t0(R0), R1\n\tMOVW\t4(R0), R2\n\tMOVW\tR13, 0(R1)\n\tMOVW\tR14, 4(R1)\n\tMOVW\tR%d, 8(R1)\n\tMOVW\t8(R2), R%d\n\tMOVW\t4(R2), R14\n\tMOVW\t0(R2), R13\n\tRET\n" m.vsp m.vsp);
  (* the write barrier (generations: the runtime's gc.c, and Gen's
   * modify): a block in R0 stored at the address in the scratch
   * register; the address remembered, in ml_refs, when the block is
   * young and the field not (an old block made to point to a young
   * one). Only R0 and the scratch register changed (R1 kept on the
   * machine's stack): the code that calls keeps its values in the
   * others. At the table's soon end (ml_refs_end: gc.c's refs_soon), a
   * minor collection asked for (ml_limit at ml_hp), the end the hard
   * one; at that one, the last entry written again, and ml_refs_lost
   * (the next minor collection scans the old blocks). *)
  if not m.aapcs then begin
    let sz = if m.arch = Arm then 8 else 16 in
    let old = glabel () and room = glabel () and fin = glabel () and lost = glabel () in
    pr "\tTEXT\tml_modify(SB), %s\n\tSUB\t$%d, %s\n\t%s\tR1, 0(%s)\n" m.frame sz m.sp mov m.sp;
    pr "\t%s\tml_young_lo(SB), R1\n\tCMP\tR1, R0\n\tBLO\t%s\n" mov fin;
    pr "\t%s\tml_young_hi(SB), R1\n\tCMP\tR1, R0\n\tBHS\t%s\n" mov fin;
    pr "\tCMP\tR1, R%d\n\tBHS\t%s\n\t%s\tml_young_lo(SB), R1\n\tCMP\tR1, R%d\n\tBHS\t%s\n" t old mov t fin;
    pr "%s:\n\t%s\tml_refs(SB), R1\n\t%s\tml_refs_end(SB), R0\n\tCMP\tR0, R1\n\tBLO\t%s\n" old mov mov room;
    pr "\t%s\tml_hp(SB), R0\n\t%s\tR0, ml_limit(SB)\n" mov mov;
    pr "\t%s\tml_refs_hard(SB), R0\n\tCMP\tR0, R1\n\tBEQ\t%s\n\t%s\tR0, ml_refs_end(SB)\n\tB\t%s\n" mov lost mov room;
    pr "%s:\n\tSUB\t$%d, R1\n\t%s\t$1, R0\n\t%s\tR0, ml_refs_lost(SB)\n" lost w mov mov;
    pr "%s:\n\t%s\tR%d, 0(R1)\n\tADD\t$%d, R1\n\t%s\tR1, ml_refs(SB)\n" room mov t w mov;
    pr "%s:\n\t%s\t0(%s), R1\n\tADD\t$%d, %s\n\t%s\n" fin mov m.sp sz m.sp (match m.arch with Arm -> "RET" | Arm64 -> "RET\t(R30)")
  end;
  (* the square root: the processor's instruction on arm64, correctly
   * rounded and its own NaN, as OCaml's (the C library's is computed,
   * a bit off sometimes: bugs/ix.md); the runtime's C calls here, a
   * double given and returned as 7c's and 5c's are. On arm the
   * instruction by its word (VFP's vsqrt.f64 d0, d0: 5l has no name for
   * it). *)
  (match m.arch with
   | Arm64 -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_fsqrt(SB), $0\n\tFMOVD\ta+0(FP), F0\n\tFSQRTD\tF0, F0\n\tRETURN\n"
   | Arm when m.aapcs -> ()
   | Arm -> pr "\tTEXT\tml_fsqrt(SB), $-4\n\tMOVD\ta+0(FP), F0\n\tWORD\t$0xeeb10bc0\n\tRET\n");
  (* a unit's initialization and its roots are named, not asked for
   * (mini-ld's weak, Link.weak: 32): a unit of a library that the
   * program does not use is not linked, its call below no call and its
   * roots' address 0, which the collector passes *)
  (* (not for GNU's ld, -gas: its programs are given every unit) *)
  if not m.aapcs then
    List.iter (fun u -> pr "\tGLOBL\t%s.Init(SB), $32, $0\n\tGLOBL\t%s.Roots(SB), $32, $0\n" (Lower.mangle u) (Lower.mangle u)) units;
  (* the units' initializations, in a handler printing an uncaught
   * exception *)
  let handler = 1 in
  let code =
    [ TryEnter (0, handler) ]
    @ List.concat_map (fun u -> [ Call (Direct (Lower.mangle u ^ ".Init"), [ 0 ], false); Drop ]) units
    @ [ TryExit 0; Int 0; Ret; Label handler; Catch 0; CallC ("ml_uncaught", 1); Ret ]
  in
  (* it and the curry functions (once for all the units) compiled by
   * compile: this back end's, or ssa's (CLI, -ssa) *)
  Buffer.add_string out (compile ({ name = "ml_program"; nparams = 0; nslots = 1; code; line = 0 } :: Lower.curry_funcs ()));
  words m out "ml_units" (string_of_int (List.length units) :: List.map (fun u -> Lower.mangle u ^ ".Roots(SB)") units);
  Buffer.contents out
languages/ml/simple/Gen.mli
8326
(* The stack machine into Plan 9's assembly, for arm (5) or arm64 (7):
 * TinyC's and tiny-ml's back end, a record per machine (mini-cc's
 * decision 1). The text is what -S prints and what mini-asm's parser
 * reads into the object, so that mini-ml -S f.ml | mini-asm makes
 * mini-ml f.ml's object.
 *
 * The stack machine's stack is in registers (R1..R8 on arm, R1..R15 on
 * arm64): a push a move, an operation an instruction. At a call or an
 * allocation every register goes to its slot on the value stack, where
 * the collector sees it, and comes back after. The value stack's top
 * is a register 5c and 7c never allocate (R10, R26), stored in
 * ml_vsp before C is called. Every function is TEXT $-4 or $-8, a frame
 * mini-ld leaves alone: the prologue and epilogue are the compiler's,
 * so that a tail call is the epilogue then a B.
 *
 * try is setjmp's: BL ml_try(SB) records the stack pointers, the return
 * address and the previous handler in the frame, and returns 0; raise
 * restores them from the latest record and returns there again, with
 * the exception in R0. (A BL over the handler to a label, tiny-ml's
 * way, is not a call mini-ld links.)
 *
 * A value is a word, and its low bit says which kind (the runtime's
 * mlvalues.h, OCaml's representation):
 *
 *     an integer n      2n + 1                      3 is the word 7
 *     anything else     the address of a block:   +--------+---------
 *                       a pair, a closure, a      | header | field 0 ...
 *                       string, a float...        +--------+---------
 *                                                  size << 10 | tag
 *
 * So integers have 31 bits on arm and 63 on arm64, a constructor
 * without argument is an integer, and no type is needed to walk the
 * memory: a word that is odd is skipped, an even one is followed.
 * The arithmetic works on the tagged words: x + y is ADD then SUB $1
 * ((2x+1) + (2y+1) - 1), and [Ir.Int 1] is MOVW $3.
 *
 * Two stacks. The machine's (R13 on arm) has the return addresses and
 * C's frames, and never a value; the value stack (R10) has every ML
 * value that must outlive a call. A function's start, mini-ml -S of
 * let rec sum l = ... on arm:
 *
 *     TEXT f1_sum<>(SB), $-4
 *     SUB  $16, R13            the machine's frame; the link register
 *     MOVW R14, 0(R13)         saved in it
 *     ADD  $36, R10            nine slots on the value stack:
 *     MOVW R0, -36(R10)        slot 0, the closure
 *     MOVW R1, -32(R10)        slot 1, the argument l
 *     MOVW $0, R9              and the seven others zeroed: a slot is
 *     MOVW R9, -28(R10) ...    a value at all times, or 0
 *
 * A pair made: the registers go to their slots, ml_vsp is set, and
 * ml_alloc (C) returns the block, after a collection when the heap is
 * full; the fields are stored from their slots. Every primitive of
 * the runtime is a call here (a string's byte, a float's sum, an
 * int32's): ssa's Emit writes them as instructions where they are
 * used (open coding: its section of them), and so the block taken
 * from the heap in place, ml_hp moved up and compared with ml_limit.
 * This module stays the simple path, -O0's; ssa's the -O3 one, the
 * start object's functions included (startup's compile).
 *
 * The collector is the runtime's (gc.c), but its contract is this
 * module's: its roots are the value stack from its base to ml_vsp,
 * the units' globals (the table [startup] writes) and what C
 * registered. It copies what it reaches to the other half of the
 * heap (Cheney's algorithm) and changes the roots to the new
 * addresses: hence no value in a register across a call, and none on
 * the machine's stack, where it would be neither found nor updated.
 *
 * design:
 * A stack of one's own. A collector that moves blocks must know of
 * each word of each frame whether it is a value. A compiler usually
 * says so in tables, one entry a call site (the return address, the
 * frame's size, its live slots), and the collector walks the machine
 * stack by them: OCaml's frame tables. Here an object file cannot
 * hold an instruction's address as data (mini-ld gives addresses,
 * and there are no relocations), so the values go where no table is
 * needed. It costs a store and a load around each call, and it
 * buys what plan_ml.md's decision 5 lists: no assembly in the
 * runtime, C called as C, and a process of the kernel that is two
 * pointers. Fergus Henderson (2002) described the scheme, for
 * Mercury compiled to C; LLVM offers it under the name shadow stack.
 *
 * others:
 * A collector may also not know: Hans Boehm's (1988), for C, takes
 * every word of the stack that could be an address of the heap for
 * one. It then cannot move a block, since it cannot change a word
 * that may be an integer, and a copying collector is out.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The garbage collector is John McCarthy's, for Lisp (1960): mark
 * what the roots reach, sweep the rest into a free list. Copying is
 * from the same decade (Marvin Minsky, 1963; Robert Fenichel and
 * Jerome Yochelson, 1969), and C. J. Cheney (1970) found how to do
 * it with no stack and no recursion: the copied blocks are the queue
 * of blocks still to scan, between two pointers of the new half. It
 * costs in proportion to what is alive, not to what died, which
 * suits a language that allocates as much as ML; and allocation is
 * the pointer moved above.
 *
 * modern:
 * OCaml's collector is generational: a small young heap collected
 * by copying, often, and what survives it promoted to an old heap,
 * marked and swept a slice at a time between the program's steps,
 * so that no pause is long. Most blocks die young and are never
 * copied. Here too since 2026-10-23 (gc.c): a young generation
 * collected by copying, its survivors promoted to the halves, which
 * a major collection copies whole, Cheney's still; so the program
 * holds two heaps (gc.c has the numbers: mini-ld 267 MB for a link
 * where 54 are alive). Generations need a write barrier: a block
 * stored in an old one is remembered (ml_modify, from SetField and
 * SetIndex), since the young collection does not scan the old.
 * (David Ungar, "Generation scavenging", 1984: the idea, for
 * Smalltalk; Henry Lieberman and Carl Hewitt, 1983, before.)
 *
 * others:
 * Exceptions. OCaml's native code keeps the handlers as records
 * linked through the machine's stack, the latest in a register:
 * try is two pushes, raise a few instructions, with no call; it is
 * why ML programs use exceptions for control (Not_found, Exit)
 * where a C++ programmer, whose throw walks tables frame by frame,
 * would not. ml_try is between the two: a call at each try.
 *
 * References: plan_ml.md, decisions 4 to 6; C. J. Cheney, "A
 * nonrecursive list compacting algorithm" (Communications of the
 * ACM 13(11), 1970), two pages; John McCarthy, "Recursive functions
 * of symbolic expressions and their computation by machine, part I"
 * (Communications of the ACM 3(4), 1960); Fergus Henderson,
 * "Accurate garbage collection in an uncooperative environment"
 * (ISMM 2002); Hans Boehm and Mark Weiser, "Garbage collection in an
 * uncooperative environment" (Software -- Practice and Experience
 * 18(9), 1988); Richard Jones, Antony Hosking and Eliot Moss, "The
 * Garbage Collection Handbook" (2011); Niklaus Wirth, "Compiler
 * Construction" (1996), for a stack machine's stack kept in
 * registers. *)

type mach

val arm : mach
val arm64 : mach
val arch : mach -> Asm.arch

(* the machine with gcc's calls of C (AAPCS): for -gas *)
val gnu : mach -> mach

(* a raise's instructions, the exception in R0 (Emit's too) *)
val raise_ : Asm.arch -> string list

(* a handler's raise of an exception it matched none of its cases of:
 * ml_reraise, the trace kept as the first raise left it *)
val reraise_ : string list

(* a unit's assembly *)
val unit_ : mach -> Ir.unit_ -> string

(* the program's start, from the units in their order: ml_start (C
 * calls it with the value stack's base), ml_try, ml_raise, the table
 * of the units' globals, each unit's Init in a handler that prints an
 * uncaught exception; that handler's function and the curry functions
 * compiled by the function given (unit_'s, or ssa's Emit) *)
val startup : mach -> (Ir.func list -> string) -> string list -> string

(* The stack machine Lower compiles to, as types: an expression pushes
 * its value, an operation pops its operands, statements are labels and
 * jumps. Nothing here knows the machine: an integer is an ML integer
 * (Gen tags it), a static block a symbol (Gen adds a word for its
 * value), and a frame's slots are numbers. Arguments are pushed from
 * the last, as OCaml evaluates them, so an operation's first operand
 * is on top. Opti rewrites this code, Ssa reads it, Gen and Emit write
 * its assembly.
 *
 * A function's code, as mini-ml -dir prints it (slot 0 is the
 * closure, 1 and 2 the parameters, the others the function's own):
 *
 *     let rec loop i acc = if i = 0 then acc else loop (i - 1) (acc + i)
 *
 *     Int 0; Get 1; Op (Cmp Eq); Jz 3      i = 0? (i pushed last: on top)
 *     Get 2; Ret                           acc
 *     Label 3
 *     Get 1; Get 2; Op Add; Set 3          acc + i, the last argument first
 *     Int 1; Get 1; Op Sub; Set 4          i - 1
 *     Block "cf3_loop<>"; Set 5            loop's closure, a static block
 *     Call (Direct "f3_loop<>", [5; 4; 3], true)   a tail call
 *
 * Two things to see. A call's operands are not on the stack but in
 * slots, named by the call: at a call nothing is left in a register
 * (Gen.mli says why, the collector). And = is [Cmp Eq], the
 * integers', because the type checker saw an int (Lower.immediates);
 * at a type it did not know, or with -unsafe-types, it is [Poly Eq],
 * which tests at run time whether both are integers and calls compare
 * for the others (Opti's eqs sees a constant, and makes it [Cmp Eq]).
 *
 * design:
 * A stack machine needs no decision from the compiler that makes its
 * code: no register to choose, no temporary to name, one construct
 * of the tree is one sequence of instructions whatever is around it.
 * The decisions are put off to Gen, which makes few (depth i of the
 * stack is register i). The same form is mini-cc's simple back
 * end's (its Ir), TinyC's and tiny-ml's; Ssa is what one moves to
 * when one wants to decide better.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * A stack machine between a compiler's two halves is as old as
 * Pascal's P-code (Zurich, the 1970s), which carried the language to
 * dozens of machines: the compiler made P-code, and a new machine
 * needed only its interpreter. Caml Light's ZINC and OCaml's
 * bytecode, Java's (1995) and WebAssembly (2017) are stack machines
 * for the same reason, compact and easy to make code for. Here the
 * code is not interpreted and never leaves the compiler. *)

(* -dir's printers (show, show_op) are derived (dune: ppx_deriving;
 * mini-ml: mlpp), ppx_deriving's text: (Ir.Call ((Ir.Direct "f"), [1],
 * false)); these are what a compiler without deriving is left with, as
 * xix does *)
let show_op _ = "NO DERIVING"
[@@warning "-32"]
let show _ = "NO DERIVING"
[@@warning "-32"]

type rel = Eq | Ne | Lt | Le | Gt | Ge [@@deriving show]

type op =
  | Add | Sub | Mul | Div | Mod | And | Or | Xor | Lsl | Lsr | Asr
  | Cmp of rel          (* integers *)
  | Poly of rel         (* compare's: inlined on integers, else the runtime's *)
  | Neg | Not | IsInt | Tag | Size
[@@deriving show]

(* a float's -x and abs x (Float1) *)
type float1 = Fneg | Fabs [@@deriving show]

type target = Direct of string | Code of int
[@@deriving show]

type t =
  | Int of int                        (* an ML integer, tagged by Gen *)
  | Block of string                   (* a static block's value: its symbol + a word *)
  | Sym of string                     (* a symbol's address: a function's code *)
  | Get of int | Set of int           (* a slot of the function's frame on the value stack *)
  | GetG of string | SetG of string   (* a global *)
  | Field of int                      (* a block by its field *)
  | SetField of int * bool            (* the value below the block stored in its field *)
  | Index                             (* a block, an index (ML) by the field; bounds checked *)
  | SetIndex of bool                  (* a block, an index, a value; bounds checked *)
  (* (the stores' bool: the value an immediate, an int, a char...: no
   * write barrier, the runtime's generations; Lower.immediates) *)
  (* a string's byte read and written in place, and its length
   * (Lower.strings_in_place; calls of the runtime otherwise); true: the
   * index checked, the safe accessors' *)
  | ByteGet of bool                   (* a string, an index by the byte there *)
  | ByteSet of bool                   (* a string, an index, a byte *)
  | StrLen                            (* a string by its length *)
  (* two floats by a new one, their sum, difference, product or
   * quotient; an integer by its float; a float by its integer: the
   * processor's instructions (Lower.floats_in_place); the runtime's
   * function that does the same (Lower.runtime_function: caml_addfloat...)
   * called otherwise, and when there is no room for the new float.
   * old: Float2 "caml_addfloat"..., the runtime's name for the operation *)
  | Float2 of op                      (* x, y by x op y: Add, Sub, Mul, Div *)
  | Float1 of float1                  (* x by -x, or by its absolute value *)
  | FloatOfInt
  | IntOfFloat
  | FloatCmp of rel                   (* x, y by x rel y, two floats (Lower.floats) *)
  (* a float of a Float.Array, its doubles in the block (the runtime's
   * Double_array_tag); true: the index checked. A call of the runtime
   * (ml_floatarray_get...) but in ssa's code on doubles (Unbox), where
   * it is a load and a store of the processor's *)
  | FloatIndex of bool                (* a float array, an index by the float there *)
  (* x by its floor, or its ceiling (true): the runtime's floor_float and
   * ceil_float, which ssa's Unbox makes the processor's (no call) *)
  | FloatRound of bool
  (* a function of C's math library on floats (exp, pow...): the
   * runtime's on blocks (exp_float), called in simple's code; C's on
   * doubles (exp), which ssa's Unbox calls; its arity *)
  | FloatCall of string * string * int
  (* an int32's operation by the processor's, a block taken from the
   * heap for its result (Lower.ints_in_place); the runtime's function
   * that does the same (int32_add...) called in simple's code, and when
   * there is no room. Int32ToInt's an int, no block.
   * old: Int32 ("int32_add", 2)..., the runtime's name and the arity *)
  | Int32 of op                       (* Add Sub Mul And Or Xor Lsl Asr Lsr Neg *)
  | Int32OfInt
  | Int32ToInt
  (* the bits of two ints' product above an int's (Wide.mul_high): the
   * runtime's ml_mul_high in simple's code, the processor's long
   * multiplication in ssa's (Lower.ints_in_place) *)
  | MulHigh
  (* a string's (or bytes') little-endian integer of n bytes (2 or 4) at
   * an index, checked: the 16 bits an int, the 32 an int32's block;
   * read, or written (the value below the index). Ir's own, a load or
   * a store in place in ssa's code, the runtime's caml_bytes_get16...
   * in simple's *)
  | BytesGet of int
  | BytesSet of int
  | FloatSetIndex of bool             (* a float array, an index, a float *)
  | Alloc of int * int                (* a tag, n values by the block, the top its field 0 *)
  | Op of op
  | Call of target * int list * bool  (* the slots of the closure then of the arguments; a tail call *)
  | CallC of string * int             (* the runtime's function of n arguments *)
  | Label of int | Jmp of int
  | Jz of int | Jnz of int            (* false is the ML 0 *)
  (* the top, an integer k from 0, by a jump to the k-th label: a jump
   * table (Lower.switches), CASE and BCASE as 5c's switch *)
  | Switch of int list
  | Drop
  | Ret
  | Raise                             (* the top raised; its place taken by the result, never seen *)
  (* a handler's that matched none of its cases: the exception raised
   * again, where it was first raised kept for a trace (OCaml's reraise) *)
  | Reraise
  | TryEnter of int * int             (* the k-th handler of the function, its code *)
  | TryExit of int
  | Catch of int                      (* the handler's entry: the exception pushed *)
  (* the .ml's line of the statement that follows (Lower: a sequence's
   * part, a let's, a branch's...), no code: the pc/line table's
   * (plan_debugger.md's stage 1b), "// line n" in the assembly *)
  | Line of int
  (* the call that follows is the source's application whose function
   * is at this span (Ast.span), no code: mini-analyze's, to name a call
   * of the SSA as its own facts name it (Lower.sites) *)
  | Site of int * int
[@@deriving show]

(* line: the line of its body in the .ml, what the pc/line table says
 * of its prologue and of what has no Line; 0 for the compiler's own
 * (a curry, a unit's start) *)
type func = { name : string; nparams : int; nslots : int; code : t list; line : int }

(* the static data *)
type data =
  | String of string * string         (* a string block: symbol, bytes *)
  | Float of string * string          (* a float's block: symbol, the literal *)
  | Boxed_int of string * int * string    (* an int32's or int64's block: symbol, 32 or 64, the literal *)
  | Closure of string * string * string   (* symbol: [entry code; n-ary code] *)
  | Exception of string * string      (* an exception: symbol, its name's string symbol *)
  | Global of string * string option  (* a global, statically a block's value *)
  | Roots of string * string list     (* the unit's globals, for the collector *)

type unit_ = { funcs : func list; data : data list }

open Ir

(* the runtime's function for a relation between two values that are not
 * both integers: not compare, whose order has a nan equal to itself,
 * when = and < have it equal to and below nothing *)
let poly_function = function
  | Eq -> "ml_equal" | Ne -> "ml_notequal" | Lt -> "ml_lessthan" | Le -> "ml_lessequal"
  | Gt -> "ml_greaterthan" | Ge -> "ml_greaterequal"

(* the runtime's function that does what a primitive of Ir does, the
 * one simple's code calls, and ssa's when not in place or no room *)
let runtime_function (p : Ir.t) =
  match p with
  | ByteGet _ -> "ml_string_get"
  | ByteSet _ -> "ml_string_set"
  | StrLen -> "ml_string_length"
  | Float2 Add -> "caml_addfloat" | Float2 Sub -> "caml_subfloat"
  | Float2 Mul -> "caml_mulfloat" | Float2 _ -> "caml_divfloat"
  | Float1 Fneg -> "caml_negfloat" | Float1 Fabs -> "caml_absfloat"
  | FloatOfInt -> "caml_floatofint"
  | IntOfFloat -> "caml_intoffloat"
  | FloatCmp r -> poly_function r
  | FloatIndex c -> if c then "ml_floatarray_get" else "ml_floatarray_unsafe_get"
  | FloatSetIndex c ->
      if c then "ml_floatarray_set" else "ml_floatarray_unsafe_set"
  | FloatRound c -> if c then "ceil_float" else "floor_float"
  | FloatCall (f, _, _) -> f
  | Int32 o ->
      "int32_" ^ (match o with
        | Add -> "add" | Sub -> "sub" | Mul -> "mul" | And -> "and" | Or -> "or"
        | Xor -> "xor" | Lsl -> "shift_left" | Asr -> "shift_right"
        | Lsr -> "shift_right_unsigned" | _ -> "neg")
  | Int32OfInt -> "int32_of_int"
  | Int32ToInt -> "int32_to_int"
  | MulHigh -> "ml_mul_high"
  | BytesGet n -> Printf.sprintf "caml_bytes_get%d" (8 * n)
  | BytesSet n -> Printf.sprintf "caml_bytes_set%d" (8 * n)
  | _ -> failwith "runtime_function: not a primitive"

let error fmt = Printf.ksprintf failwith fmt
let closure_tag = 247

let mangle s =
  String.concat ""
    (List.map (function ('a' .. 'z' | 'A' .. 'Z' | '0' .. '9' | '_' | '.') as c -> String.make 1 c | c -> "$" ^ string_of_int (Char.code c))
       (List.init (String.length s) (String.get s)))
