(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Alloc.mli *)

open Ssa
module IS = Set_

type loc = Reg of int | Mem of int | Nil | Dmem of int

let successors = Ssa_build.successors_of

let term_uses (b : block) = match b.term with Br (v, _, _) | Switch (v, _) | Ret v | Raise v | Reraise v -> [ v ] | Tail (_, vs) -> vs | _ -> []

(* the instructions after which the collector may have run, or which a
 * handler's entry follows *)
let safepoint = function
  | Alloc _ | Call _ | CallC _ | Op (Ir.Poly _, _) -> true
  (* a new float: the runtime's when there is no room *)
  | Prim ((Ir.Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | FloatIndex _ | FloatRound _
          | FloatCall _), _) | Box _ -> true
  (* an int32's block; to_int's, none *)
  | Prim ((Ir.Int32 _ | Int32OfInt), _) -> true
  | Prim (Ir.BytesGet 4, _) -> true
  (* C's exp on doubles: no allocation, but C's code uses the values'
   * registers *)
  | Dprim (Ir.FloatCall _, _) -> true
  | _ -> false

(* the instructions after which no double is in a register: a call of
 * ML's code, or of C's that computes with floats (the runtime's float
 * functions, compare's cmp: runtime.c's functions that use the
 * floating-point registers, by mini-cc -S; ml_alloc, the collector,
 * ml_modify and the C library's assembly use none, so an allocation
 * keeps them) *)
let clobbers = function
  | Call _ | CallC _ | Op (Ir.Poly _, _)
  | Prim ((Ir.Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | FloatIndex _ | FloatSetIndex _ | FloatRound _
          | FloatCall _), _)
  | Dprim (Ir.FloatCall _, _) -> true
  | _ -> false

let def (fn : func) v = Hashtbl.find fn.defs v

(* (off: mini-ml -own-slots) *)
let share_slots = ref true

(* (off: mini-ml -by-uses) *)
let by_density = ref true

(* the values that need no storage: a Zero is the constant 0, and a
 * constant is made where it is read (Emit's src)
 * old: match def fn v with Zero -> false | _ -> true *)
let real (fn : func) v = match def fn v with Zero | Const _ | Blk _ | Symb _ -> false | _ -> true

let uses (fn : func) v = List.filter (real fn) (Ssa_build.operands (def fn v))

(* liveness at the blocks' edges: a phi's operand live at its
 * predecessor's end, its definition at its block's start *)
let liveness (fn : func) : int IS.t array * int IS.t array =
  let real = real fn in
  let phi_ops (s : block) p = List.filter_map (fun phi -> match def fn phi with Phi ops -> List.assoc_opt p ops | _ -> None) s.phis in
  Liveness.ssa ~succs:(fun b -> successors fn.blocks.(b)) ~phis:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).phis)
    ~phi_uses:(fun s p -> List.filter real (phi_ops fn.blocks.(s) p))
    ~term_uses:(fun b -> List.filter real (term_uses fn.blocks.(b))) ~body:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).body)
    ~uses:(uses fn) (Array.length fn.blocks)

let alloc (fn : func) ~nregs ~nfregs ~base =
  let def = def fn and real = real fn and uses = uses fn in
  let double v = Hashtbl.mem fn.doubles v and word v = not (Hashtbl.mem fn.doubles v) in
  let n = Array.length fn.blocks in
  let live_in, live_out = liveness fn in
  (* what is live after each instruction; the values that must be in
   * memory: live across a safepoint (an allocation's fields too, read
   * after it), into a handler, or a parameter *)
  let after =
    Liveness.after ~term_uses:(fun b -> List.filter real (term_uses fn.blocks.(b)))
      ~body:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).body) ~uses live_out n in
  let memory = Hashtbl.create 64 and dmemory = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let words_in t s = IS.iter (fun x -> if word x then Hashtbl.replace t x ()) s
  and doubles_in t s = IS.iter (fun x -> if double x then Hashtbl.replace t x ()) s in
  Array.iter (fun (bl : block) ->
    List.iter (fun v ->
      let live = Hashtbl.find after v in
      (match def v with
       | Alloc (_, xs) -> words_in memory (IS.remove v live); List.iter (fun x -> Hashtbl.replace memory x ()) xs
       | ins when safepoint ins -> words_in memory (IS.remove v live)
       | _ -> ());
      if clobbers (def v) then doubles_in dmemory (IS.remove v live)) bl.body;
    (match bl.term with Try (_, _, h) -> IS.iter (fun x -> Hashtbl.replace memory x ()) live_in.(h) | _ -> ())) fn.blocks;
  (* OPTIMIZATION: a parameter not live across a safepoint may have a
   * register too, loaded from its slot at the entry (Emit), and not at
   * each use: an accessor's, a loop's bound...
   * old: Param _ | Caught _ -> memory *)
  Hashtbl.iter (fun v ins ->
    match ins with Caught _ -> Hashtbl.replace memory v () | _ -> ()) fn.defs;
  (* the others colored in the dominator tree's order, the lowest free
   * register not held by a value live there: optimal for SSA, whose
   * interference graph is chordal (Hack, 2006); none free, memory *)
  let idom = Ssa_build.dominators fn in
  let children = Dominators.children idom in
  (* OPTIMIZATION (the values chosen): which values get a register, the
   * most used first, a use in a loop counting 8 times one outside it;
   * each taken while no point has more of them live than there are
   * registers, so that the coloring below never fails (an SSA program's
   * interference: its colors are its most values live at once). Before,
   * the first in the dominator tree's order took them, an outer loop's
   * values those of the inner one, which lived in slots (arm's five:
   * tests/bench/pixels.ml).
   * old: let candidate v = real v && (not (Hashtbl.mem memory v)) && nregs > 0 in *)
  (* a loop: an edge back to a block that dominates its source; its
   * blocks those that reach the source without passing the head
   * (lib_code's Dominators.loop_depths) *)
  let depth =
    Dominators.loop_depths ~succs:(fun b -> successors fn.blocks.(b)) ~preds:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).preds) idom in
  let weight = Hashtbl.create 256 in
  let use v b = if real v then Hashtbl.replace weight v ((match Hashtbl.find_opt weight v with Some x -> x | None -> 0) + (1 lsl (3 * min depth.(b) 6))) in
  Array.iter (fun (bl : block) ->
    List.iter (fun v -> use v bl.id) bl.phis;
    List.iter (fun v -> use v bl.id; List.iter (fun x -> use x bl.id) (uses v)) bl.body;
    List.iter (fun x -> use x bl.id) (term_uses bl);
    List.iter (fun s ->
      List.iter (fun phi -> match def phi with Phi ops -> (match List.assoc_opt bl.id ops with Some x -> use x bl.id | None -> ()) | _ -> ()) fn.blocks.(s).phis)
      (successors bl)) fn.blocks;
  (* the points: each block's start, each instruction's end *)
  let npoints, at = Coloring.points live_in after in
  (* each class of values, the words and the doubles, its own registers
   * (a double's are the floating-point ones); busy at a definition:
   * the registers of the values live after it (defined above it in the
   * dominator tree, so colored already); an operand dying there frees
   * its own, which the definition may take (lib_code's Coloring) *)
  (* OPTIMIZATION (by density): a value's weight over the points it is
   * live at, so that a temporary, used once right after its definition,
   * comes before a value carried around the loop, which holds its
   * register through the whole loop for a few uses: in memory the first
   * costs a store and a load, the second a load at each use, and taking
   * it out frees a register at every point of the loop. Chaitin's
   * spill cost over the interference, as LLVM's and GCC's allocators
   * weigh: mini-quake's turbulent, its pixel loop's temporaries every
   * one stored and loaded, the registers its five loop values'
   * (plan_ml_annotations.md).
   * old: the weight alone (mini-ml -by-uses) *)
  let density v w =
    if not !by_density then w
    else
      let n = match Hashtbl.find_opt at v with Some l -> List.length l | None -> 0 in
      w * 1024 / (1 + n)
  in
  let colors cls nregs memory =
    let wanted = Hashtbl.fold (fun v w acc -> if cls v && not (Hashtbl.mem memory v) then (density v w, v) :: acc else acc) weight [] in
    let chosen = Coloring.choose ~npoints ~at ~nregs wanted in
    let candidate v = real v && Hashtbl.mem chosen v && nregs > 0 in
    let body_ok v = candidate v && IS.mem v (Hashtbl.find after v) in
    Coloring.walk ~children ~live_in ~phis:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).phis) ~body:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).body)
      ~candidate:(fun v -> if Hashtbl.mem after v then body_ok v else candidate v)
      ~busy:(fun v -> IS.remove v (Hashtbl.find after v)) ~hints:(fun _ -> []) nregs
  in
  let color = colors word nregs memory and dcolor = colors double nfregs dmemory in
  (* a body's value no one reads after needs no place; nor one in no
   * block, a phi Ssa_build's simplify took out, a value Unbox replaced
   * (each was a slot of the frame, zeroed at each call: Float.min's 13
   * of 15).
   * old: | None -> false *)
  let placed = Hashtbl.create 256 in
  Array.iter (fun (bl : block) -> List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace placed v ()) (bl.phis @ bl.body)) fn.blocks;
  let dead v =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt after v with
    | Some live -> not (IS.mem v live) && not (Hashtbl.mem memory v)
    | None -> not (Hashtbl.mem placed v) && (match def v with Param _ | Caught _ -> false | _ -> true)
  in
  (* OPTIMIZATION (shared slots): a word in memory takes the lowest slot
   * that no value live with it holds, nor its own operands, in the
   * registers' walk: two whose lives do not meet share one. A slot then
   * keeps a dead value until the next is written, a root the collector
   * updates as the others, which at worst keeps a block one collection
   * more. Every slot is zeroed at the entry, the collector scanning it:
   * Float.min, with three copies of sign_bit inlined (each value live
   * across a call its slot), zeroed 13 at each call where it returns
   * at its first test.
   * old: a slot each, the next one *)
  let shared = Hashtbl.create 64 in
  let in_slot v =
    word v && real v && (match def v with Param _ -> false | _ -> true) && not (Hashtbl.mem color v) && not (dead v)
    && not (Hashtbl.mem fn.raws v)
  in
  let walk () =
    Coloring.walk ~children ~live_in ~phis:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).phis) ~body:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).body)
      ~candidate:in_slot ~busy:(fun v -> IS.union (IS.remove v (Hashtbl.find after v)) (IS.of_list (uses v)))
      ~hints:(fun _ -> []) max_int
  in
  if n > 0 && !share_slots then Hashtbl.iter (fun v c -> Hashtbl.replace shared v c) (walk ());
  (* memory: the parameters their prologue slots, the others theirs
   * (shared), from base, then one each for a value the walk did not
   * reach; a double one of its own (Dmem), from 0 *)
  let nshared = Hashtbl.fold (fun _ c m -> max m (c + 1)) shared 0 in
  let slots = Hashtbl.create 64 and next = ref (base + nshared) and dnext = ref 0 in
  let loc v =
    match def v with
    | Zero | Const _ | Blk _ | Symb _ -> Nil
    | _ when dead v -> Nil
    | _ when double v -> (
        match Hashtbl.find_opt dcolor v with
        | Some c -> Reg c
        | None -> (match Hashtbl.find_opt slots v with Some s -> Dmem s | None -> let s = !dnext in incr dnext; Hashtbl.replace slots v s; Dmem s))
    | Param i ->
        (match Hashtbl.find_opt color v with Some c -> Reg c | None -> Mem i)
    (* an untagged integer (Untag) without a register: a slot the
     * collector does not scan, a double's *)
    | _ when Hashtbl.mem fn.raws v -> (
        match Hashtbl.find_opt color v with
        | Some c -> Reg c
        | None -> (match Hashtbl.find_opt slots v with Some s -> Dmem s | None -> let s = !dnext in incr dnext; Hashtbl.replace slots v s; Dmem s))
    | _ -> (
        match Hashtbl.find_opt color v with
        | Some c -> Reg c
        | None -> (
            match Hashtbl.find_opt shared v with
            | Some c -> Mem (base + c)
            | None -> (match Hashtbl.find_opt slots v with Some s -> Mem s | None -> let s = !next in incr next; Hashtbl.replace slots v s; Mem s)))
  in
  (* every value's place now, so that the frame's size is known; in the
   * values' order, not the table's: a slot's number would depend on the
   * stdlib's hash function (OCaml's, or mini-ml's own when it compiles
   * itself) *)
  List.iter (fun v -> ignore (loc v)) (List.sort compare (Hashtbl.fold (fun v _ vs -> v :: vs) fn.defs []));
  loc, !next, !dnext
languages/ml/ssa/Alloc.mli
4631
(* Where each SSA value lives (variants/ssa.md, phase 3b): a register,
 * a slot of the value stack, or nowhere (the constant 0, or a value no
 * one reads).
 *
 * Liveness first, a backward dataflow over the blocks to its fixpoint,
 * a phi's operand live at its predecessor's end and its definition at
 * its block's start. Then memory for the values the collector must
 * see: live across a safepoint (an allocation, whose fields are read
 * after it; a call of ML or of C; a polymorphic comparison, which may
 * call compare), live into a handler (a raise restores no register),
 * and the parameters (the prologue's slots). The others are colored in
 * the dominator tree's order, each the lowest register that no value
 * live after its definition holds: for SSA, whose interference graph
 * is chordal, that order colors optimally (Hack, Grund and Goos,
 * below). Which values those are is chosen first: the most used, a use
 * in a loop 8 times one outside it, each while no point has more of
 * them live than there are registers; the others live in memory. A
 * constant lives nowhere: Emit makes it where it is read. No value in a register is live across a call, so
 * every register is the caller's to save, as simple's and C's are.
 * A double (Unbox) is a class of its own, colored the same way with
 * the floating-point registers: the collector never reads one, so it
 * goes to memory only across a call (clobbers), into a slot that is
 * not the value stack's (Dmem).
 *
 * Liveness is the analysis met three times in the tree: here over
 * SSA's values, in mini-cc's Opti (regs) over a C function's
 * variables, in its Peep over the machine's registers; and once more
 * as nine Datalog rules (liveness_ssa.dl), which Ssa_facts gives the
 * facts for and [liveness] below the answers to compare.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Register allocation as the coloring of a graph is Gregory Chaitin's
 * and his colleagues' at IBM (1981): a node a value, an edge between
 * two values alive at the same time, a color a register, and a node
 * that cannot be colored is spilled to memory and the graph made
 * again. Coloring a graph with k colors is NP-complete, so every
 * such allocator is a heuristic, and a slow one. Massimiliano
 * Poletto and Vivek Sarkar's linear scan (1999) gave up the graph
 * for one walk over the values sorted by where they start, for
 * compilers that run while the program waits. Then it was seen
 * (Hack and others, 2005 and 2006) that the graph of a program in
 * SSA form is of a kind, chordal, that a greedy walk in the right
 * order colors with the fewest colors.
 *
 * modern:
 * What is left hard, and not done here: the phis. A phi is a move on
 * each edge into its block unless its operands got its register (Emit
 * makes them one parallel copy), and choosing registers so that most
 * such moves vanish (coalescing) is NP-complete again. ocamlopt colors a graph, with
 * linear scan as an option (-linscan). Go's compiler runs what its
 * source calls a version of linear scan, a greedy walk of the
 * function as one long block; LLVM's default allocator, Greedy,
 * took linear scan's place in LLVM 3.0 (2011).
 *
 * References: Sebastian Hack, Daniel Grund and Gerhard Goos,
 * "Register Allocation for Programs in SSA-Form" (Compiler
 * Construction 2006); G. Chaitin and others, "Register allocation
 * via coloring" (Computer Languages 6, 1981); M. Poletto and V.
 * Sarkar, "Linear scan register allocation" (ACM TOPLAS 21(5),
 * 1999). *)

(* a double's slot, Dmem, is not the value stack's but one of its own,
 * which the collector does not scan (Emit: on the machine stack) *)
type loc = Reg of int | Mem of int | Nil | Dmem of int

(* two values in memory whose lives do not meet share a slot (false:
 * a slot each; mini-ml -own-slots) *)
val share_slots : bool ref

(* which values get a register: by their weight over the points they
 * are live at (false: their weight alone, mini-ml -by-uses) *)
val by_density : bool ref

(* an instruction after which the collector may have run (an allocation,
 * a call) *)
val safepoint : Ssa.ins -> bool

(* nregs registers for the words and nfregs for the doubles (Unbox),
 * each numbered from 0; memory's slots from base; the frame's slots
 * then, and the doubles' slots *)
val alloc : Ssa.func -> nregs:int -> nfregs:int -> base:int -> (Ssa.value -> loc) * int * int

(* the liveness alone: for each block, the values live at its start
 * and at its end (mini-analyze -flow-answers prints it, for an analysis
 * written in Datalog to be checked against) *)
val liveness : Ssa.func -> int Set_.t array * int Set_.t array

3244
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Cse.mli *)

open Ssa

let on = ref true

(* an instruction whose value its operands alone give: not a read of
 * memory that a store changes (Field, Index, a string's byte, a
 * Float.Array's double: FloatIndex, a Dprim too), not an allocation,
 * not a call (compare's, C's exp: FloatCall). A constant too, so that
 * i * 4 and i * 4 are one: each 4 is a value of its own, and one costs
 * nothing more (Emit makes it where it is read).
 * old: Dprim _ every one: Licm moved rebirth's Float.Array stores out
 * of their loops *)
let pure ~set (ins : ins) =
  match ins with
  | Op (Ir.Poly _, _) -> false
  | Dprim ((Ir.Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | FloatCmp _ | IntOfFloat
           | FloatRound _), _) -> true
  | Const _ | Op _ | Tag _ | Unbox _ -> true
  | GetG g -> not (set g)
  | _ -> false

let handler (fn : func) =
  Array.exists (fun (b : block) ->
    match b.term with Try _ -> true | _ -> false) fn.blocks

(* (a global the function sets, its Init: read again after) *)
let sets (fn : func) =
  let gs = Hashtbl.create 8 in
  Hashtbl.iter (fun _ ins ->
    match ins with SetG (g, _) -> Hashtbl.replace gs g () | _ -> ()) fn.defs;
  Hashtbl.mem gs

(* (not a function with a handler, as Untag: its values in memory at
 * each raise, the handler entered from wherever its body raised) *)
let func (fn : func) : func =
  if (not !on) || handler fn then fn
  else begin
    let n = Array.length fn.blocks in
    let idom = Ssa_build.dominators fn in
    let children = Array.make n [] in
    Array.iteri (fun b d ->
      if b <> 0 && d >= 0 then children.(d) <- b :: children.(d)) idom;
    let set = sets fn in
    let same = Hashtbl.create 16 in
    let rep v = match Hashtbl.find_opt same v with Some r -> r | None -> v in
    let def v = Hashtbl.find fn.defs v in
    (* the pure instructions of the blocks that dominate this one, by
     * their text, their operands already the first of each, and what
     * the value is: one text may be a word, an untagged integer
     * (Untag's Add of a tagged and an untagged) or a double *)
    let seen = Hashtbl.create 64 in
    let rec walk b =
      let blk = fn.blocks.(b) in
      let added = ref [] in
      blk.body <- List.filter (fun v ->
        let ins = Ssa_build.map_ins rep (def v) in
        Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v ins;
        if not (pure ~set ins) then true
        else
          let key = ins, Hashtbl.mem fn.raws v, Hashtbl.mem fn.doubles v in
          match Hashtbl.find_opt seen key with
          | Some r -> Hashtbl.replace same v r; false
          | None -> Hashtbl.add seen key v; added := key :: !added; true)
        blk.body;
      List.iter walk children.(b);
      List.iter (Hashtbl.remove seen) !added
    in
    if n > 0 then walk 0;
    (* (a phi's operand may come from a block walked after it: a loop's) *)
    if Hashtbl.length same > 0 then begin
      Array.iter (fun (blk : block) ->
        List.iter (fun v ->
          Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v (Ssa_build.map_ins rep (def v))) blk.phis;
        blk.term <- Ssa_build.map_term rep blk.term) fn.blocks;
      Hashtbl.iter (fun v _ -> Hashtbl.remove fn.defs v) same
    end;
    fn
  end
languages/ml/ssa/Cse.mli
2406
(* A computation made twice made once (plan_ml_speed.md, stage 3): in
 * a function's SSA form, an instruction of the same operation and
 * operands as one in a block that dominates it, or before it in its
 * own block, is that one's value, and goes. Its uses read the first.
 * Only the pure instructions: the integers' and the doubles'
 * operations, a tag, a float's double, a global the function does not
 * set; not a field, an array's element or a byte (a store between
 * may change it), nor an allocation or a call.
 *
 *     let f a i = a.(i * 4 + 1) + a.(i * 4 + 2)
 *
 * computes i * 4 once, where the stack code made it twice. A constant
 * is numbered too: each 4 is a value of its own, and the two products'
 * operands are then one.
 *
 * Not, for now, a great optimizer in practice: alone, mini-doom's and
 * mini-quake's frames 0.996 and 0.995, mini-ml compiling 0.999, the
 * programs 0.5% smaller (with Licm 0.990 and 0.991); ix's code
 * computes few things twice where this sees them, and what a loop does
 * at each turn again is mostly memory's (a field, an element: not
 * taken) or the registers' (arm's five). Kept as the classic pass it
 * is, and for the code later passes may give it (inlining, a load no
 * store changes). bench/matrix.ml shows it at work: c's index once for
 * its read and its write, 0.870 alone, 0.793 with Licm.
 *
 * others:
 * The walk of the dominator tree with a table of the expressions
 * seen, each removed on the way back, is the classic dominator-based
 * value numbering (Briggs, Cooper and Simpson, 1997). ocamlopt's CSE
 * (asmcomp/CSEgen.ml, since 4.03) is per extended basic block, on Mach
 * code, and also knows which loads no store has changed. LLVM's GVN
 * and GCC's FRE number values across the whole function, through
 * memory too.
 *
 * References: P. Briggs, K. Cooper and L. T. Simpson, "Value
 * Numbering" (Software: Practice and Experience 27(6), 1997). *)

(* on, unless mini-ml -no-cse *)
val on : bool ref

(* an instruction whose value its operands alone give (set: a global
 * the function sets, read again after); Licm's too *)
val pure : set:(string -> bool) -> Ssa.ins -> bool

(* the function has a handler (a try); the globals it sets (Init) *)
val handler : Ssa.func -> bool
val sets : Ssa.func -> string -> bool

(* the function with its computations made twice removed, in place *)
val func : Ssa.func -> Ssa.func

(* Claude Code
