(* See Ssa_build.mli *)

module L = Ir

open Ssa

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Blocks, from the labels and the jumps *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a run of instructions, and the jump that ends it if any *)
type raw = { label : int option; code : L.t list; last : L.t option }

let ends : L.t -> bool = function
  | Jmp _ | Jz _ | Jnz _ | Switch _ | Ret | Raise | Reraise | TryEnter _ | Call (_, _, true) -> true
  | _ -> false

let split (code : L.t list) =
  let out = ref [] and label = ref None and cur = ref [] in
  let close last = out := { label = !label; code = List.rev !cur; last } :: !out; label := None; cur := [] in
  let lines_only = List.for_all (function L.Line _ | L.Site _ -> true | _ -> false) in
  List.iter (fun (i : L.t) ->
    match i with
    (* (Lines after a jump: the label's run's, no run of their own) *)
    | Label l -> if not (!label = None && lines_only !cur) then close None; label := Some l
    | i when ends i -> close (Some i)
    | i -> cur := i :: !cur) code;
  if not (!label = None && lines_only !cur) then close None;
  Array.of_list (List.rev !out)

(* the run of each label *)
let runs (raws : raw array) =
  let at = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  Array.iteri (fun i r -> Option.iter (fun l -> Hashtbl.replace at l i) r.label) raws;
  Hashtbl.find at

(* each run's successors: the next run, a label's (a switch's each
 * once) *)
let successors (raws : raw array) =
  let lbl = runs raws in
  Array.mapi (fun i r ->
    let next = if i + 1 < Array.length raws then [ i + 1 ] else [] in
    match r.last with
    | None -> next
    | Some (Jmp l) -> [ lbl l ]
    | Some (Jz l | Jnz l | TryEnter (_, l)) -> next @ [ lbl l ]
    | Some (Switch ls) -> List.sort_uniq compare (List.map lbl ls)
    | Some _ -> []) raws

(* the slots an instruction pops, and pushes *)
let arity : L.t -> int * int = function
  | Int _ | Block _ | Sym _ | Get _ | GetG _ | Catch _ -> 0, 1
  | Set _ | SetG _ | Drop | Ret | Raise | Reraise | Jz _ | Jnz _ | Switch _ -> 1, 0
  | Field _ -> 1, 1
  | SetField _ -> 2, 0
  | Index -> 2, 1
  | SetIndex _ -> 3, 0
  | ByteGet _ -> 2, 1
  | ByteSet _ | FloatSetIndex _ -> 3, 0
  | FloatIndex _ -> 2, 1
  | FloatRound _ -> 1, 1
  | FloatCall (_, _, n) -> n, 1
  | Int32 Neg | Int32OfInt | Int32ToInt -> 1, 1
  | Int32 _ | MulHigh -> 2, 1
  | BytesGet _ -> 2, 1
  | BytesSet _ -> 3, 0
  | StrLen -> 1, 1
  | Float2 _ | FloatCmp _ -> 2, 1
  | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | IntOfFloat -> 1, 1
  | Alloc (_, n) -> n, 1
  | Op (Neg | Not | IsInt | Tag | Size) -> 1, 1
  | Op _ -> 2, 1
  | Call (_, _, tail) -> 0, if tail then 0 else 1
  | CallC (_, n) -> n, 1
  | Label _ | Jmp _ | TryEnter _ | TryExit _ | Line _ | Site _ -> 0, 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Braun et al.'s construction *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the variables: a frame's slot, and a position of the stack at a
 * block's edge *)
type var = Slot_var of int | Stack_var of int

let build (f : L.func) =
  (* the entry has no predecessor: an empty one before a first label,
   * which a jump may target (opti's tails) *)
  let raws = split f.code in
  let raws = if Array.length raws > 0 && raws.(0).label <> None then Array.append [| { label = None; code = []; last = None } |] raws else raws in
  let succ = successors raws and run = runs raws in
  (* the runs the entry reaches, numbered in order *)
  let n = Array.length raws in
  let reach = Array.make n false in
  let rec visit i = if not reach.(i) then (reach.(i) <- true; List.iter visit succ.(i)) in
  if n > 0 then visit 0;
  let ids = Array.make n (-1) and count = ref 0 in
  Array.iteri (fun i r -> if r then (ids.(i) <- !count; incr count)) reach;
  let blocks = Array.init !count (fun id -> { id; phis = []; body = []; term = Ret 0; preds = [] }) in
  let raw_of = Array.make !count 0 in
  Array.iteri (fun i r -> if r then raw_of.(ids.(i)) <- i) reach;
  let bsucc b = List.map (fun i -> ids.(i)) succ.(raw_of.(b)) in
  Array.iter (fun (b : block) -> List.iter (fun s -> blocks.(s).preds <- blocks.(s).preds @ [ b.id ]) (bsucc b.id)) blocks;
  (* each block's stack at its entry *)
  let depth = Array.make !count (-1) in
  let rec flow b d =
    if depth.(b) < 0 then begin
      depth.(b) <- d;
      let r = raws.(raw_of.(b)) in
      let d = List.fold_left (fun d i -> let p, q = arity i in d - p + q) d r.code in
      let d = match r.last with Some (Jz _ | Jnz _ | Switch _) -> d - 1 | _ -> d in
      List.iter (fun s -> flow s d) (bsucc b)
    end
  in
  if !count > 0 then flow 0 0;
  (* the values *)
  let defs = Hashtbl.create 256 and where = Hashtbl.create 256 and next = ref 0 in
  let fresh b ins = let v = !next in incr next; Hashtbl.replace defs v ins; Hashtbl.replace where v b; v in
  (* each value the line of the last Line before it, in the code's order
   * (the function's before the first) *)
  let lines = Hashtbl.create 256 and line = ref f.line in
  (* a Site names the call right after it, a value's or a block's tail
   * call; any other instruction between, and it names none *)
  let sites = Hashtbl.create 16 and tail_sites = Hashtbl.create 4 in
  let site = ref None in
  let emit b ins =
    let v = fresh b ins in
    if !line > 0 then Hashtbl.replace lines v !line;
    blocks.(b).body <- blocks.(b).body @ [ v ]; v in
  (* with a handler, a slot is read and written in memory: the handler
   * would need its value at each raise *)
  let memory = List.exists (function L.TryEnter _ -> true | _ -> false) f.code in
  (* Braun et al.'s reads and seals, lib_code's: a phi, a zero where
   * nothing is written, are this IR's *)
  (* each slot's values: those written to it, and its phis (for
   * Unbox.check's [@@unboxed_float]) *)
  let slots = Hashtbl.create 64 in
  let record var v = match var with Slot_var i -> Hashtbl.add slots i v | Stack_var _ -> () in
  let new_phi (var : var) b = let v = fresh b (Phi []) in blocks.(b).phis <- blocks.(b).phis @ [ v ]; record var v; v in
  let br =
    Braun.create ~preds:(fun b -> blocks.(b).preds) ~new_phi
      ~set_operands:(fun (_ : var) phi ops -> Hashtbl.replace defs phi (Phi ops))
      ~missing:(fun (_ : var) b -> emit b Zero) !count in
  let write var b v = record var v; Braun.write br var b v and read var b = Braun.read br var b in
  let seal b = Braun.seal br b and seal_ready () = Braun.seal_ready br in
  (* the entry: the closure and the arguments, as the prologue stores them *)
  if !count > 0 then begin
    seal 0;
    for i = 0 to f.nparams do write (Slot_var i) 0 (emit 0 (Param i)) done
  end;
  Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
    let id = b.id in
    let r = raws.(raw_of.(id)) in
    let stack = ref (List.init depth.(id) (fun d -> read (Stack_var d) id) |> List.rev) in
    let push v = stack := v :: !stack in
    let pop () = match !stack with v :: rest -> stack := rest; v | [] -> failwith (f.name ^ ": ssa: the stack is empty") in
    let pops k = List.init k (fun _ -> pop ()) in
    let get i = if memory then emit id (Slot i) else read (Slot_var i) id in
    site := None;
    List.iter (fun (i : L.t) ->
      (match i with
      | Int n -> push (emit id (Const n))
      | Block s -> push (emit id (Blk s))
      | Sym s -> push (emit id (Symb s))
      | Get i -> push (get i)
      | Set i -> let v = pop () in if memory then ignore (emit id (SetSlot (i, v))) else write (Slot_var i) id v
      | GetG g -> push (emit id (GetG g))
      | SetG g -> let v = pop () in ignore (emit id (SetG (g, v)))
      | Field k -> let b = pop () in push (emit id (Field (k, b)))
      | SetField (k, imm) ->
          let b = pop () in let v = pop () in ignore (emit id (SetField (k, b, v, imm)))
      | Index -> let b = pop () in let i = pop () in push (emit id (Index (b, i)))
      | SetIndex imm ->
          let b = pop () in let i = pop () in let v = pop () in
          ignore (emit id (SetIndex (b, i, v, imm)))
      (* old: each a call of the runtime's (ml_string_get, caml_addfloat...)
       *   | ByteGet -> let vs = pops 2 in push (emit id (CallC ("ml_string_get", vs))) *)
      | ByteSet _ | FloatSetIndex _ | BytesSet _ -> let vs = pops 3 in ignore (emit id (Prim (i, vs)))
      | ByteGet _ | StrLen | Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | IntOfFloat | FloatCmp _ | FloatIndex _ | FloatRound _
      | FloatCall _ | Int32 _ | Int32OfInt | Int32ToInt | BytesGet _ | MulHigh ->
          let vs = pops (fst (arity i)) in push (emit id (Prim (i, vs)))
      | Alloc (tag, n) -> let vs = pops n in push (emit id (Alloc (tag, vs)))
      | Op o -> let p, _ = arity i in let vs = pops p in push (emit id (Op (o, vs)))
      | Call (t, slots, _) ->
          let vs = List.map get slots in
          let v = emit id (Call (t, vs)) in
          Option.iter (Hashtbl.replace sites v) !site; push v
      | CallC (g, k) ->
          let vs = pops k in
          let v = emit id (CallC (g, vs)) in
          Option.iter (Hashtbl.replace sites v) !site; push v
      | Drop -> ignore (pop ())
      | TryExit k -> ignore (emit id (TryExit k))
      | Catch k -> push (emit id (Caught k))
      | Line n -> line := n
      | Site _ -> ()
      | Label _ | Jmp _ | Jz _ | Jnz _ | Switch _ | Ret | Raise | Reraise | TryEnter _ -> ());
      (* (the site kept for the next instruction only, a Line between) *)
      match i with
      | Site (a, z) -> site := Some (a, z)
      | Line _ -> ()
      | _ -> site := None) r.code;
    let succs = bsucc id in
    (b.term <-
       match r.last, succs with
       | Some (Jmp _), [ s ] | None, [ s ] -> Jmp s
       | Some (Jz _), [ nx; l ] -> Br (pop (), nx, l)
       | Some (Jnz _), [ nx; l ] -> Br (pop (), l, nx)
       | Some (TryEnter (k, _)), [ nx; h ] -> Try (k, nx, h)
       | Some (Switch ls), _ -> Switch (pop (), List.map (fun l -> ids.(run l)) ls)
       | Some Ret, _ -> Ret (pop ())
       | Some Raise, _ -> Raise (pop ())
       | Some Reraise, _ -> Reraise (pop ())
       | Some (Call (t, slots, true)), _ ->
           (* (its Site the run's last instruction) *)
           Option.iter (Hashtbl.replace tail_sites id) !site;
           Tail (t, List.map get slots)
       | None, [] -> Ret (emit id Zero)
       | _ -> failwith (f.name ^ ": ssa: a block's end"));
    (* the stack left, for the successors *)
    List.iteri (fun d v -> write (Stack_var d) id v) (List.rev !stack);
    Braun.fill br id;
    seal_ready ()) blocks;
  Braun.seal_rest br;
  { name = f.name; nparams = f.nparams; line = f.line; blocks; defs; doubles = Hashtbl.create 1; raws = Hashtbl.create 1; slots; lines; sites; tail_sites }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Trivial phis out *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let operands = function
  | Const _ | Zero | Blk _ | Symb _ | Param _ | GetG _ | Slot _ | Caught _ | TryExit _ -> []
  | Phi ops -> List.map snd ops
  | SetG (_, v) | SetSlot (_, v) | Field (_, v) | Unbox v | Box v | Tag v -> [ v ]
  | SetField (_, a, b, _) | Index (a, b) -> [ a; b ]
  | SetIndex (a, b, c, _) -> [ a; b; c ]
  | Alloc (_, vs) | Op (_, vs) | Call (_, vs) | CallC (_, vs) | Prim (_, vs) | Dprim (_, vs) -> vs

let map_ins f = function
  | Phi ops -> Phi (List.map (fun (b, v) -> b, f v) ops)
  | SetG (g, v) -> SetG (g, f v)
  | SetSlot (i, v) -> SetSlot (i, f v)
  | Field (k, v) -> Field (k, f v)
  | SetField (k, a, b, imm) -> SetField (k, f a, f b, imm)
  | Index (a, b) -> Index (f a, f b)
  | SetIndex (a, b, c, imm) -> SetIndex (f a, f b, f c, imm)
  | Alloc (t, vs) -> Alloc (t, List.map f vs)
  | Op (o, vs) -> Op (o, List.map f vs)
  | Call (t, vs) -> Call (t, List.map f vs)
  | CallC (g, vs) -> CallC (g, List.map f vs)
  | Prim (p, vs) -> Prim (p, List.map f vs)
  | Unbox v -> Unbox (f v)
  | Box v -> Box (f v)
  | Tag v -> Tag (f v)
  | Dprim (p, vs) -> Dprim (p, List.map f vs)
  | i -> i

let map_term f = function
  | Br (v, a, b) -> Br (f v, a, b)
  | Switch (v, bs) -> Switch (f v, bs)
  | Ret v -> Ret (f v)
  | Raise v -> Raise (f v)
  | Reraise v -> Reraise (f v)
  | Tail (t, vs) -> Tail (t, List.map f vs)
  | t -> t

(* a phi whose operands are one value (and itself) is that value; until
 * none is (Braun et al.'s tryRemoveTrivialPhi, as a fixpoint: lib_code's
 * Braun.trivial), the instructions then rewritten *)
let simplify (fn : func) =
  let find =
    Braun.trivial ~phis:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).phis) ~set_phis:(fun b l -> fn.blocks.(b).phis <- l)
      ~operands:(fun phi -> match Hashtbl.find fn.defs phi with Phi ops -> Some (List.map snd ops) | _ -> None)
      (Array.length fn.blocks)
  in
  Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
    List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v (map_ins find (Hashtbl.find fn.defs v))) (b.phis @ b.body);
    b.term <- map_term find b.term) fn.blocks;
  fn

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The check: every use dominated by its definition *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let successors_of (b : block) =
  match b.term with
  | Jmp s -> [ s ]
  | Br (_, a, b) | Try (_, a, b) -> [ a; b ]
  | Switch (_, bs) -> List.sort_uniq compare bs
  | _ -> []

(* the immediate dominators (lib_code's Dominators: Cooper, Harvey and
 * Kennedy's) *)
let dominators (fn : func) =
  Dominators.idoms ~succs:(fun b -> successors_of fn.blocks.(b)) ~preds:(fun b -> fn.blocks.(b).preds)
    (Array.length fn.blocks)

let check (fn : func) =
  let idom = dominators fn in
  let dominates = Dominators.dominates idom in
  let block_of = Hashtbl.create 256 and index = Hashtbl.create 256 in
  Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
    List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace block_of v b.id; Hashtbl.replace index v (-1)) b.phis;
    List.iteri (fun i v -> Hashtbl.replace block_of v b.id; Hashtbl.replace index v i) b.body) fn.blocks;
  let fail fmt = Printf.ksprintf (fun m -> failwith (fn.name ^ ": ssa: " ^ m)) fmt in
  let defined v = if not (Hashtbl.mem block_of v) then fail "v%d used, never defined" v in
  (* v's definition before position i of block b (at its end: max_int) *)
  let before v b i =
    defined v;
    let db = Hashtbl.find block_of v in
    if db = b then (if Hashtbl.find index v >= i then fail "v%d used before its definition in b%d" v b)
    else if not (dominates db b) then fail "v%d (b%d) does not dominate its use in b%d" v db b
  in
  Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
    List.iter (fun phi ->
      match Hashtbl.find fn.defs phi with
      | Phi ops ->
          if List.sort compare (List.map fst ops) <> List.sort compare b.preds then fail "v%d: a phi's operands are not b%d's predecessors" phi b.id;
          List.iter (fun (p, v) -> before v p max_int) ops
      | _ -> fail "v%d: a phi that is not" phi) b.phis;
    List.iteri (fun i v -> List.iter (fun u -> before u b.id i) (operands (Hashtbl.find fn.defs v))) b.body;
    let term_uses = match b.term with Br (v, _, _) | Switch (v, _) | Ret v | Raise v | Reraise v -> [ v ] | Tail (_, vs) -> vs | _ -> [] in
    List.iter (fun u -> before u b.id max_int) term_uses) fn.blocks

(*****************************************************************************)
(* -dssa *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let show_op (o : L.op) = L.show_op o
let show_target = function L.Direct f -> f | L.Code k -> Printf.sprintf "field%d" k
let vs l = String.concat " " (List.map (Printf.sprintf "v%d") l)

let show_ins ins =
  match ins with
  | Const n -> Printf.sprintf "int %d" n
  | Zero -> "zero"
  | Blk s -> "block " ^ s
  | Symb s -> "sym " ^ s
  | Param i -> Printf.sprintf "param %d" i
  | Phi ops -> "phi " ^ String.concat " " (List.map (fun (b, v) -> Printf.sprintf "[b%d v%d]" b v) ops)
  | GetG g -> "getg " ^ g
  | SetG (g, v) -> Printf.sprintf "setg %s v%d" g v
  | Slot i -> Printf.sprintf "slot %d" i
  | SetSlot (i, v) -> Printf.sprintf "setslot %d v%d" i v
  | Field (k, v) -> Printf.sprintf "field %d v%d" k v
  | SetField (k, b, v, _) -> Printf.sprintf "setfield %d v%d v%d" k b v
  | Index (b, i) -> Printf.sprintf "index v%d v%d" b i
  | SetIndex (b, i, v, _) -> Printf.sprintf "setindex v%d v%d v%d" b i v
  | Alloc (t, l) -> Printf.sprintf "alloc %d %s" t (vs l)
  | Op (o, l) -> Printf.sprintf "%s %s" (show_op o) (vs l)
  | Call (t, l) -> Printf.sprintf "call %s %s" (show_target t) (vs l)
  | CallC (g, l) -> Printf.sprintf "callc %s %s" g (vs l)
  | Prim (p, l) | Dprim (p, l) ->
      let name = match p with
        | ByteGet c -> if c then "byte?" else "byte"
        | ByteSet c -> if c then "setbyte?" else "setbyte"
        | StrLen -> "length"
        | Float2 _ | Float1 _ | Int32 _ | Int32OfInt | Int32ToInt | MulHigh ->
            Lower.runtime_function p
        | FloatOfInt -> "floatofint" | IntOfFloat -> "intoffloat"
        | FloatCmp r -> "float" ^ L.show_rel r
        | FloatIndex c -> if c then "findex?" else "findex"
        | FloatRound c -> if c then "ceil" else "floor"
        | FloatCall (_, f, _) -> f
        | BytesGet n -> Printf.sprintf "bytes_get%d" (8 * n)
        | BytesSet n -> Printf.sprintf "bytes_set%d" (8 * n)
        | FloatSetIndex c -> if c then "setfindex?" else "setfindex" | _ -> "prim" in
      Printf.sprintf "%s%s %s" name (match ins with Dprim _ -> "(d)" | _ -> "") (vs l)
  | Unbox v -> Printf.sprintf "unbox v%d" v
  | Box v -> Printf.sprintf "box v%d" v
  | Tag v -> Printf.sprintf "tag v%d" v
  | Caught k -> Printf.sprintf "caught %d" k
  | TryExit k -> Printf.sprintf "untry %d" k

let show_term = function
  | Jmp s -> Printf.sprintf "jmp b%d" s
  | Br (v, a, b) -> Printf.sprintf "br v%d b%d b%d" v a b
  | Switch (v, bs) -> Printf.sprintf "switch v%d %s" v (String.concat " " (List.map (Printf.sprintf "b%d") bs))
  | Try (k, a, h) -> Printf.sprintf "try %d b%d, handler b%d" k a h
  | Ret v -> Printf.sprintf "ret v%d" v
  | Raise v -> Printf.sprintf "raise v%d" v
  | Reraise v -> Printf.sprintf "reraise v%d" v
  | Tail (t, l) -> Printf.sprintf "tail %s %s" (show_target t) (vs l)

let show (fn : func) =
  let b = Buffer.create 1024 in
  Printf.bprintf b "%s:\n" fn.name;
  Array.iter (fun (bl : block) ->
    Printf.bprintf b "b%d:%s\n" bl.id (if bl.preds = [] then "" else "\t\t; from " ^ String.concat " " (List.map (Printf.sprintf "b%d") bl.preds));
    List.iter (fun v ->
      Printf.bprintf b "\tv%d = %s%s\n" v (show_ins (Hashtbl.find fn.defs v))
        (match Hashtbl.find_opt fn.raws v with Some n -> Printf.sprintf "\t; untagged, %d bits" n | None -> "")) (bl.phis @ bl.body);
    Printf.bprintf b "\t%s\n" (show_term bl.term)) fn.blocks;
  Buffer.contents b

let func (f : L.func) = let fn = simplify (build f) in check fn; fn

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Out of SSA, to the stack machine: every value in its own slot *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a label no function of the unit uses (Lower's are the unit's) *)
let labels = ref 0

let highest (u : L.unit_) =
  List.fold_left (fun m (f : L.func) ->
    List.fold_left (fun m -> function L.Label l | Jmp l | Jz l | Jnz l | TryEnter (_, l) -> max m l | _ -> m) m f.code) 0 u.funcs

let label () = incr labels; !labels

(* The simplest correct code (plan's phase 2): each value in a slot of
 * its own, after the stack code's (its slots are the handlers'
 * functions' memory); an instruction its operands pushed from their
 * slots, its stack instruction, its result stored; a phi a parallel
 * copy at each predecessor's end (all pushed, then all stored), on an
 * edge of its own when the predecessor branches. The parameters are
 * their slots already (the prologue stores them), and a Zero's slot is
 * never written (the prologue zeroes them all). simple's Gen compiles
 * the result: its calls, allocations and handlers, unchanged *)
let out (lf : L.func) (fn : func) : L.func =
  let base = lf.nslots in
  let slot v = match Hashtbl.find fn.defs v with Param i -> i | _ -> base + v in
  let code = ref [] in
  let emit i = code := i :: !code in
  let get v = emit (L.Get (slot v)) in
  let set v = emit (L.Set (slot v)) in
  let lbl = Array.map (fun (_ : block) -> label ()) fn.blocks in
  let copies p s =
    let moves = List.filter_map (fun phi -> match Hashtbl.find fn.defs phi with Phi ops -> Some (phi, List.assoc p ops) | _ -> None) fn.blocks.(s).phis in
    List.iter (fun (_, src) -> get src) moves;
    List.iter (fun (dst, _) -> set dst) (List.rev moves)
  in
  (* the edge p -> s, a label to jump to; a block of its own for the
   * copies when p has two successors *)
  let split = ref [] in
  let edge p s ~alone =
    if fn.blocks.(s).phis = [] then lbl.(s)
    else if alone then (copies p s; lbl.(s))
    else (let l = label () in split := (l, p, s) :: !split; l)
  in
  Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
    if b.id > 0 then emit (L.Label lbl.(b.id));
    List.iter (fun v ->
      match Hashtbl.find fn.defs v with
      | Zero | Param _ -> ()
      | Const n -> emit (L.Int n); set v
      | Blk s -> emit (L.Block s); set v
      | Symb s -> emit (L.Sym s); set v
      | GetG g -> emit (L.GetG g); set v
      | SetG (g, x) -> get x; emit (L.SetG g)
      | Slot i -> emit (L.Get i); set v
      | SetSlot (i, x) -> get x; emit (L.Set i)
      | Field (k, x) -> get x; emit (L.Field k); set v
      | SetField (k, blk, x, imm) -> get x; get blk; emit (L.SetField (k, imm))
      | Index (blk, i) -> get i; get blk; emit L.Index; set v
      | SetIndex (blk, i, x, imm) -> get x; get i; get blk; emit (L.SetIndex imm)
      | Alloc (t, xs) -> List.iter get (List.rev xs); emit (L.Alloc (t, List.length xs)); set v
      | Op (o, xs) -> List.iter get (List.rev xs); emit (L.Op o); set v
      | Call (t, xs) -> emit (L.Call (t, List.map slot xs, false)); set v
      | CallC (g, xs) -> List.iter get (List.rev xs); emit (L.CallC (g, List.length xs)); set v
      | Prim ((L.ByteSet _ | L.FloatSetIndex _ as p), xs) -> List.iter get (List.rev xs); emit p
      | Prim (p, xs) -> List.iter get (List.rev xs); emit p; set v
      | Caught k -> emit (L.Catch k); set v
      | TryExit k -> emit (L.TryExit k)
      | Phi _ -> ()
      | Unbox _ | Box _ | Dprim _ -> failwith (fn.name ^ ": ssa: a double out of SSA")
      | Tag _ -> failwith (fn.name ^ ": ssa: an untagged integer out of SSA")) b.body;
    match b.term with
    | Jmp s -> let l = edge b.id s ~alone:true in emit (L.Jmp l)
    | Br (v, t, e) ->
        let lt = edge b.id t ~alone:false and le = edge b.id e ~alone:false in
        get v; emit (L.Jz le); emit (L.Jmp lt)
    | Switch (v, bs) ->
        let ls = List.map (fun s -> s, edge b.id s ~alone:false) (List.sort_uniq compare bs) in
        get v; emit (L.Switch (List.map (fun s -> List.assoc s ls) bs))
    | Try (k, body, h) -> emit (L.TryEnter (k, lbl.(h))); emit (L.Jmp (edge b.id body ~alone:false))
    | Ret v -> get v; emit L.Ret
    | Raise v -> get v; emit L.Raise
    | Reraise v -> get v; emit L.Reraise
    | Tail (t, xs) -> emit (L.Call (t, List.map slot xs, true))) fn.blocks;
  List.iter (fun (l, p, s) -> emit (L.Label l); copies p s; emit (L.Jmp lbl.(s))) (List.rev !split);
  let values = Hashtbl.fold (fun v _ m -> max m (v + 1)) fn.defs 0 in
  { lf with nslots = base + values; code = List.rev !code }

let unit_ (u : L.unit_) =
  labels := highest u;
  { u with funcs = List.map (fun (f : L.func) -> out f (func f)) u.funcs }
languages/ml/ssa/Ssa_build.mli
4048
(* The ssa back end (plan: variants/ssa.md), phase 1: a function of
 * Lower's stack machine to SSA form (Ssa's types), printed by mini-ml
 * -dssa and checked.
 *
 * The blocks are the stack code's runs between labels and jumps (a
 * try's handler a successor of the block its try ends), those the
 * entry does not reach dropped, as Gen drops dead code. The
 * construction is Braun and others' (2013, below): a frame's slot,
 * and a position of the stack at a
 * block's edge, are variables; a stack entry inside a block is a
 * value; a block is sealed when its predecessors are all filled, and
 * the phis it needed then get their operands; the trivial ones (one
 * value, and themselves) go at the end. No dominance frontiers.
 *
 * A function with a handler keeps its slots in memory (slot, setslot):
 * its handler would need each slot's value at whichever point raised,
 * which is for later. The check: every use dominated by its
 * definition (Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy's dominators), a phi's
 * operands its block's predecessors.
 *
 * Ssa's header has a function before and after. In it, reading slot
 * 4 in b3 asks b3 for the slot's value; b3 has none of its own, has
 * two predecessors, so makes a phi and asks each: b1 wrote v5, b2
 * did not and asks b0, where the slot is the parameter v3. A block
 * with one predecessor asks it and makes no phi; a phi whose
 * operands turn out to be one value is that value. A loop is why
 * blocks are sealed: its head is read before the jump back to it
 * is known, so its phi waits for its last operand.
 *
 * others:
 * The classical construction (Cytron and others, 1991) goes the
 * other way, from the definitions: compute the dominator tree, from
 * it each block's dominance frontier, the blocks where a definition
 * stops being the only one that reaches, put a phi there for each
 * variable written, then rename in one walk of the tree. It gives
 * the minimal form at once and is what LLVM's mem2reg does; it
 * needs the whole graph and the dominators first. Braun's needs
 * neither, works as the code is read, and is what a compiler that
 * makes SSA straight from a tree wants (libFirm, its authors'). Here the
 * dominators are computed anyway, but only to check the result.
 *
 * terminology:
 * A block d dominates b when every path from the entry to b goes
 * through d; b's immediate dominator is the closest one, and those
 * make a tree. SSA's rule is said with it: a definition dominates
 * each of its uses. The fast algorithm is Lengauer and Tarjan's
 * (1979); Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy's (2001), here, is a dataflow
 * iteration over the blocks in reverse postorder, a page of code,
 * and faster in practice on the graphs compilers meet.
 *
 * References: M. Braun, S. Buchwald, S. Hack, R. Leissa, C. Mallon
 * and A. Zwinkau, "Simple and Efficient Construction of Static
 * Single Assignment Form" (Compiler Construction 2013), whose
 * algorithms 1 to 4 this follows; K. Cooper, T. Harvey and K.
 * Kennedy, "A Simple, Fast Dominance Algorithm" (2001); T. Lengauer
 * and R. Tarjan, "A fast algorithm for finding dominators in a
 * flowgraph" (ACM TOPLAS 1(1), 1979). *)

(* built, the trivial phis out, checked (Failure if not) *)
val func : Ir.func -> Ssa.func

(* -dssa *)
val show : Ssa.func -> string

(* an instruction's operands; a block's successors, each once; each
 * block's immediate dominator (the entry its own) *)
val operands : Ssa.ins -> Ssa.value list
val successors_of : Ssa.block -> int list
val dominators : Ssa.func -> int array

(* an instruction's operands, a block's end's, each by f (Unbox) *)
val map_ins : (Ssa.value -> Ssa.value) -> Ssa.ins -> Ssa.ins
val map_term : (Ssa.value -> Ssa.value) -> Ssa.term -> Ssa.term

(* every use dominated by its definition (Failure if not), once more
 * after a pass that rewrites the form *)
val check : Ssa.func -> unit

(* mini-ml -ssa, phase 2: each function through SSA and back to the
 * stack machine, every value in its own slot, for simple's Gen *)
val unit_ : Ir.unit_ -> Ir.unit_

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Unbox.mli *)

open Ssa

let on = ref true

let func (fn : func) : func =
  let handler = Array.exists (fun (b : block) -> match b.term with Try _ -> true | _ -> false) fn.blocks in
  if (not !on) || handler then fn
  else begin
    let def v = Hashtbl.find fn.defs v in
    let next = ref (Hashtbl.fold (fun v _ m -> max m (v + 1)) fn.defs 0) in
    let fresh ins = let v = !next in incr next; Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v ins; v in
    let double v = Hashtbl.mem fn.doubles v in
    let mark v = Hashtbl.replace fn.doubles v () in
    (* the doubles: the floats made, then the phis that one reaches *)
    Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
      List.iter (fun v ->
        match def v with
        | Prim ((Ir.Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | FloatIndex _ | FloatRound _
                | FloatCall _), _) -> mark v
        | _ -> ()) b.body) fn.blocks;
    let changed = ref true in
    while !changed do
      changed := false;
      Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
        List.iter (fun v ->
          match def v with
          | Phi ops when (not (double v)) && List.exists (fun (_, x) -> double x) ops -> mark v; changed := true
          | _ -> ()) b.phis) fn.blocks
    done;
    (* the instructions that become a Dprim: those that make a double,
     * and a comparison or a conversion with a double operand *)
    let converted v =
      match def v with
      | Prim ((Ir.Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | FloatIndex _ | FloatRound _
              | FloatCall _), _) -> double v
      | Prim ((FloatCmp _ | IntOfFloat), xs) -> List.exists double xs
      | Prim (FloatSetIndex _, _) -> true
      | _ -> false
    in
    (* which of a Dprim's operands are floats: Float.Array's the stored
     * one alone, a conversion of an int none *)
    let floats (p : Ir.t) xs =
      match p with
      | FloatOfInt | FloatIndex _ -> List.map (fun _ -> false) xs
      | FloatSetIndex _ -> [ false; false; true ]
      | _ -> List.map (fun _ -> true) xs
    in
    (* the doubles read as words: boxed once, after their definition *)
    let boxes = Hashtbl.create 16 in
    let boxed x = if double x then (match Hashtbl.find_opt boxes x with Some b -> b | None -> let b = fresh (Box x) in Hashtbl.replace boxes x b; b) else x in
    let words xs = List.iter (fun x -> ignore (boxed x)) xs in
    (* OPTIMIZATION (unbox once): a word read as a double, unboxed once,
     * after its definition, for all its reads: a loop's constant (a
     * float literal, a parameter, a field read before it) loaded once,
     * not at each turn (mini-virtuaracing's draw, its eye's vectors). A
     * literal (a static block, made where it is read: Lower) unboxed at
     * the function's entry, once for all its reads.
     * old: an Unbox before each Dprim that reads it *)
    let unboxes = Hashtbl.create 16 and literals = Hashtbl.create 16 and entry = ref [] in
    let unboxed x =
      if double x then x
      else
        match def x with
        | Blk sym -> (
            match Hashtbl.find_opt literals sym with
            | Some u -> u
            | None ->
                let u = fresh (Unbox (fresh (Blk sym))) in
                mark u; Hashtbl.replace literals sym u; entry := u :: !entry; u)
        | _ -> (
            match Hashtbl.find_opt unboxes x with
            | Some u -> u
            | None -> let u = fresh (Unbox x) in mark u; Hashtbl.replace unboxes x u; u)
    in
    (* where each double is read as a word: a block, and whether in its
     * body (else by its end); a phi a double reaches is one, so none *)
    let reads = Hashtbl.create 16 in
    let read_at (b : block) in_body xs =
      words xs;
      List.iter (fun x ->
        if double x then
          let l = match Hashtbl.find_opt reads x with Some l -> l | None -> [] in
          Hashtbl.replace reads x ((b.id, in_body) :: l)) xs
    in
    Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
      List.iter (fun v ->
        match def v with
        | Phi ops -> if not (double v) then words (List.map snd ops)
        | Prim (p, xs) when converted v ->
            List.iter2 (fun x f -> if f then ignore (unboxed x)) xs (floats p xs)
        | ins -> read_at b true (Ssa_build.operands ins)) (b.phis @ b.body);
      match b.term with
      | Br (x, _, _) | Switch (x, _) | Ret x | Raise x | Reraise x -> read_at b false [ x ]
      | Tail (_, xs) -> read_at b false xs
      | Jmp _ | Try _ -> ()) fn.blocks;
    (* OPTIMIZATION (box where read): a double read as a word in one
     * block only, which cannot run again but through the double's own,
     * boxed there: a loop's float that leaves it by its return is boxed
     * once, not at each turn (lib_audio's Filter.chain, 4 of its 5
     * boxes a call).
     * old: always after the definition (box_after) *)
    let home = Hashtbl.create 64 in
    Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
      List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace home v b.id) (b.phis @ b.body)) fn.blocks;
    let succs (b : block) =
      match b.term with
      | Jmp s -> [ s ]
      | Br (_, s, t) | Try (_, s, t) -> [ s; t ]
      | Switch _ -> Ssa_build.successors_of b
      | _ -> []
    in
    (* b reached from itself without going through d *)
    let again b d =
      let seen = Hashtbl.create 16 in
      let rec go s =
        s = b
        || (s <> d && not (Hashtbl.mem seen s)
            && (Hashtbl.replace seen s (); List.exists go (succs fn.blocks.(s))))
      in
      List.exists go (succs fn.blocks.(b))
    in
    let sunk = Hashtbl.create 16 in
    let starts = Array.make (Array.length fn.blocks) [] in
    let ends = Array.make (Array.length fn.blocks) [] in
    (* the values in their order, not the table's (the hash function of
     * the stdlib that built mini-ml: a block's boxes in another order,
     * the fixed point's programs not the same, bugs/ix.md) *)
    List.iter (fun ((x, sites) : int * (int * bool) list) ->
      let blocks = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map fst sites) in
      match blocks, Hashtbl.find_opt home x, Hashtbl.find_opt boxes x with
      | [ b ], Some d, Some bx when b <> d && b <> 0 && not (again b d) ->
          Hashtbl.replace sunk x ();
          if List.exists snd sites then starts.(b) <- bx :: starts.(b)
          else ends.(b) <- bx :: ends.(b)
      | _ -> ())
      (List.sort compare (Hashtbl.fold (fun x sites acc -> (x, sites) :: acc) reads []));
    (* each block rewritten: a double's box after it, a word unboxed
     * before the Dprim that reads it *)
    Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
      let body = ref [] in
      let push v = body := v :: !body in
      let box_after v =
        (match Hashtbl.find_opt boxes v with
         | Some bx when not (Hashtbl.mem sunk v) -> push bx
         | _ -> ());
        match Hashtbl.find_opt unboxes v with Some u -> push u | None -> ()
      in
      List.iter box_after b.phis;
      List.iter push starts.(b.id);
      (* (nothing between the parameters: Emit loads them all at the
       * entry, and Alloc may give a later one a register an earlier one
       * leaves; what follows them goes after the last) *)
      let later = ref [] in
      List.iter (fun v ->
        (match def v with
         | Param _ -> ()
         | _ -> List.iter box_after (List.rev !later); later := []);
        (match def v with
         | Prim (p, xs) when converted v ->
             let xs = List.map2 (fun x f -> if f then unboxed x else x) xs (floats p xs) in
             Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v (Dprim (p, xs))
         | ins -> Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v (Ssa_build.map_ins boxed ins));
        push v;
        match def v with Param _ -> later := v :: !later | _ -> box_after v) b.body;
      List.iter box_after (List.rev !later);
      b.body <- List.rev !body;
      b.term <- Ssa_build.map_term boxed b.term;
      (* a double phi's word operands, unboxed at their predecessors'
       * ends *)
      List.iter (fun phi ->
        match def phi with
        | Phi ops when double phi ->
            let ops =
              List.map (fun (p, x) ->
                if double x then p, x
                else (let u = fresh (Unbox x) in mark u; ends.(p) <- ends.(p) @ [ u ]; p, u)) ops
            in
            Hashtbl.replace fn.defs phi (Phi ops)
        | _ -> ()) b.phis) fn.blocks;
    Array.iteri (fun i (b : block) -> b.body <- b.body @ ends.(i)) fn.blocks;
    (* the literals' blocks and unboxes first in the entry *)
    let lits = List.concat_map (fun u -> match def u with Unbox b -> [ b; u ] | _ -> [ u ]) (List.rev !entry) in
    if Array.length fn.blocks > 0 then fn.blocks.(0).body <- lits @ fn.blocks.(0).body;
    fn
  end

(* [@@unboxed_float] checked: the marked variable's values (Ssa.slots,
 * Lower.unboxed_floats), none boxed, each phi a double (its value
 * around a loop), none a call's result (a block). A value it is first
 * given that is only read (a float literal, a parameter, a field) is
 * unboxed once, a load, and allowed. *)
let check (fn : func) =
  Hashtbl.iter (fun (lab, slot) (name, line) ->
    if lab = fn.name then begin
      let refuse what = failwith (Printf.sprintf "line %d: %s [@@unboxed_float]: %s" line name what) in
      if Array.exists (fun (b : block) -> match b.term with Try _ -> true | _ -> false) fn.blocks then
        refuse "its function has a handler (try): its values in memory, its floats blocks";
      if not !on then refuse "floats boxed (-boxed-floats)";
      let placed = Hashtbl.create 64 in
      Array.iter (fun (b : block) -> List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace placed v ()) (b.phis @ b.body)) fn.blocks;
      let mine = List.filter (Hashtbl.mem placed) (Hashtbl.find_all fn.slots slot) in
      List.iter (fun v ->
        match Hashtbl.find fn.defs v with
        | Phi _ when not (Hashtbl.mem fn.doubles v) ->
            refuse "it is a block around a loop: every value it is given is one (a call's result, a field)"
        | Call _ | CallC _ -> refuse "it is a function's result, a block"
        | _ -> ()) mine;
      (* where a box of one goes *)
      let boxes = Hashtbl.create 8 in
      Hashtbl.iter (fun w () -> match Hashtbl.find fn.defs w with Box v when List.mem v mine -> Hashtbl.replace boxes w () | _ -> ()) placed;
      let boxed vs = List.exists (Hashtbl.mem boxes) vs in
      Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
        List.iter (fun v ->
          match Hashtbl.find fn.defs v with
          | (Call (_, vs) | CallC (_, vs)) when boxed vs -> refuse "it is boxed: passed to a function"
          | (Alloc _ | SetField _ | SetIndex _ | SetG _) as i when boxed (Ssa_build.operands i) ->
              refuse "it is boxed: stored in a block or a global"
          | Op (Ir.Poly _, vs) when boxed vs -> refuse "it is boxed: compared by compare (give the type)"
          | i when boxed (Ssa_build.operands i) -> refuse "it is boxed: an operand of what reads no double (-., abs_float)"
          | _ -> ()) b.body;
        match b.term with
        | Ret v when Hashtbl.mem boxes v -> refuse "it is boxed: returned"
        | Tail (_, vs) when boxed vs -> refuse "it is boxed: passed to a function"
        | Raise v | Reraise v when Hashtbl.mem boxes v -> refuse "it is boxed: raised"
        | _ -> ()) fn.blocks
    end) Lower.unboxed_floats
languages/ml/ssa/Unbox.mli
3151
(* A float not boxed inside a function (plan_ml_floats.md, decision 2):
 * an SSA value that is a double in a floating-point register, beside
 * the words. mini-ml's float is a block of its own (Double_tag), and
 * x *. y +. z made two, the first read once by the second then left to
 * the collector; here it is none, and one if the sum leaves as a word.
 *
 * The doubles: what Float2, FloatOfInt, FloatIndex and FloatRound make
 * (a sum, a product, a float of an int, a Float.Array's, a floor...), and a phi with a double among its operands (a
 * loop's float, in a ref that Opti's refs made a slot). Each such Prim
 * is a Dprim, its float operands doubles: a double as it is, a word
 * unboxed where it is read (Unbox, its block's two words loaded); and
 * FloatCmp and IntOfFloat too when an operand is a double. Wherever
 * else a double is read (stored, passed, returned, a field of a block,
 * Float1's operand), it is boxed once, after its definition (Box).
 *
 *     let dot (x : float) y z = (x *. 0.8) +. (y *. 0.1) +. (z *. 0.6)
 *
 *     mini-ml -dssa -boxed-floats:      mini-ml -dssa:
 *     v4 = block d0<>                   v4 = block d0<>
 *     v5 = caml_mulfloat v3 v4          v13 = unbox v3
 *     ...                               v14 = unbox v4
 *     v9 = caml_mulfloat v1 v8          v5 = caml_mulfloat(d) v13 v14
 *     v10 = caml_addfloat v9 v7         ...
 *     v11 = caml_addfloat v10 v5        v11 = caml_addfloat(d) v10 v5
 *     ret v11                           v12 = box v11
 *                                       ret v12
 *
 * five blocks before, one after. A double is not a value the collector
 * reads: Alloc keeps it in a register across an allocation, and only a
 * call (of ML or of C, or compare's) makes it go to memory, a slot of
 * the machine stack, which the collector does not scan. Not in a
 * function with a handler (its values in memory at each raise: Alloc),
 * which stays as it was.
 *
 * The same bytes: a double in a register is the double that would
 * have been in a block, and no multiplication and addition are fused
 * (FMA: ocamlopt's arm64 does; here never).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Unboxing floats is as old as compiling ML to machine code: Xavier
 * Leroy's "Unboxed objects and polymorphic typing" (POPL 1992) gave
 * Gallium's compilers floats out of their boxes where the types say
 * so, and ocamlopt's Cmmgen unboxes a let-bound float whose uses are
 * float operations, as here a value whose uses are. SML/NJ and MLton
 * went further, the whole program's representations chosen at once.
 *
 * References: Xavier Leroy, "Unboxed objects and polymorphic typing"
 * (POPL 1992); OCaml's asmcomp/cmmgen.ml (unbox_float);
 * docs/plans/plan_ml_floats.md. *)

(* on, unless mini-ml -boxed-floats *)
val on : bool ref

(* the function's doubles found and made so (fn.doubles), its code
 * rewritten in place *)
val func : Ssa.func -> Ssa.func

(* [@@unboxed_float] (Annotations.mli): each marked variable of the
 * function never boxed, a double around its loops, or the program
 * refused (Failure, its line) with what boxes it or makes it a block *)
val check : Ssa.func -> unit

5369
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Untag.mli *)

open Ssa

let on = ref true

(* the bits of c's bound: the least b with c in [-2^b, 2^b), counted by
 * shifts (mini-ml on arm has ints of 31 bits: no 1 lsl 40) *)
let bound c =
  let rec count n b = if n = 0 then b else count (n lsr 1) (b + 1) in
  count (if c >= 0 then c else lnot c) 0

let func ~bits (fn : func) : func =
  let handler = Array.exists (fun (b : block) -> match b.term with Try _ -> true | _ -> false) fn.blocks in
  if (not !on) || handler then fn
  else begin
    let def v = Hashtbl.find fn.defs v in
    (* (a value in [-2^limit, 2^limit) is an int: no wrap) *)
    let limit = bits - 1 in
    let next = ref (Hashtbl.fold (fun v _ m -> max m (v + 1)) fn.defs 0) in
    let fresh ins = let v = !next in incr next; Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v ins; v in
    let body = List.concat_map (fun (b : block) -> b.body) (Array.to_list fn.blocks) in
    (* the set, optimistic first, then each value kept while its rule
     * holds with the others' and something reads it untagged *)
    let raws = fn.raws in
    let raw x = Hashtbl.mem raws x in
    let const x = match def x with Const c -> Some c | _ -> None in
    let operand x = if raw x then Some (Hashtbl.find raws x) else Option.map bound (const x) in
    let rule v =
      match def v with
      | Prim (Ir.ByteGet _, [ _; _ ]) -> Some 8
      | Op (Ir.Asr, [ x; y ]) -> (
          match const y with
          | Some k when k >= 1 -> Some (max 0 ((if raw x then Hashtbl.find raws x else limit) - k))
          | _ -> None)
      | Op (Ir.And, [ x; y ]) -> (
          match const x, const y with
          | None, Some c when c >= 0 && raw x -> Some (bound c)
          | Some c, None when c >= 0 && raw y -> Some (bound c)
          | _ -> None)
      | Op ((Ir.Add | Sub), [ x; y ]) when raw x || raw y -> (
          match operand x, operand y with Some a, Some b -> Some (max a b + 1) | _ -> None)
      | Op (Ir.Lsl, [ x; y ]) when raw x -> (
          match const y with Some k when k >= 0 -> Some (Hashtbl.find raws x + k) | _ -> None)
      | _ -> None
    in
    (* the operands an instruction reads untagged, its result untagged or
     * not: an untagged value's own; a byte's index and the byte stored;
     * the untagged one of a tagged sum or difference (the second of a
     * difference) *)
    let reads_raw v x =
      match def v with
      | Prim ((Ir.ByteGet _ | ByteSet _), _ :: i :: rest) -> x = i || rest = [ x ]
      | Op ((Ir.Asr | And | Add | Sub | Lsl), _) when raw v -> true
      | Op (Ir.Add, [ a; b ]) -> (x = b && raw b) || (x = a && raw a && not (raw b))
      | Op (Ir.Sub, [ _; b ]) -> x = b
      | _ -> false
    in
    let users = Hashtbl.create 64 in
    List.iter (fun v -> List.iter (fun x -> Hashtbl.replace users x (v :: (match Hashtbl.find_opt users x with Some l -> l | None -> []))) (Ssa_build.operands (def v))) body;
    (* optimistic: every value whose rule holds as values become so *)
    let changed = ref true in
    while !changed do
      changed := false;
      List.iter (fun v ->
        if not (raw v) then
          match rule v with Some b when b <= limit -> Hashtbl.replace raws v b; changed := true | _ -> ()) body
    done;
    (* then down to the values whose rule still holds, and read untagged
     * by something (a byte read stays: its tag is no dearer later) *)
    changed := true;
    while !changed do
      changed := false;
      List.iter (fun v ->
        if raw v then begin
          let keep =
            match rule v with
            | Some b when b <= limit ->
                Hashtbl.replace raws v b;
                (match def v with Prim (Ir.ByteGet _, _) -> true | _ -> false)
                || List.exists (fun u -> reads_raw u v) (match Hashtbl.find_opt users v with Some l -> l | None -> [])
            | _ -> false
          in
          if not keep then (Hashtbl.remove raws v; changed := true)
        end) body
    done;
    if Hashtbl.length raws = 0 then fn
    else begin
      (* each untagged value read as a word: tagged once, after it *)
      let tags = Hashtbl.create 16 in
      let tagged x = if raw x then (match Hashtbl.find_opt tags x with Some t -> t | None -> let t = fresh (Tag x) in Hashtbl.replace tags x t; t) else x in
      let rewrite v =
        match def v with
        | Prim ((Ir.ByteGet _ | ByteSet _) as p, s :: rest) -> Prim (p, tagged s :: rest)
        | Op (o, xs) when raw v -> Op (o, xs)
        | Op (Ir.Add, [ a; b ]) when raw b -> Op (Ir.Add, [ tagged a; b ])
        | Op (Ir.Add, [ a; b ]) when raw a -> Op (Ir.Add, [ a; b ])
        | Op (Ir.Sub, [ a; b ]) -> Op (Ir.Sub, [ tagged a; b ])
        | ins -> Ssa_build.map_ins tagged ins
      in
      (* (the phis, the terms and the instructions read what they read
       * tagged first, then the tags put after their values) *)
      Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
        List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v (Ssa_build.map_ins tagged (def v))) b.phis;
        List.iter (fun v -> Hashtbl.replace fn.defs v (rewrite v)) b.body;
        b.term <- Ssa_build.map_term tagged b.term) fn.blocks;
      Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
        b.body <- List.concat_map (fun v -> match Hashtbl.find_opt tags v with Some t -> [ v; t ] | None -> [ v ]) b.body) fn.blocks;
      fn
    end
  end
languages/ml/ssa/Untag.mli
3113
(* An integer not tagged inside a function (plan_ml_speed.md, stage 2):
 * an SSA value that is n in its register, not 2n+1, where the tag would
 * be taken off again by what reads it. mini-ml's int is tagged (Lower,
 * Gen: 2n+1, the collector's way of telling it from a pointer), and
 * each operation pays for it: x + y is an ADD and a SUB, a byte read a
 * load then a shift and an OR, a byte stored a shift then the store.
 * mini-doom's span, its pixel's 35 instructions, 11 of them the tags.
 *
 * The untagged: what reads a byte (ByteGet, its result 0 to 255); x asr
 * k by a constant (one shift of the tagged x by k + 1, where tagged it
 * is a shift and an OR); x land c, x untagged, c a constant at least 0;
 * x + y, x - y, x lsl k of untagged values. Only when the value's bits
 * are known small enough that no wrap can happen: a tagged int is 31
 * bits on arm, 63 on arm64, and a register's sum of two of them may be
 * past that, where the tagged sum wrapped; such a sum would then
 * compare, shift and divide otherwise. So each untagged value has a
 * bound (a byte 8 bits, x asr 16 on arm 14, x land 63 6, a sum one
 * more than its operands'), and past 30 (62) it stays tagged. A loop's
 * counter, a sum of a tagged value: tagged, as before.
 *
 * Read as they are: by an untagged value's operation; as a byte's
 * index or the byte stored; by a tagged value plus or minus one (an ADD
 * or SUB of the register shifted by 1: t + 2n is the tagged sum).
 * Wherever else (stored, passed, compared, returned, a phi's operand)
 * it is tagged once after its definition (Tag, two instructions).
 *
 *     let pixel flat (x : int) = Char.code (Bytes.unsafe_get flat ((x asr 16) land 63))
 *
 *     mini-ml -dssa:
 *     v3 = (Ir.Op Ir.Asr) v2 v16     ; untagged, 14 bits
 *     v4 = (Ir.Op Ir.And) v3 v17     ; untagged, 6 bits
 *     v5 = (Ir.ByteGet false) v1 v4  ; untagged, 8 bits
 *     v6 = tag v5
 *     ret v6
 *
 * An untagged value is a word the collector must not read: in a
 * register it is not read; past a safepoint it goes to memory, and so
 * to a slot of the machine stack (Alloc's Dmem, a double's), not the
 * value stack. Not in a function with a handler (its values in memory
 * at each raise), which stays as it was.
 *
 * others:
 * ocamlopt keeps ints tagged in registers, but its Cmm folds the tags
 * of an expression where it can (untag_int of tag_int, the decrement
 * of a sum into the next operation: add_int and its Caddi), and its
 * instruction selection does the rest. MLton and SML/NJ have untagged
 * 32-bit words by type (Word32), their int tagged or not by the
 * program's whole representation analysis.
 *
 * References: OCaml's asmcomp/cmm_helpers.ml (untag_int, add_int);
 * Andrew Appel, "Compiling with Continuations" (1992), chapter 4 (the
 * representations of SML/NJ's data). *)

(* on, unless mini-ml -tagged-ints *)
val on : bool ref

(* the function's untagged values found (fn.raws), with what reads them
 * as words tagged, its code rewritten in place; bits: an int's (31 on
 * arm, 63 on arm64) *)
val func : bits:int -> Ssa.func -> Ssa.func

(* Claude Code

(* See Zero_alloc.mli *)

open Ssa

(* the runtime's C functions that make nothing (strings.c, floats.c:
 * a bound error raises bound_exn, made at startup) *)
let c_without_alloc =
  [ "ml_string_length"; "ml_string_get"; "ml_string_set";
    "caml_string_equal"; "caml_string_notequal"; "ml_floatarray_length" ]

let call = function
  | Ir.Direct lab when Hashtbl.mem Lower.zero_allocs lab -> None
  | Ir.Direct lab ->
      (* a function of this unit's name, f12_name<> (Lower's fun_label) *)
      let name =
        match String.index_opt lab '_', String.ends_with ~suffix:"<>" lab with
        | Some i, true -> String.sub lab (i + 1) (String.length lab - i - 3)
        | _ -> lab
      in
      Some (Printf.sprintf "calls %s, not [@@zero_alloc] in this unit" name)
  | Ir.Code _ -> Some "calls a function it does not know (a closure)"

(* what an instruction allocates, if it does *)
let why = function
  (* 247: a closure's tag (OCaml's Closure_tag, Lower's) *)
  | Alloc (tag, _) when tag = 247 -> Some "makes a closure"
  | Alloc _ -> Some "makes a block (a tuple, a record, a constructor's)"
  | Box _ -> Some "boxes a float"
  | Prim ((Ir.Float2 _ | Float1 _ | FloatOfInt | FloatIndex _ | FloatRound _ | FloatCall _), _) ->
      Some "boxes a float"
  | Prim ((Ir.Int32 _ | Int32OfInt | BytesGet 4), _) -> Some "makes an int32's block"
  | Op (Ir.Poly _, _) -> Some "compares by compare, in C (give the type)"
  | CallC (g, _) when List.mem g c_without_alloc -> None
  | CallC (g, _) -> Some (Printf.sprintf "calls C's %s, which may allocate" g)
  | Call (t, _) -> call t
  | _ -> None

let check (fn : func) =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt Lower.zero_allocs fn.name with
  | None -> ()
  | Some name ->
      let refuse what = failwith (Printf.sprintf "line %d: %s [@@zero_alloc]: it %s" fn.line name what) in
      (* a block that ends in a raise is the error's way out: what it
       * makes (the exception's block, mini-ml's at each raise) not
       * counted *)
      Array.iter (fun (b : block) ->
        match b.term with
        | Raise _ | Reraise _ -> ()
        | term ->
            List.iter (fun v -> Option.iter refuse (why (Hashtbl.find fn.defs v))) b.body;
            match term with Tail (t, _) -> Option.iter refuse (call t) | _ -> ()) fn.blocks
languages/ml/ssa/Zero_alloc.mli
1962
(* [@@zero_alloc] checked (Annotations.mli, plan_ml_annotations.md's
 * step 2): a function so marked allocates nothing, read on its SSA
 * form once every optimization is done (Unbox, Untag, Licm, Cse), so
 * after inlining and with its floats unboxed: what runs is what is
 * checked.
 *
 *     let dot (a : float array) b =
 *       let s = ref 0.0 in
 *       for i = 0 to Array.length a - 1 do s := !s +. a.(i) *. b.(i) done;
 *       !s [@@zero_alloc]
 *     (mini-ml -O3: dot [@@zero_alloc]: it boxes a float, its result)
 *
 * Refused: a block made (a tuple, a record, a constructor's, a
 * closure), a float boxed, an int32's block, a polymorphic comparison
 * (compare, in C: give the type), a call of a function not itself
 * [@@zero_alloc] in this unit (another unit's, an unknown closure, a
 * partial application), a call of C but the runtime's few that make
 * nothing (a string's length and bytes, = on strings, a float array's
 * length). A raise is allowed, and what is made on its way, in the
 * block of code that ends in it (the exception's block, which mini-ml
 * makes at each raise, Not_found's too): the error's path, not the
 * hot one, as Jane Street's check leaves it out. So is a handler.
 *
 * Only ssa's code is checked (-O3, -ssa): without it, the annotation
 * is not looked at, as OCaml 4.14 does not, since nothing is promised
 * of simple's code (its floats are blocks). The error names the
 * function's line, not the instruction's: SSA's values have none.
 *
 * others:
 * Jane Street's OCaml (flambda-backend) checks [@zero_alloc] the same
 * way, on the code after inlining, with "assume" and "opt" variants
 * and the paths that end in a raise left out unless "strict";
 * Java's real-time (RTSJ) NoHeapRealtimeThread and Rust's no_std
 * without alloc are the same promise for a whole thread or crate. *)

(* the function refused (Failure, with its line) if it is marked and
 * allocates *)
val check : Ssa.func -> unit

(* See CLI.mli *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

let usage = "usage: mini-pascal [-S] [-disk] [-seed n] [-s] file.pas...   (-h: how)"

(* -h: how, by examples, each one as it runs *)
let help = {|usage: mini-pascal [-S] [-disk] [-seed n] [-s] file.pas...
Pascal (Wirth, 1970) as Pascal-P and UCSD Pascal ran it: one pass from the text
to P-code, the code of a stack machine, and that machine. For example:
  mini-pascal hello.pas             a program compiled and run
  mini-pascal -S hello.pas          its P-code: an instruction a line, its address, its source line
  mini-pascal -disk                 the programs that come with it: HELLO.PAS, QUEENS.PAS, HANOI.PAS...
  mini-pascal QUEENS.PAS            one of them run (a name that is no file here is looked for there): the eight queens
  mini-pascal GUESS.PAS             a program that asks: readln takes the next line typed
  mini-pascal -seed 7 GUESS.PAS     random's numbers from another seed (1: the same ones every time)
The language: integer, boolean, char, subranges, arrays and records; const,
type, var; procedures and functions, nested, recursive, forward, with value and
var parameters; if, case, while, repeat, for; write, writeln, read, readln,
random. An error of the compiler is said with its line and column and nothing
is run; an error at run time (a range check, a division by zero, the stack
used up) with its number, Turbo Pascal's, and its line. The exit is then 1.
-s: the instructions the machine ran, said at the end.|}

(* a program run to its end on the console; false if it failed *)
let run (caps : < caps; .. >) (seed : int) (stats : bool) (p : Pcode.program) : bool =
  let m = Pmachine.start p in
  let chan = Console.stdin caps in
  let seed = ref (Lehmer.scramble seed) in
  let flush () : unit =
    let s = Pmachine.output m in
    if s <> "" then Console.print caps s;
    (* (seen now: a question before its line is waited for, what was
     * written before an error's message) *)
    flush (Console.stdout caps) in
  let rec go () : bool =
    let stop = Pmachine.resume ~pause:(fun (_ : Pmachine.machine) -> false) m 100_000 in
    flush ();
    match stop with
    | Pmachine.Halted -> true
    | Pmachine.Slice_over | Pmachine.Paused -> go ()
    | Pmachine.Need_line -> (
        match input_line chan with
        | l -> Pmachine.give_line m l; go ()
        | exception End_of_file -> Console.eprint caps "\nreadln: no line left\n"; false)
    | Pmachine.Need_random n ->
        (* (drawn as Talk draws them: a seed gives the same numbers here
         * and in TinyTurboPascal) *)
        seed := Lehmer.next !seed;
        Pmachine.give_random m (int_of_float (float_of_int n *. Lehmer.to_unit !seed));
        go ()
    | Pmachine.Failed (code, msg) ->
        let pc = Pmachine.pc m in
        Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "\nRuntime error %d at line %d: %s\n" code (if pc > 0 then p.lines.(pc - 1) else 0) msg);
        false in
  let ok = go () in
  if stats then Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "%d instructions\n" (Pmachine.executed m));
  ok

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : int =
  let listing = ref false and disk = ref false and stats = ref false and seed = ref 1 in
  let files : string list ref = ref [] in
  let options =
    [ ("-S", Arg.Set listing, " the P-code listed, nothing run");
      ("-disk", Arg.Set disk, " the names of the programs that come with it");
      ("-seed", Arg.Int (fun (n : int) -> seed := n), " random's seed (1)");
      ("-s", Arg.Set stats, " the instructions run, at the end") ] in
  (* a file here, or else one of the disk's *)
  let text (f : string) : string =
    match (match FS.path f with Ok p -> FS.read caps p | Error msg -> raise (Sys_error msg)) with
    | t -> t
    | exception Sys_error msg -> (match List.assoc_opt f Pascal_disk.files with Some t -> t | None -> failwith (msg ^ " (and not on the disk: -disk)")) in
  match Arg.parse_argv argv options (fun (f : string) -> files := f :: !files) usage with
  | exception Arg.Help _ -> Console.print caps (help ^ "\n"); 0
  | exception Arg.Bad msg -> Console.eprint caps msg; 1
  | () -> (
      try
        if !disk then List.iter (fun ((name, _) : string * string) -> Console.print caps (name ^ "\n")) Pascal_disk.files
        else if !files = [] then failwith usage;
        let ok = ref true in
        List.iter
          (fun (f : string) ->
            match Pascal_compile.compile (text f) with
            | Error e -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "%s:%d:%d: %s\n" f e.line e.col e.message); ok := false
            | Ok p -> if !listing then Console.print caps (Pcode.listing p) else if not (run caps !seed !stats p) then ok := false)
          (List.rev !files);
        if !ok then 0 else 1
      with Failure msg | Sys_error msg -> Console.eprint caps (msg ^ "\n"); 1)
languages/pascal/CLI.mli
4771
(* mini-pascal: Pascal compiled to P-code and run on a P-machine
 * (docs/plans/plan_pascal.md), on a terminal: a program compiled and
 * run, its readln answered by the lines typed; or its P-code listed.
 * TinyTurboPascal is the same compiler and machine in an IDE.
 * Its usage: [help] in CLI.ml, what mini-pascal -h prints.
 *
 *     sq.pas
 *        | Pascal_lexer      tokens, each with its line and column
 *        | Pascal_compile    one pass: parses, checks the types and
 *        |                   emits, with no tree between
 *     Pcode.program  ------- Pcode.listing: -S
 *        | Pmachine          fetch, decode, execute on one stack; a
 *        |                   Talk program: readln waits for a line
 *     what it writes         Pdebug: the same machine paused and read
 *                            as Pascal, for the IDE's debugger
 *
 *     program Sq;                 mini-pascal -S sq.pas
 *     var i : integer;              2  ldc 1         i := 1
 *     begin                         3  str 0,4
 *       for i := 1 to 3 do          4  ldc 3         the limit, kept
 *         writeln(i * i)            5  str 0,5       beside i
 *     end.                          6  lod 0,4       i <= the limit?
 *                                   7  lod 0,5
 *     it writes 1, 4, 9             8  leq
 *     in 52 instructions            9  fjp 20        no: out
 *     (-s)                         10  lod 0,4       i * i
 *                                  11  lod 0,4
 *                                  12  mpi
 *                                  13  ldc 0         no width asked
 *                                  14  csp wri       written
 *                                  15  csp wln
 *                                  16  lod 0,4       i := i + 1
 *                                  17  inc 1
 *                                  18  str 0,4
 *                                  19  ujp 6         again
 *                                  20  stp
 *
 * (Before them, 0 ujp 1 and 1 ent 6: over the procedures, of which
 * there are none, and the main program's frame.) Each line of code
 * was written as the compiler passed the text it stands beside, in
 * that order, and nothing was gone back to but the 20 of fjp.
 *
 * Next to ix's two compilers for a real machine it is the other end
 * of the scale. mini-cc and mini-ml build a tree, go over it several
 * times, choose registers, and leave an object file to the linker;
 * here the text goes in and a program runs, by a compiler of under a
 * thousand lines and a machine of under three hundred (Pmachine).
 * That is what made Pascal travel, and what the IDE
 * (mini-turbopascal, Tui_turbo) needs to compile at a key's press.
 *
 * evolution:
 * Niklaus Wirth designed Pascal at ETH Zurich in 1970, after the
 * committee for Algol's successor had preferred the large Algol 68
 * to his small proposal: a language to teach programming with, that
 * a compiler could read once, named for Blaise Pascal. Pascal-P
 * (1973; Pcode) carried it to every kind of computer. Kenneth
 * Bowles's UCSD Pascal (1977) made the P-machine a whole system for
 * microcomputers, editor, files and compiler, the same on each: one
 * of the three systems IBM sold for its PC in 1981, and Apple's
 * Pascal. Anders Hejlsberg's Turbo Pascal (Borland, 1983) kept the
 * one pass and dropped the P-machine: machine code written straight
 * into memory, an editor in the same program, a compilation in
 * seconds on a floppy-disk machine, for 49.95 dollars. For a decade
 * Pascal was what programming was taught in and what much of the
 * Macintosh's and the PC's software was written in.
 *
 * others:
 * Brian Kernighan's "Why Pascal Is Not My Favorite Programming
 * Language" (1981) lists what the Report's Pascal could not do for
 * real programs: an array's length is part of its type, so no
 * procedure can take a string of any length; no separate
 * compilation; no way round the types. Every dialect mended it its
 * own way (UCSD's units, Turbo's strings), no two alike, and C took
 * the systems. Wirth's own answers were new languages: Modula-2,
 * with modules, then Oberon. Hejlsberg went on to Delphi, C# and
 * TypeScript.
 *
 * References: Niklaus Wirth, "The Programming Language Pascal" (Acta
 * Informatica, 1971) and "Recollections about the Development of
 * Pascal" (History of Programming Languages II, 1993); Kathleen
 * Jensen and Niklaus Wirth, "Pascal User Manual and Report"
 * (Springer, 1974); Brian W. Kernighan, "Why Pascal Is Not My
 * Favorite Programming Language" (Bell Laboratories, 1981). Pascal-P's
 * notes and the P4 compiler's sources: Pcode. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

val main : < caps; .. > -> string array -> int
