(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Tiger_emit.mli *)

open Tiger_tree
module S = Signature
module W = Writer

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* The assembly's classes and members, each made when first needed *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

type t = {
  w : W.t;
  runtime : int;
  console : int;
  program : int;                                  (* the class of the functions *)
  library : int;                                  (* the class Tiger *)
  memo : (string, int) Hashtbl.t;                 (* what is made, by a name of ours *)
}

let memo (c : t) (key : string) (make : unit -> int) : int =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt c.memo key with
  | Some x -> x
  | None -> let x = make () in Hashtbl.replace c.memo key x; x

let static (ps : S.t list) (r : S.t) : S.meth =
  { S.has_this = false; generic = 0; vararg = false; ret = r; params = ps }
let instance (ps : S.t list) (r : S.t) : S.meth = { (static ps r) with has_this = true }

let sys (c : t) (name : string) : int =
  memo c ("type " ^ name) (fun () ->
      if name = "Console" then c.console
      else if name = "Encoding" then W.type_ref c.w c.runtime "System.Text" name
      else W.type_ref c.w c.runtime "System" name)

(* a member of the library's: its class, name and signature *)
let lib (c : t) (cls : string) (name : string) (m : S.meth) : int =
  memo c (cls ^ "::" ^ name ^ S.encode_method m) (fun () -> W.member_ref c.w (sys c cls) name m)

let object_ctor (c : t) : int = lib c "Object" ".ctor" (instance [] S.Void)

(* a class with nothing but its constructor, which calls its parent's *)
let new_class (c : t) (name : string) (parent : int) (parent_ctor : int) (args : Il.op list) : int * int =
  let cls = W.type_def c.w "" name 0x00100001 parent in
  let ctor = W.method_def c.w cls ".ctor" 0x1886 (instance [] S.Void) in
  W.set_body c.w ctor [] (Array.of_list ([ Il.Ldarg 0 ] @ args @ [ Il.Call parent_ctor; Il.Ret ])) [];
  (cls, ctor)

(* a record type: a class of fields *)
let rec record (c : t) (r : record) : int * int =
  let key = Printf.sprintf "record %d" r.rid in
  (match Hashtbl.find_opt c.memo key with
   | Some _ -> ()
   | None ->
       let cls, ctor = new_class c (Printf.sprintf "%s_%d" r.rname r.rid) (sys c "Object") (object_ctor c) [] in
       (* (known before its fields, which may be of its own type) *)
       Hashtbl.replace c.memo key cls;
       Hashtbl.replace c.memo (Printf.sprintf "ctor %d" r.rid) ctor;
       List.iteri (fun i (f, ty) ->
           Hashtbl.replace c.memo (Printf.sprintf "field %d %d" r.rid i)
             (W.field_def c.w cls f 0x0006 (sig_of c ty))) r.rfields);
  (Hashtbl.find c.memo key, Hashtbl.find c.memo (Printf.sprintf "ctor %d" r.rid))

and sig_of (c : t) (ty : ty) : S.t =
  match ty with
  | Int -> S.I4
  | String -> S.String
  | Unit -> S.Void
  | Nil -> S.Object
  | Record r -> S.Class (fst (record c r))
  | Array a -> S.SzArray (sig_of c a.elem)

let field_tok (c : t) (r : record) (i : int) : int =
  ignore (record c r);
  Hashtbl.find c.memo (Printf.sprintf "field %d %d" r.rid i)

(* the type newarr is given *)
let elem_tok (c : t) (ty : ty) : int =
  match ty with
  | Int -> sys c "Int32"
  | String -> sys c "String"
  | Record r -> fst (record c r)
  | Array _ -> memo c ("spec " ^ S.encode_type_spec (sig_of c ty)) (fun () -> W.type_spec c.w (sig_of c ty))
  | Unit | Nil -> sys c "Object"

(* a function's frame, an object: the variables its nested functions
 * use, and the link to its parent's frame *)
let rec frame (c : t) (f : func) : int * int =
  let cls = memo c ("frame " ^ f.name) (fun () ->
      let cls, ctor = new_class c ("frame_" ^ f.name) (sys c "Object") (object_ctor c) [] in
      Hashtbl.replace c.memo ("frame ctor " ^ f.name) ctor;
      (match f.parent with
       | Some p -> Hashtbl.replace c.memo ("link " ^ f.name)
                     (W.field_def c.w cls "link" 0x0006 (S.Class (fst (frame c p))))
       | None -> ());
      cls) in
  (cls, Hashtbl.find c.memo ("frame ctor " ^ f.name))

let link (c : t) (f : func) : int = ignore (frame c f); Hashtbl.find c.memo ("link " ^ f.name)

let var_field (c : t) (v : var) : int =
  memo c (Printf.sprintf "var %d" v.vid) (fun () ->
      W.field_def c.w (fst (frame c v.vfun)) (Printf.sprintf "%s_%d" v.vname v.vid) 0x0006 (sig_of c v.vty))

let method_of (c : t) (f : func) : int =
  memo c ("method " ^ f.name) (fun () ->
      let link = match f.parent with Some p -> [ S.Class (fst (frame c p)) ] | None -> [] in
      let m = if f.parent = None then static [] S.I4
        else static (link @ List.map (fun v -> sig_of c v.vty) f.params) (sig_of c f.result) in
      W.method_def c.w c.program (if f.parent = None then "Main" else f.name) 0x0096 m)

(* an exception: a class of System.Exception's, its message its name *)
let exn_ctor (c : t) (x : exn) : int * int =
  let cls = memo c (Printf.sprintf "exn %d" x.eid) (fun () ->
      let base_ctor = lib c "Exception" ".ctor" (instance [ S.String ] S.Void) in
      let cls, ctor = new_class c (Printf.sprintf "%s_%d" x.ename x.eid) (sys c "Exception") base_ctor
          [ Il.Ldstr (W.user_string c.w x.ename) ] in
      Hashtbl.replace c.memo (Printf.sprintf "exn ctor %d" x.eid) ctor;
      cls) in
  (cls, Hashtbl.find c.memo (Printf.sprintf "exn ctor %d" x.eid))

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* A method's code: the instructions, their labels, the locals *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

type code = {
  mutable ops : Il.op list;                       (* reversed *)
  mutable n : int;
  labels : (int, int) Hashtbl.t;                  (* a label to its instruction *)
  mutable nlabels : int;
  mutable locals : S.t list;                      (* reversed *)
  mutable nlocals : int;
  slots : (int, int) Hashtbl.t;                   (* a variable's local *)
  mutable clauses : (int * int * int * int * int) list;   (* by labels, and the class *)
  fn : func;
  mutable loops : (int * int) list;               (* each loop's end, and the trys around it *)
  mutable trys : int;
}

let emit (k : code) (op : Il.op) : unit = k.ops <- op :: k.ops; k.n <- k.n + 1
let label (k : code) : int = k.nlabels <- k.nlabels + 1; k.nlabels
let place (k : code) (l : int) : unit = Hashtbl.replace k.labels l k.n
let local (k : code) (ty : S.t) : int =
  k.locals <- ty :: k.locals; k.nlocals <- k.nlocals + 1; k.nlocals - 1

let finish (c : t) (k : code) (meth : int) : unit =
  let at l = Hashtbl.find k.labels l in
  let ops = Array.of_list (List.rev_map (fun op -> match op with
      | Il.Br l -> Il.Br (at l) | Il.Brfalse l -> Il.Brfalse (at l)
      | Il.Brtrue l -> Il.Brtrue (at l) | Il.Bcmp (x, u, l) -> Il.Bcmp (x, u, at l)
      | Il.Leave l -> Il.Leave (at l) | op -> op) k.ops) in
  let clauses = List.rev_map (fun (ts, te, hs, he, cls) ->
      { W.kind = 0; try_start = at ts; try_end = at te; handler_start = at hs;
        handler_end = at he; catch = cls }) k.clauses in
  W.set_body c.w meth (List.rev k.locals) ops clauses

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* Variables *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

(* the frame of [f], from the function running: its own local, or the
 * static link (argument 0, the parent's frame) followed up *)
let frame_of (c : t) (k : code) (f : func) : unit =
  if k.fn == f then emit k (Il.Ldloc 0)
  else begin
    emit k (Il.Ldarg 0);
    let rec up (g : func) =
      if g != f then
        match g.parent with
        | Some p -> emit k (Il.Ldfld (link c g)); up p
        | None -> failwith "Tiger_emit: a frame not above" in
    match k.fn.parent with
    | Some p -> up p
    | None -> failwith "Tiger_emit: main has no link"
  end

let arg_of (k : code) (v : var) : int = v.param + (if k.fn.parent = None then 0 else 1)

let slot (c : t) (k : code) (v : var) : int =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt k.slots v.vid with
  | Some i -> i
  | None -> let i = local k (sig_of c v.vty) in Hashtbl.replace k.slots v.vid i; i

let load_var (c : t) (k : code) (v : var) : unit =
  if v.escapes then (frame_of c k v.vfun; emit k (Il.Ldfld (var_field c v)))
  else if v.param >= 0 then emit k (Il.Ldarg (arg_of k v))
  else emit k (Il.Ldloc (slot c k v))

(* a variable given the value [value] pushes *)
let store_var (c : t) (k : code) (v : var) (value : unit -> unit) : unit =
  if v.escapes then (frame_of c k v.vfun; value (); emit k (Il.Stfld (var_field c v)))
  else if v.param >= 0 then (value (); emit k (Il.Starg (arg_of k v)))
  else (value (); emit k (Il.Stloc (slot c k v)))

let kind_of (ty : ty) : Il.kind = if ty = Int then Il.K_i4 else Il.K_ref

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* The library: the class Tiger, its methods on System's *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

let builtin (c : t) (name : string) : int =
  memo c ("builtin " ^ name) (fun () ->
      let str = S.String and int = S.I4 and void = S.Void in
      let char_to_string = lib c "Char" "ToString" (static [ S.Char ] str) in
      let sg, code = match name with
        | "print" -> static [ str ] void, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Call (lib c "Console" "Write" (static [ str ] void)); Il.Ret ]
        | "printi" -> static [ int ] void, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Call (lib c "Console" "Write" (static [ int ] void)); Il.Ret ]
        | "flush" -> static [] void, [ Il.Ret ]
        | "getchar" ->
            static [] str, [ Il.Call (lib c "Console" "Read" (static [] int)); Il.Dup;
                             Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.minus_one; Il.Bcmp (Il.Ne, false, 7);
                             Il.Pop; Il.Ldstr (W.user_string c.w ""); Il.Ret;
                             (* 7 *) Il.Conv (Il.K_u2, false, false); Il.Call char_to_string; Il.Ret ]
        | "ord" ->
            let length = lib c "String" "get_Length" (instance [] int) in
            (* (not one character: the program stops, status 1, as
             * fork-tiger's ord; Appel's gives -1 for "") *)
            static [ str ] int, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Callvirt length; Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.one; Il.Bcmp (Il.Eq, false, 8);
                                  Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.one;
                                  Il.Call (lib c "Environment" "Exit" (static [ int ] void));
                                  Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.minus_one; Il.Ret;
                                  (* 8 *) Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.zero;
                                  Il.Callvirt (lib c "String" "get_Chars" (instance [ int ] S.Char)); Il.Ret ]
        | "chr" -> static [ int ] str, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Conv (Il.K_u2, false, false); Il.Call char_to_string; Il.Ret ]
        | "size" -> static [ str ] int, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Callvirt (lib c "String" "get_Length" (instance [] int)); Il.Ret ]
        | "substring" ->
            static [ str; int; int ] str,
            [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Ldarg 1; Il.Ldarg 2;
              Il.Callvirt (lib c "String" "Substring" (instance [ int; int ] str)); Il.Ret ]
        | "concat" -> static [ str; str ] str, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Ldarg 1; Il.Call (lib c "String" "Concat" (static [ str; str ] str)); Il.Ret ]
        | "not" -> static [ int ] int, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.zero; Il.Ceq; Il.Ret ]
        | "exit" -> static [ int ] void, [ Il.Ldarg 0; Il.Call (lib c "Environment" "Exit" (static [ int ] void)); Il.Ret ]
        | n -> failwith ("Tiger_emit: no builtin " ^ n) in
      (* (a branch's target: the index of an instruction in the list) *)
      let m = W.method_def c.w c.library name 0x0096 sg in
      W.set_body c.w m [] (Array.of_list code) [];
      m)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* Expressions *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

let rec exp (c : t) (k : code) (x : exp) : unit =
  match x.e with
  | Nil_e -> emit k Il.Ldnull
  | Int_e n -> emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 n)
  | String_e s -> emit k (Il.Ldstr (W.user_string c.w s))
  | Var_e lv -> load c k lv
  | Op_e (a, op, b) -> exp c k a; exp c k b; oper c k a.ty op
  | Call_e (f, args) ->
      (match f.parent with Some p -> frame_of c k p | None -> ());
      List.iter (exp c k) args;
      emit k (Il.Call (method_of c f))
  | Builtin_e ("sizea", [ a ]) -> exp c k a; emit k Il.Ldlen; emit k (Il.Conv (Il.K_i4, false, false))
  | Builtin_e (name, args) -> List.iter (exp c k) args; emit k (Il.Call (builtin c name))
  | Record_e (r, es) ->
      emit k (Il.Newobj (snd (record c r)));
      List.iteri (fun i e -> emit k Il.Dup; exp c k e; emit k (Il.Stfld (field_tok c r i))) es
  | Array_e (a, size, init) ->
      (* a = new T[size]; for (i = 0; i < size; i++) a[i] = init: init
       * evaluated for each element, as fork-tiger does (Appel's
       * initArray takes it once, all the elements then the same record) *)
      let n = local k S.I4 and i = local k S.I4 in
      let arr = local k (sig_of c (Array a)) in
      exp c k size; emit k (Il.Stloc n);
      emit k (Il.Ldloc n); emit k (Il.Newarr (elem_tok c a.elem)); emit k (Il.Stloc arr);
      emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.zero); emit k (Il.Stloc i);
      let test = label k and out = label k in
      place k test;
      emit k (Il.Ldloc i); emit k (Il.Ldloc n); emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Ge, false, out));
      emit k (Il.Ldloc arr); emit k (Il.Ldloc i); exp c k init; emit k (Il.Stelem (kind_of a.elem));
      emit k (Il.Ldloc i); emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.one); emit k (Il.Binop Il.Add); emit k (Il.Stloc i);
      emit k (Il.Br test);
      place k out;
      emit k (Il.Ldloc arr)
  | Seq_e l ->
      let rec go l = match l with
        | [] -> ()
        | [ e ] -> exp c k e
        | e :: rest -> stmt c k e; go rest in
      go l
  | Assign_e (lv, e) -> assign c k lv (fun () -> exp c k e)
  | If_e (cond, t, f) ->
      let other = label k and out = label k in
      exp c k cond; emit k (Il.Brfalse other);
      exp c k t; emit k (Il.Br out);
      place k other;
      (match f with Some f -> exp c k f | None -> ());
      place k out
  | While_e (cond, body) ->
      let test = label k and out = label k in
      place k test;
      exp c k cond; emit k (Il.Brfalse out);
      loop c k out (fun () -> stmt c k body);
      emit k (Il.Br test);
      place k out
  | For_e (v, lo, hi, body) ->
      (* i = lo; limit = hi; if i <= limit: loop { body; if i >= limit
       * out; i++ } (never past int's largest) *)
      let limit = local k S.I4 in
      let top = label k and out = label k in
      store_var c k v (fun () -> exp c k lo);
      exp c k hi; emit k (Il.Stloc limit);
      load_var c k v; emit k (Il.Ldloc limit); emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Gt, false, out));
      place k top;
      loop c k out (fun () -> stmt c k body);
      load_var c k v; emit k (Il.Ldloc limit); emit k (Il.Bcmp (Il.Ge, false, out));
      store_var c k v (fun () -> load_var c k v; emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.one); emit k (Il.Binop Il.Add));
      emit k (Il.Br top);
      place k out
  | Break_e ->
      (match k.loops with
       | (out, trys) :: _ -> emit k (if k.trys > trys then Il.Leave out else Il.Br out)
       | [] -> failwith "Tiger_emit: break outside a loop")
  | Let_e (vars, body) ->
      List.iter (fun (v, init) -> store_var c k v (fun () -> exp c k init)) vars;
      exp c k body
  | Try_e (body, handlers) ->
      (* .try { body; leave } catch E1 { pop; h1; leave } catch E2 ... *)
      let result = if x.ty = Unit then -1 else local k (sig_of c x.ty) in
      let keep () = if result >= 0 then emit k (Il.Stloc result) in
      let start = label k and out = label k in
      let starts = List.map (fun _ -> label k) handlers in
      k.trys <- k.trys + 1;
      place k start;
      exp c k body; keep (); emit k (Il.Leave out);
      List.iteri (fun i (xn, h) ->
          place k (List.nth starts i);
          emit k Il.Pop;
          exp c k h; keep (); emit k (Il.Leave out);
          let stop = if i + 1 < List.length starts then List.nth starts (i + 1) else out in
          k.clauses <- (start, List.hd starts, List.nth starts i, stop, fst (exn_ctor c xn)) :: k.clauses)
        handlers;
      k.trys <- k.trys - 1;
      place k out;
      if result >= 0 then emit k (Il.Ldloc result)
  | Raise_e xn -> emit k (Il.Newobj (snd (exn_ctor c xn))); emit k Il.Throw

(* an expression whose value, if it has one, is not wanted *)
and stmt (c : t) (k : code) (x : exp) : unit =
  exp c k x;
  if x.ty <> Unit then emit k Il.Pop

and loop (_c : t) (k : code) (out : int) (body : unit -> unit) : unit =
  k.loops <- (out, k.trys) :: k.loops;
  body ();
  k.loops <- List.tl k.loops

and load (c : t) (k : code) (lv : lvalue) : unit =
  match lv with
  | Simple v -> load_var c k v
  | Field (lv, r, i) -> load c k lv; emit k (Il.Ldfld (field_tok c r i))
  | Subscript (lv, a, i) -> load c k lv; exp c k i; emit k (Il.Ldelem (kind_of a.elem))

and assign (c : t) (k : code) (lv : lvalue) (value : unit -> unit) : unit =
  match lv with
  | Simple v -> store_var c k v value
  | Field (lv, r, i) -> load c k lv; value (); emit k (Il.Stfld (field_tok c r i))
  | Subscript (lv, a, i) -> load c k lv; exp c k i; value (); emit k (Il.Stelem (kind_of a.elem))

(* an operator, its two operands pushed; a comparison leaves 0 or 1 *)
and oper (c : t) (k : code) (ty : ty) (op : Tiger_ast.oper) : unit =
  let negate () = emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.zero); emit k Il.Ceq in
  let str = S.String and int = S.I4 in
  match op, ty with
  | Tiger_ast.Plus, _ -> emit k (Il.Binop Il.Add)
  | Tiger_ast.Minus, _ -> emit k (Il.Binop Il.Sub)
  | Tiger_ast.Times, _ -> emit k (Il.Binop Il.Mul)
  | Tiger_ast.Divide, _ -> emit k (Il.Binop Il.Div)
  | (Tiger_ast.Eq | Tiger_ast.Neq), String ->
      emit k (Il.Call (lib c "String" "op_Equality" (static [ str; str ] S.Bool)));
      if op = Tiger_ast.Neq then negate ()
  | Tiger_ast.Eq, _ -> emit k Il.Ceq
  | Tiger_ast.Neq, _ -> emit k Il.Ceq; negate ()
  | _, String ->
      (* String.CompareOrdinal(a, b), then compared with 0 *)
      emit k (Il.Call (lib c "String" "CompareOrdinal" (static [ str; str ] int)));
      emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.zero);
      oper c k Int op
  | Tiger_ast.Lt, _ -> emit k (Il.Clt false)
  | Tiger_ast.Gt, _ -> emit k (Il.Cgt false)
  | Tiger_ast.Le, _ -> emit k (Il.Cgt false); negate ()
  | Tiger_ast.Ge, _ -> emit k (Il.Clt false); negate ()

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* Functions *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

let func (c : t) (f : func) : unit =
  let k = { ops = []; n = 0; labels = Hashtbl.create 16; nlabels = 0; locals = []; nlocals = 0;
            slots = Hashtbl.create 8; clauses = []; fn = f; loops = []; trys = 0 } in
  (* its frame, when it has functions of its own: local 0; its link,
   * its parameters that escape copied in *)
  if f.nested then begin
    let cls, ctor = frame c f in
    ignore (local k (S.Class cls));
    emit k (Il.Newobj ctor); emit k (Il.Stloc 0);
    (match f.parent with
     | Some _ -> emit k (Il.Ldloc 0); emit k (Il.Ldarg 0); emit k (Il.Stfld (link c f))
     | None -> ());
    List.iter (fun v -> if v.escapes then begin
        emit k (Il.Ldloc 0); emit k (Il.Ldarg (arg_of k v)); emit k (Il.Stfld (var_field c v))
      end) f.params
  end;
  let body = match f.fbody with Some b -> b | None -> failwith "Tiger_emit: a function without its body" in
  if f.parent = None then begin
    (* Tiger's strings are bytes: the console's text read and written as
     * Latin-1, a byte a character (.NET's default, UTF-8, would make
     * two of a byte above 127, and read them back as one) *)
    let latin1 = lib c "Encoding" "get_Latin1" (static [] (S.Class (sys c "Encoding"))) in
    List.iter (fun dir ->
        emit k (Il.Call latin1);
        emit k (Il.Call (lib c "Console" ("set_" ^ dir ^ "Encoding") (static [ S.Class (sys c "Encoding") ] S.Void))))
      [ "Input"; "Output" ];
    (* Main: the program's value, if an int, its exit status *)
    if body.ty = Int then exp c k body else (stmt c k body; emit k (Il.Ldc_i4 Int32.zero))
  end else exp c k body;
  emit k Il.Ret;
  finish c k (method_of c f)

let program (name : string) (p : program) : string =
  let w = W.create name in
  let runtime = W.assembly_ref w "System.Runtime" in
  let console = W.type_ref w (W.assembly_ref w "System.Console") "System" "Console" in
  let obj = W.type_ref w runtime "System" "Object" in
  let program = W.type_def w "" "Program" 0x00100181 obj in
  let library = W.type_def w "" "Tiger" 0x00100181 obj in
  let c = { w; runtime; console; program; library; memo = Hashtbl.create 64 } in
  Hashtbl.replace c.memo "type Object" obj;
  let main = method_of c p.main in
  W.set_entry_point w main;
  func c p.main;
  List.iter (func c) p.funcs;
  W.write w
languages/tiger/dotnet/Tiger_emit.mli
2620
(* Tiger to .NET: a program's tree (Tiger_tree) as an assembly's bytes
 * (Writer), which Microsoft's dotnet and mini-dotnet both run. The
 * plan's lesson 2: a language put on a machine that was not made for
 * it, Tiger's nested functions on .NET's static methods.
 *
 *     Tiger                      .NET
 *     int, string                int32, System.String
 *     a record type              a class of fields (its name and a number)
 *     an array type              T[]
 *     nil                        null
 *     = on strings               String::op_Equality: their text
 *     = on records, arrays       ceq: the same object
 *     exception e                a class of System.Exception's
 *     raise e                    newobj e; throw
 *     try ... handle e ...       .try, a catch e for each handler
 *     the program                Program::Main, its int value the exit status
 *     a function                 a static method of Program
 *     print, ord, substring...   the class Tiger's, a few instructions on
 *                                Console and String
 *
 * {b Nested functions, which .NET has not.} A function whose variables
 * a function nested in it uses (they escape: Tiger_semant) gets a
 * frame, an object of a class of its own: those variables are its
 * fields, the others stay IL's locals and arguments. A nested function
 * takes its parent's frame as its first argument, the static link, and
 * a frame keeps its parent's in its field `link`:
 *
 *     let var n := 0                       class frame_main { int n_1; }
 *         function add(k: int) =           static void add_3(frame_main link, int k)
 *           let function twice() =           frame_add_3 f = new frame_add_3();
 *                 (n := n + k;                 f.link = link; f.k_4 = k;
 *                  n := n + k)                 twice_6(f);
 *           in twice() end                 static void twice_6(frame_add_3 link)
 *     in add(5); printi(n) end               link.link.n_1 = link.link.n_1 + link.k_4 ...
 *
 * Where a C compiler keeps the frame on the stack and the static link
 * in a register, here they are objects on the heap, collected; a
 * function with no nested function has no frame at all, as Appel's
 * escape analysis lets a C compiler keep its variables in registers.
 *
 * A method's .maxstack is the writer's (Writer computes it); a try is
 * entered with an empty stack, as .NET asks: Tiger's try is a statement
 * in the programs here (inside an expression it would not be). *)

(* the assembly of this name *)
val program : string -> Tiger_tree.program -> string

type t = Knob of float * float | Switch | Selector of string list

let on (x : float) : bool = x >= 0.5
let of_bool (b : bool) : float = if b then 1. else 0.
let index (x : float) : int = int_of_float (Float.round x)

let to_string (c : t) (x : float) : string =
  match c with
  | Knob _ -> Printf.sprintf "%.3f" x
  | Switch -> if on x then "on" else "off"
  | Selector labels -> List.nth labels (index x)

let of_string (c : t) (s : string) : float option =
  match c with
  | Knob (lo, hi) -> Option.map (fun x -> Float.min hi (Float.max lo x)) (float_of_string_opt s)
  | Switch -> ( match s with "on" -> Some 1. | "off" -> Some 0. | _ -> None)
  | Selector labels ->
      let rec find i = function [] -> None | l :: rest -> if l = s then Some (float_of_int i) else find (i + 1) rest in
      find 0 labels

(* A control on a panel: what an instrument's or an effect's knob is,
 * so that a program can draw it, a patch can store it, and a text file
 * can say it.
 *
 * Every control's value is a float, whatever it looks like:
 *
 *     Knob (from, to)   turned between two values, in the control's own
 *                       units (0 to 1, dB, seconds, hertz)
 *     Switch            off (0) or on (1): a rocker
 *     Selector labels   a position (0, 1, 2, ...) of a rotary switch,
 *                       each named by its label
 *
 * so a panel is a list of named controls and a patch a list of named
 * numbers, and the text form writes a switch as on or off and a
 * selector by its label: "reverb.kind = plate", not "2". *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Control.mli (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

type t = Knob of float * float (* from, to *) | Switch | Selector of string list

(* [on x]: a switch's value read, 0.5 and above on *)
val on : float -> bool
val of_bool : bool -> float

(* [index x]: a selector's value read, rounded *)
val index : float -> int

(* [to_string c x]: "0.375", "on", "plate" *)
val to_string : t -> float -> string

(* [of_string c s]: the value [s] says, a knob's kept within its range;
 * None if it isn't one *)
val of_string : t -> string -> float option

(* See Instrument.mli *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Instrument.ml (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

type t = {
  note_on : int -> float -> unit;
  note_off : int -> unit;
  set : string -> float -> unit;
  fill : Signal.stereo -> unit;
}

let gate_samples = 0.005 *. float_of_int Signal.rate

(* the sine's state: the key sounding, its pitch and velocity; the
 * oscillator's phase (0 to 1); the gate's level, ramping to the
 * velocity or to 0; the volume knob, and its value at the last block,
 * ramped from *)
type sine = {
  mutable key : int option;
  mutable frequency : float;
  mutable velocity : float;
  mutable phase : float;
  mutable gate : float;
  mutable volume : float;
  mutable last_volume : float;
}

let sine () : t =
  let s = { key = None; frequency = 440.; velocity = 1.; phase = 0.; gate = 0.; volume = 0.5; last_volume = 0.5 } in
  let note_on key velocity =
    s.key <- Some key;
    s.frequency <- Music.midi_frequency key;
    s.velocity <- velocity
  in
  let note_off key = if s.key = Some key then s.key <- None in
  let set name value = if name = "volume" then s.volume <- Float.min 1. (Float.max 0. value) in
  let fill (out : Signal.stereo) =
    let n = Array.length out.left in
    let target = if s.key = None then 0. else s.velocity in
    let step = 1. /. gate_samples in
    let dphase = s.frequency /. float_of_int Signal.rate in
    for i = 0 to n - 1 do
      (* the gate: towards its target, a 5 ms ramp's step at a time *)
      s.gate <- (if s.gate < target then Float.min target (s.gate +. step) else Float.max target (s.gate -. step));
      (* the knob: from the last block's value to this one's *)
      let volume = s.last_volume +. ((s.volume -. s.last_volume) *. float_of_int (i + 1) /. float_of_int n) in
      let x = volume *. s.gate *. sin (2. *. Float.pi *. s.phase) in
      out.left.(i) <- x;
      out.right.(i) <- x;
      s.phase <- Float.rem (s.phase +. dphase) 1.
    done;
    s.last_volume <- s.volume
  in
  { note_on; note_off; set; fill }
lib_audio/Instrument.mli
3968
(* An instrument: a sound played live, its notes and its knobs arriving
 * while it sounds (see notes_synth.md section 1).
 *
 * The rest of audio/ renders ahead: a sound is a value (Synth.t), its
 * samples computed whole when it is played. A synthesizer can't be:
 * when a key goes down nobody knows yet when it comes up, and someone
 * may turn the filter's knob in between. So an instrument is a
 * *process*: a state, changed by events, asked for the next block of
 * samples.
 *
 *     update, 60 a second            the sound card, 44,100 a second
 *
 *     note_on 60 ----.
 *     set "volume" --+--> [ state ] --fill--> the next n samples --> Mixer
 *     note_off 60 ---'       ^  |                  (a pull: 735 a frame)
 *                            '--'
 *                     kept from block to block
 *
 * Every live block of plan_synth_teaching.md (the oscillators, the
 * ladder, the envelopes, the effects) follows the same pattern, shown
 * here on the smallest instrument there is, [sine]:
 *
 *  - its parameters and its memory in one record of mutable fields,
 *    hidden behind the .mli: the oscillator's phase, the gate's level,
 *    the knobs. Mutable, as the DSP books write them and as a sound
 *    card pulls them: a block computed in place, nothing allocated per
 *    sample, the state the process's own business;
 *  - an event (a key, a knob) changes the state *between* blocks, and
 *    is heard from the next one: an event's time is a block's
 *    boundary. With a pull per frame (a golden run, -dump-frame) a
 *    note played at frame k starts at sample 735 k; natively ~50 ms of
 *    queue lie ahead of it too, the latency of Audio.mli's two clocks;
 *  - [fill] computes a block, and a knob's new value is *ramped* over
 *    it rather than jumped to. A volume going from 0.2 to 0.8 at once
 *    is a step in the wave, heard as a click; a knob turned slowly is a
 *    step every block, a click 60 times a second, the "zipper noise"
 *    of the first digital synthesizers.
 *
 * Worked example, the ramp: the volume turned from 0.2 to 0.8, over a
 * block of 735 samples. Sample i (from 0) gets
 *
 *     0.2 + 0.6 (i + 1) / 735          0.20082, 0.20163, ..., 0.8
 *
 * neighbours 0.6 / 735 = 0.00082 apart, instead of 0.6 once. The gate
 * is ramped the same way, over 5 ms (220.5 samples: a key pressed,
 * 0 to 1 in 221 samples; released, back to 0), so a note never starts
 * or stops on a jump.
 *
 * [t] is a record of functions -- an object in all but name -- because
 * the mixer holds instruments of different kinds (this sine, the
 * Minimoog) and wants the same four things from each; the state
 * stays inside, in the closures.
 *
 * References: Will Pirkle, Designing Software Synthesizer Plug-Ins in
 * C++, 2014 (chapter 2: the plug-in's process of blocks, the
 * parameters smoothed); Steinberg's VST 2 SDK, 1999, whose
 * processReplacing (a block of samples in, a block out, in place) is
 * the shape every plug-in API has had since. *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Instrument.mli (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

type t = {
  (* a key goes down: its number (MIDI's, 60 middle C, 69 the A at 440
   * Hz: Music.midi_frequency), its velocity, 0 to 1 *)
  note_on : int -> float -> unit;
  (* the key comes up *)
  note_off : int -> unit;
  (* a knob turned, by its name, to a value; names the instrument
   * doesn't have are ignored *)
  set : string -> float -> unit;
  (* the next block: both channels written over, their length the
   * block's *)
  fill : Signal.stereo -> unit;
}

(* [sine ()]: one sine wave, playing the last key pressed until that key
 * is let go (another key's release is ignored; a key pressed while one
 * sounds changes the pitch at once, the wave going on: legato); its
 * velocity the loudness, the gate ramped over 5 ms; one knob, "volume",
 * 0 to 1, 0.5 at first. *)
val sine : unit -> t

(* the gate's ramp, in samples: 5 ms *)
val gate_samples : float
lib_audio/Mixer.ml
14891
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Mixer.mli *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Mixer.ml; its optional arguments are said (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

(* a one-shot: its samples, and how far it's been read.
 * ix: or a recording kept as it is, its volume, pan and far ear's delay
 * applied as it is mixed (play_at): mini-doom's and mini-quake's sounds
 * of the monsters, each made louder and panned at each play, were the
 * whole sound rendered again into new arrays (plan_virtuaracing.md,
 * stage 5). [len]: its length, its delay in; [scaled] = None, [samples]
 * as they are.
 * old: type shot = { samples : Signal.stereo; mutable at : int } *)
type scaled = {
  volume : float;
  gain_left : float;
  gain_right : float;
  late_left : int;
  late_right : int;
}
type shot = {
  samples : Signal.stereo;
  mutable at : int;
  len : int;
  scaled : scaled option;
}

(* a continuous voice: what it should play, its state, whether it was
 * kept since the last pull, its filter, and its pan (and the last
 * pull's, to glide from) *)
type continuous = {
  mutable voice : Synth.voice;
  mutable running : Synth.running;
  mutable kept : bool;
  mutable filter : Synth.filter option;
  memory : Filter.memory;
  mutable pan : float;
  mutable last_pan : float;
}

(* a loop: its samples, how far read (wrapping at the end), how many
 * samples of it have gone out in all (not wrapping: the loop's clock),
 * and whether it's being stopped *)
type looped = { sound : Signal.stereo; mutable pos : int; mutable played : int; mutable stopping : bool; prepare : int -> int -> unit }

(* an instrument: what it is, and whether it's being stopped *)
type played_live = { live : Instrument.t; mutable ending : bool }

type t = {
  mutable shots : shot list;
  continuous : (string, continuous) Hashtbl.t;
  loops : (string, looped) Hashtbl.t;
  instruments : (string, played_live) Hashtbl.t;
}

let max_playing = 32
let stereo = ref true
let length (s : Signal.stereo) : int = Array.length s.left
let create () : t = { shots = []; continuous = Hashtbl.create 8; loops = Hashtbl.create 2; instruments = Hashtbl.create 2 }

(* ix: loop_prepared and change_prepared, and loop and change over them *)
let loop_prepared (m : t) (name : string) (sound : Signal.stereo) (prepare : int -> int -> unit) : unit =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt m.loops name with
  | Some l when not l.stopping -> ()
  | _ -> if length sound > 0 then Hashtbl.replace m.loops name { sound; pos = 0; played = 0; stopping = false; prepare }

let change_prepared (m : t) (name : string) (sound : Signal.stereo) (prepare : int -> int -> unit) : unit =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt m.loops name with
  | Some l when (not l.stopping) && length sound > 0 ->
      (* (in floats: a tune's place times a tune's length is past an
       * int of 31 bits)
       * old: let pos = l.pos * length sound / length l.sound in *)
      let pos = int_of_float (float_of_int l.pos *. float_of_int (length sound) /. float_of_int (length l.sound)) in
      Hashtbl.replace m.loops name { l with sound; pos = min pos (length sound - 1); prepare }
  | _ -> loop_prepared m name sound prepare

let nothing (_ : int) (_ : int) : unit = ()
let loop (m : t) (name : string) (sound : Signal.stereo) : unit = loop_prepared m name sound nothing
let change (m : t) (name : string) (sound : Signal.stereo) : unit = change_prepared m name sound nothing

let stop (m : t) (name : string) : unit =
  Option.iter (fun l -> l.stopping <- true) (Hashtbl.find_opt m.loops name);
  Option.iter (fun i -> i.ending <- true) (Hashtbl.find_opt m.instruments name)

let looping (m : t) : string list = Hashtbl.fold (fun name _ acc -> name :: acc) m.loops [] |> List.sort compare

let instrument (m : t) (name : string) (live : Instrument.t) : unit =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt m.instruments name with
  | Some i when not i.ending -> ()
  | _ -> Hashtbl.replace m.instruments name { live; ending = false }

let instruments (m : t) : string list =
  Hashtbl.fold (fun name i acc -> if i.ending then acc else name :: acc) m.instruments [] |> List.sort compare

let add_shot (m : t) (shot : shot) : unit =
  (* the newest first; past max_playing, the oldest dropped *)
  m.shots <- List.filteri (fun i _ -> i < max_playing) (shot :: m.shots)

let play (m : t) (samples : Signal.stereo) : unit =
  add_shot m { samples; at = 0; len = length samples; scaled = None }

(* ix: Synth.render_stereo's of Panned (pan, louder volume (Samples x)),
 * without its arrays: each sample gain *. (x *. volume), the far ear's
 * zeros before it, the near one's after it *)
let play_at (m : t) (x : Signal.t) ~(volume : float) ~(pan : float) : unit =
  let (gain_left, gain_right) = Space.pan pan in
  let d = if !Space.ears_apart then Space.interaural_delay pan else 0 in
  let (late_left, late_right) = if pan > 0. then (d, 0) else (0, d) in
  add_shot m
    { samples = Signal.both x; at = 0; len = Array.length x + d;
      scaled = Some { volume; gain_left; gain_right; late_left; late_right } }

(* a shot's j-th sample, in each ear *)
let shot_left (s : shot) (j : int) : float =
  match s.scaled with
  | None -> s.samples.left.(j)
  | Some c ->
      let j = j - c.late_left in
      if j < 0 || j >= Array.length s.samples.left then 0.
      else c.gain_left *. (s.samples.left.(j) *. c.volume)

let shot_right (s : shot) (j : int) : float =
  match s.scaled with
  | None -> s.samples.right.(j)
  | Some c ->
      let j = j - c.late_right in
      if j < 0 || j >= Array.length s.samples.right then 0.
      else c.gain_right *. (s.samples.right.(j) *. c.volume)

(* ix: filter and pan were optional: none, 0 *)
let keep ~(filter : Synth.filter option) ~(pan : float) (m : t) (name : string) (voice : Synth.voice) : unit =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt m.continuous name with
  | Some c ->
      c.voice <- voice;
      c.filter <- filter;
      c.pan <- pan;
      c.kept <- true
  | None ->
      Hashtbl.replace m.continuous name
        { voice; running = Synth.start (); kept = true; filter; memory = Filter.silence (); pan; last_pan = pan }

(* old: pull, the mixing in float arrays (pull below, flat := false) *)
let pull_boxed (m : t) (n : int) : Signal.stereo =
  let left = Array.make n 0. and right = Array.make n 0. in
  (* the one-shots' next samples *)
  m.shots
  |> List.iter (fun s ->
         let k = min n (s.len - s.at) in
         for i = 0 to k - 1 do
           left.(i) <- left.(i) +. shot_left s (s.at + i);
           right.(i) <- right.(i) +. shot_right s (s.at + i)
         done;
         s.at <- s.at + k);
  m.shots <- List.filter (fun s -> s.at < s.len) m.shots;
  (* the continuous ones: going on, or fading out if not kept *)
  let gone = ref [] in
  m.continuous
  |> Hashtbl.iter (fun name c ->
         let samples =
           if c.kept then (
             let (samples, running) = Synth.continue c.running c.voice n in
             c.running <- running;
             samples)
           else (
             gone := name :: !gone;
             Synth.release c.running c.voice n)
         in
         let samples =
           match c.filter with
           | None -> samples
           | Some f ->
               let q = Filter.biquad f.kind ~cutoff:f.cutoff ~q:f.q in
               Array.map (Filter.step q c.memory) samples
         in
         (* the pan gliding from the last pull's to this one's, like the
          * volume (Synth.continue): no click when a source moves *)
         let (l0, r0) = Space.pan c.last_pan and (l1, r1) = Space.pan c.pan in
         Array.iteri
           (fun i x ->
             let a = float_of_int (i + 1) /. float_of_int n in
             left.(i) <- left.(i) +. (x *. (l0 +. ((l1 -. l0) *. a)));
             right.(i) <- right.(i) +. (x *. (r0 +. ((r1 -. r0) *. a))))
           samples;
         c.last_pan <- c.pan;
         c.kept <- false);
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove m.continuous) !gone;
  (* the loops: read around and around; a stopped one fades out over
   * this pull, then is gone *)
  let stopped = ref [] in
  m.loops
  |> Hashtbl.iter (fun name l ->
         let len = length l.sound in
         l.prepare l.pos n;
         for i = 0 to n - 1 do
           let fade = if l.stopping then 1. -. (float_of_int i /. float_of_int n) else 1. in
           left.(i) <- left.(i) +. (fade *. l.sound.left.(l.pos));
           right.(i) <- right.(i) +. (fade *. l.sound.right.(l.pos));
           l.pos <- (l.pos + 1) mod len
         done;
         l.played <- l.played + n;
         if l.stopping then stopped := name :: !stopped);
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove m.loops) !stopped;
  (* the instruments: a block each; a stopped one fades out over this
   * pull, like a loop, then is gone *)
  let ended = ref [] in
  m.instruments
  |> Hashtbl.iter (fun name i ->
         let block : Signal.stereo = { left = Array.make n 0.; right = Array.make n 0. } in
         i.live.fill block;
         for k = 0 to n - 1 do
           let fade = if i.ending then 1. -. (float_of_int k /. float_of_int n) else 1. in
           left.(k) <- left.(k) +. (fade *. block.left.(k));
           right.(k) <- right.(k) +. (fade *. block.right.(k))
         done;
         if i.ending then ended := name :: !ended);
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove m.instruments) !ended;
  let out : Signal.stereo = { left = Mix.limit ~soft:true left; right = Mix.limit ~soft:true right } in
  if !stereo then out else Signal.both (Signal.mono out)

(* ix: the same mixing, in the same order, in flat arrays (Float.Array):
 * by mini-ml, each sample stored in a float array was a new block and
 * the write barrier, and each continuous voice's a pair and a running
 * (Synth.continue_into); the samples the same, made float arrays at
 * the end only. mini-virtuaracing's engine, road and wind, 3.2M
 * instructions a sixtieth of a second on arm (plan_virtuaracing.md,
 * stage 5) *)
let flat = ref true

let pull (m : t) (n : int) : Signal.stereo =
  if not !flat then pull_boxed m n else begin
  let left = Float.Array.make n 0. and right = Float.Array.make n 0. in
  let add (a : Float.Array.t) (i : int) (x : float) : unit =
    Float.Array.set a i (Float.Array.get a i +. x)
  in
  m.shots
  |> List.iter (fun s ->
         let k = min n (s.len - s.at) in
         (match s.scaled with
          | None ->
              let l = s.samples.left and r = s.samples.right in
              for i = 0 to k - 1 do
                Float.Array.unsafe_set left i
                  (Float.Array.unsafe_get left i +. l.(s.at + i));
                Float.Array.unsafe_set right i
                  (Float.Array.unsafe_get right i +. r.(s.at + i))
              done
          | Some c ->
              (* (shot_left's and shot_right's, the shot's kind looked at
               * once: a sample out of the recording, a delay's, adds
               * nothing) *)
              let x = s.samples.left and nx = Array.length s.samples.left in
              let v = c.volume in
              (* OPTIMIZATION (ranges): a channel's samples whose place in
               * the recording is inside it found once, then a loop with no
               * test: the same sums. mini-quake's fight, 13 shots at once:
               * 110 arm instructions a shot and sample to 58 (29 a
               * channel), its sound 2.1M a sixtieth of a second to 0.52M
               * (with Mix.soft_clip's rational tanh)
               * old: for i = 0 to k - 1, jl = s.at + i - c.late_left and
               * jr, each tested, then add left i (c.gain_left *. (x.(jl)
               * *. c.volume)), and add right i ... *)
              let channel (out : Float.Array.t) (g : float) (late : int) :
                  unit =
                let base = s.at - late in
                for i = max 0 (-base) to min k (nx - base) - 1 do
                  Float.Array.unsafe_set out i
                    (Float.Array.unsafe_get out i
                    +. (g *. (Array.unsafe_get x (base + i) *. v)))
                done
              in
              channel left c.gain_left c.late_left;
              channel right c.gain_right c.late_right);
         s.at <- s.at + k);
  m.shots <- List.filter (fun s -> s.at < s.len) m.shots;
  let samples = Float.Array.make n 0. and gone = ref [] in
  m.continuous
  |> Hashtbl.iter (fun name c ->
         if c.kept then c.running <- Synth.continue_into c.running c.voice samples n
         else (
           gone := name :: !gone;
           let silent = { c.voice with volume = 0. } in
           ignore (Synth.continue_into c.running silent samples n));
         (match c.filter with
          | None -> ()
          | Some f ->
              let q = Filter.biquad f.kind ~cutoff:f.cutoff ~q:f.q in
              for i = 0 to n - 1 do
                let x = Float.Array.get samples i in
                Float.Array.set samples i (Filter.step q c.memory x)
              done);
         let (l0, r0) = Space.pan c.last_pan and (l1, r1) = Space.pan c.pan in
         for i = 0 to n - 1 do
           let x = Float.Array.get samples i in
           let a = float_of_int (i + 1) /. float_of_int n in
           add left i (x *. (l0 +. ((l1 -. l0) *. a)));
           add right i (x *. (r0 +. ((r1 -. r0) *. a)))
         done;
         c.last_pan <- c.pan;
         c.kept <- false);
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove m.continuous) !gone;
  let stopped = ref [] in
  m.loops
  |> Hashtbl.iter (fun name l ->
         let len = length l.sound in
         l.prepare l.pos n;
         for i = 0 to n - 1 do
           let fade = if l.stopping then 1. -. (float_of_int i /. float_of_int n) else 1. in
           add left i (fade *. l.sound.left.(l.pos));
           add right i (fade *. l.sound.right.(l.pos));
           l.pos <- (l.pos + 1) mod len
         done;
         l.played <- l.played + n;
         if l.stopping then stopped := name :: !stopped);
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove m.loops) !stopped;
  let ended = ref [] in
  m.instruments
  |> Hashtbl.iter (fun name i ->
         let block : Signal.stereo = { left = Array.make n 0.; right = Array.make n 0. } in
         i.live.fill block;
         for k = 0 to n - 1 do
           let fade = if i.ending then 1. -. (float_of_int k /. float_of_int n) else 1. in
           add left k (fade *. block.left.(k));
           add right k (fade *. block.right.(k))
         done;
         if i.ending then ended := name :: !ended);
  List.iter (Hashtbl.remove m.instruments) !ended;
  let limit (a : Float.Array.t) : Signal.t =
    Array.init n (fun i -> Mix.soft_clip (Float.Array.get a i))
  in
  let out : Signal.stereo = { left = limit left; right = limit right } in
  if !stereo then out else Signal.both (Signal.mono out)
  end

let playing (m : t) : int * int = (List.length m.shots, Hashtbl.length m.continuous)
let played (m : t) (name : string) : int option = Option.map (fun l -> l.played) (Hashtbl.find_opt m.loops name)
lib_audio/Mixer.mli
6083
(* The mixer: every sound playing, summed into the samples the sound card
 * takes (see notes_audio.md sections 5 and 10). The stateful part of
 * audio/: the sounds come and go as the game plays them.
 *
 *    play blip ---------.                        the one-shots: rendered
 *    play jump ---------+--> [ + ] --> tanh -->  once, read through as the
 *    keep "thrust" -----+      ^       samples   samples go out; the
 *    instrument "moog" -'      |                 continuous ones: advanced
 *                              |                 frame by frame; the
 *                     pull n: the next n         instruments: asked for
 *                                                the next block
 *
 * Two clocks: the game's, 60 frames a second, and the sound card's,
 * 44,100 samples a second, pulling on its own (notes_audio.md section
 * 10). The platform calls [pull] with how many samples the card needs
 * (native: SDL's queue topped up to ~50 ms ahead; a golden run: exactly
 * 735 a frame, 44,100 / 60), so the mixer never waits nor rushes. A
 * one-shot starts at the next sample pulled; a continuous sound is
 * [keep]ed each frame, and when a [pull] finds it not kept since the
 * last one, it fades out over that pull and is gone.
 *
 * The sum goes through tanh (Mix.soft_clip): many sounds at once get
 * squeezed rather than cut flat. At most [max_playing] one-shots: past
 * it, the oldest is dropped (a backend not pulling, the web one before
 * phase 4, can't pile them up forever).
 *
 * References: Game Programming Patterns, "Event Queue" (Robert
 * Nystrom, 2014: playing sounds from game code, and why a queue); SDL's
 * SDL_QueueAudio, https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL2/SDL_QueueAudio *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Mixer.mli; its optional arguments are said (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 The mixer} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type t

val create : unit -> t

(* one-shots at most at once *)
val max_playing : int

(* false: every pull mixed down to one channel, the same in both (the
 * software backend's "m" key, to hear what panning does); true by
 * default *)
val stereo : bool ref

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Playing sounds} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [play m s]: [s] from the next sample pulled *)
val play : t -> Signal.stereo -> unit

(* [play_at m x ~volume ~pan]: the recording [x] made louder and panned
 * (Synth.louder, Synth.Panned), the same samples, but mixed from [x]
 * itself as it is pulled: no new arrays at each play *)
val play_at : t -> Signal.t -> volume:float -> pan:float -> unit

(* [loop m name s]: [s] played over and over, from the next sample,
 * unless a loop [name] is already playing (so calling it every frame
 * is harmless): background music *)
val loop : t -> string -> Signal.stereo -> unit

(* [change m name s]: the loop [name] now [s], from the same point of
 * it (the same fraction of the way through: a tune made faster goes
 * on from the same note), its clock ([played]) going on; a new loop if
 * none is playing *)
val change : t -> string -> Signal.stereo -> unit

(* ix's own: [loop_prepared m name s prepare] and [change_prepared]: as
 * [loop] and [change], and before each pull [prepare pos n] is called:
 * the [n] samples of [s] from [pos] (around its end) are about to be
 * read. For a loop whose samples are computed as it is played
 * (Synth.pieces), [s] being zeros until then. *)
val loop_prepared : t -> string -> Signal.stereo -> (int -> int -> unit) -> unit
val change_prepared : t -> string -> Signal.stereo -> (int -> int -> unit) -> unit

(* [stop m name]: the loop or the instrument [name] stopped (faded out
 * over its next pull), if playing *)
val stop : t -> string -> unit

(* [keep ~filter ~pan m name v]: the continuous voice [name] playing [v] until the
 * next pull at least, through [filter] if one (its cutoff fixed at
 * [cutoff]; changed from frame to frame, the filter's memory kept),
 * panned by [pan] (0 the middle; changed from frame to
 * frame, it glides over the pull) *)
val keep : filter:Synth.filter option -> pan:float -> t -> string -> Synth.voice -> unit

(* [instrument m name i]: the instrument [i] (Instrument.mli) playing
 * from the next pull, a block of it each pull, until [stop m name];
 * nothing if an instrument [name] is already playing (so asking for it
 * every frame is harmless, as for [loop]). Its notes and knobs are the
 * caller's, through [i]'s functions: the mixer only pulls. *)
val instrument : t -> string -> Instrument.t -> unit

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Pulling samples} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [pull m n]: the next [n] samples, in both channels *)
val pull : t -> int -> Signal.stereo

(* false: the mixing in float arrays, the old way (the same samples);
 * true, the default: in flat ones, which mini-ml makes without a block
 * for each sample *)
val flat : bool ref

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 What is playing} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* one-shots playing, continuous voices kept (for tests, debug) *)
val playing : t -> int * int

(* loops playing *)
val looping : t -> string list

(* instruments playing (not those being stopped) *)
val instruments : t -> string list

(* [played m name]: how many samples of the loop [name] have gone out,
 * counting every time round -- the loop's own clock, which unlike its
 * read position does not go back to 0 at the end. None if no such loop
 * is playing. It is what a rhythm game has to time its steps by
 * (Audio.mli's [position], TinyDDR.ml): the frame
 * clock is the game's, and this one is the music's. *)
val played : t -> string -> int option

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Music.mli *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Music.ml; a constructor of Synth's said with its module where mini-ml asks; a score played a block at a time (play_score, fill_score) is ix's (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

let midi_frequency (n : int) : float = 440. *. (2. ** (float_of_int (n - 69) /. 12.))

let midi_number (name : string) : int option =
  let letter = function 'C' -> Some 0 | 'D' -> Some 2 | 'E' -> Some 4 | 'F' -> Some 5 | 'G' -> Some 7 | 'A' -> Some 9 | 'B' -> Some 11 | _ -> None in
  let n = String.length name in
  if n < 2 then None
  else
    match letter (Char.uppercase_ascii name.[0]) with
    | None -> None
    | Some semitone -> (
        let (accidental, rest) =
          match name.[1] with '#' -> (1, String.sub name 2 (n - 2)) | 'b' -> (-1, String.sub name 2 (n - 2)) | _ -> (0, String.sub name 1 (n - 1))
        in
        match int_of_string_opt rest with
        | Some octave when octave >= -1 && octave <= 9 -> Some (((octave + 1) * 12) + semitone + accidental)
        | _ -> None)

let frequency (name : string) : float = match midi_number name with Some n -> midi_frequency n | None -> 0.

let instrument ~(voice : int) ~(voices : int) : Oscillator.waveform * float =
  if voices > 1 && voice = voices - 1 then (Triangle, 0.5) else if voice = 0 then (Square, 0.3) else (Square, 0.18)

(* a drum, by its General MIDI key: short, whatever the note's length --
 * a bass drum a triangle falling from 150 to 50 Hz, a snare noise, a
 * hi-hat short bright noise. Shared by MIDI's channel 10 and a tune's
 * percussion voice (Abc.mli's clef=perc). *)
let drum ~(volume : float) (key : int) : Synth.t =
  let v source f = Synth.Voice { source; frequency = f; slide = None; seconds = 0.2; volume; fade = false; effects = []; envelope = None } in
  match key with
  | 35 | 36 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Triangle) 150. |> Synth.sliding 50. |> Synth.lasting 0.15 |> Synth.fading |> Synth.louder 2.
  | 38 | 40 -> v Synth.Noise 5000. |> Synth.lasting 0.15 |> Synth.fading
  | 42 | 44 | 46 -> v Synth.Noise 12000. |> Synth.lasting 0.05 |> Synth.fading |> Synth.louder 0.6
  | _ -> v Synth.Noise 3000. |> Synth.lasting 0.1 |> Synth.fading

let to_sound (tune : Abc.tune) : Synth.t =
  let voices = List.length tune.voices in
  let silence seconds = Synth.voice (Wave Sine) 0. |> Synth.louder 0. |> Synth.lasting seconds in
  Synth.Together
    (List.mapi
       (fun i events ->
         let (waveform, volume) = instrument ~voice:i ~voices in
         let is_drums = List.nth_opt tune.drums i = Some true in
         Synth.After
           (List.map
              (fun (e : Abc.event) ->
                match e.notes with
                | [] -> silence e.length
                | notes when is_drums ->
                    (* the drums of a clef=perc voice: each struck, and
                     * the rest of the note's time silent *)
                    Synth.Together (silence e.length :: List.map (drum ~volume:0.25) notes)
                | notes ->
                    let sounding = e.length *. 0.9 in
                    Synth.After
                      [ Synth.Together
                          (List.map
                             (fun n -> Synth.voice (Wave waveform) (midi_frequency n) |> Synth.lasting sounding |> Synth.louder (volume /. 0.5))
                             notes);
                        silence (e.length -. sounding) ])
              events))
       tune.voices)

(* a MIDI note's sound: its instrument, from its channel and program *)
let midi_voice (n : Midi.note) : Synth.t =
  let volume = 0.25 *. float_of_int n.velocity /. 127. in
  let v source f = Synth.Voice { source; frequency = f; slide = None; seconds = n.length; volume; fade = false; effects = []; envelope = None } in
  let f = midi_frequency n.key in
  if n.channel = 9 then drum ~volume n.key
  else
    match n.program / 8 with
    | 0 | 1 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Square) f |> Synth.fading |> Synth.louder 0.8
    | 3 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Sawtooth) f |> Synth.fading |> Synth.louder 0.7
    | 4 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Triangle) f |> Synth.louder 1.5
    | 5 | 6 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Sawtooth) f |> Synth.louder 0.5
    | 7 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Sawtooth) f |> Synth.louder 0.7
    | 11 -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Triangle) f
    | _ -> v (Synth.Wave Oscillator.Square) f |> Synth.louder 0.7

let render_score (score : Midi.score) : Signal.t =
  (* a little after the last note, for the drums' tails *)
  let out = Array.make (Signal.samples (score.duration +. 0.2)) 0. in
  List.iter
    (fun (n : Midi.note) ->
      let at = Signal.samples n.start and s = Synth.render (midi_voice n) in
      Array.iteri (fun i x -> if at + i < Array.length out then out.(at + i) <- out.(at + i) +. x) s)
    score.notes;
  out

(* ix: a score a block at a time. A note is rendered when its time comes
 * (Synth.render: a second or two of samples), added to the blocks it
 * sounds in, and dropped; the sums are render_score's, in its order *)
type playing = {
  mutable coming : Midi.note list; (* by their starts *)
  mutable sounding : (int * Signal.t) list; (* where each starts, its samples *)
  mutable at : int;
  length : int;
}

let play_score (score : Midi.score) : playing =
  { coming = score.notes; sounding = []; at = 0; length = Signal.samples (score.duration +. 0.2) }

let score_finished (p : playing) : bool = p.at >= p.length

let fill_score (p : playing) (out : Signal.t) : unit =
  let n = Array.length out in
  Array.fill out 0 n 0.;
  let stop = min (p.at + n) p.length in
  let rec start (notes : Midi.note list) : Midi.note list =
    match notes with
    | note :: rest when Signal.samples note.start < stop ->
        p.sounding <- p.sounding @ [ (Signal.samples note.start, Synth.render (midi_voice note)) ];
        start rest
    | rest -> rest
  in
  p.coming <- start p.coming;
  p.sounding <-
    List.filter
      (fun ((from, s) : int * Signal.t) ->
        let last = min (from + Array.length s) stop in
        for i = max from p.at to last - 1 do
          out.(i - p.at) <- out.(i - p.at) +. s.(i - from)
        done;
        from + Array.length s > stop)
      p.sounding;
  p.at <- p.at + n
lib_audio/Music.mli
4471
(* Notes and music (see notes_audio.md section 9): the notes'
 * frequencies, and tunes (Abc.mli) played by a small band of NES-like
 * instruments. MIDI comes next in the plan (phase 8).
 *
 * Western music's twelve-tone equal temperament: an octave doubles the
 * frequency, and is split into 12 semitones, each multiplying it by the
 * same ratio, 2^(1/12) = 1.0595; the reference is A4 = 440 Hz (the A
 * above middle C, ISO 16, 1975). A note n semitones from A4 is
 * 440 * 2^(n/12):
 *
 *     C4 (middle C)  -9 semitones   261.63 Hz
 *     A4              0             440
 *     E5             +7             659.26     (a fifth above: nearly 3/2)
 *     A5            +12             880        (an octave: exactly 2)
 *
 * MIDI numbers the same notes from 0, A4 being 69, middle C 60
 * (notes_audio_midi.md): frequency = 440 * 2^((n - 69) / 12).
 *
 * References: Marin Mersenne, Harmonie universelle, 1636 (the ratio
 * 2^(1/12)); the MIDI 1.0 specification, 1983; Paul Hudak and Donovan
 * Quick, The Haskell School of Music, 2018, chapter 2 (pitches as
 * numbers, "absPitch"). *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Music.mli; a score played a block at a time (play_score, fill_score) is ix's (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

(* [midi_frequency n]: MIDI note [n]'s frequency, 440 for 69 *)
val midi_frequency : int -> float

(* [midi_number name]: "A4" -> 69, "C4" -> 60, "F#5" -> 78, "Bb3" ->
 * 58 (a letter, an optional # or b, an octave from -1 to 9); None if
 * it isn't a note *)
val midi_number : string -> int option

(* [frequency name]: "A4" -> 440.; 0. if it isn't a note *)
val frequency : string -> float

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Playing tunes} *)
(*****************************************************************************)
(* A tune's voices played by the NES's band (the 2A03 chip, 1983: two
 * square channels and a triangle): the first voice on a square (the
 * melody), the last on the triangle (the bass), those in between on a
 * softer square. Each note sounds for 90% of its length, then a short
 * silence, so that two notes in a row are heard as two (a tracker's
 * "note off"); rests are silences. *)

(* [instrument ~voice ~voices]: the sound of voice number [voice] (from
 * 0) among [voices]: its waveform and volume *)
val instrument : voice:int -> voices:int -> Oscillator.waveform * float

(* [to_sound tune]: its voices together, each a sound after another *)
val to_sound : Abc.tune -> Synth.t

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Playing MIDI scores} *)
(*****************************************************************************)
(* A MIDI file's notes overlap freely (a chord, a sustained bass under a
 * melody), which a tune's one-after-another voices can't hold: a score
 * is rendered straight into one buffer, each note added at its start.
 * General MIDI's instrument families (the program / 8, 1991) mapped to
 * our few waveforms, NES-like:
 *
 *   pianos, chromatic percussion (0-15)   square, fading
 *   organs (16-23)                        square, held
 *   guitars (24-31)                       sawtooth, fading
 *   basses (32-39)                        triangle
 *   strings, ensembles (40-55)            sawtooth, softer
 *   brass (56-63)                         sawtooth
 *   reeds, pipes (64-79)                  square
 *   synth leads (80-87)                   square
 *   synth pads (88-95)                    triangle
 *   the rest                              square
 *
 * and channel 10 (9 from 0), the drums, by key: 35-36 a bass drum (a
 * triangle falling from 150 to 50 Hz), 38 and 40 a snare (noise), 42
 * to 46 hi-hats (short, bright noise), the others a short noise. The
 * velocity is the volume (127: 0.25, so that chords don't clip). *)

(* [render_score score]: its samples *)
val render_score : Midi.score -> Signal.t

(* A score a block at a time, for a player: [render_score] has a whole
 * song's samples before the first is heard (a quarter of an hour of
 * music is 40 million floats); here a note is rendered when its time
 * comes, added to the blocks it sounds in, and dropped. The samples
 * are [render_score]'s. *)
type playing

val play_score : Midi.score -> playing

(* [fill_score p out]: the next samples, [out]'s length of them; silence
 * past the end *)
val fill_score : playing -> Signal.t -> unit

val score_finished : playing -> bool

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Pitch_effect.mli *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Pitch_effect.ml (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

type t =
  | Vibrato of { rate : float; depth : float }
  | Jump of { semitones : float; at : float }
  | Arpeggio of { semitones : float list; step : float }

let semitones (k : float) : float = 2. ** (k /. 12.)

let factor (p : t) (t : float) : float =
  match p with
  | Vibrato { rate; depth } -> semitones (depth *. sin (2. *. Float.pi *. rate *. t))
  | Jump { semitones = k; at } -> if t < at then 1. else semitones k
  | Arpeggio { semitones = []; _ } -> 1.
  | Arpeggio { semitones = l; step } -> semitones (List.nth l (int_of_float (t /. step) mod List.length l))
lib_audio/Pitch_effect.mli
1976
(* Pitch effects: a voice's pitch changed over time, wobbling or
 * jumping (see notes_audio.md section 8).
 *
 * They multiply a voice's frequency by a factor that
 * changes with time t, the seconds since the voice started:
 *
 *   - a vibrato, the pitch wobbling up and down, [depth] semitones either
 *     way, [rate] times a second: 2^(depth sin (2 pi rate t) / 12). A
 *     singer's or a violinist's (5 to 7 a second, a quarter of a
 *     semitone); faster and deeper, a siren, a UFO.
 *   - a jump, [semitones] up (or down) once, at [at] seconds: a coin's
 *     two notes in one sound (sfxr's "change").
 *   - an arpeggio, the notes of a chord one after the other, [step]
 *     seconds each, around and around:
 *
 *         semitones  0  4  7  0  4  7  0 ...     C E G C E G: a C major
 *         pitch      ___                          chord, played by a
 *                       ___                       single voice
 *                          ___
 *
 *     the chiptune trick: the NES had two square channels, the C64
 *     three voices, too few to play chords; cycled every frame (1/60 s),
 *     the notes blur into one warbling chord. (Arpeggio machines and
 *     trackers' "0xy" effect: the note, x semitones up, y up, every
 *     tick.)
 *
 * The echo and the reverb, the other effects of a rendered sound, are
 * Synth's; the live ones, a sound going through them block after block,
 * audio/effects/'s.
 *
 * Reference: Tomas Pettersson, sfxr, 2007 (vibrato and "change" among
 * its parameters). *)

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/audio/Pitch_effect.mli (docs/plans/plan_audio.md) *)

type t =
  | Vibrato of { rate : float; depth : float } (* Hz, semitones *)
  | Jump of { semitones : float; at : float } (* at, in seconds *)
  | Arpeggio of { semitones : float list; step : float } (* each [step] s *)

(* [factor p t]: the frequency multiplier at [t] seconds in: 1 for no
 * change, 2 an octave up *)
val factor : t -> float -> float

lib_audio/Player.ml
4895
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Player.mli *)

type t = { fill : Signal.stereo -> unit; finished : unit -> bool }

let of_samples (s : Signal.stereo) : t =
  let at = ref 0 and length = Array.length s.left in
  let fill (out : Signal.stereo) : unit =
    let n = Array.length out.left in
    let have = max 0 (min n (length - !at)) in
    Array.blit s.left !at out.left 0 have;
    Array.blit s.right !at out.right 0 have;
    Array.fill out.left have (n - have) 0.;
    Array.fill out.right have (n - have) 0.;
    at := !at + n
  in
  { fill; finished = (fun () -> !at >= length) }

let of_mod (song : Mod.song) : t =
  let p = Mod_player.create ~loop:false song in
  { fill = Mod_player.fill p; finished = (fun () -> Mod_player.finished p) }

let of_ogg (p : Vorbis_player.t) : t =
  { fill = Vorbis_player.fill p; finished = (fun () -> Vorbis_player.finished p) }

let of_score (score : Midi.score) : t =
  let p = Music.play_score score in
  let fill (out : Signal.stereo) : unit =
    Music.fill_score p out.left;
    Array.blit out.left 0 out.right 0 (Array.length out.left)
  in
  { fill; finished = (fun () -> Music.score_finished p) }

(* a file at Signal's rate: the frame being played and where in it *)
let of_mpeg_at_rate (d : Mpeg_audio.t) : t =
  let frame : Signal.stereo ref = ref { Signal.left = [||]; right = [||] } and at = ref 0 and ended = ref false in
  let fill (out : Signal.stereo) : unit =
    let n = Array.length out.left and done_ = ref 0 in
    while !done_ < n && not !ended do
      if !at >= Array.length !frame.left then (
        match Mpeg_audio.next d with
        | None -> ended := true
        | Some f ->
            frame := f;
            at := 0)
      else
        let have = min (n - !done_) (Array.length !frame.left - !at) in
        Array.blit !frame.left !at out.left !done_ have;
        Array.blit !frame.right !at out.right !done_ have;
        at := !at + have;
        done_ := !done_ + have
    done;
    Array.fill out.left !done_ (n - !done_) 0.;
    Array.fill out.right !done_ (n - !done_) 0.
  in
  { fill; finished = (fun () -> !ended) }

(* a file at another rate: each sample out is read between two of the
 * file's (Resample's Linear), the second maybe the next frame's first:
 * two frames are held, the one being read and the one after. The
 * samples are those of the whole file resampled. *)
let of_mpeg_resampled (d : Mpeg_audio.t) (rate : int) : t =
  let k = float_of_int rate /. float_of_int Signal.rate in
  let length = int_of_float (float_of_int (Mpeg_audio.samples d) /. k) in
  let silence : Signal.stereo = { left = [||]; right = [||] } in
  let frame = ref silence and after = ref silence in
  let base = ref 0 (* the file's sample that is [frame]'s first *) and at = ref 0 (* the samples given *) in
  let fetch () : Signal.stereo = match Mpeg_audio.next d with Some f -> f | None -> silence in
  after := fetch ();
  let fill (out : Signal.stereo) : unit =
    for j = 0 to Array.length out.left - 1 do
      if !at >= length then (
        out.left.(j) <- 0.;
        out.right.(j) <- 0.)
      else
        let position = float_of_int !at *. k in
        let i = int_of_float position in
        let t = position -. float_of_int i in
        while i - !base >= Array.length !frame.left && Array.length !after.left > 0 do
          base := !base + Array.length !frame.left;
          frame := !after;
          after := fetch ()
        done;
        let i = i - !base in
        let read (s : Signal.t) (next : Signal.t) : float =
          let n = Array.length s in
          let a = if i < n then s.(i) else 0. in
          let b = if i + 1 < n then s.(i + 1) else if i + 1 = n && Array.length next > 0 then next.(0) else 0. in
          a +. (t *. (b -. a))
        in
        out.left.(j) <- read !frame.left !after.left;
        out.right.(j) <- read !frame.right !after.right;
        incr at
    done
  in
  { fill; finished = (fun () -> !at >= length) }

let of_mpeg (d : Mpeg_audio.t) : t =
  let rate = (Mpeg_audio.header d).sample_rate in
  if rate = Signal.rate then of_mpeg_at_rate d else of_mpeg_resampled d rate

let of_file (name : string) (bytes : string) : (t, string) result =
  let ends = Filename.check_suffix (String.lowercase_ascii name) in
  if ends ".mod" then Result.map of_mod (Mod.of_string bytes)
  else if ends ".mid" || ends ".midi" then Result.map of_score (Midi.parse bytes)
  else if ends ".mp3" || ends ".mp2" then Result.map of_mpeg (Mpeg_audio.create bytes)
  else if ends ".wav" then Result.map of_samples (Wav.stereo_of_string bytes)
  else if ends ".ogg" then Result.map of_ogg (Vorbis_player.create ~loop:false bytes)
  else if ends ".abc" then Result.map (fun tune -> of_samples (Synth.render_stereo (Music.to_sound tune))) (Abc.parse bytes)
  else Error "not a .mod, .mid, .mp3, .mp2, .wav, .ogg or .abc"

(* Player: a file of sound played a block at a time, whatever its
 * format.
 *
 * The sounds of a game are rendered ahead: a tree of a few notes
 * (Synth) become samples once, then played. A song is not: four
 * minutes of it are 21 million samples, twice. So what plays a song
 * gives its next samples when they are asked for, a block at a time,
 * and keeps between two blocks only what the format needs:
 *
 *                 +-- .mod --> Mod_player   the rows, four channels' place in their samples
 *    the file's   +-- .mid --> Music        the notes to come, those sounding
 *    bytes -------+-- .mp3 --> Mpeg_audio   a frame decoded (1,152 samples), where in it
 *                 +-- .wav --> Wav          its samples, where in them
 *                 +-- .ogg --> Vorbis       a packet decoded (a block), where in it
 *                 +-- .abc --> Abc, Music   a tune of a page: rendered whole
 *                         |
 *                         v
 *                    fill out            the next block, both channels
 *
 * It is the shape of an instrument's [fill] (Instrument), without the
 * keys and the knobs: the mixer pulls one as it pulls the other.
 * mini-play is this module and a loop that writes the blocks; a game's
 * music from a file is the same player given to the mixer.
 *
 * Every file ends at Signal's rate, 44,100 samples a second: a WAV or
 * an MP3 at another is resampled (Resample's linear reading), the MP3
 * as its frames come, two of them held since a sample out may be read
 * between a frame's last and the next one's first.
 *
 * others:
 * 9front has a program a format, each a filter from the file to
 * samples on its standard output (audio/mp3dec, audio/wavdec,
 * audio/oggdec, games/midi), and play(1), a script that looks at the
 * file's first bytes and runs the one that reads it into /dev/audio.
 * Here one program, and the format by the file's name. *)

type t = {
  (* the next block: both channels written over, their length the
   * block's; silence past the end *)
  fill : Signal.stereo -> unit;
  (* whether the end was reached *)
  finished : unit -> bool;
}

(* [of_samples s]: samples already there, played once *)
val of_samples : Signal.stereo -> t

(* [of_file name bytes]: the player of a file, by its name's end (.mod,
 * .mid or .midi, .mp3 or .mp2, .wav, .ogg, .abc); Error with why not *)
val of_file : string -> string -> (t, string) result

type wave = Square | Sawtooth | Triangle | Sine | Noise

type t = {
  wave : wave;
  frequency : float;
  slide : float;
  attack : float;
  sustain : float;
  decay : float;
  vibrato_rate : float;
  vibrato_depth : float;
  jump : float;
  jump_at : float;
  low_pass : float;
  low_pass_to : float;
  resonance : float;
  high_pass : float;
  echo : float;
  reverb : float;
  volume : float;
}

let default : t =
  {
    wave = Square;
    frequency = 440.;
    slide = 440.;
    attack = 0.;
    sustain = 0.1;
    decay = 0.1;
    vibrato_rate = 0.;
    vibrato_depth = 0.;
    jump = 0.;
    jump_at = 0.;
    low_pass = 0.;
    low_pass_to = 0.;
    resonance = 0.707;
    high_pass = 0.;
    echo = 0.;
    reverb = 0.;
    volume = 0.5;
  }

(* the echoes, each 0.4 of the last *)
let feedback = 0.4

let to_sound (s : t) : Synth.t =
  let source : Synth.source =
    match s.wave with
    | Square -> Wave Square
    | Sawtooth -> Wave Sawtooth
    | Triangle -> Wave Triangle
    | Sine -> Wave Sine
    | Noise -> Noise
  in
  let attack = Float.max 0.005 s.attack in
  let voice : Synth.voice =
    {
      source;
      frequency = s.frequency;
      slide = (if s.slide = s.frequency then None else Some s.slide);
      seconds = attack +. s.sustain +. s.decay;
      volume = s.volume;
      fade = false;
      effects =
        (if s.vibrato_depth > 0. then [ Pitch_effect.Vibrato { rate = s.vibrato_rate; depth = s.vibrato_depth } ] else [])
        @ if s.jump <> 0. then [ Pitch_effect.Jump { semitones = s.jump; at = s.jump_at } ] else [];
      envelope = Some { attack; decay = 0.; sustain = 1.; release = s.decay };
    }
  in
  let sound = Synth.Voice voice in
  let sound =
    if s.low_pass > 0. then
      let cutoff_to = if s.low_pass_to > 0. then s.low_pass_to else s.low_pass in
      Synth.Filtered ({ kind = Low_pass; cutoff = s.low_pass; cutoff_to; q = s.resonance }, sound)
    else sound
  in
  let sound =
    if s.high_pass > 0. then Synth.Filtered ({ kind = High_pass; cutoff = s.high_pass; cutoff_to = s.high_pass; q = 0.707 }, sound)
    else sound
  in
  let sound = if s.echo > 0. then Synth.Echo ({ delay = s.echo; feedback }, sound) else sound in
  if s.reverb > 0. then Synth.Reverb (s.reverb, sound) else sound

let duration (s : t) : float = Synth.duration (to_sound s)

(* Mutate *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let vary ~(seed : int) (s : t) : t =
  if seed = 0 then s
  else
    let st = Lehmer.make seed in
    (* times 0.7 to 1.4, evenly in ratio *)
    let scale x = x *. (0.7 *. (2. ** Lehmer.float st 1.)) in
    (* the same number of semitones for both ends of a slide *)
    let pitch = 2. ** ((Lehmer.float st 10. -. 5.) /. 12.) in
    {
      s with
      frequency = s.frequency *. pitch;
      slide = s.slide *. pitch;
      attack = scale s.attack;
      sustain = scale s.sustain;
      decay = scale s.decay;
      vibrato_rate = scale s.vibrato_rate;
      jump_at = scale s.jump_at;
      low_pass = scale s.low_pass;
      low_pass_to = scale s.low_pass_to;
      high_pass = scale s.high_pass;
    }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* sfxr's buttons *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let random (category : string) ~(seed : int) : t =
  let st = Lehmer.make (seed + String.fold_left (fun h c -> ((h * 31) + Char.code c) land 0xFFFFFF) 0 category) in
  (* in [lo, hi); evenly in ratio for [between_log], as the ear hears
   * pitches and times *)
  let between lo hi = lo +. Lehmer.float st (hi -. lo) in
  let between_log lo hi = lo *. ((hi /. lo) ** Lehmer.float st 1.) in
  let chance p = Lehmer.float st 1. < p in
  let one_of l = List.nth l (Lehmer.int st (List.length l)) in
  match category with
  | "coin" ->
      let f = between_log 400. 1600. in
      { default with
        wave = one_of [ Square; Sawtooth ];
        frequency = f; slide = f;
        sustain = between 0.02 0.1; decay = between 0.1 0.4;
        (* up an interval: a fourth, a fifth, an octave *)
        jump = one_of [ 5.; 7.; 12. ]; jump_at = between 0.03 0.12;
        volume = 0.4 }
  | "laser" ->
      let f = between_log 500. 3000. in
      { default with
        wave = one_of [ Square; Sawtooth; Sine ];
        frequency = f; slide = f *. between 0.1 0.5;
        sustain = between 0. 0.1; decay = between 0.05 0.3;
        low_pass = (if chance 0.5 then between_log 2000. 10000. else 0.);
        low_pass_to = 0. }
  | "explosion" ->
      let f = between_log 300. 3000. in
      let cutoff = between_log 1500. 6000. in
      { default with
        wave = Noise;
        frequency = f; slide = f *. between 0.1 0.5;
        sustain = between 0.05 0.3; decay = between 0.3 1.;
        low_pass = cutoff; low_pass_to = between_log 100. 400.;
        volume = 0.7 }
  | "powerup" ->
      let f = between_log 200. 700. in
      let vibrato = chance 0.5 in
      { default with
        wave = one_of [ Square; Sawtooth ];
        frequency = f; slide = f *. between 1.5 3.;
        sustain = between 0.1 0.4; decay = between 0.1 0.4;
        vibrato_rate = (if vibrato then between 8. 20. else 0.);
        vibrato_depth = (if vibrato then between 0.3 1. else 0.);
        volume = 0.35 }
  | "hit" ->
      let f = between_log 800. 4000. in
      { default with
        wave = (if chance 0.5 then Noise else Square);
        frequency = f; slide = f *. between 0.3 0.7;
        sustain = 0.; decay = between 0.05 0.2;
        low_pass = between_log 2000. 6000. }
  | "jump" ->
      let f = between_log 150. 500. in
      { default with
        frequency = f; slide = f *. between 1.5 2.5;
        sustain = between 0.02 0.1; decay = between 0.1 0.3;
        volume = 0.4 }
  | _ ->
      let f = between_log 400. 1500. in
      { default with
        wave = one_of [ Square; Sine ];
        frequency = f; slide = f;
        sustain = between 0.02 0.06; decay = between 0.02 0.08 }
lib_audio/Sfx.mli
