(* A value as bytes, and back: OCaml's format (ocaml-light's too). 20
 * bytes (the magic number, the data's length, the blocks' count, the
 * words they take on 32 and on 64 bits), then the value, depth first,
 * each thing a byte's code and what follows, the high byte first:
 *
 *   0x80 + tag + size * 16     a block of a few fields, then its fields
 *   0x40 + n                   an integer under 64
 *   0x20 + length              a string under 32 bytes, then its bytes
 *   0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03     an integer of 1, 2, 4, 8 bytes
 *   0x04, 0x05, 0x06           a block met before: how many blocks ago,
 *                              in 1, 2, 4 bytes (what is shared stays
 *                              shared, and a cycle ends)
 *   0x08                       a block: size * 1024 + tag in 4 bytes
 *   0x09, 0x0A                 a string: its length in 1, 4 bytes
 *   0x0B, 0x0C                 a float: its 8 bytes, the high or the
 *                              low one first
 *   0x0E, 0x07                 a Float.Array: its length in 1, 4 bytes,
 *                              then its floats' 8 bytes, the low first
 *   0x12, 0x18, 0x19           a custom block: its name, "_j" an int64,
 *                              "_i" an int32, then its bytes
 *
 * The same bytes as OCaml's wherever a value is the same blocks in
 * both; not a constructor's inline record (here a block of its own),
 * a float array (here a block of floats, but Float.Array's as OCaml's),
 * a closure (refused).
 *
 * old: 478 lines of C in the runtime, its tables in memory of their own
 * (mmap); here they are values, which the collector moves: see [seen].
 * Reading and writing are 4 to 6 times slower than the C's (mini-cc's):
 * a link of mini-ml 16% longer, ix built by ix 12% (plan_ml_features.md,
 * 3, has the numbers). Tried, and not faster in that build: the
 * writer's bytes its own (not a Buffer's), the collection told by a
 * block's address (not a call), no bound checked, fewer calls a value. *)

type extern_flags =
    No_sharing
  | Closures

let header_size = 20
let magic = "\x84\x95\xA6\xBE"

(* mini-ml's tags (the runtime's mlvalues.h), with Obj's two *)
let closure_tag = 247
let int32_tag = 254
let int64_tag = 255
let double_array_tag = 251

external floatarray_create : int -> Obj.t = "caml_floatarray_create"

external floatarray_get : Obj.t -> int -> float = "%floatarray_unsafe_get"
external floatarray_set : Obj.t -> int -> float -> unit = "%floatarray_unsafe_set"

(* the i-th of the header's five numbers *)
let header_int (s : string) (ofs : int) (i : int) : int =
  Int32.to_int (String.get_int32_be s (ofs + 4 * i))

(* Writing *)

(* The blocks written, each with its number: a hash table by a block's
 * address, the only name a block has. A collection moves the blocks, so
 * every slot is computed anew after one ([epoch] tells), and nothing
 * may be allocated between a slot's computation and its use. *)
type seen = {
  mutable blocks : Obj.t array;  (* a slot: a block, or 0 when free *)
  mutable numbers : int array;
  mutable count : int;
  mutable epoch : int;
}

external collections : unit -> int = "gc_collections"
(* the blocks made between the two in the old generation (gc.c's
 * old_reads: what is read is kept, most of it) *)
external old_begin : unit -> unit = "ml_old_begin"
external old_end : unit -> unit = "ml_old_end"

(* (an address's bits mixed: blocks made together are neighbours, and
 * two runs of them over the same slots are long searches; the C's
 * table, by the address alone, took 28 s for a list on arm) *)
let hash (v : Obj.t) : int =
  let h = ((Obj.magic v : int) lsr 2) * 0x9E3779B in
  h lxor (h lsr 15)

(* where v is from slot i on, or the free slot it goes to *)
let rec probe (blocks : Obj.t array) (v : Obj.t) (i : int) : int =
  let b = blocks.(i) in
  if Obj.is_int b || b == v then i
  else probe blocks v ((i + 1) land (Array.length blocks - 1))

let slot (blocks : Obj.t array) (v : Obj.t) : int =
  probe blocks v (hash v land (Array.length blocks - 1))

(* the table in n slots (a power of 2), by today's addresses *)
let rehash (t : seen) (n : int) : unit =
  let blocks = Array.make n (Obj.repr 0) and numbers = Array.make n 0 in
  t.epoch <- collections ();
  for i = 0 to Array.length t.blocks - 1 do
    let b = t.blocks.(i) in
    if not (Obj.is_int b) then begin
      let j = slot blocks b in
      blocks.(j) <- b;
      numbers.(j) <- t.numbers.(i)
    end
  done;
  t.blocks <- blocks;
  t.numbers <- numbers

(* v's number if it was written; else None, and it is given the next *)
let number (t : seen) (v : Obj.t) : int option =
  if t.count * 2 >= Array.length t.blocks then rehash t (2 * Array.length t.blocks)
  else if t.epoch <> collections () then rehash t (Array.length t.blocks);
  let i = slot t.blocks v in
  if Obj.is_int t.blocks.(i) then begin
    t.blocks.(i) <- v;
    t.numbers.(i) <- t.count;
    t.count <- t.count + 1;
    None
  end
  else Some t.numbers.(i)

type writer = {
  out : Buffer.t;
  seen : seen;
  (* No_sharing not asked: a block met before written as such (asked,
   * each copy written anew and no block counted, as OCaml's; old: the
   * flags left, tiny-ml's interfaces not OCaml's bytes) *)
  sharing : bool;
  (* the words the blocks take when read, for the header *)
  mutable words32 : int;
  mutable words64 : int;
}

(* n's low bytes, the high one first *)
let put (w : writer) (n : int) (bytes : int) : unit =
  for i = bytes - 1 downto 0 do
    Buffer.add_uint8 w.out (n asr (8 * i))
  done

let words (w : writer) (on32 : int) (on64 : int) : unit =
  w.words32 <- w.words32 + on32;
  w.words64 <- w.words64 + on64

(* n is a signed number of that many bits *)
let fits (n : int) (bits : int) : bool =
  let high = n asr (bits - 1) in
  high = 0 || high = -1

let write_int (w : writer) (n : int) : unit =
  if n >= 0 && n < 64 then put w (0x40 + n) 1
  else if fits n 8 then (put w 0x00 1; put w n 1)
  else if fits n 16 then (put w 0x01 1; put w n 2)
  (* 31 bits, as OCaml: what a machine of 32 bits can read *)
  else if fits n 31 then (put w 0x02 1; put w n 4)
  else (put w 0x03 1; put w n 8)

let write_shared (w : writer) (ago : int) : unit =
  if ago < 256 then (put w 0x04 1; put w ago 1)
  else if ago < 65536 then (put w 0x05 1; put w ago 2)
  else (put w 0x06 1; put w ago 4)

let write_string (w : writer) (s : string) : unit =
  let n = String.length s in
  if n < 32 then put w (0x20 + n) 1
  else if n < 256 then (put w 0x09 1; put w n 1)
  else (put w 0x0A 1; put w n 4);
  Buffer.add_string w.out s;
  words w (2 + n / 4) (2 + n / 8)

(* (OCaml's sizes: a custom block has a word more, its operations) *)
let write_int64 (w : writer) (n : int64) : unit =
  let b = Bytes.create 8 in
  Bytes.set_int64_be b 0 n;
  Buffer.add_string w.out "\x19_j\000";
  Buffer.add_bytes w.out b;
  words w 4 3

let write_int32 (w : writer) (n : int32) : unit =
  let b = Bytes.create 4 in
  Bytes.set_int32_be b 0 n;
  Buffer.add_string w.out "\x19_i\000";
  Buffer.add_bytes w.out b;
  words w 3 3

(* v written whole: true. Or, a block of fields, all but its last one:
 * false, and [write] goes on with it in a loop, not a call (mini-ml
 * makes a call of a tail call: a long list would be a deep stack). *)
let rec written (w : writer) (v : Obj.t) : bool =
  if Obj.is_int v then (write_int w (Obj.obj v); true)
  else if Obj.size v = 0 then (put w (0x80 + Obj.tag v) 1; true)
  else
    match if w.sharing then number w.seen v else None with
    | Some n -> write_shared w (w.seen.count - n); true
    | None ->
        let tag = Obj.tag v in
        if tag = Obj.string_tag then (write_string w (Obj.obj v); true)
        else if tag = Obj.double_tag then begin
          put w 0x0C 1;
          Buffer.add_int64_le w.out (Int64.bits_of_float (Obj.obj v));
          words w 3 2;
          true
        end
        else if tag = double_array_tag then begin
          let n = floatarray_length v in
          if n < 256 then (put w 0x0E 1; put w n 1) else (put w 0x07 1; put w n 4);
          for i = 0 to n - 1 do
            Buffer.add_int64_le w.out (Int64.bits_of_float (floatarray_get v i))
          done;
          words w (1 + 2 * n) (1 + n);
          true
        end
        else if tag = int64_tag then (write_int64 w (Obj.obj v); true)
        else if tag = int32_tag then (write_int32 w (Obj.obj v); true)
        else if tag = closure_tag then invalid_arg "output_value: functional value"
        else begin
          let n = Obj.size v in
          if tag < 16 && n < 8 then put w (0x80 + tag + n * 16) 1
          else (put w 0x08 1; put w (n * 1024 + tag) 4);
          words w (1 + n) (1 + n);
          for i = 0 to n - 2 do
            write w (Obj.field v i)
          done;
          false
        end

and write (w : writer) (v : Obj.t) : unit =
  let v = ref v in
  while not (written w !v) do
    v := Obj.field !v (Obj.size !v - 1)
  done

let to_string (v : 'a) (flags : extern_flags list) : string =
  let seen = { blocks = Array.make 64 (Obj.repr 0); numbers = Array.make 64 0; count = 0; epoch = collections () } in
  let w = { out = Buffer.create 4096; seen; sharing = not (List.mem No_sharing flags); words32 = 0; words64 = 0 } in
  Buffer.add_string w.out magic;
  put w 0 (header_size - 4);
  write w (Obj.repr v);
  (* the header's numbers, now that they are known *)
  let s = Buffer.to_bytes w.out in
  List.iteri (fun i n -> Bytes.set_int32_be s (4 * (i + 1)) (Int32.of_int n))
    [ Bytes.length s - header_size; seen.count; w.words32; w.words64 ];
  Bytes.unsafe_to_string s

let to_channel (chan : out_channel) (v : 'a) (flags : extern_flags list) : unit =
  output_string chan (to_string v flags)

let to_buffer (buff : bytes) (ofs : int) (len : int) (v : 'a) (flags : extern_flags list) : int =
  if ofs < 0 || len < 0 || ofs + len > Bytes.length buff
  then invalid_arg "Marshal.to_buffer: substring out of bounds";
  let s = to_string v flags in
  if String.length s > len then failwith "Marshal.to_buffer: buffer overflow";
  String.blit s 0 buff ofs (String.length s);
  String.length s

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Reading *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type reader = {
  src : string;
  mutable pos : int;
  (* the blocks read, by their number *)
  blocks : Obj.t array;
  mutable count : int;
  (* the block [item] last returned has its last field still to read *)
  mutable unfinished : bool;
}

let byte (r : reader) : int =
  let c = Char.code r.src.[r.pos] in
  r.pos <- r.pos + 1;
  c

(* the next bytes as a number, the high one first, after those in high *)
let rec after (r : reader) (high : int) (bytes : int) : int =
  if bytes = 0 then high else after r ((high lsl 8) lor byte r) (bytes - 1)

let unsigned (r : reader) (bytes : int) : int = after r 0 bytes

let signed (r : reader) (bytes : int) : int =
  let high = byte r in
  after r (if high >= 128 then high - 256 else high) (bytes - 1)

(* (none when the header counts none: No_sharing's, as OCaml's intern;
 * old: always, out of the table's bounds) *)
let numbered (r : reader) (v : Obj.t) : Obj.t =
  if r.count < Array.length r.blocks then r.blocks.(r.count) <- v;
  r.count <- r.count + 1;
  v

let shared (r : reader) (ago : int) : Obj.t =
  r.blocks.(r.count - ago)

let read_string (r : reader) (n : int) : Obj.t =
  let s = String.sub r.src r.pos n in
  r.pos <- r.pos + n;
  numbered r (Obj.repr s)

let read_float (r : reader) (bits : int64) : Obj.t =
  r.pos <- r.pos + 8;
  numbered r (Obj.repr (Int64.float_of_bits bits))

let read_floats (r : reader) (n : int) : Obj.t =
  let a = numbered r (floatarray_create n) in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    floatarray_set a i (Int64.float_of_bits (String.get_int64_le r.src r.pos));
    r.pos <- r.pos + 8
  done;
  a

(* "_j" an int64, "_i" an int32; before its bytes, 12 of sizes if the
 * code says so (0x18) *)
let read_custom (r : reader) (sizes : int) : Obj.t =
  let name = String.sub r.src r.pos 3 in
  let data = r.pos + 3 + sizes in
  if name = "_j\000" then begin
    r.pos <- data + 8;
    numbered r (Obj.repr (String.get_int64_be r.src data))
  end
  else if name = "_i\000" then begin
    r.pos <- data + 4;
    numbered r (Obj.repr (String.get_int32_be r.src data))
  end
  else failwith "input_value: unknown custom block"

(* the next value, whole. Or, a block of fields, with all but its last
 * one, and [r.unfinished]: [read] goes on with it in a loop, as
 * [write] does. *)
let rec item (r : reader) : Obj.t =
  r.unfinished <- false;
  let code = byte r in
  if code >= 0x80 then read_block r (code land 15) ((code lsr 4) land 7)
  else if code >= 0x40 then Obj.repr (code land 63)
  else if code >= 0x20 then read_string r (code land 31)
  else
    match code with
    | 0x00 -> Obj.repr (signed r 1)
    | 0x01 -> Obj.repr (signed r 2)
    | 0x02 -> Obj.repr (signed r 4)
    | 0x03 ->
        if Sys.word_size = 32 then failwith "input_value: integer too large";
        Obj.repr (signed r 8)
    | 0x04 -> shared r (unsigned r 1)
    | 0x05 -> shared r (unsigned r 2)
    | 0x06 -> shared r (unsigned r 4)
    | 0x08 ->
        let header = unsigned r 4 in
        read_block r (header land 255) (header lsr 10)
    | 0x09 -> read_string r (unsigned r 1)
    | 0x0A -> read_string r (unsigned r 4)
    | 0x0B -> read_float r (String.get_int64_be r.src r.pos)
    | 0x0C -> read_float r (String.get_int64_le r.src r.pos)
    | 0x0E -> read_floats r (unsigned r 1)
    | 0x07 -> read_floats r (unsigned r 4)
    | 0x12 | 0x19 -> read_custom r 0
    | 0x18 -> read_custom r 12
    | _ -> failwith "input_value: ill-formed message"

and read_block (r : reader) (tag : int) (n : int) : Obj.t =
  if n = 0 then Obj.repr [||]
  else begin
    let b = numbered r (Obj.new_block tag n) in
    for i = 0 to n - 2 do
      Obj.set_field b i (read r)
    done;
    r.unfinished <- true;
    b
  end

and read (r : reader) : Obj.t =
  let v = item r in
  let b = ref v in
  while r.unfinished do
    let last = item r in
    Obj.set_field !b (Obj.size !b - 1) last;
    b := last
  done;
  v

let data_size (b : bytes) (ofs : int) : int =
  let buff = Bytes.unsafe_to_string b in
  if ofs < 0 || ofs + header_size > String.length buff
  then invalid_arg "Marshal.data_size";
  if String.sub buff ofs 4 <> magic then failwith "Marshal.data_size: bad object";
  header_int buff ofs 1

let total_size (buff : bytes) (ofs : int) : int = header_size + data_size buff ofs

let from_string (buff : string) (ofs : int) : 'a =
  if ofs < 0 || ofs + header_size > String.length buff
  then invalid_arg "Marshal.from_string";
  if String.sub buff ofs 4 <> magic then failwith "input_value: bad object";
  if ofs + header_size + header_int buff ofs 1 > String.length buff
  then invalid_arg "Marshal.from_string";
  let blocks = Array.make (header_int buff ofs 2 + 1) (Obj.repr 0) in
  let r = { src = buff; pos = ofs + header_size; blocks; count = 0; unfinished = false } in
  (* the value made in the old generation (the runtime's old_reads);
   * old: Obj.obj (read r) *)
  old_begin ();
  match read r with
  | v -> old_end (); Obj.obj v
  | exception e -> old_end (); raise e

let from_channel (chan : in_channel) : 'a =
  let header = really_input_string chan header_size in
  let len = header_int header 0 1 in
  let s = Bytes.create (header_size + len) in
  String.blit header 0 s 0 header_size;
  (try really_input chan s header_size len
   with End_of_file -> failwith "input_value: truncated object");
  from_string (Bytes.unsafe_to_string s) 0

(* ix: OCaml's later names, for bytes: the same block (to_string's is
 * no one else's; from_bytes reads only) *)
let to_bytes (v : 'a) (flags : extern_flags list) : bytes = Bytes.unsafe_of_string (to_string v flags)
let from_bytes (buff : bytes) (ofs : int) : 'a = from_string (Bytes.unsafe_to_string buff) ofs

(* Module [Marshal]: marshaling of data structures *)

(* This module provides functions to encode arbitrary data structures
   as sequences of bytes, which can then be written on a file or
   sent over a pipe or network connection.  The bytes can then
   be read back later, possibly in another process, and decoded back
   into a data structure. The format for the byte sequences
   is compatible across all machines for a given version of Objective Caml.

   Warning: marshaling is currently not type-safe. The type
   of marshaled data is not transmitted along the value of the data,
   making it impossible to check that the data read back possesses the
   type expected by the context. In particular, the result type of
   the [Marshal.from_*] functions is given as ['a], but this is
   misleading: the returned Caml value does not possess type ['a]
   for all ['a]; it has one, unique type which cannot be determined
   at compile-type.  The programmer should explicitly give the expected
   type of the returned value, using the following syntax:
                     [(Marshal.from_channel chan : type)].
   Anything can happen at run-time if the object in the file does not
   belong to the given type.

   The representation of marshaled values is not human-readable,
   and uses bytes that are not printable characters. Therefore,
   input and output channels used in conjunction with [Marshal.to_channel]
   and [Marshal.from_channel] must be opened in binary mode, using e.g.
   [open_out_bin] or [open_in_bin]; channels opened in text mode will
   cause unmarshaling errors on platforms where text channels behave
   differently than binary channels, e.g. Windows. *)

type extern_flags =
    No_sharing                          (* Don't preserve sharing *)
  | Closures                            (* Send function closures *)
        (* The flags to the [Marshal.to_*] functions below. *)

val to_channel: out_channel -> 'a -> extern_flags list -> unit
        (* [Marshal.to_channel chan v flags] writes the representation of
           [v] on channel [chan]. *)

val to_string: 'a -> extern_flags list -> string
        (* [Marshal.to_string v flags] returns a string containing the
           representation of [v] as a sequence of bytes. *)

val to_buffer: bytes -> int -> int -> 'a -> extern_flags list -> int
        (* [Marshal.to_buffer buff ofs len v flags] marshals the value [v],
           storing its byte representation in the string [buff], starting at
           character number [ofs], and writing at most [len] characters. *)

val from_channel: in_channel -> 'a
        (* [Marshal.from_channel chan] reads from channel [chan] the byte
           representation of a structured value, as produced by one of the
           [Marshal.to_*] functions, and reconstructs and returns the
           corresponding value. *)

val from_string: string -> int -> 'a
        (* [Marshal.from_string buff ofs] unmarshals a structured value like
           [Marshal.from_channel] does, except that the byte representation
           is not read from a channel, but taken from the string [buff],
           starting at position [ofs]. *)

val header_size : int
val data_size : bytes -> int -> int
val total_size : bytes -> int -> int
        (* The bytes representing a marshaled value are composed of a fixed-
           size header and a variable-sized data part, whose size can be
           determined from the header. *)

(* ix: OCaml's later names: to_string and from_string, for bytes *)
val to_bytes : 'a -> extern_flags list -> bytes
val from_bytes : bytes -> int -> 'a

  let l1 = string_length s1 and l2 = string_length s2 in
  let s = string_create (l1 + l2) in
  string_blit s1 0 s 0 l1;
  string_blit s2 0 s l1 l2;
  bts s

                       = "caml_output"

  if ofs < 0 or ofs + len > string_length s
  then invalid_arg "output"
  else unsafe_output oc s ofs len

let set_binary_mode_in (_ : in_channel) (_ : bool) = ()

(* References (ix: before their place in OCaml's, for the signals below) *)

type 'a ref = { mutable contents: 'a }
external ref: 'a -> 'a ref = "%makemutable"
external (!): 'a ref -> 'a = "%field0"
external (:=): 'a ref -> 'a -> unit = "%setfield0"
external incr: int ref -> unit = "%incr"
external decr: int ref -> unit = "%decr"

(* ix: signals. The runtime only notes a signal; its handler is a
 * function of OCaml's, kept here by Sys.signal under the system's
 * number, and run here, where a program waits: when a read or a system
 * call (Unix's) comes back interrupted. The reading functions below
 * then ask again, unless the handler raised (Sys.Break). *)
external signal_pending : unit -> int = "ml_signal_pending"
let signal_handlers : (int * (unit -> unit)) list ref = ref []
let rec run_signals () =
  match signal_pending () with
  | 0 -> ()
  | s ->
      let rec run = function (s', f) :: rest -> if s' = s then f () else run rest | [] -> () in
      run !signal_handlers;
      run_signals ()

external input_char_or : in_channel -> int = "ml_input_char"
external unsafe_char : int -> char = "%identity"
let rec input_char ic =
  let c = input_char_or ic in
  if c >= 0 then unsafe_char c else if c = -1 then raise End_of_file else (run_signals (); input_char ic)

external input_or : in_channel -> bytes -> int -> int -> int = "caml_input"
let rec unsafe_input ic s ofs len =
  let n = input_or ic s ofs len in
  if n >= 0 then n else (run_signals (); unsafe_input ic s ofs len)

let input ic s ofs len =
  if ofs < 0 or ofs + len > bytes_length s
  then invalid_arg "input"
  else unsafe_input ic s ofs len

let rec unsafe_really_input ic s ofs len =
  if len <= 0 then () else begin
    let r = unsafe_input ic s ofs len in
    if r = 0
    then raise End_of_file
    else unsafe_really_input ic s (ofs+r) (len-r)
  end

let really_input ic s ofs len =
  if ofs < 0 or ofs + len > bytes_length s
  then invalid_arg "really_input"
  else unsafe_really_input ic s ofs len

(* ix: OCaml's later function *)
let really_input_string ic n = let s = string_create n in really_input ic s 0 n; bts s

external scan_line_or : in_channel -> int = "caml_input_scan_line"
let rec input_scan_line ic =
  let n = scan_line_or ic in
  if n = -100000 then (run_signals (); input_scan_line ic) else n

let rec input_line chan =
  let n = input_scan_line chan in
  if n = 0 then                         (* n = 0: we are at EOF *)
    raise End_of_file
  else if n > 0 then begin              (* n > 0: newline found in buffer *)
    let res = string_create (n-1) in
    ignore (unsafe_input chan res 0 (n-1));
    ignore (input_char chan);                    (* skip the newline *)
    bts res
  end else begin                        (* n < 0: newline not found *)
    let beg = string_create (-n) in
    ignore (unsafe_input chan beg 0 (-n));
    try
      bts beg ^ input_line chan
    with End_of_file ->
      bts beg
  end

external code_of_char : char -> int = "%identity"
let input_byte ic = code_of_char (input_char ic)
external input_binary_int : in_channel -> int = "caml_input_int"
  [@@raise End_of_file]
external seek_in : in_channel -> int -> unit = "caml_seek_in"
  [@@raise Sys_error]
external pos_in : in_channel -> int = "caml_pos_in"
external in_channel_length : in_channel -> int = "caml_channel_size"
  [@@raise Sys_error]
external close_in : in_channel -> unit = "caml_close_channel"

(* Output functions on standard output *)

let print_char c = output_char stdout c
let print_string s = output_string stdout s
let print_int i = output_string stdout (string_of_int i)
let print_float f = output_string stdout (string_of_float f)
(* ix: flushed, as OCaml's (ocaml-light's is not) *)
let print_endline s = output_string stdout s; output_char stdout '\n'; flush stdout
let print_newline () = output_char stdout '\n'; flush stdout

(* ix: OCaml's flushes every channel open for writing; here the two
 * the runtime knows of, a program's own being flushed when closed *)
let flush_all () = flush stdout; flush stderr

(* Output functions on standard error *)

let prerr_char c = output_char stderr c
let prerr_string s = output_string stderr s
let prerr_int i = output_string stderr (string_of_int i)
let prerr_float f = output_string stderr (string_of_float f)
let prerr_endline s =
  output_string stderr s; output_char stderr '\n'; flush stderr
let prerr_newline () = output_char stderr '\n'; flush stderr

(* Input functions on standard input *)

let read_line () = flush stdout; input_line stdin
let read_int () = int_of_string(read_line())
let read_float () = float_of_string(read_line())

type ('a, 'b, 'c) format = ('a, 'b, 'c, 'c) format4

(* Miscellaneous *)

external sys_exit : int -> 'a = "sys_exit"

let exit_function = ref (fun () -> flush stdout; flush stderr)

let at_exit f =
  let g = !exit_function in
  exit_function := (fun () -> f(); g())

let do_at_exit () = (!exit_function) ()

let exit retcode =
  do_at_exit ();
  sys_exit retcode

let nan = float_of_bits 0x7FF0000000000001L
let max_float = float_of_bits 0x7FEFFFFFFFFFFFFFL
let min_float = float_of_bits 0x0010000000000000L
let epsilon_float = float_of_bits 0x3CB0000000000000L
external int_of_float : float -> int = "%intoffloat"

(* ported from ocaml 4.02.2 *)

type ('a,'b) result = Ok of 'a | Error of 'b

(* ported from ocaml 4.0 *)

(* ix: externals, as OCaml's since 4.01: f @@ x and x |> f are the call
 * f x (mini-ml's Lower), x |> f a the call f a x, not a call of
 * Pervasives' function and then f's closure applied.
 * old: val ( @@ ) : ('a -> 'b) -> 'a -> 'b, and |>'s *)
external ( @@ ) : ('a -> 'b) -> 'a -> 'b = "%apply"
external ( |> ) : 'a -> ('a -> 'b) -> 'b = "%revapply"
(** Reverse-application operator: [x |> f |> g] is exactly equivalent to [g
    (f (x))]. *)

(* ported from ocaml 3.12 *)

(* ix: an external, as OCaml's: the value dropped, no call.
 * old: val ignore : 'a -> unit (*= "%ignore"*) *)
external ignore : 'a -> unit = "%ignore"
(** Discard the value of its argument and return [()]. *)

(* Module [Pervasives]: the initially opened module *)

(* This module provides the built-in types (numbers, booleans,
   strings, exceptions, references, lists, arrays, input-output channels, ...)
   and the basic operations over these types.

   This module is automatically opened at the beginning of each compilation.
   All components of this module can therefore be referred by their short
   name, without prefixing them by [Pervasives]. *)

(*** Predefined types *)

(*- type int *)
        (* The type of integer numbers. *)
(*- type char *)
        (* The type of characters. *)
(*- type string *)
        (* The type of character strings. *)
(*- type float *)
        (* The type of floating-point numbers. *)
(*- type bool *)
        (* The type of booleans (truth values). *)
(*- type unit = () *)
        (* The type of the unit value. *)

(*- type exn *)
        (* The type of exception values. *)
(*- type 'a array *)
        (* The type of arrays whose elements have type ['a]. *)
(*- type 'a list = [] | :: of 'a * 'a list *)
        (* The type of lists whose elements have type ['a]. *)

(*- type ('a, 'b, 'c) format *)
        (* The type of format strings. ['a] is the type of the parameters
           of the format, ['c] is the result type for the [printf]-style
           function, and ['b] is the type of the first argument given to
           [%a] and [%t] printing functions (see module [Printf]). *)

type 'a option = None | Some of 'a
        (* The type of optional values. *)

(*** Exceptions *)

external raise : exn -> 'a = "%raise"
        (* Raise the given exception value *)
(*- exception Match_failure of (string * int * int) *)
        (* Exception raised when none of the cases of a pattern-matching
           apply. The arguments are the location of the pattern-matching
           in the source code (file name, position of first character,
           position of last character). *)
exception Assert_failure of (string * int * int)
        (* Exception raised when an assertion fails. *)

(*- exception Invalid_argument of string *)
        (* Exception raised by library functions to signal that the given
           arguments do not make sense. *)
(*- exception Failure of string *)
        (* Exception raised by library functions to signal that they are
           undefined on the given arguments. *)
(*- exception Not_found *)
        (* Exception raised by search functions when the desired object
           could not be found. *)
(*- exception Out_of_memory *)
        (* Exception raised by the garbage collector
           when there is insufficient memory to complete the computation. *)
(*- exception Stack_overflow *)
        (* Exception raised by the bytecode interpreter when the evaluation
           stack reaches its maximal size. This often indicates infinite
           or excessively deep recursion in the user's program. *)
(*- exception Sys_error of string *)
        (* Exception raised by the input/output functions to report
           an operating system error. *)
(*- exception End_of_file *)
        (* Exception raised by input functions to signal that the
           end of file has been reached. *)
(*- exception Division_by_zero *)
        (* Exception raised by division and remainder operations
           when their second argument is null. *)

exception Exit
        (* This exception is not raised by any library function. *)

val invalid_arg: string -> 'a
        (* Raise exception [Invalid_argument] with the given string. *)
val failwith: string -> 'a
        (* Raise exception [Failure] with the given string. *)

(*** Comparisons *)

        (* [e1 = e2] tests for structural equality of [e1] and [e2]. *)
external (<>) : 'a -> 'a -> bool = "%notequal"
        (* Negation of [(=)]. *)
external (<) : 'a -> 'a -> bool = "%lessthan"
external (>) : 'a -> 'a -> bool = "%greaterthan"
external (<=) : 'a -> 'a -> bool = "%lessequal"
external (>=) : 'a -> 'a -> bool = "%greaterequal"
        (* Structural ordering functions. *)
external compare: 'a -> 'a -> int = "compare" "noalloc"
  [@@raise Invalid_argument]
        (* [compare x y] returns [0] if [x=y], a negative integer if [x<y],
           and a positive integer if [x>y]. *)
val min: 'a -> 'a -> 'a
        (* Return the smaller of the two arguments. *)
val max: 'a -> 'a -> 'a
        (* Return the greater of the two arguments. *)

        (* [e1 == e2] tests for physical equality of [e1] and [e2]. *)

        (* Negation of [(==)]. *)

(*** Integer arithmetic *)

(* Integers are 31 bits wide (or 63 bits on 64-bit processors).
   All operations are taken modulo $2^{31}$ (or $2^{63}$).
   They do not fail on overflow. *)

external (~-) : int -> int = "%negint"
        (* Unary negation. *)

        (* [succ x] is [x+1]. *)

        (* [pred x] is [x-1]. *)

        (* Integer addition. *)

        (* Integer subtraction. *)

        (* Integer multiplication. *)

           second argument is 0. *)

        (* Return the absolute value of the argument. *)

        (* Bitwise logical or. *)

        (* Bitwise logical exclusive or. *)

 * here too, its x lxor (-1) inlined): no call in another unit.

        (* Bitwise logical negation. *)

           replicated (an arithmetic shift). *)

   Floating-point operations do not fail on overflow or underflow,

          (* [fmod a b] returns the remainder of [a] with respect to [b]. *)

          (* [frexp f] returns the pair of the significant and the exponent
             of [f] (when [f] is zero, the significant [x] and the exponent

    Open_rdonly | Open_wronly | Open_append
  | Open_creat | Open_trunc | Open_excl
  | Open_binary | Open_text | Open_nonblock
        (* Opening modes for [open_out_gen] and [open_in_gen]. *)

    sequence. *)

        (* [open_in_gen mode rights filename] opens the file named

        (* [seek_in chan pos] sets the current reading position to [pos] for
           channel [chan]. *)

        (* Return the current reading position for the given channel. *)

        (* Return the total length (number of characters) of the given

(*** Program termination *)

val exit : int -> 'a
        (* Flush all pending writes on [stdout] and [stderr], and terminate
           the process, returning the given status code to the operating
           system (usually 0 to indicate no errors, and a small positive
           integer to indicate failure.) An implicit [exit 0] is performed

let power_float (x : float) (y : float) : float = m_pow x y
let exp_float (x : float) : float = m_exp x
let acos_float (x : float) : float = m_acos x
let asin_float (x : float) : float = m_asin x
let atan_float (x : float) : float = m_atan x
let atan2_float (y : float) (x : float) : float = m_atan2 y x
let cos_float (x : float) : float = m_cos x
let cosh_float (x : float) : float = m_cosh x
let log_float (x : float) : float = m_log x
let log10_float (x : float) : float = m_log10 x
let sin_float (x : float) : float = m_sin x
let sinh_float (x : float) : float = m_sinh x
let sqrt_float (x : float) : float = m_sqrt x
let tan_float (x : float) : float = m_tan x
let tanh_float (x : float) : float = m_tanh x
let ceil_float (x : float) : float = m_ceiling x
let floor_float (x : float) : float = m_floor x
(* C's fmod from IEEE's remainder (the quotient rounded to the nearest,
 * not truncated): |y| back where its sign is not x's; exact, as both *)
let fmod_float (x : float) (y : float) : float =
  let r = m_remainder x y in
  let a = if y < 0.0 then -. y else y in
  if x > 0.0 && r < 0.0 then r +. a else if x < 0.0 && r > 0.0 then r -. a else r

let finite (x : float) : bool = x = x && x <> infinity && x <> neg_infinity

(* (C's: 0, NaN and the infinities as they are, an exponent 0) *)
let frexp_float (x : float) : float * int =
  if x = 0.0 || not (finite x) then (x, 0)
  else
    let e = m_ilogb x + 1 in
    (m_scaleb x (- e), e)

(* (an exponent beyond any double's: ScaleB's int32 not wrapped) *)
let ldexp_float (x : float) (n : int) : float =
  m_scaleb x (if n > 100000 then 100000 else if n < -100000 then -100000 else n)

(* the fractional part, the integral part; their signs x's *)
let modf_float (x : float) : float * float =
  if x <> x then (x, x)
  else if not (finite x) then ((if x < 0.0 then (-. 0.0) else 0.0), x)
  else
    let i = m_truncate x in
    let f = x -. i in
    ((if f = 0.0 && x < 0.0 then (-. 0.0) else f), i)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Numbers read *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* -, then 0x 0o 0b or decimal, _ between digits; past 64 bits it
 * wraps, as the native runtime's *)
let int_of_string (s : string) : int =
  let n = String.length s in
  let i = ref 0 and neg = ref false and b = ref 10 and v = ref 0 in
  if !i < n && s.[!i] = '-' then begin neg := true; incr i end
  else if !i < n && s.[!i] = '+' then incr i;
  if !i + 1 < n && s.[!i] = '0' then begin
    let c = s.[!i + 1] in
    if c = 'x' || c = 'X' then begin b := 16; i := !i + 2 end
    else if c = 'o' || c = 'O' then begin b := 8; i := !i + 2 end
    else if c = 'b' || c = 'B' then begin b := 2; i := !i + 2 end
  end;
  if !i = n then failwith "int_of_string";
  while !i < n do
    let c = s.[!i] in
    if c <> '_' then begin
      let d =
        if c >= '0' && c <= '9' then code c - 48
        else if c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' then code c - 87
        else if c >= 'A' && c <= 'F' then code c - 55
        else 99 in
      if d >= !b then failwith "int_of_string";
      v := !v * !b + d
    end;
    incr i
  done;
  if !neg then - !v else !v

let is_digit (c : char) : bool = c >= '0' && c <= '9'

let is_hex (c : char) : bool =
  is_digit c || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')

let hex_value (c : char) : int =
  if is_digit c then code c - 48 else if c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' then code c - 87 else code c - 55

(* the digits from i that pass ok: where they stop *)
let rec skip (s : string) (i : int) (ok : char -> bool) : int =
  if i < String.length s && ok s.[i] then skip s (i + 1) ok else i

(* strtod's, as the native runtime's: blanks first, then a sign, then
 * digits with a point and an exponent, 0x's digits and a p exponent,
 * inf, infinity or nan; the underscores dropped; nothing after *)
let float_of_string (s : string) : float =
  let t = ref "" in
  for i = 0 to String.length s - 1 do
    if s.[i] <> '_' then t := !t ^ sub s i 1
  done;
  let s = !t in
  let n = String.length s in
  let i = skip s 0 (fun (c : char) -> c = ' ' || c = '\t' || c = '\n' || c = '\r') in
  let neg = i < n && s.[i] = '-' in
  let j = if i < n && (s.[i] = '-' || s.[i] = '+') then i + 1 else i in
  let rest = lower (sub s j (n - j)) in
  let sign (x : float) : float = if neg then -. x else x in
  if rest = "inf" || rest = "infinity" then sign infinity
  else if rest = "nan" then nan
  else if n - j > 2 && s.[j] = '0' && (s.[j + 1] = 'x' || s.[j + 1] = 'X') then begin
    (* (the digits a float, exact to 53 bits, scaled by 2's exponent) *)
    let m = ref 0.0 and k = ref (j + 2) and e = ref 0 and digits = ref 0 in
    while !k < n && is_hex s.[!k] do m := !m *. 16.0 +. float (hex_value s.[!k]); incr k; incr digits done;
    if !k < n && s.[!k] = '.' then begin
      incr k;
      while !k < n && is_hex s.[!k] do
        m := !m *. 16.0 +. float (hex_value s.[!k]); e := !e - 4; incr k; incr digits
      done
    end;
    if !digits = 0 then failwith "float_of_string";
    if !k < n && (s.[!k] = 'p' || s.[!k] = 'P') then begin
      let start = !k + 1 in
      let d = if start < n && (s.[start] = '-' || s.[start] = '+') then start + 1 else start in
      let stop = skip s d is_digit in
      if stop = d || stop <> n then failwith "float_of_string";
      e := !e + int_of_string (sub s start (stop - start));
      k := stop
    end;
    if !k <> n then failwith "float_of_string";
    sign (ldexp_float !m !e)
  end
  else begin
    let a = skip s j is_digit in
    let b = if a < n && s.[a] = '.' then skip s (a + 1) is_digit else a in
    if b - j - (if b > a then 1 else 0) = 0 then failwith "float_of_string";
    let c =
      if b < n && (s.[b] = 'e' || s.[b] = 'E') then begin
        let d = if b + 1 < n && (s.[b + 1] = '-' || s.[b + 1] = '+') then b + 2 else b + 1 in
        let stop = skip s d is_digit in
        if stop = d then failwith "float_of_string";
        stop
      end
      else b in
    if c <> n then failwith "float_of_string";
    (* (.NET's reading of the number C's syntax checked: correctly
     * rounded, which digits by hand would not be) *)
    parse (sub s i (n - i))
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Numbers written *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a format's %[-0+ #]width[.precision]: its flags, width, precision
 * (-1 none), and where its conversion is *)
type spec = {
  left : bool; zero : bool; plus : bool; space : bool; alt : bool;
  width : int; precision : int; conv : char;
}

let spec (f : string) : spec =
  let n = String.length f in
  let left = ref false and zero = ref false and plus = ref false
  and space = ref false and alt = ref false in
  let i = ref 1 in
  while !i < n && (f.[!i] = '-' || f.[!i] = '0' || f.[!i] = '+' || f.[!i] = ' ' || f.[!i] = '#') do
    let c = f.[!i] in
    if c = '-' then left := true
    else if c = '0' then zero := true
    else if c = '+' then plus := true
    else if c = ' ' then space := true
    else alt := true;
    incr i
  done;
  let width = ref 0 in
  while !i < n && is_digit f.[!i] do width := !width * 10 + code f.[!i] - 48; incr i done;
  let precision = ref (-1) in
  if !i < n && f.[!i] = '.' then begin
    incr i;
    precision := 0;
    while !i < n && is_digit f.[!i] do precision := !precision * 10 + code f.[!i] - 48; incr i done
  end;
  while !i < n && (f.[!i] = 'l' || f.[!i] = 'n' || f.[!i] = 'L') do incr i done;
  { left = !left; zero = !zero; plus = !plus; space = !space; alt = !alt;
    width = !width; precision = !precision; conv = (if !i < n then f.[!i] else 'd') }

let rec spaces (n : int) (c : string) : string = if n <= 0 then "" else c ^ spaces (n - 1) c

(* the sign and the digits padded to the width: spaces before, zeros
 * between (when the digits are a number's), or spaces after *)
let pad (sp : spec) (sign : string) (digits : string) (numeric : bool) : string =
  let len = String.length sign + String.length digits in
  let k = sp.width - len in
  if k <= 0 then sign ^ digits
  else if sp.left then sign ^ digits ^ spaces k " "
  else if sp.zero && numeric then sign ^ spaces k "0" ^ digits
  else spaces k " " ^ sign ^ digits

let sign_of (sp : spec) (neg : bool) : string =
  if neg then "-" else if sp.plus then "+" else if sp.space then " " else ""

let digit_chars = "0123456789abcdef0123456789ABCDEF"

(* n's digits in base b, n unsigned: 64 bits (an int is an int64 on
 * .NET, where the native runtime's is 63) *)
let unsigned_digits (n : int) (b : int) (upper : bool) : string =
  let off = if upper then 16 else 0 in
  let digit (d : int) : string = sub digit_chars (off + d) 1 in
  (* (the first step unsigned: n's halves by lsr, then signed) *)
  let first, last =
    if n >= 0 then (n / b, n mod b)
    else
      let q = (n lsr 1) / b * 2 in
      let r = n - q * b in
      if r >= b then (q + 1, r - b) else (q, r) in
  let s = ref (digit last) and m = ref first in
  while !m <> 0 do s := digit (!m mod b) ^ !s; m := !m / b done;
  !s

let format_int (f : string) (n : int) : string =
  let sp = spec f in
  match sp.conv with
  | 'd' | 'i' ->
      let neg = n < 0 in
      (* (min_int's digits as unsigned's: its negation is itself) *)
      let digits = if neg then unsigned_digits (- n) 10 false else unsigned_digits n 10 false in
      pad sp (sign_of sp neg) digits true
  | 'u' -> pad sp "" (unsigned_digits n 10 false) true
  | 'x' -> pad sp (if sp.alt && n <> 0 then "0x" else "") (unsigned_digits n 16 false) true
  | 'X' -> pad sp (if sp.alt && n <> 0 then "0X" else "") (unsigned_digits n 16 true) true
  | 'o' -> pad sp (if sp.alt && n <> 0 then "0" else "") (unsigned_digits n 8 false) true
  | _ -> failwith "format_int: bad format"

(* a string, a char, a boolean in a width (%-10s, %5c, %b): Printf's,
 * as the compiler makes its calls *)
let format_string (f : string) (x : string) : string =
  let sp = spec f in
  let x = if sp.precision >= 0 && sp.precision < String.length x then sub x 0 sp.precision else x in
  pad sp "" x false

external char_string : char -> string = "dotnet:static System.Char::ToString(char) -> string"

(* a char as OCaml's String.escaped writes it (String is a unit after
 * this one): a backslash before a quote and a backslash, newline, tab,
 * return and backspace by their letters, the printable as they are,
 * the others by three digits *)
let escaped_char (c : char) : string =
  match c with
  | '"' -> "\\\"" | '\\' -> "\\\\" | '\n' -> "\\n" | '\t' -> "\\t" | '\r' -> "\\r" | '\b' -> "\\b"
  | c when c >= ' ' && c < '\127' -> char_string c
  | c -> let n = code c in "\\" ^ format_int "%03d" n

let escaped (s : string) : string =
  let r = ref "" in
  for i = 0 to String.length s - 1 do r := !r ^ escaped_char s.[i] done;
  !r

(* %S and %C: OCaml's quoted, escaped *)
let format_quoted (f : string) (x : string) : string = format_string f ("\"" ^ escaped x ^ "\"")
let format_quoted_char (f : string) (c : char) : string =
  format_string f ("'" ^ (if c = '\'' then "\\'" else if c = '"' then "\"" else escaped_char c) ^ "'")

let format_char (f : string) (c : char) : string = pad (spec f) "" (char_string c) false
let format_bool (f : string) (b : bool) : string = pad (spec f) "" (if b then "true" else "false") false

(* .NET's E format, 1.500000E+003, as C's %e: 1.500000e+03 *)
let exponent (x : float) (p : int) (upper : bool) : string =
  let s = to_string x ("E" ^ format_int "%d" p) in
  let n = String.length s in
  let e = ref 0 in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do if s.[i] = 'E' then e := i done;
  let mant = sub s 0 !e in
  let x = int_of_string (sub s (!e + 2) (n - !e - 2)) in
  let x = if s.[!e + 1] = '-' then - x else x in
  mant ^ (if upper then "E" else "e") ^ (if x < 0 then "-" else "+") ^ format_int "%02d" (if x < 0 then - x else x)

let fixed (x : float) (p : int) : string = to_string x ("F" ^ format_int "%d" p)

(* %g's trailing zeros dropped, and its point if none is left *)
let trim (s : string) : string =
  let has_point = ref false in
  for i = 0 to String.length s - 1 do if s.[i] = '.' then has_point := true done;
  if not !has_point then s
  else begin
    let e = ref (String.length s) in
    for i = String.length s - 1 downto 0 do if s.[i] = 'e' || s.[i] = 'E' then e := i done;
    let k = ref (!e - 1) in
    while s.[!k] = '0' do decr k done;
    if s.[!k] = '.' then decr k;
    sub s 0 (!k + 1) ^ sub s !e (String.length s - !e)
  end

(* OCaml's %h: 0x1.8p+1, the mantissa's hexadecimal digits, its
 * trailing zeros dropped; 0x0p+0; infinity, nan *)
let hex_float (x : float) : string =
  if x = 0.0 then "0x0p+0"
  else begin
    let m, e = frexp_float x in
    (* (1.xxx: twice the mantissa, the exponent one less) *)
    let bits = truncate ((m *. 2.0 -. 1.0) *. 4503599627370496.0) in
    let s = ref "" and b = ref bits in
    for _i = 1 to 13 do s := sub digit_chars (!b land 15) 1 ^ !s; b := !b lsr 4 done;
    let n = ref 13 in
    while !n > 0 && (!s).[!n - 1] = '0' do decr n done;
    let e = e - 1 in
    "0x1" ^ (if !n > 0 then "." ^ sub !s 0 !n else "") ^ "p" ^ (if e < 0 then "-" else "+") ^ format_int "%d" (if e < 0 then - e else e)
  end

(* C's %e %f %g (and E F G) of a precision, 6 when it has none; inf
 * and nan as OCaml prints them; OCaml's %h *)
let format_float (f : string) (x : float) : string =
  let sp = spec f in
  let p = if sp.precision < 0 then 6 else sp.precision in
  let upper = sp.conv = 'E' || sp.conv = 'G' || sp.conv = 'F' in
  let neg = x < 0.0 || (x = 0.0 && 1.0 /. x < 0.0) in
  let a = if neg then -. x else x in
  if sp.conv = 'h' || sp.conv = 'H' then
    pad sp (sign_of sp neg) (if x <> x then "nan" else if a = infinity then "infinity" else hex_float a) false
  else if x <> x then pad sp "" (if upper then "NAN" else "nan") false
  else if a = infinity then pad sp (sign_of sp neg) (if upper then "INF" else "inf") false
  else
    let digits =
      match sp.conv with
      | 'e' | 'E' -> exponent a p upper
      | 'f' | 'F' -> fixed a p
      | 'g' | 'G' ->
          let p = if p = 0 then 1 else p in
          (* (the exponent the number has once rounded to p digits) *)
          let e = exponent a (p - 1) upper in
          let k = ref 0 in
          for i = 0 to String.length e - 1 do if e.[i] = 'e' || e.[i] = 'E' then k := i done;
          let x = int_of_string (sub e (!k + 1) (String.length e - !k - 1)) in
          let s = if x < p && x >= -4 then fixed a (p - 1 - x) else e in
          if sp.alt then s else trim s
      | _ -> failwith "format_float: bad format" in
    pad sp (sign_of sp neg) digits true

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Bytes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* bytes are .NET's byte[], a string a System.String of a byte a char:
 * between them by Latin-1, a copy each way *)
type encoding

external alloc : int -> bytes = "%bytes_create"
external bget : bytes -> int -> char = "%string_unsafe_get"
external bset : bytes -> int -> char -> unit = "%string_unsafe_set"
external blength : bytes -> int = "%string_length"
external latin1 : unit -> encoding
  = "dotnet:static System.Text.Encoding::get_Latin1() -> System.Text.Encoding"
external get_string : encoding -> bytes -> string
  = "dotnet:instance System.Text.Encoding::GetString(uint8[])"
external get_bytes : encoding -> string -> bytes
  = "dotnet:instance System.Text.Encoding::GetBytes(string)"

let create_string (n : int) : bytes =
  if n < 0 then invalid_arg "Bytes.create" else alloc n

external get_bytes_into : encoding -> string -> int -> int -> bytes -> int -> int
  = "dotnet:instance System.Text.Encoding::GetBytes(string,int32,int32,uint8[],int32) -> int32"

(* (one call of .NET's, not a loop: mini-dotnet's interpreter spent a
 * fifth of the reading of a Datalog file in the loop)
 * old: for i = 0 to n - 1 do bset b (o2 + i) s.[o1 + i] done *)
let blit_string (s : string) (o1 : int) (b : bytes) (o2 : int) (n : int) : unit =
  if n > 0 then ignore (get_bytes_into (latin1 ()) s o1 n b o2)

let fill_string (b : bytes) (o : int) (n : int) (c : char) : unit =
  for i = o to o + n - 1 do bset b i c done

(* (C's isprint of ASCII, as the native's: Latin-1's upper half not) *)
let is_printable (c : char) : bool = c >= ' ' && c < '\127'

(* an array of n x: .NET's T[] (newarr), generic in its element *)
external alloc_array : int -> 'a array = "%array_create"

(* Float.Array.create's: a float64[] of zeros *)
external alloc_floats : int -> Float.Array.t = "%array_create"
let caml_floatarray_create (n : int) : Float.Array.t =
  if n < 0 then invalid_arg "Float.Array.create" else alloc_floats n

let make_vect (n : int) (x : 'a) : 'a array =
  if n < 0 then invalid_arg "Array.make";
  let a = alloc_array n in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do a.(i) <- x done;
  a

let string_of_bytes (b : bytes) : string = get_string (latin1 ()) b
let bytes_of_string (s : string) : bytes = get_bytes (latin1 ()) s

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Channels *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the native runtime's (languages/ml/runtime/io.c): a buffer of 4096
 * bytes over a file's, here a .NET Stream (the console's: its bytes as
 * they are, whatever its encoding). A descriptor a number in a table
 * of the streams: 0, 1 and 2 the console's, then the files opened *)
type stream

external stdin_stream : unit -> stream
  = "dotnet:static System.Console::OpenStandardInput() -> System.IO.Stream"
external stdout_stream : unit -> stream
  = "dotnet:static System.Console::OpenStandardOutput() -> System.IO.Stream"
external stderr_stream : unit -> stream
  = "dotnet:static System.Console::OpenStandardError() -> System.IO.Stream"
external s_read : stream -> bytes -> int -> int -> int
  = "dotnet:instance System.IO.Stream::Read(uint8[],int32,int32) -> int32"
external s_write : stream -> bytes -> int -> int -> unit
  = "dotnet:instance System.IO.Stream::Write(uint8[],int32,int32)"
external s_flush : stream -> unit = "dotnet:instance System.IO.Stream::Flush"
external s_dispose : stream -> unit = "dotnet:instance System.IO.Stream::Dispose"
external s_length : stream -> int = "dotnet:instance System.IO.Stream::get_Length"
external s_seek : stream -> int -> unit = "dotnet:instance System.IO.Stream::set_Position"
external open_read : string -> stream
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.File::OpenRead -> System.IO.FileStream"
external open_write : string -> stream
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.File::OpenWrite -> System.IO.FileStream"
external create : string -> stream
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.File::Create -> System.IO.FileStream"
external exists : string -> bool = "dotnet:static System.IO.File::Exists"

type channel = {
  stream : stream;
  buf : bytes;
  mutable len : int;            (* output: the bytes buffered; input: those left, *)
  mutable pos : int;            (* from pos *)
  mutable offset : int;         (* the stream's position *)
  mutable written : bool;       (* an output channel's (flush writes) *)
}

(* (Pervasives' in_channel and out_channel are abstract: objects, each
 * a channel; out_channel says both here) *)
external chan : out_channel -> channel = "%identity"
external of_chan : channel -> out_channel = "%identity"
external chr : int -> char = "%identity"

let streams : (int * stream) list ref = ref []
let next_fd = ref 3

let stream_of (fd : int) : stream =
  let rec find (l : (int * stream) list) : stream option =
    match l with [] -> None | (n, s) :: r -> if n = fd then Some s else find r in
  match find !streams with
  | Some s -> s
  | None ->
      let s =
        if fd = 0 then stdin_stream () else if fd = 1 then stdout_stream ()
        else if fd = 2 then stderr_stream () else raise (Sys_error "bad file descriptor") in
      streams := (fd, s) :: !streams;
      s

let caml_open_descriptor (fd : int) : out_channel =
  of_chan { stream = stream_of fd; buf = create_string 4096; len = 0; pos = 0; offset = 0; written = false }

(* (an input channel's len is what is left to read: not written, the
 * native's write of it fails on a file opened to read, .NET's throws) *)
let flush_chan (c : channel) : unit =
  if c.written then begin
    if c.len > 0 then s_write c.stream c.buf 0 c.len;
    s_flush c.stream;
    c.offset <- c.offset + c.len;
    c.len <- 0
  end

let caml_flush (ch : out_channel) : unit = flush_chan (chan ch)

let putc (c : channel) (b : char) : unit =
  c.written <- true;
  if c.len = 4096 then flush_chan c;
  bset c.buf c.len b;
  c.len <- c.len + 1

let caml_output_char (ch : out_channel) (b : char) : unit = putc (chan ch) b

let caml_output (ch : out_channel) (s : string) (ofs : int) (len : int) : unit =
  let c = chan ch in
  for i = 0 to len - 1 do putc c s.[ofs + i] done

let caml_output_int (ch : out_channel) (n : int) : unit =
  let c = chan ch in
  putc c (chr ((n asr 24) land 255));
  putc c (chr ((n asr 16) land 255));
  putc c (chr ((n asr 8) land 255));
  putc c (chr (n land 255))

let fill (c : channel) : int =
  let n = s_read c.stream c.buf 0 4096 in
  if n > 0 then begin
    c.offset <- c.offset + n;
    c.len <- n;
    c.pos <- 0
  end;
  n

(* the next byte, or -1 at the end (no signals here: -2 never) *)
let ml_input_char (ch : out_channel) : int =
  let c = chan ch in
  if c.len = 0 && fill c <= 0 then -1
  else begin
    c.len <- c.len - 1;
    c.pos <- c.pos + 1;
    code (bget c.buf (c.pos - 1))
  end

(* what the buffer has, at once (filled first when it is empty) *)
let caml_input (ch : out_channel) (s : bytes) (ofs : int) (len : int) : int =
  let c = chan ch in
  if c.len = 0 && len > 0 then ignore (fill c);
  let n = if len < c.len then len else c.len in
  let n = if n < 0 then 0 else n in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do bset s (ofs + i) (bget c.buf (c.pos + i)) done;
  c.pos <- c.pos + n;
  c.len <- c.len - n;
  n

(* how far to the next newline (included), negated if the buffer ends
 * first, 0 at the end: input_line loops on it *)
let caml_input_scan_line (ch : out_channel) : int =
  let c = chan ch in
  if c.len = 0 && fill c <= 0 then 0
  else begin
    let i = ref 0 and found = ref (-1) in
    while !found < 0 && !i < c.len do
      if bget c.buf (c.pos + !i) = '\n' then found := !i + 1;
      incr i
    done;
    if !found > 0 then !found else - c.len
  end

let caml_close_channel (ch : out_channel) : unit =
  let c = chan ch in
  flush_chan c;
  s_dispose c.stream

let caml_pos_out (ch : out_channel) : int = (chan ch).offset + (chan ch).len
let caml_pos_in (ch : out_channel) : int = (chan ch).offset - (chan ch).len
let caml_channel_size (ch : out_channel) : int = s_length (chan ch).stream

let caml_seek_in (ch : out_channel) (n : int) : unit =
  let c = chan ch in
  s_seek c.stream n;
  c.offset <- n;
  c.len <- 0;
  c.pos <- 0

let caml_seek_out (ch : out_channel) (n : int) : unit =
  let c = chan ch in
  flush_chan c;
  s_seek c.stream n;
  c.offset <- n

(* output_binary_int's 4 bytes, the high one first, with its sign *)
let caml_input_int (ch : out_channel) : int =
  let n = ref 0 in
  for _i = 1 to 4 do
    let b = ml_input_char ch in
    if b < 0 then raise End_of_file;
    n := (!n lsl 8) lor b
  done;
  if !n land 0x80000000 <> 0 then !n - 0x100000000 else !n

let ml_signal_pending () : int = 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The system *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let rec has (f : open_flag) (l : open_flag list) : bool =
  match l with [] -> false | x :: r -> x = f || has f r

(* the native's open: written with Open_wronly or Open_append; made with
 * Open_creat when it is not there (or only made, Open_excl); emptied
 * with Open_trunc; at its end with Open_append. A name that cannot be:
 * Sys_error, the name its message, as the native's *)
let sys_open (name : string) (flags : open_flag list) (_perm : int) : int =
  let write = has Open_wronly flags || has Open_append flags in
  let there = exists name in
  if (not there && not (has Open_creat flags)) || (there && has Open_creat flags && has Open_excl flags) then
    raise (Sys_error name);
  let s =
    if not there || has Open_trunc flags then create name
    else if write then open_write name
    else open_read name in
  if has Open_append flags then s_seek s (s_length s);
  let fd = !next_fd in
  incr next_fd;
  streams := (fd, s) :: !streams;
  fd

external bits_to_double : int64 -> float
  = "dotnet:static System.BitConverter::Int64BitsToDouble"
external double_to_bits : float -> int64
  = "dotnet:static System.BitConverter::DoubleToInt64Bits"

let int64_float_of_bits (b : int64) : float = bits_to_double b
let int64_bits_of_float (x : float) : int64 = double_to_bits x

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Int32, Int64 *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* an int64 is .NET's int64, an int; an int32 its int32, which a call
 * of these converts to an int and back (conv.i4: the 32 bits kept, as
 * the int32's own arithmetic would) *)
let int64_neg (a : int) : int = - a
let int64_add (a : int) (b : int) : int = a + b
let int64_sub (a : int) (b : int) : int = a - b
let int64_mul (a : int) (b : int) : int = a * b
let int64_div (a : int) (b : int) : int = a / b
let int64_mod (a : int) (b : int) : int = a mod b
let int64_and (a : int) (b : int) : int = a land b
let int64_or (a : int) (b : int) : int = a lor b
let int64_xor (a : int) (b : int) : int = a lxor b
let int64_shift_left (a : int) (n : int) : int = a lsl n
let int64_shift_right (a : int) (n : int) : int = a asr n
let int64_shift_right_unsigned (a : int) (n : int) : int = a lsr n
let int64_of_int (a : int) : int = a
let int64_to_int (a : int) : int = a
let int64_of_int32 (a : int) : int = a
let int64_to_int32 (a : int) : int = a
let int64_format (f : string) (a : int) : string = format_int f a
let int64_of_string (s : string) : int = int_of_string s
let int64_of_float (x : float) : int = truncate x
let int64_to_float (a : int) : float = float a

let int32_neg (a : int) : int = - a
let int32_add (a : int) (b : int) : int = a + b
let int32_sub (a : int) (b : int) : int = a - b
let int32_mul (a : int) (b : int) : int = a * b
let int32_div (a : int) (b : int) : int = a / b
let int32_mod (a : int) (b : int) : int = a mod b
let int32_and (a : int) (b : int) : int = a land b
let int32_or (a : int) (b : int) : int = a lor b
let int32_xor (a : int) (b : int) : int = a lxor b
let int32_shift_left (a : int) (n : int) : int = a lsl n
let int32_shift_right (a : int) (n : int) : int = a asr n
let int32_shift_right_unsigned (a : int) (n : int) : int = (a land 0xFFFFFFFF) lsr n
let int32_of_int (a : int) : int = a
let int32_to_int (a : int) : int = a
(* (%x, %o, %u of a negative one: its 32 bits) *)
let int32_format (f : string) (a : int) : string =
  let c = f.[String.length f - 1] in
  format_int f (if a < 0 && (c = 'x' || c = 'X' || c = 'o' || c = 'u') then a land 0xFFFFFFFF else a)
let int32_of_string (s : string) : int =
  let n = int_of_string s in
  if n < -0x80000000 || n > 0xFFFFFFFF then failwith "Int32.of_string" else n
let int32_of_float (x : float) : int = truncate x
let int32_to_float (a : int) : float = float a

external single_bits : float -> int
  = "dotnet:static System.BitConverter::SingleToInt32Bits(float32) -> int32"
external bits_single : int -> float
  = "dotnet:static System.BitConverter::Int32BitsToSingle(int32) -> float32"

let int32_bits_of_float (x : float) : int = single_bits x
let int32_float_of_bits (b : int) : float = bits_single b

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Hashtbl *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Hashtbl.hash: the compiler's Ml::hash, the same on both runtimes
 * (not OCaml's numbers: a table's order is not its); positive *)
external ml_hash : 'a -> int = "%hash"

let hash_univ_param (_count : int) (_limit : int) (x : 'a) : int = ml_hash x land 0x3FFFFFFF

(* Sys *)

type directory_info

external command_line : unit -> string array
  = "dotnet:static System.Environment::GetCommandLineArgs() -> string[]"
external get_variable : string -> string
  = "dotnet:static System.Environment::GetEnvironmentVariable"
external null_or_empty : string -> bool = "dotnet:static System.String::IsNullOrEmpty"
external tick_count : unit -> int = "dotnet:static System.Environment::get_TickCount64"
external dir_exists : string -> bool = "dotnet:static System.IO.Directory::Exists"
external create_directory : string -> directory_info
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.Directory::CreateDirectory -> System.IO.DirectoryInfo"
external current_directory : unit -> string
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.Directory::GetCurrentDirectory"
external set_current_directory : string -> unit
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.Directory::SetCurrentDirectory"
external entries : string -> string array
  = "dotnet:static System.IO.Directory::GetFileSystemEntries"
external file_delete : string -> unit = "dotnet:static System.IO.File::Delete"
external file_move : string -> string -> bool -> unit = "dotnet:static System.IO.File::Move"

(* (the assembly's path first: the program's name, as argv.(0)) *)
let sys_get_argv () : string array = command_line ()

(* (an int of 64 bits: .NET's) *)
let sys_get_config () : string * int = ("Unix", 64)

(* (a variable set to "": not set, as .NET says null and "" alike here) *)
let sys_getenv (v : string) : string =
  let s = get_variable v in
  if null_or_empty s then raise Not_found else s

let sys_file_exists (f : string) : bool = exists f || dir_exists f

let no_such (f : string) : 'a = raise (Sys_error (f ^ ": No such file or directory"))

let sys_is_directory (f : string) : bool =
  if dir_exists f then true else if exists f then false else no_such f

let sys_remove (f : string) : unit = if exists f then file_delete f else no_such f

let sys_rename (a : string) (b : string) : unit =
  if exists a then file_move a b true else no_such a

let sys_mkdir (f : string) (_perm : int) : unit =
  if sys_file_exists f then raise (Sys_error (f ^ ": File exists")) else ignore (create_directory f)

(* the names of a directory's entries (.NET's are paths) *)
let sys_read_directory (d : string) : string array =
  if not (dir_exists d) then no_such d;
  let a = entries d in
  for i = 0 to Array.length a - 1 do
    let p = a.(i) in
    let j = ref (String.length p - 1) in
    while !j >= 0 && p.[!j] <> '/' do decr j done;
    a.(i) <- sub p (!j + 1) (String.length p - !j - 1)
  done;
  a

let sys_getcwd () : string = current_directory ()
let sys_chdir (d : string) : unit = if dir_exists d then set_current_directory d else no_such d

(* (the time since the program started, by the clock: not the
 * processor's, which .NET gives only through a Process) *)
let start_ticks = tick_count ()
let sys_time () : float = float (tick_count () - start_ticks) /. 1000.0

let sys_system_command (_ : string) : int = raise (Sys_error "Sys.command: no process here (.NET)")

(* (no signals: a handler installed is never run) *)
let ml_signal (_ : int) (_ : int) : unit = ()

let sys_close (fd : int) : unit =
  let rec remove (l : (int * stream) list) : (int * stream) list =
    match l with
    | [] -> []
    | (n, s) :: r -> if n = fd then (s_dispose s; r) else (n, s) :: remove r in
  streams := remove !streams

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Callback, Gc, Digest *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* (a value named for the C runtime's own calls: none here) *)
let register_named_value (_ : string) (_ : Obj.t) : unit = ()

(* (.NET's collector: no counters of OCaml's heap, nothing to ask) *)
let gc_counters () : int * int * int * int = (0, 0, 0, 0)
let gc_minor () : unit = ()
let gc_major () : unit = ()
let gc_full_major () : unit = ()
let gc_compaction () : unit = ()

external md5 : bytes -> bytes
  = "dotnet:static System.Security.Cryptography.MD5::HashData(uint8[]) -> uint8[]"

let md5_string (s : string) (ofs : int) (len : int) : string =
  string_of_bytes (md5 (bytes_of_string (sub s ofs len)))

(* a channel's len bytes, or all that is left (len < 0) *)
let md5_chan (ch : out_channel) (len : int) : string =
  let b = create_string 4096 and acc = ref "" and left = ref len and over = ref false in
  while not !over do
    let want = if !left < 0 || !left > 4096 then 4096 else !left in
    let n = if want = 0 then 0 else caml_input ch b 0 want in
    if n = 0 then over := true
    else begin
      acc := !acc ^ sub (string_of_bytes b) 0 n;
      if !left > 0 then left := !left - n
    end
  done;
  if !left > 0 then raise End_of_file;
  md5_string !acc 0 (String.length !acc)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Printexc *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type dotnet_type

external get_type : exn -> dotnet_type = "dotnet:instance System.Object::GetType() -> System.Type"
external type_name : dotnet_type -> string = "dotnet:instance System.Type::get_Name"

(* an exception as OCaml prints it: the predefined ones with their
 * arguments (Failure("..."), Sys_error, Invalid_argument); another,
 * Pervasives' too (Exit, Assert_failure: a unit after this one), its
 * class's name, its arguments not (no reflection of them here) *)
let ml_exn_string (e : exn) : string =
  (* (not escaped: String's escaped is a unit after this one) *)
  let quoted (s : string) = "(\"" ^ s ^ "\")" in
  match e with
  | Failure s -> "Failure" ^ quoted s
  | Invalid_argument s -> "Invalid_argument" ^ quoted s
  | Sys_error s -> "Sys_error" ^ quoted s
  | Not_found -> "Not_found"
  | End_of_file -> "End_of_file"
  | Division_by_zero -> "Division_by_zero"
  | e -> type_name (get_type e)

(* (no backtrace kept: none, at Printexc's types, which come after) *)
let ml_raise_trace () : string = ""
let caml_get_exception_backtrace () : 'a option = None
let caml_get_exception_raw_backtrace () : string = ""

external environment_exit : int -> unit = "dotnet:static System.Environment::Exit(int32)"

(* (the external's 'a: a call of it gets a value of its type, which
 * Exit never lets it use) *)
let sys_exit (n : int) : unit = environment_exit n
lib_core/dotnet/Runtime.mli
8205
(* The runtime of mini-ml -dotnet: Pervasives' externals of C, the
 * native runtime's (languages/ml/runtime/*.c), written in ML over .NET's
 * members (the plan_dotnet_languages.md's stage 3b, its decision 7's
 * externals). mini-ml -dotnet -L lib_core compiles it first, into the
 * program's assembly, and a call of an external of C is a call of the
 * function here of its name:
 *
 *   Pervasives.mli   external sqrt : float -> float = "sqrt_float" ...
 *   program.ml       sqrt 2.0
 *   assembly         call float64 Runtime::sqrt_float(float64)
 *   Runtime.ml       let sqrt_float x = m_sqrt x
 *                    external m_sqrt : float -> float
 *                      = "dotnet:static System.Math::Sqrt"
 *
 * So the assembly is .NET's alone, and Microsoft's dotnet runs it as
 * mini-dotnet does (the author: "We do want to run what is produced by
 * mini-ml -dotnet with the microsoft's dotnet and runtime"); a member
 * mini-dotnet lacks is added to its library under its .NET name
 * (languages/dotnet/runtime/Library.ml: System.Math, Double's Parse and
 * ToString(format)). What ML can do itself is ML here: int_of_string,
 * format_int, strtod's syntax; .NET does what needs exact rounding, a
 * decimal number read (Double.Parse) and a float's digits (its E and F
 * formats), from which C's %e, %f and %g are made.
 *
 * bytes are .NET's byte[] (the author's choice: "byte[] + Streams"),
 * a string a System.String of a byte a char: a %identity between them
 * a copy, by string_of_bytes and bytes_of_string here (Latin-1). The
 * channels are the native's, a buffer of 4096 bytes, over a .NET
 * Stream instead of a descriptor: the console's (Console's
 * OpenStandardOutput..., its bytes as they are, whatever its encoding)
 * or a file's (File's OpenRead, OpenWrite, Create, no enum to name);
 * the descriptors numbers in a table of them, as sys_open returns one.
 *
 *   Pervasives      stdout = open_descriptor_out 1
 *                     |  external ... = "caml_open_descriptor"
 *   Runtime         { stream = Console.OpenStandardOutput(); buf; ... }
 *                     |  output_string: caml_output, a byte at a time
 *                     |  into buf; flush: Stream.Write(buf, 0, len)
 *   .NET            System.IO.Stream (mini-dotnet's: the console's
 *                   channel, a file's descriptor)
 *
 * Differences with the native runtime: an int is an int64 (63 bits
 * natively), so %x of a negative int has 16 digits and int_of_string
 * wraps at 64 bits; no signals (ml_signal_pending 0); a file's
 * permissions not given (.NET's own); an error of .NET's (a file it
 * cannot open though it is there) its exception, not Sys_error.
 *
 * others:
 * OCaml's own runtime: C (floats.c, ints.c, io.c...), its primitives
 * named in the externals; js_of_ocaml's: JavaScript functions of the
 * primitives' names (runtime/*.js), the same idea as this unit;
 * F#'s FSharp.Core: F# over .NET, its printf in F#. *)

(* lib_core's Unix on .NET, in its place (mini-ml -dotnet -L takes
 * dotnet/'s unit of a name over lib_core's): its system calls by their
 * numbers (system/Unix.ml's unix_syscall) have no .NET form, so its
 * functions fail, by their names, where a program calls them; those a
 * .NET program has by Sys are Sys's (getcwd, chdir, unlink, rename,
 * mkdir). So the units over Unix compile (commons/'s FS, Console,
 * Procs...), and what of them a program uses without Unix runs: FS's
 * files by channels, Console's by Pervasives'. Its types those of
 * system/Unix.mli, which is its interface; a descriptor an int.
 * Generated from Unix.mli, then edited by hand. *)

lib_core/libc/arch/arm/div.s
3182
// Plan 9's, by principia and goken (libc's README.md; LICENSE).
// arm has no division: the compiler calls these (_div, _divu, _mod,
// _modu). principia's libc/arm/div.s.

// no arm instructions for those operations so must be
// provided as "builtins"

Q	= 0
N	= 1
D	= 2
CC	= 3
TMP	= 11

TEXT	save<>(SB), 1, $0
 MOVW	R(Q), 0(FP)
 MOVW	R(N), 4(FP)
 MOVW	R(D), 8(FP)
 MOVW	R(CC), 12(FP)

 MOVW	R(TMP), R(Q)		/* numerator */
 MOVW	20(FP), R(D)		/* denominator */
 CMP	$0, R(D)
 BNE	s1
 MOVW	-1(R(D)), R(TMP)	/* divide by zero fault */
s1:	RET

TEXT	rest<>(SB), 1, $0
 MOVW	0(FP), R(Q)
 MOVW	4(FP), R(N)
 MOVW	8(FP), R(D)
 MOVW	12(FP), R(CC)
/*
 * return to caller
 * of rest<>
 */
 MOVW	0(R13), R14
 ADD	$20, R13
 B	(R14)

/*
 * N / D, unsigned, D not 0: the quotient in Q, the remainder in N.
 * The denominator first shifted left under the numerator's highest
 * bit, by the largest k such that D << k <= N (D compared with N >> 16,
 * then >> 8, 4, 2 and 1: a binary search, arm's shifted operand doing
 * the shifts), then k + 1 turns, a bit of the quotient each (the carry
 * of N - D, by ADC), the denominator shifted back right. So a quotient
 * of q bits costs about 20 + 6(q + 1) instructions, at most 212 for
 * 32; mini-doom's divisions, by fixed point's 16, about a hundred.
 * (old: 32 turns always, but for the numerator's zero bytes skipped
 * first, 7 instructions each: about 230; principia's loop, below)
 */
TEXT	div<>(SB), 1, $0
 MOVW	R(Q), R(N)
 MOVW	$0, R(Q)
 MOVW	$0, R(CC)
 CMP	R(N)>>16, R(D)
 BHI	k8
 SLL	$16, R(D)
 ADD	$16, R(CC)
k8:
 CMP	R(N)>>8, R(D)
 BHI	k4
 SLL	$8, R(D)
 ADD	$8, R(CC)
k4:
 CMP	R(N)>>4, R(D)
 BHI	k2
 SLL	$4, R(D)
 ADD	$4, R(CC)
k2:
 CMP	R(N)>>2, R(D)
 BHI	k1
 SLL	$2, R(D)
 ADD	$2, R(CC)
k1:
 CMP	R(N)>>1, R(D)
 BHI	turn
 SLL	$1, R(D)
 ADD	$1, R(CC)
turn:
 CMP	R(D), R(N)
 SUB.HS	R(D), R(N)
 ADC	R(Q), R(Q)
 SRL	$1, R(D)
 SUB.S	$1, R(CC)
 BGE	turn
 RET

// old:
// TEXT	div<>(SB), 1, $0
//  MOVW	$32, R(CC)
// /*
//  * skip zeros 8-at-a-time
//  */
// e1:
//  AND.S	$(0xff<<24),R(Q), R(N)
//  BNE	e2
//  SLL	$8, R(Q)
//  SUB.S	$8, R(CC)
//  BNE	e1
//  RET
// e2:
//  MOVW	$0, R(N)
//
// loop:
// /*
//  * shift R(N||Q) left one
//  */
//  SLL	$1, R(N)
//  CMP	$0, R(Q)
//  ORR.LT	$1, R(N)
//  SLL	$1, R(Q)
//
// /*
//  * compare numerator to denominator
//  * if less, subtract and set quotent bit
//  */
//  CMP	R(D), R(N)
//  ORR.HS	$1, R(Q)
//  SUB.HS	R(D), R(N)
//  SUB.S	$1, R(CC)
//  BNE	loop
//  RET

TEXT	_div(SB), 1, $16
 BL	save<>(SB)
 CMP	$0, R(Q)
 BGE	d1
 RSB	$0, R(Q), R(Q)
 CMP	$0, R(D)
 BGE	d2
 RSB	$0, R(D), R(D)
d0:
 BL	div<>(SB)		/* none/both neg */
 MOVW	R(Q), R(TMP)
 B	out
d1:
 CMP	$0, R(D)
 BGE	d0
 RSB	$0, R(D), R(D)
d2:
 BL	div<>(SB)		/* one neg */
 RSB	$0, R(Q), R(TMP)
 B	out

TEXT	_mod(SB), 1, $16
 BL	save<>(SB)
 CMP	$0, R(D)
 RSB.LT	$0, R(D), R(D)
 CMP	$0, R(Q)
 BGE	m1
 RSB	$0, R(Q), R(Q)
 BL	div<>(SB)		/* neg numerator */
 RSB	$0, R(N), R(TMP)
 B	out
m1:
 BL	div<>(SB)		/* pos numerator */
 MOVW	R(N), R(TMP)
 B	out

TEXT	_divu(SB), 1, $16
 BL	save<>(SB)
 BL	div<>(SB)
 MOVW	R(Q), R(TMP)
 B	out

TEXT	_modu(SB), 1, $16
 BL	save<>(SB)
 BL	div<>(SB)
 MOVW	R(N), R(TMP)
 B	out

out:
 BL	rest<>(SB)
 B	out
