(* Url: the address of a thing on the network, and the relative ones.

   A URL (Tim Berners-Lee, 1994; the grammar as it stands is RFC 3986,
   2005, which calls them URIs) is five parts, each optional but the
   path, which may be empty:

       http://elm-lang.org:80/images/turtle.gif?size=96#top
       \__/   \_____________/\_________________/ \_____/ \_/
      scheme     authority          path          query  fragment
                 = host:port

   The scheme says which protocol to speak ("http": Http.mli), the
   authority whom to speak it to (a name for DNS, or an address, and a
   port, else the scheme's default: 80 for http, 443 for https), the
   path and the query what to ask them for. The fragment is never sent:
   it is for the client, a place in the page.

   Splitting a string into the five parts is easy, because the RFC
   chose the separators so that it is: its appendix B even gives the
   regular expression that does it, for any URL, valid or not,

       {|^(([^:/?#]+):)?(//([^/?#]*))?([^?#]*)(\?([^#]*))?(#(.*))?|}
             scheme        authority    path      query     fragment

   and [parse] is that regexp written out by hand: the scheme up to a
   ':' that comes before any of "/?#", the authority after "//" up to
   the next of "/?#", the path up to "?" or "#", and so on. (The tests
   check that the two agree, the regexp run by OCaml's Str.)

   The subtle part is the *relative* reference. A web page says
   <img src="../images/turtle.gif">, and a server answering "moved"
   says "Location: /new/place" (Http.mli): both mean a URL relative to
   the one they came from, the *base*, and [resolve] turns the pair
   into an absolute URL, with RFC 3986's section 5.2 algorithm: a part
   present in the reference wins, and the parts before it come from the
   base; a relative path is *merged* with the base's (the base's path
   up to its last '/', then the reference's), and "." and ".." are then
   removed as a file system would (remove_dot_segments):

       base      http://a/b/c/d;p?q
       reference ../g
       merged    /b/c/../g        (the base's path up to "c/", then "../g")
       result    http://a/b/g     (".." removed "c/")

   Worked examples (checked by the tests): all of RFC 3986's own, its
   section 5.4, 23 normal ones and 19 abnormal ones from the same base,
   e.g. "g" gives http://a/b/c/g, "//g" http://g, "?y"
   http://a/b/c/d;p?y, "../../../g" http://a/g (a ".." above the root
   stays at the root), "g?y/../x" http://a/b/c/g?y/../x (dots in a
   query are not segments); and remove_dot_segments' two traces from
   section 5.2.4, "/a/b/c/./../../g" to "/a/g" and "mid/content=5/../6"
   to "mid/6".

   Where it stands: every program of ix that follows a link.
   Http_client parses what it is given and resolves each "Location:";
   the browsers resolve every href and src of a page against the
   page's own URL (the engine's Browser_url); mini-httpd uses
   [remove_dot_segments] the other way, to see what file a request's
   path names. The file system's side of the same idea is a path
   cleaned as text: Plan 9's cleanname, and the kernel's dot-dot
   (mini-pwd, Pwd, says why there too it is done on the name).

   cs-history:
   The web's three inventions were HTML, HTTP and this one, and Tim
   Berners-Lee has said this is the one that mattered: one string that
   names anything any protocol can fetch -- a file on an FTP server, a
   newsgroup, a Gopher menu, and a page of the web among them -- so
   that a link could point at what already existed. He wrote it down
   as "Universal Resource Identifiers" (RFC 1630, 1994); the IETF,
   wary of "universal", made it "Uniform Resource Locators" (RFC 1738,
   1994). The "//" after the scheme came from the Apollo Domain file
   system's network paths; he has since said the two slashes were not
   needed.

   terminology:
   URL, URI, URN. A URI (Identifier) is the general thing, any such
   string. A URL (Locator) is a URI that says where to get the thing
   and how ("https://..."); a URN (Name) one that only names it, for
   ever, wherever it is ("urn:isbn:0262510871"). RFC 3986 speaks of
   URIs; browsers and the WHATWG's URL Standard say URL for all of
   them, as everybody does.

   others:
   Two specifications, and they disagree. RFC 3986 is a grammar: a
   string is a URI or it is not. The WHATWG's URL Standard (the
   browsers', since 2012 or so) is an algorithm that takes whatever
   was typed or found in a page and repairs it: backslashes become
   slashes, spaces are escaped, a missing slash is added, tabs and
   newlines inside are dropped. Here it is the RFC's, which is short
   and has its own test cases; a browser for today's pages ends up
   needing the other's leniency.

   Not done: percent-encoding ("%20" for a space) is kept as it is,
   neither decoded nor checked -- a URL is sent as it was written, which
   is what an HTTP client needs; and no normalization (case of the
   percent escapes, default ports removed: section 6).

   Reference: RFC 3986, "Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic
   Syntax", Tim Berners-Lee, Roy Fielding and Larry Masinter (2005),
   sections 3 (the parts), 5 (resolving) and appendix B (the regexp);
   RFC 1738 (1994), the first URL specification. *)

(* userinfo@host:port; the host as written, lowercased if a name
 * ("elm-lang.org", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"); the port as written, if any *)
type authority = { userinfo : string option; host : string; port : int option }

(* a URL, or a reference relative to one (then without a scheme, and
 * maybe without an authority): the five parts of the diagram above. A
 * part absent (None) is not the same as a part empty (Some ""): "?"
 * has an empty query, and resolves differently from "" (section 5.2.2) *)
type t = {
  scheme : string option; (* lowercased: "http" *)
  authority : authority option;
  path : string; (* "/images/turtle.gif", "../g", or "" *)
  query : string option; (* without its '?' *)
  fragment : string option; (* without its '#' *)
}

(* the five parts of a string, as appendix B's regexp finds them; Error
 * only for an authority's port that isn't a number *)
val parse : string -> (t, string) result

(* back to a string, section 5.3 (to_string (parse s) = s, but for the
 * case of the scheme and the host, and an empty port dropped) *)
val to_string : t -> string

(* [resolve base reference]: the absolute URL the [reference] means,
 * seen from [base] (which must have a scheme), section 5.2.2 (strict:
 * "http:g" is not relative, even with the base's scheme) *)
val resolve : t -> t -> t

(* section 5.2.4: "." and ".." segments removed from a path *)
val remove_dot_segments : string -> string

(* the port to connect to: the one written, else the scheme's (80 for
 * http, 443 for https); None if neither *)
val port : t -> int option

(* what an HTTP request asks for (its request line's target): the path
 * and the query, "/" for an empty path, no fragment (never sent) *)
val request_target : t -> string

(* ix: the author's playground's libs/networking/protocols/Urlencoded.ml (docs/plans/plan_browser.md) *)

(* See Urlencoded.mli *)

let kept (c : char) : bool =
  (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || String.contains "*-._" c

let escape (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  String.iter
    (fun c ->
      if kept c then Buffer.add_char b c
      else if c = ' ' then Buffer.add_char b '+'
      else Buffer.add_string b (Printf.sprintf "%%%02X" (Char.code c)))
    s;
  Buffer.contents b

let hex (c : char) : int option =
  match c with
  | '0' .. '9' -> Some (Char.code c - Char.code '0')
  | 'a' .. 'f' -> Some (Char.code c - Char.code 'a' + 10)
  | 'A' .. 'F' -> Some (Char.code c - Char.code 'A' + 10)
  | _ -> None

let unescape (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec go i =
    if i < n then
      match s.[i] with
      | '+' ->
          Buffer.add_char b ' ';
          go (i + 1)
      | '%' when i + 2 < n -> (
          match (hex s.[i + 1], hex s.[i + 2]) with
          | Some h, Some l ->
              Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr ((h * 16) + l));
              go (i + 3)
          | _ ->
              Buffer.add_char b '%';
              go (i + 1))
      | c ->
          Buffer.add_char b c;
          go (i + 1)
  in
  go 0;
  Buffer.contents b

let encode (fields : (string * string) list) : string =
  String.concat "&" (List.map (fun (name, value) -> escape name ^ "=" ^ escape value) fields)

let decode (s : string) : (string * string) list =
  String.split_on_char '&' s
  |> List.filter (fun field -> field <> "")
  |> List.map (fun field ->
         match String.index_opt field '=' with
         | Some i -> (unescape (String.sub field 0 i), unescape (String.sub field (i + 1) (String.length field - i - 1)))
         | None -> (unescape field, ""))

(* Urlencoded: a form's fields as one string -- what a browser sends
   when a form is submitted, in the URL (GET) or as the body (POST),
   and what the server's program reads back.

     q = "café au lait", lang = "fr"
       -> q=caf%C3%A9+au+lait&lang=fr

   The fields in order, each name=value, joined by '&'. In a name or a
   value, the letters, the digits and "*-._" stay as they are, a space
   is '+', and every other byte is '%' and its two hexadecimal digits,
   upper case: "é" is its two UTF-8 bytes, %C3%A9, and a '&' or a '='
   in a value is %26 or %3D, so they only ever separate. The format of
   Mosaic's forms (1993) and of every form since, its name the
   Content-Type a POST says: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

   GET or POST is the page's choice (<form method=post>): with GET the
   fields are the URL's query ("/search?q=caf%C3%A9+au+lait&lang=fr"),
   so they can be bookmarked, and end in the server's log; with POST
   they are the request's body, for what should not be (a password)
   or is not a question but an action (an order).

   [decode] is the other way, lenient as servers are: a '+' is a space,
   a '%' not followed by two hexadecimal digits is itself, a field with
   no '=' has the value "".

   Where it stands: the browser's forms (the engine's Browser_forms
   encodes what was typed, for the query or for Http.post's body) and
   a page's scripts (URLSearchParams in the web API's Script_url).
   mini-httpd answers GET only and has no use for [decode]; a server
   with a program behind a URL would start there.

   cs-history:
   Forms are what made the web more than pages to read. Dave Raggett
   proposed them in HTML+ (1993); Mosaic 2.0 (November 1993) drew
   them; and NCSA's server (Rob McCool) ran a program for the request
   and sent back what it printed -- CGI, the Common Gateway Interface,
   its input this module's string. A search box, a guest book, a shop:
   every "web application" until XMLHttpRequest (1999) was a form
   sent, a program run, a new page. The '%' and two hexadecimal digits
   is the URL's own escape (RFC 1738); the '+' for a space is older
   than that rule and the form's alone, which is why a '+' in a path
   is a plus and in a query a space.

   Reference: WHATWG URL Standard, section 5 ("application/x-www-form-
   urlencoded"); HTML 2.0 (RFC 1866), section 8.2.1, the form's
   submission. *)

(* the fields, encoded and joined: the query or the body *)
val encode : (string * string) list -> string

(* the fields of a query or a body, decoded *)
val decode : string -> (string * string) list

(* one name or value, encoded (a space as '+') *)
val escape : string -> string

(* one name or value, decoded *)
val unescape : string -> string

(* See Imap.mli *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The responses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type value = Atom of string | String of string | List of value list | Nil

type response =
  | Status of string option * string * string
  | Data of value list
  | Continue of string

type token = Open | Close | Word of string | Quoted of string

(* the tokens of a text with no literal; an atom's brackets hold spaces
 * and parentheses: BODY[HEADER.FIELDS (FROM TO)] is one *)
let tokens (s : string) : token list =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec quoted (b : Buffer.t) (j : int) : int =
    if j >= n then j
    else
      match s.[j] with
      | '\\' when j + 1 < n ->
          Buffer.add_char b s.[j + 1];
          quoted b (j + 2)
      | '"' -> j + 1
      | c ->
          Buffer.add_char b c;
          quoted b (j + 1)
  in
  let rec atom (j : int) (depth : int) : int =
    if j >= n then j
    else
      match s.[j] with
      | '[' -> atom (j + 1) (depth + 1)
      | ']' -> atom (j + 1) (max 0 (depth - 1))
      | (' ' | '(' | ')') when depth = 0 -> j
      | _ -> atom (j + 1) depth
  in
  let rec go (i : int) (acc : token list) : token list =
    if i >= n then List.rev acc
    else
      match s.[i] with
      | ' ' | '\t' | '\r' | '\n' -> go (i + 1) acc
      | '(' -> go (i + 1) (Open :: acc)
      | ')' -> go (i + 1) (Close :: acc)
      | '"' ->
          let b = Buffer.create 16 in
          let j = quoted b (i + 1) in
          go j (Quoted (Buffer.contents b) :: acc)
      | _ ->
          let j = atom i 0 in
          go j (Word (String.sub s i (j - i)) :: acc)
  in
  go 0 []

(* the values up to the list's end (a Close), and what is after it *)
let rec parse (ts : token list) : value list * token list =
  match ts with
  | [] -> ([], [])
  | Close :: rest -> ([], rest)
  | t :: rest ->
      let v, rest =
        match t with
        | Open ->
            let inner, rest = parse rest in
            (List inner, rest)
        | Quoted s -> (String s, rest)
        | Word w ->
            ((if String.uppercase_ascii w = "NIL" then Nil else Atom w), rest)
        | Close -> (Nil, rest)
      in
      let more, rest = parse rest in
      (v :: more, rest)

let values (s : string) : value list = fst (parse (tokens s))

(* a line ending in a literal's count, "... {44}": the text before it,
 * and the count ("{44+}", a client's literal that waits for no "+",
 * read the same) *)
let literal (l : string) : (string * int) option =
  let n = String.length l in
  if n > 2 && l.[n - 1] = '}' then
    match String.rindex_opt l '{' with
    | None -> None
    | Some i -> (
        let k = String.sub l (i + 1) (n - i - 2) in
        let k =
          if k <> "" && k.[String.length k - 1] = '+' then
            String.sub k 0 (String.length k - 1)
          else k
        in
        match int_of_string_opt k with
        | Some c when c >= 0 -> Some (String.sub l 0 i, c)
        | _ -> None)
  else None

(* a response's pieces: the lines' text, and the literals' bytes *)
type segment = Text of string | Literal of string

(* the first word and the rest *)
let word (s : string) : string * string =
  match String.index_opt s ' ' with
  | Some i -> (String.sub s 0 i, String.sub s (i + 1) (String.length s - i - 1))
  | None -> (s, "")

let read ~(line : unit -> string option) ~(bytes : int -> string option) :
    response option =
  let rec segments (acc : segment list) : segment list option =
    match line () with
    | None -> None
    | Some l -> (
        match literal l with
        | Some (text, n) -> (
            match bytes n with
            | Some b -> segments (Literal b :: Text text :: acc)
            | None -> None)
        | None -> Some (List.rev (Text l :: acc)))
  in
  match segments [] with
  | None -> None
  | Some segs ->
      let first, others =
        match segs with Text t :: rest -> (t, rest) | l -> ("", l)
      in
      let tag, after = word first in
      let w, text = word after in
      let status =
        others = []
        && List.mem (String.uppercase_ascii w)
             [ "OK"; "NO"; "BAD"; "BYE"; "PREAUTH" ]
      in
      if tag = "+" then Some (Continue after)
      else if status || tag <> "*" then
        Some
          (Status
             ( (if tag = "*" then None else Some tag),
               String.uppercase_ascii w,
               text ))
      else
        let ts =
          List.concat_map
            (fun s ->
              match s with Text t -> tokens t | Literal b -> [ Quoted b ])
            (Text after :: others)
        in
        Some (Data (fst (parse ts)))

let quote (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s + 2) in
  Buffer.add_char b '"';
  String.iter
    (fun c ->
      if c = '"' || c = '\\' then Buffer.add_char b '\\';
      Buffer.add_char b c)
    s;
  Buffer.add_char b '"';
  Buffer.contents b

let rec pairs (l : value list) : (string * value) list =
  match l with
  | Atom k :: v :: rest -> (String.uppercase_ascii k, v) :: pairs rest
  | _ :: rest -> pairs rest
  | [] -> []

let text (v : value) : string =
  match v with Atom s | String s -> s | List _ | Nil -> ""

let list (l : string list) : string =
  "("
  ^ String.concat " "
      (List.map
         (fun s -> if s = "" || String.contains s ' ' then quote s else s)
         l)
  ^ ")"

let texts (v : value) : string list =
  match v with List l -> List.map text l | _ -> []

let uid_set (uids : int list) : string =
  (* runs of consecutive UIDs as a:b *)
  let rec runs (l : int list) : (int * int) list =
    match l with
    | [] -> []
    | u :: rest -> (
        match runs rest with
        | (a, b) :: more when a = u + 1 -> (u, b) :: more
        | more -> (u, u) :: more)
  in
  String.concat ","
    (List.map
       (fun (a, b) ->
         if a = b then string_of_int a else Printf.sprintf "%d:%d" a b)
       (runs (List.sort_uniq compare uids)))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The client *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type t = { lines : Lines.t; mutable next : int }

let read_one (t : t) : response option =
  read ~line:(fun () -> Lines.line t.lines) ~bytes:(Lines.bytes t.lines)

let ended (t : t) : string =
  match Lines.why t.lines with Some w -> w | None -> "the connection ended"

let connect (lines : Lines.t) : (t, string) result =
  let t = { lines; next = 0 } in
  match read_one t with
  | Some (Status (None, ("OK" | "PREAUTH"), _)) -> Ok t
  | Some (Status (_, w, text)) -> Error (w ^ " " ^ text)
  | Some _ -> Error "not an IMAP server's greeting"
  | None -> Error (ended t)

let command (t : t) (cmd : string) : (response list, string) result =
  t.next <- t.next + 1;
  let tag = "a" ^ string_of_int t.next in
  Lines.send_line t.lines (tag ^ " " ^ cmd);
  let rec go (acc : response list) : (response list, string) result =
    match read_one t with
    | None -> Error (ended t)
    | Some (Status (Some tg, w, text)) when tg = tag ->
        if w = "OK" then Ok (List.rev acc) else Error (w ^ " " ^ text)
    | Some r -> go (r :: acc)
  in
  go []

let login (t : t) ~(user : string) ~(password : string) : (unit, string) result
    =
  match command t ("LOGIN " ^ quote user ^ " " ^ quote password) with
  | Ok _ -> Ok ()
  | Error e -> Error e

let select (t : t) (mailbox : string) : (string, string) result =
  match command t ("SELECT " ^ quote mailbox) with
  | Error e -> Error e
  | Ok rs ->
      let validity (r : response) : string option =
        match r with
        | Status (None, "OK", text) -> (
            match values text with
            | Atom a :: _ when String.starts_with ~prefix:"[UIDVALIDITY " a ->
                let n = String.length "[UIDVALIDITY " in
                Some (String.sub a n (String.length a - n - 1))
            | _ -> None)
        | _ -> None
      in
      Ok (match List.find_map validity rs with Some v -> v | None -> "")

let mailboxes (t : t) : ((string list * string) list, string) result =
  match command t "LIST \"\" \"*\"" with
  | Error e -> Error e
  | Ok rs ->
      Ok
        (List.filter_map
           (fun r ->
             match r with
             | Data [ Atom l; attributes; _; name ]
               when String.uppercase_ascii l = "LIST" ->
                 Some (texts attributes, text name)
             | _ -> None)
           rs)

let search (t : t) (query : string) : (int list, string) result =
  match command t ("UID SEARCH " ^ query) with
  | Error e -> Error e
  | Ok rs ->
      Ok
        (List.concat_map
           (fun r ->
             match r with
             | Data (Atom s :: uids) when String.uppercase_ascii s = "SEARCH" ->
                 List.filter_map (fun v -> int_of_string_opt (text v)) uids
             | _ -> [])
           rs)

type summary = {
  uid : int;
  flags : string list;
  labels : string list;
  thread : string;
  msgid : string;
  headers : Mail.t;
}

(* each FETCH's items, its name and value pairs *)
let fetched (rs : response list) : (string * value) list list =
  List.filter_map
    (fun r ->
      match r with
      | Data [ _; Atom f; List items ] when String.uppercase_ascii f = "FETCH"
        ->
          Some (pairs items)
      | _ -> None)
    rs

(* the value of the item whose name starts so: BODY[...] *)
let item (prefix : string) (items : (string * value) list) : value =
  match List.find_opt (fun (k, _) -> String.starts_with ~prefix k) items with
  | Some (_, v) -> v
  | None -> Nil

let header_fields = "FROM TO CC SUBJECT DATE MESSAGE-ID IN-REPLY-TO REFERENCES"

let summaries (t : t) (uids : int list) : (summary list, string) result =
  if uids = [] then Ok []
  else
    match
      command t
        (Printf.sprintf
           "UID FETCH %s (UID FLAGS X-GM-LABELS X-GM-THRID X-GM-MSGID \
            BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (%s)])"
           (uid_set uids) header_fields)
    with
    | Error e -> Error e
    | Ok rs ->
        let summary items =
          match int_of_string_opt (text (item "UID" items)) with
          | None -> None
          | Some uid ->
              Some
                {
                  uid;
                  flags = texts (item "FLAGS" items);
                  labels = texts (item "X-GM-LABELS" items);
                  thread = text (item "X-GM-THRID" items);
                  msgid = text (item "X-GM-MSGID" items);
                  headers = Mail.parse (Mail.lf (text (item "BODY[" items)));
                }
        in
        let l = List.filter_map summary (fetched rs) in
        Ok
          (List.filter_map (fun u -> List.find_opt (fun s -> s.uid = u) l) uids)

let message (t : t) (uid : int) : (string, string) result =
  match command t (Printf.sprintf "UID FETCH %d (BODY[])" uid) with
  | Error e -> Error e
  | Ok rs -> (
      match
        List.find_map
          (fun items ->
            match item "BODY[" items with String s -> Some s | _ -> None)
          (fetched rs)
      with
      | Some s -> Ok (Mail.lf s)
      | None -> Error (Printf.sprintf "no message %d" uid))

let messages (t : t) (uids : int list) : ((int * string) list, string) result =
  if uids = [] then Ok []
  else
    match
      command t
        (Printf.sprintf "UID FETCH %s (UID BODY.PEEK[])" (uid_set uids))
    with
    | Error e -> Error e
    | Ok rs ->
        Ok
          (List.filter_map
             (fun items ->
               match
                 (int_of_string_opt (text (item "UID" items)), item "BODY[" items)
               with
               | Some uid, String s -> Some (uid, Mail.lf s)
               | _ -> None)
             (fetched rs))

let store (t : t) (uids : int list) (change : string) : (unit, string) result =
  match command t (Printf.sprintf "UID STORE %s %s" (uid_set uids) change) with
  | Ok _ -> Ok ()
  | Error e -> Error e

let logout (t : t) : unit =
  (match command t "LOGOUT" with Ok _ | Error _ -> ());
  Lines.close t.lines
lib_networking/mail/Imap.mli

(* Imap: reading mail kept on the server, the Internet Message Access
   Protocol (Mark Crispin, 1986; IMAP4rev1, RFC 3501, 2003), Gmail's
   way in for a program.

   POP (1984) carried a mailbox home and emptied the server; IMAP
   leaves it there and looks at it from anywhere, which is why the
   phone and this program agree on what is read. It is harder to read
   than SMTP, and the difficulty is the lesson:

   - Commands are *tagged*, so that several can be in flight, and the
     server's answer to one ends with a line of the same tag:

       C: a3 UID SEARCH X-GM-RAW "from:alice"
       S: * SEARCH 4 9 12                    <- untagged: data
       S: a3 OK SEARCH completed             <- tagged: a3 is done

     Untagged lines also come unasked: "* 13 EXISTS", a message arrived
     while another command ran. A client takes them whenever they come.

   - *Literals*: "{1234}" at a line's end, then that many bytes, so
     that a message, any bytes, travels inside a line-based protocol:

       S: * 2 FETCH (UID 9 BODY[] {44}       <- the line, its count
       S: Subject: lunch                        44 bytes, CR LF and all,
       S:                                        that are not lines of
       S: Noon at the usual place?               the protocol
       S: )                                  <- the line goes on

   - The data is a syntax of its own, read by [read] here: atoms
     (FLAGS, \Seen, BODY[HEADER]), quoted strings, NIL, and lists in
     parentheses, nested. "* 2 FETCH (UID 9 FLAGS (\Seen))" is
     [Atom "2"; Atom "FETCH"; List [Atom "UID"; Atom "9"; Atom "FLAGS";
     List [Atom "\Seen"]]]. (Numbers are atoms: Gmail's thread ids are
     64 bits, more than an int on a 32-bit arm.)

   - *UIDs*: a message's number in its mailbox that does not change,
     while its sequence number (2 above) shifts when one before it goes;
     a client asks by UID (UID SEARCH, UID FETCH). UIDVALIDITY, given
     at SELECT, says when the UIDs were renumbered and a cache must go.

   Gmail's extensions (X-GM-EXT-1): X-GM-LABELS, a message's labels
   (Gmail has labels, not folders; "INBOX" is the label \Inbox, and
   archiving is taking it off); X-GM-THRID, its conversation; X-GM-RAW,
   a search in Gmail's own syntax, done by Gmail.

   The headers are asked as BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (...)], read by
   Mail.parse, rather than as IMAP's ENVELOPE, a structure of its own
   with no References: (which conversations need where there is no
   Gmail). PEEK: looking is not reading; BODY[], the whole message,
   marks it read (\Seen).

   Worked examples (checked by the tests): the FETCH above read, its
   literal the message; the client against mini-maild's machine
   (Imap_server): a login, INBOX selected, its messages searched,
   their headers, a body, a label taken off.

   Reference: RFC 3501, "INTERNET MESSAGE ACCESS PROTOCOL - VERSION
   4rev1" (Mark Crispin, 2003): 6 the commands, 7 the responses, 9 the
   formal syntax; Google's "Gmail IMAP Extensions"
   (developers.google.com/gmail/imap/imap-extensions). *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 The responses} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type value = Atom of string | String of string | List of value list | Nil

type response =
  (* a tagged status ("a3 OK ...", Some "a3"), or an untagged one
   * ("* OK [UIDVALIDITY 3] ...", None): its word (OK, NO, BAD, BYE,
   * PREAUTH) and the text after it, as it is *)
  | Status of string option * string * string
  (* any other untagged response: "* SEARCH 4 9" *)
  | Data of value list
  (* "+ ...": go on (IDLE, a literal the client sends) *)
  | Continue of string

(* [read ~line ~bytes]: the next response, its literals read with
 * [bytes] (Lines.line and Lines.bytes); None when the connection
 * ended *)
val read : line:(unit -> string option) -> bytes:(int -> string option) ->
  response option

(* the values of a text with no literal: a command's arguments *)
val values : string -> value list

(* a string as IMAP writes it: quoted, its backslashes and double
 * quotes escaped *)
val quote : string -> string

(* [pairs l]: "(UID 9 FLAGS (\Seen))"'s list as [("UID", Atom "9");
 * ("FLAGS", List ...)], the names in upper case *)
val pairs : value list -> (string * value) list

(* an atom's or a string's text; "" else *)
val text : value -> string

(* flags or labels as a list: "(\\Inbox \"my label\")", one with a space
 * quoted *)
val list : string list -> string

(* a list's texts; [] for what is not a list *)
val texts : value -> string list

(* "1,3:5": a set of UIDs as IMAP writes it *)
val uid_set : int list -> string

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 The client} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type t

val connect : Lines.t -> (t, string) result

(* [command t "UID SEARCH ALL"]: sent with the next tag, the responses
 * read until its own; the untagged ones, or the tagged NO or BAD's
 * text *)
val command : t -> string -> (response list, string) result

val login : t -> user:string -> password:string -> (unit, string) result

(* the mailbox's UIDVALIDITY *)
val select : t -> string -> (string, string) result

(* LIST "" "*": each mailbox's attributes and name. Gmail's own are
 * known by an attribute (RFC 6154), not by their names, which are in
 * the account's language: \All is [Gmail]/All Mail in English, and
 * [Gmail]/Tous les messages in French; \Sent, \Drafts, \Trash *)
val mailboxes : t -> ((string list * string) list, string) result

(* the UIDs a search gives, in order: "ALL", "UNSEEN",
 * "X-GM-RAW \"from:alice\"" *)
val search : t -> string -> (int list, string) result

(* what a list of messages shows *)
type summary = {
  uid : int;
  flags : string list; (* \Seen, \Answered, ... *)
  labels : string list; (* Gmail's: \Inbox, \Important, travel ... *)
  thread : string; (* Gmail's conversation, "" when none *)
  msgid : string; (* Gmail's id of the message, the same in every
                     mailbox, where a UID is the mailbox's; "" when none *)
  headers : Mail.t; (* From, To, Cc, Subject, Date and the ids, no body *)
}

val summaries : t -> int list -> (summary list, string) result

(* the whole message, LF; marked read *)
val message : t -> int -> (string, string) result

(* [store t uids change]: "+FLAGS (\\Seen)", "-X-GM-LABELS (\\Inbox)" *)
(* [messages t uids]: their whole texts, LF, in one request, not marked
 * read (BODY.PEEK[]): a mailbox fetched ahead, to be read offline *)
val messages : t -> int list -> ((int * string) list, string) result

val store : t -> int list -> string -> (unit, string) result

val logout : t -> unit

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Imap_server.mli *)

type message = {
  uid : int;
  text : string;
  flags : string list;
  labels : string list;
}

type store = {
  all_mail : string;
  messages : string -> message list;
  change : string -> int -> flags:string list -> labels:string list -> unit;
}

type t = { user : string option; mailbox : string option; logout : bool }

let start () : t * string list =
  ( { user = None; mailbox = None; logout = false },
    [ "* OK [CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 X-GM-EXT-1] mini-maild ready" ] )

let ended (t : t) : bool = t.logout
(* the messages of the mailbox selected *)
(* Gmail's Starred: the messages flagged, whatever their labels *)
let starred = "[Gmail]/Starred"

let mailbox (store : store) (user : string) (name : string) : message list =
  let l = store.messages user in
  if name = store.all_mail then l
  else if name = starred then List.filter (fun m -> List.mem "\\Flagged" m.flags) l
  else List.filter (fun m -> List.mem "\\Inbox" m.labels) l

(* "1:3,5,7:*": the UIDs in it, [top] the largest there is *)
let in_set (set : string) (top : int) (uid : int) : bool =
  let n s = if s = "*" then Some top else int_of_string_opt s in
  List.exists
    (fun part ->
      match String.split_on_char ':' part with
      | [ a ] -> n a = Some uid
      | [ a; b ] -> (
          match (n a, n b) with
          | Some a, Some b -> uid >= min a b && uid <= max a b
          | _ -> false)
      | _ -> false)
    (String.split_on_char ',' set)

(* the wire's text: CR LF *)
let crlf (s : string) : string =
  String.concat "\r\n" (String.split_on_char '\n' s)

let literal (s : string) : string =
  Printf.sprintf "{%d}\r\n%s" (String.length s) s

let list = Imap.list

(* each message's conversation: the UID of the first of its thread *)
let threads (all : message list) : (int * int) list =
  List.concat_map
    (fun tree ->
      let ms = List.map fst (Mail_thread.flatten [ tree ]) in
      let first =
        List.fold_left (fun a (m : message) -> min a m.uid) max_int ms
      in
      List.map (fun (m : message) -> (m.uid, first)) ms)
    (Mail_thread.of_mail (fun (m : message) -> Mail.parse m.text) all)

let contains (s : string) (word : string) : bool =
  let s = String.lowercase_ascii s and w = String.lowercase_ascii word in
  let n = String.length s and k = String.length w in
  let rec at i = i + k <= n && (String.sub s i k = w || at (i + 1)) in
  at 0

(* X-GM-RAW's words, each found: in From:, in Subject:, or anywhere *)
let raw_match (m : message) (query : string) : bool =
  let mail = Mail.parse m.text in
  let field name = match Mail.get mail name with Some v -> v | None -> "" in
  List.for_all
    (fun w ->
      match String.index_opt w ':' with
      | Some i when List.mem (String.sub w 0 i) [ "from"; "subject" ] ->
          contains
            (field (String.sub w 0 i))
            (String.sub w (i + 1) (String.length w - i - 1))
      | _ -> contains m.text w)
    (List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' query))

let rec matches (m : message) (criteria : Imap.value list) : bool =
  match criteria with
  | [] -> true
  | Imap.Atom a :: rest when String.uppercase_ascii a = "ALL" -> matches m rest
  | Imap.Atom a :: rest when String.uppercase_ascii a = "SEEN" ->
      List.mem "\\Seen" m.flags && matches m rest
  | Imap.Atom a :: rest when String.uppercase_ascii a = "UNSEEN" ->
      (not (List.mem "\\Seen" m.flags)) && matches m rest
  | Imap.Atom a :: q :: rest when String.uppercase_ascii a = "X-GM-RAW" ->
      raw_match m (Imap.text q) && matches m rest
  (* (a message's X-GM-MSGID is its UID here) *)
  | Imap.Atom a :: id :: rest when String.uppercase_ascii a = "X-GM-MSGID" ->
      Imap.text id = string_of_int m.uid && matches m rest
  | _ -> false

(* "BODY[HEADER.FIELDS (FROM SUBJECT)]"'s names, in lower case *)
let field_names (item : string) : string list =
  match (String.index_opt item '(', String.index_opt item ')') with
  | Some i, Some j when j > i ->
      List.map String.lowercase_ascii
        (List.filter
           (fun s -> s <> "")
           (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.sub item (i + 1) (j - i - 1))))
  | _ -> []

(* an item of a FETCH answered, and whether it marks the message read;
 * None for an item not known *)
let fetch_item (m : message) (thread : int) (item : string) :
    (string * bool) option =
  let mail = Mail.parse m.text in
  let headers (fields : Mail.field list) =
    crlf (Mail.to_string { Mail.fields; body = "" })
  in
  match String.uppercase_ascii item with
  | "UID" -> Some ("UID " ^ string_of_int m.uid, false)
  | "FLAGS" -> Some ("FLAGS " ^ list m.flags, false)
  | "X-GM-LABELS" -> Some ("X-GM-LABELS " ^ list m.labels, false)
  | "X-GM-THRID" -> Some ("X-GM-THRID " ^ string_of_int thread, false)
  | "X-GM-MSGID" -> Some ("X-GM-MSGID " ^ string_of_int m.uid, false)
  | "RFC822.SIZE" ->
      Some ("RFC822.SIZE " ^ string_of_int (String.length (crlf m.text)), false)
  | "BODY[]" -> Some ("BODY[] " ^ literal (crlf m.text), true)
  | "BODY.PEEK[]" -> Some ("BODY[] " ^ literal (crlf m.text), false)
  | "BODY[HEADER]" | "BODY.PEEK[HEADER]" ->
      Some ("BODY[HEADER] " ^ literal (headers mail.fields), false)
  | i
    when String.starts_with ~prefix:"BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS " i
         || String.starts_with ~prefix:"BODY[HEADER.FIELDS " i ->
      let names = field_names item in
      let fields =
        List.filter
          (fun (f : Mail.field) ->
            List.mem (String.lowercase_ascii f.name) names)
          mail.fields
      in
      let key =
        "BODY["
        ^ String.sub item
            (String.index item '[' + 1)
            (String.length item - String.index item '[' - 1)
      in
      Some
        ( key ^ " " ^ literal (headers fields),
          String.starts_with ~prefix:"BODY[" i )
  | _ -> None

let seen (flags : string list) : string list =
  if List.mem "\\Seen" flags then flags else flags @ [ "\\Seen" ]

(* a STORE's change of a list: set, added to, taken from *)
let changed (op : string) (old : string list) (given : string list) :
    string list =
  match op.[0] with
  | '+' -> old @ List.filter (fun x -> not (List.mem x old)) given
  | '-' -> List.filter (fun x -> not (List.mem x given)) old
  | _ -> given

(* UID FETCH set items: each message of the set, its items *)
let fetch (store : store) (user : string) (name : string) (tag : string)
    (args : Imap.value list) : string list =
  match args with
  | set :: items :: _ ->
      let items =
        match items with
        | Imap.List l -> List.map Imap.text l
        | v -> [ Imap.text v ]
      in
      (* the UID always, first *)
      let items =
        "UID" :: List.filter (fun i -> String.uppercase_ascii i <> "UID") items
      in
      let ms = mailbox store user name in
      let top = List.fold_left (fun a (m : message) -> max a m.uid) 0 ms in
      let thread = threads (store.messages user) in
      let answer (seq : int) (m : message) : string option option =
        if not (in_set (Imap.text set) top m.uid) then Some None
        else
          let t =
            match List.assoc_opt m.uid thread with Some t -> t | None -> m.uid
          in
          (* (Gmail's: the selected mailbox's own label left out of
           * X-GM-LABELS, \Inbox in INBOX; so a client must not count
           * on it, as mini-pim once did) *)
          let shown =
            if name = "INBOX" then
              { m with labels = List.filter (fun l -> l <> "\\Inbox") m.labels }
            else m
          in
          let parts = List.map (fetch_item shown t) items in
          if List.mem None parts then None
          else
            let parts = List.filter_map (fun p -> p) parts in
            if List.exists snd parts && not (List.mem "\\Seen" m.flags) then
              store.change user m.uid ~flags:(seen m.flags) ~labels:m.labels;
            Some
              (Some
                 (Printf.sprintf "* %d FETCH (%s)" seq
                    (String.concat " " (List.map fst parts))))
      in
      let answers = List.mapi (fun i m -> answer (i + 1) m) ms in
      if List.mem None answers then [ tag ^ " BAD an item not known" ]
      else
        List.filter_map
          (fun a -> match a with Some a -> a | None -> None)
          answers
        @ [ tag ^ " OK FETCH completed" ]
  | _ -> [ tag ^ " BAD UID FETCH set items" ]

(* UID STORE set item (values): FLAGS or X-GM-LABELS, set (no sign),
 * added (+) or taken off (-), the new ones answered unless .SILENT *)
let change (store : store) (user : string) (name : string) (tag : string)
    (args : Imap.value list) : string list =
  match args with
  | [ set; what; Imap.List given ] ->
      let what = String.uppercase_ascii (Imap.text what) in
      let silent = String.ends_with ~suffix:".SILENT" what in
      let given = List.map Imap.text given in
      let ms = mailbox store user name in
      let top = List.fold_left (fun a (m : message) -> max a m.uid) 0 ms in
      let signed = what <> "" && (what.[0] = '+' || what.[0] = '-') in
      let field =
        if signed then String.sub what 1 (String.length what - 1) else what
      in
      let labels = String.starts_with ~prefix:"X-GM-LABELS" field in
      if not (labels || String.starts_with ~prefix:"FLAGS" field) then
        [ tag ^ " BAD STORE FLAGS or X-GM-LABELS" ]
      else
        let one (i : int) (m : message) : string list =
          if not (in_set (Imap.text set) top m.uid) then []
          else
            let flags =
              if labels then m.flags else changed what m.flags given
            in
            let lbls =
              if labels then changed what m.labels given else m.labels
            in
            store.change user m.uid ~flags ~labels:lbls;
            if silent then []
            else
              [
                Printf.sprintf "* %d FETCH (UID %d %s %s)" (i + 1) m.uid
                  (if labels then "X-GM-LABELS" else "FLAGS")
                  (list (if labels then lbls else flags));
              ]
        in
        List.concat (List.mapi one ms) @ [ tag ^ " OK STORE completed" ]
  | _ -> [ tag ^ " BAD UID STORE set item (values)" ]

let step (store : store) (t : t) (line : string) : t * string list =
  let vs = Imap.values line in
  match vs with
  | [] -> (t, [ "* BAD empty command" ])
  | tag :: rest -> (
      let tag = Imap.text tag in
      let ok text = tag ^ " OK " ^ text and no text = tag ^ " NO " ^ text in
      let verb, args =
        match rest with
        | v :: args -> (String.uppercase_ascii (Imap.text v), args)
        | [] -> ("", [])
      in
      let verb, args =
        match (verb, args) with
        | "UID", v :: args ->
            ("UID " ^ String.uppercase_ascii (Imap.text v), args)
        | _ -> (verb, args)
      in
      match (verb, t.user, t.mailbox) with
      | "CAPABILITY", _, _ ->
          (t, [ "* CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 X-GM-EXT-1"; ok "CAPABILITY completed" ])
      | "NOOP", _, _ -> (t, [ ok "NOOP completed" ])
      | "LOGOUT", _, _ ->
          ( { t with logout = true },
            [ "* BYE mini-maild"; ok "LOGOUT completed" ] )
      | "LOGIN", _, _ -> (
          match args with
          | [ user; _ ] ->
              (* "bob@ix" is bob *)
              let u = String.lowercase_ascii (Imap.text user) in
              let u =
                match String.index_opt u '@' with
                | Some i -> String.sub u 0 i
                | None -> u
              in
              ({ t with user = Some u }, [ ok "LOGIN completed" ])
          | _ -> (t, [ tag ^ " BAD LOGIN user password" ]))
      | _, None, _ -> (t, [ no "LOGIN first" ])
      | "LIST", Some _, _ ->
          ( t,
            [
              "* LIST (\\HasNoChildren) \"/\" \"INBOX\"";
              "* LIST (\\All \\HasNoChildren) \"/\" " ^ Imap.quote store.all_mail;
              "* LIST (\\Flagged \\HasNoChildren) \"/\" " ^ Imap.quote starred;
              ok "LIST completed";
            ] )
      | ("SELECT" | "EXAMINE"), Some user, _ -> (
          match args with
          | [ name ] ->
              let name = Imap.text name in
              let name =
                if String.uppercase_ascii name = "INBOX" then "INBOX" else name
              in
              if name <> "INBOX" && name <> store.all_mail && name <> starred then
                (t, [ no ("no mailbox " ^ name) ])
              else
                let ms = mailbox store user name in
                let next =
                  List.fold_left (fun a (m : message) -> max a (m.uid + 1)) 1 ms
                in
                ( { t with mailbox = Some name },
                  [
                    "* FLAGS (\\Seen \\Answered \\Flagged \\Deleted \\Draft)";
                    Printf.sprintf "* %d EXISTS" (List.length ms);
                    "* OK [UIDVALIDITY 1] UIDs valid";
                    Printf.sprintf "* OK [UIDNEXT %d] the next UID" next;
                    ok ("[READ-WRITE] " ^ verb ^ " completed");
                  ] )
          | _ -> (t, [ tag ^ " BAD " ^ verb ^ " mailbox" ]))
      | _, _, None -> (t, [ no "SELECT first" ])
      | "UID SEARCH", Some user, Some name ->
          let uids =
            List.filter_map
              (fun (m : message) ->
                if matches m args then Some (string_of_int m.uid) else None)
              (mailbox store user name)
          in
          (t, [ String.concat " " ("* SEARCH" :: uids); ok "SEARCH completed" ])
      | "UID FETCH", Some user, Some name -> (t, fetch store user name tag args)
      | "UID STORE", Some user, Some name -> (t, change store user name tag args)
      | _ -> (t, [ tag ^ " BAD command not known: " ^ verb ]))

(* Imap_server: the server's side of IMAP, mini-maild's, as a machine:
   a line of the client's in, the response's lines out (a literal, a
   message's bytes, inside its line: "BODY[] {44}\r\n" and the bytes),
   the messages and their flags in a store the program gives it.

   The subset mini-pim speaks to Gmail, Gmail's extensions included, so
   that the tests talk to this and never to Gmail: CAPABILITY, LOGIN
   (any password), LIST, SELECT and EXAMINE, UID SEARCH (ALL, SEEN,

   (FLAGS and X-GM-LABELS, set, added, taken off, .SILENT), NOOP,

(* See Lines.mli *)

(* what the two kinds of connection have to do: send bytes, take what
 * has come (None: closed), wait for more, close; and why it ended, if
 * not by a close *)
type way = {
  send : string -> unit;
  arrived : unit -> string option;
  wait : float -> unit;
  stop : unit -> unit;
  why : unit -> string option;
}

(* [pending]: the bytes come and not yet a whole line *)
type t = { way : way; mutable pending : string; mutable ended : bool }

let make (way : way) : t = { way; pending = ""; ended = false }

let of_fd (fd : Unix.file_descr) : t =
  make
    {
      send = Tcp.send_all fd;
      arrived = (fun () -> Tcp.arrived fd);
      wait = Tcp.wait fd;
      stop = (fun () -> try Unix.close fd with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
      why = (fun () -> None);
    }

let plain (caps : < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; .. >) ~(host : string)
    ~(port : int) : (t, string) result =
  match Tcp.connect caps ~host ~port with
  | fd -> Ok (of_fd fd)
  | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> Error (Unix.error_message e)
  | exception Failure why -> Error why

let tls (caps : < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; .. >) ~(trust : X509.roots)
    ~(host : string) ~(port : int) : (t, string) result =
  match Tls_client.connect caps ~trust ~host ~port with
  | Error why -> Error why
  | Ok c ->
      (* (the TLS machine's own failure, a certificate refused, is an
       * end of the connection, its reason kept) *)
      let why () =
        match Tls_client.state c with Tls13.Failed w -> Some w | _ -> None
      in
      let arrived () =
        let data = Tls_client.receive c in
        if why () <> None || (data = "" && Tls_client.ended c) then None
        else Some data
      in
      Ok
        (make
           {
             send = Tls_client.send c;
             arrived;
             wait = Tls_client.wait c;
             stop = (fun () -> Tls_client.close c);
             why;
           })

let send_line (t : t) (line : string) : unit = t.way.send (line ^ "\r\n")

(* a whole line in [pending], taken *)
let take (t : t) : string option =
  match String.index_opt t.pending '\n' with
  | None -> None
  | Some i ->
      let line = String.sub t.pending 0 i in
      t.pending <-
        String.sub t.pending (i + 1) (String.length t.pending - i - 1);
      let n = String.length line in
      Some (if n > 0 && line.[n - 1] = '\r' then String.sub line 0 (n - 1)
            else line)


(* more of what comes, waited for until [deadline]; false when there is
 * no more *)
(* (the clock bare: a deadline bounds a wait on a connection held, as
 * select's timeout, the descriptor's, capabilities.dl; the author's choice,
 * 2026-11-04) *)
let more (t : t) (deadline : float) : bool =
  let rec go () =
    if t.ended then false
    else
      match t.way.arrived () with
      | None -> t.ended <- true; false
      | Some "" ->
          let left = deadline -. Unix.gettimeofday () in
          if left <= 0. then false else begin t.way.wait left; go () end
      | Some data -> t.pending <- t.pending ^ data; true
  in
  go ()

let bytes (t : t) (n : int) : string option =
  let deadline = Unix.gettimeofday () +. !Tcp.timeout in
  let rec go () =
    if String.length t.pending >= n then begin
      let b = String.sub t.pending 0 n in
      t.pending <- String.sub t.pending n (String.length t.pending - n);
      Some b
    end
    else if more t deadline then go ()
    else None
  in
  go ()

let line (t : t) : string option =
  let deadline = Unix.gettimeofday () +. !Tcp.timeout in
  let rec go () =
    match take t with
    | Some l -> Some l
    | None -> if more t deadline then go () else None
  in
  go ()

let talk (t : t) (step : 'm -> string -> 'm * string list) (machine : 'm)
    (finished : 'm -> bool) : 'm =
  let rec go (m : 'm) : 'm =
    if finished m then m
    else
      match line t with
      | None -> m
      | Some l ->
          let m, answer = step m l in
          List.iter (send_line t) answer;
          go m
  in
  go machine

let why (t : t) : string option = t.way.why ()

let close (t : t) : unit = t.way.stop ()

(* Lines: a connection that carries lines, over TCP or over TLS, for the
   mail's protocols (SMTP here, IMAP next).

   SMTP and IMAP are dialogues of lines ending in CR LF, and their
   machines are pure (Smtp.step: a line of the server's in, the lines
   to send back out). What is left is the socket: the bytes that come
   cut into lines, whatever pieces they came in, and the lines sent
   with their CR LF; and for IMAP's literals, a count of bytes read as
   they are. Over TLS (Tls_client) for Gmail, whose ports
   speak TLS from the first byte (465 for SMTP, 993 for IMAP: "implicit
   TLS", RFC 8314); over plain TCP for mini-maild, on this machine.

       Smtp.step   "250 OK"  ->  ["MAIL FROM:<a@ix>"]
            ^ line                  | send_line
            |                       v
       [line]: the bytes cut     "MAIL FROM:<a@ix>\r\n"
       at "\n", "\r" taken off      |
            ^                       v
       Tls_client.receive or     Tls_client.send or
       Tcp.arrived                Tcp.send_all

   (ix: the playground's Transport.t was this, a record of lines over
   TCP, TLS or a WebSocket; lib_networking's README says it was left out
   when TLS was copied. Here only the two a mail program needs.)

   A line is waited for Tcp.timeout seconds at most; a server that says
   nothing for that long, or closes, ends the dialogue.

   Worked example (checked by the tests, against mini-maild's machine
   on the other side of a pair of sockets): [talk] with Smtp's client
   sends a message, and its outcome is Sent to one. *)

type t

(* [plain caps ~host ~port]: TCP, nothing over it *)
val plain :
  < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; .. > -> host:string -> port:int ->
  (t, string) result

(* [tls caps ~trust ~host ~port]: TLS from the first byte *)
val tls :
  < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.clock; .. > -> trust:X509.roots -> host:string ->
  port:int -> (t, string) result

(* a connection already made (a test's end of a socketpair) *)
val of_fd : Unix.file_descr -> t

(* a line sent, its CR LF added *)
val send_line : t -> string -> unit

(* the next line, its CR LF taken off; None when the other side has
 * closed or said nothing for Tcp.timeout seconds *)
val line : t -> string option

(* [bytes t n]: the next [n] bytes, as they are (an IMAP literal: a
 * message inside a line, "{1234}" then that many bytes) *)
val bytes : t -> int -> string option

(* [talk conn step machine finished]: each line that comes given to
 * [step], what it answers sent, until [finished machine] or the
 * connection ends; the machine as it was then *)
val talk : t -> ('m -> string -> 'm * string list) -> 'm -> ('m -> bool) -> 'm

(* why the connection ended, when it was not closed: the TLS
 * handshake failed, the certificate refused *)
val why : t -> string option

val close : t -> unit

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A message *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type field = { name : string; raw : string }
type t = { fields : field list; body : string }

(* CR LF to LF; a lone CR is kept *)
let lf (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  String.iteri (fun i c -> if not (c = '\r' && i + 1 < String.length s && s.[i + 1] = '\n') then Buffer.add_char b c) s;
  Buffer.contents b

let is_space c = c = ' ' || c = '\t'

let parse (text : string) : t =
  let text = lf text in
  (* the headers, line by line, from [pos]; the body is what is left *)
  let rec fields acc pos =
    if pos >= String.length text then (List.rev acc, "")
    else
      let eol = match String.index_from_opt text pos '\n' with Some i -> i | None -> String.length text in
      let line = String.sub text pos (eol - pos) in
      let next = min (String.length text) (eol + 1) in
      if line = "" then (List.rev acc, String.sub text next (String.length text - next))
      else if is_space line.[0] && acc <> [] then
        (* a continuation: the field before goes on *)
        let f = List.hd acc in
        fields ({ f with raw = f.raw ^ "\n" ^ line } :: List.tl acc) next
      else
        match String.index_opt line ':' with
        | Some i when i > 0 && not (String.contains (String.sub line 0 i) ' ') ->
            fields ({ name = String.sub line 0 i; raw = String.sub line (i + 1) (String.length line - i - 1) } :: acc) next
        | _ -> (List.rev acc, String.sub text pos (String.length text - pos))
  in
  let fields, body = fields [] 0 in
  { fields; body }

let to_string (m : t) : string =
  String.concat "" (List.map (fun f -> f.name ^ ":" ^ f.raw ^ "\n") m.fields) ^ "\n" ^ m.body

let unfold (s : string) : string = String.concat "" (String.split_on_char '\n' s)
let same a b = String.lowercase_ascii a = String.lowercase_ascii b
let get_all (m : t) (name : string) : string list = List.filter_map (fun f -> if same f.name name then Some (String.trim (unfold f.raw)) else None) m.fields
let get (m : t) (name : string) : string option = match get_all m name with v :: _ -> Some v | [] -> None

let set (name : string) (value : string) (m : t) : t =
  let f = { name; raw = " " ^ value } in
  if List.exists (fun g -> same g.name name) m.fields then
    let rec go = function [] -> [] | g :: rest when same g.name name -> f :: List.filter (fun g -> not (same g.name name)) rest | g :: rest -> g :: go rest in
    { m with fields = go m.fields }
  else { m with fields = m.fields @ [ f ] }

let remove (name : string) (m : t) : t = { m with fields = List.filter (fun f -> not (same f.name name)) m.fields }
let make (fields : (string * string) list) (body : string) : t = { fields = List.map (fun (name, v) -> { name; raw = " " ^ v }) fields; body }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Addresses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type address = { display : string; mailbox : string }

let unquote (s : string) : string =
  let s = String.trim s in
  let n = String.length s in
  if n >= 2 && s.[0] = '"' && s.[n - 1] = '"' then String.sub s 1 (n - 2) else s

let address (s : string) : address option =
  let s = String.trim s in
  let between o c = match (String.index_opt s o, String.rindex_opt s c) with Some i, Some j when j > i -> Some (i, j) | _ -> None in
  let a =
    match between '<' '>' with
    | Some (i, j) -> { display = unquote (String.sub s 0 i); mailbox = String.trim (String.sub s (i + 1) (j - i - 1)) }
    | None -> (
        (* the old form: the name as a comment after the address *)
        match between '(' ')' with
        | Some (i, j) -> { display = String.trim (String.sub s (i + 1) (j - i - 1)); mailbox = String.trim (String.sub s 0 i) }
        | None -> { display = ""; mailbox = s })
  in
  if a.mailbox = "" then None else Some a

(* the commas at depth 0: not in "...", <...> or (...) *)
let addresses (s : string) : address list =
  let parts = ref [] and start = ref 0 and quoted = ref false and depth = ref 0 in
  String.iteri
    (fun i c ->
      match c with
      | '"' -> quoted := not !quoted
      | ('<' | '(') when not !quoted -> incr depth
      | ('>' | ')') when not !quoted -> decr depth
      | ',' when (not !quoted) && !depth = 0 ->
          parts := String.sub s !start (i - !start) :: !parts;
          start := i + 1
      | _ -> ())
    s;
  let parts = List.rev (String.sub s !start (String.length s - !start) :: !parts) in
  List.filter_map address parts

let address_to_string (a : address) : string =
  if a.display = "" then a.mailbox
  else
    (* RFC 5322's specials, which a bare display name cannot hold *)
    let special = String.exists (fun c -> String.contains "()<>[]:;@\\,.\"" c) a.display in
    (if special then "\"" ^ a.display ^ "\"" else a.display) ^ " <" ^ a.mailbox ^ ">"

let who (a : address) : string = if a.display <> "" then a.display else a.mailbox

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Dates *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type date = { day : Civil.date; time : Clock.time_of_day; offset : int }

let months = [ "jan"; "feb"; "mar"; "apr"; "may"; "jun"; "jul"; "aug"; "sep"; "oct"; "nov"; "dec" ]

(* the zones RFC 822 named, before numeric offsets won *)
let zones = [ ("gmt", 0); ("ut", 0); ("utc", 0); ("z", 0); ("est", -300); ("edt", -240); ("cst", -360); ("cdt", -300); ("mst", -420); ("mdt", -360); ("pst", -480); ("pdt", -420) ]

let index_of x l =
  let rec go i = function [] -> None | y :: _ when y = x -> Some i | _ :: r -> go (i + 1) r in
  go 0 l

let date (s : string) : date option =
  (* a comment "(CEST)" dropped; commas are spaces *)
  let s = match String.index_opt s '(' with Some i -> String.sub s 0 i | None -> s in
  let words = String.map (fun c -> if c = ',' then ' ' else c) s |> String.split_on_char ' ' |> List.filter (( <> ) "") in
  let words = match words with w :: rest when int_of_string_opt w = None -> rest | l -> l in
  match words with
  | d :: mon :: y :: hms :: zone -> (
      let mon = String.lowercase_ascii (if String.length mon >= 3 then String.sub mon 0 3 else mon) in
      let offset =
        match zone with
        | z :: _ when String.length z = 5 && (z.[0] = '+' || z.[0] = '-') -> (
            match int_of_string_opt (String.sub z 1 4) with
            | Some hhmm -> Some ((if z.[0] = '-' then -1 else 1) * (((hhmm / 100) * 60) + (hhmm mod 100)))
            | None -> None)
        | z :: _ -> List.assoc_opt (String.lowercase_ascii z) zones
        | [] -> Some 0
      in
      let hms = List.map int_of_string_opt (String.split_on_char ':' hms) in
      match (int_of_string_opt d, index_of mon months, int_of_string_opt y, hms, offset) with
      | Some day, Some m, Some y, (Some h :: Some mi :: sec), Some offset ->
          let year = if y < 50 then 2000 + y else if y < 100 then 1900 + y else y in
          let second = match sec with [ Some s ] -> float_of_int s | _ -> 0. in
          let day = { Civil.year; month = m + 1; day } in
          if Civil.is_valid day && h < 24 && mi < 60 then Some { day; time = { Clock.hour = h; minute = mi; second }; offset } else None
      | _ -> None)
  | _ -> None

let date_to_string (d : date) : string =
  let wd = Civil.weekday (Civil.days_from_civil d.day) in
  let a = abs d.offset in
  Printf.sprintf "%s, %d %s %d %02d:%02d:%02d %c%02d%02d"
    (String.sub (Civil.weekday_name wd) 0 3)
    d.day.day
    (String.capitalize_ascii (List.nth months (d.day.month - 1)))
    d.day.year d.time.hour d.time.minute (int_of_float d.time.second)
    (if d.offset < 0 then '-' else '+')
    (a / 60) (a mod 60)

let seconds (d : date) : float = Clock.of_local ~offset:d.offset d.day d.time

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Message-IDs *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let message_ids (s : string) : string list =
  let rec go pos acc =
    match String.index_from_opt s pos '<' with
    | None -> List.rev acc
    | Some i -> (
        match String.index_from_opt s i '>' with Some j -> go (j + 1) (String.sub s (i + 1) (j - i - 1) :: acc) | None -> List.rev acc)
  in
  go 0 []
lib_networking/mail/Mail.mli
5744
(* Mail: a message, as RFC 822 wrote it (David Crocker, 1982) and RFC
   5322 still does: header fields, an empty line, a body.

       From: Alice <alice@tiny>                 <- a field: a name, a colon,
       To: bob@tiny                                a value
       Subject: lunch
       Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 12:00:00 +0200
       Message-ID: <1@tiny>
       Received: from eudora by tiny;           <- a long value folded: a line
         Fri, 25 Sep 2026 12:00:01 +0200           starting with a space goes
                                                   on with the one before
                                                <- the empty line: headers end
       Noon at the usual place?                 <- the body, lines of text

   That is all a message is, and it has not changed since 1982: what
   came later (MIME, Mime.mli) put everything else *inside* this
   shape rather than change it. A field can appear twice (every server
   the message passed through adds a Received: at the top), so the
   fields are a list, in order, not a table; and their names are looked
   up without regard to case ("message-id" finds Message-ID).

   A field keeps its value as written, folding and all ([raw]), so that
   a message read and written again is the same bytes -- a mailbox
   rewritten after marking one message read must not change the others.
   [get] unfolds it: the line breaks removed, the space that followed
   kept (RFC 5322, 2.2.3 -- unlike iCalendar's folding, RFC 5545's,
   where the space is removed too, which is why the two do not share
   code).

   Lines end in CR LF on the wire and in LF in a file; [parse] takes
   either and keeps LF, and the protocols (Smtp, Pop3) put the CRs back.
   (ix: Smtp and Imap; no Pop3, plan_mail.md.)

   Worked example (checked by the tests): the message above parses to
   six fields; [get m "subject"] is "lunch"; [get m "received"] is
   "from eudora by tiny; Fri, 25 Sep 2026 12:00:01 +0200"; the From:
   is the address { display = "Alice"; mailbox = "alice@tiny" }; the
   date is 2026-09-25 at 12:00:00, 120 minutes east of Greenwich, which
   is 10:00 in Greenwich; and [to_string] gives back the same bytes.

   References: RFC 822, "Standard for the format of ARPA Internet text
   messages" (1982); RFC 5322, "Internet Message Format" (2008), its
   section 3.4 the addresses and 3.3 the dates. *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 A message} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a header field: its name as written, and everything after the colon
 * as written, folding kept: [{ name = "To"; raw = " bob@tiny" }] *)
type field = { name : string; raw : string }

type t = { fields : field list; body : string }

(* the text of a message, CR LF or LF; the headers end at the first
 * empty line, or at a line that is neither a field nor a continuation
 * (which is then the body's first line) *)
val parse : string -> t

(* the message written back, lines ending in LF *)
val to_string : t -> string

(* [get m name]: the first field of that name, any case, its value
 * unfolded and trimmed *)
val get : t -> string -> string option

(* every field of that name, in order *)
val get_all : t -> string -> string list

(* [set name value m]: the first field of that name given [value]
 * (the others removed), or a new one added at the end *)
val set : string -> string -> t -> t

(* [remove name m]: every field of that name gone *)
val remove : string -> t -> t

(* [make fields body]: a message from names and values *)
val make : (string * string) list -> string -> t

(* a value's line breaks removed: "a\n  b" is "a  b" *)
val unfold : string -> string

(* the wire's CR LF line ends as a file's LF *)
val lf : string -> string

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Addresses} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* "Alice <alice@tiny>": the display name and the mailbox; "alice@tiny"
 * alone has an empty display name; the old form "alice@tiny (Alice)"
 * reads the same as the first *)
type address = { display : string; mailbox : string }

val address : string -> address option

(* a list of them, separated by commas -- not the commas inside quotes,
 * angle brackets or parentheses: "\"Smith, J\" <j@tiny>, bob@tiny" is
 * two *)
val addresses : string -> address list

(* the display name quoted when it has to be *)
val address_to_string : address -> string

(* the name to show: the display name, else the mailbox *)
val who : address -> string

(* "\"Smith, J\"" is "Smith, J" (trimmed), anything else as it is *)
val unquote : string -> string

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Dates} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* "Fri, 25 Sep 2026 12:00:00 +0200": the day and time where it was
 * written, and that place's offset, in minutes east of Greenwich *)
type date = { day : Civil.date; time : Clock.time_of_day; offset : int }

(* the weekday optional, the seconds optional, two-digit years (49 is
 * 2049, 50 is 1950), and the old zone names (GMT, EST, PDT...) *)
val date : string -> date option

val date_to_string : date -> string

(* seconds since the epoch, to sort by *)
val seconds : date -> float

(*****************************************************************************)
(* {1 Message-IDs} *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the ids in a Message-ID, In-Reply-To or References value:
 * "<1@tiny> <2@tiny>" is ["1@tiny"; "2@tiny"] *)
val message_ids : string -> string list

(* See Mail_thread.mli *)

type 'a tree = Node of 'a option * 'a tree list

(* a container: the essay's, mutable as its are -- the links are made
   and broken as the messages come *)
type 'a container = { mutable message : 'a option; mutable parent : 'a container option; mutable children : 'a container list }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Subjects *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* "Re:", "RE:", "Re[2]:", "Fwd:", "Fw:", "Aw:" (German), then spaces *)
let strip_prefix (s : string) : string option =
  let s = String.trim s in
  let lower = String.lowercase_ascii s in
  let prefixes = [ "re"; "fwd"; "fw"; "aw" ] in
  List.find_map
    (fun p ->
      let n = String.length p in
      if String.length lower > n && String.sub lower 0 n = p then
        let rest = String.sub s n (String.length s - n) in
        (* "Re[2]:" *)
        let rest = if rest <> "" && rest.[0] = '[' then match String.index_opt rest ']' with Some i -> String.sub rest (i + 1) (String.length rest - i - 1) | None -> rest else rest in
        if rest <> "" && rest.[0] = ':' then Some (String.sub rest 1 (String.length rest - 1)) else None
      else None)
    prefixes

let rec base_subject (s : string) : string = match strip_prefix s with Some rest -> base_subject rest | None -> String.lowercase_ascii (String.trim s)
let is_reply (s : string) : bool = strip_prefix s <> None

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The algorithm *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* is [a] [b] or one of its descendants? (a link from [b] down to [a]
   would make a loop) *)
let rec below (a : 'a container) (b : 'a container) : bool = a == b || List.exists (fun c -> below a c) b.children

let unlink (c : 'a container) : unit =
  match c.parent with
  | Some p ->
      p.children <- List.filter (fun x -> x != c) p.children;
      c.parent <- None
  | None -> ()

let link ~(parent : 'a container) (child : 'a container) : unit =
  if not (below parent child) then begin
    unlink child;
    child.parent <- Some parent;
    parent.children <- parent.children @ [ child ]
  end

let threads ~(id : 'a -> string option) ~(references : 'a -> string list) ~(subject : 'a -> string) ~(date : 'a -> float) (messages : 'a list) : 'a tree list =
  let table : (string, 'a container) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 64 in
  let all = ref [] in
  let fresh () =
    let c = { message = None; parent = None; children = [] } in
    all := c :: !all;
    c
  in
  let container_of (i : string) : 'a container =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt table i with
    | Some c -> c
    | None ->
        let c = fresh () in
        Hashtbl.replace table i c;
        c
  in
  (* 1. the containers, and the links *)
  List.iter
    (fun m ->
      let c =
        match id m with
        | Some i -> (
            match Hashtbl.find_opt table i with
            | Some c when c.message = None -> c
            | Some _ -> fresh () (* the same id twice: kept apart *)
            | None -> container_of i)
        | None -> fresh ()
      in
      c.message <- Some m;
      let refs = List.filter (fun r -> Some r <> id m) (references m) in
      let chain = List.map container_of refs in
      (* each reference the child of the one before, unless it has a
         parent already *)
      let rec pairs = function
        | a :: (b :: _ as rest) ->
            if b.parent = None && not (below a b) then link ~parent:a b;
            pairs rest
        | _ -> ()
      in
      pairs chain;
      (* the message under the last of them: its own word wins *)
      match List.rev chain with
      | last :: _ when not (below last c) -> link ~parent:last c
      | _ -> unlink c)
    messages;
  (* 2. the roots *)
  let roots = List.filter (fun c -> c.parent = None) (List.rev !all) in
  (* 3. the empty containers pruned *)
  let rec prune ~(top : bool) (cs : 'a container list) : 'a container list =
    List.concat_map
      (fun c ->
        c.children <- prune ~top:false c.children;
        List.iter (fun k -> k.parent <- Some c) c.children;
        match (c.message, c.children) with
        | None, [] -> []
        | None, [ only ] when top -> [ only ]
        | None, kids when not top -> kids
        | _ -> [ c ])
      cs
  in
  let roots = prune ~top:true roots in
  List.iter (fun c -> c.parent <- None) roots;
  (* 4. the roots grouped by subject *)
  let subject_of (c : 'a container) : string =
    match c.message with Some m -> subject m | None -> ( match c.children with k :: _ -> (match k.message with Some m -> subject m | None -> "") | [] -> "")
  in
  let by_subject : (string, 'a container) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 64 in
  List.iter
    (fun c ->
      let s = base_subject (subject_of c) in
      if s <> "" then
        match Hashtbl.find_opt by_subject s with
        | None -> Hashtbl.replace by_subject s c
        | Some old ->
            (* the better representative: an empty one, or one that is not a reply *)
            if (c.message = None && old.message <> None) || (is_reply (subject_of old) && not (is_reply (subject_of c))) then Hashtbl.replace by_subject s c)
    roots;
  let merged =
    List.filter
      (fun c ->
        let s = base_subject (subject_of c) in
        match Hashtbl.find_opt by_subject s with
        | Some rep when rep != c && s <> "" -> (
            match (rep.message, c.message) with
            | None, None ->
                rep.children <- rep.children @ c.children;
                false
            | None, Some _ -> link ~parent:rep c; false
            | Some _, Some m when is_reply (subject m) && not (is_reply (subject_of rep)) -> link ~parent:rep c; false
            | Some _, Some _ ->
                (* two of a kind: both under a new empty container, which
                   takes [rep]'s place among the roots -- made by moving
                   [rep]'s message and replies down into a new one *)
                let moved = { message = rep.message; parent = Some rep; children = rep.children } in
                List.iter (fun k -> k.parent <- Some moved) moved.children;
                rep.message <- None;
                rep.children <- [ moved ];
                link ~parent:rep c;
                false
            | Some _, None -> link ~parent:rep c; false)
        | _ -> true)
      roots
  in
  (* 5. brothers by date; an empty container dated by its first child *)
  let rec to_tree (c : 'a container) : 'a tree = Node (c.message, sort c.children)
  and when_ (c : 'a container) : float =
    match c.message with Some m -> date m | None -> List.fold_left (fun t k -> min t (when_ k)) infinity c.children
  and sort (cs : 'a container list) : 'a tree list = List.map to_tree (List.stable_sort (fun a b -> compare (when_ a) (when_ b)) cs) in
  sort merged

let rec flatten_at (depth : int) (ts : 'a tree list) : ('a * int) list =
  List.concat_map
    (fun (Node (m, kids)) -> (match m with Some m -> [ (m, depth) ] | None -> []) @ flatten_at (depth + 1) kids)
    ts

let flatten (ts : 'a tree list) : ('a * int) list = flatten_at 0 ts

let of_mail (mail : 'a -> Mail.t) (messages : 'a list) : 'a tree list =
  let get m name = match Mail.get (mail m) name with Some v -> v | None -> "" in
  let references m =
    let refs = Mail.message_ids (get m "references") in
    let irt = Mail.message_ids (get m "in-reply-to") in
    refs @ List.filter (fun i -> not (List.mem i refs)) irt
  in
  threads
    ~id:(fun m -> List.nth_opt (Mail.message_ids (get m "message-id")) 0)
    ~references
    ~subject:(fun m -> Mime.decode_words (get m "subject"))
    ~date:(fun m -> match Mail.date (get m "date") with Some d -> Mail.seconds d | None -> 0.)
    messages
lib_networking/mail/Mail_thread.mli
3327
(* Mail_thread: a mailbox's messages as conversations, by Jamie
   Zawinski's algorithm ("message threading", 1997, written for
   Netscape Mail 2.0 and published as an essay; RFC 5256 took it for
   IMAP's THREAD=REFERENCES).

   A reply says what it answers: In-Reply-To: the one message,
   References: the whole chain back to the first (Mail.mli). So
   threading is building a tree from those links -- but the links are
   in the messages you *have*, and they name messages you may not:

       <1> the plan                    <1> (never received)
         <2> Re: the plan    --->      +-- <2> Re: the plan
           <3> Re: the plan              +-- <3> Re: the plan
         <4> Re: the plan              +-- <4> Re: the plan

   The algorithm, in the essay's steps:

   1. A *container* per Message-ID, found or made, holding its message
      if we have it, empty if we only heard of it. Each message's
      References link the containers in a chain, parent to child (a
      container keeps its first parent; no link that would make a
      loop), and the message's own container becomes the child of the
      last one.
   2. The containers with no parent are the roots.
   3. Empty containers pruned: with no children, gone; with children,
      replaced by them -- except at the top with several children,
      where the empty one stays to hold them together (a thread whose
      first message you never got).
   4. The roots grouped by subject, for the mailers that sent no
      references at all: "Re: lunch" goes under "lunch" (the subject
      less its "Re:"s, [base_subject]).
   5. Brothers sorted by date.

   Worked examples (checked by the tests): the playground's thread of
   five (its TinyEudora's Our_mail) is one tree, <plan1> at the top,
   <plan2> under it, and under that <plan3> (with <plan5> under it)
   and <plan4>; two replies to a message never received hang from an
   empty container; "Re: lunch" with no references goes under "lunch";
   a message that names itself in its References makes no loop.

   References: Jamie Zawinski, "message threading",
   https://www.jwz.org/doc/threading.html (1997, 2002); RFC 5256,
   "Internet Message Access Protocol - SORT and THREAD Extensions"
   (2008), section 2.2 the same algorithm. *)

(* a thread: a message (None: one we never received, known only by
 * the replies naming it) and its replies *)
type 'a tree = Node of 'a option * 'a tree list

(* [threads ~id ~references ~subject ~date messages]: the conversations,
 * oldest first. [references]: the ids the message names, oldest
 * first -- References:, then In-Reply-To:'s if not already there *)
val threads :
  id:('a -> string option) -> references:('a -> string list) -> subject:('a -> string) -> date:('a -> float) -> 'a list -> 'a tree list

(* the subject less its "Re:", "RE:", "Re[2]:", "Fwd:"s, trimmed, in
 * lower case: what a reply and its original share *)
val base_subject : string -> string

(* does the subject say it is a reply ("Re: ...")? *)
val is_reply : string -> bool

(* the trees flattened, depth first: each message with its depth *)
val flatten : 'a tree list -> ('a * int) list

(* the same for mail: the ids from Message-ID:, References: and
 * In-Reply-To:, the subject decoded, the date *)
val of_mail : ('a -> Mail.t) -> 'a list -> 'a tree list

(* Claude Code

(* See Mailto.mli *)

type t = {
  to_ : string list;
  cc : string list;
  bcc : string list;
  subject : string;
  body : string;
}

let hex (c : char) : int option =
  match c with
  | '0' .. '9' -> Some (Char.code c - 48)
  | 'a' .. 'f' -> Some (Char.code c - 87)
  | 'A' .. 'F' -> Some (Char.code c - 55)
  | _ -> None

(* %XX made the byte, all else as it is ('+' a plus, not a space) *)
let unescape (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec go i =
    if i >= n then ()
    else if s.[i] = '%' && i + 2 < n then
      match (hex s.[i + 1], hex s.[i + 2]) with
      | Some h, Some l ->
          Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr ((h * 16) + l));
          go (i + 3)
      | _ ->
          Buffer.add_char b s.[i];
          go (i + 1)
    else begin
      Buffer.add_char b s.[i];
      go (i + 1)
    end
  in
  go 0;
  Buffer.contents b

(* "a@x,b@y" -> the addresses: split at the commas, then each decoded
 * (a %2C in a name is no separator) *)
let addresses (s : string) : string list =
  List.filter (fun a -> a <> "")
    (List.map (fun a -> String.trim (unescape a)) (String.split_on_char ',' s))

let parse (url : string) : t option =
  let n = String.length url in
  if n < 7 || String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub url 0 7) <> "mailto:" then None
  else
    let rest = String.sub url 7 (n - 7) in
    let path, query =
      match String.index_opt rest '?' with
      | Some i ->
          (String.sub rest 0 i, String.sub rest (i + 1) (String.length rest - i - 1))
      | None -> (rest, "")
    in
    let fields =
      List.filter_map
        (fun f ->
          match String.index_opt f '=' with
          | Some i ->
              Some
                ( String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub f 0 i),
                  String.sub f (i + 1) (String.length f - i - 1) )
          | None -> None)
        (String.split_on_char '&' query)
    in
    let all name =
      List.concat_map
        (fun (k, v) -> if k = name then addresses v else [])
        fields
    in
    let one name =
      match List.assoc_opt name fields with Some v -> unescape v | None -> ""
    in
    (* (the body's lines end in CR LF, as the RFC writes them: LF here) *)
    let body = String.concat "" (String.split_on_char '\r' (one "body")) in
    Some
      { to_ = addresses path @ all "to"; cc = all "cc"; bcc = all "bcc";
        subject = one "subject"; body }
