(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-curl: a URL's bytes on standard output (curl, Daniel Stenberg,
 * 1998), after the author's mini-chrome's tools/curl: the request made
 * by Http_client, over Tcp, or inside ix's own TLS 1.3 for https://.
 * A redirection is followed with a GET, ten at most. With -v, what is
 * sent and the answer's head on standard error, as curl ("> ", "< ").
 *
 * It is the browser's network stack with no browser around it: what
 * the address bar does before anything is shown, each step a module
 * that can be looked at on its own.
 *
 *     mini-curl -v https://example.com/
 *        Url           the string cut: https, example.com, 443, /
 *        Dns, Tcp      the name's address, a connection
 *        Tls_client    the handshake (Tls13), the certificate's chain
 *                      checked against the system's roots (X509)
 *        Http          "GET / HTTP/1.1" written, the status line,
 *                      the headers and the body read
 *     * example.com, port 443, TLS             on standard error
 *     > GET / HTTP/1.1
 *     > Host: example.com
 *     > ...
 *     < HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 *     < Content-Type: text/html
 *     < ...
 *     <!doctype html>...                       on standard output
 *
 * A redirection, by mini-httpd, which answers so for a directory
 * named without its slash (the tests' served.sh has the first):
 *
 *     mini-curl -i U/sub      HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
 *                             Location: /sub/
 *     mini-curl -L -v U/sub   > GET /sub HTTP/1.1  ...  < HTTP/1.1 301 ...
 *                             > GET /sub/ HTTP/1.1 ...  < HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 *                             and /sub/'s page
 *
 * The flags are [usage]'s, and their letters curl's. Less than
 * curl's hundreds: no HEAD, no header of one's own, no upload, no
 * cookie kept between two requests (mini-chrome's has a jar),
 * HTTP/1.1 only, and the body as the server sent it (Http asks for
 * no compression).
 *
 * design:
 * A program for one layer of a system is how the layer gets tested
 * and understood. The browser draws a page or it does not; with
 * mini-curl the question becomes which of five modules failed, and
 * the answer is on the screen: no address, a connection refused, a
 * certificate not trusted, a 404, a body that is not what was
 * expected. And every test of the browser's network is a shell
 * script comparing two programs' output, this one's and the system's
 * curl's.
 *
 * Reference: curl(1), whose flags' letters these are; Daniel
 * Stenberg's history of it is told in Http_client.mli. *)

type caps = < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

let usage = "usage: mini-curl [-i] [-L] [-v] [-f] [-d data] [-o file] [--cacert file] url
  -i  the answer's head before its body
  -L  a redirection followed
  -v  the request and the answer's head said on standard error
  -f  status 22 and no body when the server answers 400 or more
  -d  data posted (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
  -o  the body written to file
  --cacert  the roots trusted for https://, in the system's place (PEM)"

type options = { head : bool; follow : bool; verbose : bool; fail : bool; data : string option; output : string option; cacert : string option; url : string option }

let rec options (o : options) (args : string list) : (options, string) result =
  match args with
  | [] -> Ok o
  | ("-i" | "--include") :: rest -> options { o with head = true } rest
  | ("-L" | "--location") :: rest -> options { o with follow = true } rest
  | ("-v" | "--verbose") :: rest -> options { o with verbose = true } rest
  | ("-f" | "--fail") :: rest -> options { o with fail = true } rest
  | ("-d" | "--data") :: data :: rest -> options { o with data = Some data } rest
  | ("-o" | "--output") :: file :: rest -> options { o with output = Some file } rest
  | "--cacert" :: file :: rest -> options { o with cacert = Some file } rest
  | flag :: _ when String.length flag > 1 && flag.[0] = '-' -> Error (Printf.sprintf "%s: not a flag of mine\n%s" flag usage)
  | url :: rest -> if o.url = None then options { o with url = Some url } rest else Error usage

(* "HTTP/1.1 200 OK" and the headers, a line each *)
let head_lines (r : Http.response) : string list =
  Printf.sprintf "%s %d %s" r.version r.status r.reason :: List.map (fun (k, v) -> k ^ ": " ^ v) r.headers

(* a request's head: its bytes up to the empty line, a line each *)
let request_lines (bytes : string) : string list =
  let rec go lines = match lines with [] | "" :: _ -> [] | l :: rest -> l :: go rest in
  go (List.map (fun l -> if String.ends_with ~suffix:"\r" l then String.sub l 0 (String.length l - 1) else l) (String.split_on_char '\n' bytes))

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let ( let* ) = Result.bind in
  let complain (s : string) : unit = Console.eprint caps (s ^ "\n") in
  (* one request at a time, each said with -v *)
  let rec fetch (o : options) ~(post : (string * string) option) (url : Url.t) (left : int) : (Http.response list, string) result =
    (if o.verbose then
       match Http_client.prepare ~post url with
       | Ok (host, port, bytes) ->
           complain (Printf.sprintf "* %s, port %d%s" host port (if url.scheme = Some "https" then ", TLS" else ""));
           List.iter (fun l -> complain ("> " ^ l)) (request_lines bytes)
       | Error _ -> ());
    let* (r : Http.response) = Http_client.once caps ~post url in
    if o.verbose then List.iter (fun l -> complain ("< " ^ l)) (head_lines r);
    match (o.follow && Http.is_redirect r.status, Http.header "Location" r.headers) with
    | true, Some location ->
        if left = 0 then Error "too many redirections"
        else
          let* next = Url.parse location in
          let* rest = fetch o ~post:None (Url.resolve url next) (left - 1) in
          Ok (r :: rest)
    | _ -> Ok [ r ]
  in
  let result =
    let* o = options { head = false; follow = false; verbose = false; fail = false; data = None; output = None; cacert = None; url = None } (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) in
    let* url = match o.url with Some u -> Ok u | None -> Error usage in
    (* example.com is http://example.com *)
    let url = if String.starts_with ~prefix:"http://" url || String.starts_with ~prefix:"https://" url then url else "http://" ^ url in
    let* parsed = Url.parse url in
    (match o.cacert with Some file -> Tls_client.trust_file caps file | None -> ());
    let post = Option.map (fun d -> ("application/x-www-form-urlencoded", d)) o.data in
    let* answers = fetch o ~post parsed 10 in
    let last = List.nth answers (List.length answers - 1) in
    if o.fail && last.status >= 400 then Error (Printf.sprintf "the server answered %d" last.status)
    else begin
      (* -i: every answer's head, a redirection's too, as curl -i -L *)
      if o.head then List.iter (fun r -> Console.print caps (String.concat "\r\n" (head_lines r) ^ "\r\n\r\n")) answers;
      (match o.output with None -> Console.print caps last.body | Some file -> FS.write caps (Fpath.v file) last.body);
      Ok ()
    end
  in
  match result with
  | Ok () -> Exit.OK
  | Error why -> complain ("mini-curl: " ^ why); Exit.Err "curl"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
networking/Httpd.ml
13013
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-httpd: a directory's files served over HTTP, to this machine
 * only (127.0.0.1), after the author's mini-chrome's tools/httpd: a
 * request read, its file answered (a directory: its index.html, or its
 * names as links), the connection closed, the next one taken. One
 * client at a time; GET only; nothing above the directory served. No
 * WebSocket here (mini-chrome's echoes one).
 *
 * The other end of the browser's conversation. A browser writes a
 * request and reads an answer (Http_client); a server does the
 * reverse with the same two messages (Http): it waits for a
 * connection, reads until the request is whole (Http.parse_request),
 * finds what the request's target names, and writes the answer
 * (Http.response_to_string).
 *
 *     the browser                          mini-httpd
 *     -----------                          ----------
 *     connect ---------------------------> accept
 *     "GET /notes/a.html HTTP/1.1" ------> root/notes/a.html read
 *          <------------------------------ "HTTP/1.1 200 OK", its type,
 *                                          its length, its bytes
 *          <------------------------------ close
 *
 * What a target names, under the directory served ([answer]):
 *
 *     /notes/a.html     that file: 200, its Content-Type from its
 *                       extension (.html, .css, .js, .png, ...)
 *     /notes/           the directory's index.html if it has one; else
 *                       a page listing what is in it, each a link
 *     /notes            301, Location: /notes/ (so that the listing's
 *                       relative links resolve)
 *     /nope             404
 *     /../secret        403: the ".." are counted before the path is
 *                       cleaned (Url.remove_dot_segments), and nothing
 *                       above the directory is ever named
 *     POST /x           405: only GET
 *
 * A query (?v=2) is dropped, %20 decoded. It listens on 127.0.0.1
 * alone: a server for the pages on one's own machine, not for the
 * Internet. Each request is a line of the log on standard output,
 * "GET /notes/ 200 153": the method, the target, the status, the
 * body's length.
 *
 * Where it stands: what mini-curl and mini-lynx are tried against
 * with no network but this machine's (their tests' served.sh and
 * session.sh), and the server's half of Http, which nothing else in
 * ix uses. The sockets are called here and not through Tcp, which
 * only connects: socket, bind, listen and accept are the four lines
 * of [listen] and [serve].
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The first web server was the program on Tim Berners-Lee's NeXT at
 * CERN (1990; the machine kept a label, "This machine is a server. DO
 * NOT POWER IT DOWN!!"): a URL's path was a file's path, as here.
 * NCSA's HTTPd (Rob McCool, 1993) was the one sites ran, and added
 * programs behind a URL (CGI). When McCool left for Netscape its users
 * went on exchanging their patches by mail, and released them together
 * in 1995 -- "a patchy server", as the story goes: Apache, the most
 * used web server for the twenty years after, and with Linux the
 * proof that software so made could run the Internet. nginx (Igor
 * Sysoev, 2004) took its place by serving ten thousand connections
 * from one loop instead of a process for each. This one serves one
 * at a time.
 *
 * others:
 * One at a time means a client that connects and says nothing holds
 * everyone else up, here for five seconds at most. The ways out are
 * the history of servers: a process per connection (fork after
 * accept, the first Unix servers and Apache), a thread per
 * connection, or one loop that asks the kernel which of its thousand
 * sockets have something to read (select, then epoll and kqueue:
 * nginx). mini-rio's file server is of the last kind, for the same
 * reason: it has other things to listen to (P9_server.mli).
 *
 * Reference: RFC 9110 (HTTP semantics): sections 9.3.1 (GET), 15
 * (status codes); "python3 -m http.server", which this stands in for. *)

type caps = < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

let usage = "usage: mini-httpd [-p port] [-max-age seconds] [directory]
  -p  the port (8000; 0: one the system chooses, said on the first line)
  -max-age  for how long a client need not ask again (Cache-Control)"

let content_type (name : string) : string =
  (* (lib_core's Filename has no extension) *)
  let base = Filename.basename name in
  let ext = match String.rindex_opt base '.' with Some i -> String.sub base i (String.length base - i) | None -> "" in
  match String.lowercase_ascii ext with
  | ".html" | ".htm" -> "text/html; charset=utf-8"
  | ".css" -> "text/css"
  | ".js" | ".mjs" -> "text/javascript"
  | ".json" -> "application/json"
  | ".txt" | ".md" | ".ml" | ".mli" -> "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
  | ".svg" -> "image/svg+xml"
  | ".png" -> "image/png"
  | ".jpg" | ".jpeg" -> "image/jpeg"
  | ".gif" -> "image/gif"
  | ".pdf" -> "application/pdf"
  | _ -> "application/octet-stream"

let chars (s : string) : char list = List.init (String.length s) (String.get s)

let escape (s : string) : string =
  String.concat "" (List.map (fun c -> match c with '&' -> "&amp;" | '<' -> "&lt;" | '>' -> "&gt;" | '"' -> "&quot;" | c -> String.make 1 c) (chars s))

(* %20 as a space; a + stays a + (a path, not a form's field) *)
let unescape (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  let rec go i =
    if i < String.length s then
      match (s.[i], if i + 2 < String.length s then int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ String.sub s (i + 1) 2) else None) with
      | '%', Some code -> Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr code); go (i + 3)
      | c, _ -> Buffer.add_char b c; go (i + 1)
  in
  go 0;
  Buffer.contents b

(* a name as a link's address: what a URL cannot hold as it is, as %XX *)
let quote (s : string) : string =
  String.concat "" (List.map (fun c -> match c with ' ' | '%' | '?' | '#' | '"' -> Printf.sprintf "%%%02X" (Char.code c) | c -> String.make 1 c) (chars s))

let html = "text/html; charset=utf-8"

let page (status : int) (text : string) : Http.response =
  Http.response status ~content_type:html
    (Printf.sprintf "<!doctype html><title>%d %s</title><h1>%d %s</h1><p>%s</p>\n" status (Http.reason status) status (Http.reason status) (escape text))

(* a directory's page: what is in it, each a link, the directories first *)
let listing (_caps : < Cap.readdir; .. >) (path : string) (dir : string) : Http.response =
  let names = List.sort compare (Array.to_list (Sys.readdir dir)) in
  let is_dir n = Sys.is_directory (Filename.concat dir n) in
  let item n = let n = if is_dir n then n ^ "/" else n in Printf.sprintf "<li><a href=\"%s\">%s</a>\n" (escape (quote n)) (escape n) in
  let dirs, files = List.partition is_dir names in
  Http.response 200 ~content_type:html
    (Printf.sprintf "<!doctype html><title>%s</title><h1>%s</h1>\n<ul>\n%s</ul>\n" (escape path) (escape path) (String.concat "" (List.map item (dirs @ files))))

let answer (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.readdir; .. >) ~(root : string) ~(max_age : int option) (request : Http.request) : Http.response =
  let target = match String.index_opt request.target '?' with Some i -> String.sub request.target 0 i | None -> request.target in
  let raw = unescape target in
  (* a/../b is b; more ".." than directories before them would go
   * above the root *)
  let above =
    let rec go depth parts = match parts with [] -> false | ".." :: rest -> depth = 0 || go (depth - 1) rest | ("" | ".") :: rest -> go depth rest | _ :: rest -> go (depth + 1) rest in
    go 0 (String.split_on_char '/' raw)
  in
  let path = Url.remove_dot_segments raw in
  let file = root ^ path in
  (* a file's version is its contents' MD5: an ETag, which a client that
   * has the file says back (If-None-Match) and gets nothing more; -max-age,
   * for how long it need not ask (Tile_cache.mli says it all) *)
  let send (file : string) : Http.response =
    try
      let bytes = FS.read caps (Fpath.v file) in
      let tag = "\"" ^ Digest.to_hex (Digest.string bytes) ^ "\"" in
      let cache = match max_age with Some n -> [ ("Cache-Control", Printf.sprintf "max-age=%d" n) ] | None -> [] in
      let r =
        if Http.header "If-None-Match" request.headers = Some tag then Http.response 304 ~content_type:(content_type file) ""
        else Http.response 200 ~content_type:(content_type file) bytes
      in
      { r with headers = (("ETag", tag) :: cache) @ r.headers }
    with Sys_error why -> page 403 why in
  if request.meth <> "GET" then page 405 (request.meth ^ " is not allowed here: only GET.")
  else if above || String.contains path '\000' || not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"/" path) then page 403 "Nothing above the directory served."
  else if not (Sys.file_exists file) then page 404 (path ^ " is not here.")
  else if not (Sys.is_directory file) then send file
  else if not (String.ends_with ~suffix:"/" path) then { (page 301 (path ^ "/")) with headers = [ ("Location", path ^ "/"); ("Content-Type", html) ] }
  else
    let index = Filename.concat file "index.html" in
    if Sys.file_exists index then send index else listing caps path file

(* a line of the log, out at once: a server's output is read while it runs *)
let say (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) (line : string) : unit =
  Console.print caps (line ^ "\n");
  flush (Console.stdout caps)

let listen (_caps : < Cap.network; .. >) (port : int) : Unix.file_descr * int =
  let sock = Unix.socket Unix.PF_INET Unix.SOCK_STREAM 0 in
  Unix.setsockopt sock Unix.SO_REUSEADDR true;
  Unix.bind sock (Unix.ADDR_INET (Unix.inet_addr_loopback, port));
  Unix.listen sock 16;
  (sock, match Unix.getsockname sock with Unix.ADDR_INET (_, p) -> p | _ -> port)

(* a request read from a connection, piece by piece, until it is whole
 * (or the client is gone, says nothing for five seconds, or it is too
 * long to be one) *)
let read_request (fd : Unix.file_descr) : Http.parsed_request =
  let buffer = Bytes.create 4096 and so_far = Buffer.create 1024 in
  let rec go () =
    match Http.parse_request (Buffer.contents so_far) with
    | Http.Incomplete when Buffer.length so_far < 1_000_000 -> (
        match Unix.select [ fd ] [] [] 5.0 with
        | [], _, _ -> Http.Bad "nothing said in five seconds"
        | _ -> (
            match Unix.read fd buffer 0 4096 with
            | 0 -> Http.Bad "the connection closed before the request's end"
            | n -> Buffer.add_subbytes so_far buffer 0 n; go ()))
    | Http.Incomplete -> Http.Bad "the request is too long"
    | r -> r
  in
  go ()

let rec serve (caps : < caps; .. >) ~(root : string) ~(max_age : int option) (sock : Unix.file_descr) : 'a =
  let fd, _ = Unix.accept sock in
  (try
     let said, (response : Http.response) =
       match read_request fd with
       | Http.Request (r, _, _) -> (r.meth ^ " " ^ r.target, answer caps ~root ~max_age r)
       | Http.Bad why -> ("?", page 400 why)
       | Http.Incomplete -> ("?", page 400 "not a whole request")
     in
     let bytes = Http.response_to_string response in
     let rec write pos = if pos < String.length bytes then write (pos + Unix.write_substring fd bytes pos (String.length bytes - pos)) in
     write 0;
     say caps (Printf.sprintf "%s %d %d" said response.status (String.length response.body))
   with Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _ -> ());
  (try Unix.close fd with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
  serve caps ~root ~max_age sock

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let rec options port root max_age args =
    match args with
    | [] -> Some (port, root, max_age)
    | "-p" :: p :: rest -> ( match int_of_string_opt p with Some p -> options p root max_age rest | None -> None)
    | "-max-age" :: n :: rest -> ( match int_of_string_opt n with Some n -> options port root (Some n) rest | None -> None)
    | flag :: _ when String.length flag > 1 && flag.[0] = '-' -> None
    | dir :: rest -> options port dir max_age rest
  in
  match options 8000 "." None (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) with
  | None -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "\n"); Exit.Err "usage"
  | Some (_, root, _) when not (Sys.file_exists root && Sys.is_directory root) -> Console.eprint caps (root ^ ": not a directory\n"); Exit.Err "directory"
  | Some (port, root, max_age) -> (
      match listen caps port with
      | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "port %d: %s\n" port (Unix.error_message e)); Exit.Err "port"
      | sock, port ->
          (* a client that left before its answer: an error of the write, not
           * a signal that ends the program *)
          Sys.set_signal Sys.sigpipe Sys.Signal_ignore;
          say caps (Printf.sprintf "serving %s on http://127.0.0.1:%d/" root port);
          serve caps ~root ~max_age sock)

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
networking/Timesync.ml
2886
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-timesync: the time a server of the network says, as the seconds
 * since 1970, on standard output; what a machine without a clock chip
 * (a Raspberry Pi) writes to its /dev/time when it starts, a
 * certificate's dates being checked against it:
 *
 *     timesync pool.ntp.org > /dev/time
 *
 * One question and its answer (SNTP): a packet of 48 bytes, its first
 * 0x1b (version 3, a client), sent to UDP's port 123; in the answer of
 * the same size the bytes 40 to 43 are the seconds since 1900 when the
 * server sent it. None of NTP's own work: no delay measured, no clock
 * slowed or hurried, one server believed; a second is what is wanted.
 *
 * history:
 * Plan 9's is aux/timesync, which also takes the time from a file
 * server or a radio clock and keeps the clock's frequency right.
 * David Mills's NTP (1985) is the protocol; SNTP its simple subset.
 *
 * References: RFC 4330, "Simple Network Time Protocol (SNTP) Version
 * 4" (2006); Plan 9's timesync(8). *)

type caps = < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.argv >

let usage = "usage: mini-timesync server
  the seconds since 1970 as the server (pool.ntp.org) says them, by SNTP"

(* 1900 to 1970, in seconds *)
let since_1900 = 2208988800.

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let result : (float, string) result =
    match List.tl (Array.to_list argv) with
    | [ server ] when server <> "" && server.[0] <> '-' -> (
        (* (an address is itself) *)
        let is_address = String.for_all (fun c -> (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c = '.') server in
        match if is_address then [ server ] else Dns.resolve caps server with
        | [] -> Error (server ^ ": no address")
        | address :: _ -> (
            match Udp.ask caps ~address ~port:123 ("\x1b" ^ String.make 47 '\000') 5. with
            | Some answer when String.length answer >= 48 ->
                (* (in floats: the seconds are past an int of 31 bits) *)
                let byte i = float_of_int (Char.code answer.[40 + i]) in
                let seconds = (byte 0 *. 16777216.) +. (byte 1 *. 65536.) +. (byte 2 *. 256.) +. byte 3 in
                if seconds < since_1900 then Error (server ^ ": no time in its answer") else Ok (seconds -. since_1900)
            | Some _ -> Error (server ^ ": an answer too short")
            | None -> Error (server ^ ": no answer")
            | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> Error (server ^ ": " ^ Unix.error_message e)))
    | _ -> Error usage
  in
  match result with
  | Ok seconds -> Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%.0f\n" seconds); Exit.OK
  | Error why -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-timesync: " ^ why ^ "\n"); Exit.Err "timesync"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

(* See Profiler.mli *)

let usage = {|usage: mini-prof [-n count] [-diff base.prof] [-a name] profile file.map...
  profile    lines "pc count" (hexadecimal pc): mini-5i -prof, mini-qemu -prof
  file.map   the link's functions: mini-ld -map's "address name" lines, or
             mini-ld -v's listing ("address: word TEXT name+0(SB), $frame")
  -diff      a profile of a shorter run taken off first (the start)
  -n         the functions shown (default 30), each with its calls (its
             first instruction's count) and its instructions a call
  -a         the function's instructions, each with its count, read from
             the program beside its map (doom for doom.map); name: mini-ml's
             in full (f1_to_rgba<>), or without its number and <> (to_rgba)
For example:
  mini-5i -prof start.prof doom -dump-frame 1 f.ppm
  mini-5i -prof walk.prof doom -dump-frame 31 f.ppm -script up:1-31
  mini-prof -diff start.prof walk.prof doom.map     30 frames, the start off
  mini-prof -diff start.prof -a to_rgba walk.prof doom.map|}

(* n added to k's count, 0 when it has none *)
let add (tbl : ('k, int) Hashtbl.t) (k : 'k) (n : int) : unit =
  Hashtbl.replace tbl k (n + match Hashtbl.find_opt tbl k with Some m -> m | None -> 0)

(* the counts of a profile, by pc *)
let read_profile (caps : < Cap.open_in ; .. >) (file : string) : (int, int) Hashtbl.t =
  let counts : (int, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 65536 in
  List.iter
    (fun (line : string) ->
      match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
      | [ pc; n ] -> (
          match (int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ pc), int_of_string_opt n) with
          | Some pc, Some n -> add counts pc n
          | _ -> ())
      | _ -> ())
    (String.split_on_char '\n' (FS.read caps (Fpath.v file)));
  counts

(* a map's or a listing's line: the function that starts there *)
let symbol (line : string) : (int * string) option =
  match List.filter (fun (w : string) -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.map (fun c -> if c = '\t' then ' ' else c) line)) with
  | [ a; name ] -> Option.map (fun (a : int) -> (a, name)) (int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ a))
  | a :: _ :: "TEXT" :: name :: _ -> (
      let a = String.sub a 0 (max 0 (String.length a - 1)) in
      let name = match String.index_opt name '+' with Some i -> String.sub name 0 i | None -> name in
      match int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ a) with Some a -> Some (a, name) | None -> None)
  | _ -> None

(* the functions of the maps, by address, each with its map *)
let functions (caps : < Cap.open_in ; .. >) (files : string list) : (int * string * string) array =
  let all =
    List.concat_map
      (fun (f : string) ->
        List.filter_map
          (fun (l : string) -> Option.map (fun ((a, name) : int * string) -> (a, name, f)) (symbol l))
          (String.split_on_char '\n' (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f))))
      files in
  let a = Array.of_list all in
  Array.sort (fun ((x, _, _) : int * string * string) ((y, _, _) : int * string * string) -> compare x y) a;
  a

(* the function [pc] is in: the last one that starts at or before it,
 * its index *)
let find (funcs : (int * string * string) array) (pc : int) : int option =
  let rec look (lo : int) (hi : int) : int =
    if lo >= hi then lo
    else
      let m = (lo + hi + 1) / 2 in
      let a, _, _ = funcs.(m) in
      if a <= pc then look m hi else look lo (m - 1) in
  let first, _, _ = if Array.length funcs = 0 then (0, "", "") else funcs.(0) in
  if Array.length funcs = 0 || pc < first then None else Some (look 0 (Array.length funcs - 1))

let name_at (funcs : (int * string * string) array) (pc : int) : string =
  match find funcs pc with Some i -> (let _, name, _ = funcs.(i) in name) | None -> "?"

(* a mini-ml name without its unit's number and its <> (a function
 * local to its file): f1_to_rgba<>, to_rgba *)
let short (name : string) : string =
  let n = if String.ends_with ~suffix:"<>" name then String.sub name 0 (String.length name - 2) else name in
  match String.index_opt n '_' with
  | Some i when i > 1 && n.[0] = 'f' && String.for_all (fun (c : char) -> c >= '0' && c <= '9') (String.sub n 1 (i - 1)) ->
      String.sub n (i + 1) (String.length n - i - 1)
  | _ -> n

(* a program's text: its word at an address, and how one is printed.
 * An ELF (Linux's): its segments, arm32 or arm64 by its machine; else
 * Plan 9's a.out, arm32, its header at 0x1000 and the text after *)
let text (s : string) : (int -> int option) * (int -> int -> string) =
  let word (o : int) : int option =
    if o >= 0 && o + 4 <= String.length s then Some (Bits.of_int32 (String.get_int32_le s o)) else None in
  let arm32 (a : int) (w : int) : string = Show_arm32.print ~addr:a (Arm32.decode w) in
  let arm64 (a : int) (w : int) : string = Show_arm64.print ~addr:a (Arm64.decode w) in
  if String.length s >= 4 && String.sub s 0 4 = "\x7fELF" then
    let elf = Elf.parse s in
    let at (a : int) : int option =
      match List.find_opt (fun (g : Elf.segment) -> g.exec && a >= g.vaddr && a + 4 <= g.vaddr + g.filesz) elf.segments with
      | Some g -> word (g.offset + a - g.vaddr)
      | None -> None in
    (at, if elf.machine = Elf.Aarch64 then arm64 else arm32)
  else ((fun (a : int) -> word (a - 0x1000)), arm32)

(* 1234567 as 1,234,567 *)
let commas (n : int) : string =
  let s = string_of_int n in
  let k = String.length s in
  String.concat "" (List.init k (fun (i : int) -> (if i > 0 && (k - i) mod 3 = 0 then "," else "") ^ String.make 1 s.[i]))

(* -a: each function named, its instructions with their counts (none:
 * not run), from its address to the next function's *)
let annotate (caps : < Cap.open_in ; Cap.stdout ; Cap.stderr ; .. >) (funcs : (int * string * string) array) (counts : (int, int) Hashtbl.t) (total : int) (name : string) : int =
  let found = ref 0 in
  Array.iteri
    (fun (i : int) ((start, f, map) : int * string * string) ->
      if f = name || short f = name then begin
        incr found;
        let stop = if i + 1 < Array.length funcs then (let a, _, _ = funcs.(i + 1) in a) else start + 4 in
        let prog = if Filename.check_suffix map ".map" then Filename.chop_suffix map ".map" else map in
        let word, show = text (FS.read caps (Fpath.v prog)) in
        let sum = ref 0 in
        for k = 0 to ((stop - start) / 4) - 1 do
          sum := !sum + (match Hashtbl.find_opt counts (start + (4 * k)) with Some n -> n | None -> 0)
        done;
        Console.print caps
          (Printf.sprintf "%s (%s): %s instructions, %.1f%%\n%14s %8s  instruction\n" f prog (commas !sum)
             (100. *. float !sum /. float (max 1 total)) "count" "address");
        for k = 0 to ((stop - start) / 4) - 1 do
          let a = start + (4 * k) in
          let n = match Hashtbl.find_opt counts a with Some n when n > 0 -> commas n | _ -> "" in
          let ins = match word a with Some w -> show a w | None -> "?" in
          Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%14s %8x  %s\n" n a ins)
        done
      end)
    funcs;
  if !found = 0 then (Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "mini-prof: no function %s in the maps\n" name); 1) else 0

let main (caps : < Cap.argv ; Cap.stdout ; Cap.stderr ; Cap.open_in ; .. >) : int =
  let rec options (top : int) (diff : string option) (fn : string option) (args : string list) =
    match args with
    | "-n" :: n :: rest -> options (int_of_string n) diff fn rest
    | "-diff" :: f :: rest -> options top (Some f) fn rest
    | "-a" :: f :: rest -> options top diff (Some f) rest
    | file :: maps when file <> "" && file.[0] <> '-' && maps <> [] -> Some (top, diff, fn, file, maps)
    | _ -> None in
  match options 30 None None (List.tl (Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps))) with
  | None -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "\n"); 2
  | Some (top, diff, fn, file, maps) -> (
      let counts = read_profile caps file in
      Option.iter
        (fun (f : string) ->
          Hashtbl.iter
            (fun (pc : int) (n : int) ->
              match Hashtbl.find_opt counts pc with Some m -> Hashtbl.replace counts pc (max 0 (m - n)) | None -> ())
            (read_profile caps f))
        diff;
      let funcs = functions caps maps in
      let total = Hashtbl.fold (fun (_ : int) (n : int) (acc : int) -> acc + n) counts 0 in
      match fn with
      (* a word in an int: mini-ml's on 32-bit arm (mini-9pi) has 31
       * bits, an instruction's condition lost *)
      | Some _ when Sys.int_size < 32 -> Console.eprint caps "mini-prof: -a needs ints of 32 bits or more\n"; 1
      | Some name -> annotate caps funcs counts total name
      | None ->
          let by : (string, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 1024 in
          Hashtbl.iter (fun (pc : int) (n : int) -> add by (name_at funcs pc) n) counts;
          (* the most first; equal counts by name (a table's order is its
           * library's) *)
          let rows = List.sort (fun ((a, n) : string * int) ((b, m) : string * int) -> if n <> m then compare m n else compare a b)
              (Hashtbl.fold (fun (f : string) (n : int) (acc : (string * int) list) -> (f, n) :: acc) by []) in
          (* a function's calls: the count of its first instruction (a
           * loop back to it counted too: rare in mini-ml's, whose first is
           * the frame's) *)
          let calls : (string, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 1024 in
          Array.iter (fun ((a, name, _) : int * string * string) ->
            match Hashtbl.find_opt counts a with Some n -> add calls name n | None -> ()) funcs;
          Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%s instructions\n%14s %6s %12s %8s  function\n" (commas total) "count" "%" "calls" "a call");
          List.iteri
            (fun (i : int) ((name, n) : string * int) ->
              if i < top && n > 0 then
                let c = match Hashtbl.find_opt calls name with Some c -> c | None -> 0 in
                let per = if c > 0 then Printf.sprintf "%.1f" (float n /. float c) else "" in
                Console.print caps (Printf.sprintf "%14s %6.1f %12s %8s  %s\n" (commas n) (100. *. float n /. float (max 1 total)) (commas c) per name))
            rows;
          0)
profilers/misc/Profiler.mli
2790
(* mini-prof: where a program's instructions went, function by function
 * (docs/plans/plan_profiler.md). It reads a profile, every instruction's
 * address and how many times it ran (mini-5i -prof, or mini-qemu -prof
 * for a whole system, there one in 1024), and the link's map of the
 * program (mini-ld -map: each function's address), and prints the
 * functions with the most instructions, with their share.
 *
 *     mini-5i -prof walk.prof doom -dump-frame 31 f.ppm -script up:1-31
 *     mini-prof walk.prof doom.map
 *
 *     1,234,567,890 instructions
 *              count      %  function
 *        234,567,890   19.0  f19_draw_column<>
 *        ...
 *
 * A count goes to the last function at or before its address. A name is
 * mini-ml's (f19_draw_column: the 19th function of its unit; <>, one
 * local to its file) or the C's and the runtime's (ml_alloc, copy<>).
 *
 * With -a name, one function's instructions instead, each with its
 * count, read from the program beside its map (doom for doom.map: an
 * ELF, arm32 or arm64, or Plan 9's a.out) and printed by mini-5i's
 * decoder, objdump's way: what a back end's change is decided on.
 *
 *          count  address  instruction
 *      1,926,000    5acd0  ldr	r1, [sl, #-84]      a loop's bound and its
 *      1,926,000    5acd4  ldr	r2, [sl, #-88]      index, from the stack
 *      1,926,000    5acd8  cmp	r2, r1              at each turn
 *
 * With -diff base, a profile of a shorter run is taken off first: the
 * same program stopped before what is measured (mini-doom's start and a
 * frame, against the start and 31), so that what is left is the frames
 * alone. Counting every instruction, and not sampling a clock, makes two
 * runs of the same program give the same counts: the difference is
 * exact.
 *
 * Where it stands: tiny-prof's twin (tiny/TinyProfiler: tiny-machine's
 * profiles, tiny-linker's maps), for m-ix's tools; it does what
 * machine/tests/profile.sh did from mini-5i -t's trace, a line of text
 * an instruction (a thousand million of them for mini-doom's start),
 * and kernels/9pi/tests/perf/pcprof.py did for mini-qemu's.
 *
 * history:
 * Unix's prof (1973) read mon.out, a histogram of the program counter
 * sampled at each clock tick, which a program compiled with -p wrote at
 * its exit; gprof (Graham, Kessler and McKusick, 1982) added who called
 * whom. Plan 9 kept prof (a program compiled with -p counts its calls
 * and their time) and added tprof, a process's pcs sampled by the kernel
 * into /proc/n/profile and read by name. An emulator counting every
 * instruction, as here and as 5i's statistics did, needs nothing of the
 * program, and is not disturbed by itself. *)

val usage : string

val main : < Cap.argv ; Cap.stdout ; Cap.stderr ; Cap.open_in ; .. > -> int
profilers/misc/Stats.ml
10373
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-stats: Plan 9's stats (principia's profilers/misc/stats.c), of which
 * it keeps one graph, the one asked for (the author, 2026-10-12:
 * "an application to display the cpu activity, a bit like xosview on
 * linux", "so we can see the 4 cores activity, whether they are idle
 * or not", "I think plan9 had such an application actually"): a strip
 * for each core of the machine, how busy it was, the newest at the
 * right, the strip moving left five times a second; and (the author,
 * 2026-11-01: "not just display cpu stats but also memory, disk, etc.") one
 * for the memory taken, one for the network's packets, one for the bytes
 * of the disk, those that the machine has.
 *
 *   cpu0  37% |        ..::||||::.            |
 *   mem   41% |______________________________.|
 *   net   12  |     .       ...               |
 *   disk 340K |  ...||..     .                |
 *
 * usage: stats [-cmed]: which: the cores, the memory, the ethernet, the disk;
 * all by default.
 *
 * What it reads is the kernel's /dev/sysstat (Devcons), a line for
 * each core, ten numbers; the ninth is the percent of its time the
 * core had nothing to run. mini-9pi's is of the last fifth of a
 * second, which is why this reads five times a second. And /dev/swap,
 * /net/ether0/stats, /dev/sdM0/ctl: Sysinfo says what each says. The
 * network and the disk are on a scale of powers of ten, as Sysinfo says
 * why; the number beside is the real one, a second's. The right
 * button's menu has exit.
 *
 * What a core "busy" is here: running a process, or in the kernel,
 * or waiting for the kernel's lock (mini-9pi has one lock for its
 * kernel: plan_multicore.md). Two games that draw much show two cores
 * busy where one of them mostly waits for the other to leave the
 * kernel.
 *
 * Not Plan 9's: its other graphs (interrupts, system calls, the load:
 * mini-9pi's sysstat says 0 for most), the machines over the network, and
 * its letters (-l for the load, here -c). Its graphs have no disk, whose
 * counter here is ours.
 *
 * history:
 * xosview (Mike Romberg, 1993) drew its meters for X from Linux's
 * /proc; Plan 9's stats (1990) reads /dev/sysstat and /dev/swap, the
 * same idea three years before: what the kernel counts is a file's
 * text, and the meter a program like any, that could as well be rc
 * and cat. *)

type caps = < Cap.draw; Cap.mouse; Cap.fork; Cap.open_in; Cap.stderr >

(* A file kept open and read again from its start, as Plan 9's stats: under
 * mini-rio each open of /dev/... asks rio's file server first, and is told
 * no, 5 times a second a file (old: opened at each sample: 32% of the
 * processor under QEMU, alone, against 17% for /dev/sysstat alone). None
 * when the machine has no such file. *)
let reader (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) path : (unit -> string option) option =
  match FS.open_in_fd caps path with
  | exception (Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _) -> None
  | fd ->
      let b = Bytes.create 4096 in
      Some (fun () ->
        try
          ignore (Unix.lseek fd 0 Unix.SEEK_SET);
          Some (Bytes.sub_string b 0 (Unix.read fd b 0 4096))
        with Unix.Unix_error _ -> None)

type event = Mouse of Mouse.state | Tick

(* a strip: its name, and at each sample how high (0 to 100) and what to say *)
type meter = { name : string; sample : unit -> int * string }

(* samples a second: a counter's growth is that many times a second's *)
let rate = 5

(* a counter's meter: how much it grew since the last sample *)
let counter (read : unit -> int option) name top : meter =
  let last = ref (match read () with Some v -> v | None -> 0) in
  { name;
    sample = (fun () ->
      match read () with
      | Some now ->
          let v = Sysinfo.grew !last now * rate in
          last := now;
          (Sysinfo.log_percent top v, Sysinfo.short v)
      | None -> (0, "?")) }

(* those of the machine, among those asked: a letter each *)
let meters (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) (asked : string) : meter list =
  let wants c = String.contains asked c in
  (* a file's meters when it is wanted, there, and says what is looked for *)
  let from c path (make : (unit -> string option) -> meter list) =
    if not (wants c) then []
    else match reader caps path with Some read -> make read | None -> [] in
  let percent name (value : unit -> int option) =
    { name;
      sample = (fun () ->
        match value () with
        | Some v -> (v, Printf.sprintf "%d%%" v)
        | None -> (0, "?")) } in
  let cpu = from 'c' "/dev/sysstat" (fun read ->
      let now () = match read () with Some t -> Sysinfo.cores t | None -> [] in
      List.mapi (fun c _ -> percent (Printf.sprintf "cpu%d" c) (fun () -> List.nth_opt (now ()) c)) (now ())) in
  let mem = from 'm' "/dev/swap" (fun read ->
      let now () = Option.bind (read ()) Sysinfo.memory in
      if now () = None then [] else [ percent "mem" now ]) in
  (* (a counter the file has, or no meter) *)
  let growing read parse name top =
    let now () = Option.bind (read ()) parse in
    if now () = None then [] else [ counter now name top ] in
  let net = from 'e' "/net/ether0/stats" (fun read ->
      growing read (fun t -> Option.map (fun (i, o) -> i + o) (Sysinfo.ether t)) "net" 10000) in
  let disk = from 'd' "/dev/sdM0/ctl" (fun read ->
      growing read (fun t -> Option.map (fun (r, w) -> r + w) (Sysinfo.disk t)) "disk" 10000000) in
  cpu @ mem @ net @ disk

(* a sample's width on the screen, in pixels; how many are kept (a
 * screen's width of them) *)
let wide = 2
let kept = 1024

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let usage () = Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "usage: %s [-cmed]\n" argv.(0)); Exit.Err "usage" in
  let asked =
    if Array.length argv = 1 then Some "cmed"
    else if Array.length argv = 2 && String.length argv.(1) > 1 && argv.(1).[0] = '-' then Some argv.(1)
    else None in
  match asked with
  | None -> usage ()
  | Some asked ->
    match meters caps asked with
    | [] -> Console.eprint caps "mini-stats: none of those here (mini-9pi's /dev/sysstat...)\n"; Exit.Err "no files"
    | all ->
        let n = List.length all in
        let display = Display.init caps in
        let font = Font.default display and mouse = Mouse.init caps in
        let ticks = Source.timer caps (1. /. float rate) in
        let white = Display.color display Display.white and black = Display.color display Display.black in
        let pale = Display.color display (Display.rgb 0xee 0xff 0xee) and green = Display.color display (Display.rgb 0x33 0x99 0x44) in
        (* the samples: meter c's k-th is history.(c).(k mod kept) *)
        let history = Array.init n (fun _ -> Array.make kept 0) in
        let said = Array.make n "" in
        let count = ref 0 in
        let left = Font.width font "cpu0 100%  " in
        (* meter c's row in the window, and in it the strip's inside *)
        let row (view : Display.image) c : Rectangle.t =
          let r : Rectangle.t = Rectangle.inset view.r 4 in
          let at k = r.min.y + ((r.max.y - r.min.y) * k / n) in
          Rectangle.v r.min.x (at c) r.max.x (at (c + 1) - 2) in
        let strip view c : Rectangle.t =
          let r = row view c in
          Rectangle.inset (Rectangle.v (r.min.x + left) r.min.y r.max.x r.max.y) 1 in
        (* a sample's column, its right side at x: pale above, green for how high *)
        let column view (g : Rectangle.t) x high =
          let x0 = max g.min.x (x - wide) in
          let y = g.max.y - ((g.max.y - g.min.y) * high / 100) in
          if x > x0 then begin
            Draw.fill view (Rectangle.v x0 g.min.y x y) pale;
            Draw.fill view (Rectangle.v x0 y x g.max.y) green
          end in
        (* its name and what it says now, in the row's middle *)
        let label (view : Display.image) c (m : meter) =
          let r = row view c in
          let y = r.min.y + (max 0 (Rectangle.dy r - Font.height font) / 2) in
          Draw.fill view (Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y (r.min.x + left - 2) r.max.y) white;
          ignore (Font.string view (Point.v r.min.x y) black font m.name);
          let w = Font.width font said.(c) in
          ignore (Font.string view (Point.v (r.min.x + left - 6 - w) y) black font said.(c)) in
        (* everything again: a new window, or one of another size *)
        let paint (view : Display.image) =
          Draw.fill view view.r white;
          List.iteri (fun c m ->
            let g = strip view c in
            label view c m;
            Draw.border view (Rectangle.inset g (-1)) 1 black;
            Draw.fill view g pale;
            let rec back k x =
              if k < !count && k < kept && x > g.min.x then begin
                column view g x history.(c).((!count - 1 - k) mod kept); back (k + 1) (x - wide)
              end in
            back 0 g.max.x) all;
          Display.flush display in
        (* a sample more: each strip moved left by the screen's own
         * pixels (as stats: no sample drawn twice), the new one at
         * the right *)
        let step (view : Display.image) =
          List.iteri (fun c (m : meter) ->
            let high, words = m.sample () in
            let g = strip view c in
            history.(c).(!count mod kept) <- high;
            said.(c) <- words;
            if g.max.x - g.min.x > wide then
              Draw.draw view (Rectangle.v g.min.x g.min.y (g.max.x - wide) g.max.y) view None (Point.v (g.min.x + wide) g.min.y);
            column view g g.max.x high;
            label view c m) all;
          incr count;
          Display.flush display in
        let rec loop view =
          match Event.select [ Event.wrap (Mouse.receive mouse) (fun m -> Mouse m); Event.wrap (Event.receive ticks) (fun () -> Tick) ] with
          | Tick -> step view; loop view
          | Mouse m ->
              if m.resized then begin let view = Display.screen display in paint view; loop view end
              else if m.buttons = 4 then (match Menu.hit view font mouse 4 [ "exit" ] 0 m.pos with Some _ -> () | None -> loop view)
              else loop view in
        let view = Display.screen display in
        paint view;
        loop view;
        Exit.OK

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

(* See Sysinfo.mli *)

let lines text = String.split_on_char '\n' text
let words line = List.filter (fun f -> f <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' line)

let cores text =
  List.filter_map (fun line ->
      match List.nth_opt (words line) 8 with
      | Some idle -> Option.map (fun i -> 100 - i) (int_of_string_opt idle)
      | None -> None)
    (lines text)

let memory text =
  List.find_map (fun line ->
      match words line with
      | [ pair; "user" ] -> (
          match String.split_on_char '/' pair with
          | [ used; all ] -> (
              match int_of_string_opt used, int_of_string_opt all with
              | Some u, Some a when a > 0 -> Some (u * 100 / a)
              | _ -> None)
          | _ -> None)
      | _ -> None)
    (lines text)

(* the number after a word that starts a line *)
let field name text =
  List.find_map (fun line ->
      match words line with
      | w :: n :: _ when w = name -> int_of_string_opt n
      | _ -> None)
    (lines text)

let ether text =
  match field "in:" text, field "out:" text with
  | Some i, Some o -> Some (i, o)
  | _ -> None

let disk text =
  List.find_map (fun line ->
      match words line with
      | [ "io"; r; w ] -> (
          match int_of_string_opt r, int_of_string_opt w with
          | Some r, Some w -> Some (r, w)
          | _ -> None)
      | _ -> None)
    (lines text)

let grew before now = if now > before then now - before else 0

(* (a table of powers of ten: no float, no log in a program of 5 samples a
 * second: tenths of a power, by what v is above the power below it) *)
let log_tenths v =
  let rec go power tens = if v >= power * 10 then go (power * 10) (tens + 10) else (power, tens) in
  if v <= 0 then 0
  else
    let power, tens = go 1 0 in
    tens + 1 + (9 * (v - power) / (power * 9))

let log_percent top v =
  if v <= 0 then 0
  else min 100 (max 1 (log_tenths v * 100 / max 1 (log_tenths top)))

let short v =
  if v < 1000 then string_of_int v
  else if v < 1000000 then string_of_int (v / 1000) ^ "K"
  else string_of_int (v / 1000000) ^ "M"

(* What the kernel's files say about the machine, for mini-stats: their text
 * read, without a screen and without a kernel.
 *
 *     /dev/sysstat      a line a core; the ninth number: percent idle
 *     /dev/swap         "1234/85000 user": the pages taken and in all
 *     /net/ether0/stats "in: 12", "out: 34": packets since the boot
 *     /dev/sdM0/ctl     "io 512 1024": bytes read and written since the boot
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * Each is a file of text that cat shows. Plan 9's stats reads /dev/sysstat,
 * /dev/swap and /net/ether0/stats just so. On Linux, top and xosview read
 * /proc the same way, though /proc's formats grew by accident; on BSD and
 * macOS the same numbers are sysctl's, a system call with a structure for
 * each.
 *
 * Two of the numbers are counters, so what is shown is how much they grew
 * since the last look ([grew]). A rate goes from nothing to millions, and a
 * strip of the screen has 30 pixels: [log_percent] gives each power of ten
 * the same height, so a trickle is seen beside a flood, and a strip already
 * drawn need not be drawn again at a new scale when the flood comes. *)

(* each core's percent busy, in the cores' order *)
val cores : string -> int list
(* the pages taken and in all, as a percent *)
val memory : string -> int option
(* packets in, packets out *)
val ether : string -> (int * int) option
(* bytes read, bytes written *)
val disk : string -> (int * int) option

(* [grew before now]: how much more; a counter that went back (none should):
 * nothing *)
val grew : int -> int -> int
(* [log_percent top v]: v on a scale where [top] is 100 and each power of ten
 * the same height; 0 is 0, 1 is above it *)
val log_percent : int -> int -> int
(* short: 7, 950, 12K, 3M *)
val short : int -> string

(* mini-qemu: QEMU's command line, the part the Pi kernels' Makefiles use
 * (plan_pi.md, "The kernels it must boot"); its usage, the options and
 * examples: [help], what mini-qemu -h prints. -smp: the Pi4's cores
 * take turns (plan_pi.md decision 3); QEMU wants 4, mini-qemu defaults
 * to 1, the fastest. *)


let usage = "usage: mini-qemu -M raspi1ap|raspi2b|raspi4b [-m size] [-smp n] [-nographic | -display none] (-kernel image | -device loader,file=F,addr=A | -bios F) [-drive file=F,if=sd] [-serial S]... [-audiodev wav,path=F] [-ips N] [-cores-parallel] [-d] [-trace N] [-prof F] [-status N] [-symbols ELF] [-meters [on|off]] [-qmp unix:path,server,nowait]"

(* -h: how, by examples, each one as it runs *)
let help = usage ^ {|
A Raspberry Pi 1 (raspi1ap), 2 (raspi2b: one of its four cores) or 4 (raspi4b), by QEMU's command line; ./mini-pi
gives each kernel its own. For example (Ctrl-A then x quits):
  cd ~/xv6/forks/arm-pi1-bis && mini-qemu -M raspi1ap -kernel kernel.img -nographic
  cd kernels/xv6 && mini-qemu -M raspi1ap -device loader,file=kernel-pi1.img,addr=0x8000 -nographic
  cd ~/xv6/forks/arm64-pi4 && mini-qemu -cpu cortex-a72 -M raspi4b -kernel kernel/kernel -m 2G -smp 1 -nographic
The UART is this terminal, raw. Accepted as QEMU's: -cpu -serial -monitor -append
-netdev -no-reboot, -device usb-kbd, usb-mouse, usb-net (Usernet, QEMU's user net),
-audiodev wav,path=F: what the Pi 1's jack plays (its PWM), a WAV file written at the end;
in a window it is also played, by SDL.
Its own: -ips N, instructions a simulated microsecond (30); -cores-parallel, the
Pi 2's started cores each on a core of the host's (built by OCaml 5; else, and by
default, they take turns: the same run each time); -d, unassigned I/O and
undefined instructions logged; -trace N, the Pi4's first N instructions (-N: every
N-th); -prof F, every 1024th PC counted into F; -status N, where the guest is,
every N seconds (-symbols ELF: its PCs named), all on standard error.
A window has meters: the processor and the network watched, a strip of graphs under
the screen and the numbers in the title (-meters off: none; -meters without a
window: a line a second on standard error).
|}

(* the board run in batches; the host's input polled (raw on a
 * terminal, Ctrl-A x to quit), the console's output written, the
 * screen shown 30 times a second of the host's, QMP served.
 *
 * claude: with a window, the board's time ([now], microseconds) is kept
 * from running ahead of the host's: an idle kernel's time skips to its
 * next tick (the WFI), so without it a key held 100ms of a person's
 * time lasted far longer in the board's, and 9pi's usb/kb repeated it
 * (its repeat starts after 160ms: "ls" gave "lsss"). QEMU keeps its
 * clock the host's too. Behind (a busy kernel), the board catches up
 * 30 ms at most ([late]): the time lost beyond is lost, as a slower
 * machine's. Without a
 * window (the tests, session.py's timed keys), it runs as fast as it
 * can, its time the instructions' only.
 *
 * [locked]: what touches the board or [out] between two runs is done
 * inside it, the board's cores going on meanwhile when each is on a
 * domain (Board.locked; else it is the call). Not inside: the wait
 * that paces, the window's picture. *)
let loop caps ~out ~graphics ~qmp ~run ~now ~input ~frame ~key ~pointer ~qmp_poll ~status ~meters ~where ~(locked : (unit -> unit) -> unit) =
  let tty = Unix.isatty Unix.stdin in
  let saved = if tty then Some (Unix.tcgetattr Unix.stdin) else None in
  Option.iter (fun (a : Unix.terminal_io) ->
    Unix.tcsetattr Unix.stdin TCSANOW { a with c_icanon = false; c_echo = false; c_isig = false; c_icrnl = false; c_vmin = 1 }) saved;
  let restore () = Option.iter (fun a -> Unix.tcsetattr Unix.stdin TCSANOW a) saved in
  let open_input = ref true and ctrl_a = ref false in
  let buf = Bytes.create 256 in
  let poll () =
    if !open_input then
      match Unix.select [ Unix.stdin ] [] [] 0.0 with
      | [ _ ], _, _ ->
          let n = try Unix.read Unix.stdin buf 0 256 with Unix.Unix_error _ -> 0 in
          if n = 0 then open_input := false;
          for i = 0 to n - 1 do
            let c = Bytes.get buf i in
            if tty && !ctrl_a && c = 'x' then (restore (); Console.print caps "\nmini-qemu: terminated\n"; exit 0);
            ctrl_a := tty && c = '\001';
            if not !ctrl_a then input c
          done
      | _ -> () in
  (* -meters: the processor and the network watched (Monitor), in a
   * strip under the screen and the window's title; without a window,
   * its line on the standard error each second *)
  let windowed = graphics && Sys.getenv_opt "DISPLAY" <> None in
  (* (in a window unless -meters off, the author's decision of plan_monitor.md: "on by default"; without one, when asked) *)
  let meters = match meters with Some on -> on | None -> windowed in
  let monitor = if meters then Some (Monitor.create ~period:(if windowed then 0.5 else 1.)) else None in
  let stamp = ref 0 in
  let meter m ~width = { Display.stamp = !stamp; text = Monitor.line m; rows = Monitor.height; pixels = Monitor.strip m ~width } in
  let display =
    if windowed then
      (match monitor with
       | Some m -> Sdl_display.create ~meter:(meter m) ~title:"mini-qemu" ()
       | None -> Sdl_display.create ~title:"mini-qemu" ())
    else Display.none in
  let qmp = Option.map Qmp.create qmp in
  let quit () = restore (); exit 0 in
  let last_frame = ref 0. and at_bol = ref true in
  let n = ref 0 in
  let paced = display != Display.none in
  (* the host's time when the board's was 0 *)
  let base = ref (CapUnix.gettimeofday caps ()) in
  let late = 0.03 in
  let pace () =
    let ahead = (float_of_int (now ()) /. 1e6) -. (CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () -. !base) in
    if ahead > 0.001 then CapUnix.sleepf caps (min ahead 0.02)
    (* OPTIMIZATION: behind by less than [late], nothing is lost yet: the
     * board catches up while its kernel waits, a wait costing the host
     * nothing. A kernel busy three tenths of the time (a mouse that
     * moves) runs those tenths at the host's 17 million instructions a
     * second, not the board's 30, and each such burst was time lost:
     * the board went at 0.7 of the host's clock with 70% of its own
     * time idle (docs/plans/plan_mini_qemu_speed.md). Short of a key's
     * repeat (160 ms held, above) even on a key held 100.
     * old: else if ahead < 0. then base := !base -. ahead *)
    else if ahead < -. late then base := !base -. (ahead +. late) in
  (try
     while true do
       run ();
       (* (where empties the board's counts: asked once, for both) *)
       if status <> None || monitor <> None then begin
         let cpus = where () in
         Option.iter (fun st -> Status.sample st cpus) status;
         Option.iter (fun m -> Monitor.sample m cpus) monitor
       end;
       if Buffer.length out > 0 then locked (fun () ->
         at_bol := Buffer.nth out (Buffer.length out - 1) = '\n';
         Console.print caps (Buffer.contents out); flush stdout; Buffer.clear out);
       incr n;
       if !n land 15 = 0 then begin
         if paced then pace ();
         (* claude: on its own line, not after a prompt *)
         Option.iter (fun st -> Option.iter (fun l -> Console.eprint caps ((if !at_bol then "" else "\n") ^ "mini-qemu: " ^ l ^ "\n"); at_bol := true)
           (Status.report st ~now:(now ()))) status;
         locked (fun () ->
           poll ();
           Usernet.poll_all ();
           Option.iter (fun q -> qmp_poll q ~quit) qmp);
         let board = now () in
         let now = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () in
         Option.iter (fun m ->
           if Monitor.tick m ~host:now ~board ~net:(Usernet.totals ()) then begin
             incr stamp;
             if display == Display.none then begin
               Console.eprint caps ((if !at_bol then "" else "\n") ^ "mini-qemu: " ^ Monitor.line m ^ "\n"); at_bol := true
             end
           end) monitor;
         if now -. !last_frame > 1. /. 30. then begin
           last_frame := now;
           let shown = ref None in
           locked (fun () -> shown := frame ());
           Option.iter (fun (g, data) -> display.Display.present g data) !shown;
           (* the mouse's events of a poll synced as one, as QEMU syncs
            * a window's *)
           let evs = display.poll () in
           locked (fun () ->
             List.iter (function Display.Key (u, down) -> key u down | Display.Quit -> quit () | _ -> ()) evs;
             let inputs = List.concat_map (function
               | Display.Motion (dx, dy) -> [ Usb.Rel_x dx; Usb.Rel_y dy ]
               | Display.Button (b, down) -> [ Usb.Button (b, down) ]
               | Display.Wheel v -> [ Usb.Wheel v ]
               | _ -> []) evs in
             if inputs <> [] then pointer inputs)
         end
       end
     done
   with e -> restore (); raise e);
  0

(* -audiodev wav,path=F: the jack's samples kept, and written as a WAV
 * file (16 bits, two channels, the rate the guest's PWM plays at) at
 * any exit, SIGTERM made one. The file is the board's time, not ours:
 * a second of it is a second the guest played, however long the
 * emulator took. *)
let wav_file (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) (file : string) : rate:int -> int -> int -> unit =
  let samples = Buffer.create 65536 and played_at = ref 44100 in
  at_exit (fun () ->
    let n = Buffer.length samples in
    let b = Buffer.create (n + 44) in
    let u32 v = Buffer.add_int32_le b (Int32.of_int v) and u16 v = Buffer.add_uint16_le b v in
    Buffer.add_string b "RIFF"; u32 (36 + n); Buffer.add_string b "WAVEfmt "; u32 16; u16 1; u16 2;
    u32 !played_at; u32 (4 * !played_at); u16 4; u16 16; Buffer.add_string b "data"; u32 n;
    Buffer.add_buffer b samples;
    FS.write caps (Fpath.v file) (Buffer.contents b));
  Sys.set_signal Sys.sigterm (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> exit 0));
  fun ~rate left right ->
    played_at := rate;
    Buffer.add_uint16_le samples (left land 0xffff);
    Buffer.add_uint16_le samples (right land 0xffff)

let main (caps : < Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >) =
  let args = List.tl (Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps)) in
  if List.mem "-h" args || List.mem "-help" args || List.mem "--help" args then (Console.print caps help; exit 0);
  let kernel = ref None and machine = ref "" and ips = ref 30 and debug = ref false and usb = ref [] in
  let qmp = ref None and graphics = ref true and wav = ref None in
  let serials = ref [] and drive = ref None and loader = ref None in
  let others = ref [] and pokes = ref [] in
  let ram = ref (2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024) and smp = ref 1 and trace = ref 0 and prof = ref None in
  let status = ref 0. and symbols = ref None and meters = ref None and cores_parallel = ref false in
  (* the board's random numbers: the host's, 4096 bytes read at a time *)
  let pool = ref "" and next = ref 0 in
  Devices.random := (fun () ->
    if !next + 4 > String.length !pool then begin
      pool := FS.with_open_in caps (fun (ch : Chan.i) -> really_input_string ch.ic 4096) (Fpath.v "/dev/urandom");
      next := 0
    end;
    let at = !next in
    next := at + 4;
    let b i = Char.code !pool.[at + i] in
    b 0 lor (b 1 lsl 8) lor (b 2 lsl 16) lor (b 3 lsl 24));
  (* QEMU's sizes: a number of MB, or with a suffix K, M, G *)
  let size s =
    let n = String.length s in
    let num k = int_of_string (String.sub s 0 k) in
    match s.[n - 1] with
    | 'G' | 'g' -> num (n - 1) lsl 30 | 'M' | 'm' -> num (n - 1) lsl 20 | 'K' | 'k' -> num (n - 1) lsl 10
    | _ -> num n lsl 20 in
  (* key=value options, after the first comma-separated word *)
  let options s = List.filter_map (fun kv -> match String.index_opt kv '=' with
    | Some i -> Some (String.sub kv 0 i, String.sub kv (i + 1) (String.length kv - i - 1)) | None -> None) (String.split_on_char ',' s) in
  let rec parse = function
    | [] -> ()
    | ("-M" | "-machine") :: m :: rest -> machine := List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' m); parse rest
    | "-kernel" :: k :: rest -> kernel := Some k; parse rest
    | "-ips" :: n :: rest -> ips := int_of_string n; parse rest
    | "-cores-parallel" :: rest -> cores_parallel := true; parse rest
    | "-d" :: rest -> debug := true; parse rest
    | "-trace" :: n :: rest -> trace := int_of_string n; parse rest
    | "-prof" :: f :: rest -> prof := Some f; parse rest
    | "-status" :: n :: rest -> status := float_of_string n; parse rest
    | "-symbols" :: f :: rest -> symbols := Some f; parse rest
    | "-meters" :: "off" :: rest -> meters := Some false; parse rest
    | "-meters" :: "on" :: rest | "-meters" :: rest -> meters := Some true; parse rest
    | "-device" :: d :: rest when List.mem (List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' d)) [ "usb-kbd"; "usb-mouse"; "usb-net" ] ->
        usb := !usb @ [ List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' d) ];
        (* a network: 10.0.2.3 is the host's name server, the first of
         * /etc/resolv.conf with an IPv4 address *)
        if List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' d) = "usb-net" then begin
          Usernet.clock := CapUnix.gettimeofday caps;
          let lines = match FS.read caps (Fpath.v "/etc/resolv.conf") with t -> String.split_on_char '\n' t | exception Sys_error _ -> [] in
          let words l = List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' l) in
          match List.find_map (fun l -> match words l with [ "nameserver"; a ] when not (String.contains a ':') -> Some a | _ -> None) lines with
          | Some a -> (try Usernet.resolver := Unix.inet_addr_of_string a with Failure _ -> ())
          | None -> ()
        end;
        parse rest
    | "-device" :: d :: rest when List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' d) = "loader" ->
        let o = options d in
        (* (cpu-num other than 0: where another core starts, QEMU's
         * raspi2b having four) *)
        (* (old: | _, _, Some n when n <> "0" -> (), the one core; now
         * the Pi 2's other cores start there, Board.start_core, and a
         * word may be put in memory: data=, data-len=4) *)
        (match List.assoc_opt "file" o, List.assoc_opt "addr" o, List.assoc_opt "cpu-num" o with
         | None, Some a, None when List.mem_assoc "data" o -> pokes := (int_of_string a, int_of_string (List.assoc "data" o)) :: !pokes
         | _, Some a, Some n when n <> "0" -> others := (int_of_string n, int_of_string a) :: !others
         | _, _, Some n when n <> "0" -> ()
         | Some f, Some a, _ -> loader := Some (f, int_of_string a)
         | _ -> Console.eprint caps "mini-qemu: -device loader needs file= and addr=\n"; exit 2);
        parse rest
    | "-bios" :: f :: rest -> loader := Some (f, 0x8000); parse rest
    | "-drive" :: d :: rest ->
        let o = options ("drive," ^ d) in
        drive := Some (List.assoc "file" o, List.assoc_opt "snapshot" o = Some "on"); parse rest
    | "-serial" :: s :: rest -> serials := !serials @ [ s ]; parse rest
    | "-qmp" :: q :: rest -> qmp := Some q; parse rest
    | "-audiodev" :: a :: rest ->
        (match String.split_on_char ',' a with
         | "wav" :: options ->
             List.iter (fun o -> if String.length o > 5 && String.sub o 0 5 = "path=" then wav := Some (String.sub o 5 (String.length o - 5))) options;
             if !wav = None then wav := Some "qemu.wav"
         | _ -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: -audiodev " ^ a ^ ": only wav,path=F\n"); exit 2);
        parse rest
    | "-display" :: "none" :: rest -> graphics := false; parse rest
    | "-nographic" :: rest -> graphics := false; parse rest
    | "-m" :: m :: rest -> ram := size (List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' m)); parse rest
    | "-smp" :: n :: rest -> smp := int_of_string (List.hd (String.split_on_char ',' n)); parse rest
    | ("-monitor" | "-device" | "-append" | "-D" | "-display" | "-cpu" | "-netdev") :: _ :: rest -> parse rest
    | ("-no-reboot" | "-S") :: rest -> parse rest
    | a :: _ -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "mini-qemu: unknown option %s\n%s   (-h: how)\n" a usage); exit 2 in
  parse args;
  match !kernel, !loader with
  | None, None -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "   (-h: how)\n"); 2
  | _ when not (List.mem !machine [ "raspi1ap"; "raspi2b"; "raspi4b" ]) ->
      Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "mini-qemu: machine %s not (yet) supported\n" !machine); 2
  | _ when !machine = "raspi4b" && (!smp < 1 || !smp > 4) ->
      Console.eprint caps "mini-qemu: raspi4b: -smp 1 to 4\n"; 2
  | kernel, loader ->
      (* the profile written at any exit: Ctrl-A x, QMP's quit, the
       * window closed, and SIGTERM (a test script's kill) made one *)
      Option.iter (fun f ->
        Prof.start ~every:1024;
        at_exit (fun () -> Out_channel.with_open_bin f (fun oc -> output_string oc (Prof.contents ())));
        Sys.set_signal Sys.sigterm (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> exit 0))) !prof;
      let log s = if !debug || !trace <> 0 then Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: " ^ s ^ "\n") in
      let out = Buffer.create 256 in
      (* claude: -symbols ELF, for -status: none when not an ELF (9pi's
       * Plan 9 a.out) *)
      let symbols = match !symbols with
        | None -> []
        | Some f ->
            (try Elf.symbols (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f)) with
             | Sys_error m | Elf.Bad m -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: -symbols: " ^ m ^ "\n"); []
             | Invalid_argument _ | Not_found -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: -symbols " ^ f ^ ": no symbols read\n"); []) in
      let status = if !status > 0. then Some (Status.create ~clock:(CapUnix.gettimeofday caps) ~every:!status ~symbols) else None in
      (* the serials, QEMU's order: the PL011, the mini UART; stdio (or
       * mon:stdio) the console, null or absent nowhere; with none said,
       * the PL011 on stdio *)
      let serials = if !serials = [] then [ "stdio" ] else !serials in
      let target i = match List.nth_opt serials i with
        | Some ("stdio" | "mon:stdio") -> Buffer.add_char out
        | Some "null" | None -> ignore
        | Some s -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: -serial " ^ s ^ ": only stdio, mon:stdio, null\n"); exit 2 in
      let read f = match FS.read caps (Fpath.v f) with
        | image -> image
        | exception Sys_error m -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: " ^ m ^ "\n"); exit 1 in
      if !machine = "raspi4b" then begin
        let sd = Option.map (fun (f, snapshot) -> Storage.file f ~snapshot) !drive in
        let board = Pi4.create { ram_size = !ram; ips = !ips; log; serial = target 0; trace = !trace; cores = !smp; usb_devices = !usb; sd } in
        (match kernel with
         | Some k ->
             let image = read k in
             if String.length image >= 4 && String.sub image 0 4 = "\127ELF" then
               (try Pi4.load_elf board image with Elf.Bad m -> Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: " ^ k ^ ": " ^ m ^ "\n"); exit 1)
             else Pi4.load_raw board image
         | None -> Console.eprint caps "mini-qemu: raspi4b: -kernel only\n"; exit 2);
        (* claude: the Pi4's framebuffer in the window and QMP's
         * screendump; the USB keyboard and mouse on its DWC2 *)
        let machine = { Qmp.screen = (fun () -> Pi4.screen board); send_keys = Pi4.send_keys board;
                        key = Pi4.key board; pointer = Pi4.pointer board } in
        loop caps ~out ~graphics:!graphics ~qmp:!qmp ~run:(fun () -> Pi4.run board ~batch:4096) ~now:(fun () -> Pi4.now board) ~input:(Pi4.input board)
          ~frame:(fun () -> Pi4.frame board) ~key:(Pi4.key board) ~pointer:(Pi4.pointer board)
          ~qmp_poll:(fun q ~quit -> Qmp.poll q machine ~quit) ~status ~meters:!meters ~where:(fun () -> Pi4.where board) ~locked:(fun f -> f ())
      end
      else begin
        let console = match List.nth_opt serials 1 with Some ("stdio" | "mon:stdio") -> 1 | _ -> 0 in
        let sd = Option.map (fun (f, snapshot) -> Storage.file f ~snapshot) !drive in
        let pi2 = !machine = "raspi2b" in
        (* (asked where it cannot be: said, and the turns) *)
        if !cores_parallel && not (pi2 && Parallel.available) then
          Console.eprint caps ("mini-qemu: -cores-parallel: " ^ (if pi2 then "this mini-qemu was built by an OCaml without domains (OCaml 5 has them)" else "raspi2b only") ^ "; the cores take turns\n");
        Board.cores_parallel := !cores_parallel;
        let board = Board.create { pi2; ram_size = (if pi2 then 1024 else 512) * 1024 * 1024; ips = !ips; log; usb_devices = !usb; sd;
                                   serial0 = target 0; serial1 = target 1; console } in
        (* the jack: to the WAV file asked for, and in a window to the host's
         * sound card *)
        let sinks = (match !wav with Some f -> [ wav_file caps f ] | None -> [])
                    @ (if !graphics && Sys.getenv_opt "DISPLAY" <> None then [ Sdl_display.audio () ] else []) in
        if sinks <> [] then Board.set_audio board (fun ~rate left right -> List.iter (fun sink -> sink ~rate left right) sinks);
        (match kernel, loader with
         | _, Some (f, addr) -> Board.load_raw board ~addr (read f)
         | Some k, None -> Board.load_kernel board (read k)
         | None, None -> ());
        if pi2 then List.iter (fun (n, addr) -> Board.start_core board n ~addr) !others;
        List.iter (fun (addr, v) -> Board.poke board ~addr v) !pokes;
        loop caps ~out ~graphics:!graphics ~qmp:!qmp ~run:(fun () -> Board.run board ~batch:4096) ~now:(fun () -> Board.now board) ~input:(Board.input board)
          ~frame:(fun () -> Board.frame board) ~key:(Board.key board) ~pointer:(Board.pointer board) ~qmp_poll:(fun q ~quit ->
            Qmp.poll q { Qmp.screen = (fun () -> Board.screen board); send_keys = Board.send_keys board;
                         key = Board.key board; pointer = Board.pointer board } ~quit)
          ~status ~meters:!meters ~where:(fun () -> Board.where board) ~locked:(Board.locked board)
      end

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> CapStdlib.exit caps (main caps))
