(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Usernet.mli *)

let host = "\010\000\002\002"
let dns = "\010\000\002\003"
let hostmac = "\082\085\010\000\002\002"

(* the host's name server, which 10.0.2.3 stands for (Main reads it in
 * /etc/resolv.conf); and where a connection the guest makes to an
 * address really goes: the gateway is this machine, the name server
 * the host's, any other itself *)
let resolver = ref Unix.inet_addr_loopback
(* the host's clock, for a conversation's age (Main sets it from its
 * Cap.clock; 0 before) *)
let clock : (unit -> float) ref = ref (fun () -> 0.)
let show a = String.concat "." (List.init 4 (fun i -> string_of_int (Char.code a.[i])))
let real a = if a = host then Unix.inet_addr_loopback else if a = dns then !resolver else Unix.inet_addr_of_string (show a)

(* a connection: the guest's address and port, the host's port; the
 * sequence numbers (ours next and first not acked, the guest's next
 * expected), the guest's window; the socket; the FINs *)
type conn = {
  gaddr : string; gport : int; haddr : string; hport : int;
  mutable snd : int32; mutable una : int32; mutable rcv : int32;
  mutable wnd : int; sock : Unix.file_descr;
  mutable hostfin : bool; mutable guestfin : bool;
}

(* a UDP conversation: the guest's address and port, the address and
 * port it sends to, the host's socket connected there, when it last
 * carried a datagram *)
type flow = { fgaddr : string; fgport : int; faddr : string; fport : int; fsock : Unix.file_descr; mutable used : float }

type t = {
  send : string -> unit; mutable guestmac : string; mutable conns : conn list; mutable flows : flow list;
  (* for who watches (Monitor): the frames' bytes each way, and the
   * last things that happened, the newest first *)
  mutable from_guest : int; mutable to_guest : int; mutable events : string list;
}

let create send = { send; guestmac = String.make 6 '\255'; conns = []; flows = []; from_guest = 0; to_guest = 0; events = [] }

let note t what = t.events <- what :: (if List.length t.events >= 8 then List.filteri (fun i _ -> i < 7) t.events else t.events)
let out t frame = t.to_guest <- t.to_guest + String.length frame; t.send frame

let get16 s o = (Char.code s.[o] lsl 8) lor Char.code s.[o + 1]
let put16 v = String.init 2 (fun i -> Char.chr ((v lsr (8 * (1 - i))) land 255))
let get32 s o = Int32.logor (Int32.shift_left (Int32.of_int (get16 s o)) 16) (Int32.of_int (get16 s (o + 2)))
let put32 v = put16 (Int32.to_int (Int32.shift_right_logical v 16) land 0xffff) ^ put16 (Int32.to_int v land 0xffff)

let cksum s =
  let sum = ref 0 and n = String.length s in
  let i = ref 0 in
  while !i + 1 < n do sum := !sum + get16 s !i; i := !i + 2 done;
  if !i < n then sum := !sum + (Char.code s.[!i] lsl 8);
  while !sum lsr 16 <> 0 do sum := (!sum land 0xffff) + (!sum lsr 16) done;
  lnot !sum land 0xffff

(* an IP packet from src (10.0.2.2, or an address beyond it: the
 * gateway's card carries them all) to the guest, in a frame *)
let ip t proto src dst payload =
  let h = "\069\000" ^ put16 (20 + String.length payload) ^ "\000\000\000\000\255" ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr proto) ^ "\000\000" ^ src ^ dst in
  let h = String.sub h 0 10 ^ put16 (cksum h) ^ String.sub h 12 8 in
  out t (t.guestmac ^ hostmac ^ "\008\000" ^ h ^ payload)

let tcp t c flags data =
  let opts = if flags land 2 <> 0 then "\002\004" ^ put16 1460 else "" in
  let seg = put16 c.hport ^ put16 c.gport ^ put32 c.snd ^ put32 c.rcv
            ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr ((20 + String.length opts) * 4)) ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr flags) ^ put16 65535 ^ "\000\000\000\000" ^ opts ^ data in
  let k = cksum (c.haddr ^ c.gaddr ^ "\000\006" ^ put16 (String.length seg) ^ seg) in
  ip t 6 c.haddr c.gaddr (String.sub seg 0 16 ^ put16 k ^ String.sub seg 18 (String.length seg - 18))

let fin = 1 and syn = 2 and rst = 4 and psh = 8 and ack = 16

let arp t f =
  let op = get16 f 20 and sip = String.sub f 28 4 and tip = String.sub f 38 4 in
  (* the gateway and the name server: one card for both *)
  if op = 1 && (tip = host || tip = dns) then
    out t (String.sub f 6 6 ^ hostmac ^ "\008\006" ^ "\000\001\008\000\006\004\000\002" ^ hostmac ^ tip ^ String.sub f 6 6 ^ sip)

let icmp t pkt hl =
  if Char.code pkt.[hl] = 8 then begin
    let m = String.sub pkt hl (String.length pkt - hl) in
    let m = "\000" ^ String.sub m 1 1 ^ "\000\000" ^ String.sub m 4 (String.length m - 4) in
    let k = cksum m in
    ip t 1 (String.sub pkt 16 4) (String.sub pkt 12 4) (String.sub m 0 2 ^ put16 k ^ String.sub m 4 (String.length m - 4))
  end

let close_conn t c = (try Unix.close c.sock with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()); t.conns <- List.filter (fun x -> x != c) t.conns

let tcpin t pkt hl =
  let gaddr = String.sub pkt 12 4 and haddr = String.sub pkt 16 4 in
  let sport = get16 pkt hl and dport = get16 pkt (hl + 2) in
  let seq = get32 pkt (hl + 4) and ackn = get32 pkt (hl + 8) in
  let off = (Char.code pkt.[hl + 12] lsr 4) * 4 and flags = Char.code pkt.[hl + 13] in
  let data = String.sub pkt (hl + off) (String.length pkt - hl - off) in
  match List.find_opt (fun c -> c.gport = sport && c.hport = dport && c.gaddr = gaddr && c.haddr = haddr) t.conns with
  | None ->
      if flags land syn <> 0 && flags land ack = 0 then begin
        (* a new one: a connection of the host's to where the guest
         * calls (10.0.2.2: this machine), else a RST. Waited for, 10 s
         * at most, the board stopped meanwhile: its clock is the
         * instructions' and jumps over an idle wait, so a connection
         * left to be made while the board ran (tried) was "timed out"
         * for the guest's kernel after 40 ms of the host's.
         * old: Unix.connect to 127.0.0.1 alone, then set_nonblock *)
        let sock = Unix.socket Unix.PF_INET Unix.SOCK_STREAM 0 in
        let c = { gaddr; gport = sport; haddr; hport = dport; snd = 0x10000l; una = 0x10000l; rcv = Int32.add seq 1l; wnd = 65535;
                  sock; hostfin = false; guestfin = false } in
        Unix.set_nonblock sock;
        let made =
          match Unix.connect sock (Unix.ADDR_INET (real haddr, dport)) with
          | () -> true
          | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINPROGRESS, _, _) ->
              (* (made or not: asked by calling again, which says EISCONN
               * of a connection made and its error of one that failed;
               * lib_core's Unix has no getsockopt_error.
               * old: Unix.getsockopt_error sock = None) *)
              (match Unix.select [] [ sock ] [] 10. with
               | _, [ _ ], _ ->
                   (match Unix.connect sock (Unix.ADDR_INET (real haddr, dport)) with
                    | () -> true
                    | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EISCONN, _, _) -> true
                    | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false)
               | _ -> false)
          | exception (Unix.Unix_error _ | Failure _) -> false in
        if made then begin
          note t (Printf.sprintf "tcp %s:%d" (show haddr) dport);
          t.conns <- c :: t.conns;
          tcp t c (syn lor ack) "";
          c.snd <- Int32.add c.snd 1l
        end
        else begin note t (Printf.sprintf "refused %s:%d" (show haddr) dport); Unix.close sock; tcp t c (rst lor ack) "" end
      end
  | Some c ->
      if flags land rst <> 0 then close_conn t c
      else begin
        if flags land ack <> 0 then begin c.una <- ackn; c.wnd <- get16 pkt (hl + 14) end;
        if String.length data > 0 && seq = c.rcv then begin
          (try ignore (Unix.write_substring c.sock data 0 (String.length data)) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
          c.rcv <- Int32.add c.rcv (Int32.of_int (String.length data));
          tcp t c ack ""
        end;
        if flags land fin <> 0 && not c.guestfin then begin
          c.guestfin <- true;
          c.rcv <- Int32.add c.rcv 1l;
          (try Unix.shutdown c.sock Unix.SHUTDOWN_SEND with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
          tcp t c ack ""
        end;
        if c.guestfin && c.hostfin && c.una = c.snd then close_conn t c
      end

(* A datagram of the guest's: given to a socket of the host's connected
 * where it goes (10.0.2.3, the name server: the host's own), one for
 * each conversation; what comes back on it is [poll]'s. *)
let udpin t pkt hl =
  let gaddr = String.sub pkt 12 4 and faddr = String.sub pkt 16 4 in
  let sport = get16 pkt hl and dport = get16 pkt (hl + 2) and len = get16 pkt (hl + 4) in
  if len >= 8 && hl + len <= String.length pkt then begin
    let now = !clock () in
    let flow =
      match List.find_opt (fun w -> w.fgport = sport && w.fport = dport && w.fgaddr = gaddr && w.faddr = faddr) t.flows with
      | Some w -> Some w
      | None -> (
          let fsock = Unix.socket Unix.PF_INET Unix.SOCK_DGRAM 0 in
          match Unix.connect fsock (Unix.ADDR_INET (real faddr, dport)) with
          | () ->
              Unix.set_nonblock fsock;
              let w = { fgaddr = gaddr; fgport = sport; faddr; fport = dport; fsock; used = now } in
              note t (Printf.sprintf "udp %s:%d" (show faddr) dport);
              t.flows <- w :: t.flows;
              Some w
          | exception (Unix.Unix_error _ | Failure _) -> Unix.close fsock; None)
    in
    Option.iter (fun w ->
      w.used <- now;
      try ignore (Unix.write_substring w.fsock pkt (hl + 8) (len - 8)) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()) flow
  end

let input t f =
  t.from_guest <- t.from_guest + String.length f;
  if String.length f >= 14 then begin
    t.guestmac <- String.sub f 6 6;
    match get16 f 12 with
    | 0x806 when String.length f >= 42 -> arp t f
    | 0x800 when String.length f >= 34 ->
        let pkt = String.sub f 14 (String.length f - 14) in
        let pkt = String.sub pkt 0 (min (String.length pkt) (get16 pkt 2)) in
        let hl = (Char.code pkt.[0] land 15) * 4 in
        (* (to any address: the gateway's card takes what leaves the
         * subnet; a ping is answered for the gateway and the name
         * server only.
         * old: if String.sub pkt 16 4 = host && ...) *)
        let dst = String.sub pkt 16 4 in
        if String.length pkt >= hl + 8 then
          (match Char.code pkt.[9] with
           | 1 when dst = host || dst = dns -> icmp t pkt hl
           | 6 when String.length pkt >= hl + 20 -> tcpin t pkt hl
           | 17 -> udpin t pkt hl
           | _ -> ())
    | _ -> ()
  end

let buf = Bytes.create 1460
let ubuf = Bytes.create 2048

(* the host's data, within the guest's window; its EOF a FIN *)
let poll t =
  (* the datagrams come back, each to its conversation's port; a
   * conversation silent for a minute is forgotten *)
  let now = !clock () in
  List.iter (fun w ->
    let rec take () =
      match Unix.read w.fsock ubuf 0 (Bytes.length ubuf) with
      | n ->
          w.used <- now;
          let d = put16 w.fport ^ put16 w.fgport ^ put16 (8 + n) ^ "\000\000" ^ Bytes.sub_string ubuf 0 n in
          let k = cksum (w.faddr ^ w.fgaddr ^ "\000\017" ^ put16 (String.length d) ^ d) in
          ip t 17 w.faddr w.fgaddr (String.sub d 0 6 ^ put16 (if k = 0 then 0xffff else k) ^ String.sub d 8 n);
          take ()
      | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> () in
    take ()) t.flows;
  let old, young = List.partition (fun w -> now -. w.used > 60.) t.flows in
  List.iter (fun w -> try Unix.close w.fsock with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()) old;
  t.flows <- young;
  List.iter (fun c ->
    let inflight = Int32.to_int (Int32.sub c.snd c.una) in
    if not c.hostfin && inflight + 1460 <= c.wnd then
      match Unix.read c.sock buf 0 1460 with
      | 0 -> c.hostfin <- true; tcp t c (fin lor ack) ""; c.snd <- Int32.add c.snd 1l
      | n -> tcp t c (psh lor ack) (Bytes.sub_string buf 0 n); c.snd <- Int32.add c.snd (Int32.of_int n)
      | exception Unix.Unix_error ((Unix.EAGAIN | Unix.EWOULDBLOCK), _, _) -> ()
      | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> c.hostfin <- true; tcp t c (fin lor ack) ""; c.snd <- Int32.add c.snd 1l) t.conns

(* a usb-net and its network; every network's host side polled (the
 * main loop's) *)
let nets = ref []

let usb ~path =
  let d = Usb.net ~path () in
  let t = create (Usb.net_input d) in
  Usb.net_output d (input t);
  nets := t :: !nets;
  d

let poll_all () = List.iter poll !nets

(* what every network carried since the start, and holds now *)
type totals = { from_guest : int; to_guest : int; tcp : int; udp : int; events : string list }

let totals () =
  List.fold_left (fun (a : totals) (t : t) ->
    { from_guest = a.from_guest + t.from_guest; to_guest = a.to_guest + t.to_guest; tcp = a.tcp + List.length t.conns;
      udp = a.udp + List.length t.flows; events = a.events @ t.events })
    { from_guest = 0; to_guest = 0; tcp = 0; udp = 0; events = [] } !nets
raspberry/usb/Usernet.mli
3839
(* The network behind a usb-net, as QEMU's user networking
 * (slirp) looks from the guest: the guest 10.0.2.15, the host and
 * gateway 10.0.2.2 (MAC 52:55:0a:00:02:02). ARP answered for 10.0.2.2,
 * an ICMP echo to it too (TTL 255, as QEMU's), a TCP connection to it
 * made to the host's 127.0.0.1 on the same port (refused: a RST), the
 * data relayed both ways in order, each side's FIN passed on. And
 * beyond the gateway, as slirp: a TCP connection to any other address
 * is one of the host's to that address; a UDP datagram is sent from a
 * socket of the host's and the answers brought back; 10.0.2.3 is the
 * name server, the host's own (/etc/resolv.conf's), so a guest that
 * has UDP resolves names. No retransmission (the guest's link is this
 * process: nothing is lost), no connection from the host, no ping
 * beyond the gateway.
 *
 * The guest's kernel has a whole network stack, and sends Ethernet
 * frames; the host gives an ordinary program sockets, not frames.
 * So this module is the other end of every conversation at once: it
 * plays the gateway's network card, and for each TCP connection the
 * guest opens it is a TCP peer on one side and the owner of a host
 * socket on the other.
 *
 *     guest's stack                 here                 the host
 *     ARP who has 10.0.2.2?  ->     "I do" (a made-up MAC)
 *     SYN to 10.0.2.2:80     ->     connect 127.0.0.1:80
 *                            <-     SYN+ACK (or RST: refused)
 *     data, seq n            ->     write to the socket; ACK back
 *                            <-     data read from the socket,
 *     ACK                    ->     under our own sequence numbers
 *     FIN                    ->     shutdown; and the socket's end
 *                            <-     of file is our FIN
 *
 * What a real TCP spends most of its code on is absent, and rightly:
 * a frame handed over in the same process is never lost, late or
 * out of order, so there is no timer, no retransmission and no
 * control of congestion. It is a way to see TCP's skeleton, the
 * handshake and the numbering of bytes, without what makes it hard.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * QEMU's user networking is slirp, a program of 1995 that gave
 * a TCP/IP connection to a home computer over a dial-up shell
 * account, with no privilege on the host: it answered the home
 * machine's packets with its own socket calls. The
 * same trick suited an emulator that should need no root and no
 * network device on the host, and 10.0.2.15 and 10.0.2.2 are its
 * defaults still.
 *
 * others:
 * The other way to network a guest is to give it real frames: a tap
 * device or a bridge on the host, and the guest is a machine on the
 * network, reachable from outside, at the price of privileges and
 * of configuration on the host. *)

type t

(* [create send]: frames for the guest given to send *)
val create : (string -> unit) -> t

(* a frame from the guest *)
val input : t -> string -> unit

(* the host's side polled: data from the connections to the guest *)
val poll : t -> unit

(* -device usb-net on [path]: the device, its network made; every
 * network polled (mini-qemu's main loop) *)
val usb : path:string -> Usb.device
val poll_all : unit -> unit

(* the host's name server, which 10.0.2.3 stands for (127.0.0.1 until
 * set) *)
val resolver : Unix.inet_addr ref

(* the host's clock, set by Main from its Cap.clock (0 before) *)
val clock : (unit -> float) ref

(* for who watches (Monitor): what every network carried since the
 * start (the frames' bytes each way), the connections and UDP
 * conversations it holds, and the last things that happened ("tcp
 * 93.184.216.34:80", "udp 10.0.2.3:53", "refused ..."), the newest
 * first *)
type totals = { from_guest : int; to_guest : int; tcp : int; udp : int; events : string list }
val totals : unit -> totals

(* The screen and the input devices, a record of functions at the edge
 * (plan_pi.md, decision 9): the board's framebuffer shown, the keys
 * pressed and the mouse moved in the window read back. SDL's (Sdl_display, the executable's
 * one module linking a C library), or none (-nographic, the tests: a
 * QMP screendump writes the framebuffer as PPM). *)

type event =
  | Key of int * bool              (* a HID usage, down *)
  | Motion of int * int            (* the mouse moved, relative *)
  | At of int * int                (* the mouse's place in the window, when it is not grabbed (tiny-machine's) *)
  | Button of int * bool           (* a mouse button (1 left, 2 right, 4 middle), down *)
  | Wheel of int                   (* -1 up *)
  | Quit

 * [stamp] another number when they have changed *)
type meter = { stamp : int; text : string; rows : int; pixels : string }

  present : Framebuffer.geometry -> string -> unit;   (* the pixels as the kernel wrote them *)
  poll : unit -> event list;
}

raspberry/video/Framebuffer.ml
2333
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Framebuffer.mli *)

type geometry = { width : int; height : int; depth : int; pitch : int; base : int }

type t = { mem : Memory.t; mutable geometry : geometry option }

let create mem = { mem; geometry = None }

let configure t g = t.geometry <- Some g

(* the screen as RGB bytes, 3 a pixel, row after row *)
let rgb t =
  match t.geometry with
  | None -> None
  | Some g ->
      let out = Bytes.create (g.width * g.height * 3) in
      let row = Bytes.create g.pitch in
      for y = 0 to g.height - 1 do
        Bytes.blit_string (Memory.read_string t.mem (g.base + (y * g.pitch)) g.pitch) 0 row 0 g.pitch;
        for x = 0 to g.width - 1 do
          let r, gr, b =
            match g.depth with
            | 16 ->
                let v = Bytes.get_uint16_le row (2 * x) in
                let r5 = (v lsr 11) land 31 and g6 = (v lsr 5) land 63 and b5 = v land 31 in
                (* shifted up, as QEMU's display: white is f8 fc f8 *)
                r5 lsl 3, g6 lsl 2, b5 lsl 3
            | 24 -> Char.code (Bytes.get row (3 * x)), Char.code (Bytes.get row ((3 * x) + 1)), Char.code (Bytes.get row ((3 * x) + 2))
            | _ ->
                (* 32 bits: red first, as 24's and as QEMU's board shows them
                 * (old: red in the word's bits 16 to 23, blue first: no kernel
                 * had asked 32 bits before mini-squeak, whose colours QEMU
                 * and this then showed differently) *)
                Char.code (Bytes.get row (4 * x)), Char.code (Bytes.get row ((4 * x) + 1)), Char.code (Bytes.get row ((4 * x) + 2)) in
          let o = 3 * ((y * g.width) + x) in
          Bytes.set out o (Char.chr r); Bytes.set out (o + 1) (Char.chr gr); Bytes.set out (o + 2) (Char.chr b)
        done
      done;
      Some (g.width, g.height, Bytes.to_string out)

(* the pixels as the kernel wrote them, pitch after pitch *)
let raw t = Option.map (fun g -> g, Memory.read_string t.mem g.base (g.pitch * g.height)) t.geometry

(* the same without a copy: the RAM's bytes, and where the pixels start *)
let direct t = Option.map (fun g -> let bytes, at = Memory.direct t.mem g.base (g.pitch * g.height) in g, bytes, at) t.geometry

let ppm (w, h, rgb) = Printf.sprintf "P6\n%d %d\n255\n" w h ^ rgb
raspberry/video/Framebuffer.mli
2047
(* The framebuffer's device side (plan_pi.md, decision 9): the geometry
 * the mailbox gave out (channel 1 or the property tags) and the pixels
 * in RAM, as RGB for a display: 16 bits (RGB565, xv6's), 24, 32 (XRGB).
 * Shown through the executable's display (SDL), written as PPM (QMP's
 * screendump).
 *
 * A framebuffer is the screen as an array in memory: a pixel is a
 * number at an address, and drawing is a store. The pixel at (x, y)
 * of a screen 16 bits deep:
 *
 *     base + y * pitch + x * 2        pitch: the bytes of a row
 *
 *     15       11 10        5 4        0
 *     |   red    |   green   |   blue   |    RGB565: 5, 6 and 5 bits
 *
 * (Green has the bit more: the eye tells greens apart best.) There
 * is no command to draw a line or a letter: the kernel's draw
 * device and, above it, the window system do all of that with
 * stores into this array, and the device's only work is to show
 * the array some tens of times a second. Here that is [raw] or
 * [direct] handed to a Display, or [rgb] made a PPM file.
 *
 * Where it stands: Devices' mailbox calls [configure] when the
 * kernel is given its framebuffer; Board's [frame] and [screen] are
 * this module's; at the other end of ix the pixels are mini-rio's
 * windows, through the kernel's draw device. *)

type geometry = { width : int; height : int; depth : int; pitch : int; base : int }

type t

val create : Memory.t -> t

(* the kernel was given a framebuffer *)
val configure : t -> geometry -> unit

(* width, height, 3 bytes a pixel, row after row; none before the kernel
 * asked for one *)
val rgb : t -> (int * int * string) option

(* the pixels as the kernel wrote them (a display's fast path: no
 * conversion; SDL has RGB565 textures) *)
val raw : t -> (geometry * string) option

(* the same in place, for a display that reads them many times a second
 * (a page's canvas): the RAM's bytes and where the pixels start in them *)
val direct : t -> (geometry * Bytes.t * int) option

(* as a raw PPM (P6) *)
val ppm : int * int * string -> string
raspberry/video/Sdl_display.ml
10003
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* The display in an SDL window (tsdl): the framebuffer as a streaming
 * texture in its own format (RGB565 for 16 bits: no conversion), sized
 * at its first frame, drawn when it changed; the keys by SDL's
 * scancodes, which are USB HID usages (SDL took them from there); the
 * mouse, relative as a USB mouse is: a click grabs the host's pointer
 * (SDL's relative mode: its motion the guest's, the host cursor gone),
 * Ctrl-Alt-G lets it go, as QEMU's window does; or, [absolute], the
 * pointer left to the host and its place in the window given (for a
 * machine whose mouse is not a USB one: tiny-machine's window). The
 * window can be resized, the frame drawn as large as fits in it, its
 * proportions kept; [fit] starts it large (tiny-machine's 640 by 480
 * is small on a large screen). The one module of mini-qemu linking a C library (plan_pi.md, decision 9). *)

open Tsdl

let ok = function Ok v -> v | Error _ -> failwith ("SDL: " ^ Sdl.get_error ())

(* the texture's format for the framebuffer's depth *)
let format = function
  | 16 -> Sdl.Pixel.format_rgb565
  | 24 -> Sdl.Pixel.format_rgb24
  | _ -> Sdl.Pixel.format_rgba32   (* red first, as QEMU's board (Framebuffer) *)

(* The jack's samples (Pwm) to the host's sound card, by SDL's queue: 512
 * at a time, the card opened at the rate the first ones come at (and
 * again when the guest changes it). The card plays at our clock, the
 * board at its own: when the board is slower, the queue runs empty and
 * SDL plays silence, the sound broken (the WAV of -audiodev is the
 * board's time, whole); when it is ahead by more than half a second
 * (a window's loop keeps it from that), what waits is dropped. A host
 * with no card is silent. *)
let audio () : rate:int -> int -> int -> unit =
  let chunk = 512 in
  let samples = Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int16_signed Bigarray.c_layout (2 * chunk) and n = ref 0 in
  (* the card and its rate; None once it could not be opened *)
  let card = ref (Some None) in
  let open_at rate =
    (match !card with Some (Some (d, _)) -> Sdl.close_audio_device d | _ -> ());
    card := None;
    match Sdl.init_sub_system Sdl.Init.audio with
    | Error _ -> ()
    | Ok () ->
        let want = { Sdl.as_freq = rate; as_format = Sdl.Audio.s16_sys; as_channels = 2; as_silence = 0; as_samples = 1024; as_size = 0l; as_callback = None } in
        (match Sdl.open_audio_device None false want 0 with
         | Error _ -> ()
         | Ok (d, _) -> Sdl.pause_audio_device d false; card := Some (Some (d, rate))) in
  fun ~rate left right ->
    samples.{2 * !n} <- left;
    samples.{(2 * !n) + 1} <- right;
    incr n;
    if !n = chunk then begin
      n := 0;
      (match !card with
       | Some (Some (_, r)) when r = rate -> ()
       | Some _ -> open_at rate
       | None -> ());
      match !card with
      | Some (Some (d, _)) ->
          if Sdl.get_queued_audio_size d > 2 * rate then Sdl.clear_queued_audio d;
          ignore (Sdl.queue_audio d samples)
      | _ -> ()
    end

let create ?(absolute = false) ?(fit = false) ?meter ~title () =
  ok (Sdl.init Sdl.Init.video);
  let window = ref None and texture = ref None and shape = ref None and last = ref "" in
  (* the meter's strip: its texture, the stamp it was drawn at, its text *)
  let strip = ref None and stamp = ref (-1) and said = ref "" and grabbed = ref false in
  let name () = (if !said = "" then title else title ^ "  " ^ !said) ^ (if !grabbed then " (Ctrl-Alt-G releases the mouse)" else "") in
  let pixels = ref (Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int8_unsigned Bigarray.c_layout 0) in
  (* the last frame drawn again: a window resized or uncovered has lost it *)
  let again = ref (fun () -> ()) in
  let present (g : Framebuffer.geometry) data =
    let m = Option.map (fun f -> f ~width:g.width) meter in
    let rows = match m with Some (m : Display.meter) -> m.rows | None -> 0 in
    if !shape <> Some g then begin
      (match !window with
       | None ->
           (* the window can be resized: the frame is drawn as large as
            * fits in it (render_set_logical_size, below, which also gives
            * the mouse's place in the frame's pixels). [fit]: it starts
            * at the largest whole number of times the frame that three
            * quarters of the screen's height hold *)
           let times =
             if not fit then 1
             else match Sdl.get_current_display_mode 0 with
               | Ok mode -> max 1 (mode.Sdl.dm_h * 3 / 4 / (g.height + rows))
               | Error _ -> 1 in
           let win = ok (Sdl.create_window title ~w:(times * g.width) ~h:(times * (g.height + rows)) Sdl.Window.(windowed + resizable)) in
           window := Some (win, ok (Sdl.create_renderer win))
       | Some (win, _) -> Sdl.set_window_size win ~w:g.width ~h:(g.height + rows));
      let _, r = Option.get !window in
      ok (Sdl.render_set_logical_size r g.width (g.height + rows));
      strip := (if rows > 0 then Some (ok (Sdl.create_texture r Sdl.Pixel.format_rgb24 Sdl.Texture.access_streaming ~w:g.width ~h:rows)) else None);
      stamp := -1;
      texture := Some (ok (Sdl.create_texture r (format g.depth) Sdl.Texture.access_streaming ~w:g.width ~h:g.height));
      pixels := Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int8_unsigned Bigarray.c_layout (String.length data);
      shape := Some g; last := ""
    end;
    (* the meter's strip and line, when they have changed *)
    let metered =
      match m, !strip with
      | Some m, Some tex when m.stamp <> !stamp ->
          stamp := m.stamp; said := m.text;
          let px = Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int8_unsigned Bigarray.c_layout (String.length m.pixels) in
          String.iteri (fun i c -> Bigarray.Array1.unsafe_set px i (Char.code c)) m.pixels;
          ok (Sdl.update_texture tex None px (g.width * 3));
          Option.iter (fun (win, _) -> Sdl.set_window_title win (name ())) !window;
          true
      | _ -> false in
    let screen = Sdl.Rect.create ~x:0 ~y:0 ~w:g.width ~h:g.height in
    let draw r tex =
      ok (Sdl.render_clear r);
      ok (Sdl.render_copy ~dst:screen r tex);
      Option.iter (fun s -> ok (Sdl.render_copy ~dst:(Sdl.Rect.create ~x:0 ~y:g.height ~w:g.width ~h:rows) r s)) !strip;
      Sdl.render_present r in
    again := (fun () -> match !window, !texture with Some (_, r), Some tex -> draw r tex | _ -> ());
    (* a frame like the last one: nothing to draw *)
    if data = !last then (if metered then let _, r = Option.get !window in draw r (Option.get !texture))
    else begin
      (* OPTIMIZATION: only the rows that changed, the first to the last,
       * are copied and given to the texture: a cursor that moves is 32
       * rows of the 768, and the whole frame, a byte at a time, was 10
       * ms of each 33, which the board's time lost
       * (docs/plans/plan_mini_qemu_speed.md).
       * old: String.iteri (fun i c -> Bigarray.Array1.unsafe_set px i (Char.code c)) data;
       *      ok (Sdl.update_texture tex None px g.pitch) *)
      let same y = String.length !last = String.length data && String.sub data (y * g.pitch) g.pitch = String.sub !last (y * g.pitch) g.pitch in
      let lo = ref 0 and hi = ref g.height in
      while !lo < !hi - 1 && same !lo do incr lo done;
      while !hi - 1 > !lo && same (!hi - 1) do decr hi done;
      last := data;
      let px = !pixels in
      for i = !lo * g.pitch to (!hi * g.pitch) - 1 do Bigarray.Array1.unsafe_set px i (Char.code (String.unsafe_get data i)) done;
      let _, r = Option.get !window and tex = Option.get !texture in
      ok (Sdl.update_texture tex (Some (Sdl.Rect.create ~x:0 ~y:!lo ~w:g.width ~h:(!hi - !lo)))
            (Bigarray.Array1.sub px (!lo * g.pitch) ((!hi - !lo) * g.pitch)) g.pitch);
      (* old: render_clear, render_copy r tex (the whole window), render_present *)
      draw r tex
    end in
  let e = Sdl.Event.create () in
  let grab on =
    grabbed := on;
    ok (Sdl.set_relative_mouse_mode on);
    Option.iter (fun (win, _) -> Sdl.set_window_title win (name ())) !window in
  let button b = if b = Sdl.Button.left then 1 else if b = Sdl.Button.right then 2 else if b = Sdl.Button.middle then 4 else 0 in
  let poll () =
    let evs = ref [] in
    let add ev = evs := ev :: !evs in
    while Sdl.poll_event (Some e) do
      (* the event's type, one of Sdl.Event's constants *)
      let k = Sdl.Event.(get e typ) in
      let is t = k = t in
      if is Sdl.Event.quit then add Display.Quit
      else if is Sdl.Event.window_event then
        (match Sdl.Event.(window_event_enum (get e window_event_id)) with `Exposed | `Size_changed -> !again () | _ -> ())
      else if is Sdl.Event.key_down && !grabbed && Sdl.Event.(get e keyboard_keycode) = Sdl.K.g
              && Sdl.get_mod_state () land Sdl.Kmod.ctrl <> 0 && Sdl.get_mod_state () land Sdl.Kmod.alt <> 0 then
        grab false
      else if (is Sdl.Event.key_down || is Sdl.Event.key_up) && Sdl.Event.(get e keyboard_repeat) = 0 then
        add (Display.Key (Sdl.Event.(get e keyboard_scancode), is Sdl.Event.key_down))
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_down && not !grabbed && not absolute then grab true   (* the grabbing click is the host's *)
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_down || is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_up then begin
        let b = button Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_button_button) in
        if b <> 0 then add (Display.Button (b, is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_down))
      end
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_motion && absolute then
        add (Display.At (Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_motion_x), Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_motion_y)))
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_motion && !grabbed then
        add (Display.Motion (Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_motion_xrel), Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_motion_yrel)))
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_wheel && !grabbed then add (Display.Wheel (- Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_wheel_y)))
    done;
    List.rev !evs in
  { Display.present; poll }
raspberry/web/MiniQemuWeb.ml
27052
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-qemu in a web page (plan_web.md, stage 1): the Pi 1's board
 * (Board) compiled by js_of_ocaml, its framebuffer a canvas, its UART
 * the page's text, a USB keyboard and mouse the page's. Main.ml is the
 * same board in a terminal and an SDL window, by QEMU's command line.
 *
 * The page gives three elements, by their ids: screen (a canvas),
 * console (the text), status (a line). What is booted is fetched: a
 * kernel's image, loaded at 0x8000, and an SD card's; their addresses
 * are the page's own variable, mini_qemu = { kernel: ..., card: ... },
 * or the address's (?kernel=kernel.img&card=card.img.gz), or
 * kernel.img beside the page and no card. A name that ends in .gz
 * (before a ?v=1, if any) is undone by the browser (DecompressionStream). The card stays in
 * memory: what is written to it lasts as long as the page.
 *
 * The keys are the UART's, a byte each (the kernel's console echoes
 * them), unless the screen was clicked: then they are a keyboard's,
 * down and up, by where the key is (the event's code: a USB usage is a
 * place on the keyboard too). The keyboard and the mouse are the
 * page's own, for a kernel built for a page ([usb] says how, and the
 * way of a Pi's kernel, ?input=usb: a USB keyboard and mouse on the
 * board).
 *
 * The board runs in turns of some milliseconds, one after the other
 * while it is behind its clock ([run]); a frame of the browser's shows
 * what changed on the screen. The board's clock goes by its
 * instructions, [ips] to a microsecond: 30 in a terminal; here what
 * the browser is measured to run ([paced]), from 6, or ?ips=N. The
 * status line says both: the instructions a second, and the board's
 * seconds for one of ours.
 *
 * What makes it fast enough to use, each a switch here and each apart
 * from the board's simple way: the instructions run often translated
 * to JavaScript (Jit, ?jit=0), memdraw's general loop run by the host
 * for a kernel that asks (Hostdraw, ?draw=kernel), the screen's rows
 * that changed and not all of it (?screen=whole), the turns
 * (?run=frames), the pace (?ips=N).
 *
 * All that the page's address may say, after a ? and with & between
 * them ([start] reads them):
 *
 *   kernel=URL     the kernel's image (default: the page's variable,
 *                  then kernel.img); card=URL the SD card's (none)
 *   jit=0          no translation: every instruction by the interpreter
 *   hot=N          a block is translated once run N times (200)
 *   draw=kernel    the kernel's own drawing loop, the host's not offered
 *   input=usb      a USB keyboard and mouse on the board, as a Pi's
 *                  (the kernel's cursor, drawn by it); what a kernel
 *                  not built for a page needs
 *   screen=whole   the whole screen drawn at each frame
 *   show=N         the screen shown each N frames of the browser's (3)
 *   run=frames     the board run inside the browser's frames, a slice
 *                  each, and not in turns between them
 *   ips=N          N instructions to the board's microsecond, fixed
 *                  (the pace measured otherwise, from 6)
 *
 * So ?jit=0&draw=kernel&input=usb&run=frames&screen=whole&ips=6 is the
 * page of before these, with the Pi's kernel by kernel=.
 *
 * An int has 32 bits here (Bits, in machine/, says what that asks). *)

module Js = Js_of_ocaml.Js
module U = Js_of_ocaml.Js.Unsafe

let call o name args = U.meth_call o name args
let str s = U.inject (Js.string s)
let get o name = U.get o (Js.string name)
let set o name v = U.set o (Js.string name) v
let document = get U.global "document"
let element id = call document "getElementById" [| str id |]
let listen o name f = ignore (call o "addEventListener" [| str name; U.inject (Js.wrap_callback f) |])
let now () : float = Js.float_of_number (call (get U.global "performance") "now" [||])
let int_of o name : int = truncate (Js.float_of_number (get o name))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The console: the UART's bytes as the page's text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the last [kept] bytes; a backspace takes one back *)
let kept = 20000
let text = Buffer.create 1024
let text_changed = ref false

let put ch =
  (match ch with
   | '\b' -> if Buffer.length text > 0 then Buffer.truncate text (Buffer.length text - 1)
   | '\r' -> ()
   | ch -> Buffer.add_char text ch);
  if Buffer.length text > 2 * kept then begin
    let last = Buffer.sub text (Buffer.length text - kept) kept in
    Buffer.clear text; Buffer.add_string text last
  end;
  text_changed := true

(* the cursor: an element of its own (the page's style makes it a block
 * that blinks), put back after the text each time *)
let cursor = lazy (
  let c = call document "createElement" [| str "span" |] in
  set c "id" (Js.string "cursor");
  set c "textContent" (Js.string "\xc2\xa0");
  c)

let show_text () =
  if !text_changed then begin
    text_changed := false;
    let e = element "console" in
    set e "textContent" (Js.bytestring (Buffer.contents text));
    ignore (call e "appendChild" [| U.inject (Lazy.force cursor) |]);
    set e "scrollTop" (get e "scrollHeight")
  end

let status s = set (element "status") "textContent" (Js.string s)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The keys and the mouse *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a key's byte for the UART; control with a letter its control
 * character; Delete is Plan 9's interrupt *)
let key_byte e =
  let key = Js.to_string (get e "key") in
  match key with
  | "Enter" -> Some 10 | "Backspace" -> Some 8 | "Tab" -> Some 9 | "Escape" -> Some 27 | "Delete" -> Some 127
  | _ when String.length key = 1 && Char.code key.[0] < 127 ->
      let c = Char.code key.[0] in
      if Js.to_bool (get e "metaKey") then None else if Js.to_bool (get e "ctrlKey") then Some (c land 31) else Some c
  | _ -> None

(* a key's USB usage (HID's keyboard page), by the event's code *)
let usages = [
  "Enter", 40; "Escape", 41; "Backspace", 42; "Tab", 43; "Space", 44; "Minus", 45; "Equal", 46; "BracketLeft", 47;
  "BracketRight", 48; "Backslash", 49; "Semicolon", 51; "Quote", 52; "Backquote", 53; "Comma", 54; "Period", 55;
  "Slash", 56; "CapsLock", 57; "Insert", 73; "Home", 74; "PageUp", 75; "Delete", 76; "End", 77; "PageDown", 78;
  "ArrowRight", 79; "ArrowLeft", 80; "ArrowDown", 81; "ArrowUp", 82; "ControlLeft", 224; "ShiftLeft", 225;
  "AltLeft", 226; "MetaLeft", 227; "ControlRight", 228; "ShiftRight", 229; "AltRight", 230; "Digit0", 39 ]

let usage code =
  let n = String.length code in
  if n = 4 && String.sub code 0 3 = "Key" then Some (4 + Char.code code.[3] - Char.code 'A')
  else if n = 6 && String.sub code 0 5 = "Digit" && code.[5] <> '0' then Some (30 + Char.code code.[5] - Char.code '1')
  else if n >= 2 && code.[0] = 'F' && int_of_string_opt (String.sub code 1 (n - 1)) <> None then
    Some (57 + int_of_string (String.sub code 1 (n - 1)))
  else List.assoc_opt code usages

(* How the keys and the mouse reach the kernel. [usb] off, the way of a
 * kernel built for a page (Board.host_key, host_pointer; mini-9pi's
 * Kweb): the keys as they are pressed, the mouse where it is on the
 * canvas, and the cursor is the browser's own, in the shape the kernel
 * gives ([cursor_show]): it follows the hand whatever the board's
 * speed. (old, and [usb] on, ?input=usb, for a kernel of the Pi: a USB
 * keyboard and mouse on the board, the mouse's moves relative and kept
 * in the canvas, the cursor drawn by the kernel in the framebuffer: a
 * mouse that moved took 5 of the 6 million instructions of a second.) *)
let usb = ref false

let on_screen () = get document "activeElement" == element "screen"

let listen_keys board =
  let key down e =
    if on_screen () then begin
      (match usage (Js.to_string (get e "code")) with
       | Some u -> if not (Js.to_bool (get e "repeat")) then (if !usb then Board.key board u down else Board.host_key u down)
       | None -> ());
      ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||])
    end
    else if down then
      match key_byte e with
      | Some b -> Board.input board (Char.chr b); ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||])
      | None -> () in
  listen document "keydown" (key true);
  listen document "keyup" (key false)

(* the mouse: how far it moved since the last frame, as one event (a
 * window's are synced so by QEMU); the browser's buttons are 0 left, 1
 * middle, 2 right, the USB mouse's bits 1 left, 2 right, 4 middle *)
let moved_x = ref 0 and moved_y = ref 0

(* the page's way: where the mouse is on the framebuffer (the canvas
 * may be shown smaller than its pixels) and its buttons (the browser's
 * bits are 1 left, 2 right, 4 middle; Plan 9's 1 left, 2 middle, 4
 * right). A button's change is given at once; a move waits for a frame
 * ([mouse_frame]) *)
let at_x = ref 0 and at_y = ref 0 and at_buttons = ref 0 and at_moved = ref false

let mouse_at canvas e =
  let scale v shown real = if shown <= 0 then v else v * real / shown in
  at_x := scale (int_of e "offsetX") (int_of canvas "clientWidth") (int_of canvas "width");
  at_y := scale (int_of e "offsetY") (int_of canvas "clientHeight") (int_of canvas "height");
  let b = int_of e "buttons" in
  at_buttons := (b land 1) lor (if b land 4 <> 0 then 2 else 0) lor (if b land 2 <> 0 then 4 else 0)

let listen_mouse board canvas =
  listen canvas "mousemove" (fun e ->
    if !usb then (moved_x := !moved_x + int_of e "movementX"; moved_y := !moved_y + int_of e "movementY")
    else (mouse_at canvas e; at_moved := true));
  let button down e =
    if !usb then begin
      let b = match int_of e "button" with 0 -> 1 | 1 -> 4 | 2 -> 2 | _ -> 0 in
      if b <> 0 then Board.pointer board [ Usb.Button (b, down) ]
    end
    else (mouse_at canvas e; at_moved := false; Board.host_pointer !at_x !at_y !at_buttons);
    ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||]) in
  listen canvas "mousedown" (fun e ->
    ignore (call canvas "focus" [||]);
    (* (not everywhere: a browser without a screen has none to keep it in) *)
    if !usb then (try ignore (call canvas "requestPointerLock" [||]) with _ -> ());
    button true e);
  listen canvas "mouseup" (button false);
  listen canvas "contextmenu" (fun e -> ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||]))

(* The page's way: a move is given every [move_every] frames, 15 times
 * a second, and 30 while a button is down (a window swept, a menu): the
 * cursor does not wait for the kernel, and each move given is a
 * window system's work (mini-rio's: 60,000 instructions) *)
let move_every = 4

let mouse_frame board frames =
  if not !usb then begin
    if !at_moved && frames mod (if !at_buttons <> 0 then move_every / 2 else move_every) = 0 then begin
      at_moved := false; Board.host_pointer !at_x !at_y !at_buttons
    end
  end
  else if !moved_x <> 0 || !moved_y <> 0 then begin
    Board.pointer board [ Usb.Rel_x !moved_x; Usb.Rel_y !moved_y ];
    moved_x := 0; moved_y := 0
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen: a canvas *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A canvas's pixel is four bytes, red, green, blue and how opaque: one
 * word of 32 bits (the browsers' machines being little-endian). The
 * framebuffer's 16 bits (RGB565, what the kernels ask) through a table
 * of its 65536 colours; 24 and 32 bits byte by byte, red first.
 *
 * The pixels are read where they are, in the board's RAM (a bytes of
 * OCaml is an array of bytes of JavaScript's here: no copy), as words
 * of 16 bits when that is their depth. (old: Board.frame's string of
 * them, compared with the last one shown: making a megabyte's string
 * 20 times a second was a quarter of the page's time, by Chrome's
 * profile; [copied] is that way still, also for a framebuffer at an
 * odd address.) *)
let copied = ref false

type screen = { canvas : U.any; context : U.any; mutable picture : U.any; mutable words : U.any;
                mutable shape : Framebuffer.geometry option; mutable shown : string; colours : U.any }

let screen_open canvas =
  let colour v =
    let r = (v lsr 11) land 31 and g = (v lsr 5) land 63 and b = v land 31 in
    (255 lsl 24) lor (((b lsl 3) lor (b lsr 2)) lsl 16) lor (((g lsl 2) lor (g lsr 4)) lsl 8) lor ((r lsl 3) lor (r lsr 2)) in
  let colours = U.new_obj (get U.global "Uint32Array") [| U.inject 65536 |] in
  for v = 0 to 65535 do U.set colours v (colour v) done;
  { canvas; context = call canvas "getContext" [| str "2d" |]; picture = U.inject 0; words = U.inject 0; shape = None; shown = ""; colours }

let screen_shape s (g : Framebuffer.geometry) =
  if s.shape <> Some g then begin
    set s.canvas "width" g.width; set s.canvas "height" g.height;
    s.picture <- call s.context "createImageData" [| U.inject g.width; U.inject g.height |];
    s.words <- U.new_obj (get U.global "Uint32Array") [| U.inject (get (get s.picture "data") "buffer") |];
    s.shape <- Some g; s.shown <- ""
  end

let screen_put s = ignore (call s.context "putImageData" [| U.inject s.picture; U.inject 0; U.inject 0 |])

(* by a copy *)
let screen_show_copied s board =
  match Board.frame board with
  | None -> ()
  | Some (g, pixels) ->
      screen_shape s g;
      if pixels <> s.shown then begin
        s.shown <- pixels;
        let byte i = Char.code (String.unsafe_get pixels i) in
        for y = 0 to g.height - 1 do
          let row = y * g.pitch and out = y * g.width in
          if g.depth = 16 then
            for x = 0 to g.width - 1 do
              U.set s.words (out + x) (U.get s.colours (byte (row + (2 * x)) lor (byte (row + (2 * x) + 1) lsl 8)))
            done
          else begin
            let n = g.depth / 8 in
            for x = 0 to g.width - 1 do
              let o = row + (n * x) in
              U.set s.words (out + x) ((255 lsl 24) lor (byte (o + 2) lsl 16) lor (byte (o + 1) lsl 8) lor byte o)
            done
          end
        done;
        screen_put s
      end

(* Only the rows written since the last time, when the board knows them
 * (Board.host_rows: a kernel built for a page writes its pixels by the
 * board's moves), and all of the screen every [whole_every] times (a
 * kernel also writes there by itself: its console's text before the
 * draw device). (old, and [whole] always: the megabyte converted and
 * put on the canvas 20 times a second, a screen that waits too.) *)
let whole = ref false
let whole_every = 10
let shows = ref 0

let screen_show s board =
  match Board.frame_direct board with
  | Some (g, bytes, at) when not !copied && g.depth = 16 && at land 1 = 0 ->
      let reshaped = s.shape <> Some g in
      screen_shape s g;
      Board.host_watch ~base:at ~pitch:g.pitch ~rows:g.height;
      incr shows;
      let rows =
        match Board.host_rows () with
        | _ when !whole || reshaped || !shows mod whole_every = 0 -> Some (0, g.height)
        | r -> r in
      (match rows with
       | None -> ()
       | Some (y0, y1) ->
           let ram = Js_of_ocaml.Typed_array.Bytes.to_uint8Array bytes in
           let pixels = U.new_obj (get U.global "Uint16Array")
               [| U.inject (get ram "buffer"); U.inject (int_of ram "byteOffset" + at); U.inject (g.pitch * g.height / 2) |] in
           let half = g.pitch / 2 and words = s.words and colours = s.colours in
           for y = y0 to y1 - 1 do
             let row = y * half and out = y * g.width in
             for x = 0 to g.width - 1 do
               U.set words (out + x) (U.get colours (U.get pixels (row + x)))
             done
           done;
           ignore (call s.context "putImageData"
                     [| U.inject s.picture; U.inject 0; U.inject 0; U.inject 0; U.inject y0; U.inject g.width; U.inject (y1 - y0) |]))
  | _ -> screen_show_copied s board

(* The cursor the kernel gave (Board.host_shape: its offset, then 16 by
 * 16 bits twice, clr and set), as the canvas's own: white where clr,
 * black where set, through a small canvas and its picture's address *)
let cursor_shown = ref 0

let cursor_show canvas =
  let n, shape = !Board.host_shape in
  if n <> !cursor_shown && String.length shape = 66 then begin
    cursor_shown := n;
    let signed i = let v = Char.code shape.[i] in if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v in
    let small = call document "createElement" [| str "canvas" |] in
    set small "width" 16; set small "height" 16;
    let context = call small "getContext" [| str "2d" |] in
    let picture = call context "createImageData" [| U.inject 16; U.inject 16 |] in
    let data = get picture "data" in
    for k = 0 to 255 do
      let bit at = Char.code shape.[at + (k / 8)] land (0x80 lsr (k land 7)) <> 0 in
      let clr = bit 2 and black = bit 34 in
      let v = if black then 0 else 255 in
      U.set data (4 * k) v; U.set data ((4 * k) + 1) v; U.set data ((4 * k) + 2) v;
      U.set data ((4 * k) + 3) (if clr || black then 255 else 0)
    done;
    ignore (call context "putImageData" [| U.inject picture; U.inject 0; U.inject 0 |]);
    let url = Js.to_string (call small "toDataURL" [||]) in
    let spot v = max 0 (min 15 (- v)) in
    set (get canvas "style") "cursor" (Js.string (Printf.sprintf "url(%s) %d %d, crosshair" url (spot (signed 0)) (spot (signed 1))))
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The loop: a frame's instructions, then what is shown *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the milliseconds of a frame the board may take (of 16.7 at 60 frames
 * a second: the rest is the screen's and the browser's; old: 12, which
 * left a sixth of the time idle by Chrome's profile); the screen every
 * [screen_every] frames (its megabyte is converted each time) *)
let budget = 14.
let screen_every = ref 3
(* a turn of the board, milliseconds (the loop: [run]) *)
let turn = 8.
let by_frames = ref false

let translated = ref true

(* The board's pace follows the browser ([paced]; ?ips=N: N, fixed).
 * The board's second is so many instructions, and a second of ours
 * should be about one of the board's: fewer than the browser runs, and
 * a game has fewer frames than it could; more, and the board's clock
 * is slow, a game in slow motion. What the browser runs is measured
 * over the frames that used all of their time ([busy]), and the pace
 * moved a third of the way to a tenth over it each second (over: the
 * faster the pace, the fewer of the kernel's ticks an instruction, and
 * the more the browser runs; a board's clock a little slow is the
 * better trade); when no frame did and the board ran all its pace
 * allowed, the pace is tried a quarter higher. It is 4
 * million a second when the interpreter runs cold code, 13 when a
 * game's loop is translated (Chrome, 2026-10-11). *)
let paced = ref true

let run ~ips kernel card =
  let sd = Option.map (fun (b : Bytes.t) : Sdhost.storage ->
    { read = (fun off len -> Bytes.sub_string b off len); write = (fun off data -> Bytes.blit_string data 0 b off (String.length data));
      size = Bytes.length b }) card in
  let board = Board.create { pi2 = false; ram_size = 512 * 1024 * 1024; ips; log = ignore; usb_devices = (if !usb then [ "usb-kbd"; "usb-mouse" ] else []); sd;
                             serial0 = put; serial1 = ignore; console = 0 } in
  Board.load_raw board ~addr:0x8000 kernel;
  (* the instructions run often translated to JavaScript (?jit=0: all by the interpreter) *)
  if !translated then Jit.attach board;
  let canvas = element "screen" in
  let screen = screen_open canvas in
  listen_keys board; listen_mouse board canvas;
  let last = ref (now ()) and frames = ref 0 in
  let pace = ref ips and busy_ms = ref 0. and busy_ran = ref 0 in
  (* what the status says: the instructions and the board's time since it was said *)
  let ran = ref 0 and since = ref (now ()) and board_since = ref 0 in
  (* The board runs in turns of [turn] milliseconds, one after the other
   * while it is behind its clock (a message to the page itself between
   * two: the browser draws and hears the keys there), every few
   * milliseconds when it waits. What is shown is a frame's
   * ([frame]). (old, and [by_frames], ?run=frames: the board run in
   * the frame's function, [budget] milliseconds of each 16.7; a frame
   * that long made Chrome draw every other one, and the board then ran
   * 14 ms of every 33: 4 parts in 10 of the time were nobody's.) *)
  let stopped = ref false and owed = ref 0. in
  let turn_of ms =
    let start = now () in
    (* the board's microseconds due: a quarter of a second at most (a page left and come back to) *)
    (* (old: until Board.now board is due, an address of time: under
     * js_of_ocaml the board's microseconds wrap after 35 minutes, and
     * the page then stopped. Now a count of them from this turn's
     * first.) *)
    (* ([owed]: what the board's clock is behind ours, less what it went
     * ahead: a board that waits skips to its next tick, 10 ms at once,
     * and with a turn every 4 ms its clock went twice as fast as ours) *)
    owed := Float.min 250_000. (!owed +. (1000. *. (start -. !last)));
    let due = truncate !owed and from = Board.now board and before = !ran in
    last := start;
    match
      while Board.now board - from < due && now () -. start < ms do
        Board.run board ~batch:4096;
        List.iter (fun (c : Status.cpu) -> ran := !ran + c.ran) (Board.where board)
      done;
      owed := !owed -. float_of_int (Board.now board - from);
      (* (a turn that used its time: what the browser can do) *)
      let took = now () -. start in
      if took >= ms then (busy_ms := !busy_ms +. took; busy_ran := !busy_ran + (!ran - before); true) else false
    with
    | exception e -> stopped := true; status ("mini-qemu: " ^ Printexc.to_string e); false
    | busy -> busy in
  let channel = U.new_obj (get U.global "MessageChannel") [||] in
  let again () = ignore (call (get channel "port2") "postMessage" [| U.inject 0 |]) in
  let rec turns _ =
    if not !stopped then begin
      if turn_of turn then again ()
      else ignore (call U.global "setTimeout" [| U.inject (Js.wrap_callback turns); U.inject 4 |])
    end in
  set (get channel "port1") "onmessage" (U.inject (Js.wrap_callback turns));
  let rec frame _ =
    let start = now () in
    if !by_frames then ignore (turn_of budget);
    if not !stopped then begin
        mouse_frame board !frames;
        incr frames;
        if !frames mod !screen_every = 0 then screen_show screen board;
        show_text ();
        if not !usb then cursor_show canvas;
        if start -. !since > 1000. then begin
          let s = (start -. !since) /. 1000. in
          status (Printf.sprintf "%.1f million instructions a second; the board's clock: %.2f s for one of ours"
                    (float_of_int !ran /. s /. 1e6) (float_of_int (Board.now board - !board_since) /. 1e6 /. s));
          if !paced then begin
            (* (most of the second: a few slow turns, a block translated,
             * the collector, are not the browser's speed) *)
            if !busy_ms > 500. *. s then begin
              let can = float_of_int !busy_ran /. !busy_ms /. 1000. *. (if !by_frames then budget /. 16.7 else 0.9) in
              pace := max 3 (min 60 (truncate (((2. *. float_of_int !pace) +. (1.1 *. can)) /. 3. +. 0.5)))
            end
            (* (the browser kept up, and the board ran nearly all its
             * pace allows: it may be able to run more) *)
            else if float_of_int !ran >= 0.85 *. float_of_int !pace *. 1e6 *. s then pace := min 60 (!pace + max 1 (!pace / 4));
            Board.set_ips board !pace
          end;
          busy_ms := 0.; busy_ran := 0;
          ran := 0; since := start; board_since := Board.now board
        end;
        ignore (call U.global "requestAnimationFrame" [| U.inject (Js.wrap_callback frame) |])
    end in
  if not !by_frames then turns ();
  frame ()

(* a file's bytes, as the buffer the browser read; a .gz undone on the
 * way; k with None if it is not there *)
let fetch name k =
  let failed _ = k None in
  let callback f = U.inject (Js.wrap_callback f) in
  let got response =
    if not (Js.to_bool (get response "ok")) then failed ()
    else begin
      let response =
        (* (the name before a ?v=1, which a page adds so that a new file is fetched) *)
        if Filename.check_suffix (List.hd (String.split_on_char '?' name)) ".gz" then
          U.new_obj (get U.global "Response") [| U.inject (call (get response "body") "pipeThrough"
            [| U.inject (U.new_obj (get U.global "DecompressionStream") [| str "gzip" |]) |]) |]
        else response in
      ignore (call (call response "arrayBuffer" [||]) "then" [| callback (fun b -> k (Some b)); callback failed |])
    end in
  ignore (call (call U.global "fetch" [| str name |]) "then" [| callback got; callback failed |])

let () =
  let search = U.new_obj (get U.global "URLSearchParams") [| U.inject (get (get U.global "location") "search") |] in
  let text v = Js.Opt.to_option (Js.Opt.map (Js.Opt.option (Js.Optdef.to_option v)) Js.to_string) in
  let page = Js.Optdef.to_option (get U.global "mini_qemu") in
  let of_address name = Js.Opt.to_option (Js.Opt.map (call search "get" [| str name |]) Js.to_string) in
  let param name = match page with Some o -> text (get o name) | None -> of_address name in
  let kernel = Option.value (param "kernel") ~default:"kernel.img" in
  let ips = match Option.bind (of_address "ips") int_of_string_opt with Some n when n > 0 -> paced := false; n | _ -> 6 in
  usb := of_address "input" = Some "usb";
  translated := of_address "jit" <> Some "0";
  (match Option.bind (of_address "hot") int_of_string_opt with Some n when n > 0 -> Jit.threshold := n | _ -> ());
  whole := of_address "screen" = Some "whole";
  by_frames := of_address "run" = Some "frames";
  (match Option.bind (of_address "show") int_of_string_opt with Some n when n > 0 -> screen_every := n | _ -> ());
  Board.host_cursor := not !usb;
  (* memdraw's general loop by the host, for a kernel that asks (?draw=kernel: not) *)
  if of_address "draw" <> Some "kernel" then Hostdraw.install ();
  let missing name = status ("mini-qemu: " ^ name ^ " could not be fetched") in
  let start kernel card =
    status "starting";
    try run ~ips (Js_of_ocaml.Typed_array.String.of_arrayBuffer kernel) (Option.map Js_of_ocaml.Typed_array.Bytes.of_arrayBuffer card)
    with e -> status ("mini-qemu: " ^ Printexc.to_string e) in
  status ("loading " ^ kernel);
  fetch kernel (function
    | None -> missing kernel
    | Some image ->
        match param "card" with
        | None -> start image None
        | Some c -> status ("loading " ^ c); fetch c (function None -> missing c | Some card -> start image (Some card)))

(* See Hostdraw.mli *)

let drawn = ref 0
let declined = ref 0

(* the chans seen, made once *)
let chans : (int * int, Memchan.t option) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 16
let chan hi lo =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt chans (hi, lo) with
  | Some c -> c
  | None -> let c = Memchan.make hi lo in Hashtbl.add chans (hi, lo) c; c

exception Decline

(* The request (Memdraw.hosted): three images of 12 words (where its
 * bytes are, how many, its chan's hi and lo, r, org, the bytes a row,
 * xbase), then r, sr, mr and the op *)
let draw mem (piece : int -> int -> bool -> int) desc =
  let words = 49 in
  let pa = piece desc (4 * words) false in
  if pa < 0 then 0
  else begin
    let w = Array.init words (fun i -> Bits.signed32 (Memory.load32 mem (pa + (4 * i)))) in
    let rect at = (w.(at), w.(at + 1), w.(at + 2), w.(at + 3)) in
    (* an image on the RAM's bytes; the same bytes, the same data (the
     * loop goes bottom up when the source is the destination) *)
    let datas = ref [] in
    let image at ~write =
      let va = Memory.load32 mem (pa + (4 * at)) and len = w.(at + 1) in
      let c = match chan w.(at + 2) w.(at + 3) with Some c when not c.Memchan.cmap -> c | _ -> raise Decline in
      let where = piece va len write in
      if where < 0 || len <= 0 then raise Decline;
      let bytes, off = Memory.direct mem where len in
      let data =
        match List.assoc_opt off !datas with
        | Some d -> d
        | None -> let d = { Memimage.bytes; onscreen = false; keep = true } in datas := (off, d) :: !datas; d in
      let r = rect (at + 4) in
      ({ Memimage.data; r; clipr = r; repl = false; chan = c; bwidth = w.(at + 10); org = (w.(at + 8), w.(at + 9));
         xbase = w.(at + 11) - off; layer = None }, off, len) in
    match
      let dst, off, len = image 0 ~write:true in
      let src, _, _ = image 12 ~write:false in
      let mask, _, _ = image 24 ~write:false in
      let ((x0, y0, x1, y1) as r) = rect 36 in
      (* what is written is the destination's *)
      if x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0 then raise Decline;
      let first = Memimage.byteaddr dst x0 y0 and last = Memimage.byteaddr dst (x1 - 1) (y1 - 1) + ((dst.chan.Memchan.depth + 7) / 8) in
      if first < off || last > off + len then raise Decline;
      Memgeneral.general dst r src (rect 40) mask (rect 44) w.(48)
    with
    | () -> incr drawn; 1
    | exception (Decline | Invalid_argument _ | Memory.Fault _ | Division_by_zero) -> incr declined; 0
  end

let install () = Board.host_draw := draw

(* memdraw's general loop, run by the emulator for the kernel it runs:
 * mini-9pi built for a web page (make WEB=1) asks its machine to
 * compose the pixels of a draw that none of its faster paths has.
 *
 *     Memdraw.draw (the kernel, ARM)          the board (the host)
 *       faster paths: a fill, a copy, a character
 *       else hosted --> web_draw --> mrc p15, 7, r0, c15, c0, 4
 *                                       --> Board.host_draw --> Hostdraw
 *                                             Memgeneral.general on the
 *                                             images in the board's RAM
 *       else Memgeneral.general (the kernel's own)
 *
 * design: the loop is not written again here. Memgeneral, Memimage and
 * Memchan are the kernel's files (this directory's dune copies them),
 * compiled for the host; an image here is the kernel's, its bytes the
 * board's RAM itself and its xbase moved by where the image's bytes
 * are in it, so that Memimage's byteaddr gives a place in the RAM:
 * nothing is copied, and two images on the same bytes are still so.
 * The pixels are the kernel's own loop's by construction. What the
 * host saves is the interpreter: a pixel composed is about a thousand
 * of the board's instructions, each some hundreds of the host's; a
 * menu of mini-rio's, 20 million instructions, was 4 seconds in a
 * page.
 *
 * Declined (0, and the kernel's loop runs): an image with a colour
 * map (Memdata's tables are not here), bytes that are not RAM in one
 * piece, a destination's rectangle outside its bytes. *)

(* Board.host_draw set to this module's *)
val install : unit -> unit

(* the draws done and declined since the start *)
val drawn : int ref
val declined : int ref
