open Arm32_isa
module U = Js_of_ocaml.Js.Unsafe
module Js = Js_of_ocaml.Js

(* a place run so many times after a jump is translated: 200, where a
 * boot under node is 13.7 s (16: 17.8 s, a block's making being a
 * quarter of a millisecond; 2000: 13.4) *)
let threshold = ref 200
(* a block's instructions at most; the instructions a block that
 * loops on itself runs before it gives the board's loop a look *)
let max_len = 64
let loop_limit = 1024

let compiled = ref 0
let reused = ref 0
let refused = ref 0
(* a kind of instruction left to the interpreter, to find a wrong
 * translation: reg (shifts by a register), pc (pc written by a
 * data-processing instruction or a load), mem (halves, signed bytes,
 * offsets shifted right) *)
(* (and to find a wrong block: no more than [most] made, the last one's
 * text printed) *)
let most = ref max_int
let made = ref 0
let without : string list ref = ref []
(* a block goes on through an unconditional jump or call *)
let follow = ref true
let has k = not (List.mem k !without)
let retexted = ref 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* What the host's code stands on *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The translated code reads and writes the emulator's own values: under
 * js_of_ocaml a record and an array are an array of JavaScript's whose
 * first element is a tag, a bool is 0 or 1, an int is the 32 bits. So,
 * in a block's text:
 *   R[k + 1]   register k (the state's r)
 *   S[2..6]    the state's n, z, c, v and next
 *   TG, PG, RT the TLB's tags, pages and rights (Mmu32's), at i + 1
 *   U8, I32    the RAM's bytes, and the same as words
 * [fields] checks the state's five places before anything is run. *)
let f_n = 2 and f_z = 3 and f_c = 4 and f_v = 5 and f_next = 6

let fields (st : state) =
  let o = Obj.repr st in
  let int_at i : int = Obj.obj (Obj.field o (i - 1)) in
  let was = st.next in
  st.next <- 0x1234564;
  let ok_next = int_at f_next = 0x1234564 in
  st.next <- was;
  let flag get set i = let was = get () in set true; let a = int_at i = 1 in set false; let b = int_at i = 0 in set was; a && b in
  ok_next
  && flag (fun () -> st.n) (fun b -> st.n <- b) f_n && flag (fun () -> st.z) (fun b -> st.z <- b) f_z
  && flag (fun () -> st.c) (fun b -> st.c <- b) f_c && flag (fun () -> st.v) (fun b -> st.v <- b) f_v
  && Obj.field o 0 == Obj.repr st.r

(* The table of the blocks by where they start (the board's key: the pc,
 * and bit 0 in user mode), emptied by a number: a block is in it when
 * its slot has its key and the number of now, and the TLB has the
 * block's physical page for that address (so an emptied TLB, each
 * switch of process, costs a look at E.miss a page of code and not the
 * table). E.miss is asked for a key not in it. *)
let runtime = {|
  var SIZE = 65536, MASK = SIZE - 1;
  var TK = new Int32Array(SIZE), TN = new Int32Array(SIZE), TP = new Int32Array(SIZE), TF = new Array(SIZE), now = 1;
  var HK = new Int32Array(SIZE), HC = new Int32Array(SIZE);
  var TG = E.TG, PG = E.PG, RT = E.RT, S = E.S, W = E.W, tr = E.tr, slots = new Map();
  E.forget = function () { now++; slots.clear(); };
  // a block of a physical page (its slot kept by the page: E.written);
  // f null: no block is worth making there, the interpreter's
  E.install = function (key, f, page) {
    var s = (key >>> 2) & MASK; TK[s] = key; TN[s] = now; TF[s] = f; TP[s] = page;
    var l = slots.get(page); if (l === undefined) slots.set(page, [s]); else if (l.length < 4096) l.push(s);
  };
  E.written = function (page) {
    var l = slots.get(page);
    if (l !== undefined) { for (var k = 0; k < l.length; k++) if (TP[l[k]] === page) TN[l[k]] = 0; slots.delete(page); }
  };
  // Block after block while each one is there, up to CHAIN instructions:
  // nothing that interrupts can have changed between two of them (a
  // block that wrote a device, or that the interpreter ended, sets
  // W[3]: back to the board's loop). A block starts at key when its
  // slot says so, of now, and the TLB still gives its physical page for
  // the key's page (looked at when the page is not the last block's),
  // which the mode may read. W[0..2], for a block that raises: the
  // instructions of its turns done, its start, those of the blocks
  // before it.
  // A key not there: one that follows the last one not found is not a
  // place a block may start (E.miss says why); a slot that had this key
  // is asked of E.miss at once (its block is put back); another key is
  // counted, and asked when it came THRESHOLD times.
  var CHAIN = 1024, last = -1, cur = null;
  // the block running: where the instruction that raised is in it (by
  // its address + 8), and a block's first run, E.miss's
  E.at = function (pc8) { return cur === null ? 1 : (cur.pos[pc8] | 0); };
  E.first = function (f) { cur = f; W[0] = 0; W[2] = 0; return f(); };
  E.run = function (key) {
    var total = 0, user = key & 1, page = -1, phys = -1;
    W[3] = 0;
    for (;;) {
      var s = (key >>> 2) & MASK;
      if (TK[s] === key && TN[s] === now) {
        // (the last block's page: the same one of the memory too, a
        // slot may be another program's at the same address)
        var g = key >>> 12, ok = g === page && TP[s] === phys;
        if (!ok) {
          var i = (g & 1023) + 1;
          // (the TLB was emptied, a switch of process: the page's
          // translation asked again, here; an abort is E.miss's to find)
          if (TG[i] !== g) { try { tr(key & -4, 0); } catch (e) { } }
          ok = TG[i] === g && PG[i] === TP[s] && (RT[i] & (user ? 4 : 1)) !== 0;
        }
        if (ok) {
          var f = TF[s];
          if (f === null) { last = key; return total; }
          page = g; phys = TP[s];
          W[0] = 0; W[2] = total; cur = f;
          var ran = f();
          // (a block that stopped before its first instruction, the
          // interpreter's: when blocks are checked)
          if (ran === 0) { last = key; return total; }
          total += ran;
          if (W[3] !== 0 || total >= CHAIN) { last = -1; return total; }
          key = S[6] | user;
          continue;
        }
      }
      else {
        if (total !== 0) { last = -1; return total; }
        if (key === last + 4) { last = key; return 0; }
        last = key;
        if (HK[s] !== key) { HK[s] = key; HC[s] = 1; return 0; }
        if (++HC[s] < E.threshold) return 0;
        HC[s] = 0;
      }
      if (total !== 0) { last = -1; return total; }
      W[2] = 0;
      total = E.miss(key);
      last = total !== 0 ? -1 : key;
      return total;
    }
  };
  E.make = function (src) { return (new Function("E", src))(E); };
  // a block's memory accesses (Jit.ml: [inlined])
  var U8 = E.U8, I32 = E.I32, RAM = E.RAM, ld32 = E.ld32, ld16 = E.ld16, ld8 = E.ld8, st32 = E.st32, st16 = E.st16, st8 = E.st8;
  E.TR = function (a, need, w) { var g = a >>> 12, i = (g & 1023) + 1; return TG[i] === g && (RT[i] & need) ? PG[i] | (a & 4095) : tr(a, w); };
  E.L32 = function (p) { return (p >>> 0) < RAM && !(p & 3) ? I32[p >> 2] : ld32(p); };
  E.L16 = function (p) { return (p >>> 0) < RAM - 1 ? U8[p] | (U8[p + 1] << 8) : ld16(p); };
  E.L8 = function (p) { return (p >>> 0) < RAM ? U8[p] : ld8(p); };
  E.S32 = function (p, v) { if ((p >>> 0) < RAM && !(p & 3)) { I32[p >> 2] = v; return 0; } st32(p, v); return 1; };
  E.S16 = function (p, v) { if ((p >>> 0) < RAM - 1) { U8[p] = v; U8[p + 1] = v >> 8; return 0; } st16(p, v); return 1; };
  E.S8 = function (p, v) { if ((p >>> 0) < RAM) { U8[p] = v; return 0; } st8(p, v); return 1; };
|}

(* a block's text around its instructions: what it reads of E once, its
 * variables (a an address, p a physical one, x set by a store that was
 * not the RAM's: the block ends after that instruction) *)
let head =
  "var R=E.R,S=E.S,W=E.W,TG=E.TG,PG=E.PG,RT=E.RT,U8=E.U8,I32=E.I32,RAM=E.RAM,tr=E.tr,ld32=E.ld32,ld16=E.ld16,ld8=E.ld8,st32=E.st32,st16=E.st16,st8=E.st8,ex=E.ex,lg=E.lg,TR=E.TR,L32=E.L32,L16=E.L16,L8=E.L8,S32=E.S32,S16=E.S16,S8=E.S8;\n\
   var f=function(){var n=0,x=0,a,p,i,v,b,q,r,y,c,t0,t1,t2,t3,t4,t5,t6,t7,t8,t9,t10,t11,t12,t13,t14,t15;\nL:for(;;){\n"

(*****************************************************************************)
(* An instruction's text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let buf = Buffer.create 8192
let p fmt = Printf.bprintf buf fmt

(* the instructions the interpreter runs for a block ([ex]'s number) *)
let insts : (int * Arm32_isa.t) array ref = ref (Array.make 1024 (0, Undefined 0))
let insts_n = ref 0
(* (an instruction at an address has one number: a block made again has
 * the same text, and its code is found by it) *)
let kept : (int * Arm32_isa.t, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 1024
(* (the block being made has one) *)
let asked = ref false
let keep addr i =
  asked := true;
  match Hashtbl.find_opt kept (addr, i) with
  | Some g -> g
  | None ->
  Hashtbl.add kept (addr, i) !insts_n;
  if !insts_n = Array.length !insts then begin
    let a = Array.make (2 * !insts_n) (0, Undefined 0) in
    Array.blit !insts 0 a 0 !insts_n; insts := a
  end;
  !insts.(!insts_n) <- (addr, i);
  incr insts_n;
  !insts_n - 1

let cond_text = function
  | EQ -> "S[3]" | NE -> "!S[3]" | CS -> "S[4]" | CC -> "!S[4]" | MI -> "S[2]" | PL -> "!S[2]" | VS -> "S[5]" | VC -> "!S[5]"
  | HI -> "S[4]&&!S[3]" | LS -> "!S[4]||S[3]" | GE -> "S[2]===S[5]" | LT -> "S[2]!==S[5]"
  | GT -> "!S[3]&&S[2]===S[5]" | LE -> "S[3]||S[2]!==S[5]" | AL -> ""

(* a register read: pc is the instruction's address + 8 *)
let reg pc r = if r = 15 then Printf.sprintf "(%d)" (Bits.mask32 (pc + 8)) else Printf.sprintf "R[%d]" (r + 1)

(* the address in a through the TLB, in p: Mmu32.translate's first line,
 * else the emulator's own ([write]; [user]: the block's mode) *)
(* A block's memory accesses are calls of a few functions made once
 * ([runtime]: TR the TLB's line or the emulator's translation; L32, L16,
 * L8 the RAM's word, half, byte, or the emulator's load; S32, S16, S8
 * the store, 1 when it was not the RAM's): the browser inlines them
 * where a block is hot. ([inlined]: their text in each block instead,
 * as it was. A block then had a call it almost never makes at each
 * access, the emulator's on a TLB's miss or a device, and the browser,
 * which compiles a block before that call was ever made, threw its
 * code away the first time each was: 852 of 1,046 such
 * deoptimizations under node for rio and cameltry, "insufficient type
 * feedback for call", and Chrome still compiling a minute into a
 * game.) *)
let inlined = ref false

let translate ~user ~write =
  let access = (if write then 1 else 0) lor (if user then 2 else 0) in
  if !inlined then p "i=((a>>>12)&1023)+1;if(TG[i]===(a>>>12)&&(RT[i]&%d))p=PG[i]|(a&4095);else p=tr(a,%d);" (1 lsl access) (if write then 1 else 0)
  else p "p=TR(a,%d,%d);" (1 lsl access) (if write then 1 else 0)

let load_word into = if !inlined then p "%s=(p>>>0)<RAM&&!(p&3)?I32[p>>2]:ld32(p);" into else p "%s=L32(p);" into
let load_byte into = if !inlined then p "%s=(p>>>0)<RAM?U8[p]:ld8(p);" into else p "%s=L8(p);" into
(* (when blocks are checked against the interpreter, each store says
 * first where it writes: [attach]'s run_checked puts the bytes back) *)
let checking = ref false
let logged n = if !checking then p "lg(p,%d);" n

let load_half into = if !inlined then p "%s=(p>>>0)<RAM-1?U8[p]|(U8[p+1]<<8):ld16(p);" into else p "%s=L16(p);" into
let store_half v =
  logged 2;
  if !inlined then p "if((p>>>0)<RAM-1){U8[p]=%s;U8[p+1]=%s>>8;}else{st16(p,%s);x=1;}" v v v else p "x|=S16(p,%s);" v
let store_word v =
  logged 4;
  if !inlined then p "if((p>>>0)<RAM&&!(p&3))I32[p>>2]=%s;else{st32(p,%s);x=1;}" v v else p "x|=S32(p,%s);" v
let store_byte v =
  logged 1;
  if !inlined then p "if((p>>>0)<RAM)U8[p]=%s;else{st8(p,%s);x=1;}" v v else p "x|=S8(p,%s);" v

(* the second operand in b; its carry out as text, None when it is the
 * flag as it was; false: a shift the interpreter keeps *)
let operand pc op2 =
  match op2 with
  | Imm { imm8; rot } ->
      let v = Arm32.imm_value ~imm8 ~rot in
      p "b=%d;" v;
      Some (if rot = 0 then None else Some (if (v lsr 31) land 1 = 1 then "1" else "0"))
  | Sreg (rm, No_shift) -> p "b=%s;" (reg pc rm); Some None
  | Sreg (rm, By_imm (LSL, n)) when n > 0 && n < 32 -> p "v=%s;b=v<<%d;" (reg pc rm) n; Some (Some (Printf.sprintf "(v>>>%d)&1" (32 - n)))
  | Sreg (rm, By_imm (LSR, n)) when n > 0 && n < 32 -> p "v=%s;b=v>>>%d;" (reg pc rm) n; Some (Some (Printf.sprintf "(v>>>%d)&1" (n - 1)))
  | Sreg (rm, By_imm (ASR, n)) when n > 0 && n < 32 -> p "v=%s;b=v>>%d;" (reg pc rm) n; Some (Some (Printf.sprintf "(v>>>%d)&1" (n - 1)))
  (* by a register's low byte (Arm32's shift): 0 leaves the value and
   * the carry, 32 and more shift everything out *)
  | Sreg (rm, By_reg (LSL, rs)) when rs <> 15 && has "reg" ->
      p "v=%s;c=R[%d]&255;b=c<32?v<<c:0;" (reg pc rm) (rs + 1);
      Some (Some "(c===0?S[4]:c<32?(v>>>(32-c))&1:c===32?v&1:0)")
  | Sreg (rm, By_reg (LSR, rs)) when rs <> 15 && has "reg" ->
      p "v=%s;c=R[%d]&255;b=c<32?(v>>>c)|0:0;" (reg pc rm) (rs + 1);
      Some (Some "(c===0?S[4]:c<32?(v>>>(c-1))&1:c===32?v>>>31:0)")
  | Sreg (rm, By_reg (ASR, rs)) when rs <> 15 && has "reg" ->
      p "v=%s;c=R[%d]&255;b=c<32?v>>c:v>>31;" (reg pc rm) (rs + 1);
      Some (Some "(c===0?S[4]:c<32?(v>>>(c-1))&1:v>>>31)")
  | _ -> None

let nz () = p "S[2]=r>>>31;S[3]=+(r===0);"

(* Arm32_fast's dp: a logical result with the shifter's carry, a sum
 * with its own *)
let logical s rd expr carry =
  (* (pc written: the value left in r, the jump is [instruction]'s) *)
  if rd = 15 then p "r=%s;" expr
  else if not s then p "R[%d]=%s;" (rd + 1) expr
  else begin
    p "r=%s;" expr; nz ();
    (match carry with Some c -> p "S[4]=%s;" c | None -> ());
    p "R[%d]=r;" (rd + 1)
  end

(* q + y + cin: cin "0", "1" or the flag *)
let sum s x y cin =
  (match cin with
   | "0" -> p "r=(%s+%s)|0;" x y
   | "1" -> p "r=(%s+%s+1)|0;" x y
   | _ -> p "c=S[4];r=(%s+%s+c)|0;" x y);
  if s then begin
    (match cin with
     | "0" -> p "c=+((r>>>0)<(%s>>>0));" x
     | "1" -> p "c=+((r>>>0)<=(%s>>>0));" x
     | _ -> p "c=+(c?(r>>>0)<=(%s>>>0):(r>>>0)<(%s>>>0));" x x);
    nz ();
    p "S[4]=c;S[5]=((%s^r)&(%s^r))>>>31;" x y
  end

(* a data-processing instruction (its condition passed); false: the
 * interpreter's *)
let dp pc op s rd rn op2 =
    let at = Buffer.length buf in
    match operand pc op2 with
    | None -> Buffer.truncate buf at; false
    | Some carry ->
        let a = reg pc rn in
        let put () = if rd <> 15 then p "R[%d]=r;" (rd + 1) in
        let arith x y cin = p "q=%s;" a; sum s x y cin; put () in
        let compare x y cin = p "q=%s;" a; sum true x y cin in
        (match op with
         | AND -> logical s rd (a ^ "&b") carry
         | EOR -> logical s rd (a ^ "^b") carry
         | ORR -> logical s rd (a ^ "|b") carry
         | BIC -> logical s rd (a ^ "&~b") carry
         | MOV -> logical s rd "b" carry
         | MVN -> logical s rd "~b" carry
         | ADD -> arith "q" "b" "0"
         | ADC -> arith "q" "b" "c"
         | SUB -> p "y=~b;"; arith "q" "y" "1"
         | SBC -> p "y=~b;"; arith "q" "y" "c"
         | RSB -> p "q=%s;y=~q;" a; sum s "b" "y" "1"; put ()
         | RSC -> p "q=%s;y=~q;" a; sum s "b" "y" "c"; put ()
         | TST -> p "r=%s&b;" a; nz (); (match carry with Some c -> p "S[4]=%s;" c | None -> ())
         | TEQ -> p "r=%s^b;" a; nz (); (match carry with Some c -> p "S[4]=%s;" c | None -> ())
         | CMP -> p "y=~b;"; compare "q" "y" "1"
         | CMN -> compare "q" "b" "0");
        true

(* a word or a byte loaded or stored (Arm32's Mem); false: the
 * interpreter's (a half, a double, as the user, a shift it keeps, pc
 * loaded) *)
let mem ~user pc ~load ~size ~rd ~rn ~offset ~up ~index ~writeback ~as_user ~interp ~count =
  let off =
    match offset with
    | Off_imm n -> Some (string_of_int n)
    | Off_reg (rm, No_shift) when rm <> 15 -> Some (reg pc rm)
    | Off_reg (rm, By_imm (LSL, n)) when rm <> 15 && n > 0 && n < 32 -> Some (Printf.sprintf "(%s<<%d)" (reg pc rm) n)
    | Off_reg (rm, By_imm (LSR, n)) when rm <> 15 && n > 0 && n < 32 && has "mem" -> Some (Printf.sprintf "(%s>>>%d)" (reg pc rm) n)
    | Off_reg (rm, By_imm (ASR, n)) when rm <> 15 && n > 0 && n < 32 && has "mem" -> Some (Printf.sprintf "(%s>>%d)" (reg pc rm) n)
    | _ -> None in
  match off with
  | Some off when size <> Dword && not as_user && not (rd = 15 && (not load || size <> Word))
                  && (has "pc" || not (load && rd = 15)) && (has "mem" || size = Word || size = Byte) ->
      let back = (index = Post || writeback) && rn <> 15 in
      p "q=%s;y=(q%s(%s))|0;a=%s;" (reg pc rn) (if up then "+" else "-") off (if index = Pre then "y" else "q");
      translate ~user ~write:(not load);
      if load then begin
        (match size with
         | Word -> load_word "v"
         | Byte -> load_byte "v"
         | Sbyte -> load_byte "v"; p "v=(v<<24)>>24;"
         | Half -> load_half "v"
         | Shalf -> load_half "v"; p "v=(v<<16)>>16;"
         | Dword -> ());
        (* (pc loaded: a jump; bit 0 would be Thumb, the interpreter's
         * refusal, nothing being written yet) *)
        if rd = 15 then p "if(v&1){ex(%d);return n+%d;}" interp count;
        if back then p "R[%d]=y;" (rn + 1);
        if rd = 15 then p "S[6]=v&~3;return n+%d;" count else p "R[%d]=v;" (rd + 1)
      end
      else begin
        (* (the value before the base is written back) *)
        p "v=%s;" (reg pc rd);
        (match size with Word -> store_word "v" | Byte -> store_byte "v" | _ -> store_half "v");
        if back then p "R[%d]=y;" (rn + 1)
      end;
      true
  | _ -> false

(* registers pushed or popped (Arm32_fast's Block, without ^); the text
 * after it when pc is loaded: the block's end. false: the
 * interpreter's *)
let block ~user pc ~load ~rn ~writeback ~mode ~regs ~interp ~count =
  if rn = 15 || regs = 0 then false
  else begin
    let nreg = ref 0 in
    for k = 0 to 15 do nreg := !nreg + ((regs lsr k) land 1) done;
    let nreg = !nreg in
    let start = match mode with IA -> 0 | IB -> 4 | DA -> 4 - (4 * nreg) | DB -> - (4 * nreg) in
    let final = match mode with IA | IB -> 4 * nreg | DA | DB -> - (4 * nreg) in
    p "q=R[%d];a=(q+(%d))|0;" (rn + 1) start;
    let j = ref 0 in
    for k = 0 to 15 do
      if (regs lsr k) land 1 = 1 then begin
        translate ~user ~write:(not load);
        (if load then load_word (Printf.sprintf "t%d" !j) else (p "v=%s;" (reg pc k); store_word "v"));
        incr j;
        if !j < nreg then p "a=(a+4)|0;"
      end
    done;
    if load then begin
      (* (pc with bit 0: Thumb, which the interpreter refuses; nothing
       * is written yet, it runs the instruction again) *)
      if regs land 0x8000 <> 0 then p "if(t%d&1){ex(%d);return n+%d;}" (nreg - 1) interp count;
      if writeback then p "R[%d]=(q+(%d))|0;" (rn + 1) final;
      j := 0;
      for k = 0 to 14 do
        if (regs lsr k) land 1 = 1 then (p "R[%d]=t%d;" (k + 1) !j; incr j)
      done;
      if regs land 0x8000 <> 0 then p "S[6]=t%d&~3;return n+%d;" !j count
    end
    else if writeback then p "R[%d]=(q+(%d))|0;" (rn + 1) final;
    true
  end

(* what the interpreter runs and the block must end after: the
 * interrupts or the translation may have changed, or a device was
 * written *)
let ends = function
  | Msr _ | Cps _ | Coproc _ | Coproc2 _ | Svc _ | Hint _ | Undefined _ | Vmsr _ | Clrex | Barrier _ -> true
  | Mem { load = false; _ } | Swp _ | Strex _ | Vldst { load = false; _ } | Vblock { load = false; _ } -> true
  | Block { psr = true; _ } -> true
  | Dp { s = true; rd = 15; _ } -> true
  | _ -> false

(* (the last instruction was the interpreter's: a block of them mostly
 * is not made) *)
let was_interpreted = ref false

(* One instruction, number k of its block, at pc. `Ended: nothing can
 * follow it in the block. *)
let instruction ~user ~start k pc (i : Arm32_isa.t) =
  let count = k + 1 in
  let pc4 = Bits.mask32 (pc + 4) and pc8 = Bits.mask32 (pc + 8) in
  (* by the interpreter: the instruction kept, run by its number; the
   * block goes on when the interpreter did (next is pc + 4) *)
  let interpreted () =
    was_interpreted := true;
    let g = keep pc i in
    (* (blocks checked against the interpreter have none of its
     * instructions: they stop before one, which the board's loop runs) *)
    if !checking then (p "S[6]=%d;return n+%d;\n" pc k; `Ended)
    else
    if ends i then (p "ex(%d);W[3]=1;return n+%d;\n" g count; `Ended)
    else (p "ex(%d);if(S[6]!==%d)return n+%d;\n" g pc4 count; `Goes) in
  (* under its condition *)
  let guarded cond body =
    let c = cond_text cond in
    if c = "" then body () else begin p "if(%s){" c; let r = body () in p "}"; r end in
  (* a store that was a device's: the block ends *)
  let stored () = p "if(x){W[3]=1;S[6]=%d;return n+%d;}" pc4 count in
  let at = Buffer.length buf in
  let fallback () = Buffer.truncate buf at; interpreted () in
  match i with
  | Dp { cond; op; s; rd; rn; op2 } when not (s && rd = 15) && (rd <> 15 || has "pc") ->
      (* (pc written, mov pc, lr: a jump; bit 0 would be Thumb, the
       * interpreter's refusal, nothing being written yet) *)
      let jump = rd = 15 && (match op with TST | TEQ | CMP | CMN -> false | _ -> true) in
      let g = if jump then keep pc i else 0 in
      if guarded cond (fun () ->
          dp pc op s rd rn op2
          && (if jump then p "if(r&1){ex(%d);return n+%d;}S[6]=r&~3;return n+%d;" g count count; true))
      then (p "\n"; if jump && cond = AL then `Ended else `Goes)
      else fallback ()
  | Mem { cond; load; size; rd; rn; offset; up; index; writeback; user = as_user } ->
      p "R[16]=%d;" pc8;
      let jump = load && rd = 15 in
      let g = if jump then keep pc i else 0 in
      if guarded cond (fun () -> mem ~user pc ~load ~size ~rd ~rn ~offset ~up ~index ~writeback ~as_user ~interp:g ~count) then begin
        if not load then stored ();
        p "\n"; if jump && cond = AL then `Ended else `Goes
      end
      else fallback ()
  | Block { cond; load; rn; writeback; mode; regs; psr = false } ->
      p "R[16]=%d;" pc8;
      let g = keep pc i in
      if guarded cond (fun () -> block ~user pc ~load ~rn ~writeback ~mode ~regs ~interp:g ~count) then begin
        if not load then stored ();
        p "\n";
        if load && regs land 0x8000 <> 0 && cond = AL then `Ended else `Goes
      end
      else fallback ()
  | Branch { cond; link; offset } ->
      let target = Bits.mask32 (pc + 8 + offset) in
      let loops = target = start && not link in
      (* (an unconditional one elsewhere: only the link here, the
       * block's maker goes on at the target or leaves) *)
      if cond = AL && not loops then begin
        if link then p "R[15]=%d;" pc4;
        `Jumps target
      end
      else begin
        ignore (guarded cond (fun () ->
          if link then p "R[15]=%d;" pc4;
          (* (to the block's start: around again, a look at the board's
           * loop every [loop_limit] instructions) *)
          if loops then p "n+=%d;if(n<%d){W[0]=n;continue L;}S[6]=%d;return n;" count loop_limit target
          else p "S[6]=%d;return n+%d;" target count;
          true));
        p "\n";
        if cond = AL then `Ended else `Goes
      end
  | Bx { cond; link; rm } when rm <> 15 ->
      (* (bit 0: Thumb, the interpreter's refusal) *)
      let g = keep pc i in
      ignore (guarded cond (fun () ->
        p "v=R[%d];if(v&1){ex(%d);return n+%d;}" (rm + 1) g count;
        if link then p "R[15]=%d;" pc4;
        p "S[6]=v&~3;return n+%d;" count;
        true));
      p "\n";
      if cond = AL then `Ended else `Goes
  | Mul { cond; s = false; rd; rm; rs; acc } when rd <> 15 && rm <> 15 && rs <> 15 && acc <> Some 15 ->
      ignore (guarded cond (fun () ->
        (match acc with
         | Some ra -> p "R[%d]=(Math.imul(R[%d],R[%d])+R[%d])|0;" (rd + 1) (rm + 1) (rs + 1) (ra + 1)
         | None -> p "R[%d]=Math.imul(R[%d],R[%d]);" (rd + 1) (rm + 1) (rs + 1));
        true));
      p "\n"; `Goes
  | Extend { cond; signed; half; rd; rn = 15; rm; rot = 0 } when rd <> 15 && rm <> 15 ->
      ignore (guarded cond (fun () ->
        (match signed, half with
         | false, false -> p "R[%d]=R[%d]&255;" (rd + 1) (rm + 1)
         | false, true -> p "R[%d]=R[%d]&65535;" (rd + 1) (rm + 1)
         | true, false -> p "R[%d]=(R[%d]<<24)>>24;" (rd + 1) (rm + 1)
         | true, true -> p "R[%d]=(R[%d]<<16)>>16;" (rd + 1) (rm + 1));
        true));
      p "\n"; `Goes
  | _ -> interpreted ()

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The blocks *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a block: where it starts (the key), its instructions' words when it
 * was translated, its code (None: not worth one) *)
type block = { key : int; words : (int * int) array; code : U.any option; mutable checked : int; pure : bool }

(* the number of the I-cache's invalidations: a block's words are
 * compared with the memory's once after each ([checked]), and after its
 * page was written (-1) *)
let age = ref 0

(* by the physical address of their first instruction: a block outlives
 * the table's emptying (Plan 9 invalidates the instructions' cache at
 * each switch of process), and is put back when its words are still
 * the memory's *)
let by_pa : (int, block) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 4096

(* the code of a text: a program run again has its pages elsewhere and
 * the same blocks *)
let by_text : (string, U.any) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 4096

let translate_block (st : state) env key pa =
  let user = key land 1 = 1 and start = key land lnot 3 in
  Buffer.clear buf;
  asked := false;
  Buffer.add_string buf head;
  let words = ref [] and native = ref 0 and places = ref [] in
  let rec go k pc pa =
    let w = Memory.load32 st.mem pa in
    Board.code_page pa;
    words := (pa, w) :: !words;
    places := (pc, k + 1) :: !places;
    let i = Arm32.decode w in
    was_interpreted := false;
    let r = instruction ~user ~start k pc i in
    if not !was_interpreted then incr native;
    let leave target = p "S[6]=%d;return n+%d;\n" target (k + 1) in
    match r with
    | `Ended -> ()
    | `Goes ->
        (* (not into the next page: its translation is another) *)
        if k + 1 < max_len && (pc + 4) land 0xfff <> 0 then go (k + 1) (pc + 4) (pa + 4)
        else leave (Bits.mask32 (pc + 4))
    | `Jumps target ->
        (* A jump or a call to a place of the same page, not yet in the
         * block: the block goes on there (a trace: the call and what is
         * called in one function of the host's). The same page: the
         * block is found by its first page's translation, and put back
         * by its words. *)
        if k + 1 < max_len && target lsr 12 = start lsr 12 && not (List.mem_assoc target !places) && !follow
        then (p "\n"; go (k + 1) target (pa - (pc land 0xfff) + (target land 0xfff)))
        else leave target in
  go 0 start pa;
  (* (where each instruction is in the block, by its address + 8, what
   * r15 is when one raises: [attach]'s blocks_done) *)
  Buffer.add_string buf "}};f.pos={";
  List.iter (fun (pc, count) -> p "\"%d\":%d," (Bits.mask32 (pc + 8)) count) !places;
  Buffer.add_string buf "};return f;";
  let words = Array.of_list (List.rev !words) in
  (* (a block the interpreter would run all of is not one) *)
  if !native * 2 < Array.length words || !native < 2 || !made >= !most then begin
    incr refused;
    { key; words; code = None; checked = !age; pure = false }
  end
  else begin
    let text = Buffer.contents buf in
    let code =
      match Hashtbl.find_opt by_text text with
      | Some c -> incr retexted; c
      | None ->
          incr compiled;
          if !made + 1 = !most then prerr_endline (Printf.sprintf "the last block made, at %x:\n%s" (key land lnot 3) text);
          let c = U.meth_call env "make" [| U.inject (Js.string text) |] in Hashtbl.replace by_text text c; c in
    incr made;
    (* (no instruction of the interpreter's in it: [attach]'s run_checked) *)
    { key; words; code = Some code; checked = !age; pure = not !asked }
  end

let same (st : state) (b : block) =
  let ok = ref true in
  Array.iter (fun (pa, w) -> if !ok && Memory.load32 st.mem pa <> w then ok := false) b.words;
  !ok

(* [attach board]: the board's blocks are this module's *)
let attach board =
  (match Sys.getenv_opt "JIT_WITHOUT" with Some l -> without := String.split_on_char ',' l | None -> ());
  (match Sys.getenv_opt "JIT_MOST" with Some n -> most := int_of_string n | None -> ());
  checking := Sys.getenv_opt "JIT_CHECK" <> None;
  if has "follow" then () else follow := false;
  if has "calls" then () else inlined := true;
  (match Sys.getenv_opt "JIT_THRESHOLD" with Some n -> threshold := int_of_string n | None -> ());
  let (st : state), (mmu : Mmu32.t), mem = Board.parts board in
  if not (fields st) then failwith "Jit: the state is not where the translated code reads it";
  let ram, _ = Memory.direct mem 0 4 in
  let u8 = Js_of_ocaml.Typed_array.Bytes.to_uint8Array ram in
  let get o name = U.get o (Js.string name) in
  let i32 = U.new_obj (get U.global "Int32Array")
      [| U.inject (get u8 "buffer"); U.inject (get u8 "byteOffset"); U.inject (Bytes.length ram / 4) |] in
  let svc (st : state) _ = Arm32.take st Supervisor_call ~ret:(st.r.(15) - 4) in
  let env = U.obj [|
    "R", U.inject st.r; "S", U.inject st; "TG", U.inject mmu.tags; "PG", U.inject mmu.pages; "RT", U.inject mmu.rights;
    "U8", U.inject u8; "I32", U.inject i32; "RAM", U.inject (Bytes.length ram);
    "W", U.inject (U.new_obj (get U.global "Int32Array") [| U.inject 4 |]); "threshold", U.inject !threshold;
    "ld16", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) -> Memory.load16 mem pa));
    "st16", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) (v : int) -> Memory.store16 mem pa v));
    "tr", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (va : int) (access : int) -> st.translate va access));
    "ld32", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) -> Memory.load32 mem pa));
    "ld8", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) -> Memory.load8 mem pa));
    "st32", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) (v : int) -> Memory.store32 mem pa v));
    "st8", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) (v : int) -> Memory.store8 mem pa v));
    "ex", U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (g : int) -> let addr, i = !insts.(g) in Arm32_fast.execute st ~addr ~svc i));
  |] in
  ignore (U.fun_call (U.new_obj (get U.global "Function") [| U.inject (Js.string "E"); U.inject (Js.string runtime) |]) [| U.inject env |]);
  let install key code pa = ignore (U.meth_call env "install" [| U.inject key; U.inject code; U.inject (pa land lnot 0xfff) |]) in
  (* where the blocks of each physical page start *)
  let in_page : (int, int list) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 1024 in
  let cells = get env "W" in
  let run_plain (code : U.any) : int = U.meth_call env "first" [| U.inject code |] in
  let run = run_plain in
  (* [checked]: a block's first run is done again by the interpreter,
   * from the same registers and flags and the same memory (the bytes
   * the block's stores wrote are put back: [log]), and what each left
   * compared: the registers, the flags, where it goes next, those
   * bytes. A block that raises, or that the interpreter's instructions
   * are part of, is not compared. To find a wrong translation:
   * JIT_CHECK=1 for Boot_jit. *)
  let log = ref [] in
  U.set env (Js.string "lg") (U.inject (Js.wrap_callback (fun (pa : int) (n : int) ->
    for k = 0 to n - 1 do log := (pa + k, (try Memory.load8 mem (pa + k) with _ -> 0)) :: !log done)));
  let run_checked key (code : U.any) : int =
    let r0 = Array.copy st.r and f0 = (st.n, st.z, st.c, st.v, st.next) in
    log := [];
    let n = run code in
    let r1 = Array.copy st.r and f1 = (st.n, st.z, st.c, st.v, st.next) in
    let wrote = List.map (fun (a, _) -> a, (try Memory.load8 mem a with _ -> 0)) !log in
    (* (the first value logged of an address is the oldest: put back last) *)
    (try List.iter (fun (a, old) -> if a < Bytes.length ram then Memory.store8 mem a old) !log with _ -> ());
    Array.blit r0 0 st.r 0 16;
    (let (a, b, c, d, e) = f0 in st.n <- a; st.z <- b; st.c <- c; st.v <- d; st.next <- e);
    let pc = ref (key land lnot 3) and trace = Buffer.create 256 in
    (try
       for _ = 1 to n do
         let w = Memory.load32 mem (st.translate !pc 0) in
         Printf.bprintf trace " %x:%08x" !pc w;
         Arm32_fast.execute st ~addr:!pc ~svc (Arm32.decode w);
         pc := st.next
       done
     with e -> Printf.bprintf trace " raised %s" (Printexc.to_string e));
    let same = ref ((st.n, st.z, st.c, st.v, st.next) = f1) in
    List.iter (fun (a, v) -> if (try Memory.load8 mem a with _ -> 0) <> v then (same := false; Printf.eprintf "  byte %x: the block's %x\n" a v)) wrote;
    for k = 0 to 14 do if st.r.(k) <> r1.(k) then same := false done;
    if not !same then begin
      Printf.eprintf "Jit: the block at %x and the interpreter differ after %d instructions:%s\n" (key land lnot 3) n (Buffer.contents trace);
      for k = 0 to 14 do
        if st.r.(k) <> r1.(k) then Printf.eprintf "  r%d: the block's %x, the interpreter's %x (it was %x)\n" k r1.(k) st.r.(k) r0.(k)
      done;
      let (a, b, c, d, e) = f1 in
      Printf.eprintf "  flags and next: the block's %b %b %b %b %x, the interpreter's %b %b %b %b %x\n%!" a b c d e st.n st.z st.c st.v st.next;
      exit 2
    end;
    n in
  let run key code = if !checking then run_checked key code else run code in
  (* A key with no block in the table, and worth asking (E.run: reached
   * by a jump often, or its slot lost): its block put back when its
   * words are still the memory's, or made, and run. Only a place
   * reached by a jump may start a block: else every instruction of a
   * loop would start one. 0: no block, the interpreter's. *)
  let miss (key : int) : int =
      match st.translate (key land lnot 3) 0 with
      | exception Arm32.Abort _ -> 0
      | pa ->
          let b =
            match Hashtbl.find_opt by_pa pa with
            | Some b when b.key = key && (b.checked = !age || same st b) -> b.checked <- !age; incr reused; b
            | _ ->
                let b = translate_block st env key pa in
                Hashtbl.replace by_pa pa b;
                let page = pa land lnot 0xfff in
                let l = Option.value (Hashtbl.find_opt in_page page) ~default:[] in
                if not (List.mem pa l) then Hashtbl.replace in_page page (pa :: l);
                b in
          (match b.code with
           | Some code -> install key code pa; if b.pure then run key code else run_plain code
           | None -> install key Js.null pa; 0) in
  U.set env (Js.string "miss") (U.inject (Js.wrap_callback miss));
  (* (a function of JavaScript's of one argument is a closure of OCaml's) *)
  Board.blocks := (Obj.magic (get env "run") : int -> int);
  Board.blocks_forget := (fun () -> incr age; ignore (U.meth_call env "forget" [||]));
  (* (a page's blocks are forgotten, and are out of the table: made again
   * when run again, their code found by their text if it is the same) *)
  Board.blocks_written := (fun pa n ->
    let page = ref (pa land lnot 0xfff) in
    while !page < pa + n do
      (match Hashtbl.find_opt in_page !page with
       | Some l ->
           List.iter (Hashtbl.remove by_pa) l; Hashtbl.remove in_page !page;
           ignore (U.meth_call env "written" [| U.inject !page |])
       | None -> ());
      page := !page + 4096
    done);
  (* the instructions a block ran when it raised: those of its turns
   * done and of the blocks before it, and up to the one that raised (r15 is its address + 8) *)
  Board.blocks_done := (fun () ->
    let cell i : int = Obj.magic (U.get cells i) in
    let b = cell 0 and t = cell 2 in
    t + b + (Obj.magic (U.meth_call env "at" [| U.inject st.r.(15) |]) : int));
  Board.blocks_on := true
raspberry/web/jit/Jit.mli
4821
(* The board's ARM instructions translated to JavaScript, for mini-qemu
 * in a web page: a run of instructions reached often becomes a
 * function of JavaScript's, which the browser then compiles to the
 * host's own instructions. The interpreter (Arm32, Board.run) is
 * untouched, and is what runs everything else.
 *
 *     Board.run, at each instruction, asks Board.blocks (this module):
 *       a block starts here --> its function runs
 *       none               --> the interpreter runs the one instruction;
 *                              a place reached by a jump 200 times is
 *                              translated
 *     a block's function runs 1 to 64 instructions, or a loop's turns,
 *     and the next block's follows it without the board's loop
 *
 *     ldr r3, [r0, #4]    R[16]=...;q=R[1];y=(q+(4))|0;a=y;
 *                         p=TR(a,1,0);v=L32(p);R[4]=v;
 *     TR: the TLB's line,     TG[i]===a>>>12 && (RT[i]&1) ? PG[i]|(a&4095) : the emulator's
 *     L32: the RAM's word,    p < RAM && !(p&3) ? I32[p>>2] : the emulator's
 *
 * terminology: a block here is straight code from a place a jump
 * reaches to an instruction that always leaves (bx, pop {pc}, mov pc),
 * a page's end or 64 instructions; a conditional branch inside it
 * leaves or goes on, and an unconditional b or bl to a place of the
 * same page is followed (a trace: the call and what is called in one
 * function). A dynamic binary translator's, or a JIT's, basic block
 * extended.
 *
 * design: what is translated and what is not.
 * - Translated: the data-processing instructions (shifts by a register
 *   too, pc written), loads and stores of words, halves and bytes, push
 *   and pop, b, bl, bx, mul, the extensions: what compiled code is
 *   mostly made of. Anything else is one call of the interpreter from
 *   inside the block, and the block ends there when that instruction
 *   may change what interrupts or how addresses are translated.
 * - The state is the emulator's own: the registers' array, the flags'
 *   fields, the TLB's arrays, the RAM's bytes, read and written where
 *   they are (js_of_ocaml's values are JavaScript's arrays). The
 *   interpreter and a block can so follow each other at any
 *   instruction, and an abort inside a block is the interpreter's.
 * - The same instructions are counted (the board's time is its
 *   instructions), and interrupts are taken where the interpreter takes
 *   them, to a block's end: looked at when the board's loop is back,
 *   and it is back after a store to a device or an instruction that
 *   may unmask them. Blocks follow each other without the board's loop
 *   for 1024 instructions at most. Boot_bench's sessions give the same
 *   console with and without; the instructions counted are within a
 *   hundredth (a tick comes some instructions later).
 * - A block is kept by the physical address of its first instruction
 *   and its words, and found for an address through the TLB: an
 *   emptied TLB (each switch of process) costs one look a page of
 *   code. A kernel built for a page says which pages of instructions
 *   it wrote (Board.blocks_written). Another kernel is trusted no
 *   further than the interpreter's decode cache trusts it: at each
 *   invalidation of the instructions' cache, and each time the TLB is
 *   emptied, every block is compared with the memory before it runs
 *   again (the Pi's own mini-9pi boots so in 33 s under node, where
 *   51 by the interpreter).
 * - A block's text is what is compiled, and the same text is compiled
 *   once: a program run again has its pages elsewhere and the same
 *   blocks.
 *
 * To find a wrong translation (Boot_jit, by the environment):
 * JIT_CHECK=1, each block's first run done again by the interpreter
 * from the same registers and memory, and the two compared;
 * JIT_WITHOUT=reg,pc,mem,follow, kinds of instructions left to the
 * interpreter; JIT_MOST=n, n blocks and no more, the last one's text
 * printed; JIT_THRESHOLD=n.
 *
 * others: QEMU's TCG translates blocks to the host's instructions
 * through its own intermediate code; v86 (an x86 PC in a page)
 * translates hot code to WebAssembly modules; jslinux interprets. Here
 * the target is JavaScript's text, which a browser compiles: no
 * backend to write.
 *
 * Bellard, "QEMU, a Fast and Portable Dynamic Translator" (USENIX
 * 2005). *)

(* [attach board]: the board's blocks are this module's, from now *)
val attach : Board.t -> unit

(* a place reached by a jump so many times is translated (200) *)
val threshold : int ref

(* the blocks compiled, put back after their slot was lost, and not
 * made (the interpreter's instructions mostly) *)
val compiled : int ref
val retexted : int ref   (* made, and their code found by their text *)
val reused : int ref
val refused : int ref

(* Claude Code

(* The syntax tree of rc, as the parser builds it and the evaluator
 * walks it. Its printer is Show_ast. (No Ast.mli: the module is its
 * types.) *)

type word =
  | Word of string * bool           (* its text, and whether it was quoted *)
  | Dollar of word                  (* $x *)
  | Count of word                   (* $#x *)
  | Join of word                    (* dollar-quote x: the list joined *)
  | Sub of word * word list         (* $x(1 2) *)
  | Paren of word list              (* (a b c) *)
  | Concat of word * word           (* a^b, or a free caret *)
  | Backquote of word option * cmd  (* `{cmd}, `sep{cmd} *)
  | Pipefd of side * cmd            (* <{cmd}, >{cmd} *)

and redir =
  | Open of rkind * int * word      (* >f >>f <f <>f, on an fd *)
  | Here of int * heredoc           (* <<tag *)
  | Dup of int * int                (* >[a=b]: fd a becomes a copy of fd b *)
  | Close of int                    (* >[a=] *)

and rkind = Write | Append | Read | RdWr

(* a here document's body is read after its line, so the parser fills
 * it in later *)
and heredoc = { tag : string; expand : bool; mutable body : string }

(* <{cmd}: we read what cmd writes; >{cmd}: we write what it reads *)
and side = Reads | Writes

and cmd =
  | Empty
  | Simple of word list
  | Redirect of redir * cmd         (* applied, then the command *)
  | Seq of cmd * cmd
  | Async of cmd                    (* cmd & *)
  | And of cmd * cmd
  | Or of cmd * cmd
  | Not of cmd
  | Pipe of int * int * cmd * cmd   (* |[a=b]: the left's fd a to the right's b *)
  | Brace of cmd
  | Subshell of cmd                 (* @ cmd *)
  | If of cmd * cmd
  | IfNot of cmd
  | While of cmd * cmd
  | For of word * word list option * cmd   (* None: for(x), over $* *)
  | Switch of word * cmd
  | Match of word * word list       (* ~ subject patterns *)
  | Fn of word list * cmd option    (* None: delete *)
  | Assign of word * word * cmd option     (* x=v, or x=v cmd *)

(* See Builtin.mli *)

open Common

let status t s = Env.set_status (Eval.env t) s
let var t name = Env.get (Eval.env t) name

let cd t args =
  match args with
  | _ :: _ :: _ -> Eval.eprint "Usage: cd [directory]\n"; status t "usage"
  | _ ->
      let dir = match args with [ d ] -> d | _ -> (match var t "home" with h :: _ -> h | [] -> "/") in
      let tries =
        if dir <> "" && (dir.[0] = '/' || String.length dir > 1 && String.sub dir 0 2 = "./") then [ dir ]
        else match var t "cdpath" with [] -> [ dir ] | cdpath ->
          List.map (fun p -> if p = "" || p = "." then dir else Filename.concat p dir) cdpath
      in
      let rec go = function
        | [] -> ()
        | d :: rest -> (
            match CapUnix.chdir (Eval.caps t) d with
            | () -> status t ""
            | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) ->
                if rest = [] then begin
                  Eval.eprint (Printf.sprintf "Can't cd %s: %s\n" dir (Unix.error_message e));
                  status t "can't cd"
                end
                else go rest)
      in
      go tries

let exit_ t args = raise (Eval.Exit (match args with s :: _ -> s | [] -> Env.status (Eval.env t)))

(* the lines of a file, read as it is read: a terminal or a pipe one
 * byte at a time, so that the commands run get the rest *)
let refill_of_fd ~prompt (fd : Unix.file_descr) : bool -> string option =
  let byte = Bytes.create 1 in
  fun continued ->
    prompt continued;
    let b = Buffer.create 80 in
    let rec go () =
      match Unix.read fd byte 0 1 with
      | 0 -> if Buffer.length b = 0 then None else Some (Buffer.contents b)
      | _ ->
          Buffer.add_char b (Bytes.get byte 0);
          if Bytes.get byte 0 = '\n' then Some (Buffer.contents b) else go ()
      | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINTR, _, _) -> go ()
    in
    go ()

let dot t args =
  let interactive, args = match args with "-i" :: rest -> true, rest | _ -> false, args in
  match args with
  | [] -> Eval.eprint "Usage: . [-i] file [arg ...]\n"; status t "usage"
  | file :: rest ->
      let found = if String.contains file '/' then Some file else Process.search ~path:(var t "path") file in
      (* 9base's words for it: file: rc (argv0): .: can't open: why *)
      let cant why =
        Eval.eprint (Printf.sprintf "%s: rc (%s): .: can't open: %s\n" file (Eval.argv0 t) why);
        raise (Eval.Error "")
      in
      match found with
      | None -> cant "No such file or directory"
      | Some path -> (
          match Unix.openfile path [ Unix.O_RDONLY; Unix.O_CLOEXEC ] 0 with
          | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> cant (Unix.error_message e)
          | fd ->
              let prompt continued =
                if interactive then
                  match var t "prompt" with
                  | p1 :: p2 :: _ -> Eval.eprint (if continued then p2 else p1)
                  | [ p1 ] -> if not continued then Eval.eprint p1
                  | [] -> ()
              in
              let lx =
                if (not interactive) && (Unix.fstat fd).Unix.st_kind = Unix.S_REG then begin
                  let ic = Unix.in_channel_of_descr fd in
                  let text = really_input_string ic (in_channel_length ic) in
                  close_in ic;
                  Lexer.of_string text
                end
                else Lexer.create ~refill:(refill_of_fd ~prompt fd)
              in
              let env = Eval.env t in
              Env.local env "*" rest (fun () ->
                Env.local env "0" [ file ] (fun () ->
                  Eval.source t ~name:(Some file) ~interactive lx)))

let eval t args =
  if args = [] then raise (Eval.Error "Usage: eval cmd ...");
  Eval.source t ~name:None ~interactive:false (Lexer.of_string (String.concat " " args ^ "\n"))

let exec t args =
  match args with
  | [] -> ()
  | _ -> Process.exec (Eval.caps t) ~path:(var t "path") ~env:(Env.export (Eval.env t)) args

(* shift more than there is: all of them, no error (builtins.c) *)
let shift t args =
  match args with
  | _ :: _ :: _ -> Eval.eprint "Usage: shift [n]\n"; status t "shift usage"
  | _ ->
      let n = match args with [ s ] -> (int_of_string_opt s ||| 0) | _ -> 1 in
      Env.set (Eval.env t) "*" (List.filteri (fun i _ -> i >= n) (var t "*"));
      status t ""

let wait t args =
  let caps = Eval.caps t in
  match args with
  | [ pid ] -> (
      match int_of_string_opt pid with
      | Some p when List.mem p (Eval.background t) -> status t (Process.wait caps p); Eval.forget t p
      | _ -> status t "")
  | _ ->
      List.iter (fun p -> status t (Process.wait caps p); Eval.forget t p) (Eval.background t)

let whatis t args =
  let env = Eval.env t in
  let bad = ref false in
  args |> List.iter (fun name ->
    let v = Env.get env name and f = Env.fn env name in
    if v <> [] then
      Eval.print (Printf.sprintf "%s=%s\n" (Show_ast.quote name)
                    (match v with [ x ] -> Show_ast.quote x | l -> "(" ^ String.concat " " (List.map Show_ast.quote l) ^ ")"));
    (match f with
     | Some body -> Eval.print (Printf.sprintf "fn %s %s\n" (Show_ast.quote name) (Show_ast.to_string Show_ast.cmd body))
     | None -> ());
    if v = [] && f = None then
      if Hashtbl.mem Eval.builtins name || name = "builtin" then Eval.print ("builtin " ^ name ^ "\n")
      else match Process.search ~path:(Env.get env "path") name with
        | Some p -> Eval.print (p ^ "\n")
        | None -> Eval.eprint (name ^ ": not found\n"); bad := true);
  status t (if !bad then "not found" else "")

let flag t args =
  let env = Eval.env t in
  match args with
  | [ c ] when String.length c = 1 -> status t (if Env.flag env c.[0] then "" else "flag not set")
  | [ c; "+" ] when String.length c = 1 -> Env.set_flag env c.[0] true; status t ""
  | [ c; "-" ] when String.length c = 1 -> Env.set_flag env c.[0] false; status t ""
  | _ -> Eval.eprint "Usage: flag [letter] [+-]\n"; status t "flag usage"

let init () =
  List.iter (fun (name, f) -> Hashtbl.replace Eval.builtins name f)
    [ "cd", cd; "exit", exit_; ".", dot; "eval", eval; "exec", exec; "shift", shift;
      "wait", wait; "whatis", whatis; "flag", flag;
      "rfork", (fun t _ -> status t ""); "finit", (fun t _ -> status t "") ]

(* The builtins: the commands the shell runs itself, because they
 * change the shell (principia's builtins.c).
 *
 *     cd [dir]         chdir; no dir: $home; a relative dir is tried in
 *                      each of $cdpath. Failing: "Can't cd dir: why",
 *                      status can't cd (checked on 9base's rc)
 *     exit [status]    end rc, with this status or $status
 *     . [-i] file args read file's commands, $* set to args; file is
 *                      searched in $path; -i: interactive (a prompt,
 *                      errors don't end it)
 *     eval args        the args joined by spaces, as commands
 *     exec cmd         replace rc with cmd (and exec alone keeps the
 *                      redirections it is given, for rc itself)
 *     shift [n]        drop n words from $*
 *     wait [pid]       for the children started with &
 *     whatis names     how rc would read each back: x=(a b c), fn f
 *                      {...}, builtin cd, /usr/bin/ls, or "x: not found"
 *     flag c [+-]      is -c set (status "" or "flag not set"), set it,
 *                      clear it
 *     rfork, finit     accepted, and nothing on a Unix host (9base: rfork
 *                      e succeeds with an empty status)
 *
 * Why cd must be a builtin, the Principia book's question: chdir
 * changes the directory of the process that calls it, and a cd program
 * would change only its own, and then exit.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Unix learned it by a bug. On the PDP-7, before fork, the shell ran
 * a command in its own process, and chdir was an ordinary command.
 * Once the shell forked a process for each command, chdir still ran,
 * said nothing, and changed nothing: only the child's directory.
 * Ritchie tells of the puzzlement, and of the fix: the command
 * moved into the shell.
 *
 * design:
 * The test for a builtin is that one question: does it change the
 * shell's own process (its directory, its variables, its input, its
 * life)? Everything else is a program, test and echo included: rc
 * has eleven builtins where bash has some sixty, most of them there
 * for speed.
 *
 * References: Dennis Ritchie, "The Evolution of the Unix Time-sharing
 * System" (AT&T Bell Laboratories Technical Journal, 1984);
 * principia's builtins.c. *)

(* register them in Eval.builtins *)
val init : unit -> unit

(* plan9port's rcmain (/usr/lib/plan9/etc/rcmain, as 9base installs it) *)
let rcmain = {|# rcmain: Plan 9 on Unix version
if(~ $#home 0) home=$HOME
if(~ $#home 0) home=/
if(~ $#ifs 0) ifs=IFS
switch($#prompt){
case 0
	prompt=('% ' '	')
case 1
	prompt=($prompt '	')
}
if(~ $rcname ?.out ?.rc */?.rc */?.out) prompt=('broken! ' '	')
if(flag p) path=(/bin /usr/bin)
if not{
	finit
	# should be taken care of by rc now, but leave just in case
}
fn sigexit
if(! ~ $#cflag 0){
	if(flag l && test -r $home/lib/profile) . $home/lib/profile
	status=''
	eval $cflag
	exit $status
}
if(flag i){
	if(flag l && test -r $home/lib/profile) . $home/lib/profile
	status=''
	if(! ~ $#* 0) . $*
	. -i '/dev/stdin'
	exit $status
}
if(flag l && test -r $home/lib/profile) . $home/lib/profile
if(~ $#* 0){
	. /dev/stdin
	exit $status
}
status=''
. $*
exit $status
|}

(* its ifs line is a blank, a tab and a newline, which a {| |} string
 * would not show *)
let rcmain =
  match String.split_on_char '\n' rcmain with
  | lines ->
      String.concat "\n"
        (List.map (fun l -> if l = "if(~ $#ifs 0) ifs=IFS" then "if(~ $#ifs 0) ifs=' \t\n'" else l) lines)

(* Plan 9's own (/rc/lib/rcmain), where rc runs on Plan 9: the
 * standard input is '#d/0', there is no $HOME nor /usr/bin *)
let rcmain_plan9 = {|# rcmain: Plan 9 version
if(~ $#home 0) home=/
if(~ $#ifs 0) ifs=' 	
'

if not{
	finit
	if(~ $#path 0) path=(. /bin)
}
fn sigexit
if(! ~ $#cflag 0){
	if(flag l && /bin/test -r $home/lib/profile) . $home/lib/profile
	status=''
	eval $cflag
}
if not if(flag i){
	if(flag l && /bin/test -r $home/lib/profile) . $home/lib/profile
	status=''
	if(! ~ $#* 0) . $*
	. -i '#d/0'

if not{
	status=''
	. $*
}
exit $status
|}

let rcmain = if Sys.os_type = "Plan9" then rcmain_plan9 else rcmain

let usage = "usage: rc [-eiIlrvxp] [-c arg] [-m rcmain] [file [arg ...]]"

(* -h: the usage, the flags, and the language by example, as it runs *)
let help = {|usage: mini-rc [-eiIlrvxp] [-c cmd] [-m rcmain] [file [arg ...]]
Plan 9's rc, faithfully: runs the file, the -c command, or the terminal's
commands (with a prompt). -e: a failed command ends rc; -x: each command
printed; -i, -I: interactive, or not; -l: a login shell ($home/lib/profile).
The language, by example, one line after the other at its prompt:
  x=(a b c); echo $x $#x $x(2)        a b c 3 b (a variable is a list)
  echo $x^.c                          a.c b.c c.c
  for(i in a b) echo $i               a, then b
  if(~ $x(1) a) echo yes; if not echo no
  fn greet { echo hello $1 }; greet you
  x=`{echo one two}; echo $#x         2: a command's output, its words
  { echo a; echo b } > f; cat f       a, then b
  ls /nonexistent >[2] /dev/null || echo failed: $status
|}

let run (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : int =
  Builtin.init ();
  let env = Env.create () in
  Env.import env (CapUnix.environment caps ());
  let argv0 = if Array.length argv > 0 then argv.(0) else "rc" in
  let main_file = ref None in
  (* cflag set always, -c's command or none: a child rc imports its
   * parent's variables, and with -c's its rcmain ran it again, not its
   * file. old: set with -c only: `<|rc file` in a mkfile (mk's rc -c)
   * started rcs without end *)
  Env.set env "cflag" [];
  let rec flags = function
    | "-c" :: cmd :: rest -> Env.set env "cflag" [ cmd ]; flags rest
    | "-m" :: file :: rest -> main_file := Some file; flags rest
    | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' && a <> "--" ->
        String.iteri (fun i c -> if i > 0 then Env.set_flag env c true) a;
        flags rest
    | "--" :: rest -> Some rest
    | rest -> Some rest
  in
  match flags (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) with
  | None -> prerr_endline usage; 1
  | Some args ->
      Env.set env "*" args;
      Env.set env "rcname" [ argv0 ];
      Env.set env "pid" [ string_of_int (CapUnix.getpid caps ()) ];
      if not (Env.flag env 'I') && Env.get env "cflag" = [] && args = [] && Unix.isatty Unix.stdin then
        Env.set_flag env 'i' true;
      Sys.set_signal Sys.sigint (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> Eval.interrupted := true));
      let t = Eval.create caps ~argv0 env in
      let text =
        match !main_file with
        | None -> rcmain
        | Some f -> FS.read caps (Fpath.v f)
      in
      let finish status =
        (* sigexit, if defined, runs once on the way out *)
        (match Env.fn env "sigexit" with
         | Some body ->
             Env.set_fn env "sigexit" None;
             Env.set_status env status;
             (try Eval.run t body with _ -> ())
         | None -> ());
        flush stdout;
        Process.code status
      in
      match Eval.source t ~name:(Some "rcmain") ~interactive:false (Lexer.of_string text) with
      | () -> finish (Env.status env)
      | exception Eval.Exit s -> finish s
      | exception (Eval.Error m | Word.Error m) ->
          if m <> "" then Eval.eprint (Printf.sprintf "rc (%s): %s\n" argv0 m);
          (* claude: an error ends rc without its sigexit, as 9base's *)
          Env.set_fn env "sigexit" None;
          finish "error"

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : int =
  match Array.to_list argv with
  | [ _; ("-h" | "--help") ] -> Console.print caps help; 0
  | _ -> run caps argv

(* mini-rc: Plan 9's shell, rc. A line typed is read, made a tree,
 * and the tree is walked: words expanded to lists of strings,
 * programs found, forked and waited for.
 *
 *     characters                            the modules, a line's way
 *        | Lexer     quotes, free carets, redirections with their fds
 *     tokens
 *        | Parser    by recursive descent, syn.y's grammar
 *     Ast.cmd  ----- Show_ast: the tree as rc's text again (whatis, -x,
 *        |           a function in the environment)
 *        | Eval      walks it
 *        |-- Word    $x, $#x, a^b, `{cmd}: a word to a list of strings
 *        |-- Glob    *.c to the file names
 *        |-- Env     variables and functions, and their export
 *        |-- Builtin cd, ., eval, exit...: what must be done in the shell
 *        '-- Process fork, exec, wait, pipe, dup: the rest
 *
 * evolution:
 * The shell, from 1965 to rc. The word and the idea are Louis
 * Pouzin's: on CTSS his RUNCOM ran commands from a file, and for
 * Multics he described the "shell", a program like any other that
 * reads commands and runs them, which could then be replaced. Ken
 * Thompson's shell for the first Unix (1971) is that program: a
 * command a line, < and >, and from 1973 the pipe; its if and goto
 * were programs. Steve Bourne's (the seventh edition, 1979) made it
 * a programming language: variables, for, case, while, functions
 * later, here documents, and `cmd`; every sh since is a superset of
 * it. Bill Joy's csh at Berkeley (1978) was for the person typing:
 * history, aliases, job control, ~. David Korn's ksh (1983) put both
 * in one. Tom Duff's rc (1989, for the tenth edition and Plan 9)
 * went the other way and removed: one kind of quote, a value that is
 * a list and is never scanned again (Word), a grammar yacc accepts
 * (Parser), and no job control, history or line editing, which on
 * Plan 9 are the window's (rio's text) and not each program's.
 *
 * others:
 * Byron Rakitzis rewrote rc for Unix (1991), with a few changes (an
 * else, where Duff has if not): the rc most Linux distributions
 * package. Its sources became es (Paul Haahr and Rakitzis, 1993), an
 * rc with closures, where pipes and redirections are functions a
 * user may redefine. Here it is Duff's rc, as plan9port and 9base
 * run it on Unix: the corpus is compared with 9base's.
 *
 * The command line: its usage, flags and a few examples are [help] in
 * CLI.ml, what mini-rc -h prints (-h and --help, not rc's flags).
 *
 * rc does not start in C: it runs a script, rcmain, which reads the
 * profile if asked, then the -c command, the file, or the terminal
 * (plan9port's rcmain, embedded here as it is in 9base; -m reads
 * another):
 *
 *     mini-rc script a b     *=(script a b); . rcmain -> . $*
 *     mini-rc -c 'cmd'       cflag=cmd; . rcmain -> eval $cflag
 *     mini-rc                . rcmain -> . -i /dev/stdin, with a prompt
 *                           if the input is a terminal, or with -i
 *
 * The environment is read first (functions included), then the flags
 * are set as variables flag reads, and $status is rc's exit code:
 * "" 0, a number that number, anything else 1.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * $status is a string because a Plan 9 process ends with one: exits
 * takes a message, empty for success, where Unix's exit takes a
 * number from 0 to 255 that each program gives its own meanings to.
 * The line above is that string made a number again, for a Unix
 * parent.
 *
 * References: Tom Duff, "Rc -- The Plan 9 Shell" (1990, in the Plan 9
 * manual's second volume): the paper to read first, short, and the
 * source of the quotations in this directory. rc(1). S. R. Bourne,
 * "The UNIX Shell" (Bell System Technical Journal, 1978). Louis
 * Pouzin, "The Origin of the Shell" (multicians.org, 2000). Paul
 * Haahr and Byron Rakitzis, "Es: A shell with higher-order functions"
 * (USENIX Winter 1993). principia's shells/rc. *)

type caps = < Eval.caps; Cap.argv; Cap.exit; Cap.stdout >

val main : < caps; .. > -> string array -> int

(* See Env.mli *)

open Common

type t = {
  vars : (string, string list) Hashtbl.t;
  fns : (string, Ast.cmd) Hashtbl.t;
  flags : (char, unit) Hashtbl.t;
}

let create () = { vars = Hashtbl.create 101; fns = Hashtbl.create 17; flags = Hashtbl.create 7 }

let get t name = Hashtbl.find_opt t.vars name ||| []

let raw_set t name v = if v = [] then Hashtbl.remove t.vars name else Hashtbl.replace t.vars name v

(* $path and $PATH are the same list, written two ways (plan9port's,
 * for Unix's programs: on Plan 9 there is $path only) *)
let set t name v =
  raw_set t name v;
  match name with
  | _ when Sys.os_type = "Plan9" -> ()
  | "path" -> raw_set t "PATH" (if v = [] then [] else [ String.concat ":" v ])
  | "PATH" -> raw_set t "path" (List.concat_map (String.split_on_char ':') v)
  | _ -> ()

let local t name v f =
  let saved = Hashtbl.find_opt t.vars name in
  set t name v;
  Fun.protect f ~finally:(fun () -> set t name (saved ||| []))

let status t = String.concat "" (get t "status")
let set_status t s = raw_set t "status" [ s ]
let ok t = String.for_all (fun c -> c = '0' || c = '|') (status t)

let fn t name = Hashtbl.find_opt t.fns name
let set_fn t name = function Some c -> Hashtbl.replace t.fns name c | None -> Hashtbl.remove t.fns name
let vars t = Hashtbl.fold (fun k v acc -> (k, v) :: acc) t.vars [] |> List.sort compare

let flag t c = Hashtbl.mem t.flags c
let set_flag t c on = if on then Hashtbl.replace t.flags c () else Hashtbl.remove t.flags c

let import t (env : string array) =
  Procs.split_env env |> List.iter (fun (name, v) ->
    if String.length name > 3 && String.sub name 0 3 = "fn#" then
      (* the function's body, as whatis prints it *)
      match Parser.parse_string v with
      | c -> set_fn t (String.sub name 3 (String.length name - 3)) (Some c)
      | exception _ -> ()
    else set t name (String.split_on_char '\001' v))

let export t : string array =
  let vars =
    Hashtbl.fold (fun k v acc -> if v = [] then acc else (k ^ "=" ^ String.concat "\001" v) :: acc) t.vars []
  in
  (* plan9port's rc ends a function's value with a newline, and needs it *)
  let fns = Hashtbl.fold (fun k c acc -> ("fn#" ^ k ^ "=" ^ Show_ast.to_string Show_ast.cmd c ^ "\n") :: acc) t.fns [] in
  Array.of_list (List.sort compare vars @ List.sort compare fns)
shell/Env.mli

(* Variables, functions, and the environment that carries both to
 * children.
 *
 * A variable is a list of strings; unset and () are the same. A local
 * assignment, x=v cmd, and a for loop's variable are dynamic: set for
 * the command, and put back after, whatever it did (principia's
 * Xlocal, Xunlocal), so a function called inside sees them.
 *
 * {b The environment.} Every variable is exported, a list joined by
 * \001 so that a child rc splits it back; an empty list is not
 * exported (on Plan 9 it is an empty /env file, which reads back as
 * (); a Unix program given X= sees one empty string -- the bug mini-mk
 * met building xix). Functions are exported too, as fn#name={body}
 * and a newline (checked on 9base's rc: fn#g={echo g} and a newline,
 * which it needs to read one back), and read back when rc starts.
 * $path is a list kept in step with $PATH, joined by :.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * On Unix the environment is an array of "NAME=value" strings that
 * exec copies into the new program's memory: a child gets a copy,
 * and nothing it does to it is seen by anyone. On Plan 9 each
 * variable is a file in /env (the kernel's env device), its
 * "components terminated by zero bytes", and a function is the file
 * /env/fn#name: reading a variable is reading a file, ls /env lists
 * them, and whether a child shares its parent's or gets a copy is
 * one bit of rfork. No getenv in the kernel's interface, no third
 * argument to main. The zero byte is what a Unix environment string
 * cannot hold, hence \001 here, as plan9port.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The environment came to Unix with the seventh edition (1979),
 * together with Bourne's shell, which needed it to hand its
 * variables down. bash exports its functions through it as rc does,
 * and its way of reading them back at startup was the Shellshock
 * hole of 2014: text from the environment given to the parser, which
 * ran what followed the function's body.
 *
 * References: principia's var.c, env.c; plan9port's rc (unix.c); Tom
 * Duff, "Rc -- The Plan 9 Shell" (1990), "Environment"; env(3) of
 * Plan 9's manual. *)

type t

val create : unit -> t

val get : t -> string -> string list
val set : t -> string -> string list -> unit

(* [local t name value f]: [f] with [name] set to [value], then put back *)
val local : t -> string -> string list -> (unit -> 'a) -> 'a

val status : t -> string
val set_status : t -> string -> unit

(* is $status true: every character a 0 or a | (status.c)? *)
val ok : t -> bool

val fn : t -> string -> Ast.cmd option
val set_fn : t -> string -> Ast.cmd option -> unit
val vars : t -> (string * string list) list   (* sorted, for whatis *)

(* the flags rc was given, and those set by the flag builtin *)
val flag : t -> char -> bool
val set_flag : t -> char -> bool -> unit

(* the environment, in (a program's name=value strings) and out *)
val import : t -> string array -> unit
val export : t -> string array

(* Claude Code

(* See Eval.mli *)
open Ast

type caps = < Process.caps; Cap.chdir; Cap.env >

type t = {
  env : Env.t;
  caps : caps;
  argv0 : string;
  mutable ifnot : bool;        (* the last if's condition was false *)
  mutable apids : int list;    (* started with & *)
}

exception Exit of string
exception Error of string

let create (caps : < caps; .. >) ~argv0 env =
  { env; caps = (caps :> caps); argv0; ifnot = false; apids = [] }

let env t = t.env
let caps t = t.caps
let argv0 t = t.argv0
let background t = t.apids
let forget t pid = t.apids <- List.filter (( <> ) pid) t.apids

let builtins : (string, t -> string list -> unit) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 17

let print s = print_string s; flush stdout
let eprint s = prerr_string s; flush stderr

(* SIGINT only sets this; the next command acts on it (trap.c's notes,
 * delivered between instructions: here, between commands) *)
let interrupted = ref false

(* how many of the files being read are read as a terminal ([source]'s
 * interactive: rcmain's . -i, or a boot script's, which has no -i flag
 * of rc's own): an interrupt goes back to the innermost one's prompt
 * (rc's runq->iflag, a flag of each file read, where Xerror stops) *)
let terminals = ref 0

let set_status t s = Env.set_status t.env s
let ok t = Env.ok t.env

(* in a child: run [f], and exit with its status *)
let child t (f : unit -> unit) : int =
  try f (); Process.code (Env.status t.env) with
  | Exit s -> Process.code s
  | Error m | Word.Error m -> if m <> "" then eprint (Printf.sprintf "rc (%s): %s\n" t.argv0 m); 1

(* a fork that failed is an error said, as Plan 9's rc (Xerror's "try
 * again"). old: Process.fork's exception, in a child (a pipe's command,
 * a backquote's) ended it in silence: mini-9pi's full table of
 * processes cut a backquote's list, no word said *)
let fork t f =
  try Process.fork t.caps f
  with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) ->
    raise (Error ("fork: " ^ Unix.error_message e))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Words *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let readdir d =
  match Sys.readdir (if d = "" then "." else d) with
  | names -> Some (Array.to_list names)
  | exception Sys_error _ -> None

let exists f = Sys.file_exists f

let rec ctx t : Word.ctx = {
  var = Env.get t.env;
  backquote = (fun _seps c ->
    let r, w = Process.pipe t.caps in
    let pid = fork t (fun () ->
      Process.close r; Process.dup2 w 1; Process.close w; child t (fun () -> run t c)) in
    Process.close w;
    let out = Process.read_all r in
    Process.close r;
    (* the command's status is the backquote's *)
    set_status t (Process.wait t.caps pid);
    out);
  pipefd = (fun side c ->
    (* the command's end is a child's fd 1 (or 0); ours stays open, and
     * its name is the word *)
    let r, w = Process.pipe t.caps in
    let mine, theirs, fd = match side with Reads -> r, w, 1 | Writes -> w, r, 0 in
    let _pid = fork t (fun () ->
      Process.close mine; Process.dup2 theirs fd; Process.close theirs; child t (fun () -> run t c)) in
    Process.close theirs;
    Printf.sprintf "/dev/fd/%d" mine);
}

and expand t w = try Word.expand (ctx t) w with Word.Error m -> raise (Error m)

and words t (ws : word list) : string list =
  List.concat_map (fun w -> List.concat_map (Glob.files ~readdir ~exists) (expand t w)) ws

and singleton t w = try Word.singleton (ctx t) w with Word.Error m -> raise (Error m)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Commands *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* -e: a failed command ends rc *)
and check t ~e = if e && Env.flag t.env 'e' && not (ok t) then raise (Exit (Env.status t.env))

(* fn sigint, if there is one; else a script ends, and the terminal
 * gets its prompt back *)
and interrupt t =
  interrupted := false;
  match Env.fn t.env "sigint" with
  | Some body -> run t body
  (* old: if Env.flag t.env 'i': mini-9pi's boot script ends by . -i
   * '#d/0' with no -i of its own, and the first interrupt ended it, the
   * first process ("panic: boot process died", 2026-10-12) *)
  | None -> if Env.flag t.env 'i' || !terminals > 0 then raise (Error "") else raise (Exit "interrupt")

and run_e t ~e (c : cmd) : unit =
  if !interrupted then interrupt t;
  match c with
  | Empty -> ()
  | Simple ws -> simple t (words t ws); check t ~e
  | Redirect (r, Simple [ Word ("exec", false) ]) -> redirect t r ~keep:true (fun () -> ())
  | Redirect (r, c) -> redirect t r ~keep:false (fun () -> run_e t ~e c)
  | Seq (a, b) -> run_e t ~e a; run_e t ~e b
  | Async c ->
      let pid = fork t (fun () ->
        let null = Process.open_file t.caps Read "/dev/null" in
        Process.dup2 null 0; Process.close null;
        child t (fun () -> run_e t ~e c)) in
      Env.set t.env "apid" [ string_of_int pid ];
      t.apids <- pid :: t.apids
  | And (a, b) -> run_e t ~e:false a; if ok t then run_e t ~e b
  | Or (a, b) -> run_e t ~e:false a; if not (ok t) then run_e t ~e b
  | Not c -> run_e t ~e:false c; set_status t (if ok t then "false" else "")
  | Pipe (l, r, a, b) ->
      let rd, wr = Process.pipe t.caps in
      let pid = fork t (fun () ->
        Process.close rd; Process.dup2 wr l; Process.close wr; child t (fun () -> run_e t ~e a)) in
      Process.close wr;
      let right =
        Process.with_fds [ r ] (fun () ->
          Process.dup2 rd r; Process.close rd; run_e t ~e b; Env.status t.env)
      in
      let left = Process.wait t.caps pid in
      set_status t (left ^ "|" ^ right)
  | Brace c -> run_e t ~e c
  | Subshell c ->
      let pid = fork t (fun () -> child t (fun () -> run_e t ~e c)) in
      set_status t (Process.wait t.caps pid);
      check t ~e
  | If (cond, body) ->
      run_e t ~e:false cond;
      t.ifnot <- true;
      if ok t then (run_e t ~e body; t.ifnot <- false)
  | IfNot body -> if t.ifnot then run_e t ~e body
  | While (cond, body) ->
      let rec loop () =
        if cond = Empty then set_status t "" else run_e t ~e:false cond;
        if ok t then (run_e t ~e body; loop ())
      in
      loop ()
  | For (x, list, body) ->
      let name = singleton t x in
      let values = match list with None -> Env.get t.env "*" | Some ws -> words t ws in
      Env.local t.env name (Env.get t.env name) (fun () ->
        values |> List.iter (fun v -> Env.set t.env name [ v ]; run_e t ~e body))
  | Switch (w, body) ->
      let subject = String.concat " " (List.map Glob.to_string (expand t w)) in
      let rec flat = function Seq (a, b) -> flat a @ flat b | Brace c -> flat c | Empty -> [] | c -> [ c ] in
      let rec go matched = function
        | [] -> ()
        | Simple (Word ("case", false) :: pats) :: rest ->
            if not matched then
              go (List.exists (fun p -> Glob.matches p subject) (List.concat_map (expand t) pats)) rest
        | c :: rest -> if matched then run_e t ~e c; go matched rest
      in
      go false (flat body)
  | Match (w, pats) ->
      let subject = String.concat " " (List.map Glob.to_string (expand t w)) in
      let pats = List.concat_map (expand t) pats in
      set_status t (if List.exists (fun p -> Glob.matches p subject) pats then "" else "no match");
      check t ~e
  | Fn (names, body) -> List.iter (fun n -> Env.set_fn t.env n body) (words t names)
  | Assign (x, v, None) -> Env.set t.env (singleton t x) (words t [ v ])
  | Assign (x, v, Some c) -> Env.local t.env (singleton t x) (words t [ v ]) (fun () -> run_e t ~e c)

and run t c = run_e t ~e:true c

(* a function, a builtin, or a program (simple.c's Xsimple) *)
and simple t (args : string list) : unit =
  match args with
  | [] -> raise (Error "empty argument list")
  | name :: rest ->
      if Env.flag t.env 'x' then eprint (String.concat " " (List.map Show_ast.quote args) ^ "\n");
      match Env.fn t.env name with
      | Some body -> Env.local t.env "*" rest (fun () -> run t body)
      | None -> command t name rest

and command t name rest =
  match name, rest with
  | "builtin", [] -> eprint "builtin: empty argument list\n"; set_status t "empty arg list"
  | "builtin", n :: r -> command t n r
  | _ -> (
      match Hashtbl.find_opt builtins name with
      | Some f -> f t rest
      | None ->
          let path = Env.get t.env "path" and env = Env.export t.env in
          let pid = fork t (fun () -> Process.exec t.caps ~path ~env (name :: rest)) in
          set_status t (Process.wait t.caps pid))

(* a redirection around [f]; with [~keep], for exec, not undone *)
and redirect t (r : redir) ~keep (f : unit -> unit) : unit =
  let target = function
    | Open (_, fd, _) | Here (fd, _) -> fd
    | Dup (a, _) | Close a -> a
  in
  let apply () =
    match r with
    | Open (k, fd, w) ->
        let file =
          match words t [ w ] with
          | [ file ] -> file
          | l ->
              let op = fst (Show_ast.arrow k) in
              (* claude: 9base's messages for < and > (not >>) end with a
               * newline of their own *)
              raise (Error (op ^ (if l = [] then " requires file" else " requires singleton")
                            ^ if k = Append then "" else "\n"))
        in
        let n =
          try Process.open_file t.caps k file
          with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) ->
            (* claude: 9base's words for it: file: rc (argv0): can't open: why *)
            eprint (Printf.sprintf "%s: rc (%s): can't open: %s\n" file t.argv0 (Unix.error_message e));
            raise (Error "")
        in
        Process.dup2 n fd;
        Process.close n
    | Here (fd, h) ->
        (* the body through a pipe, from a child *)
        let body = if h.expand then heredoc t h.body else h.body in
        let rd, wr = Process.pipe t.caps in
        let pid = fork t (fun () -> Process.close rd; Process.write wr body; 0) in
        ignore pid;
        Process.close wr;
        Process.dup2 rd fd;
        Process.close rd
    | Dup (a, b) -> Process.dup2 b a
    | Close a -> Process.close a
  in
  if keep then (flush stdout; flush stderr; apply (); f ())
  else Process.with_fds [ target r ] (fun () -> apply (); f ())

(* here.c's psubst: in a here document $name is its value, joined by
 * spaces, $1 an argument, $$ a $; a ^ right after the name is eaten,
 * and a $ before anything else is dropped (an empty name) *)
and heredoc t (s : string) : string =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) and n = String.length s in
  let idchr c = c > ' ' && not (String.contains "!\"#$%&'()+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^`{|}~" c) in
  let rec go i =
    if i < n then
      if s.[i] <> '$' then (Buffer.add_char b s.[i]; go (i + 1))
      else if i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] = '$' then (Buffer.add_char b '$'; go (i + 2))
      else begin
        let j = ref (i + 1) in
        while !j < n && idchr s.[!j] do incr j done;
        let name = String.sub s (i + 1) (!j - i - 1) in
        let v =
          match int_of_string_opt name with
          | Some k when k > 0 -> (match List.nth_opt (Env.get t.env "*") (k - 1) with Some v -> [ v ] | None -> [])
          | _ -> Env.get t.env name
        in
        Buffer.add_string b (String.concat " " v);
        go (if !j < n && s.[!j] = '^' then !j + 1 else !j)
      end
  in
  go 0;
  Buffer.contents b

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Reading commands *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let source t ~name ~interactive (lx : Lexer.t) : unit =
  let rec loop () =
    match Parser.line lx with
    | None -> ()
    | Some c ->
        (* an interrupt that came since the last line was run (its
         * command ended by it, or the prompt waiting) is not this one's:
         * the line typed after a Control-C was not run *)
        if interactive then interrupted := false;
        (try run t c with
         | (Error m | Word.Error m) when interactive ->
             if m <> "" then eprint (Printf.sprintf "rc (%s): %s\n" t.argv0 m);
             set_status t m);
        loop ()
    | exception (Parser.Error m | Lexer.Error m) ->
        let where =
          match name with
          | Some f when not interactive -> Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: " f (Lexer.line lx)
          | Some f -> f ^ ": "
          | None -> Printf.sprintf "line %d: " (Lexer.line lx)
        in
        eprint ("rc: " ^ where ^ m ^ "\n");
        set_status t "syntax error";
        if interactive then loop ()
  in
  if not interactive then loop ()
  else begin
    incr terminals;
    match loop () with
    | () -> decr terminals
    | exception e -> decr terminals; raise e
  end
