(* A tiny temperature converter with two fields where each one shows the
 * conversion of the other.
 *
 * It is the second of the 7GUIs tasks (m-ix's
 * version is examples/Gui7Temperature.ml), here with whole numbers
 * only. A click in a field, then the keys: digits, a sign, the
 * backspace; the Escape quits (or q, before a field is clicked).
 *
 * What the task asks for, and why it comes second: a change must
 * propagate in both directions, and half of what the user types is not
 * yet a number.
 *
 *     typed in Celsius     Celsius    Fahrenheit
 *     1                    1          34
 *     10                   10         50
 *     10x                  10x        50       not a number: the other
 *     10 (a backspace)     10         50       field is left alone
 *     then, in Fahrenheit:
 *     -40 (after three     -40        -40
 *     backspaces)
 *
 * - {b The model is the two texts}, not a temperature. A field must be
 *   able to show "10x" or "-" while they are being typed, and no number
 *   can represent those. The field being typed in keeps its text,
 *   whatever it is; the other field is recomputed only when that text
 *   is a number.
 * - {b There is no loop between the fields}. The message says which
 *   field was typed in, so the program can set the other one without
 *   it counting as a "change". With widgets that store their own text
 *   and report every change, setting one field from the other would
 *   trigger a callback, and the program would have to stop that echo
 *   itself.
 *
 * Its twin, examples/Gui7Temperature.ml (from the author's
 * playground), keeps the same model, the two texts, but is written in
 * lib_gui's immediate way: both fields are asked for at every frame,
 * and the one typed in is the one whose text came back changed, with
 * no message type; its numbers are floats, shown with one decimal.
 * Here it is TinyLibGUI's model, view and update: the field typed in
 * is said by its message (above).
 *
 * What is left out: fractions (tiny-ml has no floats, so we round to
 * the nearest whole number: 34 Fahrenheit gives 1 Celsius, and 1
 * Celsius gives 34), showing a field in red when its text is not a
 * number, and numbers longer than six digits.
 *
 * Exercises:
 * - show a field whose text is not a number in another colour (with
 *   one more widget, or a colour in Input);
 * - tenths: store each number as ten times its value;
 * - Kelvin: add a third field, computed from either of the two others.
 *
 * References: E. Kiss, "7GUIs: A GUI Programming Benchmark" (2014),
 * task 2. *)

(* the two fields' texts, as typed; a field's new text *)
type model = { c : string; f : string }
type msg = Celsius of string | Fahrenheit of string

(* The converter, for TinyLibGUI's run *)
val temperature : (model, msg) TinyLibGUI.gui

(* a text's whole number, and whether it is one *)
val number : string -> int * bool
tiny/TinyAppTetris.ml
10664
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt.
 *)
(* See TinyAppTetris.mli *)
(* The rules are tested on the host by feeding keys and frames to these
 * functions and printing the well as text (tests/TinyAppTetris_test.sh);
 * the picture can be tested with TinyKernelGraphics.ml. *)
open TinyLibPlayground

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Pieces *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the falling piece: which of the seven (I J L O S T Z), how many
 * quarter turns, where its square of 4 by 4 is in the well (its top
 * left cell's column and row; a row above the well is negative) *)
type piece = { kind : int; turn : int; x : int; y : int }

(* a kind's four turns, a turn four rows from the top, a row a
 * hexadecimal digit, its high bit the left cell *)
let turns =
  "0F00222200F04444" ^ "8E0064400E2044C0" ^ "2E0044600E80C440"
  ^ "6600660066006600" ^ "6C00462006C08C40"
  ^ "4E0046400E404C40" ^ "C60026400C604C80"

(* a kind's colour, a byte of the table: cyan, blue, orange, yellow, green,
 * purple, red *)
let colours = "\050\054\248\252\063\180\240"

let digit c = if c >= 'A' then Char.code c - 55 else Char.code c - 48
let filled kind turn row col =
  (digit turns.[(((kind * 4) + turn) * 4) + row] lsr (3 - col)) land 1 = 1

(* a piece's four cells in the well: a column and a row each *)
let cells { kind; turn; x; y } =
  let rec from row col acc =
    if row = 4 then acc
    else if col = 4 then from (row + 1) 0 acc
    else
      from row (col + 1)
        (if filled kind turn row col then (x + col, y + row) :: acc else acc)
  in
  from 0 0 []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The model *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* What changes when a piece lands: the well (200 cells, a row after
 * the other from the top; 0 an empty one, else a kind and 1), as
 * shapes with the panel beside it; the next piece's kind; the random
 * numbers' state; the score, the rows removed *)
type board = { 
  well : int array;
  ground : shape;
  next : int;
  seed : int;
  score : int;
  rows : int;
}

(* and what changes as it falls: the piece, the frames before it goes
 * down a row, whether the game is over; and whether the music is off
 * (m) *)
type model = {
  board : board;
  piece : piece;
  wait : int;
  over : bool;
  quiet : bool;
}

(* a piece is where it may be: in the well's sides and floor (its top
 * may be over the well), on no cell taken *)
let fits (well : int array) p =
  List.for_all (fun (c, r) ->
      c >= 0 && c < 10 && r < 20 && (r < 0 || well.((r * 10) + c) = 0))
    (cells p)

(* the frames a row takes: a second, a tenth less each level, a level every
 * ten rows *)
let delay rows = max 3 (30 - (3 * (rows / 10)))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The picture *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a cell is 16 pixels, the well's corner at (8, 8) *)
let cell kind col row =
  Move (8 + (16 * col), 8 + (16 * row), Rect (Char.code colours.[kind], 15, 15))
let shown (p : piece) =
  Group (List.map (fun (c, r) -> cell p.kind c r)
           (List.filter (fun (_, r) -> r >= 0) (cells p)))

let white = 255
let grey = 0xaa

(* the well's cells and the panel: its numbers, the next piece *)
let ground_of (well : int array) next score rows =
  let rec taken i acc =
    if i = 200 then acc
    else
      taken (i + 1)
        (if well.(i) = 0 then acc
         else cell (well.(i) - 1) (i mod 10) (i / 10) :: acc) in
  let line y name n =
    Group [ Move (184, y, Words (grey, name));
            Move (184, y + 16, Words (white, string_of_int n)) ] in
  let panel =
    Group [ Move (184, 8, Words (white, "TETRIS"));
            line 48 "score" score;
            line 96 "rows" rows;
            line 144 "level" (rows / 10) ] in
  let coming = Group [ Move (184, 192, Words (grey, "next")); 
                       shown { kind = next; turn = 0; x = 11; y = 13 } ] in
  Group (Rect (0, 288, 336) :: Move (8, 8, Rect (0x11, 160, 320))
         :: panel :: coming :: taken 0 [])

let banner =
  Move (16, 136, Group [ Rect (white, 144, 48); 
                         Move (2, 2, Rect (0, 140, 44)); 
                         Move (36, 6, Words (white, "GAME OVER"));
                         Move (20, 24, Words (grey, "space: again")) ])

let view m =
  if m.over then [ m.board.ground; shown m.piece; banner ]
  else [ m.board.ground; shown m.piece ]

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The rules *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the next piece enters at the top, another one is next: the game is
 * over if it has no room *)
let enter (well : int array) next seed score rows quiet =
  let piece = { kind = next; turn = 0; x = 3; y = 0 } in
  let seed = random seed in
  let board = { well; ground = ground_of well (seed mod 7) score rows;
                next = seed mod 7; seed; score; rows } in
  { board; piece; wait = delay rows; over = not (fits well piece); quiet }

let start seed quiet =
  let seed = random (1 + (seed land 0xffff)) in
  enter (Array.make 200 0) (seed mod 7) seed 0 0 quiet

(* the piece lands: its cells are the well's, in another well; the full
 * rows are removed (the others copied from the bottom, a full one
 * passed over); the score, by how many at once *)
let land_ { board = b; piece; quiet; _ } =
  let well = Array.make 200 0 in
  for i = 0 to 199 do well.(i) <- b.well.(i) done;
  List.iter (fun (c, r) -> if r >= 0 then well.((r * 10) + c) <- piece.kind + 1)
    (cells piece);
  let left = Array.make 200 0 in
  let full r =
    let rec from c = c = 10 || (well.((r * 10) + c) <> 0 && from (c + 1)) in
    from 0 in
  let rec down r into n =
    if r < 0 then n
    else if full r then down (r - 1) into (n + 1)
    else (for c = 0 to 9 do left.((into * 10) + c) <- well.((r * 10) + c) done;
          down (r - 1) (into - 1) n)
  in
  let n = down 19 19 0 in
  let gain =
    if n = 0 then 0 else if n = 1 then 100 else if n = 2 then 300
    else if n = 3 then 500 else 800 in
  enter left b.next b.seed (b.score + 4 + (gain * (1 + (b.rows / 10))))
    (b.rows + n) quiet

(* the piece somewhere else, if it may be there: else the same model *)
let moved m p = if fits m.board.well p then { m with piece = p; over = false } else m

(* a row down, or landed *)
let fall m =
  let lower = { m.piece with y = m.piece.y + 1 } in
  if fits m.board.well lower then
    { m with piece = lower; wait = delay m.board.rows; over = false }
  else land_ m

let rec drop m =
  if fits m.board.well { m.piece with y = m.piece.y + 1 } then drop (fall m)
  else land_ m

let frame m =
  if m.over then m
  else if m.wait > 1 then { m with wait = m.wait - 1; over = false }
  else fall m

(* the arrows (128 up: a quarter turn, where it is, or a cell to the
 * left, or to the right; 129 down; 130 left; 131 right), the space; m
 * the music off or on *)
let key k m =
  let p = m.piece in
  if k = 109 then { m with quiet = not m.quiet }
  else if m.over then (if k = 32 then start m.board.seed m.quiet else m)
  else if k = 130 then moved m { p with x = p.x - 1 }
  else if k = 131 then moved m { p with x = p.x + 1 }
  else if k = 129 then fall m
  else if k = 32 then drop m
  else if k = 128 then begin
    let turned dx = { p with turn = (p.turn + 1) mod 4; x = p.x + dx } in
    let a = moved m (turned 0) in
    if a != m then a
    else (let b = moved m (turned (-1)) in
          if b != m then b else moved m (turned 1))
  end
  else m

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The sounds *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* m-ix's Tetris's (games/puzzle/Tetris.ml, its sfxr numbers), as few
 * numbers: a piece landed, a thud; rows gone, a coin's two notes (G and
 * the C above); four at once, C E G C; a level, a slide up; the game
 * over, a slide down *)
let note hz ms = { wave = Square; hz; to_hz = hz; ms; volume = 40 }
let landed = [ { wave = Square; hz = 120; to_hz = 60; ms = 80; volume = 50 } ]
let cleared = [ note 784 60; note 1047 200 ]
let four = [ note 523 50; note 659 50; note 784 50; note 1047 400 ]
let level_up = [ { wave = Square; hz = 300; to_hz = 1200; ms = 300; volume = 40 } ]
let game_over = [ { wave = Triangle; hz = 440; to_hz = 80; ms = 700; volume = 90 } ]

(* what changed: the board, when a piece landed (or a game began) *)
let sound was m =
  if m.board == was.board || was.over then []
  else if m.over then game_over
  else
    let rows = m.board.rows - was.board.rows in
    if rows = 4 then four
    else if rows > 0 && m.board.rows / 10 > was.board.rows / 10 then level_up
    else if rows > 0 then cleared
    else landed

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The music *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Korobeiniki, m-ix's (games/puzzle/Tetris.ml, in ABC: L:1/8,
 * Q:1/4=150, K:Am), its eight bars of eighths: the melody on a square,
 * an octave bass on a triangle (the NES's band). A note is its pitch in
 * Hz (e is E5, 659; B is B4, 494; z a rest) and its eighths. *)
let melody =
  let e = 659 and b = 494 and c = 523 and d = 587
  and a4 = 440 and f = 698 and a = 880 and g = 784 in
  [
  (e, 2); (b, 1); (c, 1); (d, 2); (c, 1); (b, 1);
  (a4, 2); (a4, 1); (c, 1); (e, 2); (d, 1); (c, 1);
  (b, 3); (c, 1); (d, 2); (e, 2);
  (c, 2); (a4, 2); (a4, 4);
  (0, 1); (d, 2); (f, 1); (a, 2); (g, 1); (f, 1);
  (e, 3); (c, 1); (e, 2); (d, 1); (c, 1);
  (b, 2); (b, 1); (c, 1); (d, 2); (e, 2);
  (c, 2); (a4, 2); (a4, 4) ]

(* a bar of the bass: a note and its octave above, four times (E,,E,
 * is E2 then E3) *)
let bar low =
  [ (low, 1); (2 * low, 1); (low, 1); (2 * low, 1);
    (low, 1); (2 * low, 1); (low, 1); (2 * low, 1) ]
let bass = List.concat (List.map bar [ 82; 110; 82; 110; 73; 65; 82; 110 ])

(* 200 ms an eighth, a tenth faster each level (m-ix's faster); none
 * when the game is over or the music is off *)
let theme = [ { timbre = Square; level = 28; notes = melody };
              { timbre = Triangle; level = 48; notes = bass } ]
let music m =
  if m.over || m.quiet then None
  else Some { pace = 2000 / (10 + (m.board.rows / 10)); parts = theme }

let game = { 
    width = 288; height = 336;
    init = (fun seed -> start seed false);
    view; key; frame;
    sound; music 
}
tiny/TinyAppTetris.mli
5902
(* A tiny Tetris, a game for TinyKernel.ml built on
 * TinyLibPlayground.ml keeping the essentials of the game, using only
 * integers. The keys: the arrows left and right, up turns the piece,
 * down a row; the space drops it; m the music off and on; q quits.
 *
 * The rules: the well is 10 by 20 cells. There are seven pieces of four
 * cells, each with its own colour; one piece is falling, and the next
 * one is shown. When a row is full it is removed and everything above
 * it moves down. The game ends when a new piece cannot enter the well.
 * Every ten rows the level goes up and the pieces fall faster.
 *
 * The game is a value of TinyLibPlayground's [game] type: a model and
 * three functions. There is no loop, no clock and no drawing in this
 * file.
 *
 * Its twin is m-ix's games/puzzle/Tetris.ml, on lib_playground: the
 * author's playground's port of elm-flatris, in Elm's way, where the
 * well is the list of its full cells, a piece four cells turned by
 * computing their places again, and the falling piece's height a
 * float, for the speed of its fall. What is ours is below: the
 * rotations a table of bits, the well an array, integers only (a
 * level's speed is a number of frames); a turn that does not fit is
 * tried one cell to each side, where the twin tries two. Plan 9 has
 * its own, games/4s (not in principia; from memory).
 *
 * The parts that are not obvious:
 *
 * - {b Each rotation of a piece is 16 bits}: a 4 by 4 square, one
 *   hexadecimal digit per row, all stored in a string ([turns]). There
 *   is no table of tables, and turning a piece just means moving to
 *   the next four digits. Here are the T's sixteen digits, 4E00 4640
 *   0E40 4C40; each column of the picture is one rotation, and the
 *   high bit of a digit is the leftmost cell:
 *
 *       4  . # . .     4  . # . .     0  . . . .     4  . # . .
 *       E  # # # .     6  . # # .     E  # # # .     C  # # . .
 *       0  . . . .     4  . # . .     4  . # . .     4  . # . .
 *       0  . . . .     0  . . . .     0  . . . .     0  . . . .
 *
 *   Checking whether a piece fits is then sixteen bit tests against
 *   the well, whatever the piece: nowhere do the rules need a case per
 *   kind of piece.
 * - {b The well is an array that is never modified once it is in a
 *   model}: when a piece lands, a new array is made. So a model is a
 *   value like any other, that can be kept or compared, even though
 *   arrays in ML are mutable.
 * - {b The background belongs to the model}: the cells of the well,
 *   the score and the next piece are turned into shapes when a piece
 *   lands, and those shapes are kept in the model. The playground only
 *   redraws its first shape when it changes, so a moving piece costs
 *   five shapes, not a hundred.
 *
 * What is dropped: the shadow showing where the piece would land,
 * holding a piece aside, wall kicks further than one cell to either
 * side, dealing the seven pieces as a bag, a pause, and high scores.
 * Its sounds are m-ix's (a piece landed, rows gone, four at once, a
 * level, the game over; [sound] says which from two models), and so is
 * its music, Korobeiniki, the melody on a square and an octave bass on
 * a triangle, a tenth faster each level ([music]: the tune a model
 * wants, as [view] is the picture it wants; none when the game is
 * over).
 *
 * Exercises:
 * - the shadow; a pause; the bag of seven;
 * - showing a completed row before it is removed (a frame or two of
 *   white);
 * - two wells side by side, with keys for a second player.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Alexey Pajitnov wrote Tetris in 1984 at the Computing Centre of the
 * Soviet Academy of Sciences in Moscow, on an Electronika 60, a Soviet
 * machine of the PDP-11 family whose terminal could only show text:
 * the first cells were pairs of brackets. The pieces are the seven
 * shapes that four squares can make, counting mirror images as
 * distinct (Solomon Golomb's tetrominoes, which, combined with tennis,
 * gave the game its name). It spread from machine to machine through
 * copies before any contract existed, and Nintendo's Game Boy (1989)
 * made it the game everyone had played. A character screen, a 10 by 20
 * well, four moves: it was a small program on a small machine from day
 * one, which is why it is this machine's first game.
 *
 * modern:
 * Most of what is dropped above was added after 1984 and is now fixed
 * by the game's owners in a guideline: the seven pieces dealt as a
 * shuffled bag so that no piece is awaited too long, a table of kicks
 * tried when a rotation does not fit, holding a piece, and the shadow.
 * The original dealt pieces at random and rotated them in place; here
 * the deal is random too, and a rotation that does not fit tries
 * shifting one cell to either side.
 *
 * References:
 *  - A. Pajitnov's Tetris (1984)
 *  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetris
 *)

(* a piece (which of the seven, turned how, where), the board (the
 * well's rows, the cells fallen as shapes, what comes next, the
 * score), and the game's model *)
type piece = { kind : int; turn : int; x : int; y : int }
type board = { 
  well : int array;
  ground : TinyLibPlayground.shape;
  next : int;
  seed : int;
  score : int;
  rows : int 
}
type model = { board : board; piece : piece; wait : int; over : bool; quiet : bool }

(* The game, for TinyLibPlayground's run *)
val game : model TinyLibPlayground.game

(* the sounds of a change, from a model to the next *)
val sound : model -> model -> TinyLibPlayground.sound list

(* Korobeiniki's two parts, the melody and the bass *)
val theme : TinyLibPlayground.part list

(* the tune a model wants playing: the theme at its level's pace, None
 * when the game is over or the music is off *)
val music : model -> TinyLibPlayground.tune option

(* a piece's four cells in the well: a column and a row each *)
val cells : piece -> (int * int) list
tiny/TinyAssembler.ml
14589
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyAssembler.mli *)

open TinyMachineISA

let usage = "usage: tiny-assembler [-o file.o] file.tm"

(* -h: how, by examples, each one as it runs *)
let help = usage ^ {|

tiny-machine's assembly (TinyMachineISA's instructions, li, la, call, ret...,
the machine's csrr, csrw, eret, csrrw, amoswap, wfi, and .word .byte .ascii
.asciz .space .align .text .data) to an object, file.o by default, for
tiny-linker. In tiny/tests/TinyCPU_tests/, for example:
  tiny-assembler hello.tm                  hello.o: its words, its labels, the
                                           places a label's address goes
  tiny-linker -o hello hello.o && tiny-cpu hello        Hello, world
An error names the file and the line: hello.tm:3: not a register: r16
|}

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The numbers *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A number is a 32-bit word, kept as its two halves of 16 bits: tiny-ml's
 * ints have 31, and a word of tiny-ml's code (a tagged max_int,
 * 2147483647) or of its strings' bytes needs the 32nd. (old: an int,
 * and m32 n.) Read as int_of_string does, in decimal or after 0x, its
 * bits past 32 dropped. *)
let halves s =
  let neg = String.length s > 0 && s.[0] = '-' in
  let s = if neg then String.sub s 1 (String.length s - 1) else s in
  let base, start =
    if String.length s > 2 && s.[0] = '0' && (s.[1] = 'x' || s.[1] = 'X')
    then 16, 2 else 10, 0 in
  let digit c =
    let k = Char.code c in
    if c >= '0' && c <= '9' then k - 48
    else if c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' then k - 87
    else if c >= 'A' && c <= 'F' then k - 55
    else 99 in
  let rec go i h l =
    if i = String.length s then Some (h, l)
    else
      let d = digit s.[i] in
      if d >= base then None
      else
        let l = (l * base) + d in
        go (i + 1) (((h * base) + (l lsr 16)) land 0xffff) (l land 0xffff) in
  if String.length s <= start then None
  else match go start 0 0 with
    | Some (h, l) when neg ->
        let l = ((l lxor 0xffff) + 1) in
        Some (((h lxor 0xffff) + (l lsr 16)) land 0xffff, l land 0xffff)
    | r -> r

(* a word as an int, when it fits in 31 bits (so on both sides) *)
let int_of (h, l) =
  if h < 0x4000 || h >= 0xc000 then (sext16 h * 0x10000) + l
  else error "number out of range"

(* -1 is two words of ffff; a small number one *)
let small (h, l) = (h = 0 && l < 0x8000) || (h = 0xffff && l >= 0x8000)

type expr = Num of (int * int) | Sym of string

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The items *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* where a label's address goes in a word, the linker's to fill: the
 * whole word (.word), the immediate (addi's, a load's offset...), its
 * high or low half (la: lui then ori), or a branch's offset in words *)
type kind = Word | Abs | Hi | Lo | Pc
let kinds = [ Word, "word"; Abs, "abs"; Hi, "hi"; Lo, "lo"; Pc, "pc" ]

(* an item: an instruction's words, made from what the operands resolve
 * to, given the word's index in the item and the place's kind; .word's
 * words; or bytes, zeros, a label, an alignment, which the linker does
 * (an address's, not the file's) *)
type item =
  | Label of string
  | Words of int * ((int -> kind -> expr -> int) -> int list)
  | Data of expr list | Bytes_ of string | Space of int | Align of int | Piece
  | Section of string

let reg s =
  match String.trim s with
  | "zero" -> 0 | "sp" -> sp | "lr" -> lr
  | s when String.length s >= 2 && s.[0] = 'r' ->
      (match int_of_string_opt (String.sub s 1 (String.length s - 1)) with
       | Some n when n >= 0 && n < 16 -> n
       | _ -> error ("not a register: " ^ s))
  | s -> error ("not a register: " ^ s)

let expr s =
  let s = String.trim s in
  if String.length s = 3 && s.[0] = '\'' && s.[2] = '\'' then
    Num (0, Char.code s.[1])
  else match halves s with Some n -> Num n | None -> Sym s

(* "off(ra)" or "(ra)" *)
let mem_operand s =
  let s = String.trim s in
  match String.index_opt s '(' with
  | Some i when s.[String.length s - 1] = ')' ->
      let off = String.trim (String.sub s 0 i) in
      reg (String.sub s (i + 1) (String.length s - i - 2)),
      (if off = "" then Num (0, 0) else expr off)
  | _ -> error ("not a memory operand: " ^ s)

let one f = Words (4, fun res -> [ encode (f (res 0)) ])

(* the machine's own instructions (TinyMachineDevices runs them): a
 * register of control by its name *)
let machine name args =
  let csr s =
    match List.assoc_opt (String.trim s)
            (List.mapi (fun k n -> n, k) (Array.to_list csr_names)) with
    | Some k -> k | None -> error ("not a register of control: " ^ s) in
  let w op d a k =
    Words (4, fun _ -> [ (op lsl 24) lor (d lsl 20) lor (a lsl 16) lor k ]) in
  match name, args with
  | "csrr", [ d; c ] -> w 0x3a (reg d) 0 (csr c)
  | "csrw", [ c; a ] -> w 0x3b 0 (reg a) (csr c)
  | "eret", [] -> w 0x3c 0 0 0
  | "wfi", [] -> w 0x37 0 0 0
  | "csrrw", [ d; c; a ] -> w 0x3e (reg d) (reg a) (csr c)
  | "amoswap", [ d; a; b ] ->
      let b = String.trim b in
      if String.length b < 2 || b.[0] <> '(' || b.[String.length b - 1] <> ')'
      then error "amoswap's address: (rN)";
      w 0x3d (reg d) (reg a) (reg (String.sub b 1 (String.length b - 2)))
  | _ -> error ("bad instruction: " ^ name ^ " " ^ String.concat ", " args)

(* the instructions named by a table: the ALU's, their immediate forms,
 * the branches (old: each name looked for in the three arrays at each
 * line, and imm_name's string made for each operation) *)
type named = Op of alu | Imm of alu | Test of cmp
let named = Hashtbl.create 64
let () =
  Array.iter (fun op ->
    Hashtbl.replace named alu_names.(index alus op) (Op op);
    if has_imm op then Hashtbl.replace named (imm_name op) (Imm op)) alus;
  Array.iter (fun c ->
    Hashtbl.replace named cmp_names.(index cmps c) (Test c)) cmps

let rec instruction name args : item =
  let args =
    List.map String.trim
      (if String.trim args = "" then [] else String.split_on_char ',' args) in
  match Hashtbl.find_opt named name, args with
  | Some (Op op), [ d; a; b ] -> one (fun _ -> Alu (op, reg d, reg a, reg b))
  | Some (Imm op), [ d; a; v ] ->
      one (fun res -> Alui (op, reg d, reg a, res Abs (expr v)))
  | Some (Test c), [ d; a; t ] ->
      one (fun res -> Branch (c, reg d, reg a, res Pc (expr t)))
  | _ -> others name args

(* the others, by their names *)
and others name args =
  match name, args with
  | "lui", [ d; v ] -> one (fun res -> Lui (reg d, res Abs (expr v) land 0xffff))
  | ("ldw" | "ldb" | "stw" | "stb"), [ d; m ] ->
      one (fun res ->
        let a, off = mem_operand m in
        let s = if name.[2] = 'w' then W else B in
        if name.[0] = 'l' then Load (s, reg d, a, res Abs off)
        else Store (s, reg d, a, res Abs off))
  | "jal", [ d; t ] -> one (fun res -> Jal (reg d, res Pc (expr t)))
  | "jalr", [ d; m ] ->
      one (fun res ->
        let a, off = mem_operand m in Jalr (reg d, a, res Abs off))
  | "sys", [ n ] -> one (fun res -> Sys (res Abs (expr n)))
  (* the pseudo-instructions *)
  | "li", [ d; v ] when (match expr v with Num n -> small n | Sym _ -> false) ->
      one (fun res -> Alui (Add, reg d, 0, res Abs (expr v)))
  | ("li" | "la"), [ d; v ] ->
      Words (8, fun res ->
        [ encode (Lui (reg d, res 0 Hi (expr v)));
          encode (Alui (Or, reg d, reg d, res 1 Lo (expr v))) ])
  | "mov", [ d; a ] -> one (fun _ -> Alui (Add, reg d, reg a, 0))
  | "call", [ t ] -> one (fun res -> Jal (lr, res Pc (expr t)))
  | "j", [ t ] -> one (fun res -> Jal (0, res Pc (expr t)))
  | "ret", [] -> one (fun _ -> Jalr (0, lr, 0))
  | "nop", [] -> one (fun _ -> Alui (Add, 0, 0, 0))
  | _ -> machine name args

(* a string's escapes: backslash and n, t or 0, or the character *)
let unescape s =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  let rec go i =
    if i < String.length s then
      if s.[i] = '\\' && i + 1 < String.length s then
        (Buffer.add_char b
           (match s.[i + 1] with
            | 'n' -> '\n' | 't' -> '\t' | '0' -> '\000' | c -> c);
         go (i + 2))
      else (Buffer.add_char b s.[i]; go (i + 1)) in
  go 0; Buffer.contents b

let directive d args : item =
  match d with
  | ".word" -> Data (List.map expr (String.split_on_char ',' args))
  | ".byte" ->
      Bytes_ (String.concat "" (List.map (fun e ->
        match expr e with
        | Num (_, l) -> String.make 1 (Char.chr (l land 0xff))
        | Sym _ -> error ".byte takes numbers")
        (String.split_on_char ',' args)))
  | ".ascii" | ".asciz" ->
      let a = String.trim args in
      if String.length a < 2 || a.[0] <> '"' || a.[String.length a - 1] <> '"'
      then error ("not a string: " ^ a);
      Bytes_ (unescape (String.sub a 1 (String.length a - 2))
              ^ if d = ".asciz" then "\000" else "")
  | ".space" -> Space (int_of_string (String.trim args))
  | ".align" -> Align (int_of_string (String.trim args))
  | ".piece" -> Piece
  | ".text" -> Section "text"
  | ".data" -> Section "data"
  | _ -> error ("unknown directive " ^ d)

(* a line: labels, then an instruction or a directive; ; starts a comment *)
let parse_line line : item list =
  let line = match String.index_opt line ';' with
    | Some i when not (String.contains (String.sub line 0 i) '"') ->
        String.sub line 0 i
    | _ -> line in
  let rec go s acc =
    let s = String.trim s in
    match String.index_opt s ':' with
    | Some i when not (String.contains (String.sub s 0 i) ' ')
                  && not (String.contains (String.sub s 0 i) '"') ->
        go (String.sub s (i + 1) (String.length s - i - 1))
          (Label (String.sub s 0 i) :: acc)
    | _ when s = "" -> List.rev acc
    | _ ->
        let first c =
          match String.index_opt s c with
          | Some i -> i
          | None -> String.length s in
        let i = min (first ' ') (first '\t') in
        let name = String.sub s 0 i
        and rest = String.sub s i (String.length s - i) in
        List.rev acc
        @ [ (if name.[0] = '.' then directive name rest
             else instruction name rest) ] in
  go line []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The object *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a byte, a word's bytes (the low first: the memory's order), in
 * hexadecimal, added to the object (old: Printf's %02x, then strings
 * joined by ^, a new string at each) *)
let add_hex b n =
  Buffer.add_char b "0123456789abcdef".[n lsr 4];
  Buffer.add_char b "0123456789abcdef".[n land 15]
let add_word b (h, l) =
  add_hex b (l land 0xff); add_hex b (l lsr 8);
  add_hex b (h land 0xff); add_hex b (h lsr 8)

(* a word in decimal, signed (a branch's number as a reloc's target) *)
let decimal (h, l) =
  let rec digits h l acc =
    if h = 0 && l = 0 then acc
    else
      let r = ((h mod 10) * 0x10000) + l in
      digits (h / 10) (r / 10) (string_of_int (r mod 10) ^ acc) in
  if (h, l) = (0, 0) then "0"
  else if h < 0x8000 then digits h l ""
  else
    let l' = (l lxor 0xffff) + 1 in
    "-" ^ digits (((h lxor 0xffff) + (l' lsr 16)) land 0xffff) (l' land 0xffff)
            ""

(* A file's items as lines, in their order, for tiny-linker
 * (TinyLinker.mli has the format): a word whose operand is a number is
 * made here, one whose operand is a label is made with 0 there and a
 * reloc line says what goes in it; a branch to a number too, its
 * offset being from an address the link chooses *)
let assemble name text =
  let b = Buffer.create 4096 in
  let line s = Buffer.add_string b (s ^ "\n") in
  let at n e = name ^ ":" ^ string_of_int (n + 1) ^ ": " ^ e in
  let target e = match e with Num n -> decimal n | Sym s -> s in
  let relocs_of rs =
    (* (by offset: a list's words are made from the last) *)
    List.iter (fun (off, k, e) ->
        line ("reloc " ^ string_of_int off ^ " " ^ List.assoc k kinds ^ " "
              ^ target e))
      (List.sort (fun (a, _, _) (b, _, _) -> compare a b) rs) in
  line "tiny-object";
  (* each file on a word's boundary: one may end with bytes, the next
   * begin with code *)
  line "align 4";
  List.iteri (fun n l ->
    let items = try parse_line l with Error e -> error (at n e) in
    List.iter (fun it ->
      match it with
      | Label l -> line ("label " ^ l)
      | Align k -> line (Printf.sprintf "align %d" k)
      | Piece -> line "piece"
      | Section k -> line k
      | Space k -> line (Printf.sprintf "space %d" k)
      | Bytes_ s ->
          Buffer.add_string b "code ";
          String.iter (fun c -> add_hex b (Char.code c)) s;
          Buffer.add_char b '\n'
      | Data es ->
          Buffer.add_string b "code ";
          List.iter (fun e ->
            add_word b (match e with Num n -> n | Sym _ -> (0, 0))) es;
          Buffer.add_char b '\n';
          relocs_of (List.concat (List.mapi (fun i e ->
            match e with Sym _ -> [ (4 * i, Word, e) ] | Num _ -> []) es))
      | Words (_, f) ->
          let relocs = ref [] in
          let res i k e =
            match k, e with
            | Pc, _ | _, Sym _ -> relocs := (4 * i, k, e) :: !relocs; 0
            | Hi, Num (h, _) -> h
            | Lo, Num (_, l) -> l
            | _, Num n -> int_of n in
          let ws = try f res with Error e -> error (at n e) in
          Buffer.add_string b "code ";
          List.iter (fun w -> add_word b (w lsr 16, w land 0xffff)) ws;
          Buffer.add_char b '\n';
          relocs_of !relocs) items)
    (String.split_on_char '\n' text);
  Buffer.contents b

let main
    (caps : < Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >)
    =
  let assemble_to f out =
    TinyLibSystem.write_file caps out
      (assemble f (TinyLibSystem.read_file caps f));
    0 in
  (* x.tm's object: x.o, here *)
  let default f = Filename.chop_suffix (Filename.basename f) ".tm" ^ ".o" in
  try
    match List.tl (TinyLibSystem.argv caps) with
    | ("-h" | "--help") :: _ -> TinyLibSystem.print caps help; 0
    | [ "-o"; out; f ] when Filename.check_suffix f ".tm" -> assemble_to f out
    | [ f ] when Filename.check_suffix f ".tm" -> assemble_to f (default f)
    | _ -> TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (usage ^ "   (-h: how)\n"); 2
  with Error e ->
    TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "tiny-assembler: %s\n" e); 1

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-assembler" main
tiny/TinyAssembler.mli
6139
(* tiny-assembler: tiny-machine's assembly to an object, a file at a
 * time, for tiny-linker. Its usage, by examples, is in [help] (what
 * tiny-assembler -h prints).
 *
 * The machine was designed for it: one format, every instruction 4
 * bytes, every immediate the word's low 16 bits. So an instruction's
 * size is known from its name alone (li and la with a label: two
 * words, lui and ori), and its words are made here, at once, but for
 * what the file cannot know: where a label is. That is left as 0 in the
 * word, and a line of the object says what goes there (the words
 * 30100000, then 20200000 and 17220000, as bytes in the memory's order,
 * the low first):
 *
 *     beq   r1, zero, done        code 00001030
 *                                 reloc 0 pc done
 *     la    r2, table             code 0000202000002217
 *                                 reloc 0 hi table
 *                                 reloc 4 lo table
 *     .word main                  code 00000000
 *                                 reloc 0 word main
 *
 * The object is text, a line an item, in the file's order (the format
 * is t-ix's own):
 *
 *     tiny-object
 *     align 4                     each file starts on a word
 *     label NAME                  here, an address the link chooses
 *     code HEX                    an instruction's words, or data's
 *                                 bytes, in hexadecimal, in the
 *                                 memory's order
 *     reloc OFF KIND TARGET       in the code just before, OFF bytes in:
 *                                 word (all 32 bits), abs (the
 *                                 immediate), hi or lo (the immediate:
 *                                 the address's high or low half), pc
 *                                 (the immediate: the words from the
 *                                 next instruction to TARGET); TARGET a
 *                                 label, or a number (a branch to an
 *                                 address)
 *     space N                     N zeros (.space)
 *     piece                       (.piece) what follows, up to the next
 *                                 one, is left out by the link when
 *                                 nothing reaches it (tiny-ml's
 *                                 functions and static blocks)
 *
 * An .align stays an item: what it pads depends on the address, which
 * only the link knows (v0's kernel aligns its programs on 64 KB). Every
 * label is the program's: the link is one name space, as the
 * compilers write it (tiny-c's statics carry their file's name, tiny-ml's
 * labels their unit's).
 *
 * What makes it small:
 *
 * - {b Sizes before addresses, for free.} No instruction's size
 *   depends on where a label is (no short and long branch: a branch
 *   reaches 128 KB, la any address), so the assembler never waits for
 *   the link to know how big a word is, and the link never moves
 *   anything it placed: Szymanski's problem does not arise.
 * - {b An operand says its kind as it is read}: [instruction] builds
 *   each word by a function of what its operands resolve to, given
 *   the kind of place; a number resolves at once, a label to 0 and a
 *   reloc line.
 * - {b The machine's own instructions} (csrr, csrw, eret, csrrw,
 *   amoswap, wfi: TinyMachineDevices runs them) are assembled for any
 *   program; on tiny-cpu, or in a program of tiny-kernel's, they are
 *   illegal words, as on a real machine in user mode.
 *
 * Where it fits: tiny-c and tiny-ml write the .tm files, tiny-linker
 * reads the objects, tiny-cpu and tiny-machine run the image.
 * (old: TinyMachineCPU.ml's assembler, which read all of a program's
 * .tm files at once and wrote the image, no object between; and before
 * plan_tiny_self_hosting.md, a TinyAssembler.ml for arm64, 7a and 7l
 * made one, in git's history.)
 *
 * Its twin, mini-asm (assembler/), is Plan 9's 5a and 7a (principia's
 * assemblers/5a), and the two are opposites. mini-asm encodes nothing:
 * it parses Plan 9's syntax (TEXT, GLOBL, DATA, the destination last)
 * and marshals the instructions as it read them, the linker choosing
 * each one's words (TinyLinker's plan9-is-cleaner compares the two
 * roads). Here the words are made at once and the object is text, a
 * Unix assembler's way, which costs little since an address goes in
 * five kinds of place (word, abs, hi, lo, pc), not a table per
 * machine. The syntax is ours too, the RISC manuals' (a label and a
 * colon, the destination first, gas's .word and .align, a ; comment);
 * no #include or #define, no TEXT with its frame's size: a function is
 * a label, its frame the compiler's instructions.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The first assemblers assembled and loaded in one step: the EDSAC's
 * initial orders (David Wheeler, 1949) read orders punched on paper
 * tape as a letter and a decimal address, and stored them in memory as
 * binary. The object came with libraries and with programs too big to
 * translate again after each change: each part translated once, its
 * addresses left open, the parts bound together later.
 *
 * terminology:
 * An assembler translates mnemonics into words but leaves open the
 * addresses it cannot know; a linker puts the objects one after the
 * other and fills them in; a loader puts the result in memory and
 * jumps to it (here tiny-cpu, tiny-machine, or tiny-kernel's exec).
 * Plan 9 calls its linker the loader (5l, 7l: l for load) and gives it
 * most of the assembler's work: its assemblers do not encode.
 *
 * References: M. V. Wilkes, D. J. Wheeler and S. Gill, The Preparation
 * of Programs for an Electronic Digital Computer (1951), the initial
 * orders; T. G. Szymanski, "Assembling Code for Machines with
 * Span-dependent Instructions" (CACM, 1978), the problem a fixed
 * format avoids; J. R. Levine, Linkers and Loaders (2000). *)

(* a file's text (its name for the errors) to its object's text *)
val assemble : string -> string -> string

(* the program: its arguments (-h: how) to its exit status *)
val main : < Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. > -> int
tiny/TinyBrowser/TinyBrowserAddress.ml

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyBrowserAddress.mli *)
open TinyBrowserText

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Addresses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* an address and its #fragment, apart ("" when there is none) *)
let fragment url =
  match String.index_opt url '#' with
  | Some i ->
    String.sub url 0 i, String.sub url (i + 1) (String.length url - i - 1)
  | None -> url, ""

(* DuckDuckGo's page for text browsers: its results are plain HTML, no
 * script (as Lynx is given), each a link through a page that a <meta>
 * refresh sends on *)
let search_engine = "https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q="

(* the words of a search as a query: a space +, other than letters and
 * digits %XX *)
let query s =
  let hex = "0123456789ABCDEF" in
  let piece c =
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
       || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c = '-' || c = '.' || c = '_'
    then String.make 1 c
    else if c = ' ' then "+"
    else
      let n = Char.code c in
      "%" ^ String.make 1 hex.[n / 16] ^ String.make 1 hex.[n mod 16] in
  String.concat "" (List.init (String.length s) (fun i -> piece s.[i]))

(* What was typed, as a full address (the wire's other end's too:
 * TinyMachinePeer.www_address): a title is an English Wikipedia
 * article, a name with a dot is https://, ?words a search. *)
let absolute typed =
  let s = String.trim typed in
  if String.starts_with "http://" s || String.starts_with "https://" s then s
  else if String.length s > 1 && s.[0] = '?' then
    search_engine
    ^ query (String.trim (String.sub s 1 (String.length s - 1)))
  else begin
    let first =
      match String.index_opt s '/' with Some i -> String.sub s 0 i | None -> s in
    if String.contains first '.' && not (String.contains first ' ') then
      "https://" ^ s
    else
      "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/"
      ^ String.map (fun c -> if c = ' ' then '_' else c) s
  end

(* "https://host" of an address *)
let site url =
  match find url "://" 0 with
  | -1 -> ""
  | i ->
    (match String.index_from_opt url (i + 3) '/' with
     | Some j -> String.sub url 0 j
     | None -> url)

(* Where a link goes, from the page at [url] whose <base> is [base]
 * (Wikipedia's is //en.wikipedia.org/wiki/, and its links ./OCaml). *)
let resolve url base href =
  if href = "" then url
  else if String.starts_with "http://" href
          || String.starts_with "https://" href then href
  else if String.starts_with "//" href then "https:" ^ href
  else if href.[0] = '#' then fst (fragment url) ^ href
  else if href.[0] = '/' then site url ^ href
  else begin
    let dir =
      if base <> "" then
        (if String.starts_with "//" base then "https:" ^ base else base)
      else begin
        let u = fst (fragment url) in
        match String.rindex_opt u '/' with
        | Some i when i > String.length (site url) -> String.sub u 0 (i + 1)
        | _ -> site url ^ "/"
      end in
    dir ^ (if String.starts_with "./" href
           then String.sub href 2 (String.length href - 2) else href)
  end

(* Addresses, for TinyBrowser: what was typed as a full address, and

val resolve : string -> string -> string -> string

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyBrowserHtml.mli *)
open TinyBrowserText
open TinyBrowserTokens
open TinyBrowserLines

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The tags *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A picture of the page: where it is, the size it is shown at in
 * pixels, its alternative text, and how far it has come: -1 not asked
 * yet, -3 asked, -2 not to be had, or the rows of it received. *)
type picture = {
  pc_src : string; pc_w : int; pc_h : int; pc_alt : string;
  mutable pc_got : int }

(* An open element. Besides its tag, it records how its text should be
 * shown, combining what it says with what its parents say, so the top
 * of the stack alone tells how to show the next text. *)
type elem = {
  tag : string;
  face : int;                 (* the look of its text: bold, emph, code *)
  href : string;
  hide : bool;
  pre : bool;
  margin : int;               (* the column where its lines start *)
  mutable count : int;        (* the next number, for an <ol> *)
}

type page = {
  reader : reader;
  page_flow : flow;
  mutable stack : elem list;
  mutable tables : table list;  (* the open table, if any (at most one: see
                                 * depth) *)
  mutable space : bool;         (* whether a space was read since the last word *)
  mutable page_title : string;
  mutable page_base : string;
  mutable page_refresh : string;          (* where a <meta> refresh sends us *)
  mutable anchors : (string * int) list;  (* an element's id, and the line it
                                           * starts at *)
  mutable pictures : picture list;        (* the page's pictures, the last first *)
  mutable npictures : int;
  mutable heading : (string * int * string * bool) list;
    (* a large heading's words, the last first *)
}

let root =
  { tag = ""; face = 0; href = ""; hide = false; pre = false; margin = 0;
    count = 0 }

(* (the reader and the flow made first: tiny-ml computes a record's
 * fields in tiny-machine's 11 registers) *)
let create width =
  let reader = { tail = ""; raw = "" } and page_flow = flow width in
  { reader = reader; page_flow = page_flow; stack = [ root ]; tables = [];
    space = false; page_title = ""; page_base = ""; page_refresh = "";
    anchors = [];
    pictures = []; npictures = 0; heading = [] }

let top p = match p.stack with e :: _ -> e | [] -> root

(* The table of tags. Each tag has some of these bits:
 *  - void: the element has no end tag (like <br>);
 *  - block: it ends the current line before and after it;
 *  - spaced: it also wants a blank line before and after it;
 *  - hidden: its text is not shown;
 *  - deeper: it indents its lines.
 * The look of its text (bold, emph, code, big, under) is in the bits
 * above those, multiplied by 32. *)
let void = 1
let block = 2
let spaced = 4
let hidden = 8
let deeper = 16
let kinds = [
  "a", 0; "address", block; "area", void; "article", block; "aside", block;
  "b", bold * 32; "base", void; "blockquote", block + spaced + deeper;
  "body", block; "br", void; "button", hidden;
  "caption", block; "center", block; "code", code * 32; "col", void;
  "dd", block + deeper; "dfn", emph * 32; "div", block; "dl", block + spaced;
  "dt", block + bold * 32;
  "em", emph * 32; "embed", void;
  "figcaption", block; "figure", block + spaced; "footer", block;
  "h1", block + spaced + (bold + big) * 32;
  "h2", block + spaced + (bold + big) * 32; "h3", block + spaced + bold * 32;
  "h4", block + spaced + bold * 32; "h5", block + spaced + bold * 32;
  "h6", block + spaced + bold * 32;
  "head", hidden; "header", block; "hr", void; "html", block;
  "i", emph * 32; "img", void; "input", void + hidden; "ins", under * 32;
  "kbd", code * 32; "li", block; "link", void; "main", block; "math", hidden;
  "meta", void; "nav", block; "noscript", hidden;
  "ol", block + deeper; "p", block + spaced; "param", void;
  "pre", block + spaced + code * 32;
  "samp", code * 32; "script", hidden; "section", block; "select", hidden;
  "source", void; "strong", bold * 32;
  "style", hidden; "svg", hidden;
  "table", block; "td", block; "template", hidden; "textarea", hidden;
  "th", block + bold * 32; "title", hidden;
  "tr", block; "tt", code * 32; "u", under * 32; "ul", block + deeper;
  "var", emph * 32; "wbr", void ]

(* A tag is looked up only among the tags with the same first letter,
 * because in tiny-ml comparing two strings is a call to the runtime. *)
let by_letter =
  let a = Array.make 26 [] in
  List.iter (fun (name, k) ->
    let i = Char.code name.[0] - 97 in a.(i) <- (name, k) :: a.(i)) kinds;
  a
let kind tag =
  let i = if tag = "" then -1 else Char.code tag.[0] - 97 in
  if i < 0 || i >= 26 then 0
  else match List.assoc_opt tag by_letter.(i) with Some k -> k | None -> 0
let is k bit = k land bit <> 0
(* The classes Wikipedia uses for parts that are not worth showing on a
 * small screen (navigation boxes, edit links, ...). *)
let hidden_classes =
  [ "navbox"; "noprint"; "metadata"; "mw-editsection"; "mw-empty-elt";
    "sistersitebox"; "mw-jump-link" ]

let attr attrs a = match List.assoc_opt a attrs with Some v -> v | None -> ""

let hides k attrs =
  is k hidden
  || (let cl = attr attrs "class" in
      cl <> "" && List.exists (has_class cl) hidden_classes)
  || (let st = attr attrs "style" in
      find st "display:none" 0 >= 0 || find st "display: none" 0 >= 0)

(* the line's end a table's cell waits for, put in before what comes *)
let unbreak (t : table) c =
  if t.broken > 0 then begin c.items <- Break :: c.items; t.broken <- 0 end

(* Sends a word to the current cell if a table is open (large text is
 * not, there), to the large heading being made, or to the page's flow. *)
let emit p text =
  let e = top p in
  if not e.hide then begin
    (match p.tables with
     | t :: _ ->
       (match t.cell with
        | Some c ->
          unbreak t c;
          c.items <-
            Word (text, e.face land lnot big, e.href, p.space) :: c.items
        | None -> ())
     | [] ->
       if e.face land big <> 0 then
         p.heading <- (text, e.face, e.href, p.space) :: p.heading
       else word p.page_flow text e.face e.href p.space);
    p.space <- false
  end

(* Ends the current line. *)
let break p =
  (match p.tables with
   | t :: _ ->
     (match t.cell with
      | Some c ->
        (match c.items with
         | Break :: _ | [] -> ()
         | _ -> t.broken <- max t.broken 1)
      | None -> ())
   | [] -> end_line p.page_flow);
  p.space <- false

let paragraph p = break p; if p.tables = [] then p.page_flow.blank <- true

let text p s =
  let e = top p in
  if e.tag = "title" then p.page_title <- p.page_title ^ s
  else if e.hide then ()
  else if e.pre && p.tables = [] then begin
    let f = p.page_flow in
    let pieces = String.split_on_char '\n' s in
    List.iteri (fun i piece ->
      if i > 0 then
        (if f.made = [] then push f { runs = []; rule = false }
         else end_line f);
      verbatim f piece e.face e.href) pieces
  end
  else begin
    let n = String.length s in
    let i = ref 0 in
    while !i < n do
      if is_space s.[!i] then begin p.space <- true; incr i end
      else begin
        let j = ref !i in
        while !j < n && not (is_space s.[!j]) do incr j done;
        emit p (String.sub s !i (!j - !i));
        i := !j
      end
    done
  end

let rule p =
  if p.tables = [] then begin
    end_line p.page_flow; push p.page_flow { runs = []; rule = true }
  end

(* A large heading (<h1>, <h2>): its words laid out at half the width,
 * each of its lines two of the page's, its top half and its bottom half
 * (the same runs, their pic -2), so that the page is still rows of 16
 * pixels, each drawn on its own. *)
let lay_heading p =
  let f = p.page_flow in
  let g = flow (max 1 ((f.width - f.left) / 2)) in
  List.iter (fun (text, look, link, sp) -> word g text look link sp)
    (List.rev p.heading);
  end_line g;
  p.heading <- [];
  end_line f;
  List.iter (fun (l : line) ->
    let runs = List.map (fun (r : run) ->
      { col = f.left + (2 * r.col); text = r.text; look = r.look;
        link = r.link; pic = -1 }) l.runs in
    push f { runs = runs; rule = false };
    push f { runs = List.map (fun (r : run) ->
               { col = r.col; text = r.text; look = r.look; link = r.link;
                 pic = -2 }) runs;
             rule = false })
    (List.rev g.out)

(* The pixels the pictures of a page may have in all: they are images of
 * the kernel's, which has 2 MB for them, the windows' included. *)
let picture_room = 1048576

(* A picture: a box of the size the page says (its width and height
 * attributes), smaller if it is wider than the room it has, kept in the
 * page's pictures and drawn when its pixels come. The text never moves
 * when they do: its place is known before the picture is. Small icons
 * (under 24 pixels) are left out. Wikipedia shows math as a picture
 * whose alternative text is the TeX source, which we show instead. *)
let picture p attrs =
  let alt = attr attrs "alt" and cl = attr attrs "class"
  and src = attr attrs "src" in
  let w = number (attr attrs "width") and h = number (attr attrs "height") in
  if has_class cl "mwe-math-fallback-image-inline"
     || has_class cl "mwe-math-fallback-image-display" then begin
    let pre = "{\\displaystyle " in
    let n = String.length alt and m = String.length pre in
    (* (as text, so that a long formula wraps at its spaces) *)
    text p (if n > m + 1 && String.sub alt 0 m = pre
            then String.sub alt m (n - m - 1) else alt)
  end
  else if (w >= 24 || h >= 24) && w > 0 && h > 0 && src <> "" then begin
    let f = p.page_flow in
    let room =
      8 * (if p.tables = [] then f.width - f.left else f.width / 2) in
    let w, h = if w > room then room, max 1 (h * room / w) else w, h in
    let used =
      List.fold_left (fun n (pc : picture) -> n + (pc.pc_w * pc.pc_h)) 0
        p.pictures in
    if used + (w * h) > picture_room then
      emit p ("[" ^ (if alt = "" then "picture" else alt) ^ "]")
    else begin
      let id = p.npictures in
      p.pictures <-
        { pc_src = src; pc_w = w; pc_h = h; pc_alt = alt; pc_got = -1 }
        :: p.pictures;
      p.npictures <- id + 1;
      let cols = (w + 7) / 8 and rows = (h + 15) / 16 and link = (top p).href in
      match p.tables with
      | t :: _ ->
        (match t.cell with
         | Some c ->
           unbreak t c;
           c.items <- Pic (id, cols, rows, link) :: Break :: c.items
         | None -> ())
      | [] -> picture_block f id rows link
    end
  end

(* Some elements close implicitly when another one opens: a paragraph
 * when any block starts, a list item when the next one starts, a cell
 * when the next one starts. *)
let implied p tag k =
  let close_to names stop =
    let rec find = function
      | [] -> false
      | (e : elem) :: rest ->
        if List.mem e.tag names then true
        else if List.mem e.tag stop then false
        else find rest in
    if find p.stack then begin
      let rec pop = function
        | (e : elem) :: rest when not (List.mem e.tag names) -> pop rest
        | _ :: rest -> rest
        | [] -> [] in
      p.stack <- pop p.stack
    end in
  if is k block then begin
    (match tag with
     | "li" -> close_to [ "li" ] [ "ul"; "ol" ]
     | "dt" | "dd" -> close_to [ "dt"; "dd" ] [ "dl" ]
     | "tr" -> close_to [ "tr" ] [ "table" ]
     | "td" | "th" -> close_to [ "td"; "th" ] [ "tr"; "table" ]
     | _ -> ());
    if (top p).tag = "p" then
      p.stack <- (match p.stack with _ :: rest -> rest | [] -> [])
  end

(* Where <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=x"> sends us: x,
 * when the wait is 0 (a page that reloads itself every few minutes is
 * not followed). A search's results link through such a page. *)
let meta_refresh attrs =
  (* (not refresh, the page's below: tiny-ml exports both names) *)
  let c = attr attrs "content" in
  match String.index_opt c ';' with
  | Some i
    when String.lowercase_ascii (attr attrs "http-equiv") = "refresh"
         && number (String.trim (String.sub c 0 i)) = 0 ->
      let u = String.trim (String.sub c (i + 1) (String.length c - i - 1)) in
      let u =
        if String.length u > 4
           && String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub u 0 4) = "url="
        then String.sub u 4 (String.length u - 4) else u in
      let n = String.length u in
      if n >= 2 && (u.[0] = '\'' || u.[0] = '"') then String.sub u 1 (n - 2)
      else u
  | _ -> ""

(* A cell of a table inside a cell: the outer table lays out its cells,
 * the inner one's are a space and its rows lines. An empty block in
 * such a cell (Hacker News' vote arrow) is no line's end. *)
let inner_cell p tag =
  (tag = "td" || tag = "th")
  && (match p.tables with t :: _ -> t.depth > 0 | [] -> false)
let cell_space p =
  (match p.tables with t :: _ when t.broken = 1 -> t.broken <- 0 | _ -> ());
  p.space <- true

let open_tag p tag k attrs =
  implied p tag k;
  let e = top p in
  let hide = e.hide || hides k attrs in
  (* (in the <head>, or a <noscript>, which are hidden) *)
  if tag = "meta" && p.page_refresh = "" then p.page_refresh <- meta_refresh attrs;
  (* An element with an id is a place a link can go to (#History,
   * #cite_note-2): the line it starts at is kept. Parsoid gives nearly
   * every element an id of its own, which starts with mw, and no link
   * names those. *)
  let id = attr attrs "id" in
  if id <> "" && not hide
     && not (String.length id > 1 && id.[0] = 'm' && id.[1] = 'w') then
    p.anchors <-
      (id, p.page_flow.nlines
           + (if p.page_flow.made <> [] || p.page_flow.blank then 1 else 0))
      :: p.anchors;
  (* Inside a table, a <tr> starts a new row and a <td> or <th> a new
   * cell, whose words are kept until the end of the table. *)
  if is k block then
    (match p.tables, tag with
     | [], "table" when not hide ->
         end_line p.page_flow;
         p.tables <-
           [ { rows = []; row = []; cell = None; depth = 0; broken = 0 } ]
     | t :: _, "table" when not hide -> t.depth <- t.depth + 1; break p
     | t :: _, "tr" when t.depth = 0 && not hide ->
         if t.row <> [] then t.rows <- t.row :: t.rows;
         t.row <- []; t.cell <- None; t.broken <- 0
     | t :: _, ("td" | "th" | "caption") when t.depth = 0 && not hide ->
         let span =
           if tag = "caption" then 1000
           else max 1 (number (attr attrs "colspan")) in
         let c =
           { items = []; span = span; head = tag = "th" || tag = "caption" } in
         if tag = "caption" then begin
           t.rows <- [ c ] :: t.rows; t.cell <- Some c
         end
         else begin t.row <- c :: t.row; t.cell <- Some c end;
         t.broken <- 0; p.space <- false
     | t :: _, ("tr" | "td" | "th") when not hide ->
         if tag = "tr" then begin
           break p; if t.broken = 1 then t.broken <- 2
         end
         else cell_space p
     | _ -> ());
  if not hide then begin
    if is k spaced then paragraph p
    else if is k block && not (inner_cell p tag) then break p;
    if is k void then
      match tag with
      | "br" ->
        if p.tables = [] && p.page_flow.made = [] then
          push p.page_flow { runs = []; rule = false }
        else break p
      | "hr" -> rule p
      | "img" -> picture p attrs
      | "base" -> if p.page_base = "" then p.page_base <- attr attrs "href"
      | _ -> ()
  end;
  if not (is k void) then begin
    let face = e.face lor (k / 32) in
    let href =
      if tag = "a" && attr attrs "href" <> "" then attr attrs "href"
      else e.href in
    let margin =
      if p.tables = [] && is k deeper then
        min (e.margin + 3) (p.page_flow.width / 2)
      else e.margin in
    let pre = e.pre || (is k spaced && is k (code * 32)) in
    let el =
      { tag = tag; face = face; href = href; hide = hide; pre = pre;
        margin = margin; count = max 1 (number (attr attrs "start")) } in
    p.stack <- el :: p.stack;
    if not hide then begin
      p.page_flow.left <- margin;
      if is k block && tag = "li" then begin
        (* The bullet, or the number of an <ol>, goes in the margin. *)
        let mark = match p.stack with
          | _ :: (l : elem) :: _ when l.tag = "ol" ->
            let n = l.count in l.count <- n + 1; string_of_int n ^ "."
          | _ -> "*" in
        match p.tables with
        | [] ->
            let f = p.page_flow in
            f.at <- max 0 (margin - String.length mark - 1);
            f.made <-
              [ { col = f.at; text = mark; look = 0; link = ""; pic = -1 } ];
            (* If the number is wider than the margin, the item's text
             * starts after it. *)
            f.at <- max margin (f.at + String.length mark + 1)
        | _ -> emit p mark; p.space <- true
      end
    end
  end

let close_tag p tag k =
  let rec opened = function
    | [] -> None
    | (e : elem) :: rest -> if e.tag = tag then Some e else opened rest in
  match (if is k void then None else opened p.stack) with
  | None -> ()
  | Some was ->
      let rec pop = function
        | (e : elem) :: rest when e.tag <> tag -> pop rest
        | _ :: rest -> rest
        | [] -> [] in
      p.stack <- pop p.stack;
      let e = top p in
      if not was.hide then begin
        p.page_flow.left <- e.margin;
        if is k block then
          (match p.tables, tag with
           | t :: rest, "table" ->
               if t.depth > 0 then begin t.depth <- t.depth - 1; break p end
               else begin
                 if t.row <> [] then t.rows <- t.row :: t.rows;
                 p.tables <- rest;
                 lay_table p.page_flow t
               end
           | t :: _, ("td" | "th" | "caption") when t.depth = 0 ->
               t.cell <- None
           | _ -> ());
        (* (a heading is laid out at its end, not at a <span>'s in it) *)
        if p.heading <> [] && e.face land big = 0 then lay_heading p;
        if is k spaced && tag = "h2" && p.tables = [] then rule p;
        if is k spaced then paragraph p
        else if inner_cell p tag then cell_space p
        else if is k block then break p
      end

let token p = function
  | Text s -> text p s
  | Open (tag, attrs) -> open_tag p tag (kind tag) attrs
  | Close tag -> close_tag p tag (kind tag)

let feed p chunk = List.iter (token p) (tokens p.reader chunk false)

let finish p =
  List.iter (token p) (tokens p.reader "" true);
  (match p.tables with
   | t :: _ ->
     (if t.row <> [] then t.rows <- t.row :: t.rows);
     p.tables <- [];
     lay_table p.page_flow t
   | [] -> ());
  if p.heading <> [] then lay_heading p;
  end_line p.page_flow

let title p = p.page_title
let base p = p.page_base
let refresh p = p.page_refresh
let anchor p id = List.assoc_opt id p.anchors
let pictures p = p.npictures
let picture_of p id = List.nth p.pictures (p.npictures - 1 - id)
let count p = p.page_flow.nlines

(* The lines from the a-th to before the b-th, from the top. The lines
 * are kept last first, as they are made; an array of them from the top
 * is made again when lines have come since it was made, so that the
 * lines a scroll asks for are found at once (walking the list from its
 * end each time was a tenth of a page down). *)
let lines_between p a b =
  let f = p.page_flow in
  let n = f.nlines in
  let b = min b n and a = max a 0 in
  if a >= b then []
  else begin
    if f.cached <> n then begin
      let arr = Array.make n { runs = []; rule = false } in
      List.iteri (fun k l -> arr.(n - 1 - k) <- l) f.out;
      f.cache <- arr;
      f.cached <- n
    end;
    let rec take k acc =
      if k < a then acc else take (k - 1) (f.cache.(k) :: acc) in
    take (b - 1) []
  end

(* HTML, as TinyBrowser reads it: a page being read, the reading as a
 * whole (named after the language, as a browser's HTML parser is: what
 * each tag means is here). The tokens of TinyBrowserTokens given, one
 * after the other, to a stack of open elements, and each word of a text
 * sent to TinyBrowserLines' flow (or to a table's cell, or to a large
 * heading). What the browser
 * keeps of a page is its lines, its title, its anchors and its
 * pictures; there is no tree.
 *
 * The meaning of each tag is a row in a table (kinds) that says
 * whether it starts a block, wants a blank line around it, hides its
 * text, indents its lines, and what look it gives its text. An open
 * element combines what it says with what its parents say, so the top
 * of the stack alone tells how to show the next text:
 *
 *     <ul><li>An <b><a href="x">old</a> page</b>
 *
 *     stack (top first)        the word "old" gets
 *       a   href x               look bold, link x,
 *       b   bold                 at column 3 (the ul's margin),
 *       li                       after the bullet in the margin
 *       ul  margin 3
 *
 * Some elements close implicitly when another one opens (a paragraph
 * when a block starts, a list item at the next one, a cell at the
 * next one), the way pages written by hand expect.
 *
 * A page cut anywhere reads the same: the tests feed one a byte at a
 * time and compare its lines.
 *)

(* A page being read and turned into lines of [width] columns. *)
type page
val create : int -> page

(* [feed page bytes] gives the next message of the page; [finish page]
 * says that the page has ended. *)
val feed : page -> string -> unit
val finish : page -> unit

(* The page's <title>; the address in its <base>; where its <meta>
 * refresh sends us at once ("" when it does not). *)
val title : page -> string
val base : page -> string
val refresh : page -> string

(* how many lines there are so far; the lines from the a-th to before
 * the b-th, from the top (what the screen shows) *)
val count : page -> int
val lines_between : page -> int -> int -> TinyBrowserLines.line list

(* the line where the element with that id starts, if it came *)
val anchor : page -> string -> int option

(* The page's pictures: how many, and one by its number. A picture's
 * pc_got is -1 before it is asked for, -3 once asked, -2 when there is
 * none to be had, and the rows received so far after that. *)
type picture = {
  pc_src : string; pc_w : int; pc_h : int; pc_alt : string;
  mutable pc_got : int
}
val pictures : page -> int
val picture_of : page -> int -> picture

(* See TinyBrowserHttp.mli *)
open TinyBrowserText

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Requests *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let request url = "GET " ^ url ^ " HTTP/1.0\r\nUser-Agent: www\r\n\r\n"

(* the first line's middle: what is between its first and its last
 * space (an address typed with a space in it is still one) *)
let asked s =
  let line =
    match String.index_opt s '\n' with
    | Some i -> String.trim (String.sub s 0 i)
    | None -> String.trim s in
  match String.index_opt line ' ', String.rindex_opt line ' ' with
  | Some i, Some j when j > i && String.sub line 0 i = "GET" ->
    Some (String.trim (String.sub line i (j - i)))
  | _ -> None

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Responses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let reason status =
  match status with
  | 200 -> "OK" | 301 -> "Moved Permanently" | 302 -> "Found"
  | 304 -> "Not Modified" | 400 -> "Bad Request" | 403 -> "Forbidden"
  | 404 -> "Not Found" | 500 -> "Internal Server Error"
  | 502 -> "Bad Gateway" | _ -> ""

let response status headers body =
  "HTTP/1.0 " ^ string_of_int status ^ " " ^ reason status ^ "\r\n"
  ^ String.concat ""
      (List.map (fun (n, v) -> n ^ ": " ^ v ^ "\r\n") headers)
  ^ "Content-Length: " ^ string_of_int (String.length body) ^ "\r\n\r\n"
  ^ body

(* an empty line ends the head, its line ends \r\n or \n alone *)
let head_end s =
  let a = find s "\r\n\r\n" 0 and b = find s "\n\n" 0 in
  if a >= 0 && (b < 0 || a + 2 <= b) then a + 4
  else if b >= 0 then b + 2
  else -1

let status head =
  if not (String.starts_with "HTTP/" head) then 0
  else
    match String.index_opt head ' ' with
    | Some i when String.length head >= i + 4 ->
      number (String.sub head (i + 1) 3)
    | _ -> 0

let header head name =
  let name = String.lowercase_ascii name in
  let rec look lines =
    match lines with
    | [] -> ""
    | l :: rest ->
      (match String.index_opt l ':' with
       | Some i when String.lowercase_ascii (String.trim (String.sub l 0 i))
                     = name ->
         String.trim (String.sub l (i + 1) (String.length l - i - 1))
       | _ -> look rest) in
  match String.split_on_char '\n' head with
  | _ :: lines -> look lines
  | [] -> ""

let media_type head =
  let v = header head "Content-Type" in
  String.lowercase_ascii
    (String.trim
       (match String.index_opt v ';' with
        | Some i -> String.sub v 0 i
        | None -> v))
tiny/TinyBrowser/TinyBrowserHttp.mli
2804
(* HTTP, the part of it www and the wire's other end speak: a request
 * for a page, and its answer, a head then the page's bytes.
 *
 *     www                                    the wire's other end
 *      | GET https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OCaml HTTP/1.0
 *      | User-Agent: www
 *      | (an empty line)            ------>  fetches it (TLS, gzip,
 *      |                                     chunks: tiny-machine-fetch)
 *      |                            <------  HTTP/1.0 200 OK
 *      |                                     Content-Type: text/html; ...
 *      |                                     Content-Length: 104277
 *      |                                     (an empty line)
 *      | read as HTML, or kept in a file      the page's bytes, then the
 *      | for a helper (TinyBrowser)           connection closed
 *
 * The request is a proxy's: the whole address on its line, not only
 * its path, since the other end fetches it for us. The answer is
 * HTTP/1.0's: the page ends where the connection does, and its bytes
 * are the page's own, the site's chunks and gzip undone, so a head
 * says neither; the site's other headers are passed on. Its
 * Content-Type says what the bytes are: HTML is read, a text shown as
 * it is, and what www does not show itself is given to a program
 * that does (a WAV file to play), as Mosaic did.
 *
 * What is dropped: every method but GET, a request's other headers
 * (cookies, a range, a cache's), keeping a connection for the next
 * request, and a head's continued lines.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * HTTP/0.9 (Tim Berners-Lee, 1991) was a line "GET /path" and the
 * page, no head: Gopher's shape, which this wire spoke before. HTTP/1.0
 * (RFC 1945, 1996, what NCSA's and CERN's servers did from 1993) added
 * the status line and the headers, MIME's from mail, Content-Type among
 * them; CERN's httpd was also the first proxy (1994), asked by a
 * request with the whole address on its line, as here.
 *)

(* [request url]: www's request for [url], to the wire's other end *)
val request : string -> string

(* the address a request asks for, if it is a GET *)
val asked : string -> string option

(* [response status headers body]: an answer, with its Content-Length *)
val response : int -> (string * string) list -> string -> string

(* where the head of a response that begins [s] ends (the body's first
 * byte), -1 if it has not yet *)
val head_end : string -> int

(* a head's status (200), 0 if its first line is not HTTP's *)
val status : string -> int

(* [header head name]: the header's value, "" if it has none; a name
 * is the same in any case *)
val header : string -> string -> string

(* a head's Content-Type, without its parameters, in lowercase
 * ("text/html"); "" if it has none *)
val media_type : string -> string
