(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyBrowserLines.mli *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Lines *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let bold = 1
let emph = 2
let code = 4
let big = 8
let under = 16

type run = { col : int; text : string; look : int; link : string; pic : int }
type line = { runs : run list; rule : bool }

(* A flow wraps words into lines of a given width, starting at a left
 * margin. *)
type flow = {
  width : int;
  mutable left : int;
  mutable made : run list;  (* the line being built, last run first *)
  mutable at : int;         (* the column where the next word goes *)
  mutable out : line list;  (* the finished lines, last line first *)
  mutable nlines : int;     (* how many lines are in out *)
  mutable blank : bool;     (* whether the next line wants a blank line
                             * before it *)
  mutable glue : int;       (* the column where the word being made started *)
  mutable cache : line array;  (* the lines from the top, when there were
                                * [cached] *)
  mutable cached : int;
}

let flow width =
  { width = width; left = 0; made = []; at = 0; out = []; nlines = 0;
    blank = false; glue = 0; cache = Array.make 0 { runs = []; rule = false };
    cached = 0 }

let push (f : flow) (l : line) =
  if f.blank then begin
    (match f.out with
     | x :: _ when x.runs <> [] || x.rule ->
       f.out <- { runs = []; rule = false } :: f.out;
       f.nlines <- f.nlines + 1
     | _ -> ());
    f.blank <- false
  end;
  f.out <- l :: f.out;
  f.nlines <- f.nlines + 1

let end_line (f : flow) =
  if f.made <> [] then begin
    push f { runs = List.rev f.made; rule = false }; f.made <- []
  end

(* Adds a word to the flow, after a space if [space] is true. When the
 * word has the same look and link as the previous run, it extends that
 * run instead of starting a new one. *)
(* Moves the word being made, from the column where it started, to a
 * new line, and ends the line before it. A word can be made of several
 * pieces with no space between them (a full stop and a reference's
 * [15], a link and the comma after it), so it is only known to be too
 * long for its line when its last piece comes. *)
let carry (f : flow) =
  let g = f.glue in
  let keep = ref [] and move = ref [] in
  List.iter (fun (r : run) ->
    let n = String.length r.text in
    if r.col + n <= g then keep := r :: !keep
    else if r.col >= g then move := r :: !move
    else begin
      keep := { col = r.col; text = String.sub r.text 0 (g - r.col);
                look = r.look; link = r.link; pic = r.pic } :: !keep;
      move := { col = g; text = String.sub r.text (g - r.col) (n - g + r.col);
                look = r.look; link = r.link; pic = r.pic } :: !move
    end) (List.rev f.made);
  (* the line kept without the spaces at its end *)
  let rec strip s =
    let n = String.length s in
    if n > 0 && s.[n - 1] = ' ' then strip (String.sub s 0 (n - 1)) else s in
  f.made <- (match !keep with
    | r :: rest ->
      let t = strip r.text in
      if t = "" then rest
      else { col = r.col; text = t; look = r.look; link = r.link;
             pic = r.pic } :: rest
    | [] -> []);
  end_line f;
  let shift = g - f.left in
  f.made <- List.map (fun (r : run) ->
    { col = r.col - shift; text = r.text; look = r.look; link = r.link;
      pic = r.pic }) !move;
  f.at <- f.at - shift;
  f.glue <- f.left

let word (f : flow) text look link space =
  let len = String.length text in
  if f.made = [] then f.at <- f.left;
  let space = space && f.made <> [] in
  let space =
    if space && f.at + 1 + len > f.width then (end_line f; f.at <- f.left; false)
    else space in
  if (not space) && f.made <> [] && f.at + len > f.width && f.glue > f.left
  then carry f;
  let col = if space then f.at + 1 else f.at in
  if space || f.made = [] then f.glue <- col;
  (match f.made with
   | r :: rest
     when r.look = look && r.link = link
          && r.col + String.length r.text = f.at ->
       f.made <- { col = r.col; text = r.text ^ (if space then " " else "") ^ text;
                   look = look; link = link; pic = -1 } :: rest
   | _ ->
       (* The space between two different runs belongs to neither, so a
        * link's underline stops where its text stops. *)
       f.made <-
         { col = col; text = text; look = look; link = link; pic = -1 }
         :: f.made);
  f.at <- col + len

(* A picture of [rows] rows of the screen: a line for
 * each row, whose one run is the picture's slice there (its number
 * times 256, plus the row), at the left margin. The text goes on under
 * it. *)
let picture_block (f : flow) id rows link =
  end_line f;
  for s = 0 to rows - 1 do
    push f { runs = [ { col = f.left; text = ""; look = 0; link = link;
                        pic = (id * 256) + s } ];
             rule = false }
  done

(* Adds a text exactly as it is, with no wrapping (for <pre>). *)
let verbatim (f : flow) text look link =
  if f.made = [] then f.at <- f.left;
  if text <> "" then begin
    f.made <-
      { col = f.at; text = text; look = look; link = link; pic = -1 } :: f.made;
    f.at <- f.at + String.length text
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Tables *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The words of a cell are kept until the end of the table, when the
 * widths of its columns are known. *)
type item =
  | Word of string * int * string * bool
  | Break
  | Pic of int * int * int * string

type cell = { mutable items : item list; span : int; head : bool }
type table = {
  mutable rows : cell list list;  (* the rows so far, last row first *)
  mutable row : cell list;
  mutable cell : cell option;
  mutable depth : int;            (* how many tables are open inside it; their
                                   * cells just become text of the current cell *)
  mutable broken : int;           (* a line's end not yet in the cell, put
                                   * there before the next word: 1 a block's,
                                   * 2 an inner table's row's *)
}

let cell_words (c : cell) = List.rev c.items

(* Returns the narrowest a cell can be (its longest word) and the widest
 * it would like to be (its text with no wrapping, except at its own
 * line breaks). *)
let measure (c : cell) =
  let narrow = ref 0 and wide = ref 0 and line = ref 0 in
  List.iter (function
    | Word (t, _, _, sp) ->
        let len = String.length t in
        narrow := max !narrow len;
        line := !line + len + (if sp && !line > 0 then 1 else 0);
        wide := max !wide !line
    | Pic (_, cols, _, _) ->
        narrow := max !narrow cols; wide := max !wide cols; line := 0
    | Break -> line := 0) (cell_words c);
  !narrow, !wide

(* Computes the widths of n columns that must fit in [room]. If every
 * column fits at its widest, it gets that. Otherwise each column gets
 * its narrowest width, plus a share of the remaining room proportional
 * to how much wider it would like to be. *)
let widths rows n room =
  let narrow = Array.make n 0 and wide = Array.make n 0 in
  List.iter (fun row ->
    ignore (List.fold_left (fun k (c : cell) ->
      if k < n && c.span = 1 then begin
        let a, b = measure c in
        narrow.(k) <- max narrow.(k) a;
        wide.(k) <- max wide.(k) b
      end;
      k + c.span) 0 row)) rows;
  let sn = ref 0 and sw = ref 0 in
  for k = 0 to n - 1 do sn := !sn + narrow.(k); sw := !sw + wide.(k) done;
  if !sw <= room then wide
  else if !sn >= room then narrow
  else begin
    let w = Array.make n 0 in
    for k = 0 to n - 1 do
      w.(k) <-
        narrow.(k) + ((wide.(k) - narrow.(k)) * (room - !sn) / (!sw - !sn))
    done;
    w
  end

let gap = 2

(* Lays out a finished table into the flow: each cell is wrapped in its
 * column, and the cells of a row are put side by side. *)
let lay_table (f : flow) (t : table) =
  let rows = List.rev (List.map List.rev t.rows) in
  let rows = List.filter (fun r -> r <> []) rows in
  (* A caption spans all the columns, but counts as one here. *)
  let n =
    List.fold_left (fun m r ->
      max m (List.fold_left (fun s (c : cell) ->
        s + (if c.span >= 1000 then 1 else c.span)) 0 r)) 0 rows in
  if n > 0 then begin
    let room = f.width - f.left - (gap * (n - 1)) in
    let w = widths rows n room in
    (* A cell spanning several columns gets their widths plus the gaps
     * between them. *)
    let span_width k span =
      let s = ref 0 in
      for j = k to min n (k + span) - 1 do s := !s + w.(j) + gap done;
      !s - gap in
    let x = Array.make (n + 1) f.left in
    for k = 1 to n do x.(k) <- x.(k - 1) + w.(k - 1) + gap done;
    end_line f;
    f.blank <- true;
    List.iter (fun row ->
      let k = ref 0 in
      let laid = List.map (fun (c : cell) ->
        let cw = if !k < n then max 1 (span_width !k c.span) else 1 in
        let g = flow cw in
        List.iter (function
          | Word (text, look, link, sp) ->
            word g text (if c.head then look lor bold else look) link sp
          | Pic (id, _, rows, link) -> picture_block g id rows link
          | Break -> end_line g) (cell_words c);
        end_line g;
        let at = if !k < n then x.(!k) else x.(n) in
        k := !k + c.span;
        at, List.rev g.out) row in
      let height =
        List.fold_left (fun h (_, ls) -> max h (List.length ls)) 0 laid in
      for i = 0 to height - 1 do
        let runs = List.concat (List.map (fun (at, ls) ->
          match List.nth_opt ls i with
          | Some (l : line) ->
            List.map (fun (r : run) ->
              { col = r.col + at; text = r.text; look = r.look; link = r.link;
                pic = r.pic }) l.runs
          | None -> []) laid) in
        push f { runs = runs; rule = false }
      done) rows;
    f.blank <- true
  end
tiny/TinyBrowser/TinyBrowserLines.mli
4867
(* What TinyBrowser keeps of a page, its lines, and how words become
 * lines: a flow wraps them at the screen's width, and a table's cells,
 * kept until </table>, are laid out side by side. TinyBrowserHtml says
 * which words go where; TinyBrowser draws the lines.
 *
 * A line is a few runs, each a text at a column with a look and a
 * link; so a line costs what its text costs, and drawing one is a
 * string a run:
 *
 *     col 0                   col 22   col 24
 *     "OCaml is a dialect of" "ML"     ", with objects"
 *      look 0                  link     look 0
 *                              "./ML"
 *
 * A table is the one place where a line cannot be made at once,
 * because a column must be as wide as its widest cell, which we only
 * know at the end of the table. So the words of each cell are kept
 * (items) until </table>. Then each column gets a width: at least its
 * longest word, its whole text if there is room, and otherwise a share
 * of the remaining room proportional to what it would need. Each cell
 * is then a flow of its column's width, and the rows are laid out side
 * by side.
 *
 * others:
 * the autolayout that HTML 4's specification sketches in an appendix
 * works the same way, each column between its minimum and its maximum
 * width (from memory). Plan 9's mothra shows a table's rows as cells
 * one after the other, not in columns.
 *)

(* The look of a run is a combination of these bits (big: a large
 * heading's, drawn twice the size; under: underlined, <u> and <ins>). *)
val bold : int
val emph : int
val code : int
val big : int
val under : int

(* A run is a piece of text at a column, with a look and the address it
 * links to ("" if it is not a link); or, when [pic] is not -1, a slice
 * of a picture 16 pixels high: the picture's number times 256, plus
 * which slice (-2: the bottom half of a large heading's line). A line
 * is a list of runs, from left to right. A rule is a line drawn across
 * the screen, under a heading or for an <hr>. *)
type run = { col : int; text : string; look : int; link : string; pic : int }
type line = { runs : run list; rule : bool }

(* A flow wraps words into lines of a given width, starting at a left
 * margin. *)
type flow = {
  width : int;
  mutable left : int;
  mutable made : run list;  (* the line being built, last run first *)
  mutable at : int;         (* the column where the next word goes *)
  mutable out : line list;  (* the finished lines, last line first *)
  mutable nlines : int;     (* how many lines are in out *)
  mutable blank : bool;     (* whether the next line wants a blank line
                             * before it *)
  mutable glue : int;       (* the column where the word being made started *)
  mutable cache : line array;  (* the lines from the top, when there were
                                * [cached] *)
  mutable cached : int;
}

(* an empty flow of that width *)
val flow : int -> flow

(* Adds a finished line (after a blank one when the flow wants it). *)
val push : flow -> line -> unit

(* Ends the line being built, if it has anything. *)
val end_line : flow -> unit

(* [word flow text look link space] adds a word, after a space if
 * [space]: on this line if it fits, else on the next one, with the
 * pieces of the same word before it (a link and the comma after it). *)
val word : flow -> string -> int -> string -> bool -> unit

(* [picture_block flow id rows link]: [rows] lines, each a slice of the
 * picture [id], at the left margin. *)
val picture_block : flow -> int -> int -> string -> unit

(* [verbatim flow text look link] adds a text as it is, with no
 * wrapping (<pre>'s). *)
val verbatim : flow -> string -> int -> string -> unit

(* A cell's words, kept until the end of its table: a word (its text,
 * look, link and whether a space was before it), a line's end, or a
 * picture (its number, columns, rows and link). *)
type item =
  | Word of string * int * string * bool
  | Break
  | Pic of int * int * int * string

(* A cell spans [span] columns (a caption: 1000, all of them); a head
 * (<th>, <caption>) is bold. *)
type cell = { mutable items : item list; span : int; head : bool }
type table = {
  mutable rows : cell list list;  (* the rows so far, last row first *)
  mutable row : cell list;
  mutable cell : cell option;
  mutable depth : int;            (* how many tables are open inside it; their
                                   * cells just become text of the current cell *)
  mutable broken : int;           (* a line's end not yet in the cell, put
                                   * there before the next word: 1 a block's,
                                   * 2 an inner table's row's *)
}

(* Lays out a finished table into the flow: each cell is wrapped in its
 * column, and the cells of a row are put side by side. *)
val lay_table : flow -> table -> unit
tiny/TinyBrowser/TinyBrowserScreen.ml

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyBrowserScreen.mli *)
open TinyCalls
open TinyLibDraw
open TinyLibPlayground
open TinyLibGUI
open TinyBrowserLines
open TinyBrowserHtml

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The colours, each an image of one pixel on our connection to the
 * screen (image 0 is where we draw: the screen, or our window). The
 * numbers in d_colour are bytes of the machine's palette. Our images
 * are above the playground's (3 plus a colour's byte, up to 258), which
 * the menus and the toolbar are drawn with. *)
let c_white = 261
let c_black = 262
let c_link = 263
let c_code = 264
let c_rule = 265
let c_text = 268
let colours =
  d_colour c_white 255 ^ d_colour c_black 0 ^ d_colour c_link 23
  ^ d_colour c_code 221
  ^ d_colour c_rule 136 ^ d_colour c_text 68

(*****************************************************************************)
(* What the screen shows *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* What the screen shows. At the top, TinyLibGUI's bar of menus, with the
 * page's title, and a toolbar: Back, the address, Go. The last row
 * says how the reading goes, and the rows between show the page's
 * lines, scrolled by pixels (sc_y). A line that arrives is drawn if it
 * falls in the page's area.
 * A page is read from [nv_wire], the connection to the wire's other end,
 * -1 when the page is all there; [nv_history] holds the pages seen
 * before, each with the first line that was shown. Where the browsing
 * is (the nav) is a record of its own, as tiny-ml builds a record's
 * fields on its 11 registers. *)
type nav = {
  mutable nv_address : string;       (* the page's full address, without its
                                      * #fragment *)
  mutable nv_wire : int;
  mutable nv_history : (string * int) list;
  mutable nv_goal : int;             (* a line to show first once it has come
                                      * (back), or -1 *)
  mutable nv_goal_id : string;       (* an anchor to show once it has come
                                      * (#fragment), or "" *)
  mutable nv_pressed : bool;         (* the mouse's button is down *)
  mutable nv_fetch : int;            (* the picture [nv_wire] brings, or -1 for
                                      * the page *)
  mutable nv_hover : bool;           (* the mouse is over a link: its look is
                                      * a hand *)
}

(* the menus and the toolbar's, below the model as TinyLibGUI has them *)
type tools = {
  mutable tb_field : string;          (* the address, as shown or being typed *)
  mutable tb_mouse : mouse;           (* TinyLibGUI's: the field has the keys
                                       * when pressed in last *)
  tb_menu : menu_state;
}

(* The document being read: HTTP's answer, its head first, then its
 * body, which goes by the head's Content-Type ([dc_type], "" until the
 * head has come): read as HTML, shown as a text, or kept in a file
 * ([dc_file]) for a program that shows it. *)
type doc = {
  mutable dc_got : int;              (* the bytes read so far *)
  mutable dc_head : string;          (* the head so far, until it ends *)
  mutable dc_type : string;
  mutable dc_status : int;           (* 200, or 0 when no head said *)
  mutable dc_file : int;             (* the file a helper's bytes go to, or
                                      * -1 *)
}

type screen = {
  mutable sc_page : page;
  sc_nav : nav;
  sc_tools : tools;
  sc_cols : int;
  sc_rows : int;
  mutable sc_y : int;               (* the page's pixel at the top of its area *)
  mutable sc_drawn : int;           (* the lines before this one that are in
                                     * the area are drawn *)
  sc_doc : doc;
  mutable sc_state : string;        (* "reading", "done", or why there is no page *)
  mutable sc_msgs : string list;    (* drawing messages not yet written, last
                                     * first *)
}

let put sc m = sc.sc_msgs <- m :: sc.sc_msgs

(* What a menu's item or a button of the toolbar does ([act] below):
 * Typed is the toolbar's field, its text after a key *)
type act =
  | Back | Top | Reload | Quit | Address | Search | Go_to of string
  | Go_typed
  | Typed of string

(* The menus (TinyLibGUI's): the page, a few articles to go to, and the
 * pages seen before (the last ten, the latest first) *)
let bookmarks = [ "OCaml"; "Plan 9 from Bell Labs"; "Unix"; "Niklaus Wirth" ]
let menus sc =
  let rec first n l =
    match l with x :: rest when n > 0 -> x :: first (n - 1) rest | _ -> [] in
  let short a = if String.length a > 56 then String.sub a 0 56 else a in
  [ "Page", [ "Back       b", Back; "Top", Top; "Reload", Reload;
              "Quit       q", Quit ];
    "Go", ("Address... g", Address) :: ("Search...  s", Search)
          :: List.map (fun t -> t, Go_to t) bookmarks;
    "History",
    List.map (fun (a, _) -> short a, Go_to a) (first 10 sc.sc_nav.nv_history) ]

(* The drawing messages written. A menu that is open is over the page:
 * it is drawn again, over what the messages drew. *)
let send sc =
  if sc.sc_msgs <> [] then begin
    ignore (u_write 3 (String.concat "" (List.rev sc.sc_msgs)));
    sc.sc_msgs <- [];
    if sc.sc_tools.tb_menu.opened >= 0 then begin
      List.iter (draw 0 0 0)
        (List.tl (menu_view (sc.sc_cols * 8) (menus sc) sc.sc_tools.tb_menu));
      flush ()
    end
  end

let clip sc s =
  if String.length s > sc.sc_cols - 2 then
    String.sub s 0 (max 0 (sc.sc_cols - 2))
  else s

(* a row, filled with a colour *)
let fill_row sc row colour =
  put sc (d_fill 0 colour 0 (row * 16) (sc.sc_cols * 8) ((row * 16) + 16))

(* The page's area on the screen: from under the toolbar to the status
 * row, [area sc] pixels high. The page scrolls by pixels: its line i is
 * at area_top + 16 i - sc_y. *)
let area_top = bar_height + 32
let area sc = ((sc.sc_rows - 1) * 16) - area_top
let rows_of_page sc = area sc / 16

(* A line cut by the page area's edge (half scrolled out) is drawn first
 * into [c_strip], an image of one line kept for that, then copied to
 * its place on the screen, cut to the area: so it never draws over the
 * bar or the status line. A line all inside the area is drawn on the
 * screen itself. *)
let c_strip = 269

(* A picture's image on our connection is its number plus 272 (the
 * colours and the strip are below). *)
let image_of id = 272 + id

(* A slice of a picture (16 rows of it) into dst at row y: the rows that
 * have come, from the picture's image, and a grey box for the rest;
 * until its first rows come, its alternative text on the grey. *)
let draw_slice sc dst y (r : run) =
  let id = r.pic / 256 and s = r.pic mod 256 in
  let pc = picture_of sc.sc_page id in
  let x = r.col * 8 and from = s * 16 in
  let high = min 16 (pc.pc_h - from) in
  if high > 0 then begin
    let have = if pc.pc_got > from then min high (pc.pc_got - from) else 0 in
    if have > 0 then
      put sc
        (d_draw dst (image_of id) (-1) x y (x + pc.pc_w) (y + have) 0 from);
    if have < high then begin
      put sc (d_fill dst c_code x (y + have) (x + pc.pc_w) (y + high));
      if s = 0 && pc.pc_got <= 0 && pc.pc_w >= 24 && high = 16 then begin
        let alt = if pc.pc_alt = "" then "picture" else pc.pc_alt in
        let fits = (pc.pc_w / 8) - 1 in
        put sc (d_text dst c_text (x + 4) y
                  (if String.length alt > fits then String.sub alt 0 (max 0 fits)
                   else alt))
      end
    end
  end

(* The page's line i, put on the screen (by the strip when it is cut by
 * the area's edge, or is half of a large heading's line). The text is a
 * dark grey, bold black in the kernel's bold font (its strokes wider,
 * an m's gaps kept: drawn twice, a pixel apart, an m was a block);
 * emphasis is italic; a link is blue and underlined; code is on light
 * grey; a large heading's characters are 16 by 32, the kernel's large
 * font, its top half on one line, its bottom half (pic -2) on the next. *)
let draw_line sc i (l : line) =
  let w = sc.sc_cols * 8 and at = area_top + (i * 16) - sc.sc_y in
  let tall = List.exists (fun (r : run) -> r.look land big <> 0) l.runs in
  let whole = not tall && at >= area_top && at + 16 <= area_top + area sc in
  let dst = if whole then 0 else c_strip and y = if whole then at else 0 in
  put sc (d_fill dst c_white 0 y w (y + 16));
  if l.rule then put sc (d_fill dst c_rule 0 (y + 7) w (y + 9))
  else
    List.iter (fun (r : run) ->
      if r.pic >= 0 then draw_slice sc dst y r
      else if r.col < sc.sc_cols && r.text <> "" then begin
        let k = if r.look land big <> 0 then 2 else 1 in
        let n = min (String.length r.text) ((sc.sc_cols - r.col) / k) in
        let t = String.sub r.text 0 n and x = r.col * 8
        and ry = if r.pic = -2 then y - 16 else y in
        if r.look land code <> 0 then
          put sc (d_fill dst c_code x y (x + (n * 8)) (y + 16));
        let ink =
          if r.link <> "" then c_link
          else if r.look land bold <> 0 then c_black else c_text in
        (* (a look's bold and emph are the kernel's style's bits) *)
        let style =
          (r.look land (bold + emph))
          lor (if r.look land under <> 0 then 4 else 0)
          lor (if k = 2 then 8 else 0) in
        put sc (if style = 0 then d_text dst ink x ry t
                else d_styled dst ink x ry style t);
        if r.link <> "" then
          put sc (d_line dst c_link x (ry + (16 * k) - 1) (x + (n * 8 * k) - 1)
                    (ry + (16 * k) - 1))
      end) l.runs;
  if not whole then begin
    let y0 = max at area_top and y1 = min (at + 16) (area_top + area sc) in
    if y0 < y1 then put sc (d_draw 0 c_strip (-1) 0 y0 w y1 0 (y0 - at))
  end

(* The bar of menus, the page's title at the right of their titles, and
 * the menu open, by TinyLibPlayground's shapes (after our messages) *)
let draw_bar sc =
  send sc;
  let w = sc.sc_cols * 8 and ms = menus sc in
  let x =
    List.fold_left (fun x (t, _) -> x + (8 * String.length t) + 16) 16 ms in
  let t =
    if title sc.sc_page <> "" then title sc.sc_page else sc.sc_nav.nv_address in
  let n = max 0 (((w - x) / 8) - 1) in
  (match menu_view w ms sc.sc_tools.tb_menu with
   | bar :: opened ->
     draw 0 0 0 bar;
     draw 0 x 1
       (Words (0, if String.length t > n then String.sub t 0 n else t));
     List.iter (draw 0 0 0) opened
   | [] -> ());
  flush ()

(* The toolbar: Back, the address in a field (its end, when it is longer
 * than the field: what is typed goes after the part not shown), Go; by
 * TinyLibGUI's widgets, at their places *)
let input_box sc = 72, bar_height + 4, (sc.sc_cols * 8) - 144, 24
let laid_tools sc =
  let (x, y, w, h) = input_box sc in
  let f = sc.sc_tools.tb_field in
  let cut = max 0 (String.length f - ((w - 16) / 8)) in
  let input =
    Input (String.sub f cut (String.length f - cut),
           fun t -> Typed (String.sub f 0 cut ^ t)) in
  let (s1, b1) = place 8 y 56 h (Button ("Back", Back)) in
  let (s2, b2) = place x y w h input in
  let (s3, b3) = place (x + w + 8) y 56 h (Button ("Go", Go_typed)) in
  s1 @ s2 @ s3, b1 @ b2 @ b3

(* the toolbar on its ground (TinyLibGUI's grey), and what the mouse
 * puts over it: a button held, the field's caret *)
let draw_tools sc =
  let (shapes, boxes) = laid_tools sc in
  send sc;
  draw 0 0 bar_height (Rect (0xcc, sc.sc_cols * 8, area_top - bar_height));
  List.iter (draw 0 0 0) shapes;
  List.iter (fun (_, s) -> draw 0 0 0 s) (over boxes sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse);
  flush ()

(* the field has the keys: the mouse's button went down in it last *)
let focused sc =
  inside sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse.fx sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse.fy (input_box sc)
let focus sc on =
  sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse <-
    { sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse with
      fx = (if on then 80 else -1);
      fy = (if on then bar_height + 8 else -1) }

let draw_status sc =
  let row = sc.sc_rows - 1 in
  fill_row sc row c_code;
  let d = sc.sc_doc in
  let kb = string_of_int ((d.dc_got + 1023) / 1024) ^ " KB" in
  let text =
    (if sc.sc_state = "reading" then "reading, " ^ kb
     else if sc.sc_state = "done" then
       (if d.dc_status <> 200 && d.dc_status <> 0 then
          string_of_int d.dc_status ^ ", " else "")
       ^ kb ^ ", " ^ string_of_int (count sc.sc_page) ^ " lines"
       ^ (if sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch >= 0 then
            ", picture " ^ string_of_int (sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch + 1) ^ " of "
            ^ string_of_int (pictures sc.sc_page)
          else "")
     else sc.sc_state)
    ^ "   space -: page, b: back, g: address, q: quit" in
  put sc (d_text 0 c_black 8 (row * 16) (clip sc text))

(* The page's lines that fall in its area, from pixel [a] to pixel [b]
 * of the page, drawn; white where the page has ended. *)
let draw_between sc a b =
  let first = a / 16 and last = (b + 15) / 16 in
  let ls = lines_between sc.sc_page first last in
  List.iteri (fun k l -> draw_line sc (first + k) l) ls;
  let bottom = area_top + ((first + List.length ls) * 16) - sc.sc_y in
  let y0 = max bottom (area_top + a - sc.sc_y)
  and y1 = area_top + b - sc.sc_y in
  if y0 < y1 then put sc (d_fill 0 c_white 0 y0 (sc.sc_cols * 8) y1);
  first + List.length ls

(* the whole area drawn again *)
let redraw sc = sc.sc_drawn <- draw_between sc sc.sc_y (sc.sc_y + area sc)

let max_y sc = max 0 ((count sc.sc_page * 16) - area sc)

(* Scrolls by [d] pixels (up when negative). What stays on the screen is
 * moved there by one copy of the screen onto itself, and only the strip
 * that comes in is drawn: a scroll of a line draws one line, not the
 * screen's thirty. *)
let scroll_by sc d =
  let y = max 0 (min (sc.sc_y + d) (max_y sc)) in
  let delta = y - sc.sc_y and h = area sc and w = sc.sc_cols * 8 in
  if delta <> 0 then begin
    if abs delta >= h then begin sc.sc_y <- y; redraw sc end
    else if delta > 0 then begin
      put sc (d_draw 0 0 (-1) 0 area_top w (area_top + h - delta) 0
                (area_top + delta));
      sc.sc_y <- y;
      let first = (y + h - delta) / 16 in
      let drawn = draw_between sc (y + h - delta) (y + h) in
      if sc.sc_drawn >= first then sc.sc_drawn <- max sc.sc_drawn drawn
    end
    else begin
      put sc
        (d_draw 0 0 (-1) 0 (area_top - delta) w (area_top + h) 0 area_top);
      sc.sc_y <- y;
      ignore (draw_between sc y (y - delta));
      sc.sc_drawn <- min sc.sc_drawn ((y + h + 15) / 16)
    end
  end

(* A screenful at a time, in steps of a few lines, so that the page is
 * seen moving rather than jumping: the same lines are drawn as by a
 * jump, as each step only draws what comes in. *)
let glide sc d =
  let step = 64 in
  let rec go left =
    if left <> 0 then begin
      let s = if left > 0 then min step left else max (- step) left in
      let before = sc.sc_y in
      scroll_by sc s;
      send sc;
      if sc.sc_y <> before then go (left - s)
    end in
  go d

(* the page from line [line] on, as far as the page allows *)
let show_from sc line =
  let y = max 0 (min (line * 16) (max_y sc)) in
  if y <> sc.sc_y then begin sc.sc_y <- y; redraw sc end

(* The lines that arrived and fit below the ones on the screen; and the
 * place a page was asked to show (back, or a #fragment), once it has
 * come. *)
let show_new sc =
  if sc.sc_nav.nv_goal_id <> "" then
    (match anchor sc.sc_page sc.sc_nav.nv_goal_id with
     | Some line
       when line + rows_of_page sc <= count sc.sc_page
            || sc.sc_nav.nv_wire < 0 ->
       sc.sc_nav.nv_goal_id <- ""; show_from sc line
     | _ -> ());
  if sc.sc_nav.nv_goal >= 0
     && ((sc.sc_nav.nv_goal / 16) + rows_of_page sc <= count sc.sc_page
         || sc.sc_nav.nv_wire < 0) then begin
    let goal = sc.sc_nav.nv_goal in
    sc.sc_nav.nv_goal <- -1;
    let y = max 0 (min goal (max_y sc)) in
    if y <> sc.sc_y then begin sc.sc_y <- y; redraw sc end
  end;
  let last = min (count sc.sc_page) ((sc.sc_y + area sc + 15) / 16) in
  if sc.sc_drawn < last then begin
    List.iteri (fun k l -> draw_line sc (sc.sc_drawn + k) l)
      (lines_between sc.sc_page sc.sc_drawn last);
    sc.sc_drawn <- last
  end

(* The mouse's look: a hand over a link, the arrow elsewhere (d_cursor:
 * the machine's window or page shows it). Sent when it changes. *)
let hover sc over =
  if over <> sc.sc_nav.nv_hover then begin
    sc.sc_nav.nv_hover <- over;
    put sc (d_cursor (if over then 1 else 0))
  end
tiny/TinyBrowser/TinyBrowserScreen.mli
6495
(* TinyBrowserScreen: what www shows, and its drawing. TinyBrowser.ml's
 * browsing (where to go, what came, the keys and the mouse) changes the
 * records below and calls these to show it; the messages they make are
 * the kernel's drawing messages (TinyLibDraw), kept in [sc_msgs] and
 * written at once by [send].
 *
 *     +--------------------------------------------------+
 *     | Page  Go  History    the page's title            |  the bar: menus
 *     | [Back] [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OCaml] [Go] |  the toolbar
 *     |--------------------------------------------------|  area_top
 *     | the page's lines, scrolled by pixels (sc_y):     |
 *     | line i at area_top + 16 i - sc_y                 |  [area sc] high
 *     |--------------------------------------------------|
 *     | 360 KB, 862 lines   space -: page, b: back, ...  |  the status row
 *     +--------------------------------------------------+
 *
 * A line that arrives is drawn if it falls in the area; a scroll copies
 * what stays on the screen onto itself and draws only the strip that
 * comes in; a line cut by the area's edge is drawn in a strip image
 * first, then copied, so it never draws over the bar or the status.
 *
 * What is ours, against the twins: mini-netscape lays out boxes and
 * paints them into a framebuffer of its own (the engine's display);
 * here a page is lines of runs, each run a text at a column, drawn by
 * the kernel's text and fills, a picture's slice by a copy of its
 * image.
 *)

(* the colours, images of a pixel on the connection to the screen, and
 * the messages that make them *)
val c_white : int
val c_black : int
val c_link : int
val c_code : int
val c_rule : int
val c_text : int
val colours : string

(* What the screen shows. At the top, TinyLibGUI's bar of menus, with the
 * page's title, and a toolbar: Back, the address, Go. The last row
 * says how the reading goes, and the rows between show the page's
 * lines, scrolled by pixels (sc_y). A line that arrives is drawn if it
 * falls in the page's area.
 * A page is read from [nv_wire], the connection to the wire's other end,
 * -1 when the page is all there; [nv_history] holds the pages seen
 * before, each with the first line that was shown. Where the browsing
 * is (the nav) is a record of its own, as tiny-ml builds a record's
 * fields on its 11 registers. *)
type nav = {
  mutable nv_address : string;       (* the page's full address, without its
                                      * #fragment *)
  mutable nv_wire : int;
  mutable nv_history : (string * int) list;
  mutable nv_goal : int;             (* a line to show first once it has come
                                      * (back), or -1 *)
  mutable nv_goal_id : string;       (* an anchor to show once it has come
                                      * (#fragment), or "" *)
  mutable nv_pressed : bool;         (* the mouse's button is down *)
  mutable nv_fetch : int;            (* the picture [nv_wire] brings, or -1 for
                                      * the page *)
  mutable nv_hover : bool;           (* the mouse is over a link: its look is
                                      * a hand *)

(* the menus and the toolbar's, below the model as TinyLibGUI has them *)
type tools = {

  mutable tb_mouse : TinyLibGUI.mouse; (* the field has the keys when

  tb_menu : TinyLibGUI.menu_state;

(* The document being read: HTTP's answer, its head first, then its
 * body, which goes by the head's Content-Type ([dc_type], "" until the
 * head has come): read as HTML, shown as a text, or kept in a file
 * ([dc_file]) for a program that shows it. *)
type doc = {
  mutable dc_got : int;              (* the bytes read so far *)
  mutable dc_head : string;          (* the head so far, until it ends *)
  mutable dc_type : string;
  mutable dc_status : int;           (* 200, or 0 when no head said *)
  mutable dc_file : int;             (* the file a helper's bytes go to, or
                                      * -1 *)
}

type screen = {
  mutable sc_page : TinyBrowserHtml.page;
  sc_nav : nav;
  sc_tools : tools;
  sc_cols : int;
  sc_rows : int;
  mutable sc_y : int;               (* the page's pixel at the top of its area *)
  mutable sc_drawn : int;           (* the lines before this one that are in
                                     * the area are drawn *)

  mutable sc_state : string;        (* "reading", "done", or why there is no page *)
  mutable sc_msgs : string list;    (* drawing messages not yet written, last
                                     * first *)
}

(* Returns the position of pat in s, searching from i, or -1. *)
let find s pat i =
  let n = String.length s and m = String.length pat in
  let rec at j k = k >= m || (s.[j + k] = pat.[k] && at j (k + 1)) in
  let rec go j = if j + m > n then -1 else if at j 0 then j else go (j + 1) in
  go i

let is_space c = c = ' ' || c = '\n' || c = '\t' || c = '\r'

(* Is w one of the space-separated words of a class attribute? *)
let has_class classes w =
  w <> "" && List.mem w (String.split_on_char ' ' classes)

(* an attribute's number, 0 when it is not one *)
let number s = match int_of_string_opt s with Some n -> n | None -> 0

(* The Latin-1 letters from 0xc0 on, each without its accent; and
 * Latin Extended-A's, from 0x100 to 0x17f (the names of Central Europe:
 * c with a caron, l with a stroke, o with a double acute), the same way
 * (made from Unicode's decompositions). *)
let latin1 = "AAAAAAACEEEEIIIIDNOOOOOxOUUUUYPsaaaaaaaceeeeiiiidnooooo/ouuuuypy"
let latin_a =
  "AaAaAaCcCcCcCcDdDdEeEeEeEeEeGgGgGgGgHhHhIiIiIiIiIiIiJjKkkLlLlLlLlLlNnNnNnnNnOoOoOoOoRrRrRrSsSsSsSsTtTtTtUuUuUuUuUuUuWwYyYZzZzZzs"

(* Converts a Unicode code point to what the 128-character font can show. *)
let of_code u =
  if u < 128 then
    (if u = 9 || u = 10 then " " else if u < 32 then ""
     else String.make 1 (Char.chr u))
  else if u >= 0xc0 && u <= 0xff then String.make 1 latin1.[u - 0xc0]
  else if u = 0x152 then "OE" else if u = 0x153 then "oe"
  else if u >= 0x100 && u < 0x180 then String.make 1 latin_a.[u - 0x100]
  else match u with
  | 0x20ac -> "EUR" | 0xa3 -> "GBP" | 0xa5 -> "JPY" | 0xa7 -> "S."
  | 0xb2 -> "2" | 0xb3 -> "3" | 0xb9 -> "1" | 0xbc -> "1/4" | 0xbe -> "3/4"
  | 0xa0 | 0x2002 | 0x2003 | 0x2009 | 0x202f -> " "
  | 0xad | 0x200b | 0x200c | 0x200d | 0x200e | 0x200f | 0x2060 | 0xfeff -> ""
  | 0xa9 -> "(c)" | 0xae -> "(R)" | 0xb0 -> "o" | 0xb1 -> "+-"
  | 0xb7 | 0x2219 | 0x22c5 -> "."
  | 0xab -> "<<" | 0xbb -> ">>" | 0xbd -> "1/2" | 0xd7 -> "x" | 0xf7 -> "/"
  | 0x2010 | 0x2011 | 0x2012 | 0x2013 | 0x2014 | 0x2015 | 0x2212 -> "-"
  | 0x2018 | 0x2019 | 0x201a | 0x2032 | 0x2bc -> "'"
  | 0x201c | 0x201d | 0x201e | 0x2033 -> "\""
  | 0x2022 | 0x25cf -> "*" | 0x2026 -> "..." | 0x2192 -> "->"
  | 0x2190 -> "<-" | 0x2191 -> "^" | 0x21d2 -> "=>"
  | 0x2264 -> "<=" | 0x2265 -> ">=" | 0x2260 -> "/=" | 0x2248 -> "~"
  | 0x221e -> "inf"
  | 0x3bb -> "lambda" | 0x3b1 -> "alpha" | 0x3b2 -> "beta" | 0x3b3 -> "gamma"
  | 0x3b4 -> "delta" | 0x3b5 -> "epsilon"
  | 0x3b8 -> "theta" | 0x3bc -> "mu" | 0x3c0 -> "pi" | 0x3c3 -> "sigma"
  | 0x3c6 | 0x3d5 -> "phi" | 0x3c9 -> "omega"
  | 0x394 -> "Delta" | 0x3a3 -> "Sigma" | 0x3a9 -> "Omega"
  | 0x21a6 -> "|->" | 0x2208 -> "in" | 0x2295 -> "(+)" | 0x2021 -> "++"
  | 0x200a | 0x2061 -> "" 
  | _ -> "?"

let entity name =
  match name with
  | "amp" -> 38 | "lt" -> 60 | "gt" -> 62 | "quot" -> 34 | "apos" -> 39
  | "nbsp" -> 0xa0
  | "ndash" -> 0x2013 | "mdash" -> 0x2014 | "minus" -> 0x2212
  | "hellip" -> 0x2026
  | "lsquo" -> 0x2018 | "rsquo" -> 0x2019 | "ldquo" -> 0x201c
  | "rdquo" -> 0x201d
  | "middot" -> 0xb7 | "bull" -> 0x2022 | "times" -> 0xd7 | "copy" -> 0xa9
  | "reg" -> 0xae
  | "shy" -> 0xad
  | "rarr" -> 0x2192 | "larr" -> 0x2190 | "laquo" -> 0xab | "raquo" -> 0xbb
  | "deg" -> 0xb0
  | "eacute" -> 0xe9 | "egrave" -> 0xe8 | "aacute" -> 0xe1 | "ouml" -> 0xf6
  | "uuml" -> 0xfc
  | _ -> -1

(* Returns the code point of an entity, given the text between its &
 * and its ; (like "amp", "#8211" or "#x2013"), or -1 if it is unknown:
 * a number's, as int_of_string reads 08211 and 0x2013 *)
let entity_code s =
  let n = String.length s in
  if n > 1 && s.[0] = '#' then
    (match
       int_of_string_opt
         ("0" ^ String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub s 1 (n - 1)))
     with
     | Some u -> u
     | None -> -1)
  else entity s

(* How many bytes a UTF-8 character has, given its first byte. *)
let utf8_length b =
  if b < 0x80 then 1 else if b < 0xc0 then 1 else if b < 0xe0 then 2
  else if b < 0xf0 then 3 else 4

let ascii s =
  let n = String.length s in
  if not (String.exists (fun c -> c = '&' || Char.code c >= 128) s) then s
  else begin
    (* The result is built as a list of pieces: stretches of plain
     * ASCII copied as they are, and a replacement for each entity or
     * non-ASCII character. *)
    let pieces = ref [] and plain = ref 0 in
    let cut i =
      if i > !plain then pieces := String.sub s !plain (i - !plain) :: !pieces
    in
    let i = ref 0 in
    while !i < n do
      let c = s.[!i] in
      if c = '&' then begin
        let j = ref (!i + 1) in
        while !j < n && !j - !i < 12 && s.[!j] <> ';' && not (is_space s.[!j])
              && s.[!j] <> '&' do
          incr j
        done;
        let u =
          if !j < n && s.[!j] = ';' then
            entity_code (String.sub s (!i + 1) (!j - !i - 1))
          else -1 in
        if u >= 0 then begin
          cut !i; pieces := of_code u :: !pieces; i := !j + 1; plain := !i
        end
        else incr i
      end
      else if Char.code c >= 128 then begin
        let b = Char.code c in
        let len = utf8_length b in
        let rec follows k =
          k >= len
          || (Char.code s.[!i + k] land 0xc0 = 0x80 && follows (k + 1)) in
        let u =
          if len = 1 || !i + len > n || not (follows 1) then -1
          else if len = 2 then
            ((b land 0x1f) lsl 6) lor (Char.code s.[!i + 1] land 0x3f)
          else if len = 3 then
            ((b land 0x0f) lsl 12)
            lor ((Char.code s.[!i + 1] land 0x3f) lsl 6)
            lor (Char.code s.[!i + 2] land 0x3f)
          else 0x10000 in
        cut !i;
        pieces := (if u < 0 then "?" else of_code u) :: !pieces;
        i := !i + (if u < 0 then 1 else len);
        plain := !i
      end
      else incr i
    done;
    cut n;
    String.concat "" (List.rev !pieces)
  end

(* When a text runs to the end of a message, the next message may
 * continue it. This returns where it is safe to cut it: never in the
 * middle of an entity or of a UTF-8 character, and only after a space,
 * so that a word is never split in two. *)
let safe_end s i n =
  let rec amp j =
    if j < i || j < n - 12 then n else if s.[j] = '&' then j
    else if s.[j] = ';' || is_space s.[j] then n else amp (j - 1) in
  let a = amp (n - 1) in
  let rec lead j =
    if j > i && j > n - 4 && Char.code s.[j] land 0xc0 = 0x80 then lead (j - 1)
    else j in
  let l = if n > i && Char.code s.[n - 1] >= 0x80 then lead (n - 1) else n in
  let l = if l < n && l + utf8_length (Char.code s.[l]) > n then l else n in
  (* Back up to just after the last space. *)
  let rec space j =
    if j <= i then i else if is_space s.[j - 1] then j else space (j - 1) in
  space (min a l)

(* The text of a page as tiny-machine's font can show it, and the few
 * string functions the reading needs: TinyBrowser's lowest part, under
 * TinyBrowserTokens (a tag's attributes, a page's text) and
 * TinyBrowserHtml (classes, styles, numbers).
 *
 * The font has only 128 characters, so UTF-8 and HTML entities become
 * ASCII here: a dash becomes -, a curly quote a straight one, an
 * accented letter loses its accent (Latin-1's and Latin Extended-A's,
 * made from Unicode's decompositions), a few Greek letters their names,
 * and anything else ?.
 *
 *     "Caf&eacute; &ndash; na\xc3\xafve"  ──►  "Cafe - naive"
 *)

(* [find s pat i] is the position of pat in s, searching from i, or -1. *)
val find : string -> string -> int -> int

val is_space : char -> bool

(* Is w one of the space-separated words of a class attribute? *)
val has_class : string -> string -> bool

(* an attribute's number, 0 when it is not one *)
val number : string -> int

(* Converts a text to ASCII: entities and UTF-8 characters become what
 * the font can show. *)
val ascii : string -> string

(* [safe_end s i n]: where the text from i to the end n of a message
 * may be cut, the rest kept for the next message, which may continue
 * it: never in an entity or a UTF-8 character, and only after a space,
 * so that a word is never split in two (i when there is no such place). *)
val safe_end : string -> int -> int -> int

(* See TinyBrowserTokens.mli *)
open TinyBrowserText

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Tokens *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type token =
  | Text of string
  | Open of string * (string * string) list
  | Close of string

(* The attributes the browser uses. The others (like Parsoid's large
 * data-mw, or ids) are skipped without being copied. *)
let wanted =
  [ "href"; "class"; "style"; "src"; "alt"; "width"; "height"; "colspan";
    "start"; "id"; "http-equiv"; "content" ]

(* Parses the inside of a tag, the text between its < and its >. *)
let tag s =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec word i =
    if i < n && not (is_space s.[i]) && s.[i] <> '/' && s.[i] <> '='
       && s.[i] <> '>' then word (i + 1)
    else i in
  let rec skip i =
    if i < n && (is_space s.[i] || s.[i] = '/') then skip (i + 1) else i in
  if n > 0 && s.[0] = '/' then
    let e = word 1 in Close (String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub s 1 (e - 1)))
  else begin
    let e = word 0 in
    let name = String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub s 0 e) in
    let rec attrs i acc =
      let i = skip i in
      if i >= n then List.rev acc
      else begin
        let e = word i in
        let a = String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub s i (e - i)) in
        let rec sp j = if j < n && is_space s.[j] then sp (j + 1) else j in
        let j = sp e in
        if j < n && s.[j] = '=' then begin
          let j = sp (j + 1) in
          let q = if j < n then s.[j] else ' ' in
          let v0, v1, next =
            if q = '"' || q = '\'' then
              (match String.index_from_opt s (j + 1) q with
               | Some k -> j + 1, k, k + 1
               | None -> j + 1, n, n)
            else
              let rec un k =
                if k < n && not (is_space s.[k]) then un (k + 1) else k in
              let k = un j in
              j, k, k in
          if List.mem a wanted then
            attrs next ((a, ascii (String.sub s v0 (v1 - v0))) :: acc)
          else attrs next acc
        end
        else
          attrs (if e = i then i + 1 else e)
            (if List.mem a wanted then (a, "") :: acc else acc)
      end in
    Open (name, attrs e [])
  end

(* The reader keeps what the last message left unfinished (tail), and,
 * while we skip the content of a <style> or <script>, which is not
 * HTML, the name of that element (raw). *)
type reader = { mutable tail : string; mutable raw : string }

(* Finds the > that ends a tag, starting just after its <. A > inside
 * quotes does not count. Returns -1 if the tag is not complete yet. *)
let tag_end s i =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec go j q =
    if j >= n then -1
    else
      let c = s.[j] in
      if q <> ' ' then go (j + 1) (if c = q then ' ' else q)
      else if c = '>' then j
      else if c = '"' || c = '\'' then go (j + 1) c
      else go (j + 1) ' ' in
  go i ' '

(* Returns the tokens of a message. [last] is true when no message
 * follows, so nothing is kept for later. *)
let tokens (r : reader) chunk last =
  let s = if r.tail = "" then chunk else r.tail ^ chunk in
  let n = String.length s in
  r.tail <- "";
  let keep i = if not last then r.tail <- String.sub s i (n - i) in
  let rec go i acc =
    if i >= n then acc
    else if r.raw <> "" then begin
      let j = find s ("</" ^ r.raw) i in
      if j < 0 then begin keep (max i (n - 10)); acc end
      else (match String.index_from_opt s j '>' with
        | Some k ->
          let name = r.raw in r.raw <- ""; go (k + 1) (Close name :: acc)
        | None -> keep j; acc)
    end
    else if s.[i] = '<' then begin
      if i + 3 < n && s.[i + 1] = '!' && s.[i + 2] = '-' && s.[i + 3] = '-'
      then begin
        let j = find s "-->" (i + 4) in
        if j < 0 then begin keep i; acc end else go (j + 3) acc
      end
      else begin
        let k = tag_end s (i + 1) in
        if k < 0 then begin keep i; acc end
        else if i + 1 < n && (s.[i + 1] = '!' || s.[i + 1] = '?') then
          go (k + 1) acc
        else begin
          let t = tag (String.sub s (i + 1) (k - i - 1)) in
          (match t with
           | Open (name, _) when name = "style" || name = "script" ->
             r.raw <- name
           | _ -> ());
          go (k + 1) (t :: acc)
        end
      end
    end
    else begin
      let j =
        match String.index_from_opt s i '<' with Some j -> j | None -> n in
      let e = if j = n && not last then safe_end s i n else j in
      if e < j then keep e;
      let acc =
        if e > i then Text (ascii (String.sub s i (e - i))) :: acc else acc in
      if e < j then acc else go j acc
    end in
  List.rev (go 0 [])
tiny/TinyBrowser/TinyBrowserTokens.mli

(* The HTML tokenizer of TinyBrowser: a page's messages, as they come,
 * to its tags and its texts, which TinyBrowserHtml turns into lines.
 *
 * A message can end anywhere, even in the middle of a tag, of an
 * entity like &amp;, or of a multi-byte UTF-8 character. The reader
 * keeps the unfinished end (its tail) and reads it again in front of
 * the next message:
 *
 *     "<p>Hello <b>wo"   ──►  Open p, Text "Hello "     tail "<b>wo"
 *     "rld</b></p>"      ──►  Open b, Text "world", Close b, Close p
 *
 * Comments, <!DOCTYPE> and <?xml?> are skipped; the content of <style>
 * and <script>, which is not HTML, is skipped to its end tag; of the
 * attributes only those the browser uses are kept (Parsoid's data-mw
 * can be kilobytes), their values made ASCII by TinyBrowserText.
 *
 * others:
 * the "tokenization" chapter of the HTML standard, a state machine,
 * says everything a tokenizer must accept; this one handles the part
 * that well-formed pages use. The full-size one in ix is mini-chrome's
 * Html_lexer (its entities in Entities).
 *)

(* A tag's name and its attributes are in lower case. *)
type token =
  | Text of string
  | Open of string * (string * string) list
  | Close of string

(* What the last message left unfinished (tail), and, while we skip the
 * content of a <style> or <script>, the name of that element (raw);
 * both "" to begin. *)
type reader = { mutable tail : string; mutable raw : string }

(* [tokens reader message last]: the tokens of a message. [last] is
 * true when no message follows, so nothing is kept for later. *)
val tokens : reader -> string -> bool -> token list

(* What www does not show itself, given to a program that does, as
 * Mosaic's helpers: a Content-Type, the program in /bin, and the file
 * its bytes are kept in, in the current directory, for it to read *)
let helpers =
  [ "audio/wav", ("play", "www.wav"); "audio/x-wav", ("play", "www.wav");
    "audio/wave", ("play", "www.wav");
    "application/pdf", ("page", "www.pdf") ]

let is_html kind = kind = "text/html" || kind = "application/xhtml+xml"

(* a text as HTML's characters, for a text/plain shown in a <pre> *)
let escaped s =
  String.concat ""
    (List.init (String.length s) (fun i ->
       match s.[i] with
       | '<' -> "&lt;"
       | '&' -> "&amp;"
       | c -> String.make 1 c))

(* bytes of the body: read as HTML, as a text, or kept for a helper *)
let body sc s =
  let d = sc.sc_doc in
  if d.dc_file >= 0 then ignore (u_write d.dc_file s)
  else if is_html d.dc_type then feed sc.sc_page s
  else if String.starts_with "text/" d.dc_type then feed sc.sc_page (escaped s)

(* The head's end: the status, and what the body is (HTML when the head
 * does not say, as when there is no head) *)
let body_start sc =
  let d = sc.sc_doc in
  d.dc_status <- status d.dc_head;
  d.dc_type <- (match media_type d.dc_head with "" -> "text/html" | t -> t);
  match List.assoc_opt d.dc_type helpers with
  | Some (_, file) -> d.dc_file <- u_open file 0x601
  | None ->
    if is_html d.dc_type then ()
    else if String.starts_with "text/" d.dc_type then feed sc.sc_page "<pre>"
    else feed sc.sc_page ("<p>" ^ d.dc_type ^ ": www does not show it.</p>")

(* A message of the page: the head kept until it ends, then the body *)
let take sc s =
  let d = sc.sc_doc in
  if d.dc_type <> "" then body sc s
  else begin
    d.dc_head <- d.dc_head ^ s;
    let headless =
      String.length d.dc_head >= 5
      && not (String.starts_with "HTTP/" d.dc_head) in
    let e = if headless then 0 else head_end d.dc_head in
    if e >= 0 then begin
      let rest = String.sub d.dc_head e (String.length d.dc_head - e) in
      d.dc_head <- String.sub d.dc_head 0 e;
      body_start sc;
      body sc rest
    end
  end

(* The page's end: a helper's file closed and its program started *)
let body_end sc =
  let d = sc.sc_doc in
  if d.dc_type = "" then begin
    let rest = d.dc_head in
    d.dc_head <- "";
    body_start sc;
    body sc rest
  end;
  match List.assoc_opt d.dc_type helpers with
  | Some (prog, file) ->
    let what =
      if d.dc_file < 0 then "could not be kept in " ^ file
      else begin
        ignore (u_close d.dc_file);
        d.dc_file <- -1;
        if u_spawn ("/bin/" ^ prog) [ prog; file ] < 0 then
          "kept in " ^ file ^ ", but there is no " ^ prog ^ " to show it"
        else "kept in " ^ file ^ ", given to " ^ prog
      end in
    feed sc.sc_page ("<p>" ^ d.dc_type ^ ": " ^ what ^ ".</p>")
  | None -> ()

(* Asks for the page at [url] (a full address), which replaces the one
 * shown; its #fragment, if any, is shown when it comes. *)
let load sc url =
  if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire >= 0 then ignore (u_close sc.sc_nav.nv_wire);
  for i = 0 to pictures sc.sc_page - 1 do
    if (picture_of sc.sc_page i).pc_got >= 0 then put sc (d_free (image_of i))
  done;
  sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch <- -1;
  hover sc false;
  let address, id = fragment url in
  sc.sc_page <- create sc.sc_cols;
  sc.sc_nav.nv_address <- address;
  sc.sc_nav.nv_goal_id <- id;
  sc.sc_y <- 0;
  if sc.sc_doc.dc_file >= 0 then ignore (u_close sc.sc_doc.dc_file);
  sc.sc_doc.dc_got <- 0;
  sc.sc_doc.dc_head <- "";
  sc.sc_doc.dc_type <- "";
  sc.sc_doc.dc_status <- 0;
  sc.sc_doc.dc_file <- -1;
  sc.sc_state <- "reading";
  sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- url;
  draw_bar sc;
  draw_tools sc;
  redraw sc;
  (* the page asked of the wire's other end, on its port 70 *)
  sc.sc_nav.nv_wire <- u_dial "10.0.0.1" 70;
  if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire < 0 then begin
    sc.sc_state <- "www: no network (tiny-machine -net dir gives one)";
    finish sc.sc_page
  end
  else ignore (u_write sc.sc_nav.nv_wire (request url));
  draw_status sc

(* The pictures, once the page is all there: the next one asked of the
 * wire's other end, as "img w h address", the ones on the screen first,
 * then in the page's order. Its answer is a line "0 w h", then a row of
 * pixels a message, which go into the picture's image as they come. *)
let rec next_picture sc =
  let p = sc.sc_page in
  let pending id = (picture_of p id).pc_got = -1 in
  let rec on_screen = function
    | [] -> -1
    | (l : line) :: rest ->
        (match
           List.filter (fun (r : run) -> r.pic >= 0 && pending (r.pic / 256))
             l.runs
         with
         | r :: _ -> r.pic / 256
         | [] -> on_screen rest) in
  let rec first id =
    if id >= pictures p then -1 else if pending id then id else first (id + 1)
  in
  let id =
    match
      on_screen
        (lines_between p (sc.sc_y / 16) ((sc.sc_y + area sc + 15) / 16))
    with
    | -1 -> first 0
    | id -> id in
  if id >= 0 then begin
    let pc = picture_of p id in
    let fd = u_dial "10.0.0.1" 70 in
    if fd < 0 then begin pc.pc_got <- -2; next_picture sc end
    else begin
      pc.pc_got <- -3;
      let url = resolve sc.sc_nav.nv_address (base p) pc.pc_src in
      ignore (u_write fd ("img " ^ string_of_int pc.pc_w ^ " "
                          ^ string_of_int pc.pc_h ^ " " ^ url ^ "\r\n"));
      sc.sc_nav.nv_wire <- fd;
      sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch <- id
    end
  end;
  draw_status sc

(* A message of the picture being fetched: its first line, then its
 * rows. A row that comes is drawn at once if its slice is on the
 * screen, so a picture is painted as it arrives. *)
let picture_message sc s =
  let id = sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch in
  let pc = picture_of sc.sc_page id in
  if pc.pc_got = -3 then begin
    match String.split_on_char ' ' s with
    | [ _; w; h ] when number w = pc.pc_w && number h = pc.pc_h ->
        put sc (d_image (image_of id) 0 0 pc.pc_w pc.pc_h 255);
        pc.pc_got <- 0
    | _ -> pc.pc_got <- -2
  end
  else if pc.pc_got >= 0 && pc.pc_got < pc.pc_h then begin
    let y = pc.pc_got in
    put sc (d_pixels (image_of id) 0 y s);
    pc.pc_got <- y + 1;
    let slice = (id * 256) + (y / 16) and first = sc.sc_y / 16 in
    List.iteri (fun k (l : line) ->
      List.iter (fun (r : run) ->
        if r.pic = slice then begin
          let x = r.col * 8
          and sy = area_top + ((first + k) * 16) - sc.sc_y + (y mod 16) in
          if sy >= area_top && sy < area_top + area sc then
            put sc (d_draw 0 (image_of id) (-1) x sy (x + pc.pc_w) (sy + 1) 0 y)
        end) l.runs)
      (lines_between sc.sc_page first ((sc.sc_y + area sc + 15) / 16))
  end

(* Goes to an address, remembering where we were. A link to a place of
 * the page shown (#cite_note-2) only moves to it. *)
let go sc url =
  let address, id = fragment url in
  sc.sc_nav.nv_history <-
    (sc.sc_nav.nv_address, sc.sc_y) :: sc.sc_nav.nv_history;
  if address = sc.sc_nav.nv_address && id <> "" then begin
    (match anchor sc.sc_page id with
     | Some line -> show_from sc line
     | None -> ());
    sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- url;
    draw_tools sc;
    draw_status sc
  end
  else load sc url

(* Back to the page before, scrolled where it was: moved to if it is the
 * same page, asked for again if not. *)
let back sc =
  match sc.sc_nav.nv_history with
  | [] -> ()
  | (address, y) :: rest ->
      sc.sc_nav.nv_history <- rest;
      if address = sc.sc_nav.nv_address then begin
        let y = max 0 (min y (max_y sc)) in
        if y <> sc.sc_y then begin sc.sc_y <- y; redraw sc end;
        sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- address;
        draw_tools sc
      end
      else begin load sc address; sc.sc_nav.nv_goal <- y end

(* the link under the mouse, if any *)
let link_at sc x y =
  let col = x / 8 and line = (sc.sc_y + y - area_top) / 16 in
  if y < area_top || y >= area_top + area sc then None
  else
    match lines_between sc.sc_page line (line + 1) with
    | [ l ] ->
        (match
           List.filter (fun (r : run) ->
             r.link <> "" && col >= r.col
             && col < r.col + (String.length r.text
                               * if r.look land big <> 0 then 2 else 1))
             l.runs
         with
         | r :: _ -> Some r.link
         | [] -> None)
    | _ -> None

(* What a menu's item or a button does; false for Quit *)
let act sc a =
  (match a with
   | Back -> back sc
   | Top -> show_from sc 0
   | Reload -> load sc sc.sc_nav.nv_address
   | Quit -> ()
   | Address -> sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- ""; focus sc true; draw_tools sc
   | Search -> sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- "?"; focus sc true; draw_tools sc
   | Go_to t -> go sc (absolute t)
   | Go_typed ->
     if sc.sc_tools.tb_field = "" then
       sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- sc.sc_nav.nv_address
     else go sc (absolute sc.sc_tools.tb_field)
   | Typed t -> sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- t);
  a <> Quit

(* the toolbar as a TinyLibGUI program: its model the field's text, its
 * messages our actions (only its mouse and its keys are TinyLibGUI's) *)
let toolbar sc =
  { init = ""; view = (fun _ -> Label "");
    update = (fun a _ -> ignore (act sc a); sc.sc_tools.tb_field);
    key = (fun _ -> []) }

(* The mouse: the menus' first, then the toolbar's; over a link it is a
 * hand; the left button pressed on a link follows it; the wheel (the
 * buttons 8 and 16, Plan 9's) scrolls. A menu that closes uncovers
 * the toolbar and the page, drawn again. False for Quit. *)
let on_mouse sc x y buttons =
  let st = sc.sc_tools.tb_menu in
  let was = st.opened and item = st.item in
  let answer = menu_mouse (menus sc) st x y buttons in
  if was >= 0 && st.opened <> was then begin draw_tools sc; redraw sc end;
  if st.opened <> was || st.item <> item then draw_bar sc;
  match answer with
  | Picked a -> act sc a
  | Taken -> true
  | Ignored ->
      let (_, boxes) = laid_tools sc in
      let (field, m) =
        mouse (toolbar sc) boxes sc.sc_tools.tb_field sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse
          x y buttons in
      let changed =
        field <> sc.sc_tools.tb_field
        || over boxes m <> over boxes sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse in
      sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- field;
      sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse <- m;
      if changed then draw_tools sc;
      hover sc (link_at sc x y <> None);
      if buttons land 1 <> 0 && not sc.sc_nav.nv_pressed then
        (match link_at sc x y with
         | Some href ->
           go sc (resolve sc.sc_nav.nv_address (base sc.sc_page) href)
         | None -> ());
      sc.sc_nav.nv_pressed <- buttons land 1 <> 0;
      if buttons land 8 <> 0 then scroll_by sc (-48);
      if buttons land 16 <> 0 then scroll_by sc 48;
      true

(* What a key does; false for q, which quits. While the field has the
 * keys (a click in it, g, or s), they are TinyLibGUI's: its characters,
 * Backspace; Enter goes, Escape gives up. Otherwise the arrows are 128
 * to 131 (up, down, left, right): up and down scroll a line (the wheel
 * and the trackpad come as these: tiny-machine's window and page send
 * a step of the wheel as an arrow), left and right a screenful, as -
 * and space do. Backspace is 8 or 127. *)
let on_key sc k =
  if focused sc then begin
    (if k = 10 || k = 13 then begin
       focus sc false; ignore (act sc Go_typed)
     end
     else if k = 27 then begin
       focus sc false; sc.sc_tools.tb_field <- sc.sc_nav.nv_address
     end
     else
       sc.sc_tools.tb_field <-
         key (toolbar sc) (snd (laid_tools sc)) sc.sc_tools.tb_field
           sc.sc_tools.tb_mouse k);
    draw_tools sc;
    true
  end
  else begin
    let page = area sc - 16 in
    (if k = Char.code ' ' || k = 131 then glide sc page
     else if k = Char.code '-' || k = 130 then glide sc (- page)
     else if k = 129 then scroll_by sc 16
     else if k = 128 then scroll_by sc (-16)
     else if k = Char.code 'b' || k = 8 || k = 127 then back sc
     else if k = Char.code 'g' then ignore (act sc Address)
     else if k = Char.code 's' then ignore (act sc Search));
    k <> Char.code 'q'
  end

(* the end: the page's connection closed, the screen white *)
let quit sc =
  if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire >= 0 then ignore (u_close sc.sc_nav.nv_wire);
  hover sc false;
  for row = 0 to sc.sc_rows - 1 do fill_row sc row c_white done;
  send sc

let browse typed =
  let w, h = window_size () in
  let nav =
    { nv_address = ""; nv_wire = -1; nv_history = []; nv_goal = -1;
      nv_goal_id = ""; nv_pressed = false; nv_fetch = -1; nv_hover = false } in
  let sc =
    { sc_page = create (w / 8); sc_nav = nav;
      sc_tools = { tb_field = ""; tb_mouse = up; tb_menu = menu_closed () };
      sc_cols = w / 8; sc_rows = h / 16; sc_y = 0; sc_drawn = 0;
      sc_doc = { dc_got = 0; dc_head = ""; dc_type = ""; dc_status = 0;
                 dc_file = -1 };
      sc_state = "reading"; sc_msgs = [] } in
  put sc colours;
  put sc (d_image c_strip 0 0 (sc.sc_cols * 8) 16 255);
  load sc (absolute typed);
  send sc;
  let fds = Array.make 3 0 in
  (* [keys]: whether keys may still come. When they have ended and the
   * page is all there, the program ends and leaves the page on the
   * screen. *)
  let rec loop keys =
    if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire >= 0 || keys then begin
      let n = ref 0 in
      if keys then begin fds.(0) <- 0; fds.(1) <- 4; n := 2 end;
      if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire >= 0 then begin
        fds.(!n) <- sc.sc_nav.nv_wire; n := !n + 1
      end;
      let ready = u_ready fds !n 0 in
      if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire >= 0 && ready = sc.sc_nav.nv_wire
         && sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch >= 0 then begin
        let s = u_read sc.sc_nav.nv_wire 1024 in
        if s = "" then begin
          ignore (u_close sc.sc_nav.nv_wire);
          sc.sc_nav.nv_wire <- -1;
          let pc = picture_of sc.sc_page sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch in
          if pc.pc_got < 0 then pc.pc_got <- -2;
          sc.sc_nav.nv_fetch <- -1;
          next_picture sc
        end
        else picture_message sc s;
        send sc;
        loop keys
      end
      else if sc.sc_nav.nv_wire >= 0 && ready = sc.sc_nav.nv_wire then begin
        let s = u_read sc.sc_nav.nv_wire 1024 in
        if s = "" then begin
          body_end sc;
          finish sc.sc_page;
          ignore (u_close sc.sc_nav.nv_wire);
          sc.sc_nav.nv_wire <- -1;
          sc.sc_state <- "done";
          (* a page that sends us on (a search's result), not to itself *)
          let on =
            resolve sc.sc_nav.nv_address (base sc.sc_page)
              (refresh sc.sc_page) in
          if refresh sc.sc_page <> "" && on <> sc.sc_nav.nv_address then
            load sc on
          else begin
            show_new sc; draw_bar sc; draw_status sc;
            next_picture sc
          end
        end
        else begin
          let before = sc.sc_doc.dc_got / 16384 in
          sc.sc_doc.dc_got <- sc.sc_doc.dc_got + String.length s;
          take sc s;
          show_new sc;
          if sc.sc_doc.dc_got / 16384 <> before then draw_status sc
        end;
        send sc;
        loop keys
      end
      else if keys && ready = 4 then begin
        let s = u_read 4 12 in
        if String.length s = 12 && int16 s 8 >= 0
           && not (on_mouse sc (int16 s 0) (int16 s 4) (int16 s 8)) then quit sc
        else begin send sc; loop keys end
      end
      else if keys && ready = 0 then begin
        let typed = u_read 0 16 in
        if typed = "" then loop false
        else begin
          let rec each i =
            i >= String.length typed
            || (on_key sc (Char.code typed.[i]) && each (i + 1)) in
          if each 0 then begin send sc; loop keys end else quit sc
        end
      end
      else loop keys
    end in
  loop true
tiny/TinyBrowser.mli
6540
(* A tiny web browser, called www, that runs on tiny-kernel. The
 * full-size browser in ix lives in browsers/ (mini-netscape and
 * mini-lynx, built on the mini-chrome engine); this one keeps only the
 * essentials. The design is in docs/plans/done/plan_tiny_browser.md.
 *
 * The program has two parts. The reading turns the bytes of a page, as
 * they arrive, into the lines shown on the screen; it is most of what
 * follows, and the modules of TinyBrowser/. The browser around it, www,
 * this file, asks the wire's other end (TinyMachinePeer, which speaks
 * HTTPS for it) for the page in HTTP (TinyBrowserHttp) and then its
 * pictures, draws the lines as they come (TinyBrowserScreen, with
 * TinyLibGUI's menus and an address field), and follows links
 * (TinyBrowserAddress finds where they go).
 *
 * The main idea: {b a page is read only once, as it arrives, and turned
 * directly into lines}. There is no document tree and no style sheet.
 * Instead, the meaning of each tag is a row in a table that says
 * whether it starts a block, whether it is bold, monospace or hidden,
 * and how much it indents a list. What we keep of a page is exactly
 * what gets drawn: a list of lines, where each line is a few runs of
 * text, and each run has a column, a look (bold, etc.) and an optional
 * link.
 *
 *     messages ──► tokens ──► open tags ──► words ──► lines
 *     (raw bytes   (a tag and  (a stack giving  (wrapped    (each line a
 *      of the page, its attri-  the current     at the      list of runs,
 *      cut          butes, or   look, link and   screen      each run a text
 *      anywhere)    some text)  indentation)     width)      at a column)
 *                                                  │
 *                                          inside a table: the cells'
 *                                          words are kept and laid out
 *                                          at </table>
 *
 *     (the tokens: TinyBrowserTokens; the open tags: TinyBrowserHtml;
 *     the words, the lines and the tables: TinyBrowserLines; and
 *     TinyBrowserText under them all, the entities and UTF-8 to ASCII)
 *
 * A message can end anywhere, even in the middle of a tag, of an
 * entity like &amp;, or of a multi-byte UTF-8 character. The reader
 * keeps the unfinished end and re-reads it together with the next
 * message. This way the resulting lines are the same no matter how the
 * page was split (the tests check this by feeding a page one byte at a
 * time).
 *
 * Tables are the one place where we cannot produce a line right away,
 * because a column must be as wide as its widest cell, which we only
 * know at the end of the table. So the words of each cell are kept
 * until </table>. Then each column gets a width: at least its longest
 * word, its whole text if there is room, and otherwise a share of the
 * remaining room proportional to what it would need. Finally the rows
 * are laid out side by side.
 *
 * Characters: the machine's font has only 128 characters, so UTF-8 and
 * HTML entities are converted to ASCII here. A dash becomes -, a curly
 * quote becomes a straight one, an accented letter loses its accent,
 * and anything else becomes ?.
 *
 * What is ours, against the twins: mini-netscape reads a page into a
 * tree (html's Dom), styles it by its style sheets, lays out boxes and
 * runs its scripts; even mini-lynx, the text one, builds that tree
 * first and walks it (Line_mode's render). Here the tree is never
 * made: a page costs what its lines cost, and a page cut anywhere
 * reads the same. Dropped with it: style sheets (but a display:none,
 * hidden), scripts, forms, a page's colours and fonts, anything but
 * ASCII.
 *
 * others:
 * Plan 9's mothra (principia's browsers/mothra/) reads a page the same
 * way: a table of the tags (html.syntax.c), a stack of looks pushed at
 * a tag and popped at its end, and each word given at once to
 * libpanel's rich text (rdhtml.c's plrtstr), with no tree. Its tables
 * are rows of cells one after the other, not columns. abaco, which
 * came after it, reads a page with libhtml's parsehtml into a list of
 * items, a table one of them, sized as a whole (abaco's html.c).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Mosaic (1993) displayed a page progressively as it came over the
 * modem, and this browser works the same way: there are no style sheets
 * (CSS arrived in 1996), and the browser alone decides how each tag
 * looks. The name www comes from the command of CERN's line-mode
 * browser (1991), which wrapped pages to a terminal's 80 columns, just
 * as this one does on an 80-column screen of 8x16 characters.
 *
 * References:
 *  - docs/plans/done/plan_tiny_browser.md: the reasons for each choice, and
 *    what Wikipedia actually sends
 *  - browsers/README.md: the full-size browser this one is a tiny
 *    version of
 *  - the "tokenization" chapter of the HTML standard: everything a
 *    tokenizer must accept; we handle only the part that well-formed
 *    pages use
 *)

(* The program www: the page at [address] asked of the wire's other end
 * (HTTP's request "GET address HTTP/1.0" on port 70, TinyBrowserHttp:
 * TinyMachinePeer.www_address says what an address can be), and drawn
 * as it arrives on the screen, or in the window, the program's
 * descriptor 3. The answer's head says what its body is (Content-Type):
 * HTML is read, a text shown as it is (text/plain, in a <pre>), and a
 * WAV file or a PDF is kept in the current directory (www.wav, www.pdf)
 * and given to a program that shows it, started beside www and not
 * waited for, as Mosaic's helpers were: /bin/play, /bin/page (none on
 * tiny-kernel yet; the native tiny-www's: tiny-play or mini-play,
 * mini-page). Any other type is said not shown; a status other than 200
 * is said in the last row. At the top, TinyLibGUI's
 * menus (the page: back, top, reload, quit; a search, a few articles
 * to go to; the pages seen before) and a toolbar: Back, the address in
 * a field (a click in it, or g, gives it the keys; Enter goes there),
 * Go. s gives the field a ?: what is typed after it is searched for
 * (TinyBrowserAddress.absolute). A page whose <meta> refresh sends us
 * on at once, as a search's results do, is followed when it is all
 * there.
 * Space and - show the next and the previous screenful, the arrows a
 * line; q quits and clears. When
 * the keys end (a recorded session's) and the page is all there, the
 * program ends and leaves the page on the screen. *)
val browse : string -> unit
tiny/TinyBuildSystem.ml
22935
(* Claude Code
