let usage = "usage: tiny-c [-ir] [-o out.tm] file.c"

(* -h: how, by examples, each one as it runs *)
let help = usage ^ {|

A tiny C compiler: a C file to TinyCPU's assembly, for tiny-cpu, with its own
libc; -ir prints its stack machine's code instead. A fact.c that includes
tiny/TinyCRuntime/libc.h and prints fact(10):
  L=tiny/TinyCRuntime; (cd $L && tiny-c -o libc.tm libc.c)
  tiny-c -o fact.tm fact.c
  for f in $L/start $L/udivmod $L/libc fact
  do tiny-assembler -o $f.o $f.tm; done
  tiny-linker -o fact $L/start.o $L/udivmod.o $L/libc.o fact.o
  tiny-cpu fact                            fact 10 = 3628800
  tiny-c -ir fact.c                        fact: param 0, load 4, imm 0, ...
An error names the file and the line: fact.c: line 3: expected ;
|}

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The file: globals and functions *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* -ir: the stack machine's code instead of the machine's *)
let ir_only = ref false

let asm_name storage name = if storage = Static then name ^ "<>" else name

(* a global's init_data, as DATA at offsets *)
let rec init_data name t off =
  match t, peek () with
  | Arr (e, _), P "{" ->
      ignore (next ());
      (* the elements, counted *)
      let rec elems i =
        if accept "}" then i
        else
          (ignore (init_data name e (off + (i * size e)));
           ignore (accept ",");
           elems (i + 1)) in
      elems 0
  | Arr (Int (1, _), n), Str s ->
      ignore (next ());
      String.iteri (fun i c ->
        datum name (off + i) (Value (1, Int64.of_int (Char.code c)))) s;
      max n (String.length s + 1)
  | _ ->
      let e = rv (assign_expr ()) in
      (match e.d, e.t with
       | Const v, _ -> datum name off (Value (size t, v))
       | Addr (Global s), _ -> datum name off (Address s)
       | _ -> error (name ^ ": not a constant init_data"));
      1

let external_decl () =
  let storage, bt = base_type () in
  let rec go () =
    let name, t, pnames = declarator3 bt in
    if storage <> Typedef then no_vlong t;
    match t with
    | Func (rt, ps, _) when storage <> Typedef && peek () = P "{" ->
        (* a definition *)
        Hashtbl.replace globals name
          { vty = t; where = Global (asm_name storage name) };
        ignore (next ());
        let params = List.combine pnames ps in
        scopes := [ Hashtbl.create 8 ];
        List.iteri (fun i (p, pt) ->
          Hashtbl.replace (List.hd !scopes) p
            { vty = pt; where = Param (8 * i) }) params;
        frame := 0;
        result := rt;
        let body = block () in
        code := [];
        lower { brk = None; cont = None; cases = ref [] } body;
        if !ir_only then
          (Buffer.add_string out (name ^ ":\n");
           List.iter (fun i -> Buffer.add_string out ("\t" ^ show i ^ "\n"))
             (List.rev !code))
        else machine (asm_name storage name) (round !frame 8) (List.rev !code);
        scopes := []
    | _ ->
        let sym = asm_name storage name in
        (match storage, t with
         | Typedef, _ -> Hashtbl.replace typedefs name t
         | _, Func _ ->
             Hashtbl.replace globals name { vty = t; where = Global sym }
         | _ ->
             let t =
               if accept "=" then
                 (match t with
                  | Arr (e, 0) -> let n = init_data sym t 0 in Arr (e, n)
                  | _ -> ignore (init_data sym t 0); t)
               else t in
             Hashtbl.replace globals name { vty = t; where = Global sym };
             if storage <> Extern then globl sym (size t));
        if accept "," then go () else expect ";"
  in
  if not (accept ";") then go ()

(* a file that cannot be read or made, said apart from an error in one *)
exception File_error of string

let main
    (caps : < Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >)
    =
  let output = ref "" and file = ref "" in
  let rec args l = match l with
    | "-ir" :: r -> ir_only := true; args r
    | "-o" :: o :: r -> output := o; args r
    | f :: r -> file := f; args r
    | [] -> ()
  in
  let argl = List.tl (TinyLibSystem.argv caps) in
  if List.mem "-h" argl || List.mem "--help" argl then
    (TinyLibSystem.print caps help; 0)
  else begin
    args argl;
    if !file = "" then (TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (usage ^ "   (-h: how)\n"); 2)
    else begin
      unit_name := Filename.remove_extension (Filename.basename !file);
      (* intptr, Plan 9's uintptr's signed twin: an integer as wide as a
       * pointer (TinyMLRuntime/'s values, a word each) *)
      Hashtbl.replace typedefs "intptr" int_t;
      let read f =
        try TinyLibSystem.read_file caps f
        with Failure m -> raise (File_error m) in
      try
        let ts = tokens (Hashtbl.create 16) read !file in
        toks := Array.of_list (List.map fst ts);
        locs := Array.of_list (List.map snd ts);
        while peek () <> EOF do external_decl () done;
        let text =
          Buffer.contents out
          ^ (if !ir_only then "" else "\t.data\n" ^ Buffer.contents data)
        in
        if !output = "" then TinyLibSystem.print caps text
        else begin
          let fd =
            try TinyLibSystem.open_out caps !output
            with Failure m -> raise (File_error m) in
          TinyLibSystem.write fd text; TinyLibSystem.close fd
        end;
        0
      with
      | Failure m ->
          (* where: the last token read (a missing ; is then on its line, not
           * the next one's), in its file (an #include's); the lexer's errors
           * have none *)
          let ls = !locs in
          if Array.length ls = 0 then
            TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (!file ^ ": " ^ m ^ "\n")
          else
            (let f, l = ls.(max 0 (min (!pos - 1) (Array.length ls - 1))) in
             TinyLibSystem.eprint caps
               (f ^ ": line " ^ string_of_int l ^ ": " ^ m ^ "\n"));
          1
      | File_error m ->
          TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "tiny-c: %s\n" m); 1
    end
  end

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-c" main
tiny/TinyC.mli
10359
(* A tiny C compiler for tiny-machine, in one file, that goes through an
 * intermediate language of its own.
 *
 * The full-size compiler in ix, mini-cc (languages/c/), is a faithful
 * byte-for-byte twin of Plan 9's 5c and 7c: it has their front end,
 * their trees, their code generator, and a record per machine. This
 * file is what is left when the code only needs to be correct. (Its
 * usage, with examples, is in [help] below, which is what tiny-c -h
 * prints.) It reads one C file and writes its assembly for TinyCPU
 * (TinyMachineCPU.ml), whose words are 4 bytes: pointers too, and long
 * long is refused. Its runtime is in TinyCRuntime/ (built by
 * TinyKernel/steps/Makefile): start.tm holds the program start and
 * the system calls, udivmod.tm the unsigned division, and the rest of
 * libc is C compiled by tiny-c. Plan 9's names (print, exits), ANSI's
 * rules: the tests compare it with the host's cc (TinyC_tests/host.h).
 *
 * A file goes through these steps, each with its own type:
 *
 *     file.c
 *        | tokens     with #includes inlined and #defines expanded
 *        | the parser recursive descent producing typed trees, [expr]
 *        |            and [stmt], with conversions made explicit
 *        | lower      turns a function's tree into stack machine
 *        |            code, an [ir] list (what -ir prints)
 *        | machine    turns that list into assembly, keeping the
 *        |            stack depth d in register rd
 *     file.tm, for tiny-cpu
 *
 * Here is one function, int f(int a, int b) { return a + b * 2; }, as
 * printed by -ir and by the back end:
 *
 *     the stack machine   its stack, after   TinyCPU
 *                                            f:  addi sp, sp, -8
 *                                                stw  lr, 0(sp)
 *     param 0             &a                 addi r1, sp, 8
 *     load 4              a                  ldw  r1, 0(r1)
 *     param 8             a &b               addi r2, sp, 12
 *     load 4              a b                ldw  r2, 0(r2)
 *     imm 2               a b 2              li   r3, 2
 *     op * 4              a b*2              mul  r2, r2, r3
 *     op + 4              a+b*2              add  r1, r1, r2
 *     ret value                              mov  r13, r1
 *                                            ldw  lr, 0(sp); addi sp, sp, 8; ret
 *
 * Every argument arrives in memory, above the frame, and the result
 * goes in r13. A variable is accessed by pushing its address and then
 * loading it; a register is already an int, so only a char or a short
 * is extended. The cost is visible too: nine instructions, where an
 * optimizing compiler with both arguments in registers would need only
 * one, an add with a shifted second operand.
 *
 * What makes it small while still being a C compiler:
 *
 * - {b A stack machine in between} (IR, below): expressions become
 *   pushes and operations on a stack, and statements become labels
 *   and jumps; [-ir] prints it. The compiler plan left open the
 *   question of what an intermediate language buys compared to
 *   emitting machine instructions directly. Here is the answer: the
 *   front end knows nothing about registers or instructions, the back
 *   end knows nothing about C (its 100 lines are the whole machine),
 *   each can be read and tested on its own, and another machine is
 *   just another back end (there was arm64's, 7c's convention, until
 *   plan_tiny_self_hosting.md). The price is code quality: no
 *   Sethi-Ullman ordering, no addressing modes, and a load or store
 *   for every variable reference.
 * - {b The stack is in registers.} The back end keeps the stack
 *   machine's stack in r1..r12 (depth d in rd), so a push is a li or
 *   an addi and an operation is one instruction on two registers, as
 *   in Wirth's compilers. Only a call needs to save the live values
 *   below its arguments, into the frame. An expression deeper than 12
 *   is refused.
 * - {b Types at parse time, trees as variants.} Each expression is
 *   built already typed, with its conversions made explicit (a Conv
 *   node, scaled pointer arithmetic). Statements are a tree too
 *   ([stmt]), which [lower] turns into stack machine code, so parsing,
 *   lowering and code generation are three separate walks, each over
 *   its own type. The operators are variants, split so that every
 *   match is exhaustive; [&&], [||] and [!] are expressed with [?:],
 *   and [while] with [for].
 * - {b Its own calling convention}, simpler than 7c's: every argument
 *   in memory, 4 bytes each, from 0(sp) of the caller (so a variadic
 *   function, print, walks them from its last named one's address),
 *   the result in r13, every register but sp the callee's.
 *
 * The language supported: char, short, int, long (4 bytes, as in
 * Plan 9), signed and unsigned; pointers, arrays, structs (members,
 * . and ->, but not passed by value); enums; void;
 * globals with initializers (numbers, strings, addresses, and arrays
 * of them); static, extern, typedef; functions and prototypes, and
 * calls to variadic functions; function pointers (C's inside-out
 * declarators, and calls through any expression, as needed by t6's
 * system call table); every operator, including op=, ++,
 * --, ?:, casts, sizeof and the comma, with constant expressions
 * folded (for an array size or a case); if, while, do, for, switch,
 * break, continue, return and blocks; #include "file" and #define of a
 * name. Left out, because of what each would cost here: floats,
 * unions, bitfields, structs by value, goto, macros with arguments,
 * and #if.
 *
 * Exercises, each cheap because the stack machine sits between the
 * front end and the machine:
 * - a second back end: arm32 (with 5c's calling convention, for mini-5i
 *   and the Pi1), or x86-64; TinyCPU's took 100 lines;
 * - running the stack machine: a 60-line interpreter of its code would
 *   give a second semantics against which to compare the back end;
 * - peephole passes on the stack machine code, each a match on a list
 *   (McKeeman's idea): folding an operation on two constants,
 *   following a jump to a jump, removing a load right after a store
 *   to the same place;
 * - Sethi and Ullman's ordering: evaluating the deeper operand of an
 *   operation first keeps the stack shallower (useful with only 12
 *   registers);
 * - long long, as a value in a pair of registers; floats, as a
 *   second register class on the same stack (started once, then
 *   abandoned).
 *
 * Status: tiny-assembler reads what it writes. It
 * compiles TinyML's runtime (whose collector and primitives are in
 * C), TinyKernel's programs, and t6, a kernel in C, together with its
 * own programs. TinyML's code generator reuses this file's stack
 * machine and register stack for another language. Its twin, mini-cc,
 * has what this one leaves out: 7c's trees rewritten using Sethi and
 * Ullman's numbers, addressing modes, a register allocator, a peephole
 * pass, and an object file format.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * C was created by Dennis Ritchie (Bell Labs, 1972), out of Ken
 * Thompson's B (1969), which was itself Martin Richards's BCPL (1967)
 * cut down to fit a small machine. B and BCPL had a single type, the
 * machine word; C got its types when the PDP-11 brought bytes and
 * words of different sizes. BCPL's compiler already stopped at code
 * for an abstract stack machine, O-code, with a small back end for
 * each computer. That is how BCPL moved from machine to machine, and
 * it is the plan of this file. Steve Johnson's portable C compiler
 * (late 1970s) did the same for C using trees, and it took C and Unix
 * beyond the PDP-11.
 *
 * comeback:
 * Pascal's P-code (Zurich, 1970s; interpreted by the UCSD system) was
 * also stack machine code placed between a language and the machines.
 * Optimizing compilers abandoned it in favor of code with named
 * values, three addresses per operation, and then SSA (as in LLVM),
 * where the uses of a value are easy to find and change. Stack code
 * came back as the format that gets shipped: the Java virtual machine
 * (1995), then WebAssembly (2017), because it is compact and can be
 * checked in one pass.
 *
 * others:
 * Several small C compilers were written to be read. Small-C (Ron
 * Cain, Dr. Dobb's Journal, 1980) compiled a subset of C and was the
 * first one many people typed in. lcc (from Fraser and Hanson's book)
 * matches trees against a description of the machine. Fabrice
 * Bellard's tcc (grown out of his OTCC of 2001) goes in one pass from
 * text to machine code in memory, with no intermediate language at
 * all. Rui Ueyama's chibicc (2019) builds a tree and then emits code
 * that pushes and pops the real stack, and it is written as a history
 * of small commits. chibicc is the closest to this file: its stack is
 * the machine's, while ours is in registers.
 *
 * modern:
 * A production compiler does not keep the values of an expression in
 * a fixed stack of registers. It gives every value a name, computes
 * where each one is live, and puts values that are never live at the
 * same time in the same register (graph coloring: Gregory Chaitin,
 * 1982; or linear scan). A variable then stays in a register for a
 * whole loop, whereas here it is loaded and stored at each use.
 *
 * References:
 *  - Niklaus Wirth, Compiler Construction (1996): registers used as a
 *    stack of the expression's values, and one-pass recursive descent
 *  - Ken Thompson, "Plan 9 C Compilers" (1990): the dialect, its
 *    names and its libc
 *  - Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language (1988),
 *    appendix A: the grammar followed here
 *  - R. Sethi and J. D. Ullman, "The Generation of Optimal Code for
 *    Arithmetic Expressions" (JACM, 1970)
 *  - W. M. McKeeman, "Peephole Optimization" (CACM, 1965)
 *  - C. Fraser and D. Hanson, A Retargetable C Compiler: Design and
 *    Implementation (1995): lcc, a C compiler whose machines are its
 *    back ends
 *)

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyCPU.mli *)

let usage = "usage: tiny-cpu [-l | -prof file] image [args...]"

(* -h: how, by examples, each one as it runs *)
let help = usage ^ {|
A CPU of our own (TinyMachineCPU), an image run as a program, three system
calls the host's (r1-r3 the arguments, r1 the answer): sys 0, exit r1; sys 1,
write r3 bytes at r2 to r1 (1, 2); sys 2, read up to r3 bytes to r2. The image
is tiny-linker's (the memory's first bytes: the CPU starts at 0). In
tiny/tests/TinyCPU_tests/, for example:
  tiny-assembler hello.tm && tiny-linker -o hello hello.o
  tiny-cpu hello                the image run: Hello, world
  echo hello | tiny-cpu upper                      HELLO
  tiny-cpu -l hello             the listing: 0:  11100001  addi r1, r0, 1 ...
  tiny-cpu -prof p hello        run, and each instruction counted by its
                                address into p, for tiny-prof
|}

type caps = < Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

exception Exit of int
exception Usage

let syscall (caps : < caps; .. >) (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) n =
  let r = m.r and addr = TinyMachineCPU.addr in
  match n with
  | 0 -> raise (Exit (r.(1) land 0xff))
  | 1 ->
      let s = String.init r.(3) (fun i -> Bytes.get m.mem (addr (r.(2) + i))) in
      if r.(1) = 2 then Console.eprint caps s
      else (Console.print caps s; flush stdout);
      r.(1) <- r.(3)
  | 2 ->
      let (_ : < Cap.stdin; .. >) = caps in
      let b = Bytes.create r.(3) in
      let k = try input stdin b 0 r.(3) with Sys_error _ -> 0 in
      Bytes.iteri
        (fun i c -> if i < k then Bytes.set m.mem (addr (r.(2) + i)) c) b;
      r.(1) <- k
  | n -> TinyMachineCPU.error "unknown system call %d" n

(* [prof]: a profile counted meanwhile (-prof), the program's alone *)
let interpret caps prof image args =
  let env = TinyMachineCPU.plain ~sys:(syscall caps) in
  let env =
    match prof with
    | Some p -> TinyMachineCPU.profiled env p (fun _ -> 0, 0)
    | None -> env
  in
  let m : TinyMachineCPU.machine = TinyMachineCPU.boot image in
  (* the strings from the top down, then argv's array and nil, argv,
   * and argc at sp *)
  let top, addrs = List.fold_left (fun (top, addrs) a ->
    let top = top - String.length a - 1 in
    Bytes.blit_string (a ^ "\000") 0 m.mem top (String.length a + 1);
    top, top :: addrs) (!TinyMachineCPU.memsize, []) args in
  let n = List.length args in
  let sp = (top - (4 * (n + 3))) land lnot 7 in
  let put a v = TinyMachineCPU.store m TinyMachineISA.W a v in
  put sp n;
  put (sp + 4) (sp + 8);
  List.iteri (fun k s -> put (sp + 8 + (4 * k)) s) (List.rev addrs);
  put (sp + 8 + (4 * n)) 0;
  m.r.(TinyMachineISA.sp) <- sp;
  try while true do TinyMachineCPU.step env m done; 0 with Exit n -> n

let main (caps : < caps; Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) =
  let args = List.tl (Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps)) in
  let image f = TinyMachineCPU.image f (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f)) in
  try
    match args with
    | ("-h" | "--help") :: _ -> Console.print caps help; 0
    | [ "-l"; f ] ->
        Console.print caps
          (TinyMachineCPU.listing ~show:(fun _ -> None) ~origin:0 (image f));
        0
    | "-prof" :: out :: f :: rest ->
        let p = TinyMachineCPU.profile () in
        let status = interpret caps (Some p) (image f) (f :: rest) in
        FS.write caps (Fpath.v out) (TinyMachineCPU.profile_lines p);
        status
    | f :: rest when f.[0] <> '-' -> interpret caps None (image f) (f :: rest)
    | _ -> raise Usage
  with
  | Usage -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "   (-h: how)\n"); 2
  | TinyMachineISA.Error e | Sys_error e ->
      Console.eprint caps ("tiny-cpu: " ^ e ^ "\n"); 1

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> CapStdlib.exit caps (main caps))
tiny/TinyCPU.mli
3232
(* tiny-cpu runs the CPU alone, the way a user program runs: its
 * memory is plain memory, and a system call is handled by the host,
 * which provides three of them. Those calls, the usage and some
 * examples are in [help], which is what tiny-cpu -h prints.
 *
 * The CPU itself is not in this file; this file is only its command
 * line. The instruction set, the interpreter and their invariants are
 * in TinyMachine/TinyMachineCPU.ml, the file to read
 * first (its .mli describes the design). They live there because
 * TinyMachine.ml runs the same CPU with devices and a kernel, where a
 * system call is a trap.
 *
 * The image is tiny-linker's: the objects one after the other, their
 * labels one namespace, the first at address 0, where the CPU starts.
 * The arguments are put where the main of a C program expects them
 * (the convention of tiny-c, in TinyCRuntime/start.tm): the strings go
 * at the top of memory, and sp points to argc, followed by argv.
 * argv[0] is the name of the image.
 *
 *     2^20, the top       the argument strings, each followed by a 0
 *     sp + 8              argv[0] ... argv[n-1], their addresses, a 0
 *     sp + 4              argv: sp + 8
 *     sp, 8-aligned       argc: n
 *       ...               the stack, growing down
 *       ...               whatever the program does with the rest
 *     0                   the image: the first word of the first
 *                         object, where the pc starts
 *
 * There is no header, no segments and no loader: the image is simply
 * the first bytes of memory. The questions that an executable header
 * answers (where to load it, where to start, how much to zero) are
 * answered here by three constants: at 0, from 0, and everything.
 * mini-5i (machine/), the same program built around an ARM, has to
 * read an ELF header to get the same three answers, because that is
 * what the Linux kernel does.
 *
 * mini-5i follows Plan 9's 5i (principia's machine/5i), which is also
 * a debugger, with db's commands (:b, :c, :s, cmd.c), and a profiler
 * ($ip: every instruction counted by its address, then summed by
 * function, stats.c's iprofile). Here the two are programs of their
 * own: tiny-cpu writes the counts (-prof) for tiny-prof, and the
 * debugger is tiny-kernel's debug (TinyDebugger), not the emulator's.
 * mini-5i answers a whole system's calls, Linux's or Plan 9's; tiny-cpu
 * three, what start.tm needs.
 *
 * Status: this is the first step for running a program on this
 * machine. Programs compiled by tiny-c run here with its libc (the
 * three calls made by start.tm are the three calls provided here).
 * The same assembly, linked after a kernel, runs on TinyMachine, where
 * sys traps to that kernel instead of to OCaml. *)

(* an image's bytes, loaded and run with its arguments, its system
 * calls done here: to its exit status. With a profile, each instruction
 * run is counted into it (-prof). *)
val interpret :
  < Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. > ->
  TinyMachineCPU.profile option -> string -> string list -> int

(* the program: its arguments (-h: how) to its exit status *)
val main :
  < Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    .. > ->
  int
tiny/TinyCRuntime/libc.c

// Claude Code, Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau, LGPL (see TinyC.ml)
//
// The libc of tiny-c's programs, compiled by tiny-c: the part
// of Plan 9's that libc.h declares, in the C TinyC takes.
// print's verbs: %d %u %x %s %c %%, with l (ignored: a long is an int
// here); no widths, no long long (TinyCPU is 32 bits). %u is a verb,
// as in goken's libc (built without PLAN9PORT, its fmt.c) and the
// host's printf, the tests' reference: %ud is the number, then a d. A
// variadic function walks its arguments from its last named one: they
// are in memory, 4 bytes each (start.tm).

typedef unsigned long ulong;

extern int write(int, char*, int);

// fmt with the arguments at ap, into out; its length
static int
format(char *out, char *fmt, int *ap)
{
	char *o, *s, tmp[12];
	int n;
	unsigned v, base;

	o = out;
	for(; *fmt; fmt++){
		if(*fmt != '%'){
			*o++ = *fmt;
			continue;
		}
		fmt++;
		while(*fmt == 'l')
			fmt++;
		switch(*fmt){
		case 'd':
		case 'u':
		case 'x':
			v = *ap++;
			base = 10;
			if(*fmt == 'x')
				base = 16;
			if(*fmt == 'd' && (int)v < 0){
				*o++ = '-';
				v = -v;
			}
			n = 0;
			do {
				tmp[n++] = "0123456789abcdef"[v % base];
				v = v / base;
			} while(v);
			while(n > 0)
				*o++ = tmp[--n];
			break;
		case 's':
			s = (char*)*ap++;
			if(s == 0)
				s = "<nil>";
			while(*s)
				*o++ = *s++;
			break;
		case 'c':
			*o++ = *ap++;
			break;
		default:
			*o++ = *fmt;
		}
	}
	*o = 0;
	return o - out;
}

int
print(char *fmt, ...)
{
	char buf[1024];
	int n, done, w;

	n = format(buf, fmt, (int*)&fmt + 1);
	// a write may be short (t6's pipes give what fits), so again with
	// the rest
	for(done = 0; done < n; done += w)
		if((w = write(1, buf + done, n - done)) <= 0)
			return -1;
	return n;
}

int
sprint(char *buf, char *fmt, ...)
{
	return format(buf, fmt, (int*)&fmt + 1);
}

long
strlen(char *s)
{
	char *p;

	for(p = s; *p; p++)
		;
	return p - s;
}

char*
strcpy(char *d, char *s)
{
	char *p;

	p = d;
	while(*p++ = *s++)
		;
	return d;
}

int
strcmp(char *a, char *b)
{
	for(; *a && *a == *b; a++, b++)
		;
	return (*a & 255) - (*b & 255);
}

void*
memset(void *p, int c, ulong n)
{
	char *q;

	for(q = p; n > 0; n--)
		*q++ = c;
	return p;
}

int
atoi(char *s)
{
	int n, neg;

	n = 0;
	neg = 0;
	while(*s == ' ')
		s++;
	if(*s == '-'){
		neg = 1;
		s++;
	}
	while(*s >= '0' && *s <= '9')
		n = n * 10 + *s++ - '0';
	if(neg)
		return -n;
	return n;
}

// the heap: a bump of an array, never given back
static char heap[65536];
static char *brk = heap;

void*
malloc(ulong n)
{
	char *p;

	p = brk;
	brk = brk + ((n + 7) & ~7);
	if(brk > heap + sizeof heap)
		return 0;
	return p;
}

void
free(void *p)
{
}

(* See TinyDatabase.mli *)

(* The test, tests/TinyDatabase_test.sh, runs pipelines through this
 * database and the equivalent SQL through SQLite (Python's sqlite3),
 * and compares the resulting rows. *)

open Common

exception Error of string

(* (old: a format, Printf.ksprintf's: tiny-ml reads a format only where
 * it is written, Printf.sprintf at the call) *)
let error s = raise (Error s)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Values *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type value = Int of int | Text of string
type typ = TInt | TText
type row = value array

let show = function Int n -> string_of_int n | Text s -> s
let type_of = function Int _ -> TInt | Text _ -> TText
let truth = function Int 0 -> false | Int _ | Text _ -> true
let of_bool b = Int (if b then 1 else 0)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The file: blobs appended, and a header that commits *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the header: a magic string and the offset of the committed catalog *)
let magic = "tinydb1\n"

type key = value list

(* children.(i) holds the keys below seps.(i) (and at or above
 * seps.(i - 1)); the last child the rest *)
type node = Leaf of (key * row) array | Inner of key array * int array

(* (a descriptor, TinyLibSystem's: a number on the host and on
 * tiny-kernel) *)
type file = { fd : int; cache : (int, node) Hashtbl.t }

let read_at f off len =
  TinyLibSystem.seek f.fd off;
  let rec go acc n =
    if n >= len then String.concat "" (List.rev acc)
    else
      match TinyLibSystem.read f.fd (len - n) with
      | "" -> error "truncated file"
      | s -> go (s :: acc) (n + String.length s)
  in
  go [] 0

let write_at f off s = TinyLibSystem.seek f.fd off; TinyLibSystem.write f.fd s

(* an int as 8 bytes, the most significant first; the bytes above the
 * int's own are its sign's (tiny-ml's int has 31 bits: a larger
 * number in a file OCaml wrote is read as its low bits there) *)
(* old: Bytes.set_int64_be and get_int64_be, Int64's, which tiny-ml has
 * not *)
let int_bytes n =
  let b = Bytes.make 8 '\000' in
  let rec go i n =
    if i >= 0 then (
      Bytes.set b i (Char.chr (n land 255));
      go (i - 1) (n asr 8))
  in
  go 7 n;
  Bytes.to_string b
let int_at s p =
  let rec go n i =
    if i = 8 then n else go ((n lsl 8) lor Char.code s.[p + i]) (i + 1)
  in
  go 0 0

(* a value at the end of the file: its length, then its bytes *)
let append f (s : string) =
  let off = TinyLibSystem.seek_end f.fd in
  TinyLibSystem.write f.fd (int_bytes (String.length s) ^ s);
  off

let load f off = read_at f (off + 8) (int_at (read_at f off 8) 0)

(* A value's bytes, written by hand: an int is 8 bytes, the most
 * significant first; a string, a list and an array their length then
 * what is in them; a constructor its number first. A reader is the
 * bytes and where it is in them. *)
(* old: Marshal.to_string v [] and Marshal.from_bytes: two calls for
 * these forty lines, and 376 lines of library under them *)
let put_int b n = Buffer.add_string b (int_bytes n)
let put_str b s = put_int b (String.length s); Buffer.add_string b s
let put_list put b l = put_int b (List.length l); List.iter (put b) l
let put_value b = function
  | Int n -> put_int b 0; put_int b n
  | Text s -> put_int b 1; put_str b s
let put_values b l = put_list put_value b l

let get_int (s, p) = let n = int_at s !p in p := !p + 8; n
let get_str (s, p) =
  let n = get_int (s, p) in
  let v = String.sub s !p n in
  p := !p + n;
  v
let get_list get r =
  let rec go n = if n = 0 then [] else let x = get r in x :: go (n - 1) in
  go (get_int r)
let get_value r =
  match get_int r with 0 -> Int (get_int r) | _ -> Text (get_str r)
let get_values r = get_list get_value r

let node_bytes (n : node) =
  let b = Buffer.create 256 in
  (match n with
   | Leaf a ->
       put_int b 0;
       put_list (fun b (k, r) -> put_values b k; put_values b (Array.to_list r))
         b (Array.to_list a)
   | Inner (ks, cs) ->
       put_int b 1;
       put_list put_values b (Array.to_list ks);
       put_list put_int b (Array.to_list cs));
  Buffer.contents b

let node_of_bytes s : node =
  let r = (s, ref 0) in
  match get_int r with
  | 0 ->
      Leaf (Array.of_list (get_list (fun r ->
        let k = get_values r in
        (k, Array.of_list (get_values r))) r))
  | _ ->
      let ks = get_list get_values r in
      Inner (Array.of_list ks, Array.of_list (get_list get_int r))

let node f off =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt f.cache off with
  | Some n -> n
  | None ->
      let n = node_of_bytes (load f off) in
      Hashtbl.replace f.cache off n;
      n

let write f (n : node) =
  let off = append f (node_bytes n) in
  Hashtbl.replace f.cache off n;
  off

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Copy-on-write B-trees *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let max_entries = 16

let empty_tree f = write f (Leaf (Array.of_list []))

(* the child for a key: the number of separators at or below it *)
let child seps k =
  let rec go i =
    if i < Array.length seps && seps.(i) <= k then go (i + 1) else i
  in
  go 0

(* the entries from [from] on, in key order, read as they are pulled *)
let rec scan f off (from : key option) : (key * row) Seq.t =
  match node f off with
  | Leaf es ->
      Seq.drop_while
        (fun (k, _) -> match from with Some lo -> k < lo | None -> false)
        (Array.to_seq es)
  | Inner (seps, kids) ->
      let start = match from with Some lo -> child seps lo | None -> 0 in
      Seq.concat_map
        (fun i -> scan f kids.(i) (if i = start then from else None))
        (Seq.init (Array.length kids - start) (( + ) start))

let find f off k =
  match scan f off (Some k) () with
  | Seq.Cons ((k', r), _) when k' = k -> Some r
  | _ -> None

let insert_at a i x =
  Array.concat
    [ Array.sub a 0 i; Array.make 1 x; Array.sub a i (Array.length a - i) ]

(* the new subtree: one node, or two and the separator between *)
type split = One of int | Two of int * key * int

(* the new subtree: one node, or two and the separator between *)
let rec ins f off k r =
  match node f off with
  | Leaf es ->
      let i =
        let rec go i =
          if i < Array.length es && fst es.(i) < k then go (i + 1) else i
        in
        go 0
      in
      if i < Array.length es && fst es.(i) = k then
        error ("duplicate key " ^ String.concat ", " (List.map show k));
      let es = insert_at es i (k, r) in
      if Array.length es <= max_entries then One (write f (Leaf es))
      else
        let m = Array.length es / 2 in
        Two (write f (Leaf (Array.sub es 0 m)), fst es.(m),
             write f (Leaf (Array.sub es m (Array.length es - m))))
  | Inner (seps, kids) -> (
      let i = child seps k in
      match ins f kids.(i) k r with
      | One c ->
          let kids = Array.copy kids in
          kids.(i) <- c;
          One (write f (Inner (seps, kids)))
      | Two (a, sep, b) ->
          let seps = insert_at seps i sep and kids = insert_at kids i a in
          kids.(i + 1) <- b;
          if Array.length kids <= max_entries then
            One (write f (Inner (seps, kids)))
          else
            (* the middle separator goes up; each half keeps its children *)
            let m = Array.length seps / 2 in
            Two (write f (Inner (Array.sub seps 0 m, Array.sub kids 0 (m + 1))),
                 seps.(m),
                 write f (Inner (Array.sub seps (m + 1)
                                   (Array.length seps - m - 1),
                                 Array.sub kids (m + 1)
                                   (Array.length kids - m - 1)))))

let insert f root k r =
  match ins f root k r with
  | One root -> root
  | Two (a, sep, b) -> write f (Inner (Array.make 1 sep, Array.of_list [ a; b ]))

(* no rebalancing: an underfull node, even an empty leaf, is still right *)
let rec delete f off k =
  match node f off with
  | Leaf es ->
      write f (Leaf (Array.of_list
        (List.filter (fun (k', _) -> k' <> k) (Array.to_list es))))
  | Inner (seps, kids) ->
      let i = child seps k and kids = Array.copy kids in
      kids.(i) <- delete f kids.(i) k;
      write f (Inner (seps, kids))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The catalog *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type table = {
  name : string;
  cols : (string * typ) list;
  key : int;                       (* the key column's position *)
  root : int;
  indexes : (string * int) list;   (* a column, its index's root *)
}

type db = { file : file; mutable tables : table list }

let tables_bytes (ts : table list) =
  let b = Buffer.create 256 in
  put_list (fun b (t : table) ->
    put_str b t.name;
    put_list (fun b (c, ty) ->
      put_str b c;
      put_int b (match ty with TInt -> 0 | TText -> 1)) b t.cols;
    put_int b t.key; put_int b t.root;
    put_list (fun b (c, root) -> put_str b c; put_int b root) b t.indexes) b ts;
  Buffer.contents b

let tables_of_bytes s : table list =
  get_list (fun r ->
    let name = get_str r in
    let cols =
      get_list (fun r ->
        let c = get_str r in
        (c, if get_int r = 0 then TInt else TText)) r
    in
    let key = get_int r in
    let root = get_int r in
    { name; cols; key; root;
      indexes = get_list (fun r -> let c = get_str r in (c, get_int r)) r })
    (s, ref 0)

let open_db (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) path =
  (* (made when it is not there) *)
  let fd =
    try TinyLibSystem.open_rw caps path
    with Failure m -> failwith (path ^ ": " ^ m)
  in
  let file = { fd; cache = Hashtbl.create 256 } in
  (* (an empty file is a new database; old: one under 16 bytes, so a
   * short file that was not one was written over) *)
  let size = TinyLibSystem.seek_end fd in
  if size = 0 then begin
    write_at file 0 (magic ^ String.make 8 '\000');
    { file; tables = [] }
  end
  else if size < 16 || read_at file 0 8 <> magic then
    failwith (path ^ ": not a tiny-db file")
  else
    let off = int_at (read_at file 8 8) 0 in
    { file; tables = (if off = 0 then [] else tables_of_bytes (load file off)) }

(* the statement's changes made durable: the new catalog, then the
 * header pointing at it *)
let commit db tables =
  write_at db.file 8 (int_bytes (append db.file (tables_bytes tables)));
  db.tables <- tables

let table db name =
  match List.find_opt (fun t -> t.name = name) db.tables with
  | Some t -> t
  | None -> error ("no table " ^ name)

let replace db (t : table) =
  List.map (fun t' -> if t'.name = t.name then t else t') db.tables

(* a table's columns; a column's place among columns *)
let names (t : table) = List.map fst t.cols
let col_pos cols c =
  let rec go i = function
    | x :: rest -> if x = c then i else go (i + 1) rest
    | [] -> error ("no column " ^ c)
  in
  go 0 cols

(* an index's entry has no row *)
let no_row : row = Array.of_list []

(* a row in, its key in its table and in each index *)
let add f (t : table) (r : row) =
  let k = r.(t.key) in
  { t with root = insert f t.root [ k ] r;
           indexes =
             List.map (fun (c, root) ->
               c, insert f root [ r.(col_pos (names t) c); k ] no_row)
               t.indexes }

let remove f (t : table) (r : row) =
  let k = r.(t.key) in
  { t with root = delete f t.root [ k ];
           indexes =
             List.map (fun (c, root) ->
               c, delete f root [ r.(col_pos (names t) c); k ]) t.indexes }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The language *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type token = Name of string | Num of int | Str of string | Sym of string

(* (old: 'a' .. 'z' in the patterns, which tiny-ml does not read) *)
let is_digit c = c >= '0' && c <= '9'
let is_letter c = (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || c = '_'

let tokens (s : string) : token list =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec go i acc =
    if i >= n || s.[i] = '#' then List.rev acc
    else match s.[i] with
      | ' ' | '\t' | '\r' -> go (i + 1) acc
      | c when is_letter c ->
          let j = ref i in
          while !j < n && (is_letter s.[!j] || is_digit s.[!j]) do incr j done;
          go !j (Name (String.sub s i (!j - i)) :: acc)
      | c when is_digit c ->
          let j = ref i in
          while !j < n && is_digit s.[!j] do incr j done;
          go !j (Num (int_of_string (String.sub s i (!j - i))) :: acc)
      | ('"' | '\'') as q ->
          let j =
            match String.index_from_opt s (i + 1) q with
            | Some j -> j
            | None -> error "unclosed string"
          in
          go (j + 1) (Str (String.sub s (i + 1) (j - i - 1)) :: acc)
      | '!' | '<' | '>' when i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] = '=' ->
          go (i + 2) (Sym (String.sub s i 2) :: acc)
      | c -> go (i + 1) (Sym (String.make 1 c) :: acc)
  in
  go 0 []

type binop = Add | Sub | Mul | Div | Eq | Ne | Lt | Le | Gt | Ge | And | Or

type expr =
  | Lit of value
  | Col of string
  | Bin of binop * expr * expr
  | Not of expr
  | Neg of expr

type agg = Count | Sum of string | Min of string | Max of string

type stage =
  | Where of expr
  | Select of (string * expr) list
  | Join of string
  | Group of string list * (string * agg) list
  | Sort of (string * bool) list      (* true: descending *)
  | Take of int

(* the statements; a query's last stage may be delete or set, on the
 * rows of its table the stages before it (where only) kept *)
type stmt =
  | Create of string * (string * typ * bool) list
  | Insert of string * value list list
  | Index of string * string
  | Query of bool * string * stage list          (* explain? *)
  | Delete of string * stage list
  | Update of string * stage list * (string * expr) list
  | Help

(* the operators, by precedence (old: written where they are used, an
 * expression too deep for tiny-machine's registers) *)
let additive = [ [ Sym "+", Add; Sym "-", Sub ]; [ Sym "*", Mul; Sym "/", Div ] ]
let comparisons = [ "=", Eq; "!=", Ne; "<", Lt; "<=", Le; ">", Gt; ">=", Ge ]

(* a parser over a token list, by recursive descent: the grammar is an
 * expression's precedence and a stage's few forms *)
let parse (ts : token list) : stmt =
  let ts = ref ts in
  let peek () = match !ts with t :: _ -> Some t | [] -> None in
  let next () =
    match !ts with t :: rest -> ts := rest; t | [] -> error "unexpected end"
  in
  let expect t = if next () <> t then error "syntax error" in
  let name () = match next () with Name n -> n | _ -> error "a name expected" in
  let accept t = if peek () = Some t then (ignore (next ()); true) else false in
  let rec list f =
    let x = f () in
    if accept (Sym ",") then x :: list f else [ x ]
  in
  let literal () = match next () with
    | Num n -> Int n
    | Str s -> Text s
    | Sym "-" ->
        (match next () with
         | Num n -> Int (- n)
         | _ -> error "a number expected")
    | _ -> error "a value expected" in
  let rec expr () = binary [ [ Name "or", Or ]; [ Name "and", And ] ] not_
  and binary levels last =
    match levels with
    | [] -> last ()
    | ops :: rest ->
        let rec loop l = match peek () with
          | Some t when List.mem_assoc t ops ->
              ignore (next ());
              loop (Bin (List.assoc t ops, l, binary rest last))
          | _ -> l in
        loop (binary rest last)
  and not_ () = if accept (Name "not") then Not (not_ ()) else comparison ()
  and comparison () =
    let l = binary additive atom in
    match peek () with
    | Some (Sym ("=" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" as op)) ->
        ignore (next ());
        Bin (List.assoc op comparisons, l, binary additive atom)
    | _ -> l
  and atom () = match next () with
    | Num n -> Lit (Int n)
    | Str s -> Lit (Text s)
    | Name c -> Col c
    | Sym "-" -> Neg (atom ())
    | Sym "(" -> let e = expr () in expect (Sym ")"); e
    | _ -> error "syntax error" in
  let item () =
    let n = name () in
    if accept (Sym "=") then n, expr () else n, Col n
  in
  let aggregate () =
    let n = name () in
    expect (Sym "=");
    n, (match name () with
        | "count" -> Count
        | "sum" -> Sum (name ())
        | "min" -> Min (name ())
        | "max" -> Max (name ())
        | a -> error ("no aggregate " ^ a)) in
  let rec stages () =
    if not (accept (Sym "|")) then []
    else match name () with
      | "where" -> let e = expr () in Where e :: stages ()
      | "select" -> let items = list item in Select items :: stages ()
      | "join" -> let t = name () in Join t :: stages ()
      | "group" ->
          let rec keys () =
            match peek () with
            | Some (Name n) -> ignore (next ()); n :: keys ()
            | _ -> []
          in
          let ks = keys () in
          expect (Sym "(");
          let aggs = list aggregate in
          expect (Sym ")");
          Group (ks, aggs) :: stages ()
      | "sort" ->
          let ks = list (fun () -> let n = name () in n, accept (Name "desc")) in
          Sort ks :: stages ()
      | "take" ->
          (match next () with
           | Num n -> Take n :: stages ()
           | _ -> error "take: a number expected")
      | "delete" -> [ Take (-1) ]     (* a marker, taken apart below *)
      | "set" ->
          let items = list item in
          [ Select ((" set", Lit (Int 0)) :: items) ]
      | s -> error ("no stage " ^ s) in
  let query explain =
    let t = name () in
    let ss = stages () in
    match List.rev ss with
    | Take (-1) :: rest -> Delete (t, List.rev rest)
    | Select ((" set", _) :: items) :: rest -> Update (t, List.rev rest, items)
    | _ -> Query (explain, t, ss) in
  let stmt = match !ts with
    | Name "table" :: _ ->
        ignore (next ());
        let t = name () in
        expect (Sym "(");
        let cols = list (fun () ->
          let c = name () in
          let typ =
            match name () with
            | "int" -> TInt
            | "text" -> TText
            | ty -> error ("no type " ^ ty)
          in
          c, typ, accept (Name "key")) in
        expect (Sym ")");
        Create (t, cols)
    | Name "insert" :: _ ->
        ignore (next ());
        let t = name () in
        Insert (t, list (fun () ->
          expect (Sym "(");
          let vs = list literal in
          expect (Sym ")");
          vs))
    | Name "index" :: _ -> ignore (next ()); let t = name () in Index (t, name ())
    | Name "explain" :: _ -> ignore (next ()); query true
    | [ Name "help" ] -> ignore (next ()); Help
    | _ -> query false in
  if !ts <> [] then error "syntax error";
  stmt

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Evaluation: the stages as iterators *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* an expression compiled against its columns *)
let rec compile (cols : string list) (e : expr) : row -> value =
  match e with
  | Lit v -> fun _ -> v
  | Col c -> let i = col_pos cols c in fun r -> r.(i)
  | Not e -> let f = compile cols e in fun r -> of_bool (not (truth (f r)))
  | Neg e ->
      let f = compile cols e in
      fun r ->
        (match f r with Int n -> Int (- n) | Text _ -> error "- of a text")
  | Bin (op, a, b) ->
      let fa = compile cols a and fb = compile cols b in
      fun r ->
        let x = fa r and y = fb r in
        match op, x, y with
        | And, _, _ -> of_bool (truth x && truth y)
        | Or, _, _ -> of_bool (truth x || truth y)
        | Eq, _, _ -> of_bool (x = y)
        | Ne, _, _ -> of_bool (x <> y)
        | Lt, _, _ -> of_bool (x < y)
        | Le, _, _ -> of_bool (x <= y)
        | Gt, _, _ -> of_bool (x > y)
        | Ge, _, _ -> of_bool (x >= y)
        | Add, Int m, Int n -> Int (m + n)
        | Sub, Int m, Int n -> Int (m - n)
        | Mul, Int m, Int n -> Int (m * n)
        | Div, Int _, Int 0 -> error "division by zero"
        | Div, Int m, Int n -> Int (m / n)
        | (Add | Sub | Mul | Div), _, _ -> error "arithmetic on a text"

(* the access path for a table and its first where: a range on the key
 * or on an index, from a conjunct column op literal; or a scan. The
 * where still filters every row, so a range only has to contain the
 * rows wanted: from the value for > >= =, up to it for < <= = *)
type access =
  | Scan
  | Range of string option * value * binop   (* an index's column, or the key *)

let rec conjuncts = function
  | Bin (And, a, b) -> conjuncts a @ conjuncts b
  | e -> [ e ]

let plan (t : table) (stages : stage list) =
  let key = fst (List.nth t.cols t.key) in
  let ranges op = List.mem op [ Eq; Lt; Le; Gt; Ge ] in
  let usable = function
    | Bin (op, Col c, Lit v) when ranges op -> Some (c, v, op)
    | Bin (op, Lit v, Col c) when ranges op ->
        Some (c, v,
              match op with Lt -> Gt | Le -> Ge | Gt -> Lt | Ge -> Le | o -> o)
    | _ -> None in
  match stages with
  | Where e :: _ -> (
      let cs = List.filter_map usable (conjuncts e) in
      match List.find_opt (fun (c, _, _) -> c = key) cs with
      | Some (_, v, op) -> Range (None, v, op)
      | None -> (
          match
            List.find_opt (fun (c, _, _) -> List.mem_assoc c t.indexes) cs
          with
          | Some (c, v, op) -> Range (Some c, v, op)
          | None -> Scan))
  | _ -> Scan

let show_access (t : table) = function
  | Scan -> "scan " ^ t.name
  | Range (c, v, op) ->
      Printf.sprintf "range %s.%s %s %s%s" t.name
        (match c with Some c -> c | None -> fst (List.nth t.cols t.key))
        (List.assoc op [ Eq, "="; Lt, "<"; Le, "<="; Gt, ">"; Ge, ">=" ])
        (show v) (if c = None then " (key)" else " (index)")

let rows db (t : table) (a : access) : row Seq.t =
  let f = db.file in
  let bounded v op (k : key) =
    match op, k with (Eq | Lt | Le), v' :: _ -> v' <= v | _ -> true
  in
  let from v op = match op with Eq | Gt | Ge -> Some [ v ] | _ -> None in
  match a with
  | Scan -> Seq.map snd (scan f t.root None)
  | Range (None, v, op) ->
      Seq.map snd (Seq.take_while (fun (k, _) -> bounded v op k)
                     (scan f t.root (from v op)))
  | Range (Some c, v, op) ->
      Seq.take_while (fun (k, _) -> bounded v op k)
        (scan f (List.assoc c t.indexes) (from v op))
      |> Seq.filter_map (fun (k, _) ->
           match k with [ _; pk ] -> find f t.root [ pk ] | _ -> None)

(* a stage: its output columns and rows, from its input's *)
let stage db (cols, (rs : row Seq.t)) = function
  | Where e ->
      let f = compile cols e in
      cols, Seq.filter (fun r -> truth (f r)) rs
  | Select items ->
      let fs = List.map (fun (_, e) -> compile cols e) items in
      List.map fst items,
      Seq.map (fun r -> Array.of_list (List.map (fun f -> f r) fs)) rs
  | Join name ->
      (* a hash join: the right table in a table by the shared columns *)
      let t = table db name in
      let shared = List.filter (fun c -> List.mem c cols) (names t) in
      let h = Hashtbl.create 64 in
      Seq.iter (fun r ->
        Hashtbl.add h (List.map (fun c -> r.(col_pos (names t) c)) shared) r)
        (rows db t Scan);
      let rest = List.filter (fun c -> not (List.mem c shared)) (names t) in
      cols @ rest,
      Seq.concat_map (fun l ->
        let k = List.map (fun c -> l.(col_pos cols c)) shared in
        List.to_seq (List.rev_map (fun r ->
            Array.append l
              (Array.of_list (List.map (fun c -> r.(col_pos (names t) c)) rest)))
          (Hashtbl.find_all h k))) rs
  | Group (keys, aggs) ->
      let key = List.map (fun k -> compile cols (Col k)) keys in
      let groups = Hashtbl.create 64 and order = ref [] in
      Seq.iter (fun r ->
        let k = List.map (fun f -> f r) key in
        if not (Hashtbl.mem groups k) then order := k :: !order;
        Hashtbl.replace groups k (r :: (Hashtbl.find_opt groups k ||| []))) rs;
      let fold (a : agg) (g : row list) =
        let col c = let f = compile cols (Col c) in List.map f g in
        let ints c =
          List.map (function Int n -> n | Text _ -> error "sum of a text")
            (col c)
        in
        match a with
        | Count -> Int (List.length g)
        | Sum c -> Int (List.fold_left ( + ) 0 (ints c))
        | Min c -> List.fold_left min (List.hd (col c)) (col c)
        | Max c -> List.fold_left max (List.hd (col c)) (col c) in
      keys @ List.map fst aggs,
      List.to_seq (List.rev_map (fun k ->
        let g = Hashtbl.find groups k in
        Array.of_list (k @ List.map (fun (_, a) -> fold a g) aggs)) !order)
  | Sort ks ->
      let fs = List.map (fun (c, desc) -> compile cols (Col c), desc) ks in
      let cmp a b =
        List.fold_left (fun acc (f, desc) ->
          if acc <> 0 then acc
          else (if desc then -1 else 1) * compare (f a) (f b)) 0 fs
      in
      cols, List.to_seq (List.stable_sort cmp (List.of_seq rs))
  | Take n -> cols, Seq.take n rs

let run_query db t stages =
  let a = plan t stages in
  a, List.fold_left (stage db) (names t, rows db t a) stages

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The statements *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let print (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) s = TinyLibSystem.print caps s

(* help: a database made and queried first, then the rest; the tables
 * after it *)
let help = {|A statement a line. A table, its rows, then queries:
  table books (id int key, title text, author text, year int)
  insert books (1, "SICP", "Abelson", 1985), (2, "TAOCP", "Knuth", 1968)
  books
  books | where year > 1980 | select title, year
A query is a table, then stages, each after a |:
  where year > 1980 and not author = "Knuth"   (= != < <= > >= + - * / or)
  select title, age = 2026 - year              the columns, computed ones too
  join authors                                 on the columns of the same name
  group author (n = count, last = max year)    (count, sum c, min c, max c)
  sort year desc, title
  take 10
  delete, or set year = year + 1               last, on the rows the wheres kept
Also:
  index books year        an index on a column, which where uses
  explain QUERY           how a query reads its table
  help                    this, and the tables
|}

(* delete, or set its items (old: a case of exec, Delete (name, stages)
 * | Update (name, stages, _), an or-pattern with variables, which
 * tiny-ml does not read) *)
let change db name stages (items : (string * expr) list option) =
  let f = db.file in
  let t = table db name in
  if List.exists (function Where _ -> false | _ -> true) stages then
    error "only where before delete or set";
  (* the rows first, then the changes: the iterators read the old tree *)
  let _, (_, rs) = run_query db t stages in
  let rs = List.of_seq rs in
  let t = List.fold_left (remove f) t rs in
  let t = match items with
    | Some items ->
        let fs =
          List.map (fun (c, e) -> col_pos (names t) c, compile (names t) e)
            items
        in
        List.fold_left (fun t r ->
          let r' = Array.copy r in
          List.iter (fun (i, e) -> r'.(i) <- e r) fs;
          add f t r') t rs
    | None -> t in
  commit db (replace db t)

let exec caps db (s : stmt) =
  let f = db.file in
  match s with
  | Create (name, cols) ->
      if List.exists (fun t -> t.name = name) db.tables then
        error (Printf.sprintf "table %s exists" name);
      let key = match List.filteri (fun _ (_, _, k) -> k) cols with
        | [ _ ] ->
            let rec go i = function
              | (_, _, true) :: _ -> i
              | _ :: rest -> go (i + 1) rest
              | [] -> 0
            in
            go 0 cols
        | [] -> 0 | _ -> error "one key" in
      commit db (db.tables @
        [ { name; cols = List.map (fun (c, ty, _) -> c, ty) cols; key;
            root = empty_tree f; indexes = [] } ])
  | Insert (name, tuples) ->
      let t = table db name in
      let t = List.fold_left (fun t vs ->
        if List.length vs <> List.length t.cols then
          error (name ^ " has " ^ string_of_int (List.length t.cols)
                 ^ " columns");
        List.iter2 (fun v (c, ty) ->
          if type_of v <> ty then
            error (c ^ ": a " ^ (if ty = TInt then "int" else "text")))
          vs t.cols;
        add f t (Array.of_list vs)) t tuples in
      commit db (replace db t)
  | Index (name, c) ->
      let t = table db name in
      if not (List.mem_assoc c t.cols) then error ("no column " ^ c);
      if List.mem_assoc c t.indexes then
        error (Printf.sprintf "index on %s exists" c);
      let pos = col_pos (names t) c in
      let root =
        Seq.fold_left (fun root r ->
          insert f root [ r.(pos); r.(t.key) ] no_row)
          (empty_tree f) (rows db t Scan)
      in
      commit db (replace db { t with indexes = t.indexes @ [ c, root ] })
  | Query (explain, name, stages) ->
      let t = table db name in
      let a, (_, rs) = run_query db t stages in
      if explain then
        print caps (String.concat " | " (show_access t a :: List.map (function
          | Where _ -> "where" | Select _ -> "select"
          | Join t -> "hash join " ^ t | Group _ -> "group"
          | Sort _ -> "sort" | Take n -> Printf.sprintf "take %d" n) stages)
          ^ "\n")
      else
        Seq.iter (fun r ->
          print caps
            (String.concat "|" (Array.to_list (Array.map show r)) ^ "\n")) rs
  | Help ->
      let col (c, ty) = c ^ if ty = TInt then " int" else " text" in
      let tables = List.map (fun t ->
        "  " ^ t.name ^ " ("
        ^ String.concat ", " (List.mapi (fun i c ->
            col c ^ if i = t.key then " key" else "") t.cols)
        ^ ")"
        ^ String.concat "" (List.map (fun (c, _) -> ", index " ^ c) t.indexes)
        ^ "\n") db.tables in
      print caps
        (help
         ^ (if tables = [] then "No tables yet.\n"
            else "The tables:\n" ^ String.concat "" tables))
  | Delete (name, stages) -> change db name stages None
  | Update (name, stages, items) -> change db name stages (Some items)

let main
    (caps : < Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout;
              Cap.stderr; .. >) =
  match TinyLibSystem.argv caps with
  | [ _; ("-h" | "--help") ] ->
      (* help's first lines, a table made and queried *)
      let session =
        List.filteri (fun i _ -> i < 5) (String.split_on_char '\n' help)
      in
      print caps ("usage: tiny-db file.db\n"
                  ^ "The statements on standard input, at a terminal a prompt"
                  ^ " (# a comment).\n"
                  ^ String.concat "\n" session
                  ^ "\nThen help, at the prompt: the stages, the other"
                  ^ " statements, and the tables.\n");
      0
  | [ _; path ] ->
      let db = open_db caps path in
      (* at a terminal, a prompt, as sqlite's *)
      let tty = TinyLibSystem.isatty 0 in
      if tty then
        print caps (Printf.sprintf "tiny-db: %s; help for how, ^D to end\n" path);
      let rec loop n =
        if tty then (print caps "tiny-db> "; TinyLibSystem.flush caps);
        match TinyLibSystem.read_line caps with
        | None -> if tty then print caps "\n"; 0
        | Some line ->
            (try match tokens line with [] -> () | ts -> exec caps db (parse ts)
             with Error m ->
               TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
               TinyLibSystem.eprint caps
                 (Printf.sprintf "tiny-db: line %d: %s\n" n m));
            loop (n + 1)
      in
      let code = loop 1 in
      TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
      code
  | _ -> TinyLibSystem.eprint caps "usage: tiny-db file.db   (-h: how)\n"; 1

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-db" main
tiny/TinyDatabase.mli
9671
(* A tiny relational database, in one file, whose query language is the
 * relational algebra itself. The full-size version in ix, mini-chidb
 * (database/), is a faithful copy of chidb: it compiles SQL to a
 * program for a register machine, which works on B-trees made of
 * fixed-size pages that are changed in place. This one keeps the same
 * ideas but takes the other road at each choice. Its statements are
 * shown by example in the [help] string of the .ml (which is also what
 * help prints at its prompt, and the start of what db -h prints):
 *
 * - {b A query is a pipeline of the operators of the algebra}, read
 *   from left to right like a Unix pipe: a table, then where (sigma),
 *   select (pi, with computed columns), join (the natural join), group
 *   (with count, sum, min, max), sort, and take. SQL's
 *   SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE is the same pipeline written in a fixed
 *   order; here the user chooses the order, and the columns of each
 *   stage are the output of the previous one.
 * - {b The tree is copy-on-write}: once a node is written, it never
 *   changes. An insertion writes a new leaf and the path from it up to
 *   a new root at the end of the file. A statement then commits by
 *   writing its new catalog there too, and storing the offset of that
 *   catalog in the header of the file, which is one small write. As a
 *   result, every statement is atomic (a crash before the header is
 *   written leaves the previous state intact), nodes can be cached
 *   without ever being invalidated, and a reader holding an old root
 *   would see a consistent old database (this is not used here). The
 *   price is that the file only grows: nothing is ever reused, as in an
 *   append-only log. Nodes are values serialized by hand (an int takes
 *   8 bytes, a list is its length followed by its elements; this used
 *   to be done with Marshal). They can have any size; fixed-size pages
 *   are only needed when you change pages in place.
 * - {b Evaluation pulls rows through the stages} (one Seq per stage:
 *   the iterator model). The first where stage chooses an access path
 *   depending on its shape: a key range on the table, a range on an
 *   index, or a full scan; the explain command prints that choice. A
 *   join builds a hash table of the right-hand table.
 * - Keys are values, or lists of values compared lexicographically. The
 *   tree of a table is keyed by [key column], and the tree of an index
 *   by [value; key], so each index entry is unique and a range on the
 *   value is a range in the tree. Deletion removes the entry but does
 *   not rebalance the tree: a node may be left underfull, even empty,
 *   and searches still work correctly.
 *
 * Here is the layout of the file. The catalog offset is the only part
 * that is ever written twice:
 *
 *     0     tinydb1 and a newline     the magic number, 8 bytes
 *     8     the catalog's offset      8 bytes, rewritten by each commit
 *     16    a length, a value         what was appended: each entry
 *     ...   a length, a value         is a length (8 bytes) followed
 *     ...   a length, a value         by a node or a catalog
 *
 * A catalog describes the tables: for each table, its name, its
 * columns, which column is the key, the offset of the root of its tree,
 * and the roots of its indexes. A node is either a leaf (at most 16
 * keys with their rows) or an inner node (separator keys and the
 * offsets of its children). So a database is a tree of offsets hanging
 * from the 8 bytes of the header. Inserting into the second leaf of a
 * table creates a new tree that shares the first leaf with the old one:
 *
 *     header ---> catalog ---> root            before
 *                              /   \
 *                          leaf1   leaf2
 *
 *     header -.   catalog ---> root            after: the old tree is
 *             |                /   \           still intact, but no
 *             |            leaf1   leaf2       header points to its
 *             |              |                 catalog anymore
 *             '-> catalog' -> root'
 *                                \
 *                               leaf2'
 *
 *     the file:  leaf1 leaf2 root catalog | leaf2' root' catalog'
 *
 * Everything right of the bar was appended by the statement, and the
 * header is written only after that. A crash before the header is
 * written leaves three values in the file that nothing points to. In a
 * table of n rows, an insert rewrites as many nodes as the tree is
 * high, each with up to 16 entries: that is how fast the file grows.
 *
 * What is kept from chidb: tables with a key, int and text columns,
 * indexes, joins, and a file that outlives the program. What is added:
 * delete, update (set), group and the aggregate functions, sort, take,
 * computed columns, and atomic statements. What is dropped: SQL, NULL,
 * the register machine and its programs, the 1,024-byte pages, and
 * SQLite's file format.
 *
 * Exercises, all cheap because nodes never change:
 * - transactions of several statements: begin ... commit, where the
 *   header is written only at commit (and rollback just forgets the
 *   catalog in memory); about 10 lines, since a single statement is
 *   already a transaction;
 * - time travel: each catalog also records the offset of the catalog
 *   it replaces, and books @ 3 reads the table as it was three commits
 *   ago; all the old roots are still in the file;
 * - compaction: copy the live trees into a new file, then rename it
 *   over the old one; the rename is atomic too, and the file no longer
 *   grows forever;
 * - readers running beside a writer: a reader keeps the root it
 *   started with, as a snapshot, without any lock (LMDB's design);
 * - rebalancing on delete: merge an underfull node with a sibling.
 *
 * Where it stands: mini-chidb takes the other road at each fork (SQL,
 * a compiler to programs for a machine, 1,024-byte pages changed in
 * place), and the two read well side by side. A file that only grows,
 * plus one small write to commit, is also how TinyVCS stores things
 * (its objects file and its head). Pulling the rows of a statement
 * through stages is what Seq does; it is the shell's pipe, inside a
 * single process. Underneath, the database uses only four kernel
 * calls: open, seek, read, and write (through TinyLibSystem: Unix on
 * the host, tiny-kernel's own calls there, its seek for this). It never
 * asks for the data to actually reach the disk (no fsync), so
 * "atomic" here means safe if the program dies, not if the machine
 * does.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Edgar Codd's papers at IBM San Jose (1970 to 1972) introduced the
 * model, tables with no pointers between them, and two languages for
 * it: an algebra of operators on whole tables, and a calculus that
 * says what is wanted rather than how to get it. IBM's System R (from
 * 1974) implemented the calculus as SEQUEL, later renamed SQL;
 * Berkeley's Ingres (Michael Stonebraker) implemented QUEL, by most
 * accounts the cleaner language. SQL won, thanks to IBM's products and
 * the 1986 standard. The algebra survived inside the systems: a large
 * SQL database turns a query into a tree of algebra operators and runs
 * that tree (SQLite and mini-chidb instead turn it into a program for a
 * small machine: see Codegen and Dbm). Here the user writes the tree
 * directly, and for a pipeline that tree is just a list.
 *
 * comeback:
 * Never writing over a page was System R's first recovery scheme,
 * shadow pages (Raymond Lorie, 1977): a transaction writes new pages
 * and commits by swapping a page table. It was abandoned for the
 * write-ahead log, where the record of a change is forced to disk first
 * and the pages are updated in place later. That keeps the pages of a
 * table next to each other and commits with one sequential write, and
 * every large system has worked this way since. Shadowing came back
 * where simplicity, and readers that never wait, matter more: in
 * CouchDB's files, in LMDB (Howard Chu, 2011), and in the ZFS and
 * btrfs file systems.
 *
 * others:
 * Writing a query as a pipeline is how people write queries outside
 * SQL: the shell's grep, sort, uniq and head on lines of text, R's
 * dplyr, the languages of log tools (Splunk's, Microsoft's Kusto),
 * PRQL, and, since 2024, a pipe syntax for SQL itself proposed by
 * Google. The complaint they all answer is SQL's order: SELECT is
 * written first but runs nearly last.
 *
 * References:
 *  - R. Bayer and E. McCreight, "Organization and Maintenance of Large
 *    Ordered Indexes" (Acta Informatica, 1972): the B-tree
 *  - O. Rodeh, "B-trees, Shadowing, and Clones" (ACM Transactions on
 *    Storage, 2008): copy-on-write B-trees, the design behind LMDB
 *    and btrfs
 *  - G. Graefe, "Volcano -- An Extensible and Parallel Query Evaluation
 *    System" (IEEE TKDE, 1994): the iterator model
 *  - E. F. Codd, "A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data
 *    Banks" (CACM, 1970): the algebra
 *  - B. Sotomayor and A. Shaw, "chidb: Building a Simple Relational
 *    Database System from Scratch" (SIGCSE, 2016): chidb, which
 *    mini-chidb follows; not a Plan 9 program (principia's database/
 *    has Plan 9's ndb, and no chidb)
 *)

(* the open file with its tables; a line, parsed *)
type db
type stmt

(* one statement, done: a table made, rows added, a query planned,
 * run stage after stage and printed *)
val exec : < Cap.stdout; .. > -> db -> stmt -> unit

(* the program: its arguments (-h: how) to its exit status *)
val main :
  < Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr;
    .. > ->
  int
tiny/TinyDebugger.ml

(* Claude Code
