(* See TinyDebugger.mli *)

open TinyCalls
open TinyLibPlayground
open TinyLibGUI
open TinyMachineISA

(* what debug says: on its output, or kept for the window *)
let sink = ref None
let say s =
  match !sink with
  | Some b -> Buffer.add_string b s
  | None -> ignore (u_write 1 s)

(* what f says, as a string *)
let text f =
  let was = !sink in
  let b = Buffer.create 256 in
  sink := Some b;
  f ();
  sink := was;
  Buffer.contents b

(* the process, the trace's descriptor, where the process is (-1:
 * running), whether debug started it, its breakpoints *)
let pid = ref 0
let t = ref (-1)
let pc = ref (-1)
let started = ref false
let stops = ref []

(* the word at i in s, its low byte first (under 2^30: ML's ints) *)
let word_of s i =
  String.get_uint16_le s i + (String.get_uint16_le s (i + 2) lsl 16)

(* the program's labels, by address, from its file: after the image,
 * whose size the header says *)
let funcs = ref (Array.of_list [])
let symbols file =
  let fd = u_open file 0 in
  if fd >= 0 then begin
    let h = u_read fd 16 in
    let word i = word_of h i in
    (* (tiny-linker -n's header has a fourth word, the text's size) *)
    let split = String.length h = 16 && word 0 = 0x7a0ce6 in
    if String.length h >= 12 && (word 0 = 0x7a0ce5 || split)
       && u_seek fd ((if split then 16 else 12) + word 4) 0 >= 0 then begin
      let rec rest acc =
        let s = u_read fd 4096 in
        if s = "" then String.concat "" (List.rev acc) else rest (s :: acc) in
      funcs := TinyLibSymbols.labels (rest [])
    end;
    ignore (u_close fd)
  end

(* the next line of the trace, and a command and its answer ("" when
 * the kernel refused it). In a window, the program's output is read
 * meanwhile, before its stops (its pipe never full) *)
let output = ref (-1)
let rec next () =
  let fds = Array.make 2 !output in
  fds.(1) <- !t;
  if !output >= 0 && u_ready fds 2 0 = !output then begin
    let s = u_read !output 512 in
    if s = "" then (ignore (u_close !output); output := -1) else say s;
    next ()
  end
  else
  let s = u_read !t 4096 in
  let n = String.length s in
  if n > 0 && s.[n - 1] = '\n' then String.sub s 0 (n - 1) else s
let ask c = if u_write !t c < 0 then "" else next ()

let hex a = if a < 0 then string_of_int a else hex a

(* n bytes of the process at a, from the kernel's hexadecimal ("" when
 * outside it) *)
let bytes a n =
  let h = ask ("m " ^ string_of_int a ^ " " ^ string_of_int n) in
  let digit c = if c <= '9' then Char.code c - 48 else Char.code c - 87 in
  String.init (String.length h / 2) (fun i ->
    Char.chr ((digit h.[2 * i] * 16) + digit h.[(2 * i) + 1]))

(* a word of s at i: as hexadecimal digits (a word may be past ML's 31
 * bits), and as an instruction's (under 2^30: the others are none) *)
let digits s i =
  let d = "0123456789abcdef" in
  String.init 8 (fun k ->
    let b = Char.code s.[i + 3 - (k / 2)] in
    d.[if k mod 2 = 0 then b / 16 else b mod 16])
let instr s i =
  if Char.code s.[i + 3] >= 0x40 then None
  else
    decode (word_of s i)

(* an address by its function, main+0x14 (in hexadecimal when there is
 * none) *)
let name a =
  match TinyLibSymbols.find !funcs a with
  | Some (f, b) when a = b -> f
  | Some (f, b) -> f ^ "+" ^ hex (a - b)
  | None -> Printf.sprintf "%x" a

(* the instruction at a, as tiny-cpu -l lists it, by its function *)
let listing a =
  let s = bytes a 4 in
  let text =
    if String.length s < 4 then "?"
    else
      match instr s 0 with
      | Some i ->
          (* a jump's or a branch's target named, at a function's start *)
          let target =
            match i with
            | Jal (_, off) -> a + 4 + (4 * off)
            | Branch (_, _, _, off) -> a + 4 + (4 * off)
            | _ -> -1 in
          print a i
          ^ (match TinyLibSymbols.find !funcs target with
             | Some (f, b) when b = target -> " <" ^ f ^ ">"
             | _ -> "")
      | None -> ".word\t0x" ^ digits s 0 in
  name a ^ ":\t" ^ text ^ "\n"

(* the next stop, and why (None when the process ended, said); a stop
 * said; the next stop said, false when the process ended *)
let stopped () =
  match String.split_on_char ' ' (next ()) with
  | "stopped" :: p :: why -> pc := int_of_string p; Some why
  | "exited" :: rest -> say ("exited " ^ String.concat " " rest ^ "\n"); None
  | _ -> say "the trace ended\n"; None
let show why =
  (match why with
   | [ "step" ] -> ()
   | [ "fault"; a ] -> say ("fault at " ^ hex (int_of_string a) ^ "\n")
   | [ "illegal"; w ] -> say ("illegal " ^ hex (int_of_string w) ^ "\n")
   | _ -> say (String.concat " " why ^ "\n"));
  say (listing !pc)
let wait () = match stopped () with Some why -> show why; true | None -> false

(* an address typed: a number, pc, a function's name and maybe +n *)
let address s =
  let at base =
    if base = "pc" then (if !pc >= 0 then Some !pc else None)
    else
      match int_of_string_opt base with
      | Some a -> Some a
      | None -> TinyLibSymbols.address !funcs base in
  match String.index_opt s '+' with
  | Some i ->
      (match at (String.sub s 0 i),
             int_of_string_opt (String.sub s (i + 1) (String.length s - i - 1))
       with
       | Some a, Some k -> Some (a + k)
       | _ -> None)
  | None -> at s

let ok s = if s <> "ok" then say "?\n"

(* the registers, as the kernel says them: r1 v ... r15 v pc v *)
let regs () =
  let rec pairs l =
    match l with
    | n :: v :: rest ->
        (match int_of_string_opt v with
         | Some v -> (n, v) :: pairs rest
         | None -> [])
    | _ -> [] in
  pairs (String.split_on_char ' ' (ask "r"))
let reg name = match List.assoc_opt name (regs ()) with Some v -> v | None -> 0

(* c, s and n; false when the process ended *)
let continue () =
  if !pc >= 0 then (ignore (u_write !t "c"); pc := -1);
  wait ()
let step () =
  if !pc < 0 then (say "?\n"; true)
  else (ignore (u_write !t "s"); pc := -1; wait ())
let over () =
  let s = bytes !pc 4 in
  let call =
    String.length s = 4
    && (match instr s 0 with
        | Some (Jal (d, _)) -> d = lr
        | Some (Jalr (d, _, _)) -> d = lr
        | _ -> false) in
  if not call then step ()
  else begin
    (* the breakpoint after the call, a stop there not said; in a
     * recursive function the call's own return is told by its sp, the
     * same as at the call: one with a lower sp is a deeper call's, run
     * past *)
    let a = !pc + 4 and sp = reg "r14" in
    let mine = not (List.mem a !stops) in
    if mine then ok (ask ("b " ^ string_of_int a));
    let rec go () =
      ignore (u_write !t "c");
      pc := -1;
      match stopped () with
      | Some [ "break" ] when !pc = a && reg "r14" < sp -> go ()
      | Some [ "break" ] when !pc = a -> say (listing !pc); true
      | Some why -> show why; true
      | None -> false in
    let alive = go () in
    if alive && mine then ok (ask ("d " ^ string_of_int a));
    alive
  end


(* a word of the process, an address or an instruction: under 2^30 *)
let word a =
  let s = bytes a 4 in
  if String.length s < 4 || Char.code s.[3] >= 0x40 then None
  else
    Some (word_of s 0)

(* a slot of the value stack, at i in s: an integer (odd: n is 2n+1)
 * in decimal, a pointer in hexadecimal, _ for 0 (a slot not set yet:
 * the prologue zeroes them) *)
let value s i =
  let b k = Char.code s.[i + k] in
  if b 0 land 1 = 1 then begin
    let n =
      (b 0 lsr 1) + (b 1 lsl 7) + (b 2 lsl 15) + ((b 3 land 0x7f) lsl 23) in
    string_of_int (if b 3 >= 0x80 then n - 0x20000000 - 0x20000000 else n)
  end
  else if b 0 + b 1 + b 2 + b 3 = 0 then "_"
  else if b 3 < 0x40 then
    hex (word_of s i)
  else "0x" ^ digits s i

(* an ML function's slots, the f bytes from v: its closure's (slot 0)
 * left out, then its parameters, its variables, its spills (six at
 * most) *)
let slots v f =
  let s = bytes v f in
  let n = min (String.length s / 4) 7 in
  String.concat " " (List.init (max 0 (n - 1)) (fun k -> value s (4 * (k + 1))))
  ^ (if f / 4 > 7 then " ..." else "")

(* bt: the frames, from the pc's, by the code itself. tiny-c's and
 * tiny-ml's functions all start with addi sp, sp, -f and stw lr, k(sp):
 * a frame is f bytes, its return address at k(sp). Before those two
 * instructions have run, the return address is still in lr, the frame
 * not yet made (the first frame alone can be there); a function without
 * them (assembly: write, _start) keeps it in lr, and ends the walk
 * after the first frame. A tail call's frame is gone: the frames are
 * the callers that will be returned to. Each line is the call's place
 * (the return address less 4).
 *
 * An ML function's third instruction is addi r12, r12, v: its frame on
 * the value stack, v bytes below r12 (TinyML.ml's machine). Its slots
 * follow its name; the frames above start v lower. The first ML frame
 * is r12's when the pc is in ML, else ml_vsp's (where ML leaves r12
 * when it calls C) *)
let backtrace () =
  let r = regs () in
  let reg n = match List.assoc_opt n r with Some v -> v | None -> 0 in
  let ml b =
    match word (b + 8) with
    | Some w ->
        (match decode w with
         | Some (Alui (Add, 12, 12, v)) when v > 0 -> v
         | _ -> 0)
    | None -> 0 in
  let start pc =
    match TinyLibSymbols.find !funcs pc with Some (_, b) -> b | None -> -1 in
  let rec go k pc sp vsp =
    let b = start pc in
    let v = if b >= 0 then ml b else 0 in
    let shown = v > 0 && (k > 0 || pc >= b + 12) in
    say (string_of_int k ^ "\t" ^ name pc
         ^ (if shown then "\t" ^ slots (vsp - v) v else "") ^ "\n");
    let vsp = if shown then vsp - v else vsp in
    let frame =
      match TinyLibSymbols.find !funcs pc with
      | None -> None
      | Some (_, b) ->
          match word b, word (b + 4) with
          | Some w1, Some w2 ->
              (match decode w1, decode w2 with
               | Some (Alui (Add, 14, 14, f)), Some (Store (W, 15, 14, off))
                 when f < 0 ->
                   if pc = b then (if k = 0 then Some (reg "r15", sp) else None)
                   else if pc = b + 4 then
                     (if k = 0 then Some (reg "r15", sp - f) else None)
                   else
                     (match word (sp + off) with
                      | Some ret -> Some (ret, sp - f)
                      | None -> None)
               | _ -> if k = 0 then Some (reg "r15", sp) else None)
          | _ -> None in
    match frame with
    | Some (ret, sp) when ret > 0 && k < 64 -> go (k + 1) (ret - 4) sp vsp
    | _ -> () in
  if !pc < 0 then say "?\n"
  else begin
    let b = start !pc in
    let vsp =
      if b >= 0 && ml b > 0 then reg "r12"
      else
        match TinyLibSymbols.address !funcs "ml_vsp" with
        | Some a -> (match word a with Some v -> v | None -> 0)
        | None -> 0 in
    go 0 !pc (reg "r14") vsp
  end

(* the registers, four a line in columns, and the instruction at the pc *)
let registers () =
  let rec go l k =
    match l with
    | name :: v :: rest when name <> "pc" ->
        let r = name ^ " " ^ hex (int_of_string v) in
        say (if k mod 4 = 3 then r ^ "\n"
             else r ^ String.make (max 1 (16 - String.length r)) ' ');
        go rest (k + 1)
    | [ "pc"; v ] ->
        say ((if k mod 4 = 0 then "" else "\n") ^ listing (int_of_string v))
    | _ -> say "?\n" in
  go (String.split_on_char ' ' (ask "r")) 0

(* x: n words, four a line; x/i: n instructions *)
let words a n =
  let s = bytes a (4 * n) in
  if String.length s < 4 * n then say "?\n"
  else
    for k = 0 to n - 1 do
      if k mod 4 = 0 then say (Printf.sprintf "%x:" (a + (4 * k)));
      say ("\t" ^ digits s (4 * k));
      if k mod 4 = 3 || k = n - 1 then say "\n"
    done
let instructions a n = for k = 0 to n - 1 do say (listing (a + (4 * k))) done

(* x and x/i's n words or instructions at a *)
let examine show a rest =
  match address a, rest with
  | Some a, [] -> show a 1
  | Some a, [ n ] ->
      (match int_of_string_opt n with
       | Some n when n > 0 && n <= 256 -> show a n
       | _ -> say "?\n")
  | _ -> say "?\n"

(* a command; false to quit *)
let command line =
  match List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' line) with
  | [] -> true
  | [ "b"; a ] ->
      (match address a with
       | Some a when ask ("b " ^ string_of_int a) = "ok" -> stops := a :: !stops
       | _ -> say "?\n");
      true
  | [ "d"; a ] ->
      (match address a with
       | Some a ->
           ok (ask ("d " ^ string_of_int a));
           stops := List.filter (fun b -> b <> a) !stops
       | None -> say "?\n");
      true
  | [ "c" ] -> continue ()
  | [ "s" ] -> step ()
  | [ "n" ] -> if !pc < 0 then (say "?\n"; true) else over ()
  | [ "r" ] -> registers (); true
  | [ "bt" ] -> backtrace (); true
  | "x" :: a :: rest -> examine words a rest; true
  | "x/i" :: a :: rest -> examine instructions a rest; true
  | [ "q" ] -> false
  | _ -> say "?\n"; true

(* the commands, a line each, until q, the input's end or the process's *)
let pending = ref ""
let rec read_line () =
  match String.index_opt !pending '\n' with
  | Some i ->
      let l = String.sub !pending 0 i in
      pending := String.sub !pending (i + 1) (String.length !pending - i - 1);
      Some l
  | None ->
      let s = u_read 0 4096 in
      if s = "" then None else (pending := !pending ^ s; read_line ())
let rec loop () =
  match read_line () with
  | Some l -> if command l then loop () else false
  | None -> false

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The window *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the window's model: what was said, its lines (the last 100); the
 * command typed; the panes, made after each command; the mouse's
 * buttons as last seen; the window's size, and its buttons' shapes and
 * boxes, each with its command *)
type model = {
  log : string list; cmd : string; panes : string list; held : int;
  w : int; h : int; bar : shape list;
  boxes : ((int * int * int * int) * string action) list;
}

(* a text's lines, the tabs as spaces to the next multiple of 8 *)
let lines s =
  let untab l =
    let b = Buffer.create 80 in
    String.iter (fun c ->
      if c = '\t' then
        Buffer.add_string b (String.make (8 - (Buffer.length b mod 8)) ' ')
      else Buffer.add_char b c) l;
    Buffer.contents b in
  let n = String.length s in
  let s = if n > 0 && s.[n - 1] = '\n' then String.sub s 0 (n - 1) else s in
  if s = "" then [] else List.map untab (String.split_on_char '\n' s)

let rec last n l =
  if n <= 0 then [] else if List.length l > n then last n (List.tl l) else l

(* the panes: the registers (without r's line of the pc), the
 * instructions around the pc (=> at it, * at a breakpoint), the
 * backtrace (its first 5 frames) *)
let panes () =
  if !pc < 0 then [ "(no process)" ]
  else begin
    let r = lines (text registers) in
    let r = List.filteri (fun i _ -> i < List.length r - 1) r in
    let code =
      List.init 6 (fun k ->
        let a = !pc + (4 * (k - 1)) in
        String.concat ""
          (lines ((if a = !pc then "=> "
                   else if List.mem a !stops then " * " else "   ")
                  ^ listing a))) in
    let bt = List.filteri (fun i _ -> i < 5) (lines (text backtrace)) in
    r @ [ "" ] @ code @ [ "" ] @ bt
  end

(* what was said since, to the log, and the panes made again *)
let out = Buffer.create 1024
let shown m =
  let said = lines (Buffer.contents out) in
  Buffer.clear out;
  { m with log = last 100 (m.log @ said); panes = panes () }

(* a command run, said in the log first *)
let run_command c m =
  say ("> " ^ c ^ "\n");
  ignore (command c);
  shown m

(* the picture: the ground, the buttons, the panes, the log's last
 * lines that fit, the command typed *)
let picture m =
  let rows = (m.h - 36) / 16 in
  let top = m.panes @ [ "" ] in
  let all =
    top @ last (rows - List.length top - 1) m.log @ [ "> " ^ m.cmd ^ "_" ] in
  Rect (255, m.w, m.h)
  :: m.bar
  @ List.mapi (fun i l ->
      Move (4, 34 + (16 * i), Words (0, l)))
      all

(* a key: Escape quits, Return runs the command (q quits), s, n and c
 * run at once when nothing is typed; a click on a button its command *)
let typed k m =
  if k = 27 then None
  else if k = 13 || k = 10 then
    (if m.cmd = "q" then None else Some (run_command m.cmd { m with cmd = "" }))
  else if k = 8 || k = 127 then
    Some { m with cmd =
             (if m.cmd = "" then ""
              else String.sub m.cmd 0 (String.length m.cmd - 1)) }
  else if m.cmd = "" && (k = 115 || k = 110 || k = 99) then
    Some (run_command (String.make 1 (Char.chr k)) m)
  else if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
    Some { m with cmd = m.cmd ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr k) }
  else Some m
let moved x y b m =
  let pressed =
    if b = 0 || m.held <> 0 then []
    else List.filter (fun (box, _) -> inside x y box) m.boxes in
  match pressed with
  | (_, Send "q") :: _ -> None
  | (_, Send c) :: _ -> Some (run_command c { m with held = b })
  | _ -> Some { m with held = b }

let window () =
  let first w h =
    let bar, boxes =
      place 0 0 w 28
        (Row [
           Button ("step", "s"); Button ("next", "n");
           Button ("continue", "c");
           Button ("quit", "q") ])
    in
    shown { log = []; cmd = ""; panes = []; held = 0; w = w; h = h; bar = bar;
            boxes = boxes } in
  run_canvas
    { first = first; picture = picture; typed = typed; moved = moved }

let main () =
  let n = u_argc () in
  let windowed = n > 1 && u_arg 1 = "-window" in
  let first = if windowed then 2 else 1 in
  if n <= first then
    (say "usage: debug [-window] prog [args] | debug [-window] pid [prog]\n";
     exit 1);
  let file prog = if String.contains prog '/' then prog else "/bin/" ^ prog in
  (* in a window, the program's output and errors on a pipe *)
  let pipe = if windowed then u_pipe () else -1 in
  (match int_of_string_opt (u_arg first) with
   | Some p ->
       pid := p;
       if n > first + 1 then symbols (file (u_arg (first + 1)))
   | None ->
       let prog = u_arg first in
       let file = file prog in
       symbols file;
       let p = u_fork () in
       if p = 0 then begin
         if pipe >= 0 then begin
           List.iter (fun fd ->
             ignore (u_close fd); ignore (u_dup (pipe / 256))) [ 1; 2 ];
           ignore (u_close (pipe / 256));
           ignore (u_close (pipe mod 256))
         end;
         ignore (u_trace 0);
         ignore (u_exec file
                   (List.init (n - first) (fun i -> u_arg (i + first))));
         say ("debug: " ^ prog ^ ": not found\n");
         exit 127
       end;
       pid := p;
       started := true);
  if pipe >= 0 then begin
    ignore (u_close (pipe / 256));
    if !started then output := pipe mod 256
    else ignore (u_close (pipe mod 256))
  end;
  if windowed then sink := Some out;
  t := u_trace !pid;
  if !t < 0 && not !started then
    (say ("debug: " ^ u_arg first ^ ": no such process\n"); exit 1);
  (* (a program not found: its child said so, in the window's case on
   * the pipe, read into what is said) *)
  if !t < 0 || (!started && not (wait ())) then begin
    ignore (u_write 1 (Buffer.contents out));
    exit 1
  end;
  (* the process killed if debug started it and it still runs *)
  let quit = if windowed then (window (); true) else not (loop ()) in
  if quit && !started then ignore (u_kill !pid);
  if !started then ignore (u_waits ());
  exit 0
tiny/TinyDebugger.mli
7692
(* debug: a debugger for tiny-kernel's programs, at the level of their
 * instructions (plan_tiny_debugger.md). It starts its program stopped
 * at its first instruction (a child that calls trace(0), then exec),
 * or attaches to a process by its pid, and controls it through the
 * kernel's trace descriptor: commands written, lines read. Its own
 * commands are typed as ed's, a letter and its arguments; an address
 * is a number in hexadecimal (0x1a4) or decimal, pc for the pc, or a
 * function's name and maybe an offset (main, main+0x14):
 *
 *     b addr        a breakpoint          d addr   one removed
 *     c             continue              s        one instruction
 *     n             one instruction, over a call (jal or jalr to lr)
 *     r             the registers, and the instruction at the pc
 *     bt            the backtrace: the calls the pc is in, and an ML
 *                   function's slots on the value stack
 *     x addr [n]    n words               x/i addr [n]  instructions
 *     q             quit (the program killed, or left to run if attached)
 *
 *     debug cat f
 *     debug -window cat f
 *     debug 12 /bin/cat
 *
 * At each stop it shows why, and the instruction at the pc, by the
 * function it is in: main+0x14. The names are the labels tiny-linker
 * wrote after the image (-s, TinyLibSymbols), read from the program's
 * file: the one started, or the one named after an attached pid (the
 * kernel knows a process's image, not its file).
 *
 * How it works: debug and its program are two processes, and the
 * kernel stands between them. Every command is a line written on the
 * descriptor trace(pid) gave, every answer and every stop a line read
 * from it (TinyKernel.ml's command and stop):
 *
 *     debug                     tiny-kernel                 cat
 *     t = trace(pid)
 *     "b 4096"        ------>   the word at 4096 kept,
 *                    <------    0 written there; "ok"
 *     "c"             ------>   cat Ready ---------------->  runs
 *                                                            ... 0 at 4096:
 *                               illegal, cat Stopped  <----  a trap
 *                    <------    "stopped 4096 break"
 *     "r", "m 4096 4" ------>   its frame, its memory (the
 *                    <------    kept word, not the 0)
 *     "c"             ------>   the kept word run alone (a
 *                               step), the 0 written again,
 *                               cat Ready
 *
 * - {b A step is the timer's interrupt}: entry.tm's k_step sets the
 *   timer to ring after one instruction of the process, then runs it
 *   as any other. No instruction is decoded to find where the next
 *   one is.
 * - {b n is a breakpoint after the call}: on a jal or jalr to lr, a
 *   breakpoint at the next instruction, and c. In a recursive function
 *   a deeper call of the same one comes back there first; the sp tells
 *   them apart (lower: a deeper call's, run past), as gdb's next does.
 * - {b bt reads the code}: no frame pointer and no table of frame
 *   sizes, but every function of tiny-c's and tiny-ml's starts with
 *   addi sp, sp, -f and stw lr, k(sp), and an ML function's third
 *   instruction is addi r12, r12, v, its frame on the value stack. So
 *   the name gives the function's start, its first words the frame,
 *   the frame the return address, and that the caller. Assembly without
 *   that prologue (start.tm's write, _start) ends the walk.
 * - {b The window} (-window) is the same commands, run by
 *   TinyLibGUI's run_canvas: the registers, the instructions around the
 *   pc and the backtrace shown after each one, then what the commands
 *   said and what the program wrote (its output a pipe, read while it
 *   runs, so that it never fills), the command typed last; s, n and c
 *   at once on an empty line, and buttons for them. While the program
 *   runs (c) the window waits for its stop.
 *
 * Its sibling is trace (TinyTracer), strace's idea on the same
 * descriptor: a stop before each system call and after it.
 *
 * What is ours, where Plan 9's tools and gdb go another way:
 *
 * - {b One descriptor and a system call}, not a directory of files.
 *   trace(pid) gives it, trace(0) asks to be traced by the parent
 *   (Unix's PTRACE_TRACEME); the commands are text, as /proc's ctl.
 * - {b The kernel keeps the breakpoints}: b gives it the address, it
 *   keeps the word, m shows the kept word, c and s run it, and a fork's
 *   child gets the words back. Plan 9's db writes the breakpoint
 *   instruction itself, through /proc/n/mem, and keeps the words in its
 *   own table (db's runpcs.c, with a flag per breakpoint to skip it
 *   once when continuing from it).
 * - {b The step by the timer} (above), where db's runstep asks libmach
 *   for the addresses the instruction can go to next (machdata's foll:
 *   a branch's two) and puts temporary breakpoints there (db's
 *   trcrun.c), and Unix's PTRACE_SINGLESTEP sets the CPU's trap flag.
 * - {b bt by the prologues}, where Plan 9's linkers write each
 *   function's frame size in the symbol table (a .frame symbol, read
 *   by libmach's sym.c) and its stack walk reads it.
 * - {b The commands are gdb's letters} (b, c, s, n, bt, x/i), not db's
 *   adb syntax (main:b, :c, $c), which a reader of today knows less.
 * - {b The names are text lines after the image}, the map's format,
 *   rather than a binary symbol table, and only the functions': no
 *   line numbers, no types. A function and an instruction is what db
 *   shows too.
 * - Left out: watchpoints, conditional breakpoints, printing a C
 *   variable or an ML value by its type (that needs the compilers to
 *   describe their frames: acid's road), the kernel itself.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * On Unix a debugger drives its program with ptrace, a system call of
 * a dozen requests (peek a word, poke a word, get the registers,
 * continue, step), one word at a time, and only a parent or an
 * attached tracer may call it. Plan 9 makes a process a directory of
 * files, /proc/n: mem its memory, regs its registers, ctl a file of
 * text commands (stop, start, waitstop), note its signals; a debugger
 * is a program that reads and writes files, and can debug a process
 * of another machine by importing its /proc. The trace descriptor is
 * that idea in a single file.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Unix's first debugger was db, then adb (Steve Bourne, Seventh
 * Edition, 1979), with its terse syntax of addresses and verbs; sdb and
 * dbx added source lines, and gdb (Richard Stallman, 1986) became the
 * free one. /proc came from Tom Killian, in the Eighth Edition ("Processes
 * as Files", 1984), and Plan 9 made it a directory. Plan 9's db keeps
 * adb's syntax; acid (Phil Winterbottom, 1994) is a debugger built on a
 * language, its printing of each type a function written in acid.
 *
 * others:
 * gdb drives its program by ptrace on Unix, and by a remote protocol
 * of text packets (gdbserver, QEMU's stub) elsewhere: commands as
 * lines on a wire, as here. LLDB (2010) is built on LLVM's
 * disassemblers and its compiler's knowledge of types.
 *
 * References: plan_tiny_debugger.md (the design and its steps);
 * principia's debuggers/ (db, acid, libmach, tracers/ratrace.c), read
 * for the comparisons above, not copied;
 * T. J. Killian, "Processes as Files" (USENIX, 1984); P. Winterbottom,
 * "Acid: A Debugger Built From A Language" (USENIX, 1994); Plan 9's
 * proc(3), db(1) and ratrace(1) manual pages; S. R. Bourne, "A.
 * Debugging with adb" (Seventh Edition's manual, 1979; from memory). *)

(* the program: its command line, its commands, its exit *)
val main : unit -> unit

(* See TinyEditorLine.mli *)

(* Testing: tests/TinyEditorLine_test.sh runs scripts through this
 * editor and through 9base's sam -d, and compares the results. *)

open Common

(* the regular expressions: compile, search, search_back *)
open TinyLibRegex

(* -h: the commands by example, each one as it runs *)
let help = "usage: tiny-editor [file]: sam's command language, without the screen,
the commands on standard input, one a line, each on dot, a range of the text:
  ,p  3p  3,5p  $p  #10,#20p  all, line 3, lines 3 to 5, the last, chars 10-20
  /main/p  /main/;/^}/d      the next match; from it to a } starting a line
  =  =#                      where dot is, in lines, in characters
  a/text/ i/text/ c/text/    after dot, before it, instead (a alone: lines to .)
  d  s/old/new/g             dot gone; each old in it new (& \\1: match, group)
  m 5  t 5                   dot moved, copied, after line 5
  ,x/o/c/0/                  every o made 0 (x: a loop on matches; y: between)
  ,x/.*\\n/g/TODO/p           the lines with a TODO (g: if dot matches; v: not)
  { ... }                    several commands, a line each, on the same dot
  u  u-1  w  q               undo, redo, write, quit (r e f: read, edit, name)
  newline                    the next line printed

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Regular expressions *)
(*****************************************************************************)

exception Error of string

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Commands *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* #n n /re/ ?re? . $ *)
type simple =
  | Chars of int | Line of int | Search of dir * string | Dot | Dollar
and dir = Fwd | Back

(* a first simple address, then steps each relative to the one before
 * in its direction; a step without an address is a line: 3+/re/-, -2 *)
type chain = { first : simple option; steps : (dir * simple option) list }

(* a,b and a;b (b from a), right to left: a,b,c is a,(b,c) *)
(* old: sam's C list, simple addresses and Rel markers in one list, a +
 * inserted between two addresses by the parser (under a guard), the
 * direction an int carried along, and a look ahead in the evaluator to
 * know if a sign stood alone; , and ; were chars, compared twice *)
type addr = Chain of chain | Range of sep * chain option * addr option
and sep = Comma | Semi

type cmd = { addr : addr option; op : op }

and op =
  | Text of where * string         (* a i c *)
  | Delete
  | Subst of int * string * string * bool
  | Print
  | Eq of bool                     (* =, =# *)
  | Move of bool * chain          (* m, or t *)
  | Loop of loop * cmd
  | Block of cmd list
  | File of file * string
  | Quit
  | Newline
  | Undo of int                    (* u n, and u-n to redo *)

(* where a, i and c put their text: after, before or instead of dot *)
and where = After | Before | Instead

(* x alone (each line), x/re/ (each match), y/re/ (between them), g/re/
 * and v/re/ (if dot matches, or not) *)
(* old: Loop of char * string option * cmd: a y without a pattern could
 * be built, and ran as x does, where sam refuses it *)
and loop =
  | Lines | Matches of string | Between of string | If of bool * string

(* r w e f *)
(* old: File of char * string, whose last case, a catch-all, stood for
 * f *)
and file = Read | Write | Edit | Name

(* the input, one character of pushback; read a line at a time, when
 * the parser is at its end, so that a command typed at a terminal runs
 * once its line is complete (a text, a line more until ".") *)
(* old: all of standard input read first: at a terminal, nothing ran
 * until ^D *)
let input = ref "" and ip = ref 0
(* standard input's next line: main's, which has the capability (the
 * parser's functions, which all come here, do not pass it along) *)
let next_line : (unit -> string option) ref = ref (fun () -> None)
let refill () =
  if !ip >= String.length !input then
    match !next_line () with
    | Some l -> input := l ^ "\n"; ip := 0
    | None -> ()
let peekc () =
  refill (); if !ip < String.length !input then (!input).[!ip] else '\000'
let getc () = let c = peekc () in incr ip; c

let skipbl () =
  while peekc () = ' ' || peekc () = '\t' do incr ip done; peekc ()
let atnl () =
  if skipbl () <> '\n' && peekc () <> '\000' then
    raise (Error "newline expected")
  else incr ip
let num () =
  let s = !ip in
  while peekc () >= '0' && peekc () <= '9' do incr ip done;
  if !ip = s then 1
  else Option.get (int_of_string_opt (String.sub !input s (!ip - s)))

let lastpat = ref ""

(* a /re/, up to the delimiter or the end of the line; empty: the last *)
let regexp delim =
  let b = Buffer.create 16 in
  let rec go () =
    match getc () with
    | '\\' when peekc () = delim -> Buffer.add_char b (getc ()); go ()
    | '\\' -> Buffer.add_char b '\\'; Buffer.add_char b (getc ()); go ()
    | c when c = delim -> ()
    | '\n' | '\000' -> decr ip
    | c -> Buffer.add_char b c; go ()
  in
  go ();
  if Buffer.length b > 0 then lastpat := Buffer.contents b;
  if !lastpat = "" then raise (Error "no pattern");
  !lastpat

(* a replacement or a text: \n is a newline, \ then the delimiter the
 * delimiter; s keeps its other \s, for \1 *)
let rhs delim s =
  let b = Buffer.create 16 in
  let rec go () =
    match getc () with
    | '\\' ->
        (match getc () with
         | 'n' -> Buffer.add_char b '\n'
         | c when c = delim -> Buffer.add_char b c
         | c ->
             if s || c <> '\\' then Buffer.add_char b '\\';
             Buffer.add_char b c);
        go ()
    | c when c = delim || c = '\n' || c = '\000' -> decr ip
    | c -> Buffer.add_char b c; go ()
  in
  go ();
  Buffer.contents b

let simple () : simple option =
  match skipbl () with
  | '#' -> incr ip; Some (Chars (num ()))
  | c when c >= '0' && c <= '9' -> Some (Line (num ()))
  | ('/' | '?') as c ->
      incr ip; Some (Search ((if c = '/' then Fwd else Back), regexp c))
  | '.' -> incr ip; Some Dot
  | '$' -> incr ip; Some Dollar
  | _ -> None

let chain () : chain option =
  (* . and $ only first *)
  let later s =
    match s with Some (Dot | Dollar) -> raise (Error "address") | _ -> s in
  let first = simple () in
  let rec steps () =
    match skipbl () with
    | ('+' | '-') as c ->
        incr ip;
        let s = later (simple ()) in
        ((if c = '+' then Fwd else Back), s) :: steps ()
    (* 3/re/ is 3+/re/: the + is implied *)
    | _ ->
        (match later (simple ()) with
         | Some s -> (Fwd, Some s) :: steps ()
         | None -> [])
  in
  match first, steps () with
  | None, [] -> None
  | first, steps -> Some { first; steps }

let rec compound () : addr option =
  let left = chain () in
  match skipbl () with
  | (',' | ';') as c ->
      incr ip;
      Some (Range ((if c = ',' then Comma else Semi), left, compound ()))
  | _ -> (match left with Some c -> Some (Chain c) | None -> None)

let rec parse () : cmd option =
  let addr = compound () in
  if skipbl () = '\000' then None
  else
    let c = getc () in
    let delim () =
      match skipbl () with
      | '\n' | '\000' -> raise (Error "no pattern")
      | c
        when (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
             || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') ->
          raise (Error ("bad delimiter `" ^ String.make 1 c ^ "'"))
      | _ -> getc ()
    in
    let text () =
      if skipbl () = '\n' then begin
        (* lines until "." *)
        incr ip;
        let b = Buffer.create 64 in
        let rec lines () =
          refill ();
          let e =
            match String.index_from_opt !input !ip '\n' with
            | Some e -> e
            | None -> String.length !input in
          let l = String.sub !input !ip (e - !ip) in
          ip := e + 1;
          if l <> "." && !ip <= String.length !input + 1
             && e < String.length !input
          then (Buffer.add_string b l; Buffer.add_char b '\n'; lines ())
        in
        lines ();
        Buffer.contents b
      end
      else
        (let d = getc () in
         let t = rhs d false in
         if peekc () = d then incr ip;
         atnl ();
         t)
    in
    let word () =
      ignore (skipbl ());
      let s = !ip in
      while peekc () <> '\n' && peekc () <> '\000' do incr ip done;
      let w = String.sub !input s (!ip - s) in
      atnl ();
      String.trim w in
    let sub () =
      match skipbl () with
      | '\n' -> incr ip; { addr = None; op = Print }
      | _ -> Option.get (parse ()) in
    let op =
      match c with
      | 'a' -> Text (After, text ())
      | 'i' -> Text (Before, text ())
      | 'c' -> Text (Instead, text ())
      | 'd' -> atnl (); Delete
      | 's' ->
          let n = num () in
          let d = delim () in
          let re = regexp d in
          let t = rhs d true in
          let g =
            if peekc () = d then
              (incr ip; if peekc () = 'g' then (incr ip; true) else false)
            else false in
          atnl ();
          Subst (n, re, t, g)
      | 'p' -> atnl (); Print
      | '=' ->
          let chars = peekc () = '#' in if chars then incr ip; atnl (); Eq chars
      | 'm' | 't' ->
          (match chain () with
           | Some a -> atnl (); Move (c = 'm', a)
           | None -> raise (Error "address"))
      | 'x' when (let n = peekc () in n = ' ' || n = '\t' || n = '\n') ->
          Loop (Lines, sub ())
      | 'x' | 'y' | 'g' | 'v' ->
          let re = regexp (delim ()) in
          let loop =
            match c with
            | 'x' -> Matches re
            | 'y' -> Between re
            | _ -> If (c = 'g', re) in
          Loop (loop, sub ())
      | '{' ->
          let rec cmds acc =
            if skipbl () = '\n' then incr ip;
            if skipbl () = '}' then (incr ip; atnl (); List.rev acc)
            else
              match parse () with
              | Some c -> cmds (c :: acc)
              | None -> raise (Error "missing }")
          in
          Block (cmds [])
      | 'r' -> File (Read, word ())
      | 'w' -> File (Write, word ())
      | 'e' -> File (Edit, word ())
      | 'f' -> File (Name, word ())
      | 'q' -> atnl (); Quit
      | 'u' ->
          let redo = skipbl () = '-' in
          if redo then incr ip;
          let n = num () in
          atnl ();
          Undo (if redo then -n else n)
      | '\n' -> Newline
      | c -> raise (Error ("unknown command `" ^ String.make 1 c ^ "'"))
    in
    Some { addr; op }

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The buffer, and changes made in parallel *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let text = ref "" and dot = ref (0, 0) and file = ref "" and modified = ref false
and warned = ref false
let changes : (int * int * string) list ref = ref []   (* reversed *)
let hi = ref 0      (* the changes so far end here: the next must not start before *)

let change p0 p1 s =
  if p0 < !hi then raise (Error "changes not in sequence");
  if p0 < p1 || s <> "" then changes := (p0, p1, s) :: !changes;
  hi := p1

(* the changes applied, and their inverse: in the new text, each
 * change's range replaced by the text it replaced, in order too *)
let commit () =
  let cs = List.rev !changes in
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length !text) and at = ref 0
  and delta = ref 0 in
  let inverse = List.map (fun (p0, p1, s) ->
    Buffer.add_string b (String.sub !text !at (p0 - !at));
    Buffer.add_string b s;
    at := p1;
    let q = p0 + !delta in
    delta := !delta + String.length s - (p1 - p0);
    (q, q + String.length s, String.sub !text p0 (p1 - p0))) cs in
  if cs <> [] then begin
    Buffer.add_string b (String.sub !text !at (String.length !text - !at));
    text := Buffer.contents b;
    modified := true;
    warned := false
  end;
  changes := [];
  hi := 0;
  inverse

(* a command's inverse, with what it changed besides the text, as it
 * was before it: sam's undo puts them back too. Dot is the one before
 * the command (sam's, the one when its first change was made: after an
 * x, the first match); a w makes every other state modified (sam's
 * menu says unmodified after an undo past a w) *)
type record = {
  edits : (int * int * string) list;
  rdot : int * int;
  rmodified : bool;
  rfile : string;
}
let undos : record list ref = ref [] and redos : record list ref = ref []
let before = ref { edits = []; rdot = (0, 0); rmodified = false; rfile = "" }
let now edits = { edits; rdot = !dot; rmodified = !modified; rfile = !file }

let apply () =
  match commit () with
  | [] -> ()
  | edits -> undos := { !before with edits } :: !undos; redos := []

(* u n: n records committed from one list, their inverses pushed on
 * the other, so that a redo is an undo undone *)
let undo n =
  if !changes <> [] then raise (Error "u after a change");
  let from, onto = if n > 0 then undos, redos else redos, undos in
  for _i = 1 to abs n do
    match !from with
    | [] -> ()
    | r :: rest ->
        from := rest;
        let saved = now [] in
        changes := List.rev r.edits;
        onto := { saved with edits = commit () } :: !onto;
        dot := r.rdot; modified := r.rmodified; file := r.rfile
  done

(* where old position p is after the changes before it *)
let shift p =
  List.fold_left (fun q (p0, p1, s) ->
    if p1 <= p then q + String.length s - (p1 - p0) else q) p !changes

(* the library's errors, as this file's *)
let compile p = try compile p with Failure m -> raise (Error m)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Addresses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let len () = String.length !text

(* address.c's lineaddr: line n, relative to (q0, q1) in direction sign *)
let lineaddr n (q0, q1) sign =
  let t = !text and nc = len () in
  if sign >= 0 then begin
    if n = 0 && (sign = 0 || q1 = 0) then (0, 0)
    else begin
      let p = ref 0 and start = ref 0 in
      if n = 0 then (start := q1; p := q1 - 1)
      else begin
        let k = ref 1 in
        if not (sign = 0 || q1 = 0) then
          (p := q1 - 1; k := (if t.[!p] = '\n' then 1 else 0); incr p);
        while !k < n do
          if !p >= nc then raise (Error "address range");
          if t.[!p] = '\n' then incr k;
          incr p
        done;
        start := !p
      end;
      (* to the end of that line, its newline included *)
      while !p < nc && (let c = t.[!p] in incr p; c <> '\n') do () done;
      (!start, !p)
    end
  end
  else begin
    let p = ref q0 and e = ref q0 in
    if n > 0 then begin
      let k = ref 0 in
      while !k < n do
        if !p = 0 then (incr k; if !k <> n then raise (Error "address range"))
        else if t.[!p - 1] <> '\n' || (incr k; !k <> n) then decr p
      done;
      e := !p;
      if !p > 0 then decr p
    end;
    while !p > 0 && t.[!p - 1] <> '\n' do decr p done;
    (!p, !e)
  end

(* nextmatch: a search from p, wrapping; an empty match right at p is
 * skipped *)
let next_match pat (q0, q1) forward =
  let re = compile pat in
  let t = !text in
  if forward then begin
    let find p =
      match search re t p (len ()) with
      | Some c -> Some c
      | None -> search re t 0 (len ()) in
    match find q1 with
    | None -> raise (Error "search")
    | Some c when c.(0) = c.(1) && c.(0) = q1 ->
        (match find (if q1 + 1 > len () then 0 else q1 + 1) with
         | Some c -> (c.(0), c.(1))
         | None -> raise (Error "search"))
    | Some c -> (c.(0), c.(1))
  end
  else begin
    let find p =
      match search_back re t p with
      | Some c -> Some c
      | None -> search_back re t (len ()) in
    match find q0 with
    | None -> raise (Error "search")
    | Some c when c.(0) = c.(1) && c.(1) = q0 ->
        (match find (if q0 - 1 < 0 then len () else q0 - 1) with
         | Some c -> (c.(0), c.(1))
         | None -> raise (Error "search"))
    | Some c -> (c.(0), c.(1))
  end

(* address.c's address(): a simple address, absolute (sign 0) or
 * relative to a in a direction (1 or -1) *)
let simple_address (s : simple) (a : int * int) (sign : int) : int * int =
  match s with
  | Chars n ->
      let q0, q1 = a in
      let r =
        if sign = 0 then (n, n)
        else if sign < 0 then (q0 - n, q0 - n)
        else (q1 + n, q1 + n) in
      if fst r < 0 || snd r > len () then raise (Error "address range");
      r
  | Line n -> lineaddr n a sign
  | Search (d, pat) ->
      next_match pat a (if d = Fwd then sign >= 0 else sign < 0)
  | Dot -> !dot
  | Dollar -> (len (), len ())

let chain_address (c : chain) (a : int * int) : int * int =
  let a = match c.first with Some s -> simple_address s a 0 | None -> a in
  List.fold_left (fun a (d, s) ->
    let sign = if d = Fwd then 1 else -1 in
    match s with
    | Some s -> simple_address s a sign
    | None -> lineaddr 1 a sign) a c.steps

let rec address (ad : addr) (a : int * int) : int * int =
  match ad with
  | Chain c -> chain_address c a
  | Range (sep, l, r) ->
      let a1 = match l with Some l -> chain_address l a | None -> (0, 0) in
      if sep = Semi then dot := a1;
      let a2 =
        match r with
        | Some r -> address r (if sep = Semi then a1 else a)
        | None -> (len (), len ()) in
      if snd a2 < fst a1 then raise (Error "address order");
      (fst a1, snd a2)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Running commands *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let out = Buffer.create 4096
let flush (caps : < Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >) =
  TinyLibSystem.print caps (Buffer.contents out);
  Buffer.clear out;
  TinyLibSystem.flush caps

let print_posn (q0, q1) chars =
  let t = !text in
  let count a b =
    let n = ref 0 in
    for i = a to b - 1 do if t.[i] = '\n' then incr n done;
    !n in
  if not chars then begin
    let l1 = 1 + count 0 q0 in
    let l2 =
      l1 + count q0 q1 - (if q1 > q0 && t.[q1 - 1] = '\n' then 1 else 0) in
    Buffer.add_string out
      (if l2 <> l1 then string_of_int l1 ^ "," ^ string_of_int l2 ^ "; "
       else string_of_int l1 ^ "; ")
  end;
  Buffer.add_string out
    (if q1 <> q0 then "#" ^ string_of_int q0 ^ ",#" ^ string_of_int q1 ^ "\n"
     else "#" ^ string_of_int q0 ^ "\n")

(* the file's line in sam's menu: ' when modified *)
let menu name = (if !modified then "'" else " ") ^ "-. " ^ name ^ "\n"

let read_file (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) name =
  if name = "" then None
  else try Some (TinyLibSystem.read_file caps name) with Failure _ -> None

let rec exec
    (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >)
    (c : cmd) : unit =
  let a =
    match c.addr, c.op with
    | None, File (Write, _) -> (0, len ())
    | None, _ -> !dot
    | Some ad, _ -> address ad !dot in
  let q0, q1 = a in
  match c.op with
  | Text (w, s) ->
      (* the range the text replaces *)
      let p0, p1 =
        match w with After -> q1, q1 | Before -> q0, q0 | Instead -> q0, q1 in
      change p0 p1 s;
      dot := (p0, p0 + String.length s)
  | Delete -> change q0 q1 ""; dot := (q0, q0)
  | Subst (n, pat, rep, g) ->
      let re = compile pat in
      let n = ref n and p = ref q0 and op = ref (-1) and did = ref false
      and delta = ref 0 in
      (try
         while !p <= q1 do
           match search re !text !p q1 with
           | None -> raise Exit
           | Some m ->
               let s, e = m.(0), m.(1) in
               if s = e && s = !op then incr p
               else begin
                 p := if s = e then e + 1 else e;
                 op := e;
                 decr n;
                 if !n <= 0 then begin
                   let b = Buffer.create 16 in
                   let i = ref 0 in
                   while !i < String.length rep do
                     (match rep.[!i] with
                      | '\\' when !i + 1 < String.length rep ->
                          incr i;
                          (match rep.[!i] with
                           | d when d >= '1' && d <= '9' ->
                               let g = Char.code d - 48 in
                               if m.(2 * g) >= 0 && m.((2 * g) + 1) >= 0 then
                                 Buffer.add_string b
                                   (String.sub !text m.(2 * g)
                                      (m.((2 * g) + 1) - m.(2 * g)))
                           | c -> Buffer.add_char b c)
                      | '&' -> Buffer.add_string b (String.sub !text s (e - s))
                      | c -> Buffer.add_char b c);
                     incr i
                   done;
                   change s e (Buffer.contents b);
                   delta := !delta + Buffer.length b - (e - s);
                   did := true;
                   if not g then raise Exit
                 end
               end
         done
       with Exit -> ());
      if not !did then raise (Error "substitution");
      dot := (q0, q1 + !delta)
  | Print -> Buffer.add_string out (String.sub !text q0 (q1 - q0)); dot := a
  | Eq chars -> print_posn a chars
  | Move (m, dest) ->
      let d = chain_address dest !dot in
      let s = String.sub !text q0 (q1 - q0) in
      let p = snd d in
      if m then begin
        (* claude: as sam's move: after the range, or before it (its
         * start included: 2m1 is allowed) *)
        if q1 <= p then (change q0 q1 ""; change p p s)
        else if q0 >= p then (change p p s; change q0 q1 "")
        else raise (Error "addresses overlap");
        dot :=
          (shift p - (if p >= q1 then q1 - q0 else 0),
           shift p - (if p >= q1 then q1 - q0 else 0) + String.length s)
      end
      else (change p p s; dot := (p, p + String.length s))
  | Loop (If (g, pat), sub) ->
      let found = search (compile pat) !text q0 q1 <> None in
      if found = g then (dot := a; exec caps sub)
  | Loop (Lines, sub) ->
      let p = ref q0 in
      while !p < q1 do
        let e =
          match String.index_from_opt !text !p '\n' with
          | Some e when e < q1 -> e + 1
          | _ -> q1 in
        dot := (!p, e);
        exec caps sub;
        p := e
      done
  | Loop (k, sub) ->
      (* looper(): x on each match, y on the text between (the two
       * other loops are the cases above; tiny-ml has no or-pattern
       * that binds a name, (Matches pat | Between pat)) *)
      let x, pat =
        match k with
        | Matches p -> true, p
        | Between p -> false, p
        | _ -> raise (Error "loop") in
      let re = compile pat in
      let p = ref q0 and op = ref (if x then -1 else q0) in
      (try
         while !p <= q1 do
           match search re !text !p q1 with
           | None ->
               if x || !op > q1 then raise Exit;
               dot := (!op, q1);
               p := q1 + 1;
               exec caps sub
           | Some m ->
               let s, e = m.(0), m.(1) in
               if s = e && s = !op then incr p
               else begin
                 p := if s = e then e + 1 else e;
                 dot := if x then (s, e) else (!op, s);
                 op := e;
                 exec caps sub
               end
         done
       with Exit -> ())
  | Block cmds -> List.iter (fun c -> dot := a; exec caps c) cmds
  | File (Read, name) -> (
      match read_file caps name with
      | Some s ->
          change q0 q1 s;
          dot := (q0, q0 + String.length s);
          Buffer.add_string out ("#" ^ string_of_int (String.length s) ^ "\n")
      | None -> raise (Error ("can't open " ^ name)))
  | File (Write, name) ->
      let name = if name = "" then !file else name in
      if name = "" then raise (Error "no file name");
      TinyLibSystem.write_file caps name (String.sub !text q0 (q1 - q0));
      if name = !file && q0 = 0 && q1 = len () then begin
        modified := false;
        let differ r = { r with rmodified = true } in
        undos := List.map differ !undos; redos := List.map differ !redos
      end;
      if !file = "" then file := name;
      Buffer.add_string out (name ^ ": ");
      if q1 > q0 && (!text).[q1 - 1] <> '\n' then
        (flush caps;
         TinyLibSystem.eprint caps "?warning: last char not newline\n");
      Buffer.add_string out ("#" ^ string_of_int (q1 - q0) ^ "\n")
  | File (Edit, name) ->
      let name = if name = "" then !file else name in
      (match read_file caps name with
       | Some s ->
           change 0 (len ()) s; apply (); file := name; dot := (0, 0);
           modified := false
       | None -> raise (Error ("can't open " ^ name)));
      Buffer.add_string out (menu name)
  | File (Name, name) ->
      if name <> "" then file := name; Buffer.add_string out (menu !file)
  | Quit ->
      if !modified && not !warned then
        (warned := true; raise (Error "changed files"));
      flush caps;
      TinyLibSystem.exit caps 0
  | Undo n -> undo n
  | Newline -> (
      (* the next line, or the line dot is in if it is not one *)
      match c.addr with
      | Some _ ->
          Buffer.add_string out (String.sub !text q0 (q1 - q0)); dot := a
      | None ->
          let b0, _ = lineaddr 0 !dot (-1) and _, b1 = lineaddr 0 !dot 1 in
          let r = if (b0, b1) = !dot then lineaddr 1 !dot 1 else (b0, b1) in
          Buffer.add_string out (String.sub !text (fst r) (snd r - fst r));
          dot := r)

let main (caps : Cap.all_caps) : int =
  next_line := (fun () -> TinyLibSystem.read_line caps);
  match TinyLibSystem.argv caps with
  | [ _; ("-h" | "--help") ] ->
      TinyLibSystem.print caps help; TinyLibSystem.flush caps; 0
  | argv ->
      (match argv with
       | [ _; name ] ->
           file := name;
           text := read_file caps name ||| "";
           Buffer.add_string out (menu name)
       | _ -> ());
      let rec loop () =
        (* a command, None at the end; or an error while it is read
         * (its message said, the rest of the line thrown away): None *)
        let read =
          try Some (parse ())
          with Error m ->
            flush caps;
            TinyLibSystem.eprint caps ("?" ^ m ^ "\n");
            while peekc () <> '\n' && peekc () <> '\000' do incr ip done;
            if peekc () = '\n' then incr ip;
            None in
        match read with
        | Some None -> ()
        | Some (Some c) ->
            (* an error while it runs: its changes are dropped *)
            before := now [];
            (try exec caps c; apply ()
             with Error m ->
               changes := [];
               hi := 0;
               flush caps;
               TinyLibSystem.eprint caps ("?" ^ m ^ "\n"));
            flush caps;
            loop ()
        | None -> loop () in
      loop ();
      if !modified && not !warned then
        (flush caps; TinyLibSystem.eprint caps "?changed files\n");
      flush caps;
      0

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-editor" main
tiny/TinyEditorLine.mli
8228
(* A tiny editor, in one file, that uses sam's command language rather
 * than ed's. mini-ed (editors/ed/) is a faithful copy of ed: a buffer
 * of lines, commands that apply to ranges of lines, and g to loop over
 * lines. This editor is what Rob Pike made of ed when he designed sam
 * ("The Text Editor sam", "Structural Regular Expressions", 1987), but
 * without the screen. The commands, with examples, and the usage are
 * the [help] string of the .ml, which is what ed -h prints.
 *
 * It is tiny-kernel's ed (and sam, the same program by another name):
 * as TinyShell.ml, it asks the system only through TinyLibSystem.
 *
 * Three ideas make it sam rather than ed, and they are the core of
 * this file:
 *
 * - {b The buffer is one string, and dot is a range of characters},
 *   not a line. A line is just one kind of address among others: 3 is
 *   the range covering the third line, including its newline; #10 is
 *   the empty range just before character 10; /re/ is the next match
 *   of re, wrapping around; a,b goes from the start of a to the end of
 *   b; a;b is the same, but dot is set to a before b is evaluated.
 * - {b Loops are commands that run over matches}: x/re/cmd runs cmd
 *   with dot set to each match of re inside dot, and y/re/cmd runs it
 *   on the text between the matches. g/re/cmd and v/re/cmd run cmd on
 *   dot as a whole, or not, depending on whether dot matches re. So
 *   ed's g/re/s/a/b/ becomes ,x/.*\n/g/re/s/a/b/, and loops can nest.
 * - {b Changes are made in parallel}: a command (including its loops)
 *   only records its changes, expressed against the text as it was
 *   when the command started, and all the changes are applied together
 *   at the end. So every address and every match in a loop sees the
 *   old text. The changes must come in order and must not overlap
 *   (otherwise the error is "changes not in sequence").
 *
 * Here are the three ideas at work on a file with the single line
 * "ab ab" and the command ,x/a/c/ba/ (in the whole file, replace each
 * a by ba):
 *
 *     the text before        a  b  _  a  b  \n       dot is #0,#6, set
 *                            0  1  2  3  4  5        by the comma address
 *     x finds the a's        #0,#1 and #3,#4, both in the old text
 *     c records a change     (0, 1, ba)   (3, 4, ba)        [change]
 *     for each match
 *     both applied at once   b  a  b  _  b  a  b  \n        [commit]
 *     their inverses, kept   (0, 2, a)    (4, 6, a)         for u
 *
 * A change is a triple (from, to, new text), where the positions refer
 * to the old text; its inverse is the same kind of triple, with
 * positions in the new text. If c had made its change immediately, the
 * second match would have been searched in a text already shifted by
 * the first change. Worse, a loop whose replacement contains its own
 * pattern (here ba contains a) could keep matching what it just wrote.
 *
 * What is dropped from sam: the screen; multiple files (the b B D n X
 * Y commands and addresses that name a file); the mark (k and its
 * address); ! < > |; and cd. In a few places sam sets dot oddly after
 * a loop or a move (the range of the first change after an x, an empty
 * range after t). Here dot is simply the text the command produced;
 * after u, dot is restored to what it was before the undone command.
 *
 * {b Undo is cheap for the same reason}: a command's changes are a
 * list against the old text, so their inverse (for each change, its
 * range in the new text and the text it replaced) is also a list, and
 * is applied the same way ([commit]). Undoing pushes the inverse of
 * the inverse, so a redo is just an undo that is undone. The regexp
 * matcher is TinyLibRegex's, which grep uses too: a small backtracker
 * that returns the leftmost-longest match like sam's, with a memo of
 * (node, position) pairs. libregexp gives different answers in some
 * corner cases (see lib_core's Regex.mli, which mini-ed uses).
 *
 * The original is principia's editors/sam/ (mini-ed's is editors/ed/):
 * its parallel changes are file.c's log, the changes a command makes
 * kept aside and applied together at its end, as undo applies its own.
 * [commit] is the same trick on a list of triples; sam pages its text
 * and its logs to a temporary file, where here the text is one string.
 *
 * Exercises. Each is cheap because a command's changes are a list,
 * made against the old text and applied together:
 * - several files: one buffer and one dot per file, addresses that
 *   name a file ("name"), and X/re/cmd and Y/re/cmd that run cmd in
 *   each file whose name matches re, or does not (as in sam);
 * - | < > (as in sam): send dot to a command, replace dot by a
 *   command's output, or both. This is a change like any other, so it
 *   composes with x;
 * - store the buffer as a piece table (as Bravo, then Word did) or as
 *   a rope: a change then no longer copies the whole text, and undo
 *   gets to keep the old pieces for free;
 * - several dots instead of one: keep the matches of an x as a set of
 *   selections, and run the next command on each of them (the editing
 *   model of Kakoune and vis, which grew out of sam's x).
 *
 * Where it stands: ix has three editors, mini-ed (lines, an editor for
 * a teletype), this one (ranges, but still no screen) and mini-emacs
 * (with a screen). Recording changes and then applying them in one step is the same
 * idea as a statement in TinyDatabase and a command in TinyVCS:
 * nothing is ever half done, and undoing is cheap.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The line as the unit of editing comes from the teletype. QED
 * (Butler Lampson and Peter Deutsch, Berkeley, 1960s) addressed lines
 * because a terminal printed lines. Ken Thompson's QED for CTSS added
 * regular expressions, compiled to machine code (his 1968 paper), and
 * his ed (1969) is a cut-down QED for the first Unix. Every Unix tool
 * that reads one line at a time (grep, whose name comes from ed's
 * g/re/p, sed, awk) inherited that unit. Rob Pike wrote sam in the
 * 1980s for the Blit, a terminal with a bitmap display and a mouse.
 * Once text is selected by sweeping the mouse over it, there is no
 * reason for a selection to be whole lines, and the command language
 * was designed to work on whatever the mouse can select.
 *
 * others:
 * Acme (Pike, 1994), Plan 9's other editor, kept sam's language as a
 * single command, Edit. Kakoune and vis turned sam's x into their
 * whole way of editing: every command works on a set of selections,
 * which x and y refine. vi and Emacs kept lines and a single point,
 * and loop by repeating a command or a macro. sed and awk are the loop
 * over lines turned into a program of its own.
 *
 * modern:
 * The buffer here is an OCaml string, rebuilt entirely by each command
 * that changes it: a one-megabyte file means a megabyte copied for
 * each character typed. An editor with a screen cannot afford this.
 * Emacs uses a gap buffer (free space kept at the place where one
 * types); Word and VS Code use a piece table (the original file is
 * never changed, and the text is a list of pieces of it and of what
 * was typed); others use a rope (a tree of strings). The third
 * exercise above is one of these.
 *
 * References:
 *  - Rob Pike, "The Text Editor sam" (Software -- Practice and
 *    Experience, 1987): the command language, addresses as character
 *    ranges, and applying a command's changes together at its end
 *  - Rob Pike, "Structural Regular Expressions" (EUUG, 1987): x and y,
 *    loops over matches rather than over lines, with ed's g becoming
 *    one loop among others
 *  - C. Crowley, "Data Structures for Text Sequences" (1998): the
 *    piece table
 *  - H. Boehm, R. Atkinson, M. Plass, "Ropes: an Alternative to
 *    Strings" (Software -- Practice and Experience, 1995)
 *)

(* a command, parsed: its address, its letter, what follows *)
type cmd

(* one command, done: its address found from dot, then the changes it
 * makes, all of them applied together at its end *)
val exec :
  < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.exit; .. > -> cmd -> unit

(* the program: the files named, then the commands of its input *)
val main : Cap.all_caps -> int
