(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyEditorScreen.mli *)

(* With no system calls, the editor is tested on the host by typing keys
 * at it (tests/TinyEditorScreen_test.sh). *)

open TinyLibPlayground

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The editor *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the text is its lines, cut at the cursor's: the ones above it, the
 * nearest first, the cursor's own, the ones below. A key changes the
 * cursor's line, or moves one line from a list to the other *)
type text = {
  mutable above : string list;
  mutable line : string;
  mutable below : string list;
  mutable col : int;             (* the cursor, in its line: 0 to its length *)
  mutable row : int;             (* the cursor's line, from 0: above's length *)
  mutable goal : int;            (* the column C-n and C-p go back to *)
  mutable modified : bool;
}

(* what is typed on the last line, after a prompt: M-x's command, and
 * the answers some commands ask for *)
type answer = Command | Goto | Replace_from | Replace_to of string

(* the language of the file, by its name: its colors *)
type language = Plain | OCaml | C

(* the last line's other uses, and the keys the editor gives itself *)
type extra = {
  language : language;
  mutable search : string option;         (* C-s typed: the text looked for *)
  mutable reading : (answer * string) option;
    (* a prompt, and what is typed after it *)
  mutable recording : int list option;
    (* C-x ( typed: the keys since, the last first *)
  mutable macro : int list;               (* the last macro, for C-x e *)
  mutable queue : int list;
    (* keys to give back: a macro's, a command's *)
  mutable lexed : (string * int) list;
    (* the lines above the screen, each with the comments open at its end *)
  mutable faced : (string * int * string * int) list;
    (* the screen's: a line, the comments open before and after, its faces *)
  mutable pieced : (string * string * int * shape) list;
    (* the screen's lines as shapes: a line, its faces, the cursor's column
     * in it, its shape *)
}

(* (three records: tiny-ml makes one of 11 fields at most on
 * tiny-machine) *)
type editor = {
  t : text;
  mutable top : int;             (* the first line shown *)
  mutable killed : string;       (* what C-k took, for C-y *)
  mutable killing : bool;
    (* the last key was C-k: the next adds to killed *)
  file : string;
  mutable quitting : bool;       (* a quit was refused: the next is done *)
  mutable message : string;      (* the last line of the screen *)
  mutable prefix : int;
    (* C-x or Escape typed, waiting for its key; or 0 *)
  x : extra;
  cols : int;
  rows : int;
    (* the screen: the last two lines are not the text's *)
}

(* what a key asks of the program around the editor *)
type request = Continue | Save | Quit

let language_of (file : string) : language =
  let n = String.length file in
  let ends suffix =
    let m = String.length suffix in
    n >= m && String.sub file (n - m) m = suffix in
  if ends ".ml" || ends ".mli" then OCaml
  else if ends ".c" || ends ".h" then C
  else Plain

let create (cols : int) (rows : int) (file : string) (text : string) : editor =
  let first, rest =
    match String.split_on_char '\n' text with l :: r -> l, r | [] -> "", [] in
  let t =
    { above = []; line = first; below = rest; col = 0; row = 0; goal = 0;
      modified = false } in
  (* (the inner record made first: tiny-ml computes a record's fields
   * in tiny-machine's 11 registers, and both are 19) *)
  let x =
    { language = language_of file; search = None; reading = None;
      recording = None; macro = []; queue = []; lexed = []; faced = [];
      pieced = [] } in
  { t; top = 0; killed = ""; killing = false; file; quitting = false;
    message = ""; prefix = 0; x; cols; rows }

(* (a text that ends by a newline has an empty last line, which is
 * where one types after it: the lines joined by newlines are the text) *)
let lines (e : editor) : string list =
  List.rev e.t.above @ (e.t.line :: e.t.below)

let saved (e : editor) = e.t.modified <- false; e.message <- "Wrote " ^ e.file
let say (e : editor) (message : string) = e.message <- message

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Moving *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let up (t : text) =
  match t.above with
  | [] -> false
  | l :: rest ->
      t.below <- t.line :: t.below; t.line <- l; t.above <- rest;
      t.row <- t.row - 1; true

let down (t : text) =
  match t.below with
  | [] -> false
  | l :: rest ->
      t.above <- t.line :: t.above; t.line <- l; t.below <- rest;
      t.row <- t.row + 1; true

let forward (t : text) =
  if t.col < String.length t.line then t.col <- t.col + 1
  else if down t then t.col <- 0
let backward (t : text) =
  if t.col > 0 then t.col <- t.col - 1
  else if up t then t.col <- String.length t.line

(* n lines down, or up when n is negative; the column the goal, as far
 * as the line goes. (C-v and Escape v move the cursor a screen, and
 * the lines shown with it) *)
let move (t : text) (n : int) =
  for _i = 1 to n do ignore (down t) done;
  for _i = 1 to - n do ignore (up t) done;
  t.col <- min t.goal (String.length t.line)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Changing *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let before (t : text) = String.sub t.line 0 t.col
let after (t : text) = String.sub t.line t.col (String.length t.line - t.col)

(* a text without a newline, at the cursor *)
let insert (t : text) (s : string) =
  t.line <- before t ^ s ^ after t;
  t.col <- t.col + String.length s;
  t.modified <- true

let newline (t : text) =
  t.above <- before t :: t.above;
  t.line <- after t;
  t.row <- t.row + 1;
  t.col <- 0;
  t.modified <- true

(* the character at the cursor; at a line's end, the line below joined *)
let delete (t : text) =
  if t.col < String.length t.line then begin
    t.line <-
      before t ^ String.sub t.line (t.col + 1) (String.length t.line - t.col - 1);
    t.modified <- true
  end else
    match t.below with
    | [] -> ()
    | l :: rest -> t.line <- t.line ^ l; t.below <- rest; t.modified <- true

let backspace (t : text) =
  if t.col > 0 || t.above <> [] then (backward t; delete t)

(* C-k: the rest of the line; at its end, the newline. Several in a
 * row are one text for C-y *)
let kill (e : editor) (again : bool) =
  let t = e.t in
  let took =
    if t.col < String.length t.line then after t
    else if t.below = [] then ""
    else "\n" in
  if took = "\n" then delete t
  else if took <> "" then (t.line <- before t; t.modified <- true);
  e.killed <- (if again then e.killed ^ took else took);
  e.killing <- true

let yank (e : editor) =
  List.iteri (fun i piece -> if i > 0 then newline e.t; insert e.t piece)
    (String.split_on_char '\n' e.killed)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Searching *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* where sub is in s at from or after; -1 *)
let find (sub : string) (s : string) (from : int) : int =
  let n = String.length s and m = String.length sub in
  let rec same i j = j >= m || (s.[i + j] = sub.[j] && same i (j + 1)) in
  let rec go i = if i + m > n then - 1 else if same i 0 then i else go (i + 1) in
  go (max from 0)

(* the cursor after the next sub, from a column of its line on, then in
 * the lines below; a message when there is none (view says "Failing") *)
let look (e : editor) (sub : string) (from : int) =
  let t = e.t in
  let i = find sub t.line from in
  if i >= 0 then t.col <- i + String.length sub
  else begin
    let rec go n = function
      | [] -> None
      | l :: rest ->
          let i = find sub l 0 in
          if i >= 0 then Some (n, i) else go (n + 1) rest in
    match go 1 t.below with
    | Some (n, i) ->
        for _i = 1 to n do ignore (down t) done;
        t.col <- i + String.length sub
    | None -> e.message <- "Failing search: " ^ sub
  end

(* a key while searching: a character more to look for (from where what
 * is found starts), C-s the next one, Backspace a character less; any
 * other key ends the search, and Enter and C-g do nothing more *)
let searching (e : editor) (sub : string) (k : int) : bool =
  let m = String.length sub in
  if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
    (let sub = sub ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr k) in
     e.x.search <- Some sub; look e sub (e.t.col - m); true)
  else if k = 19 then (look e sub e.t.col; true)
  else if k = 8 || k = 127 then
    (e.x.search <- Some (String.sub sub 0 (max 0 (m - 1))); true)
  else (e.x.search <- None; k = 10 || k = 13 || k = 7)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* M-x *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the commands by their names in Emacs, each the keys it is: M-x
 * types them. goto-line and replace-string have no key: they are
 * M-x's own (answered) *)
let commands = [
  "forward-char", "\006"; "backward-char", "\002"; "next-line", "\014";
  "previous-line", "\016";
  "move-beginning-of-line", "\001"; "move-end-of-line", "\005";
  "scroll-up-command", "\022"; "scroll-down-command", "\027v";
  "beginning-of-buffer", "\027<"; "end-of-buffer", "\027>";
  "delete-char", "\004"; "delete-backward-char", "\127"; "newline", "\n";
  "kill-line", "\011"; "yank", "\025"; "recenter-top-bottom", "\012";
  "isearch-forward", "\019"; "keyboard-quit", "\007";
  "save-buffer", "\024\019"; "save-buffers-kill-terminal", "\024\003";
  "start-kbd-macro", "\024("; "end-kbd-macro", "\024)";
  "call-last-kbd-macro", "\024e";
  "execute-extended-command", "\027x";
  "goto-line", ""; "replace-string", "";
]

let prompt = function
  | Command -> "M-x "
  | Goto -> "Goto line: "
  | Replace_from -> "Replace string: "
  | Replace_to from -> "Replace string " ^ from ^ " with: "

(* Tab: what is typed made as long as all the names it starts agree *)
let complete (typed : string) : string =
  match
    List.filter (fun c -> String.starts_with typed c) (List.map fst commands)
  with
  | [] -> typed
  | first :: rest ->
      let rec common a b i =
        if i < String.length a && i < String.length b && a.[i] = b.[i] then
          common a b (i + 1)
        else i in
      String.sub first 0
        (List.fold_left (fun n c -> min n (common first c 0))
           (String.length first) rest)

(* s with each from replaced by to_, and how many were *)
let rec replace (from : string) (to_ : string) (s : string) : string * int =
  let i = find from s 0 and m = String.length from in
  if i < 0 then s, 0
  else
    (let rest, n =
       replace from to_ (String.sub s (i + m) (String.length s - i - m)) in
     String.sub s 0 i ^ to_ ^ rest, n + 1)

(* Enter after a prompt: what is typed done *)
let rec answered (e : editor) (what : answer) (typed : string) =
  let t = e.t in
  match what with
  | Command -> (
      match
        List.assoc_opt typed commands,
        List.filter (fun c -> String.starts_with typed c) (List.map fst commands)
      with
      | _ when typed = "goto-line" -> e.x.reading <- Some (Goto, "")
      | _ when typed = "replace-string" -> e.x.reading <- Some (Replace_from, "")
      | Some keys, _ ->
          e.x.queue <-
            List.init (String.length keys) (fun i -> Char.code keys.[i])
            @ e.x.queue
      | None, [ name ] when typed <> "" -> answered e Command name
      | _ -> e.message <- "No command: " ^ typed)
  | Goto -> (
      match int_of_string_opt typed with
      | Some n -> t.goal <- 0; move t (n - 1 - t.row)
      | None -> e.message <- "Not a line: " ^ typed)
  | Replace_from ->
      if typed = "" then e.message <- "Nothing to replace"
      else e.x.reading <- Some (Replace_to typed, "")
  | Replace_to from ->
      (* from the cursor to the end: the line's rest, the lines below *)
      let rest, n = replace from typed (after t) in
      let below = List.map (fun l -> replace from typed l) t.below in
      let n = List.fold_left (fun n (_, k) -> n + k) n below in
      if n > 0 then
        (t.line <- before t ^ rest; t.below <- List.map fst below;
         t.modified <- true);
      e.message <- "Replaced " ^ string_of_int n ^ " occurrences"

(* a key after a prompt: a character more, Backspace one less, Tab a
 * command's name completed, Enter done, C-g never mind *)
let reading (e : editor) (what : answer) (typed : string) (k : int) =
  let m = String.length typed in
  if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
    e.x.reading <- Some (what, typed ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr k))
  else if k = 8 || k = 127 then
    e.x.reading <- Some (what, String.sub typed 0 (max 0 (m - 1)))
  else if k = 9 && what = Command then e.x.reading <- Some (what, complete typed)
  else if k = 7 then (e.x.reading <- None; e.message <- "Quit")
  else if k = 10 || k = 13 then (e.x.reading <- None; answered e what typed)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Macros *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* C-x ( C-x ) C-x e. The keys are recorded as they come, C-x ( and
 * the C-x ) that ends them left out, and C-x e gives them back through
 * the queue, read before what is typed: a macro does what its keys
 * did, a save included. C-x e while recording ends the macro first, as
 * in Emacs *)
let macro (e : editor) (k : int) =
  match k, e.x.recording with
  | 40, None -> e.x.recording <- Some []; e.message <- "Defining kbd macro..."
  | 40, Some _ -> e.message <- "Already defining kbd macro"
  | (41 | 101), Some (_ :: _ :: l) ->
      e.x.macro <- List.rev l; e.x.recording <- None;
      if k = 41 then e.message <- "Keyboard macro defined"
      else e.x.queue <- e.x.macro @ e.x.queue
  | 41, _ -> e.message <- "Not defining kbd macro"
  | _ ->
      if e.x.macro = [] then e.message <- "No kbd macro has been defined"
      else e.x.queue <- e.x.macro @ e.x.queue

(* the next key the editor gives itself, before one typed *)
let pending (e : editor) : int option =
  match e.x.queue with k :: rest -> e.x.queue <- rest; Some k | [] -> None

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The keys *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a key is a byte: a character, a control character (C-a is 1), and
 * tiny-machine's arrows, 128 to 131: up, down, left, right *)
let key (e : editor) (k : int) : request =
  let t = e.t and again = e.killing and quitting = e.quitting
  and h = e.rows - 2 in
  e.killing <- false;
  e.quitting <- false;
  e.message <- "";
  let request = ref Continue and vertical = ref false in
  let lines n = vertical := true; move t n in
  (match e.x.recording with
   | Some l -> e.x.recording <- Some (k :: l)
   | None -> ());
  (match e.x.reading, e.x.search with
   | Some (what, typed), _ -> reading e what typed k
   | _, Some sub when searching e sub k -> ()
   | _ ->
       let prefix = e.prefix in
       e.prefix <- 0;
       if prefix = 24 then begin
         (* C-x C-s; C-x C-q and C-x C-c; C-x ( ) e, the macros *)
         if k = 19 then request := Save
         else if k = 40 || k = 41 || k = 101 then macro e k
         else if k = 17 || k = 3 then begin
           if t.modified && not quitting then
             (e.quitting <- true;
              e.message <- "Not saved: C-x C-s saves, C-x C-q again quits")
           else request := Quit
         end else e.message <- "C-x: not a command"
       end else if prefix = 27 then begin
         (* Escape, then < > v x: Meta *)
         if k = 60 then lines (- t.row)
         else if k = 120 then e.x.reading <- Some (Command, "")
         else if k = 62 then lines (List.length t.below)
         else if k = 118 then (lines (1 - h); e.top <- max 0 (e.top - (h - 1)))
         else e.message <- "Escape: not a command"
       end
       else if k = 1 then t.col <- 0
       else if k = 5 then t.col <- String.length t.line
       else if k = 6 || k = 131 then forward t
       else if k = 2 || k = 130 then backward t
       else if k = 14 || k = 129 then lines 1
       else if k = 16 || k = 128 then lines (- 1)
       else if k = 22 then (lines (h - 1); e.top <- min (e.top + h - 1) t.row)
       else if k = 4 then delete t
       else if k = 8 || k = 127 then backspace t
       else if k = 10 || k = 13 then newline t
       else if k = 11 then kill e again
       else if k = 25 then yank e
       else if k = 12 then e.top <- max 0 (t.row - h / 2)
       else if k = 19 then e.x.search <- Some ""
       else if k = 7 then e.message <- "Quit"
       else if k = 24 || k = 27 then e.prefix <- k
       else if k = 9 || (k >= 32 && k < 127) then
         insert t (String.make 1 (Char.chr k))
       else e.message <- "Not a command");
  if not !vertical then t.goal <- t.col;
  !request

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a line as it is shown: a tab is the spaces to the next column that
 * is a multiple of 8 *)
let shown (s : string) : string =
  if not (String.contains s '\t') then s
  else begin
    let pieces = String.split_on_char '\t' s in
    List.fold_left (fun acc p ->
      acc ^ String.make (8 - String.length acc mod 8) ' ' ^ p)
      (List.hd pieces) (List.tl pieces)
  end

(* the column of the screen where a line's character is *)
let column (s : string) (col : int) : int =
  let rec go i c =
    if i >= col then c
    else go (i + 1) (if s.[i] = '\t' then (c / 8 + 1) * 8 else c + 1) in
  go 0 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Colors *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let keywords = function
  | OCaml ->
      [ "and"; "as"; "assert"; "begin"; "class"; "do"; "done"; "downto";
        "else"; "end"; "exception"; "external"; "false"; "for"; "fun";
        "function"; "functor"; "if"; "in"; "include"; "lazy"; "let";
        "match"; "method"; "module"; "mutable"; "new"; "object"; "of";
        "open"; "or"; "private"; "rec"; "sig"; "struct"; "then"; "to";
        "true"; "try"; "type"; "val"; "virtual"; "when"; "while"; "with" ]
  | C ->
      [ "auto"; "break"; "case"; "char"; "const"; "continue"; "default";
        "do"; "double"; "else"; "enum"; "extern"; "float"; "for"; "goto";
        "if"; "int"; "long"; "register"; "return"; "short"; "signed";
        "sizeof"; "static"; "struct"; "switch"; "typedef"; "union";
        "unsigned"; "void"; "volatile"; "while";
        "uchar"; "ushort"; "ulong"; "vlong"; "uvlong"; "nil" ]
  | Plain -> []

(* whether p is in s at i (a character at a time: no string made) *)
let at (s : string) (i : int) (p : string) =
  let m = String.length p in
  let rec same k = k >= m || (s.[i + k] = p.[k] && same (k + 1)) in
  i + m <= String.length s && same 0

(* the text: its lines with a newline between two *)
let text (e : editor) : string = String.concat "\n" (lines e)

(* the end of a string or a character of s, from i after its opening
 * quote q *)
let rec closing (s : string) (q : char) (i : int) : int =
  if i >= String.length s then String.length s
  else if s.[i] = '\\' then closing s q (i + 2)
  else if s.[i] = q then i + 1
  else closing s q (i + 1)

(* a character of a name; OCaml's names have quotes too, x' *)
let alnum (ocaml : bool) (c : char) =
  (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
  || c = '_' || (ocaml && c = '\'')

(* [lex language keep s depth]: the face of each of s's characters, a
 * string as long as s: k a keyword (and C's #include...), c a comment, s a
 * string or a character, . the rest; depth is how many comments are
 * open at the line's start, and the result's second part at its end
 * (OCaml's nest, C's do not: 0 or 1). A string or a character ends
 * with its line: one of OCaml's that goes on below is colored wrong.
 * Without keep, only the comments open at the end are counted, and the
 * faces are "": the lines above the screen.
 * (The helpers are outside: tiny-ml loads each value a closure takes,
 * in tiny-machine's 11 registers) *)
let lex (language : language) (keep : bool) (s : string) (depth : int)
    : string * int =
  let n = String.length s and ocaml = language = OCaml in
  let opens = if ocaml then "(*" else "/*"
  and closes = if ocaml then "*)" else "*/" in
  (* the faces in runs, the last first: a face and how many characters *)
  let runs = ref [] in
  let put face k =
    if keep then
      match !runs with
      | (f, m) :: rest when f = face -> runs := (f, m + k) :: rest
      | l -> runs := (face, k) :: l in
  let rec go i depth =
    if i >= n then depth
    else if depth > 0 then begin
      if ocaml && at s i opens then (put 'c' 2; go (i + 2) (depth + 1))
      else if at s i closes then (put 'c' 2; go (i + 2) (depth - 1))
      else (put 'c' 1; go (i + 1) depth)
    end
    else if at s i opens then (put 'c' 2; go (i + 2) 1)
    else if (not ocaml) && at s i "//" then (put 'c' (n - i); 0)
    else if s.[i] = '"' then
      (let j = min n (closing s '"' (i + 1)) in put 's' (j - i); go j 0)
    (* a character, 'a' or '\n'; in OCaml a quote is also 'a, a type's
     * variable, and the end of x' *)
    else if s.[i] = '\'' && (at s (i + 2) "'" || at s (i + 1) "\\") then
      (let j = min n (closing s '\'' (i + 1)) in put 's' (j - i); go j 0)
    else if alnum ocaml s.[i] || ((not ocaml) && s.[i] = '#') then begin
      let rec stop j =
        if j < n && alnum ocaml s.[j] then stop (j + 1) else j in
      let j = stop (i + 1) in
      put
        (if keep
            && (s.[i] = '#'
                || List.mem (String.sub s i (j - i)) (keywords language))
         then 'k' else '.')
        (j - i);
      go j 0
    end
    else (put '.' 1; go (i + 1) 0)
  in
  let depth = go 0 depth in
  String.concat ""
    (List.fold_left (fun acc (f, k) -> String.make k f :: acc) [] !runs),
  depth

(* the lines' first column shown: 0, unless the cursor would be out *)
let left (e : editor) =
  let c = column e.t.line e.t.col in if c < e.cols then 0 else c - e.cols + 1

let rec take n l =
  match l with x :: rest when n > 0 -> x :: take (n - 1) rest | _ -> []

(* the screen's lines: the text's that fit (the ones shown follow the
 * cursor), a line that says the file and where the cursor is, and the
 * last one, a message or what is being typed *)
let view (e : editor) : string list =
  let t = e.t and h = e.rows - 2 in
  if t.row < e.top then e.top <- t.row
  else if t.row >= e.top + h then e.top <- t.row - h + 1;
  let l = left e and y = t.row - e.top in
  let cut s =
    let s = shown s in
    let n = String.length s in
    if l >= n then "" else String.sub s l (min e.cols (n - l)) in
  let text =
    List.map cut
      (List.rev (take y t.above) @ (t.line :: take (h - 1 - y) t.below)) in
  let text = text @ List.init (h - List.length text) (fun _ -> "") in
  let mode =
    "-- " ^ e.file ^ (if t.modified then " (modified)" else "")
    ^ " -- L" ^ string_of_int (t.row + 1) ^ " C" ^ string_of_int t.col
    ^ (if e.x.recording <> None then " Def " else " ") in
  let mode =
    if String.length mode < e.cols then
      mode ^ String.make (e.cols - String.length mode) '-'
    else String.sub mode 0 e.cols in
  let last =
    match e.x.reading, e.x.search with
    | Some (what, typed), _ -> prompt what ^ typed
    | None, Some sub ->
        (if e.message = "" then "" else "Failing ") ^ "I-search: " ^ sub
    | None, None ->
        if e.prefix = 24 then "C-x-"
        else if e.prefix = 27 then "ESC-"
        else e.message in
  text @ [ mode; String.sub last 0 (min e.cols (String.length last)) ]

(* the faces of view's text lines (its first rows - 2), each a string
 * as long as the line shown (lex's letters); none for a file of no
 * language. After view, which sets the first line shown.
 *
 * The comments open at that line are counted from the text's start.
 * So that a key does not read again the hundreds of lines above, each
 * line read is kept with the comments open at its end (lexed): a line
 * that is the very same string as the one kept at its place, all those
 * before it the same too, is not read again. A line changed is a new
 * string (a key makes one), and from it on the lines are read again.
 * The lines on the screen are kept too, with their faces (faced): a
 * line down scrolls the screen, and 21 of 22 lines are the same.
 * (old: all the lines above read at each key; goto-line 382 in
 * TinyEditorScreen.ml took more than 150 million instructions, 20
 * seconds of tiny-machine) *)
let faces (e : editor) : string list =
  if e.x.language = Plain then []
  else begin
    let h = e.rows - 2 and l = left e and language = e.x.language in
    let cut f =
      let n = String.length f in
      if l >= n then "" else String.sub f l (min e.cols (n - l)) in
    let rec skip i depth lines kept acc =
      match lines with
      | line :: rest when i < e.top ->
          let d, kept = match kept with
            | (l, d) :: more when l == line -> d, more
            | _ -> snd (lex language false (shown line) depth), [] in
          skip (i + 1) d rest kept ((line, d) :: acc)
      | rest -> e.x.lexed <- List.rev acc; depth, rest in
    let depth, rest = skip 0 0 (lines e) e.x.lexed [] in
    let old = e.x.faced in
    let rec go k depth = function
      | line :: rest when k < h ->
          let f, after =
            match
              List.filter (fun (l, d, _, _) -> l == line && d = depth) old
            with
            | (_, _, f, after) :: _ -> f, after
            | [] -> lex language true (shown line) depth in
          (line, depth, f, after) :: go (k + 1) after rest
      | _ -> [] in
    e.x.faced <- go 0 depth rest;
    List.map (fun (_, _, f, _) -> cut f) e.x.faced
  end

(* where the cursor is on the screen: its column, its line; after a
 * prompt, on the last line *)
let cursor (e : editor) : int * int =
  match e.x.reading with
  | Some (what, typed) ->
      min (e.cols - 1) (String.length (prompt what ^ typed)), e.rows - 1
  | None -> column e.t.line e.t.col - left e, e.t.row - e.top

(* The screen as shapes (TinyLibPlayground's), for a program that draws
 * it: its first n lines, each a group of pieces of one colour, cut at the
 * cursor too, so that a key changes a piece or two (TinyLibGUI draws
 * again only what changed, and of words at the same place only their
 * end); then the cursor's cell, white on black. Colours of the
 * machine's palette: Emacs's purple keywords (128), dark red comments
 * (160), green strings (8). After view and faces' screen. *)
let colour_of (face : char) =
  if face = 'k' then 128
  else if face = 'c' then 160
  else if face = 's' then 8
  else 0

let face_at (f : string) (k : int) = if k < String.length f then f.[k] else '.'

(* line i's pieces from column k on, the last first on acc *)
let rec pieces (i : int) (l : string) (f : string) (cut : int) (k : int) acc =
  let n = String.length l in
  if k >= n then acc
  else begin
    let c = face_at f k in
    let rec stop j =
      if j < n && j <> cut && face_at f j = c then stop (j + 1) else j in
    let j = stop (k + 1) in
    pieces i l f cut j
      (Move (8 * k, 16 * i, Words (colour_of c, String.sub l k (j - k))) :: acc)
  end

(* (a line's shape is kept, and given again, the very same, while its
 * text, its faces and the cursor's column in it are the same: what
 * draws it does not look into it again, TinyLibGUI's repaint) *)
let shapes (e : editor) (n : int) : shape list =
  let lines = view e in
  let fs = faces e and (cx, cy) = cursor e in
  let rec go i lines fs olds =
    match lines with
    | l :: rest when i < n ->
        let f, fs = match fs with f :: more -> f, more | [] -> "", [] in
        let cut = if i = cy then cx else -1 in
        let old, olds =
          match olds with o :: more -> Some o, more | [] -> None, [] in
        let g = match old with
          | Some (l', f', cut', g) when cut' = cut && l' = l && f' = f -> g
          | _ -> Group (List.rev (pieces i l f cut 0 [])) in
        (l, f, cut, g) :: go (i + 1) rest fs olds
    | _ -> [] in
  e.x.pieced <- go 0 lines fs e.x.pieced;
  let shown = List.map (fun (_, _, _, g) -> g) e.x.pieced in
  let line = if cy < List.length lines then List.nth lines cy else "" in
  let c = if cx < String.length line then String.sub line cx 1 else " " in
  shown
  @ (if cy < n then
       [ Move (8 * cx, 16 * cy, Group [ Rect (0, 8, 16); Words (255, c) ]) ]
     else [])
tiny/TinyEditorScreen.mli
6191
(* A tiny screen editor, in one file: the text on the screen, a cursor
 * in it, and the keys of Emacs.
 *
 * Its full-size counterpart in m-ix is
 * mini-emacs (editors/emacs/), with buffers, windows, modes and a
 * Lisp. tiny-editor (TinyEditorLine.ml) is the line editor, with sam's
 * command language and no screen. This one is what you want for
 * changing a program: one text, one window, and what you type goes
 * where the cursor is.
 *
 * mini-emacs is written after efuns (Fabrice Le Fessant's Emacs in
 * OCaml, 1998): its text a gap buffer (its Text), a key looked up in
 * keymaps, each key a command, a function on the editor's structure.
 * This one keeps Emacs's keys and their names, but a key
 * is a case of [key]'s match, with no keymap; a command's name is
 * only the keys it stands for (M-x below); the text is lines (below).
 *
 * The text is stored as its lines, split at the line of the cursor:
 *
 *     above    the lines before the cursor's line, nearest first
 *     line     the cursor's line, with col, the cursor's position in it
 *     below    the lines after it
 *
 * So typing a character creates only one new string, for the current
 * line, whatever the size of the text, and moving down a line moves
 * one string from one list to the other. (Emacs keeps a gap in a
 * single array of characters, at the place of the last change, for
 * the same reason. A list of lines split at the cursor is the same
 * idea, built from what tiny-ml has: lists, and strings that cannot
 * be modified.)
 *
 * The editor is a state plus the keys that change it. [key] takes a
 * byte and says what it asks of the surrounding program (nothing, to
 * save the file, or to quit). [view] computes the lines of the screen
 * for a state; it is recomputed after each key, and the screen redraws
 * only the lines that changed. The editor uses no system calls: the
 * surrounding program reads the keys, displays the lines and writes
 * the file. That program is tiny-kernel's emacs
 * (TinyKernel/user/emacs.ml). There are no terminal escape sequences:
 * the screen is tiny-machine's, where a program draws characters
 * wherever it wants.
 *
 * The keys, as in Emacs:
 *
 *     C-f C-b C-n C-p, the arrows    a character, a line
 *     C-a C-e                        the line's start, its end
 *     C-v, Escape v                  a screen down, up
 *     Escape <, Escape >             the text's start, its end
 *     C-d, Backspace                 the character at, before the cursor
 *     C-k, C-y                       the line's rest taken, put back
 *     C-s                            search, as it is typed; C-s the next
 *     C-l                            the cursor's line in the middle
 *     C-x C-s, C-x C-c (or C-x C-q)  save, quit
 *     C-g                            never mind
 *     M-x (Escape x, or Alt-x)       a command by its name, Tab completing
 *     C-x (, C-x ), C-x e            a macro started, ended, done again
 *
 * M-x knows each of these keys by its name in Emacs (kill-line,
 * save-buffer...), and two commands that have no key and ask on the
 * last line what they need: goto-line, and replace-string, from the
 * cursor to the end. A command is the keys it is: M-x kill-line gives
 * the editor a C-k.
 *
 * A macro is the keys typed between C-x ( and C-x ). C-x e gives them
 * again to the editor, which reads them before the keys typed
 * ([pending]): a macro does all its keys did, a search, a save, an
 * M-x. That is what a macro is in Emacs, a keyboard macro: no language,
 * the keys only.
 *
 * A file of OCaml or of C is in colors: its keywords, its comments
 * and its strings ([faces]). Each line is read on its own, but for the
 * comments, which may go on for several lines (OCaml's nest): how many
 * are open at the first line shown is counted from the text's start.
 * A string over several lines, or a C macro continued by a backslash,
 * is colored wrong; Emacs's modes get them right, with much more.
 *
 * What is left out: multiple buffers and windows, undo, the mark and
 * the region, searching backward, replacing with a question at each,
 * a macro's count (C-u), wrapping long lines (a long line is cut at
 * the edge of the screen, and the screen scrolls to follow the
 * cursor), and characters beyond ASCII.
 *)

type editor

(* [create cols rows file text]: an editor of the text, the cursor at
 * its start, on a screen of that size; file is its name, to show *)
val create : int -> int -> string -> string -> editor

(* what a key asks of the program around the editor *)
type request = Continue | Save | Quit

(* a key, a byte: a character, a control character (C-a is 1), and
 * tiny-machine's arrows, 128 to 131 (up, down, left, right) *)
val key : editor -> int -> request

(* a key the editor gives itself, a macro's or an M-x command's: the
 * program around gives it to [key] before the next one typed *)
val pending : editor -> int option

(* the screen: rows lines of at most cols characters, the last two a
 * line on the file and the cursor's place, and a message *)
val view : editor -> string list

(* the colors of view's text lines (its first rows - 2), for a file
 * whose name ends in .ml, .mli, .c or .h: each a string as long as its
 * line, a letter a character, k a keyword, c a comment, s a string or
 * a character, . the rest; [] for another file. After view *)
val faces : editor -> string list

(* [shapes e n]: the screen's first n lines as shapes, for a program
 * that draws it (emacs): each line a group of its pieces of one colour,
 * cut at the cursor too, so that a key changes a piece or two; then the
 * cursor's cell, white on black *)
val shapes : editor -> int -> TinyLibPlayground.shape list

(* where the cursor is on that screen: its column, its line *)
val cursor : editor -> int * int

(* the text, its lines with a newline between two: what is saved *)
val text : editor -> string

(* the text's lines, to write with a newline between two *)
val lines : editor -> string list

(* the program around has written the file *)
val saved : editor -> unit

(* a message, on the screen's last line until the next key *)
val say : editor -> string -> unit

(* See TinyKernelAudio.mli *)

(* OCaml builds this file too, on the host, where its sounds are tested
 * without a machine (tests/TinyKernelAudio_tests/Host.ml) *)

open TinyMemory

let per_ms = 8

(* Fixed point, and no division in a sample (tiny-machine divides by a
 * routine, a hundred instructions): the phase is in 65,536ths of a
 * period, to which a sample adds its step; the step is in 256ths of
 * those (a Hz is 8.192 of them a sample), so that a slide moves it a
 * little at each sample; the amplitude is in 65,536ths, and its first
 * 16 samples rise from nothing (2 ms: a sound that starts at its full
 * volume clicks). A noise is a random value at each period, by a
 * congruential generator. *)
let mix ring size at wave hz to_hz n volume =
  let n = max 1 n in
  let step0 = hz * 8192 / 1000 * 256 in
  let dstep = ((to_hz * 8192 / 1000 * 256) - step0) / n in
  let damp = volume * 65536 / n in
  let phase = ref 0 and step = ref step0 and amp = ref (volume * 65536)
  and noise = ref 1 in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    let v = if i < 16 then ((!amp lsr 16) * i) lsr 4 else !amp lsr 16 in
    let q = !phase land 0xffff in
    let x =
      if wave = 0 then (if q < 32768 then v else - v)
      else if wave = 1 then (
        let t = (q * 4 * v) lsr 16 in
        if t < 2 * v then t - v else (3 * v) - t)
      else if wave = 2 then ((q * 2 * v) lsr 16) - v
      else ((((!noise lsr 16) land 255) * 2 * v) lsr 8) - v in
    let r = ring + ((at + i) land (size - 1)) in
    let b = peekb r in
    let y = (if b > 127 then b - 256 else b) + x in
    pokeb r ((if y > 127 then 127 else if y < -128 then -128 else y) land 255);
    let next = (!phase + (!step lsr 8)) land 0xffffff in
    if next lsr 16 <> !phase lsr 16 then
      noise := ((!noise * 69069) + 1) land 0xffffff;
    phase := next;
    step := !step + dstep;
    amp := !amp - damp
  done

(* a sound of a message: a tone (a wave, a pitch from and to, its
 * samples, a volume), or samples *)
type sound = Tone of int * int * int * int * int | Samples of string

let sound_length snd =
  match snd with Tone (_, _, _, n, _) -> n | Samples s -> String.length s

(* samples added to the ring as a tone's are *)
let add_samples ring size at s =
  for i = 0 to String.length s - 1 do
    let r = ring + ((at + i) land (size - 1)) in
    let b = peekb r and x = Char.code s.[i] in
    let y = (if b > 127 then b - 256 else b) + (if x > 127 then x - 256 else x) in
    pokeb r ((if y > 127 then 127 else if y < -128 then -128 else y) land 255)
  done

let mix_sound ring size at snd =
  match snd with
  | Tone (wave, hz, to_hz, n, volume) -> mix ring size at wave hz to_hz n volume
  | Samples s -> add_samples ring size at s

exception Bad_sound

(* a tone's message is 11 bytes: s, then five numbers of 16 bits, the
 * low byte first (TinyLibDraw's); samples' is p, their number, then
 * them *)
let sounds s =
  let num i = Char.code s.[i] + (256 * Char.code s.[i + 1]) in
  let rec from i =
    if i = String.length s then []
    else if i + 3 <= String.length s && s.[i] = 'p'
            && i + 3 + num (i + 1) <= String.length s then
      Samples (String.sub s (i + 3) (num (i + 1))) :: from (i + 3 + num (i + 1))
    else if i + 11 > String.length s || s.[i] <> 's' then raise Bad_sound
    else begin
      let wave = num (i + 1) and hz = num (i + 3) and to_hz = num (i + 5)
      and ms = num (i + 7) and volume = num (i + 9) in
      if wave > 3 || hz > 4000 || to_hz > 4000 || ms > 1000 || volume > 127 then
        raise Bad_sound;

      Tone (wave, hz, to_hz, ms * per_ms, volume) :: from (i + 11)
    end in
  from 0
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelAudio.mli
4071
(* Tiny sound: TinyKernel.ml's part that makes the samples
 * (plan_tiny_audio.md), as TinyKernelGraphics.ml is its part that
 * makes the pixels. It asks two functions of its machine's bytes,
 * TinyMemory's peekb and pokeb.
 *
 * {b The kernel has the samples, a program says what}, as for the
 * screen: a program writes a message to /dev/audio, `s wave hz to_hz ms
 * volume` (a letter, then numbers of 16 bits, TinyLibDraw's), and the
 * kernel adds the sound to tiny-machine's ring, where the other
 * programs' sounds are already. A sound is sfxr's recipe (lib_audio's
 * Sfx.mli) cut to those five numbers: a wave, a pitch that slides, a
 * volume that falls to nothing at the end:
 *
 *       volume
 *         |\                   a square from 784 Hz, 60 ms:
 *         | \                  480 samples, each +v or -v, v
 *         |  \                 falling from the volume to 0
 *         |   \
 *         +----+---> time
 *         0    ms
 *
 * Why not samples written by the program, as Plan 9's /dev/audio and
 * m-ix's take them: a game's sound is a recipe, and made by tiny-ml's
 * code it was 2,750 instructions a sample (before tiny-ml had Bytes: a
 * string and a cons for each), the 0.7 s of Tetris's game over two
 * seconds of an 8 MHz machine. Here a sample is made where it is
 * played, with no allocation (about 230 instructions, a square's, 260 a
 * triangle's; 535 while its clamp was the prelude's min and max, each
 * a call of the runtime's compare), and a sound crosses a pipe as 11
 * bytes, not 5,600. A tune of two parts is 3.9 million instructions a
 * second: half of an 8 MHz machine, a fifth of a window's 20. Samples
 * are a message too (`p`), for what is no recipe: a WAV played
 * (TinyPlay.ml).

 *
 * Its twins are mini-9pi's /dev/audio (kernels/9pi/'s Devaudio, Plan
 * 9's audio(3)) and lib_audio: there the device takes samples only, 16
 * bits, two ears, 44,100 a second, and one program at a time (an open
 * while another has it fails, Einuse, as in principia's devaudio.c),
 * and a program mixes and makes its sounds itself, by lib_audio's Sfx
 * and Mixer. Ours: the recipe and the mixing moved into the kernel, so
 * each open of /dev/audio is a voice and several programs are heard at
 * once; a byte a sample, one ear, 8,000 a second, which a game's beeps
 * and a melody need and no more.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * This is a sound chip's bargain: the Atari 2600's TIA (1977), General
 * Instrument's AY-3-8910 (1978), the Commodore 64's SID (1982), the
 * NES's APU (1983) each had a few voices, a wave, a pitch, an envelope,
 * and a program set their registers instead of making samples, which
 * those CPUs could not afford. Samples came when CPUs could (the
 * Amiga's Paula, 1985, still with four voices mixed by the chip; the
 * PC's Sound Blaster, 1989), and a game's sound effects stayed sfxr's
 * few numbers. tiny-machine is one of those CPUs again.
 *)

(* the samples a millisecond (8,000 a second) *)
val per_ms : int

(* [mix ring size at wave hz to_hz n volume]: a sound of n samples added
 * to the ring of [size] samples at [ring] (size a power of two), from
 * the sample numbered [at] (the ring's place: at modulo size), each
 * sum kept from -128 to 127. The wave: 0 a square, 1 a triangle, 2 a
 * sawtooth, 3 noise; the pitch from hz to to_hz, a volume 0 to 127. *)
val mix : int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> unit

(* A message's sound: a tone (wave, hz, to_hz, samples, volume, as
 * [mix]'s), or samples, a byte each, signed, 8,000 a second (`p n`
 * then the n bytes, as /dev/draw's row of pixels: what is no recipe, a
 * file's sound); its length in samples; added to a ring as [mix] adds *)
type sound = Tone of int * int * int * int * int | Samples of string
val sound_length : sound -> int
val mix_sound : int -> int -> int -> sound -> unit

(* The sounds of messages, each `s wave hz to_hz ms volume` or `p n`
 * and n samples; Bad_sound when one is not a whole message or says
 * something out of range *)
exception Bad_sound
val sounds : string -> sound list
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelCalls.ml
26217
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyKernelCalls.mli *)
open TinyMemory
open TinyKernelGraphics
open TinyKernelNetwork
open TinyKernelFS
open TinyKernelMemory
open TinyKernelMachine
open TinyKernelFiles
open TinyKernelProcs
open TinyKernelDevices
open TinyKernelIO

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The system calls *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a call that may wait: tried now, and until it finishes by the
 * scheduler, the process Waiting meanwhile *)
let block p attempt =
  if not (attempt ()) then (p.state <- Waiting attempt; p.since <- -1)

let result p v = set_reg p 1 v

(* A buffer in one piece is given to the device as it is: the user's
 * memory, at the kernel's address (every buffer, with partitions; asked
 * by mem_address, which allocates nothing: mem_pieces's list at each
 * read and write slowed the kernel enough to reorder the check's last
 * lines, an echo in the background before rc's prompt). One
 * in several pieces goes through the kernel's own, the bounce (640 KB
 * at 0xb60000, TinyKernel.mli's layout), which a device sees as one:
 * a write's bytes copied in before, a read's copied back after, at
 * each try (a call that waits is tried again, and the bounce is
 * another's meanwhile). At most the bounce's size, so a read or a
 * write may do less than asked, as Unix lets them. Linux and xv6 copy
 * every call's buffer that way (copy_from_user, copyin) *)
let bounce = 0xb60000
let bounce_size = 0xa0000

let sys_rw p rw reading =
  let f = fd p (reg p 1) and va = reg p 2 and n = reg p 3 in
  if reading && not (mem_writable p.mem va n) then raise Bad;
  let finish = function Some k -> result p k; true | None -> false in
  let a = mem_address p.mem va n in
  if a >= 0 then block p (fun () -> finish (rw f a n))
  else begin
    let n = min n bounce_size in
    block p (fun () ->
      if not reading then
        user_iter p va n (fun a off k -> row_copy (bounce + off) a k);
      let r = rw f bounce n in
      (match r with
       | Some k when reading && k > 0 ->
           user_iter p va k (fun a off k -> row_copy a (bounce + off) k)
       | _ -> ());
      finish r)
  end

(* its descriptors closed, its children orphans (the records of those
 * that ended dropped), the processes it traces let go, its end said to
 * its tracer; its slot and its memory free, its status a record for
 * its parent's wait (Procs.ended). The first process's end is the
 * machine's *)
let rec exit_proc p status =
  incr deaths;
  List.iter (fun (_, f) -> drop f) p.fds;
  p.fds <- [];
  List.iter (fun q ->
    match q.traced with
    | Some t when t.tracer = p.pid -> detach t
    | _ -> ()) !procs;
  (match p.traced with
   | Some t -> t.said <- t.said @ [ "exited " ^ string_of_int status ^ "\n" ]
   | None -> ());
  List.iter (fun q -> if q.parent = p.pid then q.parent <- 0) !procs;
  ended := List.filter (fun (parent, _, _) -> parent <> p.pid) !ended;
  if p.pid = 1 then halt status;
  if p.parent <> 0 then ended := !ended @ [ (p.parent, p.pid, status) ];
  release p

and release q =
  mem_release q.mem;
  procs := List.filter (fun r -> r.pid <> q.pid) !procs

(* fork: a new slot and a partition of the parent's size, the partition
 * and the frame copied (the child's r1 0), the descriptors shared; the
 * child has none of its parent's breakpoints, their words put back in
 * its copy. It is traced by its parent's tracer when the parent's
 * children are (f), stopping at its calls if the parent does: the
 * tracer's trace(pid) gives the descriptor, its stops kept till then *)
(* A call that needs a slot or a partition: done now or, when there is none,
 * waited for while another process can run (and end, freeing one):
 * what a build of several recipes at once runs into (tiny-build -j 6:
 * six compilers of 32 MB). When none can, -1 (old: -1 at once, and
 * rc said "not found"). Tried again when a process has ended, as a
 * wait (old: at each round, a walk of the slots: with a build's forks
 * waiting, a round was longer than a tick, every process entered with
 * its time already up, and none ran an instruction) *)
let with_room p f =
  try f () with No_room ->
    block p (fun () ->
      try f (); true with
      | No_room ->
          if List.exists (fun q ->
               q.pid <> p.pid && (match q.state with Ready -> true | _ -> false))
               !procs
          then false
          else (result p (-1); true)
      | Bad -> result p (-1); true);
    match p.state with Waiting _ -> p.since <- !deaths | _ -> ()

(* a child of p's, in slot s: its descriptors and directory p's; traced
 * when p's children are; its pid the next *)
let child p s = {
  slot = s; mem = mem_empty (); pid = !next_pid; state = Ready;
  parent = p.pid; fds = p.fds; cwd = p.cwd; since = -1; traced = None;
  core = -1; doomed = false; cmd = p.cmd; memory = p.memory;
}

(* the child made a process: its trace if p's children are traced, its
 * descriptors shared, its place at the end of the round, its pid p's
 * answer *)
let adopt p q =
  incr next_pid;
  (match p.traced with
   | Some t when t.follow ->
       q.traced <- Some { t with tpid = q.pid; stops = []; said = [];
                                 watchers = 0; call = -1; ret = -1;
                                 step = false; over = -1 }
   | _ -> ());
  List.iter (fun (_, f) -> share f) p.fds;
  procs := !procs @ [ q ];
  result p q.pid

let sys_fork p = with_room p (fun () ->
  let q = child p (free_slot ()) in
  mem_copy q.mem p.mem;
  k_copy (frame q.slot) (frame p.slot) 68;
  (match p.traced with
   | Some t -> List.iter (fun (a, w) -> mem_store q.mem a w) t.stops
   | None -> ());
  set_reg q 1 0;
  adopt p q)

(* A program's file is either a raw image, run in 1 MB, or an a.out: a
 * header of three words (a magic number, the image's size, the memory
 * the program asks for), then the image (tiny-linker -a), and maybe its
 * labels, for debug (-s), which are not loaded. With tiny-linker -n, a
 * fourth word, the text's size, and another magic number. This returns
 * where the image starts in the file, its size, the memory, and the
 * text's size (0: none). *)
let aout_magic = 0x7a0ce5
let aout_split = 0x7a0ce6
let header bytes =
  let word i =
    String.get_uint16_le bytes i
    + (String.get_uint16_le bytes (i + 2) lsl 16) in
  let n = String.length bytes in
  if n >= 12 && word 0 = aout_magic then Some (12, word 4, word 8, 0)
  else if n >= 16 && word 0 = aout_split then Some (16, word 4, word 8, word 12)
  else None

(* a file of the disk as a program's, to share its text (TinyKernelMemory's
 * key; its stamp is its date and size) *)
let disk_key r i = "disk " ^ string_of_int r ^ " " ^ string_of_int i

(* Loads a file's program into p, in a partition of the size it asks for
 * (rounded up to whole megabytes), from address 0. Its arguments are put
 * as tiny-cpu leaves them (the strings at the top, then argc, argv and
 * argv's pointers: start.tm's); every register is 0 but sp. Bad if it is
 * no program, or one that leaves no room for a stack, or if there is no
 * room for its partition; in that case p is left as it was. *)
let load_prog p node argv =
  (* (an image's file never changes; a file of memory is not shared) *)
  let key, date =
    match node with
    | Some (Rom (at, _)) -> "rom " ^ string_of_int at, ""
    | Some (Disk (r, i)) -> disk_key r i, string_of_int (fs_date r i)
    | _ -> "", "" in
  let node =
    match node with
    | Some (Disk (r, i)) -> Some (Data (data (fs_contents r i)))
    | _ -> node in
  let n =
    match node with
    | Some (Data d) -> d.dsize
    | Some (Rom (_, n)) -> n
    | _ -> raise Bad in
  let first =
    match node with
    | Some (Data d) -> Bytes.sub_string d.dbytes 0 (min n 16)
    | Some (Rom (at, _)) -> k_string at (min n 16)
    | _ -> "" in
  let skip, size, memory, tsize = match header first with
    | Some (h, size, memory, tsize)
      when size <= n - h && tsize <= size && tsize land 4095 = 0 ->
        h, size, (memory + part - 1) / part * part, tsize
    | _ -> 0, n, part, 0 in
  if size > memory - 0x10000 || memory > mem_high - mem_low then raise Bad;
  (* the text written only when it is not shared already *)
  let stamp = if date = "" then "" else date ^ " " ^ string_of_int n in
  let from = if mem_load p.mem key stamp tsize size memory then 0 else tsize in
  (* Only the image is written, its statics in it (tiny-linker writes a
   * .space as zeros); the rest of the
   * partition, the stack and the heap, is left as the last process to
   * have it left it, as no program reads a word it has not written
   * (the ML runtime's stack of values and heap, libc's heap a static
   * array). It is the same at each run, but it shows the bytes of
   * another process to this one: to revisit for security, as Plan 9
   * and Linux give a page zeroed at its first touch (they have pages;
   * tiny-machine a window). (old: k_zero of the whole partition, 32 MB
   * for ml, 35 million instructions an exec: a fifth of a small unit's
   * compile) *)
  (match node with
   | Some (Data d) ->
       mem_write p.mem from
         (Bytes.sub_string d.dbytes (skip + from) (size - from))
   | Some (Rom (at, _)) -> mem_blit p.mem from (at + skip + from) (size - from)
   | _ -> ());
  let top = ref memory and ptrs = ref [] in
  List.iter (fun s ->
    top := (!top - String.length s - 1) land lnot 3;
    mem_write p.mem !top s;
    (* (its end, a 0: old, the zeros of the partition, zeroed whole) *)
    mem_store_byte p.mem (!top + String.length s) 0;
    ptrs := !ptrs @ [ !top ]) argv;
  let sp = (!top - ((List.length argv + 3) * 4)) land lnot 7 in
  mem_store p.mem sp (List.length argv);
  mem_store p.mem (sp + 4) (sp + 8);
  ignore (List.fold_left (fun at a -> mem_store p.mem at a; at + 4) (sp + 8)
            !ptrs);
  k_zero (frame p.slot) 68;
  set_reg p 14 sp;
  p.cmd <- String.concat " " argv;
  p.memory <- memory

(* exec's and spawn's (path, argv): the program's file, its arguments
 * (64 at most: a linker's line names its objects; old: 16) *)
let program p =
  let node = walk !top (names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1))) in
  let rec args i acc =
    if i >= 64 then raise Bad
    else
      let a = peek (user p (reg p 2 + (4 * i)) 4) in
      if a = 0 then List.rev acc else args (i + 1) (ustr p a :: acc) in
  node, args 0 []

(* exec(path, argv): the program and its arguments are all read before
 * the partition is changed, so a failed exec returns. A traced process
 * stops at its new program's first instruction, its breakpoints gone
 * with the old one *)
let sys_exec p =
  let node, argv = program p in
  with_room p (fun () ->
    load_prog p node argv;
    match p.traced with Some t -> t.stops <- []; stop p "exec" | None -> ())

(* spawn(path, argv): a fork and an exec in one, a child that starts
 * in the program; its pid, or -1. Nothing of the parent is copied: a
 * fork copies the parent's whole partition (16 MB for tiny-build, at
 * each recipe) for the exec to throw it away a moment later. What a
 * child does between the two (a dup, a close) the parent does around
 * the spawn: the child has the parent's descriptors at the spawn *)
let sys_spawn p =
  let node, argv = program p in
  with_room p (fun () ->
    let q = child p (free_slot ()) in
    load_prog q node argv;
    adopt p q)

(* wait(&status): a child's end, its record taken (the child itself
 * was freed when it ended); -1 without children, ended or not *)
let sys_wait p =
  let a = reg p 1 in
  if a <> 0 then ignore (user_out p a 4);
  block p (fun () ->
    match List.filter (fun (parent, _, _) -> parent = p.pid) !ended with
    | (_, pid, s) :: _ ->
        if a <> 0 then poke (user_out p a 4) s;
        ended := List.filter (fun (_, q, _) -> q <> pid) !ended;
        result p pid;
        true
    | [] ->
        if List.exists (fun q -> q.parent = p.pid) !procs then false
        else (result p (-1); true));
  (* (a shell waits most of its life: its call is retried when a process
   * ended, not at each turn) *)
  (match p.state with Waiting _ -> p.since <- !deaths | _ -> ())

let o_create = 0x200
let o_trunc = 0x400

let sys_open p =
  let ns = names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1)) and mode = reg p 2 in
  let writes = mode land 3 <> 0 in
  let node =
    match walk !top ns, dir_of ns with
    | Some n, _ -> n
    | None, Some (Dir d, last)
      when mode land o_create <> 0 && String.length last <= 64 ->
        let n = Data { (data "") with dtime = date () } in
        d := !d @ [ last, n ];
        n
    | None, Some (Disk (0, i), last)
      when mode land o_create <> 0 && String.length last <= 64 ->
        Disk (0, fs_create i last 2)
    | _ -> raise Bad in
  (* (a file of the image opened to be written is in memory from now on;
   * or a file of the disk, when its directory is there too: /bin's) *)
  let node =
    match node, dir_of ns with
    | Rom (at, n), Some (Disk (0, i), last) when writes ->
        let j = fs_create i last 2 in
        if mode land o_trunc = 0 then fs_write_at j 0 at n;
        Disk (0, j)
    | Rom (at, n), Some (Dir d, last) when writes ->
        let made =
          Data { (data (if mode land o_trunc <> 0 then "" else k_string at n))
                 with dtime = date () } in
        d := List.map (fun (name, old) ->
          if name = last then name, made else name, old) !d;
        made
    | _ -> node in
  (* (a file of the disk written: no exec shares the text it had) *)
  (match node with
   | Disk (r, i) when writes -> mem_forget (disk_key r i)
   | _ -> ());
  (* (a snapshot is read only) *)
  (match node with
   | Dir _ when writes -> raise Bad
   | Disk (r, i) when writes && (r <> 0 || fs_is_dir r i) -> raise Bad
   | Data d when mode land o_trunc <> 0 ->
       d.dbytes <- Bytes.make 0 ' '; d.dsize <- 0; d.dtime <- date ()
   | Disk (_, i) when writes && mode land o_trunc <> 0 -> fs_truncate i
   | _ -> ());
  result p (fdalloc p (match node with
    | Tty -> Console
    | Screen -> Draw { conn = connect screen font; refs = 1 }
    | Pointer -> Peek mouse
    | Speaker -> Voice { ahead = (played () + lead) land 0x3fffffff }
    | _ -> Open { node = node; off = 0; writes = writes; listing = None }))

let sys_close p =
  let k = reg p 1 in
  drop (fd p k);
  p.fds <- List.filter (fun (j, _) -> j <> k) p.fds;
  result p 0

(* pipe(fds) and box(fds): the two ends, a descriptor each, put in fds *)
let ends p r w =
  let a = user_out p (reg p 1) 4 and b = user_out p (reg p 1 + 4) 4 in
  let r = fdalloc p r in
  let w = fdalloc p w in
  poke a r;
  poke b w;
  result p 0

let sys_pipe p =
  let pi = { buf = ""; readers = 1; writers = 1 } in
  ends p (Reader pi) (Writer pi)

(* a box, its reading end and its writing end *)
let sys_box p =
  let b = { last = ""; fresh = false; posters = 1 } in
  ends p (Peek b) (Post b)

(* dial(address, port): a descriptor on a connection to the program
 * that listens on that port of the machine at that address
 * ("10.0.0.1"), when it has agreed; -1 when nothing does or nothing
 * answers. Port 0 is the echo: a link, made at once *)
let sys_dial p =
  let to_ = net_address (ustr p (reg p 1)) and port = reg p 2 in
  if to_ = "" || port < 0 || port > 0xffff || peek (net_dev + 12) = 0 then
    raise Bad;
  if port = 0 then begin
    let l = { peer = to_; lid = !next_link; asked = 0; heard = []; holders = 1 } in
    incr next_link;
    links := l :: !links;
    result p (fdalloc p (Link l))
  end
  else begin
    let c, sync = net_dial net to_ port !ticks in
    net_send sync;
    block p (fun () ->
      match c.il_at with
      | Il_established ->
          (try result p (fdalloc p (Call { il = c; callers = 1 }))
           with Bad -> il_done c; result p (-1));
          true
      | Il_closed -> result p (-1); true
      | _ -> false)
  end

(* listen(port): a descriptor on the next connection another machine
 * makes to that port of this one, which is listened on from the first
 * call (and stays so: a server is this call in a loop) *)
let sys_listen p =
  let port = reg p 1 in
  if port <= 0 || port > 0xffff || peek (net_dev + 12) = 0 then raise Bad;
  if not (List.mem port net.ns_ports) then
    net.ns_ports <- port :: net.ns_ports;
  block p (fun () ->
    match List.filter (fun c -> c.il_lport = port) net.ns_fresh with
    | c :: _ ->
        net.ns_fresh <-
          List.filter (fun d ->
            d.il_lport <> port || d.il_rport <> c.il_rport
            || d.il_peer <> c.il_peer) net.ns_fresh;
        (try result p (fdalloc p (Call { il = c; callers = 1 }))
         with Bad -> il_done c; result p (-1));
        true
    | [] -> false)

let sys_dup p = let f = fd p (reg p 1) in share f; result p (fdalloc p f)

let sys_mkdir p =
  let ns = names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1)) in
  match walk !top ns, dir_of ns with
  | None, Some (Dir d, last) when String.length last <= 64 ->
      d := !d @ [ last, Dir (ref []) ]; result p 0
  | None, Some (Disk (0, i), last) when String.length last <= 64 ->
      ignore (fs_create i last 1); result p 0
  | _ -> raise Bad

(* a name removed; a directory only if empty *)
let sys_unlink p =
  match dir_of (names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1))) with
  | Some (Dir d, last) ->
      (match List.assoc_opt last !d with
       | Some (Dir e) when !e <> [] -> raise Bad
       | Some (Disk _) -> raise Bad
       | Some _ -> d := List.filter (fun (n, _) -> n <> last) !d; result p 0
       | None -> raise Bad)
  | Some (Disk (0, i), last) ->
      (match fs_lookup 0 i last with
       | 0 -> raise Bad
       | j when fs_is_dir 0 j && fs_entries 0 j <> [] -> raise Bad
       | _ -> fs_unlink i last; result p 0)
  | _ -> raise Bad

(* link(old, new): a second name for a file, in the directory new is in:
 * the same node, so a write by either name is seen by the other (a file
 * of the image, Rom, is copied when it is first written, under the name
 * it is written by: then the names part). Not for a directory, as on
 * Unix: a directory with two parents would make the tree a graph *)
let sys_link p =
  let old = walk !top (names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1)))
  and ns = names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 2)) in
  match old, walk !top ns, dir_of ns with
  | Some n, _, _ when is_dir n -> raise Bad
  | Some (Disk (0, j)), None, Some (Disk (0, i), last)
    when String.length last <= 64 ->
      fs_link i last j; result p 0
  | Some (Disk _), _, _ -> raise Bad
  | Some node, None, Some (Dir d, last) when String.length last <= 64 ->
      d := !d @ [ last, node ]; result p 0
  | _ -> raise Bad

(* getcwd(buf, n): the current directory's path, ended by a 0, in the n
 * bytes at buf; its length, -1 when it does not fit *)
let sys_getcwd p =
  let path =
    if p.cwd = [] then "/"
    else List.fold_left (fun acc n -> acc ^ "/" ^ n) "" p.cwd in
  let n = String.length path in
  if n + 1 > reg p 2 then raise Bad;
  user_write p (reg p 1) (path ^ "\000");
  result p n

(* rawcons(on): the console raw for this process, while it lives (on
 * 1), or not (on 0). An editor's C-x C-c: ^C a key like the others.
 * Plan 9's rawon, written to /dev/consctl (which also stops the echo
 * and the line editing: tiny-kernel's console has neither) *)
let sys_rawcons p = raw := (if reg p 1 <> 0 then p.pid else 0); result p 0

(* kill(pid): its process ended as a fault ends one, its status -1; on
 * another core, at its next trap, which the cores' interrupt makes
 * now (its partition is not another's before) *)
let kill q =
  if q.core > 0 then (q.doomed <- true; poke ipi_dev q.core)
  else exit_proc q (-1)
let sys_kill p =
  match List.filter (fun q -> q.pid = reg p 1) !procs with
  | [ q ] -> kill q; result p 0
  | _ -> raise Bad

(* trace(pid): a descriptor on a process, for its tracer (debug): what is
 * written to it a command, what is read the answers and the process's
 * stops (command, stop). trace(0): the caller traced by its parent from
 * now on, so that it stops at its next exec, the way a debugger starts
 * a program; the parent's trace(pid) gives the descriptor, before or
 * after. Not for the first process, the caller itself, or a process
 * another one traces *)
let sys_trace p =
  let make q tracer =
    let t =
      { tpid = q.pid; tracer = tracer; stops = []; said = []; watchers = 0;
        calls = false; call = -1; ret = -1; step = false; over = -1;
        follow = false } in
    q.traced <- Some t;
    t in
  if reg p 1 = 0 then begin
    (match p.traced with
     | Some t -> if t.tracer <> p.parent then raise Bad
     | None -> if p.parent = 0 then raise Bad else ignore (make p p.parent));
    result p 0
  end
  else
    match List.filter (fun q ->
      q.pid = reg p 1 && q.pid <> p.pid && q.pid <> 1) !procs with
    | [ q ] ->
        let t =
          match q.traced with
          | Some t when t.tracer = p.pid -> t
          | None -> make q p.pid
          | _ -> raise Bad in
        let given () =
          let k = fdalloc p (Trace t) in
          t.watchers <- t.watchers + 1;
          result p k in
        (* on another core: called back (a traced process stays on core
         * 0), the descriptor given when it is back, its frame then its
         * registers *)
        if q.core > 0 then
          (poke ipi_dev q.core; block p (fun () -> q.core <= 0 && (given (); true)))
        else given ()
    | _ -> raise Bad

(* seek(fd, n, whence): a file's offset at n from its start (0), from
 * where it is (1) or from its end (2), as Plan 9's; the new offset *)
let sys_seek p =
  match fd p (reg p 1) with
  | Open o ->
      let size =
        match o.node with
        | Rom (_, n) -> n
        | Data d -> d.dsize
        | Disk (r, i) -> let _, n, _ = fs_kind r i in n
        | n -> String.length (contents n) in
      let off =
        reg p 2
        + (match reg p 3 with
           | 0 -> 0
           | 1 -> o.off
           | 2 -> size
           | _ -> raise Bad) in
      if off < 0 then raise Bad;
      o.off <- off;
      result p off
  | _ -> raise Bad

(* stat(path, buf): the path's entry, as its directory has it (80 bytes,
 * user.h's dirent), at buf: 0, or -1 when it is not there (old: none, a
 * program read the whole directory for one name: ls -l of /bin, three
 * times a name, 1.7 billion instructions) *)
let sys_stat p =
  let ns = names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1)) in
  match walk !top ns with
  | Some node ->
      let e = entry (match List.rev ns with n :: _ -> n | [] -> "/") node in
      user_write p (reg p 2) e;
      result p 0
  | None -> raise Bad

let sys_chdir p =
  let ns = names p.cwd (ustr p (reg p 1)) in
  match walk !top ns with
  | Some n when is_dir n -> p.cwd <- ns; result p 0
  | _ -> raise Bad

(* ready(fds, n, until): the first of n descriptors (32 at most) that a
 * read would not wait on; -1 when the clock reaches until (0: no
 * limit; with no descriptor, a sleep). What a program with a mouse, a
 * keyboard and a picture to move waits on: one closure, as any wait *)
let sys_ready p =
  let n = reg p 2 and until = reg p 3 in
  if n < 0 || n > 32 then raise Bad;
  let rec list i =
    if i >= n then []
    else
      (let k = peek (user p (reg p 1 + (4 * i)) 4) in k, fd p k)
      :: list (i + 1) in
  let l = list 0 in
  block p (fun () ->
    match List.filter (fun (_, f) -> readable f) l with
    | (k, _) :: _ -> result p k; true
    | [] ->
        if until > 0 && !ticks >= until then (result p (-1); true)
        else
          (if until > 0 && (!alarm = 0 || until < !alarm) then alarm := until;
           false))

(* by their numbers, the machine's sys n: exit, write and read first,
 * tiny-cpu's own (libc's). A call that changed the disk is committed
 * when it ends, but a write: a file's writes are committed by the next
 * call that is not one, its close at the latest (TinyKernelFS.mli) *)
let syscall p n =
  (try
    match n with
    | 0 -> exit_proc p (reg p 1)
    | 1 -> sys_rw p write false
    | 2 -> sys_rw p read true
    | 3 -> sys_fork p
    | 4 -> sys_exec p
    | 5 -> sys_wait p
    | 6 -> result p p.pid
    | 7 -> sys_open p
    | 8 -> sys_close p
    | 9 -> sys_pipe p
    | 10 -> sys_dup p
    | 11 -> sys_mkdir p
    | 12 -> sys_unlink p
    | 13 -> sys_chdir p
    | 14 -> sys_kill p
    | 15 -> sys_ready p
    | 16 -> result p !ticks
    | 17 -> sys_box p
    | 18 -> sys_dial p
    | 19 -> sys_listen p
    | 20 -> sys_getcwd p
    | 21 -> sys_link p
    | 22 -> sys_rawcons p
    | 23 -> sys_trace p
    | 24 -> sys_seek p
    | 25 -> result p (date ())
    | 26 -> sys_stat p
    (* the seed: the machine's, or the clock when it has none, so that a
     * game is another each time *)
    | 27 -> result p (match peek seed_dev with 0 -> !ticks | s -> s)
    | 28 -> sys_spawn p
    | _ -> result p (-1)
  with Bad | No_room -> result p (-1) | Disk_full -> result p (-1));
  if n <> 1 then fs_commit ()

(* A traced process that stops at its calls (trace) stops before each,
 * its tracer told the call's number and its first three registers,
 * and after it, told its result: at once, or when it ends if it waits
 * (runnable). An exit has no after (its end is said), and an exec's is
 * its stop at its new program's first instruction. *)
let returned p n =
  pause p ("ret " ^ string_of_int n ^ " " ^ string_of_int (reg p 1))
let called p n =
  syscall p n;
  match p.traced, p.state with
  | _ when not (List.exists (fun q -> q.pid = p.pid) !procs) -> ()
  | Some t, Ready when t.calls -> returned p n
  | Some t, Ready when t.step -> stop p "step"
  | Some t, Waiting _ when t.calls -> t.ret <- n
  | _ -> ()
let call p n =
  match p.traced with
  | Some t when t.call >= 0 -> t.call <- -1; called p n
  | Some t when t.calls ->
      t.call <- n;
      pause p ("call " ^ String.concat " " (List.map string_of_int
                                             [ n; reg p 1; reg p 2; reg p 3 ]))
  | _ -> syscall p n

(* a traced process whose wait ended, stopped if its tracer asked for
 * the call's end or a step *)
let waited p =
  match p.traced with
  | Some t when t.ret >= 0 -> let n = t.ret in t.ret <- -1; returned p n; true
  | Some t when t.step -> stop p "step"; true
  | _ -> false
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelCalls.mli
2171
(* TinyKernel's system calls: a process's trap with c_sys, its number
 * the sys instruction's (the trap's value), its arguments in r1..r3,
 * its result put back in r1; and what they need, a process ended, a
 * program loaded in a process's memory.
 *
 *     0 exit    1 write   2 read     3 fork    4 exec     5 wait
 *     6 getpid  7 open    8 close    9 pipe    10 dup     11 mkdir
 *     12 unlink 13 chdir  14 kill    15 ready  16 ticks   17 box
 *     18 dial   19 listen 20 getcwd  21 link   22 rawcons 23 trace
 *     24 seek   25 date   26 stat    27 seed   28 spawn
 *
 * A call that may wait (a read, a wait, a fork with no slot free) is
 * tried at once and, when it cannot finish, left as the process's
 * Waiting state, tried again by the scheduler (TinyKernelProcs.mli).
 * A buffer is the user's memory as it is when it is in one piece (a
 * partition's), else copied through the kernel's bounce (TinyKernel.mli's
 * layout), as Linux's copy_from_user and xv6's copyin copy every call's.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * a link to another machine and a trace are files of a descriptor
 * (dial, trace), read and written as any other, where Unix has sockets
 * and ptrace, each with calls of its own. spawn is fork and exec at
 * once, as POSIX's posix_spawn.
 *)

(* [exit_proc p status]: its descriptors closed, its children orphans,
 * its status for its parent, or its slot free; the first process's end
 * is the machine's *)
val exit_proc : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> int -> unit

(* [load_prog p node argv]: the program of node in p's memory, its
 * arguments as start.tm finds them (Bad if it is no program, or if
 * there is no room: p left as it was) *)
val load_prog :
  TinyKernelProcs.proc -> TinyKernelFiles.node option -> string list -> unit

(* kill(pid)'s: the process ended as a fault ends one, its status -1 *)
val kill : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> unit

(* [call p n]: system call n of p, its tracer told before and after
 * when it stops at its calls *)
val call : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> int -> unit

(* a traced process whose wait ended, stopped if its tracer asked for
 * the call's end or a step *)
val waited : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> bool
