(* See TinyKernelDevices.mli *)
open TinyKernelGraphics
open TinyKernelAudio
open TinyKernelMachine
open TinyKernelFiles

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen and the mouse (TinyKernelGraphics.ml draws) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The screen is tiny-machine's 1024 by 768 bytes. The images live in the
 * two megabytes below it, and in what the screen leaves of its own
 * megabyte. (Most of the 3 MB below those, from 10 MB, is unused; it could be
 * the images' too. Trying it once changed the recorded paint session's
 * screen, which was taken for a bug: it was paint's ball, which moves
 * with the clock, ending elsewhere because the kernel's work took
 * another time.) The font is the machine's
 * (font.tm, in the image: fonts/plan9.font), its first face made a mask
 * at the boot. A program opens
 * /dev/draw for a connection, whose image 0 is the screen, and writes
 * messages; no pixel is in its partition. *)
let screen = { r = rect 0 0 1024 768; at = 0xf00000; repl = false }
(* the mouse's look a program asks for (www, over a link) is written to
 * the machine's mouse word, which the host shows *)
let () = cursor_hook := (fun kind -> poke mouse_dev kind)
let font =
  arena 0xd00000 0x200000;
  free 0xfc0000 0x3f000;   (* old: 0xf4b000 0xb4000, after 640 by 480 *)
  font_mask (k_font ()) (k_font_size ()) (alloc 16384)

(* the mouse: a box the kernel writes (x, y, the buttons, a word each)
 * when the machine's word changed; the clock: the timer's interrupts
 * counted *)
let mouse = { last = ""; fresh = false; posters = 1 }
let ticks = ref 0

(* the date: the boot's, and the seconds since, 400 ticks each (old:
 * none, the time of the day 0 for every program) *)
let date () = peek date_dev + (!ticks / 400)

(* the earliest time a waiting process asked to be told of (0: none) *)
let alarm = ref 0

(* the machine's time (k_clock's 30 bits) at the last tick counted *)
let counted = ref 0

(* The speaker (plan_tiny_audio.md): tiny-machine plays the ring, 8,192
 * samples, 8,000 a second, and silences what it played. Each open of
 * /dev/audio is a voice: a program writes messages, each a sound or
 * samples (TinyKernelAudio.mli), which the kernel makes into the ring,
 * added to what is there already, so two programs are heard at once and
 * neither waits for the other. A voice's sounds follow one another: the
 * next one goes where the last ended, or, when the speaker passed it, a
 * little ahead of the speaker ([lead], 5 ms, more than a write takes to
 * start); a write waits until all its sounds fit, a ring (a second)
 * ahead of the speaker at most. *)
let ring = 8192
let lead = 40
let played () = peek speaker_dev
let speak v sounds =
  let now = played () in
  if (v.ahead - now) land 0x3fffffff > ring then
    v.ahead <- (now + lead) land 0x3fffffff;
  let total =
    List.fold_left (fun acc snd -> acc + sound_length snd) 0 sounds in
  let missing = total - (ring - ((v.ahead - now) land 0x3fffffff)) in
  if missing > 0 then missing
  else begin
    List.iter (fun snd ->
      mix_sound ring_at ring v.ahead snd;
      v.ahead <- (v.ahead + sound_length snd) land 0x3fffffff) sounds;
    0
  end
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelDevices.mli
2206
(* TinyKernel's devices but the disk and the network: the screen (its
 * image, the font), the mouse (a box the kernel writes), the clock (the
 * timer's ticks, the date, an alarm), the speaker (its ring of
 * samples, each voice's sounds mixed in).
 *
 * The screen is tiny-machine's 1024 by 768 bytes; TinyKernelGraphics
 * draws in it and in the images below it, a program's /dev/draw
 * connection asking by messages: no pixel is in its partition. The
 * speaker plays the ring, 8,192 samples, 8,000 a second; each open of
 * /dev/audio is a voice, whose sounds (TinyKernelAudio's) are added to
 * what the ring has, so two programs are heard at once and neither
 * waits for the other:
 *
 *     the ring   ...[played]....[lead][voice 1's next]......[voice 2's]...
 *                     ^ the speaker          ^ where its next sound goes
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * as Plan 9's, each device is a file a program opens (/dev/draw,
 * /dev/mouse, /dev/audio), and a window system serves files of the same
 * names to its windows; here the kernel mixes the voices, where Plan 9
 * has one writer of /dev/audio at a time (its devaudio is opened by
 * one, from memory).
 *)

(* the screen's image, and the font's, a mask made at the boot *)
val screen : TinyKernelGraphics.image
val font : TinyKernelGraphics.image

(* the mouse: a box the kernel writes (x, y, the buttons, a word each)
 * when the machine's word changed *)
val mouse : TinyKernelFiles.box

(* the timer's interrupts counted; the date (the boot's, and the seconds
 * since, 400 ticks each); the earliest tick a waiting process asked to
 * be told of (0: none); the machine's time at the last tick counted *)
val ticks : int ref
val date : unit -> int
val alarm : int ref
val counted : int ref

(* the ring's samples, and how far ahead of the speaker a voice starts
 * again (5 ms); the samples played so far *)
val ring : int
val lead : int
val played : unit -> int

(* a voice's sounds mixed into the ring after its last one, if they all
 * fit (a second ahead of the speaker at most): 0; else the samples
 * missing, the write waits until the speaker played them *)
val speak : TinyKernelFiles.voice -> TinyKernelAudio.sound list -> int
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelFS.ml
15455
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyKernelFS.mli *)

(* OCaml builds this file too, on the host, where it is tested with a
 * disk of bytes in memory (tests/TinyKernelFS_tests/Host.ml) *)

open TinyMemory

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The disk, and the kernel's memory the file system works in *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The transfer of block b to memory at a (command 1) or from it (2). The
 * kernel sets it to its disk device; the test sets it to a string of
 * bytes. *)
let fs_io = ref (fun b a cmd -> ignore (b + a + cmd))
let fs_read b a = !fs_io b a 1
let fs_write b a = !fs_io b a 2

let fs_bsize = 1024

(* The memory, from 10 MB up, is the kernel's area that nothing else uses.
 * It holds buffers of a block each: 0 to 2 for the levels of a write, 3
 * for a read, 4 for a block of inodes, 5 for following pointers, 6 for
 * a text to write, 7 for the disk's own block 0, 8 to 13 for marking;
 * then the inode being worked on (14), the superblock (15), and the
 * map of the blocks, a byte each, for 64 K blocks at most. *)
let fs_mem = 0xa00000
let fs_buf k = fs_mem + (k * fs_bsize)
let fs_ino = fs_buf 14
let fs_sb = fs_buf 15
let fs_map = fs_buf 16
let fs_max = 65536

(* the words are 4 bytes, the low byte first, as the machine's *)
let fs_get a =
  peekb a lor (peekb (a + 1) lsl 8) lor (peekb (a + 2) lsl 16)
  lor (peekb (a + 3) lsl 24)
let fs_set a v =
  pokeb a (v land 255);
  pokeb (a + 1) ((v lsr 8) land 255);
  pokeb (a + 2) ((v lsr 16) land 255);
  pokeb (a + 3) ((v lsr 24) land 255)

(* The superblock's words: the magic number, the disk's size in blocks,
 * the boots counted, the snapshots kept. Then the roots, an inode each:
 * root 0 is the live tree, roots 1 to 14 the snapshots, the newest
 * first. A root is the inode of a tree's inode file. *)
(* (old: 0x31534654, "TFS1": a date in no inode, names of 28 bytes; a
 * disk of it is made again at its first boot) *)
let fs_magic = 0x32534654
let fs_root r = fs_sb + 16 + (64 * r)
let fs_nsnaps () = fs_get (fs_sb + 12)

(* the disk's size (0: no disk); how many blocks are free; the blocks
 * written since the last commit (fresh: they may be written again in
 * place); whether anything changed since; where to look for a free
 * block first *)
let fs_blocks = ref 0
let fs_nfree = ref 0
let fs_fresh = ref []
let fs_changed = ref false
let fs_next = ref 1

exception Disk_full

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Inodes and their blocks *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* An inode is 16 words: its type (0 free, 1 a directory, 2 a file), its
 * size in bytes, its links, its date (the last write's, seconds since
 * 2000), then 10 direct blocks, an indirect one and a double indirect
 * one; a block of pointers has 256. [fs_slot i] says where block i of
 * a file hangs: the inode's word, how many levels of pointers are under
 * that word, and the index under them. (old: no date, 11 direct
 * blocks) *)
let fs_slot i =
  if i < 10 then 4 + i, 0, i
  else if i < 266 then 14, 1, i - 10
  else 15, 2, i - 266

(* the date a write or a new file gets: the kernel's clock (the tests'
 * own) *)
let fs_clock = ref (fun () -> 0)

(* the block under ptr at index i, levels deep (0: a hole) *)
let rec fs_find ptr level i =
  if ptr = 0 || level = 0 then ptr
  else begin
    let s = if level = 1 then 1 else 256 in
    fs_read ptr (fs_buf 5);
    fs_find (fs_get (fs_buf 5 + (4 * (i / s)))) (level - 1) (i mod s)
  end

(* block i of the inode at ino *)
let fs_block ino i =
  let k, level, j = fs_slot i in
  fs_find (fs_get (ino + (4 * k))) level j

(* Marking: the blocks a tree uses, from an inode at ino. A block already
 * marked is skipped with what is under it (the trees share most of
 * theirs). When [leaf], the inode's file is an inode file: its data
 * blocks hold inodes, whose trees are marked in turn. Each depth has its
 * own buffer, so a block is still there when the marking comes back. *)
let rec fs_mark ptr level d leaf =
  if ptr > 0 && ptr < !fs_blocks && peekb (fs_map + ptr) <> 1 then begin
    if peekb (fs_map + ptr) = 0 then pokeb (fs_map + ptr) 1;
    if level > 0 || leaf then begin
      let a = fs_buf (8 + d) in
      fs_read ptr a;
      if level > 0 then
        for k = 0 to 255 do
          fs_mark (fs_get (a + (4 * k))) (level - 1) (d + 1) leaf
        done
      else for k = 0 to 15 do fs_mark_inode (a + (64 * k)) (d + 1) false done
    end
  end

and fs_mark_inode ino d leaf =
  if fs_get ino <> 0 then
    for k = 4 to 15 do
      fs_mark (fs_get (ino + (4 * k))) (if k < 14 then 0 else k - 13) d leaf
    done

(* The collection: a block is free when no tree uses it. The trees are
 * the live one, the snapshots, and the tree of the last commit on the
 * disk (a crash would come back to it). A fresh block stays used even
 * when no tree has it yet: a write may be halfway through linking it. *)
let fs_gc () =
  for b = 1 to !fs_blocks - 1 do
    if peekb (fs_map + b) = 1 then pokeb (fs_map + b) 0
  done;
  fs_read 0 (fs_buf 7);
  fs_mark_inode (fs_buf 7 + 16) 0 true;
  for r = 0 to fs_nsnaps () do fs_mark_inode (fs_root r) 0 true done;
  fs_nfree := 0;
  for b = 1 to !fs_blocks - 1 do if peekb (fs_map + b) = 0 then incr fs_nfree done

(* a free block, now fresh; the collection runs when there is none left *)
let rec fs_alloc again =
  let n = !fs_blocks in
  let rec look b left =
    if left = 0 then 0
    else if peekb (fs_map + b) = 0 then b
    else look (if b + 1 >= n then 1 else b + 1) (left - 1)
  in
  let b = look !fs_next (n - 1) in
  if b = 0 then (if again then (fs_gc (); fs_alloc false) else raise Disk_full)
  else (
    pokeb (fs_map + b) 2;
    fs_fresh := b :: !fs_fresh;
    fs_next := b;
    decr fs_nfree;
    b)

(* Room for n new blocks, and 8 more. Even a removal needs new blocks,
 * for the copies of the directory and of the inodes on their way to the
 * root: so what makes files (a write, a creation) must leave a few to
 * what removes them, or a full disk could not be emptied (ZFS keeps such
 * a reserve too). *)
let fs_room n =
  if !fs_nfree < n + 8 then (
    fs_gc ();
    if !fs_nfree < n + 8 then raise Disk_full)

(* The block ptr in memory at a, and the block it may be written back to:
 * itself when it is fresh, a new one when a commit has it (copy on
 * write). A hole (0) is a block of zeros. *)
let fs_own ptr a =
  if ptr = 0 then (row_fill a 0 fs_bsize; fs_alloc true)
  else (fs_read ptr a; if peekb (fs_map + ptr) = 2 then ptr else fs_alloc true)

(* [fs_store ptr level i f]: block i under ptr changed by f, which is
 * given its address in memory. Each block on the way down is owned
 * first, so the change goes up as new pointers to the copies. It returns
 * where ptr now is. *)
let rec fs_store ptr level i f =
  let a = fs_buf level in
  let b = fs_own ptr a in
  if level = 0 then f a
  else begin
    let s = if level = 1 then 1 else 256 in
    let slot = a + (4 * (i / s)) in
    fs_set slot (fs_store (fs_get slot) (level - 1) (i mod s) f)
  end;
  fs_write b a;
  fs_changed := true;
  b

(* block i of the inode at ino changed by f *)
let fs_put ino i f =
  let k, level, j = fs_slot i in
  let w = ino + (4 * k) in
  fs_set w (fs_store (fs_get w) level j f)

(* Inode n of tree r, loaded at fs_ino; saved into the live tree. An
 * inode file is a file like the others: an inode's change is a write to
 * it, and goes up to the root in the superblock. *)
let fs_load r n =
  let b = fs_block (fs_root r) (n / 16) in
  if b = 0 then row_fill fs_ino 0 64
  else (
    fs_read b (fs_buf 4);
    row_copy fs_ino (fs_buf 4 + (64 * (n mod 16))) 64)
let fs_save n =
  fs_put (fs_root 0) (n / 16) (fun a ->
      row_copy (a + (64 * (n mod 16))) fs_ino 64)

let fs_word k = fs_get (fs_ino + (4 * k))
let fs_setw k v = fs_set (fs_ino + (4 * k)) v

(* a new inode of a type, its links 0: a free one, or one more at the
 * end of the inode file (whose size counts its inodes) *)
let fs_new typ =
  fs_room 4;
  let count = fs_get (fs_root 0 + 4) in
  let rec free n =
    if n >= count then n
    else (fs_load 0 n; if fs_word 0 = 0 then n else free (n + 1))
  in
  let n = free 2 in
  if n >= count then fs_set (fs_root 0 + 4) (n + 1);
  row_fill fs_ino 0 64;
  fs_setw 0 typ;
  fs_setw 3 (!fs_clock ());
  fs_save n;
  n

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Files *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the type, the size and the links of inode n of tree r; its date *)
let fs_kind r n = fs_load r n; fs_word 0, fs_word 1, fs_word 2
let fs_date r n = fs_load r n; fs_word 3
let fs_is_dir r n = fs_load r n; fs_word 0 = 1

(* Up to len bytes of inode n of tree r, from off, to memory at a; how
 * many there were. A hole reads as zeros. *)
let fs_read_at r n off a len =
  fs_load r n;
  let len = max 0 (min len (fs_word 1 - off)) in
  let rec go d =
    if d < len then begin
      let o = (off + d) mod fs_bsize in
      let k = min (len - d) (fs_bsize - o) in
      let b = fs_block fs_ino ((off + d) / fs_bsize) in
      if b = 0 then row_fill (a + d) 0 k
      else (fs_read b (fs_buf 3); row_copy (a + d) (fs_buf 3 + o) k);
      go (d + k)
    end in
  go 0;
  len

(* len bytes from memory at a, written to inode n of the live tree at off
 * (fs_write_in: whatever room it takes, for a directory's entries) *)
let fs_write_in n off a len =
  fs_load 0 n;
  let rec go d =
    if d < len then begin
      let o = (off + d) mod fs_bsize in
      let k = min (len - d) (fs_bsize - o) in
      fs_put fs_ino ((off + d) / fs_bsize) (fun b -> row_copy (b + o) (a + d) k);
      go (d + k)
    end in
  go 0;
  if off + len > fs_word 1 then fs_setw 1 (off + len);
  fs_setw 3 (!fs_clock ());
  fs_save n

let fs_write_at n off a len = fs_room ((len / fs_bsize) + 6); fs_write_in n off a len

(* a string written to inode n at off, a block at a time *)
let fs_write_string n off s =
  let rec go d =
    if d < String.length s then begin
      let k = min fs_bsize (String.length s - d) in
      row_bytes s d (fs_buf 6) k;
      fs_write_in n (off + d) (fs_buf 6) k;
      go (d + k)
    end in
  go 0

(* its size 0; its blocks are left to the collection *)
let fs_truncate n =
  fs_load 0 n;
  fs_setw 1 0;
  fs_setw 3 (!fs_clock ());
  for k = 4 to 15 do fs_setw k 0 done;
  fs_save n

(* the whole of inode n of tree r, as a string *)
let fs_contents r n =
  let size = (fs_load r n; fs_word 1) in
  let rec go at acc =
    if at >= size then String.concat "" (List.rev acc)
    else (
      let k = fs_read_at r n at (fs_buf 6) fs_bsize in
      go (at + k) (row_string (fs_buf 6) k :: acc)) in
  go 0 []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Directories *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A directory is a file of entries of 68 bytes: a name (64 bytes, ended
 * by zeros when shorter) and an inode's number. There is no "." or
 * "..": the kernel resolves ".." by the path's text. (old: 32 bytes, a
 * name of 28) *)
let fs_bytes n =
  String.concat ""
    (List.map (fun k -> String.make 1 (Char.chr ((n lsr k) land 255)))
       [ 0; 8; 16; 24 ])
let fs_entry name n =
  name ^ String.make (64 - String.length name) '\000' ^ fs_bytes n

let fs_entries r d =
  let s = fs_contents r d in
  let rec go i acc =
    if i + 68 > String.length s then List.rev acc
    else begin
      let rec len k = if k < 64 && s.[i + k] <> '\000' then len (k + 1) else k in
      let n =
        String.get_uint16_le s (i + 64)
        + (String.get_uint16_le s (i + 66) lsl 16) in
      go (i + 68) ((String.sub s i (len 0), n) :: acc)
    end in
  go 0 []

(* the inode under a name in directory d of tree r (0: none) *)
let fs_lookup r d name =
  match List.assoc_opt name (fs_entries r d) with Some n -> n | None -> 0

(* one more name for inode n, in directory d *)
let fs_link d name n =
  fs_write_string d (fs_load 0 d; fs_word 1) (fs_entry name n);
  fs_load 0 n;
  fs_setw 2 (fs_word 2 + 1);
  fs_save n

(* a new file (type 2) or directory (1) under a name in d *)
let fs_create d name typ = let n = fs_new typ in fs_link d name n; n

(* A name removed from d, the directory written again without it. The
 * inode is freed with its last name. (A program that still has it open
 * reads what is there next: Unix keeps it until the last close.) *)
let fs_unlink d name =
  let l = fs_entries 0 d in
  let n = fs_lookup 0 d name in
  fs_truncate d;
  fs_write_string d 0
    (String.concat ""
       (List.map (fun (m, k) -> fs_entry m k)
          (List.filter (fun (m, _) -> m <> name) l)));
  if n <> 0 then begin
    fs_load 0 n;
    fs_setw 2 (fs_word 2 - 1);
    if fs_word 2 <= 0 then row_fill fs_ino 0 64;
    fs_save n
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Commits, snapshots, the mount *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The commit: the superblock written, in one block. Before it the disk
 * has the last commit's tree whole, after it the new one. The fresh
 * blocks are now the commit's: a change copies them again. *)
let fs_commit () =
  if !fs_changed then begin
    fs_write 0 fs_sb;
    List.iter (fun b -> pokeb (fs_map + b) 1) !fs_fresh;
    fs_fresh := [];
    fs_changed := false
  end

(* a new file system: the inode file, with inode 0 unused and inode 1
 * the root directory *)
let fs_format n =
  row_fill fs_sb 0 fs_bsize;
  fs_set fs_sb fs_magic;
  fs_set (fs_sb + 4) n;
  fs_set (fs_root 0) 2;
  fs_set (fs_root 0 + 4) 2;
  row_fill fs_ino 0 64;
  fs_setw 0 1;
  fs_setw 2 1;
  fs_save 1

(* whether two roots are the same tree (their third word, the boot, aside) *)
let fs_same r q =
  let rec go k =
    k >= 16
    || ((k = 2 || fs_get (fs_root r + (4 * k)) = fs_get (fs_root q + (4 * k)))
        && go (k + 1))
  in
  go 0

(* The mount, at the boot, on a disk of n blocks: a blank disk is
 * formatted (and a file system keeps the size it was made with);
 * otherwise the free blocks are found by a collection, and
 * the tree the last boot left becomes a snapshot (unless it is the
 * snapshot before it again), the oldest of 14 dropped. The live tree's
 * third word is this boot's number. *)
let fs_mount n =
  let n = min n fs_max in
  fs_next := 1;
  fs_fresh := [];
  row_fill fs_map 0 n;
  pokeb fs_map 1;
  fs_read 0 fs_sb;
  if fs_get fs_sb <> fs_magic then (fs_blocks := n; fs_nfree := n - 1; fs_format n)
  else begin
    fs_blocks := min n (fs_get (fs_sb + 4));
    fs_gc ();
    let k = fs_nsnaps () in
    if k = 0 || not (fs_same 0 1) then begin
      let k = min k 13 in
      for r = k downto 1 do row_copy (fs_root (r + 1)) (fs_root r) 64 done;
      row_copy (fs_root 1) (fs_root 0) 64;
      fs_set (fs_sb + 12) (k + 1)
    end
  end;
  fs_set (fs_sb + 8) (fs_get (fs_sb + 8) + 1);
  fs_set (fs_root 0 + 8) (fs_get (fs_sb + 8));
  fs_changed := true;
  fs_commit ()

(* the snapshots: each its root and the boot it was the live tree of *)
let fs_snapshots () =
  List.init (fs_nsnaps ()) (fun i -> i + 1, fs_get (fs_root (i + 1) + 8))


(* the free blocks, counted after a collection *)
let fs_free () = fs_gc (); !fs_nfree
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelFS.mli
9030
(* Tiny file system: TinyKernel.ml's part that keeps files on the disk,
 * as TinyKernelGraphics.ml is its part that draws. The disk is the
 * root, in a union with the boot image's files (TinyKernel.mli's "The
 * files").
 *
 * It needs two things from the machine: TinyMemory's bytes, and a way
 * to move a block between the disk and memory ([fs_io]).
 *
 * {b The classic layout.} The disk is made of blocks of 1 KB. A file is
 * an inode: its type, its size, its number of links, the date of its
 * last write, and the numbers of its blocks. The first 10 blocks are
 * listed in the inode itself; after them comes an indirect block (256
 * more numbers), then a double indirect one (256 blocks of 256
 * numbers). A directory is a file whose contents are entries, each a
 * name of up to 64 bytes and an inode's number. This is the file system
 * of Unix since 1971, and of xv6.
 *
 * {b What is different: nothing is ever written over.} A classic file
 * system changes a block where it is. If the machine stops in the middle
 * of a change that touches several blocks (a new file is an inode, a
 * directory entry and a block of data), the disk is left inconsistent.
 * Unix then needed fsck at the next boot, and later file systems added a
 * log (xv6 has one). Here, a block that the last commit uses is never
 * changed. A change writes a copy of the block, which changes the
 * pointer to it, so the block holding that pointer is copied too, and so
 * on up to the root:
 *
 *      before the write             after it, before the commit
 *
 *      superblock                   superblock (in memory)
 *          |                             |
 *       root inode                   root inode'
 *          |                             |
 *      inode block                  inode block'    (the file's inode,
 *          |                             |           its new size)
 *      data block                   data block'     (the new bytes)
 *
 *      the disk still has the whole tree on the left; the commit writes
 *      the superblock, one block, and the disk has the tree on the right
 *
 * For this to work, inodes cannot sit at a fixed place on the disk, as
 * in Unix: they live in a file, the inode file, and the root of
 * everything is the inode of that file, in the superblock. Changing an
 * inode is then just a write to that file. The commit is the write of
 * block 0. Whenever the machine stops, the disk holds either the old
 * tree or the new one, never half of each, and the boot needs no fsck.
 *
 * A block written since the last commit (a fresh one) may be written
 * again in place: no commit refers to it. So a file written 1 KB at a
 * time copies its path to the root once per commit, not once per write.
 * The kernel commits after each system call that changed the disk,
 * except write: a file's writes are committed by the next call that is
 * not a write, its close at the latest.
 *
 * {b Free blocks are found by a collector.} Nothing tracks which blocks
 * become free when they are replaced. Instead, when no block is free (and
 * at the mount), the file system marks the blocks that the trees use and
 * takes the others back: a mark-and-sweep collector for the disk, as
 * TinyML's runtime is a collector for the heap. The trees are the live
 * one, the snapshots, and the last commit's tree on the disk. This
 * replaces Unix's map of free blocks, which a crash could also leave
 * wrong.
 *
 * {b Snapshots come for free.} Since an old tree is never written over,
 * keeping it costs only its root. At each boot, the tree that the last
 * boot left is kept as a snapshot (14 at most, the oldest dropped). The
 * kernel shows them as /dump/N, the files as they were at the end of
 * boot N, read only. A file deleted by mistake can be copied back from
 * there.
 *
 * Its twin in m-ix is mini-9pi's disk, '#x' (kernels/9pi/'s Kfs), on
 * lib_xv6fs's Xv6fs: xv6's file system (xv6's fs.c, which ix's
 * mini-xv6 has too, kernels/xv6's Fs), in the kernel, with a bitmap
 * of free blocks and, as here, no log and no cache. Kept from it: the
 * inode, its direct then indirect blocks, the directory as a file of
 * (name, number), names longer than xv6's 14 (ix's extension there).
 * Ours: nothing written in place, so the commit is one block where
 * xv6's log.c writes each change twice; free blocks found by a
 * collector, not a bitmap kept right; the snapshots, which xv6 has no
 * way to keep. Plan 9 itself has no disk file system in its kernel
 * (principia's kernel/filesystems/ is devfs.c, and dossrv and ramfs as
 * programs): a disk is served by a program, as Kdos says; here, as in
 * mini-9pi's Kfs and in Unix, the kernel calls it as functions.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The inode, the direct and indirect blocks, and directories as files of
 * (name, number) are from the first Unix file system (Thompson and
 * Ritchie, 1971-1974), and xv6 keeps them. Writing nothing in place is
 * the idea of shadow paging (Lorie, System R, 1977). NetApp's WAFL (Hitz,
 * Lau and Malcolm, 1994) built a file system on it, with the inode file
 * and snapshots as here; ZFS (2005) and btrfs (2007) followed. Plan 9's
 * dump (Quinlan, 1991; then Venti and Fossil, 2002) kept every day's
 * file system under /n/dump/2026/1018, which is where /dump comes from.
 * The log-structured file system (Rosenblum and Ousterhout, 1991) also
 * writes only new blocks, and also needs a cleaner, its collector.
 *
 * design:
 * A classic file system with a log (xv6's) writes each change twice,
 * once to the log and once in place, and needs code to replay the log at
 * the boot. Copying on write writes each change once, at a new place,
 * and the commit is a single block. What it costs instead is the copies
 * up to the root (a few blocks per commit) and the collector. In ML both
 * are short: the copy is one recursive function ([fs_store]), the
 * collector another ([fs_mark]).
 *
 * wib:
 * - The collector reads every inode and indirect block of every tree.
 *   That is quick on tiny-machine's disk of 8 MB, where a transfer is
 *   instant, but a real file system keeps reference counts or a space
 *   map instead (ZFS's).
 * - There is no cache: every access reads its blocks again from the
 *   disk, as t6 does. That is fine only because the disk is instant.
 * - Directories are searched in order, and a removal rewrites the
 *   directory. That is fine for directories of a few dozen names.
 * - A file removed while a program still has it open is freed at once
 *   (Unix keeps it until the last close), and its inode may be reused.
 *)

(* the transfer of block b to memory at a (command 1) or from memory to
 * the block (2): the kernel's disk device, or the test's bytes *)
val fs_io : (int -> int -> int -> unit) ref

(* raised by a write when no block is free, even after a collection *)
exception Disk_full

(* [fs_mount n]: the file system of a disk of n blocks, made when the
 * disk is blank; the last boot's tree becomes a snapshot *)
val fs_mount : int -> unit

(* the changes since the last commit, written to the disk as a whole
 * (nothing to do when there are none) *)
val fs_commit : unit -> unit

(* the snapshots: each one's tree number and the boot it was left by *)
val fs_snapshots : unit -> (int * int) list

(* the free blocks, counted after a collection *)
val fs_free : unit -> int

(* A file is an inode's number in a tree: tree 0 is the live one, which
 * can be changed, trees 1 to 14 the snapshots. Inode 1 is the root
 * directory. The types are 1 for a directory and 2 for a file, as in
 * the entries the kernel gives to ls. *)

(* [fs_kind r n]: inode n's type, size and links; [fs_date r n]: its
 * last write's date, seconds since 2000 *)
val fs_kind : int -> int -> int * int * int
val fs_date : int -> int -> int

(* what a write or a new file gets as its date: the kernel's clock *)
val fs_clock : (unit -> int) ref
val fs_is_dir : int -> int -> bool

(* [fs_lookup r d name]: the inode under name in directory d (0: none) *)
val fs_lookup : int -> int -> string -> int

(* the names and inodes of a directory, in the order they were made *)
val fs_entries : int -> int -> (string * int) list

(* [fs_read_at r n off a len]: up to len bytes of the file from off, to
 * memory at a; how many there were *)
val fs_read_at : int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> int

(* the whole file, as a string *)
val fs_contents : int -> int -> string

(* [fs_write_at n off a len]: len bytes from memory at a, to the live
 * file n at off (Disk_full when there is no room) *)
val fs_write_at : int -> int -> int -> int -> unit

(* the file emptied *)
val fs_truncate : int -> unit

(* [fs_create d name typ]: a new file (2) or directory (1) under name in
 * d; its inode *)
val fs_create : int -> string -> int -> int

(* [fs_link d name n]: a second name for file n, in d *)
val fs_link : int -> string -> int -> unit

(* [fs_unlink d name]: the name removed from d, and the inode with its
 * last name *)
val fs_unlink : int -> string -> unit

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyKernelFiles.mli *)
open TinyMemory
open TinyKernelGraphics
open TinyKernelNetwork
open TinyKernelFS
open TinyKernelMachine

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The files: a tree of ML values *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a directory is a list of names in the order they were made; the
 * console is a node too, /dev/console, and the screen, the mouse and
 * the speaker, /dev/draw, /dev/mouse and /dev/audio, and the processes,
 * /dev/ps, a line each, made when it is read (the programs are
 * in /bin, examples to look at in /examples). A file of the image is
 * read where the image has it (its address, its size) until it is
 * written: the programs, a megabyte of them, are then not the
 * collector's to copy at each collection (old: each a string, Data; a
 * collection was 3 million instructions).
 * A file or a directory on the disk (TinyKernelFS.ml) is a tree and an
 * inode's number: tree 0 is the live one, the others are the snapshots.
 * A union is several directories seen as one, as Plan 9's bind -a makes:
 * a name is looked up in each in turn, and what is made goes in the
 * first. A file written in memory is its bytes and its size, the bytes
 * doubled when a write goes past them (old: a string, made again at
 * each write: a database that grows by appends took a second for each
 * statement, tiny-db's) *)
type node =
  | Dir of (string * node) list ref
  | Data of data
  | Rom of int * int
  | Tty
  | Screen
  | Pointer
  | Speaker
  | Ps
  | Disk of int * int
  | Union of node list
and data = { mutable dbytes : bytes; mutable dsize : int; mutable dtime : int }

let data s =
  let b = Bytes.make (String.length s) ' ' in
  Bytes.blit_string s 0 b 0 (String.length s);
  { dbytes = b; dsize = String.length s; dtime = 0 }
let text d = Bytes.sub_string d.dbytes 0 d.dsize

(* a pipe: the bytes written not yet read (512 at most), its readers'
 * and its writers' descriptors (a read of an empty pipe with no writer
 * left is its end) *)
type pipe =
  { mutable buf : string; mutable readers : int; mutable writers : int }

(* an open file: a node (its offset, whether it is written), a pipe's
 * end, the console, a connection to the screen, a box's end. The
 * collector frees them; only pipes count their ends, as a reader must
 * learn that no writer is left, and a connection its descriptors, as
 * its images are not the collector's *)
type file =
  | Open of opened
  | Reader of pipe
  | Writer of pipe
  | Console
  | Draw of drawing
  | Peek of box
  | Post of box
  | Link of link
  | Call of call
  | Voice of voice
  | Trace of trace
(* (listing: a directory's entries, made at its read from the start,
 * and the reads after take theirs from it) *)
and opened = { node : node; mutable off : int; writes : bool;
               mutable listing : string option }
and drawing = { conn : conn; mutable refs : int }

(* a box: a pipe that keeps only what was last written, and whether it
 * was read since (the mouse is a place, not its history: a reader that
 * is late finds where it is, and a writer never waits). Peek reads it,
 * Post writes it; the kernel's own is the mouse, a window system's are
 * its windows' mice *)
and box = { mutable last : string; mutable fresh : bool; mutable posters : int }

(* a link to another machine (plan_tiny_network.md): so far an echo's.
 * What is written is sent there as a question, and a read gives an
 * answer's bytes, whole, in the order they came; a link has a number,
 * which its questions carry and their answers bring back *)
and link = {
  peer : string;
  lid : int;
  mutable asked : int;
  mutable heard : string list;
  mutable holders : int;
}

(* a connection to a program of another machine (TinyKernelNetwork.ml's IL):
 * a write is a message, which arrives once and in order or is sent
 * again; a read gives one whole, 0 when the other end is done; and its
 * descriptors, the last one's close saying the end *)
and call = { il : il; mutable callers : int }

(* a voice of the speaker (an open of /dev/audio): where in the samples its
 * next one goes *)
and voice = { mutable ahead : int }

(* a process traced by another, its tracer (debug: plan_tiny_debugger.md):
 * their pids, the breakpoints (an address and the word that was there),
 * what is said to the tracer and not yet read, and the tracer's
 * descriptors on it; whether it stops at its calls (trace), the call
 * it is stopped before or let in (-1: none), the call whose end it
 * waits for, to stop then (-1: none); whether it runs one instruction
 * and stops (a step), and the breakpoint it runs the word of, the 0
 * written again after (-1: none); whether its children are traced too
 * (trace -f) *)
and trace = {
  tpid : int;
  tracer : int;
  mutable stops : (int * int) list;
  mutable said : string list;
  mutable watchers : int;
  mutable calls : bool;
  mutable call : int;
  mutable ret : int;
  mutable step : bool;
  mutable over : int;
  mutable follow : bool;
}

(* The image's files (and /dev), and the tree a path starts from. They
 * are the same when there is no disk. With a disk, the boot makes the
 * top a union, Plan 9's way: the disk's root first, then /boot (the
 * image's files alone) and /dump, then the image's files again, so
 * that /bin is the disk's /bin and /boot/bin together *)
let root = Dir (ref [])
let top = ref root

(* a path's names from the root: the current directory's first unless
 * it starts with /, "." dropped, ".." the name before it removed (by
 * the text, as Plan 9's cleanname: no ".." in a directory) *)
let names cwd path =
  let start =
    if String.length path > 0 && path.[0] = '/' then [] else List.rev cwd in
  List.rev (List.fold_left (fun acc n ->
    if n = "" || n = "." then acc
    else if n = ".." then (match acc with [] -> [] | _ :: r -> r)
    else n :: acc)
    start (String.split_on_char '/' path))

let is_dir node =
  match node with
  | Dir _ | Union _ -> true
  | Disk (r, i) -> fs_is_dir r i
  | _ -> false

(* In a union, the name is looked up in each directory. The first one
 * found is the answer, unless it is a directory found in several: then
 * the answer is their union (/bin, in the disk and in the image) *)
let rec walk node ns =
  match ns, node with
  | [], _ -> Some node
  | n :: rest, Dir d ->
      (match List.assoc_opt n !d with Some c -> walk c rest | None -> None)
  | n :: rest, Disk (r, i) when fs_is_dir r i ->
      (match fs_lookup r i n with 0 -> None | j -> walk (Disk (r, j)) rest)
  | n :: rest, Union l ->
      (match List.fold_left (fun acc m ->
         match walk m [ n ] with Some c -> acc @ [ c ] | None -> acc) [] l with
       | [] -> None
       | [ c ] -> walk c rest
       | c :: more ->
           walk (if is_dir c then Union (List.filter is_dir (c :: more)) else c)
             rest)
  | _ -> None

(* a directory's names and what they are (in a union, a name once: the
 * first) *)
let rec children node =
  match node with
  | Dir d -> !d
  | Disk (r, i) ->
      List.map (fun (name, j) -> name, Disk (r, j)) (fs_entries r i)
  | Union l ->
      List.fold_left (fun acc m ->
        acc @ List.filter (fun (name, _) ->
          not (List.exists (fun (k, _) -> k = name) acc)) (children m)) [] l
  | _ -> []

(* where a directory's new names go: a union's first *)
let rec home node = match node with Union (m :: _) -> home m | _ -> node

(* the directory a path's last name is in (where it would be made: a
 * Dir, or a directory on the disk), and that name *)
let dir_of ns =
  match List.rev ns with
  | [] -> None
  | last :: r ->
      (match walk !top (List.rev r) with
       | Some n when is_dir n -> Some (home n, last)
       | _ -> None)

(* a directory read as a file: an entry of 80 bytes per name, t6's (its
 * name, its type, a first block, its size), which ls reads, but for
 * the name's 64 bytes, the disk's, and the date of the last write after
 * the size (old: t6's 20 bytes of name: the sources'
 * TinyAppTemperature.mli could not be listed, its .tmi not made; then
 * 28, and no date). The first block, which this kernel has no use for,
 * says the file's links instead: how many names it has. *)
let word n = String.init 4 (fun k -> Char.chr ((n lsr (8 * k)) land 255))

(* a node's names: the entries in the whole tree that hold the same
 * value (==), the file itself and not a copy of it *)
let links node =
  let rec count d =
    List.fold_left (fun acc (_, n) ->
      acc + (if n == node then 1 else 0)
      + (match n with Dir e -> count e | _ -> 0)) 0 !d in
  match root with Dir d -> count d | _ -> 0

(* an entry: a name, a type, the links, a size, a date; a disk's file
 * says its own (its type is 1 or 2 as here); the image's files have the
 * date 0, 2000-01-01, a directory in memory too *)
let entry name n =
  let t, size, l = match n with
    | Dir _ -> 1, 0, links n
    | Data d -> 2, d.dsize, links n
    | Rom (_, k) -> 2, k, links n
    | Disk (r, i) -> fs_kind r i
    | Union _ -> 1, 0, 1
    | _ -> 3, 0, links n in
  let date =
    match n with Data d -> d.dtime | Disk (r, i) -> fs_date r i | _ -> 0 in
  name ^ String.make (64 - String.length name) '\000'
  ^ word t ^ word l ^ word size ^ word date

(* /dev/ps's lines, which TinyKernelProcs, which has the processes, gives *)
let ps_hook = ref (fun () -> "")

let contents node =
  match node with
  | Data d -> text d
  | Rom (at, n) -> k_string at n
  | Tty | Screen | Pointer | Speaker -> ""
  | Ps -> !ps_hook ()
  | Disk (r, i) when not (fs_is_dir r i) -> fs_contents r i
  (* (made once: old, acc ^ entry, the listing copied again at each name,
   * quadratic: ls -l of /bin, 55 names each listing it twice, took 7
   * minutes when the entries went from 40 bytes to 80) *)
  | _ ->
      String.concat "" (List.map (fun (name, n) -> entry name n) (children node))

(* [place d name node]: node under name in d; a name with a slash,
 * examples/wc.c, in its directory, which is made the first time *)
let rec place d name node =
  match String.index_opt name '/' with
  | None -> d := !d @ [ name, node ]
  | Some i ->
      let dir = String.sub name 0 i
      and rest = String.sub name (i + 1) (String.length name - i - 1) in
      (match List.assoc_opt dir !d with
       | Some (Dir sub) -> place sub rest node
       | _ ->
           let sub = ref [] in
           d := !d @ [ dir, Dir sub ];
           place sub rest node)

(* the files the image carries after the kernel (TinyKernel/Makefile's): a
 * path, a line; its size, a line; its bytes; an empty path at the end.
 * A line "link" and another file's path, in place of the size, makes a
 * hard link, as link() does: the same node under a second name, with
 * no bytes (bin/utils, under the name of each of its utilities:
 * bin/cat, bin/ls...) *)
let rec load a =
  let rec line a acc =
    let c = peekb a in
    if c = 10 then acc, a + 1
    else line (a + 1) (acc ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr c)) in
  let name, a = line a "" in
  if name <> "" then begin
    let size, a = line a "" in
    match root with
    | Dir d when String.length size > 5 && String.sub size 0 5 = "link " ->
        (match walk root (names [] (String.sub size 5 (String.length size - 5)))
         with
         | Some node -> place d name node
         | None -> ());
        load a
    | Dir d ->
        let n = Option.get (int_of_string_opt size) in
        place d name (Rom (a, n));
        load (a + n)
    | _ -> ()
  end

(* TinyKernel's files: a tree of ML values, the image's files, /dev,
 * the disk's (TinyKernelFS) and unions of them, looked up by a path's

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyKernelGraphics.mli *)

(* OCaml builds this file too, on the host, where it is tested without
 * a machine (tests/TinyKernelGraphics_tests/Host.ml) *)

open TinyMemory

(* a bad message, or no memory: a program's mistake, said to it *)
exception Graphics of string

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Images *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a rectangle of the plane: from (x0, y0), up to but not (x1, y1) *)
type rect = { x0 : int; y0 : int; x1 : int; y1 : int }

(* an image: its rectangle, where its bytes are (a row after the other,
 * a byte a pixel), and whether it repeats, covering the plane *)
type image = { r : rect; at : int; repl : bool }

let rect x0 y0 x1 y1 = { x0 = x0; y0 = y0; x1 = x1; y1 = y1 }
let inter (a : rect) (b : rect) =
  rect (max a.x0 b.x0) (max a.y0 b.y0) (min a.x1 b.x1) (min a.y1 b.y1)
let width (i : image) = i.r.x1 - i.r.x0
let height (i : image) = i.r.y1 - i.r.y0

(* where the pixel at (x, y) is: a repeating image's is first taken
 * back into its rectangle (tiny-machine divides by a loop, in
 * udivmod.tm: not when the pixel is there already) *)
let back repl v n = if v >= 0 && v < n || not repl then v else ((v mod n) + n) mod n
let pixel (i : image) x y =
  i.at + (back i.repl (y - i.r.y0) (height i) * width i)
  + back i.repl (x - i.r.x0) (width i)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* draw *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* r without what a source has no pixel for, the source's (x + dx,
 * y + dy) being drawn at (x, y); one that repeats has them all *)
let within (r : rect) (s : image) dx dy =
  if s.repl then r
  else inter r (rect (s.r.x0 - dx) (s.r.y0 - dy) (s.r.x1 - dx) (s.r.y1 - dy))

(* dst's rectangle r: src's pixels from (px, py) on, where the mask's
 * (from the same point) are not 0; with a colour's table of mixes
 * (mix, below; 0: none), a colour mixed by the mask's level, a grey
 * font's edges (old: none, a mask set or not; a source of more than a
 * colour still is). Clipped to the three images. A row
 * is one of TinyMemory's three loops where it can be: a copy, a colour
 * (a source of one pixel that repeats, read once), a colour through a
 * mask (a character); a pixel at a time otherwise. A row's address is
 * the first's and so many widths (d0 and dw, s0 and sw), not a call.
 * An image drawn on itself is read before it is written: its rows from
 * the last when it moves down, a row from its last pixel when it moves
 * right. *)
let draw_mixed mix (dst : image) (r : rect) (src : image) (mask : image option)
    px py =
  let dx = px - r.x0 and dy = py - r.y0 in
  let r = within (inter r dst.r) src dx dy in
  let r = match mask with Some m -> within r m dx dy | None -> r in
  let n = r.x1 - r.x0 in
  let backwards = src.at = dst.at && (dy < 0 || (dy = 0 && dx < 0)) in
  let colour = src.repl && width src = 1 && height src = 1 in
  let ink = if colour then peekb src.at else 0 in
  if n > 0 && r.y1 > r.y0 then begin
    let d0 = pixel dst r.x0 r.y0 and dw = width dst in
    let s0 = if src.repl then 0 else pixel src (r.x0 + dx) (r.y0 + dy)
    and sw = width src in
    for k = 0 to r.y1 - r.y0 - 1 do
      let k = if backwards then r.y1 - r.y0 - 1 - k else k in
      let y = r.y0 + k and d = d0 + (k * dw) in
      match mask with
      | None when colour -> row_fill d ink n
      | None when not src.repl && not (backwards && dy = 0) ->
          row_copy d (s0 + (k * sw)) n
      | Some m when colour && not m.repl && mix <> 0 ->
          row_mix d mix (pixel m (r.x0 + dx) (y + dy)) n
      | Some m when colour && not m.repl ->
          row_mask d ink (pixel m (r.x0 + dx) (y + dy)) n
      | _ ->
          for j = 0 to n - 1 do
            let x = if backwards then r.x1 - 1 - j else r.x0 + j in
            if (match mask with
                | Some m -> peekb (pixel m (x + dx) (y + dy)) <> 0
                | None -> true)
            then pokeb (d + x - r.x0) (peekb (pixel src (x + dx) (y + dy)))
          done
    done
  end

let draw dst r src mask px py = draw_mixed 0 dst r src mask px py

(* a line from (xa, ya) to (xb, yb), both drawn, a pixel thick:
 * Bresenham's, each of its points a draw (clipped there) *)
let line (dst : image) xa ya xb yb (src : image) =
  (* (a level or an upright line is a rectangle, one draw: a link's
   * underline was a draw a pixel) *)
  if ya = yb || xa = xb then
    draw dst (rect (min xa xb) (min ya yb) (max xa xb + 1) (max ya yb + 1))
      src None (min xa xb) (min ya yb)
  else
  let dx = abs (xb - xa) and dy = abs (yb - ya) in
  let sx = if xa < xb then 1 else -1 and sy = if ya < yb then 1 else -1 in
  let rec from x y err =
    draw dst (rect x y (x + 1) (y + 1)) src None x y;
    if x <> xb || y <> yb then begin
      let across = 2 * err + dy > 0 and down = 2 * err < dx in
      from (if across then x + sx else x) (if down then y + sy else y)
        (err - (if across then dy else 0) + (if down then dx else 0))
    end
  in
  from xa ya (dx - dy)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The images' memory *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Outside the collected heap (a megabyte of pixels would be copied at
 * each collection): the free blocks, an address and a size each, by
 * address. The first that fits is taken from; a block freed joins the
 * ones it touches. *)
let blocks = ref []
let arena at n = blocks := [ at, n ]

(* (a block is whole words: an image then starts at a multiple of 4,
 * and a row of it is copied a word at a time to one that does too) *)
let words n = (n + 3) land lnot 3

let alloc n =
  let n = words n in
  let rec take = function
    | [] -> raise (Graphics "no memory for an image")
    | (a, size) :: rest when size >= n ->
        a, if size = n then rest else (a + n, size - n) :: rest
    | b :: rest -> let a, rest = take rest in a, b :: rest
  in
  let a, rest = take !blocks in
  blocks := rest;
  a

let free at n =
  let n = words n in
  let rec put = function
    | (a, size) :: rest when a < at -> (a, size) :: put rest
    | rest -> (at, n) :: rest
  in
  let rec join = function
    | (a, size) :: (b, more) :: rest when a + size = b ->
        join ((a, size + more) :: rest)
    | b :: rest -> b :: join rest
    | [] -> []
  in
  blocks := join (put !blocks)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Mixes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A pixel's byte is a colour of Plan 9's table (rgbv: TinyMachineDevices
 * says how it is made): two bits of red, two of how bright (v), four of
 * green and blue, turned by the first two so that a row of 16 is a
 * ramp. Its red, green and blue (TinyMachineDevices's formula again:
 * the machine is the host's code, which the kernel does not link): *)
let rgb i =
  let r = i lsr 6 and v = (i lsr 4) land 3 in
  let j = (i - v + r) land 15 in
  let g = j lsr 2 and b = j land 3 in
  let den = max r (max g b) in
  if den = 0 then (17 * v, 17 * v, 17 * v)
  else
    let num = 17 * ((4 * den) + v) in
    (r * num / den, g * num / den, b * num / den)

(* A colour's mixes, for a mask of levels (a grey font's): 1,024 bytes,
 * four rows of 256, a row a level of the mask's (its byte's two high
 * bits: 0, 85, 170, 255 are 0 to 3), its byte k what a pixel of colour
 * k becomes: as it was, a third of the ink, two thirds, the ink; each
 * the colour of the table nearest to the mix. Made by TinyMemory's
 * mix_table when the colour is first drawn with, from [palette] (each
 * colour's red, green and blue, 768 bytes, made at the first), and kept
 * for good: an address in [mixes] (0: not made). (old: made here, by
 * the 16 colours a mix can be near: tiny-ml's array reads, some 35
 * instructions each, were 3.5 million instructions a colour, half a
 * second of the machine's; tiny-windows' first menu, its colours made,
 * drawn so late that the click on it was taken for its last item,
 * exit) *)
let mixes = Array.make 256 0
let palette = ref 0

let mix ink =
  if !palette = 0 then begin
    palette := alloc 768;
    for i = 0 to 255 do
      let r, g, b = rgb i in
      pokeb (!palette + (3 * i)) r;
      pokeb (!palette + (3 * i) + 1) g;
      pokeb (!palette + (3 * i) + 2) b
    done
  end;
  if mixes.(ink) = 0 then begin
    let at = alloc 1024 in
    mix_table at ink !palette;
    mixes.(ink) <- at
  end;
  mixes.(ink)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The font *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The machine's font: faces of 128 characters, a face's rows one after
 * the other, a row's left pixel the low bit of its first byte. The
 * first face is 8 by 16, a row a byte, and may be all the font has
 * (xv6's font1.bin, which mini-9pi's console has too). tiny.font
 * (fonts/README.md, made of Ubuntu Mono) has three more after it:
 * bold 8 by 16, large 16 by 32 (a row two bytes), and large bold.
 * grey.font has the same faces, a pixel two bits (the depth, 2), its
 * level: 0 none, 3 the ink, 1 and 2 a third and two of it, the
 * letters' edges (a row then w / 4 bytes, each face twice as large).
 * A face is made a mask: a byte a pixel (255 where it is set, so that
 * a character's row is two words of mask for draw.tm's glyphs; 85 and
 * 170 the two greys), the characters side by side in an image of 128
 * characters' width, so that a character is a draw. *)
let mask bits depth w h at =
  let bytes = ((w * depth) + 7) lsr 3 and top = (1 lsl depth) - 1 in
  for c = 0 to 127 do
    for row = 0 to h - 1 do
      for col = 0 to w - 1 do
        let b = col * depth in
        pokeb (at + (row * 128 * w) + (c * w) + col)
          (255 / top * ((peekb (bits + (((c * h) + row) * bytes) + (b lsr 3))
                         lsr (b land 7)) land top))
      done
    done
  done;
  { r = rect 0 0 (128 * w) h; at = at; repl = false }

(* where the font's faces after the first are (0: it has none), and its
 * depth, a pixel's bits: 1, or 2 for grey.font *)
let faces = ref 0
let depth = ref 1

(* [font_mask bits size at]: the font of size bytes at bits, its first
 * face made a mask at at (16 KB), the others' place kept for styled; a
 * font of 40,960 bytes has levels (grey.font, twice tiny.font's) *)
let font_mask bits size at =
  depth := if size = 40960 then 2 else 1;
  faces := if size > 2048 then bits + (2048 * !depth) else 0;
  mask bits !depth 8 16 at

(* the mixes of src when it is a colour and the font has levels: what a
 * text is drawn with (0: none, its mask set or not) *)
let mixing (src : image) =
  if !depth = 2 && src.repl && width src = 1 && height src = 1
  then mix (peekb src.at) else 0

(* a text, its top left corner at (x, y): each character the ink src
 * through the font's mask (a byte beyond the font's 128 is a ?) *)
let text (dst : image) x y (src : image) (font : image) s =
  let n = String.length s in
  let mix = mixing src in
  (* A text all inside dst, in a colour, at a whole word (what a program
   * draws nearly always): all its characters by one call of draw.tm's
   * glyphs, which works a word at a time; with levels its glyphs_mixed,
   * a byte at a time where a row is not blank. *)
  if n > 0 && not dst.repl && src.repl && width src = 1 && height src = 1
     && x >= dst.r.x0 && y >= dst.r.y0
     && x + (8 * n) <= dst.r.x1 && y + 16 <= dst.r.y1
     && (pixel dst x y) land 3 = 0 && (width dst) land 3 = 0
  then
    if mix <> 0 then glyphs_mixed (pixel dst x y) (width dst) mix font.at s n
    else glyphs (pixel dst x y) (width dst) (peekb src.at) font.at s n
  else
    for i = 0 to n - 1 do
      let c = Char.code s.[i] in
      draw_mixed mix dst (rect (x + (8 * i)) y (x + (8 * i) + 8) (y + 16)) src
        (Some font) (8 * if c > 127 then 63 else c) 0
    done

(* a row of pixels given as they are, its left end at (x, y): the n
 * bytes of s from off, those that fall in dst. What a picture that
 * comes from elsewhere is drawn by, a row a message (Plan 9's load) *)
let pixels (dst : image) x y s off n =
  if y >= dst.r.y0 && y < dst.r.y1 then begin
    let row = dst.at + ((y - dst.r.y0) * width dst) - dst.r.x0 + x in
    let first = max 0 (dst.r.x0 - x) and last = min n (dst.r.x1 - x) in
    (* old: for k = first to last - 1 do
     *   pokeb (row + k) (Char.code s.[off + k]) done:
     * two calls of C a pixel, 300 instructions; a picture's row of 320
     * was 12 ms of the machine's time *)
    if last > first then row_bytes s (off + first) (row + first) (last - first)
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Styled text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The faces of a word processor's styles, a mask each, made when first
 * asked for: bold, large, and those two, the font's own when it has
 * them (tiny.font), else made from its first face (font1.bin): bold,
 * each stroke one pixel wider, but for a gap of one pixel, which stays
 * (drawn twice, a pixel apart, an m was a block); large, each pixel 2
 * by 2. Italic is made from the upright face, real or made, its rows
 * slanted, the top ones 3 pixels right, 6 when large (its cells 11
 * wide, 22, so that a character's slant is in its own cell). Made once,
 * at the first text that needs one: a large one is some 65,000 pixels. *)
let derived = Array.make 8 None

(* src's characters, each pixel scale by scale, bold, slanted; a
 * pixel's level kept (a grey font's) *)
let make (src : image) scale bold slant =
  let sw = width src / 128 in
  let cw = (sw * scale) + slant and ch = height src * scale in
  let w = 128 * cw in
  let at = alloc (w * ch) in
  row_fill at 0 (w * ch);
  for c = 0 to 127 do
    for row = 0 to ch - 1 do
      let shift = slant * (ch - 1 - row) / ch
      and line = src.at + (row / scale * width src) + (c * sw) in
      let level col = if col >= 0 && col < sw then peekb (line + col) else 0 in
      let set col = level col <> 0 in
      for col = 0 to (sw * scale) - 1 do
        let k = col / scale in
        if set k then pokeb (at + (row * w) + (c * cw) + col + shift) (level k)
        else if bold && set (k - 1) && not (set (k + 1)) then
          pokeb (at + (row * w) + (c * cw) + col + shift) (level (k - 1))
      done
    done
  done;
  { r = rect 0 0 w ch; at = at; repl = false }

(* kind: italic 1, large 2, bold 4 *)
let rec derive (font : image) kind =
  match derived.(kind) with
  | Some f -> f
  | None ->
      let large = kind land 2 <> 0 in
      let f =
        if kind land 1 <> 0 then
          make (if kind = 1 then font else derive font (kind land 6)) 1 false
            (if large then 6 else 3)
        else if !faces <> 0 then
          let w = if large then 16 else 8
          and at = if kind = 4 then 0 else if kind = 2 then 2048 else 10240 in
          mask (!faces + (at * !depth)) !depth w (2 * w) (alloc (256 * w * w))
        else make font (if large then 2 else 1) (kind land 4 <> 0) 0
      in
      derived.(kind) <- Some f;
      f

(* a row of fat pixels, each byte of s a colour, a square of 4 by 4: a
 * run of one colour filled at once, row by row, what is outside dst
 * left (a paint's picture, a row a message) *)
let fat (dst : image) x y s =
  let n = String.length s and i = ref 0 in
  while !i < n do
    let j = ref (!i + 1) in
    while !j < n && s.[!j] = s.[!i] do incr j done;
    let x0 = max dst.r.x0 (x + (4 * !i)) and x1 = min dst.r.x1 (x + (4 * !j)) in
    if x1 > x0 then
      for row = max dst.r.y0 y to min dst.r.y1 (y + 4) - 1 do
        row_fill (pixel dst x0 row) (Char.code s.[!i]) (x1 - x0)
      done;
    i := !j
  done

(* a text in a style, its top left corner at (x, y): bold 1, italic 2,
 * underlined 4, large 8 (16 by 32 a character); or 16, fat pixels *)
let styled (dst : image) x y (src : image) (font : image) style s =
  if style land 16 <> 0 then fat dst x y s
  else
  let kind =
    (if style land 2 <> 0 then 1 else 0)
    lor (if style land 8 <> 0 then 2 else 0)
    lor (if style land 1 <> 0 then 4 else 0)
  in
  let f = if kind = 0 then font else derive font kind in
  let scale = if style land 8 <> 0 then 2 else 1 in
  let cw = 8 * scale and fw = width f / 128 and n = String.length s in
  let mix = mixing src in
  (* bold, underlined or neither: 8 by 16 cells, the plain text's, so
   * text and its word at a time (old: a draw a character, some 13,000
   * instructions: tiny-emacs in bold, a screen of 2,400, was 30 million) *)
  if kind land 3 = 0 then text dst x y src f s
  else
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    let c = Char.code s.[i] in
    let x0 = x + (cw * i) in
    draw_mixed mix dst (rect x0 y (x0 + fw) (y + height f)) src (Some f)
      (fw * if c > 127 then 63 else c) 0
  done;
  if style land 4 <> 0 then
    draw dst
      (rect x (y + height f - (2 * scale)) (x + (cw * n)) (y + height f - scale))
      src None 0 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The messages *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a connection: a program's images by its numbers for them, 0 the one
 * it was given; the font its texts are in *)
type conn = { mutable images : (int * image) list; font : image }

let connect (screen : image) (font : image) = { images = [ 0, screen ]; font = font }
let find (c : conn) id =
  try List.assoc id c.images with Not_found -> raise (Graphics "no such image")

let release (c : conn) id =
  let i = find c id in
  if id = 0 then raise (Graphics "image 0 is not freed");
  free i.at (width i * height i);
  c.images <- List.filter (fun (k, _) -> k <> id) c.images

(* the connection's end: what the program left *)
let disconnect (c : conn) =
  List.iter (fun (id, _) -> if id <> 0 then release c id) c.images

(* What the 'c' message (the mouse's look) does: set by the kernel, which
 * writes it to the machine's mouse word; nothing on the host. *)
let cursor_hook = ref (fun (_ : int) -> ())

(* the message at s.[i], its numbers by arg: whole, its size
 * checked by messages *)
let message (c : conn) s i arg =
  let len k =
    if arg k < 0 then raise (Graphics "a negative length") else arg k in
  match s.[i] with
  | 'a' ->
      let w = arg 3 - arg 1 and h = arg 4 - arg 2 in
      if w <= 0 || h <= 0 || w > 2048 || h > 2048 then
        raise (Graphics "an image of no size, or too large");
      if List.exists (fun (k, _) -> k = arg 0) c.images then release c (arg 0);
      let made =
        { r = rect (arg 1) (arg 2) (arg 3) (arg 4);
          at = alloc (w * h); repl = arg 5 <> 0 }
      in
      row_fill made.at (arg 6 land 255) (w * h);
      c.images <- (arg 0, made) :: c.images
  | 'f' -> release c (arg 0)
  | 'c' -> !cursor_hook (arg 0)
  | 'd' ->
      let mask = if arg 2 < 0 then None else Some (find c (arg 2)) in
      draw (find c (arg 0)) (rect (arg 3) (arg 4) (arg 5) (arg 6))
        (find c (arg 1)) mask (arg 7) (arg 8)
  | 'l' ->
      line (find c (arg 0)) (arg 2) (arg 3) (arg 4) (arg 5) (find c (arg 1))
  | 's' ->
      text (find c (arg 0)) (arg 2) (arg 3) (find c (arg 1)) c.font
        (String.sub s (i + 11) (len 4))
  | 't' ->
      styled (find c (arg 0)) (arg 2) (arg 3) (find c (arg 1)) c.font (arg 5)
        (String.sub s (i + 13) (len 4))
  | _ (* 'p' *) -> pixels (find c (arg 0)) (arg 1) (arg 2) s (i + 9) (len 3)

(* a write's bytes: whole messages (the header says which), each done
 * in turn; a bad one skipped, the ones after it done, then Graphics
 * raised with the first's why. A message cut short, or unknown, ends
 * them: where the next starts is not known. (old: a bad one raised at
 * once, the rest of the write not done: a page's picture with no room
 * left, its pixels' messages after it, and the texts after those) *)
let messages (c : conn) s =
  let n = String.length s in
  let first = ref "" in
  let rec next i =
    if i < n then begin
      let arg k =
        let at = i + 1 + (2 * k) in
        if at + 2 > n then raise (Graphics "a message cut short");
        let v = Char.code s.[at] + (256 * Char.code s.[at + 1]) in
        if v >= 32768 then v - 65536 else v
      in
      let size =
        match s.[i] with
        | 'a' -> 15 | 'f' | 'c' -> 3 | 'd' -> 19 | 'l' -> 13
        | 's' -> 11 + max 0 (arg 4) | 't' -> 13 + max 0 (arg 4)
        | 'p' -> 9 + max 0 (arg 3)
        | _ -> raise (Graphics "an unknown message")
      in
      if i + size > n then raise (Graphics "a message cut short");
      (try message c s i arg
       with Graphics why -> if !first = "" then first := why);
      next (i + size)
    end
  in
  next 0;
  if !first <> "" then raise (Graphics !first)
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelGraphics.mli
9656
(* Tiny graphics: the essential of Plan 9's draw library (libdraw and
 * libmemdraw; ix's twins are lib_graphics/ and mini-9pi's
 * lib_memdraw), for tiny-machine's screen: 1024 by 768 pixels, a byte
 * each, a colour of Plan 9's table. Not a program: TinyKernel.ml's part
 * that draws (plan_tiny_windows.md).
 *
 * It asks a few functions of bytes of its machine, TinyMemory's: peekb
 * and pokeb, and a row's loops (copied, filled, a colour where a mask
 * is set, a colour mixed by a mask's levels; a text's characters),
 * which are assembly on tiny-machine and an array's on the host.
 *
 * What is kept of Plan 9's:
 *
 * - {b One operation}, [draw dst r src mask p]: the pixels of dst's
 *   rectangle r are src's from the point p on, where mask's are set
 *   (everywhere without one). A rectangle filled, a window copied to
 *   the screen, a text scrolled (an image drawn on itself), a
 *   character (the font is a mask, the ink the source) are all it.
 * - {b A colour is an image}, of one pixel, that repeats: so draw needs
 *   no colour argument, and a pattern costs nothing more.
 * - {b The kernel has the pixels, a program says what}: a program
 *   writes messages (a letter, then numbers of 16 bits) naming images
 *   by numbers of its own; [messages] decodes them for a connection.
 *   So a program draws without reaching the screen's memory, which
 *   TinyKernel.ml's partitions could not give it, and a window system
 *   forwards a program's messages after changing the numbers.
 *
 * The one operation, drawn. The pixel of dst at (x, y), for each (x,
 * y) of r, becomes the pixel of src at (x, y) moved by p - r's corner,
 * if the mask's pixel at that same point is set:
 *
 *         src (and the mask)                  dst
 *     +--------------------+          +------------------+
 *     |    p               |          |                  |
 *     |     +-------+      |          |  r +-------+     |
 *     |     | these | -----|--------> |    | here  |     |
 *     |     +-------+      |          |    +-------+     |
 *     +--------------------+          +------------------+
 *
 * r is first cut to what dst has, then to what src and the mask have
 * pixels for, so nothing is ever read or written outside an image;
 * an image that repeats has a pixel everywhere. What a program does
 * with it:
 *
 *     a rectangle filled     draw dst r colour, no mask, any p
 *                            (the colour: 1 by 1, repeating)
 *     a window shown         draw screen r window, no mask, p r's
 *                            corner in the window's coordinates
 *     a text scrolled up     draw w (all but the last line) w, no
 *                            mask, p 16 lower: drawn on itself
 *     a character            draw dst (its cell, 8 by 16) ink, the
 *                            font as the mask, p (8 * its code, 0):
 *                            the font is one image, 1024 by 16
 *
 * and as bytes, a rectangle from (10, 20) to (30, 40) of image 0
 * filled with image 1 (TinyLibDraw's d_fill 0 1 10 20 30 40), 19 bytes:
 *
 *     d   00 00   01 00   ff ff   0a 00 14 00 1e 00 28 00   00 00 00 00
 *         dst 0   src 1   no mask the rectangle             p
 *
 * Dropped: pixels of other depths and channels (one byte, the table's
 * index), alpha and Porter and Duff's operators (a mask is set or not,
 * but for a colour through a font of levels, grey.font: mixed by a
 * table made for the colour),
 * a clipping rectangle apart from an image's own, a mask's own point
 * (it is the source's, as libdraw's draw), ellipses, arcs, polygons and
 * thick lines, fonts (one, the machine's 8 by 16, its bold and its
 * large 16 by 32, and italic made of them, slanted; or font1.bin alone,
 * the bold and the large made of it too) and their cache,
 * layers and windows (TinyWindows.ml composes whole images), the
 * screen's refresh.
 *
 * The messages, each a letter then 16-bit numbers, the low byte first,
 * signed; an image 0 is the connection's own (its window, or the
 * screen):
 *
 *     a id x0 y0 x1 y1 repl colour    an image made, of that rectangle and colour
 *                                     (the one that had this number freed)
 *     f id                            freed
 *     d dst src mask x0 y0 x1 y1 px py      draw (mask -1: none)
 *     l dst src x0 y0 x1 y1           a line, both ends drawn
 *     s dst src x y n, n bytes        a text, its top left corner at (x, y)
 *     t dst src x y n style, n bytes  a text in a style: bold 1, italic 2,
 *                                     underlined 4, large 8 (16 by 32);
 *                                     or 16, fat pixels: a byte a colour,
 *                                     a square of 4 by 4
 *     p dst x y n, n bytes            a row of pixels, its left end at (x, y)
 *
 * They are a few of Plan 9's own draw messages (principia's
 * kernel/devices/screen/drawmesg.c has 27), f, d and s keeping their
 * letters; what is dropped of them is said above.
 *
 * Exercises:
 * - a row copied a word at a time where it can (draw.tm's row_copy);
 * - ellipses and filled polygons, for the playground's shapes;
 * - a mask of any level, 0 to 255, and a source of more than a colour
 *   mixed through it (here four levels, a colour's, the font's);
 * - a clipping rectangle per image, set by a message (a window's part
 *   that shows).
 *
 * Where it stands: under it TinyMemory (bytes, and three loops over a
 * row); around it TinyKernel, which gives each program a connection
 * and calls [messages] with what the program writes on its
 * descriptor 3; on the other side of those bytes TinyLibDraw, which
 * makes them, and TinyWindows, which renumbers them. In m-ix the
 * same three are lib_graphics's Draw (the program's side), the
 * kernel's draw device, and lib_memdraw (the pixels), with channels,
 * depths and alpha.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * One operation that copies a rectangle of bits, combined with what
 * is there, is BitBlt (Dan Ingalls, Xerox PARC, mid-1970s, for the
 * Alto and Smalltalk): with it windows, text, scrolling and menus
 * that pop up were one loop to make fast, and the bitmap display
 * became usable. It had sixteen ways to combine source and
 * destination, and a fill pattern beside the source. Rob Pike's
 * Blit (1982) carried it to Unix; Plan 9's draw (its third edition,
 * 2000) replaced the sixteen ways and the pattern by
 * two ideas kept here: a mask, and a source that repeats.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * In X11 a program sets up a graphics context (a function, a
 * foreground, a fill style, a tile, a stipple, a clip mask...) and
 * then calls one of many requests: fill a rectangle, copy an area,
 * draw a string. In Plan 9 a colour, a pattern, a picture and a
 * font's character are all the same thing, an image, and one call
 * with three images does what those requests do; the library is
 * small because there is one inner loop to get right.
 *
 * others:
 * The mask of levels left as an exercise is Porter and Duff's
 * compositing, which is what every system now draws with: PDF,
 * Quartz, Cairo, the HTML canvas (ix's own: lib_graphics's software
 * renderer, and mini-netscape's painting). They add paths filled
 * with antialiasing and a matrix on the coordinates; the rectangle
 * copied through a mask is still the operation at the bottom.
 *
 * References: R. Pike, "Graphics in Overlapping Bitmap
 * Layers" (ACM TOG 1983), the Blit's bitblt; R. Pike et al., "Plan 9
 * from Bell Labs" (1995) and draw(2), draw(3): the one operation, an
 * image a file's number; T. Porter and T. Duff, "Compositing Digital
 * Images" (SIGGRAPH 1984), what a mask of levels would bring; J.
 * Bresenham, "Algorithm for computer control of a digital plotter"
 * (IBM Systems Journal 1965), the line. *)

(* what a bad message or a drawing that cannot be is answered with *)
exception Graphics of string

(* a rectangle, its second corner outside it; an image: its rectangle,
 * where its bytes are in memory, whether it repeats *)
type rect = { x0 : int; y0 : int; x1 : int; y1 : int }
type image = { r : rect; at : int; repl : bool }
val rect : int -> int -> int -> int -> rect

(* The one operation, [draw dst r src mask px py]: dst's rectangle r
 * takes src's pixels from the point (px, py) on, where the mask's are
 * set (everywhere without one) *)
val draw : image -> rect -> image -> image option -> int -> int -> unit

(* the memory the images a program makes are in, outside the collected
 * heap: [arena at size] is all of it, [free at size] a block more,
 * [alloc size] a block taken, its address; [blocks] what is free (a
 * test's) *)
val arena : int -> int -> unit
val free : int -> int -> unit
val alloc : int -> int
val blocks : (int * int) list ref

(* [font_mask bits size at]: the font of size bytes at bits (font1.bin,
 * tiny.font or grey.font, whose pixels have levels: fonts/README.md),
 * its first face made a mask at at (16 KB); its other faces, when it
 * has them, kept for the styled texts *)
val font_mask : int -> int -> int -> image

(* a program's connection: its images by its own numbers, 0 the one it
 * was given to draw on; [connect screen font]. [messages] does a
 * string of them (Graphics after them when one was bad, the bad ones
 * skipped; at once when one is cut short or unknown); [disconnect]
 * frees what the program left *)
type conn
val connect : image -> image -> conn
val disconnect : conn -> unit
val messages : conn -> string -> unit
(* what the 'c' message (the mouse's look) does: set by the kernel,
 * which writes it to the machine's mouse word; nothing on the host *)
val cursor_hook : (int -> unit) ref

(* See TinyKernelIO.mli *)
open TinyMemory
open TinyKernelGraphics

open TinyKernelAudio

open TinyKernelMemory
