(*****************************************************************************)
(* Reads and writes: Some n done, None must wait *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the console's input, typed and not yet read, and its end *)
let typed = ref ""
let typed_end = ref false

(* the process that has the console raw (rawcons), or 0: its ^C is a
 * byte typed, not the kill of every process *)
let raw = ref 0
let raw_on () =
  List.exists (fun q -> q.pid = !raw) !procs

let read f a n =
  match f with
  | Link l ->
      (match l.heard with
       | [] -> None
       | m :: rest ->
           let k = min n (String.length m) in
           k_blit m 0 a k;
           l.heard <- rest;
           Some k)
  (* a message, whole (what is over n bytes is lost); the end *)
  | Call c ->
      (match il_hear c.il with
       | Some m -> let k = min n (String.length m) in k_blit m 0 a k; Some k
       | None -> if il_over c.il then Some 0 else None)
  | Console ->
      let t = !typed in
      let eot = not (raw_on ()) in
      if t = "" then (if !typed_end then Some 0 else None)
      (* ^D, but at a raw console: the read's end, nothing read, as
       * Plan 9's (old: a byte, and only the input's end ended a read) *)
      else if eot && t.[0] = '\004' then
        (typed := String.sub t 1 (String.length t - 1); Some 0)
      else begin
        (* up to a line's end, or a ^D *)
        let rec upto i =
          if i >= String.length t || i >= n then i
          else if t.[i] = '\n' then i + 1
          else if eot && t.[i] = '\004' then i
          else upto (i + 1) in
        let k = upto 0 in
        k_blit t 0 a k;
        typed := String.sub t k (String.length t - k);
        Some k
      end
  | Reader pi ->
      if pi.buf = "" then (if pi.writers = 0 then Some 0 else None)
      else begin
        let k = min n (String.length pi.buf) in
        k_blit pi.buf 0 a k;
        pi.buf <- String.sub pi.buf k (String.length pi.buf - k);
        Some k
      end
  | Writer _ | Draw _ | Post _ | Voice _ -> Some (-1)
  (* what the trace said, a line at a time; its end when the process ended *)
  | Trace t ->
      (match t.said with
       | m :: rest ->
           let k = min n (String.length m) in
           k_blit m 0 a k;
           t.said <- rest;
           Some k
       | [] -> (match traced_proc t with Some _ -> None | None -> Some 0))
  (* what was last written, once; its end when no writer is left *)
  | Peek b ->
      if b.fresh then
        (let k = min n (String.length b.last) in
         b.fresh <- false;
         k_blit b.last 0 a k;
         Some k)
      else if b.posters = 0 then Some 0
      else None
  | Open o -> (
      match o.node with
      | Rom (at, size) ->
          let k = max 0 (min n (size - o.off)) in
          row_copy a (at + o.off) k;
          o.off <- o.off + k;
          Some k
      (* a disk's file, from its blocks to the program's memory *)
      | Disk (r, i) when not (fs_is_dir r i) ->
          let k = fs_read_at r i o.off a n in
          o.off <- o.off + k;
          Some k
      | Data d ->
          let k = max 0 (min n (d.dsize - o.off)) in
          k_blit (Bytes.sub_string d.dbytes o.off k) 0 a k;
          o.off <- o.off + k;
          Some k
      (* (a directory's listing made once, not at each entry's read:
       * httpd read /bin's 55 entries one at a time, each making all
       * of them, 25.6 s; bugs/ix.md. old: let s = contents o.node) *)
      | _ ->
          let s =
            match o.listing with
            | Some s when o.off > 0 -> s
            | _ -> let s = contents o.node in o.listing <- Some s; s in
          let k = max 0 (min n (String.length s - o.off)) in
          k_blit s o.off a k;
          o.off <- o.off + k;
          Some k)

(* the network device's command (1 send, 2 take) on n bytes at the buffer *)
let net_command n cmd =
  poke net_dev net_buf; poke (net_dev + 4) n; poke (net_dev + 8) cmd

(* a packet to the wire: at the buffer, then the device's send *)
let net_send packet =
  let n = String.length packet in
  k_blit packet 0 net_buf n;
  net_command n 1

(* A traced process stopped, and the line that says why to its tracer
 * (a step ends there); stop's: where it is (its pc), then break (a
 * breakpoint's word), illegal and the word, fault and the address,
 * exec (its new program's first instruction), or step *)
let traced p = match p.traced with Some _ -> true | None -> false
let pause p line =
  p.state <- Stopped;
  match p.traced with
  | Some t -> t.step <- false; t.said <- t.said @ [ line ^ "\n" ]
  | None -> ()
let stop p why = pause p ("stopped " ^ string_of_int (reg p 16) ^ " " ^ why)

(* bytes in hexadecimal, two digits each *)
let hex_bytes l =
  let d = "0123456789abcdef" in
  String.concat "" (List.map (fun b ->
    String.make 1 d.[b lsr 4] ^ String.make 1 d.[b land 15]) l)

(* A tracer's command (plan_tiny_debugger.md), the numbers in decimal:
 * b addr, a breakpoint, the word there kept and 0 written in its place
 * (no instruction is 0: the process traps there, c_illegal); d addr,
 * the breakpoint removed, its word put back; r, the registers (r1 to
 * r15, then the pc); m addr n, n bytes in hexadecimal (1024 at most; a
 * breakpoint's are the word it hides); w addr v, a word written; y and
 * n, a stop at each call or not (trace); f, the children it forks
 * traced too, by the same tracer (trace -f); c, the stopped process
 * resumed; s, resumed for one instruction. From a breakpoint, c and s
 * run its word, then write the 0 again (run); from a call, they let
 * the call in. Bad if the command is none of these, or its address
 * not the process's. *)
let command t q words =
  let addr s =
    match int_of_string_opt s with
    | Some a when a land 3 = 0 -> ignore (user q a 4); a
    | _ -> raise Bad in
  let say m = t.said <- t.said @ [ m ^ "\n" ] in
  let unset a =
    (match List.assoc_opt a t.stops with
     | Some w -> mem_store q.mem a w
     | None -> ());
    t.stops <- List.filter (fun (b, _) -> b <> a) t.stops in
  match words, q.state with
  | [ "b"; s ], _ ->
      let a = addr s in
      if not (List.exists (fun (b, _) -> b = a) t.stops) then
        (t.stops <- t.stops @ [ a, mem_fetch q.mem a ]; mem_store q.mem a 0);
      say "ok"
  | [ "d"; s ], _ -> unset (addr s); say "ok"
  | [ "r" ], _ ->
      say (String.concat " " (List.init 16 (fun k ->
        (if k = 15 then "pc" else "r" ^ string_of_int (k + 1))
        ^ " " ^ string_of_int (reg q (k + 1)))))
  | [ "m"; s; k ], _ ->
      (match int_of_string_opt s, int_of_string_opt k with
       | Some a, Some n when n > 0 && n <= 1024 ->
           say (hex_bytes (List.init n (fun i ->
             match List.assoc_opt ((a + i) land lnot 3) t.stops with
             | Some w -> (w lsr (8 * ((a + i) land 3))) land 255
             | None -> peekb (user q (a + i) 1))))
       | _ -> raise Bad)
  | [ "w"; s; v ], _ ->
      let a = addr s in
      (match int_of_string_opt v with
       | Some v when List.exists (fun (b, _) -> b = a) t.stops ->
           t.stops <- List.map (fun (b, w) -> b, if b = a then v else w) t.stops
       | Some v -> mem_store q.mem a v
       | None -> raise Bad);
      say "ok"
  | [ "y" ], _ -> t.calls <- true; say "ok"
  | [ "n" ], _ -> t.calls <- false; say "ok"
  | [ "f" ], _ -> t.follow <- true; say "ok"
  | [ ("c" | "s") as c ], Stopped ->
      let pc = reg q 16 in
      (match List.assoc_opt pc t.stops with
       | Some w when t.call < 0 -> mem_store q.mem pc w; t.over <- pc
       | _ -> ());
      t.step <- c = "s";
      q.state <- Ready
  | _ -> raise Bad

let write f a n =
  match f with
  | Link l ->
      if n > 1024 then Some (-1)
      else begin
        l.asked <- l.asked + 1;
        net_send (ip_packet ip_icmp net_machine l.peer
          (icmp_message icmp_ask l.lid l.asked (k_string a n)));
        Some n
      end
  (* a message: now, or when the other end has acknowledged enough of
   * those before *)
  | Call c ->
      if n > il_max || il_over c.il then Some (-1)
      else if n = 0 then Some 0
      else if il_room c.il then
        (net_send (il_write c.il (k_string a n) !ticks); Some n)
      else None
  | Console -> k_console a n; Some n
  | Writer pi ->
      if pi.readers = 0 then Some (-1)
      else if String.length pi.buf = 512 then None
      else
        (let k = min n (512 - String.length pi.buf) in
         pi.buf <- pi.buf ^ k_string a k;
         Some k)
  | Open o -> (
      match o.node with
      | Data d when o.writes ->
          let at = min o.off d.dsize in
          if at + n > Bytes.length d.dbytes then begin
            let b = Bytes.make (max (at + n) (2 * Bytes.length d.dbytes)) ' ' in
            Bytes.blit d.dbytes 0 b 0 d.dsize;
            d.dbytes <- b
          end;
          Bytes.blit_string (k_string a n) 0 d.dbytes at n;
          d.dsize <- max d.dsize (at + n);
          d.dtime <- date ();
          o.off <- at + n;
          Some n
      | Disk (0, i) when o.writes ->
          (try fs_write_at i o.off a n; o.off <- o.off + n; Some n
           with Disk_full -> Some (-1))
      | _ -> Some (-1))
  (* messages, whole; a bad one is said on the console, the write -1 *)
  | Draw d ->
      (try messages d.conn (k_string a n); Some n
       with Graphics why -> puts ("draw: " ^ why ^ "\n"); Some (-1))
  | Post b -> b.last <- k_string a n; b.fresh <- true; Some n
  (* sounds, whole, when they fit in the ring, else a look again when
   * the speaker played what is missing, 20 samples a tick (old: in 10
   * ms, each look a copy of the write: play's blocks of 2,048 samples
   * copied 25 times, half the machine's instructions); a bad one, or
   * more than a ring, -1 *)
  | Voice v ->
      (match (try Some (sounds (k_string a n)) with Bad_sound -> None) with
       | Some l
         when List.fold_left (fun acc snd -> acc + sound_length snd) 0 l <= ring
         ->
           let missing = speak v l in
           if missing = 0 then Some n
           else begin
             let at = !ticks + 1 + (missing / 20) in
             if !alarm = 0 || at < !alarm then alarm := at;
             None
           end
       | _ -> Some (-1))
  (* a command to the traced process, each answered by a line but c,
   * which its next stop answers *)
  | Trace t ->
      (match traced_proc t with
       | Some q ->
           (try
              command t q (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.trim (k_string a n)));
              Some n
            with
            | Bad -> Some (-1)
            (* (a breakpoint in a shared text, and no room for its copy) *)
            | No_room -> Some (-1))
       | None -> Some (-1))
  | Reader _ | Peek _ -> Some (-1)

(* whether a read would not wait *)
let readable f =
  match f with
  | Console -> !typed <> "" || !typed_end
  | Reader pi -> pi.buf <> "" || pi.writers = 0
  | Peek b -> b.fresh || b.posters = 0
  | Link l -> (match l.heard with [] -> false | _ -> true)
  | Call c -> il_readable c.il
  | Trace t ->
      t.said <> []
      || (match traced_proc t with Some _ -> false | None -> true)
  | _ -> true

(* TinyKernel's reads and writes: what a descriptor's file does with n
 * bytes at a kernel's address, for each kind of file (a node, a pipe's
 * end, the console, a connection to the screen, a box, a link, a call,
 * a voice, a trace). Each answers at once, Some n done, or None: it
 * must wait, and TinyKernelCalls makes the call a Waiting process,
 * tried again by the scheduler.
 *
 *     read f a n   Some 0      the end (a pipe with no writer left)
 *                  Some k      k bytes put at a
 *                  Some (-1)   an error
 *                  None        nothing yet: try again later
 *
 * A trace is a file too (plan_tiny_debugger.md): its tracer writes
 * commands to it (a breakpoint, the registers, a step) and reads why
 * the process stopped.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * one read and one write for every kind of file, the devices and the
 * debugger's process included, as Plan 9's /proc/n/ctl is written to
 * and read from where Unix has ptrace's calls.
 *)

(* the console's input, typed and not yet read, and its end; the process
 * that has the console raw (rawcons), or 0, and whether it is alive *)
val typed : string ref
val typed_end : bool ref
val raw : int ref
val raw_on : unit -> bool

(* [read f a n]: up to n bytes of the file at the kernel's address a *)
val read : TinyKernelFiles.file -> int -> int -> int option

(* the network device's command (1 send, 2 take) on n bytes at its
 * buffer; a packet sent to the wire *)
val net_command : int -> int -> unit
val net_send : string -> unit

(* whether a process is traced; [pause p line]: it stopped, the line
 * said to its tracer; [stop p why]: the same, at its pc *)
val traced : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> bool
val pause : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> string -> unit
val stop : TinyKernelProcs.proc -> string -> unit

(* [write f a n]: n bytes at the kernel's address a written to the file *)
val write : TinyKernelFiles.file -> int -> int -> int option

(* whether a read would not wait *)
val readable : TinyKernelFiles.file -> bool

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The machine: entry.tm's, memory.tm's and runtime.c's functions *)

external k_init : unit -> unit = "k_init"
external k_run : int -> int = "k_run"
external k_step : int -> int = "k_step"
external k_tval : unit -> int = "k_tval"
external k_timer : int -> unit = "k_timer"
external k_ie : int -> unit = "k_ie"
external k_clock : unit -> int = "k_clock"
external k_rate : unit -> int = "k_rate"
external k_cores : unit -> int = "k_cores"
external k_window : int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> unit = "k_window"
external k_copy : int -> int -> int -> unit = "k_copy"
external k_zero : int -> int -> unit = "k_zero"
external k_end : unit -> int = "k_end"
external peek : int -> int = "peek"
external poke : int -> int -> unit = "poke"
external k_string : int -> int -> string = "k_string"
external k_blit : string -> int -> int -> int -> unit = "k_blit"
external k_console : int -> int -> unit = "k_console"
external k_font : unit -> int = "k_font"
external k_font_size : unit -> int = "k_font_size"

(* The memory. The first 32 MB are the kernel's (runtime.c says how they
 * are used): its image, the processes' frames, the images it draws, the
 * screen, its heap. The processes' memory is above, TinyKernelMemory's:
 * a partition of the size a program asks for (1 MB if it does not say),
 * found when it starts. There are at most [nslots] processes; a slot is
 * a process's frame. (old: 8 slots and 128 MB, before the cores:
 * tiny-build -j 4 runs four rc and four compilers of 32 MB) *)
let nslots = 16
let frame slot = 0xb40000 + (slot * 68)
(* The devices are at the top of memory. Their addresses are written as
 * negative numbers, which the machine takes modulo its memory size, so
 * the kernel works whatever that size is (-16 is the last 16 bytes). *)
let cons_out = -16
let halt_dev = -12
let cons_in = -8
let mouse_dev = -4
(* the network's four words (an address, a length, a command, whether
 * there is a wire), and a packet's place in memory, after the frames *)
let net_dev = -48
let net_buf = 0xb50000
(* the speaker's word (its ring's address written, the samples played
 * read), and its ring, in the megabytes nothing else uses *)
let speaker_dev = -52
let ring_at = 0xc00000
(* the disk's four words: a block, an address, a command, a status; the
 * first, read, is the disk's size in blocks (0: no disk) *)
let disk_dev = -32
(* the date at the boot, seconds since 2000-01-01 (the machine's) *)
let date_dev = -56
(* the seed, for the programs' first random numbers (the machine's;
 * 0: none) *)
let seed_dev = -60
(* The cores (plan_tiny_multicore.md): the kernel is core 0's, the
 * others run processes only (entry.tm's slave). Core k's mailbox: the
 * frame to run (0: none), the window (base, size), the slice; then
 * the trap's cause and value, posted. The interrupt between cores:
 * core k's raised by storing k at -64(r0); read, the cores that raised
 * this one's. *)
let cores = k_cores ()
let ipi_dev = -64
let mailbox k = 0xb41000 + (64 * k)
(* the interrupts taken, the cores' always when there are several *)
let k_ie sources = k_ie (if cores > 1 then sources lor 32 else sources)

(* a trap's causes (TinyMachine.ml's), the timer's period *)
let c_sys = 1
let c_illegal = 2
let c_fault = 3
let c_intr = 4
(* The timer's period is 2.5 ms of the machine's time, whatever its
 * speed: 20,000 instructions at 8 million a second. The programs count
 * time in these ticks (a game's frames, IL's waits, ping), so they run
 * at the same pace on a faster machine. *)
let tick = let r = k_rate () in if r < 400 then 20000 else r / 400

let puts s =
  for i = 0 to String.length s - 1 do pokeb cons_out (Char.code s.[i]) done
(* (what the disk has not been told yet is told first) *)
let halt status = fs_commit (); poke halt_dev status

(* TinyKernel's machine: what the kernel in ML reaches tiny-machine by,
 * the externals of entry.tm (a process run until its trap, the timer,
 * the interrupts), memory.tm (bytes copied, zeroed) and runtime.c (a
 * word read and written, strings to and from memory), and the devices'
 * addresses at the top of memory.
 *
 *     the kernel in ML   ──peek/poke──►   a device's words (-16: the last
 *                                         16 bytes, whatever the size)
 *                        ──k_run──────►   a process, until its trap: the
 *                                         cause (c_sys, c_fault...) back
 *
 * The first 32 MB are the kernel's (runtime.c says how): its image,
 * the processes' frames, the images it draws, the screen, its heap;
 * the processes' memory is above, TinyKernelMemory's. A device's
 * address is a negative number, which the machine takes modulo its
 * memory's size, so the kernel works whatever that size is.
 *
 * others:
 * Plan 9's kernel reaches its hardware the same way, a few functions in
 * assembly (each port's l.s) below C; here they are below ML, and the
 * devices are words at addresses.
 *)

(* entry.tm's: the machine set up; a process's frame run until its trap
 * (the cause back), one instruction of it; the trap's value; the timer
 * armed; the machine's clock *)

external k_tval : unit -> int = "k_tval"

 * ends; a word read, written; bytes as a string, a string into memory;

external k_console : int -> int -> unit = "k_console"
external k_font : unit -> int = "k_font"

 * its registers *)

 * (its words, its packet's buffer), the speaker (its ring's place), the

(* See TinyKernelMemory.mli *)

open TinyMemory

(* memory.tm's loops and runtime.c's words (TinyKernel.ml names them
 * too) *)
external k_copy : int -> int -> int -> unit = "k_copy"
external k_window : int -> int -> int -> int -> int -> unit = "k_window"

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Partitions *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The processes' memory is above the kernel's first 32 MB, up to 64 KB
 * below the top of the machine's 256 MB (the devices'). A partition's
 * size is a whole number of megabytes. *)
let part = 0x100000
let mem_low = 0x2000000
let mem_high = 0xfff0000

(* a process's memory: its partition's start and size (0: none yet);
 * a number, to tell two apart; its text, with segments (below); with
 * pages (further below), its root table, its size and its text's *)
type space = {
  sid : int; mutable sbase : int; mutable ssize : int;
  mutable text : text option;
  mutable root : int; mutable vsize : int; mutable tsz : int;
}
(* a program's text, shared by its runs: its block, the file it came
 * from (key, "" for none) and that file's date and size then (stamp),
 * its runs, and whether an exec may still take it: not when its file
 * was written since, or the text itself (a breakpoint) *)
and text = {
  tblock : space; key : string; stamp : string;
  mutable users : int; mutable known : bool;
}

(* the blocks given: the spaces' and the texts' *)
let used = ref []
let next_sid = ref 1

(* no partition free now (TinyKernelCalls's with_room waits for one) *)
exception No_room

let mem_empty () =
  let sp = { sid = !next_sid; sbase = 0; ssize = 0; text = None;
             root = 0; vsize = 0; tsz = 0 } in
  incr next_sid;
  sp

(* The first gap of [size] bytes between the partitions in use, ordered
 * by address, but the one of [except] (exec replaces it). *)
let room size except =
  let others = List.filter (fun sp -> sp.sid <> except) !used in
  let rec insert sp = function
    | [] -> [ sp ]
    | r :: rest ->
        if sp.sbase <= r.sbase then sp :: r :: rest else r :: insert sp rest in
  let sorted = List.fold_left (fun l sp -> insert sp l) [] others in
  let rec go at = function
    | [] -> if at + size <= mem_high then at else raise No_room
    | sp :: rest ->
        if at + size <= sp.sbase then at
        else go (max at (sp.sbase + sp.ssize)) rest in
  go mem_low sorted

(* sp given a partition of [size] bytes, its old one let go: the same
 * when it has that size already; No_room, sp as it was *)
let mem_place sp size =
  let b = if size = sp.ssize then sp.sbase else room size sp.sid in
  if sp.ssize = 0 then used := !used @ [ sp ];
  sp.sbase <- b;
  sp.ssize <- size

let release sp =
  used := List.filter (fun r -> r.sid <> sp.sid) !used;
  sp.ssize <- 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Segments *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Chosen at the boot (TinyKernel.ml: /lib/memory says segments). Off,
 * no space has a text, and every function below is the partition's *)
let segments = ref false

(* the texts given, which an exec looks in *)
let texts = ref []

let text_size sp = match sp.text with Some t -> t.tblock.ssize | None -> 0

(* sp's text let go: its block too when sp was its last run *)
let drop_text sp =
  (match sp.text with
   | Some t ->
       t.users <- t.users - 1;
       if t.users = 0 then begin
         release t.tblock;
         texts := List.filter (fun u -> u.tblock.sid <> t.tblock.sid) !texts
       end
   | None -> ());
  sp.text <- None

(* a copy of t, one process's, which no exec takes; No_room *)
let copy_text t =
  let b = mem_empty () in
  mem_place b t.tblock.ssize;
  k_copy b.sbase t.tblock.sbase b.ssize;
  let mine = { tblock = b; key = ""; stamp = ""; users = 1; known = false } in
  texts := mine :: !texts;
  mine

(* a text of its own for a process that writes in its text (the kernel
 * does, for a tracer's breakpoint): the one it shares copied, or the one
 * it alone runs no longer taken by an exec *)
let own_text sp =
  match sp.text with
  | Some t when t.users > 1 ->
      let mine = copy_text t in
      t.users <- t.users - 1;
      sp.text <- Some mine
  | Some t -> t.known <- false
  | None -> ()

(* The program of a file given to sp: tsize bytes of text (0: none, or
 * no segments), the rest of size its data. A text that runs already,
 * from the same file unchanged, is shared; else a block of its own. True
 * when the text is new, for the caller to write; No_room, sp as it was *)
let seg_load sp key stamp tsize size =
  if not !segments || tsize = 0 then (mem_place sp size; drop_text sp; true)
  else begin
    let found =
      if key = "" then None
      else List.find_opt (fun t -> t.known && t.key = key && t.stamp = stamp)
             !texts in
    let t = match found with
      | Some t -> t
      | None ->
          let b = mem_empty () in
          mem_place b tsize;
          { tblock = b; key; stamp; users = 0; known = key <> "" } in
    (try mem_place sp (size - tsize)
     with No_room -> (if found = None then release t.tblock); raise No_room);
    if found = None then texts := t :: !texts;
    t.users <- t.users + 1;
    drop_text sp;
    sp.text <- Some t;
    found = None
  end

(* the texts of a file no longer taken by an exec: it is being written *)
let mem_forget key =
  List.iter (fun t -> if t.key = key then t.known <- false) !texts

let seg_release sp = release sp; drop_text sp

(* dst a copy of src (fork's): a block of src's data's size, its bytes;
 * the text shared, but one of src's own (written), copied too *)
let seg_copy dst src =
  mem_place dst src.ssize;
  k_copy dst.sbase src.sbase src.ssize;
  drop_text dst;
  match src.text with
  | Some t when t.known -> t.users <- t.users + 1; dst.text <- Some t
  | Some t ->
      (try dst.text <- Some (copy_text t)
       with No_room -> release dst; raise No_room)
  | None -> ()

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Pages *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Chosen at the boot (/lib/memory says pages). A process's memory is
 * pages of 4 KB anywhere, by its tables (the machine's Sv32: a root of
 * 1024 entries, each a table of 1024, each a page), given when touched
 * (zeroed), shared by a fork until one side writes (copy-on-write).
 * The machine's satp has the user-only bit (tiny-machine's user_only):
 * the kernel's addresses stay physical, the tables it walks itself. *)
let pages = ref false
let page = 4096

(* The frames, the pages of the machine's memory from mem_low: a free
 * one's first word is the next free (0: none), as xv6's kalloc; those
 * never given yet are above [untouched], so the boot makes no list of
 * 57,000. A frame's users, a byte each from 0xb51000 (TinyKernel.mli's
 * layout): a table, or the processes that map it *)
let free_frames = ref 0
let untouched = ref mem_low
let nfree = ref ((mem_high - mem_low) / page)
let refs_at = 0xb51000
let refs f = peekb (refs_at + ((f - mem_low) / page))
let set_refs f n = pokeb (refs_at + ((f - mem_low) / page)) n

(* a frame, zeroed, one user; No_room *)
let frame () =
  let f =
    if !free_frames <> 0 then (let f = !free_frames in free_frames := peek f; f)
    else if !untouched < mem_high then
      (let f = !untouched in untouched := f + page; f)
    else raise No_room in
  decr nfree;
  k_zero f page;
  set_refs f 1;
  f

(* a user of frame f gone: f free with the last *)
let unref f =
  let n = refs f - 1 in
  set_refs f n;
  if n = 0 then (poke f !free_frames; free_frames := f; incr nfree)

(* an entry: a frame's number above ten bits of flags, the machine's
 * V R W X U, and one of the software's, copy-on-write (Sv32's RSW) *)
let v = 1 and r = 2 and w = 4 and x = 8 and u = 16 and cow = 256
let frame_of e = (e lsr 10) lsl 12
let entry f flags = ((f lsr 12) lsl 10) lor flags

(* the kernel's address of va's entry in sp's tables, its table made
 * when [make] (No_room); 0 without one *)
let entry_at sp va make =
  let a1 = sp.root + (4 * (va lsr 22)) in
  let e1 = peek a1 in
  let index = 4 * ((va lsr 12) land 0x3ff) in
  if e1 land v <> 0 then frame_of e1 + index
  else if make then (let t = frame () in poke a1 (entry t v); t + index)
  else 0

(* va's page there, a new one given when it was not (zeroed: memory
 * given when touched): its entry's address. The text's read only, the
 * rest writable. No_room *)
let present sp va =
  let a = entry_at sp va true in
  if peek a land v = 0 then
    poke a (entry (frame ()) (if va < sp.tsz then v lor r lor x lor u
                              else v lor r lor w lor x lor u));
  a

(* va's page the process's alone, to be written: a copy of a frame
 * another maps (a fork's, before either wrote; a text's, for a
 * breakpoint), writable again when it was before the fork *)
let unshare sp va =
  let a = present sp va in
  let e = peek a in
  if refs (frame_of e) > 1 then begin
    let g = frame () in
    k_copy g (frame_of e) page;
    unref (frame_of e);
    poke a (entry g (e land 1023))
  end;
  let e = peek a in
  if e land cow <> 0 then poke a ((e land lnot cow) lor w);
  a

(* the kernel's address of va, its page given if it was not *)
let physical sp va = frame_of (peek (present sp va)) + (va land (page - 1))

(* every page and table of sp let go *)
let pg_release sp =
  if sp.root <> 0 then begin
    for i = 0 to 1023 do
      let e1 = peek (sp.root + (4 * i)) in
      if e1 land v <> 0 then begin
        let t = frame_of e1 in
        for j = 0 to 1023 do
          let e = peek (t + (4 * j)) in
          if e land v <> 0 then unref (frame_of e)
        done;
        unref t
      end
    done;
    unref sp.root;
    sp.root <- 0
  end

(* A program of isize bytes (its image), size its memory, tsize its
 * text: a root, nothing else yet (the loader's writes give the image's
 * pages, the arguments' the top's). There must be room for all of
 * them first, so that the loader does not fail half way: No_room, sp
 * as it was *)
let pg_load sp tsize isize size =
  let tables = (size + (page * 1024) - 1) / (page * 1024) in
  if (isize / page) + 4 + tables > !nfree then raise No_room;
  pg_release sp;
  sp.root <- frame ();
  sp.vsize <- size;
  sp.tsz <- tsize

(* dst a copy of src (fork's): its tables, every page shared, a
 * writable one made read only in both, copy-on-write; the first to
 * write it gets a copy ([pg_fault]). No_room, before anything *)
let pg_copy dst src =
  let tables = ref 1 in
  for i = 0 to 1023 do
    if peek (src.root + (4 * i)) land v <> 0 then incr tables
  done;
  if !tables > !nfree then raise No_room;
  pg_release dst;
  dst.root <- frame ();
  dst.vsize <- src.vsize;
  dst.tsz <- src.tsz;
  for i = 0 to 1023 do
    let e1 = peek (src.root + (4 * i)) in
    if e1 land v <> 0 then begin
      let t = frame_of e1 and t' = frame () in
      poke (dst.root + (4 * i)) (entry t' v);
      for j = 0 to 1023 do
        let e = peek (t + (4 * j)) in
        if e land v <> 0 then begin
          let e = if e land w <> 0 then (e land lnot w) lor cow else e in
          poke (t + (4 * j)) e;
          poke (t' + (4 * j)) e;
          set_refs (frame_of e) (refs (frame_of e) + 1)
        end
      done
    end
  done

(* A fault of the process at va: a page it may have, given now (not
 * touched yet), or a copy-on-write page, its own now; true when the
 * process goes on, false when it dies (no such page, a store in its
 * text, no room) *)
let pg_fault sp va =
  if va < 0 || va >= sp.vsize then false
  else
    try
      let a = entry_at sp va false in
      if a = 0 || peek a land v = 0 then (ignore (present sp va); true)
      else if peek a land cow <> 0 then (ignore (unshare sp va); true)
      else false
    with No_room -> false

(* satp for sp: on, user mode only, its root (an ML int of 31 bits:
 * the top two bits the sign's) *)
let satp sp = if sp.root = 0 then 0 else -0x40000000 lor (sp.root lsr 12)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The way chosen *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let mem_load sp key stamp tsize isize size =
  if !pages then (pg_load sp tsize isize size; true)
  else seg_load sp key stamp tsize size
let mem_release sp = if !pages then pg_release sp else seg_release sp
let mem_copy dst src = if !pages then pg_copy dst src else seg_copy dst src
let mem_fault sp va = !pages && pg_fault sp va

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A process's addresses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A process's address va: below its text's size the text's (none with
 * partitions), above the data's, from its start. *)
let at sp va =
  match sp.text with
  | Some t when va < t.tblock.ssize -> t.tblock.sbase + va
  | Some t -> sp.sbase + va - t.tblock.ssize
  | None -> sp.sbase + va

(* The kernel's address of a process's n bytes at va; -1 if they leave
 * its memory, or (segments) are some in the text, some in the data. A
 * partition is one block: n bytes there are n bytes in the machine, one
 * after the other. *)
let pg_address sp va n =
  if va < 0 || n < 0 || va + n > sp.vsize then -1
  else if n > 0 && va / page <> (va + n - 1) / page then -1
  else try physical sp va with No_room -> -1

let mem_address sp va n =
  let ts = text_size sp in
  if !pages then pg_address sp va n
  else if va < 0 || n < 0 || va + n > ts + sp.ssize then -1
  else if n > 0 && va < ts && va + n > ts then -1
  else at sp va

(* The n bytes at va as the blocks of the machine that hold them, in
 * order, each its kernel's address and its length; None if they leave
 * the process's memory. A partition's n bytes are one block, so one
 * piece; with segments, two when they cross from the text to the
 * data. *)
let pg_pieces sp va n =
  let rec go va n =
    let k = min n (page - (va land (page - 1))) in
    if n <= k then [ physical sp va, n ]
    else (physical sp va, k) :: go (va + k) (n - k) in
  if va < 0 || n < 0 || va + n > sp.vsize then None
  else try Some (go va n) with No_room -> None

let mem_pieces sp va n =
  let ts = text_size sp in
  if !pages then pg_pieces sp va n
  else if va < 0 || n < 0 || va + n > ts + sp.ssize then None
  else if va < ts && va + n > ts then
    Some [ (at sp va, ts - va); (sp.sbase, va + n - ts) ]
  else Some [ at sp va, n ]

(* whether the kernel may write the n bytes at va for the process (a
 * read's buffer, a call's result): not in a text, which is read only.
 * With pages, each page made the process's own then (copy-on-write) *)
let pg_writable sp va n =
  let rec go p =
    if p * page >= va + n then true
    else if peek (present sp (p * page)) land (w lor cow) = 0 then false
    else (ignore (unshare sp (p * page)); go (p + 1)) in
  n = 0
  || (va >= 0 && va + n <= sp.vsize
      && (try go (va / page) with No_room -> false))

let mem_writable sp va n =
  if !pages then pg_writable sp va n else n = 0 || va >= text_size sp

(* a word, a byte, a string, n bytes of the kernel's at a, written at va;
 * a word read. The kernel has checked va ([mem_address]). A word or a
 * byte written in the text makes it the process's own (a breakpoint);
 * a string and n bytes are the loader's, which writes a new text *)
let mem_fetch sp va = if !pages then peek (physical sp va) else peek (at sp va)
(* (the kernel's address of va to be written: its page the process's
 * own, with pages; its text, with segments) *)
let own sp va =
  if !pages then frame_of (peek (unshare sp va)) + (va land (page - 1))
  else (if va < text_size sp then own_text sp; at sp va)
let mem_store sp va word = poke (own sp va) word
let mem_store_byte sp va b = pokeb (own sp va) b
let pieces sp va n =
  match mem_pieces sp va n with Some l -> l | None -> []
let mem_write sp va s =
  ignore (List.fold_left (fun off (a, k) -> row_bytes s off a k; off + k) 0
            (pieces sp va (String.length s)))
let mem_blit sp va a n =
  ignore (List.fold_left (fun off (d, k) -> row_copy d (a + off) k; off + k) 0
            (pieces sp va n))

(* What the machine gets so that a process runs in sp: its window, the
 * data's start and size, the text's (0 and 0 without one: the window
 * alone, as partitions have it), and satp (0 but with pages); on core 0
 * (entry.tm's k_window), and in another core's mailbox, at m, m + 4,
 * m + 20, m + 24, m + 28 *)
let text_base sp = match sp.text with Some t -> t.tblock.sbase | None -> 0
let mem_window sp =
  k_window sp.sbase sp.ssize (text_base sp) (text_size sp) (satp sp)
let mem_post sp m =
  poke m sp.sbase; poke (m + 4) sp.ssize;
  poke (m + 20) (text_base sp); poke (m + 24) (text_size sp);
  poke (m + 28) (satp sp)
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelMemory.mli
12547
(* Tiny memory: how tiny-kernel gives a process its memory, a
 * partition: one block of the machine's memory, its size the program's
 * (its a.out says it: tiny-linker -a), found first-fit when the program
 * starts, never grown. TinyKernel.ml's part that is about memory, as
 * TinyKernelFS.ml is its part about the disk (plan_tiny_memory.md).
 *
 * The machine does the rest with two numbers, its window: in user mode
 * every address is added to the block's start (base) and must stay
 * below its size (bound), or the process faults. So a program is
 * linked at 0 and runs anywhere, and reaches nothing but its block:
 *
 *     0x2000000                                              0xfff0000
 *     | sh, 1 MB | rc, 1 MB | ml, 32 MB    |  free  | ld, 48 MB | free |
 *                ^ base                                (first fit: the
 *     rc's address 0x100 is 0x2100000 + 0x100          first gap big
 *     in the machine; 0x100000 and above fault          enough, from the
 *                                                       bottom)
 *
 * fork asks a block of the parent's size and copies the parent's into
 * it, whole ([mem_copy]); exec asks one of the new program's size (the
 * same block when the size is the same) and writes the program's
 * image at its 0 and the arguments at its top; spawn does exec's in a
 * new process. A block is let go when the kernel lets the process go
 * ([mem_release]), when it ends (its parent's wait reads only a record
 * of its status: TinyKernelProcs.ended).
 *
 * Where it stands: TinyKernel.ml calls it for every process's memory
 * (its [user] for a word or a byte of a system call's, [mem_address];
 * its [user_iter] for a buffer, [mem_pieces]; [mem_writable] before it
 * writes one); entry.tm
 * sets core 0's window ([mem_window]), and a core given a process gets
 * its window in its mailbox ([mem_post]: plan_tiny_multicore.md). The
 * other kernels on the same machine: t6 (steps/), fixed partitions of
 * 1 MB; v6, removed, pages (tiny-machine's Sv32, which no kernel uses
 * now).
 *
 * What is ours: the block's size is a guess made when the program is
 * linked (ld's 32 MB was too small for bin/ml's link: 48 now); the
 * block is not zeroed (exec writes the image only: zeroing ml's 32 MB
 * cost 35 million instructions an exec); there is no swapping, so a
 * fork or an exec with no room waits (TinyKernelCalls's with_room).
 *
 * Segments (the boot's choice: /lib/memory says segments; the
 * Makefile's MEMORY=segments) split a process in two, its text and
 * its data, at the address tiny-linker -n put the data at (a page past
 * the text). The machine's second window maps the text (tbase,
 * tbound) and faults a store there; the data is a block as above:
 *
 *     a process's addresses         the machine's memory
 *     0       text  (read only) --> ml's text, one block for all the
 *     tsize                         ml's that run (texts, users)
 *             data, heap, stack --> this ml's block, memory - tsize
 *     memory
 *
 * exec shares a text that runs already from the same file, unchanged
 * (its key and stamp: TinyKernel.ml names them), and writes only the
 * data then; fork shares the text and copies the data. A file written
 * is forgotten ([mem_forget]): its next exec loads it again. A word
 * the kernel writes in a text (a tracer's breakpoint) makes the text
 * the process's own, a copy. A process without a text (partitions)
 * runs with the window alone: entry.tm sets the machine's split only
 * when tbound is not 0, the split's arithmetic costing 2% of the host's
 * instructions (tiny-kernel's toolchain session; 7% when every process
 * paid it).
 *
 * Pages (/lib/memory says pages; MEMORY=pages) are plan_tiny_memory.md's
 * stage 4, off by default: a process's memory is pages of 4 KB, each
 * in any frame of the machine's memory, by its tables (Sv32: a root, a
 * table for each 4 MB, an entry for each page):
 *
 *     a process's addresses     its tables          the frames
 *     0      text (R X)  -----> root -> table ---> anywhere above 32 MB,
 *            data (R W X)                          a free list through
 *            ... untouched: no entry, no frame     the free ones (xv6's
 *            stack, arguments                      kalloc), a byte of
 *     memory                                       users for each
 *
 * exec gives a root and the pages the image and the arguments write;
 * any other page is given at its first touch, zeroed ([mem_fault]: the
 * fault answered, the instruction run again). fork shares every page,
 * the writable ones made read only and copy-on-write in both: the first
 * to write gets a copy, or the page back writable when it is the last
 * user. The kernel writes a process's page only after it made the page
 * the process's own ([mem_writable], a breakpoint's [mem_store]); it
 * reaches a buffer a page at a time ([mem_pieces], TinyKernelCalls's
 * bounce for read and write). The machine translates user mode's
 * addresses only (satp's user-only bit), the kernel's staying
 * physical, and keeps them in a cache emptied at each run (k_window
 * writes satp): one core changes a process's tables, while it is not
 * running, so no other core holds them (no shootdown). Not done: a
 * text shared between execs (segments' texts; pages would need a cache
 * of a file's pages), a guard page under the stack (where a program's
 * stack ends is its runtime's: mlsys.c's), swapping.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Partitions are how IBM's OS/360 (1966) shared a machine between
 * jobs. Its MFT cut memory into a fixed number of partitions, set by
 * the operator; its MVT cut a region of the size each job asked for,
 * as this kernel does with an a.out's size, and met external
 * fragmentation: the free memory in holes too small for the next job.
 * The 360 had no relocation at run time (the loader relocated a
 * program once, as it loaded it) and protected memory by keys, one
 * for each 2 KB. A base and a bound register, tiny-machine's window,
 * are the CDC 6600's RA and FL (1964): every address added to RA and
 * checked against FL. Knuth's first volume (1968) weighs first fit
 * against best fit, with the fifty-percent rule: in a steady state
 * there are about half as many holes as blocks in use. Denning's
 * survey "Virtual Memory" (1970) presents partitions and relocation
 * as the step before pages, the order in which this kernel takes them.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Pages are in fact older: Manchester's Atlas (1962) had a "one-level
 * store", pages of 512 words that the supervisor moved between core
 * and drum, unseen by the program. IBM's 360 Model 67 (1967)
 * translated addresses for TSS/360 and CP-67, and the 370 brought
 * virtual storage to all its systems (1972). Unix got demand paging
 * on the VAX, in Berkeley's 3BSD (1979, Babaoglu and Joy). Pages
 * answer the three troubles of partitions that this kernel shows: no
 * fragmentation (any free frame will do), memory given when touched
 * rather than reserved, and a fork that copies a page only when one
 * side writes it (copy-on-write).
 *
 * evolution:
 * Segments came in between: memory cut along the program's parts
 * rather than by process. The Burroughs B5000 (1961) gave each array
 * and procedure a descriptor. The PDP-11's memory management (the
 * 11/40's and 11/45's) mapped a program's 64 KB in eight segments
 * that DEC called pages; the 11/45 had a second set for instructions,
 * and Unix's a.out said which a program wanted: 0407 one block, 0410
 * its text read-only and shared by all its runs, 0411 instructions
 * and data in two spaces. Intel's 8086 (1978) had four segment
 * registers (code, data, stack, extra) and no protection: an address
 * was the segment times 16 plus the offset. The 80286 (1982) made a
 * segment a descriptor (base, limit, rights) in a table; the 80386
 * (1985) put pages under the segments, and Unix, then Windows NT, set
 * every segment to base 0 and limit 4 GB (the flat model), pages
 * alone doing the work; AMD64 (2003) kept only FS's and GS's bases,
 * for each thread's data. Multics (1969) had both: a file was a
 * segment, mapped, and its segments were paged.
 *
 * terminology:
 * A partition (OS/360's) is set in advance; MVT called its variable
 * ones regions. A segment is a part of an address space with its own
 * base and limit (code, data, stack); ELF's segments are only the
 * parts of a file to load, and its .text a section. A page is a piece
 * of fixed size of the address space (4 KB in Sv32), the frame the
 * memory under it. Virtual memory is the whole idea (the addresses a
 * program uses are not the memory's), paging one way to do it,
 * swapping another (whole processes to the disk, as Unix V7 did). And
 * core was memory before it was a processor: magnetic cores, hence a
 * core dump.
 *
 * References:
 *  - P. Denning, "Virtual Memory" (Computing Surveys 1970): partitions,
 *    relocation, then pages
 *  - D. Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming, vol. 1 (1968), 2.5:
 *    first fit, best fit, the fifty-percent rule
 *  - T. Kilburn et al., "One-Level Storage System" (IRE Transactions
 *    on Electronic Computers, 1962): Atlas's pages
 *)

(* the processes' memory, from mem_low to mem_high; a partition's size
 * is a multiple of [part] (a megabyte) *)
val part : int
val mem_low : int
val mem_high : int

(* a process's memory: none at first ([mem_empty]), then a block, and
 * with segments a text *)
type space

(* no block of the size asked for is free now *)
exception No_room

val mem_empty : unit -> space
val mem_release : space -> unit

(* segments, or pages, not partitions: set once, at the boot *)
val segments : bool ref
val pages : bool ref

(* [mem_load sp key stamp tsize isize size]: sp given the memory of a
 * program of size bytes (its a.out's), its image isize, its old memory
 * let go; tsize of them the text (0: none; ignored with partitions),
 * shared with segments when one from the same key and stamp runs. True
 * when the image's text is to be written, else only its data (from
 * tsize). No_room, sp as it was *)
val mem_load : space -> string -> string -> int -> int -> int -> bool

(* [mem_forget key]: the texts of that file not shared by a next exec
 * (the file is being written) *)
val mem_forget : string -> unit

(* [mem_copy dst src]: dst a block of src's data's size, src's bytes,
 * and src's text, shared (fork); with pages, every page shared,
 * copy-on-write *)
val mem_copy : space -> space -> unit

(* [mem_fault sp va]: a fault of the process at va that pages answer:
 * a page not touched yet, given (zeroed), or a page a fork shares,
 * copied; true when the process goes on, false when it is to die (and
 * always without pages) *)
val mem_fault : space -> int -> bool

(* [mem_address sp va n]: the kernel's address of the n bytes at the
 * process's va, -1 if they are not all the process's, or (with pages)
 * not in one piece; a word or a byte is (an aligned word is in one
 * page) *)
val mem_address : space -> int -> int -> int

(* [mem_pieces sp va n]: the n bytes at va as the pieces of the
 * machine's memory that hold them, in order, (the kernel's address, the
 * length) each; None if they are not all the process's. One piece for
 * a partition; two with segments when they cross from the text to the
 * data; with pages, a piece a page (the frames are anywhere):
 * for a buffer, the kernel goes by them (TinyKernelProcs's user_iter) *)
val mem_pieces : space -> int -> int -> (int * int) list option

(* [mem_writable sp va n]: whether the kernel may write those bytes for
 * the process: not in its text *)
val mem_writable : space -> int -> int -> bool

(* a word read at va; a word, a byte, a string written at va; [mem_blit
 * sp va a n] the kernel's n bytes at a written at va. va is checked by
 * the caller ([mem_address]). A word or a byte written in the text
 * makes it sp's own (a copy: No_room); a string and n bytes are the
 * loader's, written where it says, in the text too *)
val mem_fetch : space -> int -> int
val mem_store : space -> int -> int -> unit
val mem_store_byte : space -> int -> int -> unit
val mem_write : space -> int -> string -> unit
val mem_blit : space -> int -> int -> int -> unit

(* the machine set to run a process in sp: core 0's windows
 * ([mem_window]: the data's, the text's), or another core's, the
 * mailbox's words at m, m + 4 (the data), m + 20, m + 24 (the text)
 * ([mem_post sp m]) *)
val mem_window : space -> unit
val mem_post : space -> int -> unit

(* See TinyKernelNetwork.mli *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Bytes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* each byte's string, made once; a number of 16 bits as the network
 * has it, the high byte first, and read back *)
let net_byte = Array.make 256 ""
let () = for c = 0 to 255 do net_byte.(c) <- String.make 1 (Char.chr c) done
let net16 v = net_byte.((v lsr 8) land 255) ^ net_byte.(v land 255)
let net_get16 s i = (256 * Char.code s.[i]) + Char.code s.[i + 1]

(* The Internet's checksum (RFC 1071): the bytes as numbers of 16 bits
 * added up, what goes over 16 bits added back in, the result's bits
 * turned. Written into the bytes it covers (at a place left 0 while
 * adding), the sum of the whole is then 0: that is the check. A
 * packet's 2,048 bytes add up to less than 2^27: an int of 31 bits
 * holds it. *)
let net_sum s =
  let n = String.length s in
  let acc = ref 0 in
  for i = 0 to (n / 2) - 1 do acc := !acc + net_get16 s (2 * i) done;
  if n land 1 = 1 then acc := !acc + (256 * Char.code s.[n - 1]);
  while !acc > 0xffff do acc := (!acc land 0xffff) + (!acc lsr 16) done;
  0xffff - !acc

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Addresses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* an address is its four bytes, a string: nothing is computed on one,
 * and 32 bits do not fit tiny-ml's int. "10.0.0.2" to it and back; ""
 * when the text is not an address *)
let net_address text =
  let n = String.length text in
  let rec go i v digits acc =
    if i = n || text.[i] = '.' then
      (if digits = 0 || v > 255 then ""
       else if i = n then acc ^ net_byte.(v)
       else go (i + 1) 0 0 (acc ^ net_byte.(v)))
    else if text.[i] >= '0' && text.[i] <= '9' then
      go (i + 1) ((10 * v) + Char.code text.[i] - 48) (digits + 1) acc
    else "" in
  let a = go 0 0 0 "" in
  if String.length a = 4 then a else ""

(* the two ends of tiny-machine's wire: the machine, and its host *)
let net_machine = net_address "10.0.0.2"
let net_peer = net_address "10.0.0.1"

(*****************************************************************************)
(* IP: the envelope *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* what a packet carries: IP's numbers *)
let ip_icmp = 1

(* a packet: IP's header of 20 bytes (version 4 and its length in
 * words, 0x45; the whole length; no fragment; 64 hops to live; what
 * it carries; the header's checksum; from; to), then what it carries *)
let ip_packet proto src dst payload =
  let head sum =
    net_byte.(0x45) ^ net_byte.(0) ^ net16 (20 + String.length payload)
    ^ net16 0 ^ net16 0 ^ net_byte.(64) ^ net_byte.(proto) ^ net16 sum
    ^ src ^ dst in
  head (net_sum (head 0)) ^ payload

(* a packet that came, if it is one for [me]: what it carries (IP's
 * number), who sent it, the bytes. Anything else is dropped without a
 * word, as on the Internet: a header that is not this plain one, a
 * length that is not the packet's, a checksum that is wrong, another's
 * address (for "", any address will do: a gateway's) *)
let ip_read me p =
  let n = String.length p in
  if n < 20 || Char.code p.[0] <> 0x45 then None
  else begin
    let total = net_get16 p 2 in
    if total < 20 || total > n || net_sum (String.sub p 0 20) <> 0
       || (me <> "" && String.sub p 16 4 <> me) then None
    else Some (Char.code p.[9], String.sub p 12 4, String.sub p 20 (total - 20))
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* ICMP: the echo *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* "are you there?" and "yes": the question's kind is 8, the answer's
 * 0, and the answer returns the question's two numbers (whose
 * question, which one of them) and its bytes *)
let icmp_ask = 8
let icmp_answer = 0

let icmp_message kind id seq data =
  (* old: let m sum = kind ^ 0 ^ net16 sum ^ net16 id ^ net16 seq ^ data in
   * m (net_sum (m 0)): the data copied at each ^ (it joins from the
   * right), ten times in all *)
  let head = net_byte.(kind) ^ net_byte.(0) in
  let rest = (net16 id ^ net16 seq) ^ data in
  head ^ net16 (net_sum (head ^ rest)) ^ rest

(* its kind, its two numbers, its bytes; None when cut or damaged *)
let icmp_read b =
  if String.length b < 8 || net_sum b <> 0 then None
  else
    Some (Char.code b.[0], net_get16 b 4, net_get16 b 6,
          String.sub b 8 (String.length b - 8))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* IL: its packets *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let ip_il = 40

(* IL's numbers have 32 bits and tiny-ml's int 31: the two ends here
 * start theirs small and stay under 2^30 (a number written as two
 * halves of 16 bits), and a packet with a larger one is not read (-1) *)
let net32 v = net16 ((v lsr 16) land 0xffff) ^ net16 (v land 0xffff)
let net_get32 s i =
  if net_get16 s i >= 0x4000 then -1
  else (65536 * net_get16 s i) + net_get16 s (i + 2)

(* a packet's seven kinds, Plan 9's numbers *)
let il_sync = 0
let il_data = 1
let il_dataquery = 2
let il_ack = 3
let il_query = 4
let il_state = 5
let il_close = 6

(* IL's header, 18 bytes after IP's: a checksum of all of it and of the
 * message, the length of both, the kind, a byte not used here, the
 * sender's port and the other's, the packet's number (its id) and the
 * last number its sender received in order (its ack); then the
 * message, in a packet of data *)
let il_message kind sport dport id ack data =
  (* (the header first, then the message joined once: ^ joins from the
   * right, and a ^ b ^ data copies data at each ^. The sum's own two
   * bytes, 0 while adding and at an even place, add nothing: the sum
   * is the rest's) *)
  let head =
    net16 (18 + String.length data) ^ net_byte.(kind) ^ net_byte.(0)
    ^ net16 sport ^ net16 dport ^ net32 id ^ net32 ack in
  let rest = head ^ data in
  net16 (net_sum rest) ^ rest

(* its kind, the two ports, its id, its ack, the message; None when
 * cut, damaged or not ours to read *)
let il_read b =
  let n = String.length b in
  if n < 18 || net_get16 b 2 <> n || net_sum b <> 0
     || Char.code b.[4] > il_close || net_get32 b 10 < 0 || net_get32 b 14 < 0
  then None
  else
    Some (Char.code b.[4], net_get16 b 6, net_get16 b 8, net_get32 b 10,
          net_get32 b 14, String.sub b 18 (n - 18))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* IL: a connection *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* where a connection is: it asked to talk (its sync sent), it was
 * asked (its own sync sent back), both know the other is there, it
 * said or was told the end, it is over *)
type il_at = Il_syncer | Il_syncee | Il_established | Il_closing | Il_closed

(* One end of a connection, in three records (tiny-ml's compiler for
 * tiny-machine makes one of ten fields at most). What it sends: its
 * next message's number; the messages sent that the other end has not
 * said it has, the oldest first; whether the program is done (the end
 * is said once everything sent has arrived); its next number when it
 * last asked where the other end is; when to act if nothing comes, how
 * many times it has since the last news (each wait is twice the one
 * before), and how many since anything at all was heard (patience).
 * What it receives: where the other end's numbers started, the last
 * received in order, and the last it said the program took; the
 * messages that came before one that is missing, those in order that
 * the program has not read. And itself: who and which ports, where it
 * is, the number its messages started from. *)
type il_sending = {
  mutable il_next : int; mutable il_unacked : (int * string) list;
  mutable il_leaving : bool; mutable il_asked : int;
  mutable il_timeout : int; mutable il_tries : int; mutable il_silent : int;
}

type il_receiving = {
  mutable il_rstart : int; mutable il_recvd : int; mutable il_told : int;
  mutable il_early : (int * string) list;
  mutable il_heard : string list;
}

type il = {
  il_me : string; il_peer : string; il_lport : int; il_rport : int;
  mutable il_at : il_at; il_start : int; il_s : il_sending;
  il_r : il_receiving;
}

(* at most 20 messages sent and not acknowledged, or received and not
 * read (Plan 9's window); a message's bytes; how long nothing may come
 * before asking, in its caller's ticks (tiny-kernel's: 2.5 ms), twice
 * as long each time; how many times before giving up *)
let il_window = 20
let il_max = 1024
let il_wait = 40
let il_patience = 5

let il_new me peer lport rport start at now =
  { il_me = me; il_peer = peer; il_lport = lport; il_rport = rport;
    il_at = at; il_start = start;
    il_s = { il_next = start + 1; il_unacked = []; il_leaving = false;
             il_asked = 0; il_timeout = now + il_wait; il_tries = 0;
             il_silent = 0 };
    il_r = { il_rstart = 0; il_recvd = 0; il_told = 0; il_early = [];
             il_heard = [] } }

(* The last message the program took. That, and not the last received,
 * is what an acknowledgement says: a sender holds at most [il_window]
 * messages not acknowledged, so it is never more than that ahead of a
 * program that reads slowly, and nothing received has to be dropped
 * for want of room. (old: the last received, il.c's; a picture's rows
 * sent 20 at once were received faster than read, those over 20
 * dropped, and asked for again one at a time: 11 s for 240 rows, 5
 * now.) *)
let il_taken c = c.il_r.il_recvd - List.length c.il_r.il_heard

(* a packet of a connection's: every one says it. But a state and a
 * close say all that was received, read or not: a state answers
 * "where are you?", for the other end to know what is missing and not
 * send again what only waits to be read; after a close nothing more
 * will be *)
let il_out c kind id data =
  let ack =
    if kind = il_close || kind = il_state then c.il_r.il_recvd
    else (c.il_r.il_told <- il_taken c; c.il_r.il_told) in
  ip_packet ip_il c.il_me c.il_peer
    (il_message kind c.il_lport c.il_rport id ack data)

let il_arm c now = c.il_s.il_timeout <- now + (il_wait lsl c.il_s.il_tries)
let il_fresh c now = c.il_s.il_tries <- 0; il_arm c now

(* whether a message may be written now; one written: its packet. It
 * is kept until the other end says it has it *)
let il_room c =
  (match c.il_at with Il_established -> true | _ -> false)
  && (not c.il_s.il_leaving)
  && List.length c.il_s.il_unacked < il_window

let il_write c data now =
  let id = c.il_s.il_next in
  c.il_s.il_next <- id + 1;
  (match c.il_s.il_unacked with [] -> il_fresh c now | _ -> ());
  c.il_s.il_unacked <- c.il_s.il_unacked @ [ id, data ];
  il_out c il_data id data

(* the program is done: the end is said by [il_tick], once what was
 * written has arrived *)
let il_done c =
  match c.il_at with
  | Il_established -> c.il_s.il_leaving <- true
  | Il_syncer | Il_syncee -> c.il_at <- Il_closed
  | _ -> ()

(* the next message for the program, taken; whether a read would not
 * wait (a message, or the end) *)
let il_hear c =
  match c.il_r.il_heard with
  | [] -> None
  | m :: rest -> c.il_r.il_heard <- rest; Some m
let il_readable c =
  (match c.il_r.il_heard with [] -> false | _ -> true)
  || (match c.il_at with Il_closing | Il_closed -> true | _ -> false)

(* whether a read has nothing more to wait for *)
let il_over c = match c.il_at with Il_closing | Il_closed -> true | _ -> false

(* the other end has everything up to [ack]: forgotten here; whether
 * that was news *)
let il_ackto c ack now =
  let left = List.filter (fun (id, _) -> id > ack) c.il_s.il_unacked in
  if List.length left < List.length c.il_s.il_unacked then
    (c.il_s.il_unacked <- left; il_fresh c now; true)
  else false

(* a message that came: dropped if it came already, if it is too far
 * ahead or if the program reads too slowly (it will be sent again);
 * kept, and given to the program with those that were waiting for it
 * when it is the next *)
let rec il_pullup c =
  match List.filter (fun (id, _) -> id = c.il_r.il_recvd + 1) c.il_r.il_early with
  | (id, data) :: _ ->
      c.il_r.il_early <- List.filter (fun (i, _) -> i <> id) c.il_r.il_early;
      c.il_r.il_recvd <- id;
      c.il_r.il_heard <- c.il_r.il_heard @ [ data ];
      il_pullup c
  | [] -> ()

let il_take c id data =
  if id > c.il_r.il_recvd && id <= c.il_r.il_recvd + il_window
     && List.length c.il_r.il_heard < il_window
     && not (List.exists (fun (i, _) -> i = id) c.il_r.il_early) then begin
    c.il_r.il_early <- (id, data) :: c.il_r.il_early;
    il_pullup c
  end

(* "where are you?" answered: what was received. And what the program
 * took is to be said again at the next tick: the other end asks
 * because it heard nothing, and the packet that said it may be the one
 * that was lost *)
let il_where c =
  c.il_r.il_told <- -1;
  [ il_out c il_state c.il_s.il_next "" ]

(* A packet for a connection where both ends talk. A question (query,
 * or data sent again, which asks too) is answered by where this end
 * is (state). An answer says what the other end received: if a
 * message sent is missing there, the oldest such is sent again, as a
 * question, so a wire that lost several is caught up one answer at a
 * time (each brings the other end one further, or is lost itself and
 * the timer asks again). It frees nothing here: only what the other
 * end's program took does. *)
let il_talk c kind id ack data now =
  if kind = il_sync then
    (if id = c.il_r.il_rstart then
       [ ip_packet ip_il c.il_me c.il_peer
           (il_message il_ack c.il_lport c.il_rport c.il_s.il_next
              c.il_r.il_rstart "") ]
     else (c.il_at <- Il_closed; []))
  else if kind = il_data || kind = il_dataquery then begin
    ignore (il_ackto c ack now);
    il_take c id data;
    if kind = il_dataquery then il_where c else []
  end
  else if kind = il_ack then (ignore (il_ackto c ack now); [])
  else if kind = il_query then (ignore (il_ackto c ack now); il_where c)
  else if kind = il_state then begin
    (* (of those sent before the question: one sent since may be on
     * its way still. il.c's qt) *)
    match
      List.filter (fun (i, _) -> i > ack && i < c.il_s.il_asked)
        c.il_s.il_unacked
    with
    | (first, message) :: _ -> [ il_out c il_dataquery first message ]
    | [] -> []
  end
  else if ack >= c.il_start && ack <= c.il_s.il_next then begin
    (* the other end is done: said back, what was not yet read stays *)
    c.il_r.il_recvd <- id;
    c.il_at <- Il_closing;
    c.il_s.il_unacked <- [];
    il_fresh c now;
    [ il_out c il_close c.il_s.il_next "" ]
  end
  else []

(* a packet that came for this connection: the packets to send back.
 * The other end is there: patience starts again *)
let il_input c kind id ack data now =
  c.il_s.il_silent <- 0;
  match c.il_at with
  | Il_closed -> []
  | Il_syncer ->
      if kind = il_sync && ack = c.il_start then begin
        c.il_r.il_recvd <- id;
        c.il_r.il_rstart <- id;
        c.il_at <- Il_established;
        il_fresh c now;
        [ il_out c il_ack c.il_s.il_next "" ]
      end
      else if kind = il_close && ack = c.il_start then (c.il_at <- Il_closed; [])
      else []
  | Il_syncee ->
      if kind = il_sync then
        (if id = c.il_r.il_rstart then [ il_out c il_sync c.il_start "" ]
         else [])
      else if kind = il_close then
        (if ack = c.il_start then c.il_at <- Il_closed; [])
      else if (kind = il_ack || kind = il_data) && ack = c.il_start then
        (c.il_at <- Il_established;
         il_fresh c now;
         il_talk c kind id ack data now)
      else []
  | Il_established -> il_talk c kind id ack data now
  | Il_closing ->
      if kind = il_close then begin
        (* the end said by both: over when the other end has heard
         * this one's; said once more by who said it first, for the
         * other to be over too (il.c: by both, the last to nobody) *)
        c.il_r.il_recvd <- id;
        let back = il_out c il_close c.il_s.il_next "" in
        if ack = c.il_s.il_next then
          (c.il_at <- Il_closed; if c.il_s.il_leaving then [ back ] else [])
        else [ back ]
      end
      else []

(* said again when nothing came in time, the next wait twice this one
 * (32 times the first at most); when nothing at all was heard for
 * [il_patience] of them, the end said once, to whoever may still
 * hear, and the connection is over *)
let il_again c kind id now =
  if c.il_s.il_silent >= il_patience then
    (c.il_at <- Il_closed; [ il_out c il_close c.il_s.il_next "" ])
  else begin
    c.il_s.il_silent <- c.il_s.il_silent + 1;
    c.il_s.il_tries <- min 5 (c.il_s.il_tries + 1);
    il_arm c now;
    [ il_out c kind id "" ]
  end

(* time passed: the packets to send. Its sync or its close again; the
 * end said, when the program is done and all has arrived; a question,
 * when messages sent were not acknowledged in time (the other end's
 * answer says which to send again: nothing is sent again blindly);
 * else what the program took acknowledged, if no packet said it yet *)
let il_tick c now =
  let late = now >= c.il_s.il_timeout in
  match c.il_at with
  | Il_closed -> []
  | Il_syncer | Il_syncee -> if late then il_again c il_sync c.il_start now else []
  | Il_closing -> if late then il_again c il_close c.il_s.il_next now else []
  | Il_established ->
      if c.il_s.il_unacked = [] && c.il_s.il_leaving then
        (c.il_at <- Il_closing;
         il_fresh c now;
         [ il_out c il_close c.il_s.il_next "" ])
      else if c.il_s.il_unacked <> [] && late then
        (c.il_s.il_asked <- c.il_s.il_next;
         il_again c il_query c.il_s.il_next now)
      else if c.il_r.il_told <> il_taken c then [ il_out c il_ack c.il_s.il_next "" ]
      else []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A machine's connections *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* What one address has: its connections, the ports it listens on, the
 * connections made by others that no program took yet, and the number
 * the next connection's messages start from and its port on this side.
 * And, for a wire's end that is the way to other machines (a
 * gateway): the addresses and ports, not its own, that it will answer
 * the next sync for, as if it were them *)
type net_stack = {
  ns_me : string; mutable ns_conns : il list; mutable ns_ports : int list;
  mutable ns_fresh : il list; mutable ns_start : int;
  mutable ns_port : int; mutable ns_gate : bool;
  mutable ns_others : (string * int) list;
}

let net_stack me start =
  { ns_me = me; ns_conns = []; ns_ports = []; ns_fresh = []; ns_start = start;
    ns_port = 5000; ns_gate = false; ns_others = [] }

let net_conn s me peer lport rport at now =
  let c = il_new me peer lport rport s.ns_start at now in
  s.ns_start <- s.ns_start + 1000;
  s.ns_conns <- c :: s.ns_conns;
  c

(* a connection asked for: it, and its first packet *)
let net_dial s peer port now =
  let c = net_conn s s.ns_me peer s.ns_port port Il_syncer now in
  s.ns_port <- 5000 + ((s.ns_port - 4999) land 0x3fff);
  c, il_out c il_sync c.il_start ""

(* time passed for every connection; those that are over forgotten *)
let net_tick s now =
  let out = List.concat (List.map (fun c -> il_tick c now) s.ns_conns) in
  s.ns_conns <-
    List.filter (fun c -> match c.il_at with Il_closed -> false | _ -> true)
      s.ns_conns;
  out

(* A packet of IL's: its connection's, by who sent it, who it is for
 * and the two ports. For none: a sync to a port listened on (or, a
 * gateway's, to an address and a port it said it would answer for,
 * once) makes a connection, its own sync sent back; anything else but
 * a close is answered by a close, which is how who dials a port nobody
 * listens on learns it *)
let net_il s now from to_ body =
  match il_read body with
  | None -> []
  | Some (kind, sport, dport, id, ack, data) -> (
      match
        List.filter
          (fun c -> c.il_peer = from && c.il_me = to_ && c.il_lport = dport
                    && c.il_rport = sport)
          s.ns_conns
      with
      | c :: _ -> il_input c kind id ack data now
      | [] ->
          let mine = to_ = s.ns_me && List.mem dport s.ns_ports
          and other = List.mem (to_, dport) s.ns_others in
          if kind = il_sync && ack = 0 && (mine || other) then begin
            if other then
              s.ns_others <- List.filter (fun o -> o <> (to_, dport)) s.ns_others;
            let c = net_conn s to_ from dport sport Il_syncee now in
            c.il_r.il_rstart <- id;
            c.il_r.il_recvd <- id;
            s.ns_fresh <- s.ns_fresh @ [ c ];
            [ il_out c il_sync c.il_start "" ]
          end
          else if kind <> il_close then
            [ ip_packet ip_il to_ from (il_message il_close dport sport 0 id "") ]
          else [])

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A packet that came *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The packets to send back, and an answer to an echo if it is one (who
 * answers, the question's two numbers, its bytes), for who asked. A
 * question is answered here, by whoever has the address: the kernel,
 * and the host's end of the wire, which is this same function. What
 * IL's packets change is in the connections: their messages, their
 * state, [ns_fresh]. *)
let net_input s now packet =
  match ip_read (if s.ns_gate then "" else s.ns_me) packet with
  | None -> [], None
  | Some (proto, from, body) ->
      let to_ = String.sub packet 16 4 in
      if proto = ip_il then net_il s now from to_ body, None
      else if proto <> ip_icmp || to_ <> s.ns_me then [], None
      else (
        match icmp_read body with
        | None -> [], None
        | Some (kind, id, seq, data) ->
            if kind = icmp_ask then
              [ ip_packet ip_icmp s.ns_me from
                  (icmp_message icmp_answer id seq data) ], None
            else if kind = icmp_answer then [], Some (from, id, seq, data)
            else [], None)
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelNetwork.mli
13678
(* Tiny network: what a kernel needs to talk over tiny-machine's wire,
 * the essential of a network stack (ix's twins are mini-9pi's
 * kernels/9pi/network/ip/, the twin of Plan 9's, and the programs'
 * lib_networking/). Not a program: TinyKernel.ml's part that speaks to
 * the network (plan_tiny_network.md), and the other end of the wire in
 * TinyMachine.ml:
 *
 *     ./tiny-machine -net tiny/tests/www -net-trace tiny-kernel
 *         then: ping, get il.txt
 *
 * The idea kept: {b the stack is functions of strings}. A packet is a
 * string; a packet that came gives the packets to send back and what a
 * program is to hear. Nothing here reads a device, keeps a clock or
 * knows who calls. So the same file is three things: the kernel's
 * stack (TinyKernel.ml takes the packets from the machine's device and
 * gives them here), the host's test of it (no machine), and the wire's
 * other end (TinyMachine.ml's -net: the host answering with this very
 * code, where mini-qemu needed a second stack, raspberry/Usernet).
 *
 * Two things are here. The first, a ping's way there and back:
 *
 *     tiny-kernel, 10.0.0.2                      the host, 10.0.0.1
 *
 *     ping: write "ping"
 *        | icmp_message: an echo's question
 *        | ip_packet: the envelope
 *     the device: send  ======= the wire =======>  net_input:
 *                                                    ip_read (for me?)
 *                                                    icmp_read (a question)
 *     net_input:        <====== the wire ========  the answer, in its
 *       ip_read, icmp_read: an answer                envelope
 *        | (who, the numbers, the bytes)
 *     ping: read "ping"
 *
 * A packet, byte by byte (a ping of four bytes: 32 in all):
 *
 *     IP's header, 20 bytes
 *     45 00 | 00 20 | 00 00 00 00 | 40 | 01 | sum | 10.0.0.2 | 10.0.0.1
 *     version  the    no fragment  hops what  the   from       to
 *     4, five  whole               left it is header's
 *     words    length                   ICMP  check
 *
 *     what it carries: ICMP, 8 and the bytes
 *     08 00 | sum | id | seq | p i n g
 *     echo?   its   whose  which
 *             own   ping   one
 *             check
 *
 * What is left out, each because the wire has two ends and one
 * program at each: Ethernet and its addresses, ARP (who has this
 * address?), routes, fragments (a packet cut to pass a narrow road),
 * options, the hops counted down. A packet that is not well made or
 * not for us is dropped without a word.
 *
 * An address is its four bytes in a string: nothing is computed on
 * one, and tiny-ml's int has 31 bits.
 *
 * The second: {b IL}, Plan 9's protocol, which makes the wire
 * reliable. A program writes messages and reads messages; each arrives
 * once, in the order written, or the connection ends. All of it:
 *
 * - a connection is opened by a sync each way, each end saying the
 *   number its messages start from;
 * - a message has a number (its id), one more than the one before;
 *   what comes twice is known by it and dropped, what comes early is
 *   kept until the one before arrives;
 * - every packet says the last number its sender's program took (its
 *   ack): what the other end has is forgotten here, and who writes is
 *   never more than 20 messages ahead of who reads;
 * - nothing is sent again blindly: who has heard no ack for a while
 *   asks (query), the other end says what it received (state), and
 *   the oldest message missing there is sent again, as a question too
 *   (data?); a program that only reads slowly has nothing sent again;
 * - close ends it, said when all that was written has arrived.
 *
 * A message lost (tiny-machine -net-lose, as -net-trace says it):
 *
 *     > sync   id 1000 ack 0              "may I talk to your port 70?"
 *     < sync   id 5000 ack 1000           "yes"
 *     > ack    id 1001 ack 5000
 *     > data   id 1001 ack 5000, 4 bytes  the request, a message
 *     < data   id 5001 ack 1001           the answer's first message
 *     < data   id 5002 ack 1001
 *     x data   id 5003 ack 1001           its third, lost
 *     < data   id 5004 ack 1001           (kept: 5003 is not there)
 *     < data   id 5005 ack 1001
 *     > ack    id 1002 ack 5002           "my program read up to 5002"
 *     < query  id 5006 ack 1001           (0.1 s after) "where are you?"
 *     > state  id 1002 ack 5002           "I received up to 5002"
 *     < data?  id 5003 ack 1001           sent again, and "now?"
 *     > state  id 1002 ack 5005           "up to 5005"
 *     > ack    id 1002 ack 5005           "and my program read them"
 *     < close  id 5006 ack 1001           "I am done"
 *     > close  id 1002 ack 5006           "so am I"
 *     < close  id 5006 ack 1002           "heard"
 *
 * Its packet, after IP's 20 bytes (IP's number for it is 40):
 *
 *     sum | length | kind | 00 | from port | to port | id, 4 bytes |
 *     of all, with the      one of seven: sync 0, data 1, data? 2,
 *     message               ack 3, query 4, state 5, close 6
 *     ack, 4 bytes | the message
 *
 * One end of a connection is in one of five places:
 *
 *     Il_syncer  --- the other's sync --->  Il_established
 *     (dialed)                                ^      |
 *     Il_syncee  --- an ack, or data ---------+      | close said
 *     (was dialed)                                   | or heard
 *                                                    v
 *                                               Il_closing --> Il_closed
 *                                                              (said by both)
 *                                 any of them, patience over: Il_closed
 *
 * The same two functions run it at both ends ([net_input]: a packet
 * came; [net_tick]: time passed), and time is a number their caller
 * gives: the kernel's ticks, a test's loop. So two of these and a
 * list between them that loses by a seed is the test
 * (TinyKernelNetwork_tests/Host.ml): every message once and in order.
 *
 * Kept from Plan 9's il.c (principia's kernel/network/ip/il.c, 1,551
 * lines): the header and its numbers, the seven kinds, the window of
 * 20 messages, the query before sending again, only what was sent
 * before the query sent again. Changed: an ack says what the program
 * took, where il.c's says what was received and drops what its reader
 * has no room for (a state and a close still say what was received);
 * the wait is fixed (0.1 s, twice that each time, over after six with
 * nothing heard) where il.c measures the round trip; the end is said
 * only when what was written has arrived (il.c drops it); the last
 * close of four is not sent. Left out: the query every ten seconds of
 * a connection where nothing is owed, so an end that waits to read does
 * not notice the other gone silent (it does when the other says the
 * end, which giving up does).
 *
 * A number of IL's has 32 bits and tiny-ml's int 31: both ends here
 * start small and stay under 2^30; a packet with more is not read.
 *
 * Against its twin, mini-9pi's stack (kernels/9pi/network/: Ip, Icmp,
 * Udp, Tcp, and Devip's files), which speaks to the Internet: there,
 * Ethernet and ARP, routes, UDP for names and the time, TCP (the
 * twin of principia's tcp.c, a stream of bytes; no IL), and a program
 * reaches it by Plan 9's files, /net/tcp/clone, its ctl and its data,
 * which libc's dial writes. Here, IL alone, since a request, a block
 * or a drawing message is a message already, and a program reaches it
 * by two system calls of TinyKernel's, dial(address, port) and
 * listen(port), each giving a descriptor of messages; port 0 is the
 * echo (ping). The world, which speaks TCP, is reached through the
 * wire's other end (TinyMachinePeer, a translator).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * IP is Cerf and Kahn's (1974), split from TCP in 1978 so that what
 * needs no reliability (a voice, a question and its answer) need not
 * pay for it: an envelope with two addresses, each network free to
 * carry it its own way, nothing promised. The echo is ICMP's (RFC
 * 792, 1981), and ping is Mike Muuss's program of 1983, named after
 * sonar. IL is Presotto and Winterbottom's, of Plan 9's first years,
 * for 9P between its machines: TCP's guarantees for messages, in less
 * than half its code (il.c against tcp.c). Nothing else spoke it, and
 * Plan 9's fourth edition (2002) went back to TCP (from memory: IL
 * did badly on long roads and through address translation).
 *
 * design:
 * The checksum is the one the Internet has had since then (RFC 1071):
 * 16-bit numbers added, the carries added back. It is weak (two words
 * swapped are not seen) and kept because it is cheap, on any machine,
 * in any order of bytes; a wire that damages more than that has its
 * own check below.
 *
 * References: RFC 791 (IP), RFC 792 (ICMP), RFC 1071 (the checksum);
 * Presotto and Winterbottom, "The IL Protocol" (Plan 9's manual,
 * volume 2). *)

(* an address, its four bytes; "" when the text is not one *)
val net_address : string -> string

(* the machine's address and its host's, at the wire's two ends *)
val net_machine : string
val net_peer : string

(* 16 bits, the high byte first; the Internet's checksum of some bytes *)

val icmp_ask : int
