(*****************************************************************************)
(* Processes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* ready to run; waiting, the rest of its system call (true when it
 * could finish); stopped for its tracer, until the tracer resumes it *)
type state = Ready | Waiting of (unit -> bool) | Stopped

(* A process: its slot (where its frame is), its memory, its pid, its
 * state, its parent's pid (0: none), its
 * descriptors, its current directory; while it waits for a child's
 * end, how many processes had ended when it last looked (-1: it waits
 * for something else); and its trace, when it is traced. The core it
 * runs on (-1: none; 0 while core 0 runs it or handles its trap), and
 * whether it was killed there, its end then at its next trap. Its
 * command line and its memory, for /dev/ps: its program's (exec's
 * arguments, the bytes it asked for), or its parent's when it was
 * forked. *)
type proc = {
  slot : int; mem : space; pid : int;
  mutable state : state; mutable parent : int;
  mutable fds : (int * file) list; mutable cwd : string list;
  mutable since : int; mutable traced : trace option;
  mutable core : int; mutable doomed : bool;
  mutable cmd : string; mutable memory : int;
}

(* the processes, in the order the scheduler goes through them; how
 * many have ended *)
let procs = ref []
let next_pid = ref 1
let deaths = ref 0

(* the children ended, not waited for: parent, pid, status *)
let ended = ref []

(* /dev/ps: a line a process, in the scheduler's order; running is on a
 * core now (the reader itself, on core 0 for its call) *)
let () =
  ps_hook := (fun () ->
    String.concat "" (List.map (fun p ->
      let state = match p.state with
        | Ready when p.core >= 0 -> "running"
        | Ready -> "ready"
        | Waiting _ -> "waiting"
        | Stopped -> "stopped" in
      string_of_int p.pid ^ " " ^ string_of_int p.parent ^ " " ^ state ^ " "
      ^ string_of_int (p.memory / 1024) ^ " " ^ p.cmd ^ "\n") !procs))

(* a register of its frame (r1..r15, the pc as 16), as entry.tm saved it *)
let reg p k = peek (frame p.slot + (4 * k))
let set_reg p k v = poke (frame p.slot + (4 * k)) v

(* a user's address, n bytes long, as the kernel reaches it; Bad if it
 * leaves the partition *)
exception Bad
let user p va n =
  let a = mem_address p.mem va n in
  if a < 0 then raise Bad else a

(* the same, n bytes the kernel writes for the user (a read's, a call's
 * result): Bad in its text too, read only with segments *)
let user_out p va n =
  if mem_writable p.mem va n then user p va n else raise Bad

(* A user's buffer, n bytes at va, piece by piece: f a off k for each
 * piece, at the kernel's address a, off bytes into the buffer, k bytes
 * long; Bad if it leaves the process's memory. A partition gives one
 * piece; pages would give one a page, not together in the machine
 * (TinyKernelMemory.mli) *)
let user_iter p va n f =
  match mem_pieces p.mem va n with
  | Some l -> ignore (List.fold_left (fun off (a, k) -> f a off k; off + k) 0 l)
  | None -> raise Bad

(* a string of the kernel's written in the user's memory at va *)
let user_write p va s =
  if not (mem_writable p.mem va (String.length s)) then raise Bad;
  user_iter p va (String.length s) (fun a off k -> k_blit s off a k)

(* a string of the user's, a path: 1024 bytes at most (old: 64, a path
 * of a few names, when a name had 20) *)
let ustr p va =
  let b = Buffer.create 64 in
  let rec go i =
    if i >= 1024 then raise Bad
    else
      let c = peekb (user p (va + i) 1) in
      if c = 0 then Buffer.contents b
      else (Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr c); go (i + 1)) in
  go 0

(* a slot: none free now is No_room, as for a partition (with_room,
 * below, waits for one) *)
let free_slot () =
  let rec go s =
    if s >= nslots then raise No_room
    else if List.exists (fun p -> p.slot = s) !procs then go (s + 1)
    else s in
  go 0

(* a descriptor's file; the lowest free descriptor (32 a process: a
 * window system has four a window), given f *)
let fd p k =
  match List.assoc_opt k p.fds with Some f -> f | None -> raise Bad
let fdalloc p f =
  let rec go k =
    if k >= 32 then raise Bad
    else if List.exists (fun (j, _) -> j = k) p.fds then go (k + 1)
    else k in
  let k = go 0 in
  p.fds <- p.fds @ [ k, f ];
  k

(* a file's one more or one less descriptor (a pipe's ends count; a
 * connection's last one frees its images) *)
let share f =
  match f with
  | Reader pi -> pi.readers <- pi.readers + 1
  | Writer pi -> pi.writers <- pi.writers + 1
  | Draw d -> d.refs <- d.refs + 1
  | Post b -> b.posters <- b.posters + 1
  | Link l -> l.holders <- l.holders + 1
  | Call c -> c.callers <- c.callers + 1
  | Trace t -> t.watchers <- t.watchers + 1
  | _ -> ()

let links = ref []
let next_link = ref 1

(* the machine's connections: TinyKernelNetwork.ml's, at its address *)
let net = net_stack net_machine 1000

(* the process a trace is of, while it has not ended *)
let traced_proc t =
  match List.filter (fun q -> q.pid = t.tpid) !procs with
  | [ q ] -> Some q
  | _ -> None

(* the trace ended (its tracer's last descriptor closed, or the tracer
 * ended): the words under the breakpoints put back, the process run
 * again if it was stopped; one stopped before a call goes back to its
 * sys, to make the call (its registers are as they were) *)
let detach t =
  match traced_proc t with
  | Some q ->
      List.iter (fun (a, w) -> mem_store q.mem a w) t.stops;
      if t.call >= 0 then set_reg q 16 (reg q 16 - 4);
      t.stops <- [];
      q.traced <- None;
      (match q.state with Stopped -> q.state <- Ready | _ -> ())
  | None -> ()

let drop f =
  match f with
  | Trace t -> t.watchers <- t.watchers - 1; if t.watchers = 0 then detach t
  | Link l ->
      l.holders <- l.holders - 1;
      if l.holders = 0 then
        links := List.filter (fun m -> m.lid <> l.lid) !links
  | Call c -> c.callers <- c.callers - 1; if c.callers = 0 then il_done c.il
  | Reader pi -> pi.readers <- pi.readers - 1
  | Writer pi -> pi.writers <- pi.writers - 1
  | Draw d -> d.refs <- d.refs - 1; if d.refs = 0 then disconnect d.conn
  | Post b -> b.posters <- b.posters - 1
  | _ -> ()
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelProcs.mli

(* TinyKernel's processes: each a slot (its frame, where entry.tm saves
 * its registers at a trap), a memory (TinyKernelMemory's space), its
 * descriptors and its directory; and what reaches a process's memory
 * from the kernel, an address checked against its space.
 *
 *     Ready ──a call that must wait──► Waiting f ──f () true──► Ready
 *       │                                (the scheduler tries f again)
 *       ├──exit, kill──► gone, its slot and memory free at once; its
 *       │                (parent, pid, status) in [ended], for the
 *       │                parent's wait
 *       └──a stop for its tracer──► Stopped ──the tracer resumes it──► Ready
 *
 * A call that waits keeps the rest of itself in Waiting, a closure that
 * says whether it could finish: there is no kernel stack per process
 * to sleep on, the scheduler calls it again.
 *
 * A process that ends is freed at once, its slot and its memory. What
 * its parent's wait needs of it, its pid and its status, is a record of
 * three numbers in [ended], taken by the wait. There is no zombie: a
 * parent that never waits (www, for the play it starts) costs a record
 * a child, not one of the 16 slots and a partition.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * Unix keeps an ended process as a zombie: its entry in the process
 * table stays, for its status, until its parent's wait (and an
 * orphan's goes to init, which waits for it). A state of its own,
 * which the scheduler, kill, a trace and the console's owner must each
 * skip; a slot taken (tiny-kernel's zombie kept its memory too); and a
 * parent that does not wait leaks them, which SIGCHLD set to SIG_IGN or
 * a double fork work around. Plan 9's pexit frees the process and puts
 * a Waitq, a message, on its parent's list (dropped past 128 of them),
 * and wait reads the next one: the status is data, not a process. The
 * same here, with no limit: the Zombie state and the tests for it are
 * gone.
 *
 * others:
 * Unix's and Plan 9's kernels sleep in the middle of a call, on a
 * kernel stack of the process's; xv6 too (sleep, wakeup). A closure
 * kept is what Mach did instead, from 1991 (Draves and others,
 * "Using continuations to implement thread management and
 * communication in operating systems"): a blocked thread's stack given
 * up, its rest a function to call.
 *)

(* ready to run; waiting, the rest of its system call (true when it
 * could finish); stopped for its tracer, until the tracer resumes it *)
type state = Ready | Waiting of (unit -> bool) | Stopped

(* A process: its slot (where its frame is), its memory, its pid, its
 * state, its parent's pid (0: none), its descriptors, its current
 * directory; while it waits for a child's end, how many processes had
 * ended when it last looked (-1: it waits for something else); and its
 * trace, when it is traced. The core it runs on (-1: none; 0 while core
 * 0 runs it or handles its trap), and whether it was killed there, its
 * end then at its next trap. Its command line and its memory, for
 * /dev/ps: its program's (exec's arguments, the bytes it asked for), or
 * its parent's when it was forked. *)
type proc = {
  slot : int;
  mem : TinyKernelMemory.space;
  pid : int;
  mutable state : state;
  mutable parent : int;
  mutable fds : (int * TinyKernelFiles.file) list;
  mutable cwd : string list;
  mutable since : int;
  mutable traced : TinyKernelFiles.trace option;
  mutable core : int;
  mutable doomed : bool;
  mutable cmd : string;
  mutable memory : int;
}

(* the processes, in the order the scheduler goes through them; the
 * next pid; how many have ended *)
val procs : proc list ref
val next_pid : int ref
val deaths : int ref

(* The children that ended and were not waited for yet: their parent's
 * pid, theirs, their status, the first ended first; dropped if the
 * parent ends first. (old: a Zombie state, the process kept whole for
 * its status until its parent's wait: www's helpers, never waited for,
 * held a slot and 4 MB each while www ran) *)
val ended : (int * int * int) list ref

(* a register of its frame (r1..r15, the pc as 16), read and written *)
val reg : proc -> int -> int
val set_reg : proc -> int -> int -> unit

(* an address of a process's outside its memory *)
exception Bad

(* [user p va n]: a user's address, n bytes long, as the kernel reaches
 * it; [user_out]: the same, for bytes the kernel writes there (Bad in
 * its text too, read only with segments) *)
val user : proc -> int -> int -> int
val user_out : proc -> int -> int -> int

(* [user_iter p va n f]: a user's buffer, piece by piece, f a off k for
 * each piece at the kernel's address a, off bytes into it, k long *)
val user_iter : proc -> int -> int -> (int -> int -> int -> 'a) -> unit

(* a string of the kernel's written in the user's memory; a string of
 * the user's (a path), read *)
val user_write : proc -> int -> string -> unit
val ustr : proc -> int -> string

(* a free slot (No_room when there is none) *)
val free_slot : unit -> int

(* a descriptor's file; the lowest free descriptor, given that file *)
val fd : proc -> int -> TinyKernelFiles.file
val fdalloc : proc -> TinyKernelFiles.file -> int

(* a file's one more descriptor; one less (a pipe's ends count, a
 * connection's last one frees its images) *)
val share : TinyKernelFiles.file -> unit
val drop : TinyKernelFiles.file -> unit

(* the links to other machines, the next one's number; the machine's
 * connections, TinyKernelNetwork's *)
val links : TinyKernelFiles.link list ref
val next_link : int ref
val net : TinyKernelNetwork.net_stack

(* the process a trace is of, while it has not ended; the trace ended,
 * the words under its breakpoints put back *)
val traced_proc : TinyKernelFiles.trace -> proc option
val detach : TinyKernelFiles.trace -> unit
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelScheduler.ml
11018
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyKernelScheduler.mli *)
open TinyKernelNetwork
open TinyKernelMemory
open TinyKernelMachine
open TinyKernelFiles
open TinyKernelProcs
open TinyKernelDevices
open TinyKernelIO
open TinyKernelCalls

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The scheduler: round robin, preemptive *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the interrupts' sources: the timer re-armed (its time is up) and
 * counted, the console's bytes taken, ^C (3) killing the foreground,
 * every process but the shell (the first: no background here), the
 * mouse's word read, the network's packets taken, each given to
 * TinyKernelNetwork.ml (what it says to send back sent, an echo's answer
 * kept for the link that asked; a connection's messages are in it,
 * where its descriptor's read finds them); whether the timer's *)
let net_news = ref false

(* whether a program has messages it has not read; the tick at which
 * the network's interrupt is taken again all the same *)
let net_behind () =
  List.exists (fun c ->
    match c.il_r.il_heard with [] -> false | _ -> true) net.ns_conns
let net_open = ref 0

(* the tick of the connections' next look at the time *)
let net_next = ref 0

let net_take () =
  let n = peek (net_dev + 4) in
  if n > 0 then begin
    net_command n 2;
    (match net_input net !ticks (k_string net_buf n) with
     | back, answer ->
         List.iter net_send back;
         (match answer with
          | Some (from, id, _, data) ->
              List.iter (fun l ->
                if l.lid = id && l.peer = from then
                  l.heard <- l.heard @ [ data ]) !links
          | None -> ()))
    (* (one packet a call: the interrupt stays while another waits, and
     * the timer's is seen between two, so a burst does not stop the
     * clock, nor the acknowledgements, which go at its ticks. old: a
     * loop here, 230 ms without a tick for seven packets of 1 KB) *);
    (* When a program has messages to read, the packets that wait are
     * left for a while (the timer's interrupt says when: one more is
     * taken every 20 ms): the network's interrupt is not taken until
     * then, and the programs run. A burst of 20 rows was taken before
     * its reader read one, 280 ms in which nothing was acknowledged,
     * and the other end asked where it was. *)
    if net_behind () then k_ie 11
  end

(* the ticks since the last one counted, the timer set for the next *)
let count_ticks () =
  let passed = (k_clock () - !counted) land 0x3fffffff in
  ticks := !ticks + (passed / tick);
  counted := (!counted + (passed / tick * tick)) land 0x3fffffff;
  k_timer (tick - (passed mod tick))

(* what each core runs, but core 0 (the processes' core says it too);
 * [back], given a process's trap on another core, is the scheduler's
 * (below) *)
let on = Array.make cores None
let back_hook = ref (fun (_ : int) (_ : proc) (_ : int) (_ : int) -> ())

let interrupts sources =
  (* the cores' traps, each from the core that raised the interrupt *)
  if sources land 32 <> 0 then begin
    let from = peek ipi_dev in
    for k = 1 to cores - 1 do
      match on.(k) with
      | Some p when from land (1 lsl k) <> 0 ->
          on.(k) <- None;
          p.core <- -1;
          !back_hook k p (peek (mailbox k + 16)) (peek (mailbox k + 20))
      | _ -> ()
    done
  end;
  if sources land 16 <> 0 then net_take ();
  if sources land 8 <> 0 then begin
    (* the machine's word: x in 12 bits, y in the next 12, the buttons above *)
    let m = peek mouse_dev in
    mouse.last <-
      word (m land 0xfff) ^ word ((m lsr 12) land 0xfff) ^ word (m lsr 24);
    mouse.fresh <- true
  end;
  if sources land 2 <> 0 then begin
    let rec take () =
      let c = peek cons_in in
      if c = -2 then typed_end := true
      else if c = 3 && not (raw_on ()) then
        (typed := "";
         List.iter (fun q -> if q.pid <> 1 then kill q) !procs;
         puts "\n";
         take ())
      else if c <> -1 then
        (typed := !typed ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr c); take ()) in
    take ()
  end;
  (* the ticks since the last one counted, by the machine's time: the
   * timer's interrupt waits while the kernel works, and a long call
   * is several ticks (old: one counted at each interrupt, the timer
   * set a tick from then; a game's second was two under a window) *)
  if sources land 1 <> 0 then begin
    count_ticks ();
    if !ticks >= !net_open || not (net_behind ()) then
      (net_open := !ticks + 8; k_ie 27);
    (* the connections' time: what they send when nothing came, and one
     * that gave up is news for who waits on it *)
    (* (every fourth tick, 10 ms: a pass over the connections is 3,400
     * instructions with one of them, which at each tick was 4 ms of a
     * picture's row; IL's waits are 40 ticks and more) *)
    (match net.ns_conns with
     | [] -> ()
     | conns ->
         if !ticks >= !net_next then begin
           net_next := !ticks + 4;
           List.iter net_send (net_tick net !ticks);
           if List.length net.ns_conns < List.length conns then
             net_news := true
         end);
    true
  end
  else false

(* the first process that can run and that [ok] takes: ready, or
 * waiting and its call now finished. A traced one whose call ended may
 * stop instead (waited), which its tracer reads: the processes looked at
 * again from the first, since the tracer may be before it, already
 * passed over (old: runnable rest, and the tracer waited for the next
 * key or alarm: trace of a process in the background stopped at a
 * wait's end) *)
let rec runnable ok l =
  match l with
  | [] -> None
  | p :: rest ->
      (match p.state with
       | Ready -> if ok p then Some p else runnable ok rest
       | Waiting attempt ->
           if p.since = !deaths then runnable ok rest
           else if attempt () then
             (p.state <- Ready;
              if waited p then runnable ok !procs
              else if ok p then Some p
              else runnable ok rest)
           else (if p.since >= 0 then p.since <- !deaths; runnable ok rest)
       | Stopped -> runnable ok rest)

(* what core 0 may run: a process on no core; what another may: one
 * not traced too (a tracer reads its frame, steps it: core 0's) *)
let anywhere p = p.core < 0
let elsewhere p = p.core < 0 && not (traced p)

(* The other cores (entry.tm's slave). A process given to core k: its
 * frame, its window and a slice in k's mailbox, then k's interrupt *)
let give k p =
  p.core <- k;
  on.(k) <- Some p;
  let m = mailbox k in
  mem_post p.mem (m + 4);
  poke (m + 12) tick;
  poke m (frame p.slot);
  poke ipi_dev k

(* each free core given a process that can run *)
let dispatch () =
  for k = 1 to cores - 1 do
    if on.(k) = None then
      match runnable elsewhere !procs with
      | Some p -> give k p
      | None -> ()
  done

(* last in the round *)
let last p = procs := List.filter (fun q -> q.pid <> p.pid) !procs @ [ p ]

(* the loop: a process run until it traps, the trap handled; the same
 * process again unless its time is up or it cannot go on (then it goes
 * last); none to run, an interrupt waited for *)
let rec schedule () =
  dispatch ();
  match runnable anywhere !procs with
  | Some p -> run p
  | None -> idle ()

(* Every process waits. What they wait for changes only by a key, the
 * mouse, or a time one of them asked for (the alarm, which the calls
 * still waiting set again when retried): the clock's other ticks are
 * counted and nothing is retried. (old: schedule () after each
 * interrupt, every closure at each tick: a quarter of the instructions
 * of a machine where nothing happened) *)
and idle () =
  ignore (k_run 0);
  let sources = k_tval () in
  ignore (interrupts sources);
  if sources land 58 <> 0 || !net_news || (!alarm > 0 && !ticks >= !alarm)
  then (alarm := 0; net_news := false; schedule ())
  else idle ()

and run p =
  match p.traced with
  | Some t when t.call >= 0 -> call p t.call; next p false
  | Some t when t.step || t.over >= 0 -> step p t
  | _ ->
      p.core <- 0;
      mem_window p.mem;
      let cause = k_run (frame p.slot) in
      next p (trapped p cause (k_tval ()))

(* A traced process run for one instruction: a step, or a breakpoint's
 * word run (its 0 written again after, the process going on). The
 * timer's interrupt ends it (or the instruction's trap), and the timer
 * is set again for the next tick; an interrupt that came before the
 * instruction ran is taken, and the process run again. A step that
 * makes a call that waits stops when the call ends (waited). *)
and step p t =
  mem_window p.mem;
  let cause = k_step (frame p.slot) in
  let ran = cause <> c_intr || k_tval () land 1 <> 0 in
  let timer = trapped p cause (k_tval ()) in
  if cause <> c_intr then count_ticks ();
  if ran && List.exists (fun q -> q.pid = p.pid) !procs then begin
    if t.over >= 0 && List.exists (fun (b, _) -> b = t.over) t.stops then
      mem_store p.mem t.over 0;
    t.over <- -1;
    match p.state with Ready when t.step -> stop p "step" | _ -> ()
  end;
  next p timer

(* a trap handled, its cause and its value; whether it was the timer's *)
and trapped p cause tval =
  if cause = c_sys then (call p tval; false)
  else if cause = c_intr then interrupts tval
  else if cause = c_illegal && traced p then
    (stop p (if tval = 0 then "break" else "illegal " ^ string_of_int tval);
     false)
  (* (a page not touched yet, or one a fork shares: pages) *)
  else if cause = c_fault && mem_fault p.mem tval then false
  else if cause = c_fault && traced p then
    (stop p ("fault " ^ string_of_int tval); false)
  else begin
    puts ("ml: " ^ string_of_int p.pid ^ ": trap " ^ string_of_int cause
          ^ " at " ^ string_of_int (reg p 16) ^ ", "
          ^ string_of_int tval ^ ": killed\n");
    exit_proc p (-1);
    false
  end

(* the same process again unless its time is up or it cannot go on
 * (the other cores given what can run first: what p's call made ready) *)
and next p timer =
  let alive = List.exists (fun q -> q.pid = p.pid) !procs in
  if alive && (not timer) && (match p.state with Ready -> true | _ -> false)
  then (dispatch (); run p)
  else begin
    p.core <- -1;
    if alive then last p;
    schedule ()
  end

(* A trap of p's on core k, handled here as core 0's (its interrupt is
 * the core's timer: its slice is up); p on k again unless its time is
 * up or it cannot go on, as [next]. Killed while it ran, it ends now. *)
let back k p cause tval =
  if p.doomed then exit_proc p (-1)
  else begin
    let timer = cause = c_intr || trapped p cause tval in
    let alive = List.exists (fun q -> q.pid = p.pid) !procs in
    if alive && (not timer) && elsewhere p
       && (match p.state with Ready -> true | _ -> false)
    then give k p
    else if alive then last p
  end;
  dispatch ()
let () = back_hook := back
tiny/TinyKernel/TinyKernelScheduler.mli
1225
(* TinyKernel's scheduler: round robin, preemptive, on one core or
 * several. Core 0 is the kernel's: it runs a process until its trap
 * (a call, a fault, the timer's interrupt), handles the trap, and runs
 * the same process again unless its time is up or it cannot go on, then
 * the next one; the other cores run processes only, their traps posted
 * to core 0 (plan_tiny_multicore.md). With none to run, it waits for
 * an interrupt: a key, the mouse, the network, the timer.
 *
 *     schedule ──► the next that can run (Ready, or Waiting and its
 *        ▲          call now finished) ──k_run──► its trap
 *        └────────── the trap handled: a call, a fault, a tick ◄──┘
 *
 * The interrupts are handled between two runs: the console's bytes
 * (^C kills the foreground), the mouse's word, the network's packets
 * given to TinyKernelNetwork, the timer's ticks counted.
 *
 * others:
 * xv6's scheduler is the same loop over a process table, each process
 * a kernel stack it switches to; here a process waiting in a call is a
 * closure (TinyKernelProcs.mli), so there is one stack, the kernel's.
 *)

(* the loop, which never returns *)
val schedule : unit -> 'a

  = "glyphs_mixed"

tiny/TinyKernel/examples/paint.c
2465
// Claude Code, Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau, LGPL (see TinyC.ml)
//
// paint: TinyKernel.ml's program that draws. The mouse paints with a
// button down (the left one black, the middle one red, the right one
// white), a ball goes across the top by the clock, c clears, q quits.
// The ball's place is the clock's: 4 pixels a period since the boot,
// back and forth, so the screen at a time does not depend on when
// paint started (old: 4 pixels a move since paint started, the ball a
// few pixels further when the boot was longer, its test's screen
// recorded again after changes elsewhere).
// One loop waiting for the three at once: ready on the mouse and the
// keys, until the ball's next move. Its pixels are the kernel's: it
// writes messages to its descriptor 3 (draw.h) and reads its mouse, 4:
// the screen's, or its window's.
#include "../libc/user.h"
#include "../libc/draw.h"

enum { Grey = 1, Black, Red, White, Blue, Yellow, Period = 50 };

// the ball's x at the n-th period: 0 to 1008 and back, 4 pixels a step
int
ball(int n)
{
	n = n % 504;
	return 4 * (n < 252 ? n : 504 - n);
}

void
clear(void)
{
	d_fill(SCREEN, Grey, 0, 0, 1024, 768);
	d_fill(SCREEN, Blue, 0, 0, 1024, 20);
	d_text(SCREEN, White, 8, 2,
		"paint: the mouse paints with a button down; c clears, q quits");
	d_line(SCREEN, Black, 0, 60, 1023, 60);
}

void
main(void)
{
	int m[3], fds[2], mouse, k, x, next, ink;
	char c;

	mouse = MOUSE;
	d_colour(Grey, GREY); d_colour(Black, BLACK); d_colour(Red, RED);
	d_colour(White, WHITE); d_colour(Blue, BLUE); d_colour(Yellow, YELLOW);
	clear();
	fds[0] = mouse;
	fds[1] = 0;
	x = ball(ticks() / Period);
	next = (ticks() / Period + 1) * Period;
	for(;;){
		if(d_flush() < 0)
			exit(1);
		k = ready(fds, 2, next);
		if(k == mouse){
			if(read(mouse, (char*)m, 12) != 12)
				break;
			ink = m[2] & 1 ? Black : m[2] & 2 ? Red :
				m[2] & 4 ? White : 0;
			if(ink && m[1] > 60)
				d_fill(SCREEN, ink, m[0] - 4, m[1] - 4,
					m[0] + 4, m[1] + 4);
		} else if(k == 0){
			if(read(0, &c, 1) != 1 || c == 'q')
				break;
			if(c == 'c')
				clear();
		} else {
			// the ball: a square of 16, between the title and the line
			d_fill(SCREEN, Grey, x, 32, x + 16, 48);
			x = ball(ticks() / Period);
			d_fill(SCREEN, Yellow, x, 32, x + 16, 48);
			// (the next period's start: a ball that is late jumps to
			// its place, one move drawn, not each one it missed)
			next = (ticks() / Period + 1) * Period;
		}
	}
	exit(0);
}
tiny/TinyKernel/fonts/Mkfont.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* Makes tiny.font (README.md) from a TrueType font: its regular and its
 * bold, each at 8 by 16 and 16 by 32, the first 128 characters, a pixel
 * set or not; or grey.font, the same with grey edges, a pixel one of
 * four levels. ix's own reader and filler draw the letters (Truetype,
 * Outline, Fill.scan), as a PDF's are drawn; FreeType is not needed.
 *
 * Neither runs the font's hinting, the programs that move a letter's
 * points onto the pixels at a small size: a stem one pixel and a third
 * wide, where it falls, is drawn one pixel or two, and the top of an
 * e, a part of two rows, is in neither. What stands for it here, as
 * FreeType's autohinter does:
 *
 * - up, the heights every letter shares made whole rows: the
 *   baseline, the lower case's top (the x's) and the capitals' (the
 *   H's), the heights between stretched to fit (old: one shift down
 *   of the whole face, as across: the e's top, a third of a row and
 *   half of the next, was lost, the author's "the top of e is
 *   missing"); a round letter's overshoot past the three (the o's
 *   top, a fifth of a pixel) on them, not in the row beyond;
 * - across, one shift of the whole face, an eighth of a pixel at a
 *   time, the one whose pixels are most nearly all in or all out (the
 *   least sum of c (1 - c), c a pixel's part covered): in a monospaced
 *   font the stems of most letters are at the same places of their
 *   cells, so one shift puts most of them on whole pixels;
 * - then each character's own shift by the same measure, across up to
 *   3/8 of a pixel from the face's (too little to be seen in the
 *   spacing), and down, by as much, for what is no letter nor digit
 *   (a letter's rows are the heights above): with the face's alone, an
 *   E's and an L's stem straddled two pixels, two wide, and the +'s
 *   bar two rows, in neither.
 *
 * A pixel is then set where [enough] of it is covered; in grey.font the
 * others are grey by how much of them is.
 *
 * And plan9.font, Plan 9's default font (-plan9), a face of 1 bit a
 * pixel from its subfont.
 *
 * Run by hand; tiny.font, grey.font and plan9.font are kept in the
 * repository, so the build needs neither this nor the fonts' sources. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

let help = {|usage: Mkfont.exe [-cell w h] [-grey] regular.ttf bold.ttf out.font
       Mkfont.exe [-cell w h] -coverage c file.ttf
       Mkfont.exe -plan9 subfont out.font
tiny-kernel's font of a TrueType font's regular and bold: 128 characters
of 8 by 16 each, then 16 by 32, a pixel set or not (fonts/README.md);
with -grey, a pixel one of 4 levels, grey at the letters' edges; with
-cell, w by h and 2w by 2h, to look at another cell (tiny-kernel reads
8 by 16 alone). With -plan9, a Plan 9 subfont as font1.bin is, one
face of 8 by 16.
  dune exec tiny/TinyKernel/fonts/Mkfont.exe -- \
    UbuntuMono-Regular.ttf UbuntuMono-Bold.ttf tiny.font
  dune exec tiny/TinyKernel/fonts/Mkfont.exe -- -grey \
    UbuntuMono-Regular.ttf UbuntuMono-Bold.ttf grey.font
  dune exec tiny/TinyKernel/fonts/Mkfont.exe -- -plan9 \
    lucm.latin1.9 plan9.font
With -coverage, the character c at 8 by 16 as it is made: its pixels'
parts covered, in tenths (9 a whole one), the face's shift, and the
pixels set beside them.
|}

(* sub-rows a pixel's row is sampled at (across, the spans are exact) *)
let subrows = 8

(* the part of a pixel covered for it to be set: at a half, a stem of
 * Ubuntu Mono's regular at 16 pixels, a pixel and a little, was two
 * pixels wide wherever it straddled two (E, F, L, T heavy, the others
 * not); at 0.7 strokes broke (an r of two pieces); at 0.6 most stems
 * are one pixel and none broke, near FreeType's hinted letters
 * (preview.py) *)
let enough = 0.6

(* a face: the font, its scale (pixels a unit), the cell's size, the
 * baseline's row; the x's height and the H's, in the font's units, and
 * the whole rows they are made; how far the round letters go past the
 * baseline (the o's bottom), the x's height (the o's top) and the H's
 * (the O's top), in the font's units *)
type face = {
  font : Truetype.t; scale : float; w : int; h : int; base : float;
  xh : float; xrows : float; cap : float; caprows : float;
  under : float; over : float; capover : float;
}

(* the pixels above the baseline of a height of the font's: up to the
 * x's, to the H's, above it (the accents, an f's top), each part
 * scaled to its rows, and the descenders as the lower case. What a
 * round letter has past the three, its overshoot (a fifth of a pixel
 * at 16), is on them, as FreeType's autohinter does at small sizes
 * (its blue zones): old: the e's, a's, o's tops a fifth of the row
 * above, in grey.font a lone grey pixel over each (the author: "I can
 * see some pixels on the e above isolated a bit") *)
let height (face : face) (y : float) : float =
  if y < 0. then
    if y >= -. face.under then 0. else (y +. face.under) *. face.scale
  else if y <= face.xh then y *. face.xrows /. face.xh
  else if y <= face.xh +. face.over then face.xrows
  else if y <= face.cap then
    let from = face.xh +. face.over in
    face.xrows +. ((y -. from) *. (face.caprows -. face.xrows) /. (face.cap -. from))
  else if y <= face.cap +. face.capover then face.caprows
  else face.caprows +. ((y -. face.cap -. face.capover) *. face.scale)

(* [coverage face c dx dy]: each pixel's part covered of character c in
 * its cell, w by h, row after row, shifted by (dx, dy); and how much of
 * it fell outside the cell across, lost *)
let coverage (face : face) (c : int) (dx : float) (dy : float) : float array * float =
  let cov = Array.make (face.w * face.h) 0. in
  let spill = ref 0. in
  let glyph =
    match Truetype.cmap face.font ~platform:3 ~encoding:1 with
    | Some f -> f c
    | None -> failwith "no Unicode cmap"
  in
  let contours =
    Outline.polygons ~tolerance:0.02
      (fun (x, y) ->
        ( (x *. face.scale) +. dx,
          (face.base -. height face y +. dy) *. float_of_int subrows ))
      (Truetype.outline face.font glyph)
  in
  Fill.scan ~rule:Fill.Nonzero ~height:(face.h * subrows) contours
    ~on_span:(fun ~y xa xb ->
      let row = y / subrows in
      if y >= 0 then begin
        let sub = float_of_int subrows in
        spill := !spill +. ((max 0. (min xb 0. -. xa)
                             +. max 0. (xb -. max xa (float_of_int face.w))) /. sub);
        for px = max 0 (int_of_float (floor xa))
            to min (face.w - 1) (int_of_float (ceil xb) - 1) do
          let part = min xb (float_of_int (px + 1)) -. max xa (float_of_int px) in
          if part > 0. then
            cov.((row * face.w) + px) <-
              cov.((row * face.w) + px) +. (part /. sub)
        done
      end);
  (cov, !spill)

(* how far a coverage's pixels are from all in or all out, and what it
 * lost outside the cell, counted as all wrong (old: not counted: the
 * m moved left, its right stem half out of the cell, was the least
 * fuzz, and an rn) *)
let fuzz ((cov, spill) : float array * float) : float =
  Array.fold_left (fun sum v -> sum +. (v *. (1. -. min 1. v))) spill cov

(* the face's shift across of least fuzz, 0 to 7/8, its printable
 * characters' together *)
let shift (face : face) : float =
  let best = ref (0., infinity) in
  for i = 0 to 7 do
    let dx = float_of_int i /. 8. in
    let f = ref 0. in
    for c = 33 to 126 do f := !f +. fuzz (coverage face c dx 0.) done;
    if !f < snd !best then best := (dx, !f)
  done;
  fst !best

(* character c's coverage at its own shift of least fuzz, from the
 * face's dx, -3/8 to 3/8 across, and down when it is no letter nor
 * digit *)
let placed (face : face) (dx : float) (c : int) : float array =
  let ch = Char.chr c in
  let upright =
    (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') || (ch >= 'A' && ch <= 'Z') || (ch >= '0' && ch <= '9')
  in
  let best = ref (coverage face c dx 0., infinity) in
  for i = -3 to 3 do
    for j = (if upright then 0 else -3) to (if upright then 0 else 3) do
      let cov = coverage face c (dx +. (float_of_int i /. 8.)) (float_of_int j /. 8.) in
      let f = fuzz cov in
      (* (the least shift of equal fuzz: a blank's, the face's) *)
      if f < snd !best -. 1e-9 || (f < snd !best +. 1e-9 && i = 0 && j = 0) then
        best := (cov, f)
    done
  done;
  fst (fst !best)

(* the least part covered of a bar's pixel set though under [enough] *)
let bar = 0.4

(* [pixels face cov]: the pixels set of a character's coverage: those
 * covered [enough]; then a level bar a pixel thick that falls on two
 * rows, half in each, in neither (an A's crossbar, which a letter
 * cannot move down for, its rows the heights'): its upper row's pixel,
 * or its row more covered, where both are covered at least [bar] and
 * neither of the two is set, and so is a neighbour in its row (a bar is
 * pixels side by side; a lone one was the tail of a curve, a speck).
 * (Ubuntu Mono's m at 8 pixels reads nearly as an n: its middle stem
 * is short, by design, FreeType draws it so too; no stroke lost.) *)
let pixels (face : face) (cov : float array) : bool array =
  let at x y =
    if x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= face.w || y >= face.h then 0.
    else cov.((y * face.w) + x)
  in
  let set = Array.map (fun v -> v >= enough) cov in
  let on x y = x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < face.w && y < face.h && set.((y * face.w) + x) in
  let split x y =
    let v = at x y in
    (not (on x y)) && v >= bar
    && not (on x (y - 1) || on x (y + 1))
    && ((v >= at x (y + 1) && v > at x (y - 1) && at x (y + 1) >= bar)
        || (v > at x (y + 1) && at x (y - 1) >= bar && v > at x (y - 1)))
  in
  let bars = ref [] in
  for y = 0 to face.h - 1 do
    for x = 0 to face.w - 1 do
      if split x y && (split (x - 1) y || split (x + 1) y) then
        bars := ((y * face.w) + x) :: !bars
    done
  done;
  List.iter (fun i -> set.(i) <- true) !bars;
  set

(* the level of a pixel of grey.font, 0 (none) to 3 (the ink): 3 where
 * tiny.font's pixel is set, else the part covered, rounded to thirds
 * (old: tiny.font's alone, a pixel set or not): the same letters, with
 * grey around them where the outline passes. The part is raised to
 * 0.6 first, the edges darker, as a gamma: at 1024 by 768, shown twice
 * as large, a stroke of one pixel and a light third looked thin (old:
 * the part itself, v *. 3.) *)
let darken = 0.6
let level (set : bool) (v : float) : int =
  if set then 3
  else min 2 (int_of_float (Float.round (Float.pow v darken *. 3.)))

(* a face's 128 characters as tiny.font has them, depth 1: a row
 * (w + 7) / 8 bytes, its left pixel the low bit of its first; or as
 * grey.font, depth 2: a pixel two bits, its level, a row w / 4 bytes *)
let bits (face : face) (depth : int) : string =
  let dx = shift face in
  let bytes = ((face.w * depth) + 7) / 8 in
  let b = Bytes.make (128 * face.h * bytes) '\000' in
  for c = 32 to 126 do
    let cov = placed face dx c in
    let set = pixels face cov in
    for row = 0 to face.h - 1 do
      for x = 0 to face.w - 1 do
        let p = (row * face.w) + x in
        let v = if depth = 1 then Bool.to_int set.(p) else level set.(p) cov.(p) in
        let i = (((c * face.h) + row) * bytes) + (x * depth / 8) in
        Bytes.set b i
          (Char.chr (Char.code (Bytes.get b i) lor (v lsl (x * depth mod 8))))
      done
    done
  done;
  Bytes.to_string b

(* the face of a font file whose characters are w pixels wide (its
 * advance, a monospaced font's: the M's), h tall, the baseline at
 * 13/16 of the cell (16: 3 rows for the descenders); the x's and the
 * H's heights each the nearest whole rows *)
let face (font : Truetype.t) (w : int) (h : int) : face =
  let glyph c =
    match Truetype.cmap font ~platform:3 ~encoding:1 with
    | Some f -> f (Char.code c)
    | None -> failwith "no Unicode cmap"
  in
  let bounds c =
    match Outline.bounds (Truetype.outline font (glyph c)) with
    | Some (_, y0, _, y1) -> (y0, y1)
    | None -> failwith "no outline"
  in
  let top c = snd (bounds c) in
  let scale = float_of_int w /. float_of_int (Truetype.advance font (glyph 'M')) in
  let xh = top 'x' and cap = top 'H' in
  { font; scale; w; h; base = float_of_int (h * 13 / 16);
    xh; xrows = Float.round (xh *. scale); cap; caprows = Float.round (cap *. scale);
    under = max 0. (-. fst (bounds 'o')); over = max 0. (top 'o' -. xh);
    capover = max 0. (top 'O' -. cap) }

(* Plan 9's default font (lucm.latin1.9, a subfont: an image of every
 * character side by side, ldepth 0, its rows from the high bit; then
 * the count, the height, the ascent, and 6 bytes a character: its x
 * in the image (2 bytes), its top and bottom rows, its left, its
 * width) as font1.bin is, a face of 8 by 16: its baseline on
 * tiny.font's, row 12; a character's ink moved left into 8 columns
 * when it is past them (its cell is 9 wide: @ and _ lose a column) *)
let plan9 (s : string) : string =
  let field o = int_of_string (String.trim (String.sub s o 12)) in
  let minx = field 12 and maxx = field 36 and h = field 48 - field 24 in
  if field 0 <> 0 then failwith "not 1 bit a pixel";
  let bw = 4 * (((maxx + 31) / 32) - (minx / 32)) in
  let info = 60 + (h * bw) + 36 and ascent = field (60 + (h * bw) + 24) in
  let byte o = Char.code s.[o] in
  let x c = byte (info + (6 * c)) lor (byte (info + (6 * c) + 1) lsl 8) in
  let ink r col = byte (60 + (r * bw) + (col / 8)) land (0x80 lsr (col mod 8)) <> 0 in
  let out = Bytes.make 2048 '\000' in
  for c = 32 to 126 do
    let top = byte (info + (6 * c) + 2) and bottom = byte (info + (6 * c) + 3) in
    let left = (byte (info + (6 * c) + 4) lxor 128) - 128 in
    let cols = ref [] in
    for r = top to bottom - 1 do
      for col = x c to x (c + 1) - 1 do
        if ink r col then cols := (col - x c + left) :: !cols
      done
    done;
    let off = List.fold_left max 0 (List.map (fun p -> p - 7) !cols) in
    for r = top to bottom - 1 do
      let row = r + 12 - (ascent - 1) in
      for col = x c to x (c + 1) - 1 do
        let p = col - x c + left - off in
        if ink r col && p >= 0 && p < 8 && row >= 0 && row < 16 then
          Bytes.set out ((c * 16) + row)
            (Char.chr (Char.code (Bytes.get out ((c * 16) + row)) lor (1 lsl p)))
      done
    done
  done;
  Bytes.to_string out

(* the four faces of tiny.font's format from font1.bin's one, as the
 * kernel makes them (TinyKernelGraphics' make): bold each stroke a
 * pixel wider but for a gap of one; large each pixel 2 by 2. Made here,
 * not by the kernel when first asked for: its time, in the middle of a
 * session, made the recorded office session's click at (300, 300)
 * missed (old: plan9.font of 2,048 bytes, the faces the kernel's) *)
let four (face : string) : string =
  let bold =
    String.map (fun c ->
      let r = Char.code c in
      Char.chr ((r lor ((r lsl 1) land lnot (r lsr 1))) land 255)) face in
  let large f =
    String.init 8192 (fun i ->
      let c = i / 64 and row = i mod 64 / 4 and half = i mod 2 in
      let r = Char.code f.[(c * 16) + row] lsr (4 * half) in
      Char.chr (List.fold_left (fun acc k ->
        if (r lsr k) land 1 = 1 then acc lor (3 lsl (2 * k)) else acc)
        0 [ 0; 1; 2; 3 ])) in
  String.concat "" [ face; bold; large face; large bold ]

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : int =
  (* -cell w h: a cell other than 8 by 16 (a preview's; tiny-kernel
   * reads 8 by 16 alone) *)
  let w, h, args =
    match Array.to_list argv |> List.tl with
    | "-cell" :: w :: h :: rest -> (int_of_string w, int_of_string h, rest)
    | args -> (8, 16, args)
  in
  try
    match args with
    | args when List.mem "-h" args || List.mem "--help" args ->
        Console.print caps help; 0
    | [ "-coverage"; c; file ] when String.length c = 1 ->
        let f = face (Truetype.of_string (FS.read caps (Fpath.v file))) w h in
        let dx = shift f in
        let cov = placed f dx (Char.code c.[0]) in
        let set = pixels f cov in
        (* a pixel's tenths covered, '.' for none *)
        let tenths v =
          if v < 0.05 then '.' else Char.chr (48 + min 9 (int_of_float (v *. 10.)))
        in
        Console.print caps
          (Printf.sprintf "shift %g, x's height %g rows, H's %g\n" dx f.xrows f.caprows);
        for y = 0 to f.h - 1 do
          let i x = (y * f.w) + x in
          Console.print caps
            (String.init f.w (fun x -> tenths cov.(i x)) ^ "  "
             ^ String.init f.w (fun x -> if set.(i x) then '#' else '.') ^ "\n")
        done;
        0
    | [ "-plan9"; subfont; out ] ->
        FS.write caps (Fpath.v out)
          (four (plan9 (FS.read caps (Fpath.v subfont))));
        0
    | ([ regular; bold; out ] | [ "-grey"; regular; bold; out ]) as args ->
        let read f = Truetype.of_string (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f)) in
        let r = read regular and b = read bold in
        let depth = if List.hd args = "-grey" then 2 else 1 in
        FS.write caps (Fpath.v out)
          (String.concat ""
             [ bits (face r w h) depth; bits (face b w h) depth;
               bits (face r (2 * w) (2 * h)) depth;
               bits (face b (2 * w) (2 * h)) depth ]);
        0
    | _ ->
        Console.eprint caps
          "usage: Mkfont.exe regular.ttf bold.ttf out.font   (-h: how)\n";
        1
  with Sys_error m | Failure m -> Console.eprint caps ("Mkfont: " ^ m ^ "\n"); 1

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
    Logging.setup caps ~name:"Mkfont";
    CapStdlib.exit caps (main caps (CapSys.argv caps)))

(* TinyKernel.ml's calls, for a program built by OCaml, so that it runs
 * on the host: what TinyLibDraw.ml, TinyLibPlayground.ml, TinyLibGUI.ml
 * and the few lines of a program on them (TinyKernel/user/office.ml...)
 * ask of tiny-kernel. On tiny-machine these names are externals
 * (TinyKernel/libml/TinyCalls.ml, which names mlsys.c's functions).
 *
 * A virtual library of dune's: this interface, and two
 * implementations, a program choosing one when it is linked:
 *
 *     stub/TinyCalls.ml     the tests': no kernel; what is drawn kept in
 *                           [drawn], for TinyKernelGraphics.ml; no key,
 *                           no clock, no network (the default)
 *     ../../sdl/TinyCalls.ml  a window of SDL's: what is drawn drawn by
 *                           TinyKernelGraphics.ml and shown, the mouse
 *                           and the keys the window's, the host's files
 *                           and clock (tiny-office, tiny-emacs... on the
 *                           host)
 *
 * The descriptors are tiny-kernel's: 0 the keys, 1 the console, 3 where
 * a program draws, 4 its mouse (a box: x, y, the buttons, a word each). *)

(* [u_write fd s]: 0 when all of s was written (where a program draws:
 * the drawing messages, TinyKernelGraphics.mli's) *)
val u_write : int -> string -> int

(* [u_read fd n]: up to n bytes, "" at the end *)
val u_read : int -> int -> string

(* [u_ready fds n until]: the first of fds' n descriptors that can be
 * read, waiting until the clock is until (0: no end), -1 then *)
val u_ready : int array -> int -> int -> int

(* the clock, 400 ticks a second *)
val u_ticks : unit -> int

(* the date, seconds since 2000-01-01 *)
val u_time : unit -> int

(* a seed for a program's first random number: the machine's, or the
 * clock when it has none *)
val u_seed : unit -> int

(* a path's entry (user.h's dirent: a name of 64 bytes, its type, links,
 * size and date, a word each), or "" when it is not there *)
val u_stat : string -> string

(* a file opened (flags as user.h's: 0 to read, 0x601 to write it anew),
 * its descriptor, or -1; closed *)
val u_open : string -> int -> int
val u_close : int -> int

(* the console raw (1) or not (0): its ^C a key *)
val u_rawcons : int -> int

(* a connection to a machine's port: -1, none on the host *)
val u_dial : string -> int -> int

(* [u_spawn path args]: a child running the program at path (args: its
 * name first), not waited for; its pid, or -1. The window's: a program
 * of tiny-kernel's /bin is its host twin (/bin/play: tiny-play, else
 * mini-play; /bin/page: mini-page), found where this one is or on the
 * PATH; the stub's: -1 *)
val u_spawn : string -> string list -> int

(* the program's arguments: how many, the i-th (0 its name) *)
val u_argc : unit -> int
val u_arg : int -> string

(* what was written where a program draws, kept for a test (the stub's;
 * the window's draws it at once and keeps nothing) *)
val drawn : Buffer.t

(* See TinyLibSystem.mli; this is the host's *)

(* a descriptor is a number, on Unix *)
let fd (n : int) : Unix.file_descr = Obj.magic n
let number (f : Unix.file_descr) : int = Obj.magic f

(* [reason f]: f's result, or Failure with the system's message *)
let reason f =
  try f () with
  | Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> failwith (Unix.error_message e)
  | Sys_error m -> failwith m

let main (name : string) (f : Cap.all_caps -> int) : unit =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
    Logging.setup caps ~name;
    CapStdlib.exit caps
      (try f caps with
       | Failure m ->
         flush_all ();
         Console.eprint caps (name ^ ": " ^ m ^ "\n");
         1))

let argv (caps : < Cap.argv; .. >) = Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps)
let environment (caps : < Cap.env; .. >) =
  Procs.split_env (CapUnix.environment caps ())
let getpid (caps : < Cap.env; .. >) = CapUnix.getpid caps ()

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The terminal *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let print (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) s = Console.print caps s
let eprint (caps : < Cap.stderr; .. >) s = Console.eprint caps s
let flush (_ : < Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >) = flush_all ()
let read_line (caps : < Cap.stdin; .. >) =
  try Some (input_line (Console.stdin caps)) with End_of_file -> None
let isatty n = Unix.isatty (fd n)

(* (a handler, unlike an ignored signal, is not inherited through exec) *)
let ignore_interrupt (_ : < Cap.signal; .. >) =
  Sys.set_signal Sys.sigint (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> ()))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Files *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let open_in (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> number (FS.open_in_fd caps file))
let open_out (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> number (FS.open_out_fd caps file 0o666))
let open_append (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> number (FS.open_append_fd caps file 0o666))
let close n = Unix.close (fd n)

let open_rw (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () ->
    if not (Sys.file_exists file) then Unix.close (FS.create_fd caps file 0o666);
    number (FS.open_rw_fd caps file))
let seek n off = ignore (reason (fun () -> Unix.lseek (fd n) off Unix.SEEK_SET))
let seek_end n = reason (fun () -> Unix.lseek (fd n) 0 Unix.SEEK_END)
let read_file (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> FS.read caps (Fpath.v file))
let read_all n = Procs.read_all (fd n)
let readdir (_ : < Cap.readdir; .. >) dir =
  try Array.to_list (Sys.readdir dir) with Sys_error _ -> []
let is_directory (_ : < Cap.readdir; .. >) file =
  try Sys.is_directory file with Sys_error _ -> false
let chdir (caps : < Cap.chdir; .. >) dir = reason (fun () -> CapUnix.chdir caps dir)

let read n max =
  let buf = Bytes.create max in
  let k = reason (fun () -> Unix.read (fd n) buf 0 max) in
  Bytes.sub_string buf 0 k

let write n s =
  let rec go at =
    if at < String.length s then
      go (at + reason (fun () ->
        Unix.write_substring (fd n) s at (String.length s - at)))
  in
  go 0
let write_file (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) file s =
  let fd = open_out caps file in
  write fd s;
  close fd

let stat (_ : < Cap.open_in; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () ->
    let st = Unix.stat file in
    st.st_kind = Unix.S_DIR, st.st_size)
let links (_ : < Cap.open_in; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> (Unix.stat file).st_nlink)
let mtime (_ : < Cap.open_in; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> int_of_float (Unix.stat file).st_mtime - 946684800)
let mkdir (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) dir =
  reason (fun () -> FS.mkdir caps dir 0o777)
let remove (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () -> FS.remove_any caps file)
let rename (_caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) a b = reason (fun () -> Unix.rename a b)
let link (_caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) a b = reason (fun () -> Unix.link a b)

let is_executable (_ : < Cap.open_in; .. >) file =
  try (Unix.stat file).st_perm land 0o100 <> 0 with Unix.Unix_error _ -> false
let set_executable (_caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) file x =
  reason (fun () -> Unix.chmod file (if x then 0o755 else 0o644))

(* (utimes with two zeros: now) *)
let touch (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) file =
  reason (fun () ->
    if Sys.file_exists file then Unix.utimes file 0.0 0.0
    else Unix.close (FS.create_fd caps file 0o666))

let getcwd (caps : < Cap.env; .. >) = CapSys.getcwd caps ()
(* (946684800: 2000-01-01 in Unix's seconds) *)
let time (caps : < Cap.clock; .. >) =
  int_of_float (CapUnix.time caps ()) - 946684800
let sleep (caps : < Cap.clock; .. >) ms =
  CapUnix.sleepf caps (float_of_int ms /. 1000.0)
let millis (caps : < Cap.clock; .. >) =
  int_of_float (CapUnix.gettimeofday caps () *. 1000.0)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Descriptors *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let save n =
  try Some (number (Unix.dup ~cloexec:true (fd n)))
  with Unix.Unix_error _ -> None
let dup2 a b = Unix.dup2 (fd a) (fd b)
let pipe (caps : < Cap.pipe; .. >) =
  let r, w = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true () in number r, number w

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Processes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let fork (caps : < Cap.fork; .. >) = CapUnix.fork caps ()

let kill (caps : < Cap.kill; .. >) pid =
  try CapUnix.kill caps pid Sys.sigkill; true with Unix.Unix_error _ -> false

let exec (caps : < Cap.exec; .. >) file (argv : string list)
    (env : string list) : string =
  try CapUnix.execve caps file (Array.of_list argv) (Array.of_list env); ""
  with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> Unix.error_message e

(* a signal by rc's name for it; OCaml numbers its own from -1: abrt,
 * alrm, fpe, hup, ill, int, kill, pipe, quit, segv, term
 * old: "signal " ^ string_of_int n, OCaml's number (-6 for an interrupt) *)
let signals =
  [| "sys: abort"; "alarm"; "sys: fp: trap"; "hangup";
     "sys: illegal instruction"; "interrupt"; "sys: kill";
     "sys: write on closed pipe"; "quit"; "sys: segmentation violation";
     "kill" |]

let status = function
  | Unix.WEXITED 0 -> ""
  | Unix.WEXITED n -> string_of_int n
  | Unix.WSIGNALED n | Unix.WSTOPPED n ->
    "signal: "
    ^ if n < 0 && -n <= Array.length signals then signals.(-n - 1)
      else string_of_int n

let wait (caps : < Cap.wait; .. >) pid = status (Procs.waitpid caps pid)
let wait_any (caps : < Cap.wait; .. >) =
  Option.map (fun (pid, st) -> pid, status st) (Procs.wait_any caps)

let shell (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.env; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. >) vars
    script =
  let env =
    List.map (fun (k, v) -> k ^ "=" ^ String.concat " " v) vars
    @ Array.to_list (CapUnix.environment caps ())
  in
  flush_all ();
  match CapUnix.fork caps () with
  | 0 ->
    (try
       CapUnix.execve caps "/bin/sh" [| "sh"; "-e"; "-c"; script |]
         (Array.of_list env)
     with _ -> ());
    Unix._exit 127
  | pid -> pid

let exit (_ : < Cap.exit; .. >) n = Unix._exit n

(* What a tool asks of the system it runs on, for a tool that runs on
 * two: tiny-shell and tiny-utils, on the host and on tiny-machine.
 * The tool's one file, TinyShell.ml or TinyUtilities.ml, names only
 * this and the pure functions of the standard library; there are two
 * files of this:
 *
 *               TinyShell.ml, TinyUtilities.ml
 *            ___________/        \___________
 *   on the host                        on tiny-machine
 *   TinyKernel/host/TinyLibSystem.ml   TinyKernel/libml/TinyLibSystem.ml
 *   (this one's), OCaml, built by      built by tiny-ml,
 *   dune or mini-mk                    on TinyLibCore/
 *   over Unix, Cap, FS, Procs          over tiny-kernel's calls
 *   Linux                              tiny-kernel
 *
 * So the interface is what both systems can give, which is the
 * smaller one's, tiny-kernel's: a descriptor is a number, a call that
 * fails raises Failure with the reason (the host's has the system's
 * message, tiny-kernel's has no reason to give), a child's status is
 * already rc's string. What tiny-kernel has not is answered there by
 * nothing: no environment but a PATH, no signal, no terminal to ask
 * about.
 *
 * m-ix has the same seam one level lower: its tools (mini-rc,
 * mini-cat...) stand on lib_core (Cap, FS, Procs) over OCaml's Unix,
 * and lib_core/system/ has that Unix twice, by Linux's system calls
 * and by Plan 9's (system/plan9/), so one tool runs on Linux and on
 * mini-9pi. Here the seam is the tools' own interface, cut to what
 * tiny-kernel gives, so that a tool cannot ask the host for what the
 * other system lacks.
 *
 * The capabilities are the host's: there, a function that reaches the
 * system takes the object that allows it, and OCaml checks it. tiny-ml
 * reads them and forgets them.
 *)

(* [main name f]: the program: f with every capability, its result the
 * exit's code; a Failure that f lets out said after name, the code 1.
 * name is for the host's logs too *)
val main : string -> (Cap.all_caps -> int) -> unit

(* the program's name, then its arguments *)
val argv : < Cap.argv; .. > -> string list

(* the variables the program was started with, each with its value *)
val environment : < Cap.env; .. > -> (string * string) list
val getpid : < Cap.env; .. > -> int

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The terminal *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* on the standard output, kept until flush; on the error's, at once *)
val print : < Cap.stdout; .. > -> string -> unit
val eprint : < Cap.stderr; .. > -> string -> unit
val flush : < Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. > -> unit

(* a line of the standard input without its end; None at the input's end *)
val read_line : < Cap.stdin; .. > -> string option

(* whether a descriptor is a terminal, where someone types *)
val isatty : int -> bool

(* an interrupt typed at the terminal is for the program that runs,
 * not for this one *)
val ignore_interrupt : < Cap.signal; .. > -> unit

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Files *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a file's descriptor: to read it, to write it from nothing (made if
 * it is not there), to write at its end. Failure with the reason *)
val open_in : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string -> int
val open_out : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> int
val open_append : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> int
val close : int -> unit

(* a file's descriptor to read and write it, at any place (a database's
 * file); made empty when it is not there. Failure with the reason *)
val open_rw : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> int

(* [seek fd off]: the next read or write at off from the file's start;
 * [seek_end fd]: at its end, which is the offset given *)
val seek : int -> int -> unit
val seek_end : int -> int

(* a file's text; Failure with the reason. [write_file caps file s]: the
 * file made s, created or emptied first *)
val read_file : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string -> string
val write_file : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> string -> unit

(* all that a descriptor gives, to its end *)
val read_all : int -> string

(* a directory's names, in no order; none when it cannot be read *)
val readdir : < Cap.readdir; .. > -> string -> string list
val is_directory : < Cap.readdir; .. > -> string -> bool

(* Failure with the reason *)
val chdir : < Cap.chdir; .. > -> string -> unit

(* [read fd max]: what fd gives next, up to max bytes, without waiting
 * for more; "" at the end. For a program that must work on its input
 * as it comes (cat at the console) *)
val read : int -> int -> string

(* all of the string, written to the descriptor *)
val write : int -> string -> unit

(* whether a file is a directory, and its size in bytes; Failure with
 * the reason when it is not there *)
val stat : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string -> bool * int

(* how many names a file has (its hard links); Failure with the reason
 * when it is not there *)
val links : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string -> int

(* the date of a file's last write, seconds since 2000-01-01 (the image's
 * files on tiny-kernel: 0); Failure with the reason when it is not
 * there *)
val mtime : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string -> int

(* a new directory; a file, or a directory that is empty, removed.
 * Failure with the reason *)
val mkdir : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> unit
val remove : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> unit

(* [link caps old new]: a second name for a file (not a directory).
 * Failure with the reason *)
val link : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> string -> unit

(* [rename caps from to]: the file, or the directory, under another
 * name. Failure with the reason *)
val rename : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> string -> unit

(* whether a file is a program to run, its x bit for its owner; [set_executable
 * caps file x]: its bit set, or cleared (tiny-kernel has no modes: no
 * file is one there, and the call does nothing) *)
val is_executable : < Cap.open_in; .. > -> string -> bool
val set_executable : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> bool -> unit

(* a file that is there written now, as far as its time says; one that
 * is not there made, empty. Failure with the reason *)
val touch : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. > -> string -> unit

(* the directory the process is in *)
val getcwd : < Cap.env; .. > -> string

(* the date, in seconds since 2000-01-01 UTC, on both sides: a 31-bit
 * integer of tiny-ml's holds them until 2034, where 1970's would not
 * fit (old: Unix's seconds on the host, 0 on tiny-kernel, which had no
 * clock of the day) *)
val time : < Cap.clock; .. > -> int

(* nothing done for so many milliseconds *)
val sleep : < Cap.clock; .. > -> int -> unit

(* a clock in milliseconds, from some start (the boot on tiny-kernel, 2.5
 * at a time, its ticks): for a time taken, the difference of two *)
val millis : < Cap.clock; .. > -> int

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Descriptors *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [save n]: a copy of descriptor n, away from the low numbers and not

val save : int -> int option

(* [dup2 a b]: b is now what a is *)

(* a pipe: where to read, where to write; not given to a program run *)

(*****************************************************************************)

(*****************************************************************************)

(* a copy of this process: 0 in the copy, the copy's number here *)
val fork : < Cap.fork; .. > -> int

(* [kill caps pid]: that process ended at once (the host's SIGKILL);
 * false when there is none, or it is not ours to end *)

(* [exec caps file argv env]: this process becomes the program in file,
 * env its variables as name=value; when it cannot, the reason *)

(* a child's end, as rc's status: "" when all went well, its code, or

(* the next child to end, and its status as wait's; None when there is
 * no child *)
val wait_any : < Cap.wait; .. > -> (int * string) option

(* [shell caps vars script]: a child that runs script by the system's
 * shell, vars among its variables (each a list of words), what was

 * assignments before it) *)
val shell :
  < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.env; Cap.open_out; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; .. > ->
  (string * string list) list -> string -> int

(* the end of this process, at once: nothing flushed *)
val exit : < Cap.exit; .. > -> int -> 'a
tiny/TinyKernel/host/TinyMemory.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* tiny-machine's memory, for a program built by OCaml: what
 * TinyKernelGraphics.ml and the programs over it ask of a machine, so that
 * they run on the host too, where they are tested first
 * (plan_tiny_windows.md). On tiny-machine these names are externals,
 * functions of C (TinyKernel/runtime.c's peekb and pokeb) and of
 * assembly (TinyKernel/draw.tm's rows); tiny-ml reads `open TinyMemory`
 * and leaves it. Here they are an array's, of the machine's 16 MB, an
 * address the same number in both: the screen's 1024 by 768 bytes are at
 * 0xf00000, and [ppm] writes them as tiny-machine -screen does. *)

let mem = Bytes.make 0x1000000 '\000'
let peekb a = Char.code (Bytes.get mem a)
let pokeb a v = Bytes.set mem a (Char.chr (v land 255))

(* a row's n bytes: copied from the first (as draw.tm's loop: not
 * Bytes.blit, which looks which way to go), filled with a colour, and
 * given a colour where the mask's byte is not 0 *)
let row_copy dst src n = for i = 0 to n - 1 do pokeb (dst + i) (peekb (src + i)) done
let row_fill dst colour n = Bytes.fill mem dst n (Char.chr (colour land 255))
let row_mask dst colour mask n =
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    if peekb (mask + i) <> 0 then pokeb (dst + i) colour
  done

(* a row's n bytes mixed by a mask's levels: where the mask's byte is
 * not 0, the byte of the table's row of its level (its two high bits)
 * that the pixel's colour is *)
let row_mix dst table mask n =
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    let m = peekb (mask + i) in
    if m <> 0 then
      pokeb (dst + i) (peekb (table + ((m lsr 6) * 256) + peekb (dst + i)))
  done

(* a text's n characters from dst, in an image [width] wide, through the
 * font's mask (1024 wide, character c at column 8c), as draw.tm's: in a
 * colour, or mixed by a table (glyphs_mixed) *)
let each_glyph row dst width font s n =
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    let c = Char.code s.[i] in
    let c = if c > 127 then 63 else c in
    for k = 0 to 15 do
      row (dst + (8 * i) + (k * width)) (font + (k * 1024) + (8 * c))
    done
  done
let glyphs dst width colour font s n =
  each_glyph (fun d m -> row_mask d colour m 8) dst width font s n
let glyphs_mixed dst width table font s n =
  each_glyph (fun d m -> row_mix d table m 8) dst width font s n

(* A colour's mixes, at at: 4 rows of 256 bytes, row l's byte k the
 * colour nearest to l thirds of the ink and the rest of colour k (row
 * 0 k, row 3 the ink), the palette's red, green and blue (3 bytes a
 * colour) at palette. Nearest by the squares of the differences, among
 * the 16 a colour can be near: for each q = 4 den + v (den the largest
 * of a colour's two-bit red, green and blue, v how bright), the one
 * whose parts are the mix's rounded, its largest 17 q; q below 4, the
 * grey 17 q. The same as a search of the 256 but for ties (the first q
 * of the least kept), in a sixteenth of the time. *)
let mix_table at ink palette =
  let c k i = peekb (palette + (3 * k) + i) in
  let nearest r g b =
    let best = ref 0 and dist = ref max_int in
    for q = 0 to 15 do
      let den = q lsr 2 and v = q land 3 and top = 17 * q in
      let part x = if den = 0 then 0 else min den (((x * den) + (top / 2)) / top) in
      let pr = part r and pg = part g and pb = part b in
      let i = (pr * 64) + (v * 16) + (((pg * 4) + pb + v - pr) land 15) in
      let d = ((c i 0 - r) * (c i 0 - r)) + ((c i 1 - g) * (c i 1 - g))
              + ((c i 2 - b) * (c i 2 - b)) in
      if d < !dist then (best := i; dist := d)
    done;
    !best
  in
  for l = 0 to 3 do
    for k = 0 to 255 do
      let part i = ((l * c ink i) + ((3 - l) * c k i) + 1) / 3 in
      pokeb (at + (l * 256) + k)
        (if l = 0 then k else if l = 3 then ink
         else nearest (part 0) (part 1) (part 2))
    done
  done

(* a string's n bytes from off, to memory at dst; and memory's n bytes
 * at a, as a string *)
let row_bytes s off dst n = Bytes.blit_string s off mem dst n
let row_string a n = Bytes.sub_string mem a n

(* the screen, w by h, as a PPM: the bytes tiny-machine -screen writes,
 * a byte's colour the machine's (old: Plan 9's table computed here, a
 * copy of TinyMachineDevices's formula) *)
let ppm w h =
  let b = Buffer.create 1000000 in
  Buffer.add_string b (Printf.sprintf "P6\n%d %d\n255\n" w h);
  for i = 0 to (w * h) - 1 do
    Buffer.add_substring b TinyMachineDevices.colours
      (3 * peekb (0xf00000 + i)) 3
  done;
  Buffer.contents b

tiny/TinyKernel/libc/draw.c

// Claude Code, Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau, LGPL (see TinyC.ml)
//
// draw.h's functions: each a message of TinyKernelGraphics.ml's (a letter,
// then numbers of 16 bits, the low byte first) put in a buffer, which
// d_flush writes whole, as the kernel wants its messages.
#include "user.h"
#include "draw.h"

char d_buf[2048];
int d_n;

// (in pieces when the descriptor is a window's pipe, which takes what
// it has room for)
int
d_flush(void)
{
	int n, k, done;

	n = d_n;
	d_n = 0;
	for(done = 0; done < n; done += k)
		if((k = write(DRAW, d_buf + done, n - done)) <= 0)
			return -1;
	return 0;
}

// room for a message of n bytes, its letter put
void
d_start(int letter, int n)
{
	if(d_n + n > sizeof d_buf)
		d_flush();
	d_buf[d_n++] = letter;
}

void
d_put(int v)
{
	d_buf[d_n++] = v;
	d_buf[d_n++] = v >> 8;
}

void
d_colour(int id, int colour)
{
	d_start('a', 15);
	d_put(id); d_put(0); d_put(0); d_put(1); d_put(1); d_put(1); d_put(colour);
}

void
d_draw(int dst, int src, int mask, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, int px, int py)
{
	d_start('d', 19);
	d_put(dst); d_put(src); d_put(mask);
	d_put(x0); d_put(y0); d_put(x1); d_put(y1); d_put(px); d_put(py);
}

void
d_fill(int dst, int src, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1)
{
	d_draw(dst, src, NOMASK, x0, y0, x1, y1, 0, 0);
}

void
d_line(int dst, int src, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1)
{
	d_start('l', 13);
	d_put(dst); d_put(src); d_put(x0); d_put(y0); d_put(x1); d_put(y1);
}

void
d_text(int dst, int src, int x, int y, char *s)
{
	int n;

	n = strlen(s);
	d_start('s', 11 + n);
	d_put(dst); d_put(src); d_put(x); d_put(y); d_put(n);
	while(*s)
		d_buf[d_n++] = *s++;
}

void
d_pixels(int dst, int x, int y, char *bytes, int n)
{
	int i;

	d_start('p', 9 + n);
	d_put(dst); d_put(x); d_put(y); d_put(n);
	for(i = 0; i < n; i++)
		d_buf[d_n++] = bytes[i];
}

tiny/TinyKernel/libc/net.c

// Claude Code, Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau, LGPL (see TinyC.ml)
//
// reach(host, port): dial, by an address ("10.0.0.1") or by a name
// ("example.com"). A name's address is asked of the wire's other end,
// on its port 53: the name written, the address read, as text. That is
// all there is of DNS here: who has names is the other end
// (tiny-machine -net-out asks its host; the page has none).
#include "user.h"

int
reach(char *host, int port)
{
	char address[64], *p;
	int fd, n;

	for(p = host; *p == '.' || (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9'); p++)
		;
	if(*p == 0)
		return dial(host, port);
	fd = dial("10.0.0.1", 53);
	if(fd < 0)
		return -1;
	write(fd, host, strlen(host));
	n = read(fd, address, 63);
	close(fd);
	if(n <= 0)
		return -1;
	address[n] = 0;
	return dial(address, port);
}

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* The kernel's calls for a program in ML: mlsys.c's functions, as
 * externals, their values ML's; -1 when the kernel refuses. On the
 * host these names are ../host/TinyCalls.ml's. An external a program
 * does not call costs it nothing. (TinyWindows.ml says its own: OCaml
 * checks that file alone.) *)
external u_write : int -> string -> int = "u_write"

(* TinyLibSystem on tiny-machine: what a tool asks of the system
 * (tiny-shell; ../host/TinyLibSystem.mli says each function), over
 * tiny-kernel's calls (mlsys.c's, beside this file; TinyCalls.ml names
 * them).
 *
 * Not in tiny/ with the other TinyLibXxx.ml: the host's file has the
 * same name, as it must (TinyShell.ml names one module), and mini-ml
 * looks for a module beside the file it compiles before anywhere else.
 *
 * A module, as the host's: the tool writes TinyLibSystem.fork for
 * both (old: a name with a dot, one name, when tiny-ml had no
 * modules). The capabilities are read and forgotten: a function's caps is a
 * value like another, that nothing looks at. Not OCaml's to compile.
 *
 * What tiny-kernel has not, and what is done about it here:
 * - an environment: a PATH only, the root, where the programs are
 * - a dup2: the descriptor closed, then copies made until the kernel
 *   gives its number (it gives the lowest free one)
 * - descriptors closed when a program is run: the ones made here
 *   (save, pipe) are remembered, and closed before the exec. Not all
 *   above 2: a window's program has its drawing at 3 and its mouse at 4
 * - a wait for one child: the kernel says the next that ended, so the
 *   others' ends are kept until asked for
 * - more than 63 arguments for a program, its name one of them: said
 *   (old: 15; a linker's line names 30 objects)
 * - a signal, a terminal to ask about, a reason for a call that
 *   failed: nothing, yes, "cannot" (old: a file written at its end,
 *   >>, refused, before the kernel's seek)
 * - a stat: a file's kind and size are read from its entry in the
 *   directory it is in, found by its path cleaned as the kernel cleans
 *   it (the current directory first, "." and ".." taken away)
 * - a rename: a copy and a remove, as 9P's mv does, and so not for a
 *   directory
 * - a file's time: touch makes a file that is not there, and does
 *   nothing to one that is
 * - a file's modes: no file is a program to run (x)
 *)

type Cap.all_caps = < >

let main name f =
  exit
    (try f () with
     | Failure m ->
         u_flush ();
         ignore (u_write 2 (name ^ ": " ^ m ^ "\n"));
         1)
let argv caps = List.init (u_argc ()) u_arg
let environment caps = [ "PATH", "/bin" ]
let getpid _caps = u_getpid ()

(* The terminal *)

let print caps s = print_string s
let eprint caps s = ignore (u_write 2 s)
let flush _caps = u_flush ()

(* what was read of the input and is not yet a line given *)
let pending = ref ""

let rec read_line caps =
  match String.index_opt !pending '\n' with
  | Some i ->
      let line = String.sub !pending 0 i in
      pending := String.sub !pending (i + 1) (String.length !pending - i - 1);
      Some line
  | None ->
      let s = u_read 0 4096 in
      if s <> "" then (pending := !pending ^ s; read_line caps)
      else if !pending = "" then None
      else (let line = !pending in pending := ""; Some line)

let isatty n = true
let ignore_interrupt _caps = ()
