let status = 0 and epc = 1 and cause = 2 and tval = 3 and tvec = 4
and time = 5 and timecmp = 6 and base = 7 and bound = 8
(* v6's (plan_tiny_os.md): the core's number, the interrupts pending
 * and enabled (a bit per source), the pages' root, and a word for the
 * kernel (the trap frame's address while in user mode, 0 in the
 * kernel: RISC-V's sscratch) *)
and core_csr = 9 and ip = 10 and ie_csr = 11
and satp = 12   (* scratch, 13, only read and written *)
(* The machine's speed in instructions per second, so that a kernel can
 * turn its time, which counts instructions, into seconds. *)
and rate_csr = 14
(* the number of cores (-cores n), which a kernel reads at its boot *)
and cores_csr = 15
(* the text's window, with split (below) *)
and tbase_csr = 16 and tbound_csr = 17
let csr_names = TinyMachineISA.csr_names
let read_only k =
  k = time || k = core_csr || k = ip || k = rate_csr || k = cores_csr

(* status: the mode, the interrupts' bit, and the two as they were
 * before the trap *)
let supervisor_bit = 1 and ie = 2 and ps = 4 and pie = 8
(* t6's (plan_tiny_os.md): the window relocates, as the 360's and the
 * PDP-10's did: a user address a is base + a, below bound, a size.
 * Kept through traps and eret, as it is the kernel's choice *)
let relocate = 16
(* Segments (plan_tiny_memory.md), with relocate: the window split in
 * two, as the PDP-11/45's text and data. A user address below tbound
 * is the text's, tbase + a, fetched or loaded, a store a fault; one at
 * or above it the data's, base + (a - tbound), below bound. So a
 * program's text, linked at 0, can be one copy for all its runs *)
let split = 32

(* an interrupt's cause is 4, its sources in tval: the bits of ip and
 * ie, the timer's the first (v0's only one) *)
let c_sys = 1 and c_illegal = 2 and c_fault = 3 and c_intr = 4
let i_timer = 1 and i_console = 2 and i_disk = 4 and i_mouse = 8
and i_net = 16 and i_ipi = 32

(* the devices, at the top of memory, reached from anywhere by a
 * negative offset from r0: the console's output -16(r0), the halt
 * -12(r0); v6's in the 32 bytes below the top, the network's in the
 * 16 below those, the speaker's word below them, the date's, the
 * seed's, the cores' interrupt's *)
(* old: 1 lsl 27, 128 MB, before the cores: four compilers of tiny-ml
 * at once, 32 MB each, did not fit *)
let memsize = 1 lsl 28
(* old: devices = memsize - 32, before the network's four words *)
(* old: devices = memsize - 48, before the speaker's word *)
let console = memsize - 16 and halt = memsize - 12 and devices = memsize - 64
let console_in = memsize - 8
let disk_block = memsize - 32 and disk_addr = memsize - 28
and disk_cmd = memsize - 24 and disk_status = memsize - 20
let mouse_dev = memsize - 4
let net_addr = memsize - 48 and net_len = memsize - 44
and net_cmd = memsize - 40 and net_status = memsize - 36
let speaker_dev = memsize - 52
(* the date at the boot, read at -56(r0): seconds since 2000-01-01 UTC
 * (an ML integer of 31 bits holds them until 2034, where 1970's would
 * not fit), the host's clock or -date's, so a run is the same each time
 * when asked; the kernel counts on from it by its ticks. The web page
 * leaves it at 0. (old: none: tiny-kernel had no clock of the day) *)
let date_dev = memsize - 56
let date = ref 0
(* a seed, read at -60(r0), for the programs' first random numbers
 * (tetris's pieces): tiny-machine's -seed, so that a run is the same
 * however long the boot took; 0, the default, says none, and the
 * kernel gives its clock instead. (old: none, a game seeded by the
 * clock alone: make check's tetris another game at each change of the
 * kernel's code) *)
let seed_dev = memsize - 60
let seed = ref 0
(* The cores (plan_tiny_multicore.md): [cores] of them, set by a host
 * before [create] (tiny-machine's -cores), 1 by default, today's
 * machine. Each its registers, its pc and its registers of control
 * (the register core its number), the memory and the devices shared;
 * core 0 starts at 0 as before, and so do the others: a kernel parks
 * them by their number, as RISC-V's cores all start at the reset's
 * address. The devices are wired to core 0: another core reaching one
 * faults, but for -64(r0), the interrupt between cores. Stored, the
 * value k raises core k's (i_ipi), saying who sent it; read, the
 * senders since the last read, a bit each (1 lsl the sender's number),
 * cleared. So a core knows whose mailbox to look at, and what it reads
 * there was written before the interrupt (an Atomic's, which orders the
 * memory between domains). *)
let cores = ref 1
let ipi_dev = memsize - 64
(* the screen, below the devices: a megabyte no kernel's image reaches
 * (old: 640 by 480, Plan 9's 1024 by 768 since its text at three
 * times in the host's window was coarse beside mini-9pi's at two) *)
let screen = 0xf00000 and width = 1024 and height = 768

exception Trap of int * int                (* cause, tval *)

exception Halt of int

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The devices (v6's): the console's input, a disk *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The console's input: -8(r0) gives the next byte, 0xffffffff when none
 * has come, 0xfffffffe at the input's end; its interrupt while bytes
 * wait. Nothing is read before a kernel asks (enables the interrupt or
 * reads the register): v0 never does. The input's end interrupts
 * too, once, until it is read. Then a file or a pipe is read
 * whole, so that a run is the same every time; a terminal is polled,
 * as a person types when they type, and its ^C (SIGINT) is a byte 3
 * for the kernel, not the machine's end (^\ quits tiny-machine, as
 * Ctrl-A x mini-qemu). *)
type console = {
  mutable queue : string; mutable next : int; mutable eof : bool;
  mutable opened : bool; mutable eof_read : bool;
}

(* bytes typed: after those not yet read *)
let console_type k s =
  k.queue <- String.sub k.queue k.next (String.length k.queue - k.next) ^ s;
  k.next <- 0

let console_read k =
  if k.next < String.length k.queue then
    (k.next <- k.next + 1; Char.code k.queue.[k.next - 1])
  else if k.eof then (k.eof_read <- true; 0xfffffffe) else 0xffffffff

let console_waiting k =
  k.next < String.length k.queue || (k.eof && not k.eof_read)

(* The disk: an image file (-d), in blocks of 1 KB. The kernel writes a
 * block's number at -32(r0), a physical address at -28(r0), then the
 * command at -24(r0), 1 to read the block into memory, 2 to write it
 * from memory; the transfer is done at once, and the disk's interrupt
 * waits until the kernel writes -20(r0) (which reads 1 while it does).
 * -32(r0) read is the disk's size, in blocks (0: no disk). [wrote] is
 * told of each block written (tiny-machine writes it to the file then:
 * a machine that ends without its halt leaves the disk as the kernel
 * last wrote it, as a crash does). *)
let bsize = 1024

type disk = {
  image : Bytes.t; mutable block : int; mutable addr : int;
  mutable done_ : bool; mutable wrote : int -> unit;
}

let disk_command d (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) cmd =
  let off = d.block * bsize in
  if d.block < 0 || d.block >= Bytes.length d.image / bsize
     || d.addr < 0 || d.addr > memsize - bsize
  then
    TinyMachineCPU.error
      "disk: block %d, address 0x%x: out of the image or the memory"
      d.block d.addr;
  (match cmd with
   | 1 -> Bytes.blit d.image off m.mem d.addr bsize
   | 2 -> Bytes.blit m.mem d.addr d.image off bsize; d.wrote d.block
   | _ -> TinyMachineCPU.error "disk: command %d" cmd);
  d.done_ <- true

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The network (plan_tiny_network.md) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A wire with two ends, this machine at one: a packet is some bytes,
 * [packet_max] at most, sent whole and received whole. The kernel
 * writes a physical address at -48(r0) and a length at -44(r0), then
 * the command at -40(r0): 1 sends the bytes there (the host's [send]
 * has them at once), 2 takes the packet that waits to there (its
 * length, read at -44(r0) before, 0 when none waits; no more than the
 * length written is copied). The network's interrupt waits while a
 * packet does. -36(r0) reads 1 when there is a wire, 0 without one:
 * a send is then lost and nothing ever comes.
 *
 * What is at the other end is the host's. It gives a packet by
 * [net_give], to arrive so many instructions from now: [flying] has
 * those on their way, by their time, and [tick] lands them. So the
 * time of the network is the machine's too, and a run with it is the
 * same every time. No more than [queue_max] wait: the next is lost,
 * as a real card's when its kernel is slow.
 *
 * An empty packet is no packet (one sent is not, one given does not
 * reach the kernel): given, it comes back to [send] at its time. That
 * is the other end's clock, in the machine's time as the rest. *)
let packet_max = 2048 and queue_max = 64

type net = {
  wired : bool; mutable naddr : int; mutable nlen : int;
  mutable waiting : string list;                 (* landed, the first first *)
  (* each with its time, the nearest first *)
  mutable flying : (int * string) list;
}

let net_command n (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) send cmd =
  let room len =
    if n.naddr < 0 || len < 0 || len > packet_max
       || n.naddr > memsize - len
    then
      TinyMachineCPU.error
        "network: %d bytes at 0x%x: too long or out of the memory"
        len n.naddr in
  match cmd with
  | 1 ->
      room n.nlen;
      if n.wired && n.nlen > 0 then
        send (Bytes.sub_string m.mem n.naddr n.nlen)
  | 2 ->
      (match n.waiting with
       | p :: rest ->
           let len = min n.nlen (String.length p) in
           room len;
           Bytes.blit_string p 0 m.mem n.naddr len;
           n.waiting <- rest
       | [] -> ())
  | _ -> TinyMachineCPU.error "network: command %d" cmd

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen, the mouse, a session's events (plan_tiny_windows.md) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A pixel's byte is a colour of Plan 9's table (its m8 pixels, rgbv:
 * libmemdraw's cmap.c, whose 256 entries this gives): two bits of red,
 * two of how bright, four of green and blue, turned by the first two
 * so that a row of 16 is a ramp; 0 is black, 255 white. *)
let colour i =
  let r = i lsr 6 and v = (i lsr 4) land 3 in
  let j = (i - v + r) land 15 in
  let g = j lsr 2 and b = j land 3 in
  let den = max r (max g b) in
  if den = 0 then (17 * v, 17 * v, 17 * v)
  else
    let num = 17 * ((4 * den) + v) in
    (r * num / den, g * num / den, b * num / den)

let colours =
  String.init 768 (fun k ->
    let r, g, b = colour (k / 3) in
    Char.chr (match k mod 3 with 0 -> r | 1 -> g | _ -> b))

(* The colour nearest to (r, g, b), by the squares of their differences,
 * for the colour of 15 bits it falls in (5 of red, of green, of blue),
 * found once each: a picture's pixels, by tiny-machine-fetch and the
 * page (old: each its own, the page's by the first pixel that fell in
 * the 15 bits) *)
let nearest =
  let known = Array.make 32768 (-1) in
  fun r g b ->
    let key = ((r lsr 3) lsl 10) lor ((g lsr 3) lsl 5) lor (b lsr 3) in
    if known.(key) < 0 then begin
      let v shift = ((key lsr shift) land 31) * 255 / 31 in
      let d k =
        let c i = Char.code colours.[(3 * k) + i] - v (10 - (5 * i)) in
        (c 0 * c 0) + (c 1 * c 1) + (c 2 * c 2) in
      let rec go k bk bd =
        if k = 256 then bk
        else
          let dk = d k in
          if dk < bd then go (k + 1) k dk else go (k + 1) bk bd in
      known.(key) <- go 1 0 (d 0)
    end;
    known.(key)

(* the mouse: its word, and whether it changed since it was read *)
type mouse = { mutable at : int; mutable moved : bool; mutable cursor : int }

(* The machine's speed, in instructions per second. A host sets it before
 * [create]; the machine gives it to the kernel in its rate register.
 * When a person watches (a window, the web page), the host holds the
 * machine to this speed (TinyMachine.ml's window says why). Without a
 * window nothing waits, and the rate only says how long a second is in
 * instructions. The default, 8 million, is the speed the web page can
 * keep up with, and the one the recorded sessions were made at. *)
let default_rate = 8_000_000
let rate = ref default_rate

let mouse_set ms x y buttons =
  let at =
    max 0 (min (width - 1) x)
    lor (max 0 (min (height - 1) y) lsl 12)
    lor (buttons lsl 24) in
  if at <> ms.at then (ms.at <- at; ms.moved <- true)

(* An event of a session, a line: "m x y buttons" the mouse, "k text"
 * keys typed (in the text \n is a new line, \ and three digits a
 * byte: \003). In a file (-events) a time comes first, the events in
 * the order of their times; a window's program (-window) writes them
 * without one, as they happen. *)
let event (ms : mouse) k line =
  let bad () = TinyMachineCPU.error "not an event: %s" line in
  let number w =
    match int_of_string_opt w with Some n -> n | None -> bad () in
  match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
  | [ "m"; x; y; buttons ] ->
      mouse_set ms (number x) (number y) (number buttons)
  | "k" :: _ ->
      let b = Buffer.create 16 and n = String.length line in
      let rec go i =
        if i < n then
          if line.[i] <> '\\' || i + 1 >= n then
            (Buffer.add_char b line.[i]; go (i + 1))
          else if line.[i + 1] = 'n' then (Buffer.add_char b '\n'; go (i + 2))
          else if i + 3 < n then (
            Buffer.add_char b
              (Char.chr (number (String.sub line (i + 1) 3) land 255));
            go (i + 4))
          else bad () in
      go 2;
      console_type k (Buffer.contents b)
  | _ -> bad ()

(* a file's: each event's time, and the event *)
let timed_events text =
  List.filter_map (fun l ->
    match String.index_opt l ' ' with
    | _ when l = "" -> None
    | Some i ->
        (match int_of_string_opt (String.sub l 0 i) with
         | Some t -> Some (t, String.sub l (i + 1) (String.length l - i - 1))
         | None -> TinyMachineCPU.error "not an event: %s" l)
    | None -> TinyMachineCPU.error "not an event: %s" l)
    (String.split_on_char '\n' text)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The speaker (plan_tiny_audio.md) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* The speaker is memory, as the screen is: a ring of [ring] bytes, a
 * sample each (signed, 0 silence), that it plays at [hz] samples a
 * second of the machine's time, one every rate / hz instructions. The
 * kernel says where the ring is by writing its address at -52(r0) (0:
 * off, the start), and reads there the samples played since, modulo
 * 2^30: where the speaker is in the ring, which the kernel writes ahead
 * of. A sample played is made 0 again, so a ring nobody writes is
 * silence and not the last second again and again (notes_audio.md's D:
 * the kernel needs no clock to clean behind the speaker).
 *
 * Nothing happens at each sample: the samples due are played when
 * somebody looks, the kernel by reading the word, the host by [hear]
 * (its window, a WAV), so the speaker costs no instruction of its own
 * and a run is the same every time. *)
let ring = 8192 and hz = 8000

type speaker = {
  mutable ring_at : int; mutable played : int; mutable since : int;
}

(* the samples due since the last look, given to [hear] and made 0 *)
let speaker_play (sp : speaker) (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) time hear =
  if sp.ring_at <> 0 then begin
    let period = max 1 (!rate / hz) in
    let d = TinyMachineCPU.m32 (time - sp.since) in
    let n = if d > 0x40000000 then 0 else d / period in
    if n > 0 then begin
      let b = Bytes.make n '\000' in
      for i = 0 to min n ring - 1 do
        let a = sp.ring_at + ((sp.played + i) land (ring - 1)) in
        Bytes.set b i (Bytes.get m.mem a);
        Bytes.set m.mem a '\000'
      done;
      hear (Bytes.unsafe_to_string b);
      sp.played <- (sp.played + n) land 0x3fffffff;
      sp.since <- TinyMachineCPU.m32 (sp.since + (n * period))
    end
  end

type machine = {
  cpu : TinyMachineCPU.machine; csr : int array; cons : console; disk : disk;
  mouse : mouse; net : net; speaker : speaker;
  mutable events : (int * string) list;
  (* the host's *)
  put : char -> unit; on_open : console -> unit; send : string -> unit;
  hear : string -> unit;
  (* a device or a register of control was touched: see [ticks] *)
  mutable touched : bool;
  (* asleep since a wfi, until an interrupt of ie's is pending *)
  mutable waiting : bool;
  (* the senders of each core's interrupt, a bit each *)
  ipis : int Atomic.t array;
  (* this core's instructions so far: in user mode, in the kernel, and
   * the kernel's idle (see [ticks]) *)
  spent : int array;
  (* the pages' translations last used in user mode, by page number:
   * the number (-1: none) and its entry (see [translate]) *)
  tlb_tag : int array; tlb_pte : int array;
}

(* whether this core is core 0, which the devices are wired to *)
let first mc = mc.csr.(core_csr) = 0

(* the sources wanting an interrupt; another core than 0 has only its
 * timer and the cores' *)
let pending mc =
  (if not (TinyMachineCPU.ult mc.csr.(time) mc.csr.(timecmp)) then i_timer else 0)
  lor (if Atomic.get mc.ipis.(mc.csr.(core_csr)) <> 0 then i_ipi else 0)
  lor (if not (first mc) then 0
       else
         (if console_waiting mc.cons then i_console else 0)
         lor (if mc.disk.done_ then i_disk else 0)
         lor (if mc.mouse.moved then i_mouse else 0)
         lor (if mc.net.waiting <> [] then i_net else 0))

let supervisor mc = mc.csr.(status) land supervisor_bit <> 0
let window_base mc = mc.csr.(base)

let trap mc cause_v tval_v epc_v =
  let c = mc.csr and st = mc.csr.(status) in
  c.(epc) <- epc_v; c.(cause) <- cause_v; c.(tval) <- tval_v;
  c.(status) <-
    supervisor_bit
    lor (if st land supervisor_bit <> 0 then ps else 0)
    lor (if st land ie <> 0 then pie else 0)
    lor (st land (relocate lor split));
  mc.cpu.pc <- TinyMachineCPU.addr c.(tvec)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The CPU's hooks: the window, the devices, the new instructions *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type access = Read | Write | Exec

(* (split tested inside relocate: a partition's access pays one test
 * more, not the split's arithmetic, which cost 7% of the host's
 * instructions in tiny-kernel's toolchain session) *)
let check mc access a =
  let a = TinyMachineCPU.addr a and c = mc.csr in
  if supervisor mc then a
  else if c.(status) land relocate <> 0 then (
    if c.(status) land split = 0 then (
      if not (TinyMachineCPU.ult a c.(bound)) then raise (Trap (c_fault, a));
      TinyMachineCPU.addr (c.(base) + a))
    else if TinyMachineCPU.ult a c.(tbound_csr) then (
      if access = Write then raise (Trap (c_fault, a));
      TinyMachineCPU.addr (c.(tbase_csr) + a))
    else (
      let d = a - c.(tbound_csr) in
      if not (TinyMachineCPU.ult d c.(bound)) then raise (Trap (c_fault, a));
      TinyMachineCPU.addr (c.(base) + d)))
  else if TinyMachineCPU.ult a mc.csr.(base)
          || not (TinyMachineCPU.ult a mc.csr.(bound))
  then raise (Trap (c_fault, a))
  else a

(* the translations' cache: 64 pages, a page in the slot of its
 * number's low bits; emptied when satp is written *)
let tlb_size = 64
let tlb_flush mc = Array.fill mc.tlb_tag 0 tlb_size (-1)
(* satp's bit 30 (tiny-kernel's pages, plan_tiny_memory.md): the pages
 * for user mode only, the supervisor's addresses physical, as the
 * PDP-11 had a set of mapping registers for its kernel and another for
 * its user; the bit clear, both translated (v6's way) *)
let user_only = 0x40000000

(* Pages (v6's): Sv32, RISC-V's 32-bit scheme (xv6's vm.c walks Sv39,
 * the 64-bit one: three levels of 9 bits for these two). With satp's
 * top bit set, an address is 10 bits of the root table's index, 10 of
 * a table's, 12 in the page; an entry is a page's number above 10 bits
 * of flags: V R W X U. A table's entry has none of R W X (no large
 * pages); a page's needs V and the access's R, W or X, and U in user
 * mode (the supervisor reaches every page: xv6's copyin walks the
 * tables anyway). Else a fault, the address in tval. Off (satp's top
 * bit clear), the window, as v0 has it. The pc stays below the
 * memory's size (the CPU keeps it modulo), so the virtual addresses a
 * program runs at do too. In user mode a page's entry is kept in the
 * cache, a walk of two loads saved at each access but the first: a
 * kernel that changes the tables writes satp before it runs the
 * process again (RISC-V's sfence.vma). *)
(* va's page's entry by the tables, from the root at satp (a fault
 * without one) *)
let tables (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) sat va =
  let entry at =
    if not (TinyMachineCPU.ult at memsize) then raise (Trap (c_fault, va));
    TinyMachineCPU.load m TinyMachineISA.W at in
  let e1 = entry (((sat land 0x3fffff) lsl 12) + (4 * (va lsr 22))) in
  if e1 land 1 = 0 || e1 land 14 <> 0 then raise (Trap (c_fault, va));
  entry (((e1 lsr 10) lsl 12) + (4 * ((va lsr 12) land 0x3ff)))

let walk mc m access va =
  let sat = mc.csr.(satp) in
  if sat land user_only <> 0 && supervisor mc then check mc access va
  else begin
    let va = TinyMachineCPU.m32 va in
    let vpn = va lsr 12 in
    let k = vpn land (tlb_size - 1) in
    let e0 =
      if supervisor mc then tables m sat va
      else if mc.tlb_tag.(k) = vpn then mc.tlb_pte.(k)
      else begin
        let e = tables m sat va in
        if e land 1 <> 0 then (mc.tlb_tag.(k) <- vpn; mc.tlb_pte.(k) <- e);
        e
      end in
    let needed = match access with Read -> 2 | Write -> 4 | Exec -> 8 in
    if e0 land 1 = 0 || e0 land needed = 0
       || (not (supervisor mc) && e0 land 16 = 0)
    then raise (Trap (c_fault, va));
    let pa = ((e0 lsr 10) lsl 12) lor (va land 0xfff) in
    if not (TinyMachineCPU.ult pa memsize) then raise (Trap (c_fault, va));
    pa
  end

(* (one test, and the pages' walk a function of its own, which looks at
 * user_only: in the host's instructions of tiny-kernel's toolchain
 * session, with partitions, translate with the walk and the cache in
 * it and user_only tested here 301.2 thousand million, this 292.9, the
 * walk in it without a cache, before the pages, 296.7) *)
let translate mc m access va =
  if mc.csr.(satp) land 0x80000000 = 0 then check mc access va
  else walk mc m access va

(* the cores' interrupt: core k's raised, from this one *)
let ipi_send mc k =
  if k >= 0 && k < Array.length mc.ipis then begin
    let bit = 1 lsl mc.csr.(core_csr) in
    let rec set () =
      let v = Atomic.get mc.ipis.(k) in
      if not (Atomic.compare_and_set mc.ipis.(k) v (v lor bit)) then set () in
    set ()
  end

(* a load and a store: the pages or the window, then memory or a device
 * (core 0's: another faults, but on the cores' word) *)
let load mc m s a =
  let a = translate mc m Read a in
  match TinyMachineCPU.word a with
  | w when w < devices -> TinyMachineCPU.load m s a
  | w when (mc.touched <- true; w = ipi_dev) ->
      Atomic.exchange mc.ipis.(mc.csr.(core_csr)) 0
  | _ when not (first mc) -> raise (Trap (c_fault, a))
  | w when w = console_in ->
      mc.on_open mc.cons; console_read mc.cons
  | w when w = disk_status -> if mc.disk.done_ then 1 else 0
  | w when w = disk_block -> Bytes.length mc.disk.image / bsize
  | w when w = mouse_dev -> mc.mouse.moved <- false; mc.mouse.at
  | w when w = net_len ->
      (match mc.net.waiting with p :: _ -> String.length p | [] -> 0)
  | w when w = net_status -> if mc.net.wired then 1 else 0
  | w when w = speaker_dev ->
      speaker_play mc.speaker m mc.csr.(time) mc.hear; mc.speaker.played
  | w when w = date_dev -> !date
  | w when w = seed_dev -> !seed
  | w when w >= devices -> 0
  | _ -> TinyMachineCPU.load m s a

let store mc m s a v =
  let a = translate mc m Write a in
  match TinyMachineCPU.word a with
  | w when w < devices -> TinyMachineCPU.store m s a v
  | w when (mc.touched <- true; w = ipi_dev) -> ipi_send mc v
  | _ when not (first mc) -> raise (Trap (c_fault, a))
  | w when w = console -> mc.put (Char.chr (v land 0xff))
  | w when w = halt -> raise (Halt (v land 0xff))
  | w when w = disk_block -> mc.disk.block <- v
  | w when w = disk_addr -> mc.disk.addr <- v
  | w when w = disk_cmd -> disk_command mc.disk m v
  | w when w = disk_status -> mc.disk.done_ <- false
  | w when w = net_addr -> mc.net.naddr <- v
  | w when w = net_len -> mc.net.nlen <- v
  | w when w = net_cmd -> net_command mc.net m mc.send v
  | w when w = speaker_dev ->
      let v = TinyMachineCPU.addr v in
      if v <> 0 && v > memsize - ring then
        TinyMachineCPU.error "speaker: a ring at 0x%x: out of the memory" v;
      mc.speaker.ring_at <- v;
      mc.speaker.played <- 0;
      mc.speaker.since <- mc.csr.(time)
  (* written, the mouse's word is its look: 0 the arrow, 1 a hand *)
  | w when w = mouse_dev -> mc.mouse.cursor <- v
  | w when w >= devices -> ()
  | _ -> TinyMachineCPU.store m s a v

(* Waiting for an interrupt: wfi (0x37, the supervisor's).
 *
 * The machine's time is the count of the instructions it ran, and a
 * window holds that count to the host's clock (20 million a second);
 * a host that cannot run so many falls behind, and the speaker's
 * samples come in gaps. A kernel with nothing to run used to wait in
 * a jump to itself (k_idle1: j k_idle1) until the timer's interrupt:
 * the host emulated thousands of jumps a tick that changed nothing but
 * the time (play's WAV and a sleep: 57 of its 192 million). A processor
 * spins the same way, burning power, so each has an instruction for
 * it: ARM's and RISC-V's wfi, x86's hlt (the 8086's already). The core
 * stops until an interrupt comes, and an emulator (QEMU) jumps its
 * clock to the next event. So here: wfi puts the core to sleep, and the
 * next ticks only count the time, at once in [ticks]'s calm stretch
 * (nothing can happen in it, by [calm]'s definition), until an
 * interrupt among ie's sources is pending; then the core goes on after
 * the wfi, taking the interrupt when status's ie is on (RISC-V's
 * rule: a source enabled in ie wakes it even when ie is off in
 * status). The machine after the sleep is the one a loop of jumps
 * leaves: the registers, the memory and the time the same.
 *
 * (old: a calm stretch that started on a jump to itself, in the
 * kernel, was not stepped either, the time added: the same speed, but
 * the machine guessed the kernel idle from a pattern of its code, a
 * guess another shape of idle loop would silently lose. wfi says it.
 * On play's WAV at -rate 20, 9.6 s of the machine: 11.0 s of the host
 * when every jump was stepped, 8.7 without.) *)

(* the words the CPU does not know: 0x3a-0x3c, csrr, csrw and eret,
 * the supervisor's, and 0x3e, csrrw d, csr, a (both at once: d the
 * register's old value, the register a's: at a trap, r1 swapped with
 * scratch frees a register); 0x3d, amoswap d, a, (b), anyone's: d the
 * word at the address in b, which becomes a, in one instruction (the atomic
 * swap a spinlock is made of, RISC-V's amoswap.w, ARM's swp). Atomic
 * between cores in turns, a turn never ending inside an instruction;
 * not with each core on a domain (tiny-machine's -cores-parallel),
 * where another core's store may come between its load and its store:
 * tiny-kernel's cores speak by mailboxes and the interrupt, not by a
 * lock *)
let extra mc (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) w =
  let op = (w lsr 24) land 0xff and d = (w lsr 20) land 15
  and a = (w lsr 16) land 15 and k = w land 0xffff in
  let c = mc.csr and next () = m.pc <- TinyMachineCPU.addr (m.pc + 4) in
  mc.touched <- true;
  if op = 0x37 then begin
    if not (supervisor mc) then raise (Trap (c_illegal, w));
    mc.waiting <- true;
    next ()
  end
  else if op = 0x3d then begin
    let at = m.r.(k land 15) in
    let old = load mc m TinyMachineISA.W at in
    store mc m TinyMachineISA.W at m.r.(a);
    if d <> 0 then m.r.(d) <- old;
    next ()
  end
  else begin
    if not (supervisor mc) || op < 0x3a || op > 0x3e
       || (op <> 0x3c && k >= Array.length csr_names)
    then raise (Trap (c_illegal, w));
    let read k = if k = ip then pending mc else c.(k) in
    match op with
    | 0x3a -> if d <> 0 then m.r.(d) <- read k; next ()
    | 0x3e ->
        let old = read k and v = m.r.(a) in
        if not (read_only k) then c.(k) <- v;
        if k = satp then tlb_flush mc;
        if d <> 0 then m.r.(d) <- old;
        next ()
    | 0x3b ->
        if not (read_only k) then c.(k) <- m.r.(a);
        if k = satp then tlb_flush mc;
        if k = ie_csr && c.(k) land i_console <> 0 then mc.on_open mc.cons;
        next ()
    | _ ->
        let st = c.(status) in
        c.(status) <-
          (if st land ps <> 0 then supervisor_bit else 0)
          lor (if st land pie <> 0 then ie else 0)
          lor (st land (relocate lor split));
        m.pc <- TinyMachineCPU.addr c.(epc)
  end

let env mc : TinyMachineCPU.env = {
  fetch =
    (fun m pc -> TinyMachineCPU.load m TinyMachineISA.W (translate mc m Exec pc));
  load = load mc;
  store = store mc;
  sys = (fun _ n -> raise (Trap (c_sys, n)));
  illegal = extra mc;
}

(* the listing's new instructions (tiny-assembler makes them) *)
let show w =
  let op = (w lsr 24) land 0xff and d = (w lsr 20) land 15
  and a = (w lsr 16) land 15 and k = w land 0xffff in
  match op with
  | 0x3a when k < Array.length csr_names ->
      Some (Printf.sprintf "csrr\tr%d, %s" d csr_names.(k))
  | 0x3b when k < Array.length csr_names ->
      Some (Printf.sprintf "csrw\t%s, r%d" csr_names.(k) a)
  | 0x3c -> Some "eret"
  | 0x37 -> Some "wfi"
  | 0x3e when k < Array.length csr_names ->
      Some (Printf.sprintf "csrrw\tr%d, %s, r%d" d csr_names.(k) a)
  | 0x3d -> Some (Printf.sprintf "amoswap\tr%d, r%d, (r%d)" d a (k land 15))
  | _ -> None

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The machine at its start, and one instruction of its time *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [put] writes a byte of the console's output, [on_open] is called
 * when a kernel first asks for the console's input; [disk] is the
 * disk's image, [events] a session's (then its keys are the console's
 * only input, and its last event the input's end); [send], when there
 * is a wire, is given each packet the machine sends; [hear] the
 * speaker's samples *)
let create ~put ~on_open ~send ~hear ~disk ~events image =
  TinyMachineCPU.memsize := memsize;
  let m : TinyMachineCPU.machine = TinyMachineCPU.boot image in
  m.r.(TinyMachineISA.sp) <- devices;
  let c = Array.make (Array.length csr_names) 0 in
  c.(status) <- supervisor_bit;
  c.(timecmp) <- 0xffffffff;
  c.(ie_csr) <- i_timer;
  c.(rate_csr) <- !rate;
  c.(cores_csr) <- !cores;
  { cpu = m; csr = c;
    cons = { queue = ""; next = 0; eof = events = Some [];
             opened = events <> None; eof_read = false };
    disk = { image = disk; block = 0; addr = 0; done_ = false; wrote = ignore };
    mouse = { at = 0; moved = false; cursor = 0 };
    events = (match events with Some l -> l | None -> []); put; on_open;
    net = { wired = send <> None; naddr = 0; nlen = 0; waiting = [];
            flying = [] };
    speaker = { ring_at = 0; played = 0; since = 0 }; hear;
    send = (match send with Some f -> f | None -> ignore); touched = false;
    waiting = false;
    ipis = Array.init !cores (fun _ -> Atomic.make 0); spent = [| 0; 0; 0 |];
    tlb_tag = Array.make tlb_size (-1); tlb_pte = Array.make tlb_size 0 }

(* core k, k > 0: its registers, its pc at 0 and its registers of
 * control, as core 0's at the start; the memory, the devices and the
 * host's functions core 0's *)
let core mc k =
  let c = Array.copy mc.csr in
  c.(status) <- supervisor_bit;
  c.(timecmp) <- 0xffffffff;
  c.(ie_csr) <- i_timer;
  c.(core_csr) <- k;
  let r = Array.make 16 0 in
  r.(TinyMachineISA.sp) <- devices;
  { mc with cpu = { r; pc = 0; mem = mc.cpu.mem }; csr = c; events = [];
            touched = false; waiting = false; spent = [| 0; 0; 0 |];
            tlb_tag = Array.make tlb_size (-1); tlb_pte = Array.make tlb_size 0 }

(* the speaker's samples due, to [hear]: the host's, between two ticks *)
let speaker_hear mc = speaker_play mc.speaker mc.cpu mc.csr.(time) mc.hear

(* a time's distance from now, in instructions: 0 when it is now or
 * passed (the differences are of 32 bits, an int's or not; more than
 * 2^30 is a time passed, the count having gone round) *)
let from_now mc t =
  let d = TinyMachineCPU.m32 (t - mc.csr.(time)) in
  if d <= 0 || d > 0x40000000 then 0 else d

(* a packet for the machine, to land [after] instructions from now
 * (at the next when 0): the host's, between two ticks or in [send] *)
let net_give mc ~after packet =
  let t = TinyMachineCPU.m32 (mc.csr.(time) + max after 1) in
  let rec place = function
    | (t', p) :: rest when from_now mc t' <= max after 1 ->
        (t', p) :: place rest
    | later -> (t, packet) :: later in
  mc.net.flying <- place mc.net.flying;
  mc.touched <- true

(* the packets whose time has come: waiting, or lost when too many do;
 * an empty one is the host's clock *)
let rec landed mc =
  match mc.net.flying with
  | (t, p) :: rest when from_now mc t = 0 ->
      mc.net.flying <- rest;
      if p = "" then mc.send ""
      else if List.length mc.net.waiting < queue_max then
        mc.net.waiting <- mc.net.waiting @ [ p ];
      landed mc
  | _ -> ()

(* the time, a session's event that is due, a packet that lands, then
 * an interrupt or a step; Halt when the kernel halts the machine *)
let tick mc (env : TinyMachineCPU.env) =
  let m = mc.cpu and c = mc.csr in
  let pc = m.pc in
  c.(time) <- TinyMachineCPU.m32 (c.(time) + 1);
  (match mc.events with
   | (t, e) :: rest when not (TinyMachineCPU.ult c.(time) t) ->
       event mc.mouse mc.cons e;
       mc.events <- rest;
       if rest = [] then mc.cons.eof <- true
   | _ -> ());
  if mc.net.flying <> [] && first mc then landed mc;
  try
    let wanted = pending mc land c.(ie_csr) in
    if wanted <> 0 then mc.waiting <- false;
    if c.(status) land ie <> 0 && wanted <> 0 then trap mc c_intr wanted pc
    else if not mc.waiting then TinyMachineCPU.step env m
  with Trap (cause_v, tval_v) ->
    trap mc cause_v tval_v
      (if cause_v = c_sys then TinyMachineCPU.addr (pc + 4) else pc)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Faster: the instructions between two looks *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [ticks mc env n] is n ticks. A tick looks at everything before its
 * instruction: a session's event that is due, the five sources of an
 * interrupt, the interrupts' bit; nearly always to find nothing, and
 * it is most of an instruction's time. But what it looks at changes
 * at few moments, all known:
 *
 * - the time reaches a session's next event, or timecmp: both are so
 *   many instructions away, counted;
 * - an instruction reads or writes a device or a register of control
 *   (the console, the disk, the mouse; status, ie, timecmp...), or
 *   traps: [touched], set by load, store and extra, and a trap leaves
 *   the loop by its exception;
 * - a packet lands: at its time, counted too;
 * - the host types a key or moves the mouse: between two calls only.
 *
 * So after one tick that looked and found the machine calm, the steps
 * that follow, until the nearest of those moments, are steps and the
 * time's count, nothing else; and an interrupt is taken at the very
 * instruction the simple loop takes it at (tiny-kernel's recorded
 * sessions, whose screens depend on it, have the same sums). With
 * [batched] false, ticks is tick n times. (tests/TinyMachine_bench.sh,
 * tiny-kernel's paint.events: by js_of_ocaml under node, 6.8 million
 * instructions a second without it, 8.1 with it; natively 15.2 and
 * 22.0.) *)
let batched = ref true

(* how many instructions from now need no look: 0 if an interrupt would
 * be taken at the next *)
let calm mc =
  let c = mc.csr in
  if c.(status) land ie <> 0 && pending mc land c.(ie_csr) <> 0 then 0
  else begin
    (* to a time t from now, less one: the tick at t must look; a t
     * already passed or more than 2^30 away is far (the differences
     * are of 32 bits, an int's or not) *)
    let until t =
      let d = TinyMachineCPU.m32 (t - c.(time)) in
      if d <= 0 || d > 0x40000000 then 0x40000000 else d - 1 in
    (* (an event already due is the next tick's: a tick takes one) *)
    let event =
      match mc.events with
      | (t, _) :: _ -> if TinyMachineCPU.ult c.(time) t then until t else 0
      | [] -> 0x40000000 in
    (* a packet lands at its tick, which must look: one less, as [until] *)
    let packet =
      match mc.net.flying with
      | (t, _) :: _ when first mc -> max 0 (from_now mc t - 1)
      | _ -> 0x40000000 in
    min packet (min event (until c.(timecmp)))
  end

(* What the instructions from here are, for [spent]: a program's (user
 * mode), the kernel's, or idle, asleep after a wfi. The steps that
 * follow one look are all of one kind: a change of mode is a trap or
 * an eret, and a wfi or a wake ends the stretch ([touched], the next
 * tick). So one look a batch counts every instruction's time, and the
 * count costs nothing that shows. (old: idle was the kernel on a jump
 * to itself, its pc's word read at each look.) *)
let what mc =
  if not (supervisor mc) then 0 else if mc.waiting then 2 else 1

let ticks mc (env : TinyMachineCPU.env) n =
  if not !batched then
    for _i = 1 to n do
      let w = what mc in
      tick mc env; mc.spent.(w) <- mc.spent.(w) + 1
    done
  else begin
    let m = mc.cpu and c = mc.csr in
    let left = ref n in
    while !left > 0 do
      let w = what mc in
      tick mc env; decr left;
      mc.spent.(w) <- mc.spent.(w) + 1;
      mc.touched <- false;
      (* the stretch's kind is the one after the tick, which may have
       * trapped or run a wfi *)
      let w = what mc in
      let k = ref (min !left (calm mc)) in
      let k0 = !k in
      left := !left - !k;
      (* asleep (wfi) until the next look: only the time moves, so it
       * moves at once *)
      if mc.waiting && !k > 0 then begin
        c.(time) <- TinyMachineCPU.m32 (c.(time) + !k);
        k := 0
      end;
      let pc = ref m.pc in
      (try
         while !k > 0 && not mc.touched do
           pc := m.pc;
           c.(time) <- TinyMachineCPU.m32 (c.(time) + 1);
           decr k;
           TinyMachineCPU.step env m
         done
       with Trap (cause_v, tval_v) ->
         trap mc cause_v tval_v
           (if cause_v = c_sys then TinyMachineCPU.addr (!pc + 4) else !pc));
      mc.spent.(w) <- mc.spent.(w) + k0 - !k;
      (* the steps not run, a device touched: they are still to do *)
      left := !left + !k
    done
  end

(* tiny-machine's machine, without a host: TinyMachineCPU's CPU with the
 * registers of control, the traps, the pages, the devices' state, and
 * one instruction of its time ([tick]). TinyMachine.mli's header says
 * what the machine is. Two programs are around it, each with its
 * loop, its console and its window: TinyMachine.ml, a terminal's (and
 * a window of the host's, another program), and TinyMachineWeb.ml, a
 * page's (a canvas), by js_of_ocaml. What a host gives is two
 * functions, [put] and [on_open], and a third when it has a network,
 * [send]; the rest it does to the machine's state between two ticks
 * (console_type, mouse_set, net_give).
 *
 *     TinyMachine: a terminal, files,      TinyMachineWeb: a page, a
 *     a window by TinyMachineWindow        canvas, by js_of_ocaml
 *            \                               /
 *             put, on_open; console_type, mouse_set; tick
 *                            |
 *     this file: the registers of control and [trap]; the window and
 *     the pages ([check], [translate]); the devices behind [load] and
 *     [store]; csrr, csrw, eret, csrrw, amoswap, wfi ([extra]); the
 *     interrupts between two instructions
 *                            |
 *             an env of five functions ([env]); step
 *                            |
 *     TinyMachineCPU: sixteen registers, a pc, the memory's bytes, and
 *     an instruction's meaning
 *
 * The layers are the hardware's own: a CPU's core knows registers and
 * memory; what an address means (a page, a device) and what an
 * instruction of privilege does are decided around it; and what is a
 * console or a disk in the world is the host's. Each can be read
 * without the one above. mini-5i and mini-qemu, in m-ix, are cut the
 * same way (Cpu and Memory, then Board and its devices, then Main and
 * the SDL or the web display).
 *
 * design:
 * A device here is a few words of memory and an interrupt's bit,
 * with no bus, no FIFO and no timing: the disk's transfer is done by
 * the instruction that asks for it. So a driver is a few lines and
 * teaches the shape (a command, a status, an interrupt to say done)
 * without a datasheet. The real ones, with their datasheets, are
 * mini-qemu's (Pl011, Sdhost, Dwc2). *)

(* A picture as w by h bytes of the machine's colours: each pixel the
 * average of the source's pixels that fall in it, on white where they
 * are transparent. *)
let reduce (img : Rgba_image.t) w h =
  let out = Bytes.create (w * h) in
  for y = 0 to h - 1 do
    let y0 = y * img.height / h
    and y1 = max ((y + 1) * img.height / h) ((y * img.height / h) + 1) in
    for x = 0 to w - 1 do
      let x0 = x * img.width / w
      and x1 = max ((x + 1) * img.width / w) ((x * img.width / w) + 1) in
      let r = ref 0 and g = ref 0 and b = ref 0 and n = ref 0 in
      for sy = y0 to min y1 img.height - 1 do
        for sx = x0 to min x1 img.width - 1 do
          let o = 4 * ((sy * img.width) + sx) in
          let a = Char.code (Bytes.get img.rgba (o + 3)) in
          let over c =
            ((Char.code (Bytes.get img.rgba (o + c)) * a) + (255 * (255 - a)))
            / 255 in
          r := !r + over 0; g := !g + over 1; b := !b + over 2; incr n
        done
      done;
      let n = max !n 1 in
      Bytes.set out ((y * w) + x)
        (Char.chr (TinyMachineDevices.nearest (!r / n) (!g / n) (!b / n)))
    done
  done;
  Bytes.to_string out

let main (caps : < Cap.network; Cap.open_in; Cap.stdout; Cap.argv; .. >) =
  let get url =
    match Http_client.get caps url with
    | Ok (r : Http.response) -> Ok r.body
    | Error why -> Error why in
  match Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps) with
  | [ _; "-picture"; w; h; source ] -> (
      let w = int_of_string w and h = int_of_string h in
      let bytes =
        if Sys.file_exists source then Ok (FS.read caps (Fpath.v source))
        else get source in
      match bytes with
      | Ok bytes -> (
          match Image_file.decode bytes with
          | img -> Console.print caps (reduce img w h); 0
          | exception Failure why ->
              Console.print caps ("www: " ^ source ^ ": " ^ why ^ "\n"); 1)
      | Error why ->
          Console.print caps ("www: " ^ source ^ ": " ^ why ^ "\n"); 1)
  | [ _; url ] -> (
      match Http_client.get caps url with
      | Ok (r : Http.response) ->
          (* the body's own framing undone, so not said *)
          let framing = [ "content-length"; "content-encoding";
                          "transfer-encoding"; "connection" ] in
          let headers =
            List.filter
              (fun (n, _) -> not (List.mem (String.lowercase_ascii n) framing))
              r.headers in
          Console.print caps (TinyBrowserHttp.response r.status headers r.body);
          0
      | Error why -> Console.print caps ("www: " ^ url ^ ": " ^ why ^ "\n"); 1)
  | _ ->
      Console.print caps
        "www: usage: tiny-machine-fetch url | -picture w h url-or-file\n";
      2

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> CapStdlib.exit caps (main caps))

(* tiny-machine-fetch: a web page's answer, for the other end of
 * tiny-machine's wire when tiny-kernel's browser asks for one (its
 * request "GET address HTTP/1.0", TinyMachinePeer.www_request). It is a
 * program apart, as tiny-machine-socket is, so that tiny-machine itself links no network
 * library: this one links ix's own (lib_networking: DNS, TCP, TLS 1.3,
 * HTTP/1.1 with its redirections, chunks and gzip). tiny-machine runs it
 * when it has -net-out, and waits for it.
 *
 *     tiny-machine-fetch https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/OCaml
 *
 * prints the answer on standard output, whatever the status (a 404's
 * page is a page), as TinyBrowserHttp's response: HTTP/1.0's status
 * line, the site's headers but those of the body's framing (its
 * length, gzip, chunks: undone here), then the body; and exits 0; if there is no answer at all, it prints why
 * on standard output, as one line starting with "www: ", and exits 1.
 *
 *     tiny-machine-fetch -picture 250 188 https://.../250px-Award.jpg
 *
 * fetches a picture (or reads it, when the source is a file: a kept
 * copy), decodes it (PNG, JPEG, GIF: lib_graphics), and prints it as 250
 * times 188 bytes, a byte a pixel in the machine's 256 colours: each
 * pixel is the average of the source's pixels that fall in it, put on
 * white where they are transparent, then the nearest colour of the
 * palette. That is the line "img w h address" of tiny-kernel's browser.
 *
 * This is the part of the web that the tiny machine does not do itself:
 * the encrypted half (plan_tiny_browser.md, section 3). Everything from
 * the first < of the page on is the machine's.
 *
 * In m-ix the same work is mini-curl's (networking/'s Curl, on the
 * same lib_networking), which runs on mini-9pi itself, and the
 * pictures are decoded by the browser there; here both are the host's,
 * so tiny-kernel has no TLS and no decoder of PNG or JPEG. *)

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyMachineISA.mli *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The instructions *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type reg = int

type alu =
  | Add | Sub | Mul | Div | Rem | And | Or | Xor | Shl | Shr | Sar | Slt | Sltu
type cmp = Eq | Ne | Lt | Ge | Ltu | Geu
type size = W | B

type instr =
  | Alu of alu * reg * reg * reg          (* d, a, b *)
  | Alui of alu * reg * reg * int
      (* d, a, imm: add and or xor shl shr sar slt sltu *)
  | Lui of reg * int
  | Load of size * reg * reg * int        (* d, a, offset *)
  | Store of size * reg * reg * int       (* the value's register, a, offset *)
  | Branch of cmp * reg * reg * int       (* d, a, offset in words, from pc + 4 *)
  | Jal of reg * int
  | Jalr of reg * reg * int
  | Sys of int

(* (old: [| ... |], which tiny-ml does not read) *)
let alus =
  Array.of_list [ Add; Sub; Mul; Div; Rem; And; Or; Xor; Shl; Shr; Sar; Slt;
                  Sltu ]
let alu_names =
  Array.of_list [ "add"; "sub"; "mul"; "div"; "rem"; "and"; "or"; "xor";
                  "shl"; "shr"; "sar"; "slt"; "sltu" ]
let cmps = Array.of_list [ Eq; Ne; Lt; Ge; Ltu; Geu ]
let cmp_names = Array.of_list [ "beq"; "bne"; "blt"; "bge"; "bltu"; "bgeu" ]
let index a x = let rec go i = if a.(i) = x then i else go (i + 1) in go 0

(* an immediate form's name: the operation's and an i, but sltiu (MIPS's) *)
let imm_name op =
  match op with Sltu -> "sltiu" | _ -> alu_names.(index alus op) ^ "i"

(* the immediate forms: those whose immediate is zero-extended *)
let unsigned_imm op = match op with And | Or | Xor -> true | _ -> false
let has_imm op = match op with Mul | Div | Rem | Sub -> false | _ -> true

let sext16 v = ((v land 0xffff) lxor 0x8000) - 0x8000

let sp = 14 and lr = 15

(* the machine's registers of control, by number (TinyMachineDevices's) *)
let csr_names =
  Array.of_list [ "status"; "epc"; "cause"; "tval"; "tvec"; "time"; "timecmp";
                  "base"; "bound"; "core"; "ip"; "ie"; "satp"; "scratch";
                  "rate"; "cores"; "tbase"; "tbound" ]

exception Error of string
(* old: Printf.ksprintf's, a format and its values *)
let error s = raise (Error s)

(* a number in hexadecimal, 0x and its digits *)
let hex n = Printf.sprintf "0x%x" n

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The words *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* opcodes: 0x01-0x0d the ALU, 0x11-0x1d its immediate forms, then the
 * rest; 0 is no instruction, so that zeroed memory stops a program.
 * An instruction's word is under 2^30 (its opcode under 0x40), so it
 * is an int for tiny-ml too, whose ints have 31 bits *)
let encode i =
  let w op d a imm =
    (op lsl 24) lor (d lsl 20) lor (a lsl 16) lor (imm land 0xffff) in
  let fits16 v = v >= -0x8000 && v < 0x8000 in
  match i with
  | Alu (op, d, a, b) -> w (1 + index alus op) d a b
  | Alui (op, d, a, imm) ->
      if not (if unsigned_imm op then imm >= 0 && imm < 0x10000
              else fits16 imm) then
        error ("immediate " ^ string_of_int imm ^ " out of range");
      w (0x11 + index alus op) d a imm
  | Lui (d, imm) -> w 0x20 d 0 imm
  | Load (s, d, a, off) ->
      if not (fits16 off) then
        error ("offset " ^ string_of_int off ^ " out of range");
      w (if s = W then 0x21 else 0x22) d a off
  | Store (s, d, a, off) ->
      if not (fits16 off) then
        error ("offset " ^ string_of_int off ^ " out of range");
      w (if s = W then 0x23 else 0x24) d a off
  | Branch (c, d, a, off) ->
      if not (fits16 off) then error "branch too far";
      w (0x30 + index cmps c) d a off
  | Jal (d, off) -> if not (fits16 off) then error "jump too far"; w 0x38 d 0 off
  | Jalr (d, a, off) -> w 0x39 d a off
  | Sys n -> w 0x3f 0 0 n

let decode w =
  let op = (w lsr 24) land 0xff and d = (w lsr 20) land 15
  and a = (w lsr 16) land 15 and imm = w land 0xffff in
  match op with
  | _ when op >= 0x01 && op <= 0x0d ->
      Some (Alu (alus.(op - 1), d, a, imm land 15))
  | _ when op >= 0x11 && op <= 0x1d && has_imm alus.(op - 0x11) ->
      let alu = alus.(op - 0x11) in
      Some (Alui (alu, d, a, if unsigned_imm alu then imm else sext16 imm))
  | 0x20 -> Some (Lui (d, imm))
  | 0x21 -> Some (Load (W, d, a, sext16 imm))
  | 0x22 -> Some (Load (B, d, a, sext16 imm))
  | 0x23 -> Some (Store (W, d, a, sext16 imm))
  | 0x24 -> Some (Store (B, d, a, sext16 imm))
  | _ when op >= 0x30 && op <= 0x35 ->
      Some (Branch (cmps.(op - 0x30), d, a, sext16 imm))
  | 0x38 -> Some (Jal (d, sext16 imm))
  | 0x39 -> Some (Jalr (d, a, sext16 imm))
  | 0x3f -> Some (Sys imm)
  | _ -> None

(* an instruction as assembly again, [pc] its address (a branch's
 * target is shown as an address) *)
let print pc i =
  let r k = "r" ^ string_of_int k in
  let target off = hex (pc + 4 + (4 * off)) in
  let mem off a = string_of_int off ^ "(" ^ r a ^ ")" in
  match i with
  | Alu (op, d, a, b) ->
      alu_names.(index alus op) ^ "\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ r a ^ ", " ^ r b
  | Alui (op, d, a, imm) ->
      imm_name op ^ "\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ r a ^ ", " ^ string_of_int imm
  | Lui (d, imm) -> "lui\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ hex imm
  | Load (s, d, a, off) ->
      (if s = W then "ldw" else "ldb") ^ "\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ mem off a
  | Store (s, d, a, off) ->
      (if s = W then "stw" else "stb") ^ "\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ mem off a
  | Branch (c, d, a, off) ->
      cmp_names.(index cmps c) ^ "\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ r a ^ ", " ^ target off
  | Jal (d, off) -> "jal\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ target off
  | Jalr (d, a, off) -> "jalr\t" ^ r d ^ ", " ^ mem off a
  | Sys n -> "sys\t" ^ string_of_int n
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachineISA.mli

(* tiny-machine's instructions and their words: what tiny-assembler
 * makes, tiny-linker fills, and TinyMachineCPU runs (its header has
 * the machine, the format and the design). A file of its own so that
 * the assembler and the linker, which need the words and not the
 * interpreter, are compiled by tiny-ml and run on tiny-kernel; the
 * interpreter keeps OCaml's 32-bit loads, which the machine's speed is
 * made of.
 *
 * In m-ix a word's two directions are two programs' and two types:
 * mini-ld's Arm encodes its opcodes (5.out.h's), mini-5i's Arm32_isa
 * decodes a word into a variant of its own, checked against objdump.
 * Here one type serves both directions, in one file, so the listing's law
 * (TinyMachineCPU's: a listing reassembled gives the same words) is a
 * test of this file. *)

(* The instructions, and their words (an immediate is a word's low 16
 * bits, encode says what does not fit); the ALU's operations and the
 * branches' tests in their opcodes' order, with their names; an
 * immediate form's name *)
type reg = int
type alu =
  | Add | Sub | Mul | Div | Rem | And | Or | Xor | Shl | Shr | Sar | Slt | Sltu
type cmp = Eq | Ne | Lt | Ge | Ltu | Geu
type size = W | B
type instr =
  | Alu of alu * reg * reg * reg          (* d, a, b *)
  | Alui of alu * reg * reg * int
      (* d, a, imm: add and or xor shl shr sar slt sltu *)
  | Lui of reg * int
  | Load of size * reg * reg * int        (* d, a, offset *)
  | Store of size * reg * reg * int       (* the value's register, a, offset *)
  | Branch of cmp * reg * reg * int       (* d, a, offset in words, from pc + 4 *)
  | Jal of reg * int
  | Jalr of reg * reg * int
  | Sys of int
val alus : alu array
val alu_names : string array
val cmps : cmp array
val cmp_names : string array
val index : 'a array -> 'a -> int
val imm_name : alu -> string
val unsigned_imm : alu -> bool
val has_imm : alu -> bool
val sext16 : int -> int
val encode : instr -> int
val decode : int -> instr option

(* an instruction as assembly, given its address *)
val print : int -> instr -> string

(* the stack pointer's register and the link's; the machine's
 * registers of control, by number (csrr's, csrw's) *)
val sp : int
val lr : int
val csr_names : string array

(* what is wrong in a program's text, said to the person *)
exception Error of string
val error : string -> 'a

(* a number in hexadecimal: 0x1f *)
val hex : int -> string

14467
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyMachinePeer.mli *)

(* an address said: "10.0.0.2" *)
let net_dotted a =
  string_of_int (Char.code a.[0]) ^ "." ^ string_of_int (Char.code a.[1])
  ^ "." ^ string_of_int (Char.code a.[2]) ^ "."
  ^ string_of_int (Char.code a.[3])

(*****************************************************************************)
(* A packet said (the host's: who watches the wire) *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a packet in a few words, for who watches the wire: "echo? 1, 4
 * bytes, from 10.0.0.2 to 10.0.0.1", "data id 1001 ack 5000, 9 bytes,
 * from ..." *)
let net_describe p =
  if String.length p < 20 || Char.code p.[0] <> 0x45
     || TinyKernelNetwork.net_sum (String.sub p 0 20) <> 0 then
    "not a packet, " ^ string_of_int (String.length p) ^ " bytes"
  else begin
    let body = String.sub p 20 (String.length p - 20) in
    let bytes data = string_of_int (String.length data) ^ " bytes" in
    let what =
      if Char.code p.[9] = TinyKernelNetwork.ip_il then (
        match TinyKernelNetwork.il_read body with
        | None -> "il, damaged"
        | Some (kind, _, _, id, ack, data) ->
            (if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_sync then "sync"
             else if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_data then "data"
             else if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_dataquery then "data?"
             else if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_ack then "ack"
             else if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_query then "query"
             else if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_state then "state"
             else "close")
            ^ " id " ^ string_of_int id ^ " ack " ^ string_of_int ack
            ^ (if data = "" then "" else ", " ^ bytes data))
      else if Char.code p.[9] <> TinyKernelNetwork.ip_icmp then
        "protocol " ^ string_of_int (Char.code p.[9]) ^ ", " ^ bytes body
      else (
        match TinyKernelNetwork.icmp_read body with
        | None -> "icmp, damaged"
        | Some (kind, _, seq, data) ->
            (if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.icmp_ask then "echo? "
             else if kind = TinyKernelNetwork.icmp_answer then "echo! "
             else "icmp " ^ string_of_int kind ^ " ")
            ^ string_of_int seq ^ ", " ^ bytes data) in
    what ^ ", from " ^ net_dotted (String.sub p 12 4)
    ^ " to " ^ net_dotted (String.sub p 16 4)
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The peer *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* Both are in the machine's instructions, so they follow its speed:
 * 5 ms and 2.5 ms of its time. *)
let latency () = !TinyMachineDevices.rate / 200

let tick () = !TinyMachineDevices.rate / 400

(* a connection to one of the peer's own ports: its line not read yet,
 * what answers it asked, or the messages left to send; after a line
 * "put name size", the file's name, its size, and its bytes so far *)
type serving = {
  conn : TinyKernelNetwork.il;
  ask : string -> (string list -> unit) -> unit;
  mutable todo : string list option;
  mutable asked : bool;
  mutable taking : (string * int * Buffer.t) option;
}

type relay = {
  take : unit -> string option;
  put : string -> unit;
  shut : unit -> unit;
}

(* a connection that is a program's outside: the bytes that came from
 * it and are not yet messages, whether it has ended *)
type relaying = {
  rconn : TinyKernelNetwork.il;
  relay : relay;
  mutable coming : string;
  mutable ended : bool;
}

type outside = {
  name : string -> string;
  connect : string -> int -> relay option;
}

type t = {
  stack : TinyKernelNetwork.net_stack;
  give : int -> string -> unit;
  said : string -> string -> unit;
  document : string -> (string list -> unit) -> unit;
  store : string -> string -> string;
  outside : outside option;
  mutable now : int;
  mutable awake : bool;
  mutable serving : serving list;
  mutable sent : int;
  mutable lost : int list;
  mutable relays : relaying list;
  mutable agreed : ((string * int * int) * relay) list;
}

let create ~give ~said ~document ~store ~outside =
  let stack =
    TinyKernelNetwork.net_stack TinyKernelNetwork.net_peer 5000 in
  stack.ns_ports <- [ 70; 53 ];
  stack.ns_gate <- outside <> None;
  { stack = stack; give = give; said = said; document = document;
    store = store; outside = outside; now = 0; awake = false;
    serving = []; sent = 0;
    lost = []; relays = []; agreed = [] }

let lose p n = p.lost <- (p.sent + n) :: p.lost

let rec messages text =
  let n = String.length text in
  if n = 0 then [] else if n <= TinyKernelNetwork.il_max then [ text ]
  else
    String.sub text 0 TinyKernelNetwork.il_max
    :: messages
         (String.sub text TinyKernelNetwork.il_max
            (n - TinyKernelNetwork.il_max))

(* a picture with its text: a first message "t w h" (how many messages
 * of text follow, then h rows of w pixels, a row a message) *)
let picture text w h pixels =
  let texts = messages text in
  (string_of_int (List.length texts) ^ " " ^ string_of_int w
   ^ " " ^ string_of_int h) :: texts
  @ List.init h (fun y -> String.sub pixels (y * w) w)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* www *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let wiki_prefix = "/wiki/" and rest_prefix = "/api/rest_v1/page/html/"

(* a Wikipedia address cut in two: its host (en.wikipedia.org) and the
 * article's title, if it is one *)
let wikipedia url =
  match String.index_opt url ':' with
  | Some i
    when String.starts_with "https://" url
         || String.starts_with "http://" url ->
      let rest = String.sub url (i + 3) (String.length url - i - 3) in
      (match String.index_opt rest '/' with
       | Some j ->
           let host = String.sub rest 0 j
           and path = String.sub rest j (String.length rest - j) in
           let title p =
             String.sub path (String.length p)
               (String.length path - String.length p) in
           if not (Filename.check_suffix host ".wikipedia.org") then None
           else if String.starts_with wiki_prefix path then
             Some (host, title wiki_prefix)
           else if String.starts_with rest_prefix path then
             Some (host, title rest_prefix)
           else None
       | None -> None)
  | _ -> None

(* (what was typed as www has it: TinyBrowserAddress.absolute) *)
let www_address typed =
  let url =
    TinyBrowserAddress.absolute (fst (TinyBrowserAddress.fragment typed)) in
  match wikipedia url with
  | Some (host, title) -> "https://" ^ host ^ rest_prefix ^ title
  | None -> url

let www_picture_request line =
  match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
  | "img" :: w :: h :: address ->
      Some (match int_of_string_opt w, int_of_string_opt h with
        | Some w, Some h when w > 0 && h > 0 && w <= TinyKernelNetwork.il_max ->
            (w, h, String.concat " " address)
        | _ -> (0, 0, ""))
  | "img" :: _ -> Some (0, 0, "")
  | _ -> None

let www_picture_kept url =
  let path =
    match String.index_opt url '?' with
    | Some i -> String.sub url 0 i
    | None -> url in
  let name = Filename.basename path in
  if name = "" || name.[0] = '.' || String.contains name '/' then None
  else Some name

let www_kept url =
  let engine = TinyBrowserAddress.search_engine in
  let n = String.length engine in
  match wikipedia url with
  | Some (_, title)
    when title <> "" && not (String.contains title '/')
         && title.[0] <> '.' ->
      Some (title ^ ".html")
  | _ ->
      (* a search's results, search-words.html *)
      let words =
        if String.starts_with engine url then
          String.sub url n (String.length url - n)
        else "" in
      if words = "" then www_picture_kept url
      else if String.contains words '/' then None
      else Some ("search-" ^ words ^ ".html")

let www_request line =
  Option.map www_address (TinyBrowserHttp.asked line)

let www_type name =
  match String.lowercase_ascii (Filename.extension name) with
  | ".html" | ".htm" -> "text/html; charset=utf-8"
  | ".txt" -> "text/plain"
  | ".wav" -> "audio/wav"
  | ".pdf" -> "application/pdf"
  | ".png" -> "image/png"
  | ".jpg" | ".jpeg" -> "image/jpeg"
  | _ -> "application/octet-stream"

let www_kept_response name body =
  TinyBrowserHttp.response 200 [ "Content-Type", www_type name ] body

let www_failed why =
  TinyBrowserHttp.response 502 [ "Content-Type", "text/plain" ] why

let out p packets =
  List.iter (fun packet ->
    p.sent <- p.sent + 1;
    if List.mem p.sent p.lost then p.said "x" packet
    else (p.said "<" packet; p.give (latency ()) packet)) packets

(* A connection the machine asks for to another address than the
 * peer's: the outside is asked first, and if it has a way there the
 * stack will answer that sync as that address (TinyKernelNetwork's
 * gateway). So a dial to a port nothing listens on fails in the machine
 * too. *)
let gate p packet =
  match p.outside, TinyKernelNetwork.ip_read "" packet with
  | Some outside, Some (proto, _, body)
    when proto = TinyKernelNetwork.ip_il
         && String.sub packet 16 4 <> TinyKernelNetwork.net_peer -> (
      let to_ = String.sub packet 16 4 in
      match TinyKernelNetwork.il_read body with
      | Some (kind, sport, dport, _, 0, _)
        when kind = TinyKernelNetwork.il_sync
             && not (List.exists (fun (c : TinyKernelNetwork.il) ->
                  c.il_me = to_ && c.il_lport = dport && c.il_rport = sport)
                  p.stack.ns_conns) -> (
          match outside.connect (net_dotted to_) dport with
          | Some relay ->
              p.stack.ns_others <- (to_, dport) :: p.stack.ns_others;
              p.agreed <- ((to_, dport, sport), relay) :: p.agreed
          | None -> ())
      | _ -> ())
  | _ -> ()

(* a relay's turn: the machine's messages to the outside; the outside's
 * bytes, 4 KB ahead at most, cut in messages while the connection has
 * room; the outside's end said when all of it was sent; the
 * connection's end the outside's *)
let relay_turn p (r : relaying) =
  let rec hear () =
    match TinyKernelNetwork.il_hear r.rconn with
    | Some m -> r.relay.put m; hear ()
    | None -> () in
  hear ();
  if (not r.ended) && String.length r.coming < 4096 then (
    match r.relay.take () with
    | Some b -> r.coming <- r.coming ^ b
    | None -> r.ended <- true);
  while r.coming <> "" && TinyKernelNetwork.il_room r.rconn do
    let n = min TinyKernelNetwork.il_max (String.length r.coming) in
    out p [ TinyKernelNetwork.il_write r.rconn (String.sub r.coming 0 n)
              p.now ];
    r.coming <- String.sub r.coming n (String.length r.coming - n)
  done;
  if r.ended && r.coming = "" then TinyKernelNetwork.il_done r.rconn

(* the connections just made taken: one for another address is its
 * relay's, one to port 53 asks an address of a name, one to port 70 a
 * document; a line that came answered; an answer's messages sent while
 * the connection has room, and after the last the end said; the
 * relays' turns *)
let serve p =
  List.iter (fun (conn : TinyKernelNetwork.il) ->
    let key = conn.il_me, conn.il_lport, conn.il_rport in
    match List.assoc_opt key p.agreed with
    | Some relay ->
        p.agreed <- List.filter (fun (k, _) -> k <> key) p.agreed;
        p.relays <-
          { rconn = conn; relay = relay; coming = ""; ended = false }
          :: p.relays
    | None ->
        let name line answer = match p.outside with
          | Some o -> (match o.name line with "" -> answer [] | a -> answer [ a ])
          | None -> answer [] in
        p.serving <-
          { conn = conn;
            ask = (if conn.il_lport = 53 then name else p.document);
            todo = None; asked = false; taking = None }
          :: p.serving)
    p.stack.ns_fresh;
  p.stack.ns_fresh <- [];
  List.iter (relay_turn p) p.relays;
  p.relays <-
    List.filter (fun (r : relaying) ->
      if TinyKernelNetwork.il_over r.rconn then (r.relay.shut (); false)
      else true) p.relays;
  List.iter (fun (s : serving) ->
    if not s.asked then (
      match TinyKernelNetwork.il_hear s.conn with
      | Some line -> (
          s.asked <- true;
          match String.split_on_char ' ' (String.trim line) with
          | [ "put"; name; size ]
            when s.conn.il_lport = 70 && int_of_string_opt size <> None ->
              s.taking <- Some (name, int_of_string size, Buffer.create 1024)
          | _ -> s.ask (String.trim line) (fun l -> s.todo <- Some l))
      | None -> ());
    (* a file being put: its messages taken until its size, then kept
     * by the host, and the answer a line, ok or why not *)
    (match s.taking with
     | Some (name, size, b) ->
         let rec take () =
           if Buffer.length b < size then
             match TinyKernelNetwork.il_hear s.conn with
             | Some m -> Buffer.add_string b m; take ()
             | None -> () in
         take ();
         if Buffer.length b >= size then begin
           s.taking <- None;
           let why = p.store name (Buffer.contents b) in
           s.todo <- Some [ (if why = "" then "ok" else why) ^ "\n" ]
         end
     | None -> ());
    let rec push () =
      match s.todo with
      | Some (m :: rest) when TinyKernelNetwork.il_room s.conn ->
          s.todo <- Some rest;
          out p [ TinyKernelNetwork.il_write s.conn m p.now ];
          push ()
      | Some [] -> TinyKernelNetwork.il_done s.conn
      | _ -> () in
    push ()) p.serving;
  p.serving <-
    List.filter (fun (s : serving) ->
      not (TinyKernelNetwork.il_over s.conn || s.todo = Some []))
      p.serving

(* what there is to do, and a clock only while there is a connection *)
let poll p =
  serve p;
  if (not p.awake) && p.stack.ns_conns <> [] then
    (p.awake <- true; p.give (tick ()) "")

let send p packet =
  if packet = "" then begin
    p.awake <- false;
    p.now <- p.now + 1;
    out p (TinyKernelNetwork.net_tick p.stack p.now)
  end
  else (
    p.said ">" packet;
    gate p packet;
    out p (fst (TinyKernelNetwork.net_input p.stack p.now packet)));
  poll p

let dial p port relay =
  let conn, sync =
    TinyKernelNetwork.net_dial p.stack TinyKernelNetwork.net_machine port
      p.now in
  out p [ sync ];
  p.relays <-
    { rconn = conn; relay = relay; coming = ""; ended = false } :: p.relays;
  poll p
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachinePeer.mli
8128
(* Tiny peer: the other end of tiny-machine's wire (plan_tiny_network.md),
 * what a host gives the machine to talk to. Not a second machine: the
 * host runs TinyKernelNetwork.ml, the stack tiny-kernel has, at the other
 * address (10.0.0.1), with no CPU under it, and a few lines on top:
 *
 *     the machine                              the host
 *
 *     tiny-kernel, 10.0.0.2                    the peer, 10.0.0.1
 *       TinyKernelNetwork.ml (by tiny-ml)      TinyKernelNetwork.ml (by OCaml)
 *            |                                        |      |
 *     the network's device  == send ==========>  [send]      [document]:
 *     (TinyMachineDevices)      <= give, later ====  [give]      a line to its
 *                                                            messages
 *
 * - a ping is answered (TinyKernelNetwork's own);
 * - on port 70, a connection's first message is a line, a document's
 *   name; the document is sent, a message at a time as the machine
 *   acknowledges, and the connection closed. One line out, a document
 *   back, the end: Gopher's shape (1991), and its port. The lines by
 *   the programs that write them: a name (get: a text), "GET address
 *   HTTP/1.0" (www: a web page, HTTP's request, answered by HTTP's
 *   response) and "img w h address" (www: a page's picture, its rows a
 *   message each, so that it is painted as it arrives);
 * - and the other way, "put name size" then the file's bytes (put):
 *   the host keeps the file, so that it outlives the machine, and the
 *   answer is a line, ok or why not.
 *
 * Where a document comes from is the host's, the one thing a terminal
 * and a page do differently: [document] is given the line and a
 * function to call with the messages, now (a file read) or later (a
 * page's fetch).
 *
 * Time is the machine's, in instructions: a packet of the peer's
 * lands [latency] after it was sent, and the peer's own clock (IL asks
 * again when nothing came) is an empty packet it gives itself, which
 * the machine returns to [send] a tick later and no kernel sees
 * (TinyMachineDevices's landed). So a run is the same each time. What is
 * lost is said, not drawn at random: [lose].
 *
 * mini-qemu's wire has a second stack at its other end, written for
 * it (raspberry/Usernet); this one is the first again. *)

type t

(* A way to a program that is not on the wire, which a host may have
 * (a terminal's: a socket; a page has none). A relay is one
 * connection's: the bytes that came from there ("" when none has,
 * None at its end), bytes sent there, its end. With an [outside] the
 * peer is a gateway: a connection the machine asks for to any other
 * address is asked of [connect] (an address as text, a port; None:
 * nothing answers), and its messages go there as bytes and come back
 * as messages, cut where the bytes happened to arrive: the machine
 * speaks IL, the outside TCP, and a program that reads lines must not
 * take a message for one. And port 53 of the peer answers a name by
 * its address as text, from [name] ("" when it has none), which is
 * all there is of DNS. *)
type relay = {
  take : unit -> string option;
  put : string -> unit;
  shut : unit -> unit;
}
type outside = {
  name : string -> string;
  connect : string -> int -> relay option;
}

(* The peer. [give after packet]: the machine's net_give, a packet to
 * land so many instructions from now. [said dir packet]: each packet
 * that crosses, for who watches (">" from the machine, "<" to it, "x"
 * to it and lost). [document line messages]: what the line names,
 * given to [messages] once, now or later. [store name bytes]: a file
 * the machine put (tiny-kernel's put: a first line "put name size",
 * then its bytes), to keep where [document] finds it again; "" when it
 * is kept, why not otherwise, which put says. The empty line, Gopher's
 * menu, is [document]'s too: what was put, a name a line. *)
val create :
  give:(int -> string -> unit) ->
  said:(string -> string -> unit) ->
  document:(string -> (string list -> unit) -> unit) ->
  store:(string -> string -> string) -> outside:outside option -> t

(* the machine's [send]: a packet of its kernel's ("": the peer's own
 * clock) *)
val send : t -> string -> unit

(* What the host does between two packets: the relays have their turn
 * (called often enough, a relay's bytes do not wait for the machine to
 * send something). And a connection from the outside to a port of the
 * machine's, where a program of its listens: the relay is its other
 * side (a host's -net-forward). *)
val poll : t -> unit
val dial : t -> int -> relay -> unit

(* the n-th packet the peer sends from now (1: the next) is lost *)
val lose : t -> int -> unit

(* a text as messages, of TinyKernelNetwork.il_max bytes at most *)
val messages : string -> string list

(* A request "GET address HTTP/1.0" asks for a web page, for
 * tiny-kernel's browser (plan_tiny_browser.md; TinyBrowserHttp, a
 * proxy's request: the whole address on its line). The peer answers
 * with an HTTP/1.0 response: its status line and headers, the site's
 * (Content-Type, which www goes by), then the page's bytes, a message at
 * a time, the site's chunks and gzip undone. Fetching is the host's (a
 * terminal's helper, or a page's fetch), but where to fetch is decided
 * here, the same for both: [www_request] gives the address a request
 * asks for, by [www_address], which turns what was typed into a URL. A
 * bare title (OCaml, Plan 9 from Bell Labs) is an English Wikipedia
 * article; a name with a dot and no scheme (example.com) is https://;
 * ?words a search (TinyBrowserAddress.absolute, www's own rules). A
 * Wikipedia article's address (/wiki/X) becomes its REST HTML
 * (/api/rest_v1/page/html/X): the article without the site's menus, and
 * the one a web page is allowed to fetch. A #fragment is dropped.
 * [www_kept] is the name of the file that holds a kept copy of a
 * Wikipedia article (X.html), of a search's results (search-words.html,
 * the words as the query has them), or of another address, its last
 * part (korobeiniki.wav), for the tests and for a machine with no way
 * out. [www_kept_response] is the answer such a copy makes, its
 * Content-Type by its name's extension ([www_type]); [www_failed] the
 * answer when there is no page, a 502 whose text says why. *)
val www_request : string -> string option
val www_address : string -> string
val www_kept : string -> string option
val www_type : string -> string
val www_kept_response : string -> string -> string
val www_failed : string -> string

(* The line "img w h address" asks for a picture of the page, w by h
 * pixels: the answer is [picture "" w h pixels] (below), with w and h 0
 * when there is none. The host decodes it and makes it that size, in
 * the machine's colours. [www_picture_request] gives what such a line
 * asks for, w, h and the address, w and h 0 for a size no answer can
 * carry (0, or w past a message's bytes). [www_picture_kept] is the
 * name of the file that holds a kept copy: the address's last part,
 * without its ?query (250px-OCaml_Logo.svg.png). *)
val www_picture_request : string -> (int * int * string) option
val www_picture_kept : string -> string option

(* What "img w h address" is answered: a first message "t w h", then t
 * messages of text, then h messages of w bytes, a row of the picture
 * each, a byte a pixel in the screen's 256 colours (w no more than a
 * message's bytes; 0 0 with no picture). [picture text w h pixels]
 * makes them. *)
val picture : string -> int -> int -> string -> string list

(* How many instructions a packet takes to cross the wire (5 ms of the
 * machine's time), and how many pass between two of the peer's looks at

(* Claude Code
