(* See TinyMachineSDL.mli *)
open Tsdl

type event =
  | Quit
  | At of int * int
  | Button of int * bool
  | Key of int * bool
  | Wheel of int

type t = {
  present : int -> int -> string -> unit; poll : unit -> event list;
  cursor : int -> unit; play : string -> unit; queued : unit -> int;
}

let key_byte usage ~shift ~ctrl =
  let plain = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890\n\027\b\t -=[]\\\000;'`,./"
  and shifted =
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ!@#$%^&*()\n\027\b\t _+{}|\000:\"~<>?" in
  if usage >= 4 && usage <= 56 then
    if ctrl && usage <= 29 then Some (usage - 3)
    else
      (match Char.code (if shift then shifted else plain).[usage - 4] with
       | 0 -> None
       | c -> Some c)
  else
    match usage with
    | 82 -> Some 128
    | 81 -> Some 129
    | 80 -> Some 130
    | 79 -> Some 131
    | 76 -> Some 127
    | _ -> None

(* the modifiers down; the key held (its usage, its byte), and when it
 * is typed again *)
type keyboard = {
  mutable shift : bool; mutable ctrl : bool; mutable alt : bool;
  mutable held : (int * int) option; mutable again : float;
}

let keyboard () =
  { shift = false; ctrl = false; alt = false; held = None; again = 0. }

let typed k now = function
  | Key ((225 | 229), down) -> k.shift <- down; []
  | Key ((224 | 228), down) -> k.ctrl <- down; []
  | Key ((226 | 230), down) -> k.alt <- down; []
  | Key (usage, true) -> (
      match key_byte usage ~shift:k.shift ~ctrl:k.ctrl with
      | Some byte ->
          k.held <- Some (usage, byte);
          k.again <- now +. 0.3;
          if k.alt then [ 27; byte ] else [ byte ]
      | None -> [])
  | Key (usage, false) ->
      (match k.held with
       | Some (u, _) when u = usage -> k.held <- None
       | _ -> ());
      []
  | Wheel v -> List.init (min 8 (abs v)) (fun _ -> if v < 0 then 128 else 129)
  | Quit | At _ | Button _ -> []

let repeated k now =
  match k.held with
  | Some (_, byte) when now >= k.again -> k.again <- now +. 0.05; Some byte
  | _ -> None

let ok = function Ok v -> v | Error _ -> failwith ("SDL: " ^ Sdl.get_error ())

let create ~title =
  ok (Sdl.init Sdl.Init.video);
  (* the window, its renderer and the frame's texture, made at the first
   * frame (and again if the frame's size changes) *)
  let window = ref None and texture = ref None and size = ref (0, 0)
  and last = ref "" in
  let pixels =
    ref (Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int8_unsigned Bigarray.c_layout 0) in
  let draw () =
    match !window, !texture with
    | Some (_, r), Some tex ->
        ok (Sdl.render_clear r);
        ok (Sdl.render_copy r tex);
        Sdl.render_present r
    | _ -> () in
  let present w h data =
    if !size <> (w, h) then begin
      (match !window with
       | None ->
           let times =
             match Sdl.get_current_display_mode 0 with
             | Ok mode -> max 1 (mode.Sdl.dm_h * 3 / 4 / h)
             | Error _ -> 1 in
           let win =
             ok (Sdl.create_window title ~w:(times * w) ~h:(times * h)
                   Sdl.Window.(windowed + resizable)) in
           window := Some (win, ok (Sdl.create_renderer win))
       | Some (win, _) -> Sdl.set_window_size win ~w ~h);
      let _, r = Option.get !window in
      (* the frame drawn as large as fits, its proportions kept; and the
       * mouse's place given in the frame's pixels *)
      ok (Sdl.render_set_logical_size r w h);
      texture :=
        Some (ok (Sdl.create_texture r Sdl.Pixel.format_rgb24
                    Sdl.Texture.access_streaming ~w ~h));
      pixels :=
        Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int8_unsigned Bigarray.c_layout
          (3 * w * h);
      size := (w, h); last := ""
    end;
    if data <> !last then begin
      last := data;
      let px = !pixels in
      String.iteri
        (fun i c -> Bigarray.Array1.unsafe_set px i (Char.code c)) data;
      ok (Sdl.update_texture (Option.get !texture) None px (3 * w));
      draw ()
    end in
  let e = Sdl.Event.create () in
  (* SDL's buttons as Plan 9's: left 1, middle 2, right 4 *)
  let button b =
    if b = Sdl.Button.left then 1
    else if b = Sdl.Button.middle then 2
    else if b = Sdl.Button.right then 4
    else 0 in
  let poll () =
    let evs = ref [] in
    let add ev = evs := ev :: !evs in
    while Sdl.poll_event (Some e) do
      let k = Sdl.Event.(get e typ) in
      let is t = k = t in
      if is Sdl.Event.quit then add Quit
      else if is Sdl.Event.window_event then
        (* a window uncovered or resized has lost its frame *)
        (match Sdl.Event.(window_event_enum (get e window_event_id)) with
         | `Exposed | `Size_changed -> draw ()
         | _ -> ())
      else if (is Sdl.Event.key_down || is Sdl.Event.key_up)
              && Sdl.Event.(get e keyboard_repeat) = 0 then
        add (Key (Sdl.Event.(get e keyboard_scancode), is Sdl.Event.key_down))
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_down || is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_up
      then begin
        let b = button Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_button_button) in
        if b <> 0 then add (Button (b, is Sdl.Event.mouse_button_down))
      end
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_motion then
        add (At (Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_motion_x),
                 Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_motion_y)))
      else if is Sdl.Event.mouse_wheel then
        add (Wheel (- Sdl.Event.(get e mouse_wheel_y)))
    done;
    List.rev !evs in
  (* the arrow, or a hand over what can be clicked, as the system draws
   * them; each made once, when first asked for *)
  let cursors = Hashtbl.create 2 in
  let cursor n =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt cursors n with
    | Some c -> Sdl.set_cursor (Some c)
    | None ->
        (match
           Sdl.create_system_cursor
             (if n = 1 then Sdl.System_cursor.hand
              else Sdl.System_cursor.arrow)
         with
         | Ok c -> Hashtbl.replace cursors n c; Sdl.set_cursor (Some c)
         | Error _ -> ()) in
  (* the sound, opened at the first samples (None: no sound here) *)
  let device = lazy (
    match Sdl.init_sub_system Sdl.Init.audio with
    | Error _ -> None
    | Ok () ->
        let spec =
          { Sdl.as_freq = 8000; as_format = Sdl.Audio.s8; as_channels = 1;
            as_silence = 0; as_samples = 256; as_size = 0l;
            as_callback = None } in
        (match Sdl.open_audio_device None false spec 0 with
         | Ok (d, _) -> Sdl.pause_audio_device d false; Some d
         | Error _ -> None)) in
  let play samples =
    match Lazy.force device with
    | None -> ()
    | Some d ->
        let queued = Sdl.get_queued_audio_size d in
        if queued <= 4000 then begin
          let samples =
            if queued = 0 then String.make 800 '\000' ^ samples else samples in
          let ba =
            Bigarray.Array1.create Bigarray.int8_signed Bigarray.c_layout
              (String.length samples) in
          String.iteri
            (fun i c ->
              Bigarray.Array1.unsafe_set ba i
                (let v = Char.code c in if v > 127 then v - 256 else v))
            samples;
          ignore (Sdl.queue_audio d ba)
        end in
  let queued () =
    match Lazy.force device with
    | Some d -> Sdl.get_queued_audio_size d
    | None -> 0 in
  { present; poll; cursor; play; queued }
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachineSDL.mli
3321
(* The SDL window of tiny-machine-window (tsdl): the one module of t-ix
 * that links a C library. It shows frames of RGB bytes, gives what is
 * done in the window as events, and sets the mouse's look.
 *
 * The window opens at the first frame, at the largest whole number of
 * times the frame that three quarters of the screen's height hold (the
 * machine's 1024 by 768 is small on a large screen). It can be resized:
 * the frame is drawn as large as fits, its proportions kept, and the
 * mouse's place is still given in the frame's pixels.
 *
 * The sound is SDL's queue, filled as the samples come (about thirty
 * times a second): when it ran empty, a tenth of a second of silence
 * goes first, the margin a late frame of the host's eats before it is
 * heard as a gap (notes_audio.md's A); past half a second queued, what
 * comes is dropped, so that a sound stays near what it goes with.
 *
 * mini-qemu has its own (raspberry/video/Sdl_display.ml), which does
 * more: 44,100 samples a second in two channels, a meter under the
 * screen, a mouse grabbed and relative as a USB mouse is. This one is
 * what tiny-machine needs, so that t-ix depends on nothing of
 * mini-qemu's. *)

(* What is done in the window: closed; the mouse's place (in the frame's
 * pixels); a mouse button (1 left, 2 middle, 4 right, as Plan 9's),
 * down or up; a key (its USB HID usage, which is SDL's scancode), down
 * or up; a step of the wheel or of two fingers on a trackpad (negative
 * up). *)
type event =
  | Quit
  | At of int * int
  | Button of int * bool
  | Key of int * bool
  | Wheel of int

(* [present w h rgb]: a frame of w by h pixels, three bytes each (red,
 * green, blue). [poll ()]: the events since the last poll. [cursor n]:
 * the mouse's look, 0 the arrow, 1 a hand (over a link). [play
 * samples]: the machine's speaker's, a byte each (signed), 8,000 a
 * second, played after those before; the sound opened at the first.
 * [queued ()]: the samples waiting to be played. *)
type t = {
  present : int -> int -> string -> unit; poll : unit -> event list;
  cursor : int -> unit; play : string -> unit; queued : unit -> int;
}

val create : title:string -> t

(* The keyboard, what tiny-machine-window and tiny/sdl/ type from the
 * window's events. A key's byte is by its USB usage (a US keyboard's,
 * SDL's scancode), with shift and control; the arrows 128 to 131 (up,
 * down, left, right), tiny-machine's choice; a key that is no byte
 * types nothing. Alt with a key is Escape then the key: Emacs's Meta,
 * M-x. A step of the wheel (or of two fingers on a trackpad) is an
 * arrow key, up or down, a step each: a key is queued, where a button
 * pressed and let go between two reads of the mouse could be missed. A
 * program scrolls by its arrows (www, emacs).
 *
 * The key held is typed again, a keyboard's repeat, done here (the
 * display says a key's press once, what a kernel's USB driver wants; a
 * game wants its arrows held): after 0.3 s, then every 0.05 s.
 *
 * [typed k now e]: the bytes the event e types (none for a modifier, the
 * mouse, Quit), now the time in seconds. [repeated k now]: the key held,
 * when it is typed again. *)
type keyboard
val keyboard : unit -> keyboard
val typed : keyboard -> float -> event -> int list
val repeated : keyboard -> float -> int option

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyMachineSocket.mli *)

let usage =
  "usage: tiny-machine-socket dial host port | listen port | name host"

(* a name's first address of the Internet's first kind (IPv4: the
 * machine's addresses are four bytes) *)
let address (_caps : < Cap.network; .. >) host =
  match
    List.filter
      (fun (a : Unix.addr_info) -> a.ai_family = Unix.PF_INET)
      (Unix.getaddrinfo host "" [ Unix.AI_SOCKTYPE Unix.SOCK_STREAM ])
  with
  | { ai_addr = Unix.ADDR_INET (a, _); _ } :: _ -> Some a
  | _ -> None

(* a connection there, if it is made in five seconds *)
let dial (caps : < Cap.network; .. >) host port =
  match address caps host with
  | None -> None
  | Some a ->
      let fd = Unix.socket Unix.PF_INET Unix.SOCK_STREAM 0 in
      Unix.set_nonblock fd;
      let made =
        try Unix.connect fd (Unix.ADDR_INET (a, port)); true
        with
        | Unix.Unix_error ((Unix.EINPROGRESS | Unix.EINTR), _, _) -> (
            (* when it can be written the try is over; asked again, a
             * connection made says it is one, one refused says why *)
            match Unix.select [] [ fd ] [] 5. with
            | _, [ _ ], _ -> (
                try Unix.connect fd (Unix.ADDR_INET (a, port)); true
                with
                | Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EISCONN, _, _) -> true
                | Unix.Unix_error _ -> false)
            | _ -> false)
        | Unix.Unix_error _ -> false in
      if made then (Unix.clear_nonblock fd; Some fd) else (Unix.close fd; None)

(* the bytes both ways, until one side ends: what is read on inp to
 * the connection, what comes from it to out *)
let relay inp out fd =
  let b = Bytes.create 4096 in
  let rec all to_ n at =
    if at < n then all to_ n (at + Unix.write to_ b at (n - at)) in
  let rec go () =
    let ready, _, _ = Unix.select [ inp; fd ] [] [] (-1.) in
    let pass from to_ =
      if List.mem from ready then (
        let n = Unix.read from b 0 4096 in
        if n = 0 then raise Exit;
        all to_ n 0) in
    pass inp fd;
    pass fd out;
    go () in
  try go () with Exit | Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()

let say (caps : < Cap.stdout; .. >) s =
  ignore (Unix.write_substring (Console.stdout_fd caps) s 0 (String.length s))

(* SIGALRM's, which ends this, in s seconds (0.: none) *)
let timer (_ : < Cap.signal; .. >) s =
  ignore
    (Unix.setitimer Unix.ITIMER_REAL { it_interval = 0.; it_value = s })

(* a named pipe of its own *)
let fifo (_ : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) =
  let f = Filename.temp_file "tiny-machine-socket" "" in
  Sys.remove f;
  Unix.mkfifo f 0o600;
  f

(* this machine's port (127.0.0.1's), listened on until the standard
 * input's end (who ran this is gone); each connection relayed by a
 * child on two named pipes, opened by the one who ran this (the child
 * waits ten seconds for it), their names said. old: the first
 * connection alone, its socket then closed, the next one's helper
 * started when this one's was seen: a connection between the two was
 * refused (make test on GitHub's runner, linux.py's GET /bin/ping) *)
let listen
    (caps : < Cap.network; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.fork; Cap.signal;
             Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) port =
  let l = Unix.socket Unix.PF_INET Unix.SOCK_STREAM 0 in
  match
    Unix.setsockopt l Unix.SO_REUSEADDR true;
    Unix.bind l (Unix.ADDR_INET (Unix.inet_addr_loopback, port));
    Unix.listen l 16
  with
  | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> Unix.close l; say caps "-\n"
  | () ->
      say caps "+\n";
      Sys.set_signal Sys.sigchld Sys.Signal_ignore;
      let rec wait () =
        let ready, _, _ = Unix.select [ Console.stdin_fd caps; l ] [] [] (-1.) in
        if not (List.mem (Console.stdin_fd caps) ready) then begin
          (match Unix.accept l with
           | fd, _ ->
               let inp = fifo caps and out = fifo caps in
               (match CapUnix.fork caps () with
                | 0 ->
                    Unix.close l;
                    Unix.close (Console.stdout_fd caps);
                    timer caps 10.;
                    let i = Unix.openfile inp [ Unix.O_RDONLY ] 0 in
                    let o = Unix.openfile out [ Unix.O_WRONLY ] 0 in
                    timer caps 0.;
                    Sys.remove inp;
                    Sys.remove out;
                    relay i o fd;
                    Unix._exit 0
                | _ -> Unix.close fd; say caps (inp ^ " " ^ out ^ "\n"))
           | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
          wait ()
        end in
      wait ()

let main
    (caps : < Cap.network; Cap.argv; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.fork;
             Cap.signal; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) =
  Sys.set_signal Sys.sigpipe Sys.Signal_ignore;
  (* (a terminal's ^C is for the kernel in the machine, which the one that
   * ran this gives it) *)
  Sys.set_signal Sys.sigint Sys.Signal_ignore;
  match List.tl (Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps)) with
  | [ "dial"; host; port ] when int_of_string_opt port <> None ->
      let fd = dial caps host (int_of_string port) in
      say caps (if fd = None then "-" else "+");
      Option.iter (relay (Console.stdin_fd caps) (Console.stdout_fd caps)) fd;
      0
  | [ "listen"; port ] when int_of_string_opt port <> None ->
      listen caps (int_of_string port);
      0
  | [ "name"; host ] ->
      Option.iter
        (fun a -> Console.print caps (Unix.string_of_inet_addr a ^ "\n"))
        (address caps host);
      0
  | _ -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "\n"); 2

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> CapStdlib.exit caps (main caps))
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachineSocket.mli

(* tiny-machine's way out to other programs (plan_tiny_network.md, "On
 * Linux"): one connection of the host's, its bytes on the standard
 * input and output. A program apart, as TinyMachineWindow is for the
 * screen: tiny-machine has no socket and looks no name up (nor has the
 * library mini-ml puts under it); it runs this beside itself, once for
 * each connection, with two pipes.
 *
 *     tiny-machine-socket dial example.com 80     a connection there
 *     tiny-machine-socket listen 8080             each one made to this
 *                                                 machine's port 8080
 *                                                 (127.0.0.1's)
 *     tiny-machine-socket name example.com        its address, a line
 *
 * dial first writes one byte, + when the connection is there (within
 * five seconds), - when it cannot be; then what is read on the
 * standard input is written to the connection and what comes from it
 * to the standard output, until either ends.
 *
 * listen writes a line, + when it listens, - when it cannot; then,
 * until its standard input ends, a line for each connection, two
 * named pipes' names: a child of its own relays the connection with
 * them, the first written to it, the second read from it, as dial's
 * input and output. (old: as dial, the first connection alone; the
 * next one's listen came later, and a connection between was refused:
 * the socket now stays, connections wait in its queue.)
 *
 *     tiny-kernel         tiny-machine                this program   the world
 *
 *     get / example.com
 *       dial, IL  ======> TinyMachinePeer: a sync for
 *                         another address: connect -> dial example.com 70
 *                                                     "+"            a TCP
 *       messages  <=====> a relay: two pipes  <=====> bytes  <=====> connection
 *
 * The machine speaks IL and the world TCP; the two are joined here
 * and in TinyMachinePeer's relay, which cuts the bytes in messages. It is
 * what a home's router does for the machines behind it (address
 * translation), a connection at a time, and what Plan 9's machines
 * needed a gateway for when the world did not speak IL.
 *
 * mini-qemu has the same way out inside itself (raspberry/'s Usernet,
 * QEMU's slirp: the guest's TCP answered, and a socket of the host's
 * opened for each of its connections); here it is a program apart, so
 * that tiny-machine links no socket.
 *
 * Not compiled by mini-ml (it asks the system for names: getaddrinfo),
 * and not in t-ix's count of tiny programs: a helper of the host's. *)

(* A program: it gives nothing to another file. *)

(* Claude Code

(* See TinyMachineWeb.mli *)

module Js = Js_of_ocaml.Js
module U = Js_of_ocaml.Js.Unsafe

let call o name args = U.meth_call o name args
let str s = U.inject (Js.string s)
let get o name = U.get o (Js.string name)
let document = get U.global "document"
let element id = call document "getElementById" [| str id |]
let listen o name f =
  ignore
    (call o "addEventListener" [| str name; U.inject (Js.wrap_callback f) |])
(* whether the page has the element asked for (getElementById's null) *)
let present e = Js.Opt.test (Obj.magic e : U.any Js.opt)
let now () : float =
  Js.float_of_number (call (get U.global "performance") "now" [||])

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The console: the machine's bytes as the page's text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the last [kept] bytes; a backspace takes one back *)
let kept = 20000
let text = Buffer.create 1024
let text_changed = ref false

let put ch =
  (match ch with
   | '\b' ->
       if Buffer.length text > 0 then
         Buffer.truncate text (Buffer.length text - 1)
   | '\r' -> ()
   | ch -> Buffer.add_char text ch);
  if Buffer.length text > 2 * kept then begin
    let last = Buffer.sub text (Buffer.length text - kept) kept in
    Buffer.clear text; Buffer.add_string text last
  end;
  text_changed := true

(* the line being typed, a terminal's (see the keys), shown after the
 * text with its cursor: an element of its own (the page's style makes
 * it a block that blinks), put back after the text each time, since
 * setting the text removes it *)
let line = Buffer.create 80
let cursor = lazy (
  let c = call document "createElement" [| str "span" |] in
  U.set c (Js.string "id") (Js.string "cursor");
  U.set c (Js.string "textContent") (Js.string "\xc2\xa0");
  c)

let show_text () =
  if !text_changed then begin
    text_changed := false;
    let e = element "console" in
    U.set e (Js.string "textContent")
      (Js.bytestring (Buffer.contents text ^ Buffer.contents line));
    ignore (call e "appendChild" [| U.inject (Lazy.force cursor) |]);
    U.set e (Js.string "scrollTop") (get e "scrollHeight")
  end

let status s =
  U.set (element "status") (Js.string "textContent") (Js.string s)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The keys and the mouse *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a key's byte: the arrows 128 to 131 (up, down, left, right),
 * tiny-machine's choice; control with a letter its control character *)
let key_byte e =
  let key = Js.to_string (get e "key")
  and ctrl = Js.to_bool (get e "ctrlKey") in
  match key with
  | "Enter" -> Some 10
  | "Backspace" -> Some 8
  | "Tab" -> Some 9
  | "Escape" -> Some 27
  | "Delete" -> Some 127
  | "ArrowUp" -> Some 128
  | "ArrowDown" -> Some 129
  | "ArrowLeft" -> Some 130
  | "ArrowRight" -> Some 131
  | _ when String.length key = 1 && Char.code key.[0] < 127 ->
      let c = Char.code key.[0] in
      if Js.to_bool (get e "metaKey") then None
      else if ctrl then Some (c land 31)
      else Some c
  | _ -> None

(* whether a program has drawn on the screen (a pixel not black), and
 * whether the keys are the screen's: it has the focus, and is drawn on *)
let lit = ref false
let screen_keys () =
  !lit && get document "activeElement" == element "screen"

(* a terminal's key: the line edited and echoed, given at Enter; ^C at
 * once, as a terminal's interrupt (tiny-kernel kills the program
 * running) *)
let terminal_key (mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine) b =
  (match b with
   | 3 -> TinyMachineDevices.console_type mc.cons "\003"
   | 8 | 127 ->
       if Buffer.length line > 0 then
         Buffer.truncate line (Buffer.length line - 1)
   | 10 ->
       Buffer.add_char line '\n';
       Buffer.add_buffer text line;
       TinyMachineDevices.console_type mc.cons (Buffer.contents line);
       Buffer.clear line
   | b when b >= 32 && b < 127 -> Buffer.add_char line (Char.chr b)
   | _ -> ());
  text_changed := true

let listen_keys (mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine) =
  listen document "keydown" (fun e ->
    (* Alt with a letter is Escape then the letter: Emacs's Meta, M-x.
     * The letter is the key's place (code: KeyX), as macOS's Option
     * makes another character of it (Option-x is ≈) *)
    let code = Js.to_string (get e "code") in
    let meta =
      Js.to_bool (get e "altKey") && String.length code = 4
      && String.sub code 0 3 = "Key" && screen_keys () in
    if meta then begin
      TinyMachineDevices.console_type mc.cons
        ("\027" ^ String.lowercase_ascii (String.sub code 3 1));
      ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||])
    end else
    match key_byte e with
    | Some b ->
        if screen_keys () then
          TinyMachineDevices.console_type mc.cons (String.make 1 (Char.chr b))
        else terminal_key mc b;
        ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||])
    | None -> ())

(* the place in the canvas's own pixels (the page may show it larger);
 * the browser's buttons are 1 left, 2 right, 4 middle, the machine's 1
 * left, 2 middle, 4 right, as Plan 9's *)
let listen_mouse (mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine) canvas =
  let int_of o name : int = truncate (Js.float_of_number (get o name)) in
  let moved e =
    let scaled v shown full = if shown > 0 then v * full / shown else v in
    let x =
      scaled (int_of e "offsetX") (int_of canvas "clientWidth")
        TinyMachineDevices.width
    and y =
      scaled (int_of e "offsetY") (int_of canvas "clientHeight")
        TinyMachineDevices.height
    and b = int_of e "buttons" in
    TinyMachineDevices.mouse_set mc.mouse x y
      ((b land 1) lor (if b land 2 <> 0 then 4 else 0)
       lor (if b land 4 <> 0 then 2 else 0));
    ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||]) in
  List.iter (fun name -> listen canvas name moved)
    [ "mousemove"; "mousedown"; "mouseup" ];
  (* The wheel, and two fingers on a trackpad: an arrow key a step, up or
   * down, as tiny-machine's window sends them (TinyMachineWindow.ml). A
   * trackpad gives many small moves: they are added up, a step each 40
   * pixels (or each line, when the browser counts in lines). *)
  let wheel = ref 0. in
  listen canvas "wheel" (fun e ->
    let dy = Js.float_of_number (get e "deltaY") in
    wheel := !wheel +. (if int_of e "deltaMode" = 0 then dy /. 40. else dy);
    let steps = truncate !wheel in
    wheel := !wheel -. float_of_int steps;
    for _i = 1 to min 8 (abs steps) do
      TinyMachineDevices.console_type mc.cons
        (String.make 1 (Char.chr (if steps < 0 then 128 else 129)))
    done;
    ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||]));
  (* (the focus by hand: the default, prevented above, would give it) *)
  listen canvas "mousedown" (fun _ -> ignore (call canvas "focus" [||]));
  listen canvas "contextmenu" (fun e -> ignore (call e "preventDefault" [||]))

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen: a canvas *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A canvas's pixel is four bytes, red, green, blue and how opaque: as
 * one word of 32 bits (the browsers' machines being little-endian),
 * the screen's byte is one store, through the table of its 256 colours *)
type screen = {
  context : U.any;
  picture : U.any;
  words : U.any;
  palette : int array;
  mutable shown : string;
}

let screen_open canvas =
  let context = call canvas "getContext" [| str "2d" |] in
  let picture =
    call context "createImageData"
      [| U.inject TinyMachineDevices.width;
         U.inject TinyMachineDevices.height |] in
  let words =
    U.new_obj (get U.global "Uint32Array")
      [| U.inject (get (get picture "data") "buffer") |] in
  let c k = Char.code TinyMachineDevices.colours.[k] in
  let palette =
    Array.init 256 (fun i ->
      (255 lsl 24) lor (c ((3 * i) + 2) lsl 16) lor (c ((3 * i) + 1) lsl 8)
      lor c (3 * i)) in
  { context; picture; words; palette; shown = "" }

let screen_show s (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) =
  let n = TinyMachineDevices.width * TinyMachineDevices.height in
  let pixels = Bytes.sub_string m.mem TinyMachineDevices.screen n in
  if pixels <> s.shown then begin
    s.shown <- pixels;
    let any = ref 0 in
    for i = 0 to n - 1 do
      let c = Char.code (String.unsafe_get pixels i) in
      any := !any lor c;
      U.set s.words i s.palette.(c)
    done;
    lit := !any <> 0;
    ignore
      (call s.context "putImageData"
         [| U.inject s.picture; U.inject 0; U.inject 0 |])
  end

(* an address's answer, whatever its status: the response and its
 * bytes; k with None if there is none *)
let fetch_response name k =
  let failed _ = k None in
  let got response =
    let bytes buffer =
      k (Some (response,
               Js_of_ocaml.Typed_array.String.of_arrayBuffer buffer)) in
    ignore
      (call (call response "arrayBuffer" [||]) "then"
         [| U.inject (Js.wrap_callback bytes);
            U.inject (Js.wrap_callback failed) |]) in
  ignore
    (call (call U.global "fetch" [| str name |]) "then"
       [| U.inject (Js.wrap_callback got); U.inject (Js.wrap_callback failed) |])

(* a file from beside the page, its bytes; k with None if it is not there *)
let fetch name k =
  fetch_response name (function
    | Some (response, bytes) when Js.to_bool (get response "ok") ->
        k (Some bytes)
    | _ -> k None)

(* a response as HTTP's, for www: its status and its Content-Type (the
 * headers a page may read of another site's, CORS's safe ones) *)
let http_answer response bytes =
  let kind : Js.js_string Js.t Js.opt =
    call (get response "headers") "get" [| str "content-type" |] in
  TinyBrowserHttp.response (get response "status")
    (Js.Opt.case kind (fun () -> [])
       (fun k -> [ "Content-Type", Js.to_string k ]))
    bytes

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The network: the wire's other end is the page *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* What the machine's wire leads to (TinyMachinePeer: tiny-kernel's own
 * stack, by OCaml, with its answers to a ping and to port 70). The
 * page gives it its documents, which is where the Internet comes in:
 * a name is a file beside the page (get); "GET address HTTP/1.0" a web
 * page for tiny-kernel's browser, and "img w h address" a picture of
 * it. The machine speaks IL to this end of its wire, and this end asks
 * the Internet as a page may: by fetch, from the sites that allow it.
 * Names, TLS, HTTP, JSON and a picture's format are the browser's. *)

(* a picture loaded by the browser, at the size [size] gives from its
 * own (w and h), drawn on a canvas that is not shown and read back, a
 * byte a pixel, each the nearest of the screen's 256 colours (no
 * dithering). k with its width, its height, its rows; None if it
 * cannot be had *)
let picture_sized url size k =
  let img = U.new_obj (get U.global "Image") [||] in
  U.set img (Js.string "crossOrigin") (Js.string "anonymous");
  listen img "error" (fun _ -> k None);
  listen img "load" (fun _ ->
    let iw : int = get img "naturalWidth"
    and ih : int = get img "naturalHeight" in
    if iw <= 0 || ih <= 0 then k None
    else begin
      let w, h = size iw ih in
      let canvas = call document "createElement" [| str "canvas" |] in
      U.set canvas (Js.string "width") w; U.set canvas (Js.string "height") h;
      let context = call canvas "getContext" [| str "2d" |] in
      (* (white under a picture with holes) *)
      U.set context (Js.string "fillStyle") (Js.string "white");
      ignore
        (call context "fillRect"
           [| U.inject 0; U.inject 0; U.inject w; U.inject h |]);
      ignore
        (call context "drawImage"
           [| U.inject img; U.inject 0; U.inject 0; U.inject w; U.inject h |]);
      match
        (try
           Some
             (get
                (call context "getImageData"
                   [| U.inject 0; U.inject 0; U.inject w; U.inject h |])
                "data")
         with _ -> None)
      with
      | None -> k None
      | Some data ->
          let at i : int = U.get data i in
          k (Some (w, h,
                   String.init (w * h) (fun i ->
                     Char.chr
                       (TinyMachineDevices.nearest (at (4 * i))
                          (at ((4 * i) + 1)) (at ((4 * i) + 2))))))
    end);
  U.set img (Js.string "src") (Js.string url)

(* The files the machine put (put): in the browser's storage, under
 * tiny-machine/ and their name, so that they are there when the page
 * is loaded again, which is a stop of the machine. Bytes as they are:
 * a byte a character of the stored string (Js.bytestring). *)
let storage () = get U.global "localStorage"
let stored_key name = "tiny-machine/" ^ name

let store name bytes =
  if name = "" || name.[0] = '.' || String.contains name '/' then
    "a name has no / and no . first"
  else
    try
      ignore
        (call (storage ()) "setItem"
           [| str (stored_key name); U.inject (Js.bytestring bytes) |]);
      ""
    with _ -> "this page's browser keeps no more"

let stored name : string option =
  let v : Js.js_string Js.t Js.opt =
    call (storage ()) "getItem" [| str (stored_key name) |] in
  Option.map Js.to_bytestring (Js.Opt.to_option v)

(* the names put, sorted *)
let stored_names () =
  let st = storage () in
  let n : int = get st "length" in
  let prefix = stored_key "" in
  let p = String.length prefix in
  List.init n (fun i -> Js.to_string (call st "key" [| U.inject i |]))
  |> List.filter (fun k -> String.length k > p && String.sub k 0 p = prefix)
  |> List.map (fun k -> String.sub k p (String.length k - p))
  |> List.sort compare

(* a line's document: the messages given to [messages], when they are
 * there. [www] is where the page's own documents are.
 * "GET address HTTP/1.0" is a web page for tiny-kernel's browser,
 * fetched by this page (Wikipedia's REST HTML allows it; a site that
 * does not allow other pages to fetch it, by CORS, cannot be reached
 * from here) and answered as HTTP's response; if the fetch fails, a
 * kept copy beside the page answers *)
let peer_document www line messages =
  let name ok =
    if line = "" || line.[0] = '.' || String.contains line '/' then None
    else Some ok in
  match TinyMachinePeer.www_picture_request line with
  | Some (w, h, url) ->
    (* a page's picture at the size asked; a kept copy beside the page
     * when the site does not allow this page to read its pictures *)
    let answer = function
      | Some (w, h, pixels) ->
          messages (TinyMachinePeer.picture "" w h pixels)
      | None -> messages (TinyMachinePeer.picture "" 0 0 "") in
    if w = 0 then answer None
    else
      picture_sized url (fun _ _ -> w, h) (function
        | Some p -> answer (Some p)
        | None ->
            match TinyMachinePeer.www_picture_kept url with
            | Some name ->
                picture_sized (www ^ name) (fun _ _ -> w, h) answer
            | None -> answer None)
  | None ->
  if TinyMachinePeer.www_request line <> None then begin
    let url = Option.get (TinyMachinePeer.www_request line) in
    let failed () =
      messages
        (TinyMachinePeer.messages
           (TinyMachinePeer.www_failed
              ("www: " ^ url ^ ": not reached\n(no network, or the site "
               ^ "does not allow a web page to fetch it)\n"))) in
    fetch_response url (function
      | Some (response, bytes) ->
          messages (TinyMachinePeer.messages (http_answer response bytes))
      | None ->
          match TinyMachinePeer.www_kept url with
          | Some kept ->
              fetch (www ^ kept) (function
                | Some page ->
                    messages
                      (TinyMachinePeer.messages
                         (TinyMachinePeer.www_kept_response kept page))
                | None -> failed ())
          | None -> failed ())
  end
  (* the empty line, Gopher's menu: what was put *)
  else if line = "" then
    messages
      (TinyMachinePeer.messages
         (String.concat "" (List.map (fun n -> n ^ "\n") (stored_names ()))))
  else
    match name line, stored line with
    | _, Some text -> messages (TinyMachinePeer.messages text)
    | None, None -> messages [ "get: no " ^ line ^ "\n" ]
    | Some name, None ->
        fetch (www ^ name) (function
          | Some text -> messages (TinyMachinePeer.messages text)
          | None -> messages [ "get: no " ^ name ^ "\n" ])

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The wire, drawn *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A network does not show itself as a screen does. So the page draws
 * the wire: the machine at the left, this page's end at the right, a
 * dot for each packet, which crosses in half a second of the page's
 * time (the packet itself took 5 ms of the machine's: too fast to
 * see), and falls when it is lost; under it, each packet's line, as
 * tiny-machine -net-trace says it. A page without these elements has
 * the network all the same. *)
type dot = {
  born : float;
  to_machine : bool;
  lost : bool;
  colour : string;
}

let dots = ref []
let lost = ref 0
let wire_lines = ref []
let wire_changed = ref false
let crossing = 500.

let wire_said dir packet =
  let line = TinyMachinePeer.net_describe packet in
  (* (without ", from 10.0.0.2 to 10.0.0.1": the direction says it) *)
  let line =
    if String.length line > 27
       && String.sub line (String.length line - 27) 7 = ", from "
    then String.sub line 0 (String.length line - 27)
    else line in
  let starts p = String.starts_with p line in
  let colour =
    if dir = "x" then "#cc0000"
    else if starts "data" then "#0055aa"
    else if starts "query" || starts "state" then "#dd8800"
    else if starts "echo" then "#222222"
    else if starts "ack" then "#999999"
    else "#228822" in
  dots :=
    { born = now (); to_machine = dir <> ">"; lost = dir = "x"; colour }
    :: !dots;
  (* the button says how many it lost *)
  if dir = "x" then begin
    incr lost;
    let button = element "lose" in
    if present button then
      U.set button (Js.string "textContent")
        (Js.string
           (Printf.sprintf "lose the next packet (%d lost so far)" !lost))
  end;
  wire_lines :=
    (dir ^ " " ^ line)
    :: (match !wire_lines with
        | a :: b :: c :: d :: e :: f :: g :: _ -> [ a; b; c; d; e; f; g ]
        | l -> l);
  wire_changed := true

let wire_show () =
  let canvas = element "wire" in
  if present canvas then begin
    let t = now () in
    let was = !dots <> [] in
    dots := List.filter (fun d -> t -. d.born < crossing) !dots;
    if was || !wire_changed then begin
      let c = call canvas "getContext" [| str "2d" |] in
      let set name v = U.set c (Js.string name) (Js.string v) in
      let w : int = get canvas "width" and h : int = get canvas "height" in
      ignore
        (call c "clearRect"
           [| U.inject 0; U.inject 0; U.inject w; U.inject h |]);
      set "strokeStyle" "#444444"; set "fillStyle" "#444444";
      set "font" "12px sans-serif";
      ignore (call c "beginPath" [||]);
      ignore (call c "moveTo" [| U.inject 100; U.inject 20 |]);
      ignore (call c "lineTo" [| U.inject (w - 130); U.inject 20 |]);
      ignore (call c "stroke" [||]);
      ignore
        (call c "fillText" [| str "the machine"; U.inject 4; U.inject 18 |]);
      ignore
        (call c "fillText" [| str "10.0.0.2"; U.inject 4; U.inject 34 |]);
      ignore
        (call c "fillText"
           [| str "this page: the Internet"; U.inject (w - 126);
              U.inject 18 |]);
      ignore
        (call c "fillText"
           [| str "10.0.0.1"; U.inject (w - 126); U.inject 34 |]);
      List.iter (fun d ->
        let f = (t -. d.born) /. crossing in
        let along = if d.lost then Float.min f 0.5 else f in
        let along = if d.to_machine then 1. -. along else along in
        let x = 100. +. (along *. float_of_int (w - 230)) in
        let y =
          if d.lost && f > 0.5 then
            20. +. ((f -. 0.5) *. 2. *. float_of_int (h - 24))
          else 20. in
        set "fillStyle" d.colour;
        ignore (call c "beginPath" [||]);
        ignore
          (call c "arc"
             [| U.inject x; U.inject y; U.inject 4; U.inject 0;
                U.inject 6.3 |]);
        ignore (call c "fill" [||])) !dots
    end;
    if !wire_changed then begin
      wire_changed := false;
      let log = element "wirelog" in
      if present log then
        U.set log (Js.string "textContent")
          (Js.string (String.concat "\n" (List.rev !wire_lines)))
    end
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The loop: a frame's instructions, then what is shown *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the milliseconds of a frame the machine may take *)
let budget = 12.

let run image disk www =
  let on_open (k : TinyMachineDevices.console) = k.opened <- true in
  (* the wire's other end, which gives packets to the machine it is
   * called by: by a reference *)
  let machine = ref None in
  let give after packet =
    Option.iter (fun mc -> TinyMachineDevices.net_give mc ~after packet)
      !machine in
  let peer =
    TinyMachinePeer.create ~give ~said:wire_said
      ~document:(peer_document www) ~store ~outside:None in
  let mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine =
    TinyMachineDevices.create ~put ~on_open
      ~send:(Some (TinyMachinePeer.send peer)) ~hear:ignore ~disk ~events:None
      image in
  machine := Some mc;
  (* the page's button: the peer's next packet is lost *)
  let button = element "lose" in
  if present button then
    listen button "click" (fun _ -> TinyMachinePeer.lose peer 1);
  let env = TinyMachineDevices.env mc in
  let canvas = element "screen" in
  let screen = screen_open canvas in
  listen_keys mc; listen_mouse mc canvas;
  text_changed := true;
  let last = ref (now ()) and running = ref true in
  (* the speed shown: the instructions and the time since it was said *)
  let done_ = ref 0 and since = ref (now ()) in
  (* the mouse's look a program asked for (www over a link): the
   * canvas's *)
  let cursor = ref 0 in
  let rec frame _ =
    let start = now () in
    (* a quarter of a second at most: a page left and come back to *)
    let due =
      truncate
        (float_of_int !TinyMachineDevices.rate
         *. Float.min 0.25 ((start -. !last) /. 1000.)) in
    last := start;
    (try
       let n = ref 0 in
       while !n < due && now () -. start < budget do
         TinyMachineDevices.ticks mc env (min 4096 (due - !n));
         n := !n + min 4096 (due - !n)
       done;
       done_ := !done_ + !n
     with
     | TinyMachineDevices.Halt code ->
         running := false;
         status
           (Printf.sprintf
              "the machine halted (%d); reload the page to boot it again"
              code)
     | TinyMachineISA.Error e ->
         running := false; status ("tiny-machine: " ^ e));
    screen_show screen mc.cpu; show_text (); wire_show ();
    if mc.mouse.cursor <> !cursor then begin
      cursor := mc.mouse.cursor;
      U.set (get canvas "style") (Js.string "cursor")
        (Js.string (if !cursor = 1 then "pointer" else "default"))
    end;
    if !running then begin
      if start -. !since > 1000. then begin
        (* of the speed the machine is meant to have *)
        let percent =
          truncate
            (100. *. float_of_int !done_
             /. ((start -. !since) /. 1000.
                 *. float_of_int !TinyMachineDevices.rate)) in
        status
          (if percent >= 97 then "Running at full speed."
           else
             Printf.sprintf
               "Running at %d%% of full speed here: everything that much slower."
               percent);
        done_ := 0; since := start
      end;
      ignore
        (call U.global "requestAnimationFrame"
           [| U.inject (Js.wrap_callback frame) |])
    end in
  frame ()

let () =
  let search =
    U.new_obj (get U.global "URLSearchParams")
      [| U.inject (get (get U.global "location") "search") |] in
  let text v =
    Js.Opt.to_option
      (Js.Opt.map (Js.Opt.option (Js.Optdef.to_option v)) Js.to_string) in
  let page = Js.Optdef.to_option (get U.global "tiny_machine") in
  let param name =
    match page with
    | Some o -> text (get o name)
    | None ->
        Js.Opt.to_option
          (Js.Opt.map (call search "get" [| str name |]) Js.to_string) in
  let image = Option.value (param "image") ~default:"boot.img" in
  let missing name =
    status ("tiny-machine: " ^ name ^ " could not be fetched") in
  status ("loading " ^ image);
  fetch image (function
    | None -> missing image
    | Some bytes ->
        (* where the documents of the wire's other end are: beside the
         * image, in www/, unless the page says *)
        let www = match param "www" with
          | Some w -> w
          | None ->
              (match String.rindex_opt image '/' with
               | Some i -> String.sub image 0 (i + 1)
               | None -> "")
              ^ "www/" in
        match param "disk" with
        | None -> run bytes Bytes.empty www
        | Some d ->
            fetch d (function
              | None -> missing d
              | Some disk -> run bytes (Bytes.of_string disk) www))
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachineWeb.mli
4397
(* tiny-machine in a web page (plan_web.md, stage 0): TinyMachineDevices's
 * machine compiled by js_of_ocaml, its screen a canvas, its console
 * the page's text, its keys and its mouse the page's. TinyMachine.ml is
 * the same machine in a terminal. Not a program of t-ix's own tools:
 * OCaml and js_of_ocaml build it (./tiny-machine -web dir tiny-kernel
 * builds the page's directory; TinyMachineWeb.html is the page).
 *
 * The page gives three elements, by their ids: screen (a canvas, 1024
 * by 768), console (the text), status (a line). The kernel's image is
 * fetched: boot.img beside the page, or what the address says
 * (?image=kernel.img&disk=fs.img: t6, whose disk's writes last
 * as long as the page), or, before both, what the page says in a
 * variable of its own, tiny_machine = { image: ..., disk: ... }, each
 * an address (docs/t-ix.html, the website's page: its files are in
 * another place, the assets').
 *
 * The keys are of two kinds, as TinyMachine's are with -window, where
 * a person types in the terminal or in the window. They are a
 * terminal's unless said otherwise: the line is shown on the console
 * as it is typed, a backspace corrects it, and Enter gives it to the
 * machine (a kernel's console echoes nothing, a terminal does). They
 * are the screen's, each byte to the machine as it is typed (a game's
 * arrows, a window's text, which the window system echoes), when the
 * screen was clicked (it then has the page's focus, and the page's
 * style frames it) and a program has drawn on it: on a black screen
 * nothing would show them. (A first version went by where the mouse
 * was: it is over the screen most of the time, and nothing was echoed.)
 *
 * The loop is the browser's: at each frame (requestAnimationFrame) the
 * instructions the time since the last one is worth, at the machine's
 * speed (TinyMachineDevices.rate), and no more than [budget] milliseconds
 * of them, so that a browser too slow for the speed still draws and
 * listens: the machine is then slower, and the status line says so,
 * as a part of the full speed. Then the screen, if it changed, and the
 * console's new text.
 *
 * The machine's wire (plan_tiny_network.md) leads to the page: its
 * other end is TinyMachinePeer, tiny-kernel's own stack run here, and the
 * page gives it its documents, which is where the Internet comes in:
 *
 *  tiny-kernel: www OCaml                this page
 *     | IL, over the wire's packets ===> TinyMachinePeer, port 70: the line
 *     |                                     | "GET address": the page fetched
 *     |                                     |   (Wikipedia's REST HTML)
 *     |                                     | "img w h address": its picture,
 *     |                                     |   read and made small by the
 *     |                                     |   browser, each pixel then the
 *     |                                     |   nearest of the screen's colours
 *  the page drawn, then   <===  IL  ===  its messages; a picture's, a
 *  its pictures a row at                  message a row
 *  each message
 *
 * A name alone (get) is a file fetched from www/ beside the image; a
 * page that cannot be fetched is a copy kept there, if there is one. A page
 * may fetch only from sites that allow it, and Wikipedia does: the
 * machine has no way out but this end of its wire. Three more
 * elements, which a page may leave out: wire (a canvas: a dot for
 * each packet, crossing in half a second of the page's time, falling
 * when lost), wirelog (the last packets, a line each, as
 * tiny-machine -net-trace says them) and lose (a button: the other
 * end's next packet is lost, and it says how many were).
 *
 * Its twin, made after it (plan_web.md's stage 1), is mini-qemu's page
 * (raspberry/web/'s MiniQemuWeb): the Pi 1's board, with the same three
 * elements and the same two kinds of keys. That one needs more to keep
 * up, the instructions run often translated to JavaScript (Jit) and
 * memdraw's general loop run by the emulator for its kernel
 * (Hostdraw), and has no network;
 * tiny-machine's instructions are few and simple, and an interpreter
 * alone runs them at the speed the kernel was made for.
 *
 * An int has 32 bits here (TinyMachineCPU.ult says what that asks). *)

(* A program: it starts when the page has loaded it, and gives nothing
 * to another file. *)
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachineWindow.ml
2449
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyMachineWindow.mli *)

(* what tiny-machine writes: a screen as a PPM, or a line "C n", the
 * mouse's look (0 the arrow, 1 a hand), which a program of the machine
 * chose by writing the mouse's word, or a line "A n" and n bytes, the
 * speaker's samples *)
type input = Screen of int * int * string | Cursor of int | Samples of string

let read_ppm ic =
  match input_line ic with
  | exception End_of_file -> None
  | line when String.length line > 2 && line.[0] = 'C' ->
      Some (Cursor (int_of_string (String.sub line 2 (String.length line - 2))))
  | line when String.length line > 2 && line.[0] = 'A' ->
      Some
        (Samples
           (really_input_string ic
              (int_of_string (String.sub line 2 (String.length line - 2)))))
  | _p6 ->
      let width, height =
        Scanf.sscanf (input_line ic) "%d %d" (fun w h -> w, h) in
      ignore (input_line ic);
      Some (Screen (width, height, really_input_string ic (3 * width * height)))

let () =
  let display = TinyMachineSDL.create ~title:"tiny-machine" in
  let x = ref 0 and y = ref 0 and buttons = ref 0 in
  let keys = TinyMachineSDL.keyboard () in
  let key byte = Printf.printf "k \\%03d\n" byte in
  set_binary_mode_in stdin true;
  try
    while true do
      (* a picture when one is there; the window's events meanwhile *)
      (match Unix.select [ Unix.stdin ] [] [] 0.01 with
       | [], _, _ -> ()
       | _ -> (
           match read_ppm stdin with
           | None -> exit 0
           | Some (Cursor n) -> display.cursor n
           | Some (Samples s) -> display.play s
           | Some (Screen (width, height, pixels)) ->
               display.present width height pixels)
       | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINTR, _, _) -> ());
      let mouse = !x, !y, !buttons and now = Unix.gettimeofday () in
      List.iter (function
        | TinyMachineSDL.Quit -> exit 0
        | TinyMachineSDL.At (ax, ay) -> x := ax; y := ay
        | TinyMachineSDL.Button (b, down) ->
            buttons := if down then !buttons lor b else !buttons land lnot b
        | e -> List.iter key (TinyMachineSDL.typed keys now e))
        (display.poll ());
      Option.iter key (TinyMachineSDL.repeated keys now);
      if (!x, !y, !buttons) <> mouse then
        Printf.printf "m %d %d %d\n" !x !y !buttons;
      flush stdout
    done
  with End_of_file -> ()
tiny/TinyMachine/TinyMachineWindow.mli
2081
(* tiny-machine's window (tiny-machine -window runs it; TinyMachine.ml
 * says why it is a program apart: this one links SDL, by
 * TinyMachineSDL, and that one nothing of C's). It knows nothing of the
 * machine: it shows the pictures it reads on its standard input, each
 * a PPM (P6: a header's three lines, then red, green and blue bytes),
 * and writes what is done in the window on its standard output, an
 * event a line:
 *
 *     m x y buttons    the mouse's place, and its buttons (1 left, 2
 *                      middle, 4 right, as Plan 9's)
 *     k \ddd           a key typed, its byte (a step of the wheel is
 *                      an arrow key, up or down)
 *
 * Between two pictures, a line "C n" sets the mouse's look: 0 the
 * arrow, 1 a hand (a program of the machine wrote it to the mouse's
 * word: www over a link); a line "A n" then n bytes are the speaker's
 * samples since the last, which the window plays (TinyMachineSDL's
 * play).
 *
 * Its input's end, or its window closed, is its end. The window starts
 * at the largest whole number of times the picture that three quarters
 * of the screen's height hold, and can be resized: the picture is
 * drawn as large as fits, and the mouse's place is still in the
 * picture's pixels.
 *
 *     tiny-machine  --- a PPM a frame, on a pipe -->  this program
 *     (no C linked) <-- an event a line, on a pipe --  (SDL)
 *
 * design:
 * A display as a separate program on two pipes costs a megabyte
 * copied a frame and buys three things: tiny-machine stays a program
 * of OCaml alone, built by mini-ml and run where there is no SDL;
 * the events' lines are the same ones a recorded session has
 * (tiny-machine -events), so a test and a person drive the machine
 * the same way; and any program that reads PPMs and writes such
 * lines is a display. It is the shape of Plan 9's terminals and of
 * a web page's canvas (TinyMachineWeb), the picture on one side and
 * what computes it on the other. *)

(* A program: it reads its standard input until its end, and gives
 * nothing to another file. *)
