(*****************************************************************************)
(* The console, a terminal *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let tty (caps : < Cap.stdin; .. >) = Unix.isatty (Console.stdin_fd caps)

(* a ^C of the terminal's, not yet given to the machine. (old: the
 * signal's handler typed it itself; when it came while console_poll
 * was reading, the bytes read replaced the queue it had just been
 * added to, and the ^C was lost: a key typed right after it did that) *)
let interrupted = ref false

let console_open (caps : < Cap.stdin; Cap.signal; .. >)
    (k : TinyMachineDevices.console) =
  if not k.opened then begin
    k.opened <- true;
    if not (tty caps) then (
      k.queue <- Procs.read_all (Console.stdin_fd caps);
      k.eof <- true)
    else
      Sys.set_signal Sys.sigint
        (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> interrupted := true))
  end

(* a terminal's bytes, when some are there *)
let console_poll (caps : < Cap.stdin; .. >) (k : TinyMachineDevices.console) =
  if !interrupted then (
    interrupted := false;
    TinyMachineDevices.console_type k "\003");
  if k.opened && not k.eof && k.next >= String.length k.queue && tty caps then
    match Unix.select [ Console.stdin_fd caps ] [] [] 0.0 with
    | [], _, _ -> ()
    | _ ->
        let b = Bytes.create 256 in
        let n = Unix.read (Console.stdin_fd caps) b 0 256 in
        if n = 0 then k.eof <- true
        else (k.queue <- Bytes.sub_string b 0 n; k.next <- 0)
    | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINTR, _, _) -> ()   (* a ^C meanwhile *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The screen as a file, and in a window *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the screen as a PPM: a header, then red, green and blue bytes, row
 * after row *)
let ppm (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine) =
  let width = TinyMachineDevices.width and height = TinyMachineDevices.height in
  let header = Printf.sprintf "P6\n%d %d\n255\n" width height in
  let h = String.length header in
  let out = Bytes.create (h + (3 * width * height)) in
  Bytes.blit_string header 0 out 0 h;
  for i = 0 to (width * height) - 1 do
    Bytes.blit_string TinyMachineDevices.colours
      (3 * Char.code (Bytes.get m.mem (TinyMachineDevices.screen + i)))
      out (h + (3 * i)) 3
  done;
  Bytes.to_string out

(* a number's 32 bits, the low byte first: a WAV's, a pcap's *)
let le32 v = String.init 4 (fun i -> Char.chr ((v lsr (8 * i)) land 255))

(* the speaker's samples as a WAV: RIFF's header, then 8 bits a sample,
 * which a WAV has unsigned (128 the silence) *)
let wav samples =
  let le16 n = String.init 2 (fun k -> Char.chr ((n lsr (8 * k)) land 255)) in
  let n = String.length samples and hz = TinyMachineDevices.hz in
  "RIFF" ^ le32 (36 + n) ^ "WAVEfmt " ^ le32 16 ^ le16 1 ^ le16 1
  ^ le32 hz ^ le32 hz ^ le16 1 ^ le16 8
  ^ "data" ^ le32 n
  ^ String.map (fun ch -> Char.chr (Char.code ch lxor 128)) samples

(* The host's window (-window) is another program's, tiny-machine-window
 * (TinyMachineWindow.ml), so that this one links no library of C's and
 * is built by ix's tools as by OCaml's: a child, given the screen on
 * its standard input, a PPM each time it changed, and writing the
 * events on its standard output; its end (the window closed) is the
 * machine's. Thirty times a second, by the host's clock: what it shows
 * is not the machine's time's, only what it types and points is.
 *
 * With a window, the machine also has a speed: it runs
 * TinyMachineDevices.rate instructions a second, which must be below
 * what the host can do. The machine's time is counted in instructions,
 * so without a fixed speed a game's pieces would fall as fast as the
 * host happens to be, faster when nothing else runs. The machine sleeps
 * when it is ahead ([due] is the host's time at which the instructions
 * run so far should be done), and it does not hurry to catch up when
 * it is behind. A recorded session has no window and never waits. The
 * kernel reads the rate from the machine and makes its tick 2.5 ms long
 * whatever the speed. So on a faster machine, a program paced by ticks
 * (a game) keeps its pace, and a program that computes (the browser)
 * finishes sooner. *)
type window = {
  to_w : Unix.file_descr; from_w : Unix.file_descr; mutable shown : string;
  mutable frame : float; mutable partial : string;
  mutable cursor : int; heard : Buffer.t;
  mutable due : float;
  now : unit -> float; sleep : float -> unit;  (* the clock, window_open's *)
}

let window_open
    (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal; Cap.clock; .. >) =
  let screen_r, to_w = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true ()
  and from_w, events_w = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true () in
  (* beside this program, by its installed name or by dune's *)
  let name =
    if Filename.check_suffix Sys.executable_name ".exe" then
      "TinyMachine/TinyMachineWindow.exe"
    else "tiny-machine-window" in
  ignore (Procs.spawn caps
    (Filename.concat (Filename.dirname Sys.executable_name) name) []
    ~stdin:screen_r ~stdout:events_w);
  Unix.close screen_r; Unix.close events_w;
  (* the window closed while a screen is written: its end is read next *)
  Sys.set_signal Sys.sigpipe Sys.Signal_ignore;
  { to_w; from_w; shown = ""; frame = 0.; partial = ""; cursor = 0;
    heard = Buffer.create 4096; due = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps ();
    now = CapUnix.gettimeofday caps; sleep = CapUnix.sleepf caps }

(* every [polled] instructions *)
let polled = 0x10000
let window_poll w (m : TinyMachineCPU.machine)
    (ms : TinyMachineDevices.mouse) k =
  let now = w.now () in
  w.due <-
    w.due +. (float_of_int polled /. float_of_int !TinyMachineDevices.rate);
  if w.due > now then w.sleep (w.due -. now)
  else if now -. w.due > 0.1 then w.due <- now;
  let now = w.now () in
  if now -. w.frame > 1. /. 30. then begin
    w.frame <- now;
    let pixels =
      Bytes.sub_string m.mem TinyMachineDevices.screen
        (TinyMachineDevices.width * TinyMachineDevices.height) in
    if pixels <> w.shown then (
      w.shown <- pixels;
      Procs.write_all w.to_w (ppm m));
    (* the mouse's look, when a program changed it *)
    if ms.cursor <> w.cursor then begin
      w.cursor <- ms.cursor;
      Procs.write_all w.to_w (Printf.sprintf "C %d\n" ms.cursor)
    end;
    (* the speaker's samples since the last picture: a line "A n", then
     * the n bytes *)
    if Buffer.length w.heard > 0 then begin
      Procs.write_all w.to_w
        (Printf.sprintf "A %d\n%s" (Buffer.length w.heard)
           (Buffer.contents w.heard));
      Buffer.clear w.heard
    end;
    match Unix.select [ w.from_w ] [] [] 0.0 with
    | [], _, _ -> ()
    | _ ->
        let b = Bytes.create 4096 in
        let n = Unix.read w.from_w b 0 4096 in
        if n = 0 then raise (TinyMachineDevices.Halt 0);
        (match
           String.split_on_char '\n' (w.partial ^ Bytes.sub_string b 0 n)
         with
         | [] -> ()
         | lines ->
             let rec go = function
               | [ last ] -> w.partial <- last
               | l :: rest -> TinyMachineDevices.event ms k l; go rest
               | [] -> () in
             go lines)
    | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINTR, _, _) -> ()
  end

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The loop: the hosts' turns, then the machine's instruction *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type options = {
  disk_file : string option; screen_file : string option;
  audio_file : string option; events_file : string option; window : bool;
  rate : int option; date : int option; seed : int option;
  net_loop : int option; net : string option; net_trace : bool;
  net_lose : int list; net_out : bool; net_forward : (int * int) list;
  net_pcap : string option; prof : string option; cores : int;
  parallel : bool }

(* The way out (TinyMachineSocket.mli): a connection of the host's is
 * a program run beside this one, tiny-machine-socket, its bytes on two
 * pipes: no socket here. What it says first (+ or -) is whether there
 * is a connection; a relay is then the pipes, as TinyMachinePeer wants
 * them. The ones that ended are waited for when the next one starts. *)
let helpers = ref []

let helper (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal; .. >)
    args =
  helpers := List.filter (fun pid ->
      match CapUnix.waitpid caps [ Unix.WNOHANG ] pid with
      | 0, _ -> true
      | _ -> false
      | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false) !helpers;
  let in_r, to_ = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true ()
  and from, out_w = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true () in
  let name =
    if Filename.check_suffix Sys.executable_name ".exe" then
      "TinyMachine/TinyMachineSocket.exe"
    else "tiny-machine-socket" in
  helpers :=
    Procs.spawn caps
      (Filename.concat (Filename.dirname Sys.executable_name) name) args
      ~stdin:in_r ~stdout:out_w
    :: !helpers;
  Unix.close in_r; Unix.close out_w;
  Sys.set_signal Sys.sigpipe Sys.Signal_ignore;
  to_, from

(* what it wrote, if it wrote: None when nothing waits, "" at its end *)
let helper_read from wait =
  match Unix.select [ from ] [] [] wait with
  | [], _, _ -> None
  | _ ->
      let b = Bytes.create 4096 in
      Some (Bytes.sub_string b 0 (Unix.read from b 0 4096))
  | exception Unix.Unix_error (Unix.EINTR, _, _) -> None

(* [first]: the bytes that came with the helper's + (a client's
 * request is often there before the + is read) *)
let helper_relay (to_, from) first : TinyMachinePeer.relay =
  let first = ref first in
  { take = (fun () ->
      if !first <> "" then (let bytes = !first in first := ""; Some bytes)
      else
        match helper_read from 0. with
        | None -> Some ""
        | Some "" -> None
        | Some bytes -> Some bytes);
    put = (fun bytes ->
      try Procs.write_all to_ bytes with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
    shut = (fun () -> Unix.close to_; Unix.close from) }

(* what the helper said first, if it has: a relay when it is +, its
 * pipes closed when it is not *)
let helper_said pipes wait =
  match helper_read (snd pipes) wait with
  | None -> None
  | Some bytes when bytes <> "" && bytes.[0] = '+' ->
      Some (Some (helper_relay pipes
        (String.sub bytes 1 (String.length bytes - 1))))
  | Some _ -> (helper_relay pipes "").shut (); Some None

(* -net-out, for "GET address HTTP/1.0": a web page fetched by
 * tiny-machine-fetch, a program beside this one (it links ix's TLS and
 * HTTP), whose output is the answer, HTTP's response. The machine waits
 * meanwhile, which changes nothing of its time. None when the helper could not fetch it (no network, no
 * such host): then its output is a line that says why. *)
let fetch (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.pipe; .. >) args =
  let in_r, in_w = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true ()
  and from, out_w = CapUnix.pipe caps ~cloexec:true () in
  let name =
    if Filename.check_suffix Sys.executable_name ".exe" then
      "TinyMachine/TinyMachineFetch.exe"
    else "tiny-machine-fetch" in
  let pid =
    Procs.spawn caps
      (Filename.concat (Filename.dirname Sys.executable_name) name) args
      ~stdin:in_r ~stdout:out_w in
  Unix.close in_r; Unix.close in_w; Unix.close out_w;
  let out = Procs.read_all from in
  Unix.close from;
  match CapUnix.waitpid caps [] pid with
  | _, Unix.WEXITED 0 -> Ok out
  | _ -> Error out

(* -net-out: a connection to an address and a port, if there is one in
 * the five seconds the helper tries for (the machine waits meanwhile);
 * a name's address, as text *)
let outside caps : TinyMachinePeer.outside =
  { connect = (fun address port ->
      let pipes = helper caps [ "dial"; address; string_of_int port ] in
      match helper_said pipes 10. with
      | Some relay -> relay
      | None -> (helper_relay pipes "").shut (); None);
    name = (fun name ->
      let to_, from = helper caps [ "name"; name ] in
      let answer =
        match helper_read from 10. with
        | Some line -> String.trim line
        | None -> "" in
      Unix.close to_; Unix.close from;
      answer) }

(* pcap: a capture's header (the magic, version 2.4, a packet's 65,535
 * bytes at most, link type 101: raw IP), and a packet after its time
 * (seconds, microseconds) and its length twice, all little-endian:
 * what tcpdump -r and Wireshark read *)
let pcap_header =
  le32 0xa1b2c3d4 ^ "\002\000\004\000" ^ le32 0 ^ le32 0 ^ le32 65535
  ^ le32 101
let pcap_packet instructions packet =
  let us =
    int_of_float (float_of_int instructions *. 1e6
                  /. float_of_int !TinyMachineDevices.rate) in
  le32 (us / 1000000) ^ le32 (us mod 1000000) ^ le32 (String.length packet)
  ^ le32 (String.length packet) ^ packet

(* The speed with a window, in instructions per second, when -rate does
 * not say. A host that cannot keep up just runs as fast as it can: a
 * 2.2 GHz Neoverse ran the native machine at 22 million a second, an
 * M3 Pro at 50 to 66 (plan_tiny_web.md, tests/TinyMachine_bench.sh). *)
let window_rate = 20_000_000

let run caps o image =
  TinyMachineDevices.rate :=
    (match o.rate with
     | Some r -> r
     | None ->
         if o.window then window_rate else TinyMachineDevices.default_rate);
  (* (946684800: 2000-01-01 in Unix's seconds) *)
  TinyMachineDevices.date :=
    (match o.date with
     | Some d -> d
     | None -> int_of_float (Unix.time ()) - 946684800);
  TinyMachineDevices.seed := (match o.seed with Some s -> s | None -> 0);
  TinyMachineDevices.cores := o.cores;
  let disk_file = o.disk_file in
  (* the disk: the file's, or a blank one of 8 MB when there is no such
   * file; each block the kernel writes, written to it at once *)
  let disk = match disk_file with
    | Some f when Sys.file_exists f ->
        Bytes.of_string (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f))
    | Some f ->
        let blank = Bytes.make (8 * 1024 * 1024) '\000' in
        FS.write caps (Fpath.v f) (Bytes.to_string blank);
        blank
    | None -> Bytes.empty in
  let disk_fd =
    Option.map (fun f -> Unix.openfile f [ Unix.O_WRONLY ] 0) disk_file in
  (* a session's keys are the console's input: the host's is then not
   * read, and a session's last event is its end. A window's keys are
   * the console's too, with the host's: a kernel that writes on the
   * console and not yet on the screen is typed at where it answers *)
  let events =
    Option.map (fun f ->
        TinyMachineDevices.timed_events (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f)))
      o.events_file in
  let stdin_keys = events = None in
  let put ch =
    Console.print caps (String.make 1 ch);
    flush (Console.stdout caps) in
  (* the wire's other end: with -net-loop, the wire itself, coming back.
   * [send] is called by the machine it gives packets to: by a reference *)
  let machine = ref None in
  let give after packet =
    Option.iter (fun mc -> TinyMachineDevices.net_give mc ~after packet)
      !machine in
  (* -net-trace: a packet's line, with the machine's time in its ms *)
  let said dir packet =
    if o.net_trace then
      Option.iter (fun (mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine) ->
        Console.eprint caps
          (Printf.sprintf "%9.1f ms  %s %s\n"
             (float_of_int mc.csr.(TinyMachineDevices.time) *. 1000.
              /. float_of_int !TinyMachineDevices.rate)
             dir (TinyMachinePeer.net_describe packet))) !machine in
  (* -net dir: the peer (TinyMachinePeer: TinyKernelNetwork.ml as the kernel
   * has it, at the other address), its documents the directory's files by
   * their names, no path; -net-lose: which of its packets are lost *)
  let document dir line messages =
    let file name =
      if name = "" || name.[0] = '.' || String.contains name '/' then None
      else FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (Filename.concat dir name)) in
    (* "GET address HTTP/1.0": a web page for tiny-kernel's browser. With
     * -net-out it is fetched; without, or when the fetch fails, a kept
     * copy in dir (OCaml.html) answers. *)
    match TinyMachinePeer.www_request line with
    | Some url ->
      let kept () =
        Option.bind (TinyMachinePeer.www_kept url) (fun name ->
          Option.map (TinyMachinePeer.www_kept_response name) (file name)) in
      let page =
        if o.net_out then
          match fetch caps [ url ] with
          | Ok answer -> answer
          | Error why ->
              (match kept () with
               | Some answer -> answer
               | None -> TinyMachinePeer.www_failed why)
        else
          match kept () with
          | Some answer -> answer
          | None ->
              TinyMachinePeer.www_failed
                ("www: " ^ url ^ ":\nno copy kept in " ^ dir
                 ^ " (with -net-out, tiny-machine fetches it)\n") in
      messages (TinyMachinePeer.messages page)
    | None ->
    (* "img w h address": a picture of a page, w by h, in the machine's
     * colours: the helper decodes it, the address's (with -net-out) or
     * a kept copy in dir *)
    match TinyMachinePeer.www_picture_request line with
    | Some (w, h, url) ->
      let none = TinyMachinePeer.picture "" 0 0 "" in
      let decode source =
        match fetch caps [ "-picture"; string_of_int w;
                           string_of_int h; source ] with
        | Ok pixels when String.length pixels = w * h ->
            Some (TinyMachinePeer.picture "" w h pixels)
        | _ -> None in
      let kept () = match TinyMachinePeer.www_picture_kept url with
        | Some name when Sys.file_exists (Filename.concat dir name) ->
            decode (Filename.concat dir name)
        | _ -> None in
      messages
        (if w = 0 then none
         else match (if o.net_out then decode url else None) with
           | Some l -> l
           | None -> (match kept () with Some l -> l | None -> none))
    | None ->
    (* the empty line, Gopher's menu: dir's files, a name a line *)
    if line = "" then
      messages (TinyMachinePeer.messages
        (String.concat "" (List.map (fun n -> n ^ "\n")
          (List.filter (fun n ->
               n.[0] <> '.'
               && not (Sys.is_directory (Filename.concat dir n)))
             (List.sort compare (Array.to_list (Sys.readdir dir)))))))
    else
      messages (match file line with
        | Some text -> TinyMachinePeer.messages text
        | None -> [ "get: no " ^ line ^ "\n" ]) in
  (* put: a file the machine keeps in dir, so that it outlives it; a
   * name only, as get's *)
  let store dir name bytes =
    if name = "" || name.[0] = '.' || String.contains name '/' then
      "a name has no / and no . first"
    else
      try FS.write caps (Fpath.v (Filename.concat dir name)) bytes; ""
      with Sys_error why | Failure why -> why in
  (* -net-pcap: the packets that crossed, written at the halt *)
  let capture = Buffer.create 4096 in
  let said dir packet =
    said dir packet;
    if o.net_pcap <> None && dir <> "x" then
      Option.iter (fun (mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine) ->
          Buffer.add_string capture
            (pcap_packet mc.csr.(TinyMachineDevices.time) packet))
        !machine in
  let peer = match o.net_loop, o.net with
    | None, Some dir ->
        let peer =
          TinyMachinePeer.create ~give ~said ~document:(document dir)
            ~store:(store dir)
            ~outside:(if o.net_out then Some (outside caps) else None) in
        List.iter (TinyMachinePeer.lose peer) o.net_lose;
        Some peer
    | _ -> None in
  let send = match o.net_loop, peer with
    | Some after, _ -> Some (give after)
    | None, Some peer -> Some (TinyMachinePeer.send peer)
    | None, None -> None in
  (* -net-forward 8080:80: a helper listens on the host's port 8080
   * for the whole run; for each connection it says two named pipes, a
   * line, and the peer dials the machine's port 80 with them as the
   * other side. One that cannot listen is said and dropped. old: a
   * helper a connection, another started when its was seen: one made
   * in between refused *)
  let waiting =
    ref (List.map (fun (host, port) ->
             host, port, helper caps [ "listen"; string_of_int host ], ref "")
           o.net_forward) in
  let forwards peer =
    waiting := List.filter_map (fun ((host, port, pipes, part) as w) ->
      let rec lines = function
        | [] -> Some w
        | [ rest ] -> part := rest; Some w
        | line :: more ->
            match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
            | [ "+" ] -> lines more
            | [ inp; out ] ->
                let opened f how = Unix.openfile f [ how; Unix.O_CLOEXEC ] 0 in
                let to_ = opened inp Unix.O_WRONLY in
                let from = opened out Unix.O_RDONLY in
                TinyMachinePeer.dial peer port (helper_relay (to_, from) "");
                lines more
            | _ ->
                Console.eprint caps
                  (Printf.sprintf "tiny-machine: -net-forward: %s %d\n"
                     "cannot listen on the host's port" host);
                (helper_relay pipes "").shut ();
                None in
      match helper_read (snd pipes) 0. with
      | None -> Some w
      | Some "" -> lines [ "-"; "" ]
      | Some bytes -> lines (String.split_on_char '\n' (!part ^ bytes)))
      !waiting in
  (* the speaker's samples: to the window, and kept for -audio *)
  let window = if o.window then Some (window_open caps) else None in
  let recorded = Buffer.create 0 in
  let listening = window <> None || o.audio_file <> None in
  let hear samples =
    Option.iter (fun w -> Buffer.add_string w.heard samples) window;
    (* -audio's from the first sound (and to the last, at the halt): the
     * silence before it is the boot's length, the one after it the
     * time to the halt, both moving with the kernel's code (old: from
     * the speaker's start to the halt, make check's korobeiniki.wav
     * another file at each change of the kernel) *)
    if o.audio_file <> None then begin
      let rec silent i =
        if i < String.length samples && samples.[i] = '\000' then
          silent (i + 1)
        else i in
      let i = if Buffer.length recorded > 0 then 0 else silent 0 in
      Buffer.add_substring recorded samples i (String.length samples - i)
    end in
  let mc : TinyMachineDevices.machine =
    TinyMachineDevices.create ~put ~on_open:(console_open caps) ~send ~hear
      ~disk ~events image in
  machine := Some mc;
  Option.iter (fun fd -> mc.disk.wrote <- (fun b ->
    ignore (Unix.lseek fd (b * TinyMachineDevices.bsize) Unix.SEEK_SET);
    ignore (Unix.write fd disk (b * TinyMachineDevices.bsize)
              TinyMachineDevices.bsize))) disk_fd;
  let m = mc.cpu and c = mc.csr in
  let env = TinyMachineDevices.env mc in
  (* -prof f: each instruction counted by where it was (the kernel's or
   * a program's, and which program: its window's base), into f at the
   * end, for tiny-prof *)
  let profile = TinyMachineCPU.profile () in
  let env = match o.prof with
    | None -> env
    | Some f ->
        at_exit (fun () ->
          FS.write caps (Fpath.v f) (TinyMachineCPU.profile_lines profile));
        (* and when killed, as by timeout: what ran so far (tiny-ml on
         * tiny-kernel, a run of minutes) *)
        Sys.set_signal Sys.sigterm (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> exit 1));
        TinyMachineCPU.profiled env profile (fun _ ->
          if TinyMachineDevices.supervisor mc then 1, 0
          else 0, TinyMachineDevices.window_base mc) in
  (* the other cores (-cores): in turns, a slice of each after core 0's
   * in this loop; or, asked and where OCaml has domains, each on its
   * own, a slice after another until one fails or core 0 halts *)
  let others =
    List.init (o.cores - 1) (fun k ->
      let h = TinyMachineDevices.core mc (k + 1) in
      h, TinyMachineDevices.env h) in
  let parallel = o.parallel && others <> [] && Parallel.available in
  if o.parallel && not Parallel.available then
    Console.eprint caps
      "tiny-machine: -cores-parallel: no domains in this OCaml; in turns\n";
  let failed = Atomic.make None in
  if parallel then
    List.iter (fun (h, env) ->
      Parallel.spawn (fun () ->
        try
          while Atomic.get failed = None do
            TinyMachineDevices.ticks h env 1024
          done
        with e -> ignore (Atomic.compare_and_set failed None (Some e))))
      others;
  (* each core's instructions, with several: how many of them were a
   * program's, the kernel's, idle (on the standard error) *)
  let spent () =
    List.iteri (fun k (h : TinyMachineDevices.machine) ->
      let u = h.spent.(0) and s = h.spent.(1) and i = h.spent.(2) in
      let all = max 1 (u + s + i) in
      let pc v = 100 * v / all in
      Console.eprint caps
        (Printf.sprintf
           "tiny-machine: core %d: %.1f M instructions: programs %d%%, \
            kernel %d%%, idle %d%%\n"
           k (float_of_int all /. 1e6) (pc u) (pc s) (pc i)))
      (mc :: List.map fst others) in
  let halted n =
    ignore (Atomic.compare_and_set failed None (Some Exit));
    if others <> [] then spent ();
    Option.iter (fun f -> FS.write caps (Fpath.v f) (ppm m)) o.screen_file;
    Option.iter (fun f ->
      TinyMachineDevices.speaker_hear mc;
      let sound = Buffer.contents recorded in
      let rec last i =
        if i > 0 && sound.[i - 1] = '\000' then last (i - 1) else i in
      FS.write caps (Fpath.v f)
        (wav (String.sub sound 0 (last (String.length sound)))))
      o.audio_file;
    Option.iter (fun f ->
        FS.write caps (Fpath.v f) (pcap_header ^ Buffer.contents capture))
      o.net_pcap;
    (* (the helpers that wait for a connection: their input's end is
     * theirs) *)
    List.iter (fun (_, _, pipes, _) -> (helper_relay pipes "").shut ()) !waiting;
    n in
  try
    while true do
      (* the hosts' turns, by the time this instruction will be *)
      let t = c.(TinyMachineDevices.time) + 1 in
      if stdin_keys && t land 1023 = 0 then console_poll caps mc.cons;
      if t land (polled - 1) = 0 && listening then
        TinyMachineDevices.speaker_hear mc;
      if t land (polled - 1) = 0 then
        Option.iter (fun w -> window_poll w m mc.mouse mc.cons) window;
      if t land (polled - 1) = 0 && !waiting <> [] then
        Option.iter forwards peer;
      (* old: TinyMachineDevices.tick mc env, an instruction a turn of
       * this loop; now the instructions to the next turn that does
       * something *)
      TinyMachineDevices.ticks mc env (1024 - (t land 1023));
      if parallel then
        (match Atomic.get failed with Some e -> raise e | None -> ())
      else
        List.iter (fun (h, env) ->
          TinyMachineDevices.ticks h env (1024 - (t land 1023))) others
    done;
    0
  with TinyMachineDevices.Halt n -> halted n

let main (caps : < Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.argv; Cap.open_in;
                   Cap.open_out; Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.pipe;
                   Cap.signal; Cap.clock; .. >) =
  let args = List.tl (Array.to_list (CapSys.argv caps)) in
  TinyMachineCPU.memsize := TinyMachineDevices.memsize;
  let image files =
    match files with
    | [ f ] when f.[0] <> '-' ->
        TinyMachineCPU.image f (FS.read caps (Fpath.v f))
    | _ -> raise Exit in
  try
    match args with
    | ("-h" | "--help") :: _ -> Console.print caps help; 0
    | "-l" :: files ->
        Console.print caps
          (TinyMachineCPU.listing ~show:TinyMachineDevices.show ~origin:0
             (image files));
        0
    | args ->
        let rec options o = function
          | "-d" :: f :: rest -> options { o with disk_file = Some f } rest
          | "-screen" :: f :: rest -> options { o with screen_file = Some f } rest
          | "-audio" :: f :: rest -> options { o with audio_file = Some f } rest
          | "-events" :: f :: rest -> options { o with events_file = Some f } rest
          | "-window" :: rest -> options { o with window = true } rest
          | "-rate" :: n :: rest
            when (match int_of_string_opt n with
                  | Some n -> n > 0 && n <= 1000
                  | None -> false) ->
              options { o with rate = Some (int_of_string n * 1_000_000) } rest
          | "-date" :: n :: rest when int_of_string_opt n <> None ->
              options { o with date = int_of_string_opt n } rest
          | "-seed" :: n :: rest when int_of_string_opt n <> None ->
              options { o with seed = int_of_string_opt n } rest
          | "-net" :: dir :: rest -> options { o with net = Some dir } rest
          | "-net-trace" :: rest -> options { o with net_trace = true } rest
          | "-net-lose" :: n :: rest when int_of_string_opt n <> None ->
              options { o with net_lose = int_of_string n :: o.net_lose } rest
          | "-net-out" :: rest -> options { o with net_out = true } rest
          | "-net-pcap" :: f :: rest -> options { o with net_pcap = Some f } rest
          | "-prof" :: f :: rest -> options { o with prof = Some f } rest
          | "-net-forward" :: ports :: rest
            when (match List.map int_of_string_opt
                          (String.split_on_char ':' ports) with
                  | [ Some _; Some _ ] -> true
                  | _ -> false) ->
              let ports =
                List.map int_of_string (String.split_on_char ':' ports) in
              options { o with net_forward =
                                 (List.hd ports, List.nth ports 1)
                                 :: o.net_forward } rest
          | "-net-loop" :: n :: rest when int_of_string_opt n <> None ->
              options { o with net_loop = int_of_string_opt n } rest
          | "-cores" :: n :: rest
            when (match int_of_string_opt n with
                  | Some n -> n >= 1 && n <= 16
                  | None -> false) ->
              options { o with cores = int_of_string n } rest
          | "-cores-parallel" :: rest -> options { o with parallel = true } rest
          | files -> run caps o (image files) in
        options { disk_file = None; screen_file = None; audio_file = None;
                  events_file = None; window = false; rate = None;
                  date = None; seed = None; net_loop = None; net = None;
                  net_trace = false; net_lose = []; net_out = false;
                  net_forward = []; net_pcap = None; prof = None; cores = 1;
                  parallel = false } args
  with
  | Exit -> Console.eprint caps (usage ^ "   (-h: how)\n"); 2
  | TinyMachineISA.Error e | Sys_error e ->
      Console.eprint caps ("tiny-machine: " ^ e ^ "\n"); 1

let () =
  Cap.main (fun caps ->
    Logging.setup caps ~name:"tiny-machine";
    CapStdlib.exit caps (main caps))
tiny/TinyMachine.mli
18390
(* A tiny machine of our own. It is the CPU of TinyMachineCPU.ml plus
 * what a kernel needs around it, designed the same way the instructions
 * were. TinyCPU.ml runs the CPU the way a user program runs, with the
 * host answering its system calls. Here nothing answers them except a
 * program that the machine itself runs, a kernel, written in the same
 * assembly. The usage and examples are in [help], which is what
 * tiny-machine -h prints.
 *
 * The image is tiny-linker's: the objects one after the other, their
 * labels one namespace, so a kernel's table can name its programs. The
 * kernel comes first, at address 0. An image
 * is simply the first bytes of memory as they are at the start. It has
 * no header, since the machine always starts at 0 in supervisor mode
 * (the Pi's kernel.img, loaded at 0x8000 by its firmware, follows the
 * same idea).
 * The kernel is TinyKernel.ml, and TinyKernel/steps/ holds the two
 * steps that came before it, each with a Makefile that builds and runs
 * it: v0/ is a page of assembly with its programs, and t6/ is a kernel
 * in C whose disk is made by tiny-mkfs. At the top of ix,
 * ./tiny-machine tiny-kernel (or t6, or v0) builds and boots one.
 *
 * Here is what the machine adds to the CPU so that it can run a kernel:
 *
 * - {b Two modes}, supervisor and user, given by a bit of [status]. The
 *   machine starts in supervisor mode at 0.
 * - {b One way in, one way out.} A trap saves the pc in [epc] and the
 *   reason in [cause] (1 for sys, 2 for an illegal word, 3 for a fault,
 *   4 for the timer). It puts the related value in [tval] (the call's
 *   number, the illegal word, or the faulting address), and saves the
 *   mode and the interrupt-enable bit in [status]. It then enters
 *   supervisor mode with interrupts off and jumps to [tvec]. [eret]
 *   undoes this: it restores the mode and the interrupt bit and sets
 *   the pc to [epc]. epc is where execution resumes: after a sys, on the
 *   faulting instruction, or on the instruction that an interrupt
 *   preempted.
 * - {b Control registers}, read by [csrr d, name] and written by
 *   [csrw name, a]: status epc cause tval tvec time timecmp base
 *   bound. time counts executed instructions (so time belongs to the
 *   program alone, and every run is the same). The timer interrupts when
 *   time reaches timecmp and interrupts are on. [wfi] sleeps until an
 *   interrupt comes: an idle kernel's loop, which the host then does
 *   not run a jump at a time. csrr, csrw, eret and wfi are illegal in
 *   user mode.
 * - {b Protection by a window.} In user mode every address, including
 *   instruction fetches, must be in [base, bound), otherwise it is a
 *   fault. There is no relocation at run time: a user program is
 *   linked at the address where it runs. What the window gives is that a program can
 *   only harm itself (like RISC-V's PMP or the 360's storage keys,
 *   without pages).
 * - {b Two devices at the top of memory}, reachable from anywhere with
 *   a negative offset from r0. A store to -16(r0) writes a byte to the
 *   console, and a store to -12(r0) halts the machine, with the stored
 *   value as the exit status. They are outside any window a kernel
 *   hands out, so only the kernel can reach them.
 *
 * Then v6 added more (an xv6-like kernel in C; it was removed on
 * 2026-10-13 and is in git's history; no kernel in ix has used pages
 * since). Each addition is kept separate so that v0 still runs as it
 * did (plan_tiny_os.md, phase 2):
 *
 * - {b 256 MB} of memory (16 MB until 2026-10-15, 128 MB until the cores),
 *   with the devices still at the top (-16(r0) is the console).
 * - {b Pages}, using Sv32 (RISC-V's 32-bit scheme with two levels; xv6
 *   on 64 bits uses Sv39's three). The top bit of satp turns paging on
 *   and the window off; a page fault puts the address in tval. With
 *   bit 30 too (tiny-kernel's pages, plan_tiny_memory.md), only user
 *   mode's addresses are translated, the kernel's physical (the
 *   PDP-11's two sets of mapping registers, the kernel's and the
 *   user's); user mode's translations are kept in a cache of 64 pages,
 *   emptied when satp is written, which a kernel does after it changed
 *   a process's tables (RISC-V's sfence.vma).
 * - {b amoswap d, a, (b)}, the atomic swap that spinlocks are built
 *   from, usable in either mode; {b core}, the core's number (0 but with
 *   -cores, below); {b scratch} and {b csrrw}, to free a
 *   first register at the start of a trap.
 * - {b Interrupts by source}: ip (pending) and ie (enabled), with one
 *   bit per source. The timer is the first source, enabled at the start
 *   as v0 expects. An interrupt's cause is 4, and tval says which
 *   sources are pending.
 * - {b Console input} at -8(r0), with its interrupt; {b a disk}
 *   (-d image, made blank, 8 MB, when there is no such file), which
 *   moves 1 KB blocks at once, with its interrupt; a block written is
 *   written to the image file then, so a machine killed leaves the
 *   disk as a crash would.
 *
 * t6 (a kernel of our own in C, in TinyKernel/steps/t6/) added one
 * more thing: bit 16 of status makes the window relocate (a user address
 * is added to base, and must stay below bound).
 * tiny-kernel's segments (plan_tiny_memory.md) split it: with 32 of
 * status too, an address below {b tbound} is the text's, added to
 * {b tbase}, and a store there faults; one above, less tbound, is the
 * data's, added to base and below bound. One copy of a program's text
 * then serves all its runs, as the PDP-11/45's text segment did.
 *
 * For a window system (plan_tiny_windows.md) there are more additions,
 * each behind an option, so that a kernel without one runs as before:
 *
 * - {b A screen} of 1024 by 768 pixels, one byte each, at 0xf00000. It
 *   is ordinary memory (a kernel draws a pixel with stb), and each byte
 *   is a colour in Plan 9's table of 256. -window shows it in a window
 *   on the host, and -screen f writes it as a PPM file at the halt.
 * - {b A mouse}: the word at -4(r0) has x in its low 12 bits, y in the
 *   next 12, and the buttons above (1 left, 2 middle, 4 right, as in
 *   Plan 9). Its interrupt is the fourth source, raised when the mouse
 *   changes and cleared when the word is read.
 * - {b The keys} arrive as console input, including the window's keys
 *   with -window (the arrows are bytes 128 to 131: up, down, left,
 *   right; a key held down repeats).
 * - {b A fixed speed} with -window: 20 million instructions per second
 *   (-rate n changes it), so that a game's time, counted in
 *   instructions, follows the host's clock and not the host's speed.
 * - {b A replayed session} (-events f): mouse and key events are read
 *   from a file, each at its time. Since time is counted in
 *   instructions, the screen at the halt is the same on every run.
 *
 * For a network (plan_tiny_network.md), again behind an option:
 *
 * - {b A wire}: four words at -48(r0), laid out like the disk's (an
 *   address, a length, a command, a status). A command either sends a
 *   packet from memory or takes the packet that is waiting; the
 *   interrupt, the fifth source, is raised while a packet waits. The
 *   other end of the wire is on the host. With -net dir, it is this
 *   program itself, running TinyKernelNetwork.ml as tiny-kernel does,
 *   at the other address; it answers pings and serves dir's files over
 *   IL (see TinyMachinePeer). -net-trace prints each packet, -net-lose n
 *   drops the n-th one, and -net-pcap f saves them for tcpdump. With
 *   -net-out, the wire leads to other machines: the host opens the
 *   connections the machine asks for to other addresses. With
 *   -net-forward h:m, the host's port h is forwarded to the machine's
 *   port m. Both use tiny-machine-socket, a separate program that has
 *   the host's sockets and runs beside this one, like the window does.
 *   With -net-loop n, the wire loops back: a packet comes back n
 *   instructions later. Packets arrive at times counted in
 *   instructions, so a run is still the same every time.
 *
 * For sound (plan_tiny_audio.md):
 *
 * - {b A speaker} that is memory, as the screen is: a ring of 8,192
 *   samples (a byte each, signed) where the kernel says, by writing its
 *   address at -52(r0); the speaker plays it, 8,000 samples a second of
 *   the machine's time, and makes each sample it played 0, so a ring
 *   nobody writes is silence. Read, the word is the samples played,
 *   where the kernel writes ahead of. The samples due are played when
 *   somebody looks (the kernel, the host), so it costs no instruction
 *   of its own. -window plays them, -audio f writes them as a WAV.
 *
 * For several cores (plan_tiny_multicore.md), behind -cores n:
 *
 * - {b Cores}: n CPUs, each with its registers, its pc and its
 *   registers of control (core its number, cores their count),
 *   sharing the memory. All start at 0 in supervisor mode, as RISC-V's
 *   cores start at the reset's address; a kernel parks the others by
 *   their core. The devices are wired to core 0: another core that
 *   reaches one faults.
 * - {b The interrupt between cores}, the sixth source (32): a store of
 *   k at -64(r0) raises core k's, from anyone; a load gives the cores
 *   that raised this one's, a bit each, and clears them. A mailbox in
 *   memory and this interrupt are all tiny-kernel's cores need.
 * - {b In turns or at once.} By default the cores take turns in one
 *   thread, a slice of up to 1,024 instructions each: a run is the same
 *   every time, and one core is the machine as it was. With
 *   -cores-parallel, where OCaml has domains (tiny-machine built by
 *   OCaml 5), each core is a domain on one of the host's cores, counting
 *   its own time; the memory is shared without a lock (a race between
 *   cores is the program's, as on hardware), the interrupt by an
 *   Atomic; amoswap is then no longer atomic, which tiny-kernel does
 *   not need.
 *
 * terminology:
 * RISC-V says hart (a hardware thread: hartid, its number) where this
 * machine says core. They differ only on a core that runs several
 * threads at once, sharing its units (Intel's Hyper-Threading, SMT),
 * which the kernel then sees as several CPUs: Linux's /proc/cpuinfo
 * counts those. tiny-machine has no such core, so a core is one CPU,
 * the word a reader knows.
 *
 * Here is all of it as a kernel sees it. Memory is 256 MB, with the
 * devices at its top. An address is taken modulo the size, so r0 minus
 * 16 is 0xffffff0: reaching a device costs no register.
 *
 *     0x000000   the image: the kernel's first word, where the machine
 *                starts in supervisor mode; the programs linked after
 *        ...     free memory, which the kernel hands out by a window
 *                (base, bound) or by pages
 *     0xf00000   the screen: 768 rows of 1024 bytes, up to 0xfc0000
 *        ...
 *     0xfffffc0  the interrupt between cores             -64(r0)
 *     0xfffffcc  the speaker: its ring's address, the     -52(r0)
 *                samples played
 *     0xfffffd0  the network: an address, a length,       -48(r0) up
 *                a command, whether there is a wire
 *     0xfffffe0  the disk: a block number, an address,    -32(r0) up
 *                a command, a status (the first read:
 *                the disk's size, in blocks)
 *     0xffffff0  console output                           -16(r0)
 *     0xffffff4  halt                                     -12(r0)
 *     0xffffff8  console input                             -8(r0)
 *     0xffffffc  the mouse                                 -4(r0)
 *
 * And here is the word that holds the mode, with what a trap and eret
 * do to it (see [trap] in TinyMachineDevices, and its [extra] for eret):
 *
 *     status      16 relocate | 8 pie | 4 ps | 2 ie | 1 supervisor
 *
 *     a trap      sets epc, cause, tval; ps and pie save the previous
 *                 mode and ie; then supervisor, ie off, pc = tvec
 *     eret        restores the mode and ie from ps and pie; pc = epc
 *
 * Only one level is saved: a kernel that enables interrupts while it
 * handles a trap must first save epc and status itself, as on RISC-V.
 * Here is the whole path of a system call in v0: a program's sys 1
 * traps; the kernel at tvec saves the program's registers and epc,
 * reads cause (1) and tval (the call's number), performs the call,
 * restores the registers of some process, and eret returns to the
 * word after the sys.
 *
 * The CPU's hooks (the [env] of TinyMachineCPU) carry all of this. The
 * fetch, the load and the store go through the pages or the window and
 * find the devices; sys raises a trap; a word the CPU does not know is
 * decoded here as csrr, csrw, eret or wfi (in supervisor mode), or
 * amoswap, or else it traps. The loop around [step] adds the rest: the time and
 * the interrupts.
 *
 * Exercises. Each one is cheap, because time is counted in instructions
 * and everything else is a hook of the CPU:
 * - the cores' turns in an order drawn from a seed (-cores takes them
 *   in a fixed one), so a race can be replayed from its seed, which
 *   real hardware never allows;
 * - a slow disk: the transfer completes N instructions after the
 *   command, so a kernel must sleep while waiting (v6's diskrw becomes
 *   xv6's);
 * - a TLB: the last translations are cached and flushed by a write to
 *   satp, so a kernel that forgets a flush shows its bug, as on real
 *   machines;
 * - the A and D bits of pages, set by loads and stores, so that a
 *   kernel can do clock page replacement.
 *
 * The machine itself is in TinyMachineDevices.ml (the control
 * registers, the traps, the pages, the state of the devices, and one
 * instruction's worth of time). This file is its terminal front end:
 * the console, the files, the window, and the main loop.
 * TinyMachineWeb.ml is the same front end for a web page.
 *
 * Where it stands: below it is TinyMachineCPU, the instructions; above
 * it are its kernels, TinyKernel (in ML, compiled by tiny-ml) and
 * the steps before it (v0 in assembly, t6 in C compiled by tiny-c).
 * Its twins are machines that ix did not design: mini-qemu's Board and
 * Pi4. There, the same five ideas (modes, trap registers, a timer,
 * devices at addresses, an image loaded at a fixed place) have ARM's
 * names and ARM's history.
 *
 * Here is the same machine under two sets of names: ours, which we
 * designed, and the Pi 4's, which ARM evolved over time (the first
 * page of a kernel written against the latter is in
 * kernels/lib_machine/pi4/l.s):
 *
 *     here                 the Pi 4 (arm64)
 *     user, supervisor     EL0, EL1 (and EL2, EL3 above)
 *     status's ps, pie     SPSR_EL1
 *     epc                  ELR_EL1
 *     cause, tval          ESR_EL1, FAR_EL1
 *     tvec                 VBAR_EL1, a table of sixteen entries
 *     eret                 eret
 *     wfi                  wfi
 *     sys                  svc
 *     time, timecmp        CNTVCT_EL0, CNTV_TVAL_EL0 and CNTV_CTL_EL0
 *     ip, ie               the GIC, a separate device
 *     -16(r0)              0xfe201000, the UART
 *     csrr, csrw           mrs, msr
 *
 * Here every trap goes to one address and the cause is in a register;
 * on ARM there is a table, with one entry per origin and kind of
 * exception. Here the interrupt controller is just two control
 * registers, which a machine with four devices can afford. On ARM it
 * is a device with its own registers, because how many interrupt lines
 * there are, and which core handles which, is the board's business,
 * not the processor's.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Two modes with a trap between them come from the Atlas (Manchester,
 * 1962), and from then on every machine that ran more than one program
 * had them: the IBM 360's supervisor state and its SVC instruction
 * (1964) gave the system call its shape. A base and a bound around a
 * program were the protection on machines before pages (the CDC 6600's
 * reference address and field length, the PDP-10's registers). With
 * relocation, they are a complete memory management scheme: a program
 * can be moved by changing one register. What they cannot do is share
 * part of a program, grow it in the middle, or leave part of it on
 * disk, which is why pages were invented, on the Atlas again.
 *
 * design:
 * Counting time in instructions is what makes this machine a tool for
 * learning. A run is a function of the image and the input: the same
 * interleaving of processes, the same screen at the halt, the same bug
 * at the same instruction, on any host and under a debugger. On a real
 * board the timer follows a crystal, and an interrupt lands wherever it
 * lands. The cost is that nothing can be learned here about the real
 * timing of devices; mini-qemu also counts instructions and has the
 * same limit.
 *
 * others:
 * Other machines were made to carry a teaching system. Wirth's RISC for
 * Project Oberon (2013 edition) runs on an FPGA and has no modes at
 * all: the language is the protection. There is also MIT's 6.004 Beta,
 * and Nisan and Schocken's Hack, whose keyboard and screen are memory
 * as here and which has no interrupts. xv6 chose a real machine (x86,
 * then RISC-V, under QEMU; the sixth edition of Unix it retells ran on
 * a PDP-11), and v6, while it was here, brought that kind of kernel to
 * our own machine.
 *
 * References:
 *  - the RISC-V privileged specification: the trap registers, their
 *    names, mret
 *  - Wirth and Gutknecht, Project Oberon (1992): a machine and its
 *    system designed together
 *  - Nisan and Schocken, The Elements of Computing Systems (Hack):
 *    devices as memory
 *)

(* the command line's: a disk's file, a window, a screen's file, a
 * sound's, events, a network's wire *)
type options

(* an image, run to the machine's halt: the hosts' turns (the console,
 * the window), then the machine's instruction; to the exit status *)
val run :
  < Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.fork;
    Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal; Cap.clock; .. > ->
  options -> string -> int

(* the program: its arguments (-h: how) to its exit status *)
val main :
  < Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal; Cap.clock; .. > ->
  int

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The chart *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A chart's data is a line: bars, the sheet it draws by its name, the
 * cells of its values, and of its labels if it has some:
 *
 *     bars budget b1:b3 a1:a3
 *
 * a range being cells of a column or of a row. The values are the
 * sheet's at each view, so a chart follows its sheet; a sheet renamed,
 * its charts are too. *)

(* the cells of a range, "b1:b3" or "a1:c1" ([] if it is none) *)
let range_cells (r : string) : string list =
  let at n = if String.length n >= 2 && n.[0] >= 'a' && n.[0] <= 'z' then
      (match int_of_string_opt (String.sub n 1 (String.length n - 1)) with
       | Some k when k >= 1 -> Some (Char.code n.[0] - 97, k - 1)
       | _ -> None)
    else None in
  match String.split_on_char ':' r with
  | [ a; b ] -> (
      match at a, at b with
      | Some (c0, r0), Some (c1, r1) when c0 = c1 && r1 >= r0 ->
        List.init (r1 - r0 + 1) (fun k -> name c0 (r0 + k))
      | Some (c0, r0), Some (c1, r1) when r0 = r1 && c1 >= c0 ->
        List.init (c1 - c0 + 1) (fun k -> name (c0 + k) r0)
      | _ -> [])
  | _ -> []

(* A chart's bars, each its label and its value (a cell that is not a
 * number, 0), from its sheet on the page; or, none, why *)
let chart_bars (page : obj list) (b : obj) : (string * int) list * string =
  let first =
    match String.split_on_char '\n' b.data with l :: _ -> l | [] -> "" in
  match String.split_on_char ' ' first with
  | "bars" :: sheet :: range :: rest -> (
      match
        List.filter (fun (s : obj) -> s.kind = "sheet" && s.called = sheet)
          page
      with
      | s :: _ ->
          let value = values s.data in
          let labels = match rest with l :: _ -> range_cells l | [] -> [] in
          let label k = match labels with [] -> "" | _ -> (
            match (if k < List.length labels then value (List.nth labels k)
                   else Str "") with
            | Num v -> string_of_int v
            | Str t -> t
            | Err e -> "#" ^ e) in
          let bars =
            List.mapi (fun k n ->
              (label k, match value n with Num v -> v | _ -> 0))
              (range_cells range) in
          if bars = [] then ([], "no cells in " ^ range) else (bars, "")
      | [] -> ([], "no sheet " ^ sheet))
  | _ -> ([], "a chart: bars SHEET b1:b3 a1:a3")

(* the bars' colours, in turn: the paint's blue, red, green, yellow,
 * orange, purple *)
let bar_colours = [ 54; 240; 42; 252; 231; 129 ]

(* A chart: a bar a value, as tall as its share of the largest (none
 * below 0), its value above it, its label under it (cut to its width);
 * the axis a grey line *)
let chart_view (page : obj list) (b : obj) : shape list =
  match chart_bars page b with
  | [], why -> [ Move (b.x + 4, b.y + 2, Words (160, why)) ]
  | bars, _ ->
      let n = List.length bars in
      let top = List.fold_left (fun m (_, v) -> max m v) 1 bars in
      let bw = max 6 ((b.w - 16) / n)
      and base = b.y + b.h - 20
      and room = b.h - 42 in
      let cut t =
        let k = max 0 ((bw - 2) / 8) in
        if String.length t > k then String.sub t 0 k else t in
      List.concat (List.mapi (fun k (label, v) ->
        let x = b.x + 8 + (k * bw) and tall = max 0 (v * room / top) in
        (if tall > 0 then
           [ Move (x + 2, base - tall,
                   Rect (List.nth bar_colours (k mod 6), bw - 4, tall)) ]
         else [])
        @ [ Move (x + 2, base - tall - 16, Words (black, cut (string_of_int v)));
            Move (x + 2, base + 2, Words (black, cut label)) ]) bars)
      @ [ Move (b.x + 4, base, Rect (grey, b.w - 8, 1)) ]

(* a name a sheet can have: a letter, then letters, digits, _ *)
let good_name (n : string) =
  n <> "" && ((n.[0] >= 'a' && n.[0] <= 'z') || (n.[0] >= 'A' && n.[0] <= 'Z'))
  && String.for_all (fun c ->
       (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
       || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c = '_') n

(* A key while the selected sheet's name is typed: a character, Backspace,
 * Enter (the name given, to the charts of the sheet too), C-g *)
let name_key (o : office) (typed : string) (k : int) =
  if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
    o.editing <- Naming (typed ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr k))
  else if (k = 8 || k = 127) && typed <> "" then
    o.editing <- Naming (String.sub typed 0 (String.length typed - 1))
  else if k = 13 || k = 10 then begin
    let s = List.nth o.page o.sel in
    if not (good_name typed) then
      o.message <- "a name: a letter, then letters, digits, _"
    else if List.exists (fun (b : obj) -> b.called = typed && b != s) o.page
    then o.message <- "another sheet is " ^ typed
    else begin
      let renamed l =
        match String.split_on_char ' ' l with
        | "bars" :: was :: rest when was = s.called ->
          String.concat " " ("bars" :: typed :: rest)
        | _ -> l in
      keep o;
      o.page <- List.map (fun (b : obj) ->
        if b == s then { b with called = typed }
        else if b.kind = "chart" then
          { b with data =
                     String.concat "\n"
                       (List.map renamed (String.split_on_char '\n' b.data)) }
        else b) o.page;
      o.editing <- Nothing
    end
  end
  else if k = 7 then o.editing <- Nothing

(* a chart of the chosen cell's column, beside its sheet (under it, if
 * the page is too narrow): its cells from the first number to the last,
 * the column at its left their labels *)
let make_chart (o : office) (c : int) =
  let s = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  let value = values s.data in
  let rows =
    List.filter (fun r ->
      match value (name c r) with Num _ -> true | _ -> false)
      (List.init 99 (fun r -> r)) in
  match rows with
  | [] ->
    o.message <- "no numbers in column " ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr (97 + c))
  | r0 :: _ ->
      let r1 = List.fold_left max r0 rows in
      let range c = name c r0 ^ ":" ^ name c r1 in
      let data =
        "bars " ^ s.called ^ " " ^ range c
        ^ (if c > 0 then " " ^ range (c - 1) else "") ^ "\n" in
      let x, y =
        if s.x + s.w + 216 <= o.where.width then s.x + s.w + 16, s.y
        else s.x, s.y + s.h + 24 in
      keep o;
      o.page <-
        o.page @ [ { kind = "chart"; x; y; w = 200; h = 120; data;
                     called = ""; page_no = s.page_no } ];
      o.sel <- List.length o.page - 1;
      o.editing <- Nothing

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The drawing *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A drawing's data is a line a shape, at its place in the drawing's
 * box:
 *
 *     box 10 10 80 30 cpu
 *     arrow 90 25 160 60
 *     text 20 70 a note
 *
 * a box and its label; an arrow, across then up or down (a block
 * diagram's connector: what the shapes draw is rectangles, and a
 * slanted line would need another kind); words. pic's idea (Brian
 * Kernighan, 1982: a picture as lines of text), drawn with the mouse. *)

let tools = [ "box"; "arrow"; "text" ]

(* a drawing's shapes: their kind, their numbers, their label *)
let figures (data : string) : (string * int list * string) list =
  List.concat_map (fun l ->
    match String.split_on_char ' ' l with
    | kind :: rest when List.mem kind tools ->
        let rec take k l =
          if k = 0 then [], l
          else (let v, r =
                  match l with
                  | v :: r ->
                    (match int_of_string_opt v with
                     | Some i -> i
                     | None -> 0), r
                  | [] -> 0, [] in
                let nums, words = take (k - 1) r in v :: nums, words) in
        let nums, words = take (if kind = "text" then 2 else 4) rest in
        [ kind, nums, String.concat " " words ]
    | _ -> []) (String.split_on_char '\n' data)

let figure_line ((kind, nums, label) : string * int list * string) : string =
  String.concat ""
    (kind :: List.map (fun n -> " " ^ string_of_int n) nums
     @ (if label = "" then [ "\n" ] else [ " "; label; "\n" ]))

(* a shape drawn, the box's corner at (ox, oy); an arrow's head is
 * rectangles narrowing to its end, along its last stretch *)
let figure_shapes (ox : int) (oy : int) (colour : int)
    ((kind, nums, label) : string * int list * string) : shape list =
  match kind, nums with
  | "box", [ x; y; w; h ] ->
      let x = ox + x and y = oy + y in
      let label =
        if 8 * String.length label > w - 4 then
          String.sub label 0 (max 0 ((w - 4) / 8))
        else label in
      [ Move (x, y, Rect (colour, w, 1)); Move (x, y + h - 1, Rect (colour, w, 1));
        Move (x, y, Rect (colour, 1, h));
        Move (x + w - 1, y, Rect (colour, 1, h));
        Move (x + ((w - (8 * String.length label)) / 2), y + ((h - 16) / 2),
              Words (colour, label)) ]
  | "arrow", [ x0; y0; x1; y1 ] ->
      let x0 = ox + x0 and y0 = oy + y0 and x1 = ox + x1 and y1 = oy + y1 in
      let head = List.init 4 (fun k ->
        if y1 > y0 then Move (x1 - k, y1 - k, Rect (colour, (2 * k) + 1, 1))
        else if y1 < y0 then
          Move (x1 - k, y1 + k, Rect (colour, (2 * k) + 1, 1))
        else if x1 >= x0 then
          Move (x1 - k, y0 - k, Rect (colour, 1, (2 * k) + 1))
        else Move (x1 + k, y0 - k, Rect (colour, 1, (2 * k) + 1))) in
      [ Move (min x0 x1, y0, Rect (colour, abs (x1 - x0) + 1, 1));
        Move (x1, min y0 y1, Rect (colour, 1, abs (y1 - y0) + 1)) ] @ head
  | "text", [ x; y ] -> [ Move (ox + x, oy + y, Words (colour, label)) ]
  | _ -> []

(* what a stroke of a tool makes, from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) *)
let stroked (tool : int) (x0 : int) (y0 : int) (x1 : int) (y1 : int)
    : string * int list * string =
  if tool = 0 then
    "box", [ min x0 x1; min y0 y1; abs (x1 - x0); abs (y1 - y0) ], ""
  else if tool = 1 then "arrow", [ x0; y0; x1; y1 ], ""
  else "text", [ x1; y1 ], ""

(* the shape a stroke made, added; a box or an arrow too small is a
 * click, not a shape *)
let draw_stroke (o : office) (tool : int)
    ((x0, y0, x1, y1) : int * int * int * int) =
  let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  if tool = 2 || (tool = 0 && abs (x1 - x0) >= 8 && abs (y1 - y0) >= 8)
     || (tool = 1 && abs (x1 - x0) + abs (y1 - y0) >= 8) then
    change o (b.data ^ figure_line (stroked tool x0 y0 x1 y1))

(* A key in a drawing: Tab another tool; a character the last shape's
 * label longer; Backspace shorter, and an empty label's shape removed;
 * C-g the drawing left *)
let sketch_key (o : office) (tool : int) (k : int) =
  let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  let figs = figures b.data in
  let relabel f = match List.rev figs with
    | (kind, nums, label) :: rest ->
      change o
        (String.concat ""
           (List.map figure_line (List.rev rest @ f kind nums label)))
    | [] -> () in
  if k = 9 then o.editing <- Sketch ((tool + 1) mod 3, None)
  else if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
    relabel (fun kind nums label ->
      [ kind, nums, label ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr k) ])
  else if k = 8 || k = 127 then
    relabel (fun kind nums label ->
      if label = "" then []
      else [ kind, nums, String.sub label 0 (String.length label - 1) ])
  else if k = 7 then o.editing <- Nothing
  else o.message <- "a drawing: Tab, the mouse, a label typed; C-g"


(* A drawing: its shapes, and the stroke being made, in blue *)
let drawing_view (b : obj) (tool : int)
    (stroke : (int * int * int * int) option) : shape list =
  List.concat_map (figure_shapes b.x b.y black) (figures b.data)
  @ (match stroke with
     | Some (x0, y0, x1, y1) ->
       figure_shapes b.x b.y blue (stroked tool x0 y0 x1 y1)
     | None -> [])

(*****************************************************************************)

(* A page's file is a document in mini-troff's format
 * (plan_typesetting.md): Markdown's lines, and \name[options]{text}
 * for what Markdown has not. Each object is a \box at its place (x, y,
 * width, height), its content the lines up to one that is a } alone:
 *
 *     \box[20 40 200 84]{
 *     # Tiny office
 *
 *     A page of **boxes**, *styled*, \u{underlined}.
 *     }
 *
 *     \box[300 40 282 114]{
 *     | a     | b      |
 *     |-------|--------|
 *     | Rent  | 500    |
 *     | Total | =b1+b2 |
 *     }
 *
 * The kind is in the content: a table is a sheet (its header the
 * columns' letters, then a row a line, what was typed in each cell;
 * its name after its box's numbers), a fence ```drawing, ```paint or
 * ```chart is that (its lines as they are), the rest text. A text's
 * styles are Markdown's, **bold**, *italic*, a line
 * "# " large, and \u{} underlined, \large{} large in a line; \ before a
 * character that would be read otherwise. So emacs edits a page as any
 * text (no count of bytes to keep right), and a Markdown file, with no
 * \box, is opened as one text box. *)

(* a text's line as Markdown, from its characters and their styles *)
let md_of_line (t : string) (st : string) : string =
  let n = String.length t in
  let all_large =
    n > 0 && String.for_all (fun c -> Char.code c land 8 <> 0) st in
  let base = if all_large then 8 else 0 in
  let stars k =
    if k = 1 then "**" else if k = 2 then "*" else if k = 3 then "***"
    else "" in
  let opens k =
    (if k land 8 <> 0 then "\\large{" else "")
    ^ (if k land 4 <> 0 then "\\u{" else "") ^ stars (k land 3) in
  let closes k =
    stars (k land 3) ^ (if k land 4 <> 0 then "}" else "")
    ^ (if k land 8 <> 0 then "}" else "") in
  let one i c =
    if c = '\\' || c = '*' || c = '{' || c = '}'
       || (i = 0 && (c = '#' || c = '|' || c = '`')) then
      "\\" ^ String.make 1 c
    else String.make 1 c in
  let rec go i was acc =
    if i >= n then String.concat "" (List.rev (closes was :: acc))
    else begin
      let k = Char.code st.[i] land lnot base in
      go (i + 1) k
        (one i t.[i]
         :: (if k <> was then opens k :: closes was :: acc else acc))
    end in
  (if all_large then "# " else "") ^ go 0 0 []

(* a Markdown line as characters and their styles: stars toggle italic
 * (one), bold (two), both (three); \u{ and \large{ open a style that
 * the next } closes; \ takes the next character as it is *)
let line_of_md (l : string) : string * string =
  let n = String.length l in
  let base, start =
    if n >= 2 && String.sub l 0 2 = "# " then 8, 2 else 0, 0 in
  let starts i w =
    i + String.length w <= n && String.sub l i (String.length w) = w in
  let rec any l = match l with k :: rest -> k lor any rest | [] -> 0 in
  let rec go i opened stars chars styles =
    let add c =
      go (i + 1) opened stars (String.make 1 c :: chars)
        (String.make 1 (Char.chr (base lor stars lor any opened)) :: styles) in
    if i >= n then
      (String.concat "" (List.rev chars), String.concat "" (List.rev styles))
    else if starts i "\\u{" then go (i + 3) (4 :: opened) stars chars styles
    else if starts i "\\large{" then
      go (i + 7) (8 :: opened) stars chars styles
    else if l.[i] = '\\' && i + 1 < n then
      go (i + 2) opened stars (String.make 1 l.[i + 1] :: chars)
        (String.make 1 (Char.chr (base lor stars lor any opened)) :: styles)
    else if l.[i] = '}' && opened <> [] then
      go (i + 1) (match opened with _ :: rest -> rest | [] -> []) stars chars
        styles
    else if l.[i] = '*' then begin
      let k = if starts i "***" then 3 else if starts i "**" then 2 else 1 in
      go (i + k) opened
        (stars lxor (if k = 1 then 2 else if k = 2 then 1 else 3)) chars styles
    end
    else add l.[i] in
  go start [] 0 [] []

(* a text box's data as Markdown's lines, and back *)
let md_of_text (data : string) : string list =
  let (t, st) = decode data in
  let rec lines i =
    match String.index_from_opt t i '\n' with
    | Some e ->
      md_of_line (String.sub t i (e - i)) (String.sub st i (e - i))
      :: lines (e + 1)
    | None ->
      [ md_of_line (String.sub t i (String.length t - i))
          (String.sub st i (String.length t - i)) ] in
  if t = "" then [] else lines 0

let text_of_md (ls : string list) : string =
  let read = List.map line_of_md ls in
  encode
    (String.concat ""
       (List.mapi (fun k (t, _) -> if k = 0 then t else "\n" ^ t) read))
    (String.concat ""
       (List.mapi (fun k (_, st) -> if k = 0 then st else "\000" ^ st) read))

(* A sheet as a table, its columns as wide as their widest cell, and
 * back (a | in a cell is \|) *)
let md_of_sheet (data : string) : string list =
  let cs = cells data in
  let col n = Char.code n.[0] - 97
  and row n =
    (match int_of_string_opt (String.sub n 1 (String.length n - 1)) with
     | Some r -> r
     | None -> 1) - 1 in
  let ncols = List.fold_left (fun m (n, _) -> max m (col n + 1)) 1 cs
  and nrows = List.fold_left (fun m (n, _) -> max m (row n + 1)) 0 cs in
  let esc s =
    String.concat ""
      (List.map (fun c -> if c = '|' then "\\|" else String.make 1 c)
         (List.init (String.length s) (fun i -> s.[i]))) in
  let cell c r = esc (typed_in data (name c r)) in
  let wide =
    List.init ncols (fun c ->
      List.fold_left (fun m r -> max m (String.length (cell c r))) 1
        (List.init nrows (fun r -> r))) in
  let pad s w = s ^ String.make (w - String.length s) ' ' in
  let line f =
    "|" ^ String.concat ""
            (List.mapi (fun c w -> " " ^ pad (f c) w ^ " |") wide) in
  line (fun c -> String.make 1 (Char.chr (97 + c)))
  :: ("|" ^ String.concat ""
              (List.map (fun w -> String.make (w + 2) '-' ^ "|") wide))
  :: List.init nrows (fun r -> line (fun c -> cell c r))

(* a table's line, its cells: between the |, trimmed, \| a | *)
let table_cells (l : string) : string list =
  let n = String.length l in
  let rec go i cur acc =
    if i >= n then List.rev acc
    else if l.[i] = '\\' && i + 1 < n && l.[i + 1] = '|' then
      go (i + 2) (cur ^ "|") acc
    else if l.[i] = '|' then go (i + 1) "" (String.trim cur :: acc)
    else go (i + 1) (cur ^ String.make 1 l.[i]) acc in
  match go 0 "" [] with _ :: cells -> cells | [] -> []

let sheet_of_md (ls : string list) : string =
  match ls with
  | _ :: _ :: rows ->
      String.concat ""
        (List.concat
           (List.mapi (fun r l ->
              List.concat
                (List.mapi (fun c t ->
                   if t = "" then [] else [ name c r ^ " " ^ t ^ "\n" ])
                   (table_cells l))) rows))
  | _ -> ""

(* a box's lines in the file *)
let box_lines (b : obj) : string list =
  let content =
    if b.kind = "sheet" then md_of_sheet b.data
    else if b.kind = "drawing" || b.kind = "paint" || b.kind = "chart" then
      (* (its lines as they are, a paint's empty rows too; not the empty
       * one after the last newline) *)
      [ "```" ^ b.kind ]
      @ (match List.rev (String.split_on_char '\n' b.data) with
         | "" :: r -> List.rev r
         | l -> List.rev l)
      @ [ "```" ]
    else md_of_text b.data in
  ("\\box[" ^ string_of_int b.x ^ " " ^ string_of_int b.y ^ " "
   ^ string_of_int b.w ^ " " ^ string_of_int b.h
   ^ (if b.called = "" then "" else " " ^ b.called) ^ "]{")
  :: content @ [ "}" ]

(* the file of a document: each page's boxes, a line \newpage between
 * two pages (LaTeX's), an empty line between two boxes *)
let text (o : office) : string =
  let page p =
    List.map box_lines (List.filter (fun (b : obj) -> b.page_no = p) o.page) in
  let blocks =
    List.concat
      (List.init o.where.pages (fun p ->
         (if p = 0 then [] else [ [ "\\newpage" ] ]) @ page p)) in
  String.concat ""
    (List.mapi (fun k ls ->
       (if k = 0 then "" else "\n")
       ^ String.concat "" (List.map (fun l -> l ^ "\n") ls)) blocks)

let obj_of (page_no : int) (x : int) (y : int) (w : int) (h : int)
    (called : string) (ls : string list) : obj =
  let lines_data l = String.concat "" (List.map (fun s -> s ^ "\n") l) in
  match ls with
  | first :: _ when String.length first > 0 && first.[0] = '|' ->
    { kind = "sheet"; x; y; w; h; data = sheet_of_md ls; called; page_no }
  | first :: rest
    when first = "```drawing" || first = "```paint" || first = "```chart" ->
      { kind = String.sub first 3 (String.length first - 3); x; y; w; h;
        data = lines_data (List.filter (fun l -> l <> "```") rest);
        called = ""; page_no }
  | _ ->
    { kind = "text"; x; y; w; h; data = text_of_md ls; called = ""; page_no }

let parse (width : int) (height : int) (s : string) : obj list =
  let is_box l =
    String.length l > 6 && String.sub l 0 5 = "\\box["
    && String.sub l (String.length l - 2) 2 = "]{" in
  let rec go p ls =
    match ls with
    | "\\newpage" :: rest -> go (p + 1) rest
    | l :: rest when is_box l ->
        let words =
          String.split_on_char ' ' (String.sub l 5 (String.length l - 7)) in
        let num v = match int_of_string_opt v with Some k -> k | None -> 0 in
        let rec content acc ls =
          match ls with
          | "}" :: rest -> List.rev acc, rest
          | x :: rest -> content (x :: acc) rest
          | [] -> List.rev acc, [] in
        let (inside, rest) = content [] rest in
        (match words with
         | [ x; y; w; h ] ->
           obj_of p (num x) (num y) (num w) (num h) "" inside :: go p rest
         | [ x; y; w; h; called ] ->
           obj_of p (num x) (num y) (num w) (num h) called inside :: go p rest
         | _ -> go p rest)
    | _ :: rest -> go p rest
    | [] -> [] in
  let ls = String.split_on_char '\n' s in
  if s = "" then []
  else if List.exists is_box ls then go 0 ls
  else
    [ obj_of 0 16 40 (width - 32) (height - 80) ""
        (match List.rev ls with "" :: r -> List.rev r | _ -> ls) ]

(* how many pages a document's file has: one, and one more a \newpage *)
let pages_in (s : string) =
  1 + List.length
        (List.filter (fun l -> l = "\\newpage") (String.split_on_char '\n' s))

(* the pages counted again, after a change: as many as its objects are
 * on, at least *)
let fit_pages (o : office) =
  o.where.pages <-
    List.fold_left (fun m (b : obj) -> max m (b.page_no + 1)) o.where.pages
      o.page

(* TinyOffice's file: a document's pages as text in mini-troff's format
 * (plan_typesetting.md), Markdown's lines, and \name[options]{text} for
 * what Markdown has not. Each object is a \box at its place (x, y,
 * width, height), its content the lines up to one that is a } alone; a
 * line \newpage between two pages (LaTeX's):
 *
 *     \box[20 40 200 84]{
 *     # Tiny office
 *
 *     A page of **boxes**, *styled*, \u{underlined}.
 *     }
 *
 *     \box[300 40 282 114 budget]{
 *     | a     | b      |
 *     |-------|--------|
 *     | Rent  | 500    |
 *     | Total | =b1+b2 |
 *     }
 *
 * The kind is in the content: a table is a sheet (its header the
 * columns' letters, then a row a line, what was typed in each cell;
 * its name after its box's numbers), a fence ```drawing, ```paint or
 * ```chart is that (its lines as they are), the rest text. A text's
 * styles are Markdown's, **bold**, *italic*, a line "# " large, and
 * \u{} underlined, \large{} large in a line. So emacs edits a page as
 * any text (no count of bytes to keep right), tiny-troff prints it,
 * and a Markdown file, with no \box, is opened as one text box.
 *
 * design:
 * a document's file is a text that other programs read, not the
 * program's values marshalled (mini-office's Saved): the format
 * outlives the program.
 *)

 * that width and height, for a Markdown file's one box) *)

(* See TinyOfficeModel.mli *)
open TinyLibGUI

(* the page's colours, bytes of the machine's palette: white, black, a
 * frame's grey, the selected box's blue, the status line's light grey,
 * selected text's pale blue *)
let white = 255
let black = 0
let grey = 153
let blue = 3
let light_grey = 204
let pale_blue = 188

(* an object of the document: its kind ("text", "sheet", "drawing",
 * "paint", "chart"), its box in pixels, its data, its name (a sheet's,
 * which a chart names; "" for the others), the page it is on (from 0) *)
type obj = {
  kind : string; x : int; y : int; w : int; h : int; data : string;
  called : string; page_no : int }

(* the window on the document: its file, its size in pixels, the page
 * shown, how many pages there are (a page with nothing on it counts) *)
type window = {
  file : string; width : int; height : int; mutable shown : int;
  mutable pages : int }

(* a text box being edited: its characters and their styles (a byte
 * each: bold 1, italic 2, underlined 4, large 8), the cursor, the
 * selection's other end (the cursor's place: none), the style of what
 * is typed next, whether the left button is selecting *)
type doc = {
  mutable txt : string; mutable sty : string; mutable cur : int;
  mutable anchor : int; mutable typing : int; mutable selecting : bool }

(* what the selected box is edited by: nothing; a text box's text; a
 * sheet's cell, its column and row, and what is being
 * typed in it (None: the cell chosen, nothing typed yet); a drawing's
 * tool (0 a box, 1 an arrow, 2 a text), and the stroke the left button
 * is making, from where it went down to where it is, in the box; a
 * paint's colour (its place in pixel_letters), its brush (0 thin, 1
 * thick), and the pixel where the left button last was, when it is
 * down; the selected sheet's new name, being typed *)
type edit = Nothing | Writing of doc | Cell of int * int * string option
  | Sketch of int * (int * int * int * int) option
  | Painting of int * int * (int * int) option | Naming of string

(* what the menus ask for: to save, to quit, to undo, to delete the
 * selected box, a new box of a kind, a drawing's tool; in a text, to
 * cut, copy, paste, a style (0: plain); in a paint, a colour, a brush,
 * the picture cleared; in a sheet, a name typed, a chart of the chosen
 * cell's column; the next page shown (1) or the one before (-1), a new
 * page after it, the page deleted *)
type command = Do_save | Do_quit | Do_undo | Do_delete | Do_add of string
  | Do_tool of int | Do_cut | Do_copy | Do_paste | Do_style of int
  | Do_ink of int | Do_brush of int | Do_clear | Do_name | Do_chart
  | Do_page of int | Do_new_page | Do_delete_page

type office = {
  mutable page : obj list;       (* the objects, the bottom one first *)
  mutable undo : obj list list;  (* the pages before, the last first *)
  mutable clean : obj list;      (* the page as it was last saved *)
  mutable sel : int;             (* the selected object, its place in page;
                                  * -1 none *)
  mutable editing : edit;        (* what the selected box is edited by *)
  mutable drag : (int * int * int * obj * bool) option;
                                 (* a box grabbed: the object, where the
                                  * mouse was, the object then, resizing *)
  mutable at : int * int;        (* the last click *)
  menu : menu_state;             (* the menus', and the mouse's buttons as
                                  * last seen *)
  mutable message : string;      (* the status line's *)
  mutable prefix : bool;         (* C-x typed *)
  where : window;                (* the file, the window's size, the page
                                  * shown *)
}

(* (eleven fields: tiny-ml's most on tiny-machine) *)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The page's objects *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the page with its i-th object replaced, or removed (None) *)
let rec replace (l : obj list) (i : int) (b : obj option) : obj list =
  match l with
  | x :: rest ->
    if i > 0 then x :: replace rest (i - 1) b
    else (match b with Some b -> b :: rest | None -> rest)
  | [] -> []

(* the topmost object under (x, y) on the page shown: its place, -1 *)
let hit (o : office) (x : int) (y : int) : int =
  let rec go i found = function
    | (b : obj) :: rest ->
      go (i + 1)
        (if b.page_no = o.where.shown && x >= b.x && x < b.x + b.w
            && y >= b.y && y < b.y + b.h then i
         else found) rest
    | [] -> found in
  go 0 (-1) o.page

(* a change about to be made: the page as it is, kept for undo *)
let keep (o : office) = o.undo <- o.page :: o.undo


(* the selected box's data changed (a change, for undo, when it is
 * other data) *)
let change (o : office) (data : string) =
  let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  if data <> b.data then
    (keep o; o.page <- replace o.page o.sel (Some { b with data }))
