(* See TinyOfficePaint.mli *)
open TinyLibPlayground
open TinyOfficeModel

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Paint *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A paint's data is its picture, a line a row of pixels, a letter a
 * pixel, its colour:
 *
 *     ..kkk..
 *     .krrrk.
 *
 * . white, k black, r red, g green, b blue, y yellow, o orange, p
 * purple, n brown, a grey (TinyLibPlayground's pixel_letters; a row
 * ends at its last colour that is not white). A pixel is a square of 4
 * by 4 on the page; a row is one word of fat pixels, its letters (made
 * the kernel's bytes when it is drawn), so a stroke draws again the
 * rows it went through, and nothing else. *)
let paint_names = [ "white"; "black"; "red"; "green"; "blue"; "yellow";
                    "orange"; "purple"; "brown"; "grey" ]

(* the picture's size in pixels, in box b *)
let paint_cols (b : obj) = max 1 ((b.w - 4) / 4)
let paint_rows (b : obj) = max 1 ((b.h - 4) / 4)

(* the pixel under (x, y), in the picture *)
let pixel_at (b : obj) (x : int) (y : int) =
  (max 0 (min (paint_cols b - 1) ((x - b.x - 2) / 4)),
   max 0 (min (paint_rows b - 1) ((y - b.y - 2) / 4)))

(* a row without the white at its end *)
let rec trim_white (row : string) =
  let n = String.length row in
  if n > 0 && row.[n - 1] = '.' then trim_white (String.sub row 0 (n - 1))
  else row

(* The pixels a stroke of a brush covers, from (c0, r0) to (c1, r1), in
 * a letter, put in the picture: a thick brush 3 pixels wide. *)
let painted (b : obj) (letter : char) (brush : int) (c0 : int) (r0 : int)
    (c1 : int) (r1 : int) : string =
  let nrows = paint_rows b and ncols = paint_cols b in
  let rows = Array.make nrows "" in
  List.iteri (fun r row -> if r < nrows then rows.(r) <- row)
    (String.split_on_char '\n' b.data);
  let set c r =
    if c >= 0 && c < ncols && r >= 0 && r < nrows then begin
      let row = rows.(r) in
      let row =
        if String.length row > c then row
        else row ^ String.make (c + 1 - String.length row) '.' in
      rows.(r) <-
        trim_white
          (String.sub row 0 c ^ String.make 1 letter
           ^ String.sub row (c + 1) (String.length row - c - 1))
    end in
  let n = max 1 (max (abs (c1 - c0)) (abs (r1 - r0))) in
  for k = 0 to n do
    let c = c0 + ((c1 - c0) * k / n) and r = r0 + ((r1 - r0) * k / n) in
    if brush = 0 then set c r
    else
      for dr = -1 to 1 do
        for dc = -1 to 1 do set (c + dc) (r + dr) done
      done
  done;
  (* (the rows up to the last one that is not white) *)
  let last = ref (-1) in
  for r = 0 to nrows - 1 do if rows.(r) <> "" then last := r done;
  String.concat "" (List.init (!last + 1) (fun r -> rows.(r) ^ "\n"))

(* a stroke painted in the selected paint (the page changed, its undo
 * kept when the stroke began) *)
let paint (o : office) (ink : int) (brush : int) (c0 : int) (r0 : int)
    (c1 : int) (r1 : int) =
  let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  o.page <-
    replace o.page o.sel
      (Some { b with data = painted b pixel_letters.[ink] brush c0 r0 c1 r1 })

(* a key in a paint: a digit a colour (0 white, 1 black...); C-g leaves it *)
let paint_key (o : office) (brush : int) (k : int) =
  if k >= 48 && k < 58 then o.editing <- Painting (k - 48, brush, None)
  else if k = 7 then o.editing <- Nothing
  else
    o.message <-
      "a paint: the left button paints; the Paint menu, or a digit a colour; C-g"

(* A paint: each row a word of fat pixels, the rows that fit, as much
 * of each as fits *)
let paint_view (b : obj) : shape list =
  let ncols = paint_cols b and nrows = paint_rows b in
  let rec rows l r =
    match l with
    | row :: rest when r < nrows ->
        let n = min ncols (String.length row) in
        (if n > 0 then
           [ Move (b.x + 2, b.y + 2 + (4 * r),
                   Words (fat_pixels,
                          if n = String.length row then row
                          else String.sub row 0 n)) ]
         else [])
        @ rows rest (r + 1)
    | _ -> [] in
  rows (String.split_on_char '\n' b.data) 0

(* See TinyOfficeSheet.mli *)
open TinyLibPlayground
open TinyOfficeModel

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The sheet *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A sheet's data is a line a cell, its name and what was typed in it:
 *
 *     a1 3
 *     a2 Rent
 *     b1 =a1*2+sum(a1:a3)
 *
 * what was typed being a number, a formula (after an =, as in every
 * spreadsheet since VisiCalc's +), or text. A cell's name is its
 * column, a to z, and its row, 1 to 99. The numbers are integers:
 * tiny-ml's, 31 bits on tiny-machine, no floating point. *)

let name (c : int) (r : int) =
  String.make 1 (Char.chr (97 + c)) ^ string_of_int (r + 1)

(* the cells typed in: their names and what was typed *)
let cells (data : string) : (string * string) list =
  List.concat_map (fun l ->
    match String.index_opt l ' ' with
    | Some i ->
      [ String.sub l 0 i, String.sub l (i + 1) (String.length l - i - 1) ]
    | None -> []) (String.split_on_char '\n' data)

let typed_in (data : string) (n : string) =
  match List.assoc_opt n (cells data) with Some s -> s | None -> ""

(* the data with what is typed in cell n changed ("": the cell emptied) *)
let set_cell (data : string) (n : string) (input : string) : string =
  let others = List.filter (fun (m, _) -> m <> n) (cells data) in
  String.concat ""
    (List.map (fun (m, s) -> m ^ " " ^ s ^ "\n")
       (if input = "" then others else others @ [ n, input ]))

(* a cell's value: a number, text (an empty cell is "", 0 in a sum), or
 * an error, said in the cell: #SYNTAX, #REF, #TEXT (text in a sum),
 * #DIV0, #CYCLE (a cell that needs itself) *)
type value = Num of int | Str of string | Err of string

exception Bad of string

(* A formula is read and computed at once, by recursive descent, with
 * no tree: expr is terms added, a term factors multiplied, a factor a
 * number, a cell, sum(a cell:a cell), a minus, or an expression in
 * parentheses. The reader: the formula, where it is, a cell's value.
 * (Functions of the reader, not a closure: tiny-ml takes a closure's
 * values in tiny-machine's 11 registers) *)
type reader = { src : string; mutable pos : int; fetch : string -> value }

let peek_char (p : reader) =
  if p.pos < String.length p.src then p.src.[p.pos] else '\000'
let rec blanks (p : reader) =
  if peek_char p = ' ' then (p.pos <- p.pos + 1; blanks p)
let digit (c : char) = c >= '0' && c <= '9'
let expect (p : reader) (c : char) =
  blanks p;
  if peek_char p = c then p.pos <- p.pos + 1 else raise (Bad "SYNTAX")
let rec number (p : reader) (k : int) =
  if digit (peek_char p) then
    (let d = Char.code (peek_char p) - 48 in
     p.pos <- p.pos + 1; number p ((k * 10) + d))
  else k

(* a cell's name read: its column and its row, from 0 *)
let cell (p : reader) : int * int =
  blanks p;
  let c = peek_char p in
  if c < 'a' || c > 'z' then raise (Bad "SYNTAX");
  p.pos <- p.pos + 1;
  let r = number p 0 in
  if r < 1 || r > 99 then raise (Bad "REF");
  Char.code c - 97, r - 1

let int_of (v : value) : int =
  match v with
  | Num k -> k
  | Str "" -> 0
  | Str _ -> raise (Bad "TEXT")
  | Err e -> raise (Bad e)

let rec expr (p : reader) : int = sum p (term p)

and sum (p : reader) (v : int) : int =
  blanks p;
  let c = peek_char p in
  if c = '+' then (p.pos <- p.pos + 1; sum p (v + term p))
  else if c = '-' then (p.pos <- p.pos + 1; sum p (v - term p))
  else v

and term (p : reader) : int = product p (factor p)

and product (p : reader) (v : int) : int =
  blanks p;
  let c = peek_char p in
  if c = '*' then (p.pos <- p.pos + 1; product p (v * factor p))
  else if c = '/' then
    (p.pos <- p.pos + 1;
     let d = factor p in
     if d = 0 then raise (Bad "DIV0") else product p (v / d))
  else v

and factor (p : reader) : int =
  blanks p;
  let c = peek_char p in
  if digit c then number p 0
  else if c = '-' then (p.pos <- p.pos + 1; - (factor p))
  else if c = '(' then
    (p.pos <- p.pos + 1; let v = expr p in expect p ')'; v)
  else if p.pos + 4 <= String.length p.src
          && String.sub p.src p.pos 4 = "sum(" then begin
    p.pos <- p.pos + 4;
    let c0, r0 = cell p in
    expect p ':';
    let c1, r1 = cell p in
    expect p ')';
    let total = ref 0 in
    for c = min c0 c1 to max c0 c1 do
      for r = min r0 r1 to max r0 r1 do
        total := !total + int_of (p.fetch (name c r))
      done
    done;
    !total
  end
  else (let c, r = cell p in int_of (p.fetch (name c r)))

let formula (s : string) (fetch : string -> value) : value =
  let p = { src = s; pos = 0; fetch } in
  try
    let v = expr p in
    blanks p;
    if p.pos < String.length s then Err "SYNTAX" else Num v
  with Bad e -> Err e

(* The values of a sheet's cells, by name, each computed once, those it
 * needs first; a cell being computed is #CYCLE meanwhile, which is
 * what a cell that needs itself gets *)
let values (data : string) : string -> value =
  let typed = cells data and memo = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let rec value n =
    match Hashtbl.find_opt memo n with
    | Some v -> v
    | None ->
        Hashtbl.replace memo n (Err "CYCLE");
        let input =
          match List.assoc_opt n typed with Some s -> s | None -> "" in
        let v =
          if input <> "" && input.[0] = '=' then
            formula (String.sub input 1 (String.length input - 1)) value
          else
            match int_of_string_opt input with
            | Some k -> Num k
            | None -> Str input in
        Hashtbl.replace memo n v;
        v in
  value


(*****************************************************************************)
(* Editing a sheet *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the grid: a column 8 characters wide, the rows' numbers in the first
 * 3 characters, the columns' letters in the first line *)
let cell_w = 64
let sheet_left (b : obj) = b.x + 25
let sheet_top (b : obj) = b.y + 17
let sheet_cols (b : obj) = max 1 ((b.w - 26) / cell_w)
let sheet_rows (b : obj) = max 1 ((b.h - 18) / 16)

(* what is typed in cell (c, r) of the selected sheet put in it *)
let put_cell (o : office) (c : int) (r : int) (t : string) =
  change o (set_cell (List.nth o.page o.sel).data (name c r) t);
  o.editing <- Cell (c, r, None)

(* the cell of box i under (x, y): chosen, nothing typed yet *)
let choose (o : office) (i : int) (x : int) (y : int) =
  let b = List.nth o.page i in
  let c = (x - sheet_left b) / cell_w and r = (y - sheet_top b) / 16 in
  o.sel <- i;
  o.editing <-
    (if x >= sheet_left b && y >= sheet_top b && c < sheet_cols b
        && r < sheet_rows b then Cell (c, r, None)
     else Nothing)

(* A key at a cell, as in a spreadsheet: a character starts what is
 * typed there, which replaces what was; Enter puts it in the cell and
 * goes down; an arrow puts it and goes that way; C-g forgets it.
 * Enter on a cell where nothing is typed brings back what was typed
 * there, to change it; Backspace there empties the cell. *)
let cell_key (o : office) (c : int) (r : int) (typed : string option)
    (k : int) =
  let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  let move dc dr =
    o.editing <-
      Cell (max 0 (min 25 (c + dc)), max 0 (min 98 (r + dr)), None) in
  let arrow () =
    if k = 128 then move 0 (-1)
    else if k = 129 then move 0 1
    else if k = 130 then move (-1) 0
    else move 1 0 in
  match typed with
  | None ->
      if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
        o.editing <- Cell (c, r, Some (String.make 1 (Char.chr k)))
      else if k = 10 || k = 13 then
        o.editing <- Cell (c, r, Some (typed_in b.data (name c r)))
      else if k >= 128 && k <= 131 then arrow ()
      else if k = 8 || k = 127 then change o (set_cell b.data (name c r) "")
      else if k = 7 then o.editing <- Nothing
      else o.message <- "a cell: type, Enter, the arrows; C-g"
  | Some t ->
      if k >= 32 && k < 127 then
        o.editing <- Cell (c, r, Some (t ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr k)))
      else if k = 8 || k = 127 then
        o.editing <-
          Cell (c, r, Some (if t = "" then ""
                            else String.sub t 0 (String.length t - 1)))
      else if k = 10 || k = 13 then (put_cell o c r t; move 0 1)
      else if k >= 128 && k <= 131 then (put_cell o c r t; arrow ())
      else if k = 7 then o.editing <- Cell (c, r, None)


(*****************************************************************************)
(* The view *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A sheet: the columns' letters and the rows' numbers in grey, the
 * grid's lines, each cell's value, a number at the cell's right, text
 * at its left (cut at the cell's edge), an error as #WHY; the chosen
 * cell in a blue frame. The values are computed again at each view: a
 * sheet is small, and it has no other place for them. *)
let sheet_view (b : obj) (chosen : (int * int) option) : shape list =
  let value = values b.data
  and ncols = min 26 (sheet_cols b)
  and nrows = min 99 (sheet_rows b) in
  let x0 = sheet_left b and y0 = sheet_top b in
  let heads =
    List.init ncols (fun c ->
      Move (x0 + (c * cell_w) + 28, b.y + 1,
            Words (grey, String.make 1 (Char.chr (97 + c)))))
    @ List.init nrows (fun r ->
        let n = string_of_int (r + 1) in
        Move (b.x + 2 + (8 * (2 - String.length n)), y0 + (16 * r),
              Words (grey, n))) in
  let lines =
    List.init (ncols + 1) (fun c ->
      Move (x0 + (c * cell_w) - 1, b.y + 1, Rect (light_grey, 1, b.h - 2)))
    @ List.init (nrows + 1) (fun r ->
        Move (b.x + 1, y0 + (16 * r) - 1, Rect (light_grey, b.w - 2, 1))) in
  let shown c r =
    let n = name c r in
    match (if typed_in b.data n = "" then Str "" else value n) with
    | Str "" -> []
    | v ->
        let t, right =
          match v with
          | Num k -> string_of_int k, true
          | Str t -> t, false
          | Err e -> "#" ^ e, false in
        let t = if String.length t > 7 then String.sub t 0 7 else t in
        let x =
          if right then x0 + (c * cell_w) + cell_w - 4 - (8 * String.length t)
          else x0 + (c * cell_w) + 2 in
        [ Move (x, y0 + (16 * r),
                Words ((match v with Err _ -> 160 | _ -> black), t)) ] in
  let cells_shown =
    List.concat_map (fun c ->
      List.concat_map (fun r -> shown c r) (List.init nrows (fun r -> r)))
      (List.init ncols (fun c -> c)) in
  let frame = match chosen with
    | Some (c, r) when c < ncols && r < nrows ->
        let x = x0 + (c * cell_w) - 1 and y = y0 + (16 * r) - 1 in
        [ Move (x, y, Rect (blue, cell_w + 1, 2));
          Move (x, y + 15, Rect (blue, cell_w + 1, 2));
          Move (x, y, Rect (blue, 2, 17));
          Move (x + cell_w - 1, y, Rect (blue, 2, 17)) ]
    | _ -> [] in
  lines @ heads @ cells_shown @ frame

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyOfficeText.mli *)
open TinyLibPlayground
open TinyOfficeModel

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A text box's data is its text, with a mark where the style changes:
 *
 *     A \{b}bold\{} word, and \{il}large italic\{}.
 *
 * the style's letters between \{ and } (b bold, i italic, u
 * underlined, l large), \{} plain, \\ a backslash. Being edited, it is
 * two strings of the same length: the characters, and their styles. *)
let letters = "biul"

let decode (data : string) : string * string =
  let n = String.length data in
  let rec go i style chars styles =
    if i >= n then
      (String.concat "" (List.rev chars), String.concat "" (List.rev styles))
    else if data.[i] = '\\' && i + 1 < n && data.[i + 1] = '{' then begin
      match String.index_from_opt data i '}' with
      | Some e ->
          let s = ref 0 in
          String.iter (fun c ->
            match String.index_from_opt letters 0 c with
            | Some k -> s := !s lor (1 lsl k)
            | None -> ()) (String.sub data (i + 2) (e - i - 2));
          go (e + 1) !s chars styles
      | None -> go n style chars styles
    end
    else begin
      let skip = if data.[i] = '\\' && i + 1 < n then 1 else 0 in
      go (i + 1 + skip) style (String.make 1 data.[i + skip] :: chars)
        (String.make 1 (Char.chr style) :: styles)
    end in
  go 0 0 [] []

let mark (s : int) =
  "\\{"
  ^ String.concat ""
      (List.init 4 (fun k ->
         if s land (1 lsl k) <> 0 then String.make 1 letters.[k] else ""))
  ^ "}"

let encode (txt : string) (sty : string) : string =
  let rec go i was acc =
    if i >= String.length txt then
      String.concat "" (List.rev (if was <> 0 then mark 0 :: acc else acc))
    else begin
      let s = Char.code sty.[i] in
      let c = if txt.[i] = '\\' then "\\\\" else String.make 1 txt.[i] in
      go (i + 1) s (c :: (if s <> was then mark s :: acc else acc))
    end in
  go 0 0 []

(* A text laid out in a width: each character's place, its x and its
 * line, and the end's (where a cursor after the last character is);
 * each line's top and height, its largest character's. A word goes to
 * the next line when it does not fit (one wider than the line is cut);
 * a newline ends a line. *)
type laid = {
  px : int array; ln : int array; top : int array; tall : int array }

let cw (sty : string) (i : int) = char_width (Char.code sty.[i] lsl 8)

let lay_out (width : int) (txt : string) (sty : string) : laid =
  let n = String.length txt in
  let px = Array.make (n + 1) 0 and ln = Array.make (n + 1) 0 in
  let x = ref 0 and l = ref 0 and i = ref 0 in
  while !i < n do
    if txt.[!i] = '\n' then
      (px.(!i) <- !x; ln.(!i) <- !l; x := 0; incr l; incr i)
    else begin
      let j = ref !i and ww = ref 0 in
      while !j < n && txt.[!j] <> ' ' && txt.[!j] <> '\n' do
        ww := !ww + cw sty !j; incr j
      done;
      if !j = !i then j := !i + 1
      else if !x > 0 && !x + !ww > width then (x := 0; incr l);
      for k = !i to !j - 1 do
        if txt.[k] <> ' ' && !x > 0 && !x + cw sty k > width then
          (x := 0; incr l);
        px.(k) <- !x; ln.(k) <- !l; x := !x + cw sty k
      done;
      i := !j
    end
  done;
  px.(n) <- !x; ln.(n) <- !l;
  let tall = Array.make (!l + 1) 16 and top = Array.make (!l + 1) 0 in
  for k = 0 to n - 1 do
    if txt.[k] <> '\n' then
      tall.(ln.(k)) <-
        max tall.(ln.(k)) (char_height (Char.code sty.[k] lsl 8))
  done;
  for k = 1 to !l do top.(k) <- top.(k - 1) + tall.(k - 1) done;
  { px; ln; top; tall }

(* the place in the text nearest (x, y): on the line there, the first
 * character whose middle is right of x, or the line's last place *)
let index_at (lay : laid) (txt : string) (sty : string) (x : int) (y : int)
    : int =
  let n = String.length txt and lines = Array.length lay.top in
  let line = ref (lines - 1) and found = ref (-1) and last = ref 0 in
  for k = 0 to lines - 1 do
    if !line = lines - 1 && y < lay.top.(k) + lay.tall.(k) then line := k
  done;
  for i = 0 to n do
    if lay.ln.(i) = !line then begin
      last := i;
      if !found < 0
         && (i = n || txt.[i] = '\n' || lay.px.(i) + (cw sty i / 2) > x)
      then found := i
    end
  done;
  if !found >= 0 then !found else !last

(* the selection, from its first character to after its last *)
let selection (d : doc) = (min d.cur d.anchor, max d.cur d.anchor)

(* the cursor put at i, no selection, what is typed next in the style
 * of the character before *)
let go_to (d : doc) (i : int) =
  let i = max 0 (min (String.length d.txt) i) in
  d.cur <- i;
  d.anchor <- i;
  if i > 0 && d.txt.[i - 1] <> '\n' then d.typing <- Char.code d.sty.[i - 1]

(* the selection replaced by a text and its styles *)
let put_text (d : doc) (t : string) (styles : string) =
  let (a, z) = selection d and n = String.length d.txt in
  d.txt <- String.sub d.txt 0 a ^ t ^ String.sub d.txt z (n - z);
  d.sty <- String.sub d.sty 0 a ^ styles ^ String.sub d.sty z (n - z);
  d.cur <- a + String.length t;
  d.anchor <- d.cur

(* A style: the selection's (set, or taken off when all of it has it
 * already), or, nothing selected, what is typed next's; 0 plain. *)
let restyle (d : doc) (bit : int) =
  let (a, z) = selection d in
  if a = z then d.typing <- (if bit = 0 then 0 else d.typing lxor bit)
  else begin
    let all = ref true in
    for i = a to z - 1 do
      if Char.code d.sty.[i] land bit = 0 then all := false
    done;
    let one i =
      let s = Char.code d.sty.[a + i] in
      String.make 1
        (Char.chr
           (if bit = 0 then 0
            else if !all then s land lnot bit
            else s lor bit)) in
    let n = String.length d.txt in
    d.sty <-
      String.sub d.sty 0 a ^ String.concat "" (List.init (z - a) one)
      ^ String.sub d.sty z (n - z)
  end

(* what was cut or copied, its characters and their styles *)
let clipboard = ref ("", "")
let copy (d : doc) =
  let (a, z) = selection d in
  clipboard := (String.sub d.txt a (z - a), String.sub d.sty a (z - a))


(*****************************************************************************)
(* Editing *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* box i's text edited, its cursor where (x, y) is, the left button
 * selecting from there if it is down *)
let edit (o : office) (i : int) (x : int) (y : int) (selecting : bool) =
  let b = List.nth o.page i in
  let (txt, sty) = decode b.data in
  let d = { txt; sty; cur = 0; anchor = 0; typing = 0; selecting } in
  go_to d
    (index_at (lay_out (b.w - 8) txt sty) txt sty (x - b.x - 4) (y - b.y - 2));
  o.sel <- i;
  o.editing <- Writing d

(* A key in a text: a character typed, in the style of what is typed
 * next; Backspace, C-d the selection or a character deleted; the
 * arrows (C-f, C-p, C-n), C-a, C-e the cursor moved; C-b bold, Tab
 * italic, C-u underlined, C-l large; C-w cut, C-y pasted; C-g no
 * selection. The box grows to show it all. *)
let write_key (o : office) (d : doc) (k : int) =
  let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
  let lay = lay_out (b.w - 8) d.txt d.sty and n = String.length d.txt in
  let (a, z) = selection d and line = lay.ln.(d.cur) in
  let vertical l =
    if l >= 0 && l < Array.length lay.top then
      go_to d (index_at lay d.txt d.sty lay.px.(d.cur) lay.top.(l)) in
  let rec back i =
    if i > 0 && lay.ln.(i - 1) = line && d.txt.[i - 1] <> '\n' then back (i - 1)
    else i in
  let rec forth i =
    if i < n && d.txt.[i] <> '\n' && lay.ln.(i + 1) = line then forth (i + 1)
    else i in
  if (k >= 32 && k < 127) || k = 10 || k = 13 then
    put_text d (String.make 1 (if k = 13 then '\n' else Char.chr k))
      (String.make 1 (Char.chr d.typing))
  else if k = 8 || k = 127 then
    ((if a = z && a > 0 then d.anchor <- a - 1); put_text d "" "")
  else if k = 4 then
    ((if a = z && z < n then d.anchor <- z + 1); put_text d "" "")
  else if k = 130 then go_to d (if a < z then a else d.cur - 1)
  else if k = 131 || k = 6 then go_to d (if a < z then z else d.cur + 1)
  else if k = 128 || k = 16 then vertical (line - 1)
  else if k = 129 || k = 14 then vertical (line + 1)
  else if k = 1 then go_to d (back d.cur)
  else if k = 5 then go_to d (forth d.cur)
  else if k = 2 then restyle d 1
  else if k = 9 then restyle d 2
  else if k = 21 then restyle d 4
  else if k = 12 then restyle d 8
  else if k = 23 then (copy d; put_text d "" "")
  else if k = 25 then (let (t, st) = !clipboard in put_text d t st)
  else if k = 7 then d.anchor <- d.cur
  else
    o.message <-
      "a text: C-b bold, Tab italic, C-u underlined, C-l large; C-w cut, C-y paste";
  let lay = lay_out (b.w - 8) d.txt d.sty in
  let last = Array.length lay.top - 1 in
  let need = lay.top.(last) + lay.tall.(last) + 6 in
  if need > b.h then o.page <- replace o.page o.sel (Some { b with h = need })

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The view *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A text box: a word for each run of characters of a style on a line,
 * at the line's bottom (a line with a large character is taller); the
 * lines that fit. Being edited, the selection under the words in pale
 * blue, a rectangle a line, and the cursor. *)
let text_view (b : obj) (txt : string) (sty : string) (editing : doc option)
    : shape list =
  let lay = lay_out (b.w - 8) txt sty and n = String.length txt in
  let fits l = lay.top.(l) + lay.tall.(l) <= b.h - 4 in
  let x0 = b.x + 4 and y0 = b.y + 2 in
  let rec runs i acc =
    if i >= n then acc
    else if txt.[i] = '\n' || not (fits lay.ln.(i)) then runs (i + 1) acc
    else begin
      let j = ref (i + 1) and l = lay.ln.(i) and c = Char.code sty.[i] lsl 8 in
      while !j < n && txt.[!j] <> '\n' && lay.ln.(!j) = l
            && sty.[!j] = sty.[i] do
        incr j
      done;
      runs !j
        (Move (x0 + lay.px.(i), y0 + lay.top.(l) + lay.tall.(l) - char_height c,
               Words (black lor c, String.sub txt i (!j - i))) :: acc)
    end in
  let marks = match editing with
    | None -> []
    | Some d ->
        let (a, z) = selection d in
        (* the selection's pieces, a line each: its line, its two ends *)
        let rec pieces i acc =
          if i >= z then acc
          else begin
            let l = lay.ln.(i) and w = if txt.[i] = '\n' then 4 else cw sty i in
            match acc with
            | (l', p, q) :: rest when l' = l && q = lay.px.(i) ->
              pieces (i + 1) ((l, p, q + w) :: rest)
            | _ -> pieces (i + 1) ((l, lay.px.(i), lay.px.(i) + w) :: acc)
          end in
        let l = lay.ln.(d.cur) in
        List.concat
          (List.map (fun (l, p, q) ->
             if fits l then
               [ Move (x0 + p, y0 + lay.top.(l),
                       Rect (pale_blue, q - p, lay.tall.(l))) ]
             else []) (pieces a []))
        @ (if fits l then
             [ Move (x0 + lay.px.(d.cur), y0 + lay.top.(l),
                     Rect (black, 2, lay.tall.(l))) ]
           else []) in
  marks @ List.rev (runs 0 [])
tiny/TinyOffice/TinyOfficeText.mli
3295
(* TinyOffice's text box: its data, how it is laid out in its box, how
 * it is edited as it is shown (WYSIWYG), and its view.
 *
 * A text box's data is its text with a mark where the style changes:
 *
 *     A \{b}bold\{} word, and \{il}large italic\{}.
 *
 * the style's letters between \{ and } (b bold, i italic, u underlined,
 * l large), \{} plain, \\ a backslash. Being edited it is decoded into
 * two strings of the same length, the characters and their styles (a
 * byte each: bold 1, italic 2, underlined 4, large 8), the doc of
 * TinyOfficeModel, and encoded back when the editing ends:
 *
 *     txt   A bold word
 *     sty   00111100000         (one byte a character; 1: bold)
 *
 * The layout fills the box's width a word at a time, each character in
 * its style's width (the kernel's fonts), a line as tall as its largest
 * character; a click is a place in the text (index_at), the inverse.
 * The file's Markdown (TinyOfficeFile) is made from the same two
 * strings.
 *
 * modern:
 * a word processor keeps its text in a piece table (the Alto's Bravo
 * had one, and mini-office's text is lib_gui's Text_edit, another), so
 * that an edit costs a few pieces whatever the text's length; here each
 * edit makes the two strings again, a box's text being small.
 *)

(* a text box's data, as its characters and their styles, and back *)
val decode : string -> string * string
val encode : string -> string -> string

(* A text laid out as the office shows it, in a width in pixels, from its
 * characters and their styles: each character's place (and the end's),
 * its x and its line; each line's top and height *)
type laid = { px : int array; ln : int array; top : int array; tall : int array }
val lay_out : int -> string -> string -> laid

(* [index_at laid txt sty x y]: the place in the text nearest (x, y) *)
val index_at : laid -> string -> string -> int -> int -> int

(* the selection, from its first character to after its last *)
val selection : TinyOfficeModel.doc -> int * int

(* the cursor put at i, no selection, what is typed next in the style
 * of the character before *)
val go_to : TinyOfficeModel.doc -> int -> unit

(* the selection replaced by a text and its styles *)
val put_text : TinyOfficeModel.doc -> string -> string -> unit

(* a style of the selection set, or taken off when all of it has it;
 * nothing selected, of what is typed next; 0 plain *)
val restyle : TinyOfficeModel.doc -> int -> unit

(* what was cut or copied, its characters and their styles; the
 * selection copied there *)
val clipboard : (string * string) ref
val copy : TinyOfficeModel.doc -> unit

(* [edit office i x y selecting]: box i's text edited, its cursor where
 * (x, y) is, the left button selecting from there if it is down *)
val edit : TinyOfficeModel.office -> int -> int -> int -> bool -> unit

(* a key in the text being edited (TinyOffice.mli's table); the box
 * grows to show it all *)
val write_key : TinyOfficeModel.office -> TinyOfficeModel.doc -> int -> unit

(* [text_view box txt sty editing]: a word for each run of characters
 * of a style on a line, the lines that fit; being edited, its selection
 * and its cursor *)
val text_view :
  TinyOfficeModel.obj -> string -> string -> TinyOfficeModel.doc option ->
  TinyLibPlayground.shape list
tiny/TinyOffice.ml
19480
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyOffice.mli *)

(* With no system calls, the office is tested on the host by typing keys
 * and moving the mouse at it (tests/TinyOffice_test.sh). *)

open TinyLibPlayground
open TinyLibGUI
open TinyOfficeModel
open TinyOfficeText
open TinyOfficeSheet
open TinyOfficeDrawing
open TinyOfficePaint
open TinyOfficeChart
open TinyOfficeFile

(* what a key or the mouse asks of the program around: nothing, to save
 * the file, to quit *)
type request = Continue | Save | Quit

let say (o : office) (m : string) = o.message <- m

let create (width : int) (height : int) (file : string) (s : string) : office =
  let page = parse width height s in
  let where = { file; width; height; shown = 0; pages = pages_in s } in
  { page; undo = []; clean = page; sel = -1; editing = Nothing; drag = None;
    at = (16, 40); menu = menu_closed (); message = ""; prefix = false; where }

let saved (o : office) =
  o.clean <- o.page;
  o.message <- "Wrote " ^ o.where.file

(* the document's file (TinyOfficeFile's), for the program around *)
let text = TinyOfficeFile.text

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Editing a box *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* what is being edited put back into its box: a text box's text, what
 * is typed in a cell *)
let commit (o : office) =
  if o.sel >= 0 then
    match o.editing with
    | Writing d -> change o (encode d.txt d.sty)
    | Cell (c, r, Some t) -> put_cell o c r t
    | _ -> ()

let finish (o : office) = commit o; o.editing <- Nothing

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The keys and the mouse *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let help =
  "the menus above; a click edits a box; its tab moves it, its corner resizes it"

let quit (o : office) : request =
  let refused = "Not saved: Save it, or Quit again" in
  if o.page == o.clean || o.message = refused then Quit
  else (o.message <- refused; Continue)


(* a new box where the last click was, of a kind, edited at once (the
 * menus' Insert) *)
let add (o : office) (kind : string) (w : int) (h : int) =
  let x, y = o.at in
  keep o;
  let rec fresh k =
    let n = "sheet" ^ string_of_int k in
    if List.exists (fun (b : obj) -> b.called = n) o.page then fresh (k + 1)
    else n in
  o.page <-
    o.page @ [ { kind; x; y; w; h; data = "";
                 called = (if kind = "sheet" then fresh 1 else "");
                 page_no = o.where.shown } ];
  let i = List.length o.page - 1 in
  o.sel <- i;
  if kind = "text" then edit o i x y false
  else if kind = "sheet" then o.editing <- Cell (0, 0, None)
  else if kind = "paint" then o.editing <- Painting (1, 0, None)
  else o.editing <- Sketch (0, None)

(* what a menu's item asks for (the keys ask for the same) *)
let command (o : office) (c : command) : request =
  match c with
  | Do_save -> commit o; Save
  | Do_quit -> commit o; quit o
  | Do_undo ->
      finish o;
      (match o.undo with
       | p :: rest -> o.page <- p; o.undo <- rest; o.sel <- -1; fit_pages o
       | [] -> o.message <- "No more undo");
      Continue
  | Do_delete ->
      finish o;
      (if o.sel >= 0 then
         (keep o; o.page <- replace o.page o.sel None; o.sel <- -1));
      Continue
  | Do_add kind ->
      finish o;
      (if kind = "sheet" then add o "sheet" (26 + (4 * cell_w)) (18 + (6 * 16))
       else if kind = "drawing" then add o "drawing" 300 160
       else if kind = "paint" then add o "paint" 200 124 else add o "text" 200 84);
      Continue
  | Do_tool t ->
      (match o.editing with
       | Sketch (_, _) -> o.editing <- Sketch (t, None)
       | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_ink k ->
      (match o.editing with
       | Painting (_, brush, _) -> o.editing <- Painting (k, brush, None)
       | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_brush k ->
      (match o.editing with
       | Painting (ink, _, _) -> o.editing <- Painting (ink, k, None)
       | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_clear ->
      (match o.editing with Painting (_, _, _) -> change o "" | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_cut ->
      (match o.editing with Writing d -> copy d; put_text d "" "" | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_copy -> (match o.editing with Writing d -> copy d | _ -> ()); Continue
  | Do_paste ->
      (match o.editing with
       | Writing d -> let (t, st) = !clipboard in put_text d t st
       | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_style bit ->
      (match o.editing with Writing d -> restyle d bit | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_name ->
      (match o.editing with
       | Cell (_, _, _) -> commit o; o.editing <- Naming ""
       | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_chart ->
      (match o.editing with
       | Cell (c, _, _) -> commit o; make_chart o c
       | _ -> ());
      Continue
  | Do_page d ->
      finish o;
      o.sel <- -1;
      let p = o.where.shown + d in
      if p >= 0 && p < o.where.pages then o.where.shown <- p
      else
        o.message <- (if d > 0 then "No next page" else "No page before");
      Continue
  | Do_new_page ->
      (* a page after the one shown, the pages after moved one on *)
      finish o;
      keep o;
      let p = o.where.shown in
      o.page <-
        List.map (fun (b : obj) ->
          if b.page_no > p then { b with page_no = b.page_no + 1 } else b)
          o.page;
      o.where.pages <- o.where.pages + 1;
      o.where.shown <- p + 1;
      o.sel <- -1;
      Continue
  | Do_delete_page ->
      (* the page shown and what is on it gone, the pages after moved
       * back *)
      finish o;
      if o.where.pages > 1 then begin
        keep o;
        let p = o.where.shown in
        o.page <-
          List.map (fun (b : obj) ->
            if b.page_no > p then { b with page_no = b.page_no - 1 } else b)
            (List.filter (fun (b : obj) -> b.page_no <> p) o.page);
        o.where.pages <- o.where.pages - 1;
        o.where.shown <- min p (o.where.pages - 1);
        o.sel <- -1
      end
      else o.message <- "The one page is not deleted";
      Continue

(* the menus: File, Edit, Insert, the box's being edited (a text's
 * Format, a sheet's, a drawing's tools, a paint's colours: the one in
 * use marked), Page last (where it stays, as a Window menu); the keys
 * at the right *)
let office_menus (o : office) : (string * (string * command) list) list =
  [ ("File", [ ("Save     C-x C-s", Do_save); ("Quit     C-x C-c", Do_quit) ]);
    ("Edit", [ ("Undo       C-_", Do_undo); ("Cut        C-w", Do_cut);
               ("Copy", Do_copy); ("Paste      C-y", Do_paste);
               ("Delete box", Do_delete) ]);
    ("Insert", [ ("Text       C-o", Do_add "text");
                 ("Sheet    C-x t", Do_add "sheet");
                 ("Drawing  C-x d", Do_add "drawing");
                 ("Paint    C-x p", Do_add "paint") ]) ]
  @ (match o.editing with
     | Writing d ->
         let mark k s = (if d.typing land k <> 0 then "* " else "  ") ^ s in
         [ ("Format", [ (mark 1 "Bold       C-b", Do_style 1);
                        (mark 2 "Italic     Tab", Do_style 2);
                        (mark 4 "Underline  C-u", Do_style 4);
                        (mark 8 "Large      C-l", Do_style 8);
                        ("  Plain", Do_style 0) ]) ]
     | Cell (_, _, _) ->
         [ ("Sheet", [ ("Name...", Do_name);
                       ("Chart of this column", Do_chart) ]) ]
     | Painting (ink, brush, _) ->
         let colour k =
           ((if k = ink then "* " else "  ") ^ List.nth paint_names k
            ^ "      " ^ string_of_int k, Do_ink k) in
         [ ("Paint",
            List.init 10 colour
            @ [ ((if brush = 0 then "* " else "  ") ^ "Thin brush", Do_brush 0);
                ((if brush = 1 then "* " else "  ") ^ "Thick brush",
                 Do_brush 1);
                ("  Clear", Do_clear) ]) ]
     | Sketch (tool, _) ->
         let mark k s = (if k = tool then "* " else "  ") ^ s in
         [ ("Draw", [ (mark 0 "Box", Do_tool 0); (mark 1 "Arrow", Do_tool 1);
                      (mark 2 "Text", Do_tool 2) ]) ]
     | _ -> [])
  @ [ ("Page", [ ("Next      C-x ]", Do_page 1);
                 ("Previous  C-x [", Do_page (-1));
                 ("New page", Do_new_page);
                 ("Delete page", Do_delete_page) ]) ]

let key (o : office) (k : int) : request =
  match o.editing with
  | Writing d when not o.prefix && k <> 24 && k <> 31 ->
      o.message <- ""; write_key o d k; Continue
  | Cell (c, r, typed) when not o.prefix && k <> 24 ->
      o.message <- ""; cell_key o c r typed k; Continue
  | Sketch (tool, _) when not o.prefix && k <> 24 ->
      o.message <- ""; sketch_key o tool k; Continue
  | Painting (_, brush, _) when not o.prefix && k <> 24 && k <> 31 ->
      o.message <- ""; paint_key o brush k; Continue
  | Naming typed when not o.prefix && k <> 24 ->
      o.message <- ""; name_key o typed k; Continue
  | _ ->
      let was = o.message in
      o.message <- "";
      if o.prefix then begin
        o.prefix <- false;
        if k = 19 then command o Do_save
        else if k = 3 || k = 17 then (o.message <- was; command o Do_quit)
        else if k = 116 then command o (Do_add "sheet")
        else if k = 100 then command o (Do_add "drawing")
        else if k = 112 then command o (Do_add "paint")
        else if k = 93 then command o (Do_page 1)
        else if k = 91 then command o (Do_page (-1))
        else (o.message <- "C-x: not a command"; Continue)
      end
      else begin
        if k = 24 then o.prefix <- true
        else if k = 15 then ignore (command o (Do_add "text"))
        else if (k = 8 || k = 127) && o.sel >= 0 then
          ignore (command o Do_delete)
        else if k = 31 then ignore (command o Do_undo)
        else if k = 7 then (o.sel <- -1; o.message <- "Quit")
        else o.message <- help;
        Continue
      end

(* where the selected box is moved by the left button, its tab above
 * it (its kind written in it, or a sheet's name); where it is resized,
 * its corner *)
let tab_text (b : obj) = if b.called <> "" then b.called else b.kind
let tab (b : obj) = (b.x, b.y - 16, (8 * String.length (tab_text b)) + 8, 16)
let corner (b : obj) = (b.x + b.w - 8, b.y + b.h - 8, 8, 8)

let on_handle (o : office) (x : int) (y : int) : bool =
  o.sel >= 0
  && (let b = List.nth o.page o.sel in
      inside x y (tab b) || inside x y (corner b))

(* box i grabbed by the mouse at (x, y), to move or to resize *)
let grab (o : office) (i : int) (x : int) (y : int) (resizing : bool) =
  keep o;
  o.drag <- Some (i, x, y, List.nth o.page i, resizing)

(* the grabbed box, the mouse now at (x, y): moved (its tab kept below
 * the menus), or resized *)
let dragged (o : office) (x : int) (y : int) =
  match o.drag with
  | Some (i, mx, my, was, resizing) when x <> mx || y <> my ->
      let moved =
        if resizing then
          { was with w = max 32 (was.w + x - mx); h = max 24 (was.h + y - my) }
        else
          { was with x = max 0 (was.x + x - mx);
                     y = max (bar_height + 16) (was.y + y - my) } in
      o.page <- replace o.page i (Some moved)
  | _ -> ()

(* (x, y) in drawing b, kept inside it *)
let in_drawing (b : obj) (x : int) (y : int) =
  (max 0 (min (b.w - 2) (x - b.x)), max 0 (min (b.h - 2) (y - b.y)))

(* The mouse on the page, its buttons b, was before. The mouse is a
 * place, not its history: a drag may be seen as a press and a let go
 * far apart, so the let go counts where it is. *)
let page_mouse (o : office) (was : int) (x : int) (y : int) (b : int) =
  let pressed k = b land k <> 0 && was land k = 0 in
  let i = hit o x y in
  match o.editing with
  | _ when pressed 1 && on_handle o x y ->
      (* the selected box's tab or corner: it is moved or resized *)
      let resizing = inside x y (corner (List.nth o.page o.sel)) in
      finish o;
      grab o o.sel x y resizing
  | Painting (ink, brush, _) when pressed 1 && i >= 0 && i = o.sel ->
      (* in the paint being edited: a stroke begins, kept for undo *)
      let (c, r) = pixel_at (List.nth o.page i) x y in
      keep o;
      paint o ink brush c r c r;
      o.editing <- Painting (ink, brush, Some (c, r))
  | Painting (ink, brush, Some (c0, r0)) ->
      (* the stroke goes on to where the mouse is, and ends where it is
       * let go *)
      let (c, r) = pixel_at (List.nth o.page o.sel) x y in
      paint o ink brush c0 r0 c r;
      o.editing <-
        Painting (ink, brush, if b land 1 <> 0 then Some (c, r) else None)
  | Writing d when pressed 1 && i >= 0 && i = o.sel ->
      (* in the text being edited: the cursor there, a selection from it *)
      let ob = List.nth o.page i in
      go_to d
        (index_at (lay_out (ob.w - 8) d.txt d.sty) d.txt d.sty (x - ob.x - 4)
           (y - ob.y - 2));
      d.selecting <- true
  | Writing d when d.selecting ->
      (* the selection follows the mouse, to where it is let go *)
      let ob = List.nth o.page o.sel in
      d.cur <-
        index_at (lay_out (ob.w - 8) d.txt d.sty) d.txt d.sty (x - ob.x - 4)
          (y - ob.y - 2);
      if b land 1 = 0 then d.selecting <- false
  | Sketch (tool, _) when pressed 1 && i >= 0 && i = o.sel ->
      (* in the drawing being edited: a stroke begins *)
      let (sx, sy) = in_drawing (List.nth o.page i) x y in
      o.editing <- Sketch (tool, Some (sx, sy, sx, sy))
  | Sketch (tool, Some (x0, y0, _, _)) ->
      (* the stroke follows the mouse; let go, it is a shape *)
      let (ex, ey) = in_drawing (List.nth o.page o.sel) x y in
      if b land 1 <> 0 then o.editing <- Sketch (tool, Some (x0, y0, ex, ey))
      else
        (o.editing <- Sketch (tool, None);
         draw_stroke o tool (x0, y0, ex, ey))
  | _ ->
  if pressed 1 then begin
    (* a click: the editing ends; in a text box, another begins *)
    finish o;
    o.at <- (x, y);
    o.sel <- i;
    if i >= 0 && (List.nth o.page i).kind = "text" then edit o i x y true
    else if i >= 0 && (List.nth o.page i).kind = "sheet" then choose o i x y
    else if i >= 0 && (List.nth o.page i).kind = "drawing" then
      o.editing <- Sketch (0, None)
    else if i >= 0 && (List.nth o.page i).kind = "paint" then
      o.editing <- Painting (1, 0, None)
  end
  else if pressed 4 || pressed 2 then begin
    (* the right button: the box under it grabbed, by its corner to
     * resize *)
    finish o;
    o.sel <- i;
    if i >= 0 then
      (let b = List.nth o.page i in
       grab o i x y (x >= b.x + b.w - 12 && y >= b.y + b.h - 12))
  end
  else if b <> 0 then dragged o x y
  else begin
    (* let go: a box grabbed and not moved is no change to undo *)
    dragged o x y;
    (match o.drag, o.undo with
     | Some _, p :: rest when p == o.page -> o.undo <- rest
     | _ -> ());
    o.drag <- None
  end

(* the mouse: the menus' first, then the page's *)
let mouse (o : office) (x : int) (y : int) (b : int) : request =
  let was = o.menu.held in
  match menu_mouse (office_menus o) o.menu x y b with
  (* (Quit's refusal kept, as C-x C-c keeps it: Quit again quits; old:
   * cleared, and a page not saved was never left by the menu) *)
  | Picked c -> (if c <> Do_quit then o.message <- ""); command o c
  | Taken -> Continue
  | Ignored -> page_mouse o was x y b; Continue

(* The view *)
(*****************************************************************************)


(* a box's frame: blue when it is selected, with its tab above it and a
 * small square at its corner, where the mouse moves it and resizes it *)
let frame (b : obj) (selected : bool) : shape list =
  let c = if selected then blue else grey
  and x1 = b.x + b.w - 1
  and y1 = b.y + b.h - 1 in
  let (tx, ty, tw, th) = tab b in
  [ Move (b.x, b.y, Rect (c, b.w, 1)); Move (b.x, y1, Rect (c, b.w, 1));
    Move (b.x, b.y, Rect (c, 1, b.h)); Move (x1, b.y, Rect (c, 1, b.h)) ]
  @ (if selected then
       [ Move (tx, ty, Rect (c, tw, th));
         Move (tx + 4, ty, Words (white, tab_text b));
         Move (x1 - 7, y1 - 7, Rect (c, 8, 8)) ]
     else [])

(* the status line: the page's message (what was just done, or why
 * not: it goes at the next key or click), or what the box being edited
 * says, or the file's name (old: a sheet's, a paint's or a drawing's
 * words over the message, and Quit's refusal not seen) *)
let status (o : office) : shape list =
  let file = o.where.file
  and width = o.where.width
  and height = o.where.height in
  let file =
    if o.where.pages > 1 then
      file ^ " (page " ^ string_of_int (o.where.shown + 1) ^ " of "
      ^ string_of_int o.where.pages ^ ")"
    else file in
  let said = if o.message <> "" then o.message else match o.editing with
    | Writing d ->
        let names =
          List.filter (fun t -> t <> "")
            (List.init 4 (fun k ->
               if d.typing land (1 lsl k) <> 0 then
                 List.nth [ "bold"; "italic"; "underlined"; "large" ] k
               else "")) in
        "text, typing "
        ^ (if names = [] then "plain" else String.concat " " names)
        ^ "; the Format menu, or C-b, Tab, C-u, C-l"
    | Cell (c, r, typed) when o.sel >= 0 ->
        (* the formula bar: the cell, what is being typed in it, or what
         * was *)
        name c r ^ ": "
        ^ (match typed with
           | Some t -> t ^ "_"
           | None -> typed_in (List.nth o.page o.sel).data (name c r))
    | Naming typed ->
        "the sheet's name: " ^ typed ^ "_ (Enter gives it, C-g not)"
    | Painting (ink, brush, _) ->
        "paint: " ^ List.nth paint_names ink
        ^ (if brush = 0 then ", thin" else ", thick")
        ^ "; the left button paints; the Paint menu, or a digit"
    | Sketch (tool, _) ->
        "drawing: " ^ List.nth tools tool
        ^ " (Tab: another); the left button draws; type a label"
    | _ -> "" in
  let m = if said <> "" then said
    else if o.prefix then "C-x-"
    else
      file ^ (if o.page == o.clean then "" else " (modified)") ^ "    "
      ^ help in
  let m =
    if String.length m * 8 > width - 8 then String.sub m 0 ((width - 8) / 8)
    else m in
  [ Move (0, height - 18, Rect (light_grey, width, 18));
    Move (4, height - 17, Words (black, m)) ]

let view (o : office) : shape list =
  let width = o.where.width and height = o.where.height in
  let i = ref (-1) in
  Rect (white, width, height)
  :: List.concat (List.map (fun (b : obj) ->
       incr i;
       if b.page_no <> o.where.shown then [] else
       let content = match o.editing with
         | Writing d when !i = o.sel -> text_view b d.txt d.sty (Some d)
         | Cell (c, r, _) when !i = o.sel -> sheet_view b (Some (c, r))
         | Sketch (tool, stroke) when !i = o.sel -> drawing_view b tool stroke
         | _ ->
             if b.kind = "text" then
               (let (t, st) = decode b.data in text_view b t st None)
             else if b.kind = "sheet" then sheet_view b None
             else if b.kind = "drawing" then drawing_view b 0 None
             else if b.kind = "paint" then paint_view b
             else if b.kind = "chart" then chart_view o.page b
             else [ Move (b.x + 4, b.y + 2, Words (black, b.kind ^ "?")) ] in
       [ Group (frame b (!i = o.sel) @ content) ]) o.page)
  @ [ Group (status o) ] @ menu_view width (office_menus o) o.menu
tiny/TinyOffice.mli

(* tiny-office: a page of objects, each a kind of document in a box,
 * in one program (docs/plans/done/plan_tiny_office.md).
 *
 * Its full-size counterpart in m-ix is mini-office (apps/office/,
 * about 5,200 lines): a document of parts (text, sheet, picture,
 * drawing, chart), each a record of functions. This is the same idea
 * cut down, the compound document of the Xerox Star and of Smalltalk:
 *
 *     the shell          the page: selecting, moving, resizing, a new
 *         |              box, deleting, undo, the file
 *     a part             what one kind of object needs: how it is
 *         |              drawn, how it is edited (here: text, sheet,
 *         |              drawing)
 *     its data           a string, whatever the kind
 *
 * The shell is this file; the parts are TinyOffice/'s modules, a kind
 * each: TinyOfficeText, TinyOfficeSheet, TinyOfficeDrawing,
 * TinyOfficePaint and TinyOfficeChart (its data read, its keys, its
 * view), on TinyOfficeModel (the page's objects, what is being edited,
 * the office's record); TinyOfficeFile reads and writes the file.
 *
 * {b Every object's data is text}, and undo is the earlier pages, kept
 * in a list (an edit makes a new page, the old one is not changed).
 *
 * {b The file of a document is in mini-troff's format}
 * (plan_typesetting.md: Markdown's lines, \name[options]{text} for what
 * Markdown has not): its pages one after the other, a line \newpage
 * between two (LaTeX's); each object a \box[x y w h]{...} around its
 * content, a text box's Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, a line "# "
 * large, \u{} underlined, \large{} large in a line; a sheet a table
 * (the columns' letters, then what was typed, a row a line), a drawing
 * or a paint a fence (```drawing, ```paint) of its lines. So a document
 * is read, or written, in emacs; and a Markdown file is opened as one text
 * box. (Being edited, a text box's data is its text with a mark where
 * the style changes, "a \{b}bold\{} word"; it is the file's Markdown
 * only in the file.)
 *
 * {b A text box is edited as it is shown} (WYSIWYG, the Alto's Bravo,
 * then MacWrite and Word): its text filled to the box's width, a word
 * that does not fit on the next line, each character in its style (the
 * kernel's fonts: bold, large 16 by 32, italic any of them slanted);
 * a line as tall as its largest character. A click puts the cursor, a
 * drag selects; the Format menu (or C-b, Tab, C-u, C-l) sets or takes
 * off a style, of the selection, or of what is typed next; Edit's Cut,
 * Copy, Paste (C-w, C-y). The box grows to show all of its text.
 * (Before, the box was edited by TinyEditorScreen, its marks shown, as
 * troff's source: the author wanted a word processor.)
 *
 * {b A sheet's data is a line a cell}: its name and what was typed in
 * it, "a1 Rent", "b1 500", "b3 =b1+b2". What was typed is a number, a
 * formula after an = (+ - * /, parentheses, cells, sum(b1:b2)), or
 * text. The values are computed at each view, each cell once, those it
 * needs first: a cell being computed counts as #CYCLE, which is what a
 * cell that needs itself shows. Integers only (tiny-ml's). It is edited
 * as any spreadsheet: a cell chosen (a click, the arrows), what is
 * typed replaces what was, shown in the status line as in a formula
 * bar, Enter puts it and goes down; Enter on a cell brings back what is
 * in it.
 *
 * {b A drawing's data is a line a shape}, at its place in the box:
 * "box 20 20 80 30 cpu", "arrow 100 35 180 90", "text 30 150 a note"
 * (pic's idea). An arrow goes across then up or down, a block
 * diagram's connector: the shapes are rectangles and words, and a
 * slanted line would need another kind. The left button drags a box or
 * an arrow, or places a text (the Draw menu, or Tab, changes the tool);
 * what is typed is the last shape's label.
 *
 * {b The menus} are pull-down menus across the top, TinyLibGUI's, as
 * in every office program since the Lisa's and the Macintosh's: File
 * (Save, Quit), Edit (Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete box), Insert
 * (Text, Sheet, Drawing, Paint), the box's being edited (a text's
 * Format, a sheet's Sheet, a drawing's Draw, a paint's Paint), and Page
 * last (Next, Previous, New page, Delete page: one page shown at a
 * time, the status line saying which). Each item shows its key.
 *
 * {b A paint's data is a line a row of pixels}, a letter a pixel, its
 * colour: ". white, k black, r red..." (TinyLibPlayground's
 * pixel_letters). A pixel is 4 by 4 on the page; the left button
 * paints, a line between the places the mouse was seen at, thin or
 * thick (3 pixels); the Paint menu, or a digit, a colour. A row is one
 * word of the kernel's fat pixels, so a stroke draws its rows again,
 * not the picture.
 *
 * {b A chart draws a sheet's cells as bars}, its data a line, "bars
 * budget b1:b3 a1:a3": the sheet by its name, the cells of the values,
 * of the labels. The values are the sheet's at each view, so a chart
 * follows its sheet. A sheet is named when made (sheet1, sheet2...), its
 * name on its tab and in its \box line; the Sheet menu, a cell chosen,
 * names it (its charts renamed too) or makes a chart of the cell's
 * column, its numbers, the column at its left their labels.
 *
 * The mouse and the keys:
 *
 *     left button          a click in a text box edits it, in a sheet
 *                          chooses a cell; elsewhere, the editing ends,
 *                          and the place is kept; on the menus, they
 *     the selected box     its tab above it (its kind) moves it; the
 *                          square at its corner resizes it
 *     right button, held   the box under it moves with the mouse; from
 *                          its bottom right corner, the box is resized
 *     C-o, C-x t, d, p     a new text box, sheet, drawing, paint,
 *                          where the last click was
 *     in a text            a character typed; Backspace, C-d; the
 *                          arrows, C-a, C-e; C-g no selection
 *     in a sheet           a character starts what is typed in the cell;
 *                          Enter, the arrows put it; C-g forgets it
 *     in a drawing         Tab another tool; the left button draws; a
 *                          character the last label's; C-g leaves it
 *     Backspace, Delete    the selected box removed
 *     C-_ (C-/)            undo: the page as it was before the last change
 *     C-x ], C-x [         the next page, the one before (Emacs's)
 *     C-x C-s, C-x C-c     save, quit (while editing too)
 *
 * {b Only what changed is drawn.} [view] is the page as shapes
 * (TinyLibPlayground's): the ground, a group for each object, one for the
 * status line. TinyLibGUI's run_canvas, which runs the office on
 * tiny-kernel (TinyKernel/user/office.ml, a few lines), compares each
 * group with the one it drew before and draws what changed: tiny-kernel
 * draws a character in some 13,000 instructions, and a page redrawn at
 * each key would be seconds of tiny-machine.
 *
 * This file uses no system calls: the program around reads the keys and
 * the mouse, draws and writes the file.
 *
 * mini-office is the author's playground's apps/office/TinyOffice.ml,
 * brought to ix under that name: a part there is a record of
 * functions (Component), a file a value marshalled behind a line
 * (Saved), the shapes floats that move, scale and rotate, the letters
 * Hershey's strokes, a text a piece table (lib_gui's Text_edit), the
 * menus Gui's, in immediate mode, and a PDF written from the view.
 * What is ours, against it: an object's kind a word and its
 * data a string, a match on the kind where a part has its functions;
 * the file text in mini-troff's format, so emacs and troff read it
 * with nothing of the office's; integers in pixels, the kernel's one
 * font and its looks; the page drawn by run_canvas where it changed;
 * PDF left to tiny-troff.
 *
 * What is left out, for now: charts other than bars (a pie, lines),
 * moving a drawing's shapes once drawn, a sheet's floating point, its
 * other functions than sum, and formulas that follow a cell moved, a
 * paint's fill and its colours other than ten, other fonts and sizes
 * (one font, 8 by 16, its bold, italic and large), colours of text,
 * paragraphs centred or justified, a text that flows from a box to the
 * next or onto the next page, and undo of the typing inside a box (undo
 * takes the document back to before the box was edited).
 *)

(* [create width height file text]: the office on a page of that size
 * in pixels, file the page's name, text the file's text ("" for a new
 * page) *)
val create : int -> int -> string -> string -> TinyOfficeModel.office

(* what a key or the mouse asks of the program around: nothing, to save
 * the file, to quit *)
type request = Continue | Save | Quit

(* a key (a byte, as the console gives it: the arrows 128 to 131), and
 * what it asks *)
val key : TinyOfficeModel.office -> int -> request

(* the mouse: where it is, its buttons (1 left, 2 middle, 4 right); and
 * what it asks of the program around (the File menu's) *)
val mouse : TinyOfficeModel.office -> int -> int -> int -> request

(* the page as shapes: the ground (white), each object's group (its
 * frame, its content), the status line's, the menus' bar and the open
 * menu *)
val view : TinyOfficeModel.office -> TinyLibPlayground.shape list

(* the page as its file's text; and the program around saying it wrote it *)
val text : TinyOfficeModel.office -> string
val saved : TinyOfficeModel.office -> unit
val say : TinyOfficeModel.office -> string -> unit

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyPlay.mli *)

open TinyCalls
open TinyLibPlayground

type wav = { rate : int; channels : int; bits : int; at : int; bytes : int }

(* numbers of 16 and 32 bits, the low byte first *)
let u16 = String.get_uint16_le
let u32 s i = u16 s i + (u16 s (i + 2) lsl 16)

(* RIFF's chunks from 12 on, each four letters, a length and its bytes
 * (an odd length padded): "fmt " says the encoding (1, PCM), the
 * channels, the rate, the bits; "data" has the samples; the others
 * are skipped *)
let wav s =
  let n = String.length s in
  if n < 12 || String.sub s 0 4 <> "RIFF" || String.sub s 8 4 <> "WAVE" then
    failwith "not a WAV file";
  let rec chunks i w =
    if i + 8 > n then w
    else begin
      let size = u32 s (i + 4) in
      let id = String.sub s i 4 in
      let w =
        if id = "fmt " && i + 24 <= n then begin
          if u16 s (i + 8) <> 1 then failwith "not PCM";
          { w with channels = u16 s (i + 10); rate = u32 s (i + 12);
                   bits = u16 s (i + 22) }
        end
        else if id = "data" then { w with at = i + 8; bytes = min size (n - i - 8) }
        else w in
      chunks (i + 8 + size + (size land 1)) w
    end in
  let w = chunks 12 { rate = 0; channels = 0; bits = 0; at = 0; bytes = 0 } in
  if w.rate = 0 || w.channels = 0 then failwith "no format";
  if w.bits <> 8 && w.bits <> 16 then failwith "not 8 or 16 bits";
  if w.rate > 96000 then failwith "more than 96,000 samples a second";
  w

(* the frames, and as many of the speaker's samples (the products
 * split, so that none passes 31 bits) *)
let frames w = w.bytes / (w.channels * w.bits / 8)
let samples w =
  let f = frames w in
  (f / w.rate * 8000) + (f mod w.rate * 8000 / w.rate)

(* At each sample, the frame at its time, k * rate / 8,000, exactly
 * and with no division a sample: the first one's computed, then each
 * next one is rate / 8,000 frames further and the remainder carried,
 * a frame more when it reaches 8,000 (Bresenham's line, of time
 * against frames). A channel's value is its top byte, signed (8 bits
 * are unsigned in a WAV, 128 the silence); the frame's, the mean of
 * two channels, the first of more. *)
let piece w s k n =
  let n = max 0 (min n (samples w - k)) in
  let size = w.bits / 8 in
  let frame = w.channels * size in
  let last = frames w - 1 in
  let channel o =
    if size = 1 then Char.code s.[o] - 128
    else (let b = Char.code s.[o + 1] in if b > 127 then b - 256 else b) in
  let at = ref ((k / 8000 * w.rate) + (k mod 8000 * w.rate / 8000))
  and left = ref (k mod 8000 * w.rate mod 8000) in
  let whole = w.rate / 8000 and part = w.rate mod 8000 in
  let b = Bytes.make n '\000' in
  for j = 0 to n - 1 do
    let o = w.at + (min last !at * frame) in
    let v =
      if w.channels = 1 then channel o
      else if w.channels = 2 then (channel o + channel (o + size)) asr 1
      else channel o in
    Bytes.set b j (Char.chr (v land 255));
    at := !at + whole;
    left := !left + part;
    if !left >= 8000 then (left := !left - 8000; incr at)
  done;
  Bytes.to_string b

let block = 2048

let play out s =
  let w = wav s in
  let n = samples w in
  let rec from k =
    if k < n then begin
      ignore (u_write out (samples_message (piece w s k block)));
      from (k + block)
    end in
  from 0
tiny/TinyPlay.mli
2705
(* tiny-play: a WAV file played, on tiny-kernel's speaker
 * (plan_tiny_audio.md, step 4). m-ix's twin is mini-play
 * (apps/media/play/, on lib_audio/formats/), which plays MOD, MIDI,
 * MP3, WAV and ABC to Plan 9's /dev/audio.
 *
 *     play /examples/korobeiniki.wav        on tiny-kernel
 *     tiny-play song.wav                    on the host (../sdl/)
 *
 * The idea kept: a file's sound is its samples made into the speaker's,
 * a block at a time, each written when the last was taken, so the
 * kernel, which takes a voice's samples a second ahead of the speaker
 * at most, paces the program, and the first is heard after a block, not
 * after the whole file:
 *
 *     the file's bytes --> [wav]: RIFF's chunks, "fmt " and "data"
 *                             |  2,048 samples at a time ([block])
 *                             v
 *         the frame at each sample's time, its channels' mean, its top
 *         8 bits ([piece]) --> /dev/audio, a message `p n` and the n bytes
 *
 * The speaker's samples are 8,000 a second, a byte each, signed: what a
 * WAV has (8 or 16 bits, one channel or two, 44,100 or 11,025 a
 * second) is made that by taking, at each of the speaker's samples, the
 * file's frame at that time (exactly, by Bresenham's stepping: no
 * division a sample), the
 * mean of its channels, and its top byte. No filter: a file of 44,100
 * a second loses what is above 4,000 Hz, and what is above folds down
 * (aliasing), which a filter before the taking would prevent.
 *
 * What is dropped: every other format (MOD, MIDI, MP3: lib_audio has
 * thousands of lines for them), floats, a WAV's other encodings
 * (24 or 32 bits, floats, ADPCM, A-law), and the -c and -s options.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * WAV is Microsoft's and IBM's RIFF (1991), itself Electronic Arts'
 * IFF (1985, the Amiga's) with its numbers little-endian: chunks, each
 * four letters and a length, so a reader skips what it does not know.
 *)

(* a WAV's sound: its rate, its channels, its bits a sample, where its
 * samples start and how many bytes they are *)
type wav = { rate : int; channels : int; bits : int; at : int; bytes : int }

(* a file's WAV, or Failure why (not RIFF's, not PCM, not 8 or 16 bits) *)
val wav : string -> wav

(* how many of the speaker's samples (8,000 a second) its sound is *)
val samples : wav -> int

(* [piece w data k n]: the speaker's samples k to k + n - 1 of the
 * file's sound, a byte each, signed *)
val piece : wav -> string -> int -> int -> string

(* the samples a block *)
val block : int

(* [play out data]: the file's sound written to out (/dev/audio), a block
 * at a time; Failure why when it is no WAV this plays *)
val play : int -> string -> unit
tiny/TinyProfiler.ml
5647
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyProfiler.mli *)

let usage = {|usage: tiny-prof [-n count] [-diff base] [-base hex] profile
         [-k file.map...] [-u file.map...]|}

(* [add tbl k n]: n added to k's count, 0 when k has none (by hand:
 * OCaml's Option.value takes ~default, ix's does not) *)
let add tbl k n =
  Hashtbl.replace tbl k
    (n + (match Hashtbl.find_opt tbl k with Some m -> m | None -> 0))

(* A profile's lines "k|u base pc count" (TinyMachineCPU.profile_lines):
 * the counts by (the kernel's?, base, pc). *)
let read_profile caps file =
  let int_of_hex h = int_of_string ("0x" ^ h) in
  let counts = Hashtbl.create 4096 in
  List.iter (fun line ->
    match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
    | [ m; b; pc; n ] ->
        let k = m = "k", int_of_hex b, int_of_hex pc in
        add counts k (int_of_string n)
    | _ -> ()) (String.split_on_char '\n' (TinyLibSystem.read_file caps file));
  counts

(* the functions of tiny-linker's maps (-map: "address label" lines),
 * by address (TinyLibSymbols's, as the function an address is in) *)
let functions caps files =
  TinyLibSymbols.labels
    (String.concat "\n" (List.map (TinyLibSystem.read_file caps) files))
let find funcs pc =
  match TinyLibSymbols.find funcs pc with Some (f, _) -> f | None -> "?"

(* 1234567 as 1,234,567 *)
let commas n =
  let s = string_of_int n in
  let k = String.length s in
  String.concat "" (List.init k (fun i ->
    (if i > 0 && (k - i) mod 3 = 0 then "," else "") ^ String.make 1 s.[i]))

(* n of total in percent, a tenth's digit, rounded: integers, which
 * tiny-ml has (its 31 bits: both scaled down first when total is
 * large, so that n * 2000 fits) (old: floats, %.1f) *)
let percent n total =
  if total = 0 then "0.0"
  else
    let g = max 1 (total / 100000) in
    let t = ((n / g * 2000 / (total / g)) + 1) / 2 in
    string_of_int (t / 10) ^ "." ^ string_of_int (t mod 10)


let main (caps : < Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; .. >) =
  let print = TinyLibSystem.print caps in
  let rec options top diff base = function
    | "-n" :: n :: rest -> options (int_of_string n) diff base rest
    | "-diff" :: f :: rest -> options top (Some f) base rest
    | "-base" :: b :: rest ->
        options top diff (Some (int_of_string ("0x" ^ b))) rest
    | file :: rest when file.[0] <> '-' ->
        (* the files after -k are the kernel's, after -u the program's *)
        let rec files k u kernel = function
          | "-k" :: rest -> files k u true rest
          | "-u" :: rest -> files k u false rest
          | f :: rest ->
              if kernel then files (f :: k) u kernel rest
              else files k (f :: u) kernel rest
          | [] -> List.rev k, List.rev u in
        Some (top, diff, base, file, files [] [] false rest)
    | _ -> None in
  match options 20 None None (List.tl (TinyLibSystem.argv caps)) with
  | None -> TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (usage ^ "\n"); 2
  | Some (top, diff, base, file, (kfiles, ufiles)) ->
      let counts = read_profile caps file in
      Option.iter (fun f ->
        Hashtbl.iter (fun k n ->
            match Hashtbl.find_opt counts k with
            | Some m -> Hashtbl.replace counts k (max 0 (m - n))
            | None -> ())
          (read_profile caps f)) diff;
      (* the totals: the kernel's, and each program's by its window's base *)
      let kernel = ref 0 and programs = Hashtbl.create 8 in
      Hashtbl.iter (fun (k, b, _) n ->
        if k then kernel := !kernel + n else add programs b n) counts;
      let user = Hashtbl.fold (fun _ n acc -> acc + n) programs 0 in
      let total = !kernel + user in
      let named = match base with
        | Some b -> b
        | None ->
            fst (Hashtbl.fold (fun b n (bb, bn) ->
                if n > bn || (n = bn && b < bb) then (b, n) else (bb, bn))
              programs (0, -1)) in
      let kfuncs = functions caps kfiles and ufuncs = functions caps ufiles in
      (* each count to its function *)
      let by = Hashtbl.create 256 in
      Hashtbl.iter (fun (k, b, pc) n ->
        let where =
          if k then
            "k", (if kfiles = [] then "(the kernel)" else find kfuncs pc)
          else if b <> named then "u", "(another program)"
          else "u", (if ufiles = [] then "(the program)" else find ufuncs pc) in
        add by where n) counts;
      (* the most first; the same counts in their names' order (a table's
       * order is its library's: OCaml's and tiny-ml's are others) *)
      let most (a, n) (b, m) = if n <> m then compare m n else compare a b in
      let rows =
        List.sort most (Hashtbl.fold (fun w n acc -> (w, n) :: acc) by []) in
      print (Printf.sprintf "%s instructions: the kernel %s%%, programs %s%%\n"
        (commas total) (percent !kernel total) (percent user total));
      if Hashtbl.fold (fun _ n k -> if n > 0 then k + 1 else k) programs 0 > 1
      then
        print (Printf.sprintf
          "programs, by their window's base: %s (-u is the one at %x)\n"
          (String.concat ", "
             (List.map (fun (b, n) -> Printf.sprintf "%x %s" b (commas n))
                (List.sort most
                   (Hashtbl.fold (fun b n acc ->
                      if n > 0 then (b, n) :: acc else acc) programs []))))
          named);
      print (Printf.sprintf "%12s %6s     function\n" "count" "%");
      List.iteri (fun i ((mode, name), n) ->
        if i < top && n > 0 then
          print (Printf.sprintf "%12s %6s  %s  %s\n" (commas n)
            (percent n total) mode name)) rows;
      0

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-prof" main
tiny/TinyProfiler.mli
6046
(* tiny-prof: where a program's instructions went, by function. It reads
 * a profile written by tiny-cpu -prof or tiny-machine -prof (every
 * instruction run, counted by its address) and tiny-linker's maps of
 * what ran (-map: each label's address), and prints the functions that
 * ran most, with their share.
 *
 *     tiny-machine -prof p boot.img          a session, counted
 *     tiny-prof p -k kernel.img.map -u bin/www.map
 *
 *     12,345,678 instructions: the kernel 58.6%, programs 41.4%
 *         count      %     function
 *       989,893   8.0  k  row_copy2
 *       862,816   7.0  u  browse
 *       ...
 *
 * The addresses of the labels come from the link itself (tiny-linker
 * writes the map as it writes the image), so the names cannot disagree
 * with what ran. A
 * count goes to the last label at or before its address. A label that
 * a compiler makes inside a function (tiny-ml's TinyBrowser.L12, tiny-c's
 * tm.L51) is not a function, so its counts go to the function before
 * it; an assembly loop's labels (row_copy2) are kept, as they say which
 * loop. tiny-ml's functions are named TinyBrowser.f151_browse: shown as browse.
 *
 * A profile of tiny-machine separates the kernel's instructions (-k
 * names its map) from the programs', and the programs by the base of
 * their window, their partition: -u names the map of one program,
 * the one with the most instructions unless -base says which. The
 * others are counted as "another program".
 *
 * With -diff base, a profile of a shorter run (the same session without
 * what is measured) is taken off first: a page down, measured as a
 * session with eight of them less the same session with none.
 *
 * A worked example: why www scrolled slowly (2026-10-16).
 *
 * The question was where the instructions of a page down go. A recorded
 * session makes it repeatable: www OCaml typed, then, once the page and
 * its pictures are in, eight spaces (eight page downs). A second session
 * is the same with one key that does nothing (x), the baseline: what
 * the first costs more than the second is the eight page downs alone.
 *
 *     printf '20000000 k www OCaml\\n\n600000000 k        \n' > pages.events
 *     printf '20000000 k www OCaml\\n\n600000000 k x\n' > base.events
 *     tiny-machine -prof base.prof -net tiny/tests/www -events base.events \
 *       tiny/TinyKernel/_make/boot.img
 *     tiny-machine -prof pages.prof -net tiny/tests/www -events pages.events \
 *       tiny/TinyKernel/_make/boot.img
 *
 * Then the maps of what ran, the kernel's and www's (tiny/TinyKernel's
 * Makefile links each with -map):
 *
 *     M=tiny/TinyKernel/_make
 *     tiny-prof -diff base.prof pages.prof -k $M/kernel.img.map \
 *       -u $M/bin/www.map
 *
 * (old: the .tm files given, in their link's order, and assembled
 * again by tiny-prof, before tiny-linker)
 *
 * The first line said how the eight page downs divided between the
 * kernel (drawing what www asks for) and www (making the messages). The
 * lines under it named the functions, and three findings came out of
 * them, each checked by profiling again after the change:
 *
 * - The kernel drew a text a character at a time, each character a
 *   whole draw (a rectangle clipped against three images, then 16 rows
 *   of row_mask): draw, row_mask and the ML around them were most of
 *   the kernel's share, some 13,000 instructions a character. Now one
 *   call of draw.tm's glyphs draws a whole text, a word at a time, and
 *   glyphs3 is 2% of the eight page downs.
 * - row_copy2, the loop copying the screen onto itself, then came first
 *   (38% of the kernel's): the glide of a page down copies the page's
 *   area at each of its steps. Unrolled, four words a turn; what is left
 *   is the price of seeing the page move.
 * - In www, ml_concat and the collector after it (mlsys.copy,
 *   mlsys.collect, ml_alloc): over half of www's share was concatenating
 *   strings to build the drawing messages, two concatenations a number.
 *   TinyLibDraw now makes the bytes of the numbers up to 1023 once.
 *   The profile also showed skip (lines_between walking the page's list
 *   of lines from its end), so the lines are kept in an array too.
 *
 * The page down went from about 7.7 million instructions to 5.4, the
 * arrow from over a million to 0.4 (plan_tiny_browser.md's status has
 * the table). A function in the list is the place to look, not the
 * answer: draw was not slow, it was called 80 times where once would
 * do; the profile says where, reading the code says why.
 *
 * mini-qemu has the same pair, with sampling: -prof F counts every
 * 1024th pc (raspberry/observe/Prof.ml), and a script maps them to a
 * kernel's functions (kernels/9pi/tests/perf/pcprof.py). Here every
 * instruction is counted: the machine is slow enough for that to cost
 * little more than running it, and two runs give the same profile.
 *
 * Plan 9's emulators had the idea first: vi and 5i count every
 * instruction fetched by its address and print, by the program's
 * symbol table, each function's count and share ($ip: principia's
 * machine/5i, stats.c's iprofile, its columns cycles, %, symbol and
 * file); mini-5i left it out. What is ours: the counts a file of their
 * own, so that a run can be taken off another (-diff), and a machine
 * with a kernel, whose counts and each program's are told apart.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Unix's prof (1973 or so) counted where the program was at each tick
 * of the clock, the kernel adding one to a histogram of addresses
 * (profil(2)); gprof (Graham, Kessler and McKusick, 1982) added who
 * called whom. A machine that is a program can do better than sample:
 * it counts every instruction, and disturbs nothing, not even the
 * kernel with its interrupts off.
 *
 * References: plan_tiny_browser.md (the profile that found where www's
 * time went, before this program existed); raspberry/observe/Prof.mli.
 *)

(* the program: its arguments to its exit status *)
val main : < Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.argv; Cap.open_in; .. > -> int
tiny/TinyShell.ml
