(* See TinyShell.mli *)

(* The tests: tests/TinyShell_test.sh runs scripts written in this
 * subset both through this shell and through 9base's rc, which must
 * print the same thing. *)

(* -h: the usage, and the language by example, as it runs *)
open Common

let help = "usage: tiny-shell [-eiI] [-c cmd | file] [arg ...]
A subset of rc's language (mini-rc is rc, faithfully): runs the file, the -c
command, or the commands typed at a terminal, with a prompt (-i: always).
-e: a command that fails, not in a condition, ends the shell.
The language, by example, one line after the other at its prompt:
  x=(a b c); echo $x $#x              a b c 3 (a variable is a list)
  echo $x^.c                          a.c b.c c.c
  for(i in a b) echo $i               a, then b
  ~ b $x && echo b is in x            ~ matches; && || ! on the statuses
  if(~ $#x 3) echo three
  fn greet { echo hello $1 }; greet you
  x=`{echo one two}; echo $#x         2: a command's output, its words
  { echo a; echo b } > f; cat f | wc -l
  ls /nonexistent >[2] /dev/null || echo failed: $status
"

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Types *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type piece =
  | Lit of string * bool     (* text, quoted *)
  | Var of string            (* $x, $1, $* *)
  | Count of string          (* $#x *)
  | Back of cmd              (* `{cmd} *)

and word = piece list        (* the pieces, joined *)

and cmd =
  | Empty
  | Simple of word list * redir list
  | Match of word list * redir list             (* ~ subject pattern... *)
  | Seq of cmd * cmd
  | Async of cmd
  | And of cmd * cmd
  | Or of cmd * cmd
  | Not of cmd
  | Pipe of cmd * cmd
  | Brace of cmd * redir list
  | Subshell of cmd
  | If of cmd * cmd
  | While of cmd * cmd
  | For of string * word list option * cmd
  | Fn of string * cmd
  | Assign of string * word list * cmd option   (* x=v, or x=v cmd *)

and redir = Open of int * mode * word | Dup of int * int

(* < > >> *)
(* old: the Unix.open_flag list itself, which said the kind only to open *)
and mode = Read | Write | Append

exception Error of string
(* (not Exit: that is the standard library's, and tiny-ml has one space of
 * names) *)
exception Exits of string

type caps =
  < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.chdir; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    Cap.stdin; Cap.stderr; Cap.stdout; Cap.exit; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal; Cap.env;
    Cap.readdir >

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Lexing *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type token =
  | WORD of word | BACKQ | SEMI | AMP | NL | EOF | PIPE | ANDAND | OROR
  | LPAREN | RPAREN | LBRACE | RBRACE | REDIR of redir

type lexer = { text : string; mutable pos : int }

let peekc lx =
  if lx.pos < String.length lx.text then Some lx.text.[lx.pos] else None
let skip lx = lx.pos <- lx.pos + 1
let wordchr c = not (String.contains " \t\n#;&|`'{}()<>^$" c)
let idchr c =
  c = '_' || ('a' <= c && c <= 'z') || ('A' <= c && c <= 'Z')
  || ('0' <= c && c <= '9')
let while_ lx p =
  while (match peekc lx with Some c -> p c | None -> false) do skip lx done

let rec token lx : token =
  let op tok = skip lx; tok in
  let two c tok1 tok2 = skip lx; if peekc lx = Some c then op tok2 else tok1 in
  match peekc lx with
  | None -> EOF
  | Some (' ' | '\t') -> skip lx; token lx
  | Some '#' -> while_ lx (( <> ) '\n'); token lx
  | Some '\\'
    when lx.pos + 1 < String.length lx.text && lx.text.[lx.pos + 1] = '\n' ->
      lx.pos <- lx.pos + 2; token lx   (* a line continued *)
  | Some '\n' -> op NL | Some ';' -> op SEMI | Some '`' -> op BACKQ
  | Some '(' -> op LPAREN | Some ')' -> op RPAREN
  | Some '{' -> op LBRACE | Some '}' -> op RBRACE
  | Some '&' -> two '&' AMP ANDAND
  | Some '|' -> two '|' PIPE OROR
  | Some '<' -> skip lx; redir lx 0 Read
  | Some '>' ->
      skip lx;
      if peekc lx = Some '>' then (skip lx; redir lx 1 Append)
      else redir lx 1 Write
  | Some _ -> WORD (word lx)

(* <file >[2]file >[2=1] *)
and redir lx fd mode : token =
  let num () =
    let start = lx.pos in
    while_ lx (fun c -> '0' <= c && c <= '9');
    match int_of_string_opt (String.sub lx.text start (lx.pos - start)) with
    | Some n -> n | None -> raise (Error "bad redirection")
  in
  let file fd =
    match token lx with
    | WORD w -> Open (fd, mode, w)
    | _ -> raise (Error "redirection without a file") in
  if peekc lx <> Some '[' then REDIR (file fd)
  else begin
    skip lx;
    let a = num () in
    if peekc lx = Some '=' then
      (skip lx; let b = num () in skip lx; REDIR (Dup (a, b)))
    else (skip lx; REDIR (file a))
  end

and word lx : word =
  let from start = String.sub lx.text start (lx.pos - start) in
  match peekc lx with
  | Some '\'' ->
      skip lx;
      let b = Buffer.create 16 in
      let rec quoted () =
        match peekc lx with
        | None -> raise (Error "eof in quotes")
        | Some '\'' ->
            skip lx;
            if peekc lx = Some '\'' then
              (skip lx; Buffer.add_char b '\''; quoted ())
        | Some c -> skip lx; Buffer.add_char b c; quoted ()
      in
      quoted ();
      let lit = Lit (Buffer.contents b, true) in
      lit :: more lx
  | Some '$' ->
      skip lx;
      let count = peekc lx = Some '#' in
      if count then skip lx;
      let start = lx.pos in
      if peekc lx = Some '*' then skip lx else while_ lx idchr;
      let var = if count then Count (from start) else Var (from start) in
      var :: more lx
  | Some '^' -> skip lx; more lx
  | _ ->
      let start = lx.pos in
      while_ lx wordchr;
      let lit = Lit (from start, false) in
      lit :: more lx

(* the pieces that follow with nothing between *)
and more lx =
  match peekc lx with
  | Some c when wordchr c || String.contains "'$^" c -> word lx
  | _ -> []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Parsing *)
(*****************************************************************************)

type parser = { lx : lexer; mutable ahead : token option }

let peek p =
  match p.ahead with
  | Some t -> t
  | None -> let t = token p.lx in p.ahead <- Some t; t
let next p = let t = peek p in p.ahead <- None; t
let expect p t = if next p <> t then raise (Error "syntax error")
let rec skipnl p = if peek p = NL then (ignore (next p); skipnl p)
(* old: the keyword's string, matched as Some "if": a misspelling was
 * silently a command's name *)
type keyword = Kbang | Kat | Kif | Kwhile | Kfor | Kin | Kfn | Ktilde

let keyword p : keyword option =
  match peek p with
  | WORD [ Lit (k, false) ] ->
      List.assoc_opt k
        [ "!", Kbang; "@", Kat; "if", Kif; "while", Kwhile; "for", Kfor;
          "in", Kin; "fn", Kfn; "~", Ktilde ]
  | _ -> None
let name p what =
  match next p with
  | WORD [ Lit (x, _) ] -> x
  | _ -> raise (Error (what ^ ": a name"))

(* x= at the start of a word: x, and what follows the = *)
let assignment (w : word) =
  match w with
  | Lit (s, false) :: rest -> (
      match String.index_opt s '=' with
      | Some i when i > 0 && String.for_all idchr (String.sub s 0 i) ->
          let v = String.sub s (i + 1) (String.length s - i - 1) in
          Some (String.sub s 0 i, if v = "" then rest else Lit (v, false) :: rest)
      | _ -> None)
  | _ -> None

(* commands separated by ; & and newlines, until [stop] *)
let rec body p stop : cmd =
  let c = and_or p in
  if stop (peek p) then c
  else
    let c =
      match next p with
      | AMP -> Async c
      | SEMI | NL -> c
      | _ -> raise (Error "syntax error") in
    if stop (peek p) then c else Seq (c, body p stop)

and and_or p =
  let c = ref (pipe p) in
  while peek p = ANDAND || peek p = OROR do
    let t = next p in
    let right = operand p pipe in
    c := if t = ANDAND then And (!c, right) else Or (!c, right)
  done;
  !c

and pipe p =
  let c = ref (unit p) in
  while peek p = PIPE do
    ignore (next p); c := Pipe (!c, operand p unit)
  done;
  !c

(* what follows a | && or ||, on its line or the next ones; the text's
 * end there is an error, rc's, and at a terminal a line to continue *)
and operand p command =
  skipnl p; if peek p = EOF then raise (Error "syntax error"); command p

and cond p =
  expect p LPAREN; let c = body p (( = ) RPAREN) in expect p RPAREN; skipnl p; c

and block p =
  expect p LBRACE; let c = body p (( = ) RBRACE) in expect p RBRACE; c

(* as in rc's grammar, ! and @ take a pipe, if while and for all the
 * rest *)
and unit p : cmd =
  let kw () = ignore (next p) in
  match keyword p, peek p with
  | Some Kbang, _ -> kw (); Not (pipe p)
  | Some Kat, _ -> kw (); Subshell (pipe p)
  | Some Kif, _ -> kw (); let c = cond p in If (c, and_or p)
  | Some Kwhile, _ -> kw (); let c = cond p in While (c, and_or p)
  | Some Kfor, _ ->
      kw ();
      expect p LPAREN;
      let x = name p "for" in
      let list =
        if keyword p = Some Kin then (ignore (next p); Some (words p))
        else None in
      expect p RPAREN;
      skipnl p;
      For (x, list, and_or p)
  | Some Kfn, _ -> kw (); let f = name p "fn" in Fn (f, block p)
  | Some Ktilde, _ -> kw (); let ws, rs = simple p in Match (ws, rs)
  | _, LBRACE -> let c = block p in Brace (c, redirs p)
  | _, WORD w when assignment w <> None ->
      ignore (next p);
      let x, v = Option.get (assignment w) in
      let value =
        match v, peek p with
        | [], LPAREN ->
            ignore (next p); let ws = words p in expect p RPAREN; ws
        | [], BACKQ -> [ one_word p ]
        | [], _ -> []
        | v, _ -> [ v ]
      in
      (match peek p with
       | WORD _ | BACKQ | REDIR _ | LBRACE -> Assign (x, value, Some (unit p))
       | _ -> Assign (x, value, None))
  | _, (WORD _ | BACKQ | REDIR _) -> let ws, rs = simple p in Simple (ws, rs)
  | _ -> Empty

(* a command's words and redirections, in any order *)
and simple p =
  let rec go ws rs =
    match peek p with
    | REDIR r -> ignore (next p); go ws (r :: rs)
    | WORD _ | BACKQ -> go (one_word p :: ws) rs
    | _ -> List.rev ws, List.rev rs
  in
  go [] []

and redirs p =
  match peek p with REDIR r -> ignore (next p); r :: redirs p | _ -> []

(* a word; a `{cmd} is one *)
and one_word p =
  match next p with
  | WORD w -> w
  | BACKQ -> [ Back (block p) ]
  | _ -> raise (Error "syntax error")

and words p =
  match peek p with
  | WORD _ | BACKQ -> let w = one_word p in w :: words p
  | _ -> []

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Matching and globbing *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* in a word being built, a character not to glob has a \000 before it *)
let escape s =
  if not (String.exists (fun c -> String.contains "*?[\000" c) s) then s
  else
    String.concat ""
      (List.map (fun c ->
         (if String.contains "*?[\000" c then "\000" else "") ^ String.make 1 c)
         (List.init (String.length s) (String.get s)))

let unescape s =
  let b = Buffer.create (String.length s) and esc = ref false in
  String.iter (fun c ->
    if c = '\000' && not !esc then esc := true
    else (esc := false; Buffer.add_char b c)) s;
  Buffer.contents b

let rec has_meta s i =
  i < String.length s
  && (if s.[i] = '\000' then has_meta s (i + 2)
      else String.contains "*?[" s.[i] || has_meta s (i + 1))

(* [matches pat s]: * ? [a-z] [~a-z], on an escaped pattern *)
let matches (pat : string) (s : string) : bool =
  let n = String.length pat and m = String.length s in
  let rec go i j =
    if i = n then j = m
    else match pat.[i] with
      | '*' -> go (i + 1) j || (j < m && go i (j + 1))
      | '?' -> j < m && go (i + 1) (j + 1)
      | '['
        when j < m && String.index_from_opt pat (min (i + 2) n) ']' <> None ->
          let close = String.index_from pat (i + 2) ']' in
          let neg = pat.[i + 1] = '~' in
          let rec member k =
            k < close
            && (if k + 2 < close && pat.[k + 1] = '-' then
                  (pat.[k] <= s.[j] && s.[j] <= pat.[k + 2]) || member (k + 3)
                else pat.[k] = s.[j] || member (k + 1))
          in
          member (if neg then i + 2 else i + 1) <> neg && go (close + 1) (j + 1)
      | '\000' when i + 1 < n ->
          j < m && pat.[i + 1] = s.[j] && go (i + 2) (j + 1)
      | c -> j < m && c = s.[j] && go (i + 1) (j + 1)
  in
  go 0 0

(* the files a pattern names, sorted, a component at a time; the
 * pattern itself when there are none. A component without a wildcard
 * after one, the g of */g, names a file only where it is there.
 * (old: every directory's g kept, there or not: */g was d/g and
 * examples/g on tiny-kernel, where 9base's rc says d/g) *)
let glob (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.readdir; .. >) (w : string) : string list =
  let rec expand dir = function
    | [] ->
        if (try ignore (TinyLibSystem.stat caps dir); true with Failure _ -> false)
        then [ dir ]
        else []
    | comp :: rest when not (has_meta comp 0) ->
        expand (dir ^ unescape comp ^ if rest = [] then "" else "/") rest
    | comp :: rest ->
        List.sort compare (TinyLibSystem.readdir caps (if dir = "" then "." else dir))
        |> List.filter (matches comp)
        |> List.concat_map (fun e ->
            if rest = [] then [ dir ^ e ]
            else if TinyLibSystem.is_directory caps (dir ^ e) then
              expand (dir ^ e ^ "/") rest
            else [])
  in
  if not (has_meta w 0) then [ unescape w ]
  else
    let comps = List.filter (( <> ) "") (String.split_on_char '/' w) in
    match expand (if w.[0] = '/' then "/" else "") comps with
    | [] -> [ unescape w ]
    | l -> l

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Variables and statuses *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let vars : (string, string list) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 64
let fns : (string, cmd) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 16

let get x =
  let find x = Hashtbl.find_opt vars x ||| [] in
  match int_of_string_opt x with
  | Some n when n > 0 ->
      (match List.nth_opt (find "*") (n - 1) with Some v -> [ v ] | None -> [])
  | _ -> find x

let set x v =
  if v = [] then Hashtbl.remove vars x else Hashtbl.replace vars x v
let status () = String.concat "" (get "status")
let set_status s = set "status" [ s ]

(* [protect f finally]: f, then finally, whether f ends or raises
 * (Fun.protect's, without its label) *)
let protect (f : unit -> unit) (finally : unit -> unit) : unit =
  (try f () with e -> finally (); raise e);
  finally ()

(* [local x v f]: f with x set to v, then x as it was *)
let local x v f =
  let old = get x in
  set x v;
  protect f (fun () -> set x old)

(* true when all its parts are: "", "0|", "|" *)
let truth s = String.for_all (fun c -> c = '0' || c = '|') s

(* an exit code: rc's, the leading number, or 1 *)
let code s =
  if truth s then 0
  else
    match int_of_string_opt (List.hd (String.split_on_char '|' s)) with
    | Some n when n > 0 -> n
    | _ -> 1

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Processes and fds *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a child's status; one a signal ended is said, as rc says it *)
let wait caps pid =
  let s = TinyLibSystem.wait caps pid in
  if String.length s >= 6 && String.sub s 0 6 = "signal" then
    TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (string_of_int pid ^ ": " ^ s ^ "\n");
  s

let die (caps : < Cap.stderr; .. >) m =
  TinyLibSystem.eprint caps ("tiny-shell: " ^ m ^ "\n"); "error"

(* f in a child, which exits with the status it leaves *)
let fork (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.stderr; .. >) (f : unit -> unit) : int =
  TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
  match TinyLibSystem.fork caps with
  (* tiny-kernel's fork fails when its eight processes are taken (the
   * host's raises); "try again" is rc's word for it *)
  | -1 -> raise (Error "try again")
  | 0 ->
      let st =
        try f (); status () with Exits s -> s | Error m -> die caps m in
      TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
      TinyLibSystem.exit caps (code st)
  | pid -> pid

(* lists, rc's way: joined by \001 *)
let environment () =
  Hashtbl.fold (fun x v acc ->
    if x = "*" then acc else (x ^ "=" ^ String.concat "\001" v) :: acc)
    vars []

let exec (caps : < Cap.exec; Cap.stderr; .. >) (argv : string list) =
  let name = List.hd argv in
  let files =
    if String.contains name '/' then [ name ]
    else
      List.map (fun d -> Filename.concat d name)
        (String.split_on_char ':' (String.concat "" (get "PATH")))
  in
  let why =
    List.fold_left (fun _ f -> TinyLibSystem.exec caps f argv (environment ()))
      "not found" files in
  TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (name ^ ": " ^ why ^ "\n");
  TinyLibSystem.exit caps 1

(* [with_fds changes f]: each fd changed (the file, or another fd), f
 * run, then each fd put back *)
(* a redirection's target: a file opened, or another fd *)
type target = To_file of string * mode | To_fd of int

let with_fds (caps : < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >)
    (changes : (int * target) list) f =
  TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
  let saved = List.map (fun (n, _) -> n, TinyLibSystem.save n) changes in
  let restore () =
    TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
    List.rev saved |> List.iter (fun (n, s) ->
      match s with
      | Some s -> TinyLibSystem.dup2 s n; TinyLibSystem.close s
      | None -> TinyLibSystem.close n)
  in
  let change (n, to_) =
    match to_ with
    | To_fd m -> TinyLibSystem.dup2 m n
    | To_file (file, mode) ->
        (* (not close-on-exec, as it was: it is closed two lines down) *)
        let f =
          try
            (match mode with
             | Read -> TinyLibSystem.open_in caps file
             | Write -> TinyLibSystem.open_out caps file
             | Append -> TinyLibSystem.open_append caps file)
          with Failure m -> raise (Error (file ^ ": " ^ m)) in
        TinyLibSystem.dup2 f n;
        TinyLibSystem.close f
  in
  (try List.iter change changes with e -> restore (); raise e);
  protect f restore

(* [into w f]: f in a child whose standard output is w *)
let into caps w r f =
  fork caps (fun () ->
    TinyLibSystem.dup2 w 1; TinyLibSystem.close w; TinyLibSystem.close r; f ())

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Evaluation *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let background = ref []
let eflag = ref false

(* a list joined to another: distributing, or pairwise *)
let join (a : string list) (b : string list) : string list =
  match a, b with
  | [], _ | _, [] -> raise (Error "null list in concatenation")
  | [ x ], l -> List.map (fun y -> x ^ y) l
  | l, [ y ] -> List.map (fun x -> x ^ y) l
  | l1, l2 when List.length l1 = List.length l2 -> List.map2 ( ^ ) l1 l2
  | _ -> raise (Error "mismatched list lengths in concatenation")

(* e: -e applies here, not in a condition *)
(* old: a global count of the conditions being run, still raised in a
 * function called from one: its failures were ignored *)
let rec run
    (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.chdir; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
             Cap.stderr; Cap.stdout; Cap.exit; Cap.pipe; Cap.readdir; .. >)
    (e : bool) (c : cmd) : unit =
  let run = run caps e and cond = run caps false and words = words caps in
  match c with
  | Empty -> ()
  | Seq (a, b) -> run a; run b
  | Async c ->
      let pid = fork caps (fun () -> child caps e c) in
      background := pid :: !background;
      set "apid" [ string_of_int pid ]
  | And (a, b) -> cond a; if truth (status ()) then run b
  | Or (a, b) -> cond a; if not (truth (status ())) then run b
  | Not c -> cond c; set_status (if truth (status ()) then "false" else "")
  | If (c, body) -> cond c; if truth (status ()) then run body
  | While (c, body) ->
      let rec loop () =
        cond c; if truth (status ()) then (run body; loop ()) in
      loop ()
  | For (x, list, body) ->
      List.iter (fun v -> set x [ v ]; run body)
        (match list with Some ws -> words ws | None -> get "*")
  | Fn (f, body) -> Hashtbl.replace fns f body
  | Assign (x, v, None) -> set x (words v)
  | Assign (x, v, Some c) -> local x (words v) (fun () -> run c)
  | Brace (c, rs) -> with_fds caps (redirs caps rs) (fun () -> run c)
  | Subshell c ->
      set_status (wait caps (fork caps (fun () -> child caps e c))); check e
  | Pipe _ ->
      (* The shell forks each stage but the last, which it runs itself,
       * and each child execs its command in place (child). So a|b|c|d
       * costs four processes, not seven: tiny-kernel has eight.
       * old: a|b|c, the tree Pipe (Pipe (a, b), c), ran a|b in a child
       * shell, which forked for a and for b, and so on to the left *)
      let rec stages c acc =
        match c with Pipe (a, b) -> stages a (b :: acc) | c -> c :: acc in
      let saved = Option.get (TinyLibSystem.save 0) in
      let pids = ref [] in
      let rec go = function
        | [ last ] -> run last
        | c :: rest ->
            let r, w = TinyLibSystem.pipe caps in
            pids := into caps w r (fun () -> child caps e c) :: !pids;
            TinyLibSystem.close w;
            TinyLibSystem.dup2 r 0;
            TinyLibSystem.close r;
            go rest
        | [] -> ()
      in
      (* a stage that cannot be forked: the ones that were are waited for *)
      (try
         protect (fun () -> go (stages c [])) (fun () ->
           TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
           TinyLibSystem.dup2 saved 0;
           TinyLibSystem.close saved)
       with ex ->
         List.iter (fun pid -> ignore (wait caps pid)) !pids; raise ex);
      let last = status () in
      (* rc's status: a|b|c is (a|b)|c, where a|b's is what a child that
       * ran it would exit with, its first number. So 1|2|3 is 1|3 *)
      let exited s =
        let n = code s in if n = 0 then "" else string_of_int n in
      let join acc s =
        match acc with None -> Some s | Some a -> Some (exited a ^ "|" ^ s) in
      set_status
        (Option.get
           (List.fold_left join None
              (List.map (wait caps) (List.rev !pids) @ [ last ])));
      check e
  (* old: Simple with a first word "~", matched as a pattern in the
   * tree, though ~ is a keyword as ! and @ are *)
  | Match (args, rs) ->
      (* ~ subject pattern ...: the words as they are, not globbed *)
      with_fds caps (redirs caps rs) (fun () ->
        match List.concat_map (word caps) args with
        | subject :: pats ->
            set_status
              (if List.exists (fun p -> matches p (unescape subject)) pats
               then ""
               else "no match")
        | [] -> set_status "no match")
  | Simple (ws, rs) ->
      let argv = words ws in
      with_fds caps (redirs caps rs) (fun () -> command caps false argv);
      check e

(* [child caps e c]: c run in a forked shell, as the last thing it does.
 * A program is then exec'd in place, as rc does, instead of in yet
 * another child that this one would only wait for *)
and child caps e c =
  match c with
  | Simple (ws, rs) ->
      let argv = words caps ws in
      with_fds caps (redirs caps rs) (fun () -> command caps true argv)
  | c -> run caps e c

and check e =
  if !eflag && e && not (truth (status ())) then raise (Exits (status ()))

(* inplace: in a child with nothing left to do, a program is exec'd
 * without a fork *)
and command caps (inplace : bool) (argv : string list) =
  match argv with
  | [] -> ()
  (* a function's body is no condition, even called from one *)
  | f :: args when Hashtbl.mem fns f ->
      local "*" args (fun () -> run caps true (Hashtbl.find fns f))
  | [ "cd" ] | [ "cd"; _ ] ->
      let dir =
        match argv with [ _; d ] -> d | _ -> String.concat "" (get "HOME") in
      (try TinyLibSystem.chdir caps dir; set_status ""
       with Failure m ->
         TinyLibSystem.eprint caps ("Can't cd " ^ dir ^ ": " ^ m ^ "\n");
         set_status "can't cd")
  | "exit" :: args ->
      raise (Exits (match args with s :: _ -> s | [] -> status ()))
  | [ "shift" ] | [ "shift"; _ ] ->
      let n =
        match argv with [ _; n ] -> (int_of_string_opt n ||| 1) | _ -> 1 in
      set "*" (List.filteri (fun i _ -> i >= n) (get "*"));
      set_status ""
  | [ "wait" ] ->
      List.iter (fun pid -> set_status (wait caps pid)) (List.rev !background);
      background := []
  | _ when inplace -> exec caps argv
  | _ -> set_status (wait caps (fork caps (fun () -> exec caps argv)))

and redirs caps rs =
  rs |> List.map (function
    | Dup (a, b) -> a, To_fd b
    | Open (n, mode, w) -> (
        match words caps [ w ] with
        | [ file ] -> n, To_file (file, mode)
        | _ -> raise (Error "a redirection needs one file")))

(* a word's values, escaped where not to glob *)
and word caps (w : word) : string list =
  let piece = function
    | Lit (s, quoted) -> [ if quoted then escape s else s ]
    | Var x -> List.map escape (get x)
    | Count x -> [ string_of_int (List.length (get x)) ]
    | Back c ->
        let r, w = TinyLibSystem.pipe caps in
        let pid = into caps w r (fun () -> child caps true c) in
        TinyLibSystem.close w;
        let out = TinyLibSystem.read_all r in
        TinyLibSystem.close r;
        set_status (wait caps pid);
        String.split_on_char '\n' out
        |> List.concat_map (String.split_on_char ' ')
        |> List.concat_map (String.split_on_char '\t')
        |> List.filter (( <> ) "")
        |> List.map escape
  in
  match w with
  | [] -> []
  | first :: rest ->
      List.fold_left (fun acc p -> join acc (piece p)) (piece first) rest

and words caps (ws : word list) : string list =
  List.concat_map (fun w -> List.concat_map (glob caps) (word caps w)) ws

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Main *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the commands of a text, each run once it is read *)
let source caps (text : string) =
  let p = { lx = { text; pos = 0 }; ahead = None } in
  let rec loop () =
    skipnl p;
    if peek p <> EOF then
      (run caps true (body p (fun t -> t = NL || t = EOF)); loop ())
  in
  loop ()

(* the commands typed at a terminal, each run once it is complete: a
 * line that leaves the parser at the end of the text, in a brace or a
 * quote, is continued, prompted by a tab; an interrupt is only for the
 * program running *)
let interactive
    (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.chdir; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
             Cap.stdin; Cap.stderr; Cap.stdout; Cap.exit; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal;
             Cap.readdir; .. >) =
  TinyLibSystem.ignore_interrupt caps;
  let buf = Buffer.create 80 in
  let rec loop () =
    TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
    TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (if Buffer.length buf = 0 then "% " else "\t");
    match TinyLibSystem.read_line caps with
    | None -> ()
    | Some line ->
        Buffer.add_string buf (line ^ "\n");
        let text = Buffer.contents buf in
        let p = { lx = { text; pos = 0 }; ahead = None } in
        (* an error at the text's end: the command goes on, on the next
         * line *)
        (match
           (try Some (body p (( = ) EOF))
            with Error m ->
              if p.lx.pos < String.length text then
                (Buffer.clear buf; set_status (die caps m));
              None)
         with
         | Some c ->
             Buffer.clear buf;
             (try run caps true c
              with
              | Error m -> set_status (die caps m)
              | Failure m -> set_status (die caps m))
         | None -> ());
        loop ()
  in
  loop ()

let start (caps : Cap.all_caps) : int =
  (* the environment, with rc's lists split back *)
  TinyLibSystem.environment caps
  |> List.iter (fun (k, v) -> set k (String.split_on_char '\001' v));
  set "pid" [ string_of_int (TinyLibSystem.getpid caps) ];
  let iflag = ref false in
  let rec flags = function
    | a :: rest
      when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-'
           && String.for_all (fun c -> String.contains "-eIi" c) a ->
        if String.contains a 'e' then eflag := true;
        if String.contains a 'i' then iflag := true;
        flags rest
    | "-c" :: cmd :: args -> set "*" args; Some cmd
    | file :: args -> set "*" args; Some (TinyLibSystem.read_file caps file)
    | [] when !iflag || TinyLibSystem.isatty 0 -> None
    | [] -> Some (TinyLibSystem.read_all 0)
  in
  let st =
    try
      (match flags (List.tl (TinyLibSystem.argv caps)) with
       | Some text -> source (caps :> caps) text
       | None -> interactive (caps :> caps));
      status ()
    with Exits s -> s | Error m -> die caps m | Failure m -> die caps m
  in
  TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
  code st

let main (caps : Cap.all_caps) : int =
  match TinyLibSystem.argv caps with
  | [ _; ("-h" | "--help") ] -> TinyLibSystem.print caps help; 0
  | _ -> start caps

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-shell" main
tiny/TinyShell.mli
7736
(* A tiny shell, in one file, with pipes, redirections, variables and
 * basic control flow. mini-rc (shell/) is a faithful copy of rc; this
 * shell is what remains when compatibility is dropped. It was written
 * after mini-rc, using what mini-rc taught. The language is a cut-down
 * version of rc's:
 *
 *     ls -l *.c | wc -l >count         words, globs, a pipe, redirections
 *     x=(a b c); echo $x $#x $x.o      lists, the only value; a.o b.o c.o
 *     for(f in *.c) cc -c $f           if(cmd) cmd   while(cmd) cmd
 *     test -f x && echo y || echo n    ! cmd   { cmds }   @{ cmds }
 *     fn f { echo $1 }; f a            functions, $* $1 $2 ...
 *     y=`{date}; sleep 1 &; wait       command output as words; &
 *     cc -c x.c >[2]errs >[2=1]        other fds
 *     ~ $x *.c && echo matched         matching: ~ subject pattern ...
 *
 * How a line is processed: its characters are split into tokens, the
 * tokens are parsed into a tree ([cmd], by recursive descent), and the
 * tree is walked ([run]). Along the way each word is turned into a
 * list of strings ([word], then [glob]). For example, with x=(a b),
 * the line echo $x.o | wc >n becomes the tree
 *
 *     Pipe (Simple [echo; $x then .o], Simple [wc] with 1 opened on n)
 *
 * and walking it creates three processes, while the shell itself does
 * everything that is not running a program:
 *
 *     the shell          makes a pipe, then forks
 *      |-- a child       its 1 is the pipe; it walks the first Simple:
 *      |    |            $x joined to .o gives a.o b.o, nothing to glob
 *      |    '-- echo     forked and exec'ed; the child waits for it and
 *      |                 exits with echo's status
 *      |                 the shell's own 0 is now the pipe (the old 0
 *      |                 is saved); it walks the second Simple: 1 is
 *      |                 now n (the old 1 is saved)
 *      '-- wc            forked and exec'ed; the shell waits for it,
 *                        restores 1, then 0, waits for the child, and
 *                        sets $status to the statuses joined by a bar
 *
 * What is kept from rc, and why it is the core:
 *
 * - {b Every value is a list of strings.} $x is never split again, so
 *   there is no need to quote $x, no "$@", and $* is exactly the
 *   arguments as they were given. The only quote is '...' (with ''
 *   inside standing for a quote).
 * - {b Adjacent words are joined, distributing over lists}: $x.o is
 *   a.o b.o c.o, and two lists of the same length are joined pair by
 *   pair. rc does this with a "free caret" that its lexer inserts.
 *   Here a word is simply its pieces with nothing between them, and ^
 *   is only a way to write two pieces with nothing between them.
 * - {b Only literal text is globbed}: a * coming from a variable or a
 *   quote stays a *. The trick is that such characters are escaped (a
 *   \000 is put before them) while the word is built, so the matcher
 *   can tell them apart; the escapes are removed once the files are
 *   found.
 * - {b Redirections are done by the shell, around the command, and
 *   undone afterwards} (the fds are saved, then restored), so a
 *   function or a brace block sees them just as a program does.
 * - {b The syntax tree is walked directly}: a child forked for a stage
 *   of a pipe or for a subshell walks its subtree and then exits, or,
 *   when the subtree is a program, execs it in place; the last stage
 *   of a pipe runs in the shell itself.
 * - {b $status is a string}: "" for success, otherwise the exit code
 *   or the signal; for a pipe it is rc's: a|b|c is (a|b)|c, and a|b
 *   counts as the exit code a child running it would have, its first
 *   number, so the statuses 1, 2 and 3 give 1|3.
 *
 * What is dropped, each of which is a few lines in mini-rc, and none of
 * which is needed by the recipes in xix's mkfiles (the test for this
 * shell): switch and if not, here documents, joining a list
 * into one word, subscripts, `sep{} and <{}, `{} inside a word, eval
 * and ., all builtins except cd, exit, shift, wait and ~, functions in
 * the environment, a $path separate from $PATH, -x, rcmain, signals
 * other than an interrupt at the prompt, and $prompt. These make good
 * exercises, roughly in that order.
 *
 * Usage: rc -h (the [help] string of the .ml) shows the language by
 * example.
 *
 * Where it stands: the shell relies on five kernel calls, fork, exec,
 * wait, pipe and dup (TinyLibSystem's: on the host over Unix, the
 * loops around them in lib_core's Procs, shared with mini-mk; on
 * tiny-kernel its calls). TinyKernel has the same five calls and a shell in
 * C built on them (its user/sh.c), and mini-9pi's calls are what
 * mini-rc's Process uses. Above this shell is mini-mk, which hands it
 * each recipe. The history of shells, from Pouzin's RUNCOM to rc, is
 * told once, in mini-rc's CLI.mli.
 *
 * design:
 * Making every value a list is what removes the need for quoting. In
 * the Bourne shell a variable is a single string, and $x is split
 * again at blanks and globbed every time it is used. So a file name
 * containing a space becomes two arguments unless every use is
 * surrounded by double quotes, and the arguments need a special form
 * to stay intact ("$@", the dollar and at sign, quoted). Most of the
 * rules a shell programmer learns are workarounds for that second
 * scan. Duff's rc splits the text once, when it is read, and keeps the
 * pieces, so there is nothing to protect later.
 *
 * others:
 * xv6's sh.c is the other shell written to be read: about 500 lines of
 * C. It also builds a tree (one struct per kind of command: exec,
 * redirection, pipe, list, background), walked by a single function,
 * runcmd, which never returns: every node runs in a child. It has no
 * variables, no control flow and no globbing. This shell instead walks
 * the tree itself and forks only for a program, the first stages of a
 * pipe, & and @. That is why a cd or an assignment inside braces is
 * still visible after them.
 *
 * A pipe stage that is a single program costs one process: the child
 * forked for it execs the program in place, as it has nothing left to
 * do, instead of forking it and waiting for it. The shell forks every
 * stage itself, from the list of stages, rather than a child for the
 * pipe on the left of the last |. So a|b|c|d is four processes, where
 * it was seven, and tiny-kernel, which has eight, runs six stages
 * under sh and rc. Past that, fork fails and the shell says "try
 * again", as rc does.
 *
 * On two systems: it is tiny-kernel's rc and the host's tiny-shell. It
 * uses only the pure functions of the standard library and, for
 * everything related to the system, TinyLibSystem, which has one
 * implementation file per side.
 *
 * References: Tom Duff, "Rc -- The Plan 9 Shell" (1990), for the
 * language and for the principle that the lists protect: input "is
 * never scanned more than once"; D. M. Ritchie and K. Thompson, "The
 * UNIX Time-Sharing System" (CACM, 1974), for fork and exec as two
 * separate calls, between which the child sets up its own file
 * descriptors, and for the shell as an ordinary program; principia's
 * shells/rc, rc's C, which mini-rc follows and this file knows only
 * through mini-rc. *)

(* the commands of a text, each run once it is read: the lexer, the
 * parser and [run] at work, without the command line around them *)
val source :
  < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.wait; Cap.chdir; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out;
    Cap.stdin; Cap.stderr; Cap.stdout; Cap.exit; Cap.pipe; Cap.signal; Cap.env;
    Cap.readdir > ->
  string -> unit

(* the program: its arguments (-h: the language by example) to its exit
 * status *)
val main : Cap.all_caps -> int

(* See TinyTracer.mli *)

open TinyCalls

let say s = ignore (u_write 2 s)

(* the calls, by their numbers (TinyKernel.ml's syscall, user.h's
 * order), and the kind of each argument: a number, a path, bytes
 * given (their length the next argument), bytes filled (as many as
 * the result says), an address *)
type arg = Num | Path | Given | Filled | Addr
let calls =
  Array.of_list [
    "exit", [ Num ]; "write", [ Num; Given; Num ]; "read", [ Num; Filled; Num ];
    "fork", []; "exec", [ Path; Addr ]; "wait", [ Addr ]; "getpid", [];
    "open", [ Path; Num ]; "close", [ Num ]; "pipe", [ Addr ]; "dup", [ Num ];
    "mkdir", [ Path ]; "unlink", [ Path ]; "chdir", [ Path ]; "kill", [ Num ];
    "ready", [ Addr; Num; Num ]; "ticks", []; "box", [ Addr ];
    "dial", [ Path; Num ]; "listen", [ Num ]; "getcwd", [ Filled; Num ];
    "link", [ Path; Path ]; "rawcons", [ Num ]; "trace", [ Num ];
    "seek", [ Num; Num; Num ]; "time", []; "stat", [ Path; Addr ]; "seed", [];
    "spawn", [ Path; Addr ] ]

(* the process whose stop is handled and its trace's descriptor; the
 * next line read, and a command and its answer ("" when the kernel
 * refused it: an address outside the process) *)
let pid = ref 0
let t = ref (-1)
let tell c = ignore (u_write !t c)
let next () =
  let s = u_read !t 4096 in
  let n = String.length s in
  if n > 0 && s.[n - 1] = '\n' then String.sub s 0 (n - 1) else s
let ask c = if u_write !t c < 0 then "" else next ()

(* n bytes of the process at a, from the kernel's hexadecimal *)
let bytes a n =
  let h = ask ("m " ^ string_of_int a ^ " " ^ string_of_int n) in
  let digit c = if c <= '9' then Char.code c - 48 else Char.code c - 87 in
  String.init (String.length h / 2) (fun i ->
    Char.chr ((digit h.[2 * i] * 16) + digit h.[(2 * i) + 1]))

(* bytes as a C string, the first 32 of them *)
let quoted s =
  let b = Buffer.create 40 in
  Buffer.add_char b '"';
  String.iteri (fun i c ->
    if i < 32 then
      match c with
      | '\n' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\n"
      | '\t' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\t"
      | '"' | '\\' -> Buffer.add_char b '\\'; Buffer.add_char b c
      | c when c >= ' ' && c <= '~' -> Buffer.add_char b c
      | c ->
          let d = "0123456789abcdef" in
          Buffer.add_string b "\\x";
          Buffer.add_char b d.[Char.code c / 16];
          Buffer.add_char b d.[Char.code c mod 16]) s;
  Buffer.add_char b '"';
  if String.length s > 32 then Buffer.add_string b "...";
  Buffer.contents b

(* a path, up to its 0, read 64 bytes at a time (fewer at the end of
 * the process's memory) *)
let path a =
  let rec go a k acc =
    let s = bytes a k in
    match String.index_opt s '\000' with
    | Some i -> acc ^ String.sub s 0 i
    | None when s = "" -> if k > 1 then go a 1 acc else acc
    | None when String.length acc > 256 -> acc ^ s
    | None -> go (a + k) k (acc ^ s) in
  quoted (go a 64 "")

let hex a =
  let d = "0123456789abcdef" in
  let rec go a =
    (if a < 16 then "" else go (a / 16)) ^ String.make 1 d.[a mod 16] in
  "0x" ^ go a

(* a call's line without its result: its name and its arguments, the
 * bytes it fills shown after it returns (r, its result; -1 before) *)
let line n args r =
  if n < 0 || n >= Array.length calls then "sys" ^ string_of_int n ^ "(...)"
  else begin
    let name, kinds = calls.(n) in
    let rec go kinds args =
      match kinds, args with
      | Given :: rest, a :: (k :: _ as more) ->
          quoted (bytes a (min k 33)) :: go rest more
      | Filled :: rest, a :: more ->
          (if r < 0 then hex a else quoted (bytes a (min r 33))) :: go rest more
      | Path :: rest, a :: more -> path a :: go rest more
      | Addr :: rest, a :: more -> hex a :: go rest more
      | _ :: rest, a :: more -> string_of_int a :: go rest more
      | _ -> [] in
    name ^ "(" ^ String.concat ", " (go kinds args) ^ ")"
  end

(* The stops, until the processes' end: before a call, its line is
 * made (its paths are read then: an exec's is gone after it); after,
 * said with its result, and the bytes the call filled. A stop for
 * another reason, a fault, is said and the process killed. The
 * processes traced: each its pid, its descriptor, and the call it is
 * in (its number, its arguments and its line made before it) *)
let fills n =
  n < Array.length calls
  && List.exists (fun k -> match k with Filled -> true | _ -> false)
       (snd calls.(n))
type traced = {
  tpid : int; fd : int; mutable pending : (int * int list * string) option;
}
let procs = ref []
let children = ref false
let say_of s =
  say ((if !children then "[" ^ string_of_int !pid ^ "] " else "") ^ s ^ "\n")

(* a stop of the process p, read from its descriptor; false when it
 * ended *)
let handle p =
  pid := p.tpid;
  t := p.fd;
  let s = next () in
  let num = int_of_string in
  let go on = p.pending <- on; tell "c"; true in
  match String.split_on_char ' ' s, p.pending with
  | [ "" ], _ -> false
  | [ "call"; "0"; a; _; _ ], _ -> say_of ("exit(" ^ a ^ ")"); go None
  | [ "call"; n; a1; a2; a3 ], _ ->
      let n = num n and args = [ num a1; num a2; num a3 ] in
      go (Some (n, args, line n args (-1)))
  | [ "ret"; n; r ], Some (_, args, text) ->
      let n = num n and r = num r in
      say_of ((if fills n then line n args r else text) ^ " = "
              ^ string_of_int r);
      (* a child forked or spawned: traced from its first call, which
       * waits for it *)
      if (n = 3 || n = 28) && r > 0 && !children then begin
        let fd = u_trace r in
        if fd >= 0 then
          procs := !procs @ [ { tpid = r; fd = fd; pending = None } ]
      end;
      go None
  | [ "stopped"; _; "exec" ], Some (_, _, text) ->
      say_of (text ^ " = 0"); go None
  | "exited" :: rest, _ -> say_of ("exited " ^ String.concat " " rest); false
  | "stopped" :: pc :: why, _ ->
      say_of ("stopped at " ^ hex (num pc) ^ ": " ^ String.concat " " why);
      ignore (u_kill p.tpid); go None
  | _ -> say_of ("trace: " ^ s); go None

(* the stops of all the processes, the first one ready first, until
 * none is left *)
let rec follow () =
  match !procs with
  | [] -> ()
  | l ->
      let fds = Array.of_list (List.map (fun p -> p.fd) l) in
      let k = u_ready fds (Array.length fds) 0 in
      (match List.filter (fun p -> p.fd = k) l with
       | [ p ] ->
           if not (handle p) then begin
             ignore (u_close p.fd);
             procs := List.filter (fun q -> q.fd <> p.fd) !procs
           end
       | _ -> procs := []);
      follow ()

let main () =
  let n = u_argc () in
  let first = if n > 1 && u_arg 1 = "-f" then 2 else 1 in
  children := first = 2;
  if n <= first then (say "usage: trace [-f] prog [args] | trace [-f] pid\n";
                      exit 1);
  let p, started =
    match int_of_string_opt (u_arg first) with
    | Some p -> p, false
    | None ->
        let prog = u_arg first in
        let file = if String.contains prog '/' then prog else "/bin/" ^ prog in
        let pid = u_fork () in
        if pid = 0 then begin
          ignore (u_trace 0);
          ignore (u_exec file
                    (List.init (n - first) (fun i -> u_arg (i + first))));
          say ("trace: " ^ prog ^ ": not found\n");
          exit 127
        end;
        pid, true in
  pid := p;
  t := u_trace p;
  (* (a program not found: its child said so) *)
  if started && (!t < 0 || next () <> "stopped 0 exec") then exit 1;
  if !t < 0 then
    (say ("trace: " ^ u_arg first ^ ": no such process\n"); exit 1);
  ignore (ask "y");
  if !children then ignore (ask "f");
  if started then tell "c";
  procs := [ { tpid = p; fd = !t; pending = None } ];
  follow ();
  if started then ignore (u_waits ());
  exit 0
tiny/TinyTracer.mli
3255
(* trace: the system calls of a process as it makes them, a line each
 * on the error output, so that trace prog > f keeps the program's
 * output apart (plan_tiny_debugger.md, section 5):
 *
 *     % trace cat f
 *     open("f", 0) = 5
 *     read(5, "hello\n", 4096) = 6
 *     hello
 *     write(1, "hello\n", 6) = 6
 *     read(5, "", 4096) = 0
 *     close(5) = 0
 *     exit(0)
 *
 *     trace -f rc -c 'cat f | wc'      the children too, [pid] a line
 *     trace 12                          a process already running
 *
 * How it works: it starts its program stopped at its first instruction
 * (a child that calls trace(0), then exec), or attaches to a process
 * by its pid, on the kernel's trace descriptor (TinyDebugger.mli has
 * its picture); then y, and a loop of stops:
 *
 *     trace                    tiny-kernel                cat
 *     "y"            ------>   a stop at each sys
 *                                                    <--- sys 2 (read)
 *                   <------    "call 2 5 8192 4096"       Stopped
 *     "c"            ------>   the read made (or waited
 *                              for: its end in runnable)
 *                   <------    "ret 2 6"                  Stopped
 *     "m 8192 6"     ------>   the bytes it read
 *                   <------    "68656c6c6f0a"
 *     "c"            ------>                         ---> runs on
 *
 * - {b Two stops, not one line after the call}: before the call an
 *   exec's path is still there (after it, the memory is the new
 *   program's), after it a read's bytes are; the kernel keeps nothing
 *   of the call and decodes nothing. trace has the table of the calls
 *   (TinyKernel.ml's syscall's numbers, user.h's order) and the kind of
 *   each argument: a number, a path, bytes given (their length the
 *   next argument), bytes filled (as many as the result says), an
 *   address.
 * - {b -f}: the command f makes the kernel trace what the process
 *   forks, by the same tracer and with the same stops; trace opens a
 *   descriptor on each child when the fork returns its pid (trace(pid)
 *   gives it, the child's stops kept till then), and waits on them all
 *   with ready.
 *
 * What is ours: a call's bytes shown as C strings, their first 32
 *   (strace's), and a read of nothing as "" rather than its buffer's
 *   address; one descriptor a process, rather than strace's one
 *   ptrace for all of them; a fault stops the process, which trace
 *   then kills.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * Plan 9's ratrace is a program over /proc: it writes startsyscall to
 * the process's ctl and reads each stop's line from /proc/n/syscall
 * (principia's debuggers/tracers/ratrace.c); the kernel adds a word to
 * ctl, not a system call. Here the same is the trace descriptor's y.
 *
 * others:
 * Linux's strace stops the process at each call's entry and exit with
 * ptrace's PTRACE_SYSCALL, as here; Solaris's truss reads /proc.
 * DTrace (Solaris, 2005) and Linux's eBPF trace without stopping the
 * process, by code the kernel runs at the call.
 *
 * References: plan_tiny_debugger.md; Plan 9's ratrace(1) and proc(3)
 * manual pages; strace(1). *)

(* the program: its command line, the stops of its processes, its exit *)
val main : unit -> unit

(* See TinyTroff.mli *)
open TinyOfficeModel

(* strings joined (TinyLibCore's String.concat, two by two) *)
let glue (l : string list) : string = String.concat "" l


(* a string's characters, each as a string *)
let chars (s : string) : string list =
  List.init (String.length s) (fun i -> String.make 1 s.[i])

(* the objects in reading order: by their page, their top, their left *)
let in_order (l : obj list) : obj list =
  List.sort (fun (a : obj) (b : obj) ->
    compare (a.page_no, a.y, a.x) (b.page_no, b.y, b.x)) l

(* the parts in reading order, a list a page (to the last page that has
 * a part) *)
let pages_of (parts : obj list) : obj list list =
  let n = List.fold_left (fun m (b : obj) -> max m (b.page_no + 1)) 1 parts in
  List.init n (fun p -> List.filter (fun (b : obj) -> b.page_no = p) parts)

(* a text's lines, each its characters and their styles *)
let styled_lines (data : string) : (string * string) list =
  let (t, st) = decode data in
  let rec go i =
    match String.index_from_opt t i '\n' with
    | Some e -> (String.sub t i (e - i), String.sub st i (e - i)) :: go (e + 1)
    | None ->
        [ (String.sub t i (String.length t - i),
           String.sub st i (String.length t - i)) ] in
  if t = "" then [] else go 0

(* a line all large: a heading *)
let heading (t : string) (st : string) =
  t <> "" && String.for_all (fun c -> Char.code c land 8 <> 0) st

(* a sheet's size, its columns and rows; each cell's value as it is
 * shown, and whether it is a number (at the right), an error *)
let sheet_size (data : string) : int * int =
  List.fold_left (fun (nc, nr) (n, _) ->
    let r =
      match int_of_string_opt (String.sub n 1 (String.length n - 1)) with
      | Some r -> r
      | None -> 1 in
    (max nc (Char.code n.[0] - 96), max nr r)) (0, 0) (cells data)

let shown (value : string -> value) (data : string) (c : int) (r : int)
    : string * bool * bool =
  let n = name c r in
  if not (List.exists (fun (m, _) -> m = n) (cells data)) then ("", false, false)
  else match value n with
    | Num k -> (string_of_int k, true, false)
    | Str s -> (s, false, false)
    | Err e -> ("#" ^ e, false, true)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Text *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a line's words filled to a width *)
let fill (width : int) (line : string) : string list =
  let words = List.filter (fun w -> w <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' line) in
  let rec go cur acc = function
    | w :: rest ->
        if cur = "" then go w acc rest
        else if String.length cur + 1 + String.length w <= width then
          go (cur ^ " " ^ w) acc rest
        else go w (cur :: acc) rest
    | [] -> List.rev (if cur = "" then acc else cur :: acc) in
  match go "" [] words with [] -> [ "" ] | l -> l

(* a text box: each line filled, a heading underlined with = *)
let text_lines (width : int) (data : string) : string list =
  List.concat (List.map (fun (t, st) ->
    if heading t st then [ t; String.make (String.length t) '=' ]
    else fill width t) (styled_lines data))

(* a sheet: its values in columns, a number at its column's right *)
let sheet_lines (data : string) : string list =
  let value = values data and (nc, nr) = sheet_size data in
  let cols = List.init nc (fun c -> c) in
  let wide = List.map (fun c ->
    List.fold_left (fun m r ->
      let (s, _, _) = shown value data c r in
      max m (String.length s)) 1 (List.init nr (fun r -> r))) cols in
  List.init nr (fun r ->
    glue (List.map2 (fun c w ->
      let (s, num, _) = shown value data c r in
      let pad = String.make (w - String.length s) ' ' in
      (if c = 0 then "" else "  ") ^ (if num then pad ^ s else s ^ pad)) cols wide))

(* the rows of a grid of characters, without the spaces at their ends,
 * nor the empty rows at its end *)
let grid_lines (g : string array array) : string list =
  let rec trim l = match l with "" :: rest -> trim rest | l -> l in
  let rows = List.init (Array.length g) (fun r ->
    let n = ref (Array.length g.(r)) in
    while !n > 0 && g.(r).(!n - 1) = " " do decr n done;
    glue (List.init !n (fun c -> g.(r).(c)))) in
  List.rev (trim (List.rev rows))

(* A drawing as characters, one for 8 by 8 pixels: a box's sides of -
 * and |, its corners +, its label in its middle; a text where it is;
 * then an arrow across then up or down, in the places left (a box's
 * side is not drawn over), its head > < v ^ before the box it goes
 * to *)
let drawing_lines (b : obj) : string list =
  let cols = (b.w + 7) / 8 and rows = (b.h + 7) / 8 in
  let g = Array.make rows (Array.make 0 " ") in
  for r = 0 to rows - 1 do g.(r) <- Array.make cols " " done;
  let inside c r = c >= 0 && c < cols && r >= 0 && r < rows in
  let put c r s = if inside c r then g.(r).(c) <- s in
  let free c r = inside c r && g.(r).(c) = " " in
  let put_free c r s = if free c r then g.(r).(c) <- s in
  let label c r s = List.iteri (fun k ch -> put (c + k) r ch) (chars s) in
  let shapes = figures b.data in
  List.iter (fun (kind, nums, text) ->
    match kind, nums with
    | "box", [ x; y; w; h ] ->
        let c0 = x / 8 and r0 = y / 8 and c1 = (x + w) / 8
        and r1 = (y + h) / 8 in
        for c = c0 to c1 do put c r0 "-"; put c r1 "-" done;
        for r = r0 to r1 do put c0 r "|"; put c1 r "|" done;
        List.iter (fun (c, r) -> put c r "+")
          [ (c0, r0); (c1, r0); (c0, r1); (c1, r1) ];
        label ((c0 + c1 + 1 - String.length text) / 2) ((r0 + r1) / 2) text
    | "text", [ x; y ] -> label (x / 8) ((y + 8) / 8) text
    | _ -> ()) shapes;
  List.iter (fun (kind, nums, _) ->
    match kind, nums with
    | "arrow", [ x0; y0; x1; y1 ] ->
        let c0 = x0 / 8 and r0 = y0 / 8 and c1 = x1 / 8 and r1 = y1 / 8 in
        let dc = if r1 <> r0 then 0 else if c1 >= c0 then 1 else -1
        and dr = if r1 > r0 then 1 else if r1 < r0 then -1 else 0 in
        let hc, hr = if free c1 r1 then c1, r1 else c1 - dc, r1 - dr in
        for c = min c0 c1 to max c0 c1 do put_free c r0 "-" done;
        for r = min r0 r1 to max r0 r1 do put_free c1 r "|" done;
        if r1 <> r0 then put c1 r0 "+";
        put hc hr
          (if dr > 0 then "v" else if dr < 0 then "^"
           else if dc > 0 then ">" else "<")
    | _ -> ()) shapes;
  grid_lines g

(* a paint: its rows, white a space *)
let paint_lines (data : string) : string list =
  let rows = List.map (fun row ->
    glue (List.map (fun ch -> if ch = "." then " " else ch) (chars row)))
    (String.split_on_char '\n' data) in
  let rec trim l = match l with "" :: rest -> trim rest | l -> l in
  List.rev (trim (List.rev rows))

(* a chart: a line a bar, its label, #s for its share of the largest
 * (30 for it), its value; or why it has none *)
let chart_lines (page : obj list) (b : obj) : string list =
  match chart_bars page b with
  | [], why -> [ "[" ^ why ^ "]" ]
  | bars, _ ->
      let top = List.fold_left (fun m (_, v) -> max m v) 1 bars
      and wide =
        List.fold_left (fun m (l, _) -> max m (String.length l)) 0 bars in
      List.map (fun (l, v) ->
        l ^ String.make (wide - String.length l) ' ' ^ "  "
        ^ String.make (max 0 (v * 30 / top)) '#' ^ " " ^ string_of_int v) bars

let to_text (width : int) (doc : string) : string =
  let parts = in_order (parse 640 480 doc) in
  let one (b : obj) =
    if b.kind = "sheet" then sheet_lines b.data
    else if b.kind = "drawing" then drawing_lines b
    else if b.kind = "paint" then paint_lines b.data
    else if b.kind = "chart" then chart_lines parts b
    else text_lines width b.data in
  let page bs =
    List.concat (List.mapi (fun k b -> (if k = 0 then [] else [ "" ]) @ one b) bs) in
  (* (a page after a form feed, as nroff's) *)
  let pages = List.map page (pages_of parts) in
  glue (List.map (fun l -> l ^ "\n")
    (List.concat (List.mapi (fun k ls ->
      (if k = 0 then [] else [ "\012" ]) @ ls) pages)))

(* HTML *)
