(* a text in HTML: & < > and the double quote written as entities *)
let esc (s : string) : string =
  glue (List.map (fun ch ->
    if ch = "&" then "&amp;"
    else if ch = "<" then "&lt;"
    else if ch = ">" then "&gt;"
    else if ch = "\"" then "&quot;"
    else ch) (chars s))

(* a style's tags, opening and closing *)
let opens (k : int) =
  (if k land 8 <> 0 then "<span class=l>" else "")
  ^ (if k land 4 <> 0 then "<u>" else "")
  ^ (if k land 2 <> 0 then "<i>" else "")
  ^ (if k land 1 <> 0 then "<b>" else "")
let closes (k : int) =
  (if k land 1 <> 0 then "</b>" else "")
  ^ (if k land 2 <> 0 then "</i>" else "")
  ^ (if k land 4 <> 0 then "</u>" else "")
  ^ (if k land 8 <> 0 then "</span>" else "")

(* a line's characters, each run of a style in its tags (without the
 * styles of base, the line's own) *)
let runs_html (t : string) (st : string) (base : int) : string =
  let n = String.length t in
  let rec go i was acc =
    if i >= n then glue (List.rev (closes was :: acc))
    else begin
      let k = Char.code st.[i] land lnot base in
      go (i + 1) k
        (esc (String.make 1 t.[i])
         :: (if k <> was then opens k :: closes was :: acc else acc))
    end in
  go 0 0 []

(* a text box: a line a paragraph, a heading an h1, an empty line an
 * empty paragraph (the page's place kept) *)
let text_html (data : string) : string =
  glue (List.map (fun (t, st) ->
    if heading t st then "<h1>" ^ runs_html t st 8 ^ "</h1>\n"
    else if t = "" then "<p>&nbsp;</p>\n"
    else "<p>" ^ runs_html t st 0 ^ "</p>\n") (styled_lines data))

(* a sheet: a table of its values *)
let sheet_html (data : string) : string =
  let value = values data and (nc, nr) = sheet_size data in
  "<table>\n"
  ^ glue (List.init nr (fun r ->
      "<tr>" ^ glue (List.init nc (fun c ->
        let (s, num, err) = shown value data c r in
        "<td"
        ^ (if num then " class=n" else if err then " class=e" else "")
        ^ ">" ^ esc s ^ "</td>")) ^ "</tr>\n"))
  ^ "</table>\n"

(* a drawing: SVG, its boxes, arrows (a line across then up or down, a
 * head of three points) and texts *)
let drawing_html (b : obj) : string =
  let num k = string_of_int k in
  let svg_text x y anchor s =
    "<text x=\"" ^ num x ^ "\" y=\"" ^ num y ^ "\" text-anchor=\"" ^ anchor
    ^ "\" dominant-baseline=\"middle\">" ^ esc s ^ "</text>" in
  "<svg width=\"" ^ num b.w ^ "\" height=\"" ^ num b.h ^ "\">\n"
  ^ glue (List.map (fun (kind, nums, text) ->
      match kind, nums with
      | "box", [ x; y; w; h ] ->
          "<rect x=\"" ^ num x ^ "\" y=\"" ^ num y ^ "\" width=\"" ^ num w
          ^ "\" height=\"" ^ num h ^ "\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"black\"/>"
          ^ (if text = "" then ""
             else svg_text (x + (w / 2)) (y + (h / 2)) "middle" text)
          ^ "\n"
      | "arrow", [ x0; y0; x1; y1 ] ->
          let dx, dy =
            if y1 > y0 then 0, -1 else if y1 < y0 then 0, 1
            else if x1 >= x0 then -1, 0 else 1, 0 in
          let p x y = num x ^ "," ^ num y in
          "<polyline points=\"" ^ p x0 y0 ^ " " ^ p x1 y0 ^ " " ^ p x1 y1
          ^ "\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"black\"/>"
          ^ "<polygon points=\"" ^ p x1 y1
          ^ " " ^ p (x1 + (6 * dx) - (4 * dy)) (y1 + (6 * dy) - (4 * dx))
          ^ " " ^ p (x1 + (6 * dx) + (4 * dy)) (y1 + (6 * dy) + (4 * dx))
          ^ "\"/>\n"
      | "text", [ x; y ] -> svg_text x (y + 8) "start" text ^ "\n"
      | _ -> "") (figures b.data))
  ^ "</svg>\n"

(* a paint: SVG, each run of a colour on a row a rectangle (white left
 * out), 4 by 4 a pixel *)
let colours =
  [ ('k', "#000"); ('r', "#f00"); ('g', "#0a0"); ('b', "#00f"); ('y', "#ff0");
    ('o', "#e90"); ('p', "#80c"); ('n', "#840"); ('a', "#888") ]

let paint_html (b : obj) : string =
  let num k = string_of_int k in
  let row r line =
    let n = String.length line in
    let rec go i acc =
      if i >= n then acc
      else begin
        let j = ref (i + 1) in
        while !j < n && line.[!j] = line.[i] do incr j done;
        go !j (match List.assoc_opt line.[i] colours with
               | Some c ->
                   ("<rect x=\"" ^ num (4 * i) ^ "\" y=\"" ^ num (4 * r)
                    ^ "\" width=\"" ^ num (4 * (!j - i))
                    ^ "\" height=\"4\" fill=\"" ^ c ^ "\"/>") :: acc
               | None -> acc)
      end in
    go 0 [] in
  let lines = String.split_on_char '\n' b.data in
  "<svg width=\"" ^ num (b.w - 4) ^ "\" height=\"" ^ num (b.h - 4)
  ^ "\" shape-rendering=\"crispEdges\">\n"
  ^ glue (List.map (fun s -> s ^ "\n")
      (List.concat (List.mapi (fun r line -> List.rev (row r line)) lines)))
  ^ "</svg>\n"

(* a chart: SVG, as the office draws it: a bar a value, its value above
 * it, its label under it, the axis a grey line *)
let bar_colours = [ "#00f"; "#f00"; "#0a0"; "#ff0"; "#e90"; "#80c" ]

let chart_html (page : obj list) (b : obj) : string =
  let num k = string_of_int k in
  let txt x y s =
    "<text x=\"" ^ num x ^ "\" y=\"" ^ num y ^ "\">" ^ esc s ^ "</text>" in
  "<svg width=\"" ^ num b.w ^ "\" height=\"" ^ num b.h ^ "\">\n"
  ^ (match chart_bars page b with
     | [], why -> txt 4 14 why ^ "\n"
     | bars, _ ->
         let n = List.length bars
         and top = List.fold_left (fun m (_, v) -> max m v) 1 bars in
         let bw = max 6 ((b.w - 16) / n) and base = b.h - 20
         and room = b.h - 42 in
         glue (List.mapi (fun k (label, v) ->
           let x = 8 + (k * bw) and tall = max 0 (v * room / top) in
           "<rect x=\"" ^ num (x + 2) ^ "\" y=\"" ^ num (base - tall)
           ^ "\" width=\"" ^ num (bw - 4) ^ "\" height=\"" ^ num tall
           ^ "\" fill=\"" ^ List.nth bar_colours (k mod 6) ^ "\"/>"
           ^ txt (x + 2) (base - tall - 4) (string_of_int v)
           ^ txt (x + 2) (base + 14) label ^ "\n") bars)
         ^ "<line x1=\"4\" y1=\"" ^ num base ^ "\" x2=\"" ^ num (b.w - 4)
         ^ "\" y2=\"" ^ num base ^ "\" stroke=\"#999\"/>\n")
  ^ "</svg>\n"

let style =
  "body{margin:16px;font:13px/16px monospace}.page{position:relative;margin-bottom:16px}.page+.page{border-top:1px dashed #ccc}.box{position:absolute;overflow:hidden}"
  ^ "p{margin:0;min-height:16px}h1,.l{font-size:26px;line-height:32px}h1{margin:0}"
  ^ "table{border-collapse:collapse}td{border:1px solid #ccc;padding:0 4px;height:15px;min-width:56px}td.n{text-align:right}td.e{color:#c00}"

let to_html (title : string) (doc : string) : string =
  let parts = in_order (parse 640 480 doc) in
  let num k = string_of_int k in
  (* a page: a block the size of its parts, each part at its place *)
  let page bs =
    let width = List.fold_left (fun m (b : obj) -> max m (b.x + b.w)) 0 bs
    and height = List.fold_left (fun m (b : obj) -> max m (b.y + b.h)) 0 bs in
    "<div class=page style=\"width:" ^ num width ^ "px;height:" ^ num height
    ^ "px\">\n"
    ^ glue (List.map (fun (b : obj) ->
        "<div class=box style=\"left:" ^ num b.x ^ "px;top:" ^ num b.y
        ^ "px;width:" ^ num b.w ^ "px;height:" ^ num b.h ^ "px\">\n"
        ^ (if b.kind = "sheet" then sheet_html b.data
           else if b.kind = "drawing" then drawing_html b
           else if b.kind = "paint" then paint_html b
           else if b.kind = "chart" then chart_html parts b
           else text_html b.data)
        ^ "</div>\n") bs)
    ^ "</div>\n" in
  glue ([ "<!doctype html>\n<html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\"><title>";
          esc title; "</title>\n<style>"; style;
          "</style></head>\n<body>\n" ]
        @ List.map page (pages_of parts)
        @ [ "</body></html>\n" ])

(*****************************************************************************)
(* PDF *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* A page of PDF for each page of the document, all the size of the
 * largest, a pixel a point: its text in Courier, one of the fonts every
 * reader has (no font carried), which at 13.33 points is 8 points a
 * character, the office's 8 by 16 (its bold, oblique and both for the
 * styles, twice the size for large); its lines and rectangles as PDF
 * draws them. Not compressed: a page is a text of drawing operators,
 * which a test reads. *)

(* a text in a PDF string: \ ( ) after a \ *)
let pdf_esc (s : string) : string =
  glue (List.map (fun ch ->
    if ch = "\\" || ch = "(" || ch = ")" then "\\" ^ ch else ch) (chars s))

(* colours, as PDF's three numbers: the paint's and the bars' *)
let pdf_colours =
  [ ('k', "0 0 0"); ('r', "1 0 0"); ('g', "0 .67 0"); ('b', "0 0 1");
    ('y', "1 1 0"); ('o', "1 .6 0"); ('p', ".53 0 .8"); ('n', ".53 .27 0");
    ('a', ".53 .53 .53") ]
let pdf_bars = [ "0 0 1"; "1 0 0"; "0 .67 0"; "1 1 0"; "1 .6 0"; ".53 0 .8" ]

(* The operators of a page of height h, its y going down as the
 * office's: a rectangle filled, one stroked, a line, a text whose top
 * is at y (its baseline 12 points lower, 24 when large), in a style *)
let fill h colour x y w hh =
  colour ^ " rg " ^ string_of_int x ^ " " ^ string_of_int (h - y - hh) ^ " "
  ^ string_of_int w ^ " " ^ string_of_int hh ^ " re f\n"
let frame_pdf h colour x y w hh =
  colour ^ " RG " ^ string_of_int x ^ " " ^ string_of_int (h - y - hh) ^ " "
  ^ string_of_int w ^ " " ^ string_of_int hh ^ " re S\n"
let line_pdf h colour x0 y0 x1 y1 =
  colour ^ " RG " ^ string_of_int x0 ^ " " ^ string_of_int (h - y0) ^ " m "
  ^ string_of_int x1 ^ " " ^ string_of_int (h - y1) ^ " l S\n"
let text_pdf h style x y s =
  let big = style land 8 <> 0 in
  "0 0 0 rg BT /F" ^ string_of_int (style land 3) ^ " "
  ^ (if big then "26.67" else "13.33") ^ " Tf " ^ string_of_int x ^ " "
  ^ string_of_int (h - y - (if big then 24 else 12))
  ^ " Td (" ^ pdf_esc s ^ ") Tj ET\n"
  ^ (if style land 4 <> 0 then
       line_pdf h "0 0 0" x (y + (if big then 30 else 15))
         (x + (String.length s * if big then 16 else 8))
         (y + (if big then 30 else 15))
     else "")

(* a text box, as the office lays it out: each run of a style on a line
 * at the line's bottom, the lines that fit *)
let text_pdf_box h (b : obj) : string =
  let (t, st) = decode b.data in
  let lay = lay_out (b.w - 8) t st and n = String.length t in
  let fits l = lay.top.(l) + lay.tall.(l) <= b.h - 4 in
  let rec runs i acc =
    if i >= n then acc
    else if t.[i] = '\n' || not (fits lay.ln.(i)) then runs (i + 1) acc
    else begin
      let j = ref (i + 1) and l = lay.ln.(i) and k = Char.code st.[i] in
      while !j < n && t.[!j] <> '\n' && lay.ln.(!j) = l && st.[!j] = st.[i] do
        incr j
      done;
      let y =
        b.y + 2 + lay.top.(l) + lay.tall.(l) - (if k land 8 <> 0 then 32 else 16) in
      runs !j (text_pdf h k (b.x + 4 + lay.px.(i)) y (String.sub t i (!j - i))
               :: acc)
    end in
  glue (List.rev (runs 0 []))

(* a sheet: its values in cells of 64 by 16, a number at the right, the
 * grid's lines grey *)
let sheet_pdf h (b : obj) : string =
  let value = values b.data and (nc, nr) = sheet_size b.data in
  glue (List.concat (List.init nr (fun r -> List.init nc (fun c ->
    let (s, num, _) = shown value b.data c r in
    let x = b.x + (64 * c) and y = b.y + (16 * r) in
    frame_pdf h ".8 .8 .8" x y 64 16
    ^ (if s = "" then ""
       else
         text_pdf h 0 (if num then x + 60 - (8 * String.length s) else x + 4)
           y s)))))

(* a drawing: its boxes stroked, its arrows a line across then up or
 * down and a head filled, its texts *)
let drawing_pdf h (b : obj) : string =
  glue (List.map (fun (kind, nums, label) ->
    match kind, nums with
    | "box", [ x; y; w; hh ] ->
        frame_pdf h "0 0 0" (b.x + x) (b.y + y) w hh
        ^ (if label = "" then ""
           else
             text_pdf h 0 (b.x + x + (w / 2) - (4 * String.length label))
               (b.y + y + (hh / 2) - 8) label)
    | "arrow", [ x0; y0; x1; y1 ] ->
        let dx, dy =
          if y1 > y0 then 0, -1 else if y1 < y0 then 0, 1
          else if x1 >= x0 then -1, 0 else 1, 0 in
        let p x y = string_of_int (b.x + x) ^ " " ^ string_of_int (h - b.y - y) in
        line_pdf h "0 0 0" (b.x + x0) (b.y + y0) (b.x + x1) (b.y + y0)
        ^ line_pdf h "0 0 0" (b.x + x1) (b.y + y0) (b.x + x1) (b.y + y1)
        ^ "0 0 0 rg " ^ p x1 y1
        ^ " m " ^ p (x1 + (6 * dx) - (4 * dy)) (y1 + (6 * dy) - (4 * dx))
        ^ " l " ^ p (x1 + (6 * dx) + (4 * dy)) (y1 + (6 * dy) + (4 * dx))
        ^ " l f\n"
    | "text", [ x; y ] -> text_pdf h 0 (b.x + x) (b.y + y) label
    | _ -> "") (figures b.data))

(* a paint: a rectangle a run of a colour on a row, 4 by 4 a pixel *)
let paint_pdf h (b : obj) : string =
  let lines = String.split_on_char '\n' b.data in
  glue (List.mapi (fun r line ->
    let n = String.length line in
    let rec go i acc =
      if i >= n then acc
      else begin
        let j = ref (i + 1) in
        while !j < n && line.[!j] = line.[i] do incr j done;
        go !j (match List.assoc_opt line.[i] pdf_colours with
               | Some c ->
                   fill h c (b.x + 2 + (4 * i)) (b.y + 2 + (4 * r))
                     (4 * (!j - i)) 4 :: acc
               | None -> acc)
      end in
    glue (List.rev (go 0 []))) lines)

(* a chart: its bars as the office draws them *)
let chart_pdf h (page : obj list) (b : obj) : string =
  match chart_bars page b with
  | [], why -> text_pdf h 0 (b.x + 4) (b.y + 2) why
  | bars, _ ->
      let n = List.length bars
      and top = List.fold_left (fun m (_, v) -> max m v) 1 bars in
      let bw = max 6 ((b.w - 16) / n) and base = b.y + b.h - 20
      and room = b.h - 42 in
      glue (List.mapi (fun k (label, v) ->
        let x = b.x + 8 + (k * bw) and tall = max 0 (v * room / top) in
        fill h (List.nth pdf_bars (k mod 6)) (x + 2) (base - tall) (bw - 4) tall
        ^ text_pdf h 0 (x + 2) (base - tall - 16) (string_of_int v)
        ^ text_pdf h 0 (x + 2) (base + 2) label) bars)
      ^ line_pdf h ".6 .6 .6" (b.x + 4) base (b.x + b.w - 4) base

(* a number of 10 digits, as the cross-reference table has them *)
let ten (k : int) =
  let s = string_of_int k in String.make (10 - String.length s) '0' ^ s

let to_pdf (doc : string) : string =
  let parts = in_order (parse 640 480 doc) in
  let pages = pages_of parts in
  let n = List.length pages in
  (* every page the size of the largest one's parts *)
  let width = List.fold_left (fun m (b : obj) -> max m (b.x + b.w)) 1 parts
  and height = List.fold_left (fun m (b : obj) -> max m (b.y + b.h)) 1 parts in
  let drawn bs = glue (List.map (fun (b : obj) ->
    if b.kind = "sheet" then sheet_pdf height b
    else if b.kind = "drawing" then drawing_pdf height b
    else if b.kind = "paint" then paint_pdf height b
    else if b.kind = "chart" then chart_pdf height parts b
    else text_pdf_box height b) bs) in
  let num k = string_of_int k in
  let font k name =
    num (3 + k) ^ " 0 obj << /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /" ^ name
    ^ " /Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding >> endobj\n" in
  (* the objects: 1 the catalog, 2 the pages, 3 to 6 the fonts, then a
   * page's and its contents' for each page, 7 and 8 the first's *)
  let page_objects k bs =
    let content = drawn bs in
    [ num (7 + (2 * k)) ^ " 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 "
      ^ num width ^ " " ^ num height
      ^ "] /Resources << /Font << /F0 3 0 R /F1 4 0 R /F2 5 0 R /F3 6 0 R >> >> /Contents "
      ^ num (8 + (2 * k)) ^ " 0 R >> endobj\n";
      num (8 + (2 * k)) ^ " 0 obj << /Length " ^ num (String.length content)
      ^ " >>\nstream\n" ^ content ^ "endstream endobj\n" ] in
  let kids =
    glue (List.init n (fun k ->
      (if k = 0 then "" else " ") ^ num (7 + (2 * k)) ^ " 0 R")) in
  let objects = [
    "1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj\n";
    "2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [" ^ kids ^ "] /Count " ^ num n
    ^ " >> endobj\n";
    font 0 "Courier"; font 1 "Courier-Bold"; font 2 "Courier-Oblique";
    font 3 "Courier-BoldOblique" ]
    @ List.concat (List.mapi page_objects pages) in
  let head = "%PDF-1.4\n" in
  (* each object's place in the file, for the cross-reference table *)
  let rec places at l =
    match l with
    | o :: rest -> at :: places (at + String.length o) rest
    | [] -> [] in
  let body = glue objects and count = List.length objects + 1 in
  head ^ body ^ "xref\n0 " ^ num count ^ "\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
  ^ glue (List.map (fun at -> ten at ^ " 00000 n \n")
      (places (String.length head) objects))
  ^ "trailer << /Size " ^ num count ^ " /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n"
  ^ num (String.length head + String.length body) ^ "\n%%EOF\n"
tiny/TinyTroff.mli
4295
(* tiny-troff: a document of mini-troff's format (plan_typesetting.md),
 * a page of tiny-office's or a Markdown file, printed as text or as
 * HTML. The office edits a page as it is shown; emacs edits it as it
 * is written (Markdown's lines, \box[x y w h]{...} around each part);
 * tiny-troff publishes it (step 6 of plan_tiny_office.md).
 *
 *     page.ixd ──▶ TinyOfficeFile.parse ──▶ the parts, in reading order
 *                                              (top, then left)
 *                                                  │
 *                              text ◀──────────────┴──────────────▶ HTML
 *
 * It reads a page with the office's own functions (TinyOffice/'s
 * parts: TinyOfficeFile, TinyOfficeText, TinyOfficeSheet...), so the
 * format is written down once. A part is printed as
 * its kind asks:
 *
 *     part      as text                          as HTML
 *     text      each line filled to the width,   a line a <p>, a large
 *               a large line underlined by =     one an <h1>; <b> <i>
 *                                                <u>, large words big
 *     sheet     its values in columns, a number  a <table> of its
 *               at its column's right            values
 *     drawing   characters, one for 8 by 8       SVG: rectangles, lines
 *               pixels: + - | for a box, its     and their heads, texts
 *               label in it, > < v ^ an arrow's
 *               head
 *     paint     its rows, white a space          SVG: a rectangle a run
 *                                                of a colour, 4 by 4 a
 *                                                pixel
 *     chart     a line a bar: its label, #s for  SVG: the bars as the
 *               its share of the largest, its    office draws them
 *               value
 *
 * As text, the parts come one after the other, an empty line between
 * two, a form feed between two pages (nroff's). As HTML, each is at
 * its place on its page (a box positioned in a block of the page's
 * parts' size), the pages one under the other, as the office shows
 * them. As PDF, a page each, all the size of the largest.
 *
 * Its twin is mini-troff (typesetting/), which reads what was written
 * for troff (a manual page's and a paper's macros, tbl, pic), LaTeX,
 * and the same Markdown's lines, into one document (Doc) laid out
 * for a terminal or a PDF in Times. What is ours: one format only,
 * the office's, read by the office's functions, so there is no
 * document type of troff's own, no roff and no LaTeX; a part kept at
 * its place on its page, where mini-troff fills a flow of
 * paragraphs; HTML, which mini-troff does not write; PDF in Courier,
 * one width for every character, so no font's metrics are needed.
 * Plan 9's troff (principia's typesetting/troff/) is the original of
 * both; Plan 9 makes HTML with other programs, troff2html from
 * troff's output and htmlroff from -ms input (principia's
 * typesetting/).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * troff (Joe Ossanna, 1973) made the documents of Unix from a text
 * with requests, for the screen (nroff) and for the phototypesetter;
 * its preprocessors (tbl, eqn, pic) turned tables, equations and
 * drawings into more requests. Here the parts are the tables and the
 * drawings, and the page they are on is both what the office shows and
 * the text troff reads: Bravo's and troff's ways to one document.
 *
 * Left out: a text that flows onto the next page, the paint as a
 * picture (a BMP: SVG's rectangles instead), and the office's own
 * colours and fonts in the HTML (the browser's monospace). *)

(* [to_text width doc]: the document as text, its lines filled to width *)
val to_text : int -> string -> string

(* [to_html title doc]: the document as a web page *)
val to_html : string -> string -> string

(* [to_pdf doc]: the document as a page of PDF, the size of its parts,
 * a pixel a point: text in Courier (13.33 points, 8 a character, as the
 * office's 8 by 16; bold, oblique, twice the size for large), laid out
 * as the office lays it out; a sheet's values in a grid, a drawing's
 * lines, a paint's and a chart's rectangles. The standard fonts, no
 * compression: about 120 lines. *)
val to_pdf : string -> string
tiny/TinyUtilities.ml
33621
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See TinyUtilities.mli *)

(* The test (tests/TinyUtilities_test.sh) runs each utility and its
 * twin, mini-wc, mini-xd..., on the same arguments, and compares what
 * they print and their exit status: the twins' output is kept where it
 * costs nothing. *)

(* (grep's patterns: compile, matches) *)
open TinyLibRegex

type caps =
  < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr;
    Cap.kill; Cap.clock; Cap.exit; Cap.env >

(* raised by a utility given arguments it does not take: the driver
 * then prints the utility's usage *)
exception Usage

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Helpers *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let print caps s = TinyLibSystem.print caps s
let complain caps tool s = TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (tool ^ ": " ^ s ^ "\n")

(* what follows the last slash of a path *)
let last_part path =
  match String.rindex_opt path '/' with
  | Some i -> String.sub path (i + 1) (String.length path - i - 1)
  | None -> path

(* a name as rc reads it back: between quotes, a quote doubled, when it
 * is empty or has a space, a control character or a quote *)
let quote name =
  if name <> "" && not (String.exists (fun c -> c <= ' ' || c = '\'') name)
  then name
  else "'" ^ String.concat "''" (String.split_on_char '\'' name) ^ "'"

(* [options letters args]: the letters of the options in front of args,
 * each of which must be one of letters, and the arguments after them.
 * "--" ends the options, and "-" alone is an argument *)
let options letters args =
  let rec go acc args =
    match args with
    | "--" :: rest -> acc, rest
    | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' ->
        let given = List.init (String.length a - 1) (fun i -> a.[i + 1]) in
        if List.for_all (fun c -> String.contains letters c) given
        then go (acc @ given) rest
        else raise Usage
    | _ -> acc, args in
  go [] args

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Filters *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* [pieces fd f]: f on each piece of what fd gives, as soon as it is
 * read, until the end *)
let rec pieces fd f =
  let s = TinyLibSystem.read fd 8192 in
  if s <> "" then begin f s; pieces fd f end

(* [lines fd f]: f on each line of fd, without its newline, as soon as
 * it is whole, and whether a newline ended it: the last one may have
 * none *)
let lines fd f =
  let rest = ref "" in
  pieces fd (fun s ->
    let s = !rest ^ s in
    let rec go i =
      match String.index_from_opt s i '\n' with
      | Some j -> f (String.sub s i (j - i)) true; go (j + 1)
      | None -> rest := String.sub s i (String.length s - i) in
    go 0);
  if !rest <> "" then f !rest false

let each_input caps tool files f =
  let one status name fd =
    try f name fd; status
    with Failure m ->
      complain caps tool ((if name = "" then "stdin" else name) ^ ": " ^ m);
      1 in
  if files = [] then one 0 "" 0
  else
    List.fold_left (fun status file ->
      match
        (try Some (TinyLibSystem.open_in caps file)
         with Failure m -> complain caps tool (file ^ ": " ^ m); None)
      with
      | None -> 1
      | Some fd ->
          let status = one status file fd in
          TinyLibSystem.close fd;
          status) 0 files

let cat caps args =
  let _, files = options "" args in
  each_input caps "cat" files (fun _ fd ->
    pieces fd (fun s -> print caps s; TinyLibSystem.flush caps))

(* the counts so far, and whether the last byte counted was inside a
 * word: a word can be cut in two by the end of a piece *)
type counts = {
  mutable lines : int;
  mutable words : int;
  mutable bytes : int;
  mutable inword : bool;
}

let counts () = { lines = 0; words = 0; bytes = 0; inword = false }

let count c s =
  for i = 0 to String.length s - 1 do
    let k = Char.code s.[i] in
    if k = 10 then c.lines <- c.lines + 1;
    if k = 32 || (k >= 9 && k <= 13) then c.inword <- false
    else if not c.inword then begin c.words <- c.words + 1; c.inword <- true end
  done;
  c.bytes <- c.bytes + String.length s

let wc caps args =
  let asked, files = options "lwc" args in
  let asked = if asked = [] then [ 'l'; 'w'; 'c' ] else asked in
  let report c name =
    let columns =
      List.filter (fun (letter, _) -> List.mem letter asked)
        [ 'l', c.lines; 'w', c.words; 'c', c.bytes ] in
    let columns = List.map (fun (_, n) -> Printf.sprintf "%7d" n) columns in
    print caps
      (String.concat " " (columns @ (if name = "" then [] else [ name ]))
       ^ "\n") in
  let total = counts () and files_counted = ref 0 in
  let status =
    each_input caps "wc" files (fun name fd ->
      let c = counts () in
      pieces fd (count c);
      report c name;
      incr files_counted;
      total.lines <- total.lines + c.lines;
      total.words <- total.words + c.words;
      total.bytes <- total.bytes + c.bytes) in
  if !files_counted > 1 then report total "total";
  status

(* the text from its nth line from the end, or from its nth line (+n).
 * tail is the one filter that reads all its input first: until the
 * end, it cannot know which lines are the last *)
let lines_of from_end n s =
  let len = String.length s in
  let start =
    if from_end then begin
      (* back from the end over n newlines, the one that ends the text
       * not counted *)
      let rec back i k =
        if i < 0 then 0
        else if s.[i] = '\n' then
          (if k = n then i + 1 else back (i - 1) (k + 1))
        else back (i - 1) k in
      if n = 0 then len
      else back (if len > 0 && s.[len - 1] = '\n' then len - 2 else len - 1) 1
    end
    else begin
      let rec skip i k =
        if k <= 1 || i >= len then i
        else if s.[i] = '\n' then skip (i + 1) (k - 1)
        else skip (i + 1) k in
      skip 0 n
    end in
  String.sub s start (len - start)

let tail caps args =
  let from_end, n, files =
    match args with
    | "-n" :: n :: rest -> true, n, rest
    | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && (a.[0] = '-' || a.[0] = '+') ->
        a.[0] = '-', String.sub a 1 (String.length a - 1), rest
    | _ -> true, "10", args in
  match int_of_string_opt n, files with
  | Some n, ([] | [ _ ]) when n >= 0 ->
      each_input caps "tail" files (fun _ fd ->
        print caps (lines_of from_end n (TinyLibSystem.read_all fd)))
  | _ -> raise Usage

let tee caps args =
  let _, files = options "" args in
  let status = ref 0 in
  let fds =
    List.concat_map (fun file ->
      try [ TinyLibSystem.open_out caps file ]
      with Failure m ->
        complain caps "tee" (file ^ ": " ^ m); status := 1; []) files in
  pieces 0 (fun s ->
    print caps s;
    TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
    List.iter (fun fd -> TinyLibSystem.write fd s) fds);
  List.iter TinyLibSystem.close fds;
  !status

(* a byte as xd -c shows it, in three columns *)
let character c =
  let k = Char.code c in
  if k = 9 then " \\t"
  else if k = 13 then " \\r"
  else if k = 10 then " \\n"
  else if k = 8 then " \\b"
  else if k < 32 || k >= 127 then Printf.sprintf " %02x" k
  else "  " ^ String.make 1 c

(* xd: 16 bytes a line after their address, as numbers of 4 bytes (the
 * last one filled with zeros), or each byte (-b), or each character
 * (-c). The bytes of a line not yet complete are kept from one piece to
 * the next *)
let xd caps args =
  let flags, files = options "bc" args in
  let size, show =
    if List.mem 'c' flags then 1, (fun g -> character g.[0])
    else if List.mem 'b' flags then
      1, (fun g -> Printf.sprintf " %02x" (Char.code g.[0]))
    else
      4, (fun g ->
        " " ^ String.concat "" (List.init 4 (fun i ->
          if i < String.length g then Printf.sprintf "%02x" (Char.code g.[i])
          else "00"))) in
  let address a = Printf.sprintf "%07x " a in
  each_input caps "xd" files (fun _ fd ->
    let pending = ref "" and addr = ref 0 in
    let line s =
      let groups =
        List.init ((String.length s + size - 1) / size) (fun j ->
          show
            (String.sub s (j * size) (min size (String.length s - (j * size)))))
      in
      print caps (address !addr ^ String.concat "" groups ^ "\n") in
    let rec whole_lines () =
      if String.length !pending >= 16 then begin
        line (String.sub !pending 0 16);
        addr := !addr + 16;
        pending := String.sub !pending 16 (String.length !pending - 16);
        whole_lines ()
      end in
    pieces fd (fun s -> pending := !pending ^ s; whole_lines ());
    (* the end: the line that is shorter than 16, empty after a text of
     * whole lines, then the address alone *)
    line !pending;
    print caps (address (!addr + String.length !pending) ^ "\n"))

(* the lines that match; -v: that do not; -i: whatever the letters'
 * case; -n: with their numbers; -c: how many; -l: the files' names.
 * The status is 0 when a line was found *)
let grep caps args =
  let flags, rest = options "vincl" args in
  match rest with
  | [] -> raise Usage
  | pattern :: files ->
      let fold s = if List.mem 'i' flags then String.lowercase_ascii s else s in
      let re = compile (fold pattern) in
      let named name = if List.length files > 1 then name ^ ":" else "" in
      let found = ref false in
      let status =
        each_input caps "grep" files (fun name fd ->
          let count = ref 0 and number = ref 0 in
          lines fd (fun line ended ->
            incr number;
            if matches re (fold line) <> List.mem 'v' flags then begin
              incr count;
              found := true;
              if not (List.mem 'c' flags || List.mem 'l' flags) then
                print caps
                  (named name
                   ^ (if List.mem 'n' flags then string_of_int !number ^ ": "
                      else "")
                   ^ line ^ (if ended then "\n" else ""))
            end);
          if List.mem 'c' flags then
            print caps (named name ^ string_of_int !count ^ "\n");
          if List.mem 'l' flags && !count > 0 then print caps (name ^ "\n")) in
      if status <> 0 then status else if !found then 0 else 1

(* the number a text starts with, after blanks: a sign and digits; 0
 * when there is none *)
let number_of text =
  let n = String.length text in
  let rec blanks i =
    if i < n && (text.[i] = ' ' || text.[i] = '\t') then blanks (i + 1)
    else i in
  let i = blanks 0 in
  let negative = i < n && text.[i] = '-' in
  let rec digits i acc =
    if i < n && text.[i] >= '0' && text.[i] <= '9' then
      digits (i + 1) ((acc * 10) + Char.code text.[i] - 48)
    else acc in
  let v = digits (if negative then i + 1 else i) 0 in
  if negative then - v else v

(* a line from its field k on: k times, blanks then what is not *)
let from_field k line =
  let n = String.length line in
  let rec skip i k =
    if k = 0 then i
    else begin
      let rec over p i = if i < n && p line.[i] then over p (i + 1) else i in
      let blank c = c = ' ' || c = '\t' in
      skip (over (fun c -> not (blank c)) (over blank i)) (k - 1)
    end in
  let i = skip 0 k in
  String.sub line i (n - i)

(* the lines of all the inputs, in order: by their bytes, or -n by the
 * number they start with; +k: from their field k (the first is 0); -r:
 * reversed; -u: one of the lines the order says equal. A line's key is
 * made once, as a pair the sort compares (the line itself after, so
 * that lines the key says equal are in the order of their bytes) *)
let sort caps args =
  let flags, rest = options "nru" args in
  let field, files =
    match rest with
    | a :: l when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '+' -> begin
        match int_of_string_opt (String.sub a 1 (String.length a - 1)) with
        | Some k when k >= 0 -> k, l
        | _ -> raise Usage
      end
    | _ -> 0, rest in
  let all = ref [] in
  let status =
    each_input caps "sort" files (fun _ fd ->
      lines fd (fun line _ -> all := line :: !all)) in
  let key line =
    let text = from_field field line in
    if List.mem 'n' flags then (number_of text, "") else (0, text) in
  let keyed = List.map (fun line -> key line, line) !all in
  let order a b = if List.mem 'r' flags then compare b a else compare a b in
  let sorted = List.sort order keyed in
  (* -u: a line whose key is the one before's is left out *)
  let rec unique = function
    | (k1, l1) :: (k2, _) :: rest when k1 = k2 -> unique ((k1, l1) :: rest)
    | x :: rest -> x :: unique rest
    | [] -> [] in
  List.iter (fun (_, line) -> print caps (line ^ "\n"))
    (if List.mem 'u' flags then unique sorted else sorted);
  status

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Walkers *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let entries caps dir = List.sort compare (TinyLibSystem.readdir caps dir)

let rec fold caps path f =
  let is_dir, size = TinyLibSystem.stat caps path in
  f path is_dir size (fun () ->
    if is_dir then
      List.map (fun e -> fold caps (Filename.concat path e) f) (entries caps path)
    else [])

(* [each_path caps tool paths f]: f on each path; one that fails is
 * reported, and the status is then 1 *)
let each_path caps tool paths f =
  List.fold_left (fun status p ->
    try f p; status
    with Failure m -> complain caps tool (p ^ ": " ^ m); 1) 0 paths

(* a directory's entries, or a file's name; all of them sorted together,
 * and quoted for rc. -l: each with its kind (d for a directory), its
 * links (how many names it has: more than one, and the others are the
 * same file) and its size *)
let ls caps args =
  let flags, paths = options "l" args in
  let names = ref [] in
  let status =
    if paths = [] then begin names := entries caps "."; 0 end
    else
      each_path caps "ls" paths (fun p ->
        let is_dir, _ = TinyLibSystem.stat caps p in
        names :=
          (if is_dir then List.map (Filename.concat p) (entries caps p) else [ p ])
          @ !names) in
  let long name =
    if not (List.mem 'l' flags) then ""
    else begin
      let is_dir, size = TinyLibSystem.stat caps name in
      (if is_dir then "d" else "-")
      ^ Printf.sprintf "%4d%9d " (TinyLibSystem.links caps name) size
    end in
  List.iter (fun name -> print caps (long name ^ quote name ^ "\n"))
    (List.sort compare !names);
  status

(* every path under a directory (under the current one, without "./",
 * when none is named), a directory before what it has *)
let walk caps args =
  let _, paths = options "" args in
  let pre p _ _ entries = print caps (p ^ "\n"); ignore (entries ()) in
  if paths = [] then begin List.iter (fun e -> fold caps e pre) (entries caps "."); 0 end
  else
    each_path caps "walk" paths (fun p ->
      let is_dir, _ = TinyLibSystem.stat caps p in
      if is_dir then
        List.iter (fun e -> fold caps (Filename.concat p e) pre) (entries caps p)
      else print caps (p ^ "\n"))

(* the kilobytes under each directory, after what it has; -a: each file
 * too *)
let du caps args =
  let flags, paths = options "a" args in
  let paths = if paths = [] then [ "." ] else paths in
  each_path caps "du" paths (fun root ->
    ignore
      (fold caps root (fun p is_dir size entries ->
         let k =
           List.fold_left (fun a b -> a + b)
             (if is_dir then 0 else (size + 1023) / 1024) (entries ()) in
         if is_dir || p = root || List.mem 'a' flags then
           print caps (string_of_int k ^ "\t" ^ quote p ^ "\n");
         k)))

(* -r: a directory with what it has, its entries first *)
let rm caps args =
  let flags, paths = options "r" args in
  if paths = [] then raise Usage;
  each_path caps "rm" paths (fun root ->
    if List.mem 'r' flags then
      fold caps root (fun p _ _ entries ->
        ignore (entries ()); TinyLibSystem.remove caps p)
    else TinyLibSystem.remove caps root)

(* -p: the directories above it too, and no complaint when it is there *)
let mkdir caps args =
  let flags, dirs = options "p" args in
  if dirs = [] then raise Usage;
  each_path caps "mkdir" dirs (fun dir ->
    if List.mem 'p' flags then begin
      (* each part of the path up to a slash, then the whole *)
      let rec make i =
        if i <= String.length dir then begin
          if i = String.length dir || dir.[i] = '/' then begin
            let d = String.sub dir 0 i in
            if not (TinyLibSystem.is_directory caps d) then
              TinyLibSystem.mkdir caps d
          end;
          make (i + 1)
        end in
      make 1
    end
    else TinyLibSystem.mkdir caps dir)

(* [into_last caps tool paths f]: f from dest for each path but the last,
 * dest being the last path, or the source's name in it when the last
 * is a directory; several sources need a directory *)
let into_last caps tool paths f =
  match List.rev paths with
  | dest :: sources when sources <> [] ->
      let into = TinyLibSystem.is_directory caps dest in
      if List.length sources > 1 && not into then begin
        complain caps tool (dest ^ ": not a directory"); 1
      end
      else
        each_path caps tool (List.rev sources) (fun from ->
          f from (if into then Filename.concat dest (last_part from) else dest))
  | _ -> raise Usage

(* a path's names from the root: the current directory's first when it
 * is relative, "." dropped and ".." resolved by the text *)
let resolved caps p =
  let p =
    if p <> "" && p.[0] = '/' then p else TinyLibSystem.getcwd caps ^ "/" ^ p in
  List.fold_left (fun acc n ->
      if n = "" || n = "." then acc
      else if n = ".." then (match acc with [] -> [] | _ :: r -> r)
      else n :: acc)
    [] (String.split_on_char '/' p)

(* The copy is written a piece at a time as the file is read, so a file
 * of any size is copied in a little memory. A file copied onto itself
 * is refused, as Plan 9's cp does: opening the copy would empty the file
 * before it is read. Only the same path is seen; two names of one file
 * (ln) are not. *)
let cp caps args =
  let _, paths = options "" args in
  into_last caps "cp" paths (fun from dest ->
    if fst (TinyLibSystem.stat caps from) then failwith "is a directory";
    if resolved caps from = resolved caps dest then failwith "the same file";
    let src = TinyLibSystem.open_in caps from in
    let fd =
      (try TinyLibSystem.open_out caps dest
       with Failure m -> TinyLibSystem.close src; failwith m) in
    pieces src (TinyLibSystem.write fd);
    TinyLibSystem.close fd;
    TinyLibSystem.close src)

let mv caps args =
  let _, paths = options "" args in
  into_last caps "mv" paths (fun from dest ->
    TinyLibSystem.rename caps from dest)

(* a second name for a file: its bytes are not copied, and a change by
 * one name is seen by the other *)
let ln caps args =
  let _, paths = options "" args in
  into_last caps "ln" paths (fun from dest -> TinyLibSystem.link caps from dest)

let touch caps args =
  let _, files = options "" args in
  if files = [] then raise Usage;
  each_path caps "touch" files (fun file -> TinyLibSystem.touch caps file)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Processes *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the processes, a line each in /dev/ps (or the file given, a copy of
 * it): its pid, its parent's, its state, its memory in KB, its command
 * line, in the scheduler's order; printed by pid, in columns under
 * their names, the numbers to the right, a program by its name alone
 * (-a: its whole command line, as Plan 9's ps -a) *)
let ps caps args =
  let flags, files = options "a" args in
  let file =
    match files with [] -> "/dev/ps" | [ f ] -> f | _ -> raise Usage in
  let rows = ref [] in
  let status =
    each_input caps "ps" [ file ] (fun _ fd ->
      lines fd (fun line _ ->
        match String.split_on_char ' ' line with
        | pid :: parent :: state :: kb :: cmd ->
            let cmd =
              if List.mem 'a' flags then String.concat " " cmd
              else match cmd with c :: _ -> last_part c | [] -> "" in
            rows := (pid, parent, state, kb, cmd) :: !rows
        | _ -> ())) in
  let pid (p, _, _, _, _) =
    match int_of_string_opt p with Some n -> n | None -> 0 in
  let all =
    ("PID", "PARENT", "STATE", "KB", "CMD")
    :: List.sort (fun a b -> compare (pid a) (pid b)) !rows in
  let width column =
    List.fold_left (fun w row -> max w (String.length (column row))) 0 all in
  let wpid = width (fun (p, _, _, _, _) -> p)
  and wparent = width (fun (_, p, _, _, _) -> p)
  and wstate = width (fun (_, _, s, _, _) -> s)
  and wkb = width (fun (_, _, _, k, _) -> k) in
  let right w s = String.make (w - String.length s) ' ' ^ s in
  if status = 0 then List.iter (fun (pid, parent, state, kb, cmd) ->
    print caps (right wpid pid ^ " " ^ right wparent parent ^ " " ^ state
                ^ String.make (wstate - String.length state + 1) ' '
                ^ right wkb kb ^ " " ^ cmd ^ "\n")) all;
  status

(* each process named by its pid ended, as a fault ends one *)
let kill caps args =
  if args = [] then raise Usage;
  List.fold_left (fun status a ->
    match int_of_string_opt a with
    | Some pid when TinyLibSystem.kill caps pid -> status
    | _ -> complain caps "kill" (a ^ ": no such process"); 1) 0 args

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The rest *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let pwd caps args =
  if args <> [] then raise Usage;
  print caps (TinyLibSystem.getcwd caps ^ "\n");
  0

(* seconds, and thousandths after a point: sleep .5 *)
let sleep caps args =
  match args with
  | [ a ] ->
      let point =
        match String.index_opt a '.' with
        | Some i -> i
        | None -> String.length a in
      let thousandths =
        String.sub
          (String.sub a (min (point + 1) (String.length a))
             (String.length a - min (point + 1) (String.length a))
           ^ "000") 0 3 in
      (match
         int_of_string_opt ("0" ^ String.sub a 0 point),
         int_of_string_opt thousandths
       with
       | Some s, Some ms when ms >= 0 ->
           TinyLibSystem.sleep caps ((s * 1000) + ms); 0
       | _ -> raise Usage)
  | _ -> raise Usage

(* the date as Plan 9's date writes it, in GMT: now, or the seconds
 * given, since 2000-01-01 as the system counts them (TinyLibSystem.time:
 * Unix's minus 946,684,800); -n: the seconds *)
let day_names = [ "Sun"; "Mon"; "Tue"; "Wed"; "Thu"; "Fri"; "Sat" ]
let month_names =
  [ "Jan"; "Feb"; "Mar"; "Apr"; "May"; "Jun";
    "Jul"; "Aug"; "Sep"; "Oct"; "Nov"; "Dec" ]

let date caps args =
  let flags, rest = options "n" args in
  let t =
    match rest with
    | [] -> TinyLibSystem.time caps
    | [ a ] ->
        (match int_of_string_opt a with
         | Some t when t >= 0 -> t
         | _ -> raise Usage)
    | _ -> raise Usage in
  if List.mem 'n' flags then print caps (string_of_int t ^ "\n")
  else begin
    let days = t / 86400 and secs = t mod 86400 in
    let leap y = (y mod 4 = 0 && y mod 100 <> 0) || y mod 400 = 0 in
    (* the year, then the month, each taken off the days while they last *)
    let rec year y d =
      let n = if leap y then 366 else 365 in
      if d < n then y, d else year (y + 1) (d - n) in
    let y, d = year 2000 days in
    let rec month m d lengths =
      match lengths with
      | n :: rest when d >= n -> month (m + 1) (d - n) rest
      | _ -> m, d in
    let m, d =
      month 0 d
        [ 31; (if leap y then 29 else 28); 31; 30; 31; 30;
          31; 31; 30; 31; 30; 31 ] in
    let two n = (if n < 10 then "0" else "") ^ string_of_int n in
    (* (2000-01-01 was a Saturday) *)
    print caps
      (List.nth day_names ((days + 6) mod 7) ^ " " ^ List.nth month_names m
       ^ " " ^ (if d < 9 then " " else "") ^ string_of_int (d + 1) ^ " "
       ^ two (secs / 3600) ^ ":" ^ two (secs / 60 mod 60) ^ ":"
       ^ two (secs mod 60) ^ " GMT " ^ string_of_int y ^ "\n")
  end;
  0

(* test: a question about files, strings or numbers, answered by the
 * status alone. Its arguments are an expression, read by recursive
 * descent, -o binding less than -a, which binds less than !:
 *
 *     either   := both [-o either]
 *     both     := negation [-a both]
 *     negation := ! negation | primary
 *     primary  := ( either ) | -e f | -f f | -d f | -s f | -n s | -z s
 *               | s = s | s != s | n -eq n (-ne -gt -lt -ge -le) | s
 *
 * The questions kept are those tiny-kernel can answer: it has no
 * permissions and no times *)
let test caps args =
  let rest = ref args in
  let peek () = match !rest with a :: _ -> Some a | [] -> None in
  let next () = match !rest with a :: l -> rest := l; a | [] -> raise Usage in
  let file f = try Some (TinyLibSystem.stat caps f) with Failure _ -> None in
  let number s =
    match int_of_string_opt s with Some n -> n | None -> raise Usage in
  let rec either () =
    let p = both () in
    if peek () = Some "-o" then begin
      ignore (next ()); let q = either () in p || q
    end
    else p
  and both () =
    let p = negation () in
    if peek () = Some "-a" then begin
      ignore (next ()); let q = both () in p && q
    end
    else p
  and negation () =
    if peek () = Some "!" then begin ignore (next ()); not (negation ()) end
    else primary ()
  and primary () =
    match next () with
    | "(" -> let p = either () in if next () <> ")" then raise Usage; p
    | "-e" -> file (next ()) <> None
    | "-f" ->
        (match file (next ()) with
         | Some (is_dir, _) -> not is_dir
         | None -> false)
    | "-d" ->
        (match file (next ()) with Some (is_dir, _) -> is_dir | None -> false)
    | "-s" ->
        (match file (next ()) with Some (_, size) -> size > 0 | None -> false)
    | "-n" -> next () <> ""
    | "-z" -> next () = ""
    | a -> begin
        match peek () with
        | Some "=" -> ignore (next ()); a = next ()
        | Some "!=" -> ignore (next ()); a <> next ()
        | Some op
          when List.mem op [ "-eq"; "-ne"; "-gt"; "-lt"; "-ge"; "-le" ] ->
            ignore (next ());
            let m = number a and n = number (next ()) in
            if op = "-eq" then m = n
            else if op = "-ne" then m <> n
            else if op = "-gt" then m > n
            else if op = "-lt" then m < n
            else if op = "-ge" then m >= n
            else m <= n
        | _ -> a <> ""
      end in
  if args = [] then 1
  else begin
    let p = either () in
    if !rest <> [] then raise Usage;
    if p then 0 else 1
  end

(* test, run as [ expression ] *)
let bracket caps args =
  match List.rev args with
  | "]" :: l -> test caps (List.rev l)
  | _ -> raise Usage

let echo caps args =
  let newline, words =
    match args with "-n" :: rest -> false, rest | _ -> true, args in
  print caps (String.concat " " words ^ (if newline then "\n" else ""));
  0

let seq caps args =
  let numbers =
    List.map (fun a ->
      match int_of_string_opt a with Some n -> n | None -> raise Usage) args in
  let first, step, last =
    match numbers with
    | [ l ] -> 1, 1, l
    | [ f; l ] -> f, 1, l
    | [ f; s; l ] -> f, s, l
    | _ -> raise Usage in
  if step = 0 then raise Usage;
  let rec go i =
    if (step > 0 && i <= last) || (step < 0 && i >= last) then begin
      print caps (string_of_int i ^ "\n"); go (i + step)
    end in
  go first;
  0

(* the last part of a path, without the suffix; -d: all but the last part *)
let basename caps args =
  let dir, args =
    match args with "-d" :: rest -> true, rest | _ -> false, args in
  let name, suffix =
    match args with [ n ] -> n, "" | [ n; s ] -> n, s | _ -> raise Usage in
  let last = last_part name in
  print caps
    ((if dir then
        (match String.rindex_opt name '/' with
         | Some i -> String.sub name 0 i
         | None -> ".")
      else if suffix <> "" && Filename.check_suffix last suffix then
        String.sub last 0 (String.length last - String.length suffix)
      else last) ^ "\n");
  0

(* the first byte where two files differ, or the one that ends first;
 * -s: only the status. Read a piece at a time, side by side (old: each
 * file whole: a compiler's output was more than a program's 1 MB on
 * tiny-kernel) *)
type compared = Same_bytes | Differ_at of int | Ends_first of string * int

let cmp caps args =
  let flags, files = options "s" args in
  match files with
  | [ f1; f2 ] -> begin
      match
        (try
           let a = TinyLibSystem.open_in caps f1 in
           Some (a, try TinyLibSystem.open_in caps f2
                    with Failure m -> TinyLibSystem.close a; failwith m)
         with Failure m -> complain caps "cmp" m; None)
      with
      | None -> 1
      | Some (fa, fb) ->
          (* pos bytes the same so far; sa and sb what is read past them *)
          let rec go pos sa sb =
            let sa = if sa = "" then TinyLibSystem.read fa 4096 else sa
            and sb = if sb = "" then TinyLibSystem.read fb 4096 else sb in
            let n = min (String.length sa) (String.length sb) in
            let rec first i =
              if i < n && sa.[i] = sb.[i] then first (i + 1) else i in
            let i = first 0 in
            if i < n then Differ_at (pos + i)
            else if n = 0 then
              (if sa = "" && sb = "" then Same_bytes
               else Ends_first ((if sa = "" then f1 else f2), pos))
            else
              go (pos + n) (String.sub sa n (String.length sa - n))
                (String.sub sb n (String.length sb - n)) in
          let r = go 0 "" "" in
          TinyLibSystem.close fa; TinyLibSystem.close fb;
          let say s = if not (List.mem 's' flags) then print caps (s ^ "\n") in
          match r with
          | Same_bytes -> 0
          | Differ_at i ->
              say (f1 ^ " " ^ f2 ^ " differ: char " ^ string_of_int (i + 1)); 1
          | Ends_first (f, n) ->
              say ("EOF on " ^ f ^ " after " ^ string_of_int n ^ " bytes"); 1
    end
  | _ -> raise Usage

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The driver *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* each utility: its name, its arguments, what it does, and itself *)
let utilities =
  [ "basename", "[-d] name [suffix]", "the last part of a path", basename;
    "cat", "[file ...]", "the files, one after the other", cat;
    "[", "expression ]", "test", bracket;
    "cmp", "[-s] file1 file2", "where two files differ", cmp;
    "cp", "from to | from ... dir", "files copied", cp;
    "date", "[-n] [seconds]", "the date, now or of seconds since 2000", date;
    "du", "[-a] [path ...]", "the kilobytes under each directory", du;
    "echo", "[-n] [word ...]", "the words", echo;
    "grep", "[-vincl] pattern [file ...]", "the lines that match", grep;
    "kill", "pid ...", "processes ended", kill;
    "ln", "old new | old ... dir", "second names for files", ln;
    "ls", "[-l] [path ...]", "a directory's entries, sorted", ls;
    "mkdir", "[-p] dir ...", "new directories", mkdir;
    "mv", "from to | from ... dir", "files renamed", mv;
    "ps", "[-a] [file]", "the processes, from /dev/ps", ps;
    "pwd", "", "the directory the process is in", pwd;
    "rm", "[-r] path ...", "files removed", rm;
    "seq", "[first [step]] last", "the numbers from first to last", seq;
    "sleep", "seconds[.thousandths]", "nothing, for that long", sleep;
    "sort", "[-nru] [+field] [file ...]", "the lines in order", sort;
    "tail", "[-n N | -N | +N] [file]", "the last lines, or from line N", tail;
    "tee", "[file ...]", "the input, to the files too", tee;
    "test", "expression", "whether it is true, by the status", test;
    "touch", "file ...", "files written now, or made", touch;
    "walk", "[path ...]", "every path under a directory", walk;
    "wc", "[-lwc] [file ...]", "the lines, words and bytes", wc;
    "xd", "[-b | -c] [file ...]", "the bytes, in hexadecimal", xd ]

let rec find name = function
  | [] -> None
  | (n, usage, _, f) :: rest ->
      if n = name then Some (n, usage, f) else find name rest

let help () =
  "usage: tiny-utils name [arg ...], or name [arg ...] by a link named after it\n"
  ^ String.concat "" (List.map (fun (n, usage, what, _) ->
      let u = n ^ " " ^ usage in
      "  " ^ u ^ String.make (max 1 (32 - String.length u)) ' ' ^ what ^ "\n")
      utilities)

let main (caps : Cap.all_caps) : int =
  let status =
    match TinyLibSystem.argv caps with
    | [] -> 1
    | arg0 :: args -> begin
        (* the utility is the name the program was run by, else its first
         * argument *)
        let called = last_part arg0 in
        let name, args =
          match find called utilities, args with
          | Some _, _ -> called, args
          | None, n :: rest -> n, rest
          | None, [] -> "", [] in
        match find name utilities with
        | Some (n, usage, f) -> begin
            try f (caps :> caps) args with
            | Usage ->
                TinyLibSystem.eprint caps ("usage: " ^ n ^ " " ^ usage ^ "\n");
                1
            | Failure m -> complain caps n m; 1
          end
        | None when name = "-h" || name = "--help" ->
            TinyLibSystem.print caps (help ()); 0
        | None -> TinyLibSystem.eprint caps (help ()); 1
      end in
  TinyLibSystem.flush caps;
  status

let () = TinyLibSystem.main "tiny-utils" main
tiny/TinyUtilities.mli
4155
(* The small programs of a system, cat, ls, wc and the others, in one
 * file and one executable.
 *
 * m-ix's utilities/ has a program per file,
 * each a faithful copy of Plan 9's, with its options and its quirks.
 * This file is what remains when compatibility is dropped: once most
 * options are gone, what the programs have in common is most of each
 * one, and it can be written once.
 *
 * {b One executable, many names.} tiny-utils wc f runs wc, and so does
 * a link named wc (BusyBox, Bruce Perens, 1995). A utility is a row of
 * a table: its name, its usage, and a function from its arguments to
 * its exit status.
 *
 * {b Most utilities are filters}: a function over the bytes of its
 * input, which arrive in pieces. cat prints each piece; wc counts, and
 * carries "inside a word" from a piece to the next; xd carries the
 * bytes of a line it has not finished; tee writes each piece to its
 * files too. Opening the files named, or reading the standard input
 * when none is, and reporting a file that cannot be opened, is done
 * once, by [each_input]. A piece is printed as soon as it is read, so
 * cat at the console, or in a pipe, does not wait for the end:
 *
 *     files named, or stdin     each_input            the utility
 *     f1 ----------------------> opened, read in -----> step on each
 *     f2 (cannot be opened) -->  pieces of 8 KB         piece, printed
 *                                "wc: f2: reason",      at once; the
 *                                the status is now 1    end of each file
 *
 * {b The others walk a file tree}, and they are one fold: [fold caps path f]
 * calls f with the path, whether it is a directory, its size, and a
 * function that folds its entries, in name order, when it is called.
 * When f calls it decides the order:
 *
 *     walk     prints the path, then calls it          pre-order
 *     du       calls it, sums its results with the     post-order
 *              path's own size, then prints the sum
 *     rm -r    calls it, then removes the path         post-order
 *     ls       does not call it: one level only
 *
 * {b The same file on two systems.} As TinyShell.ml, it names only
 * TinyLibSystem (TinyKernel/host/TinyLibSystem.mli) and the pure functions
 * of the standard library, so it is tiny-kernel's utils and the host's
 * tiny-utils.
 *
 * What is kept of the twins is their output, where it costs nothing:
 * wc's columns, xd's lines, du's kilobytes, cmp's messages, ls's
 * sorted names.
 *
 * What is dropped: most options (each utility keeps the one or two that
 * carry its idea), UTF-8 (wc counts bytes), floating point in seq, most
 * of ls -l (tiny-kernel has no owners, modes or times: it is a file's
 * kind, links and size), and
 * the wording of each program's errors: here they are all "tool: file:
 * reason". The plan, and what was found on the way:
 * docs/plans/done/plan_tiny_utilities.md.
 *
 * The originals are principia's utilities/, Plan 9's C (files/cat.c,
 * misc/wc.c, byte/xd.c, text/grep/...), known here through m-ix's
 * twins. ln has neither: Plan 9 has no second name for a file, and
 * tiny-kernel's tree has (ls -l counts them), so ln is ours, three
 * lines over TinyLibSystem.link. ps is ours too: Plan 9's reads a
 * directory a process in /proc, its status file; tiny-kernel gives one
 * file, /dev/ps, a line a process, which ps puts in columns.
 *)

type caps =
  < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr;
    Cap.kill; Cap.clock; Cap.exit; Cap.env >

(* [each_input caps tool files f]: f on each file named, as its name
 * and a descriptor open on it, or on "" and the standard input when no
 * file is named. A file that cannot be opened is reported, and the
 * result, the exit status, is then 1 *)
val each_input : caps -> string -> string list -> (string -> int -> unit) -> int

(* [fold caps path f]: f path is_directory size entries, where entries ()
 * folds each entry of a directory (none for a file), in name order *)
val fold :
  < Cap.open_in; Cap.readdir; .. > ->
  string -> (string -> bool -> int -> (unit -> 'a list) -> 'a) -> 'a

val main : Cap.all_caps -> int
