(* TinyKernel.ml's calls on the host, in a window of SDL's (see
 * ../TinyKernel/host/TinyCalls.mli): what tiny-office, tiny-emacs,
 * tiny-calc and tiny-tetris run on, as their kernel's calls on
 * tiny-machine.
 *
 * What a program writes where it draws (its descriptor 3) is done by
 * tiny-kernel's own drawing, TinyKernelGraphics.ml, in a screen of
 * TinyMemory's, and shown (TinyMachineSDL, the palette tiny-machine's)
 * when the program next waits. The window's mouse is the box of the
 * program's descriptor 4, its keys the bytes of its 0 (as tiny-machine's
 * window makes them: Alt a key's Escape, a key held typed again, the
 * wheel the arrows). An ENQ written to the console is answered in the
 * box, as tiny-windows answers it: the window's size. A file is the
 * host's, read whole when opened, written when closed; /dev/audio is the
 * window's sound, as tiny-kernel and tiny-machine make it: each open a
 * voice whose sounds TinyKernelAudio.ml makes into a ring, mixed, and
 * the ring played by the clock (to SDL's queue, TinyMachineSDL's
 * play) as tiny-machine's speaker plays its ring.
 *
 * A dial to the wire's other end, its port 70 (10.0.0.1, tiny-machine's
 * peer, TinyMachinePeer.ml), is answered here as tiny-machine answers
 * it: a request "GET address HTTP/1.0" a web page, as HTTP's response,
 * "img w h address" a picture in the machine's colours, both fetched by
 * tiny-machine-fetch (ix's own HTTP and TLS), or, with TINY_WWW=dir, a
 * copy kept in dir when the fetch fails (as tiny-machine -net dir); the
 * answer's messages read one at a time, as a link's are. *)

let width = 1024
let height = 768
let screen_at = 0xf00000
(* the connection to the drawing, as tiny-kernel makes it: the font at
 * 0x1000, the images' memory its 2 MB below the screen and what is
 * after it (TinyKernelDevices' font; a page of www's may have 1 MB of
 * pictures: old: only after the screen, 720 KB then, and Mars' article
 * ended www). The font is tiny-kernel's (plan9.font, Plan 9's), or
 * the file TINY_FONT names (TINY_FONT=tiny/TinyKernel/fonts/grey.font:
 * Ubuntu Mono with grey edges; tiny.font, the same a pixel set or not;
 * TINY_FONT=kernels/lib_machine/font1.bin: the bold and the large made
 * of its one face, as before tiny.font) *)
let conn = lazy (
  let font =
    match Sys.getenv_opt "TINY_FONT" with
    | Some file -> In_channel.with_open_bin file In_channel.input_all
    | None -> TinyFont.bits
  in
  Bytes.blit_string font 0 TinyMemory.mem 0x1000 (String.length font);
  TinyKernelGraphics.arena 0xd00000 0x200000;
  TinyKernelGraphics.free 0xfc0000 0x3f000;
  let screen =
    { TinyKernelGraphics.r = TinyKernelGraphics.rect 0 0 width height;
      at = screen_at; repl = false } in
  TinyKernelGraphics.connect screen
    (TinyKernelGraphics.font_mask 0x1000 (String.length font)
       (TinyKernelGraphics.alloc 16384)))

let display =
  lazy (TinyMachineSDL.create ~title:(Filename.basename Sys.argv.(0)))

(* The speaker, as tiny-kernel's (TinyKernel.ml's voices) and
 * tiny-machine's (its ring played, then silenced): a ring of 8,192
 * samples of TinyMemory's where the voices' sounds are added, each from
 * where it stopped or, when the speaker passed it, from where the
 * speaker is; played by the host's clock, 8,000 a second, a fifth of a
 * second ahead of it ([fed]: the samples given to SDL so far). A write
 * waits while its sounds would be more than a ring ahead. *)
let ring_at = 0xc00000
let ring = 8192
let fed = ref 0
let since = ref 0.

let feed () =
  if !since > 0. then begin
    let due =
      int_of_float ((Unix.gettimeofday () -. !since) *. 8000.) + 1600 in
    if due > !fed then begin
      let n = min (due - !fed) ring in
      let b = Bytes.create n in
      for i = 0 to n - 1 do
        let a = ring_at + ((!fed + i) land (ring - 1)) in
        Bytes.set b i (Bytes.get TinyMemory.mem a);
        Bytes.set TinyMemory.mem a '\000'
      done;
      fed := due;
      (Lazy.force display).play (Bytes.unsafe_to_string b)
    end
  end

let speak (ahead : int ref) s =
  match TinyKernelAudio.sounds s with
  | sounds ->
      let total =
        List.fold_left
          (fun n snd -> n + TinyKernelAudio.sound_length snd) 0 sounds in
      let rec room () =
        feed ();
        if !ahead < !fed then ahead := !fed;
        if total > ring - (!ahead - !fed) then (Unix.sleepf 0.01; room ()) in
      if total <= ring then begin
        room ();
        List.iter
          (fun snd ->
            TinyKernelAudio.mix_sound ring_at ring !ahead snd;
            ahead := !ahead + TinyKernelAudio.sound_length snd)
          sounds
      end
  | exception TinyKernelAudio.Bad_sound -> ()

(* TINY_SCREEN=file: the screen written there as a PPM when the program
 * ends, a TERM signal ending it (for a look without a window:
 * SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy), as tiny-machine -screen *)
let () =
  match Sys.getenv_opt "TINY_SCREEN" with
  | Some file ->
      Sys.set_signal Sys.sigterm (Sys.Signal_handle (fun _ -> exit 0));
      at_exit (fun () ->
        Out_channel.with_open_bin file (fun oc ->
          output_string oc (TinyMemory.ppm width height)))
  | None -> ()
let dirty = ref false
let drawn = Buffer.create 0

(* the screen shown, if it was drawn on since *)
let show () =
  if !dirty then begin
    dirty := false;
    let rgb = Bytes.create (3 * width * height) in
    for i = 0 to (width * height) - 1 do
      Bytes.blit_string TinyMachineDevices.colours
        (3 * Char.code (Bytes.get TinyMemory.mem (screen_at + i)))
        rgb (3 * i) 3
    done;
    (Lazy.force display).present width height (Bytes.unsafe_to_string rgb)
  end

(* the clock, 400 ticks a second *)
let start = Unix.gettimeofday ()
let u_ticks () = int_of_float ((Unix.gettimeofday () -. start) *. 400.)
(* (946684800: 2000-01-01 in Unix's seconds) *)
let u_time () = int_of_float (Unix.time ()) - 946684800
let u_seed () = u_ticks ()
(* the host's file as tiny-kernel's entry (user.h's dirent) *)
let u_stat (path : string) : string =
  match Unix.stat path with
  | st ->
      let word n =
        String.init 4 (fun k -> Char.chr ((n lsr (8 * k)) land 255)) in
      let name = Filename.basename path in
      let name =
        if String.length name > 64 then String.sub name 0 64 else name in
      name ^ String.make (64 - String.length name) '\000'
      ^ word (if st.st_kind = Unix.S_DIR then 1 else 2)
      ^ word st.st_nlink ^ word st.st_size
      ^ word (int_of_float st.st_mtime - 946684800)
  | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> ""

(* the keys typed and not read; the mouse, and whether it moved since it
 * was read; an ENQ to answer *)
let typed = ref ""
let mouse = ref (0, 0, 0)
let fresh = ref false
let enq = ref false
let keys = TinyMachineSDL.keyboard ()

(* the window's events, made keys and the mouse *)
let pump () =
  if Lazy.is_val display then begin
    let key byte = typed := !typed ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr byte) in
    let now = Unix.gettimeofday () in
    List.iter (function
      | TinyMachineSDL.Quit -> exit 0
      | TinyMachineSDL.At (x, y) ->
          let (_, _, b) = !mouse in
          mouse := (x, y, b);
          fresh := true
      | TinyMachineSDL.Button (b, down) ->
          let (x, y, bs) = !mouse in
          mouse := (x, y, if down then bs lor b else bs land lnot b);
          fresh := true
      | e -> List.iter key (TinyMachineSDL.typed keys now e))
      ((Lazy.force display).poll ());
    Option.iter key (TinyMachineSDL.repeated keys now)
  end

(* the files open: their descriptor, what is left to read of one, what
 * is written to one *)
type file =
  | Reading of string ref
  | Writing of string * Buffer.t
  | Asking of Buffer.t
  | Answer of string list ref
  | Speaker of int ref
let files = Hashtbl.create 8
let next = ref 5

let ready fd =
  (fd = 0 && !typed <> "") || (fd = 4 && (!fresh || !enq))
  || (match Hashtbl.find_opt files fd with
      | Some (Asking _) | None -> false
      | Some _ -> true)

(* tiny-machine-fetch's output for its arguments, or why not; beside
 * this program, as tiny-machine finds it *)
let fetch args =
  let dir = Filename.dirname Sys.executable_name in
  let helper =
    if Filename.check_suffix Sys.executable_name ".exe" then
      Filename.concat dir "../TinyMachine/TinyMachineFetch.exe"
    else Filename.concat dir "tiny-machine-fetch" in
  let ic = Unix.open_process_args_in helper (Array.of_list (helper :: args)) in
  let out = In_channel.input_all ic in
  match Unix.close_process_in ic with Unix.WEXITED 0 -> Ok out | _ -> Error out

(* a copy kept in TINY_WWW's directory, by its name *)
let kept name = match Sys.getenv_opt "TINY_WWW", name with
  | Some dir, Some n when Sys.file_exists (Filename.concat dir n) ->
      Some (Filename.concat dir n)
  | _ -> None

(* the answer to a line asked of port 70, its messages *)
let answer line =
  match String.split_on_char ' ' (String.trim line) with
  | "GET" :: _ when TinyMachinePeer.www_request line <> None ->
      let url = Option.get (TinyMachinePeer.www_request line) in
      TinyMachinePeer.messages (match fetch [ url ] with
        | Ok answer -> answer
        | Error why -> (
            match kept (TinyMachinePeer.www_kept url) with
            | Some f ->
                TinyMachinePeer.www_kept_response f
                  (In_channel.with_open_bin f In_channel.input_all)
            | None -> TinyMachinePeer.www_failed why))
  | "img" :: _ ->
      let w, h, url =
        Option.get (TinyMachinePeer.www_picture_request (String.trim line)) in
      let decode source =
        match fetch [ "-picture"; string_of_int w; string_of_int h; source ] with
        | Ok pixels when String.length pixels = w * h ->
            Some (TinyMachinePeer.picture "" w h pixels)
        | _ -> None in
      (match if w = 0 then None else decode url with
       | Some l -> l
       | None -> (
           match
             Option.bind (kept (TinyMachinePeer.www_picture_kept url)) decode
           with
           | Some l -> l
           | None -> TinyMachinePeer.picture "" 0 0 ""))
  | _ -> []

let rec u_ready (fds : int array) (n : int) (until : int) : int =
  show ();
  pump ();
  feed ();
  let rec first i =
    if i >= n then -1 else if ready fds.(i) then fds.(i) else first (i + 1) in
  match first 0 with
  | -1 when until > 0 && u_ticks () >= until -> -1
  | -1 -> Unix.sleepf 0.005; u_ready fds n until
  | fd -> fd

(* a word of the mouse's box: 4 bytes, the low first *)
let word v = String.init 4 (fun k -> Char.chr ((v asr (8 * k)) land 255))

let u_read (fd : int) (n : int) : string =
  if fd = 0 then begin
    ignore (u_ready [| 0 |] 1 0);
    let k = min n (String.length !typed) in
    let s = String.sub !typed 0 k in
    typed := String.sub !typed k (String.length !typed - k);
    s
  end
  else if fd = 4 then begin
    if !enq then (enq := false; word width ^ word height ^ word (-1))
    else (let (x, y, b) = !mouse in fresh := false; word x ^ word y ^ word b)
  end
  else
    match Hashtbl.find_opt files fd with
    | Some (Reading left) ->
        let k = min n (String.length !left) in
        let s = String.sub !left 0 k in
        left := String.sub !left k (String.length !left - k);
        s
    | Some (Answer ({ contents = m :: rest } as left)) ->
        if String.length m <= n then (left := rest; m)
        else (
          left := String.sub m n (String.length m - n) :: rest;
          String.sub m 0 n)
    | _ -> ""

(* the drawing's messages; one refused is said, and the write is -1, as
 * tiny-kernel's write of /dev/draw does (old: the program ended) *)
let draw s =
  match TinyKernelGraphics.messages (Lazy.force conn) s with
  | () -> dirty := true; 0
  | exception TinyKernelGraphics.Graphics why ->
      prerr_string ("draw: " ^ why ^ "\n"); dirty := true; -1

let u_write (fd : int) (s : string) : int =
  if fd = 3 then draw s
  else begin
    if fd = 1 && s = "\005" then enq := true
    else if fd = 1 then (print_string s; flush stdout)
    else if fd = 2 then (prerr_string s; flush stderr)
    else (match Hashtbl.find_opt files fd with
          | Some (Writing (_, b)) -> Buffer.add_string b s
          | Some (Speaker ahead) -> speak ahead s
          | Some (Asking b) ->
              Buffer.add_string b s;
              let asked = Buffer.contents b in
              (match String.index_opt asked '\n' with
               | Some i ->
                   Hashtbl.replace files fd
                     (Answer (ref (answer (String.sub asked 0 i))))
               | None -> ())
          | _ -> ());
    0
  end

let u_open (name : string) (flags : int) : int =
  let fd = !next in
  if name = "/dev/audio" then begin
    (* the speaker started at the first open; what was written is heard
     * to its end, as tiny-kernel's speaker plays on after a program
     * ends *)
    if !since = 0. then begin
      since := Unix.gettimeofday ();
      at_exit (fun () ->
        let last =
          Hashtbl.fold
            (fun _ f m -> match f with Speaker a -> max m !a | _ -> m)
            files 0 in
        while !fed < last + 1600 do feed (); Unix.sleepf 0.02 done;
        while (Lazy.force display).queued () > 0 do Unix.sleepf 0.02 done)
    end;
    Hashtbl.replace files fd (Speaker (ref 0)); incr next; fd
  end
  else if flags land 1 <> 0 then (
    Hashtbl.replace files fd (Writing (name, Buffer.create 4096));
    incr next;
    fd)
  else if Sys.file_exists name && not (Sys.is_directory name) then (
    Hashtbl.replace files fd
      (Reading (ref (In_channel.with_open_bin name In_channel.input_all)));
    incr next;
    fd)
  else -1

let u_close (fd : int) : int =
  (match Hashtbl.find_opt files fd with
   | Some (Writing (name, b)) ->
       Out_channel.with_open_bin name (fun oc -> Buffer.output_buffer oc b)
   | _ -> ());
  Hashtbl.remove files fd;
  0

let u_rawcons (_ : int) = 0
let u_dial (address : string) (port : int) =
  if address = "10.0.0.1" && port = 70 then (
    let fd = !next in
    Hashtbl.replace files fd (Asking (Buffer.create 64));
    incr next;
    fd)
  else -1
(* /bin/play is tiny-play, else m-ix's mini-play (/bin/page: mini-page,
 * there is no tiny-page): in the bin/ this program was run from, beside
 * its executable (dune's _build, where tiny-play is play.exe), or on the
 * PATH *)
let u_spawn (path : string) (args : string list) : int =
  let name = Filename.basename path
  and exe = Sys.executable_name and argv0 = Sys.argv.(0) in
  let dirs =
    (if String.contains argv0 '/' then [ Filename.dirname argv0 ] else [])
    @ [ Filename.dirname exe ]
    @ String.split_on_char ':'
        (Option.value (Sys.getenv_opt "PATH") ~default:"") in
  let names = [ "tiny-" ^ name; "mini-" ^ name ] in
  let found =
    List.find_opt Sys.file_exists
      (Filename.concat (Filename.dirname exe) (name ^ ".exe")
       :: List.concat_map
            (fun d -> List.map (Filename.concat d) names)
            (List.filter (( <> ) "") dirs)) in
  match found with
  | None -> -1
  | Some prog -> (
      let args = match args with _ :: rest -> rest | [] -> [] in
      try
        Unix.create_process prog (Array.of_list (prog :: args))
          Unix.stdin Unix.stdout Unix.stderr
      with Unix.Unix_error _ -> -1)
let u_argc () = Array.length Sys.argv
let u_arg (i : int) = Sys.argv.(i)

(* Claude Code

(* mini-man: a page of the manual found and shown, as Plan 9's man(1)
 * (an rc script round nroff there; round mini-troff's modules here).
 *
 *   mini-man tr         every page named tr, of any section
 *   mini-man 2 open     the one of section 2
 *   mini-man 1          section 1 listed, its pages by groups
 *   mini-man            every section listed so
 *
 * A page is a file, dir/section/name (/sys/man/1/tr): the manual is a
 * tree, and finding a page is looking in eight directories. The tree
 * is /sys/man, Plan 9's place, or /lib/man where there is none (ix's
 * card: /sys is the kernel's there); -m dir: the manual is there
 * (principia's ROOT/docs/man; ix's own pages are docs/man, written in
 * the new format, which a page says by its first line). -T pdf: the page as a PDF file, on the standard output
 * (one page then). -v: what was not understood in the page is said,
 * on the standard error (mini-troff always says it).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * man was a shell script from the start: the pages were files, the
 * formatter a program, and the command the few lines that put the two
 * together. The sections' numbers are the first edition's (1971): 1
 * the commands, 2 the system calls, 3 the library, 4 the devices, 5
 * the file formats, 6 the games, 7 the rest, 8 for who maintains the
 * system. Plan 9 kept the order and changed what is in some (3 the
 * devices, 4 the file servers, 5 the protocol, 6 the formats).
 *
 * A section is listed by groups, a page in the new format saying its
 * own as the third part of its first line, \title{grep}{1}{text}:
 *
 *   files
 *     cat     one file after another, on the standard output
 *     ...
 *   text
 *     grep    the lines that match a pattern
 *
 * Section 1 is the /bin of the manual, a hundred commands in one
 * directory; the groups are what /progs's directories are on ix's
 * card, for the eye. A page that says none (Plan 9's, by man(6)'s
 * macros) is in "other", at the end.
 *
 * others:
 * Unix's man -k (apropos, 3BSD) looks for a word in a database of the
 * NAME lines (whatis, made by makewhatis); Plan 9's lookman, in an
 * index of the words. BSD's pages say a section's title in the
 * header's middle ("General Commands Manual"), as ix's say their
 * group. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in ; Cap.readdir ; Cap.stdout ; Cap.stderr >

let usage = "usage: mini-man [-v] [-m dir] [-T pdf] [section] [title ...]\n"

exception Usage

let sections = [ "1"; "2"; "3"; "4"; "5"; "6"; "7"; "8" ]

(* the groups, in the order listed; then those not here, by name; then
 * "other" *)
let groups = [ "shell"; "files"; "text"; "calc"; "time"; "processes"; "system"; "devtools"; "languages"; "typesetting"; "apps"; "browsers"; "network"; "emulators"; "games" ]

(* A page's group and what its NAME says it is: \title's third part,
 * and the words after the dash of the line under NAME (# NAME in the
 * new format, .SH NAME by man(6)'s macros) *)
let summary (source : string) : string * string =
  let lines = String.split_on_char '\n' source in
  let group =
    match lines with
    | first :: _ when String.length first > 7 && String.sub first 0 7 = "\\title{" ->
        (match String.split_on_char '{' first with
         | [ _; _; _; g ] -> (match String.index_opt g '}' with Some i when i > 0 -> String.sub g 0 i | _ -> "other")
         | _ -> "other")
    | _ -> "other" in
  let rec after_name (l : string list) : string =
    match l with
    | ("# NAME" | ".SH NAME") :: rest ->
        (* (its paragraph: to a blank line, a heading or a request) *)
        let rec skip (l : string list) = match l with x :: more when String.trim x = "" -> skip more | l -> l in
        let rec para (l : string list) : string list =
          match l with
          | x :: more when String.trim x <> "" && x.[0] <> '#' && x.[0] <> '.' -> String.trim x :: para more
          | _ -> [] in
        String.concat " " (para (skip rest))
    | _ :: rest -> after_name rest
    | [] -> "" in
  let line = after_name lines in
  (* (after the dash: the new format's, or man(6)'s \-) *)
  let what =
    let cut (sep : string) (s : string) : string option =
      let n = String.length sep and m = String.length s in
      let rec go (i : int) : string option = if i + n > m then None else if String.sub s i n = sep then Some (String.trim (String.sub s (i + n) (m - i - n))) else go (i + 1) in
      go 0 in
    match cut "\xe2\x80\x93" line with Some w -> w | None -> (match cut "\\-" line with Some w -> w | None -> String.trim line) in
  (group, what)

(* [index caps dirs section]: the section's pages by groups, as text;
 * "" if it has none *)
let index (caps : < Cap.open_in ; Cap.readdir ; .. >) (dirs : string list) (section : string) : string =
  (* each name once, from the first tree that has it *)
  let pages = ref [] in
  List.iter (fun dir ->
    let entries = try Sys_plan9.dirread caps (dir ^ "/" ^ section) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> [] in
    List.iter (fun (e : Sys_plan9.dir) ->
      let name = if Filename.check_suffix e.name ".md" then Filename.chop_suffix e.name ".md" else e.name in
      (* (not a page: Plan 9's INDEX, lookman's) *)
      if not (List.mem_assoc name !pages) && name <> "INDEX" && name <> "" && name.[0] <> '.' then
        match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v (dir ^ "/" ^ section ^ "/" ^ e.name)) with
        | Some source -> pages := (name, summary source) :: !pages
        | None -> ()) entries) dirs;
  if !pages = [] then ""
  else begin
    let pages = List.sort compare !pages in
    let width = List.fold_left (fun w ((name, _) : string * (string * string)) -> max w (String.length name)) 0 pages in
    let named = List.sort_uniq compare (List.map (fun ((_, (g, _)) : string * (string * string)) -> g) pages) in
    let order = List.filter (fun g -> List.mem g named) groups @ List.filter (fun g -> not (List.mem g groups) && g <> "other") named @ (if List.mem "other" named then [ "other" ] else []) in
    let b = Buffer.create 4096 in
    Buffer.add_string b ("Section " ^ section ^ "\n");
    List.iter (fun g ->
      Buffer.add_string b ("\n  " ^ g ^ "\n");
      List.iter (fun ((name, (pg, what)) : string * (string * string)) ->
        if pg = g then Buffer.add_string b (Printf.sprintf "    %-*s  %s\n" width name what)) pages) order;
    Buffer.contents b
  end

let main (caps : < caps ; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  try
    let dirs = ref [ "/sys/man"; "/lib/man" ] and verbose = ref false and way = ref CLI.Text in
    let rec options (l : string list) : string list =
      match l with
      | "-m" :: d :: rest -> dirs := [ d ]; options rest
      | "-v" :: rest -> verbose := true; options rest
      | "-T" :: "pdf" :: rest -> way := CLI.Pdf; options rest
      | "-T" :: "text" :: rest -> way := CLI.Text; options rest
      | a :: _ when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' -> raise Usage
      | rest -> rest in
    let args = options (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) in
    let wanted, titles = match args with s :: rest when List.mem s sections -> ([ s ], rest) | _ -> (sections, args) in
    let missing = ref false in
    (* no title: the sections listed *)
    if titles = [] then begin
      let lists = List.filter (fun s -> s <> "") (List.map (index caps !dirs) wanted) in
      if lists = [] then begin
        Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "mini-man: no pages%s in %s\n" (match wanted with [ s ] -> " of section " ^ s | _ -> "") (String.concat " or " !dirs));
        missing := true
      end
      else Console.print caps (String.concat "\n" lists)
    end;
    List.iter (fun title ->
      let found = ref false in
      List.iter (fun section ->
        (* (the first tree that has it; a page in the new format may
         * keep its .md) *)
        let name = String.lowercase_ascii title in
        let files = List.concat_map (fun dir -> [ Printf.sprintf "%s/%s/%s" dir section name; Printf.sprintf "%s/%s/%s.md" dir section name ]) !dirs in
        match List.find_map (fun file -> match FS.read_opt caps (Fpath.v file) with Some source -> Some (file, source) | None -> None) files with
        | None -> ()
        | Some (file, source) ->
            found := true;
            let page, complaints = CLI.typeset !way None (fun _ -> None) file source in
            Console.print caps page;
            if !verbose then List.iter (fun c -> Console.eprint caps (c ^ "\n")) complaints) wanted;
      if not !found then begin Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "mini-man: no page for %s in %s\n" title (String.concat " or " !dirs)); missing := true end) titles;
    if !missing then Exit.Err "no page" else Exit.OK
  with Usage -> Console.eprint caps usage; Exit.Err "usage"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See CLI.mli *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in ; Cap.stdin ; Cap.stdout ; Cap.stderr >

let usage =
  "usage: mini-troff [-man|-ms|-md|-latex] [-T text|pdf|md] [file ...]\n\
  \  -man     the files are manual pages, man(6)'s macros\n\
  \  -ms      papers, ms(6)'s\n\
  \  -md      documents in Markdown's lines and \\name[options]{text}\n\
  \  -latex   simple LaTeX, and noweb's chunks of code in it\n\
  \           (with none: a file named .md or .ixd, or that starts\n\
  \           with a \\title, is in Markdown's lines, one named .tex\n\
  \           or .nw in LaTeX, a file with a .TH is a manual page,\n\
  \           another a paper)\n\
  \  -T text  written for a terminal (what is done with no -T)\n\
  \  -T pdf   a PDF file, on the standard output: one file read\n\
  \  -T md    the document written again, in Markdown's lines\n\
  \  -T words the PDF file's words, as text (what a typesetter is given,\n\
  \           which is not always what a terminal is)\n\
   no file: the standard input. What is not understood is said on the\n\
   standard error, with its line.\n"

exception Usage

type way = Text | Pdf | Words | Source

type package = Man | Ms | Md | Tex

(* what a file is written in, when it is not said: a manual page has a
 * .TH *)
let package_of (name : string) (source : string) : package =
  let ends (e : string) : bool = let n = String.length name and m = String.length e in n >= m && String.sub name (n - m) m = e in
  if ends ".md" || ends ".ixd" then Md else
  if ends ".tex" || ends ".nw" then Tex else
  (* (a page of the manual has no such name: its first line says) *)
  if String.starts_with ~prefix:"\\title{" (String.trim source) then Md else
  let rec go (lines : string list) = match lines with [] -> Ms | l :: rest -> if String.starts_with ~prefix:".TH" l then Man else go rest in
  go (String.split_on_char '\n' source)

let typeset (way : way) (package : package option) (load : string -> string option) (name : string) (source : string) : string * string list =
  let paper = way <> Text in
  let roff = Roff.create (if paper then Roff.Typesetter else Roff.Terminal) source in
  if paper then Roff.set_measure roff To_pdf.measure;
  Roff.set_loader roff load;
  let doc, complaints =
    match (match package with Some p -> p | None -> package_of name source) with
    | Man -> let d = Man.read roff in (d, Roff.complaints roff)
    | Ms -> let d = Ms.read roff in (d, Roff.complaints roff)
    | Md -> Ixdoc.read paper load source
    | Tex -> Latex.read paper load source in
  let said = List.map (fun (line, what) -> Printf.sprintf "%s:%d: %s: not known" name line what) complaints in
  match way with
  | Text -> (To_text.page doc, said)
  | Source -> (To_ixdoc.print paper doc, said)
  (* (with the characters the file has for others: a dash for a minus) *)
  | Words -> (To_text.page (Doc.map_text (fun (style : Doc.style) s -> To_pdf.shown style.font s) doc), said)
  | Pdf ->
      let bytes, missing, over = To_pdf.file doc in
      (bytes,
       said @ List.map (fun c -> Printf.sprintf "%s: the character %s: not in the fonts" name c) missing
       @ (if over > 0 then [ Printf.sprintf "%s: %d lines go past the paper's right edge" name over ] else []))

(* all of a descriptor *)
let contents (fd : Unix.file_descr) : string =
  let all = Buffer.create 8192 and buf = Bytes.create 8192 in
  let rec go () = match Unix.read fd buf 0 8192 with 0 -> () | n -> Buffer.add_subbytes all buf 0 n; go () | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> () in
  go (); Buffer.contents all

let main (caps : < caps ; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  try
    let way = ref Text and package = ref None in
    let rec options (l : string list) : string list =
      match l with
      | "-man" :: rest -> package := Some Man; options rest
      | "-ms" :: rest -> package := Some Ms; options rest
      | "-md" :: rest -> package := Some Md; options rest
      | "-latex" :: rest -> package := Some Tex; options rest
      | "-T" :: "md" :: rest -> way := Source; options rest
      | "-T" :: "text" :: rest | "-Ttext" :: rest -> way := Text; options rest
      | "-T" :: "pdf" :: rest | "-Tpdf" :: rest -> way := Pdf; options rest
      | "-T" :: "words" :: rest -> way := Words; options rest
      | "--" :: rest -> rest
      | a :: _ when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' -> raise Usage
      | rest -> rest in
    let files = options (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) in
    (* (a PDF file is one document) *)
    if !way = Pdf && List.length files > 1 then raise Usage;
    let failed = ref false in
    let one (name : string) (source : string) =
      (* (a file that the document names: .so, a picture's, \input's;
       * as it is named, or from where the document is, as LaTeX's are) *)
      let read (file : string) : string option = match FS.path file with Ok p -> FS.read_opt caps p | Error _ -> None in
      let load (file : string) : string option =
        match read file with
        | Some s -> Some s
        | None -> if Filename.is_relative file && Filename.dirname name <> "." then read (Filename.concat (Filename.dirname name) file) else None in
      let page, complaints = typeset !way !package load name source in
      Console.print caps page;
      List.iter (fun c -> Console.eprint caps (c ^ "\n")) complaints in
    if files = [] then one "<stdin>" (contents (Console.stdin_fd caps))
    else
      List.iter (fun file ->
        match FS.open_in_fd caps file with
        | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "mini-troff: %s: %s\n" file (Unix.error_message e)); failed := true
        | fd -> one file (Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close fd) (fun () -> contents fd))) files;
    if !failed then Exit.Err "can't open" else Exit.OK
  with Usage -> Console.eprint caps usage; Exit.Err "usage"
typesetting/troff/CLI.mli

(* mini-troff: a document typeset -- a manual page, a paper or a book,
 * for a terminal or as a PDF file.
 *
 *   mini-troff tr.1                  the page as text, on the standard output
 *   mini-troff < tr.1
 *   mini-troff -T pdf tr.1 > tr.pdf  its pages, to print or for mini-page
 *   mini-troff -ms names.ms          a paper (ms(6)'s macros)
 *   mini-troff manual.md             a document in Markdown's lines
 *   mini-troff -T md tr.1 > tr.md    a manual page written in them
 *   mini-troff -T pdf Make.nw > Make.pdf   a book: simple LaTeX and
 *                                    noweb's chunks of code
 *
 * It has troff's name and reads what was written for troff, but it is
 * not troff: the macros of a package (Man, Ms) are what it
 * knows, not the requests they were made of, and what it does not
 * know it says, with the line, on the standard error; nothing is
 * left out in silence. The whole way of a page:
 *
 *   the file --Roff--> lines --Man, Ms (on Fill; Tbl, Pic)--+
 *   the file --Ixdoc (Markdown's lines)---------------------+--> Doc.t
 *   the file --Latex (and Bib: its references)--------------+
 *
 *   Doc.t --Layout--> lines of words, each at its place
 *              --To_text--> the terminal's page
 *              --To_pdf---> the file's pages
 *   Doc.t --Ixdoc--> the document in Markdown's lines
 *
 * To come (docs/plans/done/plan_typesetting.md): the papers'
 * equations.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * troff is Joe Ossanna's (Bell Labs, 1973), for the Graphic Systems
 * C/A/T, a phototypesetter that flashed letters through a spinning
 * disc of film: four fonts mounted at a time, which is why \f takes a
 * digit from 1 to 4. After his death in 1977 Brian Kernighan rewrote
 * it not to know its typesetter (ditroff, 1979), and wrote with
 * others the programs that go before it in a pipe: eqn (with Lorinda
 * Cherry, 1974), tbl (Mike Lesk, 1975), pic (1981). Plan 9's troff
 * is that program, with Unicode; it is the oldest code in the system,
 * and reads like it.
 *
 * others:
 * TeX (Donald Knuth, 1978 and 1982) breaks a paragraph as a whole and
 * sets mathematics as no program had; LaTeX (Leslie Lamport, 1984)
 * is to it what -ms is to troff. groff (James Clark, 1990) is troff
 * again, in C++, and what a Linux has. Typst (2023) is a new language
 * with the same aim. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in ; Cap.stdin ; Cap.stdout ; Cap.stderr >

(* Words: the page read as for the PDF file (a page may say one thing
 * to a typesetter and another to a terminal, .if t and .if n) and
 * written as text: what the file's words are, for a test to compare
 * with what a reader of the file finds in it *)
(* Source: the document written in the new format (Ixdoc), read as
 * for the PDF file *)
type way = Text | Pdf | Words | Source

(* [typeset way name source]: a page's text for a terminal, or a PDF
 * file's bytes, and what was not understood in it, each "name:line:
 * what" *)
type package = Man | Ms | Md | Tex

(* (no package said: the new format if the file's name ends with .md
 * or .ixd, or if its first line is a \title; LaTeX if the name ends
 * with .tex or .nw; else a manual page if the file has a .TH, else a
 * paper) *)
(* [typeset way package load name source]; [load] reads a file the
 * document names (.so, a picture kept apart, \input), none if it may
 * not *)
val typeset : way -> package option -> (string -> string option) -> string -> string -> string * string list

val main : < caps ; .. > -> string array -> Exit.t

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Doc.mli *)

type font = Roman | Italic | Bold | Mono
type style = { font : font; size : int; shift : int }
type inline = Text of style * string | Break | Page of style * string * string
type par = { fill : bool; first : float; short : float; tabs : float list; center : bool; body : inline list }

type align = Left | Right | Center | Numeric
type cell = { align : align; span : int; filled : bool; body : inline list }
type table_row = Cells of cell list | Rule
type table = { centered : bool; boxed : bool; widths : float list; rows : table_row list }

type mark = Stroke of (float * float) list | Label of float * float * int * inline list | Image of float * float * float * float * string * Rgba_image.t
type picture = { wide : float; high : float; marks : mark list }

type block =
  | Heading of int * inline list
  | Para of par
  | Tagged of tagged
  | Indent of float * block list
  | Space of float
  | Footnote of block list
  | Keep of block list
  | Table of table
  | Picture of picture
  | Anchor of string * bool

and tagged = { tag : inline list; width : float; body : block list }

type t = { header : string * string * string; width : float; margin : float; sub : float; body : block list }

let plain : style = { font = Roman; size = 0; shift = 0 }

let letters (s : string) : string =
  if not (String.contains s '\xc2' || String.contains s '\xe2') then s
  else String.concat "" (List.filter (fun c -> c <> "\xc2\xad" && c <> "\xe2\x81\xa0" && c <> "\xe2\x80\x8b") (fst (Utf8.chars s)))

(* a text's letters, without its looks *)
let words (l : inline list) : string =
  String.concat "" (List.map (fun (i : inline) -> match i with Text (_, s) | Page (_, _, s) -> letters s | Break -> " ") l)

let map_inline (f : inline -> inline) (d : t) : t =
  let inline = f in
  let rec block (b : block) : block =
    match b with
    | Heading (level, text) -> Heading (level, List.map inline text)
    | Para p -> Para { p with body = List.map inline p.body }
    | Tagged { tag; width; body } -> Tagged { tag = List.map inline tag; width; body = List.map block body }
    | Indent (by, inner) -> Indent (by, List.map block inner)
    | Space _ | Anchor _ -> b
    | Footnote inner -> Footnote (List.map block inner)
    | Keep inner -> Keep (List.map block inner)
    | Table t ->
        Table { t with rows = List.map (fun (r : table_row) -> match r with Rule -> Rule | Cells cs -> Cells (List.map (fun (c : cell) -> { c with body = List.map inline c.body }) cs)) t.rows }
    | Picture p -> Picture { p with marks = List.map (fun (m : mark) -> match m with Stroke _ | Image _ -> m | Label (x, y, side, text) -> Label (x, y, side, List.map inline text)) p.marks } in
  { d with body = List.map block d.body }

let map_text (f : style -> string -> string) (d : t) : t =
  map_inline (fun (i : inline) -> match i with Text (style, s) -> Text (style, f style s) | Page (style, name, s) -> Page (style, name, f style s) | Break -> Break) d

let pages (page : string -> string option) (d : t) : t =
  map_inline (fun (i : inline) -> match i with Page (style, name, s) -> Text (style, (match page name with Some p -> p | None -> s)) | _ -> i) d

(* A document, whatever it was written in: what every reader makes
 * (Man, Ms, Ixdoc, Latex) and every writer takes (To_text, To_pdf, and
 * Ixdoc again).
 *
 *   man pages --Man----+                          +--To_text--> a terminal
 *   papers ----Ms------+--> Doc.t --Layout--> lines
 *   Markdown --Ixdoc---+      |                   +--To_pdf---> a PDF file
 *   books -----Latex---+      +--Ixdoc--> Markdown
 *
 * It is a tree. A paragraph is its text in fonts; what is to its right
 * of the paragraphs around it is inside an [Indent]; a paragraph that
 * hangs from a word (an option and what it does) is a [Tagged]:
 *
 *   .PP                      Para "Any combination of the options..."
 *   Any combination ...      Space 1
 *   .TP                      Tagged { tag = "-c"; width = 5;
 *   .B -c                             body = [ Para "Complement..." ] }
 *   Complement ...
 *
 *        Any combination of the options -cds may be used:
 *
 *        -c   Complement string1: replace it with a
 *        |<5>|ordered list of all other characters.
 *
 * Nothing here is troff's: no request, no register. A blank line is a
 * [Space], said by the reader and not guessed by the layout, so that a
 * page whose author closed up a list (.PD 0) stays closed up.
 *
 * Widths and indents are in ens: the width of a letter of a terminal
 * (where an em, a letter's height, is taken to be the same). A
 * [Space] is in lines.
 *
 * (docs/plans/done/plan_typesetting.md; its other blocks, a table, a
 * figure, a footnote, come with the readers that need them) *)

(* Mono is the font of what is typed: Plan 9's manual sets a command's
 * name and its options in it, where Unix's had bold *)
type font = Roman | Italic | Bold | Mono

(* size: points more than the text around, or less; shift: half lines
 * up (an exponent) or down *)
type style = { font : font; size : int; shift : int }

type inline =
  (* a line may be broken at a space of it, and after a hyphen inside
   * a word. Unicode's own characters say the rest:
   *   U+00A0  a space where it may not be broken
   *   U+2011  a hyphen after which it may not
   *   U+2212  a minus (the same)
   *   U+00AD  where a word may be cut, a hyphen added if it is
   *   U+200B  where it may be broken with nothing added
   *   U+2060  nothing at all; after a dot, no sentence ends there
   * and a tab goes to the paragraph's next stop. *)
  | Text of style * string
  (* the line ends here: between the lines of a paragraph that is not
   * filled *)
  | Break
  (* the number of the sheet an [Anchor] of this name is on, written
   * when the sheets are made (To_pdf); where there are none, a
   * terminal's, or the name is on none, the text *)
  | Page of style * string * string

type par = {
  (* filled: the words put on lines as they fit. Not filled: the lines
   * as they were written (a program's text, an example) *)
  fill : bool;
  (* how far right of the others the first line starts; less than 0:
   * to their left *)
  first : float;
  (* how much shorter than the others its lines are: a quotation, an
   * abstract, set in from both sides *)
  short : float;
  (* where a tab goes, from the paragraph's left *)
  tabs : float list;
  center : bool;
  body : inline list;
}

(* A table: rows of cells in columns as wide as their widest cell.
 *
 *     Variable   Default   Meaning
 *     CFLAGS      -FVw     C compiler flags
 *     LDFLAGS              Loader flags
 *
 * A cell is at its column's left, right or middle, or is a number
 * with its decimal point under the others'; it may go across several
 * columns (a title over the table); and it may be a text that is
 * filled in its column's width, on as many lines as it takes. *)
type align = Left | Right | Center | Numeric

type cell = {
  align : align;
  (* how many columns it goes across: 1 *)
  span : int;
  (* a text filled in the column's width *)
  filled : bool;
  body : inline list;
}

type table_row = Cells of cell list | Rule

type table = {
  centered : bool;
  (* a rule over it and under it *)
  boxed : bool;
  (* each column's width when the table says it (0 when not: its
   * widest cell's) *)
  widths : float list;
  rows : table_row list;
}

(* A picture: lines, words and pictures from files, placed in inches
 * from its lower left corner, up being up. *)
type mark =
  (* a line through points *)
  | Stroke of (float * float) list
  (* words on one line, their middle at a point (0), or their left
   * end (-1), or their right end (1) *)
  | Label of float * float * int * inline list
  (* a picture from a file: its lower left corner, how wide and how
   * high it is shown, the file's name, its pixels *)
  | Image of float * float * float * float * string * Rgba_image.t

type picture = { wide : float; high : float; marks : mark list }

type block =
  (* 1: a section's (NAME, SYNOPSIS), 2: a subsection's *)
  | Heading of int * inline list
  | Para of par
  (* the tag at the left, the body [width] to its right, starting on
   * the tag's line when the tag is shorter than that *)
  | Tagged of tagged
  | Indent of float * block list
  | Space of float
  (* said where its mark is in the text; written at the foot of the
   * sheet (at the document's end, on a terminal) *)
  | Footnote of block list
  (* what is not to be cut by the end of a sheet: a display, a figure *)
  | Keep of block list
  | Table of table
  | Picture of picture
  (* a place that a [Page] names: the sheet of the next line. Lettered:
   * a chunk of noweb's, whose number is the sheet's with a letter when
   * the sheet has several (12a, 12b) *)
  | Anchor of string * bool

and tagged = { tag : inline list; width : float; body : block list }

type t = {
  (* what is at the top of each page, at its left, in its middle and
   * at its right ("WC(1)", "", "WC(1)"); nothing if all are empty *)
  header : string * string * string;
  (* the lines' length: 65 letters for the manual on a terminal, 60 for
   * a paper; 6.5 inches and 6 on paper *)
  width : float;
  (* where the text is, from the left: a manual page's is to the right
   * of its headings, a section's at 0, a subsection's at [sub]; a
   * paper's is at 0 as its headings *)
  margin : float;
  sub : float;
  body : block list;
}

(* the text's own: Roman, its size, on the line *)
val plain : style

(* a text without the three characters that are not seen (U+00AD,
 * U+200B, U+2060): what is measured, and written *)
val letters : string -> string

(* a text's letters, without its looks: a line's end is a space *)
val words : inline list -> string

(* the same document, each text of it changed *)
val map_text : (style -> string -> string) -> t -> t
val map_inline : (inline -> inline) -> t -> t

(* each [Page] a text: the sheet its name is on, or its own text *)
val pages : (string -> string option) -> t -> t

(* See Doc_image.mli *)

let picture (name : string) (bytes : string) (wide : float) (per_inch : float) (most : float) : (Doc.block, string) result =
  let starts (w : string) : bool = String.length bytes >= String.length w && String.sub bytes 0 (String.length w) = w in
  (* (a drawing: lib_graphics's Svg draws no text, and ix's are boxes
   * with words in them) *)
  if starts "<svg" || starts "<?xml" then Error "an SVG file, not read as a picture"
  else
    match (try Ok (if starts "GIF8" then Gif.decode bytes else Image_file.decode bytes) with Failure why -> Error why | Invalid_argument why -> Error why | Not_found -> Error "a file cut short") with
    | Error why -> Error why
    | Ok img ->
        if img.width <= 0 || img.height <= 0 then Error "a picture of no pixel"
        else begin
          let own = float_of_int img.width /. per_inch in
          let w = Float.min most (if wide > 0. then wide else own) in
          (* (whole hundredths of an inch: the same by every compiler) *)
          let w = Float.max 0.01 (Float.round (w *. 100.) /. 100.) in
          let h = Float.max 0.01 (Float.round (w *. float_of_int img.height /. float_of_int img.width *. 100.) /. 100.) in
          let p : Doc.picture = { wide = w; high = h; marks = [ Doc.Image (0., 0., w, h, name, img) ] } in
          Ok (Doc.Picture p)
        end

(* Doc_image: a picture from a file, as a block of a document -- what
 * Markdown's ![words](file) and LaTeX's \includegraphics{file} are.
 *
 * The file is a PNG, a JPEG or a GIF, told by its first bytes
 * (Image_file); its pixels are read here, once, and the document has
 * them: a PDF file carries them, a terminal has the file's name in
 * their place. Not a drawing: an SVG file is said and not read
 * (lib_graphics's Svg draws no text, and a diagram is boxes with
 * words in them), nor a PDF file.
 *
 * How big it is shown is the reader's to say, a width in inches; with
 * none, a pixel is a point's part ([per_inch] pixels to the inch: 72
 * for LaTeX, as pdflatex takes a picture that says nothing; 96 for
 * Markdown, a screen's), and never wider than the line. Its height
 * follows. *)

(* [picture name bytes wide per_inch most]: the block, or why not (not
 * a picture's file, or one cut short). [wide]: the width asked, in
 * inches, 0 for the picture's own; [most]: the line's *)
val picture : string -> string -> float -> float -> float -> (Doc.block, string) result
typesetting/troff/doc/Layout.ml
14957
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Layout.mli *)

type piece = { x : float; style : Doc.style; text : string }
type row = Line of piece list | Skip of float | Foot of row list | Together of row list | Rule of float * float | Drawing of float * Doc.picture | Mark of string * bool
type look = { en : float; inch : float; width : float; tag_room : float; justify : bool }

(* a length of the document, in ens, as a whole number of the writer's
 * units. (Not when the unit is the en itself, a terminal's: half a
 * column is kept, and its writer takes the column on the left of each
 * place, as nroff does.) *)
let units (look : look) (ens : float) : float = if look.en = 1. then ens else Float.round (ens *. look.en)
type metrics = Doc.style -> string -> float

(* A paragraph's text cut where a line may be: a word (its letters,
 * maybe in several fonts), the spaces between two, a tab. *)
type atom =
  | Word of (Doc.style * string) list
  (* a word's start, up to a hyphen of its own after which the line
   * may end (non-empty; not the first letter's: -c) *)
  | Start of (Doc.style * string) list
  | Spaces of float
  | Tab
  | Newline
  (* where a line may end between two letters, with a hyphen to add if
   * it does (troff's \%, U+00AD in the text) *)
  | Soft_break

let atoms (metrics : metrics) (body : Doc.inline list) : atom list =
  let out = ref [] and word = ref [] in
  let flush () = if !word <> [] then begin out := Word (List.rev !word) :: !out; word := [] end in
  let add (a : atom) = flush (); out := (match (a, !out) with Spaces w, Spaces v :: rest -> Spaces (v +. w) :: rest | _ -> a :: !out) in
  List.iter (fun (i : Doc.inline) ->
    match i with
    | Doc.Break -> add Newline
    | Doc.Text (style, s) | Doc.Page (style, _, s) ->
        let n = String.length s in
        let rec go from i =
          let letters () = if i > from then word := (style, String.sub s from (i - from)) :: !word in
          if i >= n then letters ()
          else if s.[i] = ' ' then begin letters (); add (Spaces (metrics style " ")); go (i + 1) (i + 1) end
          else if s.[i] = '\t' then begin letters (); add Tab; go (i + 1) (i + 1) end
          else if s.[i] = '\xc2' && i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] = '\xad' then begin letters (); add Soft_break; go (i + 2) (i + 2) end
          (* (U+2060: nothing; U+200B: a word ends, with no space after) *)
          else if s.[i] = '\xe2' && i + 2 < n && s.[i + 1] = '\x81' && s.[i + 2] = '\xa0' then begin letters (); go (i + 3) (i + 3) end
          else if s.[i] = '\xe2' && i + 2 < n && s.[i + 1] = '\x80' && s.[i + 2] = '\x8b' then begin letters (); flush (); go (i + 3) (i + 3) end
          else if s.[i] = '-' && (i > from || !word <> []) && i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] <> ' ' && s.[i + 1] <> '\t' then begin
            word := (style, String.sub s from (i + 1 - from)) :: !word;
            out := Start (List.rev !word) :: !out; word := []; go (i + 1) (i + 1)
          end
          else go from (i + 1) in
        go 0 0) body;
  flush (); List.rev !out

(* the stop after x, both from the paragraph's left; past the last, a
 * tab is nothing *)
let next_stop (tabs : float list) (x : float) : float =
  match List.find_opt (fun t -> t > x +. 0.01) tabs with Some t -> t | None -> x

(* [paragraph look metrics left start before p]: the lines of p, the
 * first starting at [start] after the pieces [before] (a tag), the
 * others at [left] *)
let paragraph (look : look) (metrics : metrics) (left : float) (start : float) (before : piece list) (p : Doc.par) : piece list list =
  let lines = ref [] and line = ref (List.rev before) and x = ref start in
  (* how many spaces between words are to the left of each piece of
   * the line, the last first: what a line made even is stretched at *)
  let gaps = ref (List.map (fun _ -> 0) before) and gap = ref 0 in
  let tabs = List.map (units look) p.tabs in
  (* (this paragraph's line's end) *)
  let look = { look with width = look.width -. units look p.short } in
  (* where the line starts: its tabs' stops are from there *)
  let origin = ref start in
  (* the room between the last word and the next, not made yet: none
   * at the start of a line *)
  let space = ref 0. and has_word = ref false and soft = ref false in
  let finish (full : bool) =
    let l = List.rev !line in
    (* a line that ended because the next word did not fit, its right
     * edge put at the line's end: the room left shared between its
     * spaces *)
    let l = if look.justify && full && p.fill && not p.center && !gap > 0 && l <> [] then begin
        let last = List.nth l (List.length l - 1) in
        let each = (look.width -. (last.x +. metrics last.style last.text)) /. float_of_int !gap in
        (* (whole units, and a product that is rounded before it is
         * added: a compiler may do the two in one instruction, a
         * multiply-add with one rounding, and another in two; the same
         * file whatever compiled this) *)
        List.map2 (fun (pc : piece) (g : int) -> let more = Float.round (each *. float_of_int g) in { pc with x = pc.x +. more }) l (List.rev !gaps)
      end else l in
    (* (in the middle of what is between the paragraph's left and the
     * line's end) *)
    let l = if p.center && l <> [] then begin
        let first = List.hd l and last = List.nth l (List.length l - 1) in
        let by = left +. Float.floor ((look.width -. left -. (last.x +. metrics last.style last.text -. first.x)) /. 2.) -. first.x in
        List.map (fun (pc : piece) -> { pc with x = pc.x +. by }) l
      end else l in
    lines := l :: !lines; line := []; gaps := []; gap := 0; x := left; origin := left; space := 0.; has_word := false in
  let place (parts : (Doc.style * string) list) =
    List.iter (fun ((style : Doc.style), s) -> line := { x = !x; style; text = s } :: !line; gaps := !gap :: !gaps; x := !x +. metrics style s) parts;
    has_word := true in
  List.iter (fun (a : atom) ->
    match a with
    | Word parts | Start parts ->
        let w = List.fold_left (fun w ((style : Doc.style), s) -> w +. metrics style s) 0. parts in
        (* (troff asks for a hyphen's room after a word's start, though
         * its own hyphen is there) *)
        let room = match a with Start ((style, _) :: _) -> metrics style "-" | _ -> 0. in
        if p.fill && !has_word && !x +. !space +. w +. room > look.width +. 0.01 then begin
          (match (!soft, !line) with true, last :: _ -> line := { x = !x; style = last.style; text = "-" } :: !line; gaps := !gap :: !gaps | _ -> ());
          finish true
        end
        else begin if !has_word && !space > 0. then incr gap; x := !x +. !space end;
        space := 0.; soft := false;
        place parts
    (* (spaces before any word are the line's own: an example's indent) *)
    | Spaces w -> if !has_word && p.fill then space := !space +. w else x := !x +. w
    | Tab -> x := !origin +. next_stop tabs (!x +. !space -. !origin); space := 0.; has_word := true
    | Soft_break -> soft := true
    | Newline -> finish false) (atoms metrics p.body);
  if !line <> [] || !lines = [] || not p.fill then finish false;
  List.rev !lines

(* a text on one line, from x: a tag, a heading *)
let one_line (metrics : metrics) (x : float) (text : Doc.inline list) : piece list * float =
  let at = ref x and out = ref [] in
  List.iter (fun (i : Doc.inline) ->
    match i with
    (* (a tab in a tag has no stops to go to: a space) *)
    | Doc.Text (style, s) | Doc.Page (style, _, s) -> let s = String.map (fun c -> if c = '\t' then ' ' else c) (Doc.letters s) in out := { x = !at; style; text = s } :: !out; at := !at +. metrics style s
    | Doc.Break -> ()) text;
  (List.rev !out, !at)

(* a cell's text as one string, and its two parts if it is a number:
 * to its decimal point, and from it *)
let cell_text (c : Doc.cell) : string = String.concat "" (List.map (fun (i : Doc.inline) -> match i with Doc.Text (_, s) | Doc.Page (_, _, s) -> Doc.letters s | Doc.Break -> "") c.body)

let split_number (metrics : metrics) (c : Doc.cell) : float * float =
  let s = cell_text c in
  let style = match c.body with Doc.Text (st, _) :: _ -> st | _ -> Doc.plain in
  let at = match String.rindex_opt s '.' with Some i when i + 1 < String.length s && s.[i + 1] >= '0' && s.[i + 1] <= '9' -> i | _ -> String.length s in
  (metrics style (String.sub s 0 at), metrics style (String.sub s at (String.length s - at)))

(* A table: each column as wide as its widest cell (or as the table
 * says), three ens between two. *)
let table (look : look) (metrics : metrics) (left : float) (t : Doc.table) : row list =
  let gap = units look 3. in
  let count = List.fold_left (fun n (r : Doc.table_row) -> match r with Doc.Rule -> n | Doc.Cells cs -> max n (List.fold_left (fun k (c : Doc.cell) -> k + c.span) 0 cs)) 0 t.rows in
  let widths = Array.make (max 1 count) 0. and lefts = Array.make (max 1 count) 0. and rights = Array.make (max 1 count) 0. in
  let said = Array.make (max 1 count) false and wants = Array.make (max 1 count) false in
  List.iteri (fun k w -> if k < count && w > 0. then begin widths.(k) <- units look w; said.(k) <- true end) t.widths;
  let natural (c : Doc.cell) : float = snd (one_line metrics 0. c.body) in
  let each (f : int -> Doc.cell -> unit) = List.iter (fun (r : Doc.table_row) -> match r with Doc.Rule -> () | Doc.Cells cs -> ignore (List.fold_left (fun k (c : Doc.cell) -> f k c; k + c.span) 0 cs)) t.rows in
  each (fun (k : int) (c : Doc.cell) ->
    if c.span = 1 && not said.(k) then begin
      if c.filled then wants.(k) <- true
      else if c.align = Doc.Numeric then begin
        let l, r = split_number metrics c in
        lefts.(k) <- Float.max lefts.(k) l; rights.(k) <- Float.max rights.(k) r;
        widths.(k) <- Float.max widths.(k) (lefts.(k) +. rights.(k))
      end
      else widths.(k) <- Float.max widths.(k) (natural c)
    end
    else if c.span = 1 && c.align = Doc.Numeric then begin
      let l, r = split_number metrics c in
      lefts.(k) <- Float.max lefts.(k) l; rights.(k) <- Float.max rights.(k) r
    end);
  let wanting = Array.fold_left (fun n w -> if w then n + 1 else n) 0 wants in
  if wanting > 0 then begin
    let taken = ref (gap *. float_of_int (count - 1)) in
    Array.iteri (fun k w -> if not wants.(k) then taken := !taken +. w) widths;
    (* (tbl's: a text with no width said has the line's length shared
     * between the columns and one more; less if less is left) *)
    let share = Float.max (units look 10.) (Float.min (Float.floor ((look.width -. left) /. float_of_int (count + 1))) (Float.floor ((look.width -. left -. !taken) /. float_of_int wanting))) in
    Array.iteri (fun k w -> if w then widths.(k) <- Float.max widths.(k) share) wants
  end;
  let total = Array.fold_left (fun s w -> s +. w) (gap *. float_of_int (count - 1)) widths in
  let x0 = if t.centered then left +. Float.max 0. (Float.floor ((look.width -. left -. total) /. 2.)) else left in
  let xs = Array.make (max 1 count) x0 in
  for k = 1 to count - 1 do xs.(k) <- xs.(k - 1) +. widths.(k - 1) +. gap done;
  let rule = Rule (x0, x0 +. total) in
  let rows =
    List.concat_map (fun (r : Doc.table_row) ->
      match r with
      | Doc.Rule -> [ rule ]
      | Doc.Cells cs ->
          let cells = ref [] in
          ignore (List.fold_left (fun k (c : Doc.cell) ->
            if k < count then begin
              let last = min (count - 1) (k + c.span - 1) in
              let w = xs.(last) +. widths.(last) -. xs.(k) in
              let lines =
                if c.filled then paragraph { look with width = xs.(k) +. w; justify = false } metrics xs.(k) xs.(k) [] { fill = true; first = 0.; short = 0.; tabs = []; center = false; body = c.body }
                else begin
                  let pieces, stop = one_line metrics 0. c.body in
                  let by = match c.align with
                    | Doc.Left -> 0.
                    | Doc.Right -> w -. stop
                    | Doc.Center -> Float.floor ((w -. stop) /. 2.)
                    | Doc.Numeric -> if c.span > 1 then 0. else lefts.(k) -. fst (split_number metrics c) in
                  [ List.map (fun (p : piece) -> { p with x = p.x +. xs.(k) +. Float.max 0. by }) pieces ]
                end in
              cells := lines :: !cells
            end;
            k + c.span) 0 cs);
          let cells = List.rev !cells in
          let height = List.fold_left (fun n l -> max n (List.length l)) 1 cells in
          List.init height (fun i -> Line (List.concat_map (fun l -> match List.nth_opt l i with Some pieces -> pieces | None -> []) cells))) t.rows in
  if t.boxed then (rule :: rows) @ [ rule ] else rows

let rec blocks (look : look) (metrics : metrics) (sub : float) (left : float) (bs : Doc.block list) : row list =
  let lines (l : piece list list) : row list = List.map (fun pieces -> Line pieces) l in
  List.concat_map (fun (b : Doc.block) ->
    match b with
    | Doc.Heading (level, text) ->
        (* (a paragraph at the left: a long one takes several lines) *)
        let at = if level <= 1 then 0. else sub in
        lines (paragraph { look with justify = false } metrics at at [] { fill = true; first = 0.; short = 0.; tabs = []; center = false; body = text })
    | Doc.Footnote inner -> [ Foot (blocks look metrics sub left inner) ]
    | Doc.Keep inner -> [ Together (blocks look metrics sub left inner) ]
    | Doc.Table t -> [ Together (table look metrics left t) ]
    (* (in the middle of the line; an inch is 14.4 ens of a text of 10
     * points, 10 of a terminal's letters: [inch]) *)
    | Doc.Picture p ->
        let wide = Float.round (p.wide *. look.inch) in
        [ Drawing (left +. Float.max 0. (Float.floor ((look.width -. left -. wide) /. 2.)), p) ]
    | Doc.Para p -> lines (paragraph look metrics left (left +. units look p.first) [] p)
    | Doc.Indent (by, inner) -> blocks look metrics sub (left +. units look by) inner
    | Doc.Space n -> [ Skip n ]
    | Doc.Anchor (name, lettered) -> [ Mark (name, lettered) ]
    | Doc.Tagged { tag; width; body } ->
        let width = units look width in
        let pieces, stop = one_line metrics left tag in
        (match body with
         (* (the tag and some room after it: tmac.an's 3 points) *)
         | Doc.Para p :: rest when stop -. left < width -. look.tag_room ->
             lines (paragraph look metrics (left +. width) (left +. width +. units look p.first) pieces p) @ blocks look metrics sub (left +. width) rest
         (* (a paragraph of nothing after the tag: the tag's line was
          * ended there, and it has it to itself) *)
         | Doc.Para { body = []; _ } :: rest | rest -> Line pieces :: blocks look metrics sub (left +. width) rest)) bs

let rows (look : look) (metrics : metrics) (d : Doc.t) : row list =
  blocks { look with width = units look d.width } metrics (units look d.sub) (units look d.margin) d.body
typesetting/troff/doc/Layout.mli
4040
(* Layout: a document's blocks put on lines -- each word given its
 * place, the lines broken where the words stop fitting.
 *
 *   Para "Tr copies the standard input to the standard output with
 *         substitution or deletion of selected characters."
 *
 *   width 40, the text's margin 5:
 *
 *        Tr copies the standard input to the
 *        standard output with substitution or
 *        deletion of selected characters.
 *        ^5                                  ^40
 *
 * Lines are filled greedily, as troff's: a word goes on the line if it
 * fits, else it starts the next, and a line once left is not looked at
 * again. (TeX's way, the paragraph broken as a whole, is for later and
 * beside this one: docs/plans/done/plan_typesetting.md.) A word too long
 * for a line has the line to itself and goes past the edge.
 *
 * A line may also end inside a word, after a hyphen of its own
 * (twenty-|seven; not the first letter's, -c), if a hyphen more would
 * still fit, which is troff's test; and where the text says a word
 * may be cut (U+00AD), with a hyphen added. Nothing is hyphenated by
 * rule: a terminal's manual never was.
 *
 * It sees no font and no terminal: a word's width is the caller's
 * [metrics], so that a terminal's writer gives one for every
 * character and a typesetter's gives Times's. Widths and places are in
 * the writer's own unit, a column for a terminal, a thousandth of a
 * point for paper, and are whole numbers of it: sums of whole numbers
 * are the same whatever computes them, and a file written from them
 * the same bytes. The document's lengths, in ens, are turned into
 * that unit here ([en] says how many an en is). A place is from the
 * paper's left. What comes out is rows: a line of words, or room
 * left before the next (in lines, and maybe less than one: 0.4
 * between two paragraphs on paper). There are no pages here: the
 * writer cuts the rows into them.
 *
 * On paper a line is also made even: when it ends because the next
 * word did not fit, what room is left is shared between its spaces,
 * and the right edge is straight (troff's .ad; not a paragraph's last
 * line, nor a line that is not filled).
 *
 * A tagged paragraph, the only block with two things on a line:
 *
 *        -c   Complement string1: replace it      the tag fits in its
 *             with a lexicographically ...        width: the body starts
 *                                                 on its line
 *        -cds
 *             The three of them.                  it does not: below
 *)

(* [x]: in the writer's units *)
type piece = { x : float; style : Doc.style; text : string }

type row =
  (* (an empty one: a blank line of lines not filled) *)
  | Line of piece list
  | Skip of float
  (* a footnote's rows: the writer's to put at the sheet's foot *)
  | Foot of row list
  (* rows not to be cut by a sheet's end *)
  | Together of row list
  (* a line drawn across, from a place to another: a table's *)
  | Rule of float * float
  (* a picture, its left edge at a place *)
  | Drawing of float * Doc.picture
  (* where an anchor is (Doc.Anchor): the sheet of the next line *)
  | Mark of string * bool

(* how a page looks, which is not the document's to say; its lengths
 * in the writer's units *)
type look = {
  (* how many units an en is, and an inch *)
  en : float;
  inch : float;
  (* the line's length: the document's, put here by [rows] *)
  width : float;
  (* what must be left between a tag and its width for the body to
   * start on the tag's line *)
  tag_room : float;
  (* the lines' right edge made even *)
  justify : bool;
}

(* a text's width in a style, in the writer's units: a whole number *)
type metrics = Doc.style -> string -> float

(* (a [Doc.Page] is its own text: the writer that has sheets puts
 * their numbers in first, Doc.pages) *)
val rows : look -> metrics -> Doc.t -> row list

(* a text on one line, from a place: its pieces, and where it ends *)
val one_line : metrics -> float -> Doc.inline list -> piece list * float
typesetting/troff/doc/To_pdf.ml
14127
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See To_pdf.mli *)

(* Lengths are in thousandths of a point, whole numbers of them: a
 * letter's width in a font is so many thousandths of its size, and
 * the sizes are whole points. (Layout.mli says why whole.) *)
let point = 1000.
let paper_width = 612. *. point
let paper_height = 792. *. point
let size = 10
let leading = 12. *. point

(* an en: half the text's size *)
let en = float_of_int size *. point /. 2.

(* the header's line, the first of the text's and the last a page may
 * have; the page number's *)
let header_y = paper_height -. (54. *. point)
let first_y = paper_height -. (90. *. point)
let last_y = 72. *. point
let number_y = 42. *. point

(* (the room after a tag 3 points: tmac.an's) *)
let look : Layout.look = { en; inch = 72. *. point; width = 0.; tag_room = 3. *. point; justify = true }

let font_name (f : Doc.font) : string =
  match f with Doc.Roman -> "Times-Roman" | Doc.Italic -> "Times-Italic" | Doc.Bold -> "Times-Bold" | Doc.Mono -> "Courier"

let point_size (style : Doc.style) : int = max 1 (size + style.size)

(* what could not be written, the last first *)
let missing : string list ref = ref []

(* A character as it is written in a font: itself if the encoding has
 * it; troff's own choices (a minus, the quotes); for a few that it has
 * not, ASCII's way of saying them. *)
let written (f : Doc.font) (c : string) : string =
  match c with
  | "\xc2\xa0" -> " "
  (* (the three that are not seen: the layout's) *)
  | "\xc2\xad" | "\xe2\x81\xa0" | "\xe2\x80\x8b" -> c
  | "\xe2\x80\x91" -> "-"
  | "\xe2\x88\x92" -> if f = Doc.Mono then "-" else "\xe2\x80\x93"
  | "`" -> if f = Doc.Mono then c else "\xe2\x80\x98"
  | "'" -> if f = Doc.Mono then c else "\xe2\x80\x99"
  | _ ->
      (* (ASCII; not a byte that is no character, which is a "?" too) *)
      if (String.length c = 1 && c.[0] < '\x80') || (String.length c > 1 && Pdf_write.writes (Utf8.code c)) then c
      else
        match c with
        | "\xe2\x86\x92" -> "->" | "\xe2\x86\x90" -> "<-" | "\xe2\x89\xa4" -> "<=" | "\xe2\x89\xa5" -> ">=" | "\xe2\x89\xa0" -> "!="
        | "\xe2\x88\x99" -> "\xe2\x80\xa2"
        | _ -> if not (List.mem c !missing) then missing := c :: !missing; "?"

let shown (f : Doc.font) (s : string) : string = String.concat "" (List.map (written f) (fst (Utf8.chars s)))

(* a character's width in a font, in thousandths of its size: looked
 * up once *)
let widths : (Doc.font * string, int) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 512

let char_width (f : Doc.font) (c : string) : int =
  match Hashtbl.find_opt widths (f, c) with
  | Some w -> w
  | None ->
      let w = match Option.bind (Glyph_names.name (Utf8.code c)) (Standard_widths.width (font_name f)) with Some w -> w | None -> 500 in
      Hashtbl.add widths (f, c) w; w

let metrics (style : Doc.style) (s : string) : float =
  let total = List.fold_left (fun w c -> w + char_width style.font c) 0 (fst (Utf8.chars (shown style.font s))) in
  float_of_int (total * point_size style)

let measure (text : Doc.inline list) : float =
  let total = List.fold_left (fun w (i : Doc.inline) -> match i with Doc.Text (style, s) | Doc.Page (style, _, s) -> w +. metrics style (Doc.letters s) | Doc.Break -> w) 0. text in
  total /. en

(* a text at a place, both in thousandths of a point *)
let put (pdf : Pdf_write.t) (c : Pdf_write.content) (style : Doc.style) (x : float) (y : float) (s : string) =
  Pdf_write.text pdf c ~font:(font_name style.font) ~size:(float_of_int (point_size style)) (x /. point, y /. point) s

(* the room a rule across a table takes *)
let rule_room = Float.round (leading /. 3.)

(* how much of a sheet rows take; the rows as lines, what is to stay
 * together no longer said *)
let rec height (rows : Layout.row list) : float =
  List.fold_left (fun h (r : Layout.row) ->
    match r with
    | Layout.Line _ -> h +. leading
    | Layout.Skip n -> let down = Float.round (n *. leading) in h +. down
    | Layout.Together inner -> h +. height inner
    | Layout.Rule _ -> h +. rule_room
    | Layout.Drawing (_, p) -> h +. Float.round (p.high *. 72. *. point) +. leading
    | Layout.Foot _ | Layout.Mark _ -> h) 0. rows

let rec flat (rows : Layout.row list) : Layout.row list =
  List.concat_map (fun (r : Layout.row) -> match r with Layout.Together inner | Layout.Foot inner -> flat inner | _ -> [ r ]) rows

(* The sheets, and where each anchor is: its name, lettered, the
 * sheet's number. [draw]: what is on them is written (else they are
 * only counted, for the anchors: a quarter of the time) *)
let sheets (draw : bool) (d : Doc.t) : Pdf_write.t * int * (string * bool * int) list =
  missing := [];
  (* the lines that go past the paper's right edge *)
  let over = ref 0 in
  let pdf = Pdf_write.create ~compress:true in
  let (head_left, head_middle, head_right) = d.header in
  let width_of (s : string) = metrics Doc.plain s in
  (* the lines in the middle of the paper: its left edge to their start *)
  let width = Float.round (d.width *. en) in
  let left = Float.round ((paper_width -. width) /. 2.) in
  let page = ref (Pdf_write.content ()) and number = ref 1 and y = ref first_y and used = ref false in
  (* the anchors, the last first, and those whose line is not yet
   * placed *)
  let anchors = ref [] and waiting_anchors = ref [] in
  let placed () = List.iter (fun (name, lettered) -> anchors := (name, lettered, !number) :: !anchors) (List.rev !waiting_anchors); waiting_anchors := [] in
  (* the sheet's footnotes, the last first, and those that found no
   * room on it; the lowest line the text may have, above them *)
  let feet = ref [] and waiting = ref [] and limit = ref last_y in
  let line (at : float) (pieces : Layout.piece list) =
    if draw then begin
      List.iter (fun (p : Layout.piece) ->
        let s = shown p.style.font p.text in
        (* (an exponent, an index: a third of the size up or down) *)
        let up = float_of_int (p.style.shift * size * 1000 / 3) in
        if String.trim s <> "" then put pdf !page p.style (left +. p.x) (at +. up) s) pieces;
      match List.rev pieces with
      | (last : Layout.piece) :: _ when left +. last.x +. metrics last.style last.text > paper_width -> incr over
      | _ -> ()
    end in
  (* a rule above where the next line will stand, at [at] *)
  let across (at : float) (x0 : float) (x1 : float) =
    let y = (at +. leading -. rule_room) /. point in
    if draw then begin
      Pdf_write.pen !page 0.5;
      Pdf_write.polyline !page [ ((left +. x0) /. point, y); ((left +. x1) /. point, y) ];
      Pdf_write.stroke !page
    end in
  (* a footnote's room: its lines, and one for the rule over the first *)
  let room (rows : Layout.row list) : float = height rows +. leading in
  let finish () =
    let c = !page in
    (* the footnotes, the last line of the last on the sheet's last line *)
    if draw && !feet <> [] then begin
      (* a short rule under the text, a line's room for it and between
       * two footnotes *)
      let rule = (!limit -. Float.round (leading /. 4.)) /. point in
      Pdf_write.pen c 0.5;
      Pdf_write.polyline c [ (left /. point, rule); ((left +. (72. *. point)) /. point, rule) ];
      Pdf_write.stroke c;
      let at = ref !limit in
      List.iter (fun rows ->
        at := !at -. leading;
        List.iter (fun (r : Layout.row) ->
          match r with
          | Layout.Line pieces -> line !at pieces; at := !at -. leading
          | Layout.Skip n -> let down = Float.round (n *. leading) in at := !at -. down
          | Layout.Rule (x0, x1) -> across !at x0 x1; at := !at -. rule_room
          | _ -> ()) (flat rows)) (List.rev !feet)
    end;
    if draw && (head_left <> "" || head_right <> "") then begin
      put pdf c Doc.plain left header_y head_left;
      put pdf c Doc.plain (left +. Float.floor ((width -. width_of head_middle) /. 2.)) header_y head_middle;
      put pdf c Doc.plain (left +. width -. width_of head_right) header_y head_right
    end;
    let n = string_of_int !number in
    if draw then begin
      put pdf c Doc.plain (left +. Float.floor ((width -. width_of n) /. 2.)) number_y n;
      Pdf_write.page pdf ~width:(paper_width /. point) ~height:(paper_height /. point) c
    end;
    page := Pdf_write.content (); incr number; y := first_y; used := false;
    feet := !waiting; waiting := [];
    limit := List.fold_left (fun l rows -> l +. room rows) last_y !feet in
  let rec write (r : Layout.row) =
    match r with
    (* (no space at a page's top) *)
    | Layout.Skip n -> if !used then begin let down = Float.round (n *. leading) in y := !y -. down end
    | Layout.Line pieces ->
        if !y < !limit then finish ();
        placed ();
        line !y pieces;
        used := true; y := !y -. leading
    | Layout.Rule (x0, x1) -> across !y x0 x1; y := !y -. rule_room
    | Layout.Drawing (x, p) ->
        (* its top where the next line's letters would reach, half a
         * line of room under it *)
        let high = Float.round (p.high *. 72. *. point) in
        if !used && !y -. high < !limit && high <= first_y -. !limit then finish ();
        placed ();
        let top = !y +. Float.round (leading *. 0.7) in
        let at (px : float) (py : float) : float * float = (left +. x +. Float.round (px *. 72. *. point), top -. high +. Float.round (py *. 72. *. point)) in
        Pdf_write.pen !page 0.5;
        if draw then List.iter (fun (m : Doc.mark) ->
          match m with
          | Doc.Stroke points ->
              Pdf_write.polyline !page (List.map (fun (px, py) -> let ax, ay = at px py in (ax /. point, ay /. point)) points);
              Pdf_write.stroke !page
          | Doc.Image (px, py, w, h, _, img) ->
              let ax, ay = at px py in
              let scale : Affine.t = { a = Float.round (w *. 72. *. point) /. point; b = 0.; c = 0.; d = Float.round (h *. 72. *. point) /. point; tx = ax /. point; ty = ay /. point } in
              Pdf_write.save !page;
              Pdf_write.transform !page scale;
              Pdf_write.draw !page (Pdf_write.picture pdf img);
              Pdf_write.restore !page
          | Doc.Label (px, py, side, text) ->
              let ax, ay = at px py in
              let wide = measure text *. en in
              let from = if side < 0 then ax else if side > 0 then ax -. wide else ax -. Float.floor (wide /. 2.) in
              (* (the letters' middle on the place, not their foot) *)
              let pieces, _ = Layout.one_line metrics (from -. left) text in
              line (ay -. Float.round (float_of_int size *. point *. 0.3)) pieces) p.marks;
        used := true; y := !y -. high -. Float.round (leading /. 2.)
    | Layout.Together rows ->
        (* (on the next sheet if it does not fit on this one, unless it
         * would not fit on an empty one either) *)
        if !used && !y -. height rows +. leading < !limit && height rows <= first_y -. !limit then finish ();
        List.iter write rows
    | Layout.Foot rows ->
        (* (on this sheet if there is room under the line its mark is
         * on; else on the next) *)
        if !y -. room rows >= !limit then begin feet := rows :: !feet; limit := !limit +. room rows end
        else waiting := rows :: !waiting
    | Layout.Mark (name, lettered) -> waiting_anchors := (name, lettered) :: !waiting_anchors in
  List.iter write (Layout.rows look metrics d);
  placed ();
  finish ();
  while !feet <> [] do finish () done;
  (pdf, !over, List.rev !anchors)

(* each anchor's page as it is written: the sheet's number, and a
 * letter after it for those lettered when the sheet has several *)
let numbers (anchors : (string * bool * int) list) : (string, string) Hashtbl.t =
  let table = Hashtbl.create 64 in
  let on (n : int) = List.length (List.filter (fun ((_, lettered, k) : string * bool * int) -> lettered && k = n) anchors) in
  let seen = Hashtbl.create 64 in
  List.iter (fun ((name, lettered, n) : string * bool * int) ->
    let p = string_of_int n in
    if not lettered || on n < 2 then Hashtbl.replace table name p
    else begin
      let k = match Hashtbl.find_opt seen n with Some k -> k | None -> 0 in
      Hashtbl.replace seen n (k + 1);
      Hashtbl.replace table name (p ^ String.make 1 (Char.chr (97 + (k mod 26))))
    end) anchors;
  table

(* A page's number is known once the sheets are made, and what is
 * written with it may move what comes after to another sheet: the
 * sheets are made again with the numbers of the time before, until
 * they no longer change (LaTeX's "rerun to get cross-references
 * right", done here; twice for most documents, at most four times). *)
let file (d : Doc.t) : string * string list * int =
  let has_pages = ref false in
  ignore (Doc.map_inline (fun (i : Doc.inline) -> (match i with Doc.Page _ -> has_pages := true | _ -> ()); i) d);
  let make (draw : bool) (table : (string, string) Hashtbl.t) = sheets draw (Doc.pages (Hashtbl.find_opt table) d) in
  let same (a : (string, string) Hashtbl.t) (b : (string, string) Hashtbl.t) : bool = Hashtbl.fold (fun k v same -> same && Hashtbl.find_opt b k = Some v) a (Hashtbl.length a = Hashtbl.length b) in
  let third ((_, _, anchors) : Pdf_write.t * int * (string * bool * int) list) = numbers anchors in
  (* the sheets counted until the numbers stay the same *)
  let rec settle (table : (string, string) Hashtbl.t) (times : int) : (string, string) Hashtbl.t =
    let now = third (make false table) in
    if same now table || times >= 4 then now else settle now (times + 1) in
  let result ((pdf, over, _) : Pdf_write.t * int * (string * bool * int) list) = (Pdf_write.to_string pdf, List.rev !missing, over) in
  if not !has_pages then result (make true (Hashtbl.create 1))
  else begin
    (* (counted once, then written: for most documents what is written
     * puts nothing on another sheet, and it is the last time) *)
    let first = third (make false (Hashtbl.create 1)) in
    let written = make true first in
    if same (third written) first then result written else result (make true (settle (third written) 2))
  end
typesetting/troff/doc/To_pdf.mli
