(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Ms.mli *)

type state = {
  fill : Fill.t;
  roff : Roff.t;
  (* .RS's levels: where the text of each is, the deepest first; and
   * how far right of the deepest an .IP's body is (0: no .IP yet) *)
  mutable levels : float list;
  mutable ip : float;
  (* the sections' numbers, the first level's first *)
  mutable sections : int list;
  (* the lines set in from both sides: an abstract's *)
  mutable inset : float;
  (* a display or a program is being read: what to put back at its end *)
  mutable display : float option;
  (* some text was written: a paragraph has a space before it *)
  mutable begun : bool;
  (* what .FS put aside of the text it interrupts *)
  mutable aside : (Fill.t * Doc.font) option;
}

(* a register of the paper's, a length in ens, or what tmac.s has *)
let ens (m : state) (name : string) (default : float) : float =
  match Roff.register m.roff name with Some u when u <> 0. -> Roff.ens m.roff u | _ -> default

let lines (m : state) (name : string) (default : float) : float =
  match Roff.register m.roff name with Some u -> Roff.lines m.roff u | None -> default

let terminal (m : state) : bool = Roff.device m.roff = Roff.Terminal

(* \n(PI, \n(PD, \n(DV: a paragraph's indent, the space between two
 * paragraphs, and round a display *)
let pi (m : state) = ens m "PI" 5.
let pd (m : state) = lines m "PD" (if terminal m then 1. else 0.3)
let dv (m : state) = lines m "DV" (if terminal m then 1. else 0.5)

let base (m : state) : float = match m.levels with l :: _ -> l | [] -> 0.

(* tmac.s's .RT: what every paragraph starts from: the text's own font
 * and size, filled, at its level's place *)
let reset (m : state) =
  let f = m.fill in
  Fill.break f;
  Roff.reset_style m.roff;
  f.fill <- true; f.center <- 0; f.ti <- None; f.heading <- None;
  f.indent <- base m +. m.inset; f.short <- m.inset

(* a space that is not added to the one before it: after a display's,
 * a paragraph's own is not one more *)
let gap (m : state) (n : float) =
  match m.fill.items with
  | Fill.Gap g :: rest -> if n > g then m.fill.items <- Fill.Gap n :: rest
  | Fill.Close :: Fill.Gap _ :: _ | Fill.Open _ :: Fill.Gap _ :: _ -> ()
  | _ -> Fill.gap m.fill n

(* the space before a paragraph: none before the first *)
let space (m : state) (n : float) = if m.begun then gap m n; m.begun <- true

let text (m : state) (words : Doc.inline list) = Fill.text m.fill words (Fill.ends_sentence words) false

(* .I word after before: the word in a font, with what touches it in
 * the font there was; alone: the font from here on *)
let in_font (m : state) (f : Doc.font) (args : string list) =
  let arg k = match List.nth_opt args k with Some a -> a | None -> "" in
  if args = [] then Roff.set_font m.roff f
  else text m (Roff.inlines m.roff (arg 2) @ Roff.inlines_in m.roff f (arg 0) @ Roff.inlines m.roff (arg 1))

(* a size for a word, or from here on *)
let in_size (m : state) (by : int) (args : string list) =
  let arg k = match List.nth_opt args k with Some a -> a | None -> "" in
  if args = [] then Roff.resize m.roff (if by > 0 then "+2" else "-2")
  else begin
    let small = List.map (fun (x : Doc.inline) -> match x with Doc.Text (s, w) -> Doc.Text ({ s with size = s.size + by }, w) | Doc.Break | Doc.Page _ -> x) (Roff.inlines m.roff (arg 0)) in
    text m (Roff.inlines m.roff (arg 2) @ small @ Roff.inlines m.roff (arg 1))
  end

(* a display starts: its lines as they are, kept on one sheet, [by]
 * further right *)
let display (m : state) (by : float) =
  let f = m.fill in
  Fill.break f; space m (dv m);
  Fill.emit f (Fill.Open Fill.Keep);
  m.display <- Some f.indent;
  f.fill <- false; f.indent <- f.indent +. by

let display_end (m : state) =
  let f = m.fill in
  Fill.break f;
  (match m.display with Some back -> f.indent <- back; Fill.emit f Fill.Close | None -> ());
  m.display <- None;
  f.center <- 0; f.fill <- true; Roff.reset_style m.roff;
  gap m (dv m)

(* the next section's number at a level: "2.", "2.1." *)
let number (m : state) (level : int) : string =
  let rec bump (k : int) (l : int list) : int list =
    match l with
    | n :: rest -> if k = 1 then [ n + 1 ] else n :: bump (k - 1) rest
    | [] -> if k = 1 then [ 1 ] else 1 :: bump (k - 1) [] in
  m.sections <- bump (max 1 level) m.sections;
  String.concat "" (List.map (fun n -> string_of_int n ^ ".") m.sections)

let rec request (m : state) (name : string) (args : string list) =
  let arg k = match List.nth_opt args k with Some a -> a | None -> "" in
  let roff = m.roff and f = m.fill in
  match name with
  (* the title's lines, the authors', their institution's: each in the
   * middle of the line *)
  | "TL" -> reset m; f.center <- 100000; Roff.set_font roff Doc.Bold; if not (terminal m) then Roff.resize roff "+2"; m.begun <- true
  | "AU" -> reset m; gap m 1.; f.center <- 100000; Roff.set_font roff Doc.Italic
  | "AI" -> reset m; gap m 1.; f.center <- 100000
  | "MH" -> text m (Roff.inlines roff "Bell Laboratories"); text m (Roff.inlines roff "Murray Hill, New Jersey 07974")
  | "AB" ->
      reset m; gap m 1.;
      if arg 0 <> "no" && arg 0 <> "-" then begin
        f.center <- 1; Roff.set_font roff Doc.Italic;
        text m (Roff.inlines roff (if arg 0 = "" then "ABSTRACT" else arg 0));
        Roff.reset_style roff; gap m 1.
      end;
      (* (tmac.s's lines of 5/6 of the others, in the middle) *)
      m.inset <- Fill.column f (f.length /. 12.);
      reset m; f.ti <- Some (f.indent +. pi m)
  | "AE" -> reset m; m.inset <- 0.; reset m; gap m 1.
  | "PP" -> reset m; space m (pd m); f.ti <- Some (f.indent +. pi m); m.ip <- 0. +. m.ip
  | "LP" -> reset m; space m (pd m)
  | "QP" ->
      reset m; space m (pd m);
      let q = ens m "QI" 5. in
      f.indent <- f.indent +. q; f.short <- f.short +. q
  | "IP" ->
      reset m; space m (pd m);
      if arg 1 <> "" then m.ip <- Fill.column f (Fill.length f (arg 1));
      if m.ip = 0. then m.ip <- pi m;
      if arg 0 <> "" then begin Fill.emit f (Fill.Tag (f.indent, f.indent +. m.ip, Roff.inlines roff (arg 0))); f.tag_open <- true end;
      f.indent <- f.indent +. m.ip
  | "RS" ->
      (* further right by the .IP's indent if there is one, else by a
       * paragraph's *)
      Fill.break f;
      m.levels <- (base m +. (if m.ip > 0. then m.ip else pi m)) :: m.levels; m.ip <- 0.;
      reset m
  | "RE" -> Fill.break f; (match m.levels with _ :: rest -> m.levels <- rest | [] -> ()); m.ip <- 0.; reset m
  | "SH" | "NH" ->
      reset m; space m 1.;
      Roff.set_font roff Doc.Bold;
      let level = if name = "SH" then 1 else max 1 (int_of_float (Roff.number roff 'u' (if arg 0 = "" then "1" else arg 0))) in
      (* (the paragraph that follows, to the next macro, is the heading) *)
      f.heading <- Some level; m.ip <- 0.;
      if name = "NH" then begin
        text m (Roff.inlines roff (number m level ^ "\\ \\ "));
        f.glued <- true
      end
  (* a display: .DS L at the left, .DS C each line in the middle, else
   * further right (8 letters on a terminal, half an inch on paper) *)
  | "DS" | "ID" | "LD" | "CD" | "BD" ->
      let kind = if name = "DS" then (if arg 0 = "" then "I" else arg 0) else String.sub name 0 1 in
      let by = if arg 1 <> "" then Fill.length f (arg 1) else if terminal m then 8. else 7.2 in
      display m (if kind = "I" then by else 0.);
      if kind = "C" then f.center <- 100000
  | "DE" -> display_end m
  (* a program's text: in its font, two ems right, a tab every 8 letters *)
  | "P1" ->
      display m (if arg 0 <> "" then Fill.length f (arg 0) else if terminal m then 2. else 4.);
      Roff.set_font roff Doc.Mono;
      let w = if terminal m then 8. else 9.6 in
      f.tabs <- List.init 14 (fun k -> w *. float_of_int (k + 1))
  | "P2" -> display_end m
  | "KS" | "KF" -> Fill.break f; Fill.emit f (Fill.Open Fill.Keep)
  | "KE" -> Fill.break f; Fill.emit f Fill.Close
  | "FS" ->
      (* the text it interrupts is put aside, with its font: a footnote
       * is a text of its own, said in the middle of another *)
      m.aside <- Some ({ f with roff = f.roff }, Roff.font roff);
      f.par <- []; f.started <- false; f.glued <- false; f.sentence <- false; f.blank_end <- false; f.capture <- None; f.tag_open <- false;
      f.heading <- None; f.fill <- true; f.center <- 0; f.ti <- None; f.indent <- 0.; f.short <- 0.;
      Roff.reset_style roff;
      Fill.emit f (Fill.Open Fill.Footnote);
      if arg 0 <> "" then text m (Roff.inlines roff (arg 0))
  | "FE" ->
      Fill.break f; Fill.emit f Fill.Close;
      (match m.aside with
       | Some (was, font) ->
           f.par <- was.par; f.started <- was.started; f.first <- was.first; f.par_tabs <- was.par_tabs; f.glued <- was.glued;
           f.sentence <- was.sentence; f.blank_end <- was.blank_end; f.capture <- was.capture; f.tag_open <- was.tag_open;
           f.heading <- was.heading; f.fill <- was.fill; f.center <- was.center; f.ti <- was.ti; f.indent <- was.indent; f.short <- was.short;
           f.no_space <- was.no_space; Roff.reset_style roff; Roff.set_font roff font
       | None -> ());
      m.aside <- None
  | "I" -> in_font m Doc.Italic args
  | "B" -> in_font m Doc.Bold args
  | "CW" -> in_font m Doc.Mono args
  | "BI" | "UL" -> in_font m Doc.Italic args
  | "BX" -> in_font m Doc.Roman args
  | "R" -> if args = [] then Roff.set_font roff Doc.Roman else in_font m Doc.Roman args
  | "SM" -> in_size m (-2) args
  | "LG" -> in_size m 2 args
  | "NL" -> Roff.resize roff ""
  (* what is for another program (Plan 9's ms2html), or has nothing to
   * show here: a font's family, the date, a memorandum's kind *)
  | "HT" | "FP" | "ND" | "DA" | "TM" | "RP" | "AT" | "nm" | "hw" | "bd" | "fp" | "mk" | "rt" -> ()
  | "TS" ->
      Fill.break f;
      let table = Tbl.read roff (fun () -> block m) in
      Fill.emit f (Fill.Whole (f.indent, Doc.Table table)); m.begun <- true
  | "PS" ->
      Fill.break f;
      (* .PS <file: the picture is in a file; .PS 3i: it is 3 inches wide *)
      let all = String.concat "" args in
      let text, width =
        if String.length all > 0 && all.[0] = '<' then
          ((match Roff.load roff (String.trim (String.sub all 1 (String.length all - 1))) with Some t -> t | None -> ""), 0.)
        else begin
          let lines = ref [] in
          let rec until () =
            match Roff.next roff with
            | None | Some (Roff.Request (("PE" | "PF"), _)) -> ()
            | Some (Roff.Text s) -> lines := s :: !lines; until ()
            | Some (Roff.Request (_, _)) -> until () in
          until ();
          let w = let a = arg 0 in if a <> "" && a.[String.length a - 1] = 'i' then String.sub a 0 (String.length a - 1) else a in
          (String.concat "\n" (List.rev !lines), (match float_of_string_opt w with Some v -> v | None -> 0.))
        end in
      (match Pic.read (Roff.load roff) width (fun s -> let w = Roff.inlines roff s in Roff.reset_style roff; w) text with
       | Ok p -> Fill.emit f (Fill.Whole (f.indent, Doc.Picture p)); m.begun <- true
       | Error why -> Roff.unknown roff (".PS (a picture, " ^ why ^ ")"))
  | "EQ" ->
      (* not read yet: its lines passed over *)
      Roff.unknown roff ".EQ";
      let rec until () = match Roff.next roff with None -> () | Some (Roff.Request ("EN", _)) -> () | Some _ -> until () in
      until ()
  | _ -> if not (Fill.request f name args) then Roff.unknown roff ("." ^ name)

(* a table's cell of several lines, to its T}: a text of its own, with
 * the paper's macros in it *)
and block (m : state) : Doc.inline list * string =
  Fill.aside m.fill (fun () ->
    let rec go () : string =
      match Roff.next m.roff with
      | None -> ""
      | Some (Roff.Text s) when String.starts_with ~prefix:"T}" s -> String.sub s 2 (String.length s - 2)
      | Some (Roff.Text s) -> Fill.line m.fill s; go ()
      | Some (Roff.Request (name, args)) -> request m name args; go () in
    go ())

let read (roff : Roff.t) : Doc.t =
  let term = Roff.device roff = Roff.Terminal in
  let length = if term then 60. else 86.4 in
  let step = if term then 5. else 7.2 in
  let m = { fill = Fill.create roff 0. length (List.init 16 (fun k -> step *. float_of_int (k + 1))); roff; levels = []; ip = 0.; sections = [];
            inset = 0.; display = None; begun = false; aside = None } in
  (* tmac.s's strings: the quotation marks, the dash *)
  Roff.set_string roff "Q" (if term then "\"" else "\xe2\x80\x9c");
  Roff.set_string roff "U" (if term then "\"" else "\xe2\x80\x9d");
  Roff.set_string roff "-" (if term then "--" else "\xe2\x80\x94");
  let rec go () =
    match Roff.next roff with
    | None -> ()
    | Some (Roff.Request (name, args)) -> request m name args; go ()
    | Some (Roff.Text s) -> m.begun <- true; Fill.line m.fill s; go () in
  go (); Fill.break m.fill;
  { header = ("", "", ""); width = length; margin = 0.; sub = 0.; body = Fill.tree m.fill }

(* Ms: a paper read -- the macros of ms(6), Plan 9's tmac.s, each as
 * what it means and not as the troff it was written in.
 *
 *   .TL                       the title: its lines centered, bold
 *   The Use of Name Spaces
 *   .AU                       the authors, .AI where they are
 *   Rob Pike
 *   .AB  ...  .AE             the abstract, set in from both sides
 *   .NH                       a numbered heading: "1. Introduction"
 *   Introduction              (.NH 2: "1.1."); .SH: one with no number
 *   .PP                       a paragraph, its first line indented
 *   .LP                       one that is not
 *   .IP (1) 5                 one that hangs from a tag
 *   .RS / .RE                 what is between, further right
 *   .QP                       a quotation, set in from both sides
 *   .DS / .DE                 a display: lines as they are, kept on one
 *   .P1 / .P2                 sheet; a program's text, in its font
 *   .KS / .KE                 what is between, kept on one sheet
 *   .FS / .FE                 a footnote, said in the middle of a
 *                             sentence, written at the sheet's foot
 *   .I word .  (            the word in italic, a dot after it in the
 *                             font there was, a parenthesis before;
 *   .I                        alone: italic from here on, until .R
 *
 * It keeps what tmac.s keeps: the paragraph's indent (\n(PI), the
 * space between two (\n(PD), which a paper may set (.nr PD 0), the
 * level of .RS and each level's indent, the sections' numbers.
 * Under the macros, what a paper writes of troff's own is Fill's.
 *
 * A table (.TS) is Tbl's, a picture (.PS) Pic's. Not read yet: an
 * equation (.EQ: passed over, and said); two columns (.2C: one here);
 * the cover sheets of Bell Labs' memoranda (.TM, .RP).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * ms is Mike Lesk's (Bell Labs, 1974): the first macro package made
 * for others to use, "manuscript" macros for the papers of the
 * Computing Science Research Center, where Unix was being written;
 * nearly every paper on Unix and on Plan 9 was typed in it. Its idea
 * is the one LaTeX has made familiar: say what a line is (a title, a
 * heading, a footnote) and let the package choose how it looks. Eric
 * Allman's -me (Berkeley, 1978) and the -mm of Bell Labs' other
 * departments are its rivals of the time. *)

(* a paper's text read; what was not understood is the Roff.t's to say *)
val read : Roff.t -> Doc.t

(* Claude Code

(* See Roff.mli *)

type device = Terminal | Typesetter
type line = Request of string * string list | Text of string

type t = {
  device : device;
  (* the lines not read yet, each with its number: a macro's lines are
   * put before the others *)
  mutable input : (int * string) list;
  mutable at : int;
  strings : (string, string) Hashtbl.t;
  registers : (string, float) Hashtbl.t;
  macros : (string, string list) Hashtbl.t;
  mutable font : Doc.font;
  mutable before : Doc.font;
  mutable size : int;
  mutable shift : int;
  (* what the last .ie found, for its .el *)
  mutable taken : bool;
  (* .ec: the character that starts an escape; none after .eo *)
  mutable escape : char option;
  (* .tr: a character written as another *)
  mutable translate : (string * string) list;
  (* .hc: a character that says where a word may be cut *)
  mutable hyphen : char option;
  (* \% was before the word being read: its hyphens are not places to
   * cut it *)
  mutable whole : bool;
  (* a text's width, in ens: \w's *)
  mutable measure : Doc.inline list -> float;
  (* a file's text, by its name: .so's, a picture's *)
  mutable loader : string -> string option;
  mutable complaints : (int * string) list;
}

(* a terminal's: every character one wide *)
let letters_width (text : Doc.inline list) : float =
  List.fold_left (fun w (i : Doc.inline) -> match i with Doc.Text (_, s) | Doc.Page (_, _, s) -> w +. float_of_int (Utf8.length (Doc.letters s)) | Doc.Break -> w) 0. text

let create (device : device) (source : string) : t =
  let lines = String.split_on_char '\n' (String.concat "" (String.split_on_char '\r' source)) in
  (* (a file ends with a newline: no line after it) *)
  let lines = match List.rev lines with "" :: rest -> List.rev rest | _ -> lines in
  { device; input = List.mapi (fun i l -> (i + 1, l)) lines; at = 0; strings = Hashtbl.create 16; registers = Hashtbl.create 16;
    macros = Hashtbl.create 16; font = Doc.Roman; before = Doc.Roman; size = 0; shift = 0; taken = false; escape = Some '\\'; translate = []; hyphen = None; whole = false; measure = letters_width; loader = (fun _ -> None); complaints = [] }

let device (t : t) = t.device
let set_loader (t : t) (f : string -> string option) = t.loader <- f
let load (t : t) (name : string) : string option = t.loader name
let set_measure (t : t) (f : Doc.inline list -> float) = t.measure <- f
let line_number (t : t) = t.at
let unknown (t : t) (what : string) = t.complaints <- (t.at, what) :: t.complaints
let complaints (t : t) = List.rev t.complaints
let register (t : t) (name : string) : float option = Hashtbl.find_opt t.registers name
let set_register (t : t) (name : string) (v : float) = Hashtbl.replace t.registers name v
let set_string (t : t) (name : string) (v : string) = Hashtbl.replace t.strings name v
let font (t : t) = t.font
let set_font (t : t) (f : Doc.font) = t.before <- t.font; t.font <- f
(* .ps: +2, -2, 10 (the text's own being 10), or nothing: as it was *)
let resize (t : t) (s : string) =
  if s = "" then t.size <- 0
  else
    match int_of_string_opt (if s.[0] = '+' then String.sub s 1 (String.length s - 1) else s) with
    | None -> ()
    | Some v -> if s.[0] = '+' || s.[0] = '-' then t.size <- t.size + v else t.size <- v - 10

let reset_style (t : t) = t.font <- Doc.Roman; t.before <- Doc.Roman; t.size <- 0; t.shift <- 0

let font_named (t : t) (name : string) : Doc.font =
  match name with
  | "R" | "1" -> Doc.Roman
  | "I" | "2" -> Doc.Italic
  | "B" | "3" -> Doc.Bold
  | "L" | "5" | "CW" | "4" -> Doc.Mono
  | "P" | "" -> t.before
  | _ -> unknown t ("font " ^ name); Doc.Roman

(* A character by its name: \(em *)

(* (troff's names, those the manual and the papers use and a few
 * around them; a terminal's page has the character itself) *)
let special (device : device) (name : string) : string option =
  match name with
  (* (a terminal has no dash longer than its hyphen: Plan 9's table for
   * one, tab.utf, says so) *)
  | "em" -> Some (if device = Terminal then "-" else "—") | "en" -> Some (if device = Terminal then "-" else "–")
  | "hy" -> Some "-" | "mi" -> Some "\xe2\x88\x92" | "pl" -> Some "+" | "eq" -> Some "="
  | "bu" -> Some "•" | "sq" -> Some "□" | "dg" -> Some "†" | "dd" -> Some "‡" | "ct" -> Some "¢" | "sc" -> Some "§"
  | "->" -> Some "→" | "<-" -> Some "←" | "ua" -> Some "↑" | "da" -> Some "↓"
  | "mu" -> Some "×" | "di" -> Some "÷" | "+-" -> Some "±" | "de" -> Some "°" | "sr" -> Some "√" | "rn" -> Some "‾"
  | "<=" -> Some "≤" | ">=" -> Some "≥" | "!=" -> Some "≠" | "==" -> Some "≡" | "~=" -> Some "≅" | "ap" -> Some "∼"
  | "if" -> Some "∞" | "pd" -> Some "∂" | "gr" -> Some "∇" | "no" -> Some "¬" | "is" -> Some "∫" | "pt" -> Some "∝"
  | "es" -> Some "∅" | "mo" -> Some "∈" | "ca" -> Some "∩" | "cu" -> Some "∪" | "sb" -> Some "⊂" | "sp" -> Some "⊃"
  | "**" -> Some "*" | "or" -> Some "|" | "br" -> Some "│" | "ul" -> Some "_" | "ru" -> Some "_" | "sl" -> Some "/"
  | "aa" -> Some (if device = Terminal then "'" else "´") | "ga" -> Some "`" | "fm" -> Some (if device = Terminal then "'" else "′")
  | "co" -> Some "©" | "rg" -> Some "®" | "tm" -> Some "™"
  | "14" -> Some "¼" | "12" -> Some "½" | "34" -> Some "¾" | "lh" -> Some "☜" | "rh" -> Some "☞" | "bs" -> Some "☎"
  | "ci" -> Some "○" | "bx" -> Some "■" | "fi" -> Some "fi" | "fl" -> Some "fl" | "ff" -> Some "ff"
  | "*a" -> Some "α" | "*b" -> Some "β" | "*g" -> Some "γ" | "*d" -> Some "δ" | "*e" -> Some "ε" | "*l" -> Some "λ"
  | "*m" -> Some "µ" | "*p" -> Some "π" | "*s" -> Some "σ" | "*t" -> Some "τ" | "*f" -> Some "φ" | "*w" -> Some "ω"
  | "*D" -> Some "Δ" | "*S" -> Some "Σ" | "*W" -> Some "Ω" | "*P" -> Some "Π"
  | _ -> None

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Numbers *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* troff counts in a unit as small as its device needs. A terminal's,
 * as nroff's: 240 to the inch, a letter 24 wide (ten to the inch), a
 * line 40 high (six to the inch). A typesetter's here: a tenth of a
 * point, the text 10 points on 12, so an en is 50 and a line 120. *)
let ens (t : t) (u : float) : float = u /. (if t.device = Terminal then 24. else 50.)
let lines (t : t) (u : float) : float = u /. (if t.device = Terminal then 40. else 120.)

let scale (t : t) (unit : char) : float =
  if t.device = Terminal then
    match unit with
    | 'i' -> 240. | 'n' | 'm' -> 24. | 'v' | 'P' -> 40. | 'p' -> 240. /. 72. | 'c' -> 240. /. 2.54 | _ -> 1.
  else
    match unit with
    | 'i' -> 720. | 'n' -> 50. | 'm' -> 100. | 'v' | 'P' -> 120. | 'p' -> 10. | 'c' -> 720. /. 2.54 | _ -> 1.

(*****************************************************************************)
(* What is in a line: words in fonts *)
(*****************************************************************************)

let is_digit (c : char) = c >= '0' && c <= '9'

(* [quoted s i]: what is between the character at i and the next one
 * like it ('...'), and where the text goes on *)
let quoted (s : string) (i : int) : string * int =
  if i >= String.length s then ("", i)
  else
    match String.index_from_opt s (i + 1) s.[i] with
    | Some j -> (String.sub s (i + 1) (j - i - 1), j + 1)
    | None -> (String.sub s (i + 1) (String.length s - i - 1), String.length s)

(* a name after an escape: one letter, or ( and two *)
let name_at (s : string) (i : int) : string * int =
  let n = String.length s in
  if i >= n then ("", i)
  else if s.[i] = '(' then (String.sub s (i + 1) (min 2 (n - i - 1)), min n (i + 3))
  else (String.sub s i 1, i + 1)

let continues (s : string) : bool = String.ends_with ~suffix:"\\c" s && not (String.ends_with ~suffix:"\\\\c" s)

let rec inlines (t : t) (s : string) : Doc.inline list =
  let n = String.length s in
  let out = ref [] and run = Buffer.create 64 in
  let style () : Doc.style = { font = t.font; size = t.size; shift = t.shift } in
  (* the letters so far are in the style as it was: said before it changes *)
  let flush () =
    if Buffer.length run > 0 then begin
      let text = Buffer.contents run in
      let text = if t.translate = [] then text else String.concat "" (List.map (fun c -> match List.assoc_opt c t.translate with Some d -> d | None -> c) (fst (Utf8.chars text))) in
      out := Doc.Text (style (), text) :: !out; Buffer.clear run
    end in
  let is_letter (c : char) = (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') in
  let rec go i =
    if i < n then
      if Some s.[i] = t.hyphen then begin
        if Buffer.length run > 0 && is_letter (Buffer.nth run (Buffer.length run - 1)) && i + 1 < n && is_letter s.[i + 1] then Buffer.add_string run "\xc2\xad";
        go (i + 1)
      end
      else if s.[i] = '-' && t.whole then begin Buffer.add_string run "\xe2\x80\x91"; go (i + 1) end
      else if s.[i] <> '\\' then begin if s.[i] = ' ' || s.[i] = '\t' then t.whole <- false; Buffer.add_char run s.[i]; go (i + 1) end
      else if i + 1 >= n then ()
      else
        let c = s.[i + 1] and j = i + 2 in
        match c with
        | '\\' | 'e' -> Buffer.add_char run '\\'; go j
        (* inside a word: where it may be cut, with a hyphen (U+00AD) *)
        | '%' when Buffer.length run > 0 && is_letter (Buffer.nth run (Buffer.length run - 1)) && j < n && is_letter s.[j] -> Buffer.add_string run "\xc2\xad"; go j
        (* before a word: it is not to be cut, and its hyphens are
         * written as the ones a line does not end after (U+2011) *)
        | '%' -> t.whole <- true; go j
        (* nothing, but something: after a dot, the sentence does not end
         * there (U+2060, the word joiner) *)
        | '&' -> Buffer.add_string run "\xe2\x81\xa0"; go j
        | '|' | '^' | '{' | '}' | 'z' | '!' -> go j
        | ' ' | '0' | '~' -> Buffer.add_string run "\xc2\xa0"; go j
        (* a minus (U+2212), not a hyphen: no line ends after it *)
        | '-' -> Buffer.add_string run "\xe2\x88\x92"; go j
        | 't' | 'a' -> Buffer.add_char run '\t'; go j
        | 'c' -> go j
        | '(' | 'C' ->
            let name, k = if c = '(' then name_at s (i + 1) else quoted s j in
            (match special t.device name with
             | Some ch -> Buffer.add_string run ch
             | None -> unknown t ("\\(" ^ name); Buffer.add_string run name);
            go k
        | 'f' ->
            let name, k = name_at s j in
            flush (); set_font t (font_named t name); go k
        | 's' ->
            (* \s8, \s-2, \s+2, \s0 (as it was), \s10: two digits when
             * the first is 1, 2 or 3 *)
            let sign, k = if j < n && (s.[j] = '-' || s.[j] = '+') then (Some s.[j], j + 1) else (None, j) in
            let digits = if k + 1 < n && is_digit s.[k] && is_digit s.[k + 1] && sign = None && s.[k] >= '1' && s.[k] <= '3' then 2 else if k < n && is_digit s.[k] then 1 else 0 in
            let v = if digits = 0 then 0 else int_of_string (String.sub s k digits) in
            flush ();
            (match sign with
             | Some '-' -> t.size <- t.size - v
             | Some _ -> t.size <- t.size + v
             | None -> t.size <- (if v = 0 then 0 else v - 10));
            go (k + digits)
        | 'u' -> flush (); t.shift <- t.shift + 1; go j
        | 'd' -> flush (); t.shift <- t.shift - 1; go j
        (* a motion, a line drawn, a width asked for nothing: passed over *)
        (* a move to the right: on a terminal, that many columns *)
        | 'h' ->
            let by, k = quoted s j in
            (* (on paper: as many spaces, each half an en in Times) *)
            let cols = if t.device = Terminal then int_of_float (ens t (number t 'm' by)) else int_of_float (Float.round (ens t (number t 'm' by) *. 2.)) in
            if cols > 0 then List.iter (fun _ -> Buffer.add_string run "\xc2\xa0") (List.init cols (fun x -> x));
            go k
        | 'v' | 'x' | 'l' | 'L' | 'w' | 'X' | 'b' | 'D' -> let _, k = quoted s j in go k
        | 'o' -> let both, k = quoted s j in List.iter (fun (x : Doc.inline) -> match x with Doc.Text (_, a) | Doc.Page (_, _, a) -> Buffer.add_string run a | Doc.Break -> ()) (inlines t both); go k
        | 'k' -> go (j + 1)
        | '*' | 'n' -> let _, k = name_at s j in go k
        | '"' -> ()
        | _ -> Buffer.add_char run c; go j in
  go 0; flush (); List.rev !out

(* troff's arithmetic: from left to right, no operator before another *)
and number (t : t) (unit : char) (s : string) : float =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec term i : float * int =
    if i >= n then (0., i)
    else if s.[i] = '(' then
      let v, j = expr (i + 1) in
      (v, if j < n && s.[j] = ')' then j + 1 else j)
    else if s.[i] = '-' then let v, j = term (i + 1) in (-.v, j)
    else if s.[i] = '+' then term (i + 1)
    else if s.[i] = '\\' && i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] = 'w' then
      let text, j = quoted s (i + 2) in
      let font = t.font and before = t.before and size = t.size in
      let w = t.measure (inlines t text) in
      t.font <- font; t.before <- before; t.size <- size;
      unit_at (w *. scale t 'n') j 'u'
    else
      let j = ref i in
      while !j < n && (is_digit s.[!j] || s.[!j] = '.') do incr j done;
      let v = match float_of_string_opt (String.sub s i (!j - i)) with Some v -> v | None -> 0. in
      unit_at v !j unit
  and unit_at (v : float) (j : int) (default : char) : float * int =
    if j < n && String.contains "inmvpcPu" s.[j] then (v *. scale t s.[j], j + 1) else (v *. scale t default, j)
  and expr i : float * int =
    let v, j = term i in
    more v j
  and more (v : float) (j : int) : float * int =
    if j >= n then (v, j)
    else
      match s.[j] with
      | '+' -> let w, k = term (j + 1) in more (v +. w) k
      | '-' -> let w, k = term (j + 1) in more (v -. w) k
      (* (a factor has no unit of its own: 2*3n is 6n) *)
      | '*' -> let w, k = term (j + 1) in more (v *. w /. scale t unit) k
      | '/' -> let w, k = term (j + 1) in more (if w = 0. then 0. else v /. (w /. scale t unit)) k
      | '>' -> let w, k = term (j + 1) in more (if v > w then 1. else 0.) k
      | '<' -> let w, k = term (j + 1) in more (if v < w then 1. else 0.) k
      | '=' -> let w, k = term (if j + 1 < n && s.[j + 1] = '=' then j + 2 else j + 1) in more (if v = w then 1. else 0.) k
      | _ -> (v, j) in
  fst (expr 0)

let inlines_in (t : t) (f : Doc.font) (s : string) : Doc.inline list =
  let font = t.font and before = t.before in
  t.font <- f;
  let r = inlines t s in
  t.font <- font; t.before <- before; r

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The lines *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* \*x and \nx put in the line, and a comment (a backslash and a
 * double quote, to the line's end) taken off *)
let interpolate (t : t) (s : string) : string =
  if not (String.contains s '\\') then s
  else begin
    let n = String.length s and out = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
    let rec go i =
      if i < n then
        if s.[i] <> '\\' || i + 1 >= n then begin Buffer.add_char out s.[i]; go (i + 1) end
        else
          match s.[i + 1] with
          | '"' -> ()
          | '*' ->
              let name, j = name_at s (i + 2) in
              (match Hashtbl.find_opt t.strings name with Some v -> Buffer.add_string out v | None -> ());
              go j
          | 'n' ->
              let name, j = name_at s (i + 2) in
              let v = match Hashtbl.find_opt t.registers name with Some v -> v | None -> 0. in
              Buffer.add_string out (string_of_int (int_of_float v));
              go j
          | c -> Buffer.add_char out '\\'; Buffer.add_char out c; go (i + 2) in
    go 0; Buffer.contents out
  end

let is_blank (c : char) = c = ' ' || c = '\t'

let rec skip_blanks (s : string) (i : int) : int = if i < String.length s && is_blank s.[i] then skip_blanks s (i + 1) else i

(* a request's name and what is after it *)
let split_request (s : string) : string * string =
  let n = String.length s in
  let i = skip_blanks s 1 in
  let j = ref i in
  while !j < n && !j < i + 2 && not (is_blank s.[!j]) do incr j done;
  (* (one tab after the name is the name's end, not the first argument's start) *)
  let k = if !j < n && s.[!j] = '\t' then !j + 1 else !j in
  (String.sub s i (!j - i), String.sub s k (n - k))

(* the arguments: split at the spaces (a tab is a letter here), but
 * not at one after a backslash; an argument that starts with a double
 * quote goes to the next one, "" in it being a quote *)
let arguments (s : string) : string list =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec spaces i = if i < n && s.[i] = ' ' then spaces (i + 1) else i in
  let rec go i (acc : string list) : string list =
    let i = spaces i in
    if i >= n then List.rev acc
    else if s.[i] = '"' then begin
      let b = Buffer.create 16 in
      let rec inside j =
        if j >= n then j
        else if s.[j] = '"' then if j + 1 < n && s.[j + 1] = '"' then begin Buffer.add_char b '"'; inside (j + 2) end else j + 1
        else begin Buffer.add_char b s.[j]; inside (j + 1) end in
      let j = inside (i + 1) in
      go j (Buffer.contents b :: acc)
    end
    else begin
      (* (a width asked, \w and its text between two quotes, is one
       * piece, spaces and all) *)
      let rec word j =
        if j >= n || s.[j] = ' ' then j
        else if s.[j] = '\\' && j + 2 < n && s.[j + 1] = 'w' then word (snd (quoted s (j + 2)))
        else if s.[j] = '\\' && j + 1 < n then word (j + 2)
        else word (j + 1) in
      let j = word i in
      go j (String.sub s i (j - i) :: acc)
    end in
  go 0 []

(* a macro's line with \$1 ... \$9 put in *)
let with_arguments (args : string list) (s : string) : string =
  let n = String.length s and out = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  let rec go i =
    if i < n then
      if i + 2 < n && s.[i] = '\\' && s.[i + 1] = '$' && is_digit s.[i + 2] then begin
        (match List.nth_opt args (Char.code s.[i + 2] - Char.code '1') with Some a -> Buffer.add_string out a | None -> ());
        go (i + 3)
      end
      else begin Buffer.add_char out s.[i]; go (i + 1) end in
  go 0; Buffer.contents out

(* \\ is \ in a macro's lines: they are read twice *)
let once (s : string) : string =
  let n = String.length s and out = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
  let rec go i =
    if i < n then
      if i + 1 < n && s.[i] = '\\' && s.[i + 1] = '\\' then begin Buffer.add_char out '\\'; go (i + 2) end
      else begin Buffer.add_char out s.[i]; go (i + 1) end in
  go 0; Buffer.contents out

(* how many \{ a text opens, less the \} it has *)
let braces (s : string) : int =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec go i (d : int) : int =
    if i + 1 >= n then d
    else if s.[i] = '\\' then go (i + 2) (if s.[i + 1] = '{' then d + 1 else if s.[i + 1] = '}' then d - 1 else d)
    else go (i + 1) d in
  go 0 0

let again (t : t) (s : string) : string = if String.contains s '\\' then interpolate t (once s) else s

let is_control (s : string) : bool = String.length s > 0 && (s.[0] = '.' || s.[0] = '\'')

(* the lines up to the one that is ".." (or .name), taken off the input *)
let until (t : t) (stop : string) : string list =
  let rec go (acc : string list) : string list =
    match t.input with
    | [] -> List.rev acc
    | (_, l) :: rest ->
        t.input <- rest;
        if is_control l && fst (split_request l) = stop then List.rev acc else go (l :: acc) in
  go []

(* a condition: what it says, and the rest of the line *)
let rec condition (t : t) (s : string) : bool * string =
  let n = String.length s in
  let i = skip_blanks s 0 in
  if i >= n then (false, "")
  else
    let rest j = String.sub s j (n - j) in
    match s.[i] with
    | '!' -> let c, r = condition t (rest (i + 1)) in (not c, r)
    | 't' -> (t.device = Typesetter, rest (i + 1))
    | 'n' -> (t.device = Terminal, rest (i + 1))
    | 'o' -> (true, rest (i + 1))
    | 'e' -> (false, rest (i + 1))
    | c when is_digit c || c = '(' || c = '-' || c = '\\' ->
        let j = ref i in
        while !j < n && not (is_blank s.[!j]) do incr j done;
        (number t 'u' (String.sub s i (!j - i)) > 0., rest !j)
    | c ->
        (* 'a'b': the two the same *)
        (match String.index_from_opt s (i + 1) c with
         | None -> (false, "")
         | Some j ->
             (match String.index_from_opt s (j + 1) c with
              | None -> (false, "")
              | Some k -> (String.sub s (i + 1) (j - i - 1) = String.sub s (j + 1) (k - j - 1), rest (k + 1))))

(* a line written with another escape character (.ec), or with none
 * (.eo), as it would be with the backslash *)
let canonical (t : t) (s : string) : string =
  match t.escape with
  | Some '\\' -> s
  | e ->
      let out = Buffer.create (String.length s) in
      String.iter (fun c -> if c = '\\' then Buffer.add_string out "\\\\" else if Some c = e then Buffer.add_char out '\\' else Buffer.add_char out c) s;
      Buffer.contents out

let rec next (t : t) : line option =
  match t.input with
  | [] -> None
  | (at, raw) :: rest ->
      t.input <- rest; t.at <- at; t.whole <- false;
      let raw = canonical t raw in
      if not (is_control raw) then
        (* (a line that only closes a conditional's lines is no text) *)
        if String.trim raw = "\\}" then next t else Some (Text (interpolate t raw))
      else
        let name, _ = split_request raw in
        (* (a macro's lines are kept as they are: read when it is called) *)
        if name = "de" || name = "am" || name = "ig" then begin
          let args = arguments (snd (split_request (interpolate t raw))) in
          let stop = match (name, args) with ("ig", s :: _) | (_, _ :: s :: _) -> s | _ -> "." in
          let body = until t stop in
          (match (name, args) with
           | "de", m :: _ -> Hashtbl.replace t.macros m (List.map once body)
           | "am", _ -> unknown t ".am"
           | _ -> ());
          next t
        end
        else
          let line = interpolate t raw in
          let name, after = split_request line in
          let args () = arguments after in
          match name with
          | "" | "''" | "\\}" -> next t
          | "ds" | "as" ->
              let i = skip_blanks after 0 in
              let j = ref i in
              while !j < String.length after && not (is_blank after.[!j]) do incr j done;
              let k = skip_blanks after !j in
              let k = if k < String.length after && after.[k] = '"' then k + 1 else k in
              let v = String.sub after k (String.length after - k) and x = String.sub after i (!j - i) in
              (* (a string is read as a macro's lines are: \\ is \) *)
              let v = once v in
              Hashtbl.replace t.strings x (if name = "as" then (match Hashtbl.find_opt t.strings x with Some old -> old ^ v | None -> v) else v);
              next t
          | "nr" ->
              (match args () with
               | x :: v :: _ ->
                   let old = match Hashtbl.find_opt t.registers x with Some o -> o | None -> 0. in
                   let relative = String.length v > 0 && (v.[0] = '+' || v.[0] = '-') in
                   let v = number t 'u' v in
                   Hashtbl.replace t.registers x (if relative then old +. v else v)
               | _ -> ());
              next t
          | "so" ->
              (* another file's lines, here *)
              (match (match args () with name :: _ -> t.loader name | [] -> None) with
               | Some text ->
                   let lines = String.split_on_char '\n' (String.concat "" (String.split_on_char '\r' text)) in
                   let lines = match List.rev lines with "" :: rest -> List.rev rest | _ -> lines in
                   t.input <- List.map (fun l -> (at, l)) lines @ t.input
               | None -> unknown t ".so");
              next t
          | "ec" -> t.escape <- Some (match args () with a :: _ when a <> "" -> a.[0] | _ -> '\\'); next t
          | "eo" -> t.escape <- None; next t
          | "hc" -> t.hyphen <- (match args () with a :: _ when a <> "" -> Some a.[0] | _ -> None); next t
          | "tr" ->
              let chars = fst (Utf8.chars (String.trim after)) in
              let rec pairs (l : string list) = match l with a :: b :: rest -> (a, b) :: pairs rest | [ a ] -> [ (a, " ") ] | [] -> [] in
              t.translate <- pairs chars @ t.translate; next t
          | "rm" -> List.iter (fun m -> Hashtbl.remove t.macros m; Hashtbl.remove t.strings m) (args ()); next t
          | "if" | "ie" | "el" ->
              let yes, body = if name = "el" then (not t.taken, after) else condition t after in
              if name = "ie" then t.taken <- yes;
              let body = let i = skip_blanks body 0 in String.sub body i (String.length body - i) in
              if yes then begin
                let body = if String.starts_with ~prefix:"\\{" body then String.sub body 2 (String.length body - 2) else body in
                if String.trim body <> "" then t.input <- (at, body) :: t.input
              end
              else begin
                (* the lines to the \} that closes this one's \{ *)
                let rec skip (d : int) = if d > 0 then match t.input with [] -> () | (_, l) :: rest -> t.input <- rest; skip (d + braces l) in
                skip (braces body)
              end;
              next t
          | _ ->
              (match Hashtbl.find_opt t.macros name with
               | Some body ->
                   let args = args () in
                   t.input <- List.map (fun l -> (at, with_arguments args l)) body @ t.input;
                   next t
               | None -> Some (Request (name, args ())))
typesetting/troff/roff/Roff.mli
6721
(* Roff: troff's input read as lines -- which are requests, which are
 * text -- and a line of text turned into words in fonts. What the
 * macro packages' readers (Man) stand on; not troff.
 *
 *   .TP 10          Request ("TP", ["10"])
 *   .B -c           Request ("B", ["-c"])
 *   Complement      Text "Complement"
 *   .IR string1 :   Request ("IR", ["string1"; ":"])
 *
 * A line that starts with a dot (or a quote) is a request: a name of
 * one or two letters, then its arguments, split at the spaces, an
 * argument with spaces in it between double quotes. Any other line is
 * text, with escapes in it: \fI a font, \(em a character by its name,
 * \- a minus, \& nothing at all (so that a line can start with a dot
 * and be text).
 *
 * What is done here, before a package sees the line, is the part of
 * troff's language that a page's author uses to write his own
 * shorthand, and nothing of what the packages themselves were written
 * in:
 *
 *   .de XX ... ..     a macro of the page: its lines, read again each
 *                     time .XX is met, \$1 its first argument
 *   .ds x text        a string, \*x                 (\*(xx: two letters)
 *   .nr x 5           a register, \nx               (\n(xx)
 *   .if t ...         a line for the typesetter only; .if n: for a
 *   .ie / .el         terminal; 'a'b': two strings the same; a number
 *                     more than 0. \{ and \} round several lines
 *   .ig ... ..        lines passed over
 *   .ec c  .eo        another character than the backslash, or none
 *   .tr ab            a written as b
 *   .hc c             c in a word: where it may be cut
 *   \ and a double quote: a comment, to the line's end
 *
 * A text's words come out in Doc's terms, and what troff says by an
 * escape that is not a letter is said by the character Unicode has
 * for it, which the layout knows (Doc.mli lists them):
 *
 *   \ and a space: one the line is not broken at  U+00A0
 *   \-     a minus, not a hyphen                  U+2212
 *   \%     in a word: where it may be cut         U+00AD
 *          before one: its hyphens are not        U+2011
 *   \&     nothing; no sentence ends after it     U+2060
 *
 * Not done, and said so by name ([unknown]): text set aside and brought
 * back (.di), a macro run when the page reaches a line (.wh), a second
 * set of parameters (.ev), a macro added to (.am). The packages are
 * written with those -- tmac.an's .TP sets its tag aside to measure
 * it -- which is why the packages are not run here but read as cases
 * (docs/plans/done/plan_typesetting.md).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The dot at the start of a line is older than Unix: RUNOFF, Jerome
 * Saltzer's at MIT for CTSS (1964), had ".ctr" and ".sp" between the
 * lines of a text, to be "run off" on a typewriter. roff was its
 * descendant on the first Unix (1971), and what the PDP-11 was asked
 * for: a system to prepare the patent department's applications.
 * nroff ("new roff") was Joe Ossanna's of 1972, with the macros and
 * the registers, and troff (1973) the same language for a
 * phototypesetter. A name is two letters: two bytes, one word of the
 * PDP-11. *)

(* who reads the page: a page says ".if n" and ".if t", and a length
 * is not the same on the two (an inch is 10 ens of a terminal's
 * letters, 14.4 of a text of 10 points) *)
type device = Terminal | Typesetter

type line =
  (* its name without the dot, its arguments as they were written:
   * [inlines] and [number] read what is in them *)
  | Request of string * string list
  | Text of string

type t

(* [create device source]: a file's text, to be read line by line *)
val create : device -> string -> t

val device : t -> device

(* the next line that is not this module's own business; none at the
 * end *)
val next : t -> line option

(* the number of the source's line that [next] last gave (a macro's
 * lines have the number of the line that called it) *)
val line_number : t -> int

(*****************************************************************************)
(* What is in a line *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a text, or an argument, as words in the font and the size that the
 * escapes before them said; the font stays for the next call *)
val inlines : t -> string -> Doc.inline list

(* the same in one font, of an argument that is to be set in it:
 * the font is as it was after *)
val inlines_in : t -> Doc.font -> string -> Doc.inline list

val font : t -> Doc.font
val set_font : t -> Doc.font -> unit

(* .ps's argument: +2, -2, 10, or nothing (the text's own size) *)
val resize : t -> string -> unit

(* a register's value, in troff's basic units if it is a length; none
 * if it was never set *)
val register : t -> string -> float option

(* back to the text's own font and size *)
val reset_style : t -> unit

(* the font of a name as \f and .ft have it: I, 2, CW, P (the one
 * before) *)
val font_named : t -> string -> Doc.font

(* does the line end with \c: what follows goes on the same word *)
val continues : string -> bool

(* [number t unit text]: a length as troff writes it, 5n, 1.5i, or the
 * width of a text and 2n more (\w and the text between two quotes,
 * then u+2n), in troff's basic units; [unit] is the one of a
 * number with none ('n', 'm', 'v'). [ens] and [lines] are the two
 * ways out of the basic units. *)
val number : t -> char -> string -> float
val ens : t -> float -> float
val lines : t -> float -> float

(* how a file is read by its name, for .so and for a picture kept in
 * a file of its own: nothing is read until a program that may open
 * files says how ([load] gives none) *)
val set_loader : t -> (string -> string option) -> unit
val load : t -> string -> string option

(* how wide a text is, in ens, for \w: every character one, until a
 * writer that has fonts says otherwise *)
val set_measure : t -> (Doc.inline list -> float) -> unit

(* a text read a second time, as a macro's lines are: its \\ are \, and
 * the strings and registers named after them are put in. A table's
 * data is read so by troff, tbl having put it inside a macro. *)
val again : t -> string -> string

(* the registers and the strings: a package has its own (\n(PD) *)
val set_register : t -> string -> float -> unit
val set_string : t -> string -> string -> unit

(*****************************************************************************)

(* [unknown t what]: said by a package of a request it does not know *)
val unknown : t -> string -> unit

(* each, with its line, in the page's order *)
val complaints : t -> (int * string) list
