(* See Tbl.mli *)

(* a column's format in a row: its letter, its font, its size, its width *)
type column = { key : char; font : string; size : int; width : float }

(* a line of formats: "c s s", "lfCWp-2 | l w(3i)" *)
let formats (roff : Roff.t) (s : string) : column list =
  let n = String.length s in
  let rec go i (acc : column list) : column list =
    if i >= n then List.rev acc
    else
      let c = Char.lowercase_ascii s.[i] in
      if String.contains "lrcnas^" c then go (i + 1) ({ key = (if c = 'a' then 'l' else c); font = ""; size = 0; width = 0. } :: acc)
      else
        match acc with
        | [] -> go (i + 1) acc
        | col :: rest ->
            if c = 'f' then begin
              (* fB, fCW, f(CW) *)
              let j = if i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] = '(' then i + 2 else i + 1 in
              let k = ref j in
              while !k < n && !k < j + 2 && ((s.[!k] >= 'A' && s.[!k] <= 'Z') || (s.[!k] >= '0' && s.[!k] <= '9')) do incr k done;
              go (if !k < n && s.[!k] = ')' then !k + 1 else !k) ({ col with font = String.sub s j (!k - j) } :: rest)
            end
            else if c = 'b' then go (i + 1) ({ col with font = "B" } :: rest)
            else if c = 'i' then go (i + 1) ({ col with font = "I" } :: rest)
            else if c = 'p' || c = 'v' then begin
              let k = ref (i + 1) in
              while !k < n && (s.[!k] = '-' || s.[!k] = '+' || (s.[!k] >= '0' && s.[!k] <= '9')) do incr k done;
              let v = match int_of_string_opt (String.sub s (i + 1) (!k - i - 1)) with Some v -> v | None -> 0 in
              go !k (if c = 'p' then { col with size = v } :: rest else acc)
            end
            else if c = 'w' then begin
              let j, k =
                if i + 1 < n && s.[i + 1] = '(' then (i + 2, match String.index_from_opt s i ')' with Some k -> k | None -> n)
                else begin
                  let k = ref (i + 1) in
                  while !k < n && ((s.[!k] >= '0' && s.[!k] <= '9') || s.[!k] = '.') do incr k done;
                  (i + 1, !k)
                end in
              go (min n (k + 1)) ({ col with width = Roff.ens roff (Roff.number roff 'n' (String.sub s j (k - j))) } :: rest)
            end
            else go (i + 1) acc in
  go 0 []

let read (roff : Roff.t) (block : unit -> Doc.inline list * string) : Doc.table =
  let centered = ref false and boxed = ref false and tab = ref '\t' in
  let rows = ref [] and widths = ref [] in
  (* the formats not used yet, and the one in use when they are all used *)
  let waiting = ref [] and current = ref [] in
  (* reading formats, to the line that ends with a dot *)
  let in_formats = ref true and first = ref true in
  let format_line (s : string) =
    let s = String.trim s in
    if !first && String.length s > 0 && s.[String.length s - 1] = ';' then
      List.iter (fun o ->
        let o = String.trim o in
        if o = "center" then centered := true
        else if o = "box" || o = "allbox" || o = "doublebox" then boxed := true
        else if String.length o >= 6 && String.sub o 0 4 = "tab(" then tab := o.[4])
        (String.split_on_char ',' (String.concat "," (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.sub s 0 (String.length s - 1)))))
    else begin
      let last = String.length s > 0 && s.[String.length s - 1] = '.' in
      let s = if last then String.sub s 0 (String.length s - 1) else s in
      (* (several rows' formats on one line, with commas) *)
      List.iter (fun part -> let f = formats roff part in if f <> [] then waiting := !waiting @ [ f ]) (String.split_on_char ',' s);
      if last then in_formats := false
    end;
    first := false in
  (* a row's cells from a line of data, each in its column's format *)
  let data (s : string) =
    let format = match !waiting with f :: rest -> waiting := rest; current := f; f | [] -> !current in
    (* (a width said for a column, in whatever row's format) *)
    List.iteri (fun (k : int) (c : column) ->
      if c.width > 0. then begin
        while List.length !widths <= k do widths := !widths @ [ 0. ] done;
        widths := List.mapi (fun i w -> if i = k then c.width else w) !widths
      end) format;
    let rec cells (texts : string list) (format : column list) (acc : Doc.cell list) : Doc.cell list =
      match format with
      | [] -> List.rev acc
      | col :: rest ->
          let text, texts = match texts with t :: more -> (t, more) | [] -> ("", []) in
          (* (the columns after this one that it goes across) *)
          let rec spans (l : column list) (k : int) = match l with { key = 's'; _ } :: more -> spans more (k + 1) | _ -> (k, l) in
          let span, rest = spans rest 1 in
          let align = match col.key with 'r' -> Doc.Right | 'c' -> Doc.Center | 'n' -> Doc.Numeric | _ -> Doc.Left in
          let styled (words : Doc.inline list) : Doc.inline list =
            if col.size = 0 then words
            else List.map (fun (w : Doc.inline) -> match w with Doc.Text (st, t) -> Doc.Text ({ st with size = st.size + col.size }, t) | Doc.Break | Doc.Page _ -> w) words in
          let words (t : string) = styled (if col.font = "" then Roff.inlines roff t else Roff.inlines_in roff (Roff.font_named roff col.font) t) in
          if String.length text >= 2 && String.sub text (String.length text - 2) 2 = "T{" then begin
            (* a text of several lines; what is after its T} are the
             * row's next cells *)
            let body, after = block () in
            let after = if String.length after > 0 && after.[0] = !tab then String.sub after 1 (String.length after - 1) else after in
            let more = if after = "" then [] else String.split_on_char !tab after in
            cells (more @ texts) rest ({ align = Doc.Left; span; filled = true; body = styled body } :: acc)
          end
          else
            let text = if text = "\\^" || text = "_" || text = "\\_" || col.key = '^' then "" else text in
            cells texts rest ({ align; span; filled = false; body = words text } :: acc) in
    rows := Doc.Cells (cells (String.split_on_char !tab s) format []) :: !rows in
  let rec go () =
    match Roff.next roff with
    | None -> ()
    | Some (Roff.Request ("TE", _)) -> ()
    | Some (Roff.Request ("T&", _)) -> in_formats := true; waiting := []; go ()
    | Some (Roff.Request ("ft", a :: _)) -> Roff.set_font roff (Roff.font_named roff a); go ()
    | Some (Roff.Request (_, _)) -> go ()
    | Some (Roff.Text s) ->
        if !in_formats then format_line s
        else if s = "_" || s = "=" then rows := Doc.Rule :: !rows
        else data (Roff.again roff s);
        go () in
  go ();
  Roff.reset_style roff;
  { centered = !centered; boxed = !boxed; widths = !widths; rows = List.rev !rows }
typesetting/troff/roff/Tbl.mli
1830
(* Tbl: a table read -- what is between .TS and .TE, tbl's language.
 *
 *   .TS
 *   center, box;          the whole table: in the middle, in a box
 *   c s s                 its rows' formats, one line a row, the last
 *   l n n.                for the rows that are left: a column is l
 *   Table 1               (left), r, c (centered), n (numbers, their
 *   _                     points one under the other), or s (the cell
 *   Context switch	39	150     before it goes on across this one)
 *   System call	6	36
 *   .TE
 *
 * A row of the data is its cells with a tab between; a line that is
 * "_" or "=" is a rule. After a column's letter: fB or fCW its font,
 * w(1i) its width, p-2 its size; "|" between two is a line down the
 * table. A cell that ends with T{ is a text of several lines, to its
 * T}: filled in the column's width. .T& changes the formats part way.
 *
 * Read: the options center, box (allbox and doublebox as box) and
 * tab(c); the letters l r c n s (a as l, ^ as an empty cell), f, w
 * and p. Not kept: the lines down the table, a column's height or
 * space said by a number.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * tbl is Mike Lesk's (Bell Labs, 1975), a program that reads a
 * document, turns each table into the troff that draws it and leaves
 * the rest as it is: with eqn, of the year before, the first of the
 * "preprocessors", the way Unix had of adding a language to troff
 * without touching troff. Here a table is a value in the document,
 * read by the same pass. *)

(* [read roff block]: called after a .TS, reads to its .TE. [block]
 * reads a text block's lines, to the line that starts with T}, and
 * gives its words and what follows T} on that line: it is the
 * package's, a text block having the package's macros in it. *)
val read : Roff.t -> (unit -> Doc.inline list * string) -> Doc.table
utilities/archive/Gunzip.ml
7899
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-gunzip: Plan 9's gunzip (principia's
 * utilities/archive/gzip/gunzip.c): each file uncompressed into one of
 * the current directory, its name without its .gz (a .tgz's: .tar);
 * no file, the standard input to the standard output. -c: to the
 * standard output; -t: nothing written, the names of what is inside
 * listed (-v: with each one's length and time); -v otherwise: what is
 * uncompressed to what; -T: the output given the time in the header.
 *
 * A file may be several gzip files end to end (cat a.gz b.gz), each
 * with its header and its trailer (Gzip's), all uncompressed in turn
 * into the one output. What follows the last one and is not one is
 * said and ignored: the bytes before it are good. When the first one
 * is bad, the output is removed.
 *
 * References: gzip(1) of Plan 9's manual; RFC 1952. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

exception Usage
(* the message of a member that cannot be read *)
exception Bad of string

(* Plan 9's ctime: GMT here, as mini-date's *)
let ctime (t : float) =
  let tm : Unix.tm = Unix.gmtime t in
  Printf.sprintf "%s %s %2d %02d:%02d:%02d GMT %d\n" (String.sub "SunMonTueWedThuFriSat" (3 * tm.tm_wday) 3)
    (String.sub "JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec" (3 * tm.tm_mon) 3) tm.tm_mday tm.tm_hour tm.tm_min tm.tm_sec (tm.tm_year + 1900)

(* a member: its name, its time, its bytes, and where the next one starts *)
let member (s : string) (pos : int) =
  let p = ref pos in
  let get1 () = if !p >= String.length s then raise (Bad "unexpected eof reading file information") else (incr p; Char.code s.[!p - 1]) in
  (* (hi, lo): an int has 31 bits where mini-ml builds for arm *)
  let get4 () = let a = get1 () in let b = get1 () in let c = get1 () in let d = get1 () in (d lsl 8) lor c, (b lsl 8) lor a in
  if get1 () <> 0x1f || get1 () <> 0x8b then raise (Bad "bad gzip file magic");
  if get1 () <> 8 then raise (Bad "unknown compression type");
  let flag = get1 () in
  let reserved = flag land lnot 0x1f <> 0 in
  let hi, lo = get4 () in
  let mtime = float_of_int hi *. 65536. +. float_of_int lo in
  ignore (get1 ()); ignore (get1 ());
  if flag land 4 <> 0 then for _i = 1 to get1 () do ignore (get1 ()) done;
  let zstring () = let b = Buffer.create 32 in let rec go () = match get1 () with 0 -> Buffer.contents b | c -> Buffer.add_char b (Char.chr c); go () in go () in
  let name = if flag land 8 <> 0 then zstring () else "<unnamed file>" in
  if flag land 16 <> 0 then ignore (zstring ());
  if flag land 2 <> 0 then (ignore (get1 ()); ignore (get1 ()));
  let data, next = try Zlib.inflate_blocks_at !p s with Zlib.Corrupt m | Invalid_argument m -> raise (Bad ("inflate failed: " ^ m)) in
  p := next;
  if get4 () <> Zlib.crc32_halves data ~pos:0 ~len:(String.length data) then raise (Bad "crc mismatch");
  let hi, lo = get4 () in
  (* (the length's low 32 bits, as the file has them) *)
  let n = String.length data in
  if (hi, lo) <> ((n lsr 16) land 0xffff, n land 0xffff) then
    raise (Bad (Printf.sprintf "bad output length: expected %d got %.0f" n (float_of_int hi *. 65536. +. float_of_int lo)));
  reserved, name, mtime, data, !p

let read_all fd =
  let b = Buffer.create 65536 and chunk = Bytes.create 65536 in
  let rec go () = match Unix.read fd chunk 0 65536 with 0 -> Buffer.contents b | n -> Buffer.add_subbytes b chunk 0 n; go () in
  go ()

type options = { verbose : bool; table : bool; settimes : bool }

(* the members of [s] one after the other into [ofd] (None: -t); false
 * at a bad one. [delfile]: the output to remove when the first is bad *)
let gunzip (caps : < caps; .. >) o ~infile ~ofile ~delfile (ofd : Unix.file_descr option) (s : string) =
  let rec go pos =
    if pos >= String.length s then true
    else match member s pos with
      | exception Bad m ->
          if pos > 0 then Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "gunzip: %s: corrupted data after byte %d ignored\n" infile pos)
          else begin
            Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "gunzip: %s: %s\n" infile m);
            Option.iter (fun f -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "gunzip: removing output file %s\n" f); FS.remove_any caps f) delfile
          end;
          false
      | reserved, name, mtime, data, next ->
          if reserved then Console.eprint caps "gunzip: reserved flags set, data may not be decompressed correctly\n";
          if not o.table && o.verbose then Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "extracting %s to %s\n" name ofile);
          Option.iter (fun fd -> ignore (Unix.write_substring fd data 0 (String.length data))) ofd;
          if o.table then
            Console.print caps (if o.verbose then Printf.sprintf "%-32s %10d %s" name (String.length data) (ctime mtime) else name ^ "\n")
          else if o.settimes && mtime <> 0. && delfile <> None then Sys_plan9.set_mtime caps ofile mtime;
          go next in
  go 0

(* one file; false when it could not be *)
let gunzipf (caps : < caps; .. >) o ~stdout file =
  let fail fmt = Printf.ksprintf (fun s -> Console.eprint caps s; false) fmt in
  match FS.open_in_fd caps file with
  | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> fail "gunzip: can't open %s: %s\n" file (Unix.error_message e)
  | ifd ->
      let s = Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close ifd) (fun () -> read_all ifd) in
      if String.length s < 3 || String.sub s 0 3 <> "\x1f\x8b\x08" then fail "gunzip: %s is not a gzip deflate file\n" file
      else if o.table then gunzip caps o ~infile:file ~ofile:"" ~delfile:None None s
      else if stdout then gunzip caps o ~infile:file ~ofile:"<stdout>" ~delfile:None (Some (Console.stdout_fd caps)) s
      else
        let base = Filename.basename file in
        let ofile =
          if Filename.check_suffix base ".gz" && base <> ".gz" then Some (Filename.chop_suffix base ".gz")
          else if Filename.check_suffix base ".tgz" then Some (Filename.chop_suffix base ".tgz" ^ ".tar")
          else if base = file then None
          else Some base in
        match ofile with
        | None -> fail "gunzip: can't overwrite %s\n" file
        | Some ofile ->
            match FS.open_out_fd caps ofile 0o666 with
            | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> fail "gunzip: can't create %s: %s\n" ofile (Unix.error_message e)
            | ofd -> Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close ofd) (fun () ->
                gunzip caps o ~infile:file ~ofile ~delfile:(Some ofile) (Some ofd) s)

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let verbose = ref false and table = ref false and settimes = ref false and stdout = ref false in
  try
    let rec options = function
      | "--" :: rest -> rest
      | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' ->
          String.iteri (fun k c -> if k > 0 then match c with
            | 'v' -> verbose := true | 'c' -> stdout := true | 't' -> table := true | 'T' -> settimes := true | 'D' -> ()
            | _ -> raise Usage) a;
          options rest
      | rest -> rest in
    let ok = match options (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) with
      | [] ->
          let o = { verbose = !verbose; table = !table; settimes = false } in
          gunzip caps o ~infile:"<stdin>" ~ofile:"<stdout>" ~delfile:None
            (if !table then None else Some (Console.stdout_fd caps)) (read_all (Console.stdin_fd caps))
      | files ->
          let o = { verbose = !verbose; table = !table; settimes = !settimes && not !stdout } in
          List.fold_left (fun ok f -> gunzipf caps o ~stdout:!stdout f && ok) true files in
    if ok then Exit.OK else Exit.Err "errors"
  with Usage -> Console.eprint caps "usage: gunzip [-ctvTD] [file ....]\n"; Exit.Err "usage"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
utilities/archive/Gzip.ml
4429
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-gzip: Plan 9's gzip (principia's utilities/archive/gzip/gzip.c):
 * each file compressed into one of the current directory, its name
 * with .gz after (a .tar's: .tgz), the file itself kept; no file, the
 * standard input to the standard output. -c: to the standard output;
 * -v: what is compressed to what, on the standard error; -1 to -9,
 * the level, taken.
 *
 * The file is RFC 1952's, deflate's blocks in an envelope (Zlib.gzip):
 *
 *    1f 8b 08 | flags | mtime (4) | 00 03 | name 00 | blocks | crc32 | length
 *
 * the flags saying whether a name follows (a file's, not the standard
 * input's), the time the file's (the standard input's: now), 03 Unix
 * as the system (gzip.h's GZOSINFERNO), the CRC-32 and the length of
 * the bytes before compression, each four bytes, the low first.
 *
 * wib:
 * The header and the trailer are gzip.c's bytes, the blocks are not:
 * Zlib's deflate writes fixed codes only and ignores the level, where
 * libflate's writes a block's own codes. Any gunzip reads both; ours
 * are bigger (Zlib.mli).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Jean-loup Gailly wrote gzip in 1992 for the GNU project, to replace
 * Unix's compress, whose LZW was patented; Mark Adler wrote its
 * decompressor. Plan 9's is Russ Cox's, over libflate.
 *
 * References: gzip(1) of Plan 9's manual; P. Deutsch, RFC 1952, "GZIP
 * file format specification version 4.3" (1996). *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.clock >

exception Usage

(* a time's two halves of 16 bits: Zlib.gzip's *)
let halves (t : float) = int_of_float (t /. 65536.), int_of_float (Float.rem t 65536.)

(* everything on [fd] *)
let read_all fd =
  let b = Buffer.create 65536 and chunk = Bytes.create 65536 in
  let rec go () = match Unix.read fd chunk 0 65536 with 0 -> Buffer.contents b | n -> Buffer.add_subbytes b chunk 0 n; go () in
  go ()

let write_all fd s = ignore (Unix.write_substring fd s 0 (String.length s))

(* one file; false when it could not be *)
let gzipf (caps : < caps; .. >) ~verbose ~stdout file =
  let fail fmt = Printf.ksprintf (fun s -> Console.eprint caps s; false) fmt in
  match FS.open_in_fd caps file with
  | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> fail "gzip: can't open %s: %s\n" file (Unix.error_message e)
  | ifd ->
      Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close ifd) (fun () ->
        let d : Sys_plan9.dir = Sys_plan9.dirstat caps file in
        if d.qid_type land Sys_plan9.dmdir <> 0 then fail "gzip: can't compress a directory\n"
        else
          let base = Filename.basename file in
          let ofile =
            if stdout then "<stdout>"
            else if Filename.check_suffix base ".tar" && base <> ".tar" then Filename.chop_suffix base ".tar" ^ ".tgz"
            else base ^ ".gz" in
          match if stdout then Console.stdout_fd caps else FS.open_out_fd caps ofile 0o666 with
          | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> fail "gzip: can't open %s: %s\n" ofile (Unix.error_message e)
          | ofd ->
              if verbose then Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "compressing %s to %s\n" file ofile);
              write_all ofd (Zlib.gzip (Some file) (halves d.mtime) (read_all ifd));
              if not stdout then Unix.close ofd;
              true)

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let verbose = ref false and stdout = ref false in
  try
    let rec options = function
      | "--" :: rest -> rest
      | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' ->
          String.iteri (fun k c -> if k > 0 then match c with
            | 'v' -> verbose := true | 'c' -> stdout := true | 'D' | '1' .. '9' -> () | _ -> raise Usage) a;
          options rest
      | rest -> rest in
    match options (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) with
    | [] ->
        write_all (Console.stdout_fd caps) (Zlib.gzip None (halves (Float.round (CapUnix.time caps ()))) (read_all (Console.stdin_fd caps)));
        Exit.OK
    | files ->
        let ok = List.fold_left (fun ok f -> gzipf caps ~verbose:!verbose ~stdout:!stdout f && ok) true files in
        if ok then Exit.OK else Exit.Err "errors"
  with Usage -> Console.eprint caps "usage: gzip [-vcD] [-1-9] [file ...]\n"; Exit.Err "usage"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
utilities/archive/Tar.ml
23579
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-tar: Plan 9's tar (principia's utilities/archive/tar/tar.c), its
 * archives byte for byte: files and directories, whole trees, in one
 * file, and back.
 *
 *    tar cf a.tar dir file    a new archive of them (c), in a file (f)
 *    tar rf a.tar more        added at the end of one (r)
 *    tar tvf a.tar            what is in it (t), each line long (v)
 *    tar xf a.tar [name...]   taken out (x): all, or what is under names
 *
 * The first argument is the letters, a dash or not; f, u and g take
 * the letters' rest or the next argument (the archive, an owner's
 * number, a group's). No f: the standard input or output. z:
 * compressed by gzip, and when reading, so is a .tgz or .tar.gz. k: a
 * file that is there kept; T: the archive's times and modes given to
 * what is taken out; R: names from / kept as they are (else under the
 * current directory); P: the old format (no owners' names, names of
 * 100 characters at most); s: past a bad header to the next good one;
 * v with c, r or x: the names on the standard error.
 *
 * The archive is blocks of 512 bytes: for each file a header, then
 * its bytes, the last block's rest zeros; two zero blocks end it, and
 * it is written in records of 20 blocks, the last one filled with
 * zeros (a tape's records once):
 *
 *    | f1's header | f1's bytes | sub/'s header | sub/x's | x's bytes | 0 | 0 | 0...
 *
 * A header is text, each number in octal: the name (100 bytes), the
 * mode, the owners' numbers, the length, the time, the checksum (the
 * sum of the header's bytes, its own field counted as spaces), the
 * type (5: a directory, its name ending with /), then POSIX's ustar
 * part: the owners' names, and a prefix of 155 bytes for a longer
 * name, split at a slash.
 *
 * wib:
 * The archive is read and written in memory, whole, where tar.c reads
 * and writes a record at a time: an archive must fit. -z is gzip's
 * only (Zlib's, in the process: tar.c runs gzip, compress or bzip2 in
 * a pipe). tar.c's tv prints its modes by %M, which its main leaves
 * uninstalled (an XXX), and its lines come out garbled: here they are
 * what it meant (mini-ls's modes). -i is taken and does nothing: a
 * read error ends the program.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * tar, the tape archiver, came with Unix's seventh edition (1979),
 * after tp, and its header of 1979 is still the start of every .tar;
 * POSIX (1988) added the ustar part. Plan 9's is Geoff Collyer's.
 *
 * References: tar(1) of Plan 9's manual; IEEE Std 1003.1's pax, the
 * ustar format. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.readdir; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr; Cap.clock >

exception Usage
(* sysfatal: the words said, and the process's last ones *)
exception Fatal of string
(* past the archive's last record (tar.c's refill's nil) *)
exception End

let tblock = 512
let record = 20 * tblock

type verb = Toc | Xtract | Replace

type options = {
  argv0 : string; say : string -> unit;
  mutable verb : verb option; mutable create : bool; mutable verbose : bool; mutable compress : bool;
  mutable file : string option; mutable keep : bool; mutable settime : bool; mutable posix : bool;
  mutable relative : bool; mutable resync : bool; mutable uid : int; mutable gid : int;
}

let arname o = match o.file with Some f -> f | None -> "archive"

let write_all fd s = ignore (Unix.write_substring fd s 0 (String.length s))

let read_all fd =
  let b = Buffer.create 65536 and chunk = Bytes.create 65536 in
  let rec go () = match Unix.read fd chunk 0 65536 with 0 -> Buffer.contents b | n -> Buffer.add_subbytes b chunk 0 n; go () in
  go ()

(* a number's octal digits; a float: a time is past an int's 31 bits
 * where mini-ml builds for arm *)
let rec digits (v : float) acc =
  let q = Float.trunc (v /. 8.) in
  let acc = string_of_int (int_of_float (v -. (q *. 8.))) ^ acc in
  if q = 0. then acc else digits q acc
(* %wo: [w] characters, spaces before *)
let octal w v = let s = digits v "" in String.make (max 0 (w - String.length s)) ' ' ^ s

(* [n] bytes of [s] from [pos], up to the first NUL *)
let field (s : string) pos n = match String.index_from_opt s pos '\000' with Some k when k < pos + n -> String.sub s pos (k - pos) | _ -> String.sub s pos n

(* strtoul's octal: spaces skipped, then the digits *)
let strtoul (s : string) pos =
  let p = ref pos and v = ref 0. in
  while !p < String.length s && s.[!p] = ' ' do incr p done;
  while !p < String.length s && s.[!p] >= '0' && s.[!p] <= '7' do v := !v *. 8. +. Float.of_int (Char.code s.[!p] - 48); incr p done;
  !v

(* tar.c's hdrotoull: spaces and NULs skipped, then octal; a field
 * without digits said, and [err] *)
let number o (s : string) pos n ~name ~what ~err =
  let p = ref pos in
  while !p < pos + n && (s.[!p] = ' ' || s.[!p] = '\000') do incr p done;
  if !p < pos + n && s.[!p] >= '0' && s.[!p] <= '9' then strtoul s !p
  else begin
    if !p >= pos + n then o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s: empty %s in header\n" o.argv0 name what)
    else o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s: %s: non-numeric %s in header\n" o.argv0 name (field s !p (pos + n - !p)) what);
    err
  end

(* the sum of the header's bytes, its checksum's field as spaces *)
let chksum (h : string) =
  let sum = ref 0 in
  String.iteri (fun k c -> sum := !sum + (if k >= 148 && k < 156 then 32 else Char.code c)) h;
  !sum

(*****************************************************************************)
(* The header *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the name, the ustar prefix's before it *)
let name (h : string) =
  let n = field h 0 100 in
  if h.[345] = '\000' || field h 257 6 <> "ustar" then n else field h 345 155 ^ "/" ^ n

let is_dir h =
  let n = name h in
  h.[156] = '5' || (n <> "" && n.[String.length n - 1] = '/') || int_of_float (strtoul h 100) land 0o170000 = 0o40000
let is_link h = h.[156] = '1' || h.[156] = '2' || h.[156] = 's'

(* the length the header says, and the bytes the archive has of it
 * (GNU's lengths in binary read too) *)
let hdrsize o h =
  if h.[124] = '\xff' then (o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s: negative length, which is insane\n" o.argv0 (name h)); 0)
  else if h.[124] = '\x80' then String.fold_left (fun v c -> (v lsl 8) lor Char.code c) 0 (String.sub h 127 8)
  else int_of_float (number o h 124 12 ~name:(name h) ~what:"size" ~err:0.)
let arsize o h = if is_dir h || is_link h then 0 else hdrsize o h
let nblocks bytes = (bytes + tblock - 1) / tblock

(* tar.c's putfullname: the name in its field, or split at the slash
 * that leaves the most to the prefix; false when it cannot fit *)
let put_name o (b : Bytes.t) name =
  let n = String.length name in
  let put pos s = Bytes.blit_string s 0 b pos (String.length s) in
  if n <= 100 then (put 0 name; true)
  else if not o.posix || n > 256 then (o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: name too long for tar header: %s\n" o.argv0 name); false)
  else
    let rec split k = match String.rindex_from_opt name k '/' with
      | Some s when s <= 155 && n - 1 - s <= 100 -> Some s
      | Some s when s > 0 -> split (s - 1)
      | _ -> None in
    match split (n - 1) with
    | None -> o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: name can't be split to fit tar header: %s\n" o.argv0 name); false
    | Some s -> put 345 (String.sub name 0 s); put 0 (String.sub name (s + 1) (n - s - 1)); true

(* tar.c's mkhdr: its sprint's fields, each with the NUL after it
 * that the next field overwrites *)
let header o (d : Sys_plan9.dir) file =
  let b = Bytes.make tblock '\000' in
  let put pos s = Bytes.blit_string s 0 b pos (String.length s) in
  let trunc s = if String.length s > 32 then String.sub s 0 32 else s in
  let dir = d.qid_type land Sys_plan9.dmdir <> 0 in
  put 100 (octal 6 (Float.of_int (d.perm land 0o777)) ^ " ");
  put 108 (octal 6 (Float.of_int o.uid) ^ " ");
  put 116 (octal 6 (Float.of_int o.gid) ^ " ");
  put 124 (octal 11 (Float.of_int d.length) ^ " ");
  put 136 (octal 11 d.mtime ^ " ");
  if dir then Bytes.set b 156 '5';
  let ok = put_name o b (if dir then file ^ "/" else file) in
  if o.posix then (put 257 "ustar"; put 263 "00"; put 265 (trunc d.uid); put 297 (trunc d.gid));
  put 148 (octal 6 (Float.of_int (chksum (Bytes.to_string b))) ^ "\000");
  if ok then Some (Bytes.to_string b) else None

(*****************************************************************************)
(* c and r *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* a file to the archive, a directory with what is under it *)
let rec add (caps : < caps; .. >) o (out : Buffer.t) file =
  let path = if file <> "" && file.[0] = '#' then "./" ^ file else file in
  match Sys_plan9.dirstat caps path with
  | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: can't open %s: %s\n" o.argv0 file (Unix.error_message e))
  | (d : Sys_plan9.dir) when d.qid_type land Sys_plan9.dmdir <> 0 ->
      Option.iter (fun h ->
        Buffer.add_string out h;
        match Sys_plan9.dirread caps path with
        | entries -> List.iter (fun (e : Sys_plan9.dir) -> add caps o out (file ^ "/" ^ e.name)) entries
        | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: dirreadall %s: %s\n" o.argv0 file (Unix.error_message e)))
        (header o d file)
  | (d : Sys_plan9.dir) ->
      match FS.open_in_fd caps path with
      | exception Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: can't open %s: %s\n" o.argv0 file (Unix.error_message e))
      | fd ->
          let data = Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close fd) (fun () -> read_all fd) in
          Option.iter (fun h ->
            Buffer.add_string out h;
            (* the blocks the length says, what the file is short of them zeros *)
            let bytes = nblocks d.length * tblock in
            let data = if String.length data > bytes then String.sub data 0 bytes else data in
            Buffer.add_string out data;
            Buffer.add_string out (String.make (bytes - String.length data) '\000');
            if o.verbose then o.say (file ^ "\n"))
            (header o d file)

(*****************************************************************************)
(* t and x *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the archive's [i]th block: zeros after its end inside its last
 * record, End past that (tar.c's refill, its records of [size]) *)
let block o (s : string) ~size i =
  let off = i * tblock and len = String.length s in
  let start = off / size * size in
  if start >= len then (if len mod size = 0 then raise (Fatal ("unexpected EOF reading archive " ^ arname o)) else raise End)
  else if len - start < size && (len - start) mod tblock <> 0 then raise (Fatal ("partial block read from archive " ^ arname o))
  else if off + tblock <= len then String.sub s off tblock
  else if off >= len then String.make tblock '\000'
  else String.sub s off (len - off) ^ String.make (off + tblock - len) '\000'

(* [name] one of [pats], or under one *)
let matches name pats =
  pats = [] ||
  let name = FS.cleanname name in
  List.exists (fun p -> let p = FS.cleanname p in let n = String.length p in
    String.length name >= n && String.sub name 0 n = p && (String.length name = n || name.[n] = '/')) pats

(* %M: Plan 9's dirmodefmt, of a directory or not (the only bit an
 * archive gives) *)
let mode_string ~dir m =
  let rwx k = let b = (m lsr k) land 7 in (if b land 4 <> 0 then "r" else "-") ^ (if b land 2 <> 0 then "w" else "-") ^ (if b land 1 <> 0 then "x" else "-") in
  (if dir then "d" else "-") ^ "-" ^ rwx 6 ^ rwx 3 ^ rwx 0

(* Plan 9's ctime: GMT here, as mini-date's *)
let ctime (t : float) =
  let tm : Unix.tm = Unix.gmtime t in
  Printf.sprintf "%s %s %2d %02d:%02d:%02d GMT %d\n" (String.sub "SunMonTueWedThuFriSat" (3 * tm.tm_wday) 3)
    (String.sub "JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec" (3 * tm.tm_mon) 3) tm.tm_mday tm.tm_hour tm.tm_min tm.tm_sec (tm.tm_year + 1900)

let exists (caps : < caps; .. >) path = match Sys_plan9.dirstat caps path with _ -> true | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> false

(* tar.c's openfname: the file (its descriptor) or the directory (None)
 * made, after its parents when they are missing; None when not made *)
let make (caps : < caps; .. >) o h fname ~dir ~mode (said : string option ref) =
  let fname = FS.cleanname fname in
  let cant name err =
    (* a directory said once, and not one under it said already *)
    let under last = last = name || (String.length last > String.length name && String.sub last 0 (String.length name) = name
                                     && last.[String.length name] = '/') in
    if not (dir && (match !said with Some last -> under last | None -> false)) then begin
      if dir then said := Some name;
      o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: can't create %s: %s\n" o.argv0 name err)
    end in
  (* (a directory that is there: not made, and nothing said) *)
  let create () =
    if dir then (if exists caps fname then None else (FS.mkdir caps fname 0o777; Some None))
    else Some (Some (FS.open_out_fd caps fname mode)) in
  let parents () =
    String.iteri (fun k c -> if c = '/' && k > 0 then
      let p = String.sub fname 0 k in
      if not (exists caps p) then try FS.mkdir caps p 0o777 with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> cant p (Unix.error_message e)) fname in
  if is_link h then (o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: can't make (sym)link %s\n" o.argv0 fname); None)
  else if h.[156] = '6' then (o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: can't make fifo %s\n" o.argv0 fname); None)
  else if o.keep && exists caps fname then None
  else
    let made = try create () with Unix.Unix_error _ ->
      parents ();
      try create () with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> (if not dir || not (exists caps fname) then cant fname (Unix.error_message e)); None in
    if made <> None && o.verbose then o.say (fname ^ "\n");
    Option.map (fun fd -> fname, fd) made

(* one member: listed, or taken out *)
let extract1 (caps : < caps; .. >) o h fname ~(data : int -> string) said =
  let mtime = number o h 136 12 ~name:fname ~what:"mtime" ~err:0. in
  let bytes = hdrsize o h and dir = is_dir h in
  let mode = int_of_float (number o h 100 8 ~name:fname ~what:"mode" ~err:0.) land 0o777 in
  let mode = if dir then mode lor 0o700 else mode in
  let n = if is_link h || h.[156] = '6' then 0 else nblocks (arsize o h) in
  let fname = if o.relative && fname <> "" && fname.[0] = '/' then "." ^ fname
    else if o.relative && fname <> "" && fname.[0] = '#' then "./" ^ fname else fname in
  let out =
    if o.verb = Some Xtract then make caps o h fname ~dir ~mode said
    else begin
      let t = ctime mtime in
      Console.print caps (if o.verbose then Printf.sprintf "%s %8d %s %s %s\n" (mode_string ~dir mode) bytes (String.sub t 4 12) (String.sub t 24 4) fname
                          else fname ^ "\n");
      flush (Console.stdout caps);
      None
    end in
  let left = ref (if n = 0 then 0 else bytes) in
  for k = 0 to n - 1 do
    let b = data k in
    let w = min tblock !left in
    Option.iter (fun (_, fd) -> Option.iter (fun fd -> write_all fd (String.sub b 0 w)) fd) out;
    left := !left - w
  done;
  Option.iter (fun (path, fd) ->
    Option.iter Unix.close fd;
    if o.settime then try Sys_plan9.set_mtime caps path mtime; Sys_plan9.chmod caps path (if dir then Sys_plan9.dmdir else 0) mode with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ())
    out

let extract (caps : < caps; .. >) o (s : string) ~size pats =
  let block = block o s ~size in
  let said = ref None in
  let checked h = let c = number o h 148 8 ~name:(name h) ~what:"checksum" ~err:(-1.) in c <> -1. && int_of_float c = chksum h in
  let fatal_end what i = try block i with End -> raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "unexpected EOF %s %s" what (arname o))) in
  let rec next i =
    let h = fatal_end "instead of archive header in" i in
    if name h <> "" then begin
      let i, h =
        if checked h then i, h
        else if not o.resync then
          let c = number o h 148 8 ~name:(name h) ~what:"checksum" ~err:(-1.) in
          let o_ v = if v = 0. then "0" else "0" ^ digits v "" in
          raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "bad archive header checksum in %s: name %s...; expected %s got %s" (arname o) (field h 0 100)
                          (if c = -1. then "037777777777" else o_ c) (o_ (Float.of_int (chksum h)))))
        else begin
          o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: skipping past archive header with bad checksum in %s..." o.argv0 (arname o));
          let rec find i = let h = fatal_end "looking for archive header in" i in if checked h then i, h else find (i + 1) in
          let i, h = find (i + 1) in
          o.say (Printf.sprintf "found %s\n" (name h));
          i, h
        end in
      let fname = name h in
      let data k = try block (i + 1 + k) with End ->
        raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "unexpected EOF on archive extracting %s from %s" fname (arname o))) in
      if matches fname pats then extract1 caps o h fname ~data said
      else for k = 0 to nblocks (arsize o h) - 1 do
          ignore (try block (i + 1 + k) with End -> raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "unexpected EOF on archive %s extracting %s" (arname o) fname)))
        done;
      next (i + 1 + nblocks (arsize o h))
    end in
  next 0

(*****************************************************************************)
(* Main *)
(*****************************************************************************)

(* the compressor and decompressor tar.c would run: by the archive's
 * name, or gzip's for z (when compressing, z only) *)
let compression o ~reading = match o.file with
  | Some f when List.exists (Filename.check_suffix f) [ ".tar.gz"; ".tgz" ] && (reading || o.compress) -> Some ("gzip", "gunzip")
  | Some f when List.exists (Filename.check_suffix f) [ ".tar.Z"; ".tz" ] && (reading || o.compress) -> Some ("compress", "uncompress")
  | Some f when List.exists (Filename.check_suffix f) [ ".tar.bz"; ".tbz"; ".tar.bz2"; ".tbz2" ] && (reading || o.compress) -> Some ("bzip2", "bunzip2")
  | _ -> if o.compress then Some ("gzip", "gunzip") else None

let open_archive (caps : < caps; .. >) f ~opening =
  try opening caps f with Unix.Unix_error (e, _, _) -> raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "can't open archive %s: %s" f (Unix.error_message e)))

let read_archive (caps : < caps; .. >) o =
  let s = match o.file with
    | Some f -> let fd = open_archive caps f ~opening:FS.open_in_fd in Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close fd) (fun () -> read_all fd)
    | None -> read_all (Console.stdin_fd caps) in
  match compression o ~reading:true, o.file with
  | Some ("gzip", _), _ -> (try Zlib.gunzip s with Zlib.Corrupt m -> raise (Fatal ("gunzip: " ^ m)))
  | Some (_, cmd), _ -> raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "can't exec %s: not in ix" cmd))
  | None, Some _ ->
      (* tar.c's first read sizes the records *)
      let n = min (String.length s) record in
      if n = 0 then raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "EOF reading archive %s: " (arname o)));
      if n mod tblock <> 0 then raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "%s: archive block size (%d) error" (arname o) n));
      if n <> record then o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: blocking = %d\n" o.argv0 (n / tblock));
      s
  | None, None -> s

(* r: the archive up to its end, its two zero blocks *)
let before_end o (s : string) =
  let rec go i =
    let off = i * tblock in
    if off + tblock > String.length s then raise (Fatal ("unexpected EOF instead of archive header in " ^ arname o))
    else let h = String.sub s off tblock in if name h = "" then off else go (i + 1 + nblocks (arsize o h)) in
  String.sub s 0 (go 0)

let replace (caps : < caps; .. >) o files =
  (match compression o ~reading:false with Some _ when o.file <> None && not o.create -> raise (Fatal "cannot update compressed archive") | _ -> ());
  (* opened first, as tar.c does: an archive of . has itself, empty *)
  let fd, old = match o.file with
    | Some f when o.create -> open_archive caps f ~opening:(fun caps f -> FS.open_out_fd caps f 0o666), ""
    | Some f -> let fd = open_archive caps f ~opening:FS.open_rw_fd in fd, before_end o (read_all fd)
    | None -> Console.stdout_fd caps, "" in
  let out = Buffer.create 65536 in
  Buffer.add_string out old;
  List.iter (fun arg ->
    let arg = FS.cleanname arg in
    if arg = ".." || (String.length arg >= 3 && String.sub arg 0 3 = "../") then o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: name starting with .. is a bad idea\n" o.argv0);
    add caps o out arg) files;
  Buffer.add_string out (String.make (2 * tblock) '\000');
  Buffer.add_string out (String.make ((record - Buffer.length out mod record) mod record) '\000');
  let data = match compression o ~reading:false with
    | Some ("gzip", _) -> let t = Float.round (CapUnix.time caps ()) in Zlib.gzip None (int_of_float (t /. 65536.), int_of_float (Float.rem t 65536.)) (Buffer.contents out)
    | Some (cmd, _) -> raise (Fatal (Printf.sprintf "can't exec %s: not in ix" cmd))
    | None -> Buffer.contents out in
  if o.file <> None then ignore (Unix.lseek fd 0 Unix.SEEK_SET);
  write_all fd data;
  if o.file <> None then Unix.close fd

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let o = { argv0 = (if Array.length argv > 0 then argv.(0) else "tar"); say = Console.eprint caps; verb = None; create = false;
            verbose = false; compress = false; file = None; keep = false; settime = false; posix = true; relative = true;
            resync = false; uid = 0; gid = 0 } in
  try
    let args = ref (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) and errors = ref false in
    (match !args with
     | letters :: rest ->
         args := rest;
         let k = ref 0 in
         (* tar.c's EARGF: the letters' rest, else the next argument *)
         let arg () =
           if !k + 1 < String.length letters then (let a = String.sub letters (!k + 1) (String.length letters - !k - 1) in k := String.length letters; a)
           else match !args with a :: rest -> args := rest; a | [] -> raise Usage in
         let number () = match int_of_string_opt (arg ()) with Some n -> n | None -> 0 in
         while !k < String.length letters do
           (match letters.[!k] with
            | 'c' -> o.create <- true; o.verb <- Some Replace
            | 't' -> o.verb <- Some Toc | 'x' -> o.verb <- Some Xtract | 'r' -> o.verb <- Some Replace
            | 'v' -> o.verbose <- true | 'f' -> o.file <- Some (arg ()) | 'z' -> o.compress <- true
            | 'i' | '-' -> () | 'k' -> o.keep <- true | 'm' -> o.settime <- false | 'T' -> o.settime <- true
            | 'p' -> o.posix <- true | 'P' -> o.posix <- false | 'R' -> o.relative <- false | 's' -> o.resync <- true
            | 'u' -> o.uid <- number () | 'g' -> o.gid <- number ()
            | c -> o.say (Printf.sprintf "tar: unknown letter %c\n" c); errors := true);
           incr k
         done
     | [] -> ());
    if !errors then raise Usage;
    (match o.verb with
     | None -> raise Usage
     | Some (Toc | Xtract) ->
         let s = read_archive caps o in
         extract caps o s ~size:(if o.file <> None && compression o ~reading:true = None then max tblock (min (String.length s) record) else record) !args
     | Some Replace -> replace caps o !args);
    Exit.OK
  with
  | Usage -> o.say (Printf.sprintf "usage: %s {crtx}[PRTfgikmpsuvz] [archive] [file1 file2...]\n" o.argv0); Exit.Err "usage"
  | Fatal m -> flush (Console.stdout caps); o.say (Printf.sprintf "%s: %s\n" o.argv0 m); Exit.Err m

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

(* mini-xd: Plan 9's xd (principia's utilities/byte/xd.c): a file's
 * bytes shown, 16 a line after their address; without an option as
 * numbers of 4 bytes in hexadecimal, the high byte first.
 * A format, and a line for each one given: -c the characters (a byte
 * that is none in hexadecimal); or a size, b or 1, w or 2, l or 4, v
 * or 8 bytes, with a base, o, d or x (-bx: bytes in hexadecimal).
 * -ao, -ad, -ax: the address's base; -r: lines the same as the one
 * before are a single *; -s: the bytes of each 4 turned around first;
 * -u is xd.c's (its output not kept). Not xd.c's -R (characters of
 * several bytes).
 *
 *     echo hello, world | xd -c -b
 *     0000000   h  e  l  l  o  ,     w  o  r  l  d \n
 *           0  68 65 6c 6c 6f 2c 20 77 6f 72 6c 64 0a
 *     000000d
 *
 * A line for each format, the address before the first; the last
 * line is the file's length. Without an option the same thirteen
 * bytes are 68656c6c 6f2c2077 6f726c64 0a000000: numbers of 4 bytes,
 * the last one filled with zeros.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * Unix's program is od, the octal dump, of its first edition. Octal
 * was the PDP-11's notation: an instruction's fields are of 3 bits
 * (a register, the way it is used), a digit each. A byte of 8 bits
 * is two hexadecimal digits whatever the word around it, and Plan 9
 * named its dump for that base and made it the one without an
 * option. *)

type caps = < Cap.open_in; Cap.stdin; Cap.stdout; Cap.stderr >

exception Usage

type format = Chars | Numbers of int * int   (* how many bytes, the base *)

(* bytes as one number, the high one first, in a base, with at least
 * so many digits: divided by the base a byte at a time (8 bytes are
 * past any int) *)
let number (bytes : int list) base width =
  let rec digits bytes acc =
    if List.for_all (fun b -> b = 0) bytes then acc
    else begin
      let rem = ref 0 in
      let quotient = List.map (fun b -> let v = (!rem * 256) + b in rem := v mod base; v / base) bytes in
      digits quotient (String.make 1 "0123456789abcdef".[!rem] ^ acc)
    end in
  let s = digits bytes "" in
  String.make (max 0 (width - String.length s)) '0' ^ s

(* the digits a number of so many bytes has at most, in each base *)
let width size base = match size, base with
  | 1, 8 -> 3 | 1, 10 -> 3 | 1, _ -> 2 | 2, 8 -> 6 | 2, 10 -> 5 | 2, _ -> 4
  | 4, 8 -> 11 | 4, 10 -> 10 | 4, _ -> 8 | _, 8 -> 22 | _, 10 -> 20 | _ -> 16

let character c =
  match c with
  | '\t' -> " \\t" | '\r' -> " \\r" | '\n' -> " \\n" | '\b' -> " \\b"
  | c when c >= '\127' || c < ' ' -> Printf.sprintf " %02x" (Char.code c)
  | c -> Printf.sprintf "  %c" c

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  try
    let repeats = ref false and swizzle = ref false and abase = ref 16 and formats = ref [] in
    let rec options = function
      | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' ->
          let letters = String.sub a 1 (String.length a - 1) in
          (match letters with
           | "r" -> repeats := true
           | "s" -> swizzle := true
           | "u" -> ()
           | "ao" -> abase := 8
           | "ad" -> abase := 10
           | "ax" -> abase := 16
           | "c" -> formats := !formats @ [ Chars, !abase ]
           | _ ->
               (* a size and a base, each the last said; 4 bytes in hexadecimal when not *)
               let size = ref 4 and base = ref 16 in
               String.iter (function
                 | 'o' -> base := 8 | 'd' -> base := 10 | 'x' -> base := 16
                 | 'b' | '1' -> size := 1 | 'w' | '2' -> size := 2 | 'l' | '4' -> size := 4 | 'v' | '8' -> size := 8
                 | _ -> raise Usage) letters;
               formats := !formats @ [ Numbers (!size, !base), !abase ]);
          options rest
      | rest -> rest in
    let files = options (List.tl (Array.to_list argv)) in
    let formats = if !formats = [] then [ Numbers (4, 16), !abase ] else !formats in
    let out = Buffer.create 8192 in
    (* an address: 7 digits, zeros before on a line's first format, spaces on the others *)
    let address addr base fill =
      let s = number [ (addr lsr 24) land 0xff; (addr lsr 16) land 0xff; (addr lsr 8) land 0xff; addr land 0xff ] base 1 in
      String.make (max 0 (7 - String.length s)) fill ^ s ^ " " in
    let dump name title =
      match (match name with Some n -> FS.open_in_fd caps n | None -> Console.stdin_fd caps) with
      | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> Console.eprint caps (Printf.sprintf "xd: can't open %s\n" (Option.get name)); true
      | fd ->
          let all = Buffer.create 8192 and buf = Bytes.create 8192 in
          let rec go () = match Unix.read fd buf 0 8192 with 0 -> () | n -> Buffer.add_subbytes all buf 0 n; go () | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> () in
          go ();
          if name <> None then Unix.close fd;
          let data = Buffer.contents all in
          if title then Buffer.add_string out (Option.get name ^ "\n");
          let len = String.length data in
          (* 16 bytes at an address, zeros after the file's end; turned around by 4 when asked *)
          let line addr =
            let at k = if addr + k < len then Char.code data.[addr + k] else 0 in
            List.init 16 (fun k -> at (if !swizzle then (k land lnot 3) + (3 - (k land 3)) else k)) in
          let rec lines addr before star =
            let n = min 16 (len - addr) in
            let bytes = line addr in
            if n = 16 && !repeats && addr > 0 && before = Some bytes then begin
              if not star then Buffer.add_string out "*\n";
              lines (addr + 16) before true
            end
            else begin
              List.iteri (fun k (format, base) ->
                Buffer.add_string out (address addr base (if k = 0 then '0' else ' '));
                let shown = List.filteri (fun j _ -> j < n) bytes in
                (match format with
                 | Chars -> List.iter (fun b -> Buffer.add_string out (character (Char.chr b))) shown
                 | Numbers (size, base) ->
                     (* (a number that starts before the end is whole, with the zeros after) *)
                     List.iteri (fun j _ -> if j mod size = 0 then Buffer.add_string out (" " ^ number (List.filteri (fun i _ -> i >= j && i < j + size) bytes) base (width size base))) shown);
                Buffer.add_char out '\n') formats;
              (* the end: a line shorter than 16 (an empty one, after a file of whole lines), then the address alone *)
              if n < 16 then Buffer.add_string out (address (addr + n) !abase '0' ^ "\n")
              else lines (addr + 16) (if !repeats then Some bytes else before) false
            end in
          lines 0 None false;
          Console.print caps (Buffer.contents out); Buffer.clear out;
          false in
    let failed = match files with
      | [] -> dump None false
      | [ file ] -> dump (Some file) false
      | files -> List.fold_left (fun failed file -> dump (Some file) true || failed) false files in
    if failed then Exit.Err "error" else Exit.OK
  with Usage -> Console.eprint caps "usage: xd [-u] [-r] [-s] [-a{odx}] [-c|{b1w2l4v8}{odx}] ... file ...\n"; Exit.Err "usage"

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

 * as it is (principia's utilities/calc/misc/bclib), kept in the program
 * as mini-rc keeps rcmain. s(x), c(x), a(x), l(x), e(x), j(n,x): sine,

let text = {|scale = 50
define e(x) {
	auto a, b, c, d, e, g, w, y, t, r

	r = ibase
	ibase = A

	t = scale
	scale = t + .434*x + 1

	w = 0
	if(x<0) {
		x = -x
		w = 1
	}
	y = 0
	while(x>2) {
		x /= 2
		y++
	}

	a = 1
	b = 1
	c = b
	d = 1
	e = 1
	for(a=1; 1; a++) {
		b *= x
		c = c*a+b
		d *= a
		g = c/d
		if(g == e) {
			g = g/1
			while(y--) {
				g *= g
			}
			scale = t
			if(w==1) {
				ibase = r
				return 1/g
			}
			ibase = r
			return g/1
		}
		e = g
	}
}

define l(x) {
	auto a, b, c, d, e, f, g, u, s, t, r, z

	r = ibase
	ibase = A
	if(x <= 0) {
		z = 1-10^scale
		ibase = r
		return z
	}
	t = scale

	f = 1
	scale += scale(x) - length(x) + 1
	s = scale
	while(x > 2) {
		s += (length(x)-scale(x))/2 + 1
		if(s>0) {
			scale = s
		}
		x = sqrt(x)
		f *= 2
	}
	while(x < .5) {
		s += (length(x)-scale(x))/2 + 1
		if(s>0) {
			scale = s
		}
		x = sqrt(x)
		f *= 2
	}

	scale = t + length(f) - scale(f) + 1
	u = (x-1)/(x+1)

	scale += 1.1*length(t) - 1.1*scale(t)
	s = u*u
	b = 2*f
	c = b
	d = 1
	e = 1
	for(a=3; 1; a=a+2){
		b *= s
		c = c*a + d*b
		d *= a
		g = c/d
		if(g==e) {
			scale = t
			ibase = r
			return u*c/d
		}
		e = g
	}

define s(x) {
	auto a, b, c, s, t, y, p, n, i, r

	r = ibase
	ibase = A
	t = scale
	y = x/.7853
	s = t + length(y) - scale(y)
	if(s<t) {
		s = t
	}
	scale = s
	p = a(1)

	scale = 0
	if(x>=0) {
		n = (x/(2*p)+1)/2
	}
	if(x<0) {
		n = (x/(2*p)-1)/2
	}
	x -= 4*n*p
	if(n%2 != 0) {
		x = -x
	}

	scale = t + length(1.2*t) - scale(1.2*t)
	y = -x*x
	a = x
	b = 1
	s = x
	for(i=3; 1; i+=2) {
		a *= y
		b *= i*(i-1)
		c = a/b
		if(c==0){
			scale = t
			ibase = r
			return s/1
		}
		s += c
	}
}

define c(x) {
	auto t, r

	r = ibase
	ibase = A
	t = scale
	scale = scale+1
	x = s(x + 2*a(1))
	scale = t
	ibase = r
	return x/1
}

define a(x) {
	auto a, b, c, d, e, f, g, s, t, r, z

	r = ibase
	ibase = A
	if(x==0) {
		return 0
	}
	if(x==1) {

		if(scale<52) {

		}

	while(x > .5) {
		scale++
		x = -(1 - sqrt(1.+x*x))/x
		f *= 2

		scale++
		x = -(1 - sqrt(1.+x*x))/x
		f *= 2
	}
	s = -x*x
	b = f
	c = f
	d = 1
	e = 1
	for(a=3; 1; a+=2) {

		c = c*a + d*b
		d *= a
		g = c/d
		if(g==e) {
			scale = t
			ibase = r
			return x*c/d
		}
		e = g
	}

define j(n,x) {
	auto a,b,c,d,e,g,i,s,k,t,r

	r = ibase
	ibase = A

	t = scale
	k = 1.36*x + 1.16*t - n
	k = length(k) - scale(k)
	if(k>0) {
		scale += k
	}

	s = -x*x/4
	if(n<0) {
		n = -n
		x = -x
	}

	c = 1
	for(i=1; i<=n; i++) {
		a *= x
		c *= 2*i
	}
	b = a
	d = 1
	e = 1

		a *= s
		b = b*i*(n+i) + a
		c *= i*(n+i)
		g = b/c
		if(g==e) {
			scale = t
			ibase = r
			return g/1
		}
		e = g
	}

type caps = < Dc.caps; Cap.stderr >

(* what bc reads: the library's text under a name, a file, the standard input *)
type input = Text of string * string | File of string | Stdin

let help = {|usage: mini-bc [-c] [-l] [-s] [FILE...]
Plan 9's bc, a calculator of numbers of any size in C's notation; the files'
statements, then the standard input's, each run when read:
  echo '2^100' | mini-bc                    1267650600228229401496703205376
  echo 'scale=20; sqrt(2); 1/3' | mini-bc   1.41421356237309504880 and .33333333333333333333
  mini-bc
  define f(n) {
    if (n <= 1) return (1)
    return (n * f(n-1))
  }
  f(20)                                     2432902008176640000
  echo 'obase=16; 255; ibase=2; 1010' | mini-bc
  echo 'scale=10; 4*a(1)' | mini-bc -l      pi, by the library's arctangent
A name is one letter: a variable (x), an array (x[i]), a function (x(a, b)).
scale is how many digits follow the point; ibase and obase the bases read and
printed. if, while, for, { }, break, return, define, auto; sqrt, length, scale;
"text" is printed. An expression alone is printed, an assignment is not.
-l: the library first: s (sine), c (cosine), a (arctangent), l (logarithm),
e (exponential), j (Bessel); -c: the dc commands compiled, not run; -s: an
expression alone is not printed.
|}

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let args = List.tl (Array.to_list argv) in
  if args = [ "-h" ] || args = [ "--help" ] then (Console.print caps help; Exit.OK)
  else begin
    let compile_only = ref false and library = ref false in
    let rec options = function
      | a :: rest when String.length a > 1 && a.[0] = '-' ->
          (match a.[1] with
           | 'd' -> options rest
           | 'c' -> compile_only := true; options rest
           | 'l' -> library := true; options rest
           | 's' -> State.silent := true; options rest
           | _ -> None)
      | files -> Some files in
    match options args with
    | None -> Console.eprint caps "Usage: bc [-cdls] [file ...]\n"; Exit.Code 1
    | Some files ->
        let out = Console.stdout caps in
        State.emit := (if !compile_only then (fun s -> output_string out s; flush out) else Dc.feed caps);
        (* the inputs in turn: the library, the files, the standard input;
         * a character at a time, so that a line typed is run when read *)
        let pending = ref ((if !library then [ Text ("/sys/lib/bclib", Bclib.text) ] else []) @ List.map (fun f -> File f) files @ [ Stdin ]) in
        let current : (unit -> int) ref = ref (fun () -> -1) in
        let of_fd fd =
          let buf = Bytes.create 8192 and pos = ref 0 and len = ref 0 in
          let rec next () =
            if !pos < !len then (incr pos; Char.code (Bytes.get buf (!pos - 1)))
            else match Unix.read fd buf 0 8192 with
              | 0 -> -1
              | n -> pos := 0; len := n; next ()
              | exception Unix.Unix_error _ -> -1 in
          next in
        let rec getc () =
          let c = !current () in
          if c >= 0 then c
          else match !pending with
            | [] -> -1
            | input :: rest ->
                pending := rest;
                State.line := 0;
                (match input with
                 | Stdin -> State.file := "stdin"; current := of_fd (Console.stdin_fd caps)
                 | Text (name, text) ->
                     State.file := name;
                     let pos = ref 0 in
                     current := (fun () -> if !pos < String.length text then (incr pos; Char.code text.[!pos - 1]) else -1)
                 | File f ->
                     State.file := f;
                     (match FS.open_in_fd caps f with
                      | fd -> current := of_fd fd
                      | exception (Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _) -> State.error "cannot open input file"));
                getc () in
        let lexbuf = Lexing.from_function (fun buf _ -> let c = getc () in if c < 0 then 0 else (Bytes.set buf 0 (Char.chr c); 1)) in
        let rec statements () =
          (try Parser.stuff Lexer.token lexbuf with Parser.Error | Parsing.Parse_error -> State.error "syntax error");
          statements () in
        (try statements () with
         | State.Quit -> (try !State.emit "q" with Dc.Quit -> ())
         | Dc.Quit -> ());
        Exit.OK
  end
utilities/calc/bc/CLI.mli
2798
(* mini-bc: Plan 9's bc, the calculator with the usual notation, on
 * numbers of any size. It computes nothing: it is a compiler, from a
 * language that looks like C to dc's commands, and dc (mini-dc's
 * machine, Dc) does the arithmetic. What mini-bc -c prints:
 *
 *     a + b * c          lalblc*+ps.
 *
 *                        la lb lc   the three registers' values pushed
 *                        * +        multiplied, added
 *                        p s.       printed, and put away in register .
 *
 *     define f(x) {      [Sxlxlx*Lxs. 1QLxs.0 1Q]s<6>
 *      return (x*x)
 *     }                  a macro kept in f's register (<6>: f is the
 *                        sixth letter): the argument pushed on x's own
 *                        stack (Sx), x*x, the x of before back (Lx),
 *                        and out of one macro (1Q); or 0 at the end
 *     f(12)              12 l<6>xps.
 *
 *     if (1 < 2) 7       [ 7 ]s<128>
 *                        1  2 ><128>      run <128> if 2 > 1
 *
 * So a variable is a register of dc, a parameter or a local the top
 * of its register's stack (S pushes, L pops: recursion for free), a
 * function, an if's body or a loop a macro in a register, run by x
 * or by a comparison. State has the registers given and the macros
 * entered; the grammar's actions write the commands.
 *
 *     the text --> Lexer --> Parser --> dc's commands --> Dc --> Num
 *                            (State)    (-c: printed)
 *
 * design:
 * A small language compiled to another program's input was the way
 * of the Unix room in those years, once yacc (Stephen Johnson, 1973)
 * made a grammar cheap: eqn to troff (Kernighan and Cherry, 1975),
 * ratfor to Fortran (Kernighan), bc to dc. The hard part is written
 * once, in the program underneath; the language on top is a grammar
 * and a few lines an action. Jon Bentley's "Little Languages"
 * (Communications of the ACM, 1986) is the essay on it. Its history
 * is told with dc's, in mini-dc's CLI.mli.
 *
 * The command line: its usage and a few examples are [help] in CLI.ml,
 * what mini-bc -h prints.
 *
 * bc compiles each statement to dc's commands as it is read, and dc
 * runs them: -c prints the commands instead. The files in turn, then
 * the standard input; -l: the library before them (s, c, a, l, e, j).
 * An error is said by dc, as bc compiles it to: [file:line message]
 * printed.
 *
 * Not bc's: dc is not another program at the end of a pipe (/bin/dc)
 * but mini-dc's machine in this one, given each statement's commands
 * when bc has them; the library is in the program, not a file
 * (/sys/lib/bclib). And bc.y's if, while and for are Plan 9's, which
 * principia's bc.y has broken. *)

type caps = < Dc.caps; Cap.stderr >

val main : < caps; .. > -> string array -> Exit.t
utilities/calc/bc/Lexer.mll
1696
{
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)
(* The lexer: bc.y's yylex, in ocamllex. A name is one small letter; a
 * word of several is a keyword, known by its two first letters (print,
 * pr, prxyz are the same), and quit ends bc where it is read. A digit
 * is a token of its own (A to F too): the grammar makes the numbers. *)
open Parser

let keyword w =
  match String.sub w 0 2 with
  | "pr" -> PRINT | "if" -> IF | "wh" -> WHILE | "fo" -> FOR | "sq" -> SQRT | "re" -> RETURN
  | "br" -> BREAK | "de" -> DEFINE | "sc" -> SCALE | "ba" | "ib" -> BASE | "ob" -> OBASE
  | "di" -> FFF | "au" -> AUTO | "le" -> LENGTH
  | "qu" -> raise State.Quit
  | _ -> ERROR
}

rule token = parse
  | [' ' '\t']+ { token lexbuf }
  | '\\' _ { token lexbuf }
  | "/*" { comment lexbuf }
  | ['a'-'z'] ['a'-'z']+ as w { keyword w }
  | ['a'-'z'] as c { LETTER (String.make 1 c) }
  | ['0'-'9' 'A'-'F'] as c { DIGIT c }
  | '"' ([^ '"']* as s) '"' { QSTR s }
  | '.' { DOT }
  | "*=" { EQOP "*" } | "%=" { EQOP "%" } | "^=" { EQOP "^" } | "+=" { EQOP "+" } | "-=" { EQOP "-" } | "/=" { EQOP "/" }
  | "++" { INCR } | "--" { DECR }
  | "==" { EQ } | "<=" { LE } | ">=" { GE } | "!=" { NE }
  | '*' { STAR } | '%' { PERCENT } | '^' { CARET } | '+' { PLUS } | '-' { MINUS } | '/' { SLASH }
  | '=' { ASSIGN } | '<' { LT } | '>' { GT }
  | '(' { LPAREN } | ')' { RPAREN } | '{' { LBRACE } | '}' { RBRACE } | '[' { LBRACKET } | ']' { RBRACKET }
  | ',' { COMMA } | ';' { SEMI } | '\n' { NEWLINE } | '~' { TILDE } | '?' { QUESTION } | '_' { UNDERSCORE }
  | eof { EOF }
  | _ { ERROR }

and comment = parse
  | "*/" { token lexbuf }
  | eof { EOF }
  | _ { comment lexbuf }

utilities/calc/bc/Parser.mly
5970
/* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. */
/* The grammar: bc.y's, a statement or a definition at a time, each
 * rule's value the dc commands it compiles to (the C's bundles: here
 * strings put end to end). a + b is "la lb +"; a = e is "e dsa" then
 * "s." to drop the copy; an expression alone is printed: "ps.".
 *
 * The rules crs and blev are empty: bc.y's CRS and BLEV, there for
 * what they do when the parser passes (a register taken for the body
 * that follows; the body ended). The for loop is Plan 9's bc.y's:
 * principia's has it left out, with its if and while (bugs/goken.md). */
%{
open State
%}

%token <string> LETTER EQOP QSTR
%token <char> DIGIT
%token PRINT IF WHILE FOR SQRT RETURN BREAK DEFINE SCALE BASE OBASE FFF AUTO LENGTH
%token DOT INCR DECR EQ LE GE NE STAR PERCENT CARET PLUS MINUS SLASH ASSIGN LT GT
%token LPAREN RPAREN LBRACE RBRACE LBRACKET RBRACKET COMMA SEMI NEWLINE TILDE QUESTION UNDERSCORE EOF
/* a word that is no keyword, a character of no rule */
%token ERROR

%right ASSIGN EQOP
%left PLUS MINUS
%left STAR SLASH PERCENT
%right CARET

%start stuff
%type <unit> stuff
%type <string> e ase nase stat stat1 pstat slist re cons constant crs def fprefix lora cargs eora

%%

stuff:
  | pstat tail { output $1 }
  | def dargs RPAREN LBRACE dlist slist RBRACE
      { conout (!pre ^ $6 ^ !post ^ "0" ^ number !lev ^ "Q") $1;
        rcrs := !crs;
        output "";
        lev := 0; bindx := 0 }
  | EOF { raise Quit }
  ;

dlist:
  | tail { }
  | dlist AUTO dlets tail { }
  ;

stat:
  | stat1 { $1 }
  | nase { if !silent then $1 ^ "s." else $1 }
  ;

pstat:
  | stat1 { if !silent then $1 ^ "0" else $1 }
  | nase { if not !silent then $1 ^ "ps." else $1 }
  ;

stat1:
  | /* empty */ { "" }
  | ase { $1 ^ "s." }
  | SCALE ASSIGN e { $3 ^ "k" }
  | SCALE EQOP e { "K" ^ $3 ^ $2 ^ "k" }
  | BASE ASSIGN e { $3 ^ "i" }
  | BASE EQOP e { "I" ^ $3 ^ $2 ^ "i" }
  | OBASE ASSIGN e { $3 ^ "o" }
  | OBASE EQOP e { "O" ^ $3 ^ $2 ^ "o" }
  | QSTR { "[" ^ $1 ^ "]P" }
  | BREAK { number (!lev - bstack.(!bindx - 1)) ^ "Q" }
  | PRINT e { $2 ^ "ps." }
  | RETURN e { $2 ^ !post ^ number !lev ^ "Q" }
  | RETURN { "0" ^ !post ^ number !lev ^ "Q" }
  | LBRACE slist RBRACE { $2 }
  | FFF { "fY" }
  | IF crs blev LPAREN re RPAREN stat { conout $7 $2; $5 ^ $2 ^ " " }
  | WHILE crs LPAREN re RPAREN stat blev { conout ($6 ^ $4 ^ $2) $2; $4 ^ $2 ^ " " }
  | fprefix crs re SEMI e RPAREN stat blev { conout ($7 ^ $5 ^ "s." ^ $3 ^ $2) $2; $1 ^ "s." ^ $3 ^ $2 ^ " " }
  | TILDE LETTER ASSIGN e { $4 ^ "S" ^ $2 }
  ;

fprefix: FOR LPAREN e SEMI { $3 };

blev: /* empty */ { decr bindx };

slist:
  | stat { $1 }
  | slist tail stat { $1 ^ $3 }
  ;

tail:
  | NEWLINE { incr line }
  | SEMI { }
  ;

re:
  | e EQ e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "=" }
  | e LT e { $1 ^ $3 ^ ">" }
  | e GT e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "<" }
  | e NE e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "!=" }
  | e GE e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "!>" }
  | e LE e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "!<" }
  | e { $1 ^ " 0!=" }
  ;

nase:
  | LPAREN e RPAREN { $2 }
  | cons { " " ^ $1 ^ " " }
  | DOT cons { " ." ^ $2 ^ " " }
  | cons DOT cons { " " ^ $1 ^ "." ^ $3 ^ " " }
  | cons DOT { " " ^ $1 ^ "." ^ " " }
  | DOT { "l." }
  | LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET { $3 ^ ";" ^ array $1 }
  | LETTER INCR { "l" ^ $1 ^ "d1+s" ^ $1 }
  | INCR LETTER { "l" ^ $2 ^ "1+ds" ^ $2 }
  | DECR LETTER { "l" ^ $2 ^ "1-ds" ^ $2 }
  | LETTER DECR { "l" ^ $1 ^ "d1-s" ^ $1 }
  | LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET INCR { $3 ^ ";" ^ array $1 ^ "d1+" ^ $3 ^ ":" ^ array $1 }
  | INCR LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET { $4 ^ ";" ^ array $2 ^ "1+d" ^ $4 ^ ":" ^ array $2 }
  | LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET DECR { $3 ^ ";" ^ array $1 ^ "d1-" ^ $3 ^ ":" ^ array $1 }
  | DECR LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET { $4 ^ ";" ^ array $2 ^ "1-d" ^ $4 ^ ":" ^ array $2 }
  | SCALE INCR { "Kd1+k" }
  | INCR SCALE { "K1+dk" }
  | SCALE DECR { "Kd1-k" }
  | DECR SCALE { "K1-dk" }
  | BASE INCR { "Id1+i" }
  | INCR BASE { "I1+di" }
  | BASE DECR { "Id1-i" }
  | DECR BASE { "I1-di" }
  | OBASE INCR { "Od1+o" }
  | INCR OBASE { "O1+do" }
  | OBASE DECR { "Od1-o" }
  | DECR OBASE { "O1-do" }
  | LETTER LPAREN cargs RPAREN { $3 ^ "l" ^ func $1 ^ "x" }
  | LETTER LPAREN RPAREN { "l" ^ func $1 ^ "x" }
  | LETTER { "l" ^ $1 }
  | LENGTH LPAREN e RPAREN { $3 ^ "Z" }
  | SCALE LPAREN e RPAREN { $3 ^ "X" }
  | QUESTION { "?" }
  | SQRT LPAREN e RPAREN { $3 ^ "v" }
  | TILDE LETTER { "L" ^ $2 }
  | SCALE { "K" }
  | BASE { "I" }
  | OBASE { "O" }
  /* (a minus is all of what follows it at its own precedence: -a*b is 0 a b * -) */
  | MINUS e { " 0" ^ $2 ^ "-" }
  | e PLUS e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "+" }
  | e MINUS e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "-" }
  | e STAR e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "*" }
  | e SLASH e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "/" }
  | e PERCENT e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "%" }
  | e CARET e { $1 ^ $3 ^ "^" }
  ;

ase:
  | LETTER ASSIGN e { $3 ^ "ds" ^ $1 }
  | LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET ASSIGN e { $6 ^ "d" ^ $3 ^ ":" ^ array $1 }
  | LETTER EQOP e { "l" ^ $1 ^ $3 ^ $2 ^ "ds" ^ $1 }
  | LETTER LBRACKET e RBRACKET EQOP e { $3 ^ ";" ^ array $1 ^ $6 ^ $5 ^ "d" ^ $3 ^ ":" ^ array $1 }
  ;

e:
  | ase { $1 }
  | nase { $1 }
  ;

cargs:
  | eora { $1 }
  | cargs COMMA eora { $1 ^ $3 }
  ;

eora:
  | e { $1 }
  | LETTER LBRACKET RBRACKET { "l" ^ array $1 }
  ;

cons: constant { $1 };

constant:
  | UNDERSCORE { "_" }
  | DIGIT { String.make 1 $1 }
  | constant DIGIT { $1 ^ String.make 1 $2 }
  ;

/* a register for the body that follows; one macro more is entered */
crs:
  | /* empty */
      { let r = Printf.sprintf "<%d>" !crs in
        incr crs;
        if !crs > 220 then (error "program too big"; raise Quit);
        bstack.(!bindx) <- !lev; incr bindx; incr lev;
        r }
  ;

def:
  | DEFINE LETTER LPAREN { pre := ""; post := ""; lev := 1; bindx := 0; bstack.(0) <- 0; func $2 }
  ;

dargs:
  | /* empty */ { }
  | lora { parameter $1 }
  | dargs COMMA lora { parameter $3 }
  ;

dlets:
  | lora { local $1 }
  | dlets COMMA lora { local $3 }
  ;

lora:
  | LETTER { $1 }
  | LETTER LBRACKET RBRACKET { array $1 }
  ;
utilities/calc/bc/State.ml
1990
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* What bc's grammar keeps while it compiles (bc.y's globals), and where
 * its dc commands go.
 *
 * A function, an if's body and a loop are dc macros kept in registers:
 * a function f in the register of f's rank (<6>), a body in a register
 * taken in turn from 128 (<128>, <129>...). A break is a Q that leaves
 * as many macros as were entered since the loop: lev counts them. *)

(* the dc commands compiled: printed (bc -c), or run *)
let emit : (string -> unit) ref = ref print_string

(* -s: a statement that is an expression is not printed *)
let silent = ref false

(* the next register for a body, and where a statement's start again
 * (those of a function stay taken) *)
let crs = ref 128
let rcrs = ref 128

(* how many macros are entered where we are; those entered at each
 * loop or if around it *)
let lev = ref 0
let bstack = Array.make 10 0
let bindx = ref 0

(* a function's parameters and locals: saved before its body, restored after *)
let pre = ref ""
let post = ref ""

(* the input's name and line, for an error *)
let file = ref "stdin"
let line = ref 0

(* bc's exit: a q for dc, then the end *)
exception Quit

let output s =
  !emit (s ^ "\n");
  crs := !rcrs

(* a body kept in its register *)
let conout body register =
  !emit ("[" ^ body ^ "]s" ^ register ^ "\n");
  decr lev

let error msg =
  !emit (Printf.sprintf "c[%s:%d %s]pc\n" !file (!line + 1) msg);
  crs := !rcrs;
  bindx := 0;
  lev := 0

let number n = " " ^ string_of_int n

(* a function's register, an array's: the letter's rank, from 1 and from 221 *)
let func letter = Printf.sprintf "<%d>" (Char.code letter.[0] - 96)
let array letter = Printf.sprintf "<%d>" (Char.code letter.[0] + 124)

(* a parameter (given), a local (0): saved on its register's stack *)
let parameter s = pre := "S" ^ s ^ !pre; post := !post ^ "L" ^ s ^ "s."
let local s = pre := "0S" ^ s ^ !pre; post := !post ^ "L" ^ s ^ "s."

Plan 9's dc, the desk calculator: numbers of any size on a stack, the
operators after their operands; the file's commands, then the standard input's:
  echo '2 3 + p' | mini-dc                 5
  echo '20k 2 v p' | mini-dc               1.41421356237309504880
  echo '2 100 ^ p 16o 255 p' | mini-dc     1267650600228229401496703205376, ff
  echo '[la 1 + d sa p 5 >x]sx 0sa lxx' | mini-dc      1 to 5: a macro that runs itself
A number: digits, a point, _ for a minus. + - * / % ^ v (square root); p prints
the top, f the stack; d duplicates, c clears; sx and lx save to and load from
the register x (Sx, Lx: each register a stack); [text] is a string, x runs
it, <x >x =x run the register x if the two numbers on top compare so; k sets the
scale (the digits after the point), i and o the input and output bases; q quits.
|}

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  match List.tl (Array.to_list argv) with
  | [ "-h" ] | [ "--help" ] -> Console.print caps help; Exit.OK
  | args ->
      (* (an option, any, is the C's debugging) *)
      let files = List.filter (fun a -> a = "" || a.[0] <> '-') args in
      match files with
      | file :: _ when (try Unix.close (FS.open_in_fd caps file); (Unix.stat file).st_kind = Unix.S_DIR with Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _ -> true) ->
          let is_dir = (try (Unix.stat file).st_kind = Unix.S_DIR with Unix.Unix_error _ -> false) in
          Console.eprint caps (if is_dir then Printf.sprintf "dc: file %s is a directory\n" file else Printf.sprintf "dc: can't open file %s\n" file);
          Exit.Code 1
      | _ -> (try Dc.run caps (match files with f :: _ -> Some f | [] -> None) with Dc.Quit -> ()); Exit.OK
utilities/calc/dc/CLI.mli
2462
(* mini-dc: Plan 9's dc, the desk calculator. Numbers of any size on
 * a stack, the operator after its operands:
 *
 *     2 3 + 4 * p        what is typed
 *     2      3      +      4      *      p
 *     | 2 |  | 3 |  | 5 |  | 4 |  | 20 |  prints 20
 *            | 2 |         | 5 |
 *
 * No parenthesis and no precedence are needed, so no parser: a
 * command is one character, run as it is read (Dc), on integers that
 * grow as they must (Num).
 *
 * cs-history:
 * dc is the oldest language of Unix still in use. It was written at
 * Bell Labs in B, before C existed, and soon taken over by Robert
 * Morris and Lorinda Cherry; Doug McIlroy calls it "the senior
 * language on UNIX systems". When the PDP-11 came, dc was "the first
 * language to run" on it, before its assembler (McIlroy again). The
 * notation is Jan Lukasiewicz's (the
 * 1920s: a logic written without parentheses, the operator first;
 * with the operator last it is "reverse Polish"), which the desk
 * calculators of Hewlett-Packard made familiar to engineers, the
 * HP-35 of 1972 in every pocket.
 *
 * evolution:
 * bc is dc with the usual notation. Lorinda Cherry's bc (1975) is a
 * yacc grammar that translates a + b * c to dc's commands and pipes
 * them to dc, which does all the arithmetic: a compiler whose
 * target machine is another program. mini-bc is that still, with
 * this directory's machine linked in (the library ix_dc) where the
 * pipe was. GNU's bc (1991) computes by itself.
 *
 * The command line: its usage and a few examples are [help] in CLI.ml,
 * what mini-dc -h prints.
 *
 * Not dc's: its limits on memory, and Y, which prints them; the
 * shell of ! is rc by its path here (/bin/rc), as the C's. A 0 that z,
 * Z or X made has a byte in the C, and keeps it through an addition or
 * a multiplication (it then prints as 00.0 with a scale, or not at all
 * in another base): here only until it is computed with. And what the
 * C does after an operator found the stack empty, with blocks that are
 * no value any more, is not followed.
 *
 * References: dc(1); Robert Morris and Lorinda Cherry, "DC -- An
 * Interactive Desk Calculator" (in the Unix Programmer's Manual,
 * volume 2); M. D. McIlroy, "A Research UNIX Reader: Annotated
 * Excerpts from the Programmer's Manual, 1971-1986" (1987), for the
 * quotations; principia's utilities/calc/misc/dc.c. *)

type caps = < Dc.caps; Cap.stderr >

val main : < caps; .. > -> string array -> Exit.t
utilities/calc/dc/Dc.ml
25737
(* Claude Code
