(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* startmenu: what the start button shows (plan_desktop.md): the programs of
 * /lib/desktop/apps by their groups (Apps says why a table), each with its
 * icon. In a window of rio's popup layer, started hidden with the session:
 *
 *     window -popup -hide -label startmenu startmenu
 *
 *     +--------------+----------------+
 *     | Terminal     | [] Tetris      |
 *     | Apps       > | [] Doom        |
 *     | Games      > | [] Quake       |
 *     | Internet   > |                |
 *     | Exit         |                |
 *     +--------------+----------------+
 *
 * The mouse on a group opens it, in the same window: a second window for a
 * submenu would be one more thing to keep above the panel. A press on a
 * program opens it and hides this window; a press elsewhere is rio's, which
 * hides it. So the click is a wctl's line and no program loaded from the
 * card, and a window hidden draws as before and comes back at once.
 *
 * Why a window and not rio's Menu: a menu on the screen's own image would be
 * drawn over by a game running below it, and then copied back wrong; a
 * window is a layer of the kernel's.
 *
 * It takes the size its table needs, at the bottom left of what the screen
 * has for windows, and asks rio for it. A program that is not on the card
 * is not listed.
 *
 * startmenu -try seconds [group]: no menu; each program of the table, or
 * of that group, opened as the menu opens it, left that long, and deleted:
 * all of them looked at once (plan_desktop.md's shakedown), from rio -i or
 * a window. *)

type caps = < Cap.draw; Cap.mouse; Cap.fork; Cap.readdir; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out >

let read_file (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) path =
  try Some (FS.read caps (Fpath.v path)) with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> None

let ask (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) line =
  try
    let fd = FS.open_device_fd caps "/dev/wctl" in
    Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close fd) (fun () -> ignore (Unix.write_substring fd line 0 (String.length line)))
  with Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _ -> ()

(* the newest window: the largest number in /dev/wsys *)
let newest (caps : < Cap.readdir; .. >) =
  let names = try Sys_plan9.dirread caps "/dev/wsys" with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> [] in
  List.fold_left (fun n (d : Sys_plan9.dir) -> match int_of_string_opt d.name with Some k -> max n k | None -> n) 0 names

let try_all caps (entries : Apps.entry list) seconds =
  List.iter (fun (e : Apps.entry) ->
      let before = newest caps in
      ask caps (Apps.open_line e);
      CapUnix.sleepf caps (float seconds);
      let id = newest caps in
      if id > before then ask caps (Printf.sprintf "delete -id %d" id)) entries

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let table = match read_file caps "/lib/desktop/apps" with Some t -> Apps.parse t | None -> [] in
  let entries = List.filter (fun e -> Sys.file_exists ("/bin/" ^ Apps.program e)) table in
  if Array.length argv >= 3 && argv.(1) = "-try" then begin
    let group = if Array.length argv >= 4 then Some argv.(3) else None in
    let chosen = List.filter (fun (e : Apps.entry) -> match group with Some g -> e.group = g | None -> e.group <> "top") entries in
    try_all caps chosen (match int_of_string_opt argv.(2) with Some n -> n | None -> 30);
    Exit.OK
  end
  else
  let display = Display.init caps in
  let font = Font.default display and mouse = Mouse.init caps in
  let color r g b = Display.color display (Display.rgb r g b) in
  let paper = color 0xee 0xf2 0xf6 and side = color 0xd8 0xe2 0xec and shown = color 0x33 0x66 0x99 in
  let black = color 0 0 0 and white = color 0xff 0xff 0xff and line = color 0x33 0x55 0x77 in
  (* the icons, once: an image with its alpha *)
  let icons : (string, Display.image) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 32 in
  let load_icon name =
    if not (Hashtbl.mem icons name) then
      match Option.bind (read_file caps ("/lib/desktop/icons/" ^ name ^ ".txt")) Icon.parse with
      | Some (i : Icon.t) ->
          let r = Rectangle.v 0 0 i.w i.h in
          let image = Display.alloc display r "r8g8b8a8" ~repl:false Display.black in
          Display.load image r i.pixels;
          Hashtbl.replace icons name image
      | None -> () in
  List.iter (fun (e : Apps.entry) -> load_icon e.icon) entries;
  let w, h = Apps.size_of entries in
  ask caps (Printf.sprintf "resize -at sw %d %d" w h);
  let left = Apps.left entries in
  let draw_item (view : Display.image) (r : Rectangle.t) on item =
    if on then Draw.fill view r shown;
    let ink = if on then white else black in
    let y = r.min.y + ((Rectangle.dy r - Font.height font) / 2) in
    let word s x = ignore (Font.string view (Point.v x y) ink font s) in
    match (item : Apps.item) with
    | Run e ->
        (match Hashtbl.find_opt icons e.icon with
         | Some i ->
             let at = Point.v (r.min.x + 4) (r.min.y + ((Rectangle.dy r - Rectangle.dy i.r) / 2)) in
             Draw.draw view (Rectangle.add i.r at) i None Point.zero
         | None -> ());
        word e.name (r.min.x + 26)
    | Group (_, name) ->
        word name (r.min.x + 26);
        word ">" (r.max.x - 14)
    | Exit -> word "Exit" (r.min.x + 26) in
  (* [opened]: the group shown; [over]: the item the mouse is on, by its
   * column and row *)
  let draw (view : Display.image) opened over =
    let top = view.r.min.y + 4 in
    let cut = view.r.min.x + Apps.left_w in
    Draw.fill view (Rectangle.v view.r.min.x view.r.min.y cut view.r.max.y) side;
    Draw.fill view (Rectangle.v cut view.r.min.y view.r.max.x view.r.max.y) paper;
    let column x0 x1 items col =
      List.iteri (fun i item ->
          let y = top + (i * Apps.row_h) in
          draw_item view (Rectangle.v x0 y x1 (y + Apps.row_h)) (over = Some (col, i)) item) items in
    column (view.r.min.x + 2) cut left 0;
    (match opened with
     | Some g -> column cut (view.r.max.x - 2) (Apps.right entries g) 1
     | None -> ());
    Draw.border view view.r 1 line;
    Display.flush display in
  (* where the mouse is: the column and the row of an item there *)
  let locate (view : Display.image) opened (p : Point.t) =
    let row = Apps.row_at (view.r.min.y + 4) p.y in
    let col = if p.x < view.r.min.x + Apps.left_w then 0 else 1 in
    let items = if col = 0 then left else match opened with Some g -> Apps.right entries g | None -> [] in
    match List.nth_opt items (max row 0) with
    | Some item when row >= 0 && Rectangle.contains view.r p -> Some (col, row, item)
    | _ -> None in
  let rec loop (view : Display.image) opened over was =
    let m : Mouse.state = Event.sync (Mouse.receive mouse) in
    if m.resized then begin
      (* (shown anew, or another size: as it was at first) *)
      let view = Display.screen display in
      draw view None None;
      loop view None None m.buttons
    end
    else begin
      let found = locate view opened m.pos in
      let opened' = match found with
        | Some (_, _, Apps.Group (g, _)) -> Some g
        | Some (0, _, _) -> None
        | _ -> opened in
      let over' = match found with Some (c, r, _) -> Some (c, r) | None -> None in
      if opened' <> opened || over' <> over then draw view opened' over';
      let press = m.buttons land 1 <> 0 && was = 0 in
      match found with
      | Some (_, _, Apps.Run e) when press ->
          ask caps (Apps.open_line e);
          ask caps "hide";
          loop view opened' over' m.buttons
      | Some (_, _, Apps.Exit) when press -> ask caps "exit"; loop view opened' over' m.buttons
      | _ -> loop view opened' over' m.buttons
    end in
  let view = Display.screen display in
  draw view None None;
  loop view None None 0

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))

(* See Apps.mli *)

type size = Max | Size of int * int

type entry = { group : string; name : string; icon : string; size : size; command : string }

let groups =
  [ "apps", "Apps"; "games", "Games"; "net", "Internet"; "devtools", "Developer";
    "system", "System"; "examples", "Examples" ]

let size_of_text line s =
  if s = "max" then Max
  else
    match String.split_on_char 'x' s with
    | [ w; h ] when int_of_string_opt w <> None && int_of_string_opt h <> None ->
        Size (int_of_string w, int_of_string h)
    | _ -> failwith ("Apps: a bad size: " ^ line)

let parse text =
  let entry line =
    match List.map String.trim (String.split_on_char '|' line) with
    | [ group; name; icon; size; command ] when group <> "" && name <> "" && command <> "" ->
        if group <> "top" && not (List.mem_assoc group groups) then failwith ("Apps: no such group: " ^ line);
        { group; name; icon; size = size_of_text line size; command }
    | _ -> failwith ("Apps: not five fields: " ^ line) in
  let wanted line = let l = String.trim line in l <> "" && l.[0] <> '#' in
  List.map entry (List.filter wanted (String.split_on_char '\n' text))

let program e =
  match String.split_on_char ' ' e.command with
  | p :: _ -> p
  | [] -> e.command

let open_line e =
  (* (wctl's -label is one word) *)
  let label = String.map (fun c -> if c = ' ' then '-' else c) e.name in
  let place = match e.size with
    | Max -> "-max"
    | Size (w, h) -> Printf.sprintf "-at c %d %d" w h in
  Printf.sprintf "new %s -label %s %s" place label e.command

type item = Run of entry | Group of string * string | Exit

let of_group entries g = List.filter (fun e -> e.group = g) entries

let left entries =
  let top = List.map (fun e -> Run e) (of_group entries "top") in
  let named = List.filter (fun (g, _) -> of_group entries g <> []) groups in
  top @ List.map (fun (g, name) -> Group (g, name)) named @ [ Exit ]

let right entries g = List.map (fun e -> Run e) (of_group entries g)

let row_h = 24
let left_w = 150
let right_w = 170

let size_of entries =
  let longest = List.fold_left (fun n (g, _) -> max n (List.length (of_group entries g))) (List.length (left entries)) groups in
  (left_w + right_w, (longest * row_h) + 8)

let row_at top y = if y < top then -1 else (y - top) / row_h

let cell_w = 88
let cell_h = 64

let desk_cell (x0, y0, _, y1) i =
  let per = max 1 ((y1 - y0 - 8) / cell_h) in
  let x = x0 + 8 + ((i / per) * cell_w) and y = y0 + 8 + ((i mod per) * cell_h) in
  (x, y, x + cell_w, y + cell_h)

let double_click t0 t1 = t1 - t0 >= 0 && t1 - t0 < 500
windows/desktop/lib/Apps.mli

(* The table of programs a person opens, and the start menu's shape, without
 * a screen. The table is a text file, /lib/desktop/apps on the card, its
 * lines:
 *
 *     group | name | icon | size | command
 *
 *     games | Tetris | blocks | 400x560 | tetris
 *     games | Doom   | face   | max     | doom
 *
 * # starts a comment line. A group is a directory of the card's /progs
 * (apps, games, net, devtools, system, examples), or top: on the menu
 * itself, in no submenu.
 *
 * design:
 * Why a table and not a walk of /progs: a directory says what programs
 * there are, not which of them draw, what a person calls them, what they
 * look like or how large they want to be: curl and doom are both a file.
 * The groups stay /progs's, so that there is no second classification to
 * keep, and a test holds the table to the Makefile's lists of what is on
 * the card, so that a new game cannot be forgotten. What is not in the
 * table can still be reached: the menu has All programs, a file manager
 * on /progs.
 *
 * others:
 * freedesktop.org's .desktop files (1999 on) are the same table as a file a
 * program, installed with it: each program brings its own line, and a menu
 * is whatever is found. It suits software from many sources. Here all
 * of it is built together, and one file can be read at once. *)

type size = Max | Size of int * int

type entry = {
  group : string;
  name : string;
  icon : string;
  size : size;
  command : string;
}

(* a file's text; Failure with its line, for one that is not a table's *)
val parse : string -> entry list

(* the groups, by their directory and a person's name for them, in menu order *)
val groups : (string * string) list

(* the command's first word *)
val program : entry -> string

(* what to write to a wctl to open it: new, in the middle of what the screen
 * has, or all of it *)
val open_line : entry -> string

type item = Run of entry | Group of string * string | Exit

(* [left entries]: the menu's first column: those of top, the groups that have
 * entries, then Exit *)
val left : entry list -> item list
(* [right entries group]: the second, when that group is open *)
val right : entry list -> string -> item list

val row_h : int
val left_w : int
val right_w : int
(* the window's size for those entries: the longest of all the columns *)
val size_of : entry list -> int * int
(* [row_at top y]: which row a height is, the rows starting at [top] *)
val row_at : int -> int -> int

(* [desk_cell (x0, y0, x1, y1) i]: where the desk's icon i goes in that
 * rectangle, as (x0, y0, x1, y1): down the left side, then the next column *)
val desk_cell : int * int * int * int -> int -> int * int * int * int
(* [double_click t0 t1]: two presses at those milliseconds are one double
 * click *)
val double_click : int -> int -> bool

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Icon.mli *)

type t = { w : int; h : int; pixels : string }

let is_palette l = String.length l = 8 && l.[1] = ' ' && int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ String.sub l 2 6) <> None

let parse text =
  let lines = List.filter (fun l -> l <> "" && l.[0] <> '#') (List.map String.trim (String.split_on_char '\n' text)) in
  let palette, rows = List.partition is_palette lines in
  let colour = List.map (fun l -> (l.[0], int_of_string ("0x" ^ String.sub l 2 6))) palette in
  match rows with
  | [] -> None
  | first :: _ ->
      let w = String.length first and h = List.length rows in
      if List.exists (fun r -> String.length r <> w) rows then None
      else if List.exists (fun r -> String.exists (fun c -> c <> '.' && not (List.mem_assoc c colour)) r) rows then None
      else begin
        let b = Bytes.make (w * h * 4) '\000' in
        List.iteri (fun y r ->
            String.iteri (fun x c ->
                if c <> '.' then begin
                  let v = List.assoc c colour and o = ((y * w) + x) * 4 in
                  Bytes.set b o '\255';
                  Bytes.set b (o + 1) (Char.chr (v land 255));
                  Bytes.set b (o + 2) (Char.chr ((v lsr 8) land 255));
                  Bytes.set b (o + 3) (Char.chr ((v lsr 16) land 255))
                end) r) rows;
        Some { w; h; pixels = Bytes.to_string b }
      end

let doubled i =
  let b = Bytes.create (i.w * i.h * 16) in
  for y = 0 to (2 * i.h) - 1 do
    for x = 0 to (2 * i.w) - 1 do
      Bytes.blit_string i.pixels ((((y / 2) * i.w) + (x / 2)) * 4) b (((y * 2 * i.w) + x) * 4) 4
    done
  done;
  { w = 2 * i.w; h = 2 * i.h; pixels = Bytes.to_string b }

(* An icon as a text file: a character a pixel, its colours named first.
 *
 *     # a folder
 *     y e8b84a
 *     o a07820
 *     ................
 *     .oooo...........
 *     .oyyyo..........
 *
 * A palette line is a character, a blank, six hexadecimal digits; '.' is
 * no colour at all; # starts a comment. Each row as wide as the first.
 *
 * design:
 * Text, for the same reason as Cursors: a diff shows what changed, a
 * person with an editor can draw one, and no program running all the time
 * has to link a picture decoder. This is how a 1983 icon was made anyway,
 * squares on graph paper (Icons, in apps/files, says more of that). *)

type t = {
  w : int;
  h : int;
  (* w * h pixels, 4 bytes each, as a r8g8b8a8 image is loaded: a, b, g, r *)
  pixels : string;
}

(* None when the text is no icon: an unknown character, rows of two widths *)
val parse : string -> t option

(* twice as wide and as high, each pixel four: the desk's *)
val doubled : t -> t

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Paper.mli *)

let bands n c =
  let r = (c lsr 16) land 255 and g = (c lsr 8) land 255 and b = c land 255 in
  let at v k = v - (v * 2 * k / (3 * max 1 (n - 1))) in
  List.init n (fun k -> (at r k lsl 16) lor (at g k lsl 8) lor at b k)

let cover sw sh rgba w h =
  let out = Bytes.make (w * h * 4) '\000' in
  if sw > 0 && sh > 0 then begin
    (* the scale that covers: the larger of the two ratios, in 1/1024ths *)
    let k = max (w * 1024 / sw) (h * 1024 / sh) in
    let k = max k 1 in
    (* where the screen's corner is in the picture, the excess cut in halves *)
    let ox = ((sw * k / 1024) - w) / 2 and oy = ((sh * k / 1024) - h) / 2 in
    for y = 0 to h - 1 do
      let sy = min (sh - 1) ((y + oy) * 1024 / k) in
      for x = 0 to w - 1 do
        let sx = min (sw - 1) ((x + ox) * 1024 / k) in
        let s = ((sy * sw) + sx) * 4 and o = ((y * w) + x) * 4 in
        Bytes.set out o (Bytes.get rgba (s + 2));
        Bytes.set out (o + 1) (Bytes.get rgba (s + 1));
        Bytes.set out (o + 2) (Bytes.get rgba s)
      done
    done
  end;
  Bytes.to_string out

(* The desk's wallpaper as pixels, without a screen: a colour made a gradient,
 * or a picture made the screen's size.
 *
 * A picture is scaled to cover all the screen and keep its shape, the rest
 * cut on the two sides that are too long ("cover", as a web page's
 * background-size says it): a wallpaper with bars beside it looks unfinished,
 * one stretched looks wrong. Each pixel the nearest of the picture's: done
 * once, for a picture of a few hundred thousand pixels. *)

(* [bands c]: the colour at the top, then darker down to about a third of it,
 * in [n] steps: the colours, 0xRRGGBB *)
val bands : int -> int -> int list

(* [cover src_w src_h rgba w h]: the picture's rgba bytes, four a pixel,
 * made w by h, as a x8r8g8b8 image is loaded (b, g, r, x) *)
val cover : int -> int -> Bytes.t -> int -> int -> string
windows/desktop/lib/Prefs.ml
2665
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Prefs.mli *)

type wallpaper = Colour of int | Picture of string

type t = { wallpaper : wallpaper; clock : string; edge : string; swap : bool; accelerated : bool; volume : int option }

let colours = [ "blue", 0x3a5f85; "green", 0x3f6f4a; "teal", 0x2f6f73; "plum", 0x6a4a7a; "grey", 0x6a7480 ]

let default = { wallpaper = Colour 0x3a5f85; clock = "24"; edge = "bottom"; swap = false; accelerated = false; volume = None }

let yes v = v = "yes"

let set (t : t) line : t =
  match String.index_opt line '=' with
  | None -> t
  | Some i ->
      let key = String.trim (String.sub line 0 i) and v = String.trim (String.sub line (i + 1) (String.length line - i - 1)) in
      let rest w = String.trim (String.sub v (String.length w) (String.length v - String.length w)) in
      let starts w = String.length v > String.length w && String.sub v 0 (String.length w) = w in
      if key = "wallpaper" && starts "colour " then
        (match int_of_string_opt ("0x" ^ rest "colour ") with Some c -> { t with wallpaper = Colour c } | None -> t)
      else if key = "wallpaper" && starts "picture " then { t with wallpaper = Picture (rest "picture ") }
      else if key = "clock" && List.mem v [ "24"; "12"; "off" ] then { t with clock = v }
      else if key = "edge" && List.mem v [ "bottom"; "top" ] then { t with edge = v }
      else if key = "swap" then { t with swap = yes v }
      else if key = "accelerated" then { t with accelerated = yes v }
      else if key = "volume" then
        (match int_of_string_opt v with Some n when n >= 0 && n <= 100 -> { t with volume = Some n } | _ -> t)
      else t

let parse text = List.fold_left set default (String.split_on_char '\n' text)

let print (t : t) =
  let b v = if v then "yes" else "no" in
  String.concat ""
    [ (match t.wallpaper with
       | Colour c -> Printf.sprintf "wallpaper=colour %06x\n" c
       | Picture p -> Printf.sprintf "wallpaper=picture %s\n" p);
      Printf.sprintf "clock=%s\nedge=%s\nswap=%s\naccelerated=%s\n" t.clock t.edge (b t.swap) (b t.accelerated);
      (match t.volume with Some v -> Printf.sprintf "volume=%d\n" v | None -> "") ]

let path home = home ^ "/lib/desktop/settings"

let clock_text (t : t) hour minute =
  if t.clock = "off" then ""
  else if t.clock = "12" then
    Printf.sprintf "%d:%02d %s" (if hour mod 12 = 0 then 12 else hour mod 12) minute (if hour < 12 then "am" else "pm")
  else Printf.sprintf "%02d:%02d" hour minute

let mouse_lines (t : t) =
  [ (if t.swap then "buttonmap 321" else "buttonmap 123"); (if t.accelerated then "accelerated" else "linear") ]
windows/desktop/lib/Prefs.mli

(* A person's desktop settings: what settings writes, the panel and the
 * desk read, $home/lib/desktop/settings, a line a setting:
 *
 *     wallpaper=colour 3a5f85
 *     wallpaper=picture /usr/pad/lib/sea.jpg
 *     clock=24              (or 12, or off)
 *     edge=bottom           (or top: the panel's)
 *     swap=no               (the mouse's buttons, left and right)
 *     accelerated=no
 *     volume=70
 *
 * A line it does not know is left out, a setting not said is the default:
 * a file of an older or a newer desktop still reads.
 *
 * design:
 * No message between the programs: settings writes the file, and the panel
 * and the desk look at it again, the panel at its clock's second, the desk
 * every two seconds. A file is what Plan 9 has to share, and a program
 * started later finds what was said before. The mouse and the volume are the
 * kernel's: settings writes their device files at once, and at a session's
 * start (settings -apply), so that the file's word holds after a boot. *)

type wallpaper = Colour of int | Picture of string

type t = {
  wallpaper : wallpaper;
  clock : string;
  edge : string;
  swap : bool;
  accelerated : bool;
  volume : int option;
}

val default : t
val parse : string -> t
val print : t -> string

(* the file's place for that home *)
val path : string -> string

(* [clock_text t hour minute]: what the panel's clock says; "" for off *)
val clock_text : t -> int -> int -> string

(* what to write to /dev/mousectl, a line each *)
val mouse_lines : t -> string list

(* the colours settings offers, by their names *)
val colours : (string * int) list

(* Claude Code

(* See Taskbar.mli *)

type window = { id : int; label : string; current : bool; hidden : bool; layer : string }

let window_of id label wctl =
  let words = List.filter (fun s -> s <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' wctl) in
  match words with
  | _ :: _ :: _ :: _ :: current :: shown :: rest ->
      Some { id; label; current = current = "current"; hidden = shown = "hidden";
             layer = (match rest with l :: _ -> l | [] -> "") }
  | _ -> None

let tasks = List.filter (fun w -> w.layer = "")
let menu = List.find_opt (fun w -> w.layer = "popup" && w.label = "startmenu")

type part = Start | Overview | Task of window | Clock

let start_width = 64
let overview_width = 28
let task_width = 160
let gap = 4

let layout (r : Rectangle.t) tasks clock_width =
  let y0 = r.min.y + 2 and y1 = r.max.y - 2 in
  let start_r : Rectangle.t = Rectangle.v (r.min.x + 2) y0 (r.min.x + 2 + start_width) y1 in
  let clock_r : Rectangle.t = Rectangle.v (r.max.x - clock_width - 2) y0 (r.max.x - 2) y1 in
  let over_r : Rectangle.t = Rectangle.v (start_r.max.x + gap) y0 (start_r.max.x + gap + overview_width) y1 in
  let x0 = over_r.max.x + gap and room = clock_r.min.x - gap - (over_r.max.x + gap) in
  let n = List.length tasks in
  let w = if n = 0 then 0 else min task_width (max 0 ((room - (gap * (n - 1))) / n)) in
  let buttons = List.mapi (fun i t ->
      let x = x0 + (i * (w + gap)) in
      (Task t, Rectangle.v x y0 (x + w) y1)) tasks in
  ((Start, start_r) :: (Overview, over_r) :: buttons) @ [ (Clock, clock_r) ]

let at parts p =
  match List.find_opt (fun (_, r) -> Rectangle.contains r p) parts with
  | Some (part, _) -> Some part
  | None -> None

let shorten width_of room text =
  if width_of text <= room then text
  else begin
    let rec cut n =
      if n <= 0 then ""
      else
        let s = Utf8.sub text 0 n ^ "..." in
        if width_of s <= room then s else cut (n - 1) in
    cut (Utf8.length text - 1)
  end

let set_hidden id on ws = List.map (fun w -> if w.id = id then { w with hidden = on } else w) ws

let press ws part =
  let menu_win = menu ws in
  let hide_menu =
    match menu_win, part with
    | _, Start -> []
    | Some m, _ when not m.hidden -> [ m.id ]
    | _ -> [] in
  let ws = List.fold_left (fun ws id -> set_hidden id true ws) ws hide_menu in
  let lines = List.map (Printf.sprintf "hide -id %d") hide_menu in
  match part with
  | Start ->
      (match menu_win with
       | Some m when m.hidden -> [ Printf.sprintf "unhide -id %d" m.id ], set_hidden m.id false ws
       | Some m -> [ Printf.sprintf "hide -id %d" m.id ], set_hidden m.id true ws
       | None -> [], ws)
  | Clock -> lines, ws
  | Overview -> lines @ [ "new -popup -max -label expose expose" ], ws
  | Task t ->
      let front ws = List.map (fun w -> if w.layer <> "" then w else { w with current = w.id = t.id }) ws in
      if t.hidden then lines @ [ Printf.sprintf "unhide -id %d" t.id ], front (set_hidden t.id false ws)
      else if t.current then
        lines @ [ Printf.sprintf "hide -id %d" t.id ],
        List.map (fun w -> if w.id = t.id then { w with hidden = true; current = false } else w) ws
      else lines @ [ Printf.sprintf "current -id %d" t.id ], front ws
windows/desktop/lib/Taskbar.mli
2935
(* What the panel knows and decides, without a screen: the windows as rio
 * says them, where each button goes, what a press on one asks.
 *
 *     /dev/wsys/N/{wctl,label} --window_of--> window --layout--> buttons
 *                                                        |
 *                 a press at a point --at--> part --press--> wctl's words
 *
 * design:
 * The panel is a program like another, in a window, and rio knows nothing
 * of buttons. All it asks of rio is what any program may: read a directory
 * and two files, and write a line to a wctl. A window opened by a program
 * that never heard of a panel gets a button, because what the panel lists
 * is rio's own account of its windows.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * A list of the open programs always on the screen is Windows 95's taskbar
 * (1995), which is where the start button is from too. NeXTSTEP's Dock
 * (1989) came first with a strip of running programs, as icons. Plan 9's
 * rio has neither: its open windows are on the screen, and the hidden ones
 * are names in the right button's menu.
 *
 * others:
 * Under X a panel is also a client, but learns the windows through
 * properties a window manager agrees to set (EWMH's _NET_CLIENT_LIST and
 * _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW), and asks by sending it client messages. Here that
 * agreement is a directory and a command file. *)

type window = {
  id : int;
  label : string;
  current : bool;
  hidden : bool;
  (* wctl's last word: "" for a normal one, else desk, panel, popup *)
  layer : string;
}

(* [window_of id label wctl]: from a wctl file's read *)
val window_of : int -> string -> string -> window option

(* the ones that get a button: the normal ones *)
val tasks : window list -> window list
(* the window of the start button: a popup labelled startmenu *)
val menu : window list -> window option

type part = Start | Overview | Task of window | Clock

(* [layout r tasks clock_width]: the panel's rectangle cut in buttons: the
 * start button on the left and the overview's beside it (expose: all the
 * windows at once), the clock on the right, a button a task between, the
 * same width, narrower when there are many *)
val layout : Rectangle.t -> window list -> int -> (part * Rectangle.t) list
val at : (part * Rectangle.t) list -> Point.t -> part option

(* [shorten width_of room text]: as much of it as fits, with ... after when
 * not all does *)
val shorten : (string -> int) -> int -> string -> string

(* [press windows part]: a press on a part: the lines for wctl, and the
 * windows as they will be, so that the button changes at once and not
 * at the next look at rio's. On a task: to the front, or hidden when it
 * has the keyboard already, or back when hidden. On the overview's: expose
 * started, in a popup of all the room. The menu's shown one goes whatever
 * is pressed but the start button, which shows or hides it. *)
val press : window list -> part -> string list * window list
windows/desktop/lib/Tiles.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Tiles.mli *)

let label_h = 22
let margin = 16

let up a b = (a + b - 1) / b

let layout (area : Rectangle.t) sizes =
  let n = List.length sizes in
  if n = 0 then []
  else begin
    let cols = let rec go c = if c * c >= n then c else go (c + 1) in go 1 in
    let rows = up n cols in
    let cw = Rectangle.dx area / cols and ch = Rectangle.dy area / rows in
    List.mapi (fun i (w, h) ->
        let x0 = area.min.x + ((i mod cols) * cw) and y0 = area.min.y + ((i / cols) * ch) in
        let cell = Rectangle.v x0 y0 (x0 + cw) (y0 + ch) in
        let bw = max 1 (cw - (2 * margin)) and bh = max 1 (ch - (2 * margin) - label_h) in
        let k = max 1 (max (up (max 1 w) bw) (up (max 1 h) bh)) in
        let tw = w / k and th = h / k in
        let tx = x0 + ((cw - tw) / 2) and ty = y0 + margin + ((bh - th) / 2) in
        (cell, Rectangle.v tx ty (tx + tw) (ty + th), k))
      sizes
  end

(* Where Expose puts each window, without a screen: a grid on the area, a
 * cell a window, each window shrunk by a whole factor to fit its cell with
 * room for its name below.
 *
 *     +-----------+-----------+
 *     |  +-----+  | +-------+ |    the cells as square as the area allows:
 *     |  |  1  |  | |   2   | |    as many columns as the square root of
 *     |  +-----+  | +-------+ |    the windows, rounded up
 *     |   rc 3    |   files   |
 *     +-----------+-----------+
 *
 * A whole factor because the draw device's shrink takes one (Draw.shrink:
 * a pixel of the thumbnail for k by k of the window): a thumbnail is then
 * a little smaller than its cell, never stretched, never another shape. *)

(* [layout area sizes]: for each window's width and height, in order, its
 * cell, its thumbnail's rectangle, and k *)
val layout : Rectangle.t -> (int * int) list -> (Rectangle.t * Rectangle.t * int) list

(* the room below a thumbnail for its name *)
val label_h : int

(* See Wsys.mli *)

let read_file (caps : < Cap.open_in; .. >) path =
  try Some (FS.read caps (Fpath.v path)) with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> None

let file caps id name = read_file caps (Printf.sprintf "/dev/wsys/%d/%s" id name)

let windows (caps : < Cap.readdir; Cap.open_in; .. >) : Taskbar.window list =
  let names = try Sys_plan9.dirread caps "/dev/wsys" with Sys_error _ | Unix.Unix_error _ -> [] in
  let ids = List.filter_map (fun (d : Sys_plan9.dir) -> int_of_string_opt d.name) names in
  List.filter_map (fun id ->
      match file caps id "wctl", file caps id "label" with
      | Some wctl, Some label -> Taskbar.window_of id label wctl
      | _ -> None)
    (List.sort compare ids)

let winname caps id = file caps id "winname"

let ask (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) line =
  try
    let fd = FS.open_device_fd caps "/dev/wctl" in
    Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> Unix.close fd) (fun () -> ignore (Unix.write_substring fd line 0 (String.length line)))
  with Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _ -> ()

  read = (fun w -> Device.part w.label);
  write = (fun w data -> Window.send w (Window.Label data)) }

let text : Device.t = { Device.default with name = "text"; perm = 0o444; read = (fun w -> Device.part (Window.text w)) }

(* the pictures being read, by their window and file: one is made at a
 * read from the start, and each read is a part of it (a read of 8,000
 * bytes does not ask the screen again) *)
let pictures : (int * string, string) Hashtbl.t = Hashtbl.create 4

let picture name (image : Window.t -> Display.image) : Device.t = { Device.default with name; perm = 0o444;
  read = (fun w offset count ->
    if offset = 0 then Hashtbl.replace pictures (w.id, name) (Display.file (image w));
    match Hashtbl.find_opt pictures (w.id, name) with Some p -> Device.part p offset count | None -> "");
  closed = (fun w -> Hashtbl.remove pictures (w.id, name)) }

let window = picture "window" (fun w -> w.image)
let screen = picture "screen" (fun w -> Display.whole w.image.display)

let snarf : Device.t = { Device.default with name = "snarf";
  (* (opened to be written: what is written is all of it, as rio's) *)
  opened = (fun _ mode -> if mode land 3 <> 0 then Terminal.snarf := "");
  read = (fun _ -> Device.part !Terminal.snarf);
  write = (fun _ data -> Terminal.snarf := !Terminal.snarf ^ data) }

(* A file of a window's directory (rio's are the cases of its xfid.c;
 * xix's Device): its name, and what opening, reading, writing and
 * closing it do to its window. A file more is a value of this type,
 * and a line of Fileserver's list.
 *
 * These run in the file server's thread, which must not wait: what
 * touches a window's state is a message to its thread (Window.send),
 * and a read answered when there is something to read raises
 * P9_server.Later. One that refuses raises P9_server.Error. *)

type t = {
  name : string;
  perm : int;
  (* opened, with 9P's mode (0 to read, 1 to write, 2 both) *)
  opened : Window.t -> int -> unit;
  (* a read's offset and count; a file whose text changes under its
   * reader (the mouse) answers each read whole, whatever the offset *)
  read : Window.t -> int -> int -> string;
  write : Window.t -> string -> unit;
  (* closed, by what had it open *)
  closed : Window.t -> unit;
}

(* a file that does nothing: read empty, what is written dropped *)
val default : t
(* a read of a text: what it has from an offset, count bytes at most *)

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Fileserver.mli *)

(* a window's files: a file more is a line here *)
let devices : Device.t list =
  [ Virtual_cons.cons; Virtual_cons.consctl; Virtual_cons.kbd; Virtual_mouse.mouse; Virtual_mouse.cursor;
    Dev_wm.winname; Dev_wm.winid; Dev_wm.label; Dev_wm.text; Dev_wm.window; Dev_wm.screen; Dev_wm.snarf; Wctl.wctl ]

(* The tree. The root is what -i's process has (no window's): a wctl for
 * new, and wsys. A window's directory is what its process has, wsys
 * too, in which each window is again, as rio's. *)
type file = Root | Root_wctl | Wsys | Dir of Window.t | Dev of Window.t * Device.t

let entry (f : file) : Sys_plan9.dir =
  let rec number k (d : Device.t) = function x :: more -> if x == d then k else number (k + 1) d more | [] -> 0 in
  let name, id, code, perm, t = match f with
    | Root -> "/", 0, 0, 0o555, Sys_plan9.dmdir
    | Root_wctl -> "wctl", 0, 1, 0o666, 0
    | Wsys -> "wsys", 0, 2, 0o555, Sys_plan9.dmdir
    | Dir w -> string_of_int w.id, w.id, 0, 0o555, Sys_plan9.dmdir
    | Dev (w, d) -> d.name, w.id, number 1 d devices, d.perm, 0 in
  { name; uid = "ix"; gid = "ix"; muid = "ix"; dev_type = '\000'; dev = 0;
    qid_path = Int64.of_int ((id * 64) + code); qid_vers = 0L; qid_type = t; mode_type = t; perm;
    atime = 0.0; mtime = 0.0; length = 0 }

let refuse _ = raise (P9_server.Error "permission denied")
let absent () = raise (P9_server.Error "file does not exist")

let window_of name = Option.bind (int_of_string_opt name) Wm.find

let fs : file P9_server.fs =
  { attach = (fun _user aname ->
      if aname = "" then Root
      else match window_of aname with
        | Some win -> Dir win
        | None -> raise (P9_server.Error ("unknown window: " ^ aname)));
    walk = (fun f name ->
      match f, name with
      | (Root | Root_wctl | Wsys), ".." -> Root
      | Root, "wctl" -> Root_wctl
      | (Root | Dir _), "wsys" -> Wsys
      | Wsys, _ -> (match window_of name with Some w -> Dir w | None -> absent ())
      | (Dir w | Dev (w, _)), ".." -> Dir w
      | Dir w, _ -> (match List.find_opt (fun (d : Device.t) -> d.name = name) devices with Some d -> Dev (w, d) | None -> absent ())
      | _ -> absent ());
    stat = entry;
    opened = (fun f mode -> match f with Dev (w, d) -> d.opened w mode | _ -> ());
    read = (fun f offset count -> match f with Dev (w, d) -> d.read w offset count | _ -> "");
    entries = (fun f ->
      match f with
      | Root -> [ entry Root_wctl; entry Wsys ]
      | Wsys -> List.map (fun w -> entry (Dir w)) (List.sort (fun (a : Window.t) (b : Window.t) -> compare a.id b.id) (Wm.all ()))
      | Dir w -> List.map (fun d -> entry (Dev (w, d))) devices @ [ entry Wsys ]
      | Root_wctl | Dev _ -> []);
    write = (fun f _offset data ->
      (match f with
       | Dev (w, d) -> d.write w data
       | Root_wctl -> Wctl.written None data
       | _ -> ());
      String.length data);
    create = (fun f _ _ _ -> refuse f); remove = refuse; wstat = (fun f _ -> refuse f);
    clunk = (fun f was_open -> match f with Dev (w, d) when was_open -> d.closed w | _ -> ()) }

let serve (requests : bytes Event.channel) mine =
  let server = P9_server.make fs (fun bytes -> ignore (Unix.write_substring mine bytes 0 (String.length bytes))) in
  let pending = Buffer.create 8192 in
  let rec loop () =
    Buffer.add_bytes pending (Event.sync (Event.receive requests));
    let all = Buffer.contents pending in
    let size o = Char.code all.[o] lor (Char.code all.[o + 1] lsl 8) lor (Char.code all.[o + 2] lsl 16) in
    let rec each o = if o + 4 <= String.length all && o + size o <= String.length all then begin P9_server.request server (String.sub all o (size o)); each (o + size o) end else o in
    let rest = each 0 in
    Buffer.clear pending;
    Buffer.add_substring pending all rest (String.length all - rest);
    loop () in
  loop ()
windows/rio/Fileserver.mli

(* The files a window's process sees (Plan 9's rio is a file server:
 * its fsys.c, xfid.c; xix's Fileserver and Threads_fileserver): for
 * each window a directory of files (Device: the console in
 * Virtual_cons, the mouse in Virtual_mouse, the window's own in
 * Dev_wm, its control in Wctl), served over 9P and mounted before /dev
 * in the process's namespace. So a program in a window opens /dev/cons as it would on
 * the bare machine, and talks to the window. *)

(* The file server's thread: [serve requests mine] answers 9P's
 * requests on a pipe's end, [mine] (the other, posted in /srv, is
 * mounted by each window's process, the window's number its mount's
 * spec; the empty spec is the root, -i's process's, a wctl for new and
 * wsys; rio's own spec new, a window made by the mount, is not here:
 * one mounts a window there is, and writes its wctl). Each window's
 * directory has wsys too, as rio's: a directory by window, by number,
 * with that window's files: how a program finds the windows there are. The
 * requests are a Source's messages (a process reads the pipe), cut
 * into 9P's by their sizes. It does not return. *)
val serve : bytes Event.channel -> Unix.file_descr -> unit
windows/rio/Mouse_action.ml
3517
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Mouse_action.mli *)

type t = {
  mouse : Mouse.t; display : Display.t; desk : Display.desktop;
  set : Cursor.t option -> unit;
  (* the cursor shown: the kernel is told only when it is another (the
   * mouse on a border says its cursor at each move) *)
  mutable shown : Cursor.t option;
}

let make caps mouse display desk = { mouse; display; desk; set = (fun c -> Cursor.set caps c); shown = None }

let cursor (a : t) (c : Cursor.t option) =
  let same = match c, a.shown with Some x, Some y -> x == y | None, None -> true | _ -> false in
  if not same then begin a.shown <- c; a.set c end

(* the mouse followed until the right button is as wanted: where *)
let rec button (a : t) down = let m : Mouse.state = Event.sync (Mouse.receive a.mouse) in if (m.buttons land 4 <> 0) = down then m.pos else button a down

(* a rectangle that follows the mouse while a button is down, shown as
 * it changes (made anew at each move): what it is when the button
 * comes up *)
let band (a : t) but (rect : Point.t -> Rectangle.t) : Rectangle.t =
  let red = Display.color a.display (Display.rgb 0xdd 0x00 0x00) in
  let rec drag shown =
    let m : Mouse.state = Event.sync (Mouse.receive a.mouse) in
    Option.iter Display.free shown;
    let r = rect m.pos in
    if m.buttons land but = 0 then r
    else begin
      let shown = if Rectangle.dx r > 8 && Rectangle.dy r > 8 then begin
          let i = Display.window a.desk r (Display.rgb 0xee 0xee 0xee) in
          Draw.border i r 4 red;
          Some i
        end else None in
      Display.flush a.display;
      drag shown
    end in
  let r = drag None in
  Display.free red;
  r

let sweep (a : t) : Rectangle.t =
  cursor a (Some Cursors.cross);
  let p0 = button a true in
  let r = band a 4 (fun (p : Point.t) -> Rectangle.v (min p0.x p.x) (min p0.y p.y) (max p0.x p.x) (max p0.y p.y)) in
  cursor a None;
  r

let point (a : t) =
  cursor a (Some Cursors.sight);
  let p = button a true in
  ignore (button a false);
  cursor a None;
  Wm.at p

let drag (a : t) : (Window.t * Rectangle.t) option =
  cursor a (Some Cursors.sight);
  let p0 = button a true in
  let result = match Wm.at p0 with
    | None -> ignore (button a false); None
    | Some w -> Some (w, band a 4 (fun p -> Rectangle.add w.image.r (Point.sub p p0))) in
  cursor a None;
  result

let grab (a : t) (w : Window.t) which (m : Mouse.state) =
  Wm.front w;
  let r0 = w.image.r in
  (* (a side's two ends: the one held is the mouse's, from where it was pressed) *)
  let side k p from lo hi = if k = 0 then (min (lo + p - from) hi, max (lo + p - from) hi) else if k = 2 then (min lo (hi + p - from), max lo (hi + p - from)) else (lo, hi) in
  let r : Rectangle.t =
    if m.buttons land 4 <> 0 then begin cursor a (Some Cursors.box); band a 4 (fun p -> Rectangle.add r0 (Point.sub p m.pos)) end
    else band a (m.buttons land 3) (fun (p : Point.t) ->
        let x0, x1 = side (which mod 3) p.x m.pos.x r0.min.x r0.max.x and y0, y1 = side (which / 3) p.y m.pos.y r0.min.y r0.max.y in
        Rectangle.v x0 y0 x1 y1) in
  cursor a None;
  if r <> r0 && Wm.fits r then Window.send w (Window.Reshape r)

let hover (a : t) (m : Mouse.state) =
  if m.buttons = 0 then
    cursor a (match Wm.border m.pos, Wm.at m.pos with
      | Some (_, k), _ -> Some Cursors.corners.(k)
      | None, Some w -> w.cursor
      | None, None -> (match Wm.layer_at m.pos with Some w -> w.cursor | None -> None))

windows/rio/Processes_winshell.ml
2473
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Processes_winshell.mli *)

let flags = Sys_plan9.(rfproc lor rffdg lor rfnameg lor rfenvg lor rfnoteg lor rfnowait)

(* the window system's files before /dev, as [spec] says them, and $wsys *)
let mount_files caps srv spec =
  let served = FS.open_rw_fd caps srv in
  (try Sys_plan9.mount caps served "/mnt/wsys" Sys_plan9.mrepl spec; Sys_plan9.bind caps "/mnt/wsys" "/dev" Sys_plan9.mbefore
   with Unix.Unix_error _ -> Sys_plan9.mount caps served "/dev" Sys_plan9.mbefore spec);
  (try Fpath.v "/env/wsys" |> FS.with_open_out caps (fun (chan : Chan.o) -> output_string chan.oc srv) with Sys_error _ -> ())

(* no descriptor left open but the three, then rc *)
let run_rc caps argv =
  for fd = 3 to 63 do (try Unix.close (Obj.magic fd : Unix.file_descr) with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()) done;
  List.iter (fun rc -> try CapUnix.execv caps rc argv with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()) [ "/bin/rc"; "/boot/rc" ]

let start (caps : < Cap.chdir; Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.mount; Cap.bind; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) (w : Window.t) srv ~cd command =
  match Sys_plan9.rfork caps flags with
  | 0 ->
      (try
         mount_files caps srv (string_of_int w.id);
         (* (a directory that is not there: the window system's, and rc says nothing) *)
         (if cd <> "" then try CapUnix.chdir caps cd with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ());
         (* its console the three descriptors *)
         let cons = FS.open_rw_fd caps "/dev/cons" in
         List.iter (Unix.dup2 cons) [ Unix.stdin; Unix.stdout; Unix.stderr ];
         run_rc caps (if command = "" then [| "rc"; "-i" |] else [| "rc"; "-c"; command |])
       with Unix.Unix_error (e, fn, _) -> prerr_string ("rio: a window's process: " ^ fn ^ ": " ^ Unix.error_message e ^ "\n"));
      Unix._exit 1
  | pid -> w.pid <- pid

let init (caps : < Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.mount; Cap.bind; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. >) srv command =
  match Sys_plan9.rfork caps flags with
  | 0 ->
      (try
         mount_files caps srv "";
         run_rc caps [| "rc"; "-c"; command |]
       with Unix.Unix_error (e, fn, _) -> prerr_string ("rio: -i: " ^ fn ^ ": " ^ Unix.error_message e ^ "\n"));
      Unix._exit 1
  | _ -> ()

let note (caps : < Cap.open_out; .. >) (w : Window.t) text =
  try Fpath.v (Printf.sprintf "/proc/%d/notepg" w.pid) |> FS.with_open_out caps (fun (chan : Chan.o) -> output_string chan.oc text) with Sys_error _ -> ()

(* [start caps w srv ~cd command]: a process started for the window (w.pid

windows/rio/Rio.ml
14615
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* mini-rio: a window system, Plan 9's rio in small (principia's
 * windows/rio, 8,170 lines of C; xix's windows/, the author's in
 * OCaml, are the models; plan_rio.md). It takes the screen, the mouse
 * and the keyboard, and gives each window what looks like a machine of
 * its own: a process started in a window has its own /dev/cons, which
 * is the window. The trick is Plan 9's: rio is a file server, and the
 * window's process has rio's files mounted before /dev.
 *
 * The right button's menu, rio's: New (then a rectangle swept out with
 * that button, the cursor a cross, the rectangle shown as it grows: a
 * window, rc in it), Resize (a window pointed at, the cursor a sight,
 * then its new rectangle swept), Move (a window dragged, its outline
 * shown), Delete (a window pointed at), Hide (the same: it is then a
 * name in the menu, which brings it back), and Exit. The left button
 * on a window gives it the keyboard; Delete (or Control-C) typed in one interrupts
 * its processes. A window's border is a handle (the cursor says so
 * when the mouse is on it): the left or the middle button there pulls
 * that corner or side (its size), the right one the window (its place). In a window's scroll bar the buttons scroll its text
 * (the arrows too); in its text the left button selects, and the
 * middle one's menu has snarf, paste, send, and scroll or noscroll
 * (noscroll: a window that is full holds what its program writes until
 * one scrolls: a pager). The text is not edited:
 * what is typed goes at its end (rio's is edited anywhere; the author:
 * "I rarely used that feature of rio").
 *
 * Its modules, as xix's: Wm (the windows, which is in front, what the
 * menu does to one), Mouse_action (a rectangle swept, a window pointed
 * at or dragged), Window (a window's thread) and Terminal (its text),
 * Processes_winshell (its process), Fileserver (its files, each a
 * Device: Virtual_cons, Virtual_mouse, Dev_wm, and Wctl, by which a
 * program does what the menu does), Cursors.
 *
 * Its threads, as rio's (Rob Pike's design: each is a small loop of
 * its own, and they talk by channels):
 * - this one, the window system: the mouse and the keyboard, the menu,
 *   which window is in front; it sends the keys and the mouse to that
 *   window;
 * - the file server (Fileserver.serve): the windows' processes' requests,
 *   each sent to its window;
 * - a thread a window (Window.run).
 * None waits in a read: the mouse, the keyboard and the requests are
 * Sources (a process reads each), so a menu held open stops nothing
 * else.
 *
 * Who talks to whom, for one window:
 *
 *     the kernel:  /dev/mouse   /dev/cons   /dev/draw
 *                      |            |           ^
 *                      v            v           | the windows drawn
 *     +----------------------------------------------------+
 *     | mini-rio   the window system's thread (the menu)   |
 *     |                |  keys and mouse, to the one in    |
 *     |                v  front                            |
 *     |            window 1's thread     window 2's ...    |
 *     |                ^  a read, a write of its files     |
 *     |            the file server's thread                |
 *     +----------------^-----------------------------------+
 *                      | 9P, on the pipe posted in /srv
 *     rc, in window 1: its name space has rio's files for
 *     that window before /dev's. It reads /dev/cons: a line
 *     typed in the window. It writes it: text in the window.
 *
 * rio -i command: that command run at the start, in a process with no
 * window, whose /dev/wctl makes them: a session, as a script (Plan 9's
 * riostart; desktop is one, plan_desktop.md). rio alone starts nothing.
 *
 * reframe:
 * A window system is a multiplexer: one screen, one mouse and one
 * keyboard made into several, as a kernel makes one processor into
 * several. What a window's program is given has the names and the
 * behaviour of what the window system itself took (cons, mouse, and
 * an image to draw in), so a program cannot tell a window from the
 * bare machine and needs no library to be in one; and in Plan 9 rio
 * runs in a window of rio, as any program does.
 *
 * cs-history:
 * The line is Rob Pike's, at Bell Labs. The Blit (with Bart
 * Locanthi, 1982) was a terminal with a bitmap screen and its own
 * processor, its windows each a process, all sharing one serial
 * line to Unix. For Plan 9 he wrote 8 1/2 (1991), the window system
 * as a file server, and showed that it could be small because the
 * system did the rest: no protocol of its own, no terminal
 * emulation, the name space for the plumbing. rio (2000) is 8 1/2
 * written again as threads that talk on channels, the style of his
 * "A Concurrent Window System" (1989), and over a new draw device
 * where a window is an image the kernel keeps and a program draws
 * in it without passing by rio.
 *
 * others:
 * X (MIT, 1984; X11 in 1987) is a server too, but of its own
 * protocol, over a hundred kinds of requests on a socket, that
 * programs speak through a library; the window manager is one more
 * client; and text is not its business: a program that only prints
 * runs in xterm, a client that pretends to be a terminal of the
 * 1970s on a pseudo-terminal. Three large mechanisms where Plan 9
 * has files it already had. The price is paid elsewhere: a window
 * here is a terminal and a rectangle of pixels, with no widgets.
 *
 * References: Rob Pike, "8 1/2, the Plan 9 Window System" (USENIX,
 * Summer 1991), the paper to read first; his "The Blit: A
 * Multiplexed Graphics Terminal" (AT&T Bell Laboratories Technical
 * Journal, 1984), "A Concurrent Window System" (Computing Systems,
 * 1989) and "Rio: Design of a Concurrent Window System" (a talk,
 * 2000); rio(1), rio(4); R. Scheifler and J. Gettys, "The X Window
 * System" (ACM Transactions on Graphics, 1986); principia's book on
 * rio. *)

type caps =
  < Cap.chdir; Cap.argv; Cap.draw; Cap.mouse; Cap.keyboard; Cap.fork; Cap.exec;
    Cap.mount; Cap.bind; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; Cap.env; Cap.pipe >

type event = Mouse of Mouse.state | Keys of string list | Held of string | Asked of Window.t option * Wctl.command

let main (caps : < caps; .. >) (argv : string array) : Exit.t =
  let init =
    if Array.length argv = 1 then None
    else if Array.length argv = 3 && argv.(1) = "-i" then Some argv.(2)
    else failwith "usage: rio [-i command]" in
  let display = Display.init caps in
  let view = Display.whole display and font = Font.default display in
  let mouse = Mouse.init caps and keyboard = Keyboard.init caps in
  (* the desktop: a grey blue where no window is (ix's colours: rio's
   * desktop is grey, its borders and menus green; one sees which it is) *)
  let grey = Display.color display (Display.rgb 0x66 0x77 0x88) in
  let pid = CapUnix.getpid caps () in
  Window.pid := pid;
  let desk = Display.desktop view grey pid in
  Draw.fill view view.r grey;
  Display.flush display;
  (* the windows' files, posted as rio's (/srv/rio.user.pid there): a
   * window's process mounts them, and whoever is given $wsys *)
  let srv = Printf.sprintf "/srv/rio.%d" pid in
  let mine = P9_server.post caps (Filename.basename srv) in
  ignore (Thread.create (fun () -> Fileserver.serve (Source.reader caps mine 4000) mine) ());
  (* (the keys held, where the kernel says them: for the programs that ask, a window's kbd file) *)
  let kbd = match Keyboard.held caps with Some h -> [ Event.wrap (Keyboard.message h) (fun m -> Held m) ] | None -> [] in
  let next () = Event.select ([ Event.wrap (Mouse.receive mouse) (fun m -> Mouse m); Event.wrap (Keyboard.receive keyboard) (fun k -> Keys k);
                                Event.wrap (Event.receive Wctl.requests) (fun (w, c) -> Asked (w, c)) ] @ kbd) in
  let make = Wm.create caps desk font srv in
  let action = Mouse_action.make caps mouse display desk in
  Window.note := Processes_winshell.note caps;
  Window.restack := Wm.restack;
  Option.iter (Processes_winshell.init caps srv) init;
  (* the buttons at the event before; the window that has the mouse until they are up *)
  let held = ref 0 and selecting : Window.t option ref = ref None in
  (* the buttons at the last event, whoever had it (the menus read the
   * mouse themselves: none down after them) *)
  let was = ref 0 in
  (* The mouse for a window of a layer, which has it without coming to the
   * front: whether it took this event. A press anywhere but in a panel
   * hides the popups (a panel's own: its button that shows one must
   * not see it hidden, and shows it again). The right button on a desk
   * stays the window system's: its menu. *)
  let to_layer (m : Mouse.state) =
    let fresh = m.buttons <> 0 && !was = 0 in
    was := m.buttons;
    match !selecting with
    | Some w when w.layer <> Window.Normal ->
        Window.send w (Window.Moved m);
        if m.buttons = 0 then selecting := None;
        true
    | Some _ -> false
    | None ->
        let there = Wm.layer_at m.pos in
        let in_panel = match there with Some w -> w.layer = Window.Panel | None -> false in
        if fresh && not in_panel then
          List.iter (fun (p : Window.t) -> if not (Rectangle.contains p.image.r m.pos) then Wm.hide p) (Wm.popups ());
        (* (again: what was there may have been a popup now hidden) *)
        (match Wm.layer_at m.pos with
         | Some w when (fresh || m.buttons = 0) && not (w.layer = Window.Desk && m.buttons land 4 <> 0) ->
             Window.send w (Window.Moved m);
             if fresh then selecting := Some w;
             true
         | _ -> false) in
  let rec loop last =
    Display.flush display;
    match next () with
    | Keys [] -> loop last
    | Keys keys -> Option.iter (fun w -> Window.send w (Window.Keys keys)) (Wm.current ()); loop last
    | Held m -> Option.iter (fun w -> Window.send w (Window.Held m)) (Wm.current ()); loop last
    (* a wctl file written: what the menu does, asked by a program *)
    | Asked (_, c) when c.verb = Wctl.Exit -> ()
    | Asked (w, c) -> Wm.control caps make view.r w c; loop last
    | Mouse m when (Window.pointer := m;
                    Mouse_action.hover action m;
                    to_layer m) -> loop last
    (* the mouse in the front window, when its program reads it, is the program's *)
    | Mouse m when (match !Wm.windows with w :: _ -> w.wants_mouse && not w.hidden && Rectangle.contains w.image.r m.pos && not (Window.on_border w m.pos) | [] -> false) ->
        Window.send (List.hd !Wm.windows) (Window.Moved m); loop last
    (* a button went down in a window's scroll bar, or the left one in its
     * text: the mouse is that window's until the buttons are up (its
     * text scrolls, or is selected) *)
    | Mouse m when !selecting <> None ->
        Option.iter (fun w -> Window.send w (Window.Moved m)) !selecting;
        if m.buttons = 0 then selecting := None;
        held := m.buttons;
        loop last
    (* a button pressed on a window's border: its size, or its place (the
     * mouse is read there until the button is up) *)
    | Mouse m when m.buttons <> 0 && !held = 0 && (match Wm.border m.pos with Some (w, k) -> Mouse_action.grab action w k m; was := 0; true | None -> false) -> loop last
    (* a button pressed in a window's scroll bar is the window's: it scrolls
     * (once a press: [held] is the buttons at the event before) *)
    | Mouse m when (let fresh = m.buttons <> 0 && !held = 0 in
                    held := m.buttons;
                    fresh && (match Wm.at m.pos with Some w -> Window.in_bar w m.pos | None -> false)) ->
        (match Wm.at m.pos with
         | Some w -> (match !Wm.windows with f :: _ when f == w -> () | _ -> Wm.front w); Window.send w (Window.Moved m); selecting := Some w
         | None -> ());
        loop last
    | Mouse m when m.buttons land 4 <> 0 -> (
        (* (the menu and what follows read the mouse themselves: no button is down after) *)
        held := 0;
        was := 0;
        (* rio's menu, and under it the hidden windows, by their labels *)
        let hidden = Wm.hidden () in
        let items = [ "New"; "Resize"; "Move"; "Delete"; "Hide" ] @ List.map (fun (w : Window.t) -> w.label) hidden @ [ "Exit" ] in
        match Menu.hit view font mouse 4 items last m.pos with
        | Some 0 ->
            (* (too small a rectangle, a click: a window of 400 by 240 there) *)
            let r : Rectangle.t = Mouse_action.sweep action in
            ignore (make (if Wm.fits r then r else Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y (r.min.x + 400) (r.min.y + 240)) Wctl.plain);
            loop 0
        | Some 1 ->
            (* a window pointed at, then its new rectangle swept out *)
            (match Mouse_action.point action with
             | Some w -> let r = Mouse_action.sweep action in if Wm.fits r then Wm.reshape w r
             | None -> ());
            loop 1
        | Some 2 -> (match Mouse_action.drag action with Some (w, r) -> Wm.reshape w r | None -> ()); loop 2
        | Some 3 -> Option.iter (Wm.delete caps) (Mouse_action.point action); loop 3
        | Some 4 -> Option.iter Wm.hide (Mouse_action.point action); loop 4
        | Some k when k < 5 + List.length hidden -> Wm.show (List.nth hidden (k - 5)); loop last
        | Some _ -> ()
        | None -> loop last)
    (* the middle button in a window: its text's menu (Terminal's); what
     * it gives is typed there *)
    | Mouse m when m.buttons land 2 <> 0 ->
        held := 0;
        was := 0;
        (match Wm.at m.pos with
         | Some w ->
             Wm.front w;
             (match Terminal.menu w.text view mouse m.pos with
              | Terminal.Typed text -> if text <> "" then Window.send w (Window.Keys (fst (Utf8.chars text)))
              | Terminal.Scroll on -> Window.send w (Window.Scroll on)
              | Terminal.Nothing -> ())
         | None -> ());
        loop last
    (* the left button on a window: it comes in front, and has the mouse
     * until the button is up *)
    | Mouse m when m.buttons land 1 <> 0 ->
        (match Wm.at m.pos with Some w -> Wm.front w; Window.send w (Window.Moved m); selecting := Some w | None -> ());
        loop last
    | Mouse _ -> loop last in
  loop 0;
  List.iter (Wm.delete caps) (Wm.all ());
  (try FS.remove_any caps srv with Unix.Unix_error _ | Sys_error _ -> ());
  Display.close display;
  Exit.OK

let () = Cap.main (fun caps -> Exit.exit caps (Exit.catch (fun () -> main caps (CapSys.argv caps))))
windows/rio/Terminal.ml

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Terminal.mli *)

type t = {
  image : Display.image; r : Rectangle.t; font : Font.t;
  cols : int; rows : int;
  mutable past : string list;                  (* the lines above the last, the newest first: 1,000 at most *)
  mutable last : string;
  mutable back : int;                          (* how many lines up from the end is shown: 0, the end *)
  mutable scrolling : bool;                    (* what is shown follows what is written *)
  (* a place in the text is a line's number (how many lines were ended
   * before it: the last line's is [ended]) and a column. The text
   * selected is from a place to another, the second not in it; while
   * the left button is down, [anchor] is where it went down *)
  mutable ended : int;
  mutable selected : ((int * int) * (int * int)) option;
  mutable anchor : (int * int) option;
  mutable clicked : (int * int) * int;         (* the left button's last press: where, when (ms) *)
  mutable part : string;                       (* a character's first bytes, written without its last *)
  mutable held : int;                          (* the mouse's buttons at the event before *)
  cell : int;                                  (* a character's width *)
  ink : Display.image; paper : Display.image; bar : Display.image; mark : Display.image;
}

let kept = 1000
(* the scroll bar's width, and the space before the text (rio's is 12 and 4) *)
let bar_w = 10 and gap = 4

(* the text's own rectangle: right of the scroll bar *)
let text_r (t : t) = Rectangle.v (t.r.min.x + bar_w + gap) t.r.min.y t.r.max.x t.r.max.y

let make (image : Display.image) (r : Rectangle.t) font =
  let cell = max 1 (Font.width font "m") in
  let d = image.display in
  { image; r; font; cols = max 1 ((Rectangle.dx r - bar_w - gap) / cell); rows = max 1 (Rectangle.dy r / Font.height font);
    past = []; last = ""; back = 0; scrolling = true; ended = 0; selected = None; anchor = None; clicked = ((-1, 0), 0); held = 0; cell; part = "";
    ink = Display.color d Display.black; paper = Display.color d Display.white; bar = Display.color d (Display.rgb 0x99 0x99 0x99);
    (* (what is selected: a pale blue behind it, ix's; rio's is a grey green) *)
    mark = Display.color d (Display.rgb 0xb8 0xcc 0xe0) }

let rec take n = function [] -> [] | l :: more -> if n = 0 then [] else l :: take (n - 1) more
let rec drop n l = if n = 0 then l else match l with [] -> [] | _ :: more -> drop (n - 1) more

(* the lines shown, the first on top: [rows] of them, [back] lines before the end *)
let shown (t : t) = List.rev (take t.rows (drop t.back (t.last :: t.past)))

(* the number of the line on row k of what is shown *)
let line_at (t : t) k = t.ended - t.back - (min t.rows (1 + List.length t.past - t.back) - 1) + k

(* a row of the rectangle drawn again: its line, or nothing; what is
 * selected of it on its mark *)
let row (t : t) k line =
  let tr : Rectangle.t = text_r t in
  let y = tr.min.y + (k * Font.height t.font) in
  Draw.fill t.image (Rectangle.v tr.min.x y tr.max.x (y + Font.height t.font)) t.paper;
  (match t.selected with
   | Some ((l0, c0), (l1, c1)) ->
       let n = line_at t k in
       if n >= l0 && n <= l1 then begin
         let from = if n = l0 then c0 else 0 and upto = if n = l1 then c1 else Utf8.length line + 1 in
         if upto > from then Draw.fill t.image (Rectangle.v (tr.min.x + (from * t.cell)) y (min tr.max.x (tr.min.x + (upto * t.cell))) (y + Font.height t.font)) t.mark
       end
   | None -> ());
  ignore (Font.string t.image (Point.v tr.min.x y) t.ink t.font line)

(* the scroll bar: grey, and white where the lines shown are among all of them *)
let scroll_bar (t : t) =
  let total = 1 + List.length t.past in
  let h = Rectangle.dy t.r in
  let first = max 0 (total - t.back - t.rows) in
  let y0 = t.r.min.y + (h * first / total) and y1 = t.r.min.y + (h * (total - t.back) / total) in
  Draw.fill t.image (Rectangle.v t.r.min.x t.r.min.y (t.r.min.x + bar_w) t.r.max.y) t.bar;
  Draw.fill t.image (Rectangle.v t.r.min.x y0 (t.r.min.x + bar_w - 1) (max (y0 + 2) y1)) t.paper

let all (t : t) =
  Draw.fill t.image (text_r t) t.paper;
  List.iteri (fun k line -> row t k line) (shown t);
  scroll_bar t

let redraw = all

(* the last line ended: one more above it, the oldest forgotten; a
 * reader of what is above stays where it is, and so does what is shown
 * when it does not scroll and is full (the end is then below it) *)
let newline (t : t) =
  t.past <- take kept (t.last :: t.past);
  t.last <- "";
  t.ended <- t.ended + 1;
  if t.back > 0 || (not t.scrolling && 1 + List.length t.past > t.rows) then t.back <- min (t.back + 1) (List.length t.past)

let put (t : t) text =
  let moved = ref false and before = t.back in
  (* (a write may end inside a character: its start waits for the next) *)
  let whole, part = Utf8.chars (t.part ^ text) in
  t.part <- part;
  List.iter (fun c ->
    (match c with
     | "\n" -> newline t; moved := true
     | "\t" -> t.last <- t.last ^ String.make (8 - (Utf8.length t.last mod 8)) ' '
     | c when c >= " " -> t.last <- t.last ^ c
     | _ -> ());
    if Utf8.length t.last >= t.cols then begin newline t; moved := true end) whole;
  if t.back > 0 && before > 0 then scroll_bar t   (* (what is shown did not change: only where it is) *)
  else if !moved then all t
  else row t (min (List.length t.past) (t.rows - 1)) t.last

let erase (t : t) =
  if t.last <> "" then begin
    t.last <- Utf8.sub t.last 0 (Utf8.length t.last - 1);
    if t.back = 0 then row t (min (List.length t.past) (t.rows - 1)) t.last
  end

let scroll (t : t) n =
  let back = max 0 (min (t.back + n) (1 + List.length t.past - t.rows)) in
  if back <> t.back then begin t.back <- back; all t end

let half (t : t) = max 1 (t.rows / 2)

let at_end (t : t) = t.back = 0
let scrolling (t : t) = t.scrolling
let set_scrolling (t : t) on = t.scrolling <- on; if on then scroll t (-100000)

(* the scroll bar's rectangle, at the text's left *)
let in_bar (r : Rectangle.t) (p : Point.t) = Rectangle.contains r p && p.x < r.min.x + bar_w

(* the place in the text under a point: its row's line, the column
 * its x is in (not past the line's end) *)
let place (t : t) (p : Point.t) =
  let tr : Rectangle.t = text_r t in
  let lines = shown t in
  let k = max 0 (min (List.length lines - 1) ((p.y - tr.min.y) / Font.height t.font)) in
  line_at t k, max 0 (min (Utf8.length (List.nth lines k)) ((p.x - tr.min.x + (t.cell / 2)) / t.cell))

let contents (t : t) = String.concat "\n" (List.rev (t.last :: t.past))

(* the line of a number ("" when it is forgotten) *)
let line (t : t) n = let k = t.ended - n in if k = 0 then t.last else match List.nth_opt t.past (k - 1) with Some l -> l | None -> ""

(* the text selected, its lines ended by newlines but the last *)
let selection (t : t) =
  match t.selected with
  | None -> ""
  | Some ((l0, c0), (l1, c1)) ->
      let line = line t in
      let part n =
        let l = line n in
        let from = if n = l0 then c0 else 0 and upto = if n = l1 then c1 else Utf8.length l in
        Utf8.sub l from (max 0 (upto - from)) in
      String.concat "\n" (List.init (l1 - l0 + 1) (fun k -> part (l0 + k)))

(* What a double click at a place selects (rio's wdoubleclick, on one
 * line): after an opening bracket or quote, up to the one that closes
 * it, those inside counted (before a closing one, back to its opening
 * one; none found: nothing); at the line's start or end, the line and
 * its newline; else the word there (letters, digits, _ and what is
 * not ASCII) *)
let pairs = [ "{", "}"; "[", "]"; "(", ")"; "<", ">"; "\xc2\xab", "\xc2\xbb"; "\"", "\""; "'", "'"; "`", "`" ]

let double (t : t) ((n, c) : int * int) =
  let chars = Array.of_list (fst (Utf8.chars (line t n))) in
  let len = Array.length chars in
  (* from k by steps of d: where [close] is, the [opening]s met on the way closed first *)
  let rec matching opening close d k nest =
    if k < 0 || k >= len then None
    else if chars.(k) = close then (if nest = 0 then Some k else matching opening close d (k + d) (nest - 1))
    else matching opening close d (k + d) (if chars.(k) = opening then nest + 1 else nest) in
  let after = if c > 0 then List.assoc_opt chars.(c - 1) pairs else None
  and before = if c < len then List.find_opt (fun (_, r) -> r = chars.(c)) pairs else None in
  match after, before with
  | Some close, _ -> (match matching chars.(c - 1) close 1 c 0 with Some k -> (n, c), (n, k) | None -> (n, c), (n, c))
  | None, Some (opening, close) -> (match matching close opening (-1) (c - 1) 0 with Some k -> (n, k + 1), (n, c) | None -> (n, c), (n, c))
  | None, None ->
      if c = 0 || c >= len then (n, 0), (if n < t.ended then (n + 1, 0) else (n, len))
      else begin
        let word k = k >= 0 && k < len && (match chars.(k).[0] with 'a' .. 'z' | 'A' .. 'Z' | '0' .. '9' | '_' -> true | ch -> ch >= '\x80') in
        let rec left k = if word (k - 1) then left (k - 1) else k and right k = if word k then right (k + 1) else k in
        (n, left c), (n, right c)
      end

(* The mouse in the text's rectangle; what it means is the text's to
 * say (rio's terminal.c). A button just pressed in the scroll bar
 * scrolls, as rio's: the left one back and the right one forward, by
 * as many lines as the mouse is below the bar's top (near the top a
 * line, at the bottom a windowful); the middle one shows what is at
 * that place among all the lines. The left button in the text
 * selects: from where it goes down to where the mouse is, until it
 * comes up; a double click, what [double] says. *)
let mouse (t : t) (m : Mouse.state) =
  let fresh = m.buttons <> 0 && t.held = 0 in
  t.held <- m.buttons;
  if fresh && in_bar t.r m.pos then begin
    let lines = max 1 ((m.pos.y - t.r.min.y) / Font.height t.font) in
    if m.buttons land 1 <> 0 then scroll t lines
    else if m.buttons land 4 <> 0 then scroll t (- lines)
    else if m.buttons land 2 <> 0 then begin
      let total = 1 + List.length t.past in
      let first = total * (m.pos.y - t.r.min.y) / max 1 (Rectangle.dy t.r) in
      scroll t ((total - first - t.rows) - t.back)
    end
  end
  else if m.buttons land 1 <> 0 then begin
    let here = place t m.pos in
    if fresh then begin
      let at, msec = t.clicked in
      if at = here && m.msec - msec < 500 then begin
        (* (the button's release selects nothing else; a third click is a first) *)
        t.anchor <- None; t.clicked <- ((-1, 0), 0); t.selected <- Some (double t here); all t
      end
      else begin t.anchor <- Some here; t.clicked <- (here, m.msec) end
    end;
    (match t.anchor with
     | Some a ->
         let now = if compare a here <= 0 then Some (a, here) else Some (here, a) in
         if now <> t.selected then begin t.selected <- now; all t end
     | None -> ())
  end
  else t.anchor <- None

(* (one for all the windows; the menu opens on the item last chosen) *)
let snarf = ref "" and chosen = ref 0

type answer = [%mli]

let menu (t : t) screen mouse at =
  match Menu.hit screen t.font mouse 2 [ "snarf"; "paste"; "send"; (if t.scrolling then "noscroll" else "scroll") ] !chosen at with
  | Some 0 -> chosen := 0; (let text = selection t in if text <> "" then snarf := text); Nothing
  | Some 1 -> chosen := 1; Typed !snarf
  | Some 2 -> chosen := 2; Typed (if String.ends_with ~suffix:"\n" !snarf then !snarf else !snarf ^ "\n")
  | Some 3 -> Scroll (not t.scrolling)
  | _ -> Nothing

let reshape (t : t) (image : Display.image) r =
  let fresh = make image r t.font in
  fresh.past <- t.past;
  fresh.last <- t.last;
  fresh.ended <- t.ended;
  fresh.selected <- t.selected;
  fresh.scrolling <- t.scrolling;
  all fresh;
  fresh
windows/rio/Terminal.mli
4369
(* A window's text (Plan 9's rio shows a window's /dev/cons so: its
 * terminal.c; xix's Terminal): lines of characters in a rectangle of
 * an image, in one font whose characters are all as wide; what is
 * written is added at the end, and the lines move up when the
 * rectangle is full. The lines that left are kept (1,000 of them): one
 * scrolls back to them, and a bar on the left shows where what is
 * seen is among them all (rio's scroll bar). The mouse selects text.
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * No terminal is emulated. On Unix a window for text is a program
 * that imitates a DEC VT100: what is written to it is text mixed
 * with escape sequences (move the cursor there, clear to the end of
 * the line, this colour), which programs find in a database of
 * terminals (termcap, terminfo) and use through a library (curses),
 * and the kernel has a line discipline between the two. A window
 * here understands a newline and a tab ([put]): text goes at the
 * end, and it stays, so one scrolls back, selects it and sends
 * it again. A program that wants the whole rectangle does not
 * address a cursor: it opens the mouse and draws (Virtual_mouse,
 * Dev_wm), as the editors do. So there is no vi in a Plan 9 window,
 * and no need of clear, reset or stty.
 *
 * Ours: text is added at the end only (Rio says why); rio's can be
 * edited anywhere, as a file in an editor. *)

type t

val make : Display.image -> Rectangle.t -> Font.t -> t
(* text added: a newline ends a line, a tab goes to the next column of 8 *)
val put : t -> string -> unit
(* the last character of the last line taken back (a backspace's) *)
val erase : t -> unit
(* what is shown moved by n lines: up (back in what was written) when
 * positive, down when negative; half of what the rectangle shows, in
 * lines (the arrow keys' step, as rio's) *)
val scroll : t -> int -> unit
val half : t -> int
(* Whether what is shown follows what is written (rio's scroll and
 * noscroll; it does, at first: rio's does not, but with -s). When it
 * does not and the rectangle is full, what is written is below what is
 * shown: one scrolls to read it, and a window holds its program's
 * writes until then (a pager for any program). [set_scrolling t true]
 * shows the end. *)
val scrolling : t -> bool
val set_scrolling : t -> bool -> unit
(* whether the end of the text is shown *)
val at_end : t -> bool
(* The mouse in the text's rectangle: what it means there. A button
 * just pressed in the scroll bar scrolls, as rio's: the left one back,
 * the right one forward, by the lines the mouse is below the bar's
 * top; the middle one to that place among all the lines. The left
 * button in the text selects, from where it goes down to where the
 * mouse is until it comes up: the text selected is shown on a mark.
 * Pressed again at the same place within half a second (a double
 * click, rio's wdoubleclick): just after an opening bracket or quote,
 * what is up to the one that closes it (just before a closing one,
 * back to the one that opens it), on that line; at a line's start or
 * end, the line; else the word there. *)
val mouse : t -> Mouse.state -> unit
(* the middle button's menu (rio's button2menu, in its terminal.c),

let cons : Device.t = { Device.default with name = "cons";
  opened = (fun w _ -> w.cons_opens <- w.cons_opens + 1);
  closed = (fun w ->
    w.cons_opens <- w.cons_opens - 1;
    if w.cons_opens = 0 && w.ends then Wctl.ended w);
  read = (fun w _ count -> Device.later w (fun reply -> Window.Read (reply, count)));
  write = (fun w data -> Device.later w (fun reply -> Window.Wrote (data, reply))) }

let consctl : Device.t = { Device.default with name = "consctl"; perm = 0o222;
  write = (fun w data -> if data = "rawon" then Window.send w (Window.Raw true) else if data = "rawoff" then Window.send w (Window.Raw false));
  (* (the program that had the raw keyboard is done with it) *)
  closed = (fun w -> Window.send w (Window.Raw false)) }

  read = (fun w _ _ -> Device.later w (fun reply -> Window.Held_read reply));
  closed = (fun w -> Window.send w (Window.Held_file false)) }

(* A window's console (rio's Qcons, Qconsctl; xix's Virtual_cons; and
 * 9front's kbd): what a program in a window opens as /dev/cons.
 *
 * Two modes. Cooked: the window keeps what is typed, one corrects it
 * there, and a read gets a whole line at the newline. Raw: a read
 * gets the keys as they are typed (an editor, a game, a password).
 *
 * plan9-is-cleaner:
 * A program asks for raw by writing the word rawon in a second
 * file, /dev/consctl, and gets cooked back with rawoff, or by
 * closing it. On Unix the same is an ioctl on the terminal with a
 * structure of dozens of flags (termios; stty prints them), kept
 * by the kernel after the program dies, which is why a terminal is
 * left unusable when one is killed in raw mode. A control file of
 * words needs no call of its own, no header to compile against, and
 * works from the shell and across the network. *)

(* read: a line typed in the window, when there is one (the keys as
 * they come, when raw); written: text for the window (a write
 * answered when the window shows it: at once, but in one that does
 * not scroll and is full). Closed by the last who has it open: a
 * window made with a command goes, its command being done (rio's
 * too: its count is of all the window's files, where a program that
 * only reads another window's label would keep it there) *)
val cons : Device.t
(* "rawon" and "rawoff" written: the keys as they are typed, no line
 * kept and no echo; closed: the lines again *)
val consctl : Device.t
(* the keys held, for a program that asks (a game): a read is the next
 * change, as the kernel's /dev/kbd says it; kept from when it is opened *)
val kbd : Device.t
