(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Wctl.mli *)

type verb = [%mli]
type command = [%mli]

let verbs = [ "new", New; "resize", Resize; "move", Move; "top", Top; "bottom", Bottom; "current", Current;
              "hide", Hide; "unhide", Unhide; "delete", Delete; "scroll", Scroll; "noscroll", Noscroll; "exit", Exit ]

let plain : command =
  { verb = New; place = (fun r -> r); area = None; hidden = false; scrolling = None; id = None; arg = ""; label = ""; cd = ""; hold = false; layer = Window.Normal }

(* -edge's rectangle: along a side of the area, [size] deep *)
let along side size (work : Rectangle.t) =
  if side = "top" then Rectangle.v work.min.x work.min.y work.max.x (work.min.y + size)
  else if side = "bottom" then Rectangle.v work.min.x (work.max.y - size) work.max.x work.max.y
  else if side = "left" then Rectangle.v work.min.x work.min.y (work.min.x + size) work.max.y
  else Rectangle.v (work.max.x - size) work.min.y work.max.x work.max.y

(* -at's rectangle: a corner, a side or the middle of the area *)
let anchored where wide high (work : Rectangle.t) =
  let w = min wide (Rectangle.dx work) and h = min high (Rectangle.dy work) in
  let x = if String.contains where 'w' then work.min.x else if String.contains where 'e' then work.max.x - w else work.min.x + ((Rectangle.dx work - w) / 2) in
  let y = if String.contains where 'n' then work.min.y else if String.contains where 's' then work.max.y - h else work.min.y + ((Rectangle.dy work - h) / 2) in
  Rectangle.v x y (x + w) (y + h)

let parse text : command =
  let bad m = raise (P9_server.Error m) in
  (* (rio's numbers may be in square brackets, as it prints a rectangle) *)
  let number s =
    let s = String.concat "" (String.split_on_char '[' (String.concat "" (String.split_on_char ']' s))) in
    match int_of_string_opt s with Some n -> n | None -> bad "missing or bad wctl parameter" in
  let blank c = if c = '\n' || c = '\t' then ' ' else c in
  let verb, rest = match List.filter (fun s -> s <> "") (String.split_on_char ' ' (String.map blank text)) with
    | v :: rest when List.mem_assoc v verbs -> List.assoc v verbs, rest
    | _ -> bad "unrecognized wctl command" in
  let rec flags (c : command) = function
    | "-hide" :: more -> flags { c with hidden = true } more
    | "-scroll" :: more -> flags { c with scrolling = Some true } more
    | "-noscroll" :: more -> flags { c with scrolling = Some false } more
    | "-id" :: n :: more -> flags { c with id = Some (number n) } more
    | "-max" :: more -> flags { c with area = Some (fun work -> work) } more
    | "-at" :: where :: w :: h :: more when List.mem where [ "nw"; "n"; "ne"; "w"; "c"; "e"; "sw"; "s"; "se" ] ->
        let w = number w and h = number h in
        flags { c with area = Some (anchored where w h) } more
    | "-at" :: _ -> bad "missing or bad wctl parameter"
    | "-edge" :: side :: n :: more when List.mem side [ "top"; "bottom"; "left"; "right" ] ->
        let n = number n in
        flags { c with area = Some (along side n) } more
    | "-edge" :: _ -> bad "missing or bad wctl parameter"
    | "-desk" :: more -> flags { c with layer = Window.Desk } more
    | "-panel" :: more -> flags { c with layer = Window.Panel } more
    | "-popup" :: more -> flags { c with layer = Window.Popup } more
    | "-label" :: l :: more -> flags { c with label = l } more
    | "-cd" :: d :: more -> flags { c with cd = d } more
    | "-hold" :: more -> flags { c with hold = true } more
    | "-r" :: x0 :: y0 :: x1 :: y1 :: more -> let r = Rectangle.v (number x0) (number y0) (number x1) (number y1) in flags { c with place = (fun _ -> r) } more
    | side :: n :: more when List.mem side [ "-minx"; "-miny"; "-maxx"; "-maxy"; "-dx"; "-dy" ] ->
        (* a side's place: a number, or after a sign that much from where it is *)
        let signed = n <> "" && (n.[0] = '-' || n.[0] = '+') in
        let v = number (if signed then String.sub n 1 (String.length n - 1) else n) in
        let set old said = if not signed then said else if n.[0] = '-' then old - v else old + v in
        let edit (r : Rectangle.t) =
          if side = "-minx" then Rectangle.v (set r.min.x v) r.min.y r.max.x r.max.y
          else if side = "-miny" then Rectangle.v r.min.x (set r.min.y v) r.max.x r.max.y
          else if side = "-maxx" then Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y (set r.max.x v) r.max.y
          else if side = "-maxy" then Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y r.max.x (set r.max.y v)
          else if side = "-dx" then Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y (set r.max.x (r.min.x + v)) r.max.y
          else Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y r.max.x (set r.max.y (r.min.y + v)) in
        let before = c.place in
        flags { c with place = (fun r -> edit (before r)) } more
    | flag :: _ when flag.[0] = '-' && verb <> New -> bad "missing or bad wctl parameter"
    | rest -> c, rest in
  let c, rest = flags { plain with verb } rest in
  if verb <> New && rest <> [] then bad "extraneous text in wctl message";
  { c with arg = String.concat " " rest }

let requests : (Window.t option * command) Event.channel = Event.new_channel ()

let ask w c = ignore (Thread.create (fun () -> Event.sync (Event.send requests (w, c))) ())
let ended w = ask (Some w) { plain with verb = Delete }
let written w data = ask w (parse data)

let wctl : Device.t = { Device.default with name = "wctl";
  read = (fun w ->
    let r = w.image.r in
    Device.part (Printf.sprintf "%11d %11d %11d %11d %s %s %s" r.min.x r.min.y r.max.x r.max.y
                   (if w.current then "current" else "notcurrent") (if w.hidden then "hidden" else "visible")
                   (match w.layer with Window.Normal -> "" | Window.Desk -> "desk " | Window.Panel -> "panel " | Window.Popup -> "popup ")));
  write = (fun w data -> written (Some w) data) }
windows/rio/Wctl.mli
3556
(* A window's wctl file (rio's wctl.c, Qwctl): a program writes it what
 * the menu does with the mouse, a command a write:
 *
 *   new [-r minx miny maxx maxy] [-at where width height] [-max]
 *       [-hide] [-scroll] [-noscroll] [-label word] [-cd dir] [-hold]
 *       [-desk] [-panel] [-popup] [-edge top|bottom|left|right size]
 *       [command]
 *   resize, move    with -r, or -minx n -miny n -maxx n -maxy n -dx n
 *                   -dy n (a number after + or -: that much more or
 *                   less than it is)
 *   top, bottom, current, hide, unhide, delete, scroll, noscroll
 *   exit            the window system ends, as by its menu's Exit
 *
 * each but new and exit about the window whose file it is, or the one
 * -id n says. -at and -max say a place in what the screen has for
 * windows, whatever its size, which a script cannot compute (rc has no
 * arithmetic): where is nw, n, ne, w, c, e, sw, s or se; new, resize
 * and move take them. new -hold: its window stays when its command
 * ends. new -desk, -panel, -popup: its layer (Window.layer), a desk on
 * the whole screen if nothing else is said. -edge: along that side of
 * what the screen has, that many pixels deep; a panel so placed takes
 * that much from what windows are given. A read is the window's rectangle and what it is: four numbers
 * as the kernel's files say them, then current or notcurrent, hidden
 * or visible, and for a window of a layer, the layer's name: desk,
 * panel or popup.
 *
 * Not rio's: -at, -max, -label, -hold, the layers, -edge, exit. Not here: -pid, set; a read does not wait for the window to
 * change; a command is done after the write is answered, so what it
 * cannot do (a window that is not there, a rectangle too small) is not
 * said to its writer. *)

type verb = New | Resize | Move | Top | Bottom | Current | Hide | Unhide | Delete | Scroll | Noscroll | Exit

type command = {
  verb : verb;
  (* the rectangle wanted, from the one the window has (a new one's:
   * the window system's choice) *)
  place : Rectangle.t -> Rectangle.t;
  (* or (-at, -max) from what the screen has for windows, whatever it had *)
  area : (Rectangle.t -> Rectangle.t) option;
  hidden : bool;                (* new -hide *)
  scrolling : bool option;      (* new -scroll, -noscroll *)
  id : int option;              (* -id: another window than the file's *)
  arg : string;                 (* new's command: "" for rc itself *)
  label : string;               (* new -label: "" for its command's name *)
  cd : string;                  (* new -cd: "" for the window system's directory *)
  hold : bool;                  (* new -hold: it stays when its command ends *)
  layer : Window.layer;         (* new -desk, -panel, -popup *)
}

(* new, nothing else said: what the menu's New asks *)
val plain : command

(* a write's text; P9_server.Error with rio's words when it is no command *)
val parse : string -> command

(* The commands written, for the window system's thread, which alone
 * changes the windows there are: each with the window whose file was
 * written, none for the wctl of no window (the root of the window
 * system's files: Fileserver). The file server does not wait for it (a
 * menu may be open): a thread a command carries it. *)
val requests : (Window.t option * command) Event.channel

(* a write of a wctl file: parsed and given to that thread *)
val written : Window.t option -> string -> unit
(* a window's command ended: asks for its window to be deleted *)
val ended : Window.t -> unit

val wctl : Device.t
windows/rio/Window.ml
10887
(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Window.mli *)

(* (the two types are Window.mli's: said once, there) *)
type layer = [%mli]
type message = [%mli]
type t = [%mli]

let width = 4      (* the border's, as rio's *)

let pointer : Mouse.state ref = ref { Mouse.pos = Point.zero; buttons = 0; msec = 0; resized = false }

(* (a window's image has another name when it is another image: its
 * number; noborder, as Plan 9 says it: its program draws in all of it) *)
let pid = ref 0
let name (w : t) = Printf.sprintf "%swindow.%d.%d.%d" (if w.layer = Normal then "" else "noborder.") !pid w.id w.image.id
(* the text's rectangle: inside the border, and 2 pixels more *)
let text_r (w : t) = Rectangle.inset w.image.r (width + 2)
let in_bar (w : t) (p : Point.t) = Terminal.in_bar (text_r w) p
let on_border (w : t) (p : Point.t) = w.layer = Normal && Rectangle.contains w.image.r p && not (Rectangle.contains (Rectangle.inset w.image.r width) p)

let text (w : t) = Terminal.contents w.text
let note : (t -> string -> unit) ref = ref (fun _ _ -> ())
let restack : (t -> unit) ref = ref (fun _ -> ())

(* (a window deleted has no thread to take it: what its program does on
 * the way out, its mouse file closed, must not stop the file server.
 * Threads are cooperative: nothing runs between the test and the send) *)
let send (w : t) m = if not w.gone then Event.sync (Event.send w.inbox m)

(* The thread: the window's state is its variables. *)
let run (w : t) desk =
  let d = w.image.display in
  (* the line being typed; the lines typed and not read, and what a read
   * left of one; the reads that wait for a line *)
  let typing = Buffer.create 80 and lines = Queue.create () and rest = ref "" and readers = Queue.create () in
  (* a program that draws here: the keys as they come; the mouse's last
   * change not read yet, the reads that wait for one *)
  let raw = ref false and moved = ref None and mouse_readers = Queue.create () in
  (* (its window changed, and it was not told yet: its next mouse read says r) *)
  let reshaped = ref false in
  (* the keys held: the kernel's messages for a program that reads the
   * window's kbd file (a game), kept until read; the reads that wait *)
  let held = Queue.create () and held_readers = Queue.create () and reads_held = ref false in
  let rec serve_held () =
    if not (Queue.is_empty held) && not (Queue.is_empty held_readers) then begin
      if (Queue.take held_readers) (Queue.peek held) then ignore (Queue.take held);
      serve_held ()
    end in
  (* the border: a blue for the window that has the keyboard, pale for
   * the others (ix's colours: rio's are a grey green and a pale one) *)
  let border current_ =
    w.current <- current_;
    if w.layer = Normal then begin
      let c = Display.color d (if current_ then Display.rgb 0x33 0x66 0x99 else Display.rgb 0xb8 0xcc 0xe0) in
      Draw.border w.image w.image.r width c;
      Display.free c
    end in
  (* a read that waits answered by a line (what it does not take of it is the next read's) *)
  let rec serve () =
    if not (Queue.is_empty readers) && (!rest <> "" || not (Queue.is_empty lines)) then begin
      let reply, count = Queue.take readers in
      let line = if !rest <> "" then !rest else Queue.peek lines in
      let n = min count (String.length line) in
      (* (a reader that is gone, its program ended with its read waiting,
       * takes nothing: the line is the next reader's) *)
      if reply (String.sub line 0 n) then begin
        if !rest = "" then ignore (Queue.take lines);
        rest := String.sub line n (String.length line - n)
      end;
      serve ()
    end in
  (* /dev/mouse's line: m, then four numbers of 12 characters *)
  let serve_mouse () =
    match !moved with
    | Some (m : Mouse.state) when not (Queue.is_empty mouse_readers) ->
        moved := None;
        let letter = if !reshaped then 'r' else 'm' in
        reshaped := false;
        ignore ((Queue.take mouse_readers) (Printf.sprintf "%c%11d %11d %11d %11d " letter m.pos.x m.pos.y m.buttons m.msec))
    | _ -> () in
  (* a key typed: shown, and kept until Enter makes the line (Backspace
   * takes one back, Ctrl-U all, Ctrl-D ends the input) *)
  (* (a character is its bytes: the last one typed is taken back whole) *)
  let back () =
    let s = Buffer.contents typing in
    Buffer.truncate typing (String.length (Utf8.sub s 0 (Utf8.length s - 1))); Terminal.erase w.text in
  let key k =
    match k.[0] with
    | '\n' | '\r' -> Terminal.put w.text "\n"; Queue.add (Buffer.contents typing ^ "\n") lines; Buffer.clear typing
    | '\b' -> if Buffer.length typing > 0 then back ()
    | '\021' -> while Buffer.length typing > 0 do back () done
    | '\004' -> Queue.add (Buffer.contents typing) lines; Buffer.clear typing
    (* Delete: its processes interrupted. And Control-C, which is what a
     * hand from anywhere else types (the author, 2026-10-13, of play in
     * a window: "Ctrl-C in the windows does not interrupt play"); Plan
     * 9 has Delete alone, and Control-C is no key of a line's editing *)
    | '\127' | '\003' -> !note w "interrupt"
    (* (not the keyboard's own keys, Plan 9's runes from 0xF000: Home, Insert...) *)
    | c when c >= ' ' && not (let n = Utf8.code k in n >= 0xF000 && n < 0xF900) -> Buffer.add_string typing k; Terminal.put w.text k
    | _ -> () in
  (* the writes that wait, shown while the text's end is: one that does
   * not scroll holds them when it is full, until it is scrolled (not
   * when its program draws: the text is not what one sees) *)
  let writes = Queue.create () in
  let rec show () =
    if not (Queue.is_empty writes) && (Terminal.scrolling w.text || Terminal.at_end w.text || w.wants_mouse) then begin
      let text, reply = Queue.take writes in
      Terminal.put w.text text;
      ignore (reply "");
      show ()
    end in
  border (w.layer = Normal);
  let rec loop () =
    show ();
    Display.flush d;
    match Event.sync (Event.receive w.inbox) with
    | Keys keys ->
        if !raw then Queue.add (String.concat "" keys) lines
        else
          (* the arrows scroll, up and down; any other key is typed, at
           * the end *)
          List.iter (fun k ->
            if k = Keyboard.up then Terminal.scroll w.text (Terminal.half w.text)
            else if k = Keyboard.down then Terminal.scroll w.text (- (Terminal.half w.text))
            else begin Terminal.scroll w.text (-100000); key k end) keys;
        serve (); loop ()
    | Read (reply, count) -> Queue.add (reply, count) readers; serve (); loop ()
    | Wrote (text, reply) -> Queue.add (text, reply) writes; loop ()
    | Scroll on -> Terminal.set_scrolling w.text on; loop ()
    | Raw on -> raw := on; loop ()
    (* the mouse: the program's that reads it; else the text's own *)
    | Moved m -> (if w.wants_mouse then begin moved := Some m; serve_mouse () end else Terminal.mouse w.text m); loop ()
    | Mouse_read reply -> Queue.add reply mouse_readers; serve_mouse (); loop ()
    (* (kept for a program that has the file open: the others' would only pile up) *)
    | Held m -> if !reads_held then begin Queue.add m held; serve_held () end; loop ()
    | Held_read reply -> Queue.add reply held_readers; serve_held (); loop ()
    | Held_file on -> reads_held := on; Queue.clear held; loop ()
    (* (the first state a program reads has no button down: [pointer] is
     * the last the windows' own loop saw, and the menu and the sweep
     * that made this window read the mouse themselves, so it could
     * still say the right button of "New": mini-stats then opened its
     * menu by itself and waited in it, drawing nothing, until a click.
     * old: moved := Some !pointer) *)
    | Mouse_file true -> w.wants_mouse <- true; moved := Some { !pointer with buttons = 0 }; loop ()
    | Mouse_file false ->
        (* the program that drew here is done: the inside of the border as the text has it *)
        w.wants_mouse <- false;
        w.cursor <- None;
        let white = Display.color d Display.white in
        Draw.fill w.image (Rectangle.inset w.image.r width) white;
        Display.free white;
        Terminal.redraw w.text;
        loop ()
    | Label l -> w.label <- l; loop ()
    | Cursor c -> w.cursor <- c; loop ()
    | Front current ->
        border current;
        (* (the keyboard is another window's: no key is held here any more,
         * whatever was when it left) *)
        if not current && !reads_held then begin Queue.add "K\000" held; serve_held () end;
        loop ()
    | Reshape r ->
        (* moved: the same image, elsewhere (the kernel moves its pixels);
         * another size: another image, the text in it again *)
        let old = w.image in
        if Rectangle.dx r = Rectangle.dx old.r && Rectangle.dy r = Rectangle.dy old.r then begin
          w.image <- Display.origin old r.min r.min;
          w.text <- Terminal.reshape w.text w.image (Rectangle.inset r (width + 2))
        end
        else begin
          w.image <- Display.window desk r Display.white;
          Display.free old;
          Display.name w.image (name w);
          w.text <- Terminal.reshape w.text w.image (Rectangle.inset r (width + 2));
          !restack w
        end;
        (* (changed while hidden: its new place, kept off the screen) *)
        if w.hidden then w.image <- Display.origin w.image w.image.r.min (Point.v 20000 20000);
        border w.current;
        (* a program that draws here is told, at its next mouse read *)
        if w.wants_mouse then begin reshaped := true; moved := Some !pointer; serve_mouse () end;
        loop ()
    | Hide on ->
        (* off the screen: its place there far away, its own coordinates kept *)
        w.hidden <- on;
        w.image <- Display.origin w.image w.image.r.min (if on then Point.v 20000 20000 else w.image.r.min);
        (* (a menu shown again starts anew: its program is told) *)
        if w.layer <> Normal && w.wants_mouse then begin reshaped := true; moved := Some { !pointer with buttons = 0 }; serve_mouse () end;
        loop ()
    | Quit -> Display.free w.image; Display.flush d in
  loop ()

let make desk id r font layer =
  let image = Display.window desk r Display.white in
  let w = { id; layer; image; text = Terminal.make image (Rectangle.inset image.r (width + 2)) font; hidden = false; current = true; label = Printf.sprintf "rc %d" id; cursor = None; inbox = Event.new_channel (); pid = 0; wants_mouse = false; thread = None; ends = false; cons_opens = 0; gone = false } in
  Display.name image (name w);
  (* (no thread left for it: no window) *)
  (match Thread.create (fun () -> run w desk) () with
   | t -> w.thread <- Some t
   | exception Failure m -> Display.free image; failwith m);
  w

let quit (w : t) = send w Quit; w.gone <- true; Option.iter Thread.join w.thread
windows/rio/Window.mli

(* A window (Plan 9's rio; xix's Window and Threads_window): a
 * rectangle of the screen with a border and its text, the process
 * that runs in it, and what goes between the two.
 *
 * A window is a thread (Rob Pike's design for rio: each component
 * a process): it waits for messages on its channel and is the only one
 * to change its text and its state. The others send it what happens:
 * the window system the keys and the mouse, the file server what the
 * window's process asks of its files. A console's read that finds no
 * line typed is simply not answered yet: the thread keeps its reply
 * and goes on waiting for messages.
 *
 *     the window system --Keys, Moved, Reshape...--.
 *                                                  v
 *                                    the window's thread:
 *     the file server ---Read, Wrote of cons--->   one message at a
 *     (a 9P request of the window's process)       time, its text and
 *                                                  state its own
 *
 * design:
 * No lock. A window's state is touched by one thread, and whoever
 * wants it changed sends a message, taken when the thread is ready
 * for one: the order the messages are taken in is the order things
 * happen, and there is nothing to forget to protect. A window
 * system written as one loop over all the events must instead be a
 * state machine that remembers, for each window, what it was in the
 * middle of (a read waiting, a menu open, a rectangle being swept);
 * with a thread a window, that memory is where the thread is in its
 * code. This is Hoare's communicating sequential processes (1978), which Pike
 * took through his languages (Newsqueak, where the first such
 * window system was written; Alef, Plan 9's; then Go, 2009, whose
 * goroutines and channels are these) and the thread library rio
 * uses in C. Here they are Thread and Event's channels, a send
 * waiting for its receive ([send]). *)

(* Where it is among the others (not rio's; plan_desktop.md): most are
 * Normal. A Desk is below them all, a Panel above them all, a Popup above
 * the panels and hidden by a press anywhere else. These three have no
 * border, never have the keyboard, and take the mouse without coming to
 * the front: what a desktop's wallpaper, bar and menu need. *)
type layer = Normal | Desk | Panel | Popup

type message =
  | Keys of string list                (* typed, the window in front: characters, each its bytes *)
  | Moved of Mouse.state                (* the mouse, in the window: its program's when it reads
                                           the mouse, else the text's (the scroll bar, selecting) *)
  | Read of (string -> bool) * int      (* its console read: how to answer (false: the reader is
                                           gone, nothing was taken), how many bytes at most *)
  | Wrote of string * (string -> bool)  (* its console written: the text, and how to answer the
                                           write (with "") once it is shown: a window that does
                                           not scroll holds it while its end is not shown *)
  | Scroll of bool                      (* its text follows what is written, or not (the menu, wctl) *)
  | Raw of bool                         (* consctl's rawon, rawoff: the keys as they are typed *)
  | Mouse_file of bool                  (* its mouse file opened, or closed *)
  | Mouse_read of (string -> bool)      (* a read of it: answered at the mouse's next change *)
  | Held of string                      (* the keys down changed (/dev/kbd's message), the window in front *)
  | Held_read of (string -> bool)       (* a read of its kbd file: answered at the next change *)
  | Held_file of bool                   (* its kbd file opened, or closed: the changes are kept
                                           for it from then (a key may come before its first read) *)
  | Label of string                     (* its label written: its name is its program's to say *)
  | Cursor of Cursor.t option           (* its cursor written: the mouse's picture while in it *)
  | Front of bool                       (* it has the keyboard, or lost it: the border's colour *)
  | Reshape of Rectangle.t              (* moved (the same size), or made another size *)
  | Hide of bool                        (* off the screen, or back *)
  | Quit                                (* deleted: its image freed, its thread ends *)

type t = {
  id : int;
  layer : layer;
  (* (its image is another when its size changes: the thread's to
   * change, the window system's to read, as [hidden]) *)
  mutable image : Display.image;
  (* its text (another when its size changes): the thread's to change;
   * the window system calls its menu on the middle button
   * (Terminal.menu, which reads what is selected there), as rio's
   * mouse thread calls button2menu on a window *)
  mutable text : Terminal.t;
  mutable hidden : bool;
  (* it has the keyboard (the thread's to change: Front) *)
  mutable current : bool;
  (* what the menu calls it when hidden: "rc 3", until its program
   * writes its label (the thread's to change, as its cursor) *)
  mutable label : string;
  (* its program's cursor, shown while the mouse is in the window: the
   * program's until it writes another (less than a cursor: the arrow)
   * or closes its mouse file. rio's lasts as long as the cursor file
   * is open; ix's Cursor.set opens, writes and closes *)
  mutable cursor : Cursor.t option;
  inbox : message Event.channel;
  mutable pid : int;
  (* its program reads the mouse: the window system gives it the mouse
   * in the window, buttons and all (said by the thread, read by the
   * window system) *)
  mutable wants_mouse : bool;
  mutable thread : Thread.t option;
  (* it goes when its console is closed by all who have it open (its
   * command and what that started): a window made with a command *)
  mutable ends : bool;
  (* those: the file server's, which alone counts them *)
  mutable cons_opens : int;
  (* deleted: a message for it is dropped *)
  mutable gone : bool;
}

(* a window on the desktop, and its thread started; Failure when there
 * are too many threads (Thread.create's) *)
val make : Display.desktop -> int -> Rectangle.t -> Font.t -> layer -> t
(* a message for it: the sender waits until the thread takes it *)
val send : t -> message -> unit
(* Quit sent, and its thread ended *)
val quit : t -> unit

(* rio's pid, in each window's name (set by Rio.main, which holds Cap.env) *)
val pid : int ref

(* its image's name, for the program in it to draw there (Display.named) *)
val name : t -> string
(* whether a point is in its text's scroll bar: a press there is the
 * window's, not the window system's (rio's mouse thread asks the same
 * of a window's scroll rectangle) *)
val in_bar : t -> Point.t -> bool
(* its text, all of it (its text file) *)
val text : t -> string
(* whether a point is on its border: a handle, the window system's
 * even when the window's program reads the mouse (rio's winborder) *)
val on_border : t -> Point.t -> bool
(* a note for a window's processes (the Delete key, or Control-C: "interrupt"): the
 * window system says how *)
val note : (t -> string -> unit) ref
(* the layers put back in order, a window having been made another size:
 * its new image, the kernel puts in front of all (Wm says how) *)
val restack : (t -> unit) ref
(* where the mouse is, as the window system last saw it (a mouse file's first read) *)
val pointer : Mouse.state ref

(* Claude Code
 * Copyright (C) 2026 Yoann Padioleau. LGPL 2.1: see license.txt. *)

(* See Wm.mli *)

let windows : Window.t list ref = ref []
(* those of a layer, in no order: [windows] and what is done with it are
 * what they were without any *)
let layered : Window.t list ref = ref []
let ids = ref 0

let all () = !layered @ !windows
let find id = List.find_opt (fun (w : Window.t) -> w.id = id) (all ())
let current () = match !windows with w :: _ when not w.hidden -> Some w | _ -> None

let of_layer l = List.filter (fun (w : Window.t) -> w.layer = l) !layered
let shown_at (p : Point.t) (w : Window.t) = not w.hidden && Rectangle.contains w.image.r p
(* a popup or a panel there, over any window *)
let above (p : Point.t) =
  match List.find_opt (shown_at p) (of_layer Window.Popup) with
  | Some w -> Some w
  | None -> List.find_opt (shown_at p) (of_layer Window.Panel)

let at (p : Point.t) =
  match above p with
  | Some _ -> None
  | None -> List.find_opt (shown_at p) !windows

let layer_at (p : Point.t) =
  match above p, at p with
  | Some w, _ -> Some w
  | None, Some _ -> None
  | None, None -> List.find_opt (shown_at p) (of_layer Window.Desk)

let popups () = List.filter (fun (w : Window.t) -> not w.hidden) (of_layer Window.Popup)
let hidden () = List.filter (fun (w : Window.t) -> w.hidden) !windows

(* the panels, then the popups, back on top *)
let on_top () =
  List.iter (fun (w : Window.t) -> Display.top w.image) (of_layer Window.Panel);
  List.iter (fun (w : Window.t) -> Display.top w.image) (of_layer Window.Popup)

let restack (w : Window.t) = if w.layer = Window.Desk then Display.bottom w.image else on_top ()

let work_of (screen : Rectangle.t) (taken : Rectangle.t list) : Rectangle.t =
  List.fold_left (fun (work : Rectangle.t) (r : Rectangle.t) ->
      if r.min.x <= work.min.x && r.max.x >= work.max.x then
        if r.min.y <= work.min.y && r.max.y > work.min.y then Rectangle.v work.min.x r.max.y work.max.x work.max.y
        else if r.max.y >= work.max.y && r.min.y < work.max.y then Rectangle.v work.min.x work.min.y work.max.x r.min.y
        else work
      else if r.min.y <= work.min.y && r.max.y >= work.max.y then
        if r.min.x <= work.min.x && r.max.x > work.min.x then Rectangle.v r.max.x work.min.y work.max.x work.max.y
        else if r.max.x >= work.max.x && r.min.x < work.max.x then Rectangle.v work.min.x work.min.y r.min.x work.max.y
        else work
      else work)
    screen taken

let work screen =
  work_of screen (List.filter_map (fun (w : Window.t) -> if w.hidden then None else Some w.image.r) (of_layer Window.Panel))

let border (p : Point.t) : (Window.t * int) option =
  match at p with
  | Some w when Window.on_border w p ->
      let part x lo hi = if x < lo + 20 then 0 else if x > hi - 20 then 2 else 1 in
      let r = w.image.r in
      Some (w, 3 * part p.y r.min.y r.max.y + part p.x r.min.x r.max.x)
  | _ -> None

let front (w : Window.t) =
  (match !windows with old :: _ when old != w -> Window.send old (Window.Front false) | _ -> ());
  windows := w :: List.filter (fun x -> x != w) !windows;
  Display.top w.image;
  on_top ();
  Window.send w (Window.Front true)

let fits r = Rectangle.dx r >= 100 && Rectangle.dy r >= 50
(* (a panel may be thin) *)
let fits_layer (l : Window.layer) r = if l = Window.Normal then fits r else Rectangle.dx r > 0 && Rectangle.dy r > 0

(* (a command's label: its name, the first word without its directory) *)
let label_of (c : Wctl.command) =
  if c.label <> "" then c.label
  else if c.arg = "" then ""
  else Filename.basename (List.hd (String.split_on_char ' ' c.arg))

let create caps desk font srv r (c : Wctl.command) =
  incr ids;
  match Window.make desk !ids r font c.layer with
  | w ->
      if c.layer = Window.Normal then front w
      else begin layered := w :: !layered; restack w end;
      if label_of c <> "" then Window.send w (Window.Label (label_of c));
      w.ends <- c.arg <> "" && not c.hold;
      Processes_winshell.start caps w srv ~cd:c.cd c.arg;
      Some w
  | exception Failure m -> prerr_string ("rio: no new window: " ^ m ^ "\n"); None

(* (one of a layer keeps its place among the layers, and the keyboard
 * stays where it is) *)
let raise_ (w : Window.t) = if w.layer = Window.Normal then front w else restack w

let reshape (w : Window.t) r = raise_ w; Window.send w (Window.Reshape r)

let delete caps (w : Window.t) =
  Processes_winshell.note caps w "hangup";
  windows := List.filter (fun x -> x != w) !windows;
  layered := List.filter (fun x -> x != w) !layered;
  Window.quit w;
  if w.layer = Window.Normal then (match !windows with next :: _ -> front next | [] -> ())

let hide (w : Window.t) =
  Window.send w (Window.Hide true);
  if w.layer = Window.Normal then begin
    windows := List.filter (fun x -> x != w) !windows @ [ w ];
    (match !windows with next :: _ when not next.hidden -> front next | _ -> ())
  end

let show (w : Window.t) = Window.send w (Window.Hide false); raise_ w

let desks_down () = List.iter (fun (d : Window.t) -> Display.bottom d.image) (of_layer Window.Desk)

let bottom (w : Window.t) =
  let shown, hidden = List.partition (fun (x : Window.t) -> not x.hidden) (List.filter (fun x -> x != w) !windows) in
  windows := shown @ [ w ] @ hidden;
  Display.bottom w.image;
  desks_down ();
  Window.send w (Window.Front false);
  (match !windows with next :: _ when next != w && not next.hidden -> front next | _ -> ())

(* (rio's newrect) *)
let news = ref 0

let control caps make (screen : Rectangle.t) (w : Window.t option) (c : Wctl.command) =
  let room : Rectangle.t = work screen in
  let placed r = match c.area with Some f -> f room | None -> c.place r in
  match (match c.id with Some id -> find id | None -> (match w with Some w when List.memq w (all ()) -> Some w | _ -> None)), c.verb with
  (* (a new one needs no window: the root's wctl, one that has gone) *)
  | _, Wctl.New ->
      let x = room.min.x + 32 + (16 * !news) and y = room.min.y + 32 + (16 * !news) in
      news := (!news + 1) mod 10;
      let wide = min 600 (Rectangle.dx room - 8) and high = min 400 (Rectangle.dy room - 8) in
      (* (so far down the area that it would go under a panel: where it fits) *)
      let y = if y + high > room.max.y then room.min.y else y in
      let r = match c.layer, c.area with
        | Window.Desk, None -> c.place screen
        | _ -> placed (Rectangle.v x y (x + wide) (y + high)) in
      if fits_layer c.layer r then
        Option.iter (fun fresh ->
            Option.iter (fun on -> Window.send fresh (Window.Scroll on)) c.scrolling;
            if c.hidden then hide fresh) (make r c)
  | None, _ -> ()
  | Some w, _ -> (
      match c.verb with
      | Wctl.New | Wctl.Exit -> ()
      | Wctl.Resize -> let r = placed w.image.r in if fits_layer w.layer r && r <> w.image.r then reshape w r
      | Wctl.Move ->
          (* (its place only: the size is the window's) *)
          let r : Rectangle.t = placed w.image.r in
          let r = Rectangle.v r.min.x r.min.y (r.min.x + Rectangle.dx w.image.r) (r.min.y + Rectangle.dy w.image.r) in
          if r <> w.image.r then reshape w r
      | Wctl.Top | Wctl.Current -> if not w.hidden then raise_ w
      | Wctl.Bottom -> if not w.hidden && w.layer = Window.Normal then bottom w
      | Wctl.Hide -> if not w.hidden then hide w
      | Wctl.Unhide -> if w.hidden then show w
      | Wctl.Delete -> delete caps w
      | Wctl.Scroll -> Window.send w (Window.Scroll true)
      | Wctl.Noscroll -> Window.send w (Window.Scroll false))

(* The window manager (rio's wm.c and wind.c's lists; xix's Wm and
 * Globals): the windows there are, which is in front, and what the
 * menu does to one. The window system's thread calls these; a
 * window's own state is changed by messages to its thread. *)

(* the windows, the one in front first; the first has the keyboard
 * (the hidden ones are last) *)
val windows : Window.t list ref
(* all, those of a layer too (Window.layer), which [windows] does not have *)
val all : unit -> Window.t list
(* the one of a number (a mount's spec) *)
val find : int -> Window.t option
(* the one that has the keyboard, when it shows *)
val current : unit -> Window.t option
(* the normal one a point is in, the one in front of the others there;
 * none when a popup or a panel is there, over it *)
val at : Point.t -> Window.t option
(* the one of a layer a point is in: a popup, a panel, or a desk when no
 * window is there *)
val layer_at : Point.t -> Window.t option
(* the popups that show *)
val popups : unit -> Window.t list
(* the layers back in order, a window having a new image *)
val restack : Window.t -> unit
(* [work_of screen taken]: what is left of the screen for windows when
 * the rectangles [taken] are panels: a panel along a whole side takes
 * its depth off that side, any other takes nothing *)
val work_of : Rectangle.t -> Rectangle.t list -> Rectangle.t
(* the window whose border a point is on, and which of its corners and
 * sides, three by three from the top left (rio's whichcorner: a
 * corner is the 20 pixels at a side's end) *)
val border : Point.t -> (Window.t * int) option
(* the ones off the screen, as the menu lists them *)
val hidden : unit -> Window.t list

(* in front, with the keyboard; the one that had it told *)
val front : Window.t -> unit
(* whether a rectangle is one a window may have (100 by 50, at least) *)
val fits : Rectangle.t -> bool
(* [create caps desk font srv r c]: a window there, in front, rc started
 * in it, or new's command, as [c] says ([srv]:
 * Processes_winshell.start's); none, and said on the console, when
 * there are too many *)
val create : < Cap.chdir; Cap.fork; Cap.exec; Cap.mount; Cap.bind; Cap.open_in; Cap.open_out; .. > -> Display.desktop -> Font.t -> string -> Rectangle.t -> Wctl.command -> Window.t option
(* in front, and in another rectangle: moved (the same size), or made
 * another size *)
val reshape : Window.t -> Rectangle.t -> unit
(* its processes told to end (hangup), its thread too; the next one in front *)
val delete : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> Window.t -> unit
(* off the screen (the keyboard to the next one that shows), and back *)
val hide : Window.t -> unit
val show : Window.t -> unit
(* behind the others, the keyboard to the one then in front *)
val bottom : Window.t -> unit

(* [control caps make screen w c]: a command written to w's wctl file
 * (none: the root's), done ([make]: create, but for the rectangle and
 * the command;
 * [screen]: the screen's rectangle; less what panels take, where a new
 * window with no rectangle said is put, 600 by 400 at most, each a
 * little further than the last, as rio's). What cannot be done is not: a window
 * that is not there, a rectangle too small. top and current are one
 * here: the window in front has the keyboard *)
val control : < Cap.open_out; .. > -> (Rectangle.t -> Wctl.command -> Window.t option) -> Rectangle.t -> Window.t option -> Wctl.command -> unit

// examples/: what the code map says of it
// a GUI program on the playground: Model-View-Update down to its
// Cap.main, and its layout (places: the panel arranged in the window)
local gui(file, heart='def:places', role='the panel laid out: a box a slot', say='where the widgets are', model='type:model', init='def:initial') = {
  local at(a) = file + ':' + a,
  name: 'Model-View-Update, and its widgets: ' + std.split(heart, ':')[1],
  bones: (if model == null then [] else [{ at: at(model), role: 'the state' }])
    + (if init == null then [] else [{ at: at(init), role: 'the first state' }]) + [
    { at: at('def:update'), role: 'a frame: the widgets answered, a new model' },
    { at: at('def:view'), role: 'the widgets painted from the model' },
    { at: at('def:app'), role: 'the app: the three given to game' },
    { at: at('code:"Cap.main"'), role: 'the program: the app run, with the capabilities' },
    { at: at(heart), role: role },
  ],
  joints: (if model == null || init == null then [] else [{ from: at(init), to: at(model) }])
    + (if init == null then [] else [{ from: at('def:app'), to: at(init), say: 'starts from' }]) + [
    { from: at('def:app'), to: at('def:update'), say: 'steps with' },
    { from: at('def:app'), to: at('def:view'), say: 'draws with' },
    { from: at('code:"Cap.main"'), to: at('def:app'), say: 'runs' },
    { from: at('def:update'), to: at(heart), say: say },
  ],
};

    { from: at('def:app'), to: '../lib_playground/ways/Bigbang.ml:def:big_bang', say: 'built by' },
  ],
};

    { at: at('def:update'), role: 'a frame: model -> model' },
    { at: at('def:view'), role: 'a picture: model -> shapes' },
    { at: at('def:app'), role: 'the app: the three given to game' },
    { at: at('code:"Cap.main"'), role: 'the program: the app run, with the capabilities' },
    { at: at(heart), role: role },
  ],
  joints: [
    { from: at('def:initial_model'), to: at('type:model') },
    { from: at('type:model'), to: at('def:update'), say: 'stepped' },
    { from: at('def:update'), to: at('type:model'), say: 'the next state' },
    { from: at('type:model'), to: at('def:view'), say: 'drawn' },
    { from: at('def:app'), to: at('def:update'), say: 'steps with' },
    { from: at('def:app'), to: at('def:view'), say: 'draws with' },
    { from: at('code:"Cap.main"'), to: at('def:app'), say: 'runs' },
    { from: at(from), to: at(heart), say: say },
  ],
};

    { at: at("type:model"), role: "the state" },
    { at: at("def:initial_model"), role: "the first state" },
    { at: at("def:update"), role: "a frame: model -> model" },
    { at: at("def:view"), role: "a picture: model -> shapes" },
    { at: at("def:app"), role: "the app: the three given to the Playground" },
    { at: at("code:\"Cap.main\""), role: "the program: the app run, with the capabilities" },
    { at: at(heart), role: role },
  ],
  joints: [
    { from: at("def:initial_model"), to: at("type:model") },
    { from: at("type:model"), to: at("def:update"), say: "stepped" },
    { from: at("def:update"), to: at("type:model"), say: "the next state" },
    { from: at("type:model"), to: at("def:view"), say: "drawn" },
    { from: at("def:app"), to: at("def:update"), say: "steps with" },
    { from: at("def:app"), to: at("def:view"), say: "draws with" },
    { from: at("code:\"Cap.main\""), to: at("def:app"), say: "runs" },
    { from: at(from), to: at(heart), say: say },
  ],
};

// kernels/lib_machine/pi1/: what the code map says of it (the code map is tinybox
// codemap, in ~/github/ocaml-elm-playground; its guidelines:
// docs/claude_notes/codemapconfig_guidelines.md there)
//
// Not sources to the map, but the board's other half: start.s, the ARM
// assembly OCaml cannot say -- _start (the boot at physical addresses,
// the kernel's 1MB sections, the MMU on, the jump high), the vectors

// the template's joints, each given what flows along it
local with_says(s, says) = s + {
  joints: [s.joints[i] + { say: says[i] } for i in std.range(0, std.length(s.joints) - 1)],
};

skeletons.libsonnet

// The skeletons ix's programs share, for the code map's configs
// (the code map: ~/github/ocaml-elm-playground's tinybox codemap, its
// docs/claude_notes/codemapconfig_guidelines.md): a function of the
// files, its bones' anchors defaulting to the usual names. The shapes
// after cli are xix's (~/github/xix/skeletons.libsonnet), the same names.
{
  // a mini program: Main.ml runs Cap.main, which calls its CLI's main,
  // which parses the command line and hands it to the program's core
  // ([core]: [anchor, role] pairs, the first called by the CLI, each the
  // next's caller)
  cli(name, core, main='Main.ml', cli='CLI.ml:def:main')::
    local bones = [[main, 'the program: Cap.main, the capabilities'], [cli, 'the command line: flags, arguments']] + core;
    {
      name: name,
      bones: [{ at: b[0], role: b[1] } for b in bones],
      joints: [{ from: bones[i][0], to: bones[i + 1][0] } for i in std.range(0, std.length(bones) - 2)],
    },

  // a chain: [anchor, role, say] each, the first calling (or handing
  // its data to) the second, ... -- a path across files (a compiler's
  // passes, a request's way down); the first step's say is unused
  chain(name, steps):: {
    name: name,
    bones: [{ at: s[0], role: s[1] } for s in steps],
    joints: [{ from: steps[i][0], to: steps[i + 1][0], say: steps[i + 1][2] } for i in std.range(0, std.length(steps) - 2)],
  },

  // a one-file program (a utility, a tiny program): its Cap.main and its
  // main in [file], then its core ([anchor, role, say] each, the first
  // called by main). Extend with bones+: and joints+: for a loop.
  onefile(name, file, core, main='def:main')::
    self.chain(name, [
      [file + ':code:"Cap.main"', 'the program: Cap.main, the capabilities', ''],
      [file + ':' + main, 'the command line: flags, arguments', 'the capabilities'],
    ] + core),

  // a module's own chain, its anchors in the file: [name, role, say]
  // each, a bare definition name (def:) in [file]
  module(file, name, steps)::
    self.chain(name, [[file + ':def:' + s[0], s[1], s[2]] for s in steps]),

  // a star: [center] calls each of [callees] ([anchor, role, say] each),
  // for a main calling ten initializations, a dispatcher its commands
  calls(name, center, center_role, callees):: {
    name: name,
    bones: [{ at: center, role: center_role }] + [{ at: c[0], role: c[1] } for c in callees],
    joints: [{ from: center, to: c[0], say: c[2] } for c in callees],
  },

  // a module's star: [center] (a bare name) calls each of [callees]
  // ([name, role, say] each), all defined in [file]
  module_calls(file, name, center, center_role, callees)::
    self.calls(name, file + ':def:' + center, center_role,
               [[file + ':def:' + c[0], c[1], c[2]] for c in callees]),

  // a loop dispatching events (a window's thread over Event.select, a
  // kernel's trap handler): the loop, then a bone per case, each an
  // [anchor, role, say] (a case is code: `code:"| Key"` reaches it); the
  // cases go back to the loop
  select(name, loop, loop_role, cases):: {
    name: name,
    bones: [{ at: loop, role: loop_role }] + [{ at: c[0], role: c[1] } for c in cases],
    joints: [{ from: loop, to: c[0], say: c[2] } for c in cases]
            + [{ from: c[0], to: loop, say: 'again' } for c in cases],
  },

  // a tiny program (tiny/): started by TinyLibSystem.main on the host or
  // on tiny-kernel, not Cap.main; its core as in onefile (written as a
  // local in tiny/'s config by the 2026-11-04 pass, lifted here)
  prog(name, file, core)::
    self.chain(name, [
      [file + ':code:"TinyLibSystem.main"', 'the program: TinyLibSystem.main, the host or tiny-kernel', ''],
      [file + ':def:main', 'the command line: -h, flags, files', 'the capabilities'],
    ] + core),

  // a lib_playground program (games/, examples/, apps/ on Playground):
  // Model-View-Update down to its `let () = Cap.main` (no def:main), and
  // its heart reached from [from] (view or update); written as a local
  // in five configs by the 2026-11-04 pass, lifted here
  mvu(file, heart, role, say, from='def:view'):: {
    local at(a) = file + ':' + a,
    name: 'Model-View-Update, and its heart: ' + std.split(heart, ':')[1],
    bones: [
      { at: at('type:model'), role: 'the state' },
      { at: at('def:initial_model'), role: 'the first state' },
      { at: at('def:update'), role: 'a frame: model -> model' },
      { at: at('def:view'), role: 'a picture: model -> shapes' },
      { at: at('def:app'), role: 'the app: the three given to game' },
      { at: at('code:"Cap.main"'), role: 'the program: the app run, with the capabilities' },
      { at: at(heart), role: role },
    ],
    joints: [
      { from: at('def:initial_model'), to: at('type:model') },
      { from: at('type:model'), to: at('def:update'), say: 'stepped' },
      { from: at('def:update'), to: at('type:model'), say: 'the next state' },
      { from: at('type:model'), to: at('def:view'), say: 'drawn' },
      { from: at('def:app'), to: at('def:update'), say: 'steps with' },
      { from: at('def:app'), to: at('def:view'), say: 'draws with' },
      { from: at('code:"Cap.main"'), to: at('def:app'), say: 'runs' },
      { from: at(from), to: at(heart), say: say },
    ],
  },

  // a directory's parts as whole units (a path each, no anchor): a
  // layered picture, [path, role] each, and joints [from, to, say]
  parts(name, bones, joints):: {
    name: name,
    bones: [{ at: b[0], role: b[1] } for b in bones],
    joints: [{ from: j[0], to: j[1], say: j[2] } for j in joints],
  },
}

// tiny/TinyKernel/host/: what the code map says of it (the code map:
// tinybox codemap, ~/github/ocaml-elm-playground; its guidelines:
// docs/claude_notes/codemapconfig_guidelines.md there). What
// tiny-machine and tiny-kernel give a tiny program, made by OCaml so

// tiny/TinyKernel/steps/t6/user/: what the code map says of it (the code map:
// tinybox codemap, ~/github/ocaml-elm-playground; its guidelines:

// and sys.tm (the system calls' stubs, assembly) are ../libc/'s;
// t6tests.c is a test, off the map. cat, echo, ls, mkdir, rm and wc
// were tiny-kernel's too once; tiny-kernel's are TinyUtilities.ml's now.

};
